english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because excess water prevents oxygen from reaching the roots, causing fungal pathogens to attack. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ ayashɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii baanyɛ atutua. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: How do I know when it is safe to sow my seeds when the early rains keep stopping and starting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ kpa ni ebɔi lɛ?

english: Planting too early after a brief rain can cause seeds to germinate and dry up if the rain stops for weeks. It is best to wait until the soil is thoroughly moist down to a few inches depth and local rainfall patterns become consistent.
ga: Dumɔ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo ko sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔ kpa otsii babaoo. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashɛ ŋwɛi ŋta fioo komɛi. ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ yaa nɔ daa.

english: Leaf curling is a defense mechanism. By rolling its leaves, the pepper plant reduces the amount of leaf surface exposed to the harsh sunlight, which helps it retain water and survive extreme heat.
ga: Baai lɛ ni abɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he. kɛtsɔ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ Pepper tsei lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai lɛ anɔ ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shi ni edamɔɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa

english: Tomato flowers often drop off due to temperature stress, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When the plant gets stressed by heat or lacks steady water, it sheds flowers to save energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hewɔ. Beni tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa loo nu ni bɛ daa lɛ mli. Fɔfɔi baagbee shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to make leaves green and grow fast. It can also happen if heavy rains have washed nutrients out of the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is ready for harvesting under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is maturing when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ edara kɛji baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Why should I plant my rice seeds in straight rows instead of scattering them by hand across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja moŋ fe ni mikɛ minine baadu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting rice in straight rows makes it much easier to weed and apply fertilizer. It also ensures every rice plant gets enough sunlight, air, and space to grow strong stems and full grain heads.
ga: Omɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa. Ekwɛɔ hu koni ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa tso aná hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmãa tso ni mli wa kɛ dumɔwui ayitsei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to manufacture food that gets stored in the tuber underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to sun and preventing leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii ni ato yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ha ni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ ni etsi foliar helai anaa.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sunlight. Taller trees provide essential shade and retain soil moisture, protecting young cocoa plants until their leaves grow tough enough to handle direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaai lɛ amli baawa bɔ ni sa ni hulu la baashɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and lock it into the soil through their roots. When the crop is harvested, that natural nitrogen remains in the soil to feed your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my maize plants getting small ragged holes in the leaves and missing their center shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni ŋmei ko bɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm. They hide in the central funnel of the maize plant during the day and eat the tender growing leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni oye baai bibii lɛ dani amɛje kpo

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops each year even when I plant at the right time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ be ni sa mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops pull food out of the soil every season. If you continuously plant the same crop on the same land without adding manure, organic matter, or allowing the land to rest, the soil becomes exhausted of essential nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛji akɛ oya nɔ odu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, loo ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe lɛ fataaa he lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn pale yellow when they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ beni eji gbekɛ fioo lɛ?

english: Pale yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the primary food maize needs to grow green and strong. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea at the right time restores the deep green color and helps the plant produce large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo urea tsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔtɔi wuji.

english: Why is it bad if I put too many maize seeds in one small hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa babaoo wo bu bibioo kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting too many seeds in one spot forces the young plants to compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks that produce very small cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa loo amɛwoɔ ŋmeii kwraa.

english: Why do some of my maize stalks grow tall but fail to produce any cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ shi amɛwooo ŋmeii ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Maize stalks often fail to form cobs if they do not get enough sunlight, suffer from severe dry spells during the flowering stage, or are planted too close together without enough plant nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee ŋmeii kɛji amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Hɔmɔ ni naa wa ni anaa yɛ fɔfɔii akwɛmɔ be mli loo ni adu yɛ he kome tsɔ ni tso mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli

english: Why do high-yield certified maize seeds give better results than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specially bred by crop scientists to resist local pests, withstand dry weather, and grow uniformly large cobs. Seeds saved from past harvests lose these special traits over time, leading to smaller yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii sɔrɔtoi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nilelɔi amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii wuji daa Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baafite sui nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: How can I stop small insects like weevils from destroying my harvested maize in the storehouse?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ŋmãa ni mikpaa yɛ mi nitoohe lɛ naa?

english: Weevils thrive when maize is stored while still damp. Thoroughly drying your harvested grains until they are completely hard and storing them in airtight hermetic bags prevents insects from surviving and multiplying.
ga: Weevils lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ajie ŋmãa be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaawa kwraa, ni akɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi akahi shi ni amɛfɔ bii.

english: Maize is ready for grain harvest when the leaves turn brown and dry, the outer husks become straw-colored, and a tiny black spot forms at the base of each kernel on the cob.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi. Kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ baatsɔ jwɛi su. Ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Ebaa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi yɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my young maize leaves and caterpillars hiding inside the stalks?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛtee ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ amli?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They eat the growing center of the young plant, but applying recommended pest controls early in the morning or late evening can protect the crop before severe damage occurs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ he ni tsei bibii lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ. Shi kɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛbuɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu nii lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani nɔ ko ni mli wa aba.

english: Why does dry weather hurt my maize the most when the plant starts producing tassels at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ yeɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ awui fe fɛɛ beni tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: Tasseling and flowering is the most sensitive period in a maize plant's life because it needs plenty of water to form kernels on the cob. A dry spell at this time causes missing kernels or completely empty cobs.
ga: Blustering kɛ fɔfɔi ji nibii ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ yɛ ŋmãa tso shihilɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehe hiaa nu babaoo dani enyɛ efee dumɔwui yɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ. Be nɛɛ mli nu ni mli egbi lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ loo ŋmei lɛ feɔ efolo.

english: Why do weeds reduce my maize harvest even if I add fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than maize and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight away from your crop. Clearing weeds during the first six weeks ensures all the nutrients go directly into feeding your maize.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmãa ni amɛjuɔ ŋmãa, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Klɛŋklɛŋ otsii enumɔ lɛ mli jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa o-abele niyenii lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Can I plant cowpeas or beans between my rows of maize without damaging my maize crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ ni mifiteee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yes, planting legumes like cowpeas between maize rows actually enriches the soil because legumes capture nitrogen from the air and add it to the ground, giving you two crops from the same field while feeding the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli yɛ be mli ni okɛ niyenii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight because their tender leaves burn and lose water quickly. Planting tall companion crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides cool shade and keeps moisture in the soil until the trees are strong enough to withstand the sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu nanemɛi tsei ni kɛlɛ tamɔ plantains ni akɛ cocoa tsei bibii wo mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: When the bottom leaves of maize turn yellow in a V-shape pattern, it usually means the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer around the base of the plant helps keep the leaves green and improves yield.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaabɔle he lɛ Tso lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are there tiny worms eating ragged holes inside the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ni ekumɔ yɛ mi-ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by caterpillars, such as the fall armyworm, hiding inside the growing point. Checking your field early and applying neem powder, wood ash, or recommended botanical sprays into the central leaf funnels controls the pests before they kill the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmei ni egbee shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmei baa bibii amli lɛ baa. ni yɔɔ he ni shwereɔ yɛ lɛ Kwɛmɔ he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mra. Ni okɛ neem powder, tso mli sũ, loo tso mli tsofa ko ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ afɔ shi koni ekɛkudɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai dani amɛgbe tso lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high off the ground so their leaves can spread out and receive maximum sunlight to make food. When yam leaves get full sunlight, the plant sends that energy down to produce larger, healthier underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Kɛji akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa lɛ, tso lɛ tsɔɔ nakai hewalɛ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the green leaves on my cassava plants developing yellow patches and curling upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellow patches and twisted leaves on cassava are usually signs of cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. You can prevent this disease by planting disease-resistant cassava varieties and using healthy stems that show no signs of leaf curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ baai ni etsɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ ji ŋmeii mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. Kooloi bibii eyɛŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Obaanyɛ otsi hela nɛɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Ni okɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni tsɔɔɔ baa lɛ he okadi ko kwraa lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become soft and rotten under the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long because the underground roots drown from a lack of air. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away, keeping the roots firm and dry.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. for too long Enɛ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ hewɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress caused by sudden dry spells, extreme heat, or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist by watering regularly helps the flowers stay attached and form healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na haomɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni baa trukaa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling tightly into a cup shape and stopping new growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ hee lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl when tiny insect pests like aphids or thrips sit on the underside of the leaf and suck out the juices. Spraying the underside of the leaves with mild soapy water or neem oil cleans off these pests so the plant can resume normal leaf growth.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ba shi yɛ baa lɛ shishi ni amɛmu nu lɛ mli nu lɛ. Ni akɛ nu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ. Aloo neem fɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ejie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ. koni tsei lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛdara bɔ ni sa

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when strong winds hit my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that spread near the surface rather than growing deep into the soil. Propping up trees carrying heavy fruit bunches with strong bamboo poles supports their weight and prevents them from snapping or uprooting during storms.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Tsei ni aduawai akui ni tsii yɔɔ mli ni akɛ ŋmeii ni wa ewo mli lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ tsiimɔ ni ebaatsi enaa koni ekakumɔ loo eshishijee yɛ ahum be mli.

english: Why does the soil around my crops dry out and crack so quickly after rain stops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɛɔ oya beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ?

english: Soil dries out fast when bare ground is directly exposed to hot sun and wind, which rapidly evaporates water. Covering the soil surface around your plants with dry grass or fallen leaves traps soil moisture, keeps roots cool, and prevents the soil from cracking.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ shɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ la oya. Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa Tsei ni jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa sũ lɛ mli agbala.

english: What is cross-pollination, and why is it important for my crops to produce good seeds?
ga: Mɛni ji krɔs ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni midumɔ nii lɛ awo dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ?

english: Cross-pollination happens when pollen moves from one plant's flower to another. This natural process helps the plant form healthy seeds and strong fruits, ensuring your farm yields a full harvest rather than empty pods.
ga: Krɔs-pollination baa kɛji pollen jɛ tso kome fɔfɔi mli kɛtee ekroko mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui ni mli wa kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Ye obua oŋmɔ lɛ ni ená ŋmaa ni fa yɛ pods ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ najiaŋ.

english: Why do insects like bees visit my vegetable flowers, and are they helping or harming my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii baa mifɔfɔi kɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ? Ni ani amɛmiiye amɛmiibua loo amɛmiiye miŋmɔ lɛ awui?

english: Bees and other insects are helpful friends to your farm because they carry pollen between flowers as they feed. This movement of pollen pollinates the crop, allowing flowers to turn into heavy, healthy fruits.
ga: Wuobii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi Amɛji nanemɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ejaakɛ amɛwoɔ pollen yɛ fɔfɔi ateŋ be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ. Nɛkɛ pollen ŋmeii lɛ agbɛfaa nɛɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ pollen. Ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ aduawai ni tsii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my plants sometimes drop off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers often drop off if they fail to get pollinated by insects or wind, or if the plant suffers from extreme heat, lack of water, or pest damage before the fruit can start forming.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa, nu faaa yɛ emli, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efite lɛ dani aduawai je shishi ewo.

english: If I plant two different pepper varieties next to each other, will cross-pollination change my crops?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmɔtɔ henɔi enyɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ, Ani cross-pollination baatsake miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yes, if pollen transfers between different varieties, the seeds saved from those peppers will grow into mixed plants next season, though the fruit you harvest this season will usually look normal.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ ajie pollen kɛjɛ henɔi srɔtoi ateŋ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nakai ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ tsei ni efutu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ bei pii lɛ, yibii ni okpaa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni sa po.

english: Why do goats and wild animals always attack my young crop seedlings as soon as I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tooi kɛ koo mli kooloi tutuaa mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ be fɛɛ be kɛji midu amɛ pɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are soft, sweet, and full of water, making them an easy and attractive meal for hungry animals, especially during dry periods when green bush food is scarce.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe ŋɔɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa niyenii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ŋɔɔ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri yɛ hɔmɔ be mli beni niyenii ni jɛɔ jwɛi eŋɔli mli lɛ faaa lɛ.

english: How can I build a cheap structure to protect my farm from roaming livestock?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mama tsũ ko ni jara waaa ni baabu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ tsɔnei ni hoɔ lɛ ahe?

english: You can construct a simple fence using local bamboo poles, wooden stakes, or wire netting around your farm boundary to physically block cows, sheep, and goats from entering and trampling your crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ oma gbogbo ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Kɛ ŋmei tsei, tsei ahe tsei, loo waya ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ abɔle he. Husu awo oŋmɔ lɛ he koni tsinai, tooi kɛ tooi akanyiɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are birds and mice digging up my seeds right after I put them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi kɛ ŋmeii shwieɔ midumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Freshly turned soil signals to animals that food is hidden underneath, and seeds left too close to the surface are easily smelled and eaten by rodents and birds before they can sprout.
ga: Shikpɔŋ hee ni atsake lɛ haa kooloi leɔ akɛ niyenii yɛ shishi. Ni dumɔwui ni ashiɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ tsɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmeii kɛ okpoi yeɔ amɛ oya dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: What is the purpose of a shade net or nursery structure when starting seeds?
ga: Mɛni ji yiŋtoo ni yɔɔ shade net loo greenhouse gbɛjianɔtoo he kɛji akɛ aje dumɔwui shishi?

english: A nursery structure protects delicate young sprouts from harsh sunlight, heavy direct rainfall, and hungry pests, allowing them to grow strong stems before you move them out to the open field.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ lɛ buɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ Ye obua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni wa dani okɛ amɛ aya ŋmɔ mli.

english: How does a simple screen house or greenhouse help me grow high-value vegetables?
ga: Te ŋmɔ loo ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni madu aduawai ni jara wa waa lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: A screen house uses mesh walls to allow air and light in while completely blocking harmful insects and animals, reducing the need for strong chemicals and keeping your plants safe.
ga: Filtration tsei kɛ mesh gbogboi tsuɔ nii koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la abote mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa kwraa. Ehaa tsofai ni mli wa he hiamɔ baa shi ni ehaa otsei lɛ ahiɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Should I plant my crop seeds straight into the main field or start them in a protected nursery first?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ loo mabɔi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni abuɔ he lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Delicate crops like tomatoes, cabbage, and peppers grow best when started in a protected nursery where you can care for them closely, whereas sturdy crops like maize and beans perform better when planted directly into the main field.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tomato, kaabe, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ aje shishi yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni abuɔ he mli. ni obaanyɛ okwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa Etsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ adu lɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmãa wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important for me to clear all weeds from the ground on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Clearing all weeds removes competition for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, ensuring that your crops get all the food they need to grow healthy and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii ni yɔɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he lɛ kɛyaa, ni ehaa onibii lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: How clean does my farm ground need to be before I do a ground spray?
ga: Te esa akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli he lɛ ahe atse aha tɛŋŋ dani afɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsofa?

english: The ground should be completely clear of all visible weeds so that the spray reaches the soil directly and works effectively without hindrance from overgrown plants.
ga: Esa akɛ jwɛi fɛɛ ni anaa akafee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ akatsi enaa.

english: How does keeping my field completely weed-free improve my farming reputation and yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikwɛ miŋmɔji amli ni jwɛi bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha gbɛi ni miyɔɔ yɛ okwaayeli he lɛ aya hiɛ, ni maná yibiiwoo hu aya hiɛ?

english: A clean, weed-free farm allows crops to grow to their full potential without pest or weed interference, resulting in healthier plants and higher yields that earn praise from other farmers.
ga: Okwaafoi ni mli tse, ni jwɛi bɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa kɛyashɛɔ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná lɛ, ni jwɛi loo jwɛi bɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo ni okwaafoi krokomɛi jieɔ amɛyi.

english: How does using poultry manure help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi ashishifã ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Poultry manure is rich in natural nutrients like nitrogen and organic matter, which enrich the soil and feed your plants so they can grow strong and produce good harvests.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli niyenii tamɔ nitrogen kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ kooloi ashishifã mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ he feɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni ehaa otsei lɛ niyenii. Bɔni afee ni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do some farmers mix spirit with poultry manure fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ dãa futuɔ kooloi ashishi lɛ?

english: Adding spirit or specific liquid treatments to poultry manure helps process the organic matter, reducing unwanted pests or helping release nutrients faster for the plants to absorb.
ga: Ni akɛ dãa loo nu pɔtɛɛ ko fataa kooloi ashishifã he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa yɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe nitsumɔ mli. Tsɔɔmɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ataooo lɛ shi loo ye obua tsei ni amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ oya

english: Is poultry manure a good choice for my farm if I want to build healthy soil over time?
ga: Ani kooloi ashishifã ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji miisumɔ ni matswa shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Yes, poultry manure improves soil structure, helps the ground hold water better, and provides a slow release of natural nutrients that keep the soil healthy for future seasons.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi ashishifã haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. ni ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli nibii fiofio Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ bei.

english: What can I do to feed my crops if I cannot find poultry manure to buy?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mikɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii kɛji minyɛɛɛ mahe kooloi ashishifãi?

english: If poultry manure is not available, you can take chemical fertilizer, mix it thoroughly with water, and apply it directly as a liquid feed to your crops.
ga: Kɛji kooloi afɔfɔi bɛ Obaanyɛ okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ afutu nu mli jogbaŋŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛtsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni ji nu kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why would I mix dry fertilizer with water instead of putting it straight on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi futuɔ nu mli moŋ fe ni mikɛbaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Mixing fertilizer with water dissolves the nutrients so that plant roots can absorb them immediately, especially during warmer periods when dry fertilizer takes longer to break down.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futu nu mli lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Titri lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ mli be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani efiteɔ lɛ.

english: How do I properly prepare a liquid fertilizer mixture for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa nu ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: You measure the required amount of dry fertilizer, stir it into clean water until fully dissolved, and apply the liquid solution around the base of your plants.
ga: Osusuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni he hiaa lɛ he. Okɛfutu nu ni mli tse mli kɛyashi ebaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ atsu nii ni okɛbɔle tso lɛ shishi.

english: Does liquid fertilizer help plants recover quickly when they look weak?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhe waaa oya kɛ́ amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ?

english: Yes, because the nutrients are already dissolved in water, the roots take them in right away, giving weak or struggling plants a fast boost in growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ shwieɔ nu mli. Shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni miitao ni amɛdara oya.

english: Cassava needs loose, light, or sandy soil where its roots can expand easily. If water pools on top of your land for days after it rains, the soil is too heavy and sticky, which will cause your cassava roots to rot.
ga: Cassava he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli tse loo ŋã ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. Kɛji nu damɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni enɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sũ lɛ tsii tsɔ ni ekpɛtɛɔ he. Enɛ baaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: What will happen if I plant my cocoa trees too close together?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: If cocoa trees are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This makes them grow tall and weak with few pods, and the lack of airflow between trees encourages black pod disease to spread quickly.
ga: Kɛji adu kookoo yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Cocoa tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe tsɔi fioo pɛ. Ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ woɔ black pod hela lɛ hewalɛ koni egbɛ eshwa oya.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nutrients, especially nitrogen, or that the soil is waterlogged. Adding fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure gives the plant the energy it needs to make green, healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ. titri lɛ nitrogen loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni eha baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Tomato leaves curl up in intense heat as a natural defense to trap moisture and reduce water loss. As long as they open back up in the cooler morning, the plant is fine, but persistent curling means it needs shade or more water.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni efee adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni baaha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi. Shii abɔ ni etswaa yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ. Tso lɛ hi lolo. Shi perm ni hiɔ shi daa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni ená hulutsoo loo nu babaoo.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or tiny insects sucking energy from the stems. Mulching the soil to keep it moist and cool helps the plant hold onto its flowers so peppers can grow.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii hao amɛ. ni jieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi Mulching koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi ahe koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara.

english: Why are there small holes appearing in the leaves of my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Small holes in maize leaves are a common sign that caterpillars, such as fall armyworms, are eating the young crop. Checking inside the center shoot early and spraying neem extract or recommended treatments stops them before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ akɛ ŋmeii, tamɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ mli lɛ, miiye ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. Nibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra ni akɛ neem mli nu loo tsofai krokomɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsuɔ he nii lɛ ashwieɔ nɔ Ehaa hela lɛ kpaa dani efiteɔ he ni edara lɛ.

english: Weeds compete with your crops for the exact same survival needs—sunlight, soil water, and fertilizer. Because weeds often grow faster, they steal these resources before your crops can use them, choking your crop's growth.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha wala mli hiamɔ nii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tamɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ fɔɔ daa oya. Amɛbaaju nibii nɛɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛtsu nii. Enɛ haaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How can I tell when my yam tubers are ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he koni akpa?

english: Yam tubers are ready when the vines and leaves naturally turn yellow and dry up at the end of the rainy season. This shows that the plant has finished storing all its energy into the tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo beni wain tsei lɛ kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛto shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ naa.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are special crops that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots to feed the soil. Planting them alongside maize improves soil fertility naturally while giving you two different harvests from the same land.
ga: Peanuts ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Abɛi ni akɛ abele duɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ajieɔ nibii srɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ he kome.

english: Fresh certified seeds are tested to produce uniform, high yields and resist local diseases. Seeds saved from previous harvests lose their vigor over time, leading to uneven growth and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ akwɛɔ koni amɛwo yibii daa. Yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ maŋ lɛ mli helai ni teɔ shi woɔ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and dry up right on the tree during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by a tiny fungus that thrives in wet weather and spreads through rain splashes. When water sits on the pod, the fungus enters, rots the inside, and turns the pod hard and black.
ga: Gbɔmɔtso bibioo ko kɛ enɛ baa. No shwereɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi amli. Kɛ nu yɛ pod lɛ nɔ lɛ Fungus baabote mli.Egboɔ yɛ emli ni ehaa pod lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni efeɔ ediŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up like little cups and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ ehe tamɔ kɔɔpoo bibioo ni ekpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Tiny insects like aphids or thrips hide on the undersides of the leaves to suck out the sap. As they feed, they weaken the leaf and pass on viruses that cause the leaves to wrinkle and curl.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips Ekɛ ehe teeɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni ekɛnu nu lɛ mli nu lɛ. be mli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii Amɛhaa baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛkɛ helai ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do tiny caterpillars always hide right in the middle funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: The central funnel contains the softest, tenderest leaves that are easiest for young caterpillars to eat. Hiding deep inside also protects them from the hot sun, heavy rain, and birds.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ, ni ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ aye lɛ yɔɔ teŋgbɛ funnel lɛ mli. Kɛ́ amɛte shi amɛwo mli shɔŋŋ lɛ hu buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ okpoi ahe.

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, which is its main food. To keep growing, the plant drains food from its oldest leaves at the bottom and sends it up to protect the new growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ko bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. koni eya nɔ eda Tso lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni etsuɔ ​​amɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ebu dalɛ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ he.

english: Why does planting groundnuts make my soil better for the maize I plant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants have tiny bumps on their roots filled with helpful bacteria. These bacteria pull nitrogen food out of the air and fix it into the soil, leaving natural fertilizer behind for your next crop.
ga: Peanut tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ eyi mli obɔ lɛ Helai nɛɛ gbalaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ji nitrogen lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ ahaa dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn watery and soft if water stays on my farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛhe waaa kɛji nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water on the farm for days, the roots drown from a lack of air and begin to rot underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ ni amɛje shishi amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Extreme heat dries up the pollen inside tomato blossoms, preventing them from getting fertilized. When a flower cannot produce seeds, the plant sheds it to conserve water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Kɛji fɔfɔii nyɛɛɛ awo dumɔwui Tsei jieɔ lɛ kpo koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during strong wind and rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain roots do not dig deep into the ground; they spread out wide and shallow. When heavy bunches of fruit make the top heavy and rain softens the soil, strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of the earth.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ efooo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ Beni aduawai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ haa amɛyitsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya.

english: Why do my corn plants grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded plants block each other's sunlight and fight for nutrients in the soil. They waste all their energy stretching upward for light instead of developing thick stems and big cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe hulu la lɛ naa ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa la lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ tsohi nɛ a mi wa.

english: Why do my yam vines turn yellow and die back completely when the tuber is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni bulb lɛ efee klalo lɛ?

english: When the yam tuber underground is fully grown and full of starch, the plant has completed its job. It naturally stops sending food to the leaves, causing the top vine to dry up as a sign that it is ready for harvest.
ga: Beni sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara kwraa ni ŋmeii eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Nitsumɔhe lɛ egbe nitsumɔ naa. Amɛkpaa niyenii ni amɛkɛhaa baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Wein tso lɛ yiteŋ ni egbi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ eshɛ nikpamɔ.

english: Why do some of my crops die quickly when disease hits, while my neighbor's crops survive the same sickness?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi gboiɔ oya kɛji hela ba lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔshi nibii je hela nɛɛ nɔŋŋ mli.

english: Crops have different natural strength and disease resistance based on their variety. Some seed varieties are specifically bred to fight off local plant diseases, while weaker or local varieties can die easily unless treated early.
ga: Tsei yɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ amɛhe ni esoro no yɛ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ naa. Afɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi komɛi pɔtɛɛ koni akɛwu ashi helai ni jɛɔ tsei amli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni henɔi ni he yɔɔ oya loo ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbo oya ja atsa amɛ mra.

english: Why do the fruits and leaves on my crops crack open when they get sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai kɛ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ mli fãa kɛji hela mɔ mi lɛ?

english: Certain fungal and bacterial sicknesses attack the outer skin of fruits and leaves, causing the tissue to weaken and split open. This exposes the inside of the plant to air and rot.
ga: Fungal kɛ bacteria helai komɛi tutuaa aduawai kɛ baai lɛ asɛɛ hewolo lɛ. Enɛ haa fãji lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛgbalaa. Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ aba tso lɛ mli ni egbo.

english: What causes my crop to suddenly dry up and die within a few days after looking healthy?
ga: Mɛni haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni amɛkwɛɔ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden drying is usually caused by soil sicknesses or pests that attack the roots or the lower stem, cutting off water flow from the soil to the rest of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ helai loo ŋmeii ni tutuaa shishifãi loo shishigbɛ tsei lɛ ji nɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ trukaa. Enɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyaa tso lɛ hei krokomɛi.

english: Does the kind of seed I buy matter more than the fertilizer I apply to my land?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ he hiaa fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Both are important, but good seed variety sets the plant's natural limit. If you plant low-quality seeds, even good fertilizer cannot make them yield as high as an improved, high-quality seed variety.
ga: Enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ he miihia. Shi dumɔwui srɔtoi ni hi ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ husui ni tso ko yɔɔ. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai po nyɛŋ aha yibii babaoo tamɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni atsake amɛ lɛ.

english: Why do some plants produce smaller heads or fruits even when I treat all of them the same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi yɛ bulb bibii loo aduawai lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ amɛ fɛɛ yeɔ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ moŋ.

english: Individual plants can differ due to natural seed variations, small differences in root strength, or early insect damage that stunted that specific plant's development.
ga: Tso fɛɛ tso baanyɛ afee srɔto yɛ adebɔɔ mli dumɔwui sɔrɔtoi ahewɔ. Esoro shishifã hewalɛ fioo. loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii yɛ shishijee mli ni haa tso lɛ dalɛ kpaa.

english: Why do crops planted on one side of my farm grow larger than the same crops planted on another side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fa kome lɛ daraa fe tsei ni adu yɛ fa kroko lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Soil quality, water drainage, and sunlight are not always equal across a farm. Plants grow larger in spots where the soil holds more nutrients and moisture.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su, nu ni hoɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ jeee nɔ kome be fɛɛ be yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Tsei daa yɛ hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ toɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know if poor crop growth is caused by my farm's soil or by bad seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ jɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli loo dumɔwui gbohii amli?

english: If every different crop you plant in that specific spot grows poorly, the issue is likely the soil. If only one crop variety fails while others grow well, the seed variety is usually the reason.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi Mɔ ni odu yɛ nakai he lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ. Ekolɛ naagba lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tso henɔ kome pɛ fite yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi yaa hiɛ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui srɔtoi ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: Why are some of my coconuts full of thick flesh inside while others from the same farm are mostly water and light?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokooi lɛ ekomɛi yɛ loo ni mli edɔ yɛ mli lɛ? be mli ni ŋmeii krokomɛi babaoo jɛ ŋmɔ kome mli, nu kɛ la pɛ?

english: Fruit filling depends heavily on having enough water and nutrients like potassium during the fruiting stage, as well as the specific tree variety you planted.
ga: Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ potassium ni yɔɔ yibiiwoo be lɛ mli lɛ nɔ anáa yibii lɛ ekoŋŋ. Tsei pɔtɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ fata enɛ he.

english: Why do some tree crops take much longer to produce heavy fruit than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii ni tsii fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Trees need time to develop deep roots and thick trunks to support heavy fruits. Different varieties reach fruiting age at different speeds depending on their genetics.
ga: Be he miihia tsei koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni mli tse koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii lɛ. Henɔi srɔtoi lɛ shɛɔ yibiiwoo afii ahe yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli yɛ bɔ ni amɛfɔmɔ nii yɔɔ ha lɛ naa.

english: Why do crops planted close together stay small compared to crops planted far apart?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ feɔ bibii fe tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded together, their roots and leaves compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, leaving them with less energy to grow large.
ga: Kɛ́ abua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaadara kɛyashɛ agbo.

english: Why do buyers pay more money for cassava that is processed into gari than for raw cassava roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ ŋmei ni afee lɛ gari lɛ he nyɔmɔ babaoo fe ŋmei shishifãi ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Processing raw cassava into gari removes water and prevents it from rotting quickly. It transforms a perishable crop into a long-lasting, ready-to-eat product, which adds value and makes buyers willing to pay higher prices.
ga: Kɛ́ afee ŋmei ni afee lɛ gari lɛ, ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ mli, ni ehaaa efite oya. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ oya ni atsakeɔ amɛfeɔ nibii ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ, ni asaa he klalo akɛ ayeɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa jara lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛwo jara ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: How does harvesting my crops too early or too late affect their value when I take them to buyers?
ga: Te miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa mra loo mikɛkpaa sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ baaná amɛjara nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ beni mikɛyaa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ aŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Harvesting crops too early leaves them small and underdeveloped, while harvesting too late causes them to rot, split, or spoil. Timing your harvest correctly ensures the crops are at peak quality for selling or processing into new products.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha efee bibioo ni ehiɛɛɛ shi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmaakpamɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ agbo, ejara mli loo efite lɛ, be ni sa ni akɛkpaa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ koni ahɔ̃ɔ loo afee nibii heei.

english: If I only have a small amount of money, how should I start growing crops without losing my investment?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ shika fioo pɛ lɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabɔi tsei akwɛmɔ ni mishika ni mikɛwo mli lɛ akafite?

english: Start by cultivating a small plot of a reliable crop first. This allows you to learn how the crop behaves in your soil and secure local buyers before using your initial profits to gradually expand your farm size.
ga: Je shishi kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. reliable first Enɛ haa okaseɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ohiɛɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli dani okɛ shishijee sɛɛnamɔi lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ fiofio. Gbalamɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: How do I choose which crop to plant if I want to be sure someone will buy it after harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsei ni esa akɛ madu? Kɛji miisumɔ ni makwɛ koni mɔ ko ahe yɛ kpamɔ sɛɛ

english: Look for staple crops that local processing centers or markets constantly need, such as maize, cassava, or oil palm. Planting crops with established local demand ensures you won't be left with unsold produce.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa yɛ maŋ lɛ mli nibii ahe nitsumɔhei loo jarayeli hei, tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo mu ŋmãa. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ anaa lɛ haa ashiɔ bo nibii ni ahɔ̃ɔɔ kɔkɔɔkɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow plenty of big green leaves but fail to produce fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer or excessive water, they focus all their energy on growing tall stems and lush leaves instead of flowering and setting fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo amɛná nu babaoo lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ maa tsei lɛ ashishifãi kakadaji ni miida kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii lɛ

english: Why do the leaves of my crops curl up and turn yellow during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crop leaves curl up in high heat to reduce water loss and protect themselves from burning. If the leaves stay curled or yellow into the cooler evening, the plant is stressed and needs better soil moisture or nutrients.
ga: Tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle loo efee ŋmɔŋ yɛ fɛ̃i mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao ni ehe miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant legumes like cowpeas together with my maize, or will they steal food from each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa? Aloo amɛbaaju niyenii kɛjɛ amɛhe?

english: Planting cowpeas with maize is actually beneficial because legumes capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, helping the maize grow better while making good use of your farm space.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he diɛŋtsɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa lɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Ye obua oŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni okɛ oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Healthy soil is dark, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture well without becoming waterlogged, and contains earthworms or decayed plant matter that provides natural food for young crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɛ su ni tsuɔ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehaaa nu lɛ ahi shi. Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsei ni egboi ni eshwɛ ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ yɛ.

english: Why do some of my crops spoil within days after harvest while others can sit for months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ekomɛi fiteɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni akpaa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi baanyɛ ahi shi nyɔji babaoo lɛ?

english: Crops with high water content, like tomatoes and garden eggs, rot quickly because bacteria thrive in moisture. Crops like dried maize or cocoa have low moisture, which naturally stops them from rotting easily.
ga: Tsei ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli tamɔ tomato kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ abɔɔ mli Egboɔ oya ejaakɛ bacteria shwereɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa ni egbi loo kookoo lɛ mli nu faaa. Nɔ ni haaa efite mlɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ.

english: What causes insects to destroy my harvested maize inside my storage barn, and how do I stop it?
ga: Mɛni haa kooloi fiteɔ ŋmãa ni akpaa yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Insects are attracted to warmth and moisture remaining in harvested grain. Thoroughly sun-drying your maize until it is completely hard before sealing it in clean bags prevents insects from multiplying.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni eshwɛɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ gbalaa kooloi. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ebaawa kwraa dani okɛwo kotoku ni mli tse mli lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafɔ.

english: During the Harmattan dry season, young cocoa trees drop leaves to protect themselves from losing too much water. Planting shade trees like plantains nearby keeps the moisture in the air and soil, protecting young cocoa plants from harsh heat.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he.

english: How can I keep insects from eating my harvested maize while it is in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ be mli ni eyɔɔ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils thrive when grain is stored wet. You must dry your maize completely until the grains are hard, and then store them in airtight bags or cool, ventilated structures to prevent bugs from breeding.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo nu mli. Esa akɛ okɛ o-corn lɛ agbi kwraa kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ amli baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛwoɔ kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo nɔ kroko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli koni kooloi akafɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers start rotting a few weeks after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ bɔi fitemɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly when bruised during harvest or stored in hot, dark, humid rooms. Handle the tubers gently and keep them on raised, well-ventilated bamboo racks in the shade so air can circulate around them.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa yɛ kpamɔ be mli loo akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ, ni mli edɔ mli. Okɛ ŋmeii lɛ atsu nii blɛoo ni okɛwo ŋmeii ni awo nɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ abɔle amɛhe.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and hard instead of growing big and fleshy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe wa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaafee fɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots remain small when planted in hard, unplowed soil that restricts their growth. Loosening the earth before planting gives the tubers room to expand and absorb water easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuko nɔ, ni no haaa amɛdara. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ dani adu lɛ, ehaa bulb lɛ náa hegbɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa ni ekɛ nu shwieɔ mli mlɛo.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn pale green or yellow even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Heavy rainfall can wash essential nutrients like nitrogen out of the topsoil. Pale leaves indicate that the plant is starving for food, which can be fixed by adding manure or nitrogen rich fertilizer.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii he hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ. Abaanyɛ atsu enɛ he nii kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it helpful to plant cowpea or beans on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, crops like cowpea and beans capture nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the ground, acting as natural fertilizer for maize while preventing weeds from growing.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa yɛ be mli ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the young leaves. Spraying plants with a simple water and neem oil solution deters these pests.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ chili baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu kɛ neem fɔ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ ahe.

english: When seeds are planted together, the stalks compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing plants out allows each stalk to grow thick and produce large ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ he kome lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ashi gbɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko daa ni ewoɔ ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Why are my plantain suckers taking so long to bear fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Plantains need constant moisture and rich organic soil to grow quickly. If they suffer from drought or poor soil, their flowering is delayed by several months.
ga: Plantains he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Kɛji hɔmɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ ye amɛnɔ lɛ Amɛfɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyɔji babaoo.

english: How do I know if my soil is ready and good enough to grow tomatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo ni ehi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ tomato nɔ?

english: Good tomato soil should be dark, soft, and easy to crumble, retaining water without turning muddy. Adding dark composted animal manure makes soil fertile and spongy for tomato roots.
ga: Esa akɛ tomato shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ afee ediŋŋ, ni efee bɔdɔɔ, ni efiteɔ oya. Ebaanyɛ ehiɛ nu mli ni efeee muji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli kɛha tomato shishifãi.

english: How do I calculate how many crops I can plant on one plot of land compared to a full acre?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu ŋmɔshi nibii enyiɛ ni manyɛ madu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ acre kome he akɔntaa?

english: In Ghana, an acre is equal to about four standard land plots. Knowing the exact size of your land helps you calculate the right distance between plants so they don't crowd each other and starve for food.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, acre kome kɛ aaafee shikpɔŋ fãi ejwɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ yeɔ egbɔ. Kɛ́ ole bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ da ha pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni obu gbɛ ni sa ni ka tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ he akɔntaa. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ akafee ekome ni hɔmɔ akaye amɛ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant them too close to each other on a small plot?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko bibioo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When crops are crowded on a small space, their roots fight over soil nutrients and their leaves block sunlight from each other, resulting in tall, skinny plants that produce very little food.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔle he bibioo ko lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ tsɔi lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why should I leave one of my farm plots resting empty while I grow crops on another plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi miŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efolo yɛ be mli ni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ kroko nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving a plot of land to rest—known as fallowing—allows the soil to naturally rebuild its nutrients and moisture, making it fertile again for a much bigger harvest next season.
ga: Ale hejɔɔmɔhe ko ni ajieɔ lɛ hu akɛ desertion. Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni da kwraa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller every time I plant the exact same crop on the same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows crop-specific pests to build up in that plot.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I successfully plant crops on land that has hard-packed dirt or stony ground?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛsaa nɔ?

english: Crops need soft soil so their roots can spread out, absorb water, and breathe. Hard ground stunts root growth, causing the plant to wither quickly in dry weather.
ga: Tsei hia shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ bɔni afee ni amɛshishifãi lɛ anyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã, amɛmɔmɔ nu, ni amɛmu. Shikpɔŋ ni wa tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why does wild grass grow so much faster on my plot than the actual crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ fe tsei diɛŋtsɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Wild grasses have tough, established roots that adapt quickly to hot weather and steal water and soil nutrients before your young crops have a chance to take root.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni wa, ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ. ni baatsake ehe oya kɛya kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ amli ni ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani odumɔwui lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi.

english: Why does the soil on my cleared plot get so dry and baked after I clear all the bushes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi saatso ni ajie lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ ni etswaa beni mijie tsei bibii lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When land is cleared completely bare, direct heat from the sun bakes the soil and evaporates all its natural moisture; leaving mulch or cover crops protects the soil from drying out.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa emli nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi. Mulching loo mulching baaye abua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi.

english: Is it better for my crops if I divide my land into plots for different plants or grow everything mixed together?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji mijara shikpɔŋ lɛ mli miwo shikpɔji ni mikɛduɔ nibii srɔtoi loo midu nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni akɛfutu mli?

english: Dividing land into separate plots helps you manage the different water, shade, and fertilizer needs of each crop without tall plants overpowering smaller ones.
ga: Shikpɔŋ mlijaa yɛ shikpɔji amli Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ nu, hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa tsei srɔtoi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ tsei kakadaji ni yeɔ tsei bibii anɔ kunim lɛ bɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to try a new farming method on my land that someone brought from abroad?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ maka okwaayeli gbɛ hee ko ni mɔ ko kɛjɛ maŋsɛɛ eba lɛ makwɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: New methods can boost yields, but you should always test a new technique on a small section of one plot first to see how it responds to local rainfall and soil before using it on your entire farm.
ga: Gbɛi heei baanyɛ aha nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ. Shi esa akɛ oka ŋaai heei okwɛ yɛ fãi bibii amli. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ ko nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ be fɛɛ be koni ona bɔ ni ŋaa gbɛ lɛ tsuɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ he nii eha. dani okɛtsu nii yɛ oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli

english: What should I look for in the soil to know if a plot of land is good for farming before I secure it?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ makwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha okwaayeli dani maná?

english: Good farming land has deep, dark brown soil that feels crumbly and drains excess rainwater easily, rather than land dominated by hard clay, gravel, or swampy waterlogging.
ga: Okwaayeli shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa, ŋmei bibii, loo nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil. Leaving some larger shade trees on your farm protects the seedlings until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hɔɔ ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ oshi tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow before the corn is even ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani abele lɛ po feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient they need from the soil. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or growing beans on the land before maize helps keep the soil fertile and leaves green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he loo akɛdu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani aŋɔ ŋmei lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmeii ni eha baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli.

english: Does it matter which way I push my cassava stem cuttings into the ground?
ga: Ani bɔ ni mikɛ ŋmeii niji lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia?

english: Yes, pushing cassava stems upside down makes it hard for roots and leaves to grow properly, which lowers your yield. Always make sure the small buds on the stem are pointing upward toward the sky when planting.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ otsi ŋmei tso lɛ shishi kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ akɛ amɛakwɛ̃. Enɛ baaha nibii ni afee lɛ aba shi. Kwɛmɔ be fɛɛ be akɛ ŋmeii lɛ afee bibii. yɛ tso lɛ shishi ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi beni adu lɛ nɔ

english: What is eating ragged holes in the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yeɔ bu ni ekpɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-bibii ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those holes are usually caused by Fall Armyworms, which are small caterpillars that hide inside the growing center of maize. Checking your farm early and applying recommended pest control methods early can stop them from damaging your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ agbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ atsu nii mra. Ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ŋmɔji akafite okpamɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I avoid burning the cleared bush on my field before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni ajie yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashãa dani madu nii lɛ he?

english: Burning destroys rich organic matter and beneficial soil organisms that keep your land healthy and moist. Clearing land without burning allows the dead plant material to rot into natural manure that feeds your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa kɛ sũ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni edɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ashãaa lɛ haa tsei ni egboi lɛ amli nibii fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it risky to sow my crop seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry heat spell that can scorch seeds before they establish roots. Waiting until the rains become consistent ensures the soil stays moist enough for seeds to grow safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛfee shishifãi lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas help my soil produce better maize next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ewo ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas capture natural nitrogen food from the air and leave it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize in that same field later, the maize feeds on those leftover nutrients and grows much stronger.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen nibii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛshiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ sɛɛ mli lɛ odu ŋmãa yɛ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baaye niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ebaada waa babaoo.

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes, called blossom end rot, happen when soil moisture fluctuates wildly or lacks calcium. Watering your tomato plants regularly and evenly prevents the fruit from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ hei diji ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa loo calcium faaa. Ha o-tomato tsei lɛ nu daa kɛ be fɛɛ be koni aduawai lɛ akafite.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves in full sunlight to create food for the underground tubers to grow big. Staking keeps leaves off the hot ground and prevents diseases that thrive in dark, damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo koni ekɛfee niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji lɛ. Staking baabu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ ahe, ni ebaatsi helai ni shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests when I plant my seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to feed properly and yield larger fruits or tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ aduawai loo bulbs wuji.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct sunlight because their root systems are fragile and their leaves burn easily. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains nearby shields them from severe heat and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ waaa ni amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafee hulutsoo ni naa wa waa, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my plants with dry grass help them during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, stops the sun from evaporating moisture out of the earth, keeping the root area cool and wet for much longer.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekajie ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil that helps plants build strong leaves, or that waterlogged soil is preventing the roots from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmaa baai ni wa loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii.

english: Why does my soil produce smaller harvests when I grow maize on the exact same patch of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop in the same spot every season drains specific nutrients from the soil faster than they can recover and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ ehe awo mli ekoŋŋ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does putting dry chicken manure into the earth help my crops grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Animal manure feeds the soil with natural nutrients and organic material, which improves the soil's structure so it can store water and feed crop roots properly.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli haa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehiɛ nu mli ni eye ebua tsei shishifãi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very little fruit when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants compete heavily against one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving none of them with enough food to bear heavy yields.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei komɛi bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛdu nii babaoo.

english: Why should I cut off some of the healthy-looking branches on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Removing excess branches, called pruning, prevents the plant from wasting food on unnecessary leaves and directs all its energy into growing larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite niyenii yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. Ni okɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ awo aduawai ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ waa lɛ amli.

english: How do simple weeds actually stop my main crops from growing well?
ga: common weed Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi tso titri lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Weeds are fast-growing plants that steal soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunshine away from your main crops, leaving your crops hungry, weak, and undersized.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni daa oya ni juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii amli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ, amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ bibii.

english: Why do insects attack and eat my maize leaves more quickly during warm weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa ni amɛyeɔ mi-abɛi lɛ oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Warm weather causes pest eggs to hatch faster and accelerates the life cycle of insects, making them multiply rapidly and consume plant leaves at a much higher rate.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ afɔ̃ɔ oya ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ wala yaa oya. Enɛ haa amɛshwereɔ oya ni amɛyeɔ tsei ahe baai babaoo.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to survive; when excess rainwater collects and sits stagnant in the ground, it suffocates the roots and encourages rot-causing fungi to attack them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Beni nugbɔ nu babaoo buaa ehe naa ni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua amɛ.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure early in the growing season helps the plant stay green and produce healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot, when watering is irregular, or if the soil lacks phosphorus and calcium. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and avoiding excessive nitrogen fertilizer helps the flowers turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ phosphorus kɛ calcium Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ajie nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tomato.

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because excess water prevents air from reaching the roots, causing them to suffocate. This damp environment allows fungal diseases to thrive, so planting on raised mounds or ridges helps drain water away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haa amɛmuɔ. Shihilɛ ni mli efɔ nɛɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ yaa hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ atsɔ mli.
