english: How does adding cow dung or poultry manure help my sandy farmland?
ga: Te tsina loo kooloi ashishifã ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Animal manure acts like a natural sponge in sandy soil. It holds soil particles together, helping the land store water longer during dry spells and keeping essential plant nutrients from washing away when it rains.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli sponji yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ nɔ. Ehaa sũ mli nibii bibii lɛ feɔ ekome. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. ni ehaa tsofai ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ akaho kɛji nugbɔ nɛ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during cool, damp weather. Pruning extra branches to allow sunlight and fresh air into your farm, along with picking off infected pods early, prevents the fungus from destroying healthy pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ mli. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. kɛfata pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra he. Enɛ baatsi ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anaa.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on tender young maize leaves. Checking your fields early and applying approved treatments directly into the center funnel of the plant stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli mra ni okɛ tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ awo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tsɔne lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Curled, distorted leaves on cassava are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension officers is the best way to prevent this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei baai ni etsake lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni extension officials lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds while my crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have short roots and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil food. Clearing weeds early ensures your young crop gets all the nutrients it needs to establish a strong root system.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni odumɔwui lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why is it important to lift my yam vines onto wooden stakes off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking yam vines exposes more leaves to sunlight, which helps the plant make food to grow bigger tubers. It also keeps leaves off damp soil, reducing the spread of fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ o-sweet potato wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la babaoo ashɛ tso lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ebɔɔ niyenii ni ekɛ bulbs wuji baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ he. Ha fungal leaf helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ aba shi.

english: Is it better to plant my crops right at the start of the rains or wait until heavy rains begin?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli loo aaamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa lɛ aba?

english: Planting right at the onset of the rains allows seeds to sprout in warm soil and establish roots early. Waiting for heavy rains can lead to seeds washing away or soil becoming waterlogged, which rots young seedlings.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛwo shishifãi oya. Nugbɔnɛmɔ ni naa wa ni mɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ ashwã loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ nu. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsei bibii lɛ agbo.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight and severe heat. Without shade trees or plantains around them to block the harsh sun, the leaves dry out, turn brown, and fall off.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ he ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Bɔni afee ni amɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa lɛ, baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: What causes small green worms to eat the leaves in the center of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These worms are often Fall Armyworms, hatched from eggs laid by moths on your crop. They feed on tender leaf whorls, but applying recommended organic or chemical pest control early can protect your field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii fɔɔ oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ amli. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii. Shi atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii mra. Ebaanyɛ ebu ohegbɛ lɛ he

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help improve the soil for my next maize crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air through their roots and deposit it into the soil. When you harvest them, they leave behind enriched soil that feeds the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa amɛ Ebaashi shikpɔŋ ni baa nii koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Covering the ground with dried grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation during hot days, and stops weeds from growing easily.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ aba shi. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ mlɛo

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crops very close to each other so I can get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving plants proper space allows each one to grow larger and produce a healthier yield.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Kɛ́ oha otsei lɛ he ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni edara ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell. Sowing too early can cause seeds to germinate and then dry up and die before the main rains fully settle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔ titri lɛ aba shi kwraa.

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped around them for too long in waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is extremely hot or when watering is irregular. Giving the plants steady moisture helps them keep their flowers and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nu haa tsei lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why is it important to cut off the small extra shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ

english: Too many extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and food from the main mother plant. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main plantain tree grows big, heavy bunches of fruit.
ga: Ayɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi loo ŋmeii ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha plantain titri lɛ adara ni etsɔ aduawai wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are my maize leaves rolling up into tight tubes during the sunny afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during hot periods to reduce water loss through evaporation. It is the plant's natural defense mechanism to conserve moisture when the soil is dry.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɛɔ nu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when there is sudden water stress. The plant drops flowers to protect itself from losing excess energy during difficult weather.
ga: Pepper tsei baafɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛji nu he haomɔ ba trukaa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkafite hewalɛ ni fa fe nine yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with lots of green leaves, but the tubers underground are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa tsɔ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava focus all its energy on growing stems and leaves instead of roots. Avoid high-nitrogen fertilizers so the plant directs energy to swelling the tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii kɛ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe shishifãi. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe koni eha tso lɛ hewalɛ ni eha bulbs lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young corn turning light green and yellow at the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the tips of lower leaves indicates a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. The corn plant is moving stored nitrogen from older leaves to newer top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele tsei miitsi nitrogen ni ato lɛ kɛmiijɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛmiiya baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants turn yellow and curl upwards before flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe dani amɛmiiwo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Yellowing and upward leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by the Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies that suck sap from the underside of the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus, ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot withstand direct sunlight because intense heat burns their leaves and dries out their stems. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or bananas to shield them during their early growth.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ la ni naa wa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha amɛshishifãi lɛ agbi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo banana. Koni ekɛ hebuu aha yɛ be mli ni edaa oya lɛ

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that have special bacteria in their roots. These roots pull nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the ground, naturally fertilizing the soil for hungry crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do some plantain suckers produce big bunches while others from the same farm grow weak and slow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni jɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa oya lɛ?

english: Sword suckers with narrow, sharp leaves produce strong roots and large bunches. Broad-leaved maiden suckers grow slowly and yield small bunches because they do not form strong root systems.
ga: Sword suckers ni baai ni mli tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ woɔ shishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji. Bamboo tsei ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛfeee shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: How do I know when my yam tubers are ready for harvesting underground if I cannot see them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi kpamɔ? Ni kɛji akɛ minyɛɛɛ mana hu?

english: Yam crops signal maturity above ground when their vines and leaves stop growing, turn yellow, and completely dry up. This shows that all nutrients have finished moving down into the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tsei tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ dalɛ kɛji wain tso lɛ kɛ baai lɛ kpa dalɛ. Etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi kwraa, ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ efã kɛtee ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil and get moldy quickly even when stored under a roofed shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ ni ehiɛɔ oya eyɛ mli akɛ akɛtoɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ nɔ ko eha nɔ lɛ shishi moŋ?

english: If maize is harvested and stored with high moisture trapped inside the grains, molds and fungi will thrive. Grains must be thoroughly sun-dried on a clean surface until they are hard before storage.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmãa ni akɛto ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa babaoo emɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Muji kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ adara. Esa akɛ agbi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ he ko ni he tse kɛyashi ebaawa dani akɛto.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to grow green and healthy. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer can help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same spot of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the soil of the specific nutrients maize relies on and allows soil pests to multiply. Rotating with beans or groundnuts helps restore nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi damɔ nɔ lɛ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ayi fa babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake amɛhe lɛ, no haa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Is it better for me to water my tomato garden early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mitato abɔɔ lɛ mli nu leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Early morning is best because the plant roots can absorb the water before the heat causes it to evaporate. Watering under hot afternoon sun wastes water and can stress the plants.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ tsei shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ nu dani la ni tsoɔ lɛ atsɔ mli. Nu ni oooha yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baafite nu ni ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ ahao.

english: Why do some farmers spread dry grass on top of the soil around their vegetable plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shwieɔ jwɛi amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛduɔ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass around plants is called mulching. It keeps the soil cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly in the sun, and blocks weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni aduɔ yɛ tsei ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in a field with direct sunlight and no shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn in intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates living umbrellas that protect young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewaa bɔ ni sa.

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or is planted too close together, it uses all its energy to grow leaves at the top instead of building heavy tuber roots in the ground.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ. Ebaakɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ baai yɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee tuber shishifãi ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress, dry soil, or lacks nutrients. Ensuring steady moisture and avoiding excess chemical fertilizer helps the flowers turn into pepper fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ. Kɛ́ ahiɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be mli ni ajie tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni fa fe nine lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai ni mli edɔ.

english: How do weeds actually reduce the harvest I get from my crop fields?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aha ŋmaa ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ aba shi?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. When weeds grow close to your crops, your crops become weak and starve, resulting in a much smaller harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni hɔmɔ baaye amɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nikpamɔ lɛ baafee bibioo kwraa.

english: Why do white powdery spots appear on the leaves of my garden plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: White spots are usually a fungal disease that thrives when humidity is high and air cannot flow between closely packed plants. Giving plants enough space when planting helps keep leaves dry and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ji ŋmɔtɔ hela ko ni yaa hiɛ waa kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe waa lɛ ateŋ. Kɛ́ oha otsei lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ haa amɛgbiɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crop is wilting from lack of water or from a disease in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo hela ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ?

english: If a plant wilts from lack of water, it usually recovers after you water it in the evening. If the soil is wet but the plant stays wilted or dies suddenly, it is likely caused by a root disease or pest.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ gbo yɛ nu ni bɛ hewɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛji okɛ nu wo enɔ gbɛkɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi tso lɛ shwieɔ shi lolo loo egboɔ trukaa lɛ Ekolɛ shishifã hela loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: This usually means your soil is low on nitrogen. The maize plant naturally pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni ekɛhaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: How does growing cowpeas alongside my maize help my soil stay fertile?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni efee ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has special bacteria in its roots that grab nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, providing free nutrients for your maize.
ga: Cowpeas fata legume weku lɛ he, ni eyɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ eshishifãi amli. Enɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Na niyenii mli hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha o-corn lɛ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them survive during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, stops moisture from evaporating quickly, and keeps weeds from stealing water.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi oya, ni ehaaa jwɛi akaju nu

english: What is causing small ragged holes and powdery waste inside the leaf funnel of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Nibii ni etse kɛ sũ ni yɔɔ mi-abele bibii lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ.

english: This is typical damage from the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the central shoot of the maize plant to feed on tender leaves.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ateŋ lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ fɔɔ fitemɔ.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips that suck sap from the leaves and spread viruses that stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni shwieɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa tsei lɛ adalɛ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves drop off rapidly when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during dry spells to protect themselves from water loss; providing shade trees reduces heat stress and helps keep leaves on the tree.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ amɛhe lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo ha lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my tomato plants without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ tomato tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomatoes shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or water supply is irregular, as extreme heat prevents effective pollination.
ga: Tomatoi baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ bɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ babaoo baatsi pollination ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ naa.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into the sunlight so they can make more food, which results in larger tubers underground while keeping leaves safe from soil diseases.
ga: Akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ woɔ ŋtayaa nɔ koni egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni efee nɔ ni ayeɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa baa lɛ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I remove the extra suckers growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra suckers steal water and food from the main mother plant. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant grows large, healthy bunches.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ daa ni etsɔɔ ŋmeii agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does planting cassava stem cuttings at an angle produce a better harvest than planting them flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmei niji yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ, ehaa yibii kpakpai fe ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slanting angle encourages roots to spread out evenly near the surface, giving tubers space to swell larger and making harvesting easier.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa pɛpɛɛpɛ. ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa bulb lɛ naa gbɛ babaoo ni ekɛbaagbɛ eshwa ni ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do my crops start rotting so quickly right after I cut them on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mifolɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops rot quickly after cutting if you leave them on the farm until they are overripe. Harvesting them at the correct stage before they get too soft helps them stay fresh and resist decay.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji afolɔ. Kɛji oshi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyashi ekwɛ̃ tsɔ lɛ, Kɛ́ okpa amɛ yɛ be ni sa mli dani amɛfee blɛoo tsɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ehee ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ fitemɔ.

english: How does drying my harvested crop help keep it from spoiling?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mikpamɔ lɛ ni mikɛgbiɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa koni ekafite?

english: Drying removes excess water from the crop. When a crop is properly dried, micro-organisms cannot cause it to decay, keeping it safe from rotting after you cut it.
ga: Nibii ni agbiɔ lɛ jieɔ nu ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ nyɛŋ aha tso lɛ afite. ni otsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite beni ofo lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Is it better for me to let my produce get very ripe on the farm before harvesting?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahã minibii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani akpa?

english: No, letting produce become overripe on the plant makes it weak and vulnerable. Overripe crops rot almost immediately once they are harvested.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwere fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ. Aaafee akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ fiteɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akpa.

english: What is the best tool to use when harvesting delicate crops from my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji dɛŋdade ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Using a small, sharp knife is best because it allows you to make clean cuts and peel damaged parts carefully without bruising the rest of the crop.
ga: Kakla bibioo ni akɛtsuɔ nii Kpãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ ehaa onyɛɔ ofoɔ he ni efite lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ hiɛdɔɔ shwieɔ he ni efite lɛ nɔ ni okɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ etswaaa.

english: Why shouldn't I just cut my crops and pile them together on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifolɔɔ midumɔ nii lɛ ni mikɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Roughly cutting and dumping crops in piles causes bruising and traps heat, which speeds up decay. Gentle handling prevents immediate rotting.
ga: Nibii ni adu lɛ ni afoɔ ni ashɛrɛɔ ashwieɔ ŋtayaai amli lɛ. Ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni ehiɛɔ dɔlɛ mli. ni haa fitemɔ yaa oya. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii blɛoo lɛ, ehaaa efite amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Should I peel my crops while I am harvesting them on the field?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni mikpaa nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Peeling carefully with a small knife during harvest helps remove spoiled outer layers right away, preparing the healthy part of the crop for proper drying.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsɔne bibioo ko shwie shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ, ejieɔ kponɔgbɛ fã ni egbo lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Koni asaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ koni amɛgbi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What simple steps can I take to make sure my cut crops do not rot immediately?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma nyɛɛ blɔ nya tomi komɛ a nɔ. Mɛni abaanyɛ afee koni tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ akafite amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: To stop immediate rot, harvest crops before they become overripe, use a small knife to handle and trim them neatly, and dry them well before storage.
ga: Bɔni afee ni akpa fitemɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Kpamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani ekwɛ̃ tsɔ. Kɛ kakla bibioo ko atsu nii ni okɛfolɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni egbi dani okɛto.

english: What happens if I try to store my crop without drying it properly first?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mibɔ mɔdɛŋ akɛ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato ni migbiko lɛ jogbaŋŋ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: If a crop is not dried completely, moisture remains trapped inside. This internal moisture causes the produce to start rotting shortly after it is cut.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbiko kwraa lɛ, Fɛ̃i baakã he ahi mli. Nɛkɛ mligbɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ haa nibii ni akwɛɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji afo mli.

english: How can I tell if my drying process was done correctly for my harvested crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ gbɛ ni mitsɔɔ nɔ migbiɔ nii lɛ ja kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa lɛ?

english: You know your drying was successful when the crop remains firm and completely free from signs of rot or mold after being cut.
ga: O le kaa o ngmami ɔ ye manye benɛ ngma a hi si saminya nɛ e be nɔ́ ko nɛ tsɔɔ kaa e puɛ loo e puɛ benɛ a kpa lɛ se ɔ.

english: Does rough cutting during harvest affect how long my produce lasts?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ wala be he?

english: Yes, rough cutting tears the tissue of the crop, making open wounds where rot sets in quickly. Clean cuts with a small knife help the crop last longer.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa haa tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ mli gbalaa. Enɛ haa pilamɔ ko ni mli tse ni shwieɔ oya lɛ baa. Kɛ akɛ tsɔne bibioo ko ŋmɔɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How many years do I have to wait after planting oil palm before I can start harvesting and making money?
ga: Kɛ́ odu mu tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani obaanyɛ okpa ni oná shika?

english: Oil palm trees usually take about 3 to 4 years after field planting to produce their first harvestable fruit bunches, with full, peak yields starting around 7 to 10 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ adu mu tsei yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, amɛheɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 dani amɛkpaa amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ. Nibii ni afeɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛ nɔ ni fe fɛɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ aaafee afii 7 kɛyashi 10 mli.

english: How long does a new hybrid cocoa seedling take from planting until it bears its first pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani hybrid cocoa dumɔwui heei lɛ feɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties in Ghana start bearing fruit within 2 to 3 years after planting, compared to older traditional varieties which took 4 to 5 years.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii yɛ Ghana lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Akɛ enɛ toɔ blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ ni heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 lɛ ahe.

english: How long will an oil palm tree continue to produce fruits once I plant it?
ga: Be enyiɛ mu tso ko baaya nɔ awo yibii kɛji midu lɛ pɛ?

english: An oil palm tree can live and produce harvestable fruit for 25 to 30 years, after which it becomes too tall to harvest easily and fruit production slows down.
ga: Mu tsei baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii ni abaanyɛ akpa afii 25 kɛyashi 30, ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛfeɔ shwiili tsɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akpa amɛ mlɛo ni yibii ni anáa lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why does my cocoa tree only yield pods at certain times of the year instead of giving me fruit every month?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi pɛ amli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ daa nyɔŋ nɔ

english: Cocoa trees produce pods in response to rain patterns and dry seasons, leading to a main harvest season (usually October to February in Ghana) and a smaller light crop season (around May to June).
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ ŋmeii yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hɔmɔ be mli nibii ahetoohamɔ mli. Nɔ ni tsɔɔ kpamɔ be titri lɛ mli (bei pii lɛ October kɛyashi February yɛ Ghana) kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii be (aaafee May kɛyashi June)

english: Oil palm trees need a lot of water to form fruit bunches. During prolonged dry spells, the tree conserves water by producing fewer female flowers, which reduces the number of palm bunches weeks later.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia oil palm tsei koni amɛfee aduawai akui. Yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ buɔ nu he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi yei fioo ni amɛwoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii ni baa lɛ ayibɔ aba shi yɛ otsii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why are the tiny young pods on my cocoa trees turning black and shriveling up before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ tsɔɔ ediŋŋ ni egbɔjɔɔ dani edaa lɛ?

english: This is often caused by Black Pod disease (a fungal infection encouraged by too much shade and wet weather) or 'cherelle wilt,' which is the tree's natural way of dropping extra pods it cannot nourish.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. (fungal hela ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ tsirɛɔ lɛ) loo ‘cherry wilt’, ni ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ eshwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ eha niyenii lɛ.

english: Can I plant oil palm and cocoa trees together on the exact same plot of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu oil palm kɛ cocoa tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: It is generally not recommended to mix mature oil palm and cocoa closely together because both crops grow large and have dense leaves that compete heavily for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɔɔɔ akɛ akɛ oil palm kɛ cocoa ni eda lɛ afutu he jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ dara ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa.

english: Do young cocoa trees need direct sunlight or do they grow better under shade?
ga: Cacao tsei bibii biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ loo amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade trees (or plantains) to shield them from harsh sunlight and hold soil moisture; mature cocoa trees can handle more light if they receive adequate fertilizer and rainfall.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo (loo plantains) koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, ni eha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ baanyɛ aná la babaoo kɛji amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ.

english: Should I cut off the lower green leaves from my oil palm tree, or leave them until they dry up?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ loo mashi amɛ koni amɛgbi?

english: You should prune only dead or yellowing bottom fronds (leaves) to clear space for harvesting fruit bunches; cutting too many green leaves reduces the tree's ability to make food and lowers fruit yields.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ baai ni egbo loo ni efee ŋmɔŋ (baai) pɛ. Bɔni afee ni aha he ni abaakpa aduawai akui lɛ aya hiɛ Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa aduawai ni ewoɔ lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Can oil palm farming give me regular income throughout the year like a regular job?
ga: Ani mu tso ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ baanyɛ aha aná shika daa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ tamɔ daa nitsumɔ?

english: Yes, because mature oil palm trees produce harvestable fruit bunches every 2 to 3 weeks almost all year round, providing a steady stream of income compared to seasonal crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ mu tsei ni eda lɛ woɔ aduawai babaoo ni abaanyɛ akpa daa otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ afi lɛ mli bei babaoo mli. Enɛ haa anáa shika daa kɛ akɛto be mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Does cocoa grow the same way in every part of Ghana, or does my region make a big difference?
ga: Kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ yɛ Ghana hei fɛɛ. Aloo ani mikpokpaa lɛ haa srɔtofeemɔ kpele baa?

english: Cocoa trees need deep, fertile soil and high rainfall to yield well. Regions like the Western North have favorable rainfall patterns and forest soils that allow cocoa to thrive, whereas drier regions in northern Ghana cannot naturally support cocoa farming without extensive irrigation.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo he hiaa kookoo tsei koni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ. Kpokpai tamɔ North West yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni sa kɛ koo mli shikpɔji ni yeɔ ebuaa kookoo ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hei ni egbi yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua adebɔɔ mli kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ nu babaoo bɛ mli.

english: What kind of support can I expect from the Cocoa Health and Extension officers who visit our village?
ga: Mɛɛ yelikɛbuamɔ manyɛ makpa gbɛ kɛjɛ Cocoa Health kɛ Extension nitsulɔi ni baa wɔ akrowa lɛ adɛŋ?

english: Extension officers from the Cocoa Health and Extension Division provide free education on proper farm setup, disease detection, pruning techniques, and access to government-backed rehabilitation programs to keep your trees healthy.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni yaa hiɛ ni jɛ Cocoa Hewalɛ kɛ Nɔyaa Nitsumɔhe lɛ haa tsɔsemɔ ni aheee nɔ ko yɛ ŋmɔ mli saamɔ kpakpa, helai ni ana, ŋmɔshi nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ he. kɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa gbɛjianɔtoi ni nɔyeli fiɔ sɛɛ ni akɛsaa tsei lɛ koni eha otsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How many years after I plant my cocoa seedlings will the trees start producing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni midu kookoo dumɔwui lɛ? Ani tso lɛ baaje shishi ewo ŋmeii?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties commonly planted in Ghana begin bearing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, compared to older traditional varieties that take about 4 to 5 years.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ hybrid cocoa henɔi ni afɔɔ dumɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, kɛ akɛto blema cocoa henɔi ni heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5 lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that get burned under harsh, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a protective umbrella and retains soil moisture during dry periods.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he ni ehi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do some of the cocoa pods on my farm turn dark brown or black before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ediŋŋ dani amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads during wet and cool weather. Keeping your farm pruned to allow air flow and harvesting ripe pods promptly helps prevent the fungus from damaging your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i be mli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli, ni okpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why would an extension officer advise me to cut down a tree with swollen stems instead of giving me chemical spray?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ mafo tsei ni amɛshishifãi lɛ efuu lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ tsofai baashwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Swollen stems are a sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease, which has no chemical cure. The virus spreads to surrounding healthy trees through small insects called mealybugs, so physically removing the infected tree is the only way to save the rest of your farm.
ga: Tso ni efuu lɛ ji cocoa bud virus hela ni efuu lɛ he okadi, ni tsofa ko bɛ ni baanyɛ atsa. Virus lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii anɔ. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oye obua oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off the extra branches and green shoots growing from the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo tsei niji ni fa fe nine kɛ tsei eŋɔli ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-koko tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, often called suckers or chupons, waste the tree's water and nutrients without producing pods. Cutting them off allows the cocoa tree to focus its energy on producing large, healthy pods on its main branches.
ga: Tsoi ni fa fe nine, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ amɛ shoots loo chupon. Ebaafite nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ efeee. Cacao tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa ejwɛŋmɔ maa tso lɛ niji wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava right next to my cocoa seedlings on the same land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii, tamɔ ŋmei, yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: While intercropping with plantain is helpful for shade, cassava feeds heavily on soil nutrients and competes aggressively with young cocoa roots. It is better to plant food crops at a safe distance so they do not stunt the cocoa seedling's growth.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei ni akɛ plantains kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha hulutsoo moŋ, shi Cassava yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ni ekɛ cocoa shishifãi bibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa. Esa akɛ adu niyenii yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe bɔni afee ni kookoo tso lɛ akatsĩ edalɛ naa.

english: Cocoa trees should be spaced roughly 3 meters by 3 meters (10 feet by 10 feet) apart. Proper spacing ensures each tree gets enough sunlight and nutrients from the soil while allowing sufficient air movement to deter fungal diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ afee aaafee mitai 3 x mitai 3 (naji 10 x naji 10). Nɛkɛ jɛkɛmɔ nɛɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa tsɔɔ mli koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce a huge harvest in some months and very few pods in others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ nyɔji komɛi amli, ni nyɔji krokomɛi hu woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees follow Ghana's rainy and dry seasons. The major rainfall season triggers heavy flowering that leads to the main harvest (October to February), while the minor rain season results in a smaller harvest (May to June).
ga: Cocoa tsei nyiɛɔ Ghana nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hɔmɔ bei lɛ asɛɛ. Nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ kɛ fɔfɔi ni tsii baa ni no kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ baa. (October kɛyashi February) yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be fioo lɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ baa shi fioo. (May kɛyashi Otukwajaŋ)

english: Why is it good for me to plant beans in the same soil where I plan to plant maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mito gbɛjianɔ akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Beans naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Planting beans leaves behind rich nutrient reserves that help heavy-feeding crops like maize grow bigger and stronger in the next planting season.
ga: Beans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beans ni aduɔ lɛ shĩɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmãa be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my sorghum crop survive long dry spells much better than my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Sorghum has very deep roots that reach far down for groundwater, and its leaves can roll up tight to hold onto moisture. When water is scarce, sorghum pauses its growth instead of dying, and it recovers quickly as soon as rain falls.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ waa ni baanyɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ waa. Ni ebaai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Beni nu faaa lɛ, ŋmei lɛ baakpa shweremɔ moŋ fe ni eeegbo. ni ebaahe ejɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ pɛ

english: Why do my cassava plants drop all their leaves when the weather gets very hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava sheds its leaves on purpose during dry seasons to stop water from escaping into the warm air. The plant is not dead; it is conserving energy underground so it can sprout fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsɔɔ yiŋtoo ko nɔ eshwieɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni nu akajo foi kɛya he ni hulutsoo be lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi hewalɛ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni baai heei anyɛ akwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ.

english: These pests are Fall Armyworms, which lay eggs on young maize leaves because they love feeding on the soft stem tissue inside. Catching them early with neem extracts or approved pesticide sprays stops them before they destroy the growing point of the plant.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ ejaakɛ amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛye ŋmãa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Amɔmɔ amɛ mra Kɛtsɔ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, kpa amɛ dani amɛfite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why does my millet head produce a black, powdery soot instead of healthy grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-millet yitsei lɛ miifee sũ ni tamɔ powder diŋ yɛ ŋmaa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: That black powder is caused by a fungal infection called smut, which enters the plant through infected seeds or soil. Treating your seeds with a safe fungicide before planting helps protect the crop from developing this disease.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ soot ji nɔ ni kɛ powda diŋ lɛ baa. ni boteɔ tsei amli kɛtsɔɔ dumɔwui loo shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tsu dumɔwui ahe nii dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hela nɛɛ he.

english: Why do I need to keep standing water in my paddy field while my rice is growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahã nu ahi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ miikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Rice plants thrive in wet soil, while most aggressive weeds cannot survive under water. Keeping a controlled layer of water prevents weeds from competing with your rice for sunlight and soil nutrients.
ga: Omɔ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni jwɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ateŋ mɛi babaoo nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ nu shishi lɛ, Nu lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ tsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ.

english: Why are the tips of my rice leaves drying up and turning brown during sunny afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Rice leaf tips burn when the water level in the field drops too low or when the soil lacks potassium. Keeping proper water levels and supplying balanced nutrients prevents the sun from scorching the plant leaf tips.
ga: Omɔ baa yitsei lɛ shãa kɛji nu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ba shi tsɔ. aloo be mli ni potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu lɛ mlihiɛmɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ baaye abua ni hulu la akashã tsei ahe baai lɛ ashishigbɛ.

english: Plantain roots grow close to the soil surface and can be weakened by underground pests like root nematodes or stem borers. Staking heavy fruiting trees with strong wooden poles and keeping pests away prevents them from uprooting.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ daa ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo stem borers lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni tsii ni woɔ yibii ni tsii lɛ wo tso ni mli wa nɔ, ni okɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akabote mli lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkajie amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning purple or pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ purple loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves mean your maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, while purple leaves show a lack of phosphorus in the soil. Applying balanced fertilizer early gives the young plants the nutrients needed to stay dark green and grow fast.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. yɛ be mli ni baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja baatsu nii mra Enɛ baaha tsei bibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why are my harvested cassava tubers thin and tough instead of big and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni akpa lɛ ji mlɛo ni amɛhe wa moŋ fe ni amɛaafee wuji ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers turn out small and woody when planted in hard, unplowed soil or when exposed to long periods of severe drought during stem formation. Loosening the soil well before planting gives the roots space to expand into fat, starch-filled tubers.
ga: Cassava ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛfeɔ tsei kɛji akɛ akwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuko nɔ loo kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani adu lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ amli gbɛ lɛ mli alɛɛ ni etsɔ ŋmei ni mli ewo fɔ, ni ŋmei yɔɔ mli.

english: Why is it good to plant plantains on the same land as my newly planted cocoa shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu plantains yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni adu kookoo ŋmeii heei lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide shade, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist while its roots grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes up for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo tsei kɛha sweet potato wain tso lɛ ni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing plant that needs maximum sunlight on its leaves to produce big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off damp soil where fungal diseases spread easily.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la babaoo yɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baaha baai lɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient needed for green leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: This soft black rot is caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often triggered by inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil moisture steady helps the plant take up calcium properly.
ga: Calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ hela ni ji soft black rot nɛɛ baa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa calcium ni sa.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a light rain. Avoid applying right before heavy downpours, as torrential rain will wash the fertilizer away before the roots can absorb it.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni akɛtsuɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baajie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water builds up in the soil, allowing root rot diseases to attack. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps extra water drain away from the root zone.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni ekã shi lɛ bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ hela aba. Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking plant sap, or passing a virus to the crop. Spraying natural neem water or mild soap solution helps clear these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo ekɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baa ŋmɔshi nibii amli Kɛ adebɔɔ mli neem nu loo samla ni mli ejɔ baashwie nɔ Ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers drop off without making pods if the tree lacks water during dry weather, if insect pests damage the stems, or if there are not enough tiny insects in the farm to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii kɛji akɛ nu bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches that make them top-heavy. Supporting the stem with a strong wooden bamboo prop prevents the plant from uprooting during storms.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛyɛ jwɛi ni mli tse, ni no haa amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsei ni wa fĩ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ahum be mli.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests if I plant maize on the same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year. Alternating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Ni akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the middle down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ kɛmiiya shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for leaf growth. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plant regain its green color and produce bigger ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu eŋɔli kɛ amɛtoii wuji lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my land make my next maize crop grow much better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha mi ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ waa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, which means their roots work with natural soil organisms to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth. When you plant maize afterward, it feeds on that leftover soil food.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaye niyenii ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I avoid putting fertilizer on my farm when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can drink it. In dry soil, strong chemical fertilizers sit around the roots and can burn or destroy them instead of feeding the crop.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi. shishifãi lɛ ni ebaanyɛ eshã loo efite amɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil when it rains heavily for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rainwater fills all the spaces in the dirt without draining away, it chokes the roots and creates the right environment for fungi to cause rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hei ni etseee lɛ amli. Enɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa ni eha shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ aha ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii aba.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and turning crispy during the hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that suck sap and spread viruses, combined with heat stress. The plant curls its leaves to save water, but the insect virus stops it from fruiting properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa. kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ fata he Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Shi kooloi amli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkawo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very little fruit when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are overcrowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients. They spend all their energy growing tall to reach the sun instead of using energy to grow thick stems and heavy fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fa tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ yɛ amɛhe. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara koni amɛshɛ hulu lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, e kɛ he wami tsuɔ ní kɛ haa tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ yiblii nɛ mi wa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to make food for the tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, prevents disease, and helps the plant produce larger yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, ebaatsi helai anaa, ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo sweet potatoes wuji.

english: Why are the tiny flowers falling off my cocoa trees without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Migbee shi kɛjɛ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔko pod?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers if they experience sudden dry heat, lack of soil moisture, or poor pollination by insects. Keeping shade trees on your farm maintains the moisture cocoa flowers need to set pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna hulutsoo be ni mli egbi trukaa. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ ehiii Tsei ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ akwɛmɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto amɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do some farmers pinch off the top leaves of pepper plants when they are young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shwieɔ amɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ baai lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Pinching the main top shoot forces the pepper plant to grow side branches instead of just growing straight up. More branches mean more flowers, which leads to a bigger harvest of peppers later on.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii titrii lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaaha pepper tso lɛ afee niji ni yɔɔ esɛɛ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ. Niji babaoo tsɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo. Enɛ haa sɛɛ mli lɛ, akpaa ŋmɔtɔ babaoo.

english: Why do weeds lower my crop harvest even after I have already added fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have strong roots and grow faster than most crops. If you do not clear them, they will drink up the fertilizer and water you applied before your main crops have a chance to use them.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni wa ni amɛdaraa oya fe tsei babaoo. Kɛji ojieee amɛ Amɛbaanu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient found in fertilizers, manure, or compost that helps plants stay green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa ni anaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields after I farm on it for a few years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo yɛ be mli ni mikɛ afii fioo komɛi etsu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops pull food and nutrients out of the earth every season. Without adding manure or fertilizer, or resting the land by planting nitrogen-fixing crops like beans, the soil becomes depleted.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he. aloo okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe kɛtsɔ tsei ni haa nitrogen hiɔ shi tamɔ ŋmeii ni ooodu lɛ nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How does leaving dry corn stalks on my field after harvest help my soil for the next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmãa ni egbi ni mashi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ kpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Leaving plant remains on the ground acts like a protective blanket that traps soil moisture, prevents rain from washing away topsoil, and gradually decays into natural fertilizer.
ga: Tso ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he, ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Etsiɔ nugbɔ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ ni fiofio lɛ efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crops very close together to get more food from my small land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni maná niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stems and small produce.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them under full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight. They need partial shade from nurse crops like plantain or shade trees to retain moisture while building a strong root system.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ nurse tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ be mli ni amaa shishifã ni mli wa lɛ

english: Flowers often drop off when the plant suffers from sudden heat stress, lack of consistent soil moisture, or a shortage of plant food needed to support fruit development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na hela ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli trukaa lɛ. Fɛ̃i ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa loo tsei niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai adalɛ ni bɛ

english: Can I use local herbs or strong-smelling plants like prɛkɛsɛ to protect my stored grains from insects?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ maŋ lɛ mli tsofai loo tsei ni he yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ waa, tamɔ prachese, atsu nii kɛbu miŋmaa ni mikɛto lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe?

english: Yes, many natural plant materials contain strong oils and scents that act as natural repellents, driving away insects like grain weevils without chemicals.
ga: Hɛɛ, adebɔɔ mli tsei ahe nibii babaoo yɛ mu kɛ tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni shwieɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ dumɔwui amli ŋmeii ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii.

english: Why do bad insects attack my farm more when my plants are weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi fɔji babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ be mli ni mitsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Healthy plants produce natural protective barriers, while weak or thirsty plants become soft and defenseless, making them easier targets for insects.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ loo kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ baafee blɛoo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛbu amɛhe. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii nyɛɔ amɛtutuaa amɛ oya.

english: Root rot happens when heavy rains leave excess water trapped around the roots in poorly drained soil, encouraging fungal diseases that spoil the crop.
ga: Shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ tsɔ he fɛɛ he. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ Ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii baa.

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines turn yellow and naturally dry up, showing that the plant has finished storing energy underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to stay green and grow strong cobs, so adding compost, poultry manure, or nitrogen fertilizer can fix this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do my cassava plants keep growing very tall leaves but only produce tiny tuber roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ kɛlɛ waa shi shishifãi bibii lɛ? Shikpɔŋ shishi pɛ

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or water, cassava puts all its energy into growing tall leaves instead of storing food in the tubers underneath. Planting in well-drained soil without over-fertilizing encourages the plant to build bigger roots.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kakadaji moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato eyitso shishi. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli fe nine lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ená shishifãi wuji.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my crops right after the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants with deep, tough root systems that are already adapted to local soil. They can absorb rainwater and nutrients much faster than your planted crops, which is why clearing them early is important.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji tso ko ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni etsake ehe kɛtee jɛmɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni oduɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie amɛ mra lɛ. no hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep dropping off before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, dry soil, or uneven watering stresses the tomato plant, causing it to drop its flowers to save energy instead of letting them turn into tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Ha egbee shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite moŋ fe ni oooha etsɔ tomato.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop some of their tiny young pods before they fully grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ? Dani ebaada kwraa?

english: This is called cherelle wilt. Cocoa trees naturally drop extra young pods when the tree does not have enough water or nutrients in the soil to feed all the pods at once.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsɛnsi ni egbo. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ shikome.

english: Why do my okra pods become hard and tough to chop if I leave them on the plant for a few extra days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra ŋmɔji lɛ mli wa ni ewa akɛ abaakpa kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ gbii fioo komɛi krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Okra pods harden as they age because the plant is using its energy to form hard seeds inside for reproduction. Harvesting the pods while they are small and young keeps them soft and tender.
ga: Roselle ŋmeii lɛ mli waa beni amɛdaraa lɛ, be mli ni tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ dumɔwui ni wa yɛ emli kɛha fɔmɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwie shi beni amɛji bibii lolo ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Overwatered pepper plants develop soft, yellow, droopy leaves in wet soil, while underwatered plants look dry, brittle, and wilted during the heat of the afternoon.
ga: Pepper tsei ni awo amɛ nu fe nine lɛ baaná baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii tsei ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbi, amɛhe ejɔ, ni amɛgboi yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl up tightly during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains curl their broad leaves to protect themselves from harsh sunlight and trap moisture inside, which reduces the amount of water lost through heat.
ga: Plantain baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. Enɛ haa nu ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ mli baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do I need to clear tall trees and bushes before planting my corn field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie tsei kakadaji kɛ tsei bibii dani madu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Corn plants need full, direct sunlight all day long to manufacture food and build heavy cobs. Shading from trees slows down their growth and reduces your harvest.
ga: Abɛi tsei he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli koni amɛná niyenii ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni tsii. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaaha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ fioo, ni ebaaha okpamɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on instead of growing flat on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu lɛ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food. Lifting them off the ground prevents leaf diseases caused by damp soil and helps the plant produce much larger yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛ́ owó nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei ahe helai ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛbaa lɛ naa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni dara kwraa.

english: How do I know the exact time to plant my seeds after the long dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ eho lɛ?

english: Wait until the soil stays wet for a few days after early rains start. Planting too early in warm, dry soil causes the seeds to dry out and burn before they can germinate properly.
ga: Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ ebɔi nɛmɔ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛshã dani amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants spend all their energy fighting each other for sunshine, water, and soil food. Spacing them correctly allows every plant to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwu amɛha hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa waa ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do young cocoa trees wither and die if I cut down all the large trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily in direct sunshine. Leaving big trees or planting plantains beside them provides living shade that cools the soil and keeps the young trees alive until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ oshi tsei wuji loo odu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i, ni ebaaye ebua tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi kɛyashi amɛbaashɛ amɛdalɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which plants need to make food. Adding poultry manure or nitrogen fertilizer will restore green color and support heavy cob growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni tso lɛ he hiaa koni ekɛfee niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi ashishifã loo nitrogen ŋtayaa fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ, ni eye ebua ni ŋmei lɛ adara babaoo.

english: Why is it recommended to plant groundnuts or beans on my plot before planting maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani adu ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil to act as natural fertilizer for the next maize crop.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha sɛɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks sunlight from weed seeds so they cannot grow, while keeping moisture trapped in the soil for your crops.
ga: Mulching kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni eha jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ hulu lɛ he koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving droppings inside?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Checking your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts into the central leaves helps protect the corn.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. Ni kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem ni ajieɔ yi lɛ wo baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmãa lɛ he.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting on raised mounds or ridges lets excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: What causes my cocoa tree branches to swell up and leaves to turn yellow before the tree dies?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo niji lɛ shwieɔ shi ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ gboɔ?

english: This is Cocoa Swollen Shoot Disease, caused by a virus carried by tiny insects called mealybugs. Infected trees cannot be cured and must be cut down to prevent the disease from spreading to healthy trees.
ga: Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ amli baa. Virus ko ni kooloi bibii hiɛɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Anyɛɛɛ atsa tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ, ni esa akɛ afolɔ amɛ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why should I buy new certified seeds instead of saving seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to withstand local pests and dry weather better, producing much higher yields than saved seeds, which lose their strength over time.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛshi he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni ato. ni baafite hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli

english: Why do I keep seeing red ants crawling on my crop trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miyaa nɔ minaa ŋmeii tsuji ni shwieɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Red ants are often attracted to bushy shoots, weeds, or honeydew produced by small sap-sucking insects like mealybugs. Pruning extra branches and controlling sap-sucking pests helps keep red ants away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii, jwɛi, loo wuo ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mealybugs lɛ feɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii tsuji. Nibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ ŋmeii tsuji anaa.

english: What happens if I do not cut off the side shoots growing at the bottom of my plantains or tree crops?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mifooo sɛɛ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain loo jwɛi tso ko shishi lɛ?

english: Leaving unnecessary side shoots allows them to steal nutrients and water from the main stem. This dense growth also creates shade and moisture that attract pests like red ants and diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ ashɛrɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ afã lɛ ashwie shi ni he ehiaaa lɛ, ehaa amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ shweremɔ ni mli wa nɛɛ hu haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni gbalaa kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii tsuru kɛ helai baa.

english: Should I cut down a tree on my farm if it keeps attracting harmful ants?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛji amɛyaa nɔ amɛgbalaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ?

english: Before cutting down the entire tree, try pruning off bushy side shoots, clearing surrounding weeds, and managing minor pest infestations, as removing excess foliage usually reduces ant activity.
ga: Dani obaafo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ Bɔɔmɔdɛŋ ni ofo sɛɛ ŋmeii ni feɔ jwɛi lɛ. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. Ni okɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii atsu nii, ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, baai ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii anitsumɔ baa shi.

english: How do ants travel from one crop tree to another across my farm?
ga: Te ŋmeii feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛfãa gbɛ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Ants move easily across touching branches, overlapping leaves, exposed root systems, and tall weeds that bridge the gap between neighboring trees.
ga: Ants tsɔɔ tsei niji ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ amli mlɛo. baai ni feɔ ekome lɛ gbeleɔ shishifãi kɛ jwɛi kakadaŋŋ agboi ni tsiɔ gbɛ ni kã tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ ateŋ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my crops produce fruits or shoots that fall off before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ woɔ yibii loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Young fruits and shoots drop early when the plant is stressed by insect pests, prolonged dry weather, lack of soil nutrients, or overcrowding from unpruned shoots.
ga: Yibii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai miigba tsei lɛ anaa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo tsei ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔɔɔ amɛ

english: Why are some of my trees failing to show any fruit or leaves when it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ekomɛi ejieee yibii loo baai kpo kɛ́ be shɛ ni abaakpa nii lɛ?

english: Trees may fail to produce expected yields if hidden stem pests are blocking water and food inside the trunk, or if the soil lacks essential plant nutrients.
ga: Ekolɛ tsei lɛ wooo yibii ni akpaa gbɛ lɛ kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ tsi nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa. aloo kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do some of my crop trees take much longer to mature compared to others on the same land?
