ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ekomɛi heɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa kɛ akɛto ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ he kome lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Delayed plant growth often happens when crops are forced to compete with heavy weed growth and extra side shoots, or when they are weakened by root and stem pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei adalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ anyɛ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ jwɛi babaoo ni daa kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni fa fe nine lɛ abɔ akaŋ. aloo be mli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi anɔ lɛ egbɔjɔ tsei nɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if insects or diseases are living inside the trunk of my tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi bibii loo helai yɛ mitso lɛ shishi?

english: Internal trunk pests often leave visible clues such as tiny holes in the bark, sawdust-like powder at the base of the tree, yellowing leaves, or branches that break unexpectedly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni yeɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ shiɔ okadii ni anaa, tamɔ buji bibii yɛ tso lɛ shishi, ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔtɔ, loo tsei niji ni ekumɔ trukaa.

english: Can large wild trees like the Odum tree bring pests onto my farm crops?
ga: Ani koo mli tsei wuji, tamɔ Odam tsei lɛ baanyɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ helai aba ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli?

english: Yes, certain large forest and shade trees act as alternate homes for insects and fungi, which can easily migrate to your farm crops if branches touch or weeds connect them.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooi kɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ shia ni ji enyɔ kɛha kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛfã kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli oya kɛji tsei niji ta amɛhe loo jwɛi lɛ tsa amɛhe.

english: How does trimming branches regularly help my crop plants grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mifoɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Trimming removes dead or unproductive stems so the plant directs all its food to healthy leaves and fruit production, while also opening the canopy to light and airflow.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei ni egboi loo ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni tso lɛ akudɔ eniyenii fɛɛ kɛya baai kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebaawo lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, agbeleɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ naa koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba mli.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves usually mean your maize plants are stressed, often due to a lack of nitrogen in the soil or an attack by small pests like fall armyworms or aphids. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or inspecting the leaves for insect damage can help you address the issue early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-corn tsei lɛ miihao. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii tamɔ cutworms loo aphids ni tutuaa amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea fata he loo okwɛ baai lɛ amli kɛji kooloi efite lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni otsa naagba lɛ mra.

english: What causes my tomato fruits to rot at the bottom before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-tomato lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shishigbɛ dani eshɛɔ po?

english: This problem is called blossom end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium or when watering is uneven. Keeping the soil moisture consistent and adding calcium or organic compost to the soil before planting helps stop this from happening.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ calcium loo organic compost ni akɛaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu lɛ baaye abua ni enɛ akafee.

english: Why are powdery white spots spreading across the leaves of my okra plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii yɛŋ ni tamɔ powder yɛ mi okra baai lɛ fɛɛ ahe lɛ?

english: White spots on okra leaves are usually caused by a fungal infection called powdery mildew, which thrives in warm, humid weather when plants are crowded. Giving plants enough space for air to blow through and removing damaged leaves will help keep the fungus away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni yɔɔ okra baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Amɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ fɛ̃i mli be mli ni tsei eyi obɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ oha tso lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli, ni ojie baai ni efite lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akabote mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: During the hottest part of the day, pepper leaves lose water through evaporation faster than the roots can drink it up. The plant wilts slightly to protect itself from the intense heat, but it will naturally bounce back in the cooler evening.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Tso lɛ baagbi fioo koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ he. Shi efoɔ esɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines naturally search for sunlight to make food for the growing tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves elevated off the damp soil where diseases spread easily and exposes more of the leaves to sunlight so the tubers grow larger.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei taoɔ hulu la koni amɛkɛfee niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ he ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ nɔ ni ehaa baa lɛ naa hulu la babaoo koni ekɛ bulbs wuji aba.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing plenty of leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants produce too many leaves and few pods when they get too much nitrogen fertilizer. Cowpeas naturally capture their own nitrogen from the air, so extra nitrogen forces the plant to focus on leaf growth instead of flowering and making beans.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ woɔ baai babaoo tsɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo tsɔ kɛ́ amɛná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, nitrogen ni fa lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a fɔɔ fɔfɔi nɛ a woɔ nu.

english: Why is it important to clear all the weeds around my cassava stems before I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni wɔjie jwɛi ni bɔle ehe lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni adu ŋmei tsei dani adu.

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and ground nutrients that young cassava stems need to establish strong roots. Clearing the land thoroughly gives your cassava cuttings the space and resources they need to sprout healthily.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ŋmei tsei bibii koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Kɛ́ otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa o-cassava lɛ náa hegbɛ kɛ nibii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant my crop seeds in neat lines instead of scattering them over the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo nɔ moŋ fe ni magbɛ amɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines ensures every plant has enough space so they do not fight each other for nutrients and sunlight. It also makes it much easier for you to walk through the farm to weed, apply fertilizer, and harvest.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛyeee akaŋ yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ hulu la he yɛ amɛteŋ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo hu akɛ oootsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oyajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni okpa ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my soil is weak and needs fertilizer before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nii dani mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: If your crops grew poorly in the past season, had pale leaves, or if the soil feels hard and light in color, your soil is likely low in nutrients. Adding well-rotted animal manure or compost helps restore life and nourishment to weak soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli, eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ, loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔji ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha wala kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aba shikpɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my maize is fully mature and ready for harvesting and storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa ni akɛto?

english: Maize is ready for dry storage when the outer husks turn completely brown and dry, and the kernels become hard enough that your fingernail cannot dent them. Harvesting at this stage prevents mold and insect infestation during storage.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ akɛbaato he ko ni egbi beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi kwraa lɛ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛhaŋ otsitsii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ anaa yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I clear away all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need protection from direct, harsh sunlight. Big shade trees or tall plants like plantains act as natural shields, keeping the young cocoa leaves cool and preserving moisture in the soil until the cocoa roots grow strong.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛhe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo baai bibii lɛ amli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ waɔ.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to manufacture food for the tuber growing underground. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground with stakes helps them capture maximum sunlight while protecting the foliage from fungal diseases on the wet soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: When too many small shoots grow around the parent plantain, they fight for the same water and nutrients in the soil. Pruning extra shoots allows the main plant to focus its energy on growing a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ he lɛ Ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa tso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa dumɔwui wuji ni tsii ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up into cups during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi efeɔ kɔɔpoo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in hot weather is a pepper plant's defense mechanism. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun to conserve water and prevent itself from drying out.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ pepper tsei ahe. Tsei haa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ mli koni nu akafite ni amɛtsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the inside leaves of my young maize stalks overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ye mi-abɛi bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms. The adult moths lay eggs inside the central shoot of the maize, and once hatched, the worms hide deep within the leaves during the day to avoid heat before feeding.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms. Kplukai ni eda lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ. Ni kɛ́ efɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he dani amɛyeɔ nii.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up when the heavy rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Continuous rain creates high dampness in the air, which encourages a water mold that causes Black Pod disease. The rain splashes fungal spores from the soil and infected branches onto healthy pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli feɔ fɛ̃i waa. Enɛ haa ŋmei ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ tsuɔ nii. Nugbɔ shwieɔ fungal spores kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ lɛ kɛ tsei niji anɔ kɛyaa pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or water is inconsistent. Extreme heat stresses the plant, causing it to shed blossoms to save energy rather than trying to support fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi baa koni akɛto hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni aaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ana aduawai.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves indicate a lack of nitrogen, which is the essential plant food responsible for deep green leaves and fast growth. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen out of the upper soil.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. Eji tso niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa oya. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Excess water fills up all air spaces in the ground, suffocating the roots. Without oxygen, the cassava tubers weaken and rot-causing organisms in the soggy soil quickly break them down.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ, Cassava tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni nibii ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya.

english: Maize consumes a lot of soil nutrients, especially nitrogen. Legumes like groundnuts put nitrogen back into the soil through their roots, restoring soil fertility naturally for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. titri lɛ nitrogen Legumes, tamɔ ŋmeii, kɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koni akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I just cut any vine from my neighbor's farm and plant it on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifolɔŋ wain tso yɛ mikutsoŋnyo ŋmɔ mli ni madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Random vines from another farm might look fine on the outside, but they can carry hidden pests or diseases. Using unverified planting material can spread infections to your entire field and drastically reduce your harvest.
ga: Wein tsei ni jɛ ŋmɔ kroko mli lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ. Shi ekolɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ jɛmɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni akɛduɔ nii ni akako amɛ akwɛ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbɛ hela eshwa he ni oyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni eha ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ aba shi kwraa.

english: Why is it important to carefully inspect my vine cuttings before planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ miwein tsei lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ dani madu lɛ?

english: Inspecting vine cuttings ensures you only plant strong, disease-free materials. Starting with healthy vines gives your crops the best chance to establish strong roots, resist field diseases, and yield a large harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ owein tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa onaa nɔmimaa akɛ nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ mli pɛ oduɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ je shishi lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni ewoɔ babaoo

english: What should I look out for when selecting good vines to plant on my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ makwɛ mihe jogbaŋŋ yɛ he kɛ́ mihala wain tsei kpakpai ni mikɛbaadu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Look for vines with firm stems, fresh green leaves, and no signs of dark spots, curling leaves, holes from insects, or soft rotting areas. Choosing vibrant, clean stems ensures your crop grows strong.
ga: Taomɔ wain tsei ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ, baai ni ebɔle amɛhe, kooloi amli ŋmeii, loo hei ni egboi bɛ mli. Kɛ́ ohala tsei ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ adara waa.

english: How can I tell if a vine is sick or infected before I put it in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela emɔ wain tso ko loo hela ko emɔ lɛ dani madu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: A sick vine usually shows warning signs such as yellowing or wrinkled leaves, dark spots on the stem, soft decay, or tiny insects clinging to the joints. If you spot any of these signs, discard the vine immediately.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, wain tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ jieɔ kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii, tamɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni egbɔjɔ. ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ fioo loo kooloi bibii yɛ ni kpɛtɛɔ fãji ahe Kɛji ona okadii nɛɛ Shĩ wain tso lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Can a single diseased vine spread sickness to the other healthy crops in my farm?
ga: Wein tso kome ni hela emɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala hela kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi anɔ. Ani eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, diseases on a single vine can easily spread to neighboring healthy plants through the soil, water runoff, farm tools, or insects, which can ruin a large portion of your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, hela ko ni yɔɔ wain tso kome nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli oya kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ, nu ni hoɔ, okwaayeli nibii loo kooloi bibii anɔ, ni baanyɛ akpata oŋmɔ lɛ mli hei wuji ahiɛ.

english: If I plant an infected vine, will it heal itself once it starts growing in good soil?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu wain tso ni hela emɔ lɛ Beni ajeɔ dumɔ shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ Ani ebaaya lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: No, planting an infected vine in good soil will not cure it. The disease will grow alongside the plant, weakening it, stunting its growth, and preventing it from producing good tubers or fruits.
ga: Dabi, wein tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ lɛ tsaŋ lɛ. Hela lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛfata tso lɛ he. egbɔjɔɔ tso lɛ ni ehaa edalɛ baa shi ni ehaa ŋmeii loo aduawai kpakpai baaa.

english: Why do some of my newly planted vines rot in the soil shortly after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miwein tsei ni midu ehee lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Vines often rot in the soil if they were already carrying hidden fungal or bacterial diseases before planting, or if they were cut with dirty tools that allowed germs to infect the stem.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ wain tsei lɛ baafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ amɛhiɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo bacteria helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ dani amɛdu. Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛ nibii ni he tseee ni baanyɛ agbala helai kɛya tso lɛ shishi lɛ ŋmɔ amɛ.

english: Does the quality of the vine I plant really affect how much crop I harvest at the end of the season?
ga: Ani bɔ ni wain tsei ni miduɔ lɛ hi ha lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ he?

english: Yes, the quality of your planting vine directly determines your final harvest. Clean and strong vines develop larger root systems and yield bigger, healthier crops compared to weak or diseased vines.
ga: Hɛɛ, bɔ ni wain tsei ni oduɔ lɛ hi ha lɛ baatsɔɔ naagbee nɔ ni obaaná lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Wein tsei ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ shishifãi wuji ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ akɛto wein tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe.

english: How does taking time to select clean planting vines save me money?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ be ni okɛhalaa wain tsei ni he tse ni aduɔ lɛ haa okɛ shika baa shi?

english: Carefully selecting clean vines prevents you from wasting money and hard work on fertilizers, water, and weeding for crops that will end up failing due to early disease.
ga: Wein tsei ni he tse ni ooohala jogbaŋŋ lɛ baatsi bo gbɛ koni okafite shika kɛ nitsumɔ ni wa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baafite yɛ hela ni baa mra lɛ hewɔ.

english: What is the best way to handle my vine cuttings after taking them before they go into the soil?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ matsu miwein tso lɛ mli tsei lɛ ahe nii beni mijie amɛ dani midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Keep your vine cuttings in a cool, shaded place and plant them as soon as possible. Leaving them exposed to the hot sun dries them out and weakens them, making them easy targets for soil infections.
ga: Ha wain tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ ahi he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni odu oya bɔ ni abaanyɛ. Kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛgbi ni amɛgbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mɛi ni shikpɔŋ nɔ helai baanyɛ atswa amɛ oya.

english: How long does it usually take from the day I plant a plantain sucker until I can harvest the first bunch?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni abaanyɛ akpa klɛŋklɛŋ kuu lɛ?

english: Plantains generally take between 12 to 15 months (or up to 2 years depending on weather, soil quality, and water supply) to grow, flower, and fully mature for harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantains heɔ nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 (loo kɛyashi afii 2 ni damɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su kɛ nu jɛɛhe nɔ) dani ekwɛ̃ɔ, ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni edara ni efee klalo kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ.

english: Why do some crops take years to yield while others are ready in just a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi yeɔ afii babaoo dani amɛduɔ nii yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu yeɔ klalo yɛ nyɔji fioo pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Short-term crops like maize or vegetables complete their life cycle fast, while long-term crops like plantains and cocoa spend their first few years building deep root systems and strong trunks before they can produce fruit.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai gbeɔ amɛwala shihilɛ naa oya. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ plantains kɛ cocoa lɛ heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ dani amɛtoɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni wa dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Do I need to buy new plantain shoots every year, or will the original plant keep growing on its own?
ga: Ehe miihia ni mahe plantain tsei heei daa afi. Aloo shishijee tso lɛ baaya nɔ eda yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe?

english: You do not need to buy new shoots every year because the parent plant produces new shoots called 'suckers' at its base, which grow into the next generation of fruiting plants automatically.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni ohé ŋmeii heei daa afi. Enɛ ji akɛ, tso nyɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii heei ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘ŋmeii’ yɛ shishigbɛ ni baakwɛ̃ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛbatsɔ yibii tsei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Is it normal for a plantain stem to die after producing just one bunch of fruit?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni ja akɛ plantain tsei lɛ baagboi beni amɛwo yibii akuu kome pɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, that is the natural behavior of the plant. Each individual stem dies after fruiting, but the underground root system stays alive and feeds the younger sucker shoots next to it.
ga: Hɛɛ, nakai ji bɔ ni tsei feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa lɛ. Tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gboɔ beni ewo yibii sɛɛ. Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baahi shi ni amɛye ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ emasɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do plantain trees fall over so easily when the fruit bunches start growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that do not go very deep into the soil. As the fruit bunch grows heavy, the plant becomes top-heavy and can easily get pulled down by wind unless supported with strong wooden poles.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ bafee tsii Tso lɛ ji ŋwɛi-tsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ agbala lɛ kɛba shi oya. ja tsei ni wa fiɔ sɛɛ

english: Can I grow fast food crops like maize or vegetables between my plantain trees while waiting for them to mature?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii ni ayeɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai. Midumɔwui lɛ ateŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping fast-growing crops like maize, beans, or vegetables between young plantain shoots makes good use of land and provides quick food and income while the plantains are still growing.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ, ni ehaa niyenii kɛ shika baa oya be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ miida lolo lɛ.

english: Why do farmers around here plant plantains inside new cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ biɛ lɛ miidu plantains yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains grow faster and have massive leaves that provide vital shade for young cocoa seedlings, protecting them from harsh sunlight and keeping the soil moist during their early years.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu kookoo tsei ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli

english: How can I survive financially if the main crop I planted takes two or three years before I can harvest and sell it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahi shi yɛ shika gbɛfaŋ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii titri ni miduɔ lɛ heɔ afii enyɔ loo etɛ dani manyɛ makpa ni mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Farmers manage long-term crop waiting periods by practicing multi-cropping—planting short-term crops like cassava, maize, or peppers alongside the main crop to generate continuous income and food.
ga: Okwaafoi kwɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli nibii ni amɛduɔ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ nibii babaoo ni amɛduɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmãa loo chili ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii titrii ahe koni akɛná shika kɛ niyenii ni yaa nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and dry out during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry and windy seasons like harmattan, plantains naturally drop older leaves to conserve water and prevent the whole plant from drying out.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa tamɔ Harmattan lɛ mli lɛ, plantains lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai momo lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekɛtsi tso muu lɛ fɛɛ naa koni ekagbi.

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm in Ghana is good enough for planting plantains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ Ghana lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha plantains ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Plantains thrive best in rich, dark soil that contains plenty of decayed organic matter, holds moisture well, and does not remain flooded with standing water after heavy rains.
ga: Plantains kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni yɔɔ diŋŋ ni nibii babaoo ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbo jogbaŋŋ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni nu shwieee nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food plant needs to grow. It can also happen when heavy rain washes away nutrients or leaves the soil too waterlogged for the roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu.

english: Why is it good practice for me to plant groundnuts or beans on my plot after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth and leaves the soil tired. Groundnuts and beans are special plants that trap food from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally fertilizing it for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi. Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni mɔɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees on my land when setting up a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni miitoɔ kookoo ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very fast and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa seedlings the shade and moisture they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually a sign of tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the plant's juices, or a sickness spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmiinu ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. loo helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the heat becomes too intense, when the plant lacks water, or when there are no insects around to visit the blossoms and help them turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu bɛ tsei amli loo be mli ni kooloi bibii bɛ amɛhe lɛ Fɔfɔi baa amɛbasara amɛ ni amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa amɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Which part of a cassava stick should I cut and plant to get the best yields?
ga: Mɛɛ fã esa akɛ afolɔ ni adu koni ená yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: The middle section of a healthy, mature cassava stem is the best part to plant. The bottom base is often too woody and old, while the top green tip is too soft and dries out easily before taking root.
ga: Kasava tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eda lɛ teŋgbɛ ji fã ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu. Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ shishitoo lɛ ji tso ni egbɔ tsɔ. yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi ŋta ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ tsɔ ni egbiɔ oya dani ewoɔ shishifãi.

english: Why do my maize plants produce thin stems and small cobs when I plant the seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each plant proper distance ensures it gets enough food and light to form thick stems and big cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko to he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaha niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsɔ tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater stays on the field for too long, it drowns the roots and allows soil rot fungi to attack and destroy the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. ni oha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfite amɛ.

english: Why do tall weeds sprout and spread much faster than my planted crops after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kakadaji lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally built to survive tough conditions, so they absorb rain and soil nutrients instantly. They grow quickly to steal sunlight and water before your planted crops have time to settle in.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni adebɔɔ fee koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛmɔɔ nugbɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Amɛdaraa oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la kɛ nu dani otso lɛ naa be ni ekɛ shishifãi baa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible. The more sunlight the leaves get, the more food the plant makes to grow a large tuber underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Babaoo ni hulu la ni baa lɛ naa lɛ, babaoo ni tso lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: If I spray chemical medicine on my crops, why do the plants still end up getting sick?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsofai shwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ Mɛni hewɔ tso lɛ hela mɔ lɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Spraying chemicals only works if applied before the disease becomes too advanced, or if the correct chemical is used for that specific disease. Additionally, some diseases live deep inside the soil where surface sprays cannot reach them.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ pɛ kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli dani hela lɛ egbɛ eshwa shɔŋŋ tsɔ. loo okɛ tsofai ni sa kɛha nakai hela lɛ atsu nii Kɛfata he lɛ, helai komɛi hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Can I mix different agricultural chemicals together to make them stronger against crop diseases?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ okwaayeli tsofai srɔtoi afutu? Ani abaanyɛ akɛ amɛ afee ekome koni amɛhe awa yɛ tsei ahe helai ahe?

english: Mixing different chemicals without proper advice can destroy their effectiveness, burn your crops, or create toxic solutions. Each chemical is designed to target specific pests or diseases and must be mixed according to strict instructions.
ga: Tsofai srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ Kɛ́ gbɛtsɔɔmɔ kpakpa bɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite bɔ ni tsofa lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ. shã onibii loo ofee tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei Afee tsofa fɛɛ tsofa koni ekɛtutua tsɛŋemɔ hela loo hela pɔtɛɛ ko. ni esa akɛ afutu mli yɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni mli wa naa.

english: Why do my crops still catch diseases even when I buy fresh, healthy seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ hela lolo eyɛ mli akɛ miheɔ dumɔwui heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Even healthy seeds can become infected after planting if the soil already contains hidden disease germs, if the irrigation water is contaminated, or if insects carry diseases from neighboring farms onto your plants.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ po baanyɛ aná hela beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ momo Kɛji nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ mli ewo muji Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni jɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli baa otsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do officers advise me not to plant on the same piece of land where my crops recently died from sickness?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akadu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni hela gbe miŋmɔshi nibii nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Many plant diseases, especially fungi and bacteria, can survive in the soil for months or years. Planting new crops in the same infected soil provides the disease with a fresh food source, causing your new plants to get sick immediately.
ga: Tsei ahe helai babaoo Titri lɛ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ Baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔji loo afii babaoo. Tsei heei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni hela lɛ emɔ nɔ tsutsu lɛ haa hela lɛ naa niyenii hee. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hela baamɔ otso hee lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Is there any way to clean or treat my soil after a disease destroys my harvest so I can plant again?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni matsɔ nɔ matsumɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo matsa lɛ beni hela efite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ sɛɛ koni manyɛ madu nii ekoŋŋ?

english: You can reduce disease in the soil by exposing it to direct sun heat through plowing, resting the land without planting (fallowing), or planting non-host crops that the specific disease cannot feed on.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi kɛtsɔ hulu la ni oooha eshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hejɔɔmɔ ni aduuu (tillage) loo aduuu tsei ni jeee gbɔ ni helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi nyɛŋ aye abua.

english: Why is it important to uproot and destroy plants that are already ruined by disease instead of leaving them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie tsei ni helai efite lɛ ni akpata amɛhiɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Leaving diseased plants in the farm allows the sickness to continue breeding and multiplying. Removing and destroying them cuts off the source of infection so it cannot spread to healthy crops or infect the soil further.
ga: Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa hela lɛ yaa hiɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ. Amɛjiemɔ kɛ amɛfitemɔ lɛ shwieɔ he ni hela lɛ jɛɔ lɛ. Enɛ ji koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli loo ekɛ hela aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo.

english: Why does a small disease on one plant spread so fast until the whole farm is ruined?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hela bibioo ko ni yɔɔ tso kome nɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya aahu akɛ efiteɔ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plant diseases multiply rapidly and travel easily through splashing rain water, wind, farm tools, or even on a farmer's boots. Once one plant is infected, nearby plants quickly catch the disease.
ga: Tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ okwaayeli nibii amli amɛfãa gbɛ mlɛo. loo okwaafonyo atadei po Kɛ́ hela mɔ tso ko Tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ hela mɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why are soft leaf vegetables like lettuce more easily destroyed by rot compared to crops like cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ tamɔ lettuce lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ akɛto tsei tamɔ ŋmei he lɛ?

english: Leafy vegetables have delicate tissues that hold moisture easily and grow close to the soil surface. This soft, wet environment makes it very easy for soil bacteria and fungi to attack and rot the leaves quickly.
ga: Aduawai ni yɔɔ baai yɛ fãji ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hiɛɔ nu mli oya ni amɛdaraa ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Shihilɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni efɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo waa akɛ helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatutua amɛ ni amɛfiteɔ oya.

english: What early signs should I look out for to know that my crops are catching a disease before the whole farm gets ruined?
ga: Mɛɛ mra be mli okadii esa akɛ makwɛ jogbaŋŋ koni male kɛji miŋmɔshi nii lɛ emɔ hela dani miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ akpata?

english: Look out for yellowing leaves, dark spots, wilting during cooler parts of the day, or soft, slimy spots near the base of the plant stem. Spotting these early allows you to remove infected plants before the sickness spreads.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmɔŋ, he ni edɔ, kɛ baai ni egbo yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ. aloo hei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tso lɛ shishi. Nibii nɛɛ akwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ojieɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ dani hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: What does crop rotation mean, and how does it stop diseases from killing my plants?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ shishi? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa helai ni miifite mitsei lɛ?

english: Crop rotation means changing the type of crop you plant in a field each season. Because specific diseases usually attack specific plant families, changing the crop starves and kills the leftover disease germs in the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ oŋmɔ mli lɛ atsakemɔ tsɔɔ akɛ obaatsake nibii ni oduɔ yɛ oŋmɔ mli lɛ daa afi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, helai komɛi sumɔɔ ni amɛtutua tsei awekui komɛi. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ gbeɔ hɔmɔ ni egbeɔ helai ni eshwɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do some of the flowers on my crops drop off without making any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Crops produce male flowers and female flowers. Fruit only forms when pollen moves from a male flower to a female flower; if a female flower receives no pollen, it drops off without producing fruit.
ga: Tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei. Yibii baa pɛ kɛji pollen lɛ jɛ fɔfɔi hii amli kɛtee fɔfɔi yei amli. Kɛji fɔfɔi yei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ pollen nɔ lɛ, amɛbaagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: What is the difference between male and female flowers on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Male flowers produce yellow powdery dust called pollen, while female flowers have a small bump at their base that turns into the actual fruit once pollen touches them.
ga: Fɔfɔi hii jieɔ sũ ŋmɔŋ ni atsɛɔ lɛ pollen. Yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi yei lɛ yɛ bɔɔt bibii. yɛ shishigbɛ, ni bafeɔ anɔkwa yibii kɛji akɛ pollen lɛ ta amɛhe.

english: Why is the inside of a female flower wet or sticky when it opens?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi yei amli lɛ mli fũuɔ loo ekpɛtɛɔ he kɛ́ amɛmiifɔ lɛ?

english: The natural liquid inside a female flower acts as a trap that catches pollen grains from male flowers and helps them stick so the flower can be fertilized.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli nu ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi yei lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ amale ni akɛmɔɔ fɔfɔi hii lɛ amli muji. ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he koni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ awo fɔmɔ nii.

english: Why do some crop flowers only stay open for a short time in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi komɛi fɛ̃ɔ be kukuoo pɛ leebi lɛ?

english: Flowers open when they are moist and ready to receive pollen. Once the hot afternoon sun comes, they dry up, so pollination must happen early while the flower is fresh.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ kɛji amɛhe edɔ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaaŋɔ pollen. Kɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ba lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbi. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ pollination aba mra. Be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ yɔɔ ehee lolo lɛ

english: Can I manually transfer pollen from one flower to another to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ minine ajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Yes, hand pollination involves taking pollen from a male flower and gently placing it onto a female flower, which is very helpful when natural insects are scarce.
ga: Hɛɛ, nine nɔ fɔfɔi ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ biɔ ni ajie fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi nuu lɛ mli lɛ fiofio. ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi yei anɔ Enɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa kɛ́ adebɔɔ mli kooloi fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Why must I be extremely gentle when doing hand pollination on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee blɛoo nɛkɛ beni mikɛ miniji miiwo miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Flower reproductive parts are thin and fragile. Handling them roughly can crush the delicate structures, killing the flower completely so no fruit will grow.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ fɔmɔ hei lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. nɔkwɛmɔ ni mli wa Baanyɛ akumɔ nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ. ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ gboɔ kwraa, no hewɔ lɛ ewooo yibii

english: What happens if I crush or break the male flower while trying to pollinate?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ fɔfɔi nuu ko shwie shi loo mifo mli beni miitao mawo lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Crushing the male flower destroys the pollen grains and damages the stem, making the pollen useless for fertilizing the female flower.
ga: Kɛ́ akumɔ fɔfɔi hii lɛ, efiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ, ni efiteɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa pollen lɛ he ehiaaa yɛ fɔfɔi yei lɛ afɔmɔ mli.

english: How do tiny insects in my field help my crops produce more fruits?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Insects like bees and midges walk over male flowers, pick up pollen on their bodies, and naturally deposit it onto female flowers while searching for nectar.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni nyiɛɔ fɔfɔi hii anɔ lɛ buaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ amɛgbɔmɔtsei lɛ anɔ lɛ anaa, ni amɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmli amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi yei anɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛtaoɔ ŋmeii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some of my fruits end up small, misshapen, or empty inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miyibii lɛ daraaa lɛ? yɛ su ko ni ejaaa Aloo nɔ ko bɛ emli?

english: Misshapen fruits happen when a female flower receives too little pollen or gets physically damaged during pollination, preventing proper seed and fruit growth.
ga: Yibii ni efite lɛ baa kɛji fɔfɔi yei lɛ ná pollen fioo tsɔ loo amɛfite yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ yɛ pollen be mli. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui kɛ aduawai nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Do I need special training to do hand pollination on delicate crops like cocoa?
ga: Ani tsɔsemɔ krɛdɛɛ he miihia mi koni manyɛ makɛ mi nine awo tso ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ kookoo mli?

english: Yes, because flowers are very small and sensitive, learning the right technique prevents you from damaging the flowers and losing potential harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa kwraa ni amɛhe waaa. Kɛ́ okase ŋaai ni ja lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni okafite ofɔfɔi lɛ ni okɛ hegbɛ ni oyɔɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ mli lɛ akafite.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because their tender leaves burn easily under full sun. Large forest trees act like umbrellas, shielding young cocoa from excessive heat, retaining soil moisture, and creating the cool, humid climate cocoa needs to grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Koo mli tsei wuji tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ofee kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli. Ehe miihia ni kookoo akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with very thin stems when I plant them under dense forest shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ́ adu yɛ koo ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava needs direct sunlight to produce food for root growth. When planted in heavy shade, the crop wastes its energy stretching upward to reach for light, resulting in tall, weak stems and small, poor tubers.
ga: Cassava he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ená niyenii kɛha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa la lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni kɛlɛ, ni bɛ hewalɛ, kɛ yitsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do crops planted right next to big forest trees grow smaller than crops planted further away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ ji bibii fe tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Large forest trees have massive root systems that swallow up most of the water and nutrients in the surrounding soil. Food crops planted too close cannot compete with these big roots and end up stunted from lack of nourishment.
ga: Koo mli tsei wuji yɛ shishifãi wuji ni miɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ babaoo. Niyenii tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛŋ amɛkɛ shishifãi wuji nɛɛ abɔ akaŋ ni amɛbaagbe naa ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my crops yield so much food during the first year after clearing forest land, but produce less in later years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wo yibii babaoo nɛkɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi ni mijie koo lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ? Shi ani ebaawo yibii fioo yɛ afii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli?

english: Forest land accumulates layers of decayed leaves and organic matter over decades, making the soil rich in natural nutrients. After a few harvests, the crops consume these initial nutrients, so yields drop unless you replenish the soil.
ga: Kooi amli hei buaa baai ni egboi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ anaa yɛ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli. Yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ shishijee niyenii nɛɛ baatsu nii. No hewɔ lɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi ja okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so fast and aggressively right after I clear trees to start my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa beni mijie tsei lɛ koni mije okwaayeli shishi pɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Weed seeds can lie dormant in dark forest soil for years. Clearing the trees exposes the soil to direct sunlight and rainwater, which acts as a trigger for thousands of dormant seeds to sprout all at once.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ awɔ. yɛ koo mli shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ nɔ afii babaoo Tsei ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni kanyaa dumɔwui ni ewɔ lɛ. Dumɔwui akpei abɔ kwɛ̃ shikome.

english: Why does leaving dry fallen leaves around the roots of my crops help them survive dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mishi baai ni egbee shi ni egboi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Dry leaves act as mulch, creating a protective blanket over the ground. This shade keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation during hot days, and gradually rots into rich plant food.
ga: Baai ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni afee tsɔne ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ shade nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli, ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii.

english: Why do my crops get more leaf diseases when planted very close to the edge of a dense forest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa folier helai babaoo kɛ́ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ koo ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Dense forest trees block wind flow and trap stagnant, humid air around your crops. Damp, still air prevents leaves from drying quickly after rain, creating ideal conditions for fungal diseases to sprout and spread.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ kooi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa ni amɛmɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ ni bɔleɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ dioo lɛ tsiɔ baai anaa koni amɛkagbi oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my maize plants wilt quickly if I plant them right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji midu yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain often wets only the top layer of dry soil while the deep ground remains hot. If a short dry spell follows, the shallow roots of young seedlings quickly scorch in the hot, drying earth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ pɛ. be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli edɔ lolo Kɛji akɛ be kuku ko ni mli egbi nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tsei bibii ashishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baashã oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do plantain suckers take much longer to produce fruit when planted in hard, packed soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are soft and fleshy, requiring loose, airy soil to spread out easily. In hard, compacted soil, the roots struggle to penetrate the earth, limiting the plant's ability to take up water and nutrients for quick fruiting.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛ loo. Enɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni edɔ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ hãaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai koni enyɛ ewo yibii oya.

english: Why do new hybrid crop seeds produce food faster than the old seeds saved from previous harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ woɔ niyenii oya fe dumɔwui momoi ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically developed to grow faster, resist common diseases, and channel most of their energy into early flowering and fruiting rather than just growing tall stems.
ga: Afee dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛdara oya. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛhaa fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo mra Moŋ lɛ, ekwɛ̃ɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko kɛkɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn stalks even fully grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs a lot of nutrients to stay green and strong, so adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer around the base helps the leaves stay healthy to feed the growing corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Niyenii babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii afata he kɛbɔle he. Koni lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛha ŋmãa toi ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why shouldn't I place fertilizer directly against the main stem of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts that can burn and destroy tender stems if placed directly against them. Placing fertilizer a few inches away from the stem in a ring allows the roots to absorb the food safely without burning the plant.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ashã ni efite ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ akɛma shi shiŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wo ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔɔ niyenii lɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛshãaa tso lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when the dry sun season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily in harsh sunlight, and their short roots cannot reach deep water. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby gives them living shade and keeps the soil cool until the trees are mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Ni shishifãi kukuji lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ tsei bibii, yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the soil for too long without draining, the roots drown and rot, so planting cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli.

english: How does covering my nursery beds with dry grass help my vegetables during hot weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni akɛhaa ŋmɔ mli saatsoi anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-aduawai lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass or dead leaves on top of the soil acts like a blanket that blocks direct sunlight, stopping moisture from evaporating out of the ground so plant roots stay cool and moist longer.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the heat gets too high or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly soaked. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulch helps the flowers stay on and produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be babaoo ba amɛnɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ trukaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do groundnut plants push yellow stems back down into the soil after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ tsiɔ amɛshishifãi ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut flowers bloom above ground, but once pollinated, the plant forms sharp stems called 'pegs' that push down into the earth so the actual groundnuts can grow safely underground away from sun and pests.
ga: Peanut fɔfɔii fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ abɔi pollination Tso lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ ni tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni anɔkwa ŋmeii anyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe, ni hulu la kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ akashɛ amɛhe.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make energy that gets sent down underground to build large tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward the sun and prevents ground diseases from spoiling the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni ekɛfee hewalɛ ni akɛmajeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛfee bulbs agboi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la mli ni ehaaa helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ afite.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites hiding under the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early keeps the leaves flat so the plant can grow well.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy windstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that struggle to support the heavy weight of a full cluster of plantains when strong winds blow. Supporting the main stalk with a strong wooden Y-stick prop keeps the plant standing upright until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni tamɔ Y fiɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow from the tip down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the leaf tips usually means your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure will help the plant recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that spread a virus to the plant. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or appropriate sprays prevents the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛ neem fɔ loo spray ni sa tsu nii lɛ ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves and caterpillar droppings in the funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ larva mli ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ nɔ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. The caterpillars hide inside the central leaves of the maize plant to feed, and spraying early in the morning or late evening with approved treatments protects your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji fall armyworm tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye nii. Ni kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why is it important to let cut seed yams dry in the shade before I plant them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni aha ŋmeii ni afo lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Drying cut seed yams in the shade allows the cut area to form a hard protective scab, which prevents rot-causing bacteria and fungi in the soil from destroying the seed before it sprouts.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potatoes ni afo lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaha hei ni afo lɛ lɛ afee ŋmeii ni wa. Enɛ haaa muawai kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ sũ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ akafite dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when the heat and dry winds start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside your cocoa provides living umbrellas that protect the young cocoa plants from heat and drying winds.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ odu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ o-cocoa lɛ masɛi lɛ, ebaaha o-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, which results in weak, thin plants that produce very small yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli, ni no haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crops with dry grass or maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he sũ? Akɛ jwɛi loo ŋmãa tsei ŋmɔɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry crop material, called mulching, keeps the ground cool, traps moisture so you water less often, and stops weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Eŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo ni otsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and stunt their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni ehaa amɛdalɛ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow very fast and steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your crops. Removing weeds within the first few weeks after planting allows your crops to grow quickly and stay healthy.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu nii yɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa onibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava is typically ready to harvest 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and the ground around the base of the plant begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishi bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the soil becomes too dry or when the temperature becomes extremely high. Keeping the soil evenly moist and planting at the right time helps the flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: When the bottom leaves of maize turn yellow in a V-shape pattern, the plant is hungry for nitrogen. Maize moves the remaining nitrogen in its body to the top leaves to keep growing, showing that your soil needs nitrogen fertilizer or compost.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, no lɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Abɛi tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni eshwɛ yɛ egbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ eda. Etsɔɔ kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very bushy with tall leafy stems but yield very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ waa ni eyɛ baai kakadaji shi ewoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen compared to potassium. Nitrogen makes the plant spend all its energy growing big leaves above ground instead of feeding and swelling the roots underneath.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛto potassium he. Nitrogen haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e yeɔ ní nɛ e haa nɛ sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ sisi ɔ puɛɔ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy seasons when moisture stays on the pods. Clearing weeds and pruning shade trees lets sunlight and air dry out the pods so the fungus cannot grow.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni nu shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ. Tsei ni ajieɔ jwɛi kɛ amɛhe ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi. Fungus nyɛŋ adara.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl upward into tight cups and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, mites, or whiteflies feeding on leaf sap, or by a virus carried by those insects. Controlling these tiny pests early prevents the leaves from twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, mites, loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ lɛ bibii ni yeɔ kooloi bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cowpea plants getting covered in a fine white dust?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sũ yɛŋ kpakpa ehà mi-cowpea tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This white dust is a fungal infection called powdery mildew, which thrives during periods of warm, humid days and cooler nights. It blocks sunlight from reaching the leaf, reducing your cowpea yield.
ga: Nɛkɛ sũ yɛŋ nɛɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. ni shwereɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli, ni gbɛkɛ mli lɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni etsĩɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsina ŋmãa ni anáa lɛ ba shi.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow around the edges and split open easily in the wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ ni amɛkuɔ oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ tswa amɛ lɛ?

english: Outer yellowing in plantains often points to a lack of potassium in the soil or an attack by Panama disease (a soil fungal wilt) that blocks the plant from drawing up food and water from its roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ plantains mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ potassium faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo Panama hela lɛ shishijee. (shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmei) ni tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkajie niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants look like they were chewed into ragged holes overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni atsɔ amɛ awo bu mli nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: This is the signature work of Fall Armyworms. The caterpillars hide inside the center funnel (whorl) of the corn plant during the hot day and crawl out at night to eat the soft young leaves.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworms nitsumɔ krɛdɛɛ ko. Kplukai lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmãa (ring) lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni efoɔ kɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ koni eyaye baai bibii lɛ.

english: Why do my green cowpea pods have tiny holes bored into them with small caterpillars inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-green cowpea pods lɛ yɛ bu bibii ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: These holes are made by the Maruca pod borer caterpillar. The adult moth lays eggs on the cowpea flowers, and as soon as the young caterpillars hatch, they bore directly into the developing pods to feed on the seeds.
ga: Maruca nubu lɛ mli ŋshɔŋlooi lɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ buji nɛɛ. Moth ni eda lɛ woɔ ewui yɛ tsina fɔfɔi anɔ. Ni kɛji ŋmeii lɛ fɔ pɛ kɛkɛ Amɛfoɔ ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛye dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes suddenly from very dry to very wet. Extreme heat stresses the plant so much that it rejects the flowers to save water.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛyaa nɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ waa aahu akɛ amɛkpooɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu nu he.

english: Why do my yam vines start turning brown and dying off early before harvest time arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Premature dying of yam vines is often caused by Yam Anthracnose disease, a fungal infection favored by heavy rain, which causes dark spots that join together until the leaf and stem dry out completely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni ji anthracnose lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii tsei ni gboiɔ oya lɛ baa. ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛbaa Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ feɔ ekome kɛyashiɔ be mli ni baai kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kwraa.

english: How can I protect my vegetable leaves from insects using simple local plants like scent leaf?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-vegetable baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe kɛtsɔ maŋ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ onion baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Scent leaves contain strong natural oils that smell bitter and repellent to bugs. When you crush scent leaves, soak them in water, and spray the liquid on your vegetables, the scent drives insects away without damaging your crops or costing money.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli fɔ ko ni mli wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni shwieɔ kooloi bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni ŋɔɔ lɛ amli. Beni okɛ baai ni shãa lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ Okɛwo nu mli ni okɛ nu lɛ afɔ o-vegetables lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akabote ohe ni efiteee onibii loo efiteee shika.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves and stay strong. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients out of the soil or leaves the roots flooded.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo ekɛ nu ewo shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop during the afternoon heat even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense sun, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it up from the ground. They wilt temporarily to protect themselves from drying out, but usually recover in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaagbo yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehaa ehe jɔɔ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why are my cassava roots small and thin even though the leaves on top look healthy and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: If the soil is packed too hard or has too much nitrogen, the plant puts all its strength into growing tall leaves above ground instead of pushing big tubers into the earth. Loose, well-drained soil encourages the plant to expand its roots.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ nitrogen babaoo Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ moŋ fe ni eeetsi bulb agbo lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by sudden hot dry weather, lack of water, or poor pollination. If the air is too hot, the pollen fails, and the plant drops the flower to conserve its energy for survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa, nu ni bɛ, loo fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ Pollen lɛ baafee nɔ ni bɛ sɛɛnamɔ. Ni tsei shiɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha wala.

english: Why do my tiny vegetable seedlings collapse and rot at the stem right after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai bibii ni aduɔ lɛ Mine lɛ gbee shi ni egboɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: This is caused by excess moisture around young roots, which creates a fungus that rots delicate seedling stems at soil level. Keeping the nursery beds moist but not soaked helps young stems stay upright and strong.
ga: Fɔ̃ ni fa fe nine ni bɔleɔ shishifãi bibii lɛ ahe lɛ kɛ enɛ baa, ni haa ŋmei ko ni haa dumɔwu lɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ahã gbekɛbii akwɛmɔ saatso lɛ mli edɔ shi jeee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei bibii lɛ teɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Can soaking herbs in water and spraying it on my crops make them strong enough to resist diseases?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ nu mli ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baaha amɛhe awa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo helai?

english: Yes, water prepared with aromatic leaves like scent leaf or neem contains natural compounds that coat the plant's surface. This protective layer acts like a shield, making it harder for fungal spots and bacteria to take root.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni akɛ baai ni ŋɔɔ tamɔ baai ni ŋɔɔ loo neem saa lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa tso lɛ hiɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɛkɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he nɛɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ gãimlibi. Enɛ haa ewaa waa akɛ fungal kɛ bacteria spots lɛ baawo shishifãi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and dry up when I clear all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijie tsei kakadaji fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that cannot handle full, direct sunlight. They need shade from taller plants like plantains or temporary shade trees to keep them cool and moist while their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo tsei krokomɛi ni haa hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ adɛŋ. Koni tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds seem to grow much faster than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni midu jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants built to survive under tough conditions with very little nourishment. Their roots grow faster and spread wider, allowing them to steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer before your planted crops can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni ama koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai ni niyenii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Amɛshishifãi lɛ dara oya ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã babaoo. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do my garden eggs split open on the plant right before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ fãa yɛ tsei anɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Fruit splitting happens when a dry spell is followed by sudden heavy rain or overwatering. The fruit absorbs water too quickly, causing the inside to swell faster than the skin can stretch, which cracks the outer layer open.
ga: Yibii amli gbalamɔ baa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa loo nu babaoo nyiɛ hulutsoo be sɛɛ. Yibii shwieɔ nu oya tsɔ. Enɛ haa emli lɛ fũuɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ fãa.

english: Young cocoa trees have sensitive leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. Shade trees protect them from harsh heat and help soil hold moisture until the cocoa plants grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is lacking nitrogen, an essential plant food. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to feed the new leaves at the top, showing that the soil needs fertilizer or manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt during the hot afternoon heat even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense heat, tomato plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the soil. The plant temporarily wilts to protect itself from drying out, and it usually recovers as the temperature cools in the evening.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive water. When stressed, the plant sacrifices its flowers to save energy and protect its own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu babaoo hao amɛ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei kɛ fɔfɔi shaa afɔle koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala he.

english: Why does my yam crop need a long wooden stick to climb on to give me big tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ? Kwɔ ni oyahe yitso agbo lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: Yam vines need to reach high sunlight to make food for the plant. Staking holds the leaves up off the ground, allowing the plant to catch maximum light and store that extra energy underground as large, healthy yams.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Staking haa baai lɛ holeɔ amɛhe nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ naa la babaoo ni ekɛ hewalɛ kroko toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can a dry stick cut from a cassava plant grow into a whole new crop with roots?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei ni egbi ni afolɔ lɛ adara ni etsɔ tsei heei ni shishifãi yɔɔ mli?

english: Cassava stems contain growth nodes packed with stored food. When cut and buried in moist soil, these nodes wake up, sending roots down into the earth to find water and shoots up toward the sun to grow leaves.
ga: Cassava tso lɛ yɛ shweremɔ hei ni niyenii ni ato eyi mli obɔ. Kɛji akɛ afo ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ Nodes nɛɛ baate shi. Kɛtsɔ shishifãi ni amɛtsuɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛyatao nu lɛ nɔ. ni efoɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he koni ekɛ baai akwɛ̃.

english: Why does a plantain stem die after producing just one bunch of plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ gboiɔ beni amɛwo ŋmei kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A single plantain stem is designed to fruit only once in its lifetime. After the main stem produces its bunch and dies, it naturally feeds the young suckers growing around its base so they can grow into the next crop.
ga: Afee plantain kome koni ewo yibii shikome pɛ yɛ eshihilɛ mli. Beni tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ kwɛ̃ ni egbo sɛɛ lɛ Ebaaha tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ niyenii. natural base Bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant groundnuts or beans in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ miŋa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil, feeding neighboring heavy-feeding plants like maize.
