ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛtsɔ tsei ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow thin and produce smaller fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mitso titri lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni ewo yibii bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with crops for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Because weeds grow aggressively, they steal food away from your crops, leaving the crops weak and undernourished.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli yɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ hewɔ No hewɔ lɛ amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli.

english: The first rain can deceive seeds into sprouting, but if a dry spell follows before the main rains settle in, the topsoil will dry out quickly and kill the delicate young roots.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ baanyɛ alaka dumɔwui ni amɛkwɛ̃. Shi kɛji hɔmɔ ba nyiɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ nɛ lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni efiteɔ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants suffer from excessive heat and direct sunlight. Without shade crops like plantains or shade trees, sunlight scorches their tender leaves and dries out the moisture in the soil, causing leaves to turn brown and dry up.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ tsɔɔ asarasu ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: What causes small holes in my maize leaves and tiny caterpillars hiding inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli Ekɛ ehe ewo baa lɛ mli?

english: This is usually caused by Fall Armyworms, a destructive pest that eats maize leaves and damages the growing tips. Early detection and spraying with recommended insecticides or neem extract early in the morning or evening can save your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ ona tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu lɛ mra ni okɛshwie nɔ Leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: Why do white powdery flies swarm around my cassava leaves and make them twist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powda ŋmeii yɛŋ miiho mi-cassava baai lɛ ahe ni amɛmiiha amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: These are whiteflies, tiny insects that suck sap from cassava leaves and transmit viruses like Cassava Mosaic Disease. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties is the best long-term way to keep your plants healthy.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii yɛŋ. Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ ŋmei baa mli nu lɛ ni amɛkɛ helai tamɔ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ haa mɔ. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn pale yellow even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ waa moŋ?

english: Yellowing leaves often indicate a lack of essential nutrients in the soil, particularly nitrogen, or poorly drained soil that chokes root growth. Adding well-rotted manure or balanced fertilizer helps restore the soil's nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ. titri lɛ nitrogen loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Will putting extra fertilizer on my crops make them grow twice as fast?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fata miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ, ebaaha amɛkwɛ̃ oya fe tsutsu lɛ shii enyɔ?

english: No, applying too much fertilizer can burn plant roots, damage the soil, and cause plants to grow lots of leaves without producing good yield. Following the recommended dose ensures plants get just what they need without harm.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ baa babaoo ni ewooo yibii kpakpai. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛhaa lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko baaa enɔ.

english: How do I know the best time to plant my maize when the rain starts unexpectedly early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa beni nugbɔ jeɔ shishi mra ni mikpaaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the rains become steady for at least two consecutive heavy rainfalls to ensure the soil holds enough moisture, or choose quick-maturing seed varieties if the planting season is shortened.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi kɛ hoo lɛ, nugbɔ nɛɔ shii enyɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa. Aloo halamɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra kɛji akɛ be ni akɛkwɛɔ lɛ lɛ efo mli kuku.

english: Is it bad if I keep planting maize on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Ani ejaaa kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi?

english: Yes, planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop pests to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and stops pests.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yaa hiɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akpa.

english: Why are my tomato fruits turning black and rotting from the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite kɛmiijɛ shishi dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This condition is called Blossom End Rot, caused by a lack of calcium or irregular watering while the fruit is forming. Keeping soil moisture consistent and adding agricultural lime or wood ash to the soil prevents it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ Blossom End Rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni faaa loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ lime loo tso ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by small pests like thrips or mites sucking the sap, or by a virus carried by insects. Removing infected plants early and managing insects with proper spraying prevents it from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Kɛ́ ojie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ akwɛ kooloi lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do small insects bore holes into my harvested dried corn while stored in sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwieɔ bu yɛ ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikpaa lɛ mli beni mikɛtoɔ kotokui amli lɛ?

english: These insects are grain weevils, which multiply when corn is stored before it is completely dry or in unsealed bags. Thoroughly drying corn to low moisture levels and storing it in airtight Hermetic bags prevents weevils from damaging the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji ŋmãa ŋmeii. Enɛ mli lɛɛɔ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ to dani egbi kwraa loo akɛwo kotoku ko ni akɛwo mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi tsu nii ni akɛgbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmãa lɛ naa koni ekafite ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many flowers, but only a few of them turn into actual cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers must be fertilized through pollination to grow into pods. Because cocoa flowers are shaped in a complex way, only tiny insects like midges can transfer pollen from flower to flower; without them, unpollinated flowers simply drop off.
ga: Esa akɛ atsɔ pollination nɔ awo cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ejaakɛ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ su ko ni mli wa. Kplukai bibii, tamɔ midges pɛ baanyɛ ajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko mli. Kɛ amɛbɛ Fɔfɔi ni bɛ pollination lɛ baagbee shi.

english: What is cocoa pollination, and how does it help my farm yield more cocoa?
ga: Mɛni ji kookoo mli ŋmɔtɔ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔ lɛ ni ewo kookoo babaoo?

english: Pollination is the process where tiny midges carry pollen from one cocoa flower to another. This fertilizes the blossom, triggering it to swell into a tiny pod (cherelle) rather than falling off the tree, directly increasing your total yield.
ga: Pollination ji gbɛ ni aŋkroaŋkroi bibii tsɔɔ nɔ amɛwoɔ pollen kɛjɛɔ kookoo fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ agbɔ. Wo lɛ hewalɛ ni egbɛ eshwa ni etsɔ ŋmeii bibii (cherelles) moŋ fe ni eeejɛ tso lɛ nɔ egbee shi. Enɛ haa onitsumɔ lɛ fɛɛ yaa hiɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do tiny insects on my farm actually help my cocoa flowers grow into pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Tiny biting midges live in damp leaf litter and crawl inside cocoa blossoms to feed. As they move around, pollen sticks to their bodies and gets carried to other flowers, which turns those flowers into healthy growing pods.
ga: ŋmeii bibii Hiɔ shi yɛ baai ni mli efɔ mli. ni amɛkpãa amɛhe amɛwoɔ kookoo fɔfɔi amli koni amɛye niyenii Beni amɛyaa kɛbaa lɛ Pollen lɛ kpɛtɛɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ he ni akɛyaa fɔfɔi krokomɛi anɔ. ni haa nakai fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni daa waa

english: Why did I harvest fewer cocoa pods this year compared to what I harvested last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpa kookoo ŋmeii fioo pɛ afi nɛɛ kɛ akɛto nɔ ni mikpa nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Seasonal changes in rainfall, humidity, and temperature affect how many pollinating insects are active, which directly changes how many flowers successfully turn into pods from one year to the next.
ga: Be mli tsakemɔi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ, latsaa, kɛ dɔlɛ mli saa pollinator ayibɔ he. Enɛ tsakeɔ fɔfɔi ni tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii daa afi lɛ ayibɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do some of my tiny young cocoa pods turn black and dry up before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi dani eda lɛ?

english: This often happens due to poor pollination or Cherelle wilt, where the tree naturally drops young pods it cannot support due to lack of water, nutrients, or proper fertilization during flowering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ pollination ni ehiii loo Cherelle wilt hewɔ, ni no haa tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aye abua lɛ yɛ nu, niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii amli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do cocoa trees planted in full sunlight sometimes produce fewer pods than trees under shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, kookoo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo fe tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight dries out cocoa flowers quickly and destroys the moist environment that pollinating midges need to survive, leading to lower pollination rates and fewer pods.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ gĩɔ oya ni efiteɔ shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa ni ŋmeii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ ahi shi lɛ. Enɛ haa pollination lɛ baa shi ni pods lɛ hu baa shi.

english: When is the main season for cocoa flowers to start pollinating in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be titri ni kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: Cocoa flowering and pollination mostly happen at the start of the rainy seasons—around April to May for the main crop and September to October for the minor crop—when high moisture helps pollinating insects thrive.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii kɛ pollination babaoo baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. Aaafee April kɛyashi May kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii titrii. kɛ September kɛyashi October kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo yeɔ ebuaa pollinators lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ.

english: Is it possible for me to hand-pollinate my cocoa flowers myself to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mafee kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ koni maná yibii babaoo?

english: Yes, hand pollination involves using small tools or your hands to manually transfer pollen from one flower to another, which can significantly boost pod production beyond what natural insects achieve.
ga: Hɛɛ, nɔ ni fata nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ he ji ni okɛ dɛŋdade bibioo ko loo oniji atsu nii ni okɛ onine ashɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha podfeemɔ aya hiɛ waa. Kɛfata nɔ ni adebɔɔ mli kooloi baanyɛ afee lɛ he lɛ

english: What can I keep on my farm soil to protect the insects that pollinate my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ makɛto sũ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli koni mikɛbu kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Leaving decaying plantain trunks, cocoa husks, and damp leaf litter on the ground provides a moist breeding ground for midges, while avoiding heavy chemical sprays during flowering keeps them alive.
ga: Plantain tsei ni egboi, kookoo tsɔji, kɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ ajiemɔ. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli yɛ be mli ni etsiɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ tsofai ni tsii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he Yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: How many months does it take for a cocoa flower to grow into a fully mature pod after it gets pollinated?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eye emuu yɛ be mli ni ajie ŋmeii lɛ awo mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Once a flower is successfully pollinated, it takes about five to six months for the small cherelle to develop into a fully grown, ripe pod ready for harvesting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ye omanye yɛ pollination mli lɛ Eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 5-6 dani cherry fɔfɔi bibii lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni asaa he kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do some of my pawpaw trees produce flowers but never grow any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mipapaya tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi shi ewooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Pawpaw trees have sexes; male trees only produce pollen and no fruit, while female trees need that pollen to produce fruit. Keeping roughly one male tree for every five to ten female trees nearby ensures all your female trees get pollinated and bear fruit.
ga: Pawpaw tsei kɛ amɛhe feɔ yakayaka nii. Tsei ni ji hii lɛ woɔ pollen pɛ ni amɛwooo yibii. Yɛ be mli ni tsei yei ahe hiaa nakai pollen lɛ koni amɛwo yibii lɛ. Tsei yei akwɛmɔ ji aaafee 1 kɛha tsei yei 5-10 fɛɛ ni yɔɔ akutso lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tso fɛɛ tso ni ji yoo lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my cocoa saplings wither and die when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a living umbrella that gives young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs until its roots fully establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ masɛi lɛ adumɔ Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni haa kookoo bibioo lɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from having more plants?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani kɛ́ midu babaoo lɛ, ebaawooo babaoo?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight each other for sun, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of getting many heavy cobs, crowded maize plants grow thin and weak, producing tiny ears or no grain at all.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmãa ni tsii babaoo baa lɛ, ŋmãa ni afee lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa toi bibii loo dumɔwui bɛ kwraa.

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, that natural fertilizer remains in the ground to feed and strengthen your next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji okpa amɛ Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha o-abele tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii ni ewo lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants turning yellow and curling up into tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies sucking the plant sap and spreading viruses. Controlling these pests early keeps the plant healthy enough to photosynthesize and form peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ tso mli nu kɛ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ fotosintɛsis feɔ chili ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without setting any fruit during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air put immense stress on tomato plants. The plant sheds its flowers to conserve water and survive, rather than risking energy on growing fruit it cannot support without sufficient water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ kɛ haomɔ babaoo baa tomato tsei anɔ. Tsei ni shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛha wala aya nɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ohewalɛ awo oshara mli ni ooodu aduawai ni tso lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ nɔ kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ.

english: How can I stop free-roaming cattle from destroying my cassava plot during the dry season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ akpa tsinabii ni nyiɛɔ amɛhe lɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmɔji yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Planting living fences of dense, non-edible shrubs or building sturdy hedges around your farm boundary creates a physical barrier that prevents wandering livestock from entering and grazing on your crops.
ga: Hedɔɔ ni hiɛ ka ni aduɔ lɛ ji jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ yeli. aloo gbogbo ni mli wa ni oootswa yɛ Oŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ ahe Ehaa gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ko ni tsiɔ kooloi ni nyiɛɔ kɛyaa kɛbaa lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote oŋmɔshi nibii amli ni amɛye niyenii.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly after I clear my farm, and how can I suppress them naturally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi enaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Weed seeds lie buried in the soil and sprout as soon as sunlight hits the open ground. Planting fast-growing cover crops covers the exposed soil, blocking light and choking out weeds before they can establish.
ga: Afuɔ jwɛi dumɔwui awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji hulu la shɛ he ni agbele lɛ pɛ. Nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni shwereɔ oya lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha jwɛi lɛ afee shade ni ojie amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Multiple shoots coming from the same root compete for the mother plant's energy and nutrients. Pruning extra suckers leaves only one strong follower stem, allowing the main tree to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo ni jɛɔ shishifã kome mli lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ ahe ekoŋŋ lɛ, eshiɔ tso kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso titri lɛ baanyɛ afee kui wuji ni tsii.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are fully mature and ready to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is mature when its lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving sparse foliage at the top. Harvesting too early results in watery roots with little starch, while waiting too long turns the tubers woody.
ga: Yucca lɛ eda kwraa kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ashiɔ baai ni egbɛ eshwã ŋwɛigbɛ. Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi ni nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ omɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha yitso lɛ atsɔ tso.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. They require shade crops like plantain or temporary shade trees during their first two to three years to protect their leaf tissues from burning and to keep the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my growing maize plants turning yellow at the tips instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛyitseiaŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves at the base of maize plants usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main nutrient crops use to make green leaves, so when it runs out, the plant starves itself from the bottom leaves up to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ kɛ́ etee Tso lɛ hɔmɔ baaye lɛ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my land produce smaller maize harvests every year if I keep planting maize in the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ kpaaa ŋmãa fioo daa afi lɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be hu?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of the specific nutrients that crop loves most and allows soil-borne pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil nitrogen naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei lɛ sumɔɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the soil when heavy rains flood my farm for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits around the roots for too long, it suffocates them and causes fungal rot, which is why planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges is essential in wet areas.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, amɛmuɔ ni amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ he hiaa yɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread dry fertilizer around my crops when the ground is hot and completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi shwieɔ ehe lɛ? Dumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ ni egbi kwraa lɛ.

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve so the crop's roots can drink them in. When applied to dry soil under scorching sun, the concentrated chemical salts stay on top and burn the plant's roots instead of feeding them.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ nɔ ni amɛshãa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaaha amɛ niyenii.

english: Why do I need to cut long wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei kakadaji lɛ? Koni eha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yam vines produce tubers through their leaves catching sunlight. Lifting the leaves off the ground with stakes gives them full sunlight exposure, improves air circulation to prevent leaf diseases, and significantly enlarges the root tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛtsɔɔ baai ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ koni akafoli helai aba. ni egbɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli babaoo

english: Why do my bearing plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy rainstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that stay near the top layer of soil. When the heavy bunches get wet and heavy, the top weight easily pulls the shallow roots out of wet, soft soil, so farmers must prop the trunks with sturdy bamboo or wooden poles.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsii, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ tsii lɛ Tsii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baagbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ. Eshiɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ kɛ bɔdɔɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okwaafoi lɛ kɛ ŋmeii loo tsei ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off without turning into any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of insect pollinators. Keeping the soil consistently moist and cool helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ jieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ falɛ faaa lɛ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi shi pɛpɛɛpɛ ni eyɛ fɛ̃i lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I pinch off some of the healthy extra branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing side shoots (suckers) forces the tomato plant to send its energy and food toward growing bigger, healthier tomatoes instead of wasting nutrients on extra stems and leaves that don't produce good fruit.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tomato tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii awo tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni daraa lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ tsei kɛ baai ni fa fe nine ni wooo yibii lɛ anɔ lɛ,

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and take over my field when I leave wide gaps between my crop rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛyeɔ mihegbɛ lɛ nɔ beni mishiɔ gbɛjegbɛi wuji yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Bare, unshaded soil gives weed seeds all the sunlight and warmth they need to sprout quickly. Spacing crops correctly creates a full leaf cover (canopy) that blocks sunlight from reaching the ground, naturally suppressing weed growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni shade bɛ nɔ lɛ haa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Tsei ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta (ŋta) ni eyi obɔ ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide essential shade and retain soil moisture, protecting the young cocoa during its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli

english: How do I know which part of a cassava stem I should cut and plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male mi-cassava tso lɛ fã ni esa akɛ mafo ni madu?

english: The best part to plant is the hard, mature middle section of a healthy stem. Avoid the soft, watery top parts and the woody base, and always ensure the leaf buds are pointing upwards toward the sky when you plant them.
ga: Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ dumɔ mli ji tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ ni wa, ni eda. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu yɔɔ mli kɛ tsei ni akɛfee shishitoo lɛ ahe. Ni kwɛmɔ be fɛɛ be akɛ baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ miitsɔɔ ŋwɛi beni oduɔ nii lɛ.

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs to spread its leaves to catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, improves airflow, and allows the plant to produce larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa tsei feɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves from the tip inward usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to grow healthy green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele babaoo he miihia koni ekwɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant groundnuts or beans before planting corn on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii dani adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the season ends, these plants leave natural food in the soil, which helps the next corn crop grow much better without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ be lɛ ba naagbee Tsei nɛɛ shiɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kwraa ni akɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on the leaves and spreading a virus. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or recommended sprays helps keep the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the center of my corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets the growing center of corn plants. Inspecting fields early and applying local treatments like neem extract or recommended insecticides into the central leaf funnel can stop them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa tsei ni daraa lɛ ateŋ. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ maŋ lɛ mli tsofai tamɔ neem mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ ateŋ ŋshɔi lɛ amli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ akpa enɛɛmɛi dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot, when the plant lacks sufficient water, or when there are no bees or wind to pollinate them. Consistent watering and light mulching help keep the soil cool and reduce flower drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni tsei bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ni baaha amɛwo ŋmeii. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa shi.

english: Allowing too many shoots to grow around one plantain stem creates competition for food and water. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong suckers, ensuring the main stem gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajieɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni fa lɛ ashwieɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni he wa, ni ehaa ŋmeii titri lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaa plantains akuu agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Why does paddy rice grow better when there is standing water on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ be mli ni nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Standing water controls unwanted weeds that compete with rice for light and food, while keeping the root environment moist and temperature-stable for healthy growth.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ kudɔɔ jwɛi ni ataooo ni kɛ ŋmãa yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la kɛ niyenii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or planting beans in the soil before maize helps bring back the healthy green color and improves yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo adu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani adu ŋmei lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller every year if I keep planting the same crop on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibioo daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season. Rotating different crops on the land gives the soil time to rebuild nutrients and reduces pest buildup.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ atsakemɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛsaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree during rainy weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus spread by wet conditions and high humidity. Pruning overgrown cocoa branches lets sunlight in and helps airflow keep the pods dry, reducing rot.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ. Kookoo tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha hulu la abote mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu atsɔ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi. Ha fitemɔ aba shi

english: Leaf curling in peppers is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites that spread viruses. Controlling these insects early protects your plants from stunted growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaabu otsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ he.

english: Why are tiny worms chewing holes right inside the center of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii Aaaye bu ko yɛ mibi lɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which attack the tender central leaves of maize. Catching them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts protects the growing point of the plant.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ he.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks for my yams to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni sweet potato akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to make food that grows big tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground, exposing leaves to sun while protecting them from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo yɛ hulu la mli yɛ be mli ni atsĩɔ helai hu anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal food and water from the main mother plantain stem. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce big bunches.
ga: Tsofai krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ ashishifã titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii titri lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii agbo.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high or when plants do not get consistent water. Keeping the soil evenly moist prevents stress so flowers can form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ nu daa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafee haomɔ koni fɔfɔii lɛ atsɔ tomatoi.

english: How does my cassava crop manage to stay alive during the dry season without rain?
ga: Te mi-cassava tsei lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during prolonged dry spells to conserve water, while storing nutrients inside its thick underground roots until rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: If I plant beans in the same farm as my maize, will it help or hurt my maize?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ Ani ebaaye ebua loo ebaaye mi-ŋmãa lɛ awui?

english: Planting beans with maize helps your crop. Beans trap nitrogen gas from the air and release it into the soil, acting as a natural food source for the maize.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa onibii. Beans mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha ŋmãa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food for green leaves. It can also happen when the soil is too wet and waterlogged, preventing the roots from breathing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. ni ji baai eŋɔli niyenii titri Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the juices from underneath the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: My cassava plants are growing very tall with lots of green leaves, so why are the tubers under the ground still so small?
ga: Mi yucca tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ waa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or excessive water early on, it spends all its energy building leaves up top instead of storing starch and food in the roots underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmei loo nu babaoo nɔ mra lɛ, Ekɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ebɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii ni eshiɔ lɛ yɛ ŋwɛi. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ ngmɔ kɛ níhi nɛ haa nɔ he wami ɔ toɔ a sisi nɛ ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ mi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high, when the soil dries out suddenly, or when the plant lacks important nutrients like phosphorus during its flowering stage.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ trukaa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: Why do groundnut plants need soft, loose soil around them when they start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ he hiaa ŋmei tsei lɛ? Be ni esa akɛ aje fɔfɔii afeemɔ shishi

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, they grow long stems called pegs that must push down into the soil to form the actual nuts. If the soil is hard and packed tight, the pegs cannot sink into the ground.
ga: Beni afee ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ pollen sɛɛ lɛ, tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ pin lɛ baafee. ni esa akɛ ashɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni akɛfee ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Pin lɛ nyɛŋ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How long does it take after I plant my seed yam for the green vines to start coming out of the ground?
ga: Be enyiɛ mikɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ du lɛ sɛɛ dani wain tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baaje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam seeds typically take between three to six weeks to wake up and sprout above the soil, depending on how warm and moist the ground is.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ heɔ aaafee otsii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ dani amɛteɔ shi ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Edamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die when I clear all the big trees away from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi ni migboi beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect them from strong direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains nearby, the intense heat dries out the young leaves and scorches the stems.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii biɔ hulutsoo be koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baaha baai bibii lɛ agbi ni ebaashã tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that struggle to support a heavy bunch of fruit when the soil becomes soft and soaked with rain. Planting them deeper and supporting heavy stalks with bamboo poles keeps them upright.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni nugbɔ enɛ. Tsei ni tsii ni aduɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni akɛ ŋmei tsei fiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Black pod is caused by a tiny fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, cool weather. Rain splashes the fungus from the soil onto the pods, especially if the farm is overgrown and air cannot circulate.
ga: Fungi bibii kɛ pods diji baa. No gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ fɛ̃i be mli. Nugbɔ haa ŋmeii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei babaoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli.

english: If I plant beans together with my maize in the same field, will the beans steal food from the maize?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa fata ŋmãa he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Ani ŋmeii lɛ baaju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: No, beans and cowpeas actually help maize. They absorb nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which enriches the soil and acts as a natural food source for your maize.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ yɛ ŋmãa he. Amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ, ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛhaa o-ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe nɔ. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines grow plenty of green leaves but give me small yams when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ehaa mi sweet potato bibii kɛji mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer makes yam plants spend all their energy growing thick leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below ground.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa sweet potato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ɔ tsei ni etse amɛhe banee yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: If I apply my fertilizer right when heavy rain is falling, will it help my crops grow faster?
ga: Kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ani ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara oya?

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer away from your farm into streams before crop roots can absorb it, wasting your money and starving the crops.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa faai amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Eheɔ bo shika ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide shade and moisture, protecting young cocoa trees until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off without producing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛwooo tomato lɛ?

english: Extremely hot weather or irregular watering stresses tomato plants, forcing them to shed their flowers to conserve moisture instead of making fruit.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Excess rain fills all the small air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots and allowing fungal rot to spread quickly through the wet tubers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ŋmeii gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids that attack young leaves and spread plant viruses that distort growth.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni tutuaa baai bibii ni egbɛɔ tsei ahe helai ni fiteɔ amɛdalɛ lɛ eshwaa

english: Why do weeds make my crops look thin and weak even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔi lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients faster than your crops can take them up.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni boteɔ mli ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe bɔ ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same land every year reduce my harvest each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ haa miŋmãa lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Maize continuously pulls the same nutrients out of the soil every season; rotating with cowpea or groundnuts puts natural nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ akɛ cowpeas loo peanuts tsake lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during strong winds even when they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top, making them easy for strong winds to push over if root pests have weakened their grip.
ga: Plantain lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni aduawai akui ni tsii yɔɔ nɔ, ni no haa ewaaa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatsɔ amɛhe kɛji shishifãi lɛ amli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ha amɛmɔmɔ lɛ gbɔjɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots. Direct, harsh sunlight causes them to lose water faster than their roots can absorb it, which scorches the leaves. Planting shade crops like plantains protects them while they establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha nu lɛ afite oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ ashã. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he be mli ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: How many years will it take for my cocoa farm to start bearing pods after planting?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ebɔi pods feemɔ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Traditional cocoa varieties usually take 3 to 5 years to bear pods, while improved hybrid varieties can start producing in about 2 to 3 years if given proper water, shade, and nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema kookoo henɔi lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baabɔi yibiiwoo yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji amɛná nu, hulutsoo kɛ niyenii ni sa.

english: Why do many of the tiny flowers on my cocoa trunk drop off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii No hewɔ lɛ, kookoo babaoo ni yɔɔ mi kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only a small percentage get pollinated by tiny insects called midges. Flowers that are not pollinated naturally fall off so the tree can save its energy for developing healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Shi oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ ji nɔ ni kooloi bibii shwieɔ amɛmli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ato hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni ekɛfee fɔfɔi ni mli wa.

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during rainy and high-humidity conditions. Removing infected pods regularly and pruning branches to improve airflow helps prevent it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ daa ni afoɔ tsei aniji koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enaa.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my land is good enough to grow healthy cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Good cocoa soil is deep, dark, and well-draining with plenty of decayed plant matter. If rainwater sits on top of the soil for days without sinking in, the land may be too clay-heavy, which can rot cocoa roots.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli kwɔ, eyɛ ediŋŋ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Tsei ni miigboi babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo ni eboteee mli lɛ, Ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ babaoo yɛ mli. Enɛ baaha kookoo shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Why is it necessary to cut off extra branches from my growing cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ kookoo tso ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or excess branches so sunlight and air can pass through the tree. This reduces dampness that promotes fungal diseases and helps the tree direct more energy into growing larger, healthier pods.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni egboi loo ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Plantains are great because they provide essential shade for young cocoa. However, cassava should be planted far from young cocoa trees because it competes heavily for soil nutrients and water.
ga: Plantains he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa ejaakɛ ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ waa. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ adu plantains yɛ he ko ni kɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, esa akɛ amɛye akaŋ babaoo koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ.

english: What are the small insects damaging my cocoa leaves and young shoots, and how do they affect my harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ kooloi bibii miifite mi-kookoo baai kɛ mi-kookoo bibii lɛ? Ni te amɛnáa mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: These are likely capsids (mirids), which suck sap from shoots and pods. Their feeding creates wounds that dry out branches, lower pod production, and can eventually kill whole cocoa trees if left untreated.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji capsids (mirids), ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei akui kɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ. Amɛ niyenii lɛ haa pilamɔi ni haa tsei lɛ aniji lɛ gbiɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni baa lɛ baa shi, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbe cacao tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ.

english: Dropping leaves is a natural survival mechanism. By shedding older leaves during dry spells, the cocoa tree reduces water loss through evaporation and conserves moisture inside its trunk until rain returns.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ. Kɛtsɔ baai momoi ni amɛshwieɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ haa nu ni jɛɔ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ mli baa lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ tso lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Fermentation stops the bean from germinating, destroys bitter compounds, and creates the rich chocolate flavor and brown color buyers look for. Drying unfermented beans leaves them purple and bitter.
ga: Fɛ̃i haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ. Ekpãtãa nibii ni mli edɔ lɛ ahiɛ ni ehaa tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ kɛ su ni ji ŋmɔtɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmei ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ, ehaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and sensitive roots that dry out quickly in harsh sunlight. They require temporary shade crops, such as plantains or cassava, to protect them and retain soil moisture while their root systems mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo yucca. Koni abu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he ni ekwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: How does COCOBOD monitor my farm, and what do their field officers check for?
ga: Te COCOBOD feɔ tɛŋŋ ekwɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ? Ni mɛni ji nɔ ni ŋmɔ mli onukpai lɛ kwɛɔ mli?

english: COCOBOD officers inspect farms to check tree health, identify diseases like Swollen Shoot Virus early, assess soil conditions, and ensure proper farming practices so you get higher pod yields.
ga: COCOBOD nitsulɔi lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmɔji amli koni amɛkwɛ bɔ ni tsei lɛ yɔɔ ha, ni amɛyɔseɔ helai tamɔ bud swelling virus lɛ mra. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ mli ni okwɛ akɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni sa tsuɔ nii koni onine ashɛ pod yibii babaoo nɔ.

english: Why do many of the flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers but shed up to 90% of them. The tree drops extra flowers to save water and nutrients for the pods it can realistically support to maturity.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi kɛyashi 90% yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔi krokomɛi ni ekɛto nu kɛ niyenii kɛha pods ni baanyɛ aye abua dalɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: What happens to my crop if I plant cocoa trees too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting cocoa trees too closely causes their root systems to fight for nutrients and water. It also creates a dark, humid environment under the canopy that encourages fungal diseases like Black Pod.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli edɔ hu baa ŋwɛitsu lɛ shishi ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji ahe hewalɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off non-producing branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ aniji ni wooo yibii lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak, dead, or unproductive shoots so air and sunlight can circulate through the tree. This reduces fungal growth and allows the tree to direct its food energy straight into forming large pods.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni egboi, loo ni wooo yibii lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la anyɛ atsɔ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ niyenii hewalɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: How can I tell if the soil in my district is suitable for growing cocoa successfully?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ hi kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ omanye?

english: Good cocoa soil is deep, fertile, well-drained, and capable of holding moisture without waterlogging. If water stands on top of your land for days after heavy rain, the roots may rot.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa mli kwɔ, ewoɔ nii, ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni nu bɛ mli Kɛji nu hi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Shishifãi lɛ hu baanyɛ agbo.

english: How do I know the exact time a cocoa pod is fully ripe and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A ripe cocoa pod changes color—green pods turn bright yellow, while red or purple pods turn orange-yellow. A ripe pod also makes a distinct hollow sound when gently tapped with your knuckles.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Pods tsuru loo purple lɛ baatsake kɛya ŋmɔŋ-ŋmei. Pods ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ hu feɔ gbee ni yɔɔ srɔto ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ okɛ onine tswa fioo.

english: Black Pod is caused by a water mold that thrives in damp, overly shaded, and unweeded farms during the rainy season. Clearing weeds and removing infected pods helps keep the rot from spreading.
ga: Nu mli ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Shade babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ tsɔ. ni ajieee jwɛi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow and dropping off during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves during dry spells are a sign of heat stress or nutrient deficiency. The tree drops leaves to conserve internal moisture when rainfall drops or when the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ ji hulutsoo he haomɔ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛha amɛmli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ loo kɛ́ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I continue growing food crops like cassava inside my mature cocoa farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ maya nɔ madu niyenii, tamɔ ŋmei, yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ ni eda lɛ mli?

english: Food crops grow well alongside young cocoa, but once cocoa trees mature, their dense canopy blocks the light that food crops need. The mature roots will also compete heavily with food crops for water and plant nutrients.
ga: Niyenii tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe. Shi kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ da lɛ, ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ la ni niyenii tsei taoɔ lɛ naa. Shishifãi ni eda lɛ kɛ tsei ni yeɔ niyenii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, an essential food for crops. Nitrogen moves to the newest growth first, leaving old leaves hungry, which signals that your soil needs compost or fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii Nitrogen lɛ yaa ŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ amli klɛŋklɛŋ. Shi baai momo lɛ hɔmɔ Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is it harmful to burn dry bushes on my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashã tsei ni egbi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu lɛ?

english: Burning grass gives a quick layer of ash, but it destroys beneficial soil microbes and organic matter that hold moisture. Over time, burning makes your soil dry, hard, and unproductive.
ga: Jwɛi ni ashã lɛ baatswa sũ lɛ oya. Shi efiteɔ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ nibii ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ. Beni be hoɔ lɛ Shãa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbiɔ, ewaa ni ewooo yibii.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my young crops so often?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ ehe bahiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ tsei bibii amli lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast growers that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crop roots. Removing them early gives your crops full access to the resources they need to build strength.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the trees during rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and damp shade. Pruning extra branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the trees and stop the fungus from growing.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ. Tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tso lɛ mli gĩɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. In heavy clay soil or waterlogged land, excess water suffocates the roots and encourages rot, which is why planting on raised soil mounds helps water drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa loo hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating large holes in my vegetable leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye buji wuji ni yɔɔ mi-vegetables baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Moths lay tiny eggs under leaves that hatch into hungry caterpillars. Catching them early or using natural neem leaf sprays prevents them from consuming the leaves your plant needs to capture sunlight.
ga: Moths woɔ wɔji bibii. Yɛ baai ni efo lɛ ashishi lɛ, ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Aloo okɛ adebɔɔ mli neem baa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye baa ni he hiaa otso lɛ koni ená hulu la lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall sticks to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tsei kakadaji koni enyɛ ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in full sunlight to create energy for the plant. Staking the vines elevates the leaves away from ground pests and maximizes sunlight exposure, resulting in bigger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã koni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe, ni ebaaha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso ni da.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over when the bunch of fruit grows large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ ewo yibii wuji lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that cannot easily balance heavy fruit loads, especially in high winds. Propping the stem with a strong wooden pole supports the weight until the fruit matures.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. ni nyɛŋ ahi shi mlɛo kɛ aduawai ni tsii, titri lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua etsitsinɔnii lɛ kɛyashi aduawai lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: How do I know if the soil is wet enough to plant after the first rain of the season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rainfall often only wets the top layer of soil, which can dry out quickly and kill newly sprouted seeds. It is safer to wait until two or three steady rains have deeply soaked the ground before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ agbi oya ni ebaanyɛ egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa dani odu.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my high-yielding hybrid maize harvest to plant next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially cross-bred to yield high results only for the first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose their special traits, leading to uneven growth and much smaller yields in the second year.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ tsɔɔ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛsui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa baa, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi kwraa yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Is it safe for me to apply urea fertilizer directly at the base of my newly sprouted crops?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ urea baawo tsei heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, putting urea directly at the base of a tender sprout can burn the young stem and roots. This weakens the bottom of the plant and causes it to tilt or fall over.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ urea wo tsei bibii lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishigbɛ fã lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa etsiɔ ehe loo egbeeɔ shi.

english: When is the right time for me to start putting urea fertilizer on my young crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ni mikɛ urea woɔ mli lɛ shishi?

english: Urea should be applied after the plant has established a healthy root system, usually a few weeks after sprouting. Always place it a short distance away from the main stem rather than right against it.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ urea awo tso lɛ mli beni etswa shishifãi ni mli wa ema shi sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Ha ekɛ tso titri lɛ akabɔ he be fɛɛ be. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ lɛ kɛ tso tso titli ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Can applying fertilizer too close to a young sprout cause the stem to grow weak?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he ni bɛŋkɛ tsei bibii lɛ tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ?

english: Yes, harsh chemical fertilizers like urea placed too close to a delicate young sprout damage the tender stem base, making it lose its strength and bend easily.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni mli wa tamɔ urea ni akɛwoɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe tsɔ lɛ baafite tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Enɛ haa ehewalɛ baa shi ni ekotoɔ oya.

english: Why are my young crops leaning over or falling sideways after they emerge from the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ shwieɔ shi loo egbeeɔ shi yɛ afã beni eje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plants tilt or fall sideways when their base and early roots are not strong enough to support them, often due to shallow planting or fertilizer damage around the stem.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ afã kɛji amɛshishi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua amɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji dumɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ ni efiteɔ.

english: What causes the base of my young plant stem to look weak and loose in the soil?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ miifee tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: A weak base usually means the plant roots did not anchor properly in the soil during early germination, or chemical burning at the stem destroyed its support structure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishitoo ni bɛ hewalɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso shishifãi lɛ ehiɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ mra lɛ. loo tsofai ni shãa tso lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ nɔ ni fiɔ esɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young crops pull out of the soil so easily when there is a light wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso bibioo lɛ jieɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko miitswa lɛ?

english: Crops uproot easily when their root foundation is shallow or damaged during early growth, preventing them from gripping the soil firmly.
ga: Tsei lɛ shishifãi shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ shishitoo lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo efite yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ. Etsiɔ enaa koni ekakpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ.

english: How deep should I plant my seeds so that the young crops grow strong and straight?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu dumɔwui lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ koni dumɔwui lɛ adara ni amɛhe wa ni amɛdamɔ shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Seeds need to be planted deep enough—usually two to three times their size—so the initial roots build a solid base underground that keeps the plant standing upright.
ga: Esa akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ mli shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa. (Be pii lɛ, amɛdaraa fe shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ.) No hewɔ lɛ shishijee shishifãi lɛ feɔ shishitoo ni ma shi shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni dumɔwu lɛ adamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: How can I make sure the base of my plant stays strong right after it sprouts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mitso lɛ shishitoo lɛ baahi shi jogbaŋŋ beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ?

english: To build a strong base, plant seeds at the correct depth, firm the soil gently around them, and avoid placing strong fertilizers directly against the tender stem.
ga: Bɔni afee ni oma shishitoo ni wa Dumɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ni sa, ni okɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ ama shi blɛoo. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa ni akɛwoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: How do I know if my planted seeds have failed or if I should just keep waiting for them to emerge?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwu ko ni midu lɛ ehiii loo esa akɛ mamɛ ni eya nɔ eda?

english: If seeds take much longer than expected to sprout, inspect a few planting spots carefully; if seeds are soft or rotted, the early process went wrong and re-planting may be needed.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ Kwɛmɔ he ni adu lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ loo amɛgbo Shishijee gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ eyaaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ekolɛ ehe baahia ni adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my farm look uneven with some crops standing tall and others tilting from the start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee, ni ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi damɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ekrokomɛi hu etsɔ amɛhe kɛjɛ shishijee lɛ?

english: Uneven growth often shows that early planting methods were inconsistent or that fertilizer was misplaced on some sprouts, weakening their base while others grew normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ tsɔɔ shishijee dumɔ gbɛi ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. aloo ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo dumɔwui komɛi anɔ yɛ he ni esaaa Enɛ haa shishitoo lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi daraa bɔ ni sa.

english: If I open a new farm site far away from home, how can I tell if the soil there is good for growing crops?
ga: Kɛji migbele ŋmɔ hee ni kɛ shia teŋ jɛkɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha tsei akwɛmɔ?

english: Look at the wild plants growing there naturally. Dark soil with thick, healthy green weeds usually means the land is fertile, while sandy or pale soil will need extra animal manure or compost before your crops can grow well.
ga: Naa koo mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ ni jwɛi eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, shikpɔji ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ loo shikpɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baabi ni akɛ ŋmei loo kooloi ŋmei afata he dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: My farm labor is limited and workers are hard to find, so how can I stop weeds from taking over my crop field?
ga: Nitsumɔ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ faaa ni ewa akɛ aaana nitsulɔi. No hewɔ lɛ, te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye midumɔi lɛ anɔ?

english: You can cover the soil around your crops with dry grass or cocoa husks, which is called mulching. This blocks sunlight so weeds cannot sprout easily, saving you the stress of clearing the farm constantly by yourself.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni jwɛi loo kookoo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching. ni baatsi hulu la lɛ naa No hewɔ lɛ jwɛi lɛ kwɛɛɛ mlɛo. Ehaa haomɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni bo diɛŋtsɛ obaatsuɔ daa lɛ mli baa lɛ baa shi.

english: What does it mean to link different crops together by planting them on the same field?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ ni akɛaabɔ he lɛ shishi?

english: Planting two or more crops together, like maize and cassava, is called intercropping. The fast-growing crop is harvested early for quick food, while the slower crop takes over the space later, maximizing how much food you get from one plot.
ga: Nibii enyɔ loo nɔ ni fe nakai ni aduɔ yɛ he kome, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa. Atsɛɔ lɛ intercropping. Akpaa tsei ni daa oya lɛ mra. koni efee niyenii ni ayeɔ oya Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ baaye he lɛ sɛɛ mli. Enɛ ji koni niyenii ni onine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo.

english: I need to feed my family quickly, so which crops mature fast enough to harvest in a short time?
ga: Ehe bahia ni makwɛ miweku lɛ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛɛ tsei daa oya bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ be kukuoo mli?

english: Crops like maize, cowpeas, and green vegetables like okra grow quickly and can be harvested in 2 to 3 months, giving your household fast food and income while waiting for long-season crops like yam or cassava.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, tsina ŋmãa, kɛ aduawai eŋɔli tamɔ okra lɛ daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, ni ehaa oweku lɛ niyenii oya kɛ shika be mli ni amɛmɛɔ be mli nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Since my farm is far from the market, why do my harvested cassava roots spoil so fast before I can move them?
ga: Ejaakɛ miŋmɔ lɛ kɛ jara lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ. Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani mijieɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ he kroko lɛ?

english: Cassava roots start to rot within two days after harvest because air enters the wounds made when digging them up. To prevent loss, only harvest the amount you can transport or process immediately.
ga: Cassava shishifãi jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni akpa lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ pilamɔ ni baa kɛ́ atsa lɛ mli lɛ mli. koni akafite Kpamɔ shika pɛ ni obaanyɛ okɛya loo okɛtsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops when I am working alone on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ kɛ́ mikome too mitsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh conditions, so they steal water and nutrients faster than farm crops. Planting cover crops like groundnuts early fills the open ground so weeds have no space to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ mra Ebaaha he lɛ agbele kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ jwɛi bɛ he ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How do leguminous plants like beans help other crops grow better in the same soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa tsei krokomɛi ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Beans have special natural linkages in their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the dirt. This acts like free fertilizer for crops planted beside or after them.
ga: Beans yɛ adebɔɔ mli tsakpaa krɛdɛɛ ko kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa tsei ni adu yɛ emasɛi. loo no sɛɛ

english: How can I plan my planting so my household has food throughout the year instead of all at once?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ koni mishiabii lɛ aná niyenii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ moŋ fe ni makwɛ amɛ fɛɛ shikome?

english: You can use staggered planting, which means sowing a small section of your field every two weeks. This makes your crops mature at different times so you harvest fresh food continuously.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ adu ŋmɔ lɛ fã bibioo ko daa otsii enyɔ. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ oya nɔ okpa niyenii hee.

english: Why do my young crops wither quickly when I clear all the big trees off my new farm plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cutting down every tree leaves young crops exposed to direct sun heat and harsh winds. Keeping a few tall trees gives light shade and keeps moisture in the soil so young plants do not burn.
ga: Tsei fɛɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ naa dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli baa lɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ Fioo komɛi baaha hulutsoo ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi bɔni afee ni tsei bibii lɛ akashã.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my crops in straight lines instead of scattering seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows ensures every plant gets equal space, air, and sunlight. It also creates clear walking paths, making it much easier and faster for you to weed and apply fertilizer.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa he ko, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ehaa gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anyiɛɔ lɛ hu feɔ faŋŋ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo ni oya kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot hold enough water under direct, harsh sunlight. They require temporary shade crops, like plantains, to shield them from excessive heat while their root systems develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant as many cocoa trees as possible close together so I can get more harvest from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe bɔ ni manyɛ koni maná ŋmaa babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting trees too close forces them to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with tall, weak trees that produce fewer cocoa pods and allow diseases to spread rapidly between branches.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa onáa tso kakadaŋŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ kookoo ŋmeii fioo pɛ, ni ehaa helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ tsei lɛ aniji ateŋ.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the plant is starving for essential soil nutrients like nitrogen or magnesium, or that the soil around the roots is too waterlogged for the tree to feed properly.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen loo magnesium, loo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli eyi kɛ nu aahu akɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ eye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to cut off healthy-looking branches from my cocoa tree if I want it to yield more pods?
