ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli kɛji miisumɔ ni ewo ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes useless shoots and extra branches so the tree can direct its energy into developing pods instead of growing unnecessary leaves. It also lets sunlight and fresh air pass through the tree, which prevents fungal rot.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa kɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmɔtɔi yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ najiaŋ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu tsɔɔ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ baaye abua ni fungal akafite.

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop flowers they cannot support, but heavy flower loss usually happens when the tree is stressed by dry weather, attacked by tiny insects, or lacking beneficial midges to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ. Shi bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ waa lɛ baa kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao tsei lɛ, kooloi bibii tutuaa amɛ, loo amɛbɛ gbɛ ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni amɛaatsɔ nɔ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: How do weeds growing around the base of my trees prevent my crops from growing well?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi tsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ atsĩ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal fertilizer, moisture, and space directly from your crop's root zone, effectively starving your trees before they can absorb the soil's nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ he ko kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ dani enyɛɔ eŋɔɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do extension agents recommend planting plantain alongside new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni woɔ nibii ahe adafi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei heei ahe lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and produce large, wide leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing vital canopy shade and humidity for delicate young cocoa plants while giving you food to harvest early on.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hia kɛha kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii ni obaakpa mra.

english: Excess rain and cool humidity create the perfect environment for fungal spores to spread. When wet weather persists and trees are too dense for wind to dry the pods, fungal diseases like black pod quickly infect the fruit.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ baa. Kɛji akɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ tee nɔ ni tsei lɛ amli eyi obɔ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ agbi ŋmeii lɛ, ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji baanyɛ atswa aduawai lɛ oya.

english: Why is that green plant growing on top of my cocoa tree branch causing the branch to dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei eŋɔli ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi kookoo niji lɛ anɔ lɛ miiha tsei lɛ aniji lɛ miigbi lɛ?

english: That plant is mistletoe, a parasite that drills its roots directly into your cocoa tree's branches to suck out water and nutrients, slowly starving and killing the branch it lives on.
ga: Nakai tso lɛ ji mistletoe. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwieɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa kookoo niji amli koni ekɛmu nu kɛ niyenii, ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ fiofio ni efiteɔ tsei niji ni amɛhiɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my old cocoa trees stop producing as many pods even when the rainfall is good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso momo lɛ kpa ŋmɔtɔ babaoo feemɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 25 years, their internal transport systems slow down and their roots become less efficient at pulling nutrients from the soil, causing pod production to naturally drop off unless the trees are pruned back heavily or replanted.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tsei lɛ ye afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, amɛmli gbɛfaa gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ baa shi. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbala niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa pod feemɔ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ja afo tso lɛ mli waa loo adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep wilting and drying up when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense sunlight and dry heat. They need shade crops like plantains planted beside them to act as living umbrellas, keeping the leaves safe from sun damage and retaining moisture in the soil.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ latsaa ni mli egbi lɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la efitee baai lɛ. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: When is the best time for me to plant my maize during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: You should plant your maize right after the first two or three steady rains of the major season. Planting in moist soil helps the seeds germinate quickly, whereas planting too early in dry soil can cause the seeds to dry out or be eaten by pests.
ga: Esa akɛ odu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi fioo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi loo tsɛŋemɔ helai aye amɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear the land and make big soil mounds before planting yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ofee shikpɔŋ agbo ko dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii adu lɛ?

english: Yams grow underground and need loose, soft soil to expand into large tubers. Building mounds gathers rich topsoil into one place, prevents water from swamping the roots, and makes it easy for the yams to grow big.
ga: Sweet potatoes kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Gɔŋ ni afee lɛ buaa shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni jara wa lɛ naa yɛ he kome. Tsĩ nu naa koni ekaho shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni eha ŋmeii akwɛ̃ mlɛo

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each plant enough space ensures it gets all the resources it needs to grow strong and yield big crops.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa enáa nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ eda ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Planting maize on the same land every season drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows pests to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts fixes nitrogen back into the soil and keeps it fertile.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii pɔtɛɛi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on cassava are usually signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. You can manage this by using disease-resistant cassava stems for planting and destroying infected plants early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ yucca nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii beni oduɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ofiteɔ amɛ mra lɛ nɔ.

english: Fertilizer is best applied when the plants are actively growing, such as two to three weeks after germination and again during flowering. Always apply fertilizer when the soil is damp so the plant roots can absorb the nutrients easily without burning.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ tsei lɛ miida waa, tamɔ otsii 2-3 yɛ be mli ni amɛje kpo lɛ sɛɛ. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be fɛɛ be kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ koni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni shãaa.

english: What is eating small holes in my pepper leaves overnight, and how can I stop it?
ga: Pepper baai amli buji bibii ni ayeɔ Mɛni ji nyɔɔŋ kome? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Holes created overnight are usually caused by night-feeding caterpillars like armyworms or beetles. Inspecting your farm early in the morning, clearing nearby weeds, and applying recommended organic or mild chemical sprays will protect the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ niyenii gbɛkɛ, tamɔ cutworms loo beetles lɛ ji mɛi ni feɔ bu ni afee nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ. Ni kɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ajieɔ yi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil gets too dry, or when the plant lacks essential nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil consistently moist and feeding the plant helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akpɛtɛ he ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly and choke my crops right after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni efiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji nugbɔ enɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Rain activates dormant weed seeds buried in the topsoil, causing them to sprout rapidly. Weeds naturally grow faster than crops and steal water and nutrients, so removing them while they are small prevents them from crowding your main crops.
ga: Nugbɔ baaha jwɛi dumɔwui ni ehiɛ edɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. Afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya. Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe adebɔɔ mli tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkawo otsei titrii lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong, direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and quickly dries out the soil. Retaining larger shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantain beside young cocoa provides natural shade and preserves soil moisture.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Curled and yellow-patterned cassava leaves are typically caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings prevents this disease and ensures healthy root growth.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela kɛbaa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava ni afolɔ ni ana he odaseyeli akɛ helai nyɛɔ eyeɔ lɛ ni aaadu lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ hela nɛɛ naa ni eha shishifãi lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my maize turning pale yellow early in the season instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn pale yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed to make food and grow strong. Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves regain their dark green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha niyenii feemɔ kɛ shweremɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛná amɛ su ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain tsei titri lɛ etee.

english: When too many sucker shoots grow around one plantain stem, they compete for nutrients, water, and sunlight in the soil. Removing excess shoots and leaving only two or three strong ones allows the main plant to produce much larger, heavier bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Plantain kome he lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashiɔ ŋmeii 2-3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ tsei niji ni dara ni tsii babaoo.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts alongside my maize help the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have tiny beneficial bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally enriches the soil, giving nearby maize plants extra nutrients to feed on.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ helai bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi ni heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ naa niyenii babaoo ni amɛyeɔ.

english: Yam leaves need to spread high up in direct sunlight to capture solar energy and build large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground, which prevents leaf rot diseases and maximizes sunlight exposure.
ga: Esa akɛ agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli koni emɔ hulu hewalɛ ni efee ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni baa lɛ akafite ni hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo.

english: Why does my land produce less harvest if I plant the same crop on the same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil while allowing pests and diseases that prefer that crop to build up in the soil. Rotating different crops each season gives the soil time to recover and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni tsei lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni atsakeɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ lɛ mli.

english: Pepper flowers usually drop off when the plant suffers stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of balanced nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist with organic mulch helps protect the flowers so they can form peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni sa ni bɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ organic mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay small and weak even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than cultivated crops and aggressively steal nutrients, water, and sunlight from the soil before your crops can reach them. Clearing weeds early in the growth cycle ensures your crops get all the nourishment available.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. ni ekɛ ekãa juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ amɛdalɛ mli lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Why should I wait for a few strong rains before sowing my maize seeds instead of planting after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa fioo dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui moŋ fe ni madu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain often warms up dry soil without soaking deep enough, which can cause sown seeds to sprout and then wither if dry weather returns. Waiting for steady, deep rain ensures the soil stays wet enough for seeds to germinate and develop deep roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛwooo mli jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ni adu lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbo kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ ku esɛɛ eba. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni baa be fɛɛ be lɛ mɛmɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why is my cocoa farm suddenly producing very few pods this year compared to previous years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ trukaa yɛ afi nɛɛ mli kɛ akɛto afii ni eho lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: A sudden drop in cocoa pods can be caused by nutrient-depleted soil, extended drought, or hidden pest and disease attacks like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, which slowly weakens the trees from within.
ga: Ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ hewɔ ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ baa shi trukaa lɛ. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ, tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ fiofio kɛjɛɔ emli lɛ.

english: Do cocoa trees naturally stop bearing fruit as they get older, or does low production always mean disease?
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ kpaɔ yibiiwoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Aloo nibii ni afee lɛ fioo lɛ tsɔɔ hela be fɛɛ be?

english: Cocoa trees peak in production between 10 to 20 years of age. After 25 to 30 years, their yields naturally decline due to old age, though severe diseases can cause an even faster drop in healthy, young trees.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ afii 10 kɛyashi 20 lɛ. Yɛ afii 25 kɛyashi 30 sɛɛ lɛ, nibii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ hela ni naa wa baanyɛ aha tsei bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aba shi oya moŋ.

english: How can I tell if my low crop yield is due to tired soil or because my trees are sick with a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi lɛ jɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ hewɔ loo hela emɔ mitsei lɛ?

english: Tired soil usually causes a slow, even decline across the whole farm over years, whereas disease causes distinct signs like yellowing swollen branches, blackening pods, or individual trees dying rapidly in patches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔji ni efite lɛ haa shwieɔ shi fiofio. Ehiɔ shi daa yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hela lɛ kɛ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ baa, tamɔ tsei niji ni efuu ni ji ŋmɔŋ, tsei aŋkroaŋkroi ni gboɔ oya, ni amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: What causes the pods on my cocoa trees to turn black and rot before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa?

english: This is Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection triggered by heavy rain, high humidity, and dense shade. Rain drops splash fungal spores from the soil onto the pods, causing them to rot.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, latsaa ni naa wa, kɛ hulutsoo ni mli wa kɛbaa. Nugbɔ nɛɔ, ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. ha egbo

english: Is there a specific disease in Ghana that makes cocoa stems swell up and die?
ga: Ani hela ko yɛ ni yɔɔ Ghana pɔtɛɛ ni haa kookoo tsei lɛ fũuɔ ni amɛgboiɔ?

english: Yes, that is Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease (CSSVD). It is spread by tiny mealybug insects and causes swollen stems, leaf discoloration, and eventual death of the tree within two to three years.
ga: Hɛɛ, no ji hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe (CSSVD). Mealybugs bibii ji mɛi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kuu lɛ fuɔ, ebaa lɛ su tsakeɔ, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ mli.

english: Should I leave diseased or rotten cocoa pods hanging on the tree, or cut them off?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi kookoo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ loo efite lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ loo mafolɔ amɛ?

english: You must cut off diseased pods and remove them from the farm immediately. Leaving them on the tree allows fungal spores to spread to healthy pods during rains.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ojie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ ashi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ agbɛ ashwã tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli yɛ nugbɔ be mli.

english: How do crop diseases spread from my neighbor's cocoa farm to my farm?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni tso hela ko gbɛ eshwa kɛjɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛba miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Diseases spread through wind, rain splashes, shared farm tools that haven't been cleaned, infected planting pods, and pests like mealybugs carrying viruses from farm to farm.
ga: Helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Nugbɔ ni shwieɔ shi Okwaafoi anitsumɔ nibii ni ajaa ni atsuuu he lɛ emɔ tsei amli ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mealybugs ni hiɛɔ helai kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees grow lots of healthy leaves but fail to set any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shi enyɛɛɛ efee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Excessive foliage with low pod production often means the trees are getting too much shade or nitrogen, lack phosphorus for flowering, or are dropping flowers due to severe insect attacks like capsids.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai babaoo kɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiná hulutsoo loo nitrogen babaoo. Fosfɔs ni bɛ kɛha fɔfɔii loo fɔfɔii ni gbeeɔ shi yɛ kooloi bibii ni tutuaa amɛ waa, tamɔ capsids lɛ hewɔ.

english: Can applying fertilizer save a cocoa tree that is already dying from a disease?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ahere kookoo tso ni hela miigbe lɛ lɛ yiwala?

english: Fertilizer helps healthy trees grow stronger and nourishes poor soil, but it cannot cure a viral disease like Swollen Shoot. Sick, virus-infected trees must be cut out to prevent spreading the disease to healthy ones.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ hewalɛ. Shi enyɛŋ etsa helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ. Esa akɛ afolɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amli lɛ koni hela akagbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are the beans inside my harvested cocoa pods small and flat instead of heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo yibii ni yɔɔ mi kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ ji bibii ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsii lɛ?

english: Flat or light cocoa beans are caused by severe dry weather during pod filling, poor soil nutrients, or insect feeding by pests like capsids (akate) that drain nutrients from developing pods.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa yɛ be mli ni awoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni yeɔ niyenii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ capsids (akates) ni jieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Which direction should the buds point when I am planting cassava stems in my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ beni aduɔ ŋmei tsei yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Always make sure the small nodes or buds on the cassava stem point upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the plant will waste energy trying to grow shoots in the wrong direction, resulting in weak growth and fewer tubers.
ga: Kwɛmɔ be fɛɛ be akɛ fãi lɛ afee bibioo. loo ŋmeii bibii Yɛ ŋmei tso ko ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ Kɛji okɛ tsei kwɛ ŋwɛi Tsei fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ ŋmeii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Enɛ haa edalɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ baa.

english: How do I pick the right plantain sucker from an old tree to plant on my new field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui ni sa kɛjɛ mitsei momo lɛ amli koni mikɛdu yɛ mishikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ?

english: Look for suckers with narrow, spear-shaped leaves and a thick base, often called 'sword suckers.' These shoots have strong energy reserves and grow into healthier, faster-yielding plantain trees compared to suckers with broad, flat leaves.
ga: Taomɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ lance kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli tse. Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ amɛ ‘klante ŋmeii’, ŋmeii nɛɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni mli wa ni akɛtoɔ he. ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ plantains ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii oya. Kɛ akɛto ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe

english: Can I put fresh chicken droppings directly on my young plants to help them grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ hee awo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Fresh chicken manure is very strong and generates heat as it decomposes, which can burn plant roots. It is best to mix the manure with dry leaves or let it sit and rot for a few weeks before applying it around your crops.
ga: Kooloi afɔfɔi ni afee ehee lɛ mli wa waa ni ekɛ dɔlɛ baa be mli ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso shishifãi ashã. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ afutu baai ni egbi loo oha egbo otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛwo onibii amli.

english: How do I keep my soil fertile without buying expensive commercial fertilizers every year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni miheee jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa daa afi?

english: You can keep your soil rich by adding organic material like decomposed animal manure, dry farm leaves, or crop leftovers back into the soil. Rotating your heavy-feeding crops with leguminous plants like beans or groundnuts also naturally restores nutrients.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi kɛtsɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ kooloi ashishifãi ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. baai ni egbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ ni haa kooloi niyenii babaoo kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava is fully matured and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. A key sign is when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, leaving a longer bare stem, and the ground around the stem begins to swell and crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, ni enɛ damɔ ŋmei lɛ henɔ lɛ nɔ. Okadi titri ji be mli ni baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Ashi tso kakadaŋŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishifã lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why is my plantain tree taking so long to bring out its fruit flower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Plantains require plenty of water and rich nutrients, especially potassium, to start flowering. If the soil is too dry or lacks organic matter, the plant slows down its development and delays bringing out the flower stem.
ga: Nu babaoo kɛ niyenii babaoo he miihia plantains. Titri lɛ, potassium ni akɛjeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ baaha eshweremɔ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaaha fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: Is it safe to plant cassava and plantain together on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ he kome?

english: Yes, cassava and plantain can grow well together. Cassava roots expand under the soil while plantain leaves grow tall above, allowing you to maximize space and harvest two different food crops from one piece of land.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei kɛ plantain baanyɛ afee ekome kɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Cassava shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ be mli ni plantain baai lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ feɔ babaoo ni okpaa niyenii srɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: How much space should I leave between my plantain trees when planting?
ga: Gbɛ enyiɛ esa akɛ maŋmɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Plantain trees should be spaced about 3 meters (around 10 feet) apart. Giving them enough space prevents them from shading each other out and ensures each tree gets enough water and nutrients to yield heavy bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ afee mitai 3 (aafee naji 10). Kɛ́ aha he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi amɛhe naa. ni ekwɛɔ koni tso fɛɛ tso aná nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha efee tso ni tsii.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When heavy rains leave water standing on the farm, the soil becomes waterlogged, which starves the roots of air and leads to rot; planting cassava on raised mounds helps rainwater drain off easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu tsiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nu baatsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain trees splitting and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigba ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves split naturally in strong winds so the main trunk doesn't break. However, if the leaf edges turn brown or yellow quickly, it usually means the plant needs more water or potassium nutrients from the soil.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ fãa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ba. No hewɔ lɛ, tso titri lɛ fãaa. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ asɛɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ oya lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nu loo potassium nibii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and burn under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture needed for young cocoa seedlings to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he waa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa koni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when my field stays flooded after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When rain stays on the farm for too long, water fills up all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots. Without air, the plant roots cannot absorb nitrogen from the soil, causing the leaves to lose their healthy green color.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Tso shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ ahe su ni ji eŋɔli ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: This leaf curling is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny white flies. The disease weakens the leaves so they cannot produce food properly, leading to smaller tuber yields.
ga: Nɛkɛ baai lɛ ni ebɔle ehe nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Hela nɛɛ ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ woɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tuber yibiiwoo lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without producing any tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat destroys the pollen inside the tomato blossom, preventing the flower from forming seeds and fruit. To save energy, the plant drops the unfertilized flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa fɔfɔii woɔ dumɔwui kɛ aduawai. koni akɛ hewalɛ ato Tso lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi ni afɔɔɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my maize crops grow thin and tall with tiny cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ mli tse ni ekɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, they fight for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition causes the plants to grow tall and weak searching for light, leaving little energy to grow big cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ la taomɔ mli. Enɛ haa hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshwɛɔ kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni akwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I pour granular fertilizer right against the stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ granular fertilizer woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts. Placing it directly against the plant stem burns the tender plant tissue and destroys feeder roots, which can stunt or kill the crop.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli ŋmei babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. ni efiteɔ niyenii halɔ lɛ shishifãi Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo egbo.

english: Why do seed store maize seeds yield more harvest than seeds I saved from my own last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛtoɔ dumɔwui ahe lɛ wo yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikpa kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ ni mikpa nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds from agro-dealers are specially bred for strength and high yield. Saved hybrid seeds lose these special traits after the first harvest, leading to weaker plants and smaller yields in the next season.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni jɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo. Dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ nibii krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: What causes tiny holes in my cabbage leaves and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ kaabeji baai anɔ Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa?

english: Small caterpillars, such as the Diamondback moth larvae, eat the leaves from the underside. You can manage them by checking under leaves early and spraying natural pest controls like Neem seed extract.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ Diamondback ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ. Obaanyɛ okwɛ amɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni oookwɛ mra lɛ nɔ. kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi tamɔ neem dumɔwui amli nu lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ.

english: Why should I wait for the rains to settle before planting my yam sets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ omɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ akpa dani odu sweet potato tsei?

english: Yam seed pieces need steady soil moisture to wake up from dormancy and grow roots. If planted in dry soil, the heat can bake or rot the yam set before it leaves the ground.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fãi lɛ taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛte shi kɛjɛ wɔɔhe ni amɛye amɛbua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Dɔlɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii ni asaa he lɛ agbo dani amɛje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know my groundnuts are ready to harvest without digging up my entire farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ efee klalo akɛ makpa ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Groundnuts show maturity above ground when leaves begin turning yellow and dry out. You can test by digging up two or three sample plants; if the inside of the pods has dark brown veins and markings, the crop is ready.
ga: Peanuts daa yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ ni ooofo mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ okadii. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need for leafy green growth. Adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help the plant regain its green color and increase yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ organic fertilizer loo nitrogen fertilizer fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leguminous crops like cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Growing them after maize naturally restores plant food to your field so your next crop grows stronger without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ odu amɛ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha tsei niyenii aku sɛɛ aba oŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa atsu nii.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like potassium. Mulching the soil around the plant to keep it moist and cool helps the flowers stay attached and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium, shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli Kɛ́ tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why do my garden eggs grow very fast with large leaves but fail to set fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ be mli ni amɛyɛ baai wuji shi amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen, they direct all their energy into making tall stems and big leaves instead of flowers and fruit. Balancing your soil with phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to stop leafy growth and produce plentiful fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo tsei lɛ ashishifãi kakadaji kɛ baai wuji. Yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai najiaŋ Kɛ́ akɛ fɔsfɔs kɛ potassium to shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekpaa baai lɛ adalɛ ni ewoɔ aduawai babaoo.

english: How long can cassava remain unharvested in the soil before it spoils?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmei baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni akpaaa lɛ dani efite?

english: Cassava is a resilient crop that can safely stay stored in the ground for 12 to 24 months after planting. However, leaving it in the ground too long past its maturity can cause the tubers to become woody, tough, and less suitable for eating or selling.
ga: Cassava ji tso ko ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi ni abaanyɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ shweshweeshwe nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 24 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Shi, kɛ́ ashi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ kɛyashi egbɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmeii lɛ afee tsei, amɛhe awa ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ loo ahɔ̃ɔɔ.

english: Why are my young hybrid cocoa trees flowering so much earlier than traditional cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-hybrid cacao tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi mra kwraa fe blema cacao lɛ?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties are bred specifically to mature quickly and produce pods within 18 to 24 months, whereas older traditional varieties often take 3 to 5 years. Early flowering is a normal feature of these improved crop varieties.
ga: Akwɛɔ kookoo henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛshwere oya ni amɛwo ŋmeii yɛ nyɔji 18 kɛyashi 24 mli, yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5. Fofɔi ni baa mra lɛ ji nɔ ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ nɛɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves roll up inward during the sunny afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants curl their leaves during peak heat as a survival mechanism to conserve water and prevent scorching. If the leaves unfold again in the evening or after watering, it is a normal reaction to heat and not a disease.
ga: Tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛtsi shãa naa. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ loo beni awo amɛ nu sɛɛ lɛ Abuɔ enɛ akɛ eji nɔ ko ni yaa nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni ejeee hela.

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can easily be weakened by tiny soil worms called nematodes or root weevils. Staking heavy bunches with wooden poles and piling rich earth around the plant base gives them strong support against high winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ oya. Atsɛɔ lɛ hu akɛ nematodes loo shishifãi ŋmeii. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ waa ni akɛ sũ ni jara wa fɔ̃ɔ amɛshishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa.

english: Why are my harvested yam tubers growing in bent, twisted shapes instead of straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmeii amli moŋ fe ŋmeii ni ja lɛ?

english: Yams twist and deform when their roots strike hard, compact soil or underground stones during growth. Loosening the soil deeply when building your yam mounds allows the tubers to expand smoothly and grow long.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ ni efiteɔ kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ ni mli wa, ni mli edɔ loo tɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ beni afee sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ, ebaaha sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ ni etsɛ.

english: Why are tiny green insects sticking to the soft shoots of my cowpea plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miikpɛtɛ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ ashishifãi bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Those tiny insects are aphids, which suck sap from young shoots and leave sticky liquids on the leaves. Spraying them early with a mild soapy water solution or neem leaf extract keeps them from spreading and damaging your plants.
ga: Nakai kooloi bibii lɛ ji aphids. Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ ni amɛshiɔ nu ni mli tse yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Ni akɛ nu ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ loo nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ neem baai amli lɛ baashwie nɔ kɛjɛ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni ekagbɛ eshwa ni efite otsei lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my young pawpaw tree is male or female before it starts fruiting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mipapaya tso bibioo lɛ ji nuu loo yoo dani ebɔi yibiiwoo?

english: You cannot easily tell when they are very young seedlings. You have to wait until they start flowering—male trees produce long, hanging branches with many small flowers that do not yield fruit, while female trees produce larger flowers directly on the main trunk that swell into fruit.
ga: Onyɛŋ ole be ni amɛji gbekɛbii bibii kwraa lɛ mlɛo. Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi ebaaje fɔfɔii afeemɔ shishi. Tsei ni ji hii lɛ woɔ niji kakadaji kɛ fɔfɔi bibii. Mɛi babaoo wooo yibii. yɛ be mli ni tsei yei woɔ fɔfɔi agboi yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni shwereɔ ni ewoɔ aduawai.

english: Why do some of my crop plants produce plenty of flowers but all the flowers fall off without growing into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi fɛɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by severe heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. In some crops, it is also because the flowers were not pollinated by insects, or the plant is a male tree whose only job is to provide pollen to female plants.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo sũ mli niyenii kpakpai haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Yɛ tsei komɛi amli lɛ, enɛ baanyɛ aba akɛ koolooi kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Aloo, tso ji tso nuu ni enitsumɔ pɛ ji ni ekɛ pollen aha tsei yei.

english: Why should I not move my cocoa seedlings to the main farm when they are extremely young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ woɔ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli be mli ni amɛdarako kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Very young seedlings have soft leaves and fragile root systems that easily dry out and die under the hot sun. Keeping them in the nursery until they develop a strong stem and several firm leaves gives them the strength to survive the move to the main field.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii waa lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni waaa ni egbiɔ oya ni egboɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ mli kɛyashi amɛbaaná tsei ni wa kɛ baai babaoo ni wa lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings droop and die when I move them straight from the shade into the hot open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie amɛ kɛjɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ ko ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings get shocked when exposed to sudden harsh weather. They need a process called hardening off, where you gradually expose them to more sunlight and less water over a few days so they can adapt to the open field.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ ahe feɔ amɛ yaa kɛ́ amɛyashɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa ni baa trukaa lɛ ahe. Amɛbiɔ gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ hardening. he ni okɛ amɛ woɔ hulu la babaoo kɛ nu fioo mli fiofio yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli. koni amɛnyɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ amli

english: Why do I need to pull out some healthy young maize plants if they are growing too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mijieɔ ŋmãa bibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛji amɛdara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When plants grow too close, they fight each other for ground water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Removing a few plants (thinning) leaves enough food and space for the remaining crops to grow tall and produce big, healthy ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ dara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa shikpɔŋ shishi nu he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la. Tsei komɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli. Nɛkɛ (ni shwieɔ shi) nɛɛ haa niyenii kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo ŋmãa toi wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why are my pepper plants producing small flowers when the plants themselves are still very tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ji bibioo kwraa lɛ?

english: Plants often flower early as a survival reaction when they experience stress from hot weather, dry soil, or lack of nutrients. The plant feels threatened and tries to produce seeds quickly before it dies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei fɔɔ mra akɛ nɔ ni haa amɛhiɔ shi kɛ́ amɛkɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ kpe. Tso lɛ nuɔ he akɛ awo ehe gbeyei ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ewo dumɔwui oya dani egbo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cassava plants rolling up and dropping off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells to save water. By shedding leaves, the plant reduces the amount of moisture lost to the hot air, allowing its underground stem and roots to stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni akɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ, ebaaha nu ni tso lɛ fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why do weeds harm my young crops much faster than my fully grown crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi tutuaa mi tsei bibii lɛ oya fe mi tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young crops have short roots and small leaves, so weeds easily steal their soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Older crops have deep root systems and wide leaves that shade out weeds and withstand the competition.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji kɛ baai bibii. No hewɔ lɛ jwɛi lɛ juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ oya. Tsei ni edara lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ akaŋshii.

english: How do I know when the right time has come to harvest my cassava tubers from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei shishifãi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack open. You can also dig carefully near the roots to inspect if the tubers have reached a good size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ. Obaanyɛ otsa shishifãi lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ hu koni ona kɛji ŋmeii lɛ dalɛ sa.

english: Why should I pick seed yam from my best-performing plants instead of just using any small yam left over from the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahala sweet potato tso ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe fɛɛ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, o kɛ ngmlɛfia bibii nɛ tsu ní ɔ nɛ tsu ní. ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ jara lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Seed material carries the traits of its parent plant. Using seeds from healthy, disease-free, and high-yielding plants increases the chances that your next harvest will also be strong and produce large tubers.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ahe nibii lɛ tamɔ tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni hela bɛ amɛhe, ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ amli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa hegbɛ ni oyɔɔ akɛ okpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ebaawo bulbs wuji lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: What does it actually mean if I grow my crops organically, and will my plants still grow strong without store-bought chemical fertilizers?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛji mikɛ mitsei lɛ tsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ? Ni ani mitsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lolo kɛji akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shwapo mli ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ fataaa he?

english: Organic farming means using natural inputs like compost, animal manure, and beneficial plants instead of artificial chemicals. Your crops can grow very strong because natural fertilizers feed the living soil over time, improving its structure and water retention rather than giving just a temporary chemical boost.
ga: Organic okwaayeli tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ baatsu nii yɛ tsofai ni akɛfee lɛ najiaŋ. Oŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ adara waa ejaakɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ ni hiɛ ka lɛ niyenii yɛ be ni sa mli. Afee gbɛjianɔtoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ nu ni ahiɔ mli Yɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii be kukuoo pɛ ni akɛaaha lɛ najiaŋ

english: Why do my crops grow faster and look greener when I mix dried animal dung into the soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Animal manure acts like rich, long-lasting food for the soil. As it breaks down, it slowly releases essential nutrients like nitrogen that build strong leaves and stem strength, while also helping the soil hold onto water longer during hot days.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni jara wa, ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Be ni efiteɔ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni woɔ baai kɛ tsei lɛ ahewalɛ fiofio. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes when there hasn't been rain for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔne ko lɛ? Gbii babaoo nɛ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is your maize plant's natural defense against heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun and wind, helping it trap moisture inside and survive dry spells until the next watering.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni emɔɔ nu ni mli ewo mli lɛ mli ni ehiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ nu ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Is it safe to water my vegetable crops with water drawn straight from a nearby river during the dry season?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikɛ nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ baafɔ mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, river water is often rich in beneficial organic sediments that naturally feed your crops. However, you should ensure the river water is clear and not polluted upstream by washing powders or chemical runoff, which could harm delicate plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, faa mli nu lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ koni faa lɛ mli nu lɛ mli atse ni nɔ ni akɛjieɔ muji loo tsofai ni hoɔ lɛ akafite faa lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aye tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa lɛ awui.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise me to plant groundnuts or beans in the same farm as my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ baawo ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ mi-cassava lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special root nodules that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. Cassava uses a lot of soil nutrients, so growing them together naturally feeds the cassava without exhausting the land.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Cassava kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa ŋmei niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ efooo.

english: What will happen to my land if I plant only maize on the exact same piece of ground every single year?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and builds up crop-specific pests in the ground. Changing crops or growing different varieties together breaks pest cycles and gives the soil time to recover.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni amɛfeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ anɔ Atsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi Amɛfeɔ ekome, amɛfoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe.

english: Why does the top layer of my farm soil turn hard and pale after heavy rains, making it tough for young seeds to sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ yiteŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ? Ehaa ewaa kɛhaa dumɔwui bibii akɛ amɛakwɛ̃

english: Heavy rainfall can beat down on bare dirt, washing away rich topsoil and compacting the surface as it dries. Covering your soil with dried leaves, grass, or mulch cushions the impact of rain, keeping the ground soft and easy for roots to penetrate.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ muji kɛya. Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni egbiɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi, loo ŋmɔtɔ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ baa shi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni shishifãi baanyɛ abote mli oya.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is tired and needs extra organic matter before I clear it for the new season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni akɛ nibii krokomɛi ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli dani mafo mli kɛha be hee lɛ?

english: Tired soil often shows clear signs: water pools on top instead of sinking in, crop leaves turn yellow early, and yields drop despite good rain. Adding compost or fallen foliage restores the soil's energy and structure for future planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ jieɔ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo: nu ŋshɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ moŋ fe ni ebaagbee shi. Tso lɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ oya. ni nibii ni afeɔ lɛ ba shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli dumɔwui.

english: Why are the bottoms of my young garden eggs and tomatoes turning soft and black before they are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei kɛ mi-tomato ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashishi feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ediŋŋ dani amɛshwereɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: This condition is usually blossom-end rot, caused when the plant cannot draw enough calcium from the soil due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant transport calcium directly into the growing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔii anaagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium lɛ yaa aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do young plantain suckers need shade from larger trees when first planted, but do fine in direct sun later on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ he hiaa ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji adɛŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ? Shi ebaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli sɛɛ mli.

english: Young plantain suckers have shallow, tender roots and broad leaves that dry out quickly under full sun. As they grow older, their root systems go deeper to find groundwater and support mature leaves built to absorb full sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ amɛdara lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatao shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni amɛfiɔ baai ni eda ni ama koni amɛŋɔ hulu la lɛ kwraa lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Why are my maize plants growing so small on the part of my land where old plastic bags are buried?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miida bibii yɛ he ni afuu plastic kotokui momoi yɛ lɛ?

english: Plastic bags do not decay in the soil. They create physical barriers underground that trap plant roots, preventing them from spreading deep to search for water and nutrients, which keeps the crop small and weak.
ga: Plastic kotokui lɛ fiteee yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛfeɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkɛmɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ. Etsiɔ enaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa shɔŋŋ koni eyatao nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa.

english: If I burn plastic refuse and trash on my field, will the ash help or hurt my crop soil?
ga: Kɛ mishã plastic jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani sũ baaye abua loo ebaaye miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ awui?

english: Burning plastic and trash releases harmful chemicals and toxins into the ground. Instead of nourishing the soil like wood ash does, burnt plastic leaves behind toxic residue that can burn tender crop roots and stop seeds from sprouting.
ga: Plastic kɛ jwɛi ni ashãa lɛ jieɔ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsofai fɔji kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ tamɔ tso sũ Plastic ni ashã lɛ shĩɔ nibii ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni eshwɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã tso shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ekpa dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why does my soil become so hard and refuse to grow healthy vegetables after rubbish has been buried in it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa waa ni ekpooɔ akɛ ebaadu aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ beni efu jwɛi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil needs air, moisture, and earthworms to stay soft and fertile. When rubbish and plastic are buried, they choke the soil, killing off helpful organisms and compacting the earth so roots cannot breathe or grow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii koni ehi shi bɔdɔɔ ni ewo yibii. Kɛji akɛ afu jwɛi kɛ plastic Amɛbaatsi shikpɔŋ. Egbeɔ bɔɔ nii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu loo amɛdara.

english: Does leaving water sachet rubbers on my farm field stop rain from feeding my plant roots?
ga: Ani nu ni miishi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni ekaye mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ?

english: Yes, spread-out plastic acts like a plastic roof underground or on top of the soil. It blocks rainwater from soaking deep into the earth, causing water to run off instead of feeding your crops' root systems.
ga: Hɛɛ, plastic ni akɛwoɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ plastic ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi loo shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Etsiɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛjeɔ kpo moŋ fe ni eeebote ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Is it safe for me to use water flowing from the village gutter to water my garden vegetables during the dry season?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ akrowa lɛ mli nubu lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii kɛwo mibɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Gutter water usually contains dissolved soaps, chemicals, and human waste, which act like mild poison to crops. It can damage plant roots, stunt leaf growth, and transfer harmful bacteria onto crops that people eat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, samla ni mli edɔ, tsofai, kɛ gbɔmɛi ashwiei yɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ nubu mli lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofa ni mli ejɔ fioo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ Ebaanyɛ efite tsei shishifãi. Ha baai lɛ adalɛ aba shi ni okɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aya ŋmɔshi nibii ni gbɔmɛi yeɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plants growing near blocked roadside gutters get sick and rot so easily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛjegbɛ he nubu ko ni atsĩ naa lɛ masɛi lɛ hela mɔ lɛ ni efiteɔ oya lɛ?

english: Blocked gutters trap dirty, stagnant water filled with rotting trash. This creates a breeding ground for destructive fungus and pests that spread to nearby crops, causing root rot and leaf decay.
ga: Nu tsɔji ni atsĩ naa lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu ni mli ewo muji, ni ekã shi ni jwɛi ni egboi eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ fɔɔ yɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi kɛ baai fiteɔ.

english: What happens to my young seedlings when heavy rains wash town refuse and plastics into my farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ maŋ lɛ mli jwɛi kɛ plastic baa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Flooding trash smothers young seedlings, preventing light from reaching them. Additionally, dirty urban waste carries toxic chemical runoff that can shock and poison tender roots, slowing down their growth.
ga: Jwɛi ni hoɔ nu ashwieɔ shi lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Etsiɔ la naa koni ekashɛ he. Kɛfata he lɛ, tsofai fɔji ni hoɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jwɛi ni mli ewo muji lɛ baanyɛ ahi mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ aya shoofeemɔ mli ni amɛtsɔ poison. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo.

english: Why do my crops wilt and die when I plant them close to where people dump household rubbish?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu yɛ he ni mɛi shwieɔ amɛshia jwɛi lɛ yɛ lɛ?

english: Decomposing garbage leaks a dark, toxic liquid known as leachate into the surrounding dirt. This liquid strips oxygen from the soil and burns crop roots, causing the plants to wilt as if they were poisoned.
ga: Jwɛi ni fiteɔ lɛ jieɔ nu ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni atsɛɔ lɛ leachate lɛ kɛyaa muji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli. Nu nɛɛ gbalaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eshãa tsei shishifãi. Ehaa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ nɔ ni awo amɛ tsofa.

english: Can food crops like cassava suck up poisonous chemicals from ground where rubbish is dumped?
ga: Ani niyenii tsei tamɔ ŋmei baanyɛ ajie tsofai fɔji kɛjɛ shwɛmɔhei?

english: Yes, plant roots act like sponges and absorb whatever liquids are in the soil. If the ground contains chemical poisons from decomposing trash, crops can draw those toxins up into their roots and stems, affecting their health and safety.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei shishifãi tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni amɛmɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji tsofai fɔji ni jɛɔ jwɛi ni fiteɔ lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nakai tsofai fɔji lɛ kɛya amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni saa gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ kɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ he lɛ

english: Can plastic bags buried in the earth make my vegetables turn yellow and bitter?
ga: Ani plastic kotokui ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baaha mi-aduawai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: As buried plastics sit in hot soil, they slowly break down and release harmful chemical additives. These chemicals disrupt how the plant takes in essential minerals, leading to yellowing leaves and poor fruit development.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu plastic yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ Plastic lɛ baafite Efite ni ejieɔ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Tsofai nɛɛ tsiɔ gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛnáa minerals ni he hiaa lɛ naa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni aduawai lɛ hu shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting so fast within just a few days after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli beni mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots do not have a tough outer protective skin like yams do. Once dug out of the soil, air enters small cuts on the root, causing a natural chemical breakdown that turns the flesh brown and soft within two to three days.
ga: Cassava shishifãi bɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni buɔ mɔ he waa tamɔ ŋmei. Kɛji akɛ atsa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ boteɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ amli, ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni fiteɔ nii baa. Enɛ baaha loo lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni efee blɛoo yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting green shoots even when I stack them inside a dark barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shweremɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ewo duŋ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yams are living underground stems that naturally follow a seasonal clock. When the warm, humid season arrives, the tuber automatically wakes up from its rest period and uses its stored food to sprout new shoots, even without light.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni tsɔɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be mli ŋmɛlɛtswai anaa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ, Yitso lɛ teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ hejɔɔmɔ mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. ni okɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ atsu nii ni okɛwo ŋmeii heei yɛ be mli ni la bɛ po lɛ.

english: Why do insects quickly destroy my maize grains when I stack and store them in my crib?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mibua amɛnaa ni mikɛto ŋmãa ko mli lɛ?

english: If maize is harvested before the grains are fully dried in the field, trapped moisture creates a warm, humid environment in the stack. This attracts pests like weevils, which lay eggs inside the soft grains and eat them from the inside.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmãa dani dumɔwui lɛ gĩ kwraa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa ŋmãa lɛ mli. Enɛ gbalaa kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii, ni amɛwoɔ amɛwui yɛ dumɔwui bibii lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛmli.

english: Is it safe to stack my harvested cocoa pods on the ground for a few days before breaking them open?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oookɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ awo shikpɔŋ gbii fioo komɛi dani amɛtswa?

english: Yes, leaving freshly harvested cocoa pods in small piles for two to four days before cracking them actually helps the sugar inside the white pulp sweeten, which improves the final fermentation and chocolate flavor of the beans.
ga: Hɛɛ, ni ji kookoo ŋmeii ni akpa ehee lɛ ni ashɛrɛɔ ashwieɔ. yɛ ŋtayaa bibioo mli Ehiɔ shi gbii enyɔ kɛyashi ejwɛ dani efoɔ diɛŋtsɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni sugar ni yɔɔ loo yɛŋ lɛ mli lɛ afee nɔ ni ŋɔɔ waa. Enɛ haa naagbee ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsokolate ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves compete fiercely for limited soil food, water, and sunlight. The plants stretch upward to search for sun instead of spending energy on growing thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tse lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la ni faaa lɛ. Tsei baajie amɛhe kpo koni amɛtao hulu lɛ, ni no najiaŋ lɛ, amɛbaafite hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my main plantain tree produce very small bunches after many young suckers grow around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso titri lɛ feɔ kui bibii waa beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo ebɔle shishigbɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain stem shares its underground food reserve with all the suckers growing around it. When too many suckers are left attached, they drain energy away from the main mother tree, leaving it with less power to form big fruit bunches.
ga: Plantain tso lɛ kɛ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ jaa niyenii ni eyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ Ebaajie hewalɛ kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshwɛɔ ni akɛfeɔ aduawai akui wuji.

english: Why do the lower leaves and branches of my tree crops turn yellow and die as the tree gets taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛniji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: As a crop tree grows taller, its upper canopy develops dense leaves that block light from reaching the bottom. The tree naturally stops feeding the dark lower branches because they can no longer absorb sunlight to produce food.
ga: Beni tso lɛ daa lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni mli eyi obɔ ni tsiɔ la naa koni ekashɛ shishigbɛ. Tso lɛ kpaɔ eshishigbɛ niji ni yɔɔ ediŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ejaakɛ enyɛɛɛ eŋɔ hulu la ni ekɛfee niyenii dɔŋŋ.

english: Dropping leaves is a natural survival defense for cassava. When water is scarce, the plant intentionally sheds its leaves to stop losing moisture through evaporation, keeping its underground root alive until the rains come back.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ŋmei he. Beni nu faaa lɛ Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkpa ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Koni akɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers keep falling off without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat or a sudden lack of water and soil nutrients like nitrogen. The plant drops flowers to save its own life rather than spending precious energy on growing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ trukaa. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔii ashwãa koni amɛkɛhere amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala yiwala. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ ni jara wa kɛdu aduawai

english: How can I tell by looking at my cocoa pods that they are ripe enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛ mikwɛ mi-kookoo lɛ mli akɛ eshɛ bɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: When cocoa pods ripen, the pod husk changes color from green or red to a bright yellow or orange. Additionally, when you gently tap a ripe pod, it makes a hollow sound because the beans inside have detached slightly from the inner wall.
ga: Kɛji kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Kɛfata he lɛ, kɛ́ otswa pod lɛ blɛoo lɛ, efeɔ gbee ko ni mli ewo muji. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ etse amɛhe fioo kɛjɛ mligbɛ gbogboi lɛ ahe.

english: What is this thing called 'fertilizer,' and how does it actually help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘fertilizer’ nɛɛ ni te eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ jogbaŋŋ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer is like food for your soil and plants. Just like human beings need good food to grow strong, fertilizer adds essential nutrients back into the soil so your crops can produce bigger leaves, stronger roots, and a much better harvest.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tamɔ niyenii kɛha oshikpɔŋ kɛ tsei. Taakɛ niyenii kpakpa he hiaa adesai koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo baai wuji. Shishifãi lɛ mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Ni kpamɔ lɛ hu hi kwraa fe no.

english: How do I know if my crops are hungry and need fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli?

english: When crops lack plant food, their leaves often turn pale yellow instead of deep green, they grow very slowly, and they produce small or weak fruits. Healthy, well-fed crops grow quickly with thick, dark green leaves.
ga: Kɛ tsei bɛ tsei niyenii lɛ Bei pii lɛ ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Amɛdaraa blɛoo waa. ni amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii loo ni yɔɔ blɛoo Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ayeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya kɛ baai ni mli tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What is the difference between natural animal manure and store-bought chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Animal manure improves the overall health of the soil and releases nutrients slowly over a long time, while store-bought chemical fertilizer gives plants a quick, powerful dose of specific nutrients to boost their growth fast.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ fɛɛ yaa hiɛ ni ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa lɛ fiofio yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli, yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni aheɔ yɛ shwapoi amli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ oya ni haa amɛdaraa oya.

english: People keep talking about 'improved seeds'—what are they and why should I buy them instead of keeping seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mɛi wieɔ ‘Dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ’ lɛ ahe be fɛɛ be. Mɛni ji amɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Improved seeds are special seeds selected and tested by plant scientists to produce higher yields, resist common crop diseases, and survive bad weather better than traditional seeds saved from previous harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji dumɔwui krɛdɛɛi ni tsei ahe nilelɔi halaa ni amɛkaa amɛkwɛɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ tsei ahe helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa amli jogbaŋŋ fe blema dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do some plants on my farm grow very tall and healthy while others right next to them stay small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa waa lɛ? yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Crops grow unevenly when some spots in the farm have richer soil, more water, or less shade, or if pests and diseases attack certain plants more than others.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛ́ hei komɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ, nu babaoo, loo hulutsoo be faaa. Aloo kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai Tutuaa tsei komɛi fe ekrokomɛi.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow and wilting early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ?

english: Leaves usually turn yellow early when the plant is not getting enough nutrients from the soil, is suffering from lack of water, or has tiny pests attacking its leaves and roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya kɛji tsei lɛ naaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu efo amɛmli, loo kooloi bibii ebote mli. Etutuaa baai kɛ shishifãi

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Most crops show clear signs when mature: grains turn hard and dry, leaves change from green to brown, and fruits reach their full size and color. Harvesting too early gives you light, undeveloped crops, while waiting too long causes them to rot or get eaten by pests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo baajie okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ: Dumɔwui lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ. Baai lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli kɛyaa asarasu. ni aduawai lɛ baashɛ amɛdalɛ kɛ amɛhe su fɛɛ he. Kɛ́ okpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha okɛ ohe awo mli ni obɛ shweremɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ amɛmɛ be babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛgboi loo tsɛŋemɔ helai baaye amɛ.

english: Should I harvest crops as soon as they look mature and healthy, or should I wait until every single plant on the farm is ready?
ga: Esa akɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji amɛfee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyi obɔ kɛ hewalɛ pɛ. Aloo esa akɛ mamɛ ni tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ afee klalo?

english: It is best to harvest healthy, mature plants as soon as they are ready. Leaving ripe crops in the field while waiting for slower plants exposes your best food to rain, insects, and birds.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni edara lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛfee klalo. Kɛ́ oshi ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be mli ni omɛɔ ni tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ lɛ, ebaaha oná niyenii ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ nugbɔ, kooloi bibii, kɛ okpoi amli.

english: Why is it dangerous to let weeds grow close to my young crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mahã jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the water, sunshine, and soil food that your young crops need to grow. If you leave weeds in your farm, your crops will stay small and starved.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni he hiaa onibii bibii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ mli. Kɛji oshi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee bibii ni hɔmɔ baaye bo.

english: What does it mean when someone says a crop is 'thriving,' and how can I get my whole farm to look that way?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni mɛi kɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii miikwɛ̃ lɛ tsɔɔ? ‘Eshwereɔ’ ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ afee nakai?

english: A crop is thriving when it looks vibrant, dark green, bushy, and free from diseases or insect damage. You achieve this by planting improved seeds, keeping weeds away, and feeding the soil with proper fertilizer.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ omanye kɛji amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ wala, amɛji eŋɔli, amɛji jwɛi, ni helai loo kooloi fiteee amɛ. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ooodu, jwɛi ni ooojie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni oooha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato leaves curl during peak heat to reduce their surface area and slow down water loss, which is a natural way the plant protects itself from drying out under strong sunlight.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa be mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi he ni nu lɛ fiteɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and dry out when the sun becomes too intense?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni hulu lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excessive heat and direct sunlight burn the delicate leaf tissues and dry up soil moisture rapidly, breaking down chlorophyll in the leaves and causing them to turn yellow and wither.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baa lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni egbiɔ sũ mli nu lɛ oya. Efiteɔ klorofil ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni ehaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll tightly into tubes during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves inward to trap humidity close to the leaf surface and reduce exposure to the hot air, helping the crop conserve water until the next rain.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛmɔmɔ nu ni bɛŋkɛ baa lɛ hiɛ lɛ ni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɔ amɛhiɛɔ nu mli kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ ni baa lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my young vegetable plants with dried grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, shields the ground from hot direct sunlight, keeps the soil cool and moist for the roots, and prevents weed growth.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni shwereɔ lɛ naa

english: How will growing my vegetables in a greenhouse help them perform better than in the open field?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔ mli?
