english: A greenhouse creates a controlled space that protects crops from extreme heat, heavy downpours, and destructive pests, allowing plants to grow faster and yield higher-quality produce.
ga: Greenhouses feɔ he ko ni akudɔɔ ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will it not be too hot inside a plastic greenhouse structure for me to grow vegetables in our climate?
ga: Ani edɔɔɔ tsɔ yɛ plastic greenhouse mli kɛha aduawai adumɔ yɛ wɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ mli?

english: Greenhouses designed for hot regions use shade netting and ventilation gaps to regulate temperature and humidity, creating a mild environment that protects crops from direct sun burn.
ga: Greenhouses ni afee aha hei ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ shade netting kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ŋmeii tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkudɔ hulutsoo kɛ latsaa. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli jɔ ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni shãa amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he lɛ baa.

english: Can I successfully grow vegetables like pepper and spinach in small containers around my home?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu aduawai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsɛnsii bibii amli. Ani ebaanyɛ ebɔle shia lɛ he?

english: Yes, growing crops in containers or sacks at home allows you to control soil quality and watering easily, giving vegetables the right balance of sunlight and moisture in limited spaces.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni oookwɛ yɛ tsɛnsii loo kotokui amli yɛ shia lɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ nu ni oooha lɛ nɔ mlɛo. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ naa hulu la kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ husu.

english: Why do I need to shade my nursery beds with palm fronds before the seeds sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ ŋmei tsei aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Shading seedbeds shields fragile seeds and young shoots from intense sun heat and heavy raindrops, giving seedlings a safe, moist environment to establish strong roots.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ asa lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ buɔ dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Ha dumɔwui lɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, ni efɔ koni amɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: When crops experience severe heat stress or lack sufficient water, they drop their blossoms as a survival response to conserve moisture and energy.
ga: Kɛ tsei kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kpe loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ amɛhe lɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ gbeeɔ shi akɛ wala yibiiwoo hetoo koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why are my vegetable seedlings growing very tall and thin instead of thick and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ miida waa ni amɛmiifee mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Seedlings grow tall and skinny when they do not receive enough direct sunlight, as they stretch rapidly toward the light source to meet their energy needs.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛji amɛnaaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã oya kɛya he ni kane lɛ jɛɔ lɛ koni amɛtsu amɛ hewalɛ he hiamɔ nii ahe nii.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up like small tubes during the hot hours of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun, which helps the plant conserve water and survive intense heat during the middle of the day.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ baaye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛbu nu he ni amɛjo dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ naa foi.

english: Why do my vegetable plants look limp and wilted by midday even if the ground was moist in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ leebi po

english: During peak sun hours, crops lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it up from the ground, causing temporary wilting until temperatures drop in the evening.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off without producing any fruits during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants, forcing them to shed their flowers to conserve energy and moisture instead of spending resources on growing new fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa chili tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai heei

english: Is it true that spraying pesticides on my crops in the hot afternoon sun can burn their leaves?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã?

english: Yes, spraying during hot hours causes liquid droplets on leaves to evaporate quickly or act like small magnifying glasses, which can scorch the leaves and weaken the crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha nu ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ atsɔ oya loo efee tamɔ glase bibioo ko ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã baai ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii agbɔjɔ.

english: When is the best time of day for me to apply fertilizer so my crops absorb it properly?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Applying fertilizer early in the morning allows the soil moisture to dissolve the nutrients so plant roots can absorb them before midday heat dries out the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ ni ehaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ dani shwane mli latsaa lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi.

english: Why is it better for me to weed around my crops in the early morning rather than late in the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mafo jwɛi yɛ he lɛ? Leebi ŋmɔshi nibii Yɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ leebi lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Weeding early in the morning prevents exposed soil from losing too much moisture in the afternoon heat and avoids disturbing crop roots when they are already stressed by direct sunlight.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ ni hulu lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ akafite ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ shwane latsaa be mli. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei shishifãi ni haoɔ amɛhe lɛ ahe kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ miigba amɛnaa.

english: Does harvesting my tomatoes early in the morning keep them fresh longer than picking them in the afternoon?
ga: Ani tomato ni oootsi leebi lɛ baaha ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ fe bɔ ni oootsi shwane mli lɛ?

english: Yes, crops harvested early in the morning are cool and full of water absorbed overnight, which helps them stay firm and last longer before spoiling compared to warm afternoon harvests.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni akpa leebi lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu ni ajie nyɔɔŋ kome mli lɛ eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ dani egboɔ. Kɛ akɛto ŋmaakpamɔ ni afeɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ he lɛ he

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die if I do not plant shade crops like plantain next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ gbo kɛji miduuu tso ko ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantain yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight; fast-growing plantains provide vital shade and keep the microclimate cool and moist for the cocoa to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ bibioo ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ koni kookoo lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why does my cassava crop survive long dry spells much better than my cabbage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ hi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ fe mi-cabbage lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep root systems and tough foliage designed to store moisture and endure high heat, whereas leafy vegetables have shallow roots and soft leaves that dry out quickly in the sun.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni mli wa ni afee koni amɛhiɛ fɛ̃i mli ni amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. yɛ be mli ni aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛhe lɛ, amɛgbiɔ oya.

english: Why do seeds take longer to sprout if I plant them in dry, hot soil during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds need cool, consistent moisture to trigger germination; extreme heat and dry soil keep the seed dormant to prevent the young sprout from burning upon emerging.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ fɛ̃i, fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ daa koni ewo amɛkwɛ̃mɔ he hewalɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ akashã kɛji amɛje kpo.

english: How do I know it is the right time to plant my maize when the rainy season starts?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni sa ni esa akɛ odu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: You should wait until the soil stays consistently moist for a few days after a heavy rain. Planting during the very first light rain is risky because if a dry spell follows, your seeds will dry up in the soil and fail to grow.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii fioo komɛi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Abuɔ dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli akɛ eji oshara Ejaakɛ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why is it important to leave proper space between my cassava stems when planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi gbɛ ni sa yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ adu lɛ?

english: Giving cassava plants enough distance allows their underground roots room to expand into large, heavy tubers. If planted too close together, their leaves fight for sunlight and their roots fight for nutrients, resulting in small, thin yields.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ha ŋmei tsei lɛ, ehaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni efeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baai lɛ kɛ hulu la he akaŋ ni shishifãi lɛ hu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni anáa lɛ faaa ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Leaf curling in peak heat is the plant's natural self-defense mechanism to save water. By reducing the leaf surface area exposed to direct sun, the plant slows down water loss until the air cools in the evening.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbuɔ nu he. Kɛtsɔ baai ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei baaha nu ni baafite lɛ asɛɛ afo kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. When nitrogen is scarce, the corn plant naturally moves the available nutrient from its older bottom leaves up to feed the new growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nitrogen faaa lɛ, Abele tsei lɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I leave cleared grass to rot on my land instead of burning it before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha jwɛi ni he tse lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mashã lɛ dani madu?

english: Leaving cleared grass to decompose creates a layer of organic mulch. This layer keeps the soil cool, traps rainwater in the ground for longer periods, and gradually breaks down into rich food for your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ jwɛi lɛ gbɛ ni efite lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nugbɔ nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ, ni fiofio lɛ, efoɔ mli ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni jara wa kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off unpollinated when day temperatures get too high or when the plant lacks sufficient water. Extreme heat stresses the plant, causing it to shed flowers to save energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni pollination bɛ mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do some of my corn seeds sprout within four days while others in the same row take much longer or fail completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbii ejwɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu kwɛɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɛkɛ sɛɛkuu nɛɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ ani eheɔ be babaoo loo eji nɔ ni etɔ̃tɔ̃ kwraa?

english: Seeds sprout based on how deep they were planted and how much soil moisture reached them. Seeds buried too deep struggle to push up through the soil, while seeds planted too shallow can dry out or get damaged by insects.
ga: Dumɔwui akwɛ̃mɔ damɔ dumɔ mlibotemɔ kɛ sũ mli nu ni shɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni afu amɛ tsɔ lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbi loo kooloi bibii baanyɛ afite amɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting shoots in the storage barn even without soil or water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ loo nu bɛ jɛmɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers have an internal natural clock. After a resting period following harvest, internal biological changes force the tuber to use its stored water and nutrients to shoot out new buds in preparation for the next growing season.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa yɛ mli. Yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ hejɔɔmɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli tsakemɔi nyɛɔ bulb lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii heei ni ekɛsaa ehe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster than my crop seeds after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are native to the local environment and extremely resilient. They naturally react faster to moisture and absorb soil nutrients more aggressively than cultivated crops, allowing them to shoot up quickly.
ga: Jwɛi ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni jɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli, ni amɛhe wa waa. Amɛfeɔ amɛnii yɛ adebɔɔ naa oya kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ba, ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods after all the giant forest trees around my farm are cut down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ beni afo tsei wuji ni ebɔle miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Young and maturing cocoa trees thrive best under moderate shade. Without larger trees to filter the intense sunlight, direct heat scorches the cocoa leaves, dries out the surrounding soil, and causes stress that reduces pod yields.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii ni eda lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛji tsei wuji komɛi bɛ ni baatsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã kookoo baai lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ agbi ni ekɛ haomɔ ni haa pod yibiiwoo baa shi lɛ baa.

english: How should I position plantain suckers in the soil when planting so they grow strong and healthy?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ plantain tsei lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ midu koni amɛdara ni amɛná hewalɛ?

english: Plantain suckers should be planted upright in deep, well-dug holes mixed with fertile topsoil. Placing them properly ensures the root system anchors well to support heavy bunches and withstand strong winds.
ga: Esa akɛ adu plantain tsei ni ja lɛ yɛ bu ni mli kwɔ ni atsa jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii babaoo efutu mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛto he jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛfi ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ ni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young plantain plants turning yellow instead of rich green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ midumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often indicate that the plantain lacks nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that the soil is waterlogged. Adding organic manure and ensuring proper drainage helps restore healthy leaf color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ plantain lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: Select tall 'sword suckers' that have narrow, spear-like leaves and thick bases. These suckers grow faster, produce bigger bunches, and resist diseases better than water suckers with broad leaves.
ga: Halamɔ ‘klante tsei’ kakadaŋŋ agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli tse. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ daa oya, amɛfeɔ kui wuji, ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe fe nu mli tsei ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Should I cut off the dry leaves hanging around my plantain stems?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni egbi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko? Ani plantain tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjeɔ kpo?

english: Yes, cutting off dead or diseased leaves prevents pests and fungal diseases from spreading. It also improves airflow around the plants and allows sunlight to reach lower crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai ni egboi loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ hu yaa hiɛ. tsei ni eha hulu la lɛ shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe

english: Why do farmers plant plantains alongside young cocoa seedlings in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa needs in its first few years.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: What other food crops can I grow between my plantains during the first year?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii manyɛ madu yɛ mi plantain tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli?

english: You can intercrop short-term plants like cassava, maize, or legumes between plantain rows. This maximizes your land, suppresses weeds, and provides early harvest while the plantains are still growing.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu be kukuoo mli nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ baaha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo, ebaajie jwɛi lɛ, ni ebaaha okpa mra be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ miida lolo lɛ.

english: Why is it helpful to cover the soil around plantain roots with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ akɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egboi baawo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle plantain shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mulching the soil with dry crop leaves retains moisture during dry spells, keeps the roots cool, stops weeds from taking over, and slowly rots into nutrient-rich soil food.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ahe baai ni egbi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ akahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye nɔ ni amɛfite fiofio koni amɛkɛha shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Is goat manure good for my crop fields, and how should I apply it?
ga: Ani too ŋmei hi kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ? Ni te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli?

english: Goat manure is an excellent natural fertilizer high in nutrients. It should be dried or composted before putting it around crops so that it does not generate too much heat and damage plant roots.
ga: Too ŋmei ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli. Esa akɛ agbi loo afee amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dani akɛwo tsei ahe koni amɛkadɔ fe nine ni amɛkafite tsei lɛ ashishifãi.

english: Can I let my goats roam freely in my plantain farm to eat weeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha mitooi lɛ ayashara shi yɛ mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni amɛye jwɛi?

english: It is risky to let goats roam free because they will eat young plantain leaves and peel the bark off stems. Instead, keep them tethered or collect fresh weeds to feed them in a pen.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ tooi ni amɛnyiɛ amɛhe lɛ, eyɛ oshara ejaakɛ amɛyeɔ plantain baai bibii ni amɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsɔi lɛ. Mohu ɔ, mo fĩ mɛ aloo o bua jwɛi ehehi a nya konɛ e wa ngɛ ngmɔ ɔ mi.

english: How does keeping goats alongside growing crops help reduce my farming expenses?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tooi akwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shika ni akɛkwɛɔ tooi lɛ aba shi?

english: Goats feed on farm weeds and crop leftovers, saving you labor costs on weeding. In return, their manure provides free rich fertilizer, reducing the need to purchase expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Tooi yeɔ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔwoo toɔ jwɛi shwiemɔ mli. Yɛ najiaŋ lɛ, amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni aheee nɔ ko. Enɛ haa ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to burn the cleared bushes on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mashã jwɛi ni ajie yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli dani madu lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic material in the soil that holds moisture and nutrients. Over time, burning kills beneficial soil organisms and leaves your land dry and weak, leading to lower crop yields.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni yɔɔ sũ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ toɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Shãa gbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. ni eha oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni egbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my crops even when my crops are already taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ fe jwɛi lɛ momo?

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizer, and essential nutrients from the soil underneath, even if they look small. Keeping your field clean ensures all the food in the soil goes directly into growing your crops.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ sũ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eji bibioo moŋ Oŋmɔji lɛ amli ni oooha ehe atse lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why should I leave measured space between my seeds instead of planting many together in one place?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu babaoo? Dumɔwui ni abua naa yɛ he kome

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing gives each plant enough root room and air to grow strong and produce a bigger harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ teŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa shishifãi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and a heavy bunch makes the stalk top-heavy. Supporting your bearing trees with sturdy wooden forks or props prevents strong winds from breaking or uprooting them.
ga: Plantain lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ tsii yɛ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ okɛ fɔk loo tso ni wa fĩ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekakumɔ loo ejie amɛ.

english: What is eating the inner leaves of my young maize plants and leaving small holes behind?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ ni eshiɔ bu bibii yɛ sɛɛ?

english: That damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworms hiding inside the center of the plant. Inspecting your field early and spraying recommended pest controls directly into the leaf funnel will protect your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ baa. Odumɔi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni akɛbuɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ahe ŋaa lɛ ni oooshwie baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads in cool, overly wet, and dark farms. Pruning excess tree branches lets in sunlight and air to keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fuŋɔ ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔji ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni edɔ tsɔ, ni ŋmɔ tso niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni eha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba koni eha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies that transmit plant viruses. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or appropriate sprays stops the damage from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ neem fɔ loo spray ni sa nɔ lɛ obaanyɛ otsi nɔ ni efite lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my cassava roots become soft and rot inside the ground during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava root rot happens when water gathers and sits around the tubers in heavy soil. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away safely from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu shwie shi ni ebɔle tuber lɛ he yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves show that your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an important food for growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea when the crops are young helps them stay green and grow large ears.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-abele lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli beni amɛji bibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛnáa toii wuji.

english: Should I pour my fertilizer directly against the main stem of my plant?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafɔse ŋmɔshi nibii awo mitso lɛ shishigbɛ titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, placing fertilizer right against the stem can burn and damage the plant tissues. Always place the fertilizer a few inches away in a circle or line so the outer roots can safely absorb it.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ ashã ni efite. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo he ko ni kɛ bo teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi yɛ kooyigbɛ loo line mli bɔni afee ni kponɔgbɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow roots and delicate leaves that easily burn in direct heat. They need temporary shade crops like plantains around them to trap moisture and shield them from harsh sunlight while their roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Yes, but you must keep enough distance between them. Cassava provides quick food and temporary shade, but its roots compete aggressively for soil nutrients and water if planted too close to young cocoa.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi ehe miihia ni okɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ahi amɛteŋ. Cassava ji niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ oya kɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo. Shi amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo bibii tsɔ

english: How do I know if my farm land has good soil for growing cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ?

english: Good cocoa soil is deep, dark, and crumbles easily in your hand. It must hold moisture well without becoming waterlogged, as stagnant water rots the tree roots.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli kwɔ, eyɛ ediŋ, ni efoɔ oya yɛ nine mli. Esa akɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ, shi jeee ni nu ehi mli ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is missing essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that heavy rains have soaked the ground so much that the roots are suffocating and cannot absorb food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe niyenii.

english: Curling is a natural defense behavior where the plant reduces its leaf surface area to trap moisture and prevent water from evaporating too quickly in severe heat.
ga: Oyitsɔi ni ooofee lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli subaŋ ko ni buɔ mɔ he. Tsei lɛ baa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shi koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya tsɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers fall off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the tree experiences extreme heat, water stress, or a shortage of tiny pollinating insects like midges, which rely on moist decaying leaves under the trees to survive.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ shɛ latsaa ni naa wa he. nu mli haomɔ loo ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni damɔ tsei ashishi baai ni mli ewo fɔ ni egboɔ lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and hard while still on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛhe wa be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in wet, dark conditions. Opening up the farm canopy to let in light and fresh air stops the fungus from thriving.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni efɔ kɛ duŋ. Kɛ́ agbele ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋwɛitsu lɛ koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aba lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do weeds around my crop make them grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi babaoo ebɔle he lɛ? Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ blɛoo nɛkɛ?

english: Weeds aggressively steal sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients directly from your crop's root zone, effectively starving your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii titri lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from a mature cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata kookoo tso ni eda lɛ he lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary foliage so the tree can focus its energy and nutrients directly on producing large, healthy cocoa pods rather than excess leaves.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa amɛhewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona baai ni fa fe nine

english: How can I tell when cocoa pods are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Ripe pods change color from green or deep red to a bright yellow or orange, and they give off a hollow sound when gently tapped with your knuckles.
ga: Pods ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ su kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse. Ni efeɔ gbɛɛmɔ ko ni mli ewo muji kɛ́ okɛ onine tswa lɛ fioo.

english: Why do my harvested plantains spoil and rot so quickly after I cut them from the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ ni egboɔ oya beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once cut, plantains release a natural gas called ethylene that speeds up ripening. In warm weather, this gas makes the fruit soften and spoil rapidly if left unhandled or stored in hot, enclosed spaces.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo lɛ, plantains lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene ni haa ekwɛ̃ɔ oya. yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Gas nɛɛ haa aduawai lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛfiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ ni akɛtsuuu nii loo akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni afo he.

english: Why do my plantain trees give smaller bunches when many small shoots grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ haa ŋmeii bibii be mli ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛi babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso wulu lɛ he.

english: The small shoots, called suckers, steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from the main tree. Removing extra suckers leaves more energy for the main stem to grow large, healthy bunches.
ga: Tso bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛdaraa ni edaa ni ehaa ehe waa.

english: What can I do to keep my excess plantains from going to waste when I cannot sell them all at once?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni plantains krokomɛi ni miyɔɔ lɛ akafite be mli ni minyɛɛɛ mahɔ̃ɔ fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: You can process fresh plantains into long-lasting products like plantain flour or dried chips. This preserves the harvest and allows you to sell at a higher price when fresh plantains are scarce.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ plantains heei afee nibii ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ plantain ashikishaŋ loo ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi ni ehaa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ kɛ́ dumɔwui heei ni adu lɛ faaa.

english: How can I tell if my plantain tree is healthy enough to start producing fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-plantains lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: A healthy plantain tree usually produces around 25 to 30 large green leaves before sending out its central flower trunk, which typically happens around 8 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ woɔ baai agboi 25 kɛyashi 30 dani amɛtsuɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa aaafee nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my plantain plants turning yellow and dry before the fruit is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani aduawai lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are often a sign that the plant lacks important soil nutrients like nitrogen or potassium, or that the roots are not getting enough water during dry spells.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ sũ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium. aloo shishifãi lɛ anine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and open up space around my young crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ ni magbele he ni mitsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with young crops for water and nutrients in the soil. Clearing them opens up sunlight and air movement, which young plants need to make food and grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ yaa. Esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ afee niyenii ni amɛdara waa.

english: How can I stop my plantains from getting bruised and damaged when carrying them from my farm to the village market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi plantains lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkafite beni mikɛ amɛ yaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa akrowa lɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Transporting crops in padded baskets or stacked wooden crates keeps bunches from crushing each other. Keeping them covered away from direct sunlight during transit also prevents heat damage.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ awoɔ tsɛnsii ni akɛ tsɔi ewo mli loo adekai ni ato mli lɛ amli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akatswa amɛhe. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ kpo yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ dɔlɛ ni efiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over when the heavy fruit bunches appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ miigbee shi beni aduawai babaoo jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and do not grip deep into the soil. As the bunch gets heavy, wind or weight can easily pull the plant down, so supporting the stem with bamboo poles or wooden stakes is necessary.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛshɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji kuu lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ loo tsiimɔ baanyɛ agbala tsei kɛba shi mlɛo. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ ŋmei loo tsei ni akɛfee ŋmei afi tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How does planting broad-leaf crops like plantain help the soil on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ baai babaoo tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The wide leaves of plantains act like an umbrella, protecting the topsoil from being washed away by heavy rains and keeping the soil cool and moist for other nearby plants.
ga: Plantain baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ebuɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie nɔ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa tsei krokomɛi feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. bɛŋkɛ

english: What is a good, reliable crop for a young person starting a small farm in Ghana to grow for quick income?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛha oblahii kɛ oblayei ni jeɔ ŋmɔ bibioo ko shishi yɛ Ghana koni amɛdu koni amɛná shika oya?

english: Plantains and quick-growing vegetables like okra or peppers are good starting crops because they suit the local soil, require standard management, and are always in high demand at local markets.
ga: Plantains kɛ aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ okra loo peppers ji shishijee tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛhi kɛha maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔji. Ehe miihia ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ataoɔ amɛ waa yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under full sunlight. They need temporary shade trees or tall crops like plantains to shelter them, preserve moisture, and keep them cool while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii kakadaji tamɔ plantains kɛha wɔɔhe. Ha hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ahi shi be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown and soft right on the tree during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in excessive moisture and humidity. It spreads quickly when cocoa trees are planted too close together or when weed growth prevents fresh air from circulating through the farm.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be ni fe nine mli. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ adu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. aloo be mli ni jwɛi ni miida lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow even though it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? He ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing of lower maize leaves is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize requires heavy amounts of nitrogen to maintain green leaves and grow sturdy stems, so yellow leaves mean the soil nutrients have been exhausted.
ga: Abɛi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni eha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli kɛ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ etee.

english: Why does my maize farm produce small cobs with missing grains on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ni dumɔwui komɛi fataaa he?

english: Missing grains on a maize cob happen when pollination fails. High heat or dry winds can dry out the maize silks before pollen can fertilize every seed site, leaving gaps where corn kernels should grow.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi baanyɛ aha ŋmãa siliki lɛ agbi dani pollen lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwu lɛ hei fɛɛ afee ŋmãa. Enɛ haa he ko baa ni esa akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small and thin even after growing for over a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ waa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nɔ ni fe afi edu amɛ moŋ?

english: Cassava roots fail to swell if the soil is too hard and compacted, or if there is too much nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is too high, the plant spends all its energy growing bush leaves instead of swelling its roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ ni ebɔle ehe. aloo nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji nitrogen lɛ fa tsɔ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Yam tubers rot underground when water collects around the roots due to poor drainage in heavy clay soil. Stagnant water creates an environment where soil fungi and rot-causing bacteria multiply and attack the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shihilɛ ko baa ni sũ mli ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛtutua ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do the stems of my cassava plants develop black spots and drop leaves during heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ anɔ ŋmeii diji kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Damp and humid conditions during the rainy season allow cassava bacterial blight and fungal spores to spread quickly across leaves and stems, causing leaf drop and stem dieback.
ga: Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni baa yɛ baa lɛ mli kɛ cassava fungal spores lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa baai lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli oya. Enɛ haa baai lɛ laajeɔ ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ gboɔ.

english: Why do my plantain plants easily fall over during strong rains and wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and top-heavy stems filled with water. If they are planted too shallowly or are carrying heavy fruit bunches without supportive wooden props, strong winds will easily uproot them.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ shishifã ni tsii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo ehiɛ aduawai ni tsii ni tso bɛ he Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ajie shishifãi lɛ oya.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, mites, or whiteflies that feed on the underside of young leaves and transmit viruses that distort plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, mites, loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Eyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ ni ekɛ helai ni haa tsei lɛ adalɛ fiteɔ lɛ haa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or when there is an imbalance of nutrients, preventing the flower from successfully setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejaaa loo niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ejaaa Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato fɔfɔi nyɛŋ awo yibii.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant steals nutrients from its older, lower leaves to keep the young top leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli koni eha baai bibii ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ adara.

english: When cassava is planted too close, the plants compete for sunlight and stretch upwards instead of spreading out and growing large tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tso lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ ni ekɛ ehe aaawo mli moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshwa ni ekwɛ ŋmei wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when the soil dries out completely, preventing the flowers from getting pollinated and forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafee pollination ni amɛkawo yibii.

english: Why is it harmful if I put chemical fertilizer right against the stem of my maize plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ fata mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the plant's skin and roots. It should be placed a few inches away in the soil so the roots can safely suck up the nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ hewolo kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ amɛ ato he ko ni kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi 2-3 koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do armyworms hide inside the center funnel of my young maize plants during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe ewoɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Armyworms dislike direct sunlight and extreme heat, so they crawl deep into the shaded, moist center whorl of the maize plant to feed safely during the day.
ga: Asraafoi amli ŋmeii sumɔɔɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛkpãa kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋtayaa ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye nii shweshweeshwe yɛ gbi lɛ mli.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my main crop improve my soil?
ga: Te cowpea ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, which means their roots work with helpful soil microbes to trap nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil to feed surrounding crops.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛjie kɛya sũ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot much faster if I leave them sitting under the direct sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight cooks the inside of harvested yams and makes them lose water rapidly, creating ideal warm and moist conditions for rot-causing fungi to break them down.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha nu lɛ afite oya. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mli edɔɔ, ni mli edɔ baa koni ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ akumɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl upward during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural way of protecting itself from losing too much water; by curling, less leaf surface area is exposed to direct heat and strong winds.
ga: Baai ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso ko tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni nu babaoo akafite. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ, baa lɛ hiɛ he ni hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baaa lɛ tsɔ.

english: Why does Striga weed choke my cereal crops even when I clear the weeds around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ miigba mi ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa lɛ? Beni mijie jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ po sɛɛ.

english: Striga is a parasitic weed that attaches its own roots directly to the roots of maize or sorghum underground, stealing food and water before it even emerges above the soil.
ga: Striga ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni ekɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpãa ŋmãa loo ŋmãa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Koni eju niyenii kɛ nu dani eje kpo po.

english: Why shouldn't I plant all my maize seeds right next to each other in one big pile?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ yɛ ŋmãa agbo kome mli lɛ?

english: Crops need personal space to feed properly. Planting seeds too close causes them to fight for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and very small harvests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ he miihia amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why do some farmers plant a small section of cassava every week instead of planting everything on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmãa fioo ko daa otsi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadu nɔ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting in stages spreads out your harvest over time. This ensures you always have fresh cassava for your family or to sell at the market across several months, rather than everything maturing and risking spoilage all at once.
ga: Dumɔ ni ooodu yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ baagbɛ okpamɔ lɛ eshwa yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmãa hee kɛha oweku loo jara ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ nyɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ahoɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara akɛ ebaafite fɛɛ shikome lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my stored maize grains get insects and spoil after just a few weeks in my storage room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli kooloi yɔɔ ni egboɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grain holds hidden moisture that attracts bugs and mold. Drying your grains completely in the sun before storing them in clean, airtight containers keeps them safe and dry for many months.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa ehee lɛ hiɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni gbalaa kooloi kɛ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ ogbala odumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulu mli dani okɛwo tsɛnsi ko ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe ni amɛgbi nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop growing well when large trees block the sunlight from reaching them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ jogbaŋŋ beni tsei wuji tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ ehe lɛ?

english: Crops use direct sunlight as fuel to make their own food. Without enough sunlight, pepper plants grow tall and thin but produce very few flowers and peppers.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tsofa ni amɛkɛfeɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii. Kɛji hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ bɛ Pepper tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ pepper fioo ko pɛ.

english: What happens to my soil if I grow yam on the exact same plot of land year after year without resting it?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop needs from the ground. Resting the land or rotating with crops like cowpeas puts good food back into the soil so future crops grow strong.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hejɔɔmɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ baaha niyenii kpakpa aba. Ku osɛɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Bɔni afee ni wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ waa

english: How does putting dried chicken manure around my plantain trees actually help them produce bigger fruit?
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te midumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii wuji amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: Manure acts like rich food for the soil. As rain breaks it down, it releases essential plant nutrients that the roots absorb, helping the trunk grow thick and support much larger, heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni jara wa kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛyaa tso lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa plantain tsei ni dara ni tsii babaoo lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my groundnuts so I don't pull them up too early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? koni akagbala ŋmeii lɛ oya tsɔ

english: Groundnuts signal maturity when the leaves begin to turn yellow and dry up. Opening a few test pods will reveal dark spots on the inner shell, showing the nuts are fully formed inside.
ga: Peanuts tsɔɔ dalɛ be mli ni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ. Test pod lɛ fã ko ni agbeleɔ lɛ jieɔ hei ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ yɛ mligbɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ kpo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ebɔi amɛhe kwraa yɛ mli.

english: Curling leaves are a crop's natural way of reducing surface area to prevent water loss during extreme heat. If the leaves recover by evening, the plant is managing, but if they stay limp, the soil needs water.
ga: Leaf curling ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ baa shi koni nu akafite yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji baai lɛ he wa yɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ Shi kɛji baai lɛ ji gbekɛbii lolo Shikpɔŋ lɛ hu he miihia nu.

english: Why do tiny caterpillars keep eating holes in my cabbage leaves, and where do they come from?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii sumɔɔ ni amɛye bu ni yɔɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ amli lɛ? Ni nɛgbɛ amɛjɛɔ?

english: Small moths lay tiny, nearly invisible eggs on the underside of cabbage leaves. When those eggs hatch into hungry caterpillars, they chew the leaves, which can be controlled by checking leaves early or spraying neem water.
ga: Kplukai bibii fɔɔ wɔji bibii. Shwɛ fioo ni anaaa amɛ yɛ kaabii baai lɛ ashishi. Kɛ́ nakai wɔji lɛ fɔ lɛ, amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ. Ebaaye baai lɛ. Abaanyɛ akudɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ baai lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ mra. loo okɛ neem nu afɔ nɔ

english: Why is it important for me to count and keep track of how many bags of cocoa I harvest every week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makane ni makwɛ kookoo kotokui enyiɛ ni mikpaa yɛ otsi mli lɛ?

english: Tracking your daily or weekly yields helps you see if your farm output is growing or dropping over time. It allows you to plan your farm expenses accurately and know if your care practices are actually working.
ga: Nibii ni afeɔ daa gbi loo otsi fɛɛ otsi lɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ baaye abua bo ni ona kɛji nibii ni afeɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ etee hiɛ loo eba shi yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni otoɔ oŋmɔ mli shika he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ ni oleɔ kɛji okwɛmɔ nifeemɔi lɛ miitsu nii diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and die when I clear all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct harsh sunlight overheats their tender leaves and dries out soil moisture quickly. Keeping shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains creates a cooler environment that protects cocoa seedlings during their first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha baai bibii lɛ adɔ fe nine ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: Pepper flowers often drop without producing fruit when the plant experiences heat stress or extreme dry weather. When it gets too hot, the plant sheds its flowers to save water and energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa. Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing leaves in a V-pattern usually mean your maize crop lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants use to make healthy green leaves, so applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tamɔ V lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛfee baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does putting dry grass around the base of my tomato plants help them stay healthy in dry hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, called mulching, acts like a blanket that blocks direct sunlight from hitting the ground. This keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating fast, allowing your plants to access moisture for much longer.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekatswa shikpɔŋ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight and soil food. This competition forces the plants to stretch upward to reach light instead of growing thick stems and big cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛná la. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves in full sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, increasing sunlight exposure and protecting the plant from soil-borne leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa lɛ ahe.

english: Why does grass growing close to my young crops make them look weak and stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ haa jwɛi lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds and grass have aggressive roots that steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your main crops get all the food they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when rain falls continuously for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater stays trapped in the soil for too long, it drowns the root system and encourages fungi to attack and rot the tubers before harvest.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ baafo nu mli ni ewo ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfite amɛ dani akpa.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants have ragged holes with dark green dust inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center leaf whorl during the day to feed on young leaves. Identifying this early allows you to spray recommended treatments before the central growing tip is destroyed.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baa teŋgbɛ ŋmeii amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baa bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ni oooyɔse mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ shwieɔ nɔ dani ŋwɛi ŋta ni yaa hiɛ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die during the day even when the soil has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ? Ani nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: This sudden wilting is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil disease that enters the roots and blocks the internal water tubes of the stem. Because water cannot travel up to the leaves, the plant wilts rapidly under sun heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni eboteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ mli nu paipii lɛ anaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu nyɛɛɛ aya baai lɛ anɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and burning in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, full sunlight during their first couple of years. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides a living canopy that shelters them from severe heat and retains soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli tamɔ plantains kɛ cocoa bibii lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and put up wooden stakes for my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni mikɛ tsei ama shi kɛha sweet potato wain tsei lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can capture maximum sunlight. When the leaves get plenty of light, the plant converts that solar energy into food, producing larger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Tsei tsakeɔ hulu hewalɛ amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji shwereɔ

english: This V-shaped yellowing is a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea around the crop during its early growing stage helps restore dark green, healthy leaves.
ga: Nɛkɛ su ni tamɔ V ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea wo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ shishijee be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by uneven watering which prevents the plant from absorbing calcium. Regular, consistent watering helps the plant absorb calcium and keeps the tomato fruit healthy.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ be fɛɛ be ni haaa amɛná calcium lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ calcium lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa tomato yibii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply chemical fertilizer directly against the main stem of my young plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ tsei bibii lɛ ashishifã titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Concentrated chemical fertilizer touching the stem can chemically burn the delicate skin and shallow roots. Placing fertilizer in a small ring a few inches away allows the roots to safely absorb the nutrients as rain dissolves them.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofa ko aba hewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli He ni jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ shweshweeshwe beni nugbɔ lɛ miiho lɛ.

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during prolonged dry spells to reduce water loss and survive the drought. Once the rains return, the plant quickly shoots out fresh leaves while the tubers underground remain safe.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛba nu ni fiteɔ lɛ shi ni ehi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baajie baai heei oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: If too many sucker shoots grow at once, they compete with the main plant for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Pruning extra suckers leaves more energy for the main plantain tree to produce big, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miida shikome lɛ, Nakai ŋmeii lɛ kɛ tso ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ehaa plantain titri lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ tsei niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my maize leaves have ragged holes in them with powdery waste inside the top funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii yɛ ŋwɛi ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the leaf whorl. Applying targeted bio-pesticides or neem extract into the center funnel early in the morning controls the caterpillars before they destroy the plant's growing point.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ wo gbɛjegbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi lɛ dani amɛfite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling inward and stopping new fruits from forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso kɛmiiya mli ni amɛmiikpa aduawai heei ni baa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or whiteflies transmitting plant viruses. Controlling these insects early keeps the leaves healthy and allows pepper pods to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ mli waa ni eyeɔ ebuaa pepper pods lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why does lowland rice grow much better when there is shallow standing water around the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ ebɔle ŋmãa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Shallow standing water smothers competing weeds that try to steal nutrients while providing the high, constant moisture level rice plants need to fill out heavy grain heads.
ga: Nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni damɔ shi lɛ hu baagbe jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ ni miitao amɛju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ. kɛ hulutsoo ni nɔ kwɔ ni yaa nɔ daa Ehe miihia ni akɛ dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii awo ŋmãa tsei amli ekoŋŋ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I put more chemical spray than the extension officer told me to use?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofai babaoo shwie nɔ fe bɔ ni tsofa ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛtsu nii lɛ?

english: Applying more than the recommended dosage can burn the leaves and stem, stunt plant growth, or even kill the crop completely. It also wastes money and can leave harmful residues on the harvested produce.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ni fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha baa kɛ shishifãi lɛ ashã. ehaa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi loo efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii po kwraa. Eji shika fitemɔ hu, ni ebaanyɛ eshi nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ nibii ni akpaa lɛ amli.

english: Why do insects keep destroying my farm even after I spray them with pest medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yaa nɔ amɛfiteɔ miŋmɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ efɔ nɔ moŋ.

english: Pests can survive if the chemical is mixed incorrectly, applied at the wrong time of day, or if the same pesticide is used repeatedly, which causes insects to build up resistance to the medicine.
ga: Kooloi baanyɛ ahi shi kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai futu mli yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ, akɛwo mli yɛ be ni esaaa mli, loo akɛ tsofa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii shii abɔ. ni haa kooloi bibii nyɛɔ amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ tsofa lɛ

english: Is it good to store my harvested grains inside airtight plastic drums?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ baawo plastic tsinsii ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli?

english: Storing grains in airtight drums is great for keeping insects out, but the grains must be completely dried first. If damp grains are sealed in a drum, heat and moisture will build up, causing mold and rotting.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ tsɛnsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ ji nɔ ko ni tsiɔ kooloi bibii anaa waa. Shi esa akɛ ŋmaa lɛ agbi kwraa klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛji akɛ atsĩ dumɔwui ni mli efɔ lɛ anaa yɛ tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ, Dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i baabua amɛhe naa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why does it take up to two years for tree crops like cocoa or citrus to start giving good fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei tamɔ kookoo loo citrus heɔ afii enyɔ dani amɛjeɔ yibii woɔ lɛ?

english: During the first two years, tree crops spend their energy establishing deep root systems and strong trunks. They need this foundation to absorb enough water and nutrients to support heavy yields later on.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛmaa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei akutsei ni wa. Shishitoo nɛɛ he miihia amɛ koni amɛnu nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛye amɛbua ŋmɔshi nibii wuji sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings wilt and die in the afternoon even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: Young plants lose water rapidly through their leaves during peak afternoon heat. If their roots are still small, they cannot draw groundwater fast enough to replace what was lost, causing heat stress and wilting.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ daraaa lolo lɛ Enyɛŋ ejie shikpɔŋ shishi nu oya bɔ ni sa ni ekɛto nɔ ni elaaje lɛ najiaŋ. Enɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very few leaves when planted close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛbaai fioo pɛ yɔɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they shade each other and fight for sunlight. The plants stretch upward quickly to reach the sun instead of growing thick stems and leaves.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Tsei lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ oya koni amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaana ŋmeii kɛ baai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when there is too much rain on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water fills up air spaces in the soil, suffocating the plant roots. Without air, roots cannot take up essential nutrients like nitrogen, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I pour fertilizer right at the base of my stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain salts that can draw moisture out of tender stems and roots, causing chemical burns. Fertilizer should be placed in a ring a short distance away from the stem where feeding roots can safely reach it.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli ŋmeii ni baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli. Nɔ ni kɛ tsofa shãa baa Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo lɛ mli. ni niyenii shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe lɛ

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my planted crops right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants with aggressive root systems naturally adapted to the local soil. They absorb moisture and plant food much faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ko ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni ekɛ ehe ewo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Amɛheɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛduɔ niyenii oya kwraa fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to germinate after I bury them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are buried too deep to reach oxygen, planted in dry soil, or if heat and poor storage damaged the living embryo inside the seed before planting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fiteɔ fɔmɔ kotokui ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ dani aduɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily and can die under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, providing the vital shade and cool soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ambrela. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni kookoo bibioo lɛ ahi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to create energy and make big tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the leafy vines off the dirt so they can catch more sunlight and stays safe from fungal diseases caused by wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ wain tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni sũ ni mli efɔ kɛbaa lɛ ahe

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea around the base of the plant will help restore the leaves to a healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and convert it into natural food in the soil. This enriches the earth and helps feed the neighboring maize crop naturally.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa efeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Ragged holes inside the central funnel of maize are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. Catching them early and applying organic mixtures or approved pest controls directly into the plant funnel will protect your crop from severe damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli ŋmeii ni etse amɛhe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite nii waa. Ni kɛ okɛ nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛbuɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo nibii ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ fitemɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why should I cover the dry dirt around my pepper plants with dried grass or palm leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo ŋmei tsei ni egbi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the dirt with organic material is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket that keeps the hot sun from drying out the soil, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Why is it a bad idea to plant maize on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows soil-borne pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like beans gives the soil a chance to recover.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ shii abɔ He kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa hegbɛ ni ekɛ ehe woɔ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Which way up am I supposed to plant my cassava stem cuttings into the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ matsɔ nɔ madu ŋmei niji awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the tiny buds (nodes) on the bark pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the new sprouts to grow incorrectly, leading to weak plants and a poor harvest.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii bibii (joints) ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaatsi dumɔwui heei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛkpaa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields when I plant the seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and ground nutrients. Giving each plant proper space lets its roots and leaves expand so it can produce larger cobs or fruits.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛwo ŋmeii loo aduawai wuji.

english: Why are my tomato plants drooping and drying up even though I give them plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miigboi ni amɛmiigbi eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by bacterial wilt or root rot in the dirt, which clogs the inside of the plant's stem and stops water from moving up to the leaves. You can prevent this by using disease-free seed varieties and avoiding overwatering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ji helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ mligbɛ ni ehaa nu nyɛɛɛ aya baai lɛ anɔ. Obaanyɛ otsi enɛ naa kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni hela bɛ mli ni okɛbaatsu nii kɛ nu ni oooha fe nine lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if the crop seeds I am buying from the dealer are genuine and certified?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ ji anɔkwale ni aŋmala he odaseyeli?
