english: Certified seeds come in sealed bags with an official tag or stamp from the seed regulatory authority. Look for labels showing the seed variety, purity percentage, lot number, and an official signature or stamp proving it was inspected.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ baa yɛ kotokui ni atsĩ naa ni amralo kadimɔ loo naasɔomɔ ni jɛ dumɔwui ahe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli. Taomɔ woji ni tsɔɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ. Hetsemɔ oha mlijaa, nɔkwɛmɔnɔ yibɔ, kɛ maŋ lɛ waonaa gbɛi loo naatsii ni tsɔɔ akɛ akwɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: What does the official approval stamp on a seed packet actually mean for my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni amralo lɛ naatsii ni tsɔɔ akɛ akpɛlɛ nɔ yɛ dumɔwui ahe paketii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: The official stamp means the seed batch was tested in a laboratory and field-checked by agricultural inspectors to guarantee high germination rates, good yields, and freedom from seed-borne diseases.
ga: Nɔ ni maŋ lɛ tsɔɔ ji akɛ, aka dumɔwui lɛ akuu lɛ akwɛ yɛ laboratori mli ni okwaayeli he nilelɔi lɛ ekwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛna nɔmimaa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ babaoo, amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai, ni helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli baa lɛ hu bɛ mli.

english: If you planted local open-pollinated varieties, you can save seeds, but if you planted hybrid seeds, saving them for the next season will result in weak plants and a low harvest. It is best to buy fresh certified seeds each season.
ga: Kɛji odu pollinated henɔi ni agbele naa lɛ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ ato. Shi kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ Okɛto kɛha be ni baa lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ hu akafee nɔ ni hi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa afi.

english: Why do some of my maize seeds sprout quickly while others in the same row do not grow at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu kwɛɛɛ oya lɛ? Yɛ nɛkɛ sɛɛkuu nɛɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ, edako kwraa?

english: Seeds need uniform soil moisture, proper planting depth, and good quality to sprout together. Old or uncertified seeds often have uneven germination, whereas certified seeds are tested to sprout uniformly.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa. Dumɔwui ni mli kwɔ ni sa ni amɛhiɛ su kpakpa bɔni afee ni amɛfee ekome kɛkwɛ̃ Dumɔwui ni eda loo ni bɛ he odaseyeli lɛ fɔɔ shweremɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Yɛ be mli ni akaa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ akwɛɔ koni amɛkwɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cassava plants turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil, poor drainage, or damage from pests. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai efiteɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant faces extreme heat, drought, or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist during the flowering stage helps the plant retain flowers and form fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ yashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why is my tomato crop growing tall and bushy with lots of leaves but very few tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔ mli ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli shi tomato fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes tomato plants grow thick stems and leaves instead of flowers. Balancing nitrogen with phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to set more flowers and fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni mli tse yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Nitrogen kɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai babaoo.

english: If I plant high-yielding hybrid seeds, do I still need to put fertilizer in my soil?
ga: Kɛji midu dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ Ani ehe miihia ni mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii lolo?

english: Yes, hybrid seeds are bred to grow fast and produce high yields, but they need adequate nutrients from the soil to achieve that. Without fertilizer or fertile soil, hybrid seeds cannot reach their full potential.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ anɔ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi nɛkɛ dumɔwui nɛɛ he miihia niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛnyɛ amɛshɛ enɛ he. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ ni baa nii bɛ lɛ, Hybrid dumɔwui lɛ hu nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he.

english: When planted too closely, crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow tall and thin, resulting in much smaller yields than properly spaced crops.
ga: Kɛ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ shwiili kɛ shwiili. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baafee bibioo fe be mli ni akɛ tsei lɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: What causes cocoa leaves to curl up and turn brown during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Cocoa leaves curl and dry up due to intense sun exposure and dry winds during Harmattan. Planting temporary shade trees like plantains and mulching around the roots helps protect young trees from drying out.
ga: Cocoa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi yɛ harmattan beaŋ lɛ hewɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ dumɔwui, kɛ shishifãi ni akɛwo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to stay green and strong. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients deep into the soil beyond the reach of young roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same plot drains the specific soil nutrients that maize loves. It also allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil, leading to lower yields over time.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni abele sumɔɔ ni ejieɔ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai hu ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Leaf rolling is your maize plant's natural defense against heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface exposed to direct sunlight to stop water from evaporating out of its tissues.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Tsei haa hulu la ni shɛɔ amɛhiɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ mli koni nu akajɛ fãji lɛ amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop most of their lower leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava sheds its leaves when water is scarce to save energy and moisture. The plant goes into a resting state to survive the dry spell, and it will sprout fresh green leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ kɛji nu faaa koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ akafite. Tsei boteɔ shihilɛ ni mli wa mli koni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Ni kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, ebaakwɛ̃ ni etsɔ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ.

english: Why are small ragged holes appearing in the central funnel of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the leaf whorl. They feed on the tender young leaves inside the stalk before the leaves unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ dani baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my ripening tomatoes turning dark and rotted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It occurs when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering or dry soil conditions while the fruit is forming.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni yɔɔ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ.

english: Planting seeds too close together actually lowers your yield. Crowded crops fight each other for sun, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in tall, thin stalks with very small or empty cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi diɛŋtsɛ. Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni dumɔwui bibii bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than young crops. They quickly steal the fertilizer and soil nutrients meant for your crop, effectively starving your plants even when water is available.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei bibii. Amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaadu onibii lɛ mli lɛ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ moŋ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their flowers before any small pods can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ŋmeii bibii lɛ baanyɛ adara lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from stress such as sudden dry spells, lack of nutrients, or a shortage of tiny pollinating insects like midges that help turn flowers into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛna haomɔ tamɔ hulutsoo be ni baa trukaa, niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa, loo nibii bibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting in the storage barn before planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Stored yams sprout when heat and moisture build up in the storage area. Warm temperatures signal to the dormant yam root that conditions are right to break sleep and begin growing.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni ato lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛji dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i bua amɛhe naa yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. He ni mli edɔ lɛ tsɔɔ sweet potato shishifãi ni ewɔ lɛ akɛ shihilɛi lɛ ja koni amɛfo amɛwɔ lɛ mli ni amɛbɔi dalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under the harsh sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist, helping the young cocoa survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil or the ground is too waterlogged for roots to absorb food properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a light rain while the crops are growing. Avoid applying on bone-dry soil as it can burn the roots, or right before heavy rain which washes it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wui yɔɔ nɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ. aloo dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. It stops the plant from making food properly, which leads to small tubers.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. ni kɛ mɔ yaa yitso bibioo ko mli

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, damp, and shady conditions. Clearing weeds and pruning shade trees helps sunlight and air dry out the pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ hulutsoo kɛbaa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ahe jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my maize leaves and dark droppings in the central funnel?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai anɔ ni eyɛ ŋmãa ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the growing center of the plant during the day and eat the tender green leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ he yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai eŋɔli bibii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra shoots growing around my main plantain trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: Leaving too many young shoots causes them to fight the main tree for nutrients, water, and sunlight. Keeping only one or two strong suckers gives you bigger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii bibii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha oná tso ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do I need to use tall sticks to support my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ atsu nii kɛfi sweet potato wain tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need stakes so their leaves can lift off the ground to catch sunlight. Sunlight gives the plant energy to swell and grow large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ko bɔni afee ni anyɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Hulu la haa tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfuuɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant hold onto its blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, called mulching, protects the soil from hot sun, keeps moisture in the ground longer, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do strong winds easily break or snap my plantain trees during storms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ shwieɔ loo efoɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ oya yɛ ahum be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trunks are not made of hard wood like cocoa or mango trees; they are made of soft, water-filled leaf sheaths. Because they carry heavy leaves and fruit bunches, strong winds can easily snap the main stem.
ga: Akɛ tsei ni wa tamɔ cacao loo mango tsei feeee plantain tsei lɛ. Akɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ fee amɛ. Akɛni baai kɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ akumɔ tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ mlɛo.

english: If a strong wind breaks my plantain tree in half, will the stem grow back on its own?
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko ha dumɔwui lɛ gbá mli enyɔ Ani tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ?

english: No, a broken plantain stem cannot heal or grow back from where it snapped. Once completely broken, that main stalk is ruined and must be cut down to allow fresh shoots to grow from the base.
ga: Dabi, plantain tsei ni ekumɔ lɛ nyɛŋ atsa loo amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ kɛjɛ he ni ekumɔ lɛ. Beni efo fɛɛ lɛ Tso lɛ tso titri lɛ efite ni esa akɛ afo lɛ sɛɛ koni ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ.

english: After a windstorm, how do I know which plantain trees can be saved and which ones are totally ruined?
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ sɛɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ male plantains ni abaanyɛ ahere amɛyiwala? Ni mɛɛ tsei akpãtã amɛhiɛ kwraa?

english: If the main stem is completely snapped or folded over, the plant is ruined and needs to be cut down. If it is only slightly bent, you can leave it for a few days to monitor whether it stays standing or eventually collapses.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ shishitso titri lɛ ekumɔ loo ebɔle kwraa Tso lɛ baafite ni ehe baahia ni afo lɛ. Kɛji obɔle lɛ fioo pɛ Obaanyɛ oshi lɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni okwɛ kɛji ebaadamɔ shi shiŋŋ loo yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaakumɔ.

english: How can I tell if a plantain stem is infected or damaged on the inside?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ hela eba plantain tso ko mli loo efite kɛjɛ emli?

english: You need to cut into the stem near the base to expose the inside. Healthy tissue looks clean and light, while damaged or diseased tissue shows dark rot, holes, or discoloration.
ga: Esa akɛ ofo tso lɛ shishi lɛ ni obɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ koni emli lɛ ajie kpo. Tissue ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ehe tse ni ekpɛɔ. yɛ be mli ni fãji ni efite loo hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ baajie ediŋŋ, bu, loo su ni tsakeɔ lɛ kpo.

english: If I find sick or damaged plantain stalks, why is it bad to leave even one on my farm?
ga: Kɛji mina dumɔwui ni hela mɔ amɛ loo amɛfite Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mashi tso ko po yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaving even a single infected stalk allows diseases and pests like weevils to survive and multiply, which can quickly spread to healthy plants across your whole farm.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tso kome po ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ lɛ lɛ, ehaa helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛshwereɔ. ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli oya yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut completely ruined plants immediately instead of leaving them until harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mifo tsei ni efite lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni mashi amɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Ruined plants rot quickly on the farm, attracting harmful insects and fungal diseases. Removing them right away keeps the area clean and protects your surrounding healthy crops.
ga: Tsei ni akpata hiɛ lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Egbalaa kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai. Kɛ́ ajie amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha he lɛ he atse, ni ebaabu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle he lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I need to cut a ruined plantain stalk right down to the base instead of leaving a tall stump?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ plantain tsei ni efite lɛ kɛyaa shishigbɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mashi tso kakadaŋŋ ko lɛ?

english: Leaving a tall stump creates a home for pests and fungal rot that can travel underground into the roots. Cutting right down near the base stops rot from reaching the underground stem.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni damɔ shi lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ aya shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ feɔ shia. Kɛ́ afo shi yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tso lɛ he.

english: What is the reason for clearing around the base of the plantain stem when I am inspecting my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie plantain shishitoo he lɛ beni mikwɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Exposing the base allows you to clearly see if there is any hidden pest damage, stem splitting, or rot at the ground level before it causes the tree to fall over.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie shishitoo lɛ kpo lɛ, obaana jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ efite, tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni ekumɔ, loo egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tso lɛ baagbee nɔ.

english: If I cut a broken plantain tree right down to the ground, will I lose that plant forever?
ga: Kɛ mifo dumɔwui ni ekumɔ lɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ Ani nakai tso lɛ baafite mi kɛya naanɔ?

english: Not necessarily. As long as the underground root base is healthy, cutting away the broken top stalk encourages new, healthy shoots called suckers to sprout and replace the old plant.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi shishitoo lɛ mli wa lɛ, tsei ni ekumɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ woɔ tsei heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni atsɛɔ amɛ tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛye tsei momo lɛ anajiaŋ.

english: Is it better to just cut off broken leaves or remove the entire plantain stem when wind damage happens?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaafolɔ baai ni ekumɔ loo ajie plantain tsei lɛ fɛɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ fite nii?

english: If only a few leaves are torn, you can cut off just the leaves. But if the main stem itself snaps or cracks deeply, trimming the leaves won't help—the whole stem must be removed from the base.
ga: Kɛji baai fioo pɛ elaaje lɛ, baai lɛ pɛ abaanyɛ afo. Shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ efo loo efo waa lɛ, baai lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ eyeee ebuaaa. Esa akɛ ajie tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need plantains planted next to them during their first two years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ yɛ emasɛi lɛ? Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing plantains next to them creates a natural leaf canopy that provides essential shade and keeps the soil cool while the cocoa establishes itself over the first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ amɛdu dumɔwui ni daa oya yɛ Together masɛi lɛ, amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ toɔ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: How long will it take for my new hybrid cocoa farm to start producing its first flowers and pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi hybrid cocoa ŋmɔ hee lɛ aje eklɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ afeemɔ shishi?

english: With proper clearing, shade management, and care, modern hybrid cocoa varieties typically begin showing their first flowers and bearing small pods around two years after planting.
ga: Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni sa, shade kɛ kwɛmɔ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfee tsofai lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi klɛŋklɛŋ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii. Aaafee afii enyɔ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate that the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key nutrient responsible for leafy growth and building strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni haa baa lɛ daa kɛ tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, prevents hot sunlight from drying out the earth, preserves moisture for the roots, and stops weed seeds from sprouting.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ha shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni otsi jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stems and low harvest yields.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi.

english: Why is it important to wait for the major rainy season before sowing my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni amɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ dani adu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Dry soil keeps seeds dormant or leaves them vulnerable to insects. Sowing right after steady rains begin ensures the seeds absorb enough water to germinate quickly and build deep root systems.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni egbi yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi. aloo eha dumɔwui lɛ afee nɔ ni kooloi bibii nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ nɔ Kɛ́ adu amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. ni efee shishifã gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli kwɔ

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my young cassava so much more than mature plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi yucca bibioo lɛ dalɛ baa shi fe mi tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young crops have small roots and few leaves, making them easily overwhelmed by aggressive weeds that steal sunlight, water, and soil food before the crop can establish itself.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ baai fioo. Ehaa jwɛi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo Enɛ juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtoɔ amɛhe shi.

english: Why do I need to mount wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo tso ko nɔ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbing vines that need to spread their leaves in the air to catch sunlight. Lifting the vines off the ground prevents leaf diseases and directs energy into growing larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni shwereɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛná hulu la lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni awóɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa, ni etsɔɔ hewalɛ gbɛ kɛyaa tsei wuji ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ.

english: How will I know underground cassava tubers are ready for harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ ni okɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava plants signal maturity when their lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the soil surrounding the base of the main stem begins to crack as the mature tubers expand beneath the surface.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiida kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso wulu lɛ shishi jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb ni eda lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are the blossom ends of my garden eggs and tomatoes turning dark and soft while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛ tomatoi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Dark, soft bottoms on developing fruits are usually caused by irregular soil moisture, which prevents the plant roots from taking up calcium properly while the fruit is forming.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni ejaaa lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa tso shishifãi lɛ aná calcium ni sa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ.

english: Does cutting green fronds off my palm trees reduce how much fruit the tree will produce?
ga: Ani mi-palm tso lɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ baaha yibii ni tso lɛ baawo lɛ aba shi?

english: Cutting too many healthy green fronds reduces the palm tree's ability to absorb sunlight and make food, which can lower your fruit yields. You should only cut low, mature, or yellowing fronds when gathering material for farm use.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ehaa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛjieɔ hulu la ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii lɛ baa shi. Enɛ baaha aduawai ni owoɔ lɛ aba shi. Esa akɛ ofolɔ baai kukuji lɛ pɛ. Eda loo eyɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛji abua nibii ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anaa.

english: How do I know which palm fronds are safe to cut without damaging the main plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni esa akɛ afo ni efiteee tso titri lɛ?

english: Always harvest the bottom-most fronds that hang downward. Leave the upright center fronds around the top untouched, as cutting the crown will stunt the palm tree's growth or kill it.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, kpamɔ baai ni fĩɔ shi fe fɛɛ lɛ. Ha baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ adamɔ shi jaŋŋ kɛbɔle he fɛɛ. Mɔ ko mɔ ko etaaa ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ afo ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei tso lɛ agbɔjɔ loo ebaaha ŋmei lɛ agbo.

english: How do I prepare harvested palm fronds so I can weave them into mats for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa ŋmei tsei ni akpa lɛ koni mikɛfee ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsɔji?

english: After cutting the fronds, scrape away the rough outer back skin to expose the tough, flexible inner material. Extracting this inner stem gives you smooth strips that can be woven without snapping.
ga: Kɛji ofo baai lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, shwiemɔ kponɔgbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ koni ejie nibii ni yɔɔ mli ni nyɛɔ efoɔ ni ewa lɛ kpo. Kɛ́ ojie mligbɛ tso lɛ, ebaaha oná tsɔne ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni abaanyɛ akpɛ ni efoŋ.

english: Why do I need to scrape the back of the palm stem before extracting the inside part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi nine lɛ sɛɛ dani majie mligbɛ lɛ?

english: Scraping removes the hard, uneven outer bark, dirt, and sharp edges. This makes it easier to extract the clean, flexible inner fibers needed to craft smooth, durable drying mats.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee, muji, kɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaajie mligbɛ tsɔji ni he tse ni nyɛɔ efoɔ lɛ. Enɛ he miihia koni anyɛ afee tsɔji ni akɛgbiɔ nii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: What inner part of the palm stalk is actually used to make weaving strips?
ga: Mɛɛ tso lɛ fã ji nɔ ni akɛfeɔ tsɔji ni akpɛɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: The inner core of the stalk contains long, tough plant fibers. Once stripped out from under the outer skin, these fibers dry flat and provide the strength needed for mats and baskets.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsɔi kakadaji ni wa yɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛji ajie kɛjɛ hewolo lɛ shishi lɛ, nɛkɛ tsɔji nɛɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛhaa hewalɛ ni he hiaa kɛha tsɔji kɛ tsɛnsii.

english: Why is it better to dry my harvested cocoa on palm frond mats instead of directly on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaagbi kookoo ni akpa lɛ yɛ tsei anɔ moŋ fe ni aaagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Drying crops directly on the ground exposes them to dirt, pests, and ground dampness. Spreading crops on clean palm mats allows air to circulate properly, drying the crop faster and keeping it clean.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa muji, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ agbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashwã tso ni he tse nɔ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbiɔ oya ni ehaa amɛhe tseɔ.

english: Why do my harvested crops spoil or go mouldy if I do not dry them properly after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ fiteɔ loo efoɔ kɛji migbiko lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Freshly harvested crops contain natural moisture. If they are left packed together without being spread on drying mats in the sun, trapped water creates a moist environment where destructive fungi and mould thrive.
ga: Nibii ni akpa ehee lɛ mli nu yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ he kome ni agbɛɛɛ ashwãaa tsɔne nɔ koni egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli Nu ni emɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ ada yɛ.

english: Can I use elevated palm frond platforms to protect drying crops from rain and animals?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmei tso ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ abu ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ nugbɔ kɛ kooloi ahe?

english: Yes, weaving mats from palm fronds and placing them on raised wooden legs keeps your drying crops off the wet soil, away from free-roaming farm animals, and allows airflow from both above and below.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tsei ahe tsei ahe tsɔi ni okɛwo tsei ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ akabote shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni nyiɛɔ amɛhe lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ shishi fɛɛ.

english: How long do woven palm frond mats usually last when used outdoors on the farm?
ga: Be enyiɛ tsɔji ni akɛ tsei ahe tsei fee lɛ hiɔ shi kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: If properly dried before use and stored off the ground when rain comes, well-woven palm frond mats can last one to two harvest seasons before becoming brittle and needing replacement.
ga: Kɛji akɛ agbi lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani akɛtsu nii ni akɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ kpo nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ. Palm leaf mat ni akpɛ́ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi be kome loo bei enyɔ dani etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe baahia ni atsake.

english: What is the best way to store my palm drying mats when the harvest season is over?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ ŋmei ŋmɔji toɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ naagbee?

english: Brush off all food dust, ensure the mats are fully dry in the sun, then roll them up and store them elevated off the ground in a dry shed to protect them from moisture and termites.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ niyenii mli sũ fɛɛ. Kwɛmɔ ni tsɔne lɛ mli agbi kwraa yɛ hulu lɛ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, shwie nɔ ni okɛto shikpɔŋ yɛ tsũ ko ni mli egbi mli koni ebu tsɔne lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmeii ahe.

english: Why should I avoid burning the cleared bush on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsei ni ajie yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashãa dani madu nii lɛ he?

english: Burning clears the land quickly, but it destroys essential organic matter and beneficial soil organisms that feed your crops, leaving the soil dry and less fertile over time.
ga: Shãa baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Shi efiteɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbiɔ ni ewoɔ nii babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Is it safe for me to plant my cassava immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is better to wait until the rains become steady. Planting after just one early rain can cause stem cuttings to dry out and die if a long dry spell follows before the main rainy season settles.
ga: Ehi akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baashɛ shi. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ aniji lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi kɛji hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ ba dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ bashɛ.

english: How does leaving crop stalks on my soil after harvest help my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ahe ŋmeii ni mashi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Leaving old crop stalks on the field acts as a cover that protects the soil from hot sun, retains water, and breaks down into natural food for your next batch of crops.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi tsei momoi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ehaa nu hiɔ mli, ni ehaa niyenii ni okɛbaatsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to grow strong green leaves, or that water is sitting too long in the soil and choking the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii tso titri ni he hiaa koni baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ akwɛ̃. Aloo nu hiɔ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: If I only have a small amount of fertilizer, when is the best time to give it to my plants?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tsei amli?

english: Apply fertilizer when the plant is actively growing and forming roots or flowers, rather than all at once at planting, so the crops can use every bit of nutrients before rains wash them away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni tso lɛ miida ni efee shishifãi loo fɔfɔii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu fɛɛ shikome Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ anyɛ atsu niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ he nii dani nugbɔ lɛ afɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of leafy branches but very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen causes them to put all their energy into leafy growth rather than flowers. Crops need balanced nutrients like phosphorus and potassium to turn flowers into healthy fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tso ko lɛ, ehaa efiteɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛduɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Tsei hia niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasiam. Koni ekɛtsake fɔfɔii ni etsɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and provide wide leaves that shade the young cocoa, keeping the soil cool and moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing stalks fight each other for light, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak, tall plants with very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsoi ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni dumɔwui bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off before producing peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat or dry soil stress as a way to save water and protect the main stem from drying out.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ he. Koni akɛ nu akafite ni abu tso titri lɛ he koni ekagbi.

english: Why are my cassava roots small and thin even though the plant leaves look large and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa moŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots cannot expand if the soil is too hard and compact, or if the soil has high nitrogen levels that force the plant to grow leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ alɛɛ mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa babaoo ni haa tso lɛ baa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why is it necessary to completely cut down a cocoa tree when only a few branches look diseased?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ fɛɛ lɛ? He ni niji fioo pɛ hela emɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Once a viral infection like swollen shoot gets inside a cocoa tree, it travels through the entire tree root system. Cutting off only branches does not eliminate the disease, so the whole tree must be removed to protect the surrounding healthy trees.
ga: Kɛji hela ko ni jɛɔ hela ko mli, tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ, bote kookoo tso lɛ mli Etsɔɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ amli. Nine kome pɛ ni aaafo lɛ haŋ hela lɛ aya. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ajie tso muu lɛ fɛɛ koni akɛbu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ahe.

english: Can using the same cutlass on a sick cocoa tree spread disease to my healthy trees?
ga: Ani dagger kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ cacao tso ni hela mɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela lɛ ashwã mi tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, plant sap containing fungi or bacteria sticks to metal tools. Washing your cutlass with clean water and soap or heating the blade slightly between trees prevents carrying diseases across your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso mli nu ni fungi loo bacteria yɔɔ mli lɛ kpɛtɛɔ dade nibii ahe. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli tse kɛ samla miifɔ tsɔji ahe Aloo okɛ tsɔji ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ awo mli la fioo kɛkɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni helai akabote oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: If I cut off diseased leaves early, will my cocoa tree heal itself and bear pods again?
ga: Kɛji ofolɔ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya Ani cacao tso lɛ baatsa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni efee ŋmeii ekoŋŋ?

english: For mild fungal issues like leaf spot, removing bad leaves helps, but for major viral diseases, the plant cannot cure itself. Removing the entire infected tree is the only permanent solution.
ga: Kɛha fungal naagbai ni waaa, tamɔ baa mli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, baa ni woɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua. Shi kɛha helai ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ atsa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Tsei fɛɛ ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tsabaa pɛ ni hiɔ shi daa.

english: What kind of support does the Ghana Cocoa Board offer to help me if my diseased cocoa farm has to be cut down?
ga: Mɛɛ yelikɛbuamɔ Ghana Cocoa Board lɛ kɛhaa kɛji ehe bahia ni afo mi-cocoa ŋmɔ ni hela emɔ mi lɛ mli?

english: The Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) provides compensation payments to assist farmers whose trees are removed, along with free hybrid cocoa seedlings and extension officers to help clear and replant the farm.
ga: Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) lɛ miiwo nyɔmɔ koni eye ebua okwaafoi ni ajie amɛtsei lɛ. Kɛfata hybrid cocoa dumɔwui ni aheee nɔ ko kɛ extension nitsulɔi ni baaye abua ni ajie ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni adu ekoŋŋ lɛ he.

english: Is it safe to plant new young cocoa seedlings in the same spot where a diseased tree was cut down?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu kookoo tso hee yɛ he ni afo tso ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, but only after properly clearing out the old tree roots and letting the land rest briefly. This removes any hiding places for insects that carry plant sickness.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi beni ajie tsei momoi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe be kukuoo ko sɛɛ pɛ kɛkɛ. Enɛ baajie hei ni tsei amli helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ kɛya.

english: How many years will I have to wait before a newly planted cocoa seedling starts producing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa seedlings provided for replanting grow faster than older varieties and typically start producing their first crop within two to three years.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ hybrid kookoo dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni adu ekoŋŋ lɛ daa oya fe tsutsu henɔi lɛ. ni bei pii lɛ, ejeɔ eklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shishi yɛ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli.

english: What fast-growing crops can I plant on my cocoa land right after cutting down old trees?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni daa oya manyɛ madu yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mifo tsei momo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You can plant food crops like plantain, cassava, and maize. Plantains provide vital shade for young cocoa seedlings, while providing food and temporary income while you wait for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu niyenii nibii tamɔ plantains, cassava kɛ ŋmãa. Plantains haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ náa hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ha niyenii kɛ shika ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ be kukuoo mli be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: How does sickness move from one cocoa tree to neighboring healthy ones?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni hela jeɔ cacao tso kome nɔ kɛyaa cacao tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ?

english: Diseases often travel through small insects like mealybugs that feed on infected sap and crawl to adjacent plants, or through wind and rain splashing disease spores across leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ tsɔɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs ni yeɔ nu ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli ni amɛkpãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni gbɛɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai eshwaa baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some cocoa trees on my farm catch disease easily while others right beside them stay healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ helai yeɔ cacao tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi fe nɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ? Ná hewalɛ kpakpa

english: Trees with stronger root systems, better access to soil nutrients, and proper shade are naturally more resilient, whereas stressed or older trees catch diseases much faster.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli wa lɛ Hewalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ni kɛji amɛyɛ hulutsoo be ni sa lɛ, amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni haoɔ loo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ baaná hela oya kwraa.

english: What visual signs show that my cocoa trees are healthy and free from plant disease?
ga: Okadii ni anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni tso helai bɛ amɛhe.

english: A healthy cocoa tree shows vibrant green or reddish young leaf flushes, smooth bark, clear brown pods without dark patches, and no unusual swellings on its stems.
ga: Cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo etsuru, amɛhewolo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɛ he. ni fũu ko ni ejaaa bɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my maize crops drying up early even when it rains a little bit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ fioo po lɛ?

english: When temperatures rise due to changing weather patterns, the soil loses water much faster through evaporation. Even if it rains slightly, the intense heat dries out the soil before the crop roots can absorb enough water to stay green.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be tee hiɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahewɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kwraa yɛ la ni hoɔ lɛ hewɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ fioo moŋ Shi latsaa ni naa wa waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli.

english: The first rain is often a false start followed by a long dry spell. If seeds germinate immediately, the young seedlings will die from heat and drought before the main rains actually start.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ji amale shishijee. Nɔ ni nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Tsei bibii lɛ baagboi yɛ latsaa kɛ hɔmɔ mli dani nugbɔ lɛ aje shishi.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my pepper plants without turning into peppers during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ pepper yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When the weather becomes unusually hot or the soil dries out, pepper plants experience heat stress and drop their flowers as a survival mechanism to conserve energy and stay alive.
ga: Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi. Pepper tsei naa dɔlɛ mli haomɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi akɛ wala gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he ni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and burn when I remove all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshã beni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive. Big trees block harsh direct sunlight and keep the air humid; without them, the intense sun burns the leaves and dries out the soil quickly.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi. Tsei wuji tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ amɛbɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya.

english: Covering the ground, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It blocks direct heat from the sun, keeps the soil cool, and stops water from evaporating so your crops stay hydrated longer.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Etsĩɔ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge leafy branches but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen from incorrect fertilizer use, the plant uses all its energy to grow leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ mli. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ ŋmeii baato shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer on my field when the soil is very dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi waa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve safely. If applied to dry soil, the high concentration of fertilizer chemicals will draw water out of the plant roots and burn them.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni fa babaoo lɛ jieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli ni eshãa amɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and weak with small cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete with each other for light, water, and nutrients. They stretch tall to reach sunlight instead of developing strong stems and full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa shɔŋŋ koni amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaama tsei ni wa kɛ tsei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do insects attack my crops more during the hot dry season than during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Hotter temperatures allow many pest populations to multiply much faster, while heat-stressed crops become too weak to defend themselves, making them easy targets for insects.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔi babaoo yaa hiɛ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni hulutsoo haoɔ amɛ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛbu amɛhe he. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why are crop varieties that my father grew successfully no longer yielding well on my farm today?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mitsɛ du lɛ yeɔ omanye waa lɛ wooo yibii kpakpai dɔŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Local weather patterns, rainfall timing, and soil quality have shifted over the decades. Older traditional seeds may not be adapted to the higher temperatures and erratic rains experienced today.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su etsake yɛ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli. Ekolɛ blema dumɔwui ni etsɛ lɛ nyɛŋ atsake amɛhe amɛwo hulutsoo be ni yaa hiɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni ejaaa ni yaa nɔ amrɔ nɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my coconut trees look weak even after I apply fertilizer to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ awo ŋmei tso mli ŋmei po lɛ, etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve and be absorbed; if applied during dry conditions, in the wrong spot, or in improper quantities, the tree cannot use the nutrients to gain strength.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli ni ekɛ ehe awo mli. Kɛ akɛwo he ko ni egbi, yɛ he ni esaaa, loo akɛtsu nii yɛ bɔ ni esaaa mli lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛha ehewalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What actually happens to my crops when I give them fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli?

english: Fertilizer acts like nutritious food for plants, supplying essential elements that restore soil richness so struggling crops can build strong stems, healthy leaves, and good fruit.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli kɛhaa tsei. Kɛtsɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ ni ekɛhaa lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ haomɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ awo tsei ni wa, baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is fertilizer always necessary for coconut trees to produce well?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia be fɛɛ be koni ŋmei tsei awo yibii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Coconut trees take a lot of nutrients from the earth over time, so without adding fertilizer back into old or poor soil, the trees become too weak to support heavy yields.
ga: Kokoo tsei lɛ naa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa shikpɔŋ momo loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ he ekoŋŋ lɛ. Tso lɛ baagbɔjɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ewo ŋmaa babaoo.

english: When is the best time to give fertilizer to my plants so they gain maximum strength?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa awo mitsei lɛ amli koni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist, usually at the beginning or middle of the rainy season, so the roots can easily drink up the dissolved nutrients.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee loo teŋgbɛ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni mli edɔ lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why are my crops not growing as strong or tall as they are supposed to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shi waa loo ekwɛɛɛ shi tamɔ bɔ ni esa akɛ efee lɛ?

english: Crops struggle to grow when the soil lacks vital nutrients, when water is scarce, or when pests attack their roots, leaving the plant with no energy to expand.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛ́ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ nu faaa loo kɛ́ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua shishifãi lɛ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaafɔ bii.

english: How can I tell if my coconut tree is struggling and needs extra food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-koko tso lɛ yɛ naagba ko ni ehe miihia ni aha lɛ niyenii kroko?

english: A struggling coconut tree often shows pale or yellow leaves, slow growth, thin trunks, and produces very few or small fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tsei ni miiwuu lɛ baa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔŋ, amɛdaraa blɛoo, amɛwoɔ tsei bibii, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo loo amɛwoɔ yibii bibii kwraa.

english: If my plant is already very weak, will adding fertilizer fix it immediately?
ga: Kɛji wɔtso lɛ egbɔjɔ waa momo lɛ Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baasaa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer helps, but recovery takes time; a weak plant must first rebuild its root system and receive enough water before it can fully show renewed strength.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua, shi helatsamɔ heɔ be. Esa akɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ama amɛshishifãi lɛ ekoŋŋ klɛŋklɛŋ. Ni ná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa dani obaanyɛ ojie ohewalɛ hee lɛ kpo kwraa.

english: Why do my coconut trees flower but fail to produce full, healthy nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-coconut tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi shi ewooo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When a tree lacks essential plant food like potassium or suffers from water stress, it drops its flowers or produces light, empty nuts because it lacks the strength to fill them.
ga: Beni tso ko bɛ tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium, loo nu he haomɔ miipiŋ lɛ. Tsei baagbee shi loo amɛbaawo ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni amɛhe waaa ejaakɛ amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaawo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my neighbor's crops look green and strong while mine look lifeless?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyɛ hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni minɔ̃ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni wala bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Differences in plant health are usually down to soil richness, proper fertilizer use, adequate water supply, and keeping weeds away from the crop's root zone.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahewalɛ srɔtofeemɔi damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɔmɔ nɔ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ashishifãi ahe

english: What causes young coconut trees to stall and stop developing after planting?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ais ni amɛdaraa beni adu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Young trees stall when they are planted in poor soil without added nutrients or shade, causing the young roots to struggle to support new leaf growth.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ baaya wɔɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ ni niyenii loo hulutsoo bɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa koni amɛye amɛbua baai heei lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning light green and yellow while the rest of the plant stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ kã he eji ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of young maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which helps it grow green and strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or urea fertilizer around the roots gives the plant the quick food boost it needs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo urea fataa he Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ oya.

english: Why is my cassava crop growing very tall with thick green leaves, but when I dig it up, the cassava roots are very tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi kɛ́ atsa lɛ, ani ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ bibioo kwraa?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen (often from raw animal manure), they put all their energy into growing leaves instead of growing food underground. Cassava needs potassium in the soil to feed the tubers so they expand big and heavy.
ga: Kɛ tsei ná nitrogen babaoo Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛduɔ baai yɛ niyenii ni amɛaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ najiaŋ. Cassava he miihia potassium yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii bɔni afee ni amɛdara ni amɛtsii.

english: Why do my crops get smaller yields every year if I keep planting maize on the exact same piece of land without stopping?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mikpaaa lɛ?

english: Planting maize in the same spot every season drains all the specific nutrients maize needs and allows soil pests to build up. Alternating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nutrients to the soil and keeps it fertile naturally.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmã yɛ he kome daa be lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ hoɔ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmãa aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before any peppers can grow on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani pepper lɛ baanyɛ ada lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme hot sun or dry soil because they are trying to save water to stay alive. Giving them shade during the hottest hours and watering them regularly around the root zone helps the flowers stick and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji hulu la ni mli edɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Ejaakɛ amɛmiitao ni amɛbu nu koni amɛhi shi. Ni akɛ hulutsoo bei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa he fɛɛ he lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ shishifã lɛ tsu nii daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up after I clear all the shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijie tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are tender and cannot handle direct afternoon sunlight without scorching. Leaving high shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains nearby protects young cocoa from sun damage and keeps moisture in the surrounding air.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shwane mli ni amɛshãaa. Kɛ́ oshi tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo odu tsei ni shwereɔ oya yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he, ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do my yam vines struggle to grow well when I let them trail along the hot ground instead of tying them to sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ miitao ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Beni mihaa efoɔ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mafi lɛ tso nine ko he lɛ?

english: Yam vines need their leaves exposed to sunlight and air to make energy for the tubers underground. Guiding the vines up bamboo or wooden stakes keeps them off the hot, dusty soil and allows the leaves to trap maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tsei lɛ wo ŋmei loo tsei anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔɔ ni sũ akafee nɔ ko. ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ

english: Why do the funnels of my young maize plants have ragged holes and small green caterpillars inside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn plant lɛ cone lɛ mli lɛ yɛ bu ni etse kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that burrows into the growing center of young corn plants. Catching them early by inspecting the leaves and applying neem oil mixture or recommended insecticide into the plant funnels stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni miida lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Afeɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ baai lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ ni akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ko ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛfutuɔ mli lɛ woɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my healthy green tomatoes turn dark, sunken, and rotten right before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ, efoɔ nu mli, ni egboɔ dani etsɔɔ etsuru lɛ?

english: This condition, called blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot pull up enough calcium from the soil due to dry spells between waterings. Keeping the soil evenly damp with mulch helps tomato roots absorb calcium continuously and prevents fruit rot.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ hɔmɔ ni baa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ lɛ teŋ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tomato shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium be fɛɛ be, ni ehaa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees keep falling over and snapping near the roots right before the bunches are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni tsii lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛmiikumɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe dani ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots, so a heavy bunch acts like a weight pulling the tree down during high winds. Supporting the trees with sturdy wooden Y-stakes or bamboo poles pushed beneath the heavy bunch holds them upright until harvest.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei niji ni tsii lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ muji ni gbalaa tso lɛ kɛbaa shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ tsei ni tamɔ Y loo tsei ni wa ni akɛtsiɔ tsei ni tsii lɛ ashishi lɛ fi tso lɛ sɛɛ. Hiɛ tsei lɛ amli ja kɛyashi kpamɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my leafy vegetables taste watery or slightly bitter after I pick them during heavy rainfall days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli nu fioo loo amɛmli edɔ beni mikpa amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa gbi ko nɔ lɛ?

english: During heavy rains, plants absorb excess water quickly, diluting the natural sugars and flavor compounds inside the leaves. Harvesting leafy greens early in the morning on sunny days allows the leaves to concentrate their nutrients and hold a better, sweeter flavor.
ga: yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Tsei shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ oya. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli sugars kɛ nibii ni haa tso lɛ mli ŋɔɔ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ leebi maŋkpa yɛ gbi ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ babaoo, ni amɛnuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛmli ŋɔɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and weak when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe waaa beni midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and food to grow thick, strong stalks and produce a good harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli niyenii. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell that can dry out the soil and kill young seedlings. Waiting for the rains to become regular ensures the soil stays moist enough for seeds to germinate and grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni ebaanyɛ egbe tso bibioo lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni amɛdara.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant is missing important soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that water is sitting too long around the roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or improving drainage helps restore the green color.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu eta shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he loo nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How does leaving weeds around my crops reduce my yield?
ga: jwɛi ni ebɔleɔ he lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ Te baafee tɛŋŋ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi?

english: Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your crops need to thrive. Clearing weeds early ensures your main crops get all the food and water required to produce heavy fruits or grains.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo aduawai loo ŋmaa ni tsii.

english: Pruning unnecessary branches allows sunlight and air to move freely through the canopy. This prevents fungal diseases like black pod from spreading and helps the tree direct its energy into forming cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli oya. Koni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods lɛ akagbɛ ashwã. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛfee kookoo ŋmeii

english: Why do farmers plant plantain suckers next to young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide big leaves that act as living shade umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa seedlings cool and moist until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why is it bad to grow maize on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like beans or peanuts restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ.

english: These holes are typically caused by caterpillars such as the fall armyworm hiding inside the plant funnel. Applying safe pest management methods early prevents them from destroying the growing tip of the maize.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ fall armyworms ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tsei amli ŋmeii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛkwɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmei lɛ yitsei ni miida lɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are ready for harvesting without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and shed, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack as the swollen roots expand underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi ni efuu lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when they experience extreme heat or lack of water. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the flowers stay on the plant and develop into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow during the dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant is suffering from nitrogen deficiency or extreme water stress. When the soil is too dry, roots cannot absorb the nutrients required to keep the leaves green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli loo nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa miipiŋ lɛ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛha baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why does putting too much chemical fertilizer at once burn my crops instead of making them grow faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ shãa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeha amɛkwɛ̃ oya lɛ?

english: Too much fertilizer increases salt levels in the soil, which actually draws water out of the plant roots instead of feeding them. This dehydrates the crop quickly, causing the leaves to scorch and die.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata he lɛ, ehaa ŋmei ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Enɛ baaha nu afo tso lɛ mli oya. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Is it better for my tomato crops if I water them early in the morning or in the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mi-tomato tsei lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛmli leebi loo mikɛ hulu ha amɛ shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because midday heat causes water to evaporate before roots can absorb it, and wet leaves in hot sun can get damaged or attract fungal diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ gbi lɛ mli dɔlɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔɔ. Ni baai ni efɔ ni hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baanyɛ aná amɛ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them survive during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around No hewɔ lɛ mikɛ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts as a protective blanket. It keeps the soil cool, traps moisture underneath so roots stay hydrated longer, and stops unwanted weeds from growing.
ga: Mulch ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shishi koni shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni eha jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ akakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their flowers instead of turning them all into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can support with food and water. Dropping up to 90 percent of their flowers is a natural behavior so the tree can focus its strength on growing healthy pods from the rest.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná kɛjɛ niyenii kɛ nu mli. Fɔfɔi ni shɛɔ oha mlijaa 90 ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli subaŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ ama ŋmɔshi nibii ni he wa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ ekrokomɛi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small plantain shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Leaving too many shoots causes them to fight with the main plant for soil nutrients and water. Removing extra shoots leaves only two or three strong ones, ensuring the main tree produces larger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ awuu koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha niji 2-3 pɛ ahi shi koni tso titri lɛ awo panicles wuji.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my yam vines if the yam tuber grows deep underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi yɛ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves above ground need direct sunlight to make energy, which then travels down to feed and swell the tuber underground. Weeds block sunlight and steal valuable soil nutrients needed by the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛkɛ lɛ, efãa kɛyaa shi koni eyatao niyenii ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Jwɛi tsiɔ hulu la naa ni ejuɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa ni tubers lɛ taoɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to be harvested without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the main stem at ground level becomes noticeably thick.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni tso lɛ shishifã titri ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ eyɛ faŋŋ akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Pepper flowers drop without fruiting due to extreme heat, insufficient water, or lack of pollination by insects. Keeping the soil consistently moist and adding compost helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ hewɔ. Nu loo kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Kɛ́ oooha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my land improve the soil for the next crop I plant?
ga: Te tsina ŋmeii ni madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants have friendly bacteria on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop finishes growing, that stored nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ yɛ helai ni haa mɔ he feɔ naanyo yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ egbe naa lɛ Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: During peak heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. Adding dry grass around the base of the plant keeps the soil cool and holds moisture longer so the plant does not stress.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛfataa Tsei lɛ ashishitoo he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei enaaa nɔnyɛɛ.

english: Is it safe to use water carried from a nearby stream or dam for my young maize crop during the dry period?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa loo faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii kɛha mi-baby corn ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, as long as the water is fresh and free from harsh chemicals or salt. Sourcing water from nearby streams or dams during dry spells helps young crops stay alive until the main rains arrive.
ga: Hɛɛ, be fɛɛ be ni nu lɛ mli tse ni tsofai ni mli wa loo ŋoo bɛ mli lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa kɛjɛɔ faai loo faai ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔi wuji lɛ baashɛ.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable crops early in the morning or late at night?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ tsei anɔ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil absorbs the moisture before the hot sun turns it into steam, and any water on the leaves dries quickly so diseases do not spread.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ tsɔɔ mli etsɔɔ lasu. Ni nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ gbiɔ oya koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning yellow and falling off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing and dropping leaves is a plant's way of saving water when it feels thirsty. The plant sheds leaves to cut down on water loss, but regular watering will help it grow new, healthy leaves.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ nu he kɛ́ kumai miiye amɛ. Tsei ni shwieɔ baai koni nu ni laajeɔ lɛ aba shi Shi nu ni afɔɔ amɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni baai heei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my bean plants producing many flowers, but the flowers drop off before making pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ?

english: Bean flowers drop when the air becomes too hot and dry or when the plant does not get enough steady water. Keeping the soil evenly moist prevents the plant from shedding its blossoms.
ga: Pea fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ daa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ baatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crop is wilting because it needs water or because it is sick with a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho ejaakɛ nu he miihia amɛ loo hela emɔ amɛ?

english: A thirsty crop usually droops during the hottest part of the day and bounces back in the cool evening after watering. A diseased plant stays wilted even after you give it water and during cool nights.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ fɔɔ shwiemɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Ni ebaaku esɛɛ eba yɛ gbɛkɛ ni mli ejɔ mli beni efɔ nu lɛ sɛɛ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ baaya nɔ agbi kɛji okɛ nu ha amɛ po kɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why is my cassava able to survive long dry spells while my maize dies without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ gboɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava stores extra food and water deep inside its underground roots and can drop its leaves to sleep through the dry season, whereas maize has shallow roots and needs constant water to stay alive.
ga: Cassava toɔ niyenii kɛ nu yɛ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ, ni ebaanyɛ eshi ebaai lɛ ni amɛkã shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli fɛɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni nu he miihia lɛ daa koni ehi shi.

english: Why is my maize growing tall and thin without producing big cobs?
