ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni toi wuji bɛ he lɛ?

english: Maize grows tall and weak when seeds are planted too close together, causing them to fight for sunlight, water, and food. Spacing them properly allows each plant to get enough nutrients to grow thick stalks and large cobs.
ga: Abɛi daa ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Enɛ haa akaŋshii baa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why did my okra seeds fail to sprout after I planted them in dry ground and watered them only once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ shikome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need moisture continuously for several days to soften their hard outer shells and push roots out. If the soil dries completely after the first day, the seed stops growing and dies.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ gbii babaoo mli koni amɛha kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ mli awa ni amɛtsi shishifãi lɛ kɛje kpo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi lɛ sɛɛ Dumɔwui lɛ kpaɔ amɛkwɛ̃mɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why does putting dry grass around my yam mounds make the yams grow larger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ miibɔle Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni ato lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Covering yam mounds with dry grass acts like a protective blanket. It blocks the scorching sun from drying out the soil, keeps the roots cool, and slowly decays into rich food for the tubers.
ga: Kɛ akɛ jwɛi ha sweet potatoes ni ato lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ mɔ he. Etsĩɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛfite fiofio ni amɛfee niyenii ni jara wa kɛha ŋmeii lɛ.

english: What is the difference between the main crop season and the light crop season for crops like oil palm and cocoa?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ oil palm kɛ cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be titri kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ teŋ?

english: The main crop season comes after periods of heavy rainfall when trees have enough water to produce abundant, large fruits. The light season occurs during periods of lower rainfall, causing trees to produce smaller yields and fruits as they conserve water and energy.
ga: Be titri ni ŋmɔ lɛ daa lɛ baa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be ko sɛɛ. Enɛ ji be mli ni tsei lɛ náa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni amɛwo babaoo. La be lɛ baa be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo. Enɛ haaa tsei awo yibii kɛ nu babaoo ejaakɛ amɛbuɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my oil palm trees produce much smaller fruit bunches during dry periods of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii babaoo yɛ afi lɛ mli hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees depend heavily on water to fill out their fruit bunches. During dry months or light rain seasons, the tree slows down fruit development to protect itself from water stress, leading to smaller bunches.
ga: Mu tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nu nɔ waa koni amɛkɛwo amɛyibii akui lɛ amli ekoŋŋ. Yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ loo nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, la fioo pɛ yɔɔ. Tsei haa aduawai lɛ yaa hiɛ fioo koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu mli haomɔ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji niji bibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their blossoms during extremely hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive heat stresses pepper plants, causing flower pollen to dry out before pollination occurs. To protect itself from losing water, the plant sheds its blossoms until cooler conditions return.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ baa. Bɔni afee ni obu ohe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he Tsei lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or roots that are flooded with water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or improving field drainage helps the leaves regain their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo afee ni nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do flower blossoms drop off my cocoa trees without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers but can only support a small percentage as pods. If the tree lacks sufficient nutrients, water, or pollination by tiny insects, it drops excess flowers to save energy.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi ebaanyɛ eŋɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ. Kɛji tso ko bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, loo kooloi fioo ko pɛ ni shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaajie fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why are the bottom fronds of my oil palm trees turning brown and dry while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: It is natural for older lower fronds to die off as the tree grows taller and focuses energy on new top leaves and fruit. However, if young upper leaves also turn yellow, the soil may be missing key nutrients like potassium.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ baagboi be mli ni tso lɛ daa ni baai heei kɛ aduawai lɛ shwereɔ yɛ ŋmeii heei anɔ lɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get soft black spots on the bottom while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ diji ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɛ shishigbɛ kɛ́ adu lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering where the soil dries out completely between rains.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow tall with many leaves but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai kakadaji babaoo shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil contains too much nitrogen, cassava plants put all their energy into growing leaves and stems above ground instead of sending nutrients down to build large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛba shi koni ekɛfee bulbs agboi

english: Why do plantain leaves split and tear into strips when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain baai lɛ fãa ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves naturally tear along their side veins during windy weather. This deliberate design reduces wind resistance, preventing the whole trunk from snapping or being uprooted.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ fãji ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ amli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Nɛkɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ afee nɛɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ mɔ naa lɛ baa shi. Etsiɔ tsei lɛ anaa koni akakumɔ loo ajie kɛjɛ amɛshishi.

english: How does heavy shade from big trees affect how my crops grow?
ga: Te hulutsoo ni mli wa ni jɛɔ tsei wuji amli lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food and grow strong. While light shade protects young seedlings from scorching, heavy shade starves crops of light, causing weak stems and lower harvests.
ga: Tsei hia hulu la ni tsoɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛye niyenii ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Eyɛ mli akɛ hulutsoo be ni mli tse lɛ baabu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ shãa he moŋ. Shi hulutsoo be ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ baaha tso lɛ akaná la. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants keep wilting and drying up when I plant them in an open field without any larger trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight because their tender leaves burn and lose moisture faster than roots can draw water. They require shade from trees or plantains to shield them until their roots and branches mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, cacao tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛshwieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei loo tsei bibii amli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛniji lɛ baadara.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb up tall wooden stakes instead of just spreading across the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce energy for growing big underground tubers. Lifting the vines off the ground also protects the leaves from rotting in damp soil.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hu buɔ tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of a maize plant mean the crop lacks nitrogen. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to the top leaves to keep growing, which makes the lower leaves lose their green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa baa lɛ mli koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara. Enɛ haa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of green leaves, but the tubers under the ground are very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa tsɔ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or grows in heavy shade, it puts all its energy into growing tall stems and bushy leaves instead of storing energy in the root tubers underground.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ tsei kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: Why do my tomato plants produce lots of flowers, but the flowers dry up and drop off without forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather becomes too hot or when soil water levels swing suddenly between very dry and very wet. This stress causes the plant to drop flowers to protect itself.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ nɔ ni edɔ waa teŋ. Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu ehe.

english: Why do my watermelons crack open right on the farm before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miitswa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Watermelons split open when heavy rain or sudden watering follows a long dry period. The inside of the fruit expands rapidly with water faster than the outer skin can stretch.
ga: Watermelons tswaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa loo nu ho trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amligbɛ lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya kɛ nu oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why does swamp rice grow well in flooded water while my maize rots and dies if water sits on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋshɔŋ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu afua mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ ni egboɔ kɛji nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have internal air passages in their stems that carry oxygen down to their roots underwater, whereas maize roots cannot breathe in standing water and drown.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa nu shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi nyɛŋ amu nu ni yɔɔ dioo mli ni amɛgboi.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or mites feeding under the leaves, or by viral diseases spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli.

english: Why does my main plantain tree grow so slowly when there are many small shoots growing around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ be mli ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛi babaoo ni miida yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ he?

english: The small shoots, called suckers, compete directly with the main plantain tree for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight, which starves the main stem and slows its growth.
ga: Tso bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu. Niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la, ni baaha tso titri lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ebaaha ekwɛ̃ fioo.

english: Why do groundnut flowers open above the soil, but the actual nuts end up growing underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fɔfɔii gbeleɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, shi ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, they grow long stems called pegs that bend down and push themselves deep into the soil, where the nuts safely form away from heat and animals.
ga: Beni amɛwo ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen sɛɛ lɛ Amɛyɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs. ni baabɔle ehe ni ekɛ ehe awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ afee, shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ahe.

english: Is it better for me to burn my land before planting, or should I leave the cleared plants on the ground?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã shikpɔŋ lɛ dani adu nii loo esa akɛ mashi tsei ni ajie lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Leaving cleared vegetation on the ground without burning keeps the soil cool and moist, protects it from being washed away by rain, and saves you the heavy labor and costs required to manage burnt land.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni ajie lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ashãaa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Tsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa ni ekɛ nitsumɔ ni tsii kɛ shika ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ ni eshã lɛ nɔ lɛ akatsu nii.

english: Does burning bush help kill pests in the soil, or does it harm my crops in the long run?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni ashãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi loo eyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awui yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: While burning may clear surface pests temporarily, it destroys essential soil life like earthworms and beneficial bacteria, leaving the soil hard and nutrient-poor, which hurts crop growth over time.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ shãa baanyɛ ajie ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli moŋ, shi ekpataa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahiɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli. Enɛ saa tsei lɛ adalɛ he yɛ gbɛ fɔŋ nɔ yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli.

english: Will my plantain suckers get enough nutrients if I do not burn the bush before planting them?
ga: Ani mi plantain suckers lɛ baaná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛji mishãaa jwɛi lɛ dani midu?

english: Yes, as the unburned leaves and weeds rot on the ground, they slowly break down into natural fertilizer, giving your plantains a steady supply of nutrients without burning up the valuable organic matter.
ga: Nakai eji, ejaakɛ baai kɛ jwɛi ni ashãko lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaafee fiofio Efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii Ehaa o-plantains lɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ daa ni eshãaa nibii ni jara wa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my plantains struggle to grow when the sun gets very hot during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems and large leaves that lose moisture quickly in strong heat. Protecting the soil with a layer of unburned plant cover helps trap moisture in the ground so the roots stay hydrated.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai wuji ni kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa ba lɛ, amɛmli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni shãaa lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How does leaving plant debris on my farm help prevent weeds from growing back quickly?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ oya?

english: A thick layer of unburned plant matter acts like a cover over the soil, blocking sunlight from reaching weed seeds beneath it and significantly slowing down their ability to sprout.
ga: Tsei ni ashãko lɛ ni mli tse lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔ ko. Etsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ahe. ni ehaa amɛnyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ baa shi waa.

english: I want to start a plantain farm, but my soil gets dry very fast. What simple step can I take during land preparation to keep the soil moist?
ga: Miisumɔ ni obɔi plantain ŋmɔ shi shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya waa. Mɛni ji nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni atsɔɔ nɔ asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Avoid burning the bush after clearing. Chopping the weeds and leaves and spreading them over the field creates a natural blanket that stops water from evaporating out of the soil.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ jwɛi lɛ ni oooshã beni ojie jwɛi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ he. Jwɛi kɛ baai ni afoɔ ni agbɛɔ ashwãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ko ni tsiɔ nu naa koni ekajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops perform better when I leave organic leaves on the ground instead of burning them away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mishi mi-organic baai lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ lɛ?

english: Unburned organic leaves act like a sponge that absorbs rain, keeps the earth soft for root growth, and continuously feeds your crops as the leaves rot into rich topsoil.
ga: Organic baai ni ashãko lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji, ni amɛmɔɔ nugbɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo kɛha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ. ni okɛ niyenii aha onibii lɛ be fɛɛ be be mli ni baai lɛ fiteɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why does burning my farm make my workload harder in the long run?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ ni mashã lɛ baaha minitsumɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni wa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Fire exposes the bare ground to direct heat, making the soil hard to dig and triggering fast-growing weeds to invade quickly, which forces you to spend much more time and energy weeding later.
ga: La haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli taomɔ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni ewoɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛba oya Enɛ nyɛɔ onɔ ni okɛ be kɛ hewalɛ babaoo atsuɔ jwɛi lɛ ahe nii yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: How can I prepare my land for planting plantains if I do not have enough money to hire extra help?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ asaa shikpɔŋ kɛha plantains dumɔ? Kɛji obɛ shika ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛbaahe yelikɛbuamɔ kroko?

english: You can clear the vegetation with a cutlass and leave it directly on the soil instead of gathering and burning it. This saves you the money and energy needed for fire control and heavy farm cleanup.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ dade ajie tsei lɛ ni okɛshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaabua naa ni ashã lɛ Enɛ haa shika kɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni he hiaa kɛha la nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔ mli saamɔ baa shi.

english: How can I reduce the money I spend on labor when starting a new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafo shika ni mifiteɔ yɛ nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔwoo mli lɛ shi kɛ́ mije ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: By choosing not to burn your cleared farm, you eliminate the labor needed to clear ash and fight off aggressive fire-loving weeds, allowing you to manage the field easily with less hired labor.
ga: Halamɔ ni akɛshãaa ŋmɔji ni ajie lɛ Enɛ baajie nitsumɔ ni he hiaa koni akɛjie sũ lɛ ni akɛwuu ashi jwɛi ni sumɔɔ la lɛ kɛya. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ kɛ nitsumɔ fioo pɛ.

english: How do I know if my land has the right soil for planting maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni sa kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Good maize soil holds moisture well without becoming waterlogged, feels dark and rich, and isn't too sandy or hard clay. Getting your soil checked by an extension officer helps you confirm if it has the right nutrients before you invest in planting.
ga: Abɛi shikpɔŋ kpakpa baanyɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni nu bɛ mli. Enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ duŋ ni eyɛ nii. Ejeee ŋã tsɔ loo nɔ ni wa tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni extension nitsulɔ ko baafee lɛ baaye abua bo ni okwɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni sa dani okɛ shika awo dumɔ mli.

english: Why do crops grow very well on one side of my farm but fail on the other side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fa kome shi amɛkwɛɛɛ yɛ fa kroko lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil depth, water drainage, and nutrient levels can vary across a single piece of land. Areas where water collects or where the soil is too hard will cause crops to struggle compared to richer, well-drained spots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ, nu ni hoɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baanyɛ afee srɔtoi yɛ he fɛɛ he. Hei ni nu buaa ehe naa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii afee mlɛo kɛ akɛto hei ni baa nii ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Is it true that every type of fruit or crop I plant has its own specific disease?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ aduawai loo ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni miduɔ lɛ yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehela?

english: Yes, almost every crop has specific diseases that target it, such as black pod in cocoa or mosaic virus in cassava. Learning the specific signs for your crop helps you spot problems early before they spread.
ga: Hɛɛ, nɔ ni miihe ashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ yɛ hela pɔtɛɛ ko ni esa akɛ ekɛ ehiɛ afɔ nɔ, tamɔ black pod ni yɔɔ cocoa mli loo mosaic virus ni yɔɔ cassava mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okase okadii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona naagbai mra. Dani naagba lɛ baagbɛ eshwa

english: How can I tell if my plant is sick from a disease or just needs water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela emɔ mitso lɛ loo nu kɛkɛ he miihia lɛ?

english: Thirsty plants usually droop during the hot afternoon and revive in the cool morning, whereas diseased plants show permanent signs like spots, yellow patches, stunted growth, or rotting stems even after you water them.
ga: Tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ fɔɔ shwiemɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni amɛbaa wala mli ekoŋŋ yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ baatsɔɔ okadii ni hiɔ shi daa tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. stunted growth Aloo tso lɛ shishi lɛ miifite beni okɛ nu wo mli po sɛɛ.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing on cassava is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by small whiteflies or infected stem cuttings. Using disease-free planting stems stops this from happening.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yucca mosaic hela lɛ kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. Akɛ ŋmeii bibii loo tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ haa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni hela bɛ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi enɛ naa.

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in damp, overly shaded farms. Pruning heavy shade trees and clearing weeds helps air flow through the farm to prevent it.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Tsei ni tsii ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni aaafolɔ ashwie shi ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ aya nɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ebu he.

english: Who can I call in my area to help me identify a plant disease I don't recognize?
ga: Namɔ manyɛ matsɛ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ koni eye ebua mi ni mana tso hela ko ni mileee he nɔ ko?

english: You can reach out to your local agricultural extension officer from the Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA), who can visit your farm, identify the disease, and give you the correct treatment advice.
ga: Obaanyɛ oya okwaafoi anitsumɔ he nitsulɔ ni jɛ Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe (MoFA) lɛ ŋɔɔ, ni baanyɛ ayasara okwaafoi lɛ, ni ena hela lɛ, ni ewo bo ŋaa yɛ tsofafeemɔ ni ja he.

english: How can I be sure that the seeds I buy in the market will give me a high harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ baawo yibii babaoo?

english: To guarantee good yields, buy certified seeds in sealed packages from registered agro-dealers rather than loose market seeds, as certified seeds are tested to resist diseases and produce better crops.
ga: koni akɛha nibii kpakpai aba Hemɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase yɛ kotokui ni akɛwo mli lɛ amli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ adɛŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohe dumɔwui yɛ jarayelihe lɛ Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, akaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ akwɛɔ koni amɛnyɛŋ helai amɔ amɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I stop a plant disease from spreading from one tree to the rest of my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tsei ahe helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa miŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ amli lɛ naa?

english: You should prune and safely destroy infected leaves or branches, sanitize your cutlasses with soap or alcohol between trees, and immediately remove dead plants so insects don't carry the disease to healthy ones.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ baai loo tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ shweshweeshwe. Okɛ samla loo dãa agbe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ. ni ojie tsei ni egboi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni kooloi akatsɔ helai amɛha tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off before making pepper?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani pepper lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, lack of water, missing soil nutrients, or attacks from tiny pests like thrips. Ensuring steady watering and pest control keeps the flowers intact.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Aloo tutuamɔi ni jɛɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips mli. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Why should I leave my farmland to rest for a season instead of planting crops on it every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ koni miyajɔɔ mihe be kome yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii daa afi lɛ?

english: Just like a human body gets exhausted without rest, soil loses its nutrients when crops are grown continuously. Leaving the land to rest gives it time to recover naturally, allowing organic matter to rebuild so your future crops will yield much more.
ga: Taakɛ bɔ ni adesa gbɔmɔtso lɛ nijiaŋ jeɔ wui kɛji ejɔɔɔ ehe lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ be mli ni aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii be fɛɛ be lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aaaha ejɔɔ ehe lɛ haa enáa be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ ehee ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni onibii ni obaadu wɔsɛɛ lɛ awo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my young maize plants turn yellow and stay small if I plant them before the main rains start fully?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛhiɔ shi bibii kɛji midu amɛ dani nugbɔ wuji lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛyaa lɛ?

english: Young maize roots need a steady supply of soil moisture to absorb essential nutrients like nitrogen. When rains are irregular at the start of the season, the roots suffer from water stress and cannot feed the plant, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ daa lɛ he miihia ŋmeii bibii lɛ ashishifãi koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli. Nu he haomɔ saa shishifãi lɛ ahe ni amɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛ ha tso lɛ niyenii. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Cassava roots need space underground to expand, and their leaves need space to catch sunlight. Planting them too close forces the plants to fight for water, light, and soil nutrients, resulting in small, thin tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ shishi he ko koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Ni esa akɛ ebaai lɛ aná he ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehe woɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, yitso lɛ ji bibioo ni eyɛ mlɛo.

english: Why should I cut off some of the leaves and extra branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai kɛ niji ni eshwɛ lɛ ekomɛi?

english: When tomato plants grow too many leaves, they spend all their energy maintaining foliage instead of building fruit. Trimming useless leaves and side shoots directs the plant's energy straight into producing larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Kɛji tomato tso ko yɛ baai babaoo Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii. Baai ni he ehiaaa kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ koni ekɛwo tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my pepper plants without turning into peppers after I spray chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper beni mikɛ tsofai eshwie nɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers need beneficial insects like bees to pollinate them before they can form peppers. Spraying harsh chemicals during the flowering stage kills these helpful insects and shocks the plant, causing it to drop its flowers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii, koni amɛwo amɛmli dani amɛfee pepper. Tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ baagbe nɛkɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ. ni eha tso lɛ he fee lɛ yaa Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji fɔfɔi lɛ ni gbee shi.

english: Why do agricultural officers ask me to cover the bare soil around my crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ biɔ ni mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass acts like a protective shade that stops the sun from drying out the ground too quickly. It holds moisture around the roots longer and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Mulch ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo be ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa koni ekagbi shikpɔŋ lɛ oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ, ni ehaaa jwɛi lɛ akaye nɔ.

english: Why is it harmful to plant garden eggs on the exact same piece of land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmeii yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Specific pests and soil diseases that attack garden eggs build up in the ground over time. Changing to a different crop, like maize or beans, starves those specific pests and keeps your soil healthy.
ga: Nibii pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni tutuaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Ni oootsake kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi anɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Ebaaha hɔmɔ aye tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi ni ebaaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds while my crops are still tiny seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji dumɔwui bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are weak and easily overpowered by fast-growing weeds. Clearing weeds early ensures your young crops get all the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without having to compete.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ yeɔ amɛnɔ kunim oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni odumɔwui lɛ aná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe akaŋ akaŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for the crop I plant next?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha tsei ni miduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil. When the crop is harvested, that trapped nitrogen stays in the earth as free fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa efeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I harvest my maize as soon as the cobs look big and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikpaa ŋmãa kɛji ŋmãa lɛ fee tamɔ agbo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ pɛ?

english: While green maize can be eaten fresh, the grains inside are still filling up with starch. Allowing the cobs to dry fully on the plant lets the grains reach maximum weight and hardness, which makes them last much longer in storage.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ abaanyɛ aye ŋmãa ni eŋɔli lɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ, shi ŋmãa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmãa lolo. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmei lɛ agbi kwraa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ ashɛ amɛhe ni tsii fe fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe ni wa fe fɛɛ. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ atoɔ he gbɛjianɔ be kakadaŋŋ fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded together, they struggle and compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients like nitrogen. This lack of nutrients causes their lower leaves to turn yellow and reduces the overall harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ Amɛwuɔ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii tamɔ nitrogen he. Niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ ni bɛ lɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa yibiiwoo fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Fall Armyworms usually have an inverted white 'Y' mark on their heads and four dark spots arranged in a square on their tail ends. They leave large, ragged holes in the leaves and deposit saw-dust-like waste inside the central shoot of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms lɛ yɛ ‘Y’ okadi yɛŋ ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ yɛ amɛyitsei anɔ kɛ ŋmeii diji ejwɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ amɛtsitsii lɛ anaa. Amɛshiɔ bu agboi ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli ni amɛbua jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmeii anaa yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer near the roots instead of spreading it on the plant stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ moŋ fe nɔ ni mawo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: A crop's roots are designed to absorb water and dissolved nutrients from the soil. Placing fertilizer directly on stems can cause chemical burns to the plant, whereas putting it near the roots feeds the crop safely and efficiently.
ga: Afee tsei shishifãi koni amɛgbala nu kɛ niyenii ni mli edɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsofa ashã tso lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii shweshweeshwe ni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and tender leaves that cannot survive heavy sun and dry winds. Planting shade crops like plantains or shade trees alongside cocoa keeps the soil moist and shields the young trees from hot sunlight.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebuɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava plants have tall stems with big green leaves but very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ lɛ? baai wuji eŋɔli Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to push most of their energy into growing leaves and stems above ground instead of developing tubers below. Balancing soil nutrients helps the plant store energy in large roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmei tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtoɔ hewalɛ amɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi wuji lɛ amli.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts between my crop rows improve my farm soil?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni midu yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have natural bacteria in their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil. This enriches the ground naturally, feeding neighboring crops without extra commercial fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa tsei ni yeɔ naagbai lɛ niyenii ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are too high or when water supply is irregular. Extreme heat prevents proper pollination, so the plant sheds the unpollinated flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ akafite hewalɛ lɛ, amɛfoɔ fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do swollen, watery bumps appear on the branches of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ edema je kpo yɛ mi-kookoo niji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Swollen branches on cocoa trees are a sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease, spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. The disease blocks the flow of nutrients inside the tree, reducing yield and eventually killing the plant if left unchecked.
ga: Kookoo tsei aniji ni efuu lɛ ji kookoo hela hela, ni koolooi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Hela nɛɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi, ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ agbo kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's hybrid maize harvest produce smaller ears than fresh certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ wo toi bibii fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yields, but their offspring lose those strong, high-performing traits in the second generation. Planting fresh certified seeds every season ensures consistent crop size and better disease resistance.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi amɛshwiei lɛ baafite amɛsui ni mli wa ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni aduɔ daa be lɛ haa tso lɛ dalɛ yaa nɔ daa ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when heavy rain sits on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits continuously without draining, it smothers the roots and creates damp conditions where harmful soil fungi multiply, causing the tubers to rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu yɔɔ be fɛɛ be ni ejeee kpo lɛ Nu lɛ hoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ faa yɛ mli lɛ baa. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize crops turning yellow while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build strong, green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure around the roots helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni akɛfataa he lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: What is the actual benefit of putting dried animal manure on my field instead of just using chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi diɛŋtsɛ ni yɔɔ kooloi ashishifãi ni egbi ni akɛaawo ŋmɔji amli yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔji amli kɛkɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ he?

english: Animal manure improves your soil like a sponge, helping it hold onto water much longer during dry spells and feeding the soil naturally over time, while chemical fertilizers only give a quick boost of food directly to the plant without improving the soil itself.
ga: Manure haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo tamɔ sponji. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. ni ekɛ niyenii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kɛ niyenii pɛ fataa tsei ahe tɛ̃ɛ oya ni ehaaa sũ lɛ aya hiɛ kwraa.

english: Why do people advise me to plant plantains on my farmland before putting down new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants dry out easily under the hot sun. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the vital shade and cooler moisture young cocoa seedlings need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi oya. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa shade ni he hia kɛ hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ. Ehe miihia ni kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How do I choose the right cassava sticks from my farm to cut and plant for the next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei ni sa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mafolɔ ni madu kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Select mature, healthy plants that are 8 to 12 months old and free from diseases. Cut your planting sticks from the firm middle section of the main stem, avoiding the soft green top parts and the overly dry bottom base.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 ni hela bɛ amɛhe. Kpɔ̃ɔ niji kɛjɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ teŋgbɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ shishi ni egbi tsɔ lɛ he.

english: Why is it bad if I sow my maize seeds very close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops end up fighting each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with tall, thin plants with small, weak cobs instead of strong plants with large yields.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tso kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmei bibioo ni bɛ hewalɛ yɔɔ mli yɛ tso ni wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do I need to erect tall wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mato tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves high into the air to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food for the growing underground tuber. Keeping leaves off the wet ground also protects them from fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni miida lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ baai lɛ to shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ hu, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: What is causing small, dark caterpillars to eat holes inside the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ lɛ yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds on the soft growing leaves of young maize. You can manage them by checking your crop early and applying recommended pesticides or localized treatments like neem leaf extractions into the central funnel.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ni oookwɛ mli mra lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akɛtsaa he ko he ko ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii, tamɔ neem baai ni ajieɔ kɛyaa faa ko ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. When temperatures get too hot or the soil dries out completely, the plant sheds its blossoms to save energy and water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Trees bloom to conserve energy and water.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable garden in the middle of the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: It is much better to water early in the morning so the plant roots can drink water before the heat of the day sets in. Watering in the hot afternoon causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before reaching the plant roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu lɛ leebi bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu nu lɛ dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ aba.Nu ni oooha yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani eshɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my stored maize grains develop tiny holes and turn into white powder after a few months in the room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni etsɔ powda yɛŋ beni ehi tsu lɛ mli nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ?

english: Grain insects called weevils eat through the stored maize from the inside out. To stop this, ensure your maize is sun-dried until it is bone-dry before storing it in airtight bags (like PICS bags) or treating it with approved grain storage dust.
ga: Grain-bearing insects called weevils eat stored corn from the inside out. Bɔni afee ni okpa enɛ Kwɛmɔ ni o-ŋmã lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi fãji lɛ agbi dani okɛwo vacuum kotoku mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku) loo okɛ sũ ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu he nii.

english: Why do the maize seeds I buy from certified seed companies grow so much better than the seeds I saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ahe nitsumɔhei ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are produced under strict quality standards to ensure high germination rates, disease resistance, and genetic purity. When you plant saved seeds from hybrid crops, the plants lose those special qualities, resulting in uneven growth, weaker crops, and lower yields.
ga: Certified seeds are produced under strict quality standards to ensure high germination rates, disease resistance and genetic purity. Beni oduɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ. The plant will lose those special properties. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ egbɔjɔ. ni nibii ni anáa lɛ ba shi

english: Why do my crops grow at different heights and mature at different times when I use my own saved seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa yɛ hei srɔtoi ni amɛdaraa yɛ bei srɔtoi amli beni mikɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ midumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their genetic uniformity over time due to natural cross-pollination. Certified seeds are carefully bred and multiplied so that every plant in your field has the exact same genetics, causing them to grow at the same pace and mature all at once.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ laajeɔ bɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ha yɛ be mli yɛ adebɔɔ mli cross-pollination hewɔ. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni agbɛɔ amɛshwãa. Enɛ ji koni tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aná fɔmɔ su kome pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛdaraa oya nɔŋŋ ni amɛdaraa shikome.

english: Why does my crop yield drop so drastically if I keep replanting seeds from the same farm year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi waa kɛji midu dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Crops experience genetic degeneration over generations when seeds are reused. The plants lose their vigor, produce smaller fruits, and become more vulnerable to local pests and diseases compared to fresh certified seeds.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ naa fitemɔ kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli kɛji akɛ atsake dumɔwui lɛ. Tsei lɛ ahe waaa, amɛwoɔ yibii bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ oya kɛha maŋ lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: What is the difference between the foundation seeds created by researchers and the certified seeds sold in shops?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ shishitoo dumɔwui ni niiamlitaolɔi fee lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ shwapoi amli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Foundation seeds are the pure early-stage seeds produced directly by plant researchers to preserve a new crop variety. Private seed companies then plant those foundation seeds to multiply them into large quantities of certified seeds, which are packaged and tested specifically for farmers to grow.
ga: Primer dumɔwui ji dumɔwui krɔŋŋ ni tsei ahe niiamlitaolɔi feɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkɛbu tsei srɔtoi heei ahe. No sɛɛ lɛ, dumɔwui ahe nitsumɔhei ni ji aŋkroaŋkroi lɛ duɔ nakai shishijee dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛha amɛfee dumɔwui babaoo ni awo he odaseyeli. ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli ni akaa lɛ akwɛɔ pɔtɛɛ koni okwaafoi lɛ akwɛ

english: Why do newly developed certified crop varieties handle drought and dry weather better than my traditional seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei srɔtoi heei ni afee ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ tsuɔ hɔmɔ kɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi ahe nii jogbaŋŋ fe mi blema dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Plant breeders specifically select parent plants with traits like deeper root systems or efficient water use to create improved varieties. When these breeder traits are passed down to certified seeds, the resulting crops naturally handle heat and dry spells much better.
ga: Mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ halaa tsei ni ji fɔlɔi ni yɔɔ sui tamɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ koni akɛfee tsei srɔtoi ni hi fe tsutsu lɛ. Beni akɛ fɔlɔi asui nɛɛ haa dumɔwui ni awo amɛ he odase lɛ. Tsei ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ nyɛɔ amɛkpeɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ naa jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do certified seeds produce fruits and grains that are much more uniform in size and quality?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ woɔ yibii kɛ ŋmaa ni amɛdalɛ kɛ amɛhe feɔ ekome kwraa lɛ?

english: Certified seeds originate from pure breeder lines where every seed carries identical genes. This means all the plants absorb nutrients and flower in the same way, producing uniform crops that are easier to harvest and sell for higher market prices.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛlɔi diɛŋtsɛ adɛŋ. Dumɔwui fɛɛ yɛ wala yibii kome. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei fɛɛ ŋɔɔ niyenii kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei ni amɛhe yɔɔ ekome ni akpamɔ waaa ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do crops grown from certified seeds seem to resist common farm pests better than local varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli mli lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ fe tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Agricultural researchers actively breed natural pest and disease resistance into breeder and foundation seeds. These defensive traits stay strong in certified seeds, giving your growing crops built-in protection against common field diseases.
ga: Okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi kɛ ekãa miikwɛ adebɔɔ mli helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shishitoo dumɔwui lɛ. Nɛkɛ hebuu sui nɛɛ yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi waa yɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ amli. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii ni okwɛɔ lɛ hebuu ni ama awo mli kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli helai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why can't I buy certified seeds directly from government research institutions in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ nɔyeli niiamlitaomɔ he ko ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ?

english: By law in Ghana, government research centers focus on developing new crop varieties and producing breeder and foundation seeds. The law leaves the commercial multiplication and sale of certified seeds to licensed private seed companies so seeds are widely distributed to local markets.
ga: Taakɛ mla ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ, Nɔyeli lɛ niiamlitaomɔ hei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa tsei srɔtoi heei afeemɔ nɔ. kɛ broodstock dumɔwui kɛ shishifãi afeemɔ. Mla lɛ shiɔ jarayeli nitsumɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ ahɔ̃ɔmɔ ehaa aŋkroaŋkroi, dumɔwui nitsumɔhei ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni aja dumɔwui lɛ babaoo kɛya maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ.

english: Why is it illegal for me to produce and sell my own seeds as 'certified seeds' to other farmers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bo diɛŋtsɛ odumɔwui afeemɔ kɛ amɛhɔ̃ɔmɔ ji akɛ No hewɔ lɛ ani eji mlakwamɔ akɛ oooha ‘dumɔwui ni awo he odase’ okwaafoi krokomɛi?

english: Ghanaian seed laws reserve certified seed production for licensed seed companies to protect farmers from poor-quality or diseased seeds. Producing certified seeds requires specialized inspection, lab testing, and field isolation that standard farming does not provide.
ga: Ghana dumɔwui mla toɔ dumɔwui afeemɔ he odaseyeli kɛha dumɔwui nitsumɔhei ni yɔɔ gbɛŋmɛɛ wolo. Koni abu okwaafoi ahe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni ehiii loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe. Dumɔwui afeemɔ ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ biɔ kwɛmɔi krɛdɛɛi. Laboratory kaa kɛ ŋmɔ mli mligbalamɔ ni okwaayeli ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ haaa.

english: How can I be sure that the seed packet I buy from an agro-dealer in Ghana will actually grow strong crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwui ahe paketii ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ dɛŋ lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Official certified seeds in Ghana come sealed with authorized certification tags from regulatory inspectors. These tags prove that the seed batch passed strict tests for disease freedom, high germination rate, and genetic purity before being sold.
ga: Akɛ odaseyeli okadi ni mlai ahe nilelɔi eŋmɛ gbɛ lɛ fĩɔ dumɔwui ni maŋ lɛ eŋmɛ gbɛ yɛ Ghana lɛ naa. Nɛkɛ kadimɔi nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui akuu lɛ etsɔ kaa ni mli wa mli kɛha hela bɛ mli. shweremɔ ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ fɔmɔ nii ahe tsemɔ dani ajaa

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there are no plantain trees planted next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui komɛi bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct, hot sunlight. Planting plantains nearby provides fast-growing leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool soil moisture it needs to survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaha baai lɛ adara oya, ni amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves and small worms hiding inside the stalks?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni Akɛtee yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ anɔ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that eats young corn leaves and stem growing points. Spraying targeted safe insecticides or applying neem oil early in the morning or late evening helps protect your crop before the worms destroy the harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ shwie nɔ loo okɛ neem fɔ wo nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe dani kooloi lɛ akpata amɛhiɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which crops need to build healthy green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen-based fertilizer will help your corn regain its deep green color and produce larger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii awo baai ni wa, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in tiny knots on their roots. When the plant roots break down after harvest, that nitrogen stays behind in the soil as free food for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds prevent my crops from growing big even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi tsiɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkadara eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ amɛmli moŋ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that steal water, light, and fertilizer away from your main crops. Clearing weeds early ensures all the nutrients you add go straight into feeding your crops instead of wild plants.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu, la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni okɛfataa he lɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Yɛ koo mli tso najiaŋ

english: Why shouldn't I sow my maize seeds right after the very first rainy day of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry stretch before the main rains begin. Seeds planted too early will sprout with the first moisture but then dry out and die in the soil during the hot spell that follows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔi wuji lɛ jeɔ shishi. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ. Shi no sɛɛ lɛ, egbiɔ ni egboɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Which way should I point the eyes on a cassava stem cutting when sticking it into the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ miifo ŋmei lɛ, nɛgbɛ esa akɛ makwɛ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the buds or leaf nodes pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the new shoots to curve around underwater, making the plant weak and reducing root tuber yield.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii loo baai lɛ ashishigbɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha tsei heei atsɔ nu shishi. Ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa shishifãi ni baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Yams are climbing vines that need physical support to lift their green leaves off the ground toward sunlight. Exposing more leaves to sunshine allows the plant to make more food, resulting in much larger tubers under the ground.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa gbɔmɔtsoŋ yelikɛbuamɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai eŋɔli lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Babaoo ni hulu la kpɛɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, babaoo ni tso lɛ baanyɛ awo niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa.

english: Why should I cut off extra baby shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Having too many shoots around one plantain stem causes them to fight for nutrients, leading to small bunches. Cutting off extra shoots leaves only one main stem and one strong sucker, ensuring big, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Ni ooona plantain tsei ahe tsei babaoo tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛwuu kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ. causing a small bouquet Kɛ́ afo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii titri kome pɛ kɛ ŋmeii kome ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ shwɛɔ koni ekɛfee panicle agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Black rotted bottoms on tomatoes, known as blossom-end rot, happen when the plant cannot get enough calcium, usually due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the roots draw up calcium steadily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni fiteɔ yɛ tomato nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ blossom end fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjie calcium be fɛɛ be.

english: How do I know if my soil is good enough for growing cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ?

english: Good cocoa soil should be deep, dark, well-drained, and rich in organic matter. It must hold moisture during dry periods without staying waterlogged when heavy rains fall.
ga: Esa akɛ kookoo shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ afee nɔ ni mli kwɔ, ni eyɛ ediŋŋ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo Esa akɛ ato ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ akabote mli.

english: How far apart should I plant my cocoa seedlings on the farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Cocoa trees are usually planted 3 meters by 3 meters apart so their branches and roots have enough space to grow without competing for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduɔ kookoo tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji mitai etɛ koni eha tsei niji kɛ shishifãi lɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛdara ni amɛkɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akaŋ akaŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily by direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide essential shade and protect soil moisture while the young cocoa matures.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he, yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the cocoa tree is receiving too much direct sunlight without enough shade cover, or the soil lacks vital nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ cacao tso lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Aloo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes the green cocoa pods on my trees to turn black and rot?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp conditions during rainy seasons when air cannot flow freely between overcrowded trees.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abɔle tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience severe stress, such as prolonged dry weather, lack of key nutrients, or pest attacks that weaken the plant.
ga: Cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ. niyenii mli nibii titrii ni bɛ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to prune the extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ kookoo tso nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to let sunlight and fresh air inside, which reduces fungal diseases and directs the tree's energy into producing bigger, healthier pods.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote mli. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What are these tiny insects damaging my young cocoa shoots and pods?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni miifite mi-kokoo ŋmɔji kɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ?

english: These are likely capsids, which are destructive pests that suck sap from young stems and pods, leaving dark spots that dry out the plant tissue and reduce yields.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji capsids, ni ji kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Eshiɔ hei ni tsuɔ ni haa tso lɛ mli fãji egbiɔ ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: How long will my newly planted cocoa trees take before they start bearing pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi-cacao tso ni midu ehee lɛ baaje shishi ekwɛ̃?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties start bearing fruit in about 2 to 3 years, while older traditional varieties usually take 4 to 5 years to produce pods.
ga: Kookoo ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛwoɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees stop producing pods and drop leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebaa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry Harmattan weather, cocoa trees naturally shed leaves to conserve internal water and protect themselves from drought, which temporarily pauses pod production.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be mli lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛ nu ato amɛmli ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he. Enɛ baaha pod feemɔ akpa.

english: My farmland stays very damp and cool ('dwoodwoo') most of the year; what crops grow best in this kind of wet soil?
ga: Miŋmɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni eyɛ fɛ̃i (‘dwoodwoo’) yɛ afi lɛ mli babaoo. Mɛɛ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ tamɔ nɛkɛ nɔ?

english: Damp, cool land holds water well, which is great for moisture-loving crops like sugarcane, cocoyam, and leafy vegetables, but crops like cassava or groundnuts will rot if the land does not drain properly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ lɛ hiɛɔ nu jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ ŋmei, kookoo kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai, shi ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei baafite kɛji akɛ atsɔko shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do crops grow much stronger on land where leaves have rotted for years compared to bare land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii daa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baai egbo afii babaoo lɛ nɔ fe shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Decayed leaves create organic matter that acts as natural food for the soil, helping it hold moisture better and providing essential nutrients that plant roots need to grow.
ga: Baai ni egboi lɛ feɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei shishifãi lɛ adalɛ.

english: Does it matter how deep I push my maize seeds into the ground when planting?
ga: Ani bɔ ni mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ mihaa beni miduɔ lɛ he hiaa mi?

english: Yes, planting seeds too deep starves them of oxygen before they reach sunlight, while planting too shallow exposes them to birds and heat drying them out; a depth of about 3 to 5 centimeters is ideal.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ baaye amɛ dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha okpoi aná amɛ ni latsaa lɛ baaha amɛgbi. A depth of about 3 to 5 centimeters is ideal.

english: Why do I get smaller harvests when I plant my crops very close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and groundwater, leading to thin stems and smaller yield.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with thick green leaves, but the roots under the ground stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil forces the cassava plant to spend all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛbaa lɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ ŋmei baato shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I clear all the large forest trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ koo mli cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight; large trees act as living umbrellas that shade the young crops and protect the soil from drying out.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo tsei, ni amɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ hulutsoo, ni amɛbuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp conditions; pruning thick leaves to let sunlight and wind into the farm helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ahe tsei lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ amli tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow with small holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bu bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Holes in yellowing leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the plant, which prevents the leaf from catching sunlight to feed the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ amli lɛ baa, ni no haaa baai lɛ amɔmɔ hulu la ni amɛkɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Watering early in the morning gives roots time to drink before the sun heat evaporates the water, preventing soil from drying out too fast and protecting leaves from heat stress.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ leebi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ nu dani hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya tsɔ. ni ebuɔ baai ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: If I leave my land to rest without planting for two years, why does my crop yield improve when I return?
ga: Kɛji mishi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni miduuu nii afii enyɔ Mɛni hewɔ mi nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ hi fe tsutsu lɛ beni miku misɛɛ kɛba lɛ?

english: Resting land allows wild plants to grow and naturally decay, restoring depleted nutrients and repairing soil structure without needing chemical inputs.
ga: He ni mɛi jɔɔ amɛhe yɛ lɛ haa koo mli tsei daa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Ehaa niyenii mli nibii ni efite lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni esaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni ekɛ tsofai tsuuu nii

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning brown and drying up while still attached to the branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi be mli ni amɛkpɛtɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ he lolo lɛ?

english: When leaves dry up and hang on the tree instead of falling off, it usually means the tree suffered a sudden blockage of water, often caused by severe dry weather or root-damaging fungal diseases.
ga: Beni baai lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ tsei ahe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbee shi lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu miitsi tso lɛ naa trukaa. Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to cut down whole cocoa trees when they start showing sick leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔfolɔ kookoo tsei muu fɛɛ kɛ́ amɛje shishi amɛba hela lɛ?

english: Certain serious cocoa diseases, like the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, have no chemical cure. Cutting down infected trees creates a barrier that stops the sickness from spreading to the healthy parts of your farm.
ga: Kokoo helai komɛi ni naa wa waa, tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ bɛ tsofa ni akɛtsaa amɛ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ feɔ gbɛtsii nii ko ni tsiɔ hela lɛ gbɛ koni ekagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli hei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if a dry-looking cocoa tree is completely dead or just suffering from heat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ cacao tso ni tamɔ nɔ ni egbi lɛ egbo kwraa loo hulutsoo lɛ miipiŋ kɛkɛ?

english: You can scrape a small piece of the outer bark on the main stem with your fingernail or a small knife. If the layer underneath is green and wet, the tree is alive; if it is brown and dry, that section is dead.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli fãi bibii ajie. yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ nɔ kɛ onineshi loo tsɔne bibioo ko. Kɛji shishigbɛ fã lɛ ji eŋɔli ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo. Kɛji akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nakai fã lɛ egbo

english: Why did my cocoa farm stop bringing out pods even though the trees are still standing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ ekpa ŋmeii lɛ ajiemɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ damɔ shi lolo lɛ?

english: A sudden stop in pod production can happen when the soil loses its natural food, when trees get too old without pruning, or when pests feed on the tiny flowers before they can grow into pods.
ga: Pod feemɔ ni akpaa trukaa lɛ baanyɛ aba kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ sɛɛ fo. Beni tso lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni afɔɔɔ lɛ Aloo be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ fɔfɔi bibii. Dani ebaada ni etsɔ pod

english: Why is my farm giving very low harvests after farming on the same land for many years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi waa yɛ be mli ni mikɛ afii babaoo etsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees suck up nutrients from the ground every season. Over time, the soil becomes empty and exhausted unless you put back food through fertilizers, organic compost, or proper soil cover.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ nuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee efolo ni egbɔjɔ ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii ekoŋŋ. organic compost loo shikpɔŋ ni sa ni akɛhaa nɔ

english: Can direct sunlight cause my cocoa trees to wither and dry up?
ga: Ani hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha cacao tsei lɛ agbo ni amɛgbi?

english: Yes, cocoa plants naturally prefer partial shade. Constant harsh sun dries out the soil quickly and burns the leaves, which causes the tree to lose moisture faster than its roots can pull it from the ground.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kookoo tsei sumɔɔ hulutsoo fã ko yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Hulu la ni naa wa ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya ni ehaa baai lɛ shãa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ mli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What can I do to keep my cocoa trees from dying during the long dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mi-kokoo tsei lɛ akagboi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can protect your trees by leaving shade trees on the farm to block hot winds, and by spreading dried leaves or grass around the base of the cocoa trees to trap moisture in the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu otsei lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni oooshi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he lɛ nɔ. kɛtsɔ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa Kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ he koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: How long should I wait before replanting cocoa after clearing a farm that died from disease?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani madu kookoo ekoŋŋ beni ajie helai kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to clear out all old infected roots and plant temporary shade crops like plantains for a few months to ensure the disease in the soil dies out before introducing fresh cocoa seedlings.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaajie shishifãi momo ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, nyɔji fioo komɛi koni ana nɔmimaa akɛ hela ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ gboɔ dani aduɔ kookoo dumɔwui heei.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning black and decaying before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani akpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, wet conditions. Clearing heavy weeds and pruning extra branches allows sunlight and air to dry the farm and reduce the rot.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni duŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ babaoo kɛ jwɛi ni afoɔ babaoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii baa shi.

english: Can putting too much chemical spray or fertilizer make my crops dry up?
ga: Ani tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ babaoo baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi?

english: Yes, using too much chemical fertilizer can burn the crop's roots by pulling water away from the plant, which makes the branches and leaves wither very quickly.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi kɛtsɔ nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ aniji kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi oya waa.

english: How do I know if heavy rain will wash away the fertilizer I just put on my maize farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwo mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɛɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist, but avoid doing so right before a heavy downpour. Slightly covering granular fertilizer with soil prevents rainwater from washing it off the surface of your field.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Shi kaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa. Ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ahe Kɛ shikpɔŋ, ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up during hot dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni egbiɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in dry weather is often the plant's natural defense to reduce water loss and protect itself from extreme heat, though it can also indicate stress from tiny pests like thrips or whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe koni ekɛba nu ni efiteɔ lɛ shi ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ haomɔ ni jɛɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies mli po.

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing stems and foliage instead of developing roots. Balancing the soil with potassium encourages tubers to swell.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai lɛ. yɛ shishifãi ni baa lɛ najiaŋ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ potassium ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa bulbs ni efuu lɛ.

english: Why are the blossoms falling off my bean plants before they turn into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi yɛ mi-bean tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ pods lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when plants face extreme heat, water stress during flowering, or attacks from blossom thrips that feed on delicate flower parts before pollination happens.
