ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ shɛ latsaa ni naa wa he. Nu mli haomɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli loo fɔfɔii a-thrips, ni yeɔ fɔfɔii lɛ ahe nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee pollination lɛ tutuamɔ.

english: Yellow leaves typically mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which the crop needs to produce green leaf pigments. Adding manure, compost, or urea fertilizer restores their green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hiaa koni amɛfee baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo urea fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise planting maize in straight rows with specific spacing rather than scattering seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni ja mli ni sɛɛgbɛ kroko yɔɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ dumɔwui adumɔ najiaŋ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each plant gets adequate sunlight, air, and soil nutrients without overcrowding, while straight rows make weeding, fertilizing, and harvesting much faster.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli fe nine. yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi ŋta ni ja lɛ haa anyɛɔ ajieɔ jwɛi, awoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ oya.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my soil fertile again for next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni efee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Legumes pull nitrogen from the air and store it in root nodules. When the crop matures, that nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei lɛ dara Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni odu lɛ niyenii.

english: Yams are ready to dig up when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up, showing that the plant has finished transferring its nutrients down into the tuber.
ga: Afee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ sweet potato kɛji baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: When should I stop applying water to my vegetable farm before picking the crop?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ makpa mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu shwiemɔ dani mahala ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Reduce or stop heavy watering right as fruits begin ripening to full color, as excess moisture at this stage can cause tomato and pepper fruits to split or rot on the vine.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ nu ni tsii ni oooha lɛ nɔ loo okpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛshwereɔ kɛyashɛɔ su ni yeɔ emuu lɛ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato kɛ pepper aduawai lɛ agbá loo amɛgbo yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and decay on the trees during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease caused by a fungal infection that spreads in wet, dark conditions. Pruning shade trees and excess cocoa branches allows sunlight and airflow to dry the pods out.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela ni tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni efɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo kɛ kookoo niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight because their foliage is delicate. Without taller shade plants like plantain or forest trees to cover them, intense sun burns their leaves and dries out the moisture they need to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ waaa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ agbi.

english: Why are there small holes in my young maize leaves with worms hiding inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii yɛ ni akɛtee tsɔne lɛ mli?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that lays eggs on maize. The hatched caterpillars feed on the soft growing center of the plant, leaving ragged holes and weakening the plant if left untreated.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa nɔ. Lalabii ni efɔ lɛ yeɔ tso lɛ mli hei ni gbekɛbii lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa buji ni etsilɛ baa, ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ.

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny flies called whiteflies. The disease stops the plant leaves from making food properly, which leads to smaller cassava roots underground.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Fɔlɔi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Hela nɛɛ haaa tso baai lɛ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Maize uses up specific plant foods like nitrogen from the dirt very quickly. Planting maize continuously in the same soil drains those nutrients faster than the soil can rebuild them naturally.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ tsei amli niyenii komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen, ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee ehee ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after I clear and weed my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mijie jwɛi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can sleep in the ground for years. When you clear the bush and expose the soil, direct sunlight and rain trigger those wild seeds to germinate much faster than planted crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ aka shikpɔŋ afii babaoo. Kɛji otsi jwɛi lɛ amli ni ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, hulu la kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha nakai koo mli dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots in the ground. When the fruit bunch grows heavy at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy, making it easy for wind to pull the shallow roots out of the soil unless supported with wooden poles.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ shwiili yɛ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ baaná shwiili babaoo yɛ ŋwɛi. ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ aaaje shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ja tso tsei fiɔ sɛɛ

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as very high heat, too little water, or too much fertilizer. Dropping flowers helps the plant save energy to stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa he. nu fioo pɛ loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli.

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium or experiences irregular watering while the fruit is growing rapidly, causing the bottom tissue of the tomato to collapse.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ loo afɔɔ lɛ nu be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida oya lɛ. Enɛ haa fãji ni yɔɔ tomato lɛ shishi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cowpea plants turning bright yellow even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Too much water fills up the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the plant roots. When roots cannot breathe, they stop absorbing food from the ground, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nu babaoo eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu Ekpaa niyenii ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ŋmɔmɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do my yams start shrinking and growing green sprouts while stored in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ ni eda ni ebatsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli beni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that continue to breathe after harvest. As weather warms up, the yam uses its own stored food energy to grow shoots, causing the tuber to dry out and lose weight.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli wo la lɛ, Sweet potatoes kɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii hewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ ŋmeii. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ egbiɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why is it important to water my fresh crops immediately after planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ nu awo miŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu lɛ?

english: Freshly planted crops or cuttings lose moisture quickly in the sun. Watering them right away prevents them from wilting and helps the soil settle closely around their roots so they can start drinking water immediately.
ga: Nibii ni adu ehee loo nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ mli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ. Nu ni oooha amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa ni eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehi shi shiŋŋ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe bɔni afee ni amɛje nu numɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Should I wait until I finish planting the whole field before I start watering my crop plants?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mamɛ ni madu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ naa dani mabɔi tsei lɛ anɔ nu shwiemɔ?

english: No, it is best to water crops in batches as you plant them. If you wait until the end of the day, the first set of crops you planted may dry out and die under the hot sun before receiving any water.
ga: Dabi, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha tsei lɛ nu yɛ kui amli be mli ni aduɔ amɛ lɛ. Kɛji omɛ kɛyashi gbi lɛ naagbee Klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii ni odu lɛ baanyɛ agbi ni egbo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi dani enine ashɛ nu nɔ.

english: Why should I water my newly transplanted crops before I take a break from working on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo tsei ni midu ehee lɛ nu dani mikɛ mihe awo ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ mli?

english: Young plants experience shock when moved into new soil and dry out very quickly. Giving them water right before you rest ensures their roots stay moist and do not burn in the heat while you are away.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ ahe feɔ amɛ yaa kɛji ajie amɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ hee nɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya waa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo amɛmli dani okɛ ohe jɔɔ ohe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛshishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkashã yɛ latsaa be mli ni obɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: How often do newly planted stem cuttings need water on a hot day?
ga: Shii enyiɛ niji ni adu ehee lɛ he hiaa nu yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ?

english: Fresh stem cuttings need water immediately and frequently until their roots form. On hot days, you must ensure the soil around them stays consistently moist so the cut ends do not dry out.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii heei ni afo lɛ biɔ ni afɔ amɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni afɔ amɛ shii abɔ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baaje kpo. Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okwɛ koni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ aná hulutsoo be fɛɛ be bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anaagbee akagbi.

english: How do crop roots actually absorb water from the ground after I water them?
ga: Te tsei shishifãi lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛjieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikɛ nu ewo amɛnɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops use tiny root hairs to pull in water that is held in the soil. When water sits in the soil around the plant, the roots slowly suck it up and push it to the leaves to keep the crop healthy and cool.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ shishifãi bibii tsuɔ nii. Ekɛ nu ni emɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ mli. Kɛji nu yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ mli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ holeɔ lɛ fiofio ni amɛtsiɔ kɛyaa baai lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni edɔ.

english: Is it good or bad if water stays standing on the surface of my farm land after I water my crops?
ga: Ani ehi loo ehiii kɛji nu baahi miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikɛ nu efɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ sɛɛ?

english: Water needs to stay in the soil long enough for the roots to drink it, but if it stands on top of the soil for too long, it can drown the roots and cause root rot. The water should soak in steadily so the roots can absorb it without suffocating.
ga: Esa akɛ nu lɛ ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ anu nu lɛ. Shi kɛji nu lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbo ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Esa akɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ awo mli pɛpɛɛpɛ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ ni amɛkafo mli.

english: Why does water sit in the topsoil for a short while before disappearing after I pour it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fioo dani elaajeɔ beni afɔse lɛ ashwie shi lɛ?

english: Topsoil acts like a sponge that needs a short moment to soak up liquid. This brief period where water stands on the land gives the crop's roots the necessary time to drink before the moisture drains deeper or evaporates.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ gbɛ ni ji akɛ, eheɔ be fioo dani ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi. Be kuku ni nu damɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ be ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛnu dani nu ni mli edɔ lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ loo etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Can I use water collected on my own farmland to irrigate my young plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni mibua naa kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ nu?

english: Yes, standing rainwater or clean surface water collected directly on your land is safe and convenient for watering young plants, as long as it is free from dangerous farm chemicals or oil.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ nu ni damɔ shi loo nu ni mli tse ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni abua naa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei bibii ni akɛ nu haa amɛ. Shii abɔ ni tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo ŋmɔ mli fɔ bɛ mli lɛ.

english: What happens to a plant if I give it water but let it sit in dry soil for a long time afterward?
ga: Mɛni baa tso lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ nu wo enɔ shi miha ehi shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ no sɛɛ?

english: If you pour water on dry soil and do not maintain the moisture, the dry surrounding earth will quickly suck the water away from the plant's root zone, leaving the plant thirsty again very quickly.
ga: Kɛji okɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ehiɛɛɛ mli lɛ, Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ mli oya. ni ehaa kumai yeɔ tso lɛ oya ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my newly planted crops are absorbing enough water from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso ni midu ehee lɛ miihe nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: If crops are absorbing enough water, their stems will stand firm and upright, and their leaves will look fresh and open rather than curled, soft, or drooping.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ ŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, tso lɛ shishi lɛ baafee ja ni ebaadamɔ shi shiŋŋ. ni baai lɛ baafee tamɔ ehee ni amɛgbele. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, efee blɛoo, loo egbee shi lɛ

english: Will planting my maize seeds very close together give me a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Ani ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, planting seeds too close together causes plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks and smaller cobs. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light to produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I put fertilizer in the soil at the exact same time I bury my crop seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kome too mli ni mifuɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Fresh seeds do not have roots yet to take up nutrients. Applying fertilizer too early can burn the delicate emerging roots or get washed away by rain before the plant is big enough to use it.
ga: Dumɔwui heei bɛ shishifãi ni baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ lolo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi heei ashã loo nugbɔ ahoɔ amɛ dani tsei lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants burn and dry up when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that protects the cocoa leaves from sun damage and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he lɛ baa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves, and why do I see caterpillars inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-abele baai bibii lɛ amli Ni mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that eats the tender leaves inside the heart of the maize plant. Catching them early and applying suitable control measures keeps them from destroying the growing shoot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ gbɛi ni sa ni akɛbaakwɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with big green leaves, but the tubers underground remain small and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ lolo?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava put all its energy into leaf and stem growth instead of root development. Balanced soil nutrients and loose soil allow the plant to direct energy down into swelling the roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee shishifãi Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my crops turning yellow after three days of continuous heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rains can wash away essential nitrogen from the root zone (leaching) and flood the air pockets in the soil. Without air and available nitrogen, plant leaves turn pale or yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli (leaching) kɛ nu afua kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nitrogen bɛ Tso lɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Peppers often drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant drops flowers to conserve energy for survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning dark black and rotten before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, usually caused by irregular watering. Irregular soil moisture prevents the plant from taking up enough calcium while the fruit is growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa lɛ haaa tsei lɛ aná calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay after harvest, that nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tso shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha sɛɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is it important for me to put tall stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matswa shwɛmɔ wulu koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves off the damp ground so they can catch maximum sunlight to feed the tubers underground, while reducing the risk of fungal leaf diseases from soil contact.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛha ŋmɔtɔi lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa fungal leaf hela ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do officers cut down cocoa trees on my farm even when some leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ folɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Ani baai lɛ yɛ eŋɔli lolo?

english: Diseases like the swollen shoot virus spread inside the cocoa tree long before the leaves fully wither. Cutting down infected trees prevents the disease from spreading through the roots and air to healthy trees on your farm and neighboring farms.
ga: Helai tamɔ bud swollen virus lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa cacao tso lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ dani baai lɛ shwieɔ kwraa. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akatsɔ shishifãi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ anɔ.

english: If my sick cocoa farm is cut down for rehabilitation, will my land still be good for planting fresh cocoa?
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo mi-kookoo ŋmɔji ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli koni akɛfee amɛ ehee Ani he ni miyɔɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi lolo kɛha kookoo hee ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, the soil remains fertile and healthy. Cutting down sick trees removes the source of the virus, allowing you to treat the land and plant new, stronger cocoa seedlings that can thrive without catching the old disease.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ kã he eji nɔ ni baa nii ni eyɛ hewalɛ. Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ he ni hela lɛ jɛɔ lɛ kɛyaa. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he ni oduɔ kookoo dumɔwui heei ni mli wa ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni helai momoi akamɔ bo.

english: What is the main benefit of completely replanting an old cocoa farm that is no longer producing well?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi titrii ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔji momo ni woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ dɔŋŋ lɛ ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ kwraa lɛ he?

english: Replanting allows you to replace weak, old trees with modern hybrid cocoa varieties that grow faster, resist diseases better, and produce much higher pod yields once they mature.
ga: Kɛ́ odu ekoŋŋ lɛ, onyɛɔ okɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo tsei ni shwereɔ oya lɛ yeɔ tsei ni egbɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ anajiaŋ. Helai ahewalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa pod yibii babaoo baa kɛji amɛdara.

english: How many years does it take for a newly replanted cocoa seedling to start bearing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Improved cocoa varieties usually start flowering and producing their first pods within two to three years if they receive proper shade, water, and care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi ni amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli kɛji akɛ aha amɛ hulutsoo, nu kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa.

english: Why do old cocoa trees gradually stop giving as many pods as they used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fiofio lɛ, kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii babaoo tamɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 30 years, their root systems and branches become less efficient at pulling nutrients from the soil, making them tired and more prone to disease.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tso ko ye afii 20 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, eshishifãi kɛ eniji lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, etɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe, ni helai baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ oya.

english: Cocoa trees drop excess flowers when they are stressed by drought, poor soil nutrients, or insect pests, saving their energy to keep the tree alive during tough conditions.
ga: Cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when planted in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot handle harsh heat. They need shade from temporary companion crops like plantains to keep them cool and moist while their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kɛ amɛhe yeɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do successful cocoa farmers keep permanent shade trees on their farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi ni yeɔ omanye lɛ duɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa yɛ amɛŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Shade trees protect full-grown cocoa from harsh dry-season sun, retain soil moisture, suppress weeds, and create a cooler climate that helps cocoa trees produce fruit for decades.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ shade lɛ buɔ kookoo ni eda lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi anaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni haa cacao tsei lɛ woɔ yibii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn dry and drop off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind sucks moisture out of the leaves faster than roots can drink from the dry soil. The tree drops its leaves to conserve water so the main stem does not dry out.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛto nu. Bɔni afee ni tso titri lɛ akagbi

english: Why is it important for me to prune branches from my cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or useless branches so sunlight and air can pass through the tree, which prevents damp diseases like black pod and directs all food into pod growth.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai ni mli ewo fɔ tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ naa ni ehaa niyenii fɛɛ daa yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize crops perform poorly if I plant them in late August instead of earlier in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu yɛ August naagbee gbɛ moŋ fe be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: In southern and coastal Ghana, the major rainy season winds down around August into a brief dry spell. Planting during this window means your young plants won't get enough natural rainwater to properly fill the grains.
ga: Ghana kooyigbɛ kɛ ŋshɔnaa kpokpai Nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baa yɛ August mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ebafeɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku. Dumɔwui ni ooodu yɛ samflɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ odumɔwui lɛ naaa adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ awo mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: What does resting my land for a season actually do for my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hejɔɔmɔ be kome he baa sɛɛnamɔ kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Giving your land a break allows the soil time to naturally rebuild nutrients and starves pest populations that would normally multiply by feeding on your continuous crops season after season.
ga: Kɛ́ oha oshikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ lɛ, ehaa enáa be ni ekɛtswaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni oha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ ayibɔ aba shi kɛtsɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ni oooya nɔ oye yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my vegetables turn brown and dry up when I farm near the coast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mifee okwaa yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Coastal farmland often faces salty ocean breezes and sandy soil that loses water quickly. The salt damages tender leaves while the fast-draining sand pulls moisture away from plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋshɔnaa okwaayeli hei lɛ naa ŋshɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ shikpɔji ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya lɛ. Nu fiteɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋã ni hoɔ oya lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers without producing any fruit during the dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ewooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High heat and low moisture cause stress in tomato plants. When the plant feels it doesn't have enough water to support full fruits, it sheds its flowers to save energy and survive.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulutsoo ni baa shi kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Beni tso lɛ nuɔ he akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii ni eyi obɔ lɛ bɛ. Ebaashwie efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato ni ehi shi.

english: How can I keep my vegetable soil moist when the rains reduce in August and September?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha aduawai ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni nugbɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ August kɛ September mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around your crop roots with dried grass or leaves—known as mulching—blocks direct sunlight, keeps the soil cool, and traps moisture so plants can survive dry weather.
ga: Ale shikpɔŋ ni bɔle otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei anyɛ ahi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli.

english: Why do caterpillars and pests attack my farm so aggressively right after the dry spell ends?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ waa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba naagbee amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The return of light rains causes crops to sprout fresh, tender leaf shoots. Adult pests seek out these young leaves because they are soft and easy for new larvae to feed on.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo ni ekuɔ esɛɛ eba lɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ tsei bibii heei. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni eda lɛ taoɔ nɛkɛ baai bibii nɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ŋmeii heei baaye.

english: Is it better to burn weeds after clearing my farm or leave them on the ground?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi beni mijie miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ loo mashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Leaving cleared weeds to rot on the farm protects the topsoil from baking under the hot sun and decomposes into free organic manure, whereas burning destroys essential soil nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ oha jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he koni ekashã yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko yɛ be mli ni shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why does cassava survive better in poor sandy soil compared to maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ kɛ akɛto ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Cassava develops tough, deep root tubers that store water and food over long periods, allowing it to survive in loose, nutrient-poor soil where shallow-rooted crops like maize fail.
ga: Cassava feɔ ŋmeii ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni hiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ ejɔ, ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ nɔ, he ni tsei ni shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ baafee nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the big trees off my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily in strong, direct sunlight. Leaving taller trees or planting plantains creates shade umbrellas that protect them while they establish deep roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni ashiɔ loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa ni buɔ tsei lɛ ahe beni amɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow very tall with lots of leaves but produce almost no peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi pepper ko kwraa bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer forces them to focus all their energy on leaf growth instead of blooming. Using fertilizers rich in phosphorus and potassium encourages flowering and fruit formation.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaanyɛ amɛnɔ ni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni phosphorus kɛ potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ.

english: I have one coconut tree on my farm that produces huge fruits compared to the rest. How can I use seeds from just this one tree to plant new ones?
ga: Miyɛ ŋmei tso kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni woɔ yibii wuji kɛ akɛto tsei krokomɛi lɛ ahe. Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ tso nɛɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ atsu nii ni mikɛwo ehee?

english: To grow new trees from your best coconut tree, choose mature, fully ripe nuts that fall or are ready to harvest from that specific tree. Place those selected nuts in a nursery bed with shade and adequate water until they sprout, ensuring only seedlings from that superior mother tree are transplanted to your field.
ga: Koni okwɛ tso hee kɛjɛ o-coconut tso ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ mli? Halamɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni egbee shi loo ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmeii tso lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii ni ahala lɛ awo ŋmeii akwɛmɔhe ko ni hulutsoo kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃. Enɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ fɔlɔ tso ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ mli lɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni abaajie kɛya oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: If I plant a good variety of coconut next to poor quality ones, will seeds from the good tree still produce good seedlings?
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmei srɔtoi ni hi yɛ ŋmei srɔtoi ni baa shi lɛ masɛi lɛ, Ani dumɔwui ni jɛ tsei kpakpai amli lɛ baawo dumɔwui kpakpai lolo?

english: Not always. Bees and wind carry pollen from nearby poor-quality trees to your good tree's flowers, which can mix their traits. To keep the variety as pure as possible, collect seeds from areas where only desirable varieties grow together, or select seeds over multiple generations from isolated top-performing trees.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Wuobii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ pollen ni jɛɔ tsei ni bɛ sɛɛnamɔ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ yaa tsei kpakpai ahe fɔfɔi amli. ni baanyɛ afee amɛsui lɛ ekome Bɔni afee ni srɔtofeemɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni aaanyɛ Moŋ lɛ, buamɔ dumɔwui anaa kɛjɛ he ko ni srɔtofeemɔi ni osumɔɔ ni okɛ amɛ afee ekome pɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Aloo halamɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛ tsei ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ yinɔi babaoo ni eho lɛ amli.

english: Can I grow a new coconut tree by cutting a branch from my best tree and planting it in the soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmei tso hee kɛtsɔ mitso ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ mli ŋmeii ni mikɛbaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, coconut trees cannot grow from branch cuttings or shoots like cassava or cocoa trees can through grafting. Coconuts can only be multiplied by planting the mature nut (seed) itself.
ga: Dabi, anyɛɛɛ akwɛ ŋmei tsei kɛjɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsei kɛtsɔ ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Abaanyɛ agbɛ ŋmeii ashwã kɛtsɔ ŋmeii (dumɔwui) ni eda lɛ pɛ nɔ.

english: Should I cut down my old trees that produce very small fruits to plant a better variety?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo tso momo ni woɔ yibii bibii waa lɛ mli koni madu tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, removing low-yielding or poor-quality trees clears valuable land, sunlight, and soil nutrients for better varieties. Replacing poor performers gradually allows you to upgrade your farm's overall harvest without losing all your income at once.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni wooo yibii babaoo loo tsei ni ehiii lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli atse koni amɛfɔ jogbaŋŋ. Abaafee shwɛlɔi fɔji lɛ anajiaŋdamɔlɔi lɛ fiofio. Ehaa okɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii fɛɛ ni onáa lɛ yaa hiɛ ni oshika fɛɛ ni onáa lɛ sɛɛ efooo shikome.

english: How many years can a traditional large coconut tree live and keep producing fruits on my farm?
ga: Afii enyiɛ kusum mli ŋmei tso agbo ko baanyɛ ahi shi ni ewo yibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Traditional tall coconut trees are very long-lived and can continue bearing fruit for 60 to 80 years or more. While their yield may slow down slightly as they get very old, proper soil care and weed control keep them productive for most of their lifespan.
ga: Kusum mli ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ waa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛya nɔ amɛwo yibii afii 60 kɛyashi 80 krokomɛi loo nɔ ni fe nakai. Eyɛ mli akɛ yibiiwoo lɛ baanyɛ aba shi fioo kɛji mɔ ko ye afii moŋ. Shi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha amɛwo yibii amɛwala be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do some coconut trees grow very tall before fruiting while others stay short and bear fruit quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akokoshi tsei komɛi daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei tsei komɛi yɛ kuku ni amɛwoɔ yibii oya lɛ?

english: These are different varieties of coconut. The tall varieties grow slowly, take 6 to 10 years to produce fruit, but live up to 80 years. Dwarf varieties stay shorter, produce fruit much faster (in 3 to 4 years), but generally have a shorter overall lifespan.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii srɔtoi. Henɔi ni kɛlɛ lɛ daraa blɛoo, ni eheɔ afii 6 kɛyashi 10 dani ewoɔ yibii, shi ebaanyɛ ehi shi kɛyashi afii 80. Dwarf henɔi lɛ wala be kukuoo. Etsuɔ nii oya (yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli) shi bei pii lɛ ewala be fɛɛ feɔ kuku.

english: Why are some trees on my farm growing much bigger and healthier than the ones planted right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi daraa jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Trees vary because of natural seed genetics, slight differences in soil fertility underneath them, or varying access to sunlight and water. Selecting seeds only from the naturally bigger and stronger mother trees helps ensure your next batch grows more uniformly.
ga: Tsei lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ adebɔɔ mli dumɔwui ahewɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ mli baa lɛ yɛ srɔto fioo. loo hulu la kɛ nu ni anáa lɛ srɔtoi. Dumɔwui ni ahalaa kɛjɛɔ nyɛ tsei ni dara ni amɛhe wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ pɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni ogbɛjianɔtoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How far apart should I space large coconut trees when planting a new farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei heei kɛjɛ amɛhe lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Large coconut trees need about 8 to 10 meters of space between each tree. Because they grow wide leaf canopy tops and extensive root systems, this spacing prevents them from shading each other out and competing for soil nutrients.
ga: Kokoo tsei wuji biɔ ni tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ afee mitai 8 kɛyashi 10, ejaakɛ amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Nɛkɛ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ nɛɛ haaa amɛtsi amɛhe ni amɛkaye niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ.

english: What is the best way to nurse young tree seedlings before moving them out into the main farm?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ dumɔwui bibii dani ajieɔ amɛ kɛyaa ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Keep young seedlings in rich soil under light shade canopy, watering them regularly so the soil stays moist but not waterlogged. This protects fragile young roots from harsh sunlight until the plant is strong enough for field planting.
ga: Ha tsei bibii ahi shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo shishi kɛ kane ni mli jɔ. Okɛ nu awo mli daa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ shi nu akafee nɔ ni yɔɔ mli. Enɛ buɔ shishifãi bibii ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ he waa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu yɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: How can agricultural extension officers help me identify which crop varieties are best for my farm?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ ni mana tsei srɔtoi ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Extension officers testing crop varieties can advise you on high-yielding, disease-resistant seeds tailored to your local soil and climate. They can also show you best practices for propagation and field management to maximize your farm's productivity.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋaa yɛ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo, ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔɔ bo gbɛi ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbɛɔ ashwãa kɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ hu koni oŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers must be fertilized by tiny insects called midges to form pods. If there are not enough midges or if the weather is too dry for them, the unpollinated flowers dry up and fall off the tree.
ga: Esa akɛ kooloi bibii awo kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Atsɛɔ nakai midge bɔni afee ni efee pod. Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo bɛ loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: What is hand pollination, and how can it help me get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua mi ni makpã nii babaoo?

english: Hand pollination is when you manually move pollen from one flower to another using a small brush or tool. This ensures that more flowers get fertilized, leading to many more fruits or pods than relying on natural insects alone.
ga: Nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ ji be mli ni okɛ onine shwieɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ kɛtsɔ brɔsh loo dɛŋdade bibioo ko nɔ. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi babaoo aná fɔmɔ nii. Enɛ haa anáa aduawai loo ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ adebɔɔ mli kooloi bibii pɛ anɔ.

english: How do insects in my field actually help my crop plants grow better food?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛná niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Insects like bees and midges visit flowers to feed, and in the process, they carry pollen from flower to flower. This fertilizes the flowers so they can develop into healthy fruits, seeds, or pods.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni saraa fɔfɔi kɛha niyenii Ni yɛ nɛkɛ gbɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛwoɔ pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ aduawai, dumɔwui, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why do some of my crops bloom with many flowers but never produce any actual fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi miifɔlɔ kɛ fɔfɔii babaoo shi amɛwooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: A plant might produce flowers, but if those flowers are not pollinated or if the plant is stressed by extreme heat or lack of water, it drops the flowers before it can spend energy turning them into fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ baanyɛ awo fɔfɔi. Shi kɛji akɛ nakai fɔfɔi lɛ ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ hu? Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi dani amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ lɛ atsu nii ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why did my farm yield less harvest this year compared to last year even though I did the same work?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo afi nɛɛ kɛ akɛto afi ni eho lɛ he lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mitsuɔ nii nakai nɔŋŋ moŋ.

english: Crop yields change from year to year due to changes in rainfall patterns, soil nutrients getting used up, or shifts in insect populations. Rotating crops and replenishing soil nutrients helps keep yields steady over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakeɔ daa afi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ tsakemɔi ahewɔ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ miije shishi miiho. loo tsakemɔi ni baa kooloi ayibɔ mli Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young crop plants turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is lacking key nutrients in the soil, like nitrogen, or that the soil is either too dry or flooded with water. Adding compost or proper fertilizer helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii titri yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ sũ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young crop plants wither and burn when left under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have tender stems and leaves that lose water very fast in intense heat. They need temporary shade and regular watering until their roots grow deep enough to find groundwater.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛ baai ni nu fiteɔ oya waa kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, ni afɔ amɛ nu daa kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawo wu bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛna shikpɔŋ shishi nu.

english: When plants are crowded, their roots and leaves compete with each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Giving each plant enough space allows it to feed well and grow strong stems.
ga: Beni tsei ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni eyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni enáa ŋmeii ni wa.

english: How does cutting off extra branches help my crop tree produce bigger fruits?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mitso lɛ ni ewo yibii wuji eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Pruning removes old, shaded, or diseased branches that drain energy from the plant. This allows the tree to direct all its water and nutrients to healthy foliage, flowers, and growing fruit.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji momoi lɛ. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ jieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ kɛyaa baai, fɔfɔii, kɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does the dry Harmattan season affect my crops so badly, and how can I protect the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Harmattan hɔmɔ lɛ miigba miŋmɔshi nibii ahe waa lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu shikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: Harmattan winds are extremely dry and suck moisture out of plant leaves and soil very quickly. Covering the soil around your crops with dry leaves or grass traps water in the ground and protects root systems.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ oya. Okɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi tsɔnei abɔle onibii ahe koni nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ebu shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How long does a rubber tree take from planting before it starts producing latex?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani rɔbɔt tso ko jeɔ latɛs feemɔ shishi?

english: Rubber trees usually take about 6 to 7 years of growth before their trunks become thick enough—around 50 centimeters in circumference—for tapping to begin safely without damaging the tree.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, rɔbɔt tsei heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛshishifã lɛ shwereɔ bɔ ni sa. (aaafee sɛntimitai 50 yɛ ebɔlehe) koni eje shishi etswa tso lɛ shweshweeshwe ni efiteee tso lɛ.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or maize inside my young rubber farm during the first few years?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ mi rɔbɔt ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli?

english: Yes, during the first 3 to 4 years when rubber trees are still small, you can intercrop with short-term crops like maize or vegetables to earn income, provided you keep a clear space around each young rubber tree.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 ni rɔba tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ mli. Obaanyɛ okɛ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai adu. koni ona shika Esa akɛ okwɛ he ko ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Rɔba tso bibioo lɛ eko fɛɛ eko

english: Can rubber trees grow well in swampy areas on my farm where water stands for a long time?
ga: Ani rɔbɔt tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nu ema shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: No, rubber trees require well-drained soil; standing water causes root rot, which makes the leaves turn yellow and can eventually kill the tree.
ga: Dabi, shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia rɔba tsei. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaanyɛ egbe tso lɛ.

english: Why does latex stop flowing from my rubber trees during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ latɛs ni jɛɔ rɔbɔt tsei amli lɛ kpaɔ shwiemɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: During the dry season, rubber trees shed their leaves to conserve moisture, which drops the water pressure inside the trunk and temporarily slows down or stops latex flow.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Rɔba tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai koni hulutsoo akahi shi. Enɛ baaha nu ni yɔɔ tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ nɔ aba shi. ni eha late lɛ hoɔ blɛoo loo be kukuoo ko.

english: Why do extension officers recommend tapping rubber trees early in the morning instead of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ jɛmɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ atswa rɔbɔt tsei lɛ leebi moŋ fe shwane lɛ?

english: Internal water pressure in the tree is highest in the cool early morning, allowing the liquid latex to flow much longer and faster than during the hot afternoon.
ga: Nu ni tsiimɔ yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ fa fe fɛɛ yɛ leebi maŋkpa ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli ejɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ hoɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni eyaa oya fe shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do some of my rubber trees give thick white latex while others give thin, watery liquid?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ rɔbɔt tsei komɛi jieɔ latɛs yɛŋ ni mli tse lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni rɔbɔt tsei komɛi jieɔ latɛs ni mli tseee lɛ?

english: Latex thickness depends on soil moisture, tree health, and tapping frequency; tapping a tree too often drains its nutrients, causing the latex to become thin and watery.
ga: Latex lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. tso lɛ hewalɛnamɔ kɛ bɔ ni atswaa lɛ shii abɔ lɛ Kɛ́ ota tso lɛ he shii abɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afite. Enɛ haa latɛs lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni efeɔ nu.

english: If I cut the bark of my rubber tree to harvest latex, will the bark ever grow back?
ga: Kɛji ofolɔ rɔbɔt tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ koni okɛbu latɛs lɛ naa. Ani ŋshɔŋloo lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, rubber trees naturally heal and regenerate their bark over several years, allowing you to tap other sections of the trunk while the old bark restores itself.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, rɔbɔt tsei lɛ tsaa amɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii heei yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli. Ehaa otswaa tso lɛ fãi krokomɛi yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ yibii momo lɛ baafee ehe ehee.

english: What happens if I leave harvested raw rubber latex in the sun without processing it?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi mi-latex ni akpa lɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni mikɛtsuuu nii?

english: Raw latex naturally spoils and forms lumpy, low-quality coagulum due to bacteria in the air; adding formic acid helps it solidify cleanly into high-grade rubber sheets.
ga: Latex ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ helai ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ahewɔ. Formic acid ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa ewaa jogbaŋŋ ni etsɔɔ rɔba ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young rubber seedlings turning white and powdery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ rɔbɔt tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ feɔ eyɛŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by powdery mildew, a fungal infection common in humid weather that attacks soft new leaves and slows down the seedling's overall growth.
ga: Powdery mildew kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ ni baatutua baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ adalɛ aba shi.

english: How much land do I need to plant with rubber for a processing factory to accept me as an outgrower farmer?
ga: Shikpɔŋ enyiɛ esa akɛ rɔba nitsumɔhe ko atsu nii koni enyɛ ekpɛlɛ okwaafoi ni bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: Most processing factories look for smallholder farmers with at least 1 to 2 hectares, as this guarantees a steady volume of latex that makes factory collection routes economical.
ga: Nitsumɔhei ni tsuɔ nibii ahe nii lɛ ateŋ babaoo taoɔ okwaafoi bibii ni kɛ hoo lɛ amɛyɛ shikpɔŋ hectares 1 kɛyashi 2, ejaakɛ enɛ haa anyɛɔ anáa latɛs be fɛɛ be, ni no haa gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuaa nibii anaa yɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ feɔ nɔ ni jara waaa.

english: How do I know if my land is properly prepared before planting young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ asaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani maduɔ kokoo tsei bibii?

english: A good foundation for cocoa requires clearing weeds, ensuring deep soil that drains water well, and marking proper planting distances. This helps young roots spread easily without competing for nutrients.
ga: Shishitoo kpakpa kɛha kookoo biɔ ni ajie jwɛi. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni otsɔɔ he ni sa ni esa akɛ adu lɛ Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo ni amɛyeee akaŋ yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he.

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade protection because full sunlight burns their delicate leaves. Planting shade crops like plantains provides temporary living shelter to help young cocoa survive its first couple of years.
ga: Esa akɛ abu kookoo dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ hulu la he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa anáa shihilɛhe yɛ be kukuoo mli koni eye ebua kookoo bibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do many of the small flowers on my cocoa trees fall off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Ani tsei babaoo shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed extra flowers if they don't get pollinated by tiny insects called midges, or if the tree is stressed by drought or lack of soil nutrients.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. aloo kɛji akɛ hɔmɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa

english: What is causing my healthy green cocoa pods to suddenly turn black and rot?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ trukaa ni egbo?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, dark, and overly wet conditions. Clearing weeds and letting sunlight airflow through the farm helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fungi ni shwereɔ yɛ fɛ̃i, duŋ, kɛ nu tsɔ shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ahaa hulu la kpɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I consult a trained Cocoa Board extension officer instead of using traditional farming methods alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mayabi Cocoa Board lɛ He Nitsulɔ ni atsɔse lɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ blema okwaayeli gbɛi pɛ baatsu nii lɛ

english: Trained extension officers are equipped with updated scientific knowledge about disease prevention, correct chemical usage, and modern techniques that help protect your crop investment and increase yield.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni atsɔse amɛ ni amɛyaa hiɛ lɛ yɛ jeŋ nilee ni yɔɔ ŋmɛnɛ yɛ helai atsimɔ he. Tsofai kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaai ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe ni ehaa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it necessary to cut off extra shoots and side branches from my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo mi-cacao tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ esɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unneeded branches called 'suckers' that steal food from the main tree. Removing them directs energy toward flowering and developing larger, healthier pods.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘tsoji’ ni juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛjiemɔ lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baa lɛ anɔ.

english: Fertilizer is best applied early in the rainy season when the soil is moist, allowing roots to absorb nutrients easily to feed new leaves, flowers, and growing pods.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa baa, fɔfɔii, kɛ ŋmeii heei.

english: Why do I need to cover my harvested cocoa beans under plantain leaves for a few days before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-kookoo ni mikpa lɛ haa plantain baai ashishi gbii fioo komɛi dani migbiɔ lɛ?

english: This process is called fermentation. It removes the sweet pulp, turns the purple beans brown, and develops the rich chocolate flavor required by cocoa buyers.
ga: Atsɛɔ gbɛ nɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ebaajie loo ni ŋɔɔ lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni amɛná tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ kookoo lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the branches on some of my cocoa trees swelling up and losing their leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ekomɛi anɔ lɛ efuu ni amɛbaai lɛ miiho lɛ?

english: Swollen branches are a main sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease, spread by tiny mealybug insects. Because there is no chemical cure, affected trees must be removed to protect the rest of the farm.
ga: Niji ni efuu lɛ ji okadi titri ni tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko ni ji cocoa bud virus, ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji mealybugs lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Ejaakɛ tsofa ko bɛ ni akɛtsaa tsei ni ena hela lɛ koni akɛbu ŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: What are those tiny insects causing dark patches on my cocoa stems and pods?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ni kɛ okadii diji ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ kɛ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baa?

english: These are likely capsids (commonly called akate), which suck sap from the crop. Their feeding leaves wounds that dry out stems and damage young pods, requiring proper pest control to manage.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji capsids. (ni afɔɔ lɛ tsɛmɔ akɛ akate) ni shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli nu lɛ Niyenii haa pilamɔi ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbiɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ baa. Enɛ biɔ ni akudɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ amɛkwɛmɔ mli.

english: Coconut trees naturally take between 3 to 7 years to bear fruit depending on the variety. Dwarf varieties bear faster in about 3 to 4 years, while tall varieties take longer but produce fruits for more decades.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli ŋmei tsei heɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Edamɔ tso lɛ nɔ Dwarf tso lɛ woɔ yibii mra, yɛ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni tso ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo shi ebaawo yibii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my coconut trees turning yellow and dying off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the tree lacks key soil nutrients like potassium or nitrogen, or it is not getting enough water during dry periods. Adding compost or manure around the base helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium loo nitrogen. aloo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni enine shɛɛɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he kɛbɔle Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Can I plant maize or cassava between my coconut trees while they are still small?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ be mli ni mibii lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, planting food crops like maize, legumes, or cassava between young coconut palms makes good use of land and provides quick income without harming the growing trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ. loo ŋmei Yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa shika baa oya ni eyeee tsei ni miida lɛ awui.

english: Why do tiny immature coconuts fall off my trees before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ daraaa lɛ? Koni migbee shi kɛjɛ mitso lɛ nɔ dani etsɔ agbo?

english: Early fruit drop happens mainly when the tree experiences water stress during dry spells or lacks proper nutrients. Mulching the base of the tree with dry grass or husks retains water and prevents fruit loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso yibii ni fiteɔ mra lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli loo niyenii ni sa bɛ enɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmãa ŋmɔtɔ ha tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ ahi mli ni ebaatsi yibii lɛ ni elaaje lɛ naa.

english: What is the main difference between dwarf coconut palms and tall coconut palms?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ titri ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso bibioo kɛ ŋmei tso kakadaŋŋ teŋ?

english: Dwarf palms grow shorter, produce fruit much earlier, and are easier to harvest without climbing, whereas tall palms grow very high, live longer, and withstand dry weather better.
ga: Dwarf palms lɛ daa kuku. Ehaa nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ baa oya kwraa Ni eyɛ mlɛo akɛ abaakpa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akwɔ ŋwɛi. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ daraa waa, amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ, ni amɛŋmɛɔ amɛtsui shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I choose the healthiest coconut seedlings to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ ni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Pick seedlings with thick shoots, vibrant green leaves, quick leaf splitting, and strong roots. Avoid seedlings with pale leaves, thin stems, or visible insect damage.
ga: Halamɔ dumɔwui ni ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe. Baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ, baai lɛ fãa oya ni shishifãi lɛ hu wa. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni baai lɛ tsuɔ, tsei bibii, loo koolooi ni efite lɛ ahe.

english: What is eating V-shaped holes into the leaves of my coconut trees?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yeɔ bu ni tamɔ V ni yɔɔ mi ŋmei tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Rhinoceros beetle, which bores into young fronds. Clearing dead wood and decaying plant waste around your farm removes their breeding grounds.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ ji nɔ ni rhinoceros ŋmeii lɛ kɛbaa. ni boteɔ baai bibii amli Ejieɔ tsei ni egboi kɛ tsei amli sũi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ baajie he ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ lɛ kɛya.

english: How can I keep my coconut farm green and healthy through the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Covering the soil around the base of each palm with coconut husks or dry leaves traps moisture in the soil and prevents the hot sun from drying out the root zone.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo baai ni egbi shwie tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli, ni ebaatsi hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shishifãi ni egbi lɛ adɔ fe nine.

english: Why should I adopt modern coconut farming techniques instead of using only old methods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaai ni akɛfeɔ ŋmei lɛ atsu nii moŋ fe ni akɛ blema gbɛi lɛ baatsu nii lɛ?

english: Modern farming techniques teach proper tree spacing, disease prevention, and soil feeding, which can double your nut yields and protect your farm from total crop failure.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli he ŋaai tsɔɔ akɛ gbɛ kã tsei ateŋ. Helai atsimɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpa ni akɛhaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ baanyɛ aha o-bean ni ooofee lɛ aya hiɛ toi enyɔ. ni obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant coconut trees far apart from each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu ŋmei tsei ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Coconut palms need wide spacing so their large fronds can capture sunlight fully and their roots can spread out to get nutrients without fighting neighboring trees for food and water.
ga: Ehe miihia ni aŋmɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ahe shɔŋŋ bɔni afee ni baai wuji lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ hulu la lɛ fɛɛ. Ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã koni amɛye niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ awuu kɛha niyenii kɛ nu.

english: Why does grass grow back so quickly on my farm right after I finish clearing it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ beni mijie jwɛi lɛ?

english: Grass seeds and underground root stems remain alive in the soil even after you clear the surface. When rain and sunshine hit the freshly cleared soil, those hidden seeds germinate very quickly to take over the open space.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po. Beni nugbɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ hee ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ nɔ lɛ. Nɛkɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya waa ni amɛhaa hei ni agbele naa lɛ anɔ.

english: You should walk through your farm at least two to three times a week. Regular visits help you spot early signs of pest attacks, leaf diseases, or water stress before they become severe and destroy your harvest.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ otsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ yɛ otsi mli. Saramɔi ni afeɔ daa lɛ baaye abua bo ni ona okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, tsei ahe helai, loo nu mli haomɔ miiba mra. Dani ebaafee basabasa ni efite onibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plants are lacking nitrogen in the soil, which is an essential nutrient for leaf growth. It can also happen when heavy rainfall washes away nutrients or leaves the roots standing in too much water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii lɛ loo eha shishifãi lɛ damɔ nu babaoo mli.

english: How can I tell if insects are damaging my crops before I actually see the bugs?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi bibii miifite miŋmɔshi nibii dani mana amɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You can identify early pest damage by checking for tiny holes in the leaves, curled leaf tips, sticky liquid on the stems, or small dark spots. These are clear signs that insects are feeding on your plants.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ mra kɛtsɔ bu bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni ebɔle ehe, nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ. loo ŋmɔtɔ bibii Enɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii miiye otsei lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. Giving them steady moisture and proper fertilizer helps flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔii kɛji akɛ amɛmiihao, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa. aloo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ fɔmɔ nii ni sa yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ chili ŋmeii.

english: Why do my maize plants yield very small cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too tightly together, their roots compete heavily for the same water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to form large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baatswa nu he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmei agbo ni mli wa.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow thin and weak when planted under large shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Cassava needs direct, strong sunlight to produce energy and grow big root tubers. When big trees block the light, the cassava plant stretches upward to find sun, resulting in tall, weak stems and tiny tubers.
ga: Cassava he miihia hulu la ni naa wa, ni yɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba ni ekwɛ shishifãi wuji. Kɛ tsei wuji tsi la lɛ naa lɛ Kasaa tso lɛ baakpã kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛlɛɔ, ni amɛgbɔjɔ, ni amɛyitsei lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why should I place fertilizer near the root base of my plants instead of scattering it everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mitsei lɛ ashishigbɛ moŋ fe ni magbɛ amɛshwã he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer near the roots ensures your crop gets direct access to the nutrients. If you scatter it broadly, nearby weeds will consume it, or rain will wash it away before your crop can absorb it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji ogbɛ eshwa babaoo lɛ Jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaye lɛ. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, nugbɔ baaho lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why is it necessary to prune excess branches and unwanted shoots from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ niji ni fa fe nine kɛ ŋmeii ni ataooo kɛjɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches that waste the tree's energy and block airflow. Good airflow and sunlight reduce fungal diseases like black pod and encourage the tree to put energy into growing pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni etsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ kɛ hulu la haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ pod blackening baa shi ni ewoɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ awo pod ni miida lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl upward during the hottest period of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon is a natural defense mechanism to reduce water loss during intense heat. If the leaves uncurl when the sun goes down, the plant is fine, but if they remain curled, the crop needs watering.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni haa nu ni fiteɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Kɛji baai lɛ shwieee shi beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ Tso lɛ hi. Shi kɛji akɛ ebɔle ehe lolo lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia tso lɛ.

english: How do I know when my cocoa pods are actually ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-kokoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ he koni akpa?

english: Cocoa pods change color when ripe, usually turning from green to bright yellow, or from dark red to orange-yellow. Harvesting them at full maturity ensures maximum bean size and good quality.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su be mli ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse mli. loo kɛjɛ tsuru ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛtee ŋmɔŋ-ɔranji nɔ. Nikpamɔ beni edara kwraa lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ ni fe fɛɛ kɛ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ he.

english: Why must I ferment my cocoa beans under banana leaves for a few days after harvesting instead of drying them immediately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee cocoa ŋmeii lɛ yɛ banana baai ashishi gbii fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha amɛgbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fermentation develops the chocolate flavor and rich brown color inside the cocoa beans. Drying them immediately without fermentation leaves them bitter and lowers their market price.
ga: Kɛ́ afee kookoo lɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, ehaa tsokolate mli ŋɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ. Kɛ́ egbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ fataaa he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ aba ni ebaaha jara nɔ jara aba shi.

english: Traditional cocoa trees usually take 3 to 5 years to start bearing fruit, but improved hybrid varieties can start producing pods in about 2 to 3 years with good soil care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, blema cacao tsei lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Shi hybrid henɔi ni atsake lɛ baanyɛ aje pods feemɔ shishi yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do cocoa flowers grow directly on the main trunk and thick branches instead of the small twigs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ kɛ niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe niji bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods are heavy fruit. The plant naturally produces flowers on the thick trunk and sturdy branches so the tree can easily support the weight of the heavy pods without breaking.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔtɔ ji aduawai ni tsii. Tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ niji ni mli wa anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ anɔ mlɛo ni efoŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to prune extra shoots and dry branches from our cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔfo wɔ kookoo tsei lɛ aniji krokomɛi kɛ tsei niji ni egbi lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-productive shoots and dead wood, directing the tree's nutrients into producing bigger pods while allowing air and sunlight to pass through to prevent disease.
ga: Tso ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei ni wooo yibii kɛ tsei ni egboi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ mli niyenii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ mli koni helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that spreads during heavy rains and high humidity. Clearing infected pods and letting sunlight into the farm helps control it.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, black pod hela kɛbaa Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ hulu la ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni eboteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akudɔɔ amɛ.

english: What causes young cocoa leaves to curl up, turn brown, and die?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ blɔfo ni amɛgboiɔ?

english: Curled and brown leaves are often caused by sap-sucking pests like mirids (capsids) or extended dry weather. Spraying recommended treatments and providing shade can protect the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mirids (capsids) loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baa. Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛ shade ni akɛwoɔ he ŋaa lɛ baanyɛ abu baai lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil needs fertilizer to help my cocoa yield better?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛha kookoo lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Slow growth, yellowing leaves, and small pod production often show that the soil lacks nutrients. Adding recommended fertilizers or organic manure restores soil fertility for better yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, kɛ ŋmɔji bibii tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ koni ewo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why is it necessary to weed around my cocoa trees regularly even after they are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni wɔjie jwɛi ni bɔle ehe lɛ? Cacao tsei daa eyɛ mli akɛ cacao tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Weeds compete with cocoa trees for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, and they can harbor harmful pests. Keeping the ground clean ensures your trees get all the nutrients they need.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ kookoo tsei yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or plantain inside my young cocoa farm without harming the trees?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo plantain yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli. Ani manyɛ mafee enɛ ni miyeee tso lɛ awui?

english: Yes, planting food crops alongside young cocoa provides necessary shade and extra income, as long as they are spaced properly so they do not steal water and nutrients from the young cocoa.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ haa anáa hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa kɛ shika kroko ni fata he. Shii abɔ ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ jɛmɛ bɔni afee ni akaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kookoo bibioo lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Leaves turning yellow starting from the bottom usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or composted manure helps the plant build food and turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do I have to cut my cassava stems into pieces to plant instead of using seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afolɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ amli bibii bibii koni akɛdu yɛ dumɔwui ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Cassava plants rarely grow strong crops from seeds. Planting cut stems ensures the new crop grows fast, stays identical to the strong parent plant, and produces large food tubers much quicker.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cassava tsei lɛ kwɛɛɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli. Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ, ebaawo tsei heei adalɛ oya. Ehiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛ ni nyɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. ni amɛfeɔ niyenii yitsei wuji oya kwraa.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop in the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ nɔ leebi moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the ground. Drooping is the plant's natural way of reducing leaf surface exposed to the heat, and it recovers when the evening cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Defoliation ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa baa lɛ nɔ hulutsoo baa shi. ni ebaahe ejɔ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ edɔ

english: Why do my crop seeds rot in the soil when I plant right after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi aduawai dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds need oxygen to breathe and sprout. When heavy rain completely floods the soil air pockets, the seeds suffocate and wet fungal organisms rot them before they can germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa koni amɛmu ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli eyiɔ nu. Dumɔwui lɛ baafo ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ baagboi dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same spot of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil strips away specific nutrients and encourages pests like armyworms to build up in the field. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or beans restores soil fertility and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ komɛi kɛjɛ mli. ni ewo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ asraafoi awuiyelɔi lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Okɛ ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni ekpaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather gets extremely hot or when water levels fluctuate sharply. Severe heat stresses the plant and prevents proper pollination, so keeping the soil moist and mulched protects the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ nu lɛ mli tsɔ oya. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ afee nɔ ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I spread dry grass or leaves around the base of my vegetable plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ashwã he lɛ? Mi aduawai tso lɛ
