english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass, called mulching, prevents soil moisture from drying out in the sun. It also blocks sunlight from reaching weed seeds, keeping your farm cleaner.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ akagbi yɛ hulu lɛ mli. Etsiɔ hulu la hu naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔ lɛ mli tseɔ

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunshine to make energy for growing heavy tubers underground. Lifting the vines on stakes elevates them into the sunlight and prevents leaf diseases caused by sitting on damp ground.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la babaoo koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni tsii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ awó wein tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaha wein tsei lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ hulu la mli, ni ebaatsi tso lɛ he helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ ni ooota lɛ mli baa lɛ naa.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my orange tree if I want bigger fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tso niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ ŋmei tso mli kɛji miitao aduawai wuji?

english: Removing weak or crowded branches opens up the tree so sunlight and fresh air can circulate to stop diseases. It also directs the tree's food and water straight into growing fewer, larger, and healthier fruits.
ga: Niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ naa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli koni helai akpa. Ekudɔɔ tso lɛ niyenii kɛ nu lɛ hu tɛ̃ɛ koni ewo yibii fioo, agbo, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I keep my crops alive when the rains stop for a long time?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Crops need continuous moisture to draw nutrients from the ground. When rains fail, spreading dry grass or leaves around the roots of your crops (mulching) acts like a blanket, trapping moisture in the soil and protecting roots from the hot sun.
ga: Tsei hia nu ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni okɛaawo oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he

english: Which food crops are best to plant when I expect very little rainfall?
ga: Mɛni ji niyenii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu beni mikpaa nugbɔ fioo ko pɛ gbɛ lɛ?

english: Crops like cassava, cowpeas, and millet have deep root systems or tough leaves that allow them to search for deep water and survive long dry periods much better than crops with shallow roots.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei, tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo baai ni wa ni haa amɛtaoɔ nu ni mli kwɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli be kakadaŋŋ fe tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ.

english: Is there a simple way for me to check if my soil has enough water for my crops?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni matsɔ nɔ makwɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: You can push a dry stick or your finger about two inches into the soil near your crops. If it comes out feeling cool with damp dirt clinging to it, your soil still has enough moisture for the plants.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tso nine ni egbi loo onine awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli aaafee inchi enyɔ ni bɛŋkɛ onibii lɛ. Kɛji enuɔ he akɛ edɔ ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa lolo ni baaha tsei akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow after heavy rains fall on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes essential plant nutrients deep down into the ground where small roots cannot reach them. Excess water also fills up all the air pockets in the soil, making it hard for roots to breathe.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. not accessible Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hu eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaamu.

english: What can I do to prevent heavy rain from washing away my topsoil and young crops?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anɔ?

english: Planting your crops in ridges across a slope rather than up and down it helps slow down flowing rainwater, forcing the water to sink into the soil instead of carrying your seeds and topsoil away.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji lɛ ahe kɛtsɔɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ŋwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Enɛ nyɛɔ nu lɛ nɔ ni eboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeeŋɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ.

english: Why do the roots of my crops rot when rain water stands on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen from the soil to stay healthy. When standing water covers your field for too long, it cuts off air to the roots, causing them to suffocate and decay.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ ha oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni haa egbɔjɔɔ ni egboɔ

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds during the rainy season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: It is best to wait until the rainy season has fully established after two or three steady, deep rains. Sowing after the very first light rain is risky because the ground can quickly dry up, killing young sprouting seeds.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaje shishi kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa ni nɛɔ daa enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ gboiɔ.

english: Why are my plants growing tall and thin instead of producing thick stems and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaana ŋmeii kɛ aduawai ni mli tse lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together or grow under heavy tree shade, they stretch upward searching for light. This wastes energy on height instead of building strong stems and healthy fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ ashishi Tso lɛ shwieɔ ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eyatao la. Enɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ yɛ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ tsohi nɛ a he wa kɛ yiblii nɛ ngɛ he wami.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the hot afternoon even when there was rain recently?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ enɛ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ?

english: In extreme afternoon heat, leaves lose water into the air faster than roots can pull water from the ground. Wilting is the plant's natural self-defense mechanism to curl up and reduce leaf area exposed to the sun.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Wilting ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe ni ekɛbaa he ni baai lɛ shɛɔ yɛ hulu la lɛ nɔ lɛ shi.

english: Why do my crops drop their flowers before producing any fruit during unpredictable weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni bɛ faŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: When a plant experiences severe weather stress—such as a sudden drought or unexpected heavy rain—it drops its flowers to save energy and water so the main plant can survive.
ga: Beni tsei kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni naa wa kpeɔ, tamɔ hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ. Tsei shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni tso titri lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the food plants need to grow green and strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer like urea will help bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii kɛha tsei ni miisumɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with many leaves, but the tubers underground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing tall stems and lush leaves above ground instead of sending nutrients down to expand the tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ tsei kakadaji kɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛba shi koni ekɛgbala ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ

english: Under strong sunshine, pepper leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can pull it from the ground. The plant wilts to protect itself from losing more moisture and will usually recover once the sun goes down.
ga: yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baafite lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and die off completely when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ egbi kwraa ni egbo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yam plants naturally dry up above ground once the underground tuber has finished growing and storing food. The dying vine is a signal that the yam is mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji akɛ agbe shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ akwɛmɔ naa ni amɛto niyenii. Wein tsei ni miigboi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potatoes lɛ eda ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil cool, helping the young cocoa survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hɔɔŋ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and produce tiny cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When seeds are planted too close, their roots fight each other for water and nutrients in the soil, and their leaves block sunlight from reaching each plant, leaving none of them with enough strength to form big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ tso fɛɛ tso he. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ eko kwraa bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha efee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young corn leaves with small droppings inside the funnel of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etse kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the inner leaves of the maize plant and eats the tender leaves before they unfold. Spraying recommended treatments into the funnel early can stop them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei amli baai amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛgbeleɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Akɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ afɔse tsofa lɛ awo ŋmeii amli mra. baanyɛ akpa

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning dark brown and sunken before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efoɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused when tomato plants cannot pull enough calcium from the soil, often due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil moisture steady helps the plant carry calcium to the growing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsɔɔ calcium lɛ gbɛ kɛyaa aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Garden egg flowers drop off without setting fruit when temperatures are extremely high, when plants don't get enough water, or when insects like bees are not around to transfer pollen from flower to flower.
ga: Eggplants ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo be mli ni kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii bɛŋkɛɛɛ amɛ. Koni akɛ pollen ajie kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko mli

english: Why do the seeds I saved from last year's hybrid maize harvest produce weaker plants with smaller yields this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ miiwo tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni wooo yibii babaoo lɛ afi nɛɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are special first-generation crosses bred for high yield, but their offspring do not keep the same strong traits. Replanting saved hybrid seed leads to mixed, lower-yielding plants, so buying fresh seed each season gives better results.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui ji klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ hybrids krɛdɛɛi ni atsɔse amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi amɛseshibii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ sui ni mli wa ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli. Hybrid dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ baaha tsei ni ji hybrid lɛ aba ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui heei ni ooohe daa be lɛ baaha yibii kpakpai aba.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my cocoa tree if I want it to grow well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo niji komɛi kɛji miisumɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or weak branches that steal food and water from the rest of the tree. When you trim unnecessary branches, the tree sends all its energy into growing strong stems and healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni egboi loo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ mli lɛ jieɔ tso lɛ niji lɛ. Beni ofoɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ tsei akutsei ni wa kɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni wa.

english: My cocoa farm has become very thick and bushy; will this affect my harvest?
ga: Mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli miifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ani enɛ baaná minikpamɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, when cocoa trees become too thick, sunlight and fresh air cannot pass through the canopy. This dark, damp environment encourages diseases like black pod to spread and prevents the trees from flowering properly.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni cacao lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ. Hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa nyɛɛɛ atsɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Shihilɛ ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ woɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji ahe hewalɛ, ni ehaaa tso lɛ awo fɔfɔi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What harm does it do if I leave dry and dead branches on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ awui baaba kɛji mishi niji ni egboi ni egbi yɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Dead branches act as hiding places for insects and pests. They also harbor harmful fungi and diseases that can easily spread to healthy parts of the cocoa tree and ruin your crop.
ga: Niji ni egboi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ teɔ shi amɛwoɔ amɛhe. Amɛhiɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ oshara kɛ helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kookoo tso lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli oya ni amɛfite onibii lɛ hu.

english: How does clearing away extra leaves and branches help my cocoa tree produce more pods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai kɛ eniji ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Removing extra growth allows sunlight to reach the inner trunk and main branches where cocoa flowers form. More sunlight on these areas stimulates the tree to produce more flowers, leading to a higher pod yield.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie shweremɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha hulu la lɛ ashɛ tso lɛ mligbɛ kɛ niji wuji ni kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ yɛ lɛ ahe. Hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ hei nɛɛ baawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji pod yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to put fertilizer on my cocoa land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mawo mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees continuously draw nutrients out of the soil to grow leaves and pods. Adding fertilizer replaces those lost nutrients, keeping the soil rich enough to support heavy yields year after year.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be koni amɛha baai kɛ ŋmeii akwɛ̃. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye niyenii ni elaaje lɛ najiaŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii bɔ ni sa ni ewoɔ nii babaoo daa afi.

english: How does applying fertilizer to the soil actually help my cocoa crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Fertilizer acts as food for the soil. The cocoa roots absorb these essential nutrients and carry them up to nourish the entire tree, resulting in stronger roots, healthier leaves, and larger cocoa pods.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Cocoa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ ni amɛwoɔ amɛ koni amɛha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shishifãi ni wa Baai lɛ yɛ hewalɛ. ni kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ dara fe no

english: Will applying fertilizer help my old cocoa trees yield well again?
ga: Ani mi-kookoo tso momo lɛ ni mikɛwo mli lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, older cocoa trees often sit in worn-out soil that has lost its goodness. Adding the right fertilizer feeds the depleted soil, giving aging trees the boost they need to produce good yields again.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, cacao tsei ni egbɔ lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛtara shikpɔŋ ni efite nɔ ni amɛhilɛ-kɛhamɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ehe miihia ni tsei ni egbɔ lɛ awo yibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need direct sunlight to reach inside their branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ he hiaa mi cacao tso lɛ koni eshɛ eniji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Sunlight helps the leaves make food for the tree and keeps the farm dry. Dry conditions prevent dangerous molds and fungi from growing on the cocoa pods and branches.
ga: Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii amɛhaa tsei lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ. Shihilɛ ni mli egbi lɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ kookoo tsei kɛ tsei aniji anɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees have enough space and airflow between them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ amɛteŋ?

english: If you can comfortably walk through your farm and see sunlight filtering down through the canopy to the ground, your trees have good airflow and light to grow healthily.
ga: Kɛji obaanyɛ otsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli mlɛo ni ona hulu ni miikpɛ kɛmiitsɔ hulutsoo be lɛ mli kɛmiiba shikpɔŋ lɛ Otsei lɛ hu yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ la ni baaha amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the overall benefit of keeping my cocoa farm trimmed and well-fed throughout the year?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni makwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ he?

english: A well-trimmed and fertilized farm suffers far less from pests and diseases, uses soil nutrients efficiently, and rewards you with bigger pods and higher total cocoa yields.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni awo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ naaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo. Kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni ewo bo nyɔmɔ kɛ ŋmeii wuji kɛ kookoo yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni fa babaoo.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or when heavy rains wash away nutrients. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the leaves regain their green color so the plant can grow strong.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil, helping companion crops like maize grow better without needing as much bought fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni fata he, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛhe ŋmãa babaoo tamɔ nɛkɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb up into sunlight so their leaves can produce food for the growing tuber under the ground. Staking also lifts leaves off the wet soil, preventing diseases and helping the plant make larger yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the fruit starts growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that cannot easily support heavy bunches when strong winds blow. Propping up the main stem with a sturdy wooden pole gives the tree extra support until the plantains are ready for harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ aye abua ŋmɔlɔ ni tsii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aye abua lɛ babaoo kɛyashi be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why is it important to leave some large shade trees on my land when planting new cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi tsei wuji yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ midu kookoo hee lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Large shade trees protect young cocoa from harsh heat, keep the soil cool and moist, and shield the farm from harsh winds.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. ni ebu ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he

english: Cocoa flowers often fall off due to dry soil conditions, lack of plant food, or damage from sucking pests like mirids. Maintaining good shade and keeping the soil moist helps the flowers stay attached and form pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ hewɔ lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tso niyenii ni bɛ loo ni kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii ni nuɔ lɛ efite. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo kpakpa haa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ hiɔ shi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and turning yellow on the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by viruses carried by tiny flying insects called whiteflies, or by extreme heat stress. Keeping insects away early in the season and keeping the plant watered helps prevent this damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni foɔ lɛ woɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni haa tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly loo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ to he ko yɛ be lɛ mli mra ni okɛ nu haa otsei lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akafite nɛkɛ nii nɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when the soil stays too wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ?

english: When heavy rain fills the soil with water for too long, air cannot reach the roots, causing the cassava to drown. This wet environment allows rot-causing fungi and bacteria to grow quickly and spoil the tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. drown the cassava Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni mli efɔ nɛɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ daa oya ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers without producing any peppers during hot spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛ pepper baaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants get stressed when soil temperatures are very high or when water is scarce, causing them to shed flowers to survive. Covering the soil around the plants with dried grass or leaves helps keep the root zone cool and moist.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ naa haomɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa waa loo nu faaa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ amɛfɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why can swamp rice grow directly in standing water while my cassava and maize will die if flooded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi-cassava kɛ ŋmãa lɛ baagboi kɛji nu afua lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal pathways in their stems that move air down from the leaves directly to the submerged roots. Other crops lack these air tubes and suffocate when their roots are trapped under standing water.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko ni yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ jɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei krokomɛi bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ efo nu ni yɔɔ dioo shishi.

english: In which direction should I align my crop rows to make sure all my plants get equal sunlight?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ mato miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ koni tsei fɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Planting rows from North to South allows sunlight to pass evenly over the plants from morning to evening, preventing tall plants from blocking sunlight from shorter neighbor plants throughout the day.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli kɛjɛɔ kooyigbɛ kɛyaa anaigbɛ lɛ haa hulu la boteɔ tsei lɛ amli pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛjɛɔ leebi kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ. Tsi tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei kukuji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ naa yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why does the hot afternoon sun seem to cause more stress to my vegetables than the morning sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa mi-aduawai lɛ haoɔ fe leebi hulu lɛ?

english: Morning sun provides gentle light needed for growth while temperatures are still cool, whereas afternoon sun comes with intense heat that rapidly dries out soil moisture and strains the plant's water supply.
ga: Leebi hulu la lɛ haa la ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni he hiaa koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shwane hulu lɛ baa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni ehaa tsei lɛ nu ni amɛnáa lɛ he feɔ shoo.

english: Cassava leaves fold or droop during extreme heat to reduce the leaf surface exposed to direct sunlight, helping the plant hold onto water until temperatures cool down.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ fɔ̃ɔ amɛhe loo amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ bei amli koni hulu la ni baa baa lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants shed their flowers whenever the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, pepper plants drop their blossoms to conserve energy and water, protecting the main body of the plant from dying due to heat stress.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Ebuɔ tso lɛ fã titri lɛ he koni ekagbo yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like tubes on extremely sunny days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up inward to trap moisture and decrease exposure to intense sunlight, which slows down water loss through evaporation during dry spells.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli koni amɛmɔmɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛha hulu la ni naa wa lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa nu ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and turn brown when planted in an open sunny field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct heat and bright sunlight; they require temporary shade crops like plantains to shelter them until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why do farmers cover the tops of fresh yam mounds with dry leaves after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ baai ni egbi haa sweet potatoes heei lɛ anɔ beni amɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Dry leaves act as a protective cap that blocks strong sunlight from heating up the soil inside the mound, keeping the seed yam cool so it does not rot or burn before sprouting.
ga: Baai ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni haa hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli adɔ. Ha sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ afee fɛ̃i koni amɛkafite loo amɛkashã dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help them survive intense sunshine?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishitoo yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛjeɔ hulu ni naa wa lɛ mli?

english: Dry grass acts as mulch that shades the bare soil from direct sunlight, keeping the root zone cool and preventing groundwater from evaporating quickly.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch ni buɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa shishifã lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ shwieɔ oya.

english: Can planting tall crops like maize alongside shorter crops help protect them from strong heat?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛlɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kukuji ahe lɛ baanyɛ abu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he?

english: Yes, taller crops can act as a natural barrier that casts partial shade over sensitive, shorter plants, creating a cooler microclimate that shields them from scorching heat.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni kɛlɛ baanyɛ atsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbogboi ni haa hulutsoo fã ko yɛ tsei kukuji ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko ni buɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he lɛ baa.

english: Why do my tomatoes get soft, pale patches on the side facing direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Yɛ fã ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: This condition is called sunscald, which happens when intense direct sunlight overheats the fruit skin, cooking the tissue under the surface when there are not enough leaves to shade the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ scald. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni aduawai lɛ ahewolo lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ shishi fãji lɛ feɔ kɛji baai ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ bɛ.

english: Why should I test my soil before I start planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka mishikpɔŋ lɛ makwɛ dani mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: Testing your soil is like taking your land for a medical check-up. It shows you exactly which nutrients your soil is missing so you only spend money on the exact fertilizers your crops need to thrive.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛyaa koni ayakwɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ. Etsɔɔ bo niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ ni bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ oshika miifite yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛshwere lɛ pɛ he.

english: Why does planting beans or cowpeas make my soil richer for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo kɛha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans have special roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When the roots decompose, they leave behind natural food that feeds your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Beni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli niyenii akɛ niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I use a planting machine instead of planting my seeds by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛduɔ nii atsu nii moŋ fe ni mikɛ nine baadu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Mechanized planters place every seed at the exact same depth and distance apart. This ensures all your seeds sprout evenly and don't compete with each other for water and sunlight.
ga: Mɔ ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛ dumɔwui fɛɛ dumɔwui woɔ he ko ni mli kwɔ kɛ bɔ ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ ha lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ hulu la he.

english: Why do these new hybrid seed varieties perform better than the seeds I saved from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɛkɛ dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee ekome nɛɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to fight off local diseases, withstand drought, and produce heavier yields. Saved seeds lose their strength over seasons and become weak against pests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni akɛwu ashi maŋ lɛ mli helai. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ ni ekɛ yibiiwoo ni tsii baa Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ he waaa yɛ be lɛ mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aye amɛ oya.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural self-defense against heat. The plant curls its leaves into tubes to hide from the direct sun and trap moisture inside so it does not dry out.
ga: Baai lɛ ni oootsi lɛ ji gbɛ ni otsɔɔ nɔ obuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli dɔlɛ he. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli amɛwoɔ tsɔnei amli koni amɛkɛtee hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni amɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ koni amɛkagbi.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for help caused by a lack of nitrogen or roots sitting in too much water. When soil stays flooded, roots drown and cannot absorb nutrients for the foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ foɔ amɛbiɔ yelikɛbuamɔ ni nitrogen ni bɛ loo shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu babaoo mli lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe niyenii ni haa tsei lɛ baa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunshine. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as natural umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and moist in its early stages.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ shishijee fãi lɛ amli.

english: Plants shed their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat or lack of water. The plant discards the flowers to conserve energy so it can stay alive during dry periods.
ga: Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my tomatoes very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mitatoi lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Crowding plants forces their roots to fight for food and water underground. It also blocks airflow between leaves, creating a damp environment where diseases spread quickly.
ga: Tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ koni amɛwu amɛtao niyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ hu naa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni helai srɔtoi baa mli lɛ baa. gbɛɔ eshwaa oya

english: Why do I need to cut off the bottom leaves of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ?

english: Trimming bottom leaves prevents rainy-season soil from splashing diseases onto the foliage. It also forces the plant to send its food energy into growing big fruit rather than extra leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afo shishigbɛ baai lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔshiimɔ be mli sũ lɛ akagbɛ hela eshwa baai lɛ anɔ. Enyɛɔ tsei anɔ hu koni amɛkɛ amɛ niyenii hewalɛ lɛ atsu nii kɛwo aduawai wuji amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsu baai babaoo kɛya.

english: Leaves turn yellow mainly when the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or when the roots are sitting in too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or improving drainage helps the leaves get green and healthy again.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ titri lɛ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ yɛ nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he loo nu ni hoɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How far apart should I space my cassava stems when planting them on my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo ŋmei tsei lɛ amli kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stems should generally be planted about one meter apart from each other. Giving them enough space prevents them from competing for sunlight and soil nutrients, allowing bigger tubers to grow under the ground.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei lɛ aaafee mita kome kɛjɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ aha amɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii wuji baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally adapt to soak up water and nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing food and water from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu kɛ niyenii amli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Okɛ ohe awo mli mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli.

english: Is it better for me to apply fertilizer when the ground is dry or after rain?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist, not completely dry or flooded. Moist soil helps the roots dissolve and absorb the nutrients quickly without burning the crop.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Egbi kwraa loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ niyenii mli oya ni amɛshãaa tso lɛ.

english: What is making small holes in the leaves of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Mi pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Small holes in leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like beetles or caterpillars feeding on them. Inspecting under the leaves and applying an approved organic or safe insecticide early in the morning can protect the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi ni okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ eji nɔ ko ni wala bɛ mli loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ awo mli leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests when I plant the exact same crop on it every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating different crops, like planting beans before maize, restores nutrients naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ dani aduɔ ŋmãa. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees grow better when I keep large trees scattered on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ migbɛ tsei wuji ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily under direct heat. Shade trees act like umbrellas to shield young cocoa from harsh sunlight while dropping leaves that turn into rich soil manure.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela koni amɛkɛbu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ashɛrɛɔ baai ni bafeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii lɛ ashwieɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants curl up and droop in the afternoon heat even if I watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: In hot afternoon weather, leaves lose water faster than roots can drink it from the soil, causing wilting to conserve moisture. Covering the soil around the plant base with dry grass helps keep roots cool and moist.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha amɛgbi koni ŋmɔtɔ akahi shi. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do some of the seeds I plant fail to sprout out of the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are planted too deep, if the soil is too dry, or if insects eat them underground. Planting seeds at a shallow depth in moist soil ensures they can break through easily.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. loo kooloi bibii ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi dumɔwui Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ boteɔ mli mlɛo.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains turn to powder and get tiny bugs inside the storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ji powder ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? yɛ nitoo kotoku mli

english: Stored grains attract insects like weevils if the corn is not dried completely before bagging or if moisture gets in. Drying grain until it crackles and using airtight storage bags keeps insects out without heavy chemicals.
ga: Nibii ni ato lɛ baagbala kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛwo kotoku mli loo kɛji akɛ ŋmeii yɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni agbiɔ kɛyashiɔ ebaagbala Ni akɛ vacuum storage bags atsu nii koni ŋmeii lɛ akaje mli ni tsofai ni tsii bɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed to produce food. Without enough nitrogen, the plant cannot make chlorophyll, causing its leaves to turn pale or yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha niyenii feemɔ Kɛji nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee chlorophyll. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does my maize crop make big leaves but small ears if I apply fertilizer too late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa agboi shi etoi bibii kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa wo mli yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crops use nutrients differently depending on their growth stage. Early fertilizer builds stems and leaves, but if applied too late, the plant cannot shift that energy into filling out the grain inside the cobs.
ga: Tsei kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa lɛ naa. Shishijee lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ tsei kɛ baai. Shi kɛji akɛ okɛwo mli sɛɛ tsɔ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ atsake nakai hewalɛ lɛ ni ekɛ dumɔwui awo ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch unnaturally high to reach the light, making their stems weak and thin.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa he ko ni nɔ kwɔ waa koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni efeɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do my tall maize plants easily fall over when a heavy rainstorm hits the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei kakadaji lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ahum ni naa wa miitswa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize falls over when its root system is too weak or shallow to anchor the heavy top of the plant, often caused by poor soil depth, overcrowding, or high winds blowing softened wet soil.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ loo amɛmli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua tso lɛ shishifãi ni tsii lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. overcrowding Aloo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko miitswa kɛmiitsɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my cassava crop drop its leaves during the dry season and grow new ones when the rain comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, ebaa ehee lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during droughts to stop water from escaping through leaf pores. This survival trick lets the root stay alive underground until fresh rainfall triggers new leaf growth.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu akatsɔ baai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli. Nɛkɛ yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaa nɛɛ haa shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ haa baai heei kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why does placing dry grass around the roots of my plantains help them survive hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) acts like a shade blanket. It keeps the soil cool, protects the roots from direct heat, and traps moisture in the ground for much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulching) shwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛtsiɔ hulu lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ebuɔ shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be babaoo

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their small flowers before they turn into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Mɛi enyiɛ dani etsɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce many extra flowers, but if the tree feels stressed by heat, lack of water, or low soil food, it drops flowers to preserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi krɛdɛɛi babaoo. But if the plant feels stressed from heat, lack of water, or low food in the soil The plant will drop flowers to conserve energy for its own survival.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and soft before they fully ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efee blɛoo dani ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ?

english: This problem is caused by a shortage of calcium in the growing fruit, often due to irregular soil watering that prevents the plant's roots from taking up calcium evenly.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ naagba nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ naa calcium daa.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites living under the leaves, or by plant viruses spread by these insects that distort normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ mli

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and adapted to the local soil. They sprout instantly and absorb moisture faster than farm crops, which need more time to establish delicate root systems.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔji ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Amɛkwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛheɔ nu oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ heɔ be babaoo dani anyɛɔ amaa shishifã ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during dry spells to reduce water loss and stay alive. The plant is not dead; it is protecting itself while the roots underneath continue to hold the crop safely.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu ni efiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni ehi wala mli. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ebuɔ ehe he yɛ be mli ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ eshishi lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build strong stems and green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shi waa.

english: Why do my pepper plants roll their leaves inward during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl inward during high heat to hide from direct sunlight and reduce the amount of water evaporating from their surface, keeping the plant cool and hydrated.
ga: Ha ni ebɔle ehe kɛya mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekɛtee hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ baa shi. Ha tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and overly shaded environments. It spreads when rain droplets splash fungal spores from wet soil or infected leaves onto the pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ fe nine. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji nugbɔshiimɔi shwie fungal spores kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ loo baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛshwie ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my plantain tree die right after harvesting one bunch of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbo trukaa beni mikpa aduawai akuu kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain stem is designed to flower and produce fruit only once in its life cycle. Once harvest is complete, the main stem naturally dies so its nutrients can feed the young shoots (suckers) growing around its base.
ga: Afee plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli. Kɛ́ agbe kpamɔ lɛ naa lɛ Tso titri lɛ baagbo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii bibii (ŋmei) ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ niyenii.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive shade. Without proper balance or insect visits to pollinate them, the plant aborts the blossoms to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo hulutsoo babaoo hao amɛ. Kɛji akɛ nɔ ko bɛ ni ŋmɛɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ loo kooloi ni baa koni amɛbafee pollination lɛ, Tsei lɛ baafo fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop dark, rotten patches at the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egboɔ yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This is blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium while the fruit is growing, often caused by irregular watering where the soil flips between too wet and too dry.
ga: Enɛ ji blossom end rot, ni baa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔ lɛ daa, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ teŋ.

english: How can I tell that my yams under the ground are fully ripe and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yam tubers reach full maturity when the above-ground leaves and vines dry up and turn brown, showing that the plant has stopped growing and transferred all its stored energy into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛdalɛ he beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛto lɛ etee ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over so easily whenever a heavy rain wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Maize falls over when its root foundation is weak, which happens if seeds were planted too shallow, spaced too closely together, or if stem borer pests have chewed through the base of the stalk.
ga: Abɛi baagbee shi kɛ́ eshishifãi lɛ ashishitoo lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. Gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ fa tsɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ ŋmɔ tso lɛ ni etsɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are native to the soil, meaning their roots absorb water and nutrients much faster and more aggressively than cultivated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya kwraa kɛ hewalɛ fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: How does planting my crops on uneven or sloping land affect how they grow?
ga: Te mitsei lɛ ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ etseee loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ saa amɛdalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Uneven land causes rainwater to collect in low areas while washing away topsoil and fertilizers from higher spots. This makes crops in lower sections risk root rot from excess water, while crops on upper slopes may suffer from nutrient starvation and thirst.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ haa nugbɔ nu buaa ehe naa yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, yɛ be mli ni efoɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ oshara akɛ shishifãi lɛ baafite kɛjɛ nu ni fa fe nine mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ gɔji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ana niyenii ni esaaa kɛ kumai.

english: What can I do to keep heavy rains from washing away my topsoil on sloping farmland?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: You can dig contour bunds or plant rows of grass across the slope instead of down the hill. These barriers slow down runoff water, giving it time to soak into the ground while trapping soil and nutrients on your field.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa jwɛi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ loo odu jwɛi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ooojɛ gɔŋ lɛ shishi. Nɛkɛ gbɛtsii nii nɛɛ haa nu ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa enáa be ni ekɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehiɛɔ sũ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ oyale mli.

english: Why does the lower stem of my grafted seedling look different from the upper part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwu ni akɛwo tso mli lɛ shishigbɛ tso lɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Grafted plants are made by joining two different plants together. The bottom part (rootstock) provides strong roots to resist soil diseases, while the top part (scion) comes from a high-quality mother plant chosen to produce abundant latex or fruit.
ga: Akɛ tsei enyɔ ni akɛfataa he lɛ feɔ tsei ni akɛwo mli lɛ. Shishigbɛ fã (shishifã) lɛ haa shishifãi ni wa koni ekɛte shi ewo helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛigbɛ fã lɛ (nine) lɛ jɛ nyɛ tso ko ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ahala koni ekɛ latɛs loo aduawai babaoo aba lɛ mli.

english: If a branch grows out from the bottom stem below the join mark on my seedling, should I cut it off?
ga: Kɛji niji dara kɛjɛ shishigbɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ fã ni yɔɔ dumɔwu lɛ nɔ lɛ shishi. Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ?

english: Yes, you should cut it off immediately. That lower shoot comes from the rootstock plant, which produces low-quality yield. If left to grow, it will steal food and water from the high-yielding top part of your tree.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ ofo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Tso lɛ shishifãi ni baa shi lɛ jɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli, ni no haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi lɛ baa. Kɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ Ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ anɔgbɛ fãi lɛ amli.

english: Why should I buy grafted rubber seedlings instead of just planting seeds I collected from old trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe gumdrop dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei momoi amli lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Seeds from rubber trees do not grow into exact copies of their parent tree and often give unpredictable, lower yields. Grafted seedlings guarantee that every tree in your farm will produce high amounts of latex uniform in quality.
ga: Dumɔwui ni jɛɔ rɔba tsei amli lɛ edaaa kɛfeɔ tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ he mfoniri pɛpɛɛpɛ. ni bei pii lɛ, amɛwoɔ yibii ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba ni baa shi. Dumɔwui ni akɛwo tso mli lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baawo nu ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: How do I know which rubber tree clone or variety is best for my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male muji tai loo tai henɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Different varieties are bred for specific qualities like fast trunk growth, resistance to strong winds, or early latex production. Extension officers recommend specific certified clones based on your local rainfall patterns and soil type.
ga: Afɔ henɔi srɔtoi koni amɛná sui pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ tsei ni daa oya kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ. loo afee latex oya Extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ muji ni awo he odaseyeli pɔtɛɛ ko he ŋaa yɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do crops planted in the middle of my farm sometimes look healthier than those at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsei ni adu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Soil depth, moisture retention, and shade levels often change across a single plot. The middle of a field usually holds water and organic matter better, whereas border areas may face more sun exposure, wind drying, or nutrient competition from nearby wild bushes.
ga: shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ mli kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome mli. Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahiɛmɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, husu hei baanyɛ akpe hulu babaoo, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi loo akaŋshii kɛha niyenii ni jɛɔ koo mli jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young seedlings stop growing for a few weeks right after I transplant them into the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ otsii fioo komɛi beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: This is called transplant shock. The young plant is focusing its energy underground to rebuild damaged roots and establish itself in the new soil before it can start growing new leaves on top.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Tso bibioo lɛ miibua ehewalɛ naa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛma shishifãi ni efite lɛ ekoŋŋ ni ekɛ ehe awo shikpɔŋ hee nɔ. Dani baai heei baaje kpo yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin without producing much yield when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are overcrowded, they compete for sunlight. They waste all their energy stretching upward to reach the sun instead of developing thick stems, strong roots, and abundant fruits or latex.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛshɛɔ hulu lɛ he lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofee tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ aduawai babaoo loo latɛs.

english: Why do some branches on my tree turn pale and weak while the rest of the tree looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji komɛi ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Pale branches are often shaded out by upper leaves and fail to get enough sunlight to make plant food. They can also be a sign of early localized pest damage or nutrient blockage in that specific branch.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋwɛi baai lɛ haa tsei niji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfee tsei niyenii. Ebaanyɛ efee okadi hu ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai efite he ni eyɔɔ lɛ mra loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nakai tso lɛ nine pɔtɛɛ lɛ naa lɛ.

english: When the bottom leaves turn yellow in a V-shape pattern, it usually means your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen is an essential food plant roots take from the soil to stay green and grow strong.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei shishifãi jieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up and stop growing well?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from under the leaves, or by a virus spread by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for limited food in the soil, water, and sunlight, leaving every plant weak and malnourished.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ kɛha niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la ni faaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ amɛmli.

english: Why do young cocoa trees die when I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. They need partial shade from nurse crops like plantains to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Heavy rain can cause water to settle around cassava roots, preventing oxygen from reaching them. Soil saturated with water creates an ideal environment for harmful fungi and bacteria that rot the tubers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha nu abɔle ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ tuber rot baa lɛ.

english: Why do dry leaves or straw put around my crops help them survive the dry season?
ga: No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni akɛbɔle Miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass (called mulching) acts like an umbrella, keeping the soil cool and stopping moisture from evaporating into the hot air.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ umbrella Ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when temperatures get too high, when water is irregular, or when the plant experiences sudden stress from extreme dry heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni tsei naa haomɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ latsaa ni mli egbi waa lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to cut off side shoots from my tomato plants as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ ahe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ afã be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Cutting off small side shoots helps the plant direct all its food and energy into developing bigger, healthier fruits rather than wasting energy on extra stems and leaves.
ga: ŋmeii bibii ni afoɔ ni ashiɔ lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akudɔ eniyenii kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ tsei ashishifãi kɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking also prevents leaves from lying in wet soil where diseases easily spread.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ yɛ he ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ nɔ.

english: How do weeds growing nearby actually hurt the growth of my main crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ saa miŋmɔ titri lɛ dalɛ he yɛ gbɛ fɔŋ nɔ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm; their aggressive roots steal fertilizer and water intended for your crops, and their tall foliage blocks vital sunlight.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ basabasa lɛ baaju ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Ni baai kakadaji lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa lɛ naa.

english: How do I know which specific crops will grow best on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops depend heavily on your soil type, how much water the land holds, and local weather patterns. Getting your soil tested or observing what crops naturally thrive in your immediate area helps you pick crops that will give you high yields without wasting money.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ henɔ nɔ. Nu babaoo ni shikpɔŋ lɛ toɔ kɛ he ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi yɔɔ ha lɛ fa babaoo Oshikpɔŋ lɛ kaa loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ akutso lɛ mli lɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ohala tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni okɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naaa.

english: If I have a large piece of land, is it better to plant just one crop or mix different crops together?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ shikpɔŋ wulu ko Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ tso kome loo tsei srɔtoi ni akɛfutu mli?

english: Planting different crops together, known as intercropping, protects you against total loss if a pest attacks or the weather fails. It also keeps the soil healthy because different plants use and return different nutrients to the ground.
ga: Tsei babaoo ni ooodu yɛ he kome, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ intercropping lɛ buɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ nibii ni baafite kwraa lɛ ahe kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai batutua bo loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ bafee nɔ ni ehiii. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ tsei kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that your plants are hungry for nutrients, particularly nitrogen, or that too much water is choking their roots. Adding compost, animal manure, or the right fertilizer will give them the food they need to stay green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha niyenii kpakpai. titri lɛ nitrogen Aloo nu babaoo yɛ ni shishifãi lɛ miihoso. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha amɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does planting legumes like beans or groundnuts help the other crops on my farm?
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi. yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Legumes have a special ability to take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil. When you harvest them, they leave that rich nitrogen behind, which naturally fertilizes the soil for heavy-feeding crops like cassava or maize.
ga: Legumes yɛ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛkɛjieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okpa amɛ Amɛshiɔ nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛsɛɛ. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei.

english: Why do my crops wither quickly during short dry spells even when I water them occasionally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli yɛ be kɛ bei amli moŋ.

english: Light watering only dampens the top layer of soil, which makes plant roots stay near the surface where the sun easily dries them out. Watering deeply encourages roots to grow far down into the ground where moisture stays hidden much longer.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ fioo lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ he ni hulu la baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbi mlɛo lɛ. Nu ni awoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ baahi shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ.

english: What happens to my crops when a heavy downpour comes after a long dry period?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ?

english: Sudden heavy rain after a drought can shock dry plants, wash away valuable topsoil, and rot roots if the water pools on the land. Creating simple drainage paths on your farm helps excess water flow away safely without damaging your crops.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ hɔmɔ sɛɛ baanyɛ aha tsei aya dry shock mli. Ekɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa lɛ tsuɔ nii. ni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni hoɔ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ooofee yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe ni efiteee oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are my harvest yields reducing every year even though I use the same farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ lɛ?

english: Growing the exact same crop in the same spot season after season drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating your crops each season gives the soil time to rest and rebuild its strength.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ ehewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How exactly do weeds slow down the growth of my main crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ dalɛ baa shi?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal essential sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. By removing weeds early, you ensure all the land's nourishment goes straight into growing your food.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ aya tɛ̃ɛ kɛya oniyenii lɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from intense heat, irregular watering, or a lack of key minerals in the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps the flowers stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo minerals ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why can cassava stay alive through long dry seasons much better than maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cassava is a naturally hardy crop that stores food and water underground in its large roots and sheds its leaves during extreme dry spells to conserve moisture, allowing it to survive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava ji tso ko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛ niyenii kɛ nu toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ eshishifãi wuji lɛ amli. ni eshwieɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa koni ekɛha hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi Ha ehi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why is April usually the best time for us to start buying seeds and preparing to plant in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ April ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ wɔje dumɔwui ahemɔ shishi ni wɔsaa wɔhe koni wɔdu yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: April marks the beginning of the major rainy season in most parts of Ghana. Planting during this time ensures that seeds get enough moisture from the rains to germinate quickly and establish strong root systems before any dry spell.
ga: April ji nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ shishijee yɛ Ghana hei babaoo. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. ni amɛma shishifãi ni mli wa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba

english: How do I know if the crop seeds I buy from market traders are good enough for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔ?

english: Good planting seeds should be whole, clean, dry, and free from insect holes or mold. You can test them by putting a sample in a bucket of water; seeds that sink are usually healthy and full, while seeds that float are often damaged or empty inside.
ga: Esa akɛ adu dumɔwui kpakpai ni eye emuu, ni he tse, ni egbi, ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bɛ mli. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ko ni okɛaawo nu baagi mli lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni egbo lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛyi obɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni hoɔ yɛ nu hiɛ lɛ fiteɔ loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Is it better for me to buy planting seeds directly from another farmer or from market traders?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ kɛjɛ okwaafoi krokomɛi adɛŋ tɛ̃ɛ loo kɛjɛ jarayelɔi adɛŋ?

english: Buying certified seeds from specialized dealers or reputable farmers is usually safer than buying grain from general market traders. Market traders often sell crops meant for eating, which may have been heat-treated, stored poorly, or mixed with different varieties that won't grow well together.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ jarayelɔ ko ni he esa loo okwaafonyo ko ni ehe gbɛi waa ŋɔɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe fe dumɔwui ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ jarayelɔ babaoo dɛŋ. Bei pii lɛ, jarayelɔi hɔ̃ɔ nibii ni amɛduɔ koni amɛye. Ekolɛ akɛ amɛ etsu nii yɛ la mli, akɛtooo jogbaŋŋ, loo akɛ henɔi srɔtoi efutu mli. ni shwereee jogbaŋŋ yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli

english: Why do buyers pay so much attention to the size and physical appearance of my fruits before buying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ susuɔ mi-fruit lɛ dalɛ kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ he waa dani amɛheɔ lɛ?

english: Buyers inspect fruit appearance because consumers and processing companies prefer uniform, unblemished produce. External spots or small sizes often indicate pest damage, disease, or poor nutritional content, which lowers the selling price.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kwɛɔ bɔ ni aduawai lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ mli ejaakɛ mɛi ni heɔ lɛ kɛ nitsumɔhei ni feɔ aduawai lɛ sumɔɔ aduawai ni yaa nɔ daa, ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he. Bei pii lɛ, kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii loo amɛdalɛ bibioo tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii efite, hela, loo niyenii ni esaaa. ni haa jara ni akɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ baa shi

english: Why is my plant growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but it isn't producing any fruit yet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi nɔ ko kwraa bɛ ni jɛɔ mli baa lolo?

english: Excessive leaf growth without fruit usually happens when the plant gets too much nitrogen fertilizer and not enough phosphorus or potassium. It can also mean the plant is still in its vegetative growth stage or is not receiving enough direct sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yaa hiɛ fe nine ni yibii bɛ mli lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ ni enáaa phosphorus loo potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ hu akɛ tso lɛ yɛ e-vegetative stage lɛ mli lolo loo enine shɛɛɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do international buyers reject some of our harvested crops from being sold overseas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ majimaji ateŋ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ wɔkpamɔi lɛ ekomɛi ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Export markets have strict rules regarding crop size, appearance, pest damage, and chemical residues. If produce does not meet these exact specifications, it cannot be shipped overseas because it might spoil during transport or fail international food safety inspections.
ga: Jarayelihei ni akɛ nibii yaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ yɛ mlai ni mli wa yɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ, amɛhefɛo, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe. kɛ tsofai ni eshwɛ Kɛji akɛ nibii ni afee lɛ eshɛɛɛ nɛkɛ shishitoo mlai nɛɛ ahe lɛ Anyɛɛɛ akɛ amɛ amaje majimaji ateŋ ejaakɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite yɛ gbɛfaa mli loo amɛkafee majimaji ateŋ niyenii shweshweeshwefeemɔ he kwɛmɔi.

english: Why should I sort my harvested fruits into different groups before taking them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majara mi yibii ni mikpa lɛ amli awo kui srɔtoi amli lɛ? Dani akɛbaajara nɔ?

english: Sorting allows you to separate high-quality produce from damaged ones so you can sell the best items at a higher price. It also prevents diseased or bruised fruits from touching and spoiling the healthy ones during storage and transport.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ haa onyɛɔ ogbalaa nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛɔ nibii ni efite lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni onyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu koni aduawai ni hela emɔ amɛ loo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ akataa aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ kɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my crop drop off before the actual fruits can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when plants experience stress caused by sudden heat, lack of water, or pest infestation. It can also happen if insects like bees are not available to pollinate the flowers properly.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ ni dɔlɛ trukaa, nu ni bɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ tsei lɛ kɛbaa lɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔii amli ŋmeii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I save seeds from the fruits I harvest this season to plant again next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ aduawai ni mikpaa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: While you can replant seeds from traditional open-pollinated crops, seeds saved from hybrid crop varieties will not produce the same high yield or disease resistance as the original plant. It is best to buy fresh certified hybrid seeds every season.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ blema tsei ni agbele naa lɛ amli lɛ adu ekoŋŋ moŋ, shi dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ tsei srɔtoi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baahaaa yibii babaoo loo helai nyɛŋ amɔ amɛ tamɔ shishijee tsei lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa be mli.

english: Why do produce buyers only come to our farms looking for crops during specific months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baa wɔŋmɔji amli koni amɛbakwɛ nibii ni aduɔ yɛ nyɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ko mli pɛ lɛ?

english: Buyers time their purchases around peak consumer demand, factory processing schedules, and seasonal harvest windows. Harvesting during these periods ensures buyers can quickly transport and sell fresh produce before it spoils.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ be ni amɛheɔ lɛ toɔ amɛ jarayelɔi ahiamɔ nii ni fe fɛɛ lɛ anaa. Nitsumɔhe lɛ nitsumɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo kɛ be ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ bei nɛɛ amli lɛ haa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛkɛ nibii heei ni amɛwo lɛ yaa oya ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ dani amɛfiteɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen, which acts like food for their growth. Adding compost, manure, or the right fertilizer puts nitrogen back into the soil so the maize can grow strong and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii koni ekwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni ŋmãa lɛ atsɔ hewalɛ ni efee eŋɔli

english: What causes my corn plants to stay very short and weak even after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛhe waaa yɛ nugbɔ po sɛɛ?
