english: Stunted corn often happens when the soil lacks nutrients, is packed too tightly for roots to spread, or is damaged by tiny pests in the ground. Adding organic matter helps roots breathe and soak up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni ji dwarf lɛ baa be mli ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyi obɔ kɛ nibii tsɔ ni shishifãi nyɛŋ akwɛ̃. loo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ efite lɛ, kɛ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmuɔ ni amɛmɔɔ niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves of my young corn plants rolling up tightly during the daytime?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Corn leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing water when the sun is very hot. However, if they stay rolled up during cool mornings and evenings, it means the roots are suffering from drought or pest damage.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Shi, kɛji amɛtee nɔ amɛbɔle amɛhe yɛ leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ, No tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ miikpe hɔmɔ loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my bean plants have many leaves but fail to produce plenty of bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo shi ewooo ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: When bean plants get too much fertilizer or water, they spend all their energy growing leaves instead of flowers. Giving them balanced soil nutrients helps them focus on producing more bean pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ná ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu babaoo Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni amɛdaraa lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa ni akɛhaa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii babaoo ni amɛbaafee lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it dangerous if the leaves of my bean crop have small holes and brown spots on them?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara kɛji akɛ mi-bean tso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii? Ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ?

english: Holes and brown spots mean insects or fungal diseases are attacking your crop. Catching this early allows extension officers to show you safe ways to treat the field before the whole crop gets destroyed.
ga: Buji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii loo ŋmɔtɔ helai miitutua oŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ ni ooomɔ mra Enɛ baaha sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔmɔ nitsulɔi lɛ atsɔɔ bo nifeemɔi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe dani akpata ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do my young bean stems turn soft and fall over right at the soil level?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tsei bibii lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛmiigbee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by stem rot fungi that thrive in overly wet soil. Planting in well-drained soil and using healthy seeds prevents this fungus from killing your young crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei ko ni egbo ni shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ fe nine nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ odu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ ni okɛ dumɔwui kpakpai tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ ŋmei nɛɛ naa koni ekagbe otsei bibii lɛ.

english: Why does planting maize and beans together in the same field help both crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans naturally fix nitrogen from the air into the soil, which acts as food for the maize. In return, tall maize plants help shade the ground and keep the soil moist for the beans.
ga: Beans saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmãa lɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: If your crops grow very slowly, produce pale leaves, or give tiny harvests year after year, your soil is exhausted. Adding compost, animal manure, or rotating crops brings the soil back to life.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onibii lɛ daraa blɛoo waa, eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ, loo ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ afi fɛɛ afi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ efo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ aná wala ekoŋŋ.

english: Can giving my crops too much water destroy them just like a drought does?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ hɔmɔ?

english: Yes, too much water drowns the roots by cutting off their oxygen. Rotten roots cannot drink water or feed the plant, causing the crop to turn yellow, wilt, and die.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu babaoo baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo yɛ oxygen ni afoɔ lɛ hewɔ. Shishifãi ni egboi nyɛŋ anu nu loo amɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Ehaa tsei feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛgbiɔ, ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: How can Plant Protection officers help me when my crops are failing in the field?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ kɛ́ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Plant Protection (PPRS) officers visit your farm to inspect sick crops, identify the exact pests or diseases damaging your yield, and give you proven solutions backed by scientific research.
ga: Tsei Ahe Bulɛ Nitsulɔi (PPRS) baa oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛyakwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ. Kwɛmɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela loo hela pɔtɛɛ ni miifite onibii lɛ. ni ekɛ tsabaai ni ana he odaseyeli ni jeŋ nilee mli niiamlitaomɔ fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa.

english: Why is it so hard for my newly planted crops to survive between November and February?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa waa akɛ mitsei ni midu ehee lɛ baahi shi yɛ November kɛ February teŋ lɛ?

english: November to February is the main dry season in Ghana, when hot weather and low rainfall dry out the soil quickly. Young plants lack deep root systems, so they struggle to absorb enough moisture during these months.
ga: Alemle kɛyashi Oflɔŋ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri yɛ Ghana. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo pɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi oya. Tsei bibii lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nyɔji nɛɛ amli.

english: How does strong sunshine during the dry months affect my young crops?
ga: Te hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ saa mi tsei bibii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Intense sunshine dries out the topsoil and causes young plants to lose water through their leaves faster than they can absorb it. This can scorch the leaves and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ ni ehaa tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ nu lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ ni etsĩ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Should I start planting my new farm at the beginning of the dry season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmɔ hee yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Planting at the start of the dry season is risky because the soil loses moisture rapidly. It is better to plant when there is adequate soil moisture so young roots can establish themselves safely.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii mra yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, eyɛ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Esa akɛ adu be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa bɔni afee ni shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ ama shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my crops growing so slowly during their very first year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dara blɛoo yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the first year, plants focus most of their energy on developing strong underground roots rather than growing tall. You should not rush this process, as strong roots are essential for long-term health.
ga: Yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ, tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni wa ni amɛaana lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ̃. Esaaa akɛ okɛ oyaiyeli tsuɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ he nii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ he miihia kɛha hewalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Is it a problem if I try to force my young plants to produce early in the first year?
ga: Ani ebaafee naagba kɛji mibɔ mɔdɛŋ akɛ manyɛ tso bibioo ko nɔ koni ewo yibii yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Yes, pushing young plants to produce too early weakens them. The plant needs its first year to settle into the soil and build a strong foundation to support future harvests.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ otsi tsei bibii awo yibii amli mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛgbɔjɔ. Eheɔ tsei lɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ dani amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛfeɔ shishitoo ni wa ni baaye abua wɔsɛɛ ŋmaakpamɔi lɛ.

english: Why does my new farm seem to suffer more in hot weather compared to my neighbor's older farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔ hee lɛ naa amanehulu babaoo yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ momo lɛ he lɛ?

english: New farms have young plants with shallow roots that cannot reach deeper water in the soil. Older farms have deep root systems and established shade, making them better equipped to handle dry weather.
ga: Okwaafoi hee lɛ yɛ tsei bibii ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ nu he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Okwaafoi momo lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ yɔɔ mli, ni amɛyɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa osaa ohe jogbaŋŋ koni onyɛ otsu kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi lɛ ahe nii.

english: How does hot weather affect the moisture in my soil?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ saa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Hot air and strong sunlight pull water out of the ground through evaporation. Without rain, the top layer of soil becomes hard and dry, making it difficult for roots to survive.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ lasu ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbiɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaahi shi.

english: What should I do to keep the soil moist around my new plants when there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee koni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle mihe lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ? Tsei heei lɛ mli fũuɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: You can protect soil moisture by adding mulch—like dry leaves or straw—around the base of plants. This blocks direct sunlight from drying out the earth and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ, tamɔ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni okɛbaabɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: What soil conditions should I look for before putting new seedlings in the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛ esa akɛ makwɛ dani madu dumɔwui heei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You should make sure the soil has enough dampness and cool temperature so the young roots do not dry out immediately. Avoid planting in dry, dusty soil during high heat.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ajɔ bɔ ni sa. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi bibii lɛ akagbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi, ni sũ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ dumɔ he yɛ be mli ni dɔɔ waa lɛ.

english: How do weather and atmospheric conditions change how much water my crops need?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsakeɔ nu ni he hiaa mi tsei lɛ?

english: When the atmosphere is hot, dry, and windy, crops lose water much faster through their leaves. During these times, plants need extra soil moisture to prevent wilting and stress.
ga: Kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ, egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya kwraa. Yɛ nɛkɛ bei nɛɛ amli lɛ Tsei he miihia shikpɔŋ nɔ nu babaoo koni amɛkagbo kɛ haomɔ.

english: Maize is ready to harvest around 90 to 120 days after planting, when the leaves turn yellow and brown and the seeds become hard. Harvesting at this stage prevents insects, mold, and birds from destroying the grain in the field.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa aaafee gbii 90 kɛyashi 120 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ, beni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmɔŋ ni ŋmeii lɛ mli wa lɛ. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmeii, ŋmeii, kɛ okpoi akafite ŋmaa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do some crop seeds sprout in just 3 days while crops like maize take up to 120 days to fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbii 3 pɛ mli, yɛ be mli ni tsei tamɔ ŋmãa heɔ gbii 120 dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Different crops have different life cycles. Quick-sprouting seeds like leafy vegetables germinate fast and mature in weeks, whereas grain crops like maize take up to 120 days because they need time to grow strong stalks, flower, and build up heavy, nutrient-rich kernels.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ wala shihilɛi srɔtoi. Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni amɛbaadara yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ heɔ gbii 120, yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ejaakɛ eheɔ be dani ŋmeii ni wa, fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui ni tsii, ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Cassava roots reach full maturity between 10 to 12 months. If left in the ground longer, especially during heavy rains, water builds up around the roots and invites soil fungi that cause decay.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 10 kɛyashi 12 teŋ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Nu buaa ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni efɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ nine.

english: How do I know if the money I spend on fertilizer will actually bring me a higher profit at harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shika ni mifiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baaha maná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo diɛŋtsɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: You can check this by comparing the cost of one bag of fertilizer against the value of the extra crop yield it produces. If the extra harvest sold at the market earns you more money than what you spent on the fertilizer, the practice is profitable.
ga: Obaanyɛ oma enɛ nɔ mi kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ jara ni okɛtoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni anáa lɛ ahe jara lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ nibii ni fa fe nine ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ haa onáa shika babaoo fe bɔ ni ofiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ. Sɛɛnamɔ ba nakai nifeemɔ lɛ he.

english: Do I need a smartphone app to keep track of my crop quantities and farm sales?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni maná smartphone app ko ni mikɛkwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni mihɔ̃ɔ lɛ anɔ?

english: No, you do not need an app. A simple paper notebook where you write down the date, quantity harvested, expense costs, and selling prices works just as well to keep your records clear.
ga: Dabi, app lɛ he ehiaaa bo. Wolo folo ni okɛŋmalaa gbi lɛ nɔ lɛ Nikpamɔ yibɔ Shika ni afiteɔ Kɛ jarayeli jara lɛ hu tsuɔ nii koni eha oniŋmaa lɛ mli aka shi faŋŋ.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are a sign that the pepper plant is under heat stress, lacks enough water, or is being attacked by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ pepper tso lɛ yɛ latsaa he haomɔ shishi. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids lɛ tutuaa lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers fall off the tree before turning into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when there are not enough midges (tiny insects) to pollinate them, or when the tree is stressed by dry weather and lacks nutrients to support pod growth.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kooloi bibii yɛ jɛmɛ. (koolooi bibii) ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee pollination loo be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi kɛ niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa pod lɛ dalɛ ni bɛ lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rains when the fruit bunch grows large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni aduawai akui lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that struggle to support the heavy weight of mature bunches. Supporting the stem with strong wooden poles prevents the wind and fruit weight from uprooting the tree.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi panicles ni eda lɛ amli tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ tso lɛ yibii lɛ amli tsiimɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie tso lɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas alongside my main crops help my farm grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ ni edaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer for neighboring crops while maturing quickly.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yɛ be mli ni edaa oya.

english: Why does my soil turn hard and dry quickly even after I apply water to my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni egbiɔ oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ?

english: Soil gets hard when it lacks organic matter. Adding compost or animal manure improves the soil structure, working like a sponge to hold moisture around crop roots for longer periods.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa kɛ́ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji koni ekɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli. shishifãi ni aduɔ lɛ be kakadaŋŋ

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under harsh, direct sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and have large leaves that provide shade and help keep the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself during its first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ ŋmɛɔ ehe shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines produce bigger tubers when I support them with wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ naa bulbs wuji beni mikɛ tsei ni akɛfee tsei fiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to make food through their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground and spreads them out to catch sunlight, which directs more energy into growing large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛhoo kɛtsɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ baaha hewalɛ babaoo aba koni akɛye ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough room and food to produce a full yield.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK helps restore the green color and boosts healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant cowpea or groundnuts on my field after harvesting a maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the land for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa jɛmɛ kɛha odumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I build my soil ridges across a hillside instead of straight down the hill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matswa ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mafo gɔŋ lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Making ridges across a slope acts like mini-dams that slow down flowing rainwater. This prevents heavy rains from washing away your topsoil and crop nutrients, allowing water to soak into the root zone.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ faa bibioo ko. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya Enɛ baatsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ tsei lɛ amli niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nu baanyɛ abote shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: What is eating holes inside the leaves of my young maize and leaving brown dirt in the middle?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ni eshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which feed inside the central leaves of maize plants. You can manage them by applying recommended biopesticides or neem leaf extracts early in the morning or evening.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tso mli nu ni ajieɔ yi yɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ atsu nii kɛkwɛ amɛnɔ.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and turning yellow even though I water the farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa tsei lɛ daa moŋ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by a viral disease spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Watering alone will not cure it; you need to control whiteflies early and plant disease-resistant seed varieties.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni jɛɔ muawai amli ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ pɛ lɛ tsaŋ lɛ. Esa akɛ okudɔ ŋmeii lɛ mra. kɛ dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ

english: Why do my cassava roots begin to rot if I leave them in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Too much water in waterlogged soil cuts off oxygen to the root zone, causing fungi to grow and rot the mature cassava. It is best to harvest mature tubers before the heavy rainy season fully settles in.
ga: Nu babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii shwereɔ ni ehaa ŋmei ni eda lɛ fiteɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa bulbs ni edara jogbaŋŋ lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my maize so the rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo ŋmãa mli koni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ?

english: Apply your initial fertilizer 10 to 14 days after planting when the soil is moist, and bury it slightly near the root zone rather than scattering it on top so rainwater does not sweep it away.
ga: Okɛ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, yɛ gbii 10 kɛyashi 14 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ni ofu lɛ fioo yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛshwie nɔ koni nugbɔ nu lɛ akaho.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow tall. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer to the soil helps bring back their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my rice leaves look like they have been burnt at the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ashã ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Burnt leaf tips on rice are often caused by a fungal disease called blast, which spreads easily when plants are crowded or get too much nitrogen fertilizer. Giving plants enough space and balancing your fertilizer prevents this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blast ji nɔ ni kɛ baa yitsei ni shwieɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ tsei lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ to he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my cocoa trees without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they do not get enough shade, suffer from dry spells, or are attacked by small insects like mirids. Keeping shade trees on your farm and protecting young trees helps flowers stay on to become pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafite amɛ fɔfɔii kɛji amɛnáaa hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ekɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo kooloi bibii tamɔ atatui ni shwieɔ shi lɛ tutuaa lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ tsei bibii ahebuu Yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are my plantain plants falling over easily before the fruits are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants fall over when tiny pests called stem borers eat into the trunk near the roots, making the base weak. Clearing weed growth and using clean suckers when planting keeps the base strong and upright.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji kooloi bibii ni ale amɛ akɛ stem borers lɛ yeɔ nii kɛboteɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni bɛŋkɛɔ shishifãi lɛ. make the base weak Jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛ sucker ni he tse ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ́ adu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishitoo lɛ mli waa ni ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to turn watery and rot in the soil?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ náa nu ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots rot when rainwater stays around the roots for too long without draining away. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges lets excess water flow off and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni efooo. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli ni eye ebua ni ewaje shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are dark brown spots spreading on my yam leaves and causing them to dry up early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ miigbɛ eshwa mi sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ ni ehaa amɛgbiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Dark spots on yam leaves are usually caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose that thrives in warm, wet weather. Planting disease-free seed yams and clearing away old infected leaves stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose ni yaa hiɛ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ahe tsɔi ni tsuɔ ediŋŋ lɛ baa. Dumɔ sweet potatoes ni hela bɛ mli ni ojie baai momo ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ebaaha helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die even when I water the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting is often caused by bacteria living in the soil that block water from moving up inside the stem. Rotating your tomato field with non-vegetable crops every season stops these bacteria from building up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, muawai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tsiɔ nu naa koni ekaya ŋwɛi yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tso lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni jeee aduawai tsake he ni oduɔ tomato yɛ lɛ daa be lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ akabɔle ohe.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from young leaves. Spraying your pepper crop with organic neem solution or mild pesticides keeps these insects away and leaves flat.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ organic neem solution loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mli ejɔ waa shwie pepper tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ amɛhe ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my groundnut shells empty when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut ŋmɔji lɛ amli efee efolo kɛ́ akpa lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut shells happen when the soil lacks calcium while the pods are forming underground. Spreading agricultural lime or wood ash on your soil before planting gives groundnuts the calcium they need to fill out the nuts.
ga: Peanut ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ calcium yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miifee yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ lime loo tso sũ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani odu lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ aná calcium ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do pests attack my cowpea flowers before any pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ afee lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers attract small pests like flower thrips that eat the flower buds before pods grow. Spraying your farm with recommended insect control right when the first flowers appear protects the blooms so full pods can form.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii tamɔ fɔfɔi thrips, ni yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni akɛbuɔ kooloi ahe lɛ afɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi lɛ je kpo pɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni eha ŋmeii lɛ eyi obɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to check where my farm water comes from before I start planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ he ni miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ jɛɔ dani mibɔi dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Checking your water source ensures it does not contain high salt levels, harmful chemicals, or diseases that can stunt crop growth, ruin your soil, or kill young seedlings before they produce food.
ga: Nu jɛɛhei amli kwɛmɔ haa anaa akɛ nu jɛɛhei lɛ bɛ ŋmei babaoo. tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara loo helai ni baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii agbɔjɔ, efite shikpɔŋ, loo efite tsei bibii dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo niyenii.

english: Why has the water in my farm pond turned green, and is it safe to use on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni yɔɔ nubu ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ eŋɔli lɛ? Ni ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Water turns green when algae grows in it due to sunlight and excess nutrients. While mild green water is usually safe, thick green algae can clog your irrigation pipes, reduce oxygen, and harbour bacteria that weaken delicate crops.
ga: Nu lɛ feɔ eŋɔli kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ dara yɛ hulu la ni fa fe nine kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ hewɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ bei pii lɛ nu ni mli tse lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe moŋ, shi ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ paipii amli, eha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa shi, ni ekɛ helatsɛmɛi ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ agbɔjɔɔ lɛ ahi shi.

english: Bad irrigation water often causes leaf tips to turn brown or yellow, leaves to drop off early, or white salty crusts to form on top of the soil, which prevents plants from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ. baai lɛ shwieɔ shi mra loo ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ko baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni haaa tsei lɛ ana niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: If my irrigation water looks green and dirty, what can I do to clean it before giving it to my plants?
ga: Kɛji mi nu ni mikɛshwieɔ shi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ muji Mɛni mafee koni matsumɔ mli dani mikɛha mi tso lɛ?

english: You can clean green water by filtering it through sand and fine cloth screens to remove algae, or by covering your water tanks with dark shade netting to block sunlight so algae cannot grow.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsumɔ nu ni ji eŋɔli lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋã ni akɛshwieɔ shi kɛ mama kpakpa nɔ ni oootsɔ mli koni ojie ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ ŋshɔŋlooi ni yɔɔ su diŋ ni akɛhaa nu ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ koni ebu he kɛjɛ hulu la he lɛ nɔ. Koni algae akakwɛ̃

english: How do I know if I am watering my crops correctly when starting a new garden?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ nu miiha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mije abɔɔ hee shishi?

english: Proper watering keeps the soil moist around the roots like a wrung-out sponge, without leaving puddles on top. Overwatering rots root systems, while underwatering dries out plants and stops them from growing.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shishifãi lɛ amli efɔ tamɔ sponji ni ajie kɛjɛ mli. ni eshiuuu nu ŋmɔtɔ ko yɛ nɔ Nu ni awoɔ fe nine lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Be mli ni eyɔɔ nu shishi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ agbi ni ekpa dalɛ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to apply water to my crops in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛ nu baatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: Early morning is the best time because the soil is cool, allowing crop roots to drink the water before the hot afternoon sun evaporates it from the ground.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔ. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and stop growing when water sits around their roots for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ beni nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When water covers the roots for too long, it suffocates them, preventing them from feeding the plant and causing leaves to turn yellow and decay.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ha shishifãi lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ebaaha okɛ ohe awo mli Ehaaa anyɛ akɛ niyenii aha tsei lɛ ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: What basic steps should I take to prepare my land's water supply before I invest money in buying seeds?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛi titrii esa akɛ matsɔ nɔ masaa nu jɛɛhe yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mikɛ mishika awo dumɔwui amli?

english: Before buying seeds, locate a reliable water source that does not dry up in the dry season, test that the water is clean, and ensure you have a simple way to channel or pump it to your field.
ga: Dani obaahe tsei dumɔwui Taomɔ nu jɛɛhe ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni gĩii yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kaa nu lɛ okwɛ akɛ ehe tse. Ni kwɛmɔ ni oná gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Koni okɛ nu aya loo okɛpomp kɛya oŋmɔji amli

english: What type of water source is safest for irrigating fresh vegetables?
ga: Mɛɛ nu jɛɛhe ji nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ kɛha aduawai heei ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Clean groundwater from wells or clear, flowing river water is best. Avoid using stagnant gutter water or polluted streams near cities, as they carry germs that make your harvested food unsafe to eat.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli tse ni jɛɔ nu bu mli loo faa mli nu ni mli tse lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ nu ni jɛɔ nu ŋshɔi ni ekã shi loo faai ni mli ewo muji ni bɛŋkɛ maji lɛ amli lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, helai komɛi yɛ ni haa niyenii ni okpa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ.

english: Why does the water inside my plastic storage tank get smelly and slimy after a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni yɔɔ mi plastic ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ ni ehiii yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Sunlight warming standing water creates dark slime and bacteria inside plastic tanks. Keeping your storage tanks fully covered and stored under tree shade stops sunlight from spoiling the water.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi ni hulu lɛ edɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ diŋ kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baa plastic tankii amli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ŋtayaai lɛ ewo tsei ashishi kwraa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la lɛ he, ni ebaatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekafite.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants dry up and drop off during the heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight and hot dry winds. Planting shade crops like plantains nearby creates a cool, humid environment that shields the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ baa. Enɛ buɔ kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ehe wa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ enáa hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do I need to build a palm-frond shade over my fresh vegetable nursery bed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee ŋmei tso ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Newly sprouted vegetable seedlings are fragile. A shade canopy made of palm fronds protects tender sprouts from being dry-scorched by the midday sun or crushed by heavy rainfall.
ga: Aduawai dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ waaa. Shade ni akɛ ŋmei tsei ahe baai fee lɛ buɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe koni hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ akashã amɛ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akakumɔ amɛ.

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the leaves block sunlight from reaching each other and the roots fight for nutrients in the soil. This leads to tall, thin plants with small tubers instead of large, heavy yields.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. ni shishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛyitsei bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa yɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ najiaŋ.

english: When too many suckers grow around a main plantain stem, they steal food and water from the parent plant. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest ones, which helps the main tree produce large, full bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ, amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ niji wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do I need to tie my tomato plants to wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fĩɔ tsei ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Lifting tomato vines off the ground keeps the fruits away from soil pests and excessive moisture that cause rotting. It also improves air circulation, which prevents leaf diseases from spreading.
ga: Tomato wain tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa aduawai lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni haa egboɔ lɛ kpaaa gbee. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ hu yaa hiɛ, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ tsei amli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or that excessive water around the roots is preventing the plant from taking up nutrients. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or improving field drainage helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu babaoo ebɔle he. Shishifãi lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekaná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaafata he loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli su lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do you recommend covering the ground around my pepper plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛɔ akɛ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It traps moisture in the dirt during hot dry spells, keeps root temperatures cool, and stops weeds from taking over your crop.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Ha shishifã lɛ mli latsaa lɛ afee fɛ̃i. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye onibii anɔ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously exhausts specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply. Rotating maize with beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks disease cycles naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo yaa hiɛ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli helai ni baa lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme dry heat, irregular watering, or excessive fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot weather helps flowers stay on the vine and develop into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ na haomɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔlɔ mli baa lɛ. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛfataa he Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why must I clear tall weeds away from my yam mounds as soon as the vines start climbing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni abua naa lɛ mli kɛji wain tsei lɛ je shishi amɛkwɔ pɛ?

english: Yam vines rely on their leaves receiving maximum sunlight to create food that builds big tubers underground. Tall weeds cast shade over the vines and steal fertilizer from the soil, causing smaller yam harvests.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ baai ni hulu la kpɛɔ amɛ waa lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛfee niyenii ni feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Jwɛi kakadaji haa wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ feɔ bibioo.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily damaged by intense direct sunlight and heat. Plantain plants grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture needed for young cocoa trees to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize crop turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or that the roots are waterlogged. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea helps the plants regain their healthy green color and build strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa su ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Pruning opens up the canopy so sunlight and air can pass through the tree. This reduces humidity around the trunk, preventing black pod disease and encouraging the tree to put its energy into growing cocoa pods rather than excess leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo ni yɔɔ tso lɛ he lɛ aba shi, ni ebaatsi black pod hela lɛ naa. ni ewoɔ tsei hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ kookoo ŋmeii moŋ fe ni amɛaaná baai krokomɛi.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots spoil so quickly after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya beni mifo amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots contain high moisture and start a natural deterioration process once cut from the plant. Leaving tubers unharvested in the soil until needed, or rapidly processing them into gari or flour, prevents them from rotting within two to three days.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ni amɛjeɔ adebɔɔ mli fitemɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ shishi kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli pɛ. Ni ashiɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akpaaa kɛyashi ehe baahia. loo afee lɛ oya ni afee lɛ gari loo ashikishaŋ. Enɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ gbii enyɔ komɛi amli.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a brief dry spell before the main rains settle in. Planting too early means the seeds may germinate and then dry up and die from lack of continuous soil moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Dani nugbɔ titri lɛ baa lɛ Dumɔ mra tsɔ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni bɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ.

english: What causes the central leaves of my young maize plants to look chewed up with small holes?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ feɔ bu bibii?

english: This pattern of damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the growing point of the maize plant. Checking crops early and applying safe, approved treatments directly into the plant funnel helps protect the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa tsei lɛ adaa yɛ hei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ awo tso lɛ ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Covering the soil with organic material—known as mulching—keeps the soil cool under hot weather, reduces water evaporation, prevents weeds from growing, and slowly decays into natural fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aba shi Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha onibii.

english: Maize uses up a lot of nitrogen from the soil. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and naturally put it back into the ground through their roots, restoring soil fertility for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves toward the sun for energy. Staking also lifts the leaves off the wet ground, reducing soil-borne fungal diseases and allowing the plant to direct energy into forming large underground tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu lɛ he koni amɛná hewalɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shikpɔŋ kɛbaa lɛ aba shi ni eha tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow poorly even after I have applied fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that quickly steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. Removing weeds early ensures that your crops get the full benefit of nutrients in the soil.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ ana niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he sɛɛ fɛɛ.

english: Leaving proper space allows each plant to get enough sunlight, air, and soil nutrients. When plants are crowded, they fight for water and food, which results in thin stalks and smaller cobs.
ga: He ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛbaatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and provide living shade, protecting the young cocoa plants and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ehaa hulutsoo. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi cacao lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to manufacture food for the underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they capture maximum light and avoid rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛná niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ená la babaoo ni ekwa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up. Alternating with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nitrogen to the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is it bad to throw fertilizer right at the base of my plant's main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer directly touching the stem can burn and damage the plant tissue. Placing it in a small ring a short distance away allows the feeder roots underground to safely absorb the nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli ni baashɛ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ ashã ni efite tso lɛ fãji. Ekɛwoɔ ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo mli Kɛ́ ohi he ko ni kɛ jɛmɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ fioo lɛ, ehaa niyenii halɔ lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii kpakpai lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why is covering the soil with dry grass around my vegetable plants helpful?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ oookɛ muji awo mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil, or mulching, traps moisture so you water less often, keeps the root area cool under hot sunshine, and prevents weeds from sprouting.
ga: Mulching loo mulching baaha ŋmɔtɔ aba mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu awo mli shii abɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot dry spells to save water and protect its underground roots. Once the rainy season returns, the plant will sprout fresh new leaves.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji akɛ ebote nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei.

english: Why does removing weeds early in the season help my crops produce a bigger yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer from your crops. Clearing them early ensures your crops get all the available resources while they are forming flowers and fruits.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ aná be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai.

english: Why should I cut off extra small branches and suckers from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii kɛ tsei ashishifãi lɛ? kɛjɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli

english: Removing unwanted branches, called pruning, redirects the tree's energy into growing big cocoa pods instead of extra leaves. It also improves air flow to prevent black pod disease.
ga: Niji ni ataooo lɛ ni afoɔ Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi. Ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ lɛ yaa kookoo ŋmɔji wuji ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai babaoo baafata he. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ koni ekɛtsi black pod hela lɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and developing sticky spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curling and sticky leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the leaf juices. Controlling these insects early prevents them from spreading plant viruses across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baa nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni ebɔle ehe ni ekpɛtɛɔ he lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbɛ tsei ahe helai amɛshwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow root systems and tender leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight and heat. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa creates a canopy that shelters the young seedlings and preserves soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli tamɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why are some of my cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the tree during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, overly wet, and humid conditions. Pruning extra tree branches to let in sunlight and air circulation helps prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ duŋ mli Fɛ ni edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ lɛ, ŋmei krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmei lɛ akagbɛ eshwa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need for leaf growth. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni baai lɛ adara lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ahe afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha amɛdaramɔ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans in my field help my maize crop grow better later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni mi-ŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, that trapped nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okpa amɛ Nakai nitrogen ni emɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Maize plants curl their leaves to protect themselves from water loss. By rolling the leaf inward, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun and dry wind, saving moisture until the weather cools down.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu akafite. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ awo mli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Tomatoes often drop their flowers when the afternoon temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes rapidly from very dry to very wet. Providing steady water and light shade can help the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the tender central leaves of young maize. Early detection and spraying recommended organic neem extracts or approved insecticides directly into the plant funnel can stop them.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmei bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ anɔ. Akɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ ana mra ni akɛ organic neem mli nu lɛ afɔ nɔ. Aloo, tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛaawo tso lɛ ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ akpa enɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and turning yellowish-green with irregular patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ni yɔɔ srɔto lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies that suck plant sap. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by agricultural officers is the best way to prevent this infection.
ga: Kasava mosaic hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies plant sap sucker lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Ni aduɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi etsɔɔ mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay thin and woody even after a full year in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei yɛ be mli ni mikɛ afi muu fɛɛ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots remain thin if the soil is too hard and compact, or if plants are sown too close together. Loosening the soil into mounds or ridges and giving each plant enough space allows the roots to expand freely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baakã he ahi shi bibioo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni ajieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛfeɔ gɔji loo ŋmeii Ni ahaa tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã amɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy winds even when the trunk looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and tiny worm-like pests called nematodes can weaken them by feeding on the root system. Planting clean suckers and building soil mounds around the base gives the roots stronger support against wind.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. kɛ kooloi bibii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ kɛtsɔ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛyeɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni he tse ni adu sũ ni ebɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Officer, why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the bottom up?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen, which is the main plant nutrient responsible for leaf growth and green color. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or adding compost early in the season fixes this issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Eji tso lɛ mli niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa kɛ eŋɔli su. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea tsu nii, loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Officer, why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and burn when I clear away all the big trees from my plot?
ga: Agent Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa kɛ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa protects the tender leaves from scorching and retains soil moisture during their early growth stage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ shishijee be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Officer, what is eating holes in the funnel leaves of my young maize crop overnight?
ga: Officer Mɛni ye bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ amli nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This damage is typically caused by fall armyworms, which burrow inside the growing core of the maize plant to feed. Checking the field early and applying targeted controls or neem oil solutions protects the leaves before the plant is ruined.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni egbee shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli koni ekɛye niyenii He lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ targeted control loo neem mu ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu baai lɛ ahe dani tso lɛ afite.

english: Officer, why are my cassava roots rotting in the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ?

english: Cassava root rot occurs when water accumulates around the root system in poorly drained soil, encouraging fungal growth. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ ehe. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Officer, why do my crops grow tall and thin with very small yields when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Agent Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper field spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to grow strong stems and produce heavy yields.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tsei ni wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Officer, why are the blossoms on my pepper plants falling off instead of turning into peppers?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when plants face severe heat stress, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Maintaining steady moisture in the soil helps the plant retain its flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Officer, why is my land yielding fewer bags of produce each year even though I plant the same crop?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil over time. Rotating crops with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the land and restores soil health naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be yɛ be ni sa mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ ni ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii fata he. Ekɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Officer, why are my seeds failing to sprout after I plant them into dry soil?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds require a steady supply of soil moisture to break their seed coat and start growing. Planting into dry ground leads to low germination rates or causes sprouted roots to dry up and die.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ daa koni amɛkumɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni amɛbɔi dalɛ. Dumɔ yɛ hei ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ aha ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ loo eha shishifãi lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Officer, which fast-growing crops can I plant alongside my main farm to bring in quick cash and profits?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ wulu lɛ masɛi koni maná shika kɛ sɛɛnamɔ oya?

english: Short-cycle vegetable crops like tomatoes, garden eggs, or leafy greens mature within a few months, providing quick harvests and regular cash flow to help pay for farm inputs while main crops grow.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ tomato, abɔɔ mli ŋmeii, loo aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmaa oya kɛ shika ni yaa nɔ daa ni yeɔ ebuaa kɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ahe nyɔmɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Officer, why do tiny insects destroy my stored maize grains within a few weeks of harvest?
ga: Ofisa, mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yɔɔ? Koni mafite mi-abele dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli kɛjɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Grain weevils attack maize if the harvested grain is stored with too much moisture or kept in unsealed containers. Thoroughly drying the maize before storage and using airtight bags or storage chemicals keeps insects out.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tutuaa ŋmãa kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ to he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli loo akɛto tsɛnsii ni atsĩ naa mli. Abɛi ni agbiɔ dani akɛtoɔ Ni akɛ vacuum bags loo tsofai ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe lɛ atsu nii koni ŋmeii akabote mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn even forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen gives leaves their deep green color and helps plants grow big; without it, the plant steals nitrogen from older leaves to feed the new top growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa. Kɛ́ ebɛ lɛ, tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my land produce smaller maize harvests if I plant maize on the exact same plot every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients. Planting it repeatedly drains specific minerals like nitrogen and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil year after year.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ jieɔ mineral pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen, ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when trees suffer from dry weather, lack essential soil nutrients, or when there are not enough tiny insects in the farm to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na shihilɛi ni mli egbi. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants look bushy and healthy but drop their flowers before growing peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔ mli ni eyɛ hewalɛ lɛ? Shi ha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo dani okɛ ŋmeii lɛ awo mli.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer—which makes the plant grow mostly leaves—or during extreme heat and dry spells when water is scarce.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ baai babaoo. aloo yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa mli kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni nu faaa lɛ.

english: Why do my okra leaves wilt and droop in the afternoon sun even if I watered them earlier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra baai lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu ha amɛ mra moŋ?

english: In hot sun, okra leaves lose moisture through evaporation faster than roots can absorb water. Drooping is the plant's natural defense to protect itself by reducing the leaf surface exposed to direct sunlight.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, Roselle baai lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu. Defoliation ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu ni ekɛbuɔ ehe he kɛtsɔ baa lɛ nɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot inside the soil during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water in wet soil fills air pockets, suffocating cassava roots by cutting off oxygen. This weakens the tubers and allows rot-causing soil organisms to invade them.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui amli obɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa sũ mli nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ baatutua amɛ.

english: Why do I need to make raised earth mounds before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose, and well-drained soil to stretch and swell. Planting in hard, flat ground stops the tubers from growing deep, resulting in small or misshapen yams.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛgbala ni efuu. Dumɔ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni wa Ebaatsi yitso lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa.

english: What causes my tomato leaves to curl up tightly and turn pale?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies feeding on the plant, or by severe heat stress causing the plant to roll its leaves to save water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ tsei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu nu he lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over in strong wind when they start bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ beni ebɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that become top-heavy when carrying bunches. Additionally, tiny soil worms called nematodes can damage the roots, weakening the plant's grip in the ground.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛhe wa waa kɛ́ amɛmiiwo ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛfata he lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ baanyɛ afite shishifãi. Ehaa tsei ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akpɛtɛɔ he lɛ baa shi.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my maize help my maize grow stronger?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ kɛfataa ŋmãa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ewa?

english: Cowpeas and other leguminous plants have roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the neighboring maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Eyɛ shishifãi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ

english: Do crops have male and female parts that need to meet before I get fruit?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nuu kɛ yoo fãi ni esa akɛ amɛfee ekome dani abaanyɛ awo yibii?

english: Yes, many crops like maize, watermelons, and cocoa have male parts that produce pollen and female parts that receive it. Insects, wind, or rain transfer pollen from male to female flowers, which fertilizes the plant so it can produce fruits or seeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei babaoo, tamɔ abele, watermelon, kɛ kookoo yɛ hii ahe nibii ni woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yei ahe nibii ni nine shɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ. Koolooi, kɔɔyɔɔ, loo nugbɔ jieɔ pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi hii amli kɛyaa fɔfɔi yei anɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ yibii loo dumɔwui.

english: Why do some of my tomato flowers fall off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off if they are not properly pollinated, which often happens during extreme heat, dry winds, or heavy rains when bees and insects are not flying around to move pollen between flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ awooo amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nugbɔ nɛɔ waa, be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii krokomɛi efoŋ kɛbɔle amɛhe koni amɛjie pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ lɛ.

english: Is it true that I can manually help my cocoa trees produce more pods using my hands?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ manyɛ maye mabua cacao tso lɛ ni ekɛ miniji afee ŋmɔtɔ babaoo?

english: Yes, hand pollination involves taking pollen from a male flower part and gently placing it onto the female flower part using a small brush or toothpick, which ensures more flowers turn into healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, nɔ ni fata nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ he ji ni ajie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fã ni ji nuu lɛ mli ni akɛ brɔshi loo ŋmɔtɔ bibioo ko awo fɔfɔi lɛ fã ni ji yoo lɛ nɔ blɛoo. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi babaoo afee kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Seeds need the right balance of water, warmth, and air to wake up. If they are buried too deep, flooded with water, or attacked by soil insects and fungi, they will rot before they can push through the dirt.
ga: Nu, dɔlɛ, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia dumɔwui koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, nu shwieɔ nɔ loo kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa lɛ. Amɛbaagboi dani abaanyɛ ashwie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two specific parent plants to produce high yields. The seeds harvested from those crops lose their original vigor, so planting them will give you an uneven crop with much smaller yields.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ fɔ̃ɔ fɔlɔi enyɔ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ nakai tsei lɛ amli lɛ baafite amɛshishijee hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okwɛ lɛ, ebaaha oná ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni wooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why does my maize crop turn yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ?

english: Yellow maize leaves usually show that the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient that acts like food for the plant, or that the soil is waterlogged and choking the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛha tsei. aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and die shortly after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can drown the roots in soggy soil, creating perfect conditions for soil fungi to cause root rot. When the roots rot, the plant can no longer drink water once the sun comes back out, causing it to wilt.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aha shishifãi lɛ afite. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ egbo lɛ, tso lɛ nyɛŋ anu nu dɔŋŋ kɛ́ hulu la lɛ ku esɛɛ eba. ha egbi

english: Yellowing and curling leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Virus, a plant disease spread by tiny whiteflies that suck sap from the leaves and weaken the plant.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ nɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Enɛ ji tso hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. No shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to give small harvests even if pests are not eating the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa yibii babaoo aba miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ yeee baai lɛ po?

english: Weeds act like uninvited guests at a meal; their roots aggressively steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your crops, leaving your plants too weak to produce large fruits or grains.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbɔi ni afɔ̃ko amɛ nine yɛ niyeli lɛ shishi. Amɛshishifãi lɛ juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli waa. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, otsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce small bunches compared to my neighbor's farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ akɛto mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Plantains produce smaller bunches if the parent plant was weak, if the soil lacks potassium, or if too many suckers are growing around the main plant and stealing its nutrients.
ga: Plantains baawo ŋmeii bibii. Kɛji tso nyɛ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium Aloo ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ ehe lɛ. tso titri lɛ ni ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Can I use any water from a nearby river or gutter to water my tomato plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa loo nubu ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli lɛ awo mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli nu?

english: No, dirty or contaminated water carries hidden bacteria and fungi that can rot your crops' roots or spoil the leaves. You should always ensure the water is clean before giving it to your crops so they stay healthy.
ga: Dabi, nu ni mli ewo muji loo nɔ ni mli ewo muji lɛ yɛ helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni baanyɛ afite tsei shishifãi loo amɛha baai lɛ afite. Esa akɛ okwɛ akɛ nu lɛ mli tse dani okɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does dirty water affect the overall growth of my vegetable crops?
ga: Te nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ saa mi-aduawai lɛ fɛɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Dirty water contains bad microbes and pollutants that block plant roots from taking in food, causing your vegetables to stunt, turn yellow, or die from diseases.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli nibii bibii ni ehiii kɛ nibii ni fiteɔ nii ni tsiɔ tso shishifãi anaa koni amɛkabote tso lɛ niyenii mli. Ehaa o-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi. etsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo egbo yɛ helai srɔtoi amli

english: Is it safe to let standing, muddy water sit around the roots of my crops?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oooshi nu lɛ mli atatu kɛ atatu ni ebɔle he? Mi ŋmɔshi nibii shishifãi?

english: No, stagnant muddy water suffocates crop roots and creates a breeding ground for diseases. Water should flow cleanly and drain properly to keep the plant roots healthy.
ga: Dabi, nu ni akɛfee klon lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa helai fɔɔ yɛ. Esa akɛ nu lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni eho jogbaŋŋ koni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if the water I am using for my crops is safe enough for them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu ni mikɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe bɔ ni sa kɛha amɛ?

english: Safe water should be clear, free of bad smells, and clean from dirt or chemical oils. Clean water keeps crop stems firm and leaves green without causing sudden wilting or leaf spots.
ga: Esa akɛ nu ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ mli atse. ŋmɔlɔ gbonyo ko bɛ mli ni ehe tse kɛjɛ muji loo tsofa mli fɔ he Nu ni he tse haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo baai lɛ ahe ŋmɔtɔ baaa trukaa.

english: What does biosecurity mean when I am taking care of my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji biosecurity shishi kɛji mikwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Biosecurity simply means taking strict precautions—like using clean water, washing your farm tools, and keeping dirt out—to prevent diseases and pests from entering your farm and damaging your crops.
ga: Biosafety tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ akwɛ he jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ nu ni mli tse ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Okwaafoi anitsumɔ nibii ahe saamɔ kɛ muji hebuu Enɛ haa helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ boteɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni amɛfiteɔ oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I clean my cutlass and hoe before moving to a different crop field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsumɔ mi-dagger kɛ mi-hoe lɛ he dani mikɛ amɛ aya ŋmɔ kroko mli?

english: Farm tools can easily carry unseen plant diseases and soil pests from an infected crop field to a healthy one. Cleaning your tools stops you from spreading crop sickness across your farm.
ga: Okwaayeli he nibii baanyɛ ajie tsei ahe helai ni anaaa kɛ sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛ okwaayeli shikpɔji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ oya. Kɛ́ otsumɔ odɛŋdadei lɛ, ebaatsi bo gbɛ koni okagbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why should I be careful about letting visitors walk freely through my vegetable garden?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ mihe jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɔi ni baa jɛmɛ lɛ ni maha amɛnyiɛ mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ he?
