english: Visitors can unknowingly carry soil-borne fungal spores or tiny insect eggs on their boots and clothes from other farms, bringing crop diseases straight into your clean field.
ga: Saralɔi baanyɛ amɛkɛ fungal spores ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi bibii akui aba. ni oleee yɛ bɔɔtu kɛ ŋmɔ mli atadei krokomɛi anɔ koni okɛ ŋmɔ mli helai aya oŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to inspect my crops early every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli daa leebi lɛ?

english: Checking your farm every morning helps you spot early signs of pest attacks, wilting, or leaf disease so you can treat the plants quickly before the problem spreads and ruins your harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ebatutua bo mra. wilting loo foliar disease koni onyɛ otsa tsei oya dani naagba lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni efite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crop leaves look weak or droopy when I check them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ loo egbɔjɔ kɛ́ mikwɛ mli leebi lɛ?

english: Weak or droopy leaves in the morning often signal root damage caused by dirty water, underground pests, or disease, which you can catch and treat early through daily checks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni egbee shi leebi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ efite shishifãi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ shishi tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni obaanyɛ omɔ ni otsa mra kɛtsɔ daa gbi kwɛmɔ nɔ

english: What specific signs should I look for when checking my crop leaves during my daily farm walk?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii pɔtɛɛ esa akɛ matao beni mikwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe baai amli yɛ be mli ni minyiɛɔ ŋmɔ mli daa gbi lɛ?

english: You should look for tiny holes eaten by pests, strange spots, yellowing edges, or powdery white dust on the leaves, as these are early signs that your crop is becoming sick.
ga: Esa akɛ otao bu bibioo ko. He ni ŋmeii lɛ ŋmɔɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo sũ yɛŋ ni tamɔ powda yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, enɛɛmɛi ji klɛŋklɛŋ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ onibii lɛ miibɔi hela.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient needed for green leaves. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen out of the topsoil, or the soil may simply need manure or nitrogen fertilizer to feed the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he baahia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen awo mli koni akɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my plot make the next season's maize crop grow much better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which works with beneficial soil bacteria to capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. When the cowpea plant decays, it leaves behind natural fertilizer that nourishes your next maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛkɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji cowpea tso lɛ fite Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaha o-corn ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees get burned easily under full, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, shielding the tender cocoa plants from heat and conserving soil moisture.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Buu kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i nɔ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, humid conditions. When there is too much shade or poor airflow around the trees, moisture lingers on pods, allowing the fungus to attack them.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be fa tsɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ ehiii lɛ, Fɛ̃i baakã ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Ha ŋmeii lɛ atutua amɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat, dry winds, or irregular watering. The plant drops its blossoms as a survival response to conserve moisture and energy during stressful weather.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi akɛ wala hetoo koni amɛbu fɛ̃i kɛ hewalɛ he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and twisting together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies sucking the plant's juices, or by severe hot and dry weather. The plant curls its leaves to reduce water loss and protect itself.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ waa ni egbiɔ waa mli Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why do my yam vines need long wooden poles to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ koni ekɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural vines that need to lift their leaves up toward sunlight to make energy. Staking keeps the foliage off the damp soil, preventing fungal leaf diseases while maximizing sunlight to build bigger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wain tso ni esa akɛ ewo ebaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la mli koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi fungal leaf helai anaa yɛ be mli ni ohaa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ babaoo koni efee bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot inside the ground when heavy rain falls for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater stays trapped in wet soil without proper drainage, the roots drown from lack of oxygen and quickly rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ bɛ mli lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ, ni amɛbaafite oya.

english: Why do my harvested groundnuts develop harmful mold when stored in sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts ni mikpa lɛ lɛ feɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara kɛji akɛ akɛto kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts mold when they are bagged before being completely dried. Any moisture left inside the shells creates a warm, damp environment in the sack where toxic fungi like aflatoxin-producing mold can easily grow.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛwo kotoku mli lɛ, ŋmeii baatsɔ ŋmeii dani amɛgbi kwraa. Fɛ̃i ni eshwɛ yɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa kotoku lɛ mli. Fungi ni yɔɔ gbeyei, tamɔ nɔ ni feɔ aflatoxin lɛ baanyɛ adara oya.

english: Why would buyers abroad reject my harvested crop even if it looks good to me when I pick it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ maŋsɛɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ mikpamɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ ehi jogbaŋŋ beni mikpa lɛ lɛ?

english: International buyers check for hidden issues like chemical pesticide residues, tiny insect eggs inside fruits, or hidden infections. Even if produce looks clean on the surface, failing safety or quality tests at the border leads to rejection.
ga: Majimaji ateŋ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kwɛɔ naagbai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ tsofai ni eshwɛ, kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ amli, loo helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni he tse yɛ hiɛ moŋ, Shi shweshweeshwefeemɔ loo nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ he kaai ni afeɔ yɛ husu lɛ naa lɛ ni anyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli lɛ hu kɛ kpoomɔ baa.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in a wide open field with no shade trees or plantains around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo dumɔwui lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni tsei loo dumɔwui ni haa hulutsoo bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and sensitive to harsh sunlight and hot winds. Planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides living shade that keeps the soil cool and moist, protecting tender cocoa leaves until the trees are strong enough to handle direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛnuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he waa. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ. Ebuɔ kookoo baai ni mli tse lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ he waa bɔ ni sa ni hulu la lɛ baashɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do I get a smaller harvest when I plant many corn seeds close together in one spot to save space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mináa yibiiwoo ni baa shi kɛ́ midu ŋmãa ŋmeii babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome koni mikɛha he ko akafite lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Because no single plant gets enough nutrients, all of them stay small and produce tiny ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ tsei fɛɛ ji bibii ni amɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi bibii.

english: Why do I need to spend time putting tall wooden stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ be ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves up high to catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to grow large tubers underground. Staking also lifts leaves off the damp soil, protecting the plant from fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ tsei ahe tsei kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in the shape of a V while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, a main food crops need to grow strong. The maize plant naturally pulls nitrogen out of its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titri ni esa akɛ ekwɛ̃ ni wa Abele tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and look dead during hot afternoons even when the soil was watered in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi moŋ?

english: On hot days, pepper leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can drink it up. The plant temporarily wilts to close its pores and save water, then bounces back in the evening when the weather cools down.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Tso lɛ baaŋmɛ eshishifãi lɛ be kukuoo ko ni ekɛ nu lɛ baato he. Kɛkɛ lɛ, ekuɔ esɛɛ ebaa ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off the plant before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant experiences water stress. If conditions are harsh, the plant drops flowers to save energy and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Kɛji shihilɛi lɛ ehiii Tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ he.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with big bushy green leaves, but giving me small, thin tubers when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ jwɛi wuji ni baai eŋɔli yɔɔ mli lɛ? Shi kɛ́ akpa lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to spend all its energy making tall stems and big leaves instead of storing food in the underground roots. Cassava needs balanced soil nutrients like potassium to form thick tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kakadaji kɛ baai wuji, moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Niyenii nibii ni sa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium, he miihia cassava koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni mli tse.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in my farm before planting corn the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani wɔdu ŋmãa yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the earth and acts as natural fertilizer for your next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my plantain tree die after producing just one bunch of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gboɔ beni ewo aduawai akuu kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain stem is designed to produce fruit only once in its life. After the bunch matures, the main stem naturally dies back so its underground root system can feed the younger sucker shoots growing around its base.
ga: Afee plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli. Beni kuu lɛ eda kwraa sɛɛ lɛ, tso titri lɛ baagbo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young corn leaves with powdery green dirt inside the center whorl?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ muji ni tamɔ powder yɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaa lɛ mli lɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which crawls into the hidden center fold of young maize plants to eat the tender inner leaves, leaving behind droppings that look like wet sawdust.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Amɛshiɔ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni efɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and provide temporary shade and moisture, acting as natural umbrellas to protect the young cocoa during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛhaa be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: How long will it take for my new cocoa seedlings to start bearing pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi-cocoa dumɔwui heei lɛ aje shishi amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start flowering and producing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas traditional cocoa varieties may take 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5.

english: Why do flowers grow directly on the main trunk and thick branches of my cocoa tree instead of the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ tso titri lɛ kɛ niji ni mli tse lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ baai lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: This is a natural growth pattern called cauliflory. The tree produces flowers on its thick trunk and main limbs so it can support the heavy weight of ripe cocoa pods without breaking weak outer twigs.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli dalɛ gbɛ ni ale lɛ akɛ kɔliflower. Tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei akutsei ni mli tse kɛ amɛniji titrii anɔ. Enyɛɔ ekwɛɔ kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ amli tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ nɔ ni ekuuu kponɔgbɛ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Why are many of the small flowers on my cocoa tree dropping off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ji No hewɔ lɛ, mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ fã ni fa lɛ gbeeɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands more flowers than they can support as full pods. Only flowers pollinated by tiny insects (midges) become pods; the tree sheds the rest to save energy for the growing pods.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ fɔfɔi ni eyi obɔ mli. Fɔfɔi ni kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ pɛ bafeɔ ŋmeii. Tso lɛ shwieɔ nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa tree turning completely black and rotting while hanging on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛmiifite yɛ be mli ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and dark conditions. Removing infected pods promptly and trimming overgrown shade trees helps stop the spread.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ duŋ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya, ni afo tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why are the tips of my young cocoa branches drying up and turning brown like they were burned?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo niji bibii lɛ ayiteŋ egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ashã amɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by tiny insects called mirids (or capsids) that suck sap from fresh shoots and inject toxins. Spraying approved control treatments at the right time protects the new shoots.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mirids (loo capsids), ni amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei heei amli lɛ ni amɛkɛ tsofai fɔji woɔ mli. Nɔ ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei heei ahe.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off the extra side branches and sap-sucking shoots from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji ni eshwɛ kɛ tsei ni miinu nu lɛ kɛjɛ mikoo tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes useless shoots that steal nutrients away from pod production. It also allows sunlight and air to move freely through the tree canopy, reducing fungal dampness and boosting yield.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei ni he ehiaaa ni juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ pod feemɔ mli lɛ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hu tsɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ. Ha fungal ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aba shi ni oha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my mature cocoa trees produce fewer pods when the tall forest trees around them grow too thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso ni eda lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɛ be mli ni koo mli tsei kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ miida lɛ? edaa tsɔ

english: While young cocoa needs shade, mature cocoa needs adequate sunlight to make food and form pods. Overly dense forest trees block light and create damp conditions that reduce yield and cause diseases.
ga: Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo bibioo he miihia hulutsoo. Kookoo ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛfee niyenii ni efee ŋmeii. Tsei babaoo ni yɔɔ kooi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli lɛ tsiɔ la naa ni ehaa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni ekɛ helai baa lɛ baa.

english: How can I tell if a cocoa pod on my tree is fully ripe and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color: green pods turn bright yellow, while red or purple pods turn orange-yellow. Additionally, a ripe pod makes a hollow sound when tapped because the seeds inside loosen from the shell wall.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su: Eŋɔli tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ tsuru loo ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ-ŋmɔŋ. Pods ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ hu feɔ gbee ni mli ewo muji kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ gbogboi lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Why must I heap my freshly extracted cocoa beans under banana leaves for several days before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafee kookoo ŋmeii ni ajie ehee lɛ? yɛ banana baai ashishi gbii babaoo dani egbi dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Heaping and covering fresh beans causes fermentation. This essential process kills the seed germ, removes bitter juices, and creates the rich chocolate flavor and dark brown color buyers look for.
ga: Beans heei ni akɛtoɔ he ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɛkɛ gbɛ ni he hiaa nɛɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai. Jiemɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛjɛ mli ni efee tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ kɛ su ni mli kwɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ.

english: How do I care for my young cocoa seedlings right after getting them so they do not die before planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ mi-kookoo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu lɛ? Enɛ ji koni kookoo tsei lɛ akagboi dani adu.

english: Young seedlings need to stay in a shaded area and receive water daily to keep their roots moist. Keeping them out of harsh direct sunlight before transplanting prevents them from wilting or dying from shock.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akɛ tsei bibii awo hulutsoo be mli ni aha amɛ nu daa gbi koni amɛshishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ hulu lɛ shɛɛɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ dani okɛ amɛ wo he kroko lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagboi loo amɛkagboi yɛ shoofeemɔ hewɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize turn yellow and look weak instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant is starving for nutrients like nitrogen or is not getting enough water. Healthy maize leaves stay dark green when the soil has rich food for the plant to grow to full size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye ŋmãa tso lɛ nibii tamɔ nitrogen loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa enáaa. Abɛi baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ adara kɛyashɛ egbɔmɔtso lɛ he.

english: What causes my tomatoes to get dark rot spots at the bottom before they fully grow?
ga: Mɛni haa tomatoi lɛ shishi feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ diŋ dani amɛdaraa?

english: This rot happens when the plant lacks calcium or receives uneven watering while forming fruit. Ensuring consistent water supply helps the tomato plant grow healthy fruit without rotting.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa kɛji akɛ calcium bɛ tso lɛ mli loo akɛ nu haa lɛ be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai miifee lɛ. Nu ni anáa daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfiteee.

english: Can I save seeds from my harvested maize to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahere dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli ni madu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: You can save seeds from traditional or open-pollinated varieties, but if you planted hybrid seeds, saved seeds will produce weak plants with small harvests. It is best to buy fresh hybrid seeds each cycle for strong growth.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ blema loo dumɔwui ni agbele naa lɛ amli lɛ ato. Shi kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ji hybrid Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ŋmaa kpakpa aba. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛfee hybrid be fɛɛ be koni amɛdara waa.

english: Select thick, healthy stems from plants that are 8 to 12 months old. Take cuttings from the hard middle section of the stem, as young or soft wood will not sprout strong roots.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ amli tsei ni mli tse ni mli wa. Kpɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ fã ni wa, ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei bibii loo tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ shishifãi ni wa baakwɛɛɛ.

english: When is the right time to put fertilizer on my crops so it works best?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ aba?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist and the crop is actively growing, usually a few weeks after sprouting and right before flowering. Applying it during dry soil conditions can burn the roots.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii 2-3 yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ kɛ dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi. Kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ ashã.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer or water to my plants during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu woɔ mitsei lɛ amli yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High heat makes water evaporate before roots can take it in, and strong afternoon heat combined with fertilizer can burn and damage tender plant leaves.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ nu lɛ. Ni shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataa he lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ahe baai lɛ ashã ni efite.

english: Why do extension officers take small soil samples from different parts of my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ buaa shikpɔŋ bibii ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ anaa lɛ? In my branch?

english: Taking small soil samples from multiple spots shows what nutrients your land is missing. This test helps you know the exact type and amount of fertilizer your crop needs to thrive.
ga: Shikpɔŋ bibii ni oooŋɔ kɛjɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ tsɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ka nɛɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni oleɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa otso lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha.

english: How can I check a few plants to see if pests are in my farm before my whole crop is destroyed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ tsei fioo komɛi koni mana kɛji ŋmeii komɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani akpata ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ?

english: Walk through your field weekly and inspect the leaf undersides and stems of a few random plants. Spotting insects or eggs on a small sample of plants allows you to treat the problem early.
ga: Nyiɛmɔ kɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa otsi ni okwɛ tsei fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ. Nibii bibii loo ŋmeii ni ataoɔ yɛ tsei bibii ahe nɔkwɛmɔnii anɔ. Ehaa onyɛɔ otsuɔ naagbai ahe nii mra.

english: How do I know my yam tubers are fully mature underground without digging them all up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mikɛ amɛ fɛɛ efoŋ?

english: Observe the vines above ground. When the leaves naturally turn yellow and begin to dry up, it means the vine has finished feeding the yam, and the tuber underground is mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Kadimɔ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛbɔi ŋmɔlɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ wain tso lɛ egbe sweet potato lɛ niyenii naa. Ni ŋmeii lɛ edara kwraa ni amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do the young cocoa pods on my trees shrivel up and turn black before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbo ni amɛmiifee ediŋŋ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Young cocoa pods often shrivel—a condition called cherelle wilt—when the tree lacks enough water or nutrients to feed all its pods, or when fungal diseases like black pod attack them during wet weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ale lɛ akɛ Cao Cao Cherel hela. Beni tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha etsitsii lɛ fɛɛ aye abua loo be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ lɛ tutuaa amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods now that they are older, even though the trees are very large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni edara lɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ da waa moŋ?

english: As cocoa trees grow very old, their stems and large branches require more energy just to stay alive, leaving less energy for pods. Pruning heavy branches and feeding the soil helps older trees focus energy back into pod growth.
ga: Ejaakɛ kookoo tso lɛ etsɛ waa. No hewɔ lɛ tsei akutsei wuji kɛ tsei niji biɔ hewalɛ babaoo koni amɛhi shi. Kɛtsɔ pod lɛ ni oooshi kɛ hewalɛ fioo lɛ nɔ. Niji ni tsii ni afoɔ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni edara lɛ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why do cocoa flowers keep falling off my tree without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers must be pollinated by tiny insects called midges to turn into pods. If the weather is too dry or if sprays kill these beneficial insects, the flowers cannot form pods and will simply drop off.
ga: Esa akɛ kooloi bibii awo kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ bafeɔ pod. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo kɛji nɛkɛ tsofai ni yeɔ ebuaa ni gbeɔ kooloi nɛɛ fɔfɔi lɛ efeŋ ŋmeii ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: Why do agricultural extension officers tell me to cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees when my parents never did that?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mifo kookoo niji babaoo kɛji mifɔlɔi efeee nakai kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning extra branches lets sunlight and fresh air reach all parts of the tree. This dries out humidity that causes fungal diseases and directs the tree's energy into growing flowers and pods instead of excess leaves.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa lɛ mli egbiɔ, ni etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛyaa fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmɔtɔi ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai ni fa fe nine baatsu nii.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant leguminous crops like beans alongside my main farm crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans have special roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer in the soil, which feeds and strengthens neighboring crops without expensive chemicals.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa tsei ni yeɔ naagbai lɛ niyenii ni ewoɔ amɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ tsofai ni jara wa tsuuu nii.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out and crack so fast after the rain stops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɛɔ oya beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ?

english: Soil dries quickly when it lacks organic material like decayed leaves or manure, which act like a sponge to hold water. Keeping crop residue on top of the ground shields the soil from the hot sun.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ bɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni haa nu hiɔ Tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is starving for soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that water is standing around the roots for too long, preventing the plant from breathing and absorbing food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛmu niyenii.

english: Why is it better to harvest beans and vegetables early in the morning rather than in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ abaakpa ŋmei kɛ aduawai leebi fe shwane lɛ?

english: Harvesting early in the morning keeps the produce cool and filled with moisture absorbed overnight. Crops harvested in the hot afternoon heat wilt quickly and spoil faster before reaching the market.
ga: Nikpamɔ leebi lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ mli nyɔɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ. Tsei ni akpaa yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ oya dani amɛshɛɔ jara nɔ.

english: How do I know if a sickness on my farm crops is caused by insects or by bad weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ helai ni baa miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ jɛ kooloi loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii lɛ amli?

english: Insect damage usually leaves visible bite holes, sticky spots, or curled leaves where pests feed. Weather-related sickness, like fungal diseases from heavy rains, usually appears as brown or black water-soaked spots across whole leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ŋmɔɔ bu, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ amɛhe, loo baai ni ebɔle amɛhe yɛ hei ni ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ nii yɛ lɛ. Helai ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛbaa, tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli baa Bei pii lɛ amɛjeɔ kpo akɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni nu ewo mli yɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why do new crop varieties recommended by government officers mature faster than our traditional seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni nɔyeli mli onukpai lɛ jieɔ he ŋaa lɛ shwereɔ oya fe wɔ dumɔwui ni wɔfɔɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties are specifically bred to focus their growth rapidly and resist local dry spells or pests, allowing them to flower and yield fruit in a shorter season than older wild varieties.
ga: Atsɔ tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama amɛdalɛ oya kɛ amɛhe ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ hulutsoo be loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be kukuoo mli fe koo mli tsei ni egbɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know when my prekese pods are ready to be harvested from the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi prekase pods lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: Prekese pods are ready to harvest when they turn from green to a deep chocolate-brown color and naturally drop to the ground or snap off easily, giving off a strong, sweet aroma.
ga: Prekese pods lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛtsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli mli kɛtee tsokolate ni mli edɔ mli. ni egbee shikpɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa loo egbee shi mlɛo Ehaa ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ waa

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually show that your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer early in the growing period fixes this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ baai lɛ ashishi fee ŋmɔŋ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-abele lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he mra yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the exact same spot on my farm every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize in the same spot repeatedly drains the soil of the specific nutrients maize needs and lets maize pests build up in the dirt. Switching to beans or groundnuts for a season restores the soil strength.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni ŋmãa he hiaa lɛ. ni aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmãa loo ŋmãa nɔ be kome lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in flat, heavy soil. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsii lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food and grow large tubers underground. Staking gets the vines off the damp ground, improving sunlight exposure and preventing leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baajie wain tso lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ekɛtsiɔ baa helai anaa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the roots helps the plant hold onto flowers until fruit forms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni amɛhaaa amɛ daa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ebɔle he lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects hiding under the leaves or by a virus spread by pests. Spraying the leaves with a mild neem oil mixture helps protect the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Ni akɛteeɔ baai ashishi loo kɛjɛɔ helai ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Akɛ neem fɔ ni mli ejɔ ni akɛfutuɔ baai lɛ baashwie nɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni abu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I cut off extra small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Jiemɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: Too many shoots around one plantain stalk fight over the same food and water in the soil, leading to tiny fruit bunches. Removing extra shoots so only one or two remain ensures big, heavy plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo ni ebɔle plantain tso kome he lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Ehaa aduawai lɛ feɔ tso bibioo ko. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi lɛ, ehaa plantain lɛ feɔ agbo ni etsiiɔ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my vegetables so the water does not waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ aduawai anɔ nu koni akafite nu?

english: The best time to water crops is early in the morning before the sun gets strong. Watering in the heat of midday causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the plant roots can drink it.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ tsei anɔ nu ji leebi dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. They need shade trees or companion crops like plantains to act as living umbrellas, protecting them from intense heat and keeping the soil moist during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo tsei ni fata amɛhe, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: What happens to my maize crop if rain does not fall for a month or two while it is growing?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ nyɔŋ kome loo enyɔ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: When water is scarce, maize leaves roll up to save moisture, growth slows down, and if drought happens during the flowering stage, the cobs will fail to fill with corn grains.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. slow growth Ni kɛji hɔmɔ ba yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ nyɛŋ awo ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves dry up and drop off when I am away from the farm during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ mibɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Vegetable plants rely on steady soil moisture to carry nutrients upward and keep cool; without water, the leaves cannot produce food for the plant, leading to tissue death.
ga: Aduawai tsei damɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ nɔ koni amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i. Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, baai nyɛŋ afee niyenii aha tso lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fãji gbele.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize stalks turning yellow while the upper leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to maintain healthy green leaves and strong stems.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi ni wa.

english: Yam tubers need soft, deep, and loose soil mounds to grow well. Hard or stony soil blocks the growing root, forcing the tuber to bend and stay small.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni mli edɔ he miihia sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi tsiɔ shishifãi ni miida lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ bibioo.

english: Why do my tomato fruits rot on the vine when I let the branches rest directly on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato yibii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛ́ mishi niji lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Allowing tomato plants to lie on wet ground exposes the leaves and fruits to fungal diseases and crawling pests. Staking the plants keeps the fruit elevated, dry, and healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tomato tsei ni amɛkã shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ amɛ baai kɛ amɛyibii lɛ anɔ oya. Tso lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa aduawai lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ, amɛgbiɔ, ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: If I leave weeds to grow freely on my farm for several weeks, how does it affect my crop?
ga: Kɛ miha jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli otsii babaoo Te ebaaná miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds compete heavily with your crops for soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunshine, which starves your crops and results in weak plants with low harvest yields.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la, ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni no haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ baa.

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when stressed by severe heat, irregular watering, or pest damage, preventing the flowers from developing into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why are the leaves of my cowpea plants curling up and covered with tiny sticky bugs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ ehà amɛhe lɛ?

english: Those sticky insects are aphids sucking vital sap out of the leaves, which causes the foliage to curl and weakens the plant's overall growth.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi ni shwieɔ shi nɛɛ ji aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tso lɛ dalɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and watery if I leave them in the ground too long after they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛdara sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once cassava reaches full maturity, keeping tubers underground in wet soil causes the stored starch to break down, resulting in rotting and loss of root quality.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei lɛ to shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei ni ato lɛ akumɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni shishifãi lɛ ahe ehiii kwraa.

english: Why do weeds make my cocoa trees produce fewer pods if I do not clear them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi-cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo kɛji mikɛ jwɛi tsuuu nii daa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your cocoa trees' root system. When weeds take over, your crop gets starved of food, resulting in smaller tree growth and fewer pods.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ jwɛi lɛ ye Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye amɛ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ baa.

english: Will cutting off extra branches from my cocoa tree hurt the crop or help it grow better?
ga: Ani niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ baaye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui loo ebaaye ebua ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Pruning extra or weak branches actually helps your crop. It directs the tree's energy into producing pods rather than maintaining useless leaves, and it allows sunlight and air to reach the lower trunk, preventing diseases.
ga: Niji krokomɛi loo niji bibii ni oookpa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua onibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. ni ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ koni helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and drying up in full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. They need temporary shade plants like plantains or shade trees above them until they mature and grow a stronger canopy.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo yɛ tsei anɔ. Kɛyashi amɛbaadara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Can I plant plantains next to my cocoa seedlings on the same land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting plantains alongside young cocoa is very beneficial. Plantains grow quickly to provide necessary shade for the young cocoa while also giving you food and income before the cocoa trees start producing.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Plantains lɛ daa oya koni ekɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa aha kookoo bibii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika dani cacao tsei lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed their flowers before the small pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii bibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they are under stress from prolonged dry spells, low soil nutrients, or extreme heat. Keeping the soil covered with mulch and ensuring proper shade helps the tree retain its flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛyɔɔ hɔmɔ he haomɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Niyenii ni faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa Muji kɛ hulutsoo ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast during the rainy season when farms are too damp and dark. Clearing weeds and trimming overcrowded branches lets air flow in to dry the pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. ni ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli Enɛ ji be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ waa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei niji ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛboteɔ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is losing its richness and needs extra plant food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ehiɛ edɔ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ tsei niyenii krokomɛi afata he?

english: When soil loses its strength, crop leaves turn pale green or yellow instead of deep green, and trees grow slowly or produce small pods. Adding fertilizer or organic compost restores vital nutrients to the soil.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ fite Tso lɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. ni tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio loo ebaafee ŋmeii bibii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli.

english: Is it safe to plant cassava right next to my young cocoa stems?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ mi kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe?

english: It is best to leave space between cassava and young cocoa. Cassava is a heavy feeder with spreading roots that steal water and nutrients from young cocoa roots, which can stunt your cocoa's growth.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi gbɛ ko yɛ tapioka lɛ kɛ kookoo ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ teŋ. Cassava ji niyenii ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli ni eyɛ shishifãi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. Enɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kookoo shishifãi bibii amli. ni baanyɛ atsĩ kookoo lɛ dalɛ naa

english: How do I protect my farm crops from dying during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkagboi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: You can protect your crops by leaving dead leaves on the soil around the base of your plants (mulching). This blanket keeps the soil cool and locks in moisture like a sponge during dry weather.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ baai gbohii ni oooshi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle otsei lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ (mulching). Blanket yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli tamɔ sponji yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ.

english: Cocoa pods are ready for harvest when their color changes completely—usually from green to bright yellow, or from red to orange. Harvesting only fully ripe pods ensures the beans inside are fully developed.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni amɛhe su tsake kwraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse mli. aloo kɛjɛ tsuru mli kɛyashi akutu mli Nibii ni akpaa ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ pɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if the seeds I buy at the market meet the required quality standards?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ yeɔ shishitoo mlai ni ataoɔ lɛ anɔ?

english: Certified quality seeds come in sealed packages labeled with official government inspection tags, ensuring high germination rates and freedom from seed-borne diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ana he odaseyeli baa yɛ kotokui ni atsĩ naa ni nɔyeli lɛ kwɛmɔ kadimɔ yɔɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ babaoo, ni helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli baa lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is an essential nutrient maize plants need to build strong leaves and grow healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa ŋmãa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni amɛdara waa.

english: Tomatoes shed flowers when they suffer from high heat or dry soil stress, which prevents proper pollination and causes the plant to drop blossoms to save energy.
ga: Tomato baafɔ̃ kɛ́ edɔ waa loo haomɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli baa lɛ miipiŋ. ni tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa lɛ. ni eha tsei afɔlɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged or poorly drained soils where heavy rains trap excess water, allowing rot-causing fungi to attack the tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ loo nu shwieee nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ni ekɛ nu ni fa fe nine toɔ Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and tender leaves that burn easily under harsh sun, which is why they require shade crops like plantains for shelter during their first years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Enɛ hewɔ ni kookoo tsei he hiaa tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui, koni amɛha amɛhi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking leaf sap, or by viruses spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛjɛ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why do my cowpea crops grow plenty of green leaves but very few pod beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi pea pods lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas produce excessive leaves instead of beans when the soil has too much nitrogen or when plants receive excess nitrogen fertilizer, encouraging vegetative growth over fruiting.
ga: Cowpea woɔ baai babaoo tsɔ yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ Ehaa tsei lɛ daraa moŋ fe aduawai ni baa shi.

english: Missing grains happen when dry weather or poor soil moisture occurs during the flowering stage, preventing full pollination of the cob silks.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii ba yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli. Etsiɔ cob fibers lɛ anaa koni ekafee pollination kwraa.

english: Plantain plants have shallow, fibrous roots that struggle to anchor heavy bunches of fruit when strong winds hit soft, wet soil.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛmɔ aduawai ni tsii amli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow into strange crooked shapes instead of straight smooth tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ yitso ni ja ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ?

english: Yams grow deformed or crooked when the soil is hard, stony, or compacted, which physically blocks the growing tuber from pushing smoothly downward.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ehiii loo ebɔleɔ ehe kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, tɛi yɔɔ mli, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni no haaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anyɛ ashɛ shishi blɛoo.

english: Why do crops struggle to grow well on rocky farmland compared to soft black soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ okwaayeli shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ he lɛ?

english: Rocks prevent plant roots from spreading deep into the earth to find water and nutrients. Stony ground also dries out much faster during hot weather because it cannot hold onto water like soft topsoil does.
ga: Tɛi tsiɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatao nu kɛ niyenii. Tɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hu gbɛ́ɔ oya kwraa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, enyɛɛɛ ehiɛ nu mli tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm turn hard like stone when the hot sun comes after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tamɔ tɛ beni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When rain washes away organic topsoil, bare clay is left exposed. The strong heat bakes this wet clay into a hard crust, making it tough for seeds to sprout or water to soak down into the roots.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ho nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko baashwɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ shãa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɛɛ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, ewa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ loo nu baabote shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Do the rocks on my farm give any food to my crops, or do they only cause problems for the roots?
ga: Ani tɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii? Aloo ekɛ naagbai baa shishifãi lɛ pɛ anɔ?

english: As rocks slowly break down over many years through weather and water, they release natural minerals like potassium, calcium, and iron into the ground, which crops draw up to stay healthy.
ga: Beni tɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi fiofio fiofio afii babaoo kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ nu nɔ lɛ Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ potassium, calcium kɛ dade kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why can cassava grow on dry, stony ground while my cocoa seedlings die on that same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi-kookoo tsei lɛ gboi yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ.

english: Cassava has strong, thick tuber roots that store extra water and food for dry times. Cocoa has delicate roots that require deep, moist soil and plenty of shade to survive.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa, ni mli tse ni haa nu kɛ niyenii babaoo hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Cocoa yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli efɔ kɛ hulutsoo bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ ehi shi.

english: If I pour chemical fertilizer directly around the stem of my crop, will it grow faster?
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ Ani ebaada oya?

english: No, concentrated fertilizer is strong like salt and will burn the stem and young roots. You should place fertilizer in a small circle a short distance away from the stem so the roots can take it in safely.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli wa tamɔ ŋmei. Ebaaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ ashã. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo mli yɛ kooyigbɛ bibii amli. kɛjɛ tso lɛ he fioo bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ abote mli shweshweeshwe

english: If I use a knapsack sprayer for weed chemicals, can I use that same sprayer to water my vegetable leaves later?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ sɛɛgbɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi nɔ lɛ tsu nii kɛgbe jwɛi Ani manyɛ mikɛ nakai tsɔne lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii kɛshwie baai lɛ anɔ nu sɛɛ mli?

english: No, leftover chemical particles in the tank can harm or kill your vegetables. It is best to keep separate sprayers, or wash the container multiple times with soap and plenty of clean water before using it for anything else.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni ashiɔ yɛ tanki lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye o-vegetables lɛ awui loo efite amɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ ahi he kroko. aloo okɛ samla kɛ nu ni mli tse babaoo afɔ tsɛnsii amli shii abɔ. dani okɛtsu nii kɛfee nɔ kroko

english: Curling leaves is a plant's natural way of protecting itself from losing water. By rolling up, less leaf surface is exposed to the blazing sun, helping the maize keep its moisture until evening.
ga: Leaf curling ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ nu ni elaajeɔ lɛ he. kɛji akɛ abɔle ehe lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɛɛ baa lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Is it good to pour cold water on my crops in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔse nu ni mli ejɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: It is better to water early in the morning or late in the evening. Cold water put on hot plants causes stress, and droplets left on the leaves in strong sunlight can magnify the heat and scorch the plant.
ga: Ehi akɛ oooha nu lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Nu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsei ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa. Ni nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baai anɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha la ni tsoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni eshã tso lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin when I plant them under big trees, but fail to yield fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo nɛkɛ beni midu yɛ tso agbo ko shishi shi etsuuu nii lɛ?

english: Plants stretch upward to search for sun when they are heavily shaded. Without enough direct sunlight, the crop cannot manufacture enough energy to produce flowers and fruits.
ga: Tsei baagbala amɛhe koni amɛyatao hulu lɛ kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso waa. Kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ faaa lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ hu nyɛŋ ajie hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai aba.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce many flowers, but the flowers drop off without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Flower dropping happens when a plant is stressed by extreme heat, poor soil nutrients, or erratic watering. To protect itself, the plant drops its flowers because it does not have enough energy to mature the fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ ni akɛbuɔ ohe No sɛɛ lɛ tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ shi ejaakɛ ebɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛaawo yibii lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive, shallow roots and tender leaves that dry out quickly under direct sunlight and dry winds. Planting shade crops like plantains around them keeps the soil cool and protects the leaves from sun damage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he.

english: Yellowing along the center of maize leaves is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and produce heavy ears, which can be corrected by applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-decomposed manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekɛ toi ni tsii aba. Abaanyɛ atsake enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers fall off without growing into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when watering is irregular. Extreme heat or heat stress makes the plant drop its blooms to save energy rather than feeding new fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo dɔlɛ he haomɔ haa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii heei.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants shrinking and curling upward like tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Upward leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies attacking the undersides of the leaves. Controlling these pests early with recommended organic or chemical sprays keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni tutuaa baa lɛ shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water sits around them for too long in poorly drained soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my harvested yams come out bent and covered in thick root hairs instead of being long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ ebɔle ehe ni shishifãi ahe yitsɔi ni mli tse ehà nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams bend and grow extra roots when the soil is hard, shallow, or rocky. Creating deep, loose soil mounds allows the yam tuber to expand downward easily without pushing against hard earth.
ga: Sweet potatoes baabɔle ni eshishifãi babaoo baakwɛ̃ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, ekɔɔɔ he eko, loo eyɛ tɛi. Gɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni etse ehe lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ oya kɛyaa shi ni amɛtsiii amɛhe kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over right when the bunch of plantains becomes big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ amɛje shishi amɛdara lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that struggle to hold up the heavy weight of a mature bunch, especially in high winds. Supporting the main stem with strong bamboo or wooden prop sticks prevents the tree from uprooting.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua tso ni eda lɛ muji ni tsii lɛ. Titri lɛ, yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tso loo tso ni wa fĩ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekaje shishi.

english: Why does my maize grain shatter into fine dust instead of clean meal when I take it to the mill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ sũ bibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee niyenii ni he tse kɛ́ mikɛtee ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Maize shatters if the grain is dried too much before milling or if the mill machine uses incorrect blade settings. Ensuring the grain is dried to the correct moisture level (around 12-13%) prevents grain breakage during processing.
ga: Abɛi baagbala kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbi tsɔ dani ashɛre. Aloo kɛji akɛ grinder lɛ kɛ blade setting ni ejaaa miitsu nii. Kɛji akɛ akwɛ koni ŋmaa lɛ agbi kɛyashɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ ni sa (aaafee 12-13%) lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmaa lɛ akakumɔ yɛ be mli ni atsuɔ he nii lɛ.

english: How do weevils keep damaging my stored beans even when I tie the sacks tightly?
ga: Te ŋmeii baanyɛ afite mi-kɔfi ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ aha tɛŋŋ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ kotoku lɛ fĩ shi shiŋŋ moŋ?

english: Weevils often lay tiny, unseen eggs on the beans while they are still in the field before harvest. These eggs hatch inside the sealed sacks, so using specialized airtight (hermetic) storage bags is necessary to suffocate the insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii fɔɔ wɔji bibii. Anaaa lɛ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo dani akpaa. Nɛkɛ wɔji nɛɛ fɔɔ kotokui ni atsĩ naa lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotoku krɛdɛɛ ko (vacuum) atsu nii koni akɛtsi kooloi bibii lɛ anaa.

english: Why does my processed cassava flour turn dark and smell sour after drying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tapioca ashikiŋsha ni afee lɛ lɛ su diŋɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni egbi lɛ?

english: Cassava flour darkens and turns sour if fresh roots take too long to dry after grating, which allows fermentation and mold to develop. Pressing out excess water quickly and drying the grated cassava under bright sun or a clean dryer preserves the white color and neutral taste.
ga: Cassava starch lɛ baafee ediŋŋ ni ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ shishifãi heei lɛ heɔ be babaoo tsɔ ni amɛgbiɔ beni ajie amɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwie shi oya ni okɛ ŋmei ni atswa lɛ agbi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi loo yɛ ŋmei ni he tse mli lɛ, ebaaha ehiɛ su yɛŋ kɛ eŋɔɔmɔ ni bɛ sɛɛnamɔ ko.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nutrients like nitrogen or is getting too much water. Nitrogen helps plants make green food, so adding fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps them regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye onibii tamɔ nitrogen loo enine eshɛ nu babaoo nɔ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara waa.

english: What causes the bottom of my tomatoes to turn black and rot before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egbo dani ekwɛ̃?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes, known as blossom-end rot, happen when the plant cannot take up enough calcium or gets irregular watering. Keeping the soil moist consistently and adding wood ash or lime to the soil helps prevent this.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo ahaa amɛ nu be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni okɛ tso sũ loo lime fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: How do I know if my cassava plants are getting enough space underground to grow big tubers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ bulbs wuji?

english: Cassava tubers need room to expand under the soil. If you plant them too close together, their roots fight for food and stay thin; leaving about 1 meter of space between plants gives the roots enough room to swell into large, heavy tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia he ko ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji odu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ niyenii he akaŋ ni amɛhiɔ shi mlɛo. Kɛ́ ashi tsei lɛ aaafee mita kome kɛjɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: The first rain of the season can be misleading because hot, dry days often return right after it. If your seeds sprout and the soil dries out completely, the tender young roots will burn and die, so it is safer to wait until the rains become steady.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ alaka mɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, gbii ni mli edɔ ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ fɔɔ sɛɛkuu yɛ no sɛɛ. Kɛji odumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Shishifãi bibii lɛ baashã ni amɛgboi. No hewɔ lɛ, eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ ba shi.

english: Yam vines need direct sun to make food that feeds the growing tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground toward the sun, which prevents leaf diseases and helps you get much bigger yams at harvest.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni miida lɛ niyenii. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ he ni edɔ lɛ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ folier hela naa ni ehaa onáa sweet potatoes ni da babaoo kɛji akpa.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal food and water from the main mother plant. Removing all but one or two strong shoots ensures the main plant gets all the energy it needs to produce large, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do experienced farmers cover the ground around their crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi haa he ni amɛŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, called mulching, keeps the hot sun from drying out the earth. It traps moisture so you water less often and stops heavy rain from washing away your rich topsoil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi haa lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Emɔɔ nu ni mli ewo nu lɛ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akafɔ shii abɔ ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak even when I have put fertilizer in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than cultivated crops and will steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your plants full access to the nutrients they need to grow well.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ. ni ebaaju ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa otsei lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they suffer from severe heat, dry soil, or attacks from small insects like mirids. Providing enough shade trees and protecting the farm from sucking insects keeps the flowers healthy so they turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen tutua amɛ. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ hulutsoo ni sa ni abu ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni nuɔ amɛ lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why are green caterpillars eating the center leaves of my young maize plants so fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely fall armyworms, which feed on the tender heart of the maize plant where new leaves grow. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended control methods before they dig deep inside will save your harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni baai heei ekwɛ̃ kɛjɛ mli lɛ ahe loo bibii lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akudɔɔ lɛ atsu nii dani otsa mli shɔŋŋ lɛ baaha okɛ be akafite yɛ okpamɔ lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight because their root systems are shallow and leaves burn easily. They need temporary shade, like plantains or shade trees, to protect them and keep the soil moist while they grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni baai lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Enɛ ji koni abu amɛhe ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves, but produce tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen from the soil or fertilizer, it spends all its energy growing leaves and stems instead of feeding the tubers. Balanced soil nutrients encourage the plant to store energy underground.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ. Ekɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ tsei ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni eeeha bulb lɛ niyenii. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize plants turn yellow in a V-shape while the top leaves remain green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a major food crops need to grow green. The plant moves the limited nitrogen it has from its older bottom leaves up to the younger top leaves to stay alive.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titri ni he hiaa koni akɛdu tsei eŋɔli Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen fioo kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and tall without strong stems when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛbɛ ŋmeii ni wa beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are overcrowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch upward quickly to reach the sun, making their stems weak and thin instead of sturdy.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe oya koni amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ gbɔjɔmɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee hewalɛ.

english: Why should I remove some of the young shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ

english: The extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and food from the main plant. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main plant gets enough nutrients to produce large, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi loo tsei lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ mli tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo plantains wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves look droopy in the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In extreme heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the soil. They droop to protect themselves from drying out, but usually recover in the cooler evening once water loss slows down.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛkotoɔ shi koni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli beni nu ni elaajeɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Why do black spots appear on my cocoa pods and cause them to rot during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii diji ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: The black spots are caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and humid weather. Clearing weeds and pruning shade branches lets air in to dry the pods faster and reduce the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ fɛ̃i, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ shihilɛi amli. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo nɔ lɛ ahe jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ oya ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cassava plants curling up and showing sticky wet spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai bibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by small pests like mealybugs or aphids that suck the sweet sap from the leaves. As they feed, they excrete a sticky substance called honeydew, which makes the leaves curl and weakens the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. be mli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ Ejieɔ nɔ ko ni shãa mɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nectar lɛ kpo. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant is stressed by irregular watering. Extreme heat prevents proper pollination, so the plant drops its unpollinated flowers to save energy.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ ni ekɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ miihao lɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shiiɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my crop harvests get smaller every year if I keep planting maize on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ faaa daa afi kɛji miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop year after year drains the exact same nutrients out of the soil until it is exhausted. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts helps put essential nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛbaafite. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do I know if my crops are dying from a disease or just wilting because of the heat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji helai miigbe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo amɛmiigbo kɛkɛ kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ mli?

english: If crops wilt during the hot afternoon sun but recover and stand upright in the cool morning, they are just heat-stressed. If they remain limp, turn yellow, or dry up overnight, a plant disease or root pest is attacking them.
