ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii gĩ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli Shi ehe wa lɛ ni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa mli. Kɛji amɛnyiɛ lolo kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛgbiɔ nyɔɔŋ kome Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso hela loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ji nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ miitutua amɛ.

english: If I notice one sick plant in my field, will the sickness spread to my other crops?
ga: Kɛji miyɔse tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani hela lɛ baagbɛ eshwa miŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, crop diseases are often caused by tiny fungi, bacteria, or viruses that travel through wind, rainwater splashes, or farming tools from diseased plants to nearby healthy ones.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmei bibii, bacteria, loo virus ni tsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai baa. nugbɔ nu loo okwaayeli nibii ni akɛshwieɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen manure or fertilizer, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves above ground instead of storing starch in its root tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Pepper blossoms drop without forming fruit when the plant suffers from sudden heat waves, dry soil during flowering, or a lack of essential soil nutrients like calcium.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni ewooo yibii kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ trukaa hulutsoo be mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. aloo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the soil is running out of nitrogen, causing the plant to pull remaining nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed its newer leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen lɛ efo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants burn and brown when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn under direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or banana trees planted nearby to act as umbrellas until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantain loo banana tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do some of my crop seeds fail to sprout after I plant them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if the soil is too dry, if they are buried too deep for oxygen to reach them, or if underground insects and soil fungus eat them before they can emerge.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he Aloo kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ye amɛ dani amɛje kpo.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plant cowpeas alongside my maize instead of maize alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmãa masɛi moŋ fe ŋmãa pɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil as plant food, naturally fertilizing the maize growing next to them.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii kɛhaa tsei lɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ ehe

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused when tomato plants cannot get enough calcium, usually because the moisture in the soil is uneven due to irregular watering or rainfall.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebalɛ nakai ji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ejaaa yɛ nu loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni ejaaa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do destructive worms appear inside my maize stalks during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmãa toi amli yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Rainy weather creates ideal conditions for pests like the fall armyworm, whose adult moths lay eggs on green leaves that hatch into caterpillars that bore directly into the maize stalk.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms. Kpɔŋɔi ni eda lɛ fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ baai eŋɔli ni shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt during the hottest part of the afternoon even when the soil feels wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Tomato plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it up during peak afternoon heat. As long as they bounce back by evening, it is a natural defense mechanism to conserve moisture, but deep root growth helps reduce this stress.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli. Shii abɔ ni amɛbaaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba gbɛkɛ mli lɛ. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ hu ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Shi shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa nɔnyɛɛ nɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why does rainwater sit on top of my farm for days instead of soaking into the soil for my crops to drink?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ enɛ eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mafolɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anu nu?

english: Heavy rains on compacted or hard clay soil cannot sink into the ground easily. Breaking up the hard soil surface with a hoe and adding organic matter like manure creates tiny pockets that allow water to filter down to crop roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei gbá shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmei fata he lɛ, ehaa kotokui bibii baa. ni haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli

english: Is it better for my vegetable crops if I water them lightly every morning or give them a heavy soak twice a week?
ga: Ani ebaahi aha mi-aduawai lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu fioo ko wo amɛmli daa leebi loo mikɛ nu ni mli wa wo amɛmli shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli?

english: Giving crops a deep soak less frequently encourages roots to grow deep into the soil searching for water, making the crops stronger and more resistant to heat, whereas light daily watering keeps roots shallow and weak.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo nu ni mli kwɔ mli shii abɔ lɛ, ewoɔ shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛdara kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatao nu. Ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ dɔlɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ ooshwie nu fioo daa gbi lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee mlɛo ni amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually show that the plant is starving for nitrogen. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant pulls nutrients away from its older lower leaves and sends them to the young upper leaves to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Beni nitrogen fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli. ni akɛmajeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ koni amɛhi shi

english: Why should I wait until the soil is moist before applying chemical fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Crop roots can only absorb food that is dissolved in water. Applying fertilizer to dry soil leaves the fertilizer useless on the surface and can burn and damage the plant's delicate root tips.
ga: Tso shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa nu mli shwieɔ shi lɛ pɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni he ehiaaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ebaanyɛ eshã ni efite tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete intensely for sunlight, air, soil water, and food. The plants waste all their energy growing tall to out-reach their neighbors for light instead of developing large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii he akaŋshii mli waa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei nɛɛ baawo ŋmeii wuji lɛ, amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ koni amɛkɛ la aha amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme stress, such as very high temperatures, uneven watering, or a lack of phosphorus in the soil, because they cannot support fruit under stressful conditions.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa, tamɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ ji akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛdu aduawai yɛ shihilɛi ni haoɔ mɔ mli.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings burn and die if I remove all the big trees from my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani midu lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight and high heat. Leaving larger trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides living shade that protects young cocoa until its leaves toughen up.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha hulutsoo ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi baai lɛ mli baawa.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants curl up and dry out when the hot harmattan winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ tswa lɛ?

english: Dry harmattan winds strip moisture out of leaves very quickly, and pests like mealybugs multiply faster in hot, dry conditions. Cassava plants curl their leaves to slow down water loss and defend against pest damage.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya. Ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mealybugs lɛ faa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu lɛ akafite amɛ fioo, ni amɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ anaa.

english: Why do the leaves of my garden egg plants develop a white powdery dust during warm, humid weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baai lɛ feɔ sũ yɛŋ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ?

english: That white dust is a fungal infection called powdery mildew, which thrives when humidity is high and airflow between plants is poor. Spacing plants properly allows air to dry the leaves and prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nakai sũ yɛŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Amɛshwereɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ ehiii. Kɛ́ ashi gbɛ yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ agbiɔ, ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips that feed on the leaf juices underneath. They suck out the plant's food and can spread plant sicknesses, causing the foliage to wrinkle and stunt overall growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli nu ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛmuɔ tsei aniyenii ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ tsei ahe helai amɛshwã. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛdalɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my young maize leaves with small brown dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ muji bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide deep inside the center funnel of the maize plant to feed on soft new leaves, and applying pest controls early helps prevent them from destroying the growing point.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadi. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkafiteɔ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm by competing directly with your crops. They steal the vital nutrients and fertilizer from the soil that your crops need to feed on, causing your crop to starve despite receiving enough water.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ akaŋ ni amɛkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehe hiaa ni otsei lɛ aye nii lɛ mli. Hɔmɔ aye onibii lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po.

english: Why should I wait for the ground to be moist before putting fertilizer around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani mawo ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so the crop roots can suck it up. If you apply fertilizer to dry soil in hot sun, it can burn the delicate plant roots or evaporate into the air before the crop gets any benefit.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛshwie shi bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ wo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, Sensitive plant shishifãi baanyɛ ashã loo amɛfo kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ ko.

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that can pull nitrogen food directly out of the air and put it into the soil through their roots. When the crop finishes, that natural food stays in the ground to nourish the next crop you plant.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni baanyɛ agbala nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Nakai adebɔɔ mli niyenii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Planting too closely actually lowers your total harvest because the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing gives each maize plant enough space to build thick stalks and large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ odu nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha onibii fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ aba shi. Enɛ ji akɛ, tsei wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ sũ lɛ mli. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa he lɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmãa tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmãa wuji.

english: Why do I need to put plantain suckers near my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ plantain tsei lɛ ama kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have big leaves that act like natural shade umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist during its first years in the field.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii ni ekɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves up toward full sunlight so they can manufacture food. Keeping the leaves off the damp ground helps the plant create energy to grow big tubers while protecting it from soil diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔni afee ni amɛná niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa hewalɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ bulbs wuji, yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ ehe hu kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when the heat becomes too intense or when watering is irregular. Extreme heat prevents the flowers from forming seeds inside, so the plant drops the flower instead of growing a fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa mli loo kɛ́ awo amɛ nu be fɛɛ be. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo dumɔwui yɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii.

english: Cassava is typically mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the base of the stem begins to crack open. You can dig up one stem to verify that the roots are thick and firm before harvesting the whole field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa Obaanyɛ otsa tso kome ni okwɛ akɛ shishifãi lɛ mli edɔ ni ehi shi shiŋŋ dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food they need to grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rain washes the soil nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do people advise me to plant beans together on the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans have special root leaves that pull natural plant food from the air and store it in the ground, which enriches the soil and helps the nearby maize grow bigger.
ga: Beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ amɛhe gbalaa tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni edaraa.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects sucking the juice from the leaves, or by extreme heat and drought stressing the plant so it closes up to conserve moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ ni haa tso lɛ haoɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. No hewɔ lɛ, agbe naa koni hulutsoo akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why shouldn't I bury my seed maize very deep in the dirt when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifuɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu?

english: If seeds are buried too deep, the baby sprout uses up all its stored energy trying to push through the heavy soil and dies before reaching the surface sunlight.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Gbekɛbii lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli ni amɛgboi dani hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba amɛnɔ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight with their leaves, which gives the plant enough energy to grow large yams underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaji lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo yɛ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛduɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does putting dry grass on the soil around my plants help them grow better in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ jwɛi woɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mitsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Dry grass acts like a protective blanket over the soil, keeping the hot sun from evaporating water quickly so the soil stays moist longer for your plants.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee nu oya. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ aha tsei lɛ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crop yields smaller even when I add fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops before your plants have a chance to take them up.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. dani otsei lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ lɛ.

english: Waterlogged soil starves the underground roots of air, allowing rot-causing fungi and bacteria to multiply rapidly and destroy the cassava tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye shikpɔŋ shishi kɔɔyɔŋ shishifãi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ faa oya ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small flowers before they turn into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Dani ebaatsɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop their flowers when stressed by sudden dry weather or excessive heat to conserve their water and energy to stay alive.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni baa trukaa loo latsaa ni naa wa hao amɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ wala nɔ lɛ he.

english: Why are my mature tomatoes cracking open right on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ miitswa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they get a sudden large amount of water after a dry period, causing the inside of the fruit to swell faster than the outer skin can stretch.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ kɛji akɛ nu babaoo bote mli trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa tso yibii lɛ mligbɛ lɛ fuɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛre.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow much better when I clear weeds away from them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ mijie jwɛi lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Removing them makes sure your crops get all the food and space they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa niyenii kɛ he fɛɛ he ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Yellow lower leaves on maize are usually a sign that the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when water collects on my land after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When water sits in the ground for too long, the roots drown and soil fungi cause them to rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha amɛgboi.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up small and twisted when planted in hard soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, deep soil to push downward easily. Hard or compact soil blocks their natural growth, forcing the tubers to stay small or turn into strange shapes.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya shi mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsiɔ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ naa. ni haa yitso lɛ feɔ bibioo loo ehiɛ yɔɔ srɔto

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking the sap from under the leaves, or by a plant virus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai amli

english: Why do insect pests attack my cowpea crop more than my cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa mi cowpea tsei lɛ fe mi yucca tsei lɛ?

english: Cowpeas produce sweet flowers and soft leaves that insects love to eat, while cassava leaves contain natural bitter compounds that keep many insects away.
ga: Cowpea woɔ fɔfɔi ni ŋɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni kooloi sumɔɔ ni amɛye. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, nɔ ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni shwieɔ kooloi bibii babaoo yɛ ŋmeii baai amli.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when the plant does not get enough steady water to support fruit formation.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yaa nɔ daa ni baaye abua ni amɛwo yibii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my okra plants growing very tall with big leaves but no pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Ani eyɛ baai wuji shi ebɛ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer makes okra put all its energy into growing tall stalks and leaves instead of producing flowers and pods.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa okra kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei kɛ baai ni kɛlɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii

english: Why do groundnut plants need soil heaped around them after they flower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei tsei lɛ taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni abua amɛhe naa beni amɛwo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: After flowering, groundnut plants send small stems called pegs into the soil. The nuts actually grow underground attached to these pegs, so loose soil helps them bury easily.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmei tso lɛ wo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​ŋmeii bibii. Ale amɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ ŋmeii nɛɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfuɔ amɛhe mlɛo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient in the soil. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen away, or the soil may be exhausted from continuous farming, requiring organic manure or fertilizer to restore it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen lɛ. Aloo ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ yɛ okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ hewɔ. ni biɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii koni akɛku sɛɛ afee lɛ ekoŋŋ

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the field. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas returns nitrogen naturally to the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsake lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot in the ground during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits in the field without proper drainage, it drowns the roots and creates the wet conditions that soil fungi need to cause root rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔji amli ni nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ bɛ mli lɛ. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he hiaa koni eha shishifãi lɛ agbo lɛ baa.

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not anchor deeply into the soil. As the heavy fruit bunch grows, the plant becomes top-heavy, and wet soil weakens the root grip, making wooden support poles necessary.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni aduawai akuu ni mli tse lɛ miida lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. Ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ akpɛtɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa ehe hiaa ni akɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ sɛɛ lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without growing into young pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers require tiny insects like midges for pollination before pods can form. If the weather is too dry, if shade is missing, or if the tree lacks water and nutrients, it naturally drops flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ biɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ pollination agents dani pods baanyɛ afee. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ lɛ, hulutsoo bɛ, loo kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii. Fɔfɔi baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso ama shi koni mi-sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural vines that need to spread their leaves towards sunlight to make energy. Lifting the vines off the damp ground prevents leaf diseases and ensures maximum sunlight hits the leaves, leading to larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wain tso ni esa akɛ egbɛ baai lɛ eshwa kɛya hulu la lɛ he koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba. Kɛ́ owó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ tsei lɛ ahe helai anaa, ni ebaaha hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso ni da.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their small fruits before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop young fruit when they experience water stress from irregular watering, extreme heat, or a shortage of key soil nutrients like calcium, causing the plant to shed what it cannot support.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii kɛji amɛna nu mli haomɔ yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ, ni no haa tsei lɛ jieɔ nibii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhi shi lɛ kpo.

english: What will happen if I plant my seeds very close together to fit more crops on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni tsei babaoo akwɛ̃ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too closely forces crops to compete against each other for sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak, thin plants with low yields and increased spread of fungal diseases.
ga: Amɛdumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa, amɛwoɔ yibii fioo, ni ŋmeii helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my main crops after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that are naturally adapted to local conditions, with seeds already waiting in the soil. They absorb water and nutrients far more aggressively than cultivated crops, which is why early weeding is essential.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. ni dumɔwui miimɛ momo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya kwraa fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. no hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is typically caused by viruses transmitted by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies, or it is a stress reaction to extreme heat and dry soil as the plant tries to conserve moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ tomato mli lɛ baa, loo akɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli baa beni tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekwɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoyam leaves droop during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Cocoyam leaves have large surface areas that lose water faster through heat than the roots can absorb during peak daylight. The plant naturally wilts slightly to conserve water and will bounce back once temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Cocoa baai lɛ yɛ he ko ni da ni nu fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ dɔlɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛhiɛ nu mli. ni ebaaku esɛɛ eba kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cowpea plants fold up tightly at night?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants fold their leaves at night to reduce moisture loss and hold in warm air around their stems, which protects them from cold night temperatures.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ gbɛkɛ koni ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aba shi, ni ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ abɔle tso lɛ he, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ fɛ̃i ni mli edɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ he.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling inward when the weather gets hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism where the tomato plant reduces its leaf surface area to prevent excess water evaporation during hot, dry spells.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tomato tsei haa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ baa shi koni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ akashwie shi yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do my lower maize leaves turn yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to feed the young, growing top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cocoyam plants grow huge green leaves but produce very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen, the crop spends all its energy developing leaves above ground instead of storing nutrients in the tuber below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when stressed by extreme heat or uneven watering to save energy rather than produce fruit it cannot support.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni naa wa loo nu ni afɔɔɔ amɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ni anyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ he gbɛ lɛ

english: Why does my yam vine keep reaching for trees instead of growing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ miishɛ tso lɛ he moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally grow toward high sunlight to produce energy. Staking yam vines off the ground gives them maximum sunlight, which helps them build large tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ daa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ adu sweet potato wain tsei kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni afeɔ yitso agbo.

english: Why do weeds grow very fast in open fields but stop growing under thick crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli tse mli shi amɛkpaa kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Most weeds require direct sunlight to grow. A dense crop canopy blocks sunlight from reaching the ground, effectively starving young weeds.
ga: Jwɛi babaoo biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ dani amɛdara. Dumɔwui ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ jwɛi bibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava drops leaves during dry periods as a survival trick to reduce water loss. Once the rains return, the plant quickly grows new leaves.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei baa shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baaná baai heei oya.

english: Why do my young plantain leaves become soft and weak after heavy flooding on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ efee blɛoo ni amɛhe waaa yɛ nu afua ni naa wa ni ba ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess water sitting on the field drowns plant roots by cutting off air. When roots cannot breathe, they stop taking up nutrients, causing the foliage above to wilt.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni ta ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu lɛ, amɛbaakpa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ namɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋwɛi baai lɛ baagboi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize crops turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape pattern, it usually means the crop is starving for nitrogen, an essential plant food. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen deep into the soil where young roots cannot reach it, so applying fertilizer like urea helps the plant regain its dark green color.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmãa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ fãi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ he miihia ŋmãa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but producing tiny tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ tuber bibioo ko yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or water, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing heavy leaves and stems instead of storing food in the ground. Planting in well-drained soil without over-fertilizing encourages the plant to direct its energy down into forming large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi ni tsii lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ najiaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli fe nine lɛ baawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ awo bulbs agboi afeemɔ mli.

english: Why do extension officers encourage us to plant cowpea or groundnuts on the land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ mɛi hewalɛ ni adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ dani adu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have tiny nodules on their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. When the legume crop is harvested, that natural plant food remains in the dirt to feed the next crop of maize without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa Adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni akɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli.

english: Maize plants roll their leaves inward to protect themselves from intense heat and reduce the amount of water lost through evaporation. It is a natural survival trick, but if the leaves stay rolled up early in the morning, it is a sign that the farm urgently needs water.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni amɛha nu ni laajeɔ kɛyaa lasu mli lɛ aba shi. Eji adebɔɔ yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaa. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lolo leebi maŋkpa lɛ Eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia ŋmɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers dry up and drop off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed their flowers when they experience severe water stress during dry spells or lack sufficient nutrients. The tree drops its blossoms to save its own life, and inadequate shade can make the heat worse, causing higher flower drop.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa ba amɛnɔ yɛ hɔmɔ bei amli loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Tso lɛ gbee shi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala. Ni hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ baanyɛ aha latsaa lɛ aya hiɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi babaoo ni shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start growing shoots in the barn even without being planted in moist soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ aduuu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living roots that enter a natural resting phase after harvest, but once that period ends, internal growth triggers wake the yam up to sprout. Storing the tubers in a cool, dark, and well-ventilated structure slows down this natural wake-up signal.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji shishifãi ni hiɛ ka ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ shihilɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Shi kɛ́ nakai be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Mligbɛ dalɛ lɛ kanyaa sweet potato lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ wo he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni haa mɔ teɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: What causes my tomato leaves to curl up and turn yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Curling and yellowing tomato leaves are typically caused by Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus, which is carried and spread from plant to plant by tiny whitefly insects. Controlling whiteflies using proper field cleaning or organic sprays stops the virus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus, ni ji ŋmei bibioo ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Spreads from one plant to another. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔ mli saamɔ ni sa loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii anɔ lɛ tsu nii ni akudɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do my pepper fruits get black, sunken patches at the bottom before they are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi diji ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shishigbɛ dani amɛshwereɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on pepper fruits—known as blossom-end rot—happen when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium, usually caused by irregular watering. Keeping the soil moisture steady helps the plant transport calcium evenly to the developing fruit.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ aduawai anɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium lɛ yaa aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why are my garden egg plants stunted with swollen bumps on their roots when I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii ni efuu yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Swollen roots with small bumps indicate an attack by microscopic soil worms called root-knot nematodes that suck juices and block water intake. Rotating your field with crops like marigolds or cassava helps cleanse the soil of these pests.
ga: Shishifãi ni efuu ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sũ mli ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ root-knot nematodes ni nuɔ nu lɛ mli nui lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ nu lɛ naa lɛ etutua amɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ tamɔ marigold loo ŋmei. Ye obua ni otsumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ ahe.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during strong winds even when they look green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and top-heavy canopies, especially when carrying a heavy bunch of fruit. Leaving too many shoots growing around one mother plant weakens the main root hold, so removing extra shoots and propping heavy plants with bamboo sticks prevents blow-downs.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni tsii. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ aduawai babaoo miiwo. Ni aaashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ tso ni yɔɔ fɔlɔ kome lɛ he lɛ baaha shishifãi titrii lɛ ahe ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ afee mlɛo. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni akɛ ŋmeii tsei tsu nii kɛfi tsei ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ akakumɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize once the rain starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first light shower because the ground can dry out quickly. Wait until the rain wets the soil deeply for a few steady days so seeds have enough moisture to sprout and survive.
ga: Kaadu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi oya. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii fioo komɛi koni eha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up to protect themselves from intense heat and save water by reducing evaporation. It is a natural survival reaction showing that the plant is heat-stressed and needs moisture.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛtsi hulutsoo ni fe nine lɛ naa ni ekɛbu nu he kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ ni ebaa shi lɛ nɔ. Eji adebɔɔ mli wala yibiiwoo ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ naa dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni amɛmiitao ŋmɔtɔ.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each plant proper spacing allows the roots enough room to expand and produce bigger tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee bulbs wuji.

english: If some seeds fail to sprout, should I plant new ones in those empty gaps?
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui komɛi ekwɛɛɛ Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui heei yɛ nakai ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: Yes, replanting missing spots early—known as supplying—ensures you do not waste land space, giving you a full farm and a much higher total yield at harvest time.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ atsake hei ni elaaje lɛ mra. Ale lɛ hu akɛ nihɔɔmɔ Ebaaye ebua ni okwɛ koni okafite shikpɔŋ nɔ he ko. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni fa babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why do the yellow bottom leaves on my maize die off while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ kã he eji eŋɔli lɛ?

english: This happens when the soil lacks enough nitrogen. The maize plant sacrifices its older, lower leaves to move nutrients upward to feed the new growth and developing cobs.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei kɛ baai ni egbɔ kɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ shaa afɔle koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aya ŋwɛi koni amɛkɛha ŋmeii heei ni miida kɛ ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off before producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when plants experience stress from severe dry heat, irregular watering, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping soil evenly moist helps the plant keep its blossoms.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: How can I easily tell if my farmland soil is healthy and fertile?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni ebaa nii?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, feels soft, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture well without staying waterlogged, and contains earthworms or decayed leaf matter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Ehaa mɔ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo Ejeɔ kpo oya yɛ nine mli Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni nu bɛ mli ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo baai bibii ni fiteɔ yɛ jɛmɛ

english: Yam roots need soft, loose soil to expand easily. If planted in hard or compacted ground without high mounds, the roots cannot push downward and become stunted or deformed.
ga: Sweet potato shishifãi taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ ni gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ bɛ nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ shi ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why is it better to buy certified seeds instead of planting saved grain from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially produced to resist local diseases, sprout at the same time, and produce much higher yields than saved grain, which weakens over generations.
ga: Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni ekɛte shi ewo maŋ lɛ mli helai. kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli Ni yibiiwoo lɛ fa kwraa fe dumɔwui ni ato lɛ. ni baagbɔjɔ kɛjɛ yinɔ kome mli kɛya yinɔ kroko mli

english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for maize. Their leaves also shade the ground to prevent weeds and keep soil moist.
ga: Cowpeas mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa. Amɛbaai lɛ hu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni jwɛi akabote mli ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting early when I store them in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛ́ akɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that enter a natural sleeping phase after harvest. When warm air and moisture hit them in storage, the yam thinks rain has come and starts using its stored energy to sprout new leaves.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni yɔɔ wala mli ni amɛboteɔ shihilɛ ni amɛhiɛ bɛ mli mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ tswa he ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ Sweet potato lɛ susuɔ akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ ni ebɔi ehewalɛ ni ekɛto lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ koni ekɛwo baai heei.

english: Why do some of my harvested yams go soft and light while waiting in the barn to be sold?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ ekomɛi yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harvested yams are mostly water. When stored in hot or dry conditions, water evaporates through their skin, causing the tuber to shrink, lose weight, and feel soft.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni akpaa lɛ ateŋ babaoo ji nu. Kɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ loo he ko ni egbi Nu lɛ baatsɔ hewolo lɛ nɔ efo. Ehaa yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi, ehaa shwiili lɛ baa shi ni enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo.

english: Why is my land giving me smaller yam tubers now than it did years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmeii bibii fe afii ni eho lɛ?

english: Soil gets tired when crops take up nutrients every year without a break. Over time, the natural food in the soil runs low, so new crops do not have enough energy to produce big tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nijiaŋ jeɔ wui beni tso lɛ nine shɛɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baafee bibioo. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant yams on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting yams in the same spot repeatedly draws out the exact same soil nutrients every year and allows yam-specific pests and soil diseases to build up in that ground.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ lɛ, ebaagbala niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that act like greedy neighbors. They drink up the water and eat the fertilizer nutrients before your crop roots can absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ. Amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers when the afternoon sun gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ shwane hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: When heat gets too high, the plant enters survival mode to save water. It drops its flowers because it cannot support forming new fruits under severe heat stress.
ga: Kɛji latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ lɛ tso lɛ yaa wala shihilɛ mli koni ekɛbu nu he. Efiteɔ fɔfɔi ejaakɛ enyɛɛɛ eye ebua aduawai heei ni baa yɛ latsaa ni naa wa shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops turning yellow during the dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the plant is missing nitrogen, which gives leaves their rich green color, or that water is too scarce for the roots to suck up soil nutrients.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli Aloo nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with tiny fruits when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii waa lɛ, be mli ni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight. They spend all their energy stretching upward to reach the light instead of making thick stems and big fruits.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛyashɛ la lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ tso nɛ mi wa nɛ e woɔ yiblii nguahi.

english: What causes my yams to rot in the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani anyɛɔ akpaa?

english: When heavy rain leaves water standing in the soil, the soil gets waterlogged. Without air reaching the tubers, fungal rot organisms thrive and decay the yams under ground.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu kpɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nu baatsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ko shɛɛɛ yitso lɛ he lɛ, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are tiny insects causing the fresh leaves on my pepper plants to curl up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miibɔle baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Very small pests like aphids suck the sap and juice out of young, tender leaves. Damaged tender tissue grows unevenly, causing the leaf to twist and curl inward.
ga: Nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui waa, tamɔ aphids lɛ, nuɔ nu kɛ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ amli lɛ. Tisu ni efite lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli.

english: Why are my maize crops turning yellow and producing very small cobs even when it rains well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Soil gets exhausted when you plant heavy-feeding crops continuously without replenishing nutrients. Yellowing leaves and small yields mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to build strong leaves and healthy cobs.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ oya nɔ okwɛ tsei ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni okɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fataaa he. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ yibiiwoo ni faaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ biɔ ni tsei lɛ awo baai ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is completely exhausted and needs a rest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli ewo muji ni ehe miihia ni mafo mli?

english: Exhausted soil shows clear signs: crops take much longer to grow, leaves look pale or stunted, harvests shrink significantly year after year, and plants become easily damaged by mild dry spells.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ jieɔ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛhe ejɔ. Nikpamɔ lɛ eba shi kwraa afi fɛɛ afi. Ni hɔmɔ fioo ko fiteɔ tsei oya.

english: Why is it risky for me to rely only on cocoa instead of growing other food crops on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mihe baawo oshara mli ni mikɛ mihe afɔ̃ kookoo pɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni madu niyenii krokomɛi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Relying on a single cash crop leaves you vulnerable if prices fall, bad weather hits, or disease strikes. Planting other food crops like cassava, yam, or plantain ensures your family has food and alternative income sources throughout the year.
ga: Shika ŋmɔshi nibii kome pɛ ni oookɛ ohe afɔ̃ nɔ lɛ kɛ bo woɔ oshara mli kɛji nibii ajara ba shi. Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii loo hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa mɛi lɛ jio lɛ, niyenii krokomɛi tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, loo ŋmei ni ooodu lɛ baaha oweku lɛ aná niyenii kɛ shika gbɛ kroko ni amɛaatsɔ nɔ amɛná shika yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant groundnuts or beans together with my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have a special ability to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that helps neighboring crops grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛkɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it safe to grow cassava or plantain on the same plot where I have young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu cassava loo plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miyɔɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting food crops like plantain alongside young cocoa is beneficial because fast-growing plantains provide necessary shade and moisture to protect fragile cocoa seedlings from scorching sunlight.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantain ni akɛfataa kookoo bibii ahe lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa koni akɛbu kookoo dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: When soil has too much leaf-boosting nutrient or too much shade, cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves above ground instead of storing starch in its root tubers.
ga: Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni haa baai babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo baa. Yucca kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before they can turn into young pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔii dani amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience severe environmental stress, such as extreme heat, sudden drought, or loss of canopy shade, causing the tree to drop flowers to save energy for survival.
ga: Cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi ni naa wa, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ kpe. loo hulutsoo ni baa shi Enɛ haa tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do my young plantain suckers dry up and die during the dry season while mature plantain trees stay alive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui wuji lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo lɛ?

english: Young plantain suckers have short, shallow root systems that cannot reach moisture deep underground, unlike mature trees whose deep roots can access underground water during dry spells.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni yɔɔ kuku ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ he. Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ tsei ni edara lɛ, amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: What crop should I plant after harvesting maize to help my soil recover naturally?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei esa akɛ madu yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ koni eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ ehe awo mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Planting leguminous crops like cowpeas or soybeans after a maize harvest helps restore nitrogen to the soil that the heavy-feeding maize crop pulled out during its growth.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa loo soybeans mli yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni haa ŋmãa mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ waa yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ nɔ.

english: What actually happens to my soil if I plant the exact same crop on the same plot of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi?

english: Continuous mono-cropping drains specific soil nutrients faster than the soil can naturally rebuild them, while also allowing crop-specific pests and soil diseases to build up and ruin future harvests.
ga: Monocultures ni yaa nɔ edaa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii komɛi hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee ehee ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai feɔ nibii ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow if I plant them in September before the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ September mli dani nugbɔ nɛ?

english: Seeds need consistent moisture to sprout and build strong roots. Planting in dry soil during warm periods causes seeds to dry out, rot, or stay dormant until sufficient rainfall arrives.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi, amɛgboi, loo amɛyawɔ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa baanɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has enough moisture for me to start planting after a long dry spell?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli eyi kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha manyɛ mabɔi tsei akwɛmɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You can test moisture by taking a handful of soil from a few inches deep and squeezing it into a ball; if it holds its shape without crumbling or dripping water, it has enough moisture for planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ sũ ni mli kwɔ fioo ni oooŋɔ ni okɛmiifee bɔɔlu lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ehi shi shiŋŋ ni ebɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo nu ni hoɔ lɛ, no lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: What happens to my maize or grain crops if water stops coming right when they start flowering?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa loo ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji nu lɛ kpa kɛji ebɔi fɔfɔi?

english: Water stress during flowering causes crops to drop their flowers or produce empty, unfilled grain heads because the plant conserves water for its own survival rather than seed production.
ga: Nu mli haomɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi loo amɛwoɔ dumɔwui ni bɛ nɔ ko ni edako. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei toɔ nu he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee dumɔwui

english: Why is it bad for my crop growth if I leave lots of stones and old plant debris in my farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ ehiii kɛji mishi tɛi kɛ tsei momoi babaoo yɛ miŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Stones and heavy debris block young root growth, create uneven soil coverage, and trap excess heat, which prevents crop roots from reaching nutrients and water evenly.
ga: Tɛi ni tsii kɛ sũ ni etse ehe lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi bibii lɛ adalɛ naa. Bɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni ekɛ dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ emɔɔ Enɛ haaa tsei shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu be fɛɛ be.

english: Does clearing weeds and trash from my farm before planting really help my crops grow faster?
ga: Ani jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani miduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya?

english: Yes, removing weeds and trash eliminates competition for light, water, and soil nutrients, allowing young crops to grow rapidly without being choked or shaded out.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa akaŋshii ni akɛtaoɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛdaraa oya ni hulu lɛ tsiii amɛnaa loo ehaaa amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my harvested grains rot or mold quickly when I store them after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya loo ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mikɛto beni akpa kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grains rot in storage if they are harvested with high moisture levels or mixed with wet dirt and crop residue, which trap humidity and invite mold and insects.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akpa amɛ yɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli loo akɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ efutu mli. Enɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi bibii baa.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my grains so they do not spoil in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa nii? Koni ŋmaa lɛ akafite yɛ ŋmɔji amli?

english: Grains are ready for harvest when the leaves turn yellow or brown, the stems dry out, and the seeds become hard enough that you cannot easily dent them with your fingernail.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo asarasu, tsei lɛ agbi, ni dumɔwui lɛ wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛgbala nineshi tsitsii lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up and turn yellow when there is a drought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Rolling up leaves is a crop's defense mechanism to reduce water loss from sunlight, while leaf yellowing shows the plant is shutting down non-essential parts to keep its main stem alive.
ga: Baai ni akpɛ́ɔ lɛ ji tso hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni haa nu ni hulu la fiteɔ lɛ baa shi. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miikpa hei ni he ehiaaa lɛ koni eha tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ akafite.

english: Which crops are best for me to plant if I do not have an irrigation pump and rely only on rain?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ makwɛ kɛji mibɛ nu pɔmp ni mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ɔ nugbɔ pɛ nɔ?

english: Drought-tolerant crops like millet, sorghum, cassava, and cowpeas handle irregular rainfall much better than water-heavy crops like tomatoes or lowland rice.
ga: Nibii ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei baanyɛ akpee nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ fe nibii ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli tamɔ tomato loo ŋmei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: How can joining a local farmers' group help me deal with dry weather and water shortages?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ okwaafoi akuu ko ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni mikɛ mihe baawo mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni matsu kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ he nii?

english: Farmer groups allow members to pool money to buy or rent shared irrigation equipment, schedule collective water usage, and buy inputs in bulk at cheaper rates.
ga: Okwaafoi akui ŋmɛɔ amɛmli bii lɛ gbɛ ni amɛbua shika naa koni amɛkɛhe loo amɛha nu shwiemɔ nibii ni akɛhaa. Tsɔɔmɔ nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ fɛɛ ni ohé nibii ni akɛfeɔ lɛ babaoo yɛ jara ni baa shi nɔ

english: Why do my yam tubers end up small and twisted instead of big and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni egbɛ eshwa moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose soil to expand easily. If the ground is hard or full of rocks, the tuber cannot grow outward easily, which causes it to turn out small, misshapen, or twisted.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni egbɛ eshwa oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ Tubers lɛ hu nyɛŋ adara kɛya kponɔgbɛ mlɛo. Enɛ haa efeɔ bibii, ni esaaa loo etsakeɔ.

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during long dry spells to save water and keep the underground stem alive. Once the rains return, the plant grows fresh leaves and continues growing.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baaná baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Maize seeds need continuous moisture in the soil to sprout and build strong roots. Planting too early in dry soil can cause the seeds to dry out, rot, or get eaten by insects before they germinate.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi, amɛgboi, loo kooloi aye amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing lots of green leaves but very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes tomato plants put all their energy into leaves instead of flowering. Using a balanced fertilizer with phosphorus helps the plant produce flowers and fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai amli moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni phosphorus yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai.

english: Why is it good for me to plant beans on the same plot where I grew maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Maize drains nutrients from the soil, but beans put nitrogen back into the earth through their roots. Rotating them refreshes the soil naturally without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ atsake shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai krokomɛi awo mli.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that spreads in damp, overly shaded cocoa farms. Pruning extra shade branches and removing infected pods early stops the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kookoo ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shade mli lɛ ni ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices from young leaves. Controlling these insects early prevents leaves from twisting and keeps the plant bearing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni ekatsɔ ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do caterpillars attack my maize crop so fast in the minor season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-abele lɛ oya yɛ sɛkɛndi be mli lɛ?

english: Pests like the fall armyworm multiply quickly during warmer dry spells when crops are stressed. Checking the center leaves of young maize regularly allows you to treat the crop before caterpillars cause major damage.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworm lɛ fɔɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli beni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ haomɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni otsa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani ŋmãa lɛ afite lɛ waa.

english: Why do my maize plants keep falling over when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over if planted too close together, sown too shallowly, or lacking strong root support. Space seeds properly and mound extra soil around the base of the stalks to anchor them.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Dumɔ he ni mli ekwɔɔɔ tsɔ loo shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ bɛ lɛ Dumɔ dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ krokomɛi ato tso lɛ shishi koni ekɛ amɛ ahi shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to make food and grow green. Adding organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the maize regain its dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it good for my land if I plant beans or cowpeas together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil and helps feed nearby maize plants without extra cost.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii ni awooo he nyɔmɔ kroko.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and shrinking in size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee bibioo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by extreme sun heat, irregular watering, or tiny insects like whiteflies carrying viruses. Giving plants consistent water and shade can help keep them healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli dɔlɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni hiɛ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe Nu kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees are like delicate babies that burn under direct sun. They need temporary shade crops like plantains to protect them from heat and keep soil moist while their roots grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ abifabii ni he waaa ni shãa yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Why does my plantain stalk die right after harvesting one bunch of plantains from it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwu lɛ gbo amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikpa plantains kuu ko kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: A plantain stalk only flowers and fruits once in its lifetime. After producing a bunch, that stem dies so the plant can direct its energy into growing new shoots at the base for future harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii shikome pɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli. Beni ajie tso lɛ yibii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ shishifã lɛ gboɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo tsei heei yɛ shishigbɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ kpamɔ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, severe dry spells, or overwatering. Maintaining steady soil moisture helps the flowers stay on and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni naa wa loo nu babaoo yɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔi.

english: Cassava sheds leaves in dry heat to save water and prevent drying out completely. When the rainy season returns, the plant easily sprouts new leaves and continues growing underground.
ga: Cassava kɛ la ni mli egbi shwieɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekɛtsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbi kwraa. Kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baawo baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ eda yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How do I know when my seed yams are ready to be planted into the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Seed yams are ready when their resting period ends and small green shoots begin to emerge from the top end, showing that the tuber is active and ready to grow into a vine.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ baafee klalo kɛji hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ ba naagbee. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ bɔi kpojee kɛjɛ ŋwɛi naagbee lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bulb lɛ miitsu nii ni efee klalo akɛ ebaada ni etsɔ wain tso.

english: Why does my cassava rot if rain collects on my field, while rice grows fine in flooded soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? While rice grows well in soil that is flooded?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe, so standing water smothers and rots them. Rice plants have special hollow stems that pump air down to their roots even when under water.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ. Omɔ tsei yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni mli ewo muji ni shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu shishi po.

english: Why do my groundnut flower stems bend down and push themselves into the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut fɔfɔi lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi amɛhe kɛmiiya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts bloom above ground, but after pollination, the plant grows a stalk called a peg that pushes into the soil. The actual groundnut pod can only grow and ripen underground in the dark.
ga: Peanuts fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi yɛ pollination sɛɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs ni tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Anɔkwale ŋmeii baanyɛ adara ni amɛshwere yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ duŋ mli pɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which the plant needs for green growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost early in the season helps keep the leaves green and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo mli yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ebaaha amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my groundnut crop produce empty pods with no seeds inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods occur when the soil lacks calcium during pod development. Adding agricultural lime or gypsum to the soil around flowering time helps the pods fill out with healthy seeds.
ga: Peanut pods ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium yɛ pods lɛ shweremɔ be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ lime loo okwaayeli mli gypsum fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my oil palm seedlings growing very slowly and turning pale green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm dumɔwui lɛ miida blɛoo waa ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Pale green leaves on young oil palms are often a sign of magnesium or potassium deficiency in depleted soil. Applying balanced fertilizer specifically suited for oil palms restores leaf color and speeds up growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ mu tsei anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ magnesium faaa loo potassium ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ pɔtɛɛ aha mu tso lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ ahe afee fɛo ekoŋŋ ni eha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when exposed to extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Regular watering and providing light shade during extremely hot days help flowers turn into fruit.
