ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafite amɛ fɔfɔii kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Cassava naturally sheds and curls its leaves during dry spells to save water and protect itself from drought. Once the rains resume, the plant quickly revives and produces fresh green leaves.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Koni okɛ nu akafite ni obu ohe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba wala mli oya ni ebaana baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when planted in open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them protects the seedlings until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni ooodu yɛ masɛi Enɛ baaye abua ni abu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very tall and leafy but produce almost no tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi tomato ko kwraa bɛ lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil makes tomato plants put all their energy into growing leaves instead of flowers. Using fertilizers higher in phosphorus encourages the plant to set blossoms and fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa tomato tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and heavy fruit bunches make the plant top-heavy during strong winds. Propping up the main stem with sturdy bamboo poles supports the weight until harvest.
ga: Plantain shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ haa tso lɛ tsiɔ ehe yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tso ni wa to tso titri lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsɔne lɛ mli tsiimɔ lɛ kɛyashi ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Yam tubers rot underground when soil stays waterlogged for too long or when tiny soil pests attack the tubers, allowing fungus to enter. Planting on raised mounds improves drainage and prevents rot.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii tutua ŋmeii lɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii boteɔ mli. Ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaaa efite.

english: Why do my harvested onions sprout green shoots and go soft quickly in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onions ni mikpa lɛ shwereɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo oya yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Onions sprout and decay when stored in damp, warm, or poorly ventilated spaces. Keeping them in a dry, dark, and well-ventilated shed slows down sprouting and keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Sabolai baakwɛ̃ ni egbo kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni edɔ, edɔ, loo kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ amɛ ato he ko ni egbi, ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli. Enɛ baaha ekwɛ̃mɔ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaaha ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why did my maize plants grow leaves and stalks, but fail to produce any corn cobs to eat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ yɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ? Shi ani obɛ ŋmãa ko ni oyeɔ?

english: Maize needs adequate water and nutrients right when it flowers and forms cobs. If the plant faces drought, poor soil, or overcrowding during that critical period, it uses all its energy just to stay alive rather than making grains.
ga: Nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia abɛi kɛji ewo fɔfɔi ni efee ŋmeii. Kɛji tsei kɛ hɔmɔ, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo mɛi ni eyi obɔ kɛ gbɔmɛi babaoo kpe yɛ nakai be ni mli wa lɛ mli lɛ, Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛhi wala mli kɛkɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaafee ŋmaa.

english: Why do my crops die off completely in the middle of the season even after sprouting well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboiɔ kwraa yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛmiikwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Young crops often die if an early dry spell hits right after germination, or if the soil lacks key nutrients to help the roots grow deep enough to survive heat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii gboiɔ kɛji hɔmɔ ba beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii ni baaye abua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara kɛya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Should I keep planting the traditional maize seeds I know, or try new seed varieties?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maya nɔ madu blema ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mile lɛ? loo kaa dumɔwui heei okwɛ

english: Traditional seeds are familiar, but new certified seed varieties are specifically bred to survive dry spells, resist local pests like armyworms, and give higher yields in shorter rainy seasons.
ga: Kusum dumɔwui ji nɔ ni ale jogbaŋŋ. Shi dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ Atsɔse amɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Eteɔ shi ewoɔ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ cutworms. ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo lɛ mli

english: Is it safe to plant only maize on my entire farm, or should I plant other crops alongside it?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmãa pɛ yɛ miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli? Aloo esa akɛ mikɛ tsei krokomɛi afata he?

english: Planting only maize is risky because drought or pests can destroy your whole farm. Mixing maize with legumes like cowpea or groundnuts protects your food supply and improves soil fertility.
ga: Abele pɛ ni ooodu lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ hɔmɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui baanyɛ akpata oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa futu mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu niyenii ni oyɔɔ lɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo.

english: Why shouldn't I put four or five maize seeds in one hole to get more crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ejwɛ loo enumɔ woɔ bu kome mli koni maná yibii babaoo?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole forces the plants to compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil food, resulting in thin, weak stalks with no cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ehe awo nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmei bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: How do I know the right time to put my maize seeds in the ground during the rainy season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Wait until the soil has received two or three heavy rains that soak deep into the ground, ensuring the young roots will have enough moisture to survive if the rain stops for a few days.
ga: Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi bibii lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi.

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide deep inside the center whorl of the maize plant to feed on tender leaves before the cob forms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai bibii dani ŋmãa lɛ baa lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the plant is starving for nitrogen in the soil, which often happens when soil is overworked or washed away by heavy surface water.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ atsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii fe nine loo nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ho.

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's natural way of protecting itself from losing moisture through its leaves when the heat is extreme and water in the soil is low.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni elaajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ lɛ he kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa ni nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa.

english: How can I stop insects from destroying the little maize I manage to harvest while it is stored at home?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi ni fiteɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ anaa? Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa nii yɛ be mli ni mikɛtoɔ shia lɛ?

english: Insects thrive on moisture, so you must dry your harvested maize thoroughly until the grains are hard before storing them in clean, sealed bags or treated storage containers.
ga: Kplukai shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ amɛyashɛ ŋmɔtɔ he. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ogbi ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee shiŋŋ dani okɛwo kotokui ni he tse ni atsĩ naa loo ŋmãa ni akɛ tsofa ewo mli lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and short roots that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Plantain trees or temporary shade trees are needed to protect them from heat and keep the soil moist while their root systems develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo he miihia kɛha dumɔwui loo tsei koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn plants turning yellow while the rest of the plant is still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni baai krokomɛi ni eshwɛ lɛ ji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young corn usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for green leaf growth. Applying compost, manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer early in the season will help restore green leaves and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ ni eha amɛdaramɔ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does my cassava plant have lots of tall stem and leafy branches but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ kɛ niji ni yɔɔ baai kakadaŋŋ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are crowded, cassava puts all its energy into growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in its underground roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei babaoo yɔɔ jɛmɛ. Yucca kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: What causes tiny holes in the leaves of my young maize plants with brown powdery dirt left inside the leaf fold?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ yɛ muji ni tamɔ powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ yɛ baa lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common insect pest that hides inside the growing center of maize plants. Catching them early and applying organic treatments like neem oil or approved pesticides protects the leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ hei lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off during hot weather without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil cause stress to tomato plants, forcing them to drop their blossoms to save water and energy. Mulching the soil with dry grass and keeping water consistent helps keep the flowers on the plant.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ afolɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie tsei lɛ anɔ, ni aha nu lɛ ahi shi daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field help my maize grow better next season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas out of the air and put it naturally into the soil through their roots. When the legume plant decays, it leaves behind enriched soil for crops planted after it.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ fite Ebaashi shikpɔŋ ni baa shi kɛha tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ no sɛɛ.

english: Why don't the corn seeds I saved from my last harvest yield as well as the hybrid seeds I bought from the agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ jeee nɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto yɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni mihe kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for strength and high yield in the first generation. Seeds collected from that harvested crop lose those special traits, resulting in weaker plants and smaller cobs if replanted.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ kɛha hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and stunted even when there is plenty of rain falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most farm crops and quickly steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients before your crops can reach them. Clearing weeds within the first month gives your crops the space and food they need to stay strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested yams turn soft and rot so quickly inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni efiteɔ oya yɛ mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot easily if they are stored in hot, poorly ventilated spaces or if they get bruised during harvest. Keeping yams off the ground in a cool, shady, and airy barn prevents moisture buildup and spoilage.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli. aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔlɔ ko yɛ be mli ni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potatoes lɛ to shikpɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ akabua ehe naa ni efite.

english: Why should I make mounds or ridges before planting root crops like sweet potatoes and cassava instead of planting on flat land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matswa gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ dani madu shishifãi tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ? Instead of planting on flat land

english: Mounds and ridges loosen hard soil so roots can expand easily into large tubers, while also raising plants above heavy water runoff so their roots do not drown or rot after heavy rains.
ga: Gɔji kɛ ŋshɔkei lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛtsɔ bulb agboi oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, aduɔ tsei yɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji koni shishifãi lɛ akabote nu mli loo amɛkafite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ.

english: Pale yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build strong green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away or floods the roots so they cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ loo eha shishifãi lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ nu, ni eha amɛmumɔ shwie shi.

english: How do groundnuts and cowpeas help make my farm soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii baanyɛ aye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are special plants that can feed on nitrogen from the air and store it in tiny knots on their roots. When the crop is harvested and leaves decay, that trapped food stays in the soil to feed whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto amɛshishifãi bibii amli kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni baai lɛ egbo. Niyenii ni ekã lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than most crops. When you apply fertilizer, the weeds steal the water, light, and plant food first before your crops get a chance to take them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei babaoo. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei amli dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa hegbɛ eyeɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my cocoa trees instead of turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree is stressed by dry weather, lacks soil nutrients, or when tiny insects that pollinate the flowers are missing. Without proper pollination and enough water, the tree cannot support the flowers and lets them drop.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao tso lɛ. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii Pollinators lɛ laaje. Kɛji akɛ pollination ni sa kɛ nu ni sa bɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ ni eha fɔfɔi lɛ gbee shi.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and soft while still growing on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo yɛ be mli ni edaa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium to the fruit, which usually occurs when watering is irregular or the soil dries out suddenly while the tomatoes are growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha aduawai lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩɔ trukaa be mli ni tomatoi lɛ miida lɛ.

english: When temperatures get too high, pepper plants lose water quickly and get stressed. To protect themselves from dying, they shed their flowers so they do not spend energy making fruits.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ nu fiteɔ oya ni amɛhaoɔ amɛhe. Bɔni afee ni obu ohe kɛjɛ gbele he Amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akawo yibii.

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or thrips that hide under the leaves, or a virus carried by insects. As they suck the plant juices, the leaves twist up and the plant stops growing.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni kooloi bibii hiɛɔ beni amɛmuɔ tso nu lɛ Baai lɛ tsɔɔ sɛɛ ni tso lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water for too long. Excessive moisture allows soil fungi to enter and destroy the roots underground, especially in flat fields with poor drainage.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ. Titri lɛ, yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when strong winds or heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and do not go deep into the ground. When the bunch grows heavy, the plant becomes top-heavy, making it easy for wind to uproot it unless you prop it up with wooden poles.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji kuu lɛ da lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatswa ni efo shishifãi lɛ. Ja okɛ tso ko tsu nii ni okɛfi sɛɛ.

english: Why are my seed yams sprouting early in the barn before I am ready to plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ miikwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mifee klalo akɛ madu lɛ?

english: Seed yams sprout when the storage barn gets too warm or humid. Heat and trapped moisture signal to the yam root that it is time to wake up and grow, even if the planting season has not arrived.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛ́ shĩa lɛ mli edɔ loo edɔ tsɔ. Dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni amɔmɔ lɛ tsɔɔ sweet potato shishifãi lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛte shi ni amɛdara, eyɛ mli akɛ amɛdalɛ be lɛ shɛko lolo moŋ.

english: Why should I use pegs and rope to plant my crops in straight lines instead of scattering them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ ŋtayaai kɛ kpãa atsu nii ni mikɛdu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni magbɛ amɛshwã?

english: Planting in straight lines using pegs ensures each crop gets equal access to sunlight, air, and soil nutrients. It also makes it much easier to walk through your field to weed and harvest without accidentally stepping on young plants.
ga: Nibii ni akɛduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋtayaai anɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa nyiɛmɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔji amli kɛyaa jwɛi kɛ ŋmaa lɛ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa ni okɛ onaji efɔɔɔ tsei bibii anɔ yɛ oshara mli.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition weakens the plants, resulting in thin stems and smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do my young seedlings wilt and drop leaves right after I transplant them into the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛbaai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Transplanting causes shock because tiny roots get disturbed when moved. Moving seedlings during cooler times, like late afternoon, and putting them into moist, well-dug holes helps the roots recover and absorb water quickly.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mɔ kroko mli lɛ kɛ shoofeemɔ baa yɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ ahewɔ. Egbaa mɔ naa kɛji ootsi ehe Okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo mli yɛ be ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli, tamɔ shwane mli, ni okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo bu ko ni mli efɔ ni atsa jogbaŋŋ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛŋɔ nu oya.

english: How deep should I dig holes when transplanting my young seedlings into the field?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafo bu mli kɛyashɛ he ni eshɛ ha tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui bibii miiwo ŋmɔ mli?

english: The hole should be deep and wide enough so the plant's roots spread comfortably and sit at the same soil level as they were in the nursery. Planting too shallow dries out the roots, while planting too deep can rot the main stem.
ga: Esa akɛ bu lɛ mli kwɔ ni elɛɛ bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu nɔ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ adu ni mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ agbo.

english: Why do wild weeds seem to grow much faster than my newly planted crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu ehee lɛ?

english: Weeds are hardy wild plants naturally adapted to steal water and nutrients quickly from open soil. Because young crops grow slowly at first, weeds can easily overshadow and choke them if you do not clear them early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii oya kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei bibii baakwɛ̃ fiofio yɛ shishijee mli. Jwɛi baanyɛ aha amɛhe afee duŋ ni amɛtsi amɛhe naa oya kɛji ojieee amɛ mra.

english: How often should I clear weeds away from my young plants during their early stage?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mra be mli dumɔwui lɛ amli?

english: Young plants need weed-free space on a regular monthly basis because their root systems are still small and delicate. Keeping weeds away every month ensures your crop gets uninterrupted light and food to grow strong.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ he miihia he ko ni jwɛi bɛ daa nyɔŋ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifã lɛ ji bibioo lolo ni ebɛ hewalɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa nyɔŋ nɔ lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa la kɛ niyenii ni yaa nɔ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will weeds around my crops actually reduce my harvest, or do they just make the farm look untidy?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ baaha mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi diɛŋtsɛ loo ebaaha ŋmɔ lɛ afee tamɔ nɔ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he kɛkɛ?

english: Weeds directly cut down your harvest size by stealing water, light, and fertilizer meant for your crops. They also act as hiding places for harmful pests and diseases that can attack your farm.
ga: Jwɛi haa onibii ni okpaa lɛ baa shi tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ nu, kane, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejuɔ kɛhaa onibii lɛ nɔ. Amɛji hei hu ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ oshara ni baanyɛ atutua oŋmɔ lɛ teɔ shi yɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young plants turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your young plant is lacking key nutrients like nitrogen, often because weeds are stealing its food or water is pooling around the roots. Clearing weeds and improving soil drainage helps leaves turn green again.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ odumɔwui lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ jwɛi miiju niyenii loo nu ebua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ooojie kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ oye obua baai lɛ ni amɛtsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does a young plant stop growing or die if its stem gets wounded while I am weeding?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso bibioo ko kpaɔ dalɛ loo egboɔ kɛji etso lɛ pila beni mijieɔ jwɛi lɛ?

english: A plant's outer stem carries water and nutrients from the roots to the leaves. Wounding the stem with a cutlass cuts off this food supply line and leaves open cuts where rot and insects can enter.
ga: Tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ tso lɛ woɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa baai lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ tso lɛ fɔ tso lɛ he lɛ, efoɔ niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ mli, ni ehaa gbɛ ko ni kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ atsɔ mli abote mli.

english: Why do my young crops seem to grow very slowly above the ground during the first few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ daa blɛoo waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: In the first few months, a young plant focuses most of its energy underground to build a deep, strong root system. Once the roots are fully settled and finding water, the leaves and stem will begin to grow much faster.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛma shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ egbe naa ni ana nu lɛ Baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ baabɔi dalɛ oya kwraa.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby creates a canopy that protects the delicate cocoa leaves from sun damage and keeps the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ

english: Leaving too many side shoots (suckers) forces the main plantain tree to share its water and nutrients, resulting in small fruit bunches. Pruning extra suckers ensures all food goes into producing large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi sɛɛ ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha plantain titri lɛ aja nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji aduawai bibii bibii. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha plantain tso agbo ko ni tsii aba.

english: Pepper plants often drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extended dry periods or extremely high heat. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant hold onto its flowers and form fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔ ko ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli, tamɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɔ́ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, which often happens when soil moisture fluctuates between very wet and very dry.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ nɔ ni efɔ waa kɛ nɔ ni egbi waa lɛ teŋ.

english: This leaf damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which feed on the growing centers of young maize plants during the night or early morning.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni daraa lɛ ateŋ gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ baa.

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest when the main stem turns woody and brown, lower leaves yellow and shed, and small cracks begin to appear in the soil around the base of the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji tso lɛ shishifã lɛ tsɔ tso kɛ asarasu. Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. kɛ ŋmeii bibii Amɛjeɔ shishi amɛjeɔ kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward to catch maximum sunlight for photosynthesis, which supplies the energy needed for large tubers to expand beneath the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la babaoo kɛha fotosintɛsis. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ŋmeii wuji lɛ aya nɔ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller maize yields now than it did five years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo fe afii enumɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop in the same soil every season drains essential plant nutrients over time. Rotating crops or allowing the land to rest helps restore essential soil nutrients naturally.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei komekomei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ amli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ afite yɛ be ni sa mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: The first rain is often followed by a sudden dry spell before regular rains fully set in. Planting too early causes seeds to germinate and then wither in dry, hot soil before steady water arrives.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ nɛɔ kwraa. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ dani nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ aba.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas alongside my main crop helps the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ masɛi lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and other legumes pull nitrogen directly from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant grows and breaks down, that nitrogen is released, acting as natural fertilizer for neighboring crops.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei dara ni amɛfite Nakai nitrogen lɛ jeɔ kpo. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that cannot handle direct heat and hot sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or banana trees planted nearby to act as living umbrellas and keep the soil moist while the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo banana tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear the weeds around the base of my young cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi kɛjɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ashishi daa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from young cocoa plants. Clearing a small circle around each tree reduces competition so the tree gets all the food it needs to grow faster.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei bibii amli. ŋwɛibɔfoi bibii amlijaa ni bɔleɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa akaŋshii baa shi. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ anine ashɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ nɔ koni eda oya.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green and grow well. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure will fix this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni esa akɛ ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli ni eda jogbaŋŋ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: What is making small holes in my maize leaves and leaving green dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli ni eshiɔ muji eŋɔli yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides in the center leaf whorl during the day and eats the new leaves, leaving behind droppings that look like coarse green dirt.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe teeɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni eyeɔ baa heei. Muji ni tamɔ muji eŋɔli ni mli edɔ pɛ ji nɔ ni eshwɛ.

english: How do I know if my stored cassava stem cuttings are still good for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei niji ni ato lɛ sa lolo kɛha dumɔ?

english: Healthy cassava stems feel firm and have moist green skin right under the outer bark when you scratch it lightly. If the stem snaps easily like dry wood or looks hollow inside, it has lost its water and will not sprout.
ga: Kasava tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa ni amɛyɛ hewolo ni mli efɔ, ni ji eŋɔli yɛ kponɔgbɛ shishi kɛji okɛ amɛ shwie shi fioo. Kɛji tso lɛ fãa oya tamɔ tso ni egbi loo etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ bu yɛ emli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ mli nu efo mli ni edaŋ.

english: Why must I make high soil mounds before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose earth to expand into large tubers. High mounds keep the soil loose, improve water drainage during heavy rains so the tubers do not rot, and make harvesting much easier.
ga: Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli. koni yitso lɛ akagbo Ni ehaa nikpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why are the leaf edges of my pepper plants curling upwards and looking wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids hiding under the leaves. Spraying with neem oil or insecticidal soap helps remove these insects so new leaves can grow flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi nɛɛ ni eha baai heei lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomatoes turning dark brown and soft before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishi feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot and happens when the plant lacks calcium or receives irregular watering. Keeping the soil constantly moist helps the plant carry calcium from the roots into the fruits.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot ni ebaa kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ calcium loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans together with maize help my soil stay rich?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have tiny nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth. This naturally feeds the soil and improves the growth of nearby crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: It is best to water early in the morning because the air is cooler and the water sinks deep into the root zone instead of evaporating instantly in the hot sun.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu lɛ leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni nu lɛ baabote shishifã lɛ mli shɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni eeetsɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Officer, why should I leave space between my maize plants instead of planting them very close together to get more yield?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo?

english: When maize is planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This makes them grow thin and tall with small cobs. Spacing them properly gives each plant enough resources to produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ha amɛfee mlɛo ni amɛkwɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground, preventing diseases and helping the plant catch maximum sunlight to make bigger yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo koni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed leaves during severe dry weather to reduce water loss and protect themselves from dying of thirst. Planting shade trees around your cocoa keeps the soil moist and protects the leaves from burning heat.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ. Koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni obu ohe kɛjɛ kumai he. Tsei ni aduɔ koni ekɛ hulutsoo aha yɛ Cocoa he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and using organic fertilizer helps the flowers stay attached and produce pepper.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Wild weeds are naturally adapted to surviving in local conditions and are very efficient at grabbing water and food quickly. Your farm crops need extra care and early weeding because they are less aggressive than wild plants.
ga: Kooloi amli jwɛi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shihilɛi amli. Ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni abua naa oya lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra. Ejaakɛ efeee basabasa tamɔ koo mli tsei

english: When soil gets flooded with water, it starves the cassava roots of air, allowing rot fungi to grow. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away quickly so the roots can breathe.
ga: Beni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ akashɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ shwereɔ. Yucca ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: Maize removes the same nutrients from the soil every season, leaving the soil empty and weak. Planting legumes like cowpea or groundnuts every other season puts natural food (nitrogen) back into the soil for your maize.
ga: Abele jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ. Aduɔ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii daa Be lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii (nitrogen) baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛhaa o-ŋmei.

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so the roots can drink it in safely. Applying dry fertilizer on dry soil can burn the plant roots and waste your money because the crop cannot absorb it.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anu lɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi tsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi ni efite shika ejaakɛ tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ.

english: If too many small shoots (suckers) grow around the main plantain tree, they steal water and food from the mother plant. Leaving only two or three shoots ensures the main tree gets enough strength to grow heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Niji enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ haa tso titri lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ tso ni tsii.

english: Why are small holes suddenly appearing on my young maize leaves with tiny dark dirt inside the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii jeɔ kpo trukaa yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni muji ni tsuɔ fioo ko yɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by young caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm hiding in the leaf funnel to eat the tender growing parts. Checking your fields early allows you to catch them before they destroy the growing point of the maize.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii bibii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai amli koni amɛye ŋmeii ni shwereɔ waa lɛ. Gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua bo ni omɔ amɛ dani amɛfite hei ni ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees if I mix too much water with the farm medicine before spraying?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cocoa tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ nu babaoo futu ŋmɔ mli tsofa lɛ mli dani mikɛshwie nɔ?

english: Adding too much water dilutes the medicine, making it weak and ineffective against pests. It can also cause excess liquid to pool on the leaves, which harms the crop and washes away the protection.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nu babaoo fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsofa lɛ mli agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa tsofa lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Ebaanyɛ eha nu ni fa fe nine abua ehe naa yɛ baai lɛ anɔ hu. Enɛ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui ni efoɔ hebuu lɛ he.

english: How does standing or excess water on my farm affect the health of my cocoa trees?
ga: Te nu ni ekã shi loo nu ni fa fe nine yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa mi cacao tsei lɛ ahewalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Too much water smothers tree roots and weakens the plant. Weakened cocoa trees become soft and vulnerable, making them easy targets for pests and fungal diseases.
ga: Nu babaoo haa tso shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Kakao tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ bafeɔ nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa efeɔ he ko ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ ashɛ he oya.

english: Is it possible to wash my cocoa trees if I accidentally apply the wrong medicine mixture?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ afɔ cacao he kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni ejaaa tsu nii yɛ oshara mli?

english: Yes, if you catch it quickly, rinsing the cocoa leaves and pods with clean water can help remove chemical spills or overly harsh mixtures before they burn the plant or attract unwanted pests.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji omɔ lɛ oya. Kookoo baai kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛ nu ni mli tse baafɔ he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ajie tsofai ni egbɛ eshwa loo nibii ni mli wa fe nine lɛ kɛjɛ mli dani amɛshã tso lɛ loo amɛgbala kooloi ni ataooo amɛ.

english: Can I transfer pests to my healthy cocoa trees just by touching them with my hands?
ga: Ani manyɛ majie tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛya mi cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ minine ni mikɛbaata amɛhe kɛkɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, touching infested plants or pests and then touching healthy cocoa can carry tiny insects, eggs, or plant fluids directly onto your healthy crops, spreading the infestation.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ mɔ ko ta tso loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko he, ni no sɛɛ lɛ eta kookoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ kooloi bibii, ŋmeii, loo tso mli nu aba. tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni gbɛɔ basabasafeemɔ lɛ eshwaa lɛ anɔ

english: Why do insects and pests seem to swarm cocoa trees that have been damaged or incorrectly sprayed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii kɛ kooloi bibii shwieɔ cacao tsei ni efite loo ni afɔ amɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Pests are drawn to stressed plants. When cocoa trees suffer chemical burns or damage, they release scents and produce weakened tissue that attracts insects seeking an easy feeding spot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai gbalaa tsei ni haoɔ amɛhe lɛ. Kɛji tsofai shã cacao tsei loo amɛfite lɛ Ejieɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ fãji ni egbɔjɔ baa koni ekɛgbala kooloi bibii ni miitao niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: How do insects spread from an infested section of my cocoa farm to the healthy trees?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛjɛɔ hei ni hela lɛ emɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli?

english: Insects move through flying, crawling, wind carrying them, or by hitchhiking on farm tools, clothing, and hands when workers move through the field without cleaning up.
ga: Kplukai nyiɛɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋwɛi, ŋwɛi ŋwɛi, ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ woɔ amɛ. aloo kɛtsɔ tsɔne ni akɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii, atadei, kɛ niji fãa gbɛ beni nitsulɔi tsɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛtsumɔko mli lɛ nɔ.

english: What steps should I take if my hands come into contact with pests while working on the farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji miniji kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kpe beni mitsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You should wash your hands thoroughly with clean water and soap before touching any healthy cocoa trees or pods to prevent transferring pests and diseases across your farm.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ nu ni mli tse kɛ samla afɔ oniji ahe jogbaŋŋ dani ota cacao tsei loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii kɛ helai agbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What is the Akate insect, and how does it attack my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni ji Acate Kooloi? Ni te efee tɛŋŋ etutua mi-cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Akate (cocoa mirids or capsids) are destructive sap-sucking insects in Ghana that feed on young cocoa shoots and pods, causing them to develop dark wounds, dry up, and die.
ga: Akate (kooko mirids loo capsids) ji kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛ Ghana. Amɛyeɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ kookoo ŋmeii. Enɛ haa amɛnáa pilamɔi ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: What kind of damage does the pest known as Atee do to a cocoa crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Atee lɛ fiteɔ kookoo tsei?

english: Atee is a bug that pierces cocoa pods and stems to feed, leaving open wounds on the crop that rot the pods and weaken the overall tree.
ga: Arti ji kooloo ko ni tsɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔji kɛ eshishifãi amli koni etao niyenii. Enɛ haa pilamɔi ni agbele naa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa crop is becoming infested by pests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai emɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ amli?

english: Look out for dark spots on pods, wilting young shoots, dieback of branch tips, or physical signs of insects crawling on the stems and leaves of your cocoa trees.
ga: Look for dark spots on the pods. Tsoi bibii ni egbo, tsei niji ni egboi, loo gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii miiho yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow strong and green. Heavy rains can also wash these nutrients away, leaving the plant hungry.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara ni amɛfee eŋɔli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ kɛya. hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei

english: Why does my cassava produce very bushy top leaves but only small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɔɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or grows in very rich soil, it spends all its energy growing leaves instead of roots. Adding potassium and phosphorus to the soil helps the roots swell into large tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmei yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ potassium kɛ phosphorus wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Pepper flowers usually drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as extremely hot weather, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. The plant sheds its flowers to conserve energy for survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ babaoo kpe. Tsei shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha wala.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant my maize seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Planting maize seeds too close together forces the plants to compete for sunlight, ground water, and soil nutrients. This competition results in weak, thin stalks and tiny corn cobs instead of healthy, large yields.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa anáa ŋmãa bibii kɛ ŋmãa bibii. Mohu ɔ, o náa ngma nɛ hi nɛ e he wa.

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is very beneficial. Cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, which naturally fertilizes the maize and improves your soil for future planting.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ afee ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli dumɔwui.

english: What causes the leaves of my tomato plants to curl up tightly and turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Tomato leaf curl is commonly spread by tiny insects called whiteflies that transmit a virus to the plant. It can also happen when the weather is very hot and dry, causing the plant to curl its leaves to save moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ tomato baa curl lɛ eshwaa, ni amɛhaa hela lɛ yaa tsei amli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ koni ekɛto ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Why are the leaves and pods on my young cocoa trees turning black during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, dark, and wet conditions. Clearing weeds and pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and air flow to dry out the field and prevent the fungus.
ga: Blɔfo diŋ hela jɛɔ ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, duŋ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛ amɛhe ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ baa.

english: Why are small worms eating into the stems of my young cabbage plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-cabbage tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ?

english: These worms are larvae hatched from eggs laid by small moths. They bore into the cabbage stem to feed on the wet inside tissue, which blocks water from moving up the plant and causes it to wilt and die.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni fɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli. Amɛfoɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ kaaba tsei amli koni amɛye mligbɛ fã ni efɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ nu naa koni ekaya tso lɛ nɔ ni ehaa egboɔ ni egboɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my yams after planting them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa sweet potatoes beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and completely dry up. This signal means the plant has stopped growing leaves and has stored all its energy inside the underground yam tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ tsɔ adebɔɔ mli su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi kwraa lɛ. Okadi nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa baai lɛ akwɛmɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ewo sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What causes my harvested maize to develop small holes and powdery dust while stored in bags?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii baa mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ mli? kɛ sũ be mli ni akɛtoɔ kotokui amli lɛ

english: Insects called grain weevils burrow into stored maize to eat and lay eggs if the grain was not dried properly before storage. Ensuring your maize is thoroughly dry and storing it in airtight bags keeps these pests out.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ seed moths lɛ baafo ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli koni amɛye ni amɛwo ŋmeii kɛji akɛ agbiko dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani akɛto. Kwɛmɔ ni o-corn lɛ agbi kwraa ni okɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli koni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ akabote mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient found in fertilizers or compost that helps plants grow green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni anaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa eŋɔli ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I clear away all the big trees from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot withstand strong, direct sunlight. They need shade from larger trees or nurse crops like plantain to shield them from heat and conserve moisture while they are developing.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni kwɛɔ nɔ, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni amɛha hulutsoo ahi shi be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: What causes the bottoms of my green tomatoes to turn black and rot before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egbo dani ekwɛ̃?

english: This issue is called blossom end rot, which happens when the tomato plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil, often caused by irregular watering.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why should I stick my cassava cuttings into the soil at an angle instead of straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mafee nɔ ni ja?

english: Planting cassava stems at a slanting angle encourages roots to grow evenly near the surface, producing bigger tubers that are also much easier to harvest.
ga: Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daa pɛpɛɛpɛ. ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa bulbs wuji baa, ni ekpamɔ waaa kwraa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and weak with small cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leaving no single plant with enough food to produce big cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei komɛi bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Extreme heat stresses the pepper plant, forcing it to drop its flowers to save energy and water rather than attempting to form fruits under severe conditions.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni okɛ nɔ ko aba yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa waa amli lɛ

english: Why does my garden egg crop produce plenty of flowers but very few actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii diɛŋtsɛ fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Garden eggs need insects like bees to carry pollen between flowers; if there are no insects around or if chemical sprays drive them away, flowers drop without growing into fruit.
ga: Abɔɔ mli ŋmeii he miihia kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii koni amɛwo pollen yɛ fɔfɔi ateŋ. Kɛji kooloi bɛ jɛmɛ Aloo kɛji tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ haaa kooloi lɛ aya he ko. Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow bent, small, and misshapen in heavy soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ebɔle, bibii ni efite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow by pushing outward under the ground. If the soil is hard or compacted, the tuber cannot expand easily and becomes twisted or stunted.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo ebɔle ehe lɛ Tse lɛ mli ŋmeii nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni amɛfee ŋmeii loo amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves turn yellow and drop off when heavy rain leaves standing water in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil prevents roots from breathing air. Without oxygen, the roots rot and can no longer drink water or take up food for the plant.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu kɔɔyɔɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛha tso lɛ nu loo niyenii dɔŋŋ.

english: Why does leaving weeds near my cowpea plants reduce my harvest even if I give them fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ amɛmli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal away the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your cowpeas, while also hiding harmful insect pests.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha o-cowpeas lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ teeɔ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plants are lacking nitrogen, which is like food for their growth. This usually happens when the soil nutrients are exhausted or when heavy rains wash the nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa kɛji niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsiɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why am I finding small worms eating the inside leaves of my corn stalks early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei amli baai lɛ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Those are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that targets young maize. They hide in the center leaf funnel to eat the soft tender growth, which can destroy the crop if not treated early with the right pesticide or neem solution.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni gbeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra. kɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tsofa

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies that move from plant to plant. The virus stops the plant from making food properly, which reduces the size and yield of the roots underneath.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Whiteflies bibii ni fãa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Virus tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ adalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is tired and needs fertilizer before planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii dani adu nii?

english: If crops from your last harvest grew slowly, produced small fruit, or if weeds like spear grass are taking over, your soil is tired. Stiff, hard, or light sandy soil that dries out very quickly is also a clear sign that nutrients are low.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okpa yɛ naagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ da blɛoo, ewo yibii bibii, loo kɛji jwɛi tamɔ akpɔlɔ jwɛi lɛ ye nɔ. Etsɛŋ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni wa, loo ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ fioo ni egbiɔ oya lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii faaa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce flowers that drop off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop without forming pods if the trees don't get enough water, if insect pests damage the flowers, or if the soil lacks key nutrients like potassium and boron needed for the flowers to turn into healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii kɛji tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kpata fɔfɔii ahiɛ Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ potassium kɛ boron ni he hiaa koni fɔfɔi lɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why should I plant my cassava mounds apart from each other instead of close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-cassava piles lɛ srɔtoi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mikɛbaabɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need enough space and sunlight under the ground to swell up big. Planting them too close together forces the crops to fight for soil nutrients and light, resulting in many small roots instead of large tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hulu la yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛdara. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ la mli lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shishifãi bibii babaoo yɛ yitsei wuji najiaŋ

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with very strong, deep root systems built to survive tough conditions. When rain falls, weed seeds resting in the soil absorb water and grow faster than cultivated crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni ama amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ gbalaa nu ni amɛdaraa oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves drop down and wilt in the afternoon heat even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, tomato plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. The leaves wilt temporarily to protect the plant from drying out, but they usually recover by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni tso lɛ akagbi. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do small insects turn my harvested maize grains into dust while stored in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tsɔɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli sũ be mli ni akɛtoɔ kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Those insects are grain weevils that lay eggs inside the corn kernels if the grain was not dried completely before bagging. The insects eat the inside of the grain, leaving behind hollow shells and powder.
ga: Kplukai lɛ ji dumɔwui amli ŋmeii ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii amli kɛji ŋmeii lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛwoɔ kotoku mli. Kplukai yeɔ ŋmãa mli nibii. Nɔ ni eshwɛ ji ŋshɔŋloo lɛ kɛ powda ni mli ewo muji lɛ pɛ.

english: Why is it good for my soil to plant groundnuts or beans together with my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii feɔ ekome lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and put it back into the soil. This naturally feeds the corn crop and keeps the soil fertile for longer periods.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I make my yams grow very big and heavy?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aha sweet potato lɛ adara ni etsii?

english: To grow large yams, you need to plant in soft, deeply loosened soil using large mounds or ridges. This gives the tubers plenty of space to expand easily while receiving the nutrients and water they need.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni odu sweet potatoes agboi Ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔji wuji loo ŋmeii agboi atsu nii ni okɛdu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli ejɔ waa nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ náa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã mlɛo yɛ be mli ni amɛnáa niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my yams stay small even after leaving them in the ground for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ ji bibioo lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Small yams usually result from hard or compacted soil that prevents the tuber from expanding, or from poor soil nutrients and heavy weed competition that steal food from the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni mli edɔ ni haaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. aloo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii kɛ jwɛi akaŋshii ni naa wa ni juɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli.

english: Is red soil good for growing crops like yams?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ tsuru hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Red soil can be good for crops because it generally drains water well and doesn't easily stay waterlogged, but it can become hard when dry and may need organic manure to help it hold nutrients better.
ga: Shikpɔŋ tsuru baanyɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nu shwieee nɔ oya. Shi shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee shiŋŋ kɛji egbi, ni ekolɛ ehe baahia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli koni eye ebua lɛ ni ehiɛ niyenii mli nibii amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does soil color matter when I am picking a place to farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ su he hiaa beni mihalaa ŋmɔ mli he ko lɛ?

english: Soil color tells you about its contents; dark soils usually have plenty of rotted leaves and manure (organic matter), while red soils often contain iron and drain water fast but may need extra feeding to grow heavy crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ su tsɔɔ bo nɔ ni yɔɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni egboi kɛ kooloi afɔfɔi yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Shikpɔji tsuru lɛ fɔɔ dade (nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli) babaoo yɛ mli, yɛ be mli ni shikpɔji tsuji lɛ fɔɔ dade babaoo ni nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Shi ekolɛ niyenii krokomɛi he baahia koni akɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii.

english: What should I do if the land I want to farm on has very hard red soil?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji shikpɔŋ ni misumɔɔ ni matsu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ tsuru ni wa waa?

english: Hard red soil needs to be broken up deeply with a hoe or plow, and mixed with animal manure or decayed plants to loosen it up so roots and tubers can breathe and grow.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei atsa shikpɔŋ tsuru ni wa lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. ni akɛ kooloi loo tsei amli ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ futuɔ mli koni ekɛjie lɛ koni shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ amu ni amɛdara.

english: How do I know if a piece of land is fertile enough for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii bɔ ni sa kɛha okwaayeli?

english: Fertile land usually has dark topsoil, soft ground that dig easily, good moisture retention without standing water, and healthy wild weeds or trees growing on it naturally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hei ni baa nii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ŋmɔmɔ waaa Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni nu damɔɔɔ shi. ni koo mli jwɛi loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ hu yɛ.

english: What is the best way to prepare raw land before I plant for the first season?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ asaa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ dani aduɔ nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ mli?

english: Clear the bush, remove large stones, break up the top layer of hard earth, and gather the rich topsoil into mounds or ridges to create a soft, nutrient-rich bed for seeds.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ jwɛi lɛ Ojie tɛi wuji kɛjɛ mli. Efiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. ni obua sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ anaa awo gɔji loo ŋmeii amli koni efee hei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli kɛha dumɔwui.

english: Why do crops grow well in one part of my farm but remain small in another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã ko mli shi amɛyaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibioo yɛ fã kroko lɛ?

english: Soil conditions vary across a farm; one part may have deeper, softer topsoil with better moisture, while another part might have hard clay, rocks, or washed-away topsoil.
ga: Esoro shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ yɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli. Ekolɛ fã kome yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni nu yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa, tɛi, loo sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni nu efo lɛ yɛ ekrokomɛi amli.

english: How can I improve poor land without buying expensive commercial chemical fertilizers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ aya hiɛ ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ jarayeli mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: You can naturally improve poor land by adding poultry manure or cow dung, leaving crop leaves to rot on the farm, or planting cover crops like beans that add nitrogen back into the dirt.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha hei ni ohiafoi yɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ kooloi loo tsina ŋmei ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Ni aaaha baai lɛ agbo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Aloo tso ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni kɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is making soil mounds better than planting directly on flat ground for tuber crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gɔŋ ni afeɔ lɛ hi fe ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Mounds collect all the good topsoil into one raised pile, giving tubers soft earth to grow downward easily while protecting the roots from suffocating in flooded water during heavy rains.
ga: Gɔŋ lɛ buaa ŋwɛi sũ kpakpai lɛ fɛɛ anaa yɛ ŋtayaa kome mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ daa kɛyaa shishigbɛ mlɛo. Kɛfata he lɛ, ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe koni amɛkafo yɛ nu ni eyi obɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and delicate root systems that cannot tolerate harsh direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around them creates living umbrellas that keep the soil cool and moist until the cocoa plants become strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which maize needs to build green foliage and grow strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the leaves turn green again and produce big corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli ni eda waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii agboi.

english: Why are small green caterpillars chewing holes inside the middle of my maize stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye bu yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which attack the central growing leaf (the funnel) of maize. Catching them early and applying approved biopesticides or a mixture of neem extract and fine sand directly into the funnel stops them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ (channel) lɛ. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua. ni okɛ tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo neem mli nu kɛ ŋã kpakpa ni akɛfutu mli lɛ awo tsɔne lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my cassava cuttings too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei niji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, they compete for sunlight, water, and nutrients. This forces them to grow tall, thin stems above ground while leaving very little energy to form large tubers under the soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛdara ni amɛdara ni amɛfee tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshwɛɔ koni amɛfee bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without growing into any fruits during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extremely high temperatures cause heat stress, which damages pollen and prevents tomato blossoms from being fertilized. When pollination fails, the plant drops its flowers to save water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ waa lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa. Enɛ fiteɔ pollen ni haaa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why should I pinch off the top growing tips of my pepper plants when they are young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-pepper tso lɛ naa be mli ni eji bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Pinching the main top tip stops the plant from growing straight up and encourages it to sprout multiple bushy side branches. More branches mean more flowers, which leads to a larger harvest of peppers.
ga: Kɛ́ atswa tso lɛ naagbee titri lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ daa tɛ̃ɛ ni ewoɔ lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ niji awo ŋmɔ mli ni niji babaoo yɔɔ mli. Niji babaoo tsɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmɔtɔ babaoo.

english: Dropping leaves is a natural survival trick cassava uses to prevent water from evaporating into the dry air. The plant rests during the dry spell while preserving the tubers safe beneath the soil until rains return.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaa ni akɛ yucca tsuɔ nii koni ekɛtsi nu naa koni ekatsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ yaa wɔɔhe yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Can I plant cowpeas alongside my maize, and how does it help my field?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa masɛi? Ni te eyeɔ ebuaa mihegbɛ lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is very beneficial. Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air into the soil to feed the maize, while their broad leaves cover the ground to stop weeds and conserve soil moisture.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛye ŋmãa. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛtsi jwɛi lɛ anaa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are some of my bean seeds failing to sprout out of the ground after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bean seeds fail to emerge if they are buried too deep in the soil, if the soil is packed too tightly for air to reach them, or if the soil stays overly soggy, causing the seeds to rot before sprouting.
ga: Beans lɛ ejeŋ kpo kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ he, loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lolo Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: How can I tell that my yam tubers under the ground are fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato tubers ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yam tubers are ready when the vines and leaves above ground naturally turn yellow and begin to dry up at the end of the rainy season. This signals that the plant has stored all its energy into the tubers below.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo beni wain tso lɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ eto ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, a key nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni tsei ni yɔɔ niyenii mli lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the daytime temperatures get too hot or when the plants do not get enough steady water. Stress causes the plant to drop its blooms to save energy for survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ nɔ. Haomɔ haa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he gbɛjianɔ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves twist up and get yellow spots on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Twisted leaves with yellow patches are caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny flies called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant stem varieties is the best way to keep your harvest healthy.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela kɛ baai ni etsilɛ, ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. Fɔlɔi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Stem henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.
