english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly droop and die even when the ground is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni egboɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a soil organism that blocks water from traveling up inside the stem. Rotating your crops with crops like maize helps clear the soil over time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, bacteria wilt ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Enɛɛmɛi ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tsiɔ nu naa koni ekaho kɛbote tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa tsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli tseɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up before they are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods turn black because of Black Pod Disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shaded conditions. Trimming excess tree branches to let in sunlight and fresh air helps prevent the disease.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ black pod hela lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aba lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baa mɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when heavy bunches grow on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be mli ni jwɛi ni mli edɔ miikwɛ̃ yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over because microscopic soil worms called nematodes eat the roots, leaving the tree with a weak grip in the dirt. Supporting the main trunk with bamboo poles prevents the heavy tree from collapsing.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ sũ mli ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ yeɔ shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ akpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tso fiɔ tso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei ni tsii akagbee nɔ.

english: Why do my orange trees drop many of their small fruits before they are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-citrus tso lɛ miiho aduawai bibii babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Citrus trees naturally drop weak fruit if they don't have enough water or nutrients to grow every single fruit to full size. Proper watering and feeding help the tree hold onto its harvest.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ baajie aduawai bibii kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha aduawai fɛɛ aduawai adara kɛyashɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ashwie tso lɛ nɔ nu jogbaŋŋ ni aha lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why is it important for me to put stakes up for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ matswa tso koni mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb up stakes so their leaves can spread out and catch direct sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which goes down into the ground to build big yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni egbeeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni efeɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my rice grains turn white and hollow instead of filling up with rice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ yɛ futafuta ni amɛhe ewo muji yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmãa eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: White, empty rice heads are typically caused by stem borer insects that eat the inside of the plant stem, cutting off the flow of nutrients to the grain heads while they are forming.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmãa yitsei yɛŋ ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa. Enɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ dumɔwu lɛ yitso lɛ nɔ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Planting maize on the same spot every year drains the soil of the specific food maize needs and allows maize pests to build up in the dirt. Switching to legumes like beans or groundnuts puts good nutrients back into the land.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ haa abɛi lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ baa shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa nɔ lɛ, ehaa niyenii kpakpai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do experienced farmers tell me to plant plantains on the same field with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ baakɛɛ mi akɛ midu plantains yɛ ŋmɔ ni mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast with wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, protecting young cocoa plants from heat and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: How do crops like groundnuts or cowpeas help improve the soil for my next crop season?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei baafee tɛŋŋ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha mikwɛ̃mɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay, that stored nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi fite Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my corn leaves turn pale yellow when there is continuous heavy rain for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes away nutrients like nitrogen from the topsoil and floods the roots, making it hard for the corn plant to absorb food and air.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa ŋmãa tso lɛ akɛ ebaaŋɔ niyenii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ.

english: What causes small holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the central funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ mi ŋmã tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋta lɛ mli

english: This is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing tip of the maize plant and eats the tender leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛgbeleɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with lots of leaves, but the tubers underground remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava put all its energy into growing stems and leaves instead of sending food down to build big underground tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ yeɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii kɛba shi koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my yam mounds regularly instead of leaving them to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Okɛ sweet potato ato he daa Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha ekwɛ̃

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients away from the yam roots, causing the underground yams to stay small and yield poorly.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ sweet potato shishifãi amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without forming any fruits when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fruit set. When pollination fails, the plant sheds the unfertilized flower.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baafite pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, anyɛɛɛ akpɛtɛ aduawai lɛ ahe. Kɛji pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Tso lɛ baafite fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the plant's sap and spreading plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why does my soil get hard like cement when dry, and how does that affect my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa tamɔ simenti kɛ́ egbi lɛ? Ni te enɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter like leaves or manure. Hard soil prevents plant roots from spreading easily and stops water from soaking down into the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni wa haaa tsei ashishifãi agbɛ ashwã mlɛo, ni ehaaa nu abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my crop dry up and fall off during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ bei amli lɛ?

english: When water is scarce, plants intentionally drop their oldest lower leaves to save water and energy for the young shoots and fruit at the top.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa lɛ Tsei lɛ baajɛ amɛtsuiŋ amɛshɛrɛ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ amɛshwie koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha ŋmeii bibii kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: How far apart should I plant my maize seeds in the soil?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛjɛ he ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to gather sunlight, soil nutrients, and water without competing with its neighbors. If seeds are planted too close together, the crops become thin and produce smaller ears.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbuaa hulu la naa. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ akutsoŋbii akaŋ Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bibii.

english: Why is it important for me to pay attention to how deep I place seeds in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ bɔ ni mikɛ midumɔwui lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ha lɛ nɔ?

english: If you plant seeds too deep, they run out of energy before reaching the sunlight and die underground. If you plant them too close to the top, birds eat them or the hot sun dries them out before they can sprout.
ga: Kɛji odu dumɔwui lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ Hewalɛ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ dani hulu la lɛ shɛɔ enɔ ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji odu lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ ŋwɛi tsɔ lɛ Okpoi baaye amɛ loo amɛbaahã amɛya hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ kɛyashi amɛbaagbi dani amɛbaakwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plant is starving for nitrogen or that the soil is holding too much standing water. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or draining excess water will help the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli loo ajie nu ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How close to the stem of my crop should I place fertilizer?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ he tɛŋŋ?

english: You should never put fertilizer right against the plant stem because it can burn the plant. Place it a few centimeters away in a small ring around the stem where the outer roots can reach it safely.
ga: Esaaa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ tso lɛ shishi tsɔ ejaakɛ enɛ baashã tso lɛ. Okɛwo ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ mli sɛntimitai fioo komɛi, he ni kponɔgbɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It keeps moisture in the ground during hot days, stops weeds from growing, and keeps the plant roots cool.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Why do some of my crops grow very tall but produce very little food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ waa shi amɛwoɔ niyenii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: When plants are overcrowded, they stretch upward quickly to search for sunlight. Because they spend all their energy growing stems to reach the light, they have little energy left over to produce grains or fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baagbala amɛhe oya koni amɛyatao hulu la. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛkɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ tso ni miida lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshwɛɔ amɛ koni amɛkɛwo dumɔwui loo yibii.

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and air can flow through. This prevents wetness that causes diseases like black pod and encourages the tree to grow more pods.
ga: Kpojiemɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Bɔni afee ni atsĩ ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ helai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ diji baa lɛ naa ni awo tsei hewalɛ koni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ babaoo.

english: When is the best time for me to remove weeds from my crop field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔji amli?

english: Weeds should be removed during the first few weeks after your crop sprouts. Clearing weeds early stops them from stealing light, water, and plant food while your crop is young and fragile.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli beni tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju la, nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tsei amli. Yɛ be mli ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji gbekɛbii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ

english: Why are small insects creating holes in the leaves of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miifee bu yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pests like caterpillars and beetles chew on leaves to feed themselves. Leaf damage prevents the plant from using sunlight to make food, which slows down growth and reduces your final harvest.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ koni amɛye amɛhe niyenii. Baai lɛ ni fiteɔ lɛ haaa tso lɛ kɛ hulu la atsu nii kɛhoo nii. Enɛ baaha shweremɔ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaaha onaagbee ŋmaa lɛ aba shi.

english: How can I tell if my young crops are suffering from too much heat from the sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ miina hulutsoo be babaoo?

english: When crops get overheated and lack water, their leaves wilt, curl inward, or turn crispy and brown at the tips during the afternoon to protect themselves from drying out.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ mli edɔ fe nine ni nu efo mli lɛ Tso lɛ baai lɛ baagbi. curl inward Aloo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛnaagbɛ yɛ shwane mli koni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Should I buy imported crop seeds or stick to the local seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ loo mikɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ akpɛtɛ he?

english: Imported seeds are often bred for high yields, but local seeds are already adapted to Ghana's specific soil, local pests, and weather. Using certified improved local seeds gives you reliable yields while resisting native diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afɔɔ dumɔwui ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ baa lɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ etsake amɛhe amɛwo Ghana maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔji, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli momo. Kɛ akɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui ni awo he odase ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha yibiiwoo ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ aba yɛ be mli ni ekɛ maŋ lɛ mli helai nyɛɔ eshiɔ.

english: Why do foreign crop varieties seem to get attacked by insects more easily on my farm than local crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ maŋsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ŋmeii yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa amɛ oya fe maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Local crop varieties have developed natural defenses against local insects over many years. Foreign varieties often lack this natural protection, making them easier targets for local pests unless they are given extra care.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ efee adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ahe yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, maŋsɛɛ kooloi lɛ bɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ baatutua amɛ. ja akwɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ

english: How can I be sure that the crops I plant this season will actually produce a good yield and not waste my money?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai diɛŋtsɛ ni mifiteee shika?

english: Yield assurance comes from using healthy certified seeds, testing your soil to supply the right nutrients, keeping weeds under control early, and ensuring your crops get adequate water throughout their growth stages.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ jɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsɔɔ akɛ amɛhe wa lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli. Kaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ kɛji niyenii ni sa yɔɔ mli. Jwɛi ahe nitsumɔ mra Ni okwɛ koni otsei lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛdalɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Is food crop production in Ghana reliable enough to guarantee a steady harvest every year?
ga: Ani niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmaakpamɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ aba daa afi?

english: Yes, crop production is reliable when good farming practices are used. While weather can change, using proper planting techniques, soil management, and crop protection ensures strong and steady production.
ga: Hɛɛ, anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ anɔ kɛ́ akɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi kpakpai tsu nii. Eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ baanyɛ atsake moŋ Shi kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui ahe ŋaai ni ja tsu nii, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahebuu lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ aba.

english: Why do crops planted in my soil grow differently from the same seeds planted in another region?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ daraa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni adu yɛ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ he lɛ?

english: Crops respond directly to local soil conditions, sunlight, and rainfall patterns. Differences in soil fertility, water drainage, and heat levels across regions naturally change how fast and strong a crop grows.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ hereɔ shikpɔŋ, hulu la kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ henɔi anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu ni hoɔ, kɛ dɔlɛ mli yɛ hei srɔtoi. Etsakeɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii yaa oya kɛ bɔ ni amɛhe wa ha lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Does every crop need the same basic conditions to grow well, regardless of where the seed comes from?
ga: Shishijee shihilɛ kome he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Nɛgbɛ dumɔwui lɛ jɛɔ kɛbaa?

english: All crops around the world need three core basics: good soil nutrients, proper moisture, and sunlight. However, the exact amount of water and shade required varies depending on the specific crop type.
ga: Nibii titrii etɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ je lɛŋ he fɛɛ he: Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kpakpai. hulutsoo be ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛ hulu la, shi kɛlɛ, nu kɛ hulutsoo be ni he hiaa lɛ baasoro lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ naa.

english: How does compost or animal manure help my crops grow better than relying only on rainfall and sunshine?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo nɔ ni mikɛ mihe baafɔ̃ nɔ lɛ?

english: Sunlight and rain provide energy and water, but soil manure acts like food for the plant. It enriches the soil with essential nutrients and helps the ground hold onto moisture during hot dry spells.
ga: Hulu kɛ nugbɔ haa hewalɛ kɛ nu. Shi sũ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛha tsei. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni edɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and stunt growth even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraa kwraa eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is starving for key nutrients like nitrogen, or that water is pooling around the roots and suffocating them. Heavy rain can wash nutrients out of the soil if it is not well drained.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ miiye tso lɛ loo nu ebɔle ehe. shishifãi kɛ ŋmɔlɔ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahe kɛji akɛ ajieee nu kɛjɛɛɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: The major rainy season provides consistent moisture and cooler soil temperatures, allowing plants to absorb nutrients constantly. The minor season has shorter rain spells and higher heat, which slows down plant development.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ haa nugbɔshiimɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ ni mli ejɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Be ni ji enyɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: What causes local farm produce to taste and feel different compared to imported crops brought from abroad?
ga: Mɛni haa maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli nibii lɛ ŋɔɔ ni amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛsoro amɛhe kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ ahe?

english: Differences in soil mineral content, fresh sunlight exposure, and harvest timing affect taste. Local produce matures naturally on the plant in our soil, whereas imported food is often picked early for long transport.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shika tsuru ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ mli ni hulu la hee shɛɔ nɔ Kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ saa nɔ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ he. Kuu lɛ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ wɔshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, ahalaa niyenii ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ mra. kɛha gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to protect their soft leaves from bright sunlight and heat. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains or leaving shade trees nearby creates a protective shield that keeps the seedlings cool and moist while they build strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ dɔlɛ he. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni ashiɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni ehaa shishifãi ni wa baa.

english: Why do I have to tie my yam vines to tall wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ sweet potato wain tsei fĩɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil, which also prevents diseases and rot caused by wet ground.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ helai kɛ fitemɔ ni hei ni efɔ lɛ hu kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when there is heavy rainfall for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water around the roots, it smothers them and allows fungi to grow, so planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, shishifãi lɛ gbalaa nu lɛ ni amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ daa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli.

english: Why should I cut away most of the young shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ ateŋ babaoo? Ajieɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients and water in the soil. Removing all but one or two strong suckers leaves enough food for the mother tree to yield a large, heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo yibii akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize crop turning yellow before the corn is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a maize plant are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure early in the season keeps the leaves green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmãa babaoo taoɔ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmãa ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli yɛ ŋmãa lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ baa lɛ afee eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ.

english: Beans and other legumes have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Maize feeds on this extra nitrogen, so growing them together naturally improves soil fertility without extra cost.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi yeɔ nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, adebɔɔ mli nanemɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ ni shika kroko fataaa he.

english: Why do small bugs attack my cowpea pods as soon as they start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea ŋmɔji lɛ kɛji amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Young cowpea pods are soft and sweet, which attracts sap-sucking insects and pod borers looking for food. Planting early in the season or spraying with natural neem leaf extracts can protect the pods during their early development.
ga: Cowpea ŋmeii bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛmli ŋɔɔ. Enɛ gbalaa kooloi ni nuɔ nu kɛ pod borers ni miitao niyenii lɛ. Kɛ́ adu mra yɛ be lɛ mli loo akɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu ŋmeii lɛ ahe yɛ shishijee be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the plants suffer from extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering or mulch helps the flowers stay attached and form healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Curled leaves are typically caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites that suck the sap from under the leaves and spread plant viruses. Washing the leaves with soapy water or applying bio-pesticides helps eliminate these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ shishi lɛ mli ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baa tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli ewo saamɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer to my farm when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Crop roots cannot absorb dry fertilizer, and concentrated fertilizer on dry soil can actually burn and damage the roots. Fertilizer should always be applied when the soil is damp after rain so the plant can safely absorb the nutrients.
ga: Tso shishifãi nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite shishifãi lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ koni tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out the topsoil. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain or cassava alongside them creates natural shade and keeps the ground moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ lɛ mli gĩɔ. Nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ he kome. Ebaaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo aba ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tips downward in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛnaa kɛmiiba shi yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the leaf tip and moves down the central vein usually means your soil lacks nitrogen. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure around the plants will restore their green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baa lɛ naagbee ni etsɔɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni bɔle Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee amɛhe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special bacteria in their roots that fix nitrogen from the air into the soil naturally. Rotating them with maize restores soil nutrients without high costs and reduces crop diseases.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhaa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmãa tsu nii lɛ, ehaa sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ baa shi ni shika babaoo he ehiaaa, ni ehaa tsei ahe helai baa shi.

english: What causes ragged holes in my young maize leaves and soft brown dirt inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ kɛ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that hides deep inside the plant's central funnel to feed. Checking your farm early and applying recommended pesticides or neem extract directly into the funnel early in the morning helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ koni eye niyenii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo ŋmeii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the weather gets extremely hot, when water supply is irregular, or when small pests like thrips feed on the flowers. Maintaining consistent watering and providing light shade during intense heat helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Be mli ni nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi mli lɛ jeee nɔ ni sa Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips yeɔ fɔfɔi. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings collapse and rot right at the soil level in the nursery bed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is a disease called 'damping-off,' caused by soil fungi that thrive in overly wet conditions with poor airflow. You can prevent it by not overwatering the seedbed, raising the seedbed for good drainage, and giving the seedlings enough sunlight.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘Damp’ lɛ ji nɔ ni ŋmei ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ eyaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ nu ni okɛhaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fe nine lɛ nɔ. Wo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni nu atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni ekɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa aha dumɔwui lɛ

english: Why should I cover my yam mounds with dried grass or leaves right after planting the yam setts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha mi sweet potato pile lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu lɛ?

english: Yam setts in bare soil mounds can easily dry out or rot due to extreme soil temperatures. Placing grass or leaf mulch over the mound shields the soil from direct heat and traps moisture so the yam sett can sprout safely.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni kpɛtɛɔ gɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ he Ebaanyɛ egbi loo egbo oya ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaabu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why should I cut off small green shoots growing directly from the main trunk of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ cacao tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: These shoots, known as water shoots or chupons, consume heavy amounts of water and food that the tree needs to make cocoa pods. Removing them allows the tree to direct all its energy toward producing heavy flowers and large pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akɛ Nam ŋmeii loo Chupon. Eyeɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo, ni tsei he hiaa koni amɛkɛfee kookoo ŋmeii. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni tsii kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl upward and roll together during the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ekome yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon heat is a pepper plant's natural way of reducing water loss by exposing less leaf surface to the sun. If the leaves open back up in the evening, the plant is managing, but constant curling indicates it needs extra watering or soil mulching.
ga: Baai lɛ ni aaakpã mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji pepper tso lɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa nu ni elaajeɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ baa lɛ nɔ ni ekɛwoɔ hulu la fioo ko nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji baai lɛ gbele gbɛkɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ. Shi ŋmɔlɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni awo nu loo ŋmɔlɔ kroko afata he.

english: Cassava plants signal maturity when their lower leaves turn yellow and drop, leaving a bare stem with leaves only at the top. You can test-harvest one plant to confirm the root size before harvesting the rest of the farm.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiida kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ yitso ni bɛ nɔ ko ni baai yɔɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ eshwɛ. Obaanyɛ oka tso kome ni okpa lɛ okwɛ koni ona shishifãi lɛ adalɛ dani okpa ŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight. Without taller trees or plantains to provide shade, the hot sun burns their leaves and dries out the soil before their roots are strong enough to survive.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he waa. Kɛji tsei kakadaji loo tsei bibii ni baaha hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ lɛ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi.

english: Why does my plantain stem die after it produces just one cluster of plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gboi beni afee kuu kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain stem is designed by nature to fruit only once. Once it gives a harvest, it naturally dies off and passes its food and energy to the young shoots growing around its roots for the next harvest.
ga: Adebɔɔ ji nɔ ni fee plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ. Kɛ efɔ lɛ Ebaagbo yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ baaha ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ. shishifãi kɛha kpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why do my yam vines produce smaller tubers if I do not give them wooden poles to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji mihaaa amɛkwɔ tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need plenty of sunlight to make food for growing big tubers under the ground. Staking holds the vines up so all the leaves catch maximum sunlight and stay clean from damp soil.
ga: Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia sweet potato baai koni ekɛ niyenii aha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ wain tso lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ fɛɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. ni oha ehe atse kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ

english: How do groundnuts manage to form their pods deep inside the soil after flowering above ground?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii feɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ?

english: After the groundnut flower opens and gets pollinated on top of the stem, the plant grows a long stalk called a peg. This peg grows downwards, pushes into the dirt, and expands into a pod underground.
ga: Beni ŋmeii fɔfɔi lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni amɛwo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ, Tsei hu yɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs. Nɛkɛ pin nɛɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shi, ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei ko mli.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which helps leaves stay healthy and green. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient out of the soil, or the soil may simply be tired.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, usually caused by extremely high afternoon temperatures, prolonged dry spells without water, or lack of proper nutrients in the soil.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ he. Bei pii lɛ, shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni nu bɛ mli loo niyenii ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why should I put fertilizer on my farm only when the ground is moist after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli pɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ?

english: Crop roots cannot absorb dry fertilizer directly. Moisture dissolves the fertilizer into a liquid so roots can easily drink it in; applying it to dry soil can scorch and burn the roots.
ga: Tso shishifãi nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Fɛ̃i haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ nu bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu lɛ mlɛo. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni esha amɛ.

english: Why do the roots of my cassava tubers rot in the ground during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When heavy rain leaves the ground completely waterlogged for days, the roots choke from lack of air and rot under the mud.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu yiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ muji lɛ shishi.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that hide under the leaves to suck out the plant's juices, or by viruses spread by these insects while they feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛ nu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I see small holes and fine sawdust on the stems of my growing maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This damage comes from stem borer caterpillars. Tiny moths lay eggs on the maize leaves, and when the caterpillars hatch, they bore into the stem to feed on the soft tissue inside.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ jɛɔ tsei ni shwieɔ shi lɛ amli. ŋmei bibioo Ewoɔ ŋmei baa nɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ Efoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni eye ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: How can I protect my mouth and body when spraying chemical medicine on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu midaaŋ kɛ migbɔmɔtso he kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai miifɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Agrochemicals can be very toxic if ingested or absorbed through the skin. Always wear protective clothing like face masks, long sleeves, and gloves, avoid eating or smoking while spraying, and wash your hands and face thoroughly immediately after application.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei waa kɛji akɛ mɔ ko ye loo etsɔ hewolo nɔ etsɔ mli. Wo atadei ni buɔ mɔ he tamɔ hiɛ nɔhamɔ, nine kakadaŋŋ agboi, kɛ glɔvs be fɛɛ be. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ niyeli loo tawa shɛremɔ he beni okɛ tsofa lɛ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ. Ni okɛ oniji kɛ ohiɛ afɔ ohe jogbaŋŋ kɛji okɛtsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Is it safe to harvest and eat my crops right after applying farm medicine?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni maye kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofa tsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, every farm chemical has a required waiting period (pre-harvest interval) after application. Eating crops too soon allows toxic chemicals to enter your mouth and body, which can cause severe illness.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔ mli tsofai fɛɛ biɔ be ni akɛmɛɔ. (dani akpa) yɛ nitsumɔ sɛɛ Nibii ni aduɔ oya ni ayeɔ lɛ haa tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei boteɔ odaaŋ kɛ ogbɔmɔtso mli. Enɛ baanyɛ ekɛ helai ni naa wa aba.

english: What happens if I use more farm medicine on my crops than the instructions say?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai babaoo tsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ fe bɔ ni gbɛtsɔɔmɔi lɛ kɛɛ lɛ?

english: Using more medicine than required will not cure the crop faster; instead, it can burn the leaves, damage the plant's health, pollute the soil, and waste your money. Always follow exact dosage guidelines.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nɔ ni fe bɔ ni he hiaa tsu nii lɛ, enyɛŋ eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsa oya. Shi ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ ashã. efiteɔ tsei ahewalɛ Mujiwoo ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ oshika ni efiteɔ Nyiɛmɔ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi pɔtɛɛ ni kɔɔ bɔ ni esa akɛ akɛ tsofa lɛ aha lɛ he lɛ sɛɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why is it not working when I only spray farm medicine on top of my crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etsuuu nii kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofa lɛ shwie mitsei lɛ ahe baai pɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Many crop pests and fungal diseases hide on the undersides of leaves and around lower stems. Spraying underneath the leaves targets these hidden pests directly, making the treatment effective.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ashishi kɛ shishigbɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ nɛkɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ha tsofafeemɔ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my crops stay sick even after I spray medicine all over the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hela mɔ amɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa shwie ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ moŋ?

english: Simply smearing or spraying medicine broadly across leaves is often ineffective if you don't target the actual site of infection. You must inspect where the disease lives—such as underneath leaves or near damaged stems—and apply the treatment directly there.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofa ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ loo ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii kɛji akɛ okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ emaaa he diɛŋtsɛ ni hela lɛ yɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ okwɛ he ni hela lɛ hiɔ, tamɔ yɛ baai ashishi loo he ni bɛŋkɛ tsei ni efite lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ tsofafeemɔ gbɛ̀i ni yɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ atsu nii

english: How should I treat disease sores or rot on the main trunk of my crop trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsa hela loo fitemɔ ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: For stem or trunk rot, you should first clean or trim off the infected outer bark, then carefully apply the recommended treatment directly onto and under the affected region so the medicine reaches the active infection.
ga: Kɛha tsei loo tsei ni egboi lɛ Esa akɛ otsumɔ loo ofɔlɔ kponɔgbɛ fã ni hela emɔ lɛ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ awo he ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ eshishi jogbaŋŋ. koni tsofa lɛ ashɛ hela lɛ he

english: Can I just pour leaf medicine on the ground to cure a disease on my plant's stem?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafɔse tsofa-feemɔ baai awo shikpɔŋ koni mikɛtsa helai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: No, surface and stem diseases require direct contact. Pouring medicine on the soil won't reach the diseased parts on the upper stem or leaves properly, so you must apply the medicine directly to the affected plant parts.
ga: Dabi, ŋwɛi kɛ shishi helai biɔ ni mɔ ko ashɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ eshɛɛɛ tso lɛ shishi loo baai lɛ ahe hei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ awo tso lɛ fãi ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend trimming diseased branches before applying medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afo tsei niji ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ dani akɛ tsofa atsu nii lɛ?

english: Trimming infected branches removes the main source of the disease and allows sunlight and air to reach the plant. Applying medicine after trimming ensures the chemical protects the healthy parts without wasting spray on dead tissue.
ga: Niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni aaafolɔ lɛ jieɔ hela lɛ jɛɛhe titri lɛ kɛyaa. ni ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe Tsofa lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa tsofa lɛ buɔ hei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe ni efiteee tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ fãji ni egboi lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Does cutting off extra leaves and small branches from my crops help them grow better?
ga: Mifoɔ baai kɛ tsei niji bibii kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli. Ani eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, carefully trimming excess or diseased foliage improves air movement and sun exposure, reducing humidity where mold and pests thrive while helping the plant direct its strength toward fruiting.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ofolɔ baai ni fa fe nine loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ hulutsoo be lɛ shi yɛ hei ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui shwereɔ yɛ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I split a heavily diseased farm section into smaller parts before treating it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ aja miŋmɔ ni helai emɔ mi waa lɛ mli awo fãi bibii amli lɛ? Dani abaatsa lɛ?

english: Dividing a sick portion of your farm allows you to manage the workload systematically—trimming infected branches in one section at a time and ensuring medicine is applied thoroughly under the leaves without missing spots.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ mlijaa ni hela mɔɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ onitsumɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo naa. Kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ amɛ fã kome mli lɛ nɔ. ni ona nɔmimaa akɛ abaawo tsofa lɛ yɛ baa lɛ shishi pɛpɛɛpɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ ni elaaje.

english: How do I know the best time of the year to start planting my crops in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: Ghana generally has two main rainy seasons—the major season (starting around April or May) and the minor season (starting around September or November depending on your region). Planting right at the start of these rain seasons ensures your seeds get enough moisture to sprout and establish strong roots.
ga: Ghana yɛ nugbɔ bei titrii enyɔ: shishijee be (jeɔ shishi yɛ Abɛibe loo May) kɛ nɔ ni ji enyɔ be (jeɔ shishi yɛ September loo Alemle. (Enɛ damɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ.) Dumɔ mra yɛ nugbɔ be lɛ mli lɛ baaha odumɔwui lɛ ana nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my maize crops yield less produce when I plant them during the minor season compared to the major season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto shishijee be lɛ he lɛ?

english: The minor season typically receives shorter and less predictable rainfall than the major season. Because crops get less total water during their critical growth and flowering stages, they produce smaller ears with fewer grains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa kuku ni anyɛɛɛ atsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ fe shishijee be lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ naaa nu fɛɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ kɛ fɔfɔii ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ woɔ toi bibii kɛ dumɔwui fioo.

english: What farm work should I be doing during the dry season from December to February when there is no rain?
ga: Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli kɛjɛ December kɛyashi February, ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, mɛɛ nitsumɔ esa akɛ matsu?

english: The dry season is the best time for clearing land, stumping, preparing farm tools, and buying quality seeds. Doing this early ensures your field is completely ready before the first major rains arrive.
ga: Hɔmɔ be lɛ ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛkpaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, asaa tsei akutsei, ni asaa okwaayeli dɛŋdadei. ni ohé dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ Nifeemɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baaha oyale lɛ afee klalo dani klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ wulu lɛ aba.

english: Why should I clear my land early before the rains start instead of waiting for the rain to fall first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mra lɛ? Dani nugbɔ baanɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Clearing land early allows cut weeds and grass to dry up properly before planting. If you wait until the heavy rains fall, the ground becomes muddy and difficult to clear, which causes delay in planting your seeds on time.
ga: He lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni afo lɛ agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ dani aduɔ. Kɛji omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛ waa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bafeɔ muji ni ewaa akɛ abaajie. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui adumɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ be naa.

english: Is it better to burn the cleared bushes on my field or leave them to rot in the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi ni ajie yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ loo maha egbo yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: Leaving cleared vegetation to decay naturally on the field acts as a protective cover (mulch) that keeps the soil cool, retains water, and converts into natural plant food, whereas burning destroys helpful soil nutrients.
ga: Tsei ni ajie lɛ ni ashiɔ koni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he. Eji mulch (mulch) ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehiɛɔ nu mli, ni ehaa efeɔ tsei adebɔɔ mli niyenii. yɛ be mli ni shãa fiteɔ niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when there is too much rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive rain fills all the small spaces in the soil with water, pushing out the air roots need to breathe. Without air, the roots cannot suck up plant food like nitrogen, causing the leaves to lose their green color.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa hei bibii shwieɔ shi. Nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amu kɛje kpo. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ tso mli niyenii tamɔ nitrogen, ni no haa baai lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do cassava plants survive dry weather while other crops wither and dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei hiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi gboɔ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep taproots that reach water stored deep underground. It can also drop its leaves during dry spells to conserve water, then sprout fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shɛɔ nu ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ he. Abaanyɛ ashɛrɛ baai hu ashwie yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni akɛbu nu he. Kɛkɛ lɛ, baai heei jeɔ kpo kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do my seeds need moisture in the ground before they can start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu he hiaa mi dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Seeds stay dormant or 'asleep' until water softens their hard outer coat. Moisture triggers the seed to awaken and use its internal energy to push out its first root and shoot.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi loo ‘wɔɔ’ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nu haa kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli waa. Fɛ̃i lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ teɔ shi ni amɛkɛ amɛmli hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsiɔ klɛŋklɛŋ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin with small leaves when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ baai bibii beni midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients. They stretch upward rapidly to beat their neighbors to the light, making them weak and prone to falling over in wind.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe oya koni amɛtswa amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ amɛshwie la lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya.

english: Why does planting beans or groundnuts in my field help my next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food in the soil through their roots. This enriches the land with natural fertilizer for crops planted in that same spot later.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ sɛɛ mli.

english: When is the best time for me to start preparing my farmland before the major rainy season begins?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ masaa mishikpɔŋ ni miduɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ aje shishi?

english: You should start land preparation towards the end of the dry season, around January or February. Clearing land early ensures you are ready to plant immediately once the first steady rains begin, giving your crops a head start.
ga: Esa akɛ oje shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ shishi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ naagbee. Aaafee January loo February Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha ofee klalo akɛ obaadu nii kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ je shishi pɛ. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ

english: What can I do to keep moisture in my soil when the dry season is just starting?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eje shishi pɛŋ lɛ?

english: You can cover the soil around your crops with dried grass or plant leaves, a practice called mulching. This acts as a blanket that protects the ground from direct sunlight and slows down water evaporation.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ahe baai Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo.

english: Why is it important for me to change the type of crops I plant on my land every season instead of planting the same crop repeatedly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ daa afi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ lɛ

english: Planting different crops each season prevents pests and diseases from building up in the soil and keeps the ground from losing all its nutrients, leading to healthier crops and better yields.
ga: Nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ baatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa. ni etsĩ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do some new crop varieties perform better than the traditional seeds I usually plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei No hewɔ lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi komɛi tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni miduɔ daa lɛ.

english: Improved crop varieties are specially developed to resist local pests and diseases, endure short dry spells better, and grow faster so you can harvest more food.
ga: Afee tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kukuoo mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa. ni okwɛ oya bɔni afee ni onyɛ okpa niyenii babaoo.

english: Is it better to plant all my cassava at once or plant small portions at different times?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmei lɛ fɛɛ shikome loo yɛ fãi bibii amli? Yɛ bei srɔtoi amli?

english: Planting in small batches at different times allows you to harvest fresh cassava continuously over a long period, rather than having all your crops mature at the same time and potentially spoil.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ kui bibii amli yɛ bei srɔtoi amli Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmei hee be fɛɛ be be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha onibii fɛɛ akwɛ̃ shikome lɛ. ekome ni ebaanyɛ egbo.

english: How does a crop like cassava stay alive in the soil during long periods without rain?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tso ko tamɔ ŋmei ahi shikpɔŋ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Cassava stores water and energy in its underground roots and drops its top leaves during dry periods to conserve moisture, allowing it to survive underground until the rains return.
ga: Cassava kɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ toɔ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli ni ekɛ ebaai lɛ shwieɔ ŋwɛi yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ koni ekɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Ha ehi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my maize plants produce smaller cobs when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food to produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli niyenii, gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I know if my soil lacks plant food when I look at my crop leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsei ahe nibii bɛ mli kɛ́ mikwɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ?

english: If lower leaves turn pale yellow while the plant is young, the soil is usually lacking nitrogen. Adding compost, animal manure, or the right fertilizer restores green leaves and healthy growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do insect pests suddenly appear in large numbers right after the dry season ends?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ jeɔ kpo babaoo yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba naagbee amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The warm weather and first rains cause dormant pest eggs in the soil and bushes to hatch, while fresh young leaves springing up provide abundant food for the insects to multiply quickly.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni ehiɛ edɔ baa. Yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ jwɛi ni afɔ lɛ amli Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, baai heei ni ji bibii ni jeɔ kpo lɛ haa niyenii babaoo ni ŋmeii lɛ náa koni amɛshwere oya.

english: Why do my harvested crops rot faster if I harvest them during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mikpa yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harvesting during intense heat causes tubers and fruits to lose water quickly and trap internal heat, which speeds up decay. Harvesting early in the cool morning keeps your produce fresh for longer.
ga: Nikpamɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ aduawai lɛ amli nu fiteɔ oya ni amɛhiɛɔ hulutsoo mli yɛ mli. ni haa fitemɔ yaa oya Nikpamɔ yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa onibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods as a natural survival mechanism to conserve water. Once the rains start again, the plant will quickly grow new green leaves and continue swelling its roots underneath.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he. Kɛ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei eŋɔli oya ni ebaaya nɔ eha eshishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ shishi.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly under the hot afternoon sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during intense heat to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to direct sunlight. This helps the plant retain water and prevent drying out during hot afternoons.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli koni ebaa baa lɛ nɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli, ni ehaaa amɛgbi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my papaya trees produce plenty of flowers but never grow any pawpaw fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi papaya tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi miduuu papaya tso kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Papaya trees have different sexes: male, female, and hermaphrodite. Male trees produce pollen flowers but cannot produce fruit themselves; you need female or hermaphrodite trees in your farm to harvest pawpaw.
ga: Papaya tsei lɛ ahe yɛ srɔtoi: nuu, yoo kɛ hermaphrodite. Tsei ni ji hii lɛ woɔ pollen shi amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii. Esa akɛ oná tsei ni ji yei loo tsei ni hiɛ hii loo yei yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni onyɛ okpa Pawpaw.

english: Why do the tiny flowers on my cocoa trees drop off before growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers require tiny insects like midges to move pollen from flower to flower. If dry weather, heavy rain, or lack of shade keeps these insects away, unfertilized cocoa flowers will simply drop off.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi he miihia kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, koni amɛjie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, nugbɔ nɛɔ waa, loo hɔɔŋ bɛ jɛmɛ. Ha nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ laaje Koo fɔfɔi ni afɔɔɔ amɛ fɔ lɛ baagbee shi.

english: How do groundnut pods end up growing under the dirt when the flowers bloom above the soil?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni fɔfɔii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: After a groundnut flower is pollinated above ground, it sends out a stem called a 'peg' that grows downwards and pushes into the soil, where the actual nut pod develops away from direct sunlight.
ga: Beni ashɛɔ ŋmeii fɔfɔi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Etsuɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ ni daa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Bean pods lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwereɔ yɛ he ko ni hulu la kpɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do bees and tiny flies keep visiting the blossoms on my garden egg plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ saramɔ lɛ?

english: Garden egg flowers need insects to shake and carry pollen from flower to flower to fertilize them. Without these insect visits, the blossoms cannot develop into proper garden egg fruits.
ga: Eggplant ni yɔɔ abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia kooloi ni baakpokpo amɛ ni amɛkɛ pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ koni ekɛwo amɛmli. Kɛji kooloi nɛɛ bɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi nyɛŋ atsɔ aduawai yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops turning reddish-purple instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ magenta yɛ eŋɔli najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks enough phosphorus nutrient, or cold/wet soil is preventing the roots from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo, shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ/ni mli edɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does a seed yam stored in my dark barn know when it is time to sprout without any soil?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni sweet potato dumɔwui ni ato yɛ mi ŋmɔ ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ mli lɛ leɔ be ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ni sũ bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seed yams have a natural internal biological clock, called dormancy. When changes in humidity and air temperature signal the natural planting season, the yam breaks dormancy and shoots out sprouts even without light or water.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui yɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni wala yɔɔ mli. Atsɛɔ lɛ wɔɔhe. Kɛji akɛ tsakemɔi ni ba yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli latsaa mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli shweremɔ be lɛ eba lɛ, Sweet potatoes baawɔ ni ebaakwɛ̃ kɛji kane loo nu bɛ po.

english: Why do many young suckers grow around my main plantain stem, and should I clear them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii babaoo miida yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain tso titri lɛ Ni ani esa akɛ mafɔ amɛhe?

english: Plantains multiply naturally by growing suckers from their underground stem. Leaving too many suckers causes competition for food and water, leading to smaller bunches, so you should prune away all but one or two strong suckers.
ga: Agbɛɔ dumɔwui ashwaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo ni agbele mli lɛ, ebaaha akaŋshii aba kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Efeɔ ŋmeii bibii No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ofo ŋmeii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ ni mli wa.

english: Why are my pepper fruits very hot during dry weather but milder when it rains a lot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ mli edɔ waa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ? Shi ani edɔɔ waa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa?

english: Peppers produce a chemical called capsaicin for self-defense, which makes them spicy. Heat and drought stress cause the plant to produce higher concentrations of capsaicin, making the peppers much hotter than during rainy periods.
ga: Chili ŋmɔtɔ feɔ tsofa ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ capsaicin koni ekɛbu ehe. ni haa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ haa tsei jieɔ capsaicin ni fa babaoo. Ehaa chili lɛ mli dɔɔ waa fe nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient, or that the soil is too full of water, which stops the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo sũ lɛ mli nu babaoo Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil needs extra nutrients before I plant my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia niyenii krokomɛi dani madu?

english: If your previous harvest was very small, your crops grew slowly, or weeds on the plot look pale and weak, your soil is likely tired and needs organic manure or compost.
ga: Kɛji okpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ ji bibioo kwraa Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa fiofio Aloo jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ. Etamɔ nɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ hu efite ni ehe baahia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli.

english: Planting the same crop every time drains the exact same nutrients from the soil continuously and allows specific pests and crop diseases to multiply in that plot.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai komɛi babaoo yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by a sickness spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into powder after sitting in my barn for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ tsɔɔ powda beni eta ŋmãa ŋmãa mli nyɔji fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Maize turns to powder because small insects called weevils burrow inside the dry seeds to eat and lay eggs. Storing grains in airtight bags or using safe grain dust stops them.
ga: Abele tsɔɔ sũ ejaakɛ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ shwieɔ ŋmaa ni egbi mli koni amɛye ni amɛwo amɛwui. Kɛ akɛ ŋmaa to vacuum kotokui amli loo akɛ ŋmaa sũ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tsu nii lɛ, ebaakpa enɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up prematurely before the yams underground grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ miiho oya lɛ? Dani shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ baadara?

english: Early drying of yam vines is often caused by a leaf disease called anthracnose or severe lack of soil moisture, which kills the leaves before they can finish feeding the tuber.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose loo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbiɔ oya. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gboiɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ gbeɔ niyenii lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the soil when heavy rains fall for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo lɛ sɛɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to survive. When water collects and cannot drain away fast enough, it suffocates the roots and causes rot-causing germs to grow.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nu bua ehe naa ni ajieee oya bɔ ni sa Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha helai ni fiteɔ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up like narrow straws during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ jwɛi bibii amli lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Rolling leaves is a plant's natural way of protecting itself from heat. By rolling up, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun to save its water.
ga: Baai ni atsiɔ lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. kɛtsɔ shwiemɔ nɔ Tsei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni ekɛbu nu he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field with no trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ko bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under harsh sunlight. They need temporary shade from crops like plantains or shade trees to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the daytime temperatures get too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when there are no insects around to shake and pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii bɛ ni baakpokpo ni amɛha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why does my cassava plant sprout fresh green leaves after the dry season destroys all the old ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ yɛ be mli ni hɔmɔ ko kpata baai momoi lɛ fɛɛ ahiɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cassava stores food energy underground in its roots. Even when hot, dry weather causes the top leaves to wither, the roots remain alive underground and send up fresh shoots as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava kɛ niyenii hewalɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ eshishifãi amli. Shi kɛlɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ aha baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. Shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛtsuɔ ŋmeii heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ.

english: Why should I cut back my old cocoa trees instead of pulling them out of the soil completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tsei momoi moŋ fe ni majie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Cutting back old cocoa trees close to the ground encourages the healthy root system to sprout vigorous new shoots, allowing the tree to rejuvenate and produce fresh pods much faster than planting a new seedling.
ga: Kookoo tsei momo ni afoɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ feɔ ehee ni ewoɔ ŋmeii heei oya fe dumɔwui heei ni aduɔ.

english: Why do plantain suckers keep growing back even after insects destroy the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi bibii efite tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ moŋ?

english: Plantains grow from an underground stem structure called a corm. As long as the corm remains healthy beneath the soil, it will continue to send up new suckers to replace damaged stems.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni atsɛɔ amɛ rhizomes lɛ amli. Shii abɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ baahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ Ebaaya nɔ ekɛ ŋmeii heei amaje koni ekɛye ŋmeii ni efite lɛ najiaŋ.

english: What causes my tree crops to sprout fresh shoots right from the base of the trunk when the top branches get damaged?
ga: Mɛni haa mitso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii heei kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛji ŋwɛi niji lɛ efite?

english: When a tree experiences stress or damage to its upper branches, it triggers dormant buds at the base of the trunk to wake up and sprout new growth as a natural survival reaction to rebuild its leaves.
ga: Kɛ tso ko na nɔnyɛɛ loo efite eniji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ Ekanyaa ŋmeii ni ehiɛ edɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ koni amɛte shi ni amɛdara ekoŋŋ akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala yibiiwoo nifeemɔ koni ekɛfee baai heei.

english: How does a crop virus spread from one sick plant to all the other healthy crops on my farm?
ga: Tse mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Plant viruses are usually carried from plant to plant by sap-sucking insects like aphids, whiteflies, or mealybugs, as well as through infected farm tools or contaminated sap during pruning.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, whiteflies, loo mealybugs lɛ tsɔɔ tsei amli helai kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ loo nu ni mli ewo muji yɛ be mli ni afoɔ tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Can a crop recover on its own once a plant virus takes over its system?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe kɛji tso mli hela ko baye egbɛjianɔtoo lɛ nɔ pɛ?

english: Once a virus spreads through a plant's internal sap system, the crop usually cannot cure itself. It is best to remove and destroy infected plants so the virus does not spread to healthy neighbor crops.
ga: Enɛ ji be mli ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛɛɛ atsa amɛhe. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni akpata amɛhiɛ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell if a disease has taken hold inside my crops before the leaves even start dying?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela emɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani baai lɛ aje shishi amɛgboi?

english: Internal plant sickness often shows up as unexpected wilting during cool mornings, yellowing leaf veins, stunted new growth, or soft spots along the lower stem before the entire plant dies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei amli hela he okadii jeɔ kpo akɛ shwiemɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli, baai lɛ amli fãji ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni shwereɔ. aloo hei ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ tso lɛ he dani tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gboɔ.

english: Why do crop diseases seem to stay in my soil even after I harvest all the sick plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai hiɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikpa tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ fɛɛ moŋ?

english: Many plant pathogens form tough spores or survive on leftover root pieces in the soil, waiting for fresh crops to be planted so they can infect new roots.
ga: Tsei amli helai babaoo feɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni hi jogbaŋŋ loo amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shishifãi ni eshwɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ. Kɛtsɔ tsei heei ni aaamɛ ni adu koni shishifãi heei lɛ anyɛ aná hela lɛ nɔ.

english: If I cut off the diseased branches of my tomato plants, will the plant sprout back stronger?
ga: Kɛ mifo mi-tomato tso lɛ niji ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ, Ani tomato tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ ni efee hewalɛ?

english: Pruning away diseased or weak stems helps the plant redirect its energy and nutrients into clean, healthy growth and fruit production, as long as the main stem and roots remain healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ loo ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsakeɔ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa dalɛ ni he tse, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo mli. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ shishifãi titri lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ baahi shi shiŋŋ lɛ

english: Why do weeds sprout back so much faster than my maize crops after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya fe mi-ŋmãa lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have wild, deep root systems and quick-response seeds designed to absorb water and nutrients immediately, allowing them to regrow faster than cultivated crops like maize.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, ni ji adebɔɔ mli nibii, kɛ dumɔwui ni tsuɔ nii oya ni afee koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛkwɛɔ ekoŋŋ oya fe tsei ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and need partial shade to survive. Without shade plants like plantain or forest trees to shield them, the strong sun burns their leaves and dries out soil moisture faster than their small roots can absorb it.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa ni amɛbiɔ hulutsoo fioo koni amɛhi shi. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ, tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gĩɔ oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. E nibii lɛ baafee nɔ ni shwieɔ nu.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the small shoots grow around the base of my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii shwereɔ yɛ mi plantains titrii lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: If too many shoots grow around one plant, they all fight for the same water and nutrients in the soil. Cutting away extra shoots leaves only one or two strong ones, ensuring the main plant gets enough energy to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso kome he lɛ ŋmeii fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaashi tsei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso ni hereɔ tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ niji wuji ni tsii.

english: How often should I water my plantain crops to get a good harvest?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi plantain tsei lɛ nu koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: Plantains require a steady supply of moisture to grow well, especially during dry spells. Giving them regular water helps them build strong stems and produce large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Ehe miihia ni plantains lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Titri lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛtswaa tsei ni wa ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni tsii ni dara.

english: Is it safe and helpful to use well water on my farm crops when rains are late?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe ni sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ mikɛ nu bu mli nu baatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ?

english: Yes, well water is an excellent moisture source during dry periods. Using it keeps your crops hydrated so they do not wither before harvest.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, shikpɔŋ shishi nu ji hulutsoo jɛɛhe ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ okɛtsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni onibii lɛ anáa nu bɔni afee ni amɛkagboi dani akpa.

english: What can I do to keep moisture in the soil around my plantain plants for longer?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle mihe lɛ mli ahi shi? Plantains kɛha be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Placing organic mulch, such as dry grass or plant leaves, around the base of your crops traps water in the ground and prevents it from drying out quickly in the sun.
ga: Organic mulch tamɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ahe baai ni akɛwoɔ mli. Nɔ ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa egbi oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli.
