english: Why do my plantain leaves turn brown and dry up during the hot, sunny months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves are very large and lose water rapidly in strong heat. If the roots cannot find enough soil water, the leaves drop moisture and turn brown.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ dara waa ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa ba. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ baafite ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What is the best way to start planting plantain suckers on a new piece of land?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajeɔ plantains dumɔ shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ?

english: Dig deep, wide holes filled with rich topsoil and compost, then plant healthy suckers and water them deeply to help their roots establish quickly.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ bu ko ni mli kwɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii eyi mli obɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, dumɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni okɛ nu awo mli jogbaŋŋ koni eye ebua eshishifãi lɛ ni amɛma shi oya.

english: How do I know if my young plantain crops are healthy and growing properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ midumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛmiida jogbaŋŋ?

english: Healthy plantains have dark green, upright leaves and thick, sturdy stems. Stunted growth, yellowing leaves, or thin stems indicate that the crop lacks water or nutrients.
ga: Plantains ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni ja, ni ji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ, kɛ tsei ni mli tse ni mli wa. Tso lɛ dalɛ ni eyaaa hiɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, loo eshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu loo niyenii bɛ tso lɛ mli.

english: Can I grow plantains alongside other crops like vegetables on the same plot?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu plantains yɛ tsei krokomɛi, tamɔ aduawai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, plantains provide broad leaf shade that protects smaller crops from intense midday heat, while ground-level crops help keep the soil shaded and moist.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains haa baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ gbi lɛ mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do some farmers in my village harvest much larger plantain bunches than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ kpaa plantain tsei ni dara kwraa fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Farmers who harvest larger bunches usually ensure their crops get consistent water throughout the year, proper spacing, and rich soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehe hiaa ni okwaafoi ni kpaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ akwɛ koni amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nu be fɛɛ be yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii amli

english: How does adding extra water to plantain plants increase my total crop yield?
ga: Te nu kroko ni mikɛfataa midumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aha midumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Water acts as the transport system for nutrients from soil into the crop. Giving extra water allows the plant to produce larger leaves and feed bigger, heavier fruit bunches.
ga: Nu tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Nu kroko ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaha tso lɛ awo baai wuji ni ekɛ niyenii aha aduawai wuji ni tsii.

english: How does adopting better crop care practices help my family and the nation of Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛkwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ ni mikɛtsu nii lɛ eye ebua miweku lɛ kɛ Ghana?

english: Improving your farm's productivity ensures a reliable food supply and income for your family, while contributing to local markets and strengthening Ghana's food security.
ga: Nibii ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa anáa niyenii kɛ shika ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ahaa oweku lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa maŋ lɛ mli jarayeli ni ewajeɔ Ghana niyenii he shweshweeshwefeemɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants drying up and turning brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. They need temporary shade trees like plantains nearby to shield them from excessive heat and help retain moisture in their early stage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ ahe miihia amɛ. Koni ekɛtsi dɔlɛ ni fe nine naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ shishijee mli

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize crop turning yellow before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves near the base of maize plants usually show a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which the crop needs to maintain healthy leaves and develop stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ akwɛ baai ni mli wa nɔ ni amɛná ŋmeii.

english: When cassava stems are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to tall, thin stems with very small tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Ebaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ yitsei bibii waa.

english: Tomato flowers often fall off when daytime temperatures get too high or when the plant experiences sudden dry spells without enough moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. aloo beni tsei lɛ naa hɔmɔ trukaa ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why does my maize grow better when I plant cowpeas in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, which feeds the maize crop and improves the fertility of the surrounding soil naturally.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo

english: Does placing tall wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb really increase my harvest?
ga: Tsoi ni kɛlɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli Ani sweet potato wain tsei ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛkwɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ ni ehaa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high up so they catch more sunlight to feed the plant, while keeping the leaves off the damp soil prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ adara babaoo koni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛkɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni baa helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling upward like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ chili tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap from young leaves, or by viruses spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ

english: Why should I remove some of the small suckers growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: Removing extra suckers stops them from taking water and nutrients away from the main stem, ensuring the main plant produces a heavy, large bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ, no haaa amɛjie nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Heavy rains wash away loose fertilizer from the surface soil or push it deep underground before the roots of your crops can absorb it.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ dani ŋmɔshi nibii shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why is it risky to plant seeds immediately after the very first light rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ fioo ko nɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, be lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara.

english: The first light rain can trigger seeds to sprout, but if a dry spell follows right after, the tender seedlings will dry out and die before the main rains arrive.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui akwɛ̃. Shi kɛji hɔmɔ ba yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ Tender dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔ wulu lɛ baa.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to protect their soft leaves from harsh sunlight and extreme heat. Keeping larger trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides shade and retains soil moisture, helping the seedlings survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Tsei wuji loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ akwɛmɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I plant my cassava on raised mounds instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots easily rot if they sit in trapped water after heavy rains. Planting on raised mounds allows excess rainwater to drain away quickly while keeping the soil loose so the roots can expand easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji amɛtara nu ni damɔ shi mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, an important food for growth. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the leaves stay green and boosts the maize growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha ŋmãa lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Is it good for my land if I plant cowpeas together on the same plot with my maize?
ga: Ani ehi kɛji mikɛ cowpeas kɛ ŋmãa du yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is beneficial. Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the maize while giving you two harvests from one plot.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he. Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ baa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ amli ni eshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common crop pest. Checking your farm early and putting recommended control solutions directly into the plant funnel can stop them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ni afɔɔ namɔ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ awo dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔ lɛ akpa dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to manufacture food for growing big tubers under the ground. Staking keeps the leaves high above the ground where they can catch sunlight and stay safe from mud and leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ muji kɛ baai helai ahe.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crops very close to each other in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each crop correct spacing allows them to grow stronger and produce larger harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Why should I leave dry grass around the base of my pepper plants instead of clearing it completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi jwɛi lɛ yɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ he moŋ fe ni mafo mli kwraa lɛ?

english: Covering the ground around your plants with dry grass—called mulching—keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, prevents water from evaporating too quickly, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi haa Enɛ (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off before making any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of proper soil food. Watering them regularly and feeding the soil with compost helps the plant keep its flowers to produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni sa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he. Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ebuɔ efɔfɔi lɛ ahe ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: How can I apply fertilizer so that heavy rain does not wash it away from my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo ŋmɔshi nii koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akafite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: To stop fertilizer from washing away, dig a small hole or ring a few centimeters away from the plant stem, put the fertilizer inside, and cover it back with soil when the ground is moist.
ga: Koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akaho. Tsɔmɔmɔ bu bibioo ko. loo ring ni kɛ tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai 2-3 lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli. ni okɛ sũ aha nɔ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ.

english: How long does it typically take for cassava to mature and be ready for harvest on my farm?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei lɛ shwereɔ ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava usually takes between 8 to 12 months to fully mature depending on the variety, but some fast-growing improved varieties can be harvested around 6 months after planting.
ga: Kɛjɛ bɔ ni ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ heɔ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 dani eshɛɔ ŋmei lɛ he. Shi abaanyɛ akpa ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi ni atsake amɛ ni amɛdaraa oya lɛ aaafee nyɔji 6 sɛɛ beni adu amɛ.

english: How much yield weight can I expect to harvest from a single plant after six months of growth?
ga: Yibii enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ kɛjɛ tso kome mli yɛ nyɔji enumɔ ni ekɛda lɛ sɛɛ?

english: With proper spacing, fertile soil, and adequate water, an improved crop variety can yield around 1.5 to 2 kilograms per plant within a six-month period.
ga: kɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ ni sa kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ lɛ baanyɛ awo aaafee kilogram 1.5 kɛyashi 2 yɛ tso kome mli yɛ nyɔji enumɔ mli.

english: Why do different varieties of the same crop mature at different times?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties have different genetic characteristics. Early-maturing varieties are bred to complete their growth cycle faster, while traditional varieties take longer to develop full root systems and fruit.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ fɔmɔ sui srɔtoi. Afɔɔ tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ koni amɛgbe amɛdalɛ be lɛ naa oya. Yɛ be mli ni blema tsofai srɔtoi lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛnáa shishifãi kɛ aduawai ni yeɔ emuu lɛ.

english: How well do improved crop varieties adapt to our local weather and soil conditions in Ghana?
ga: Te tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baatsake amɛhe amɛwo wɔmaŋ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Improved crop varieties are specially bred to thrive in local tropical conditions, making them resilient to high temperatures and capable of taking up nutrients effectively from local soil types.
ga: Akwɛ tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛshwere yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa enyɛɔ eshiɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa, ni ebaanyɛ ená niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ

english: If my crops are growing unevenly, is it caused by plant disease or just normal variation?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ Ebaanyɛ ejɛ tsei ahe helai loo tsakemɔi ni baa daa kɛkɛ mli.

english: Uneven growth can occur naturally due to slight differences in soil nutrients or water, but if plants show leaf yellowing or severe stunting, it is usually a sign of plant disease or pest attack that requires attention.
ga: Dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ baanyɛ aba yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ srɔtofeemɔi fioo ni yɔɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ loo nu mli lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ jieɔ baai ni egbɔjɔ loo egbɔjɔ waa kpo hu? Bei pii lɛ eji tso hela loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni he hiaa ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he okadi.

english: Why should I apply treatment to my crops before I even see any signs of sickness?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ dani mana hela he okadii?

english: Preventive treatments protect young plants from fungal spores and insect attacks before they cause permanent damage, ensuring all plants stay healthy and grow uniformly.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa lɛ buɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ kooloi bibii ahe dani amɛfiteɔ amɛ daa. Enɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do plants planted on the exact same day sometimes grow at different speeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsei ni adu yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ daa oya oya lɛ?

english: Even when planted on the same day, plants may grow at different rates because of tiny differences in sunlight, weed competition, or how much water and fertilizer reaches each individual root zone.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ gbi kome nɔ po lɛ Tsei hu baanyɛ ada yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ hulu la hewɔ. Jwɛi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli loo nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shɛɔ shishifãi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he lɛ.

english: What kind of food or fertilizer do my crops need to grow big and heavy quickly?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii he hiaa koni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ adara ni egbɔjɔ oya?

english: Crops need a balanced mix of nitrogen for leaf growth, phosphorus for root development, and potassium for heavy fruit or tuber weight. Applying compost or NPK fertilizer gives them these necessary nutrients.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛfutuɔ tsei jogbaŋŋ lɛ he miihia tsei koni baai lɛ adara. Fosfɔs kɛha shishifãi adalɛ kɛ potassium kɛha aduawai ni tsii loo ŋmeii ni tsii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo NPK ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha nɛkɛ niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ aba.

english: How can I tell if my tubers are ready to harvest without digging up the whole field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-bulbs lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can tell a crop is reaching maturity when the lower leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off naturally. You can also carefully dig up one or two test plants to check the tuber size.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii miishɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa kaa tso kome loo enyɔ hu koni okwɛ bulb lɛ dalɛ.

english: What can I do to keep my young crops from dying during sudden dry spells?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mi dumɔwui lɛ akagboi yɛ hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ mli?

english: Placing dry grass or leaves around the base of your young plants as mulch keeps the soil moist, reduces heat stress on roots, and helps plants survive periods without rain.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni okɛaawo Otsei bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ekɛ dɔlɛ ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ bei ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under strong sunlight. They need partial shade from nurse plants like plantain or shade trees to protect them while their root systems develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ nurse tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the tree during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, damp conditions. Pruning excess branches to let sunlight and air flow through the farm helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellowing starting at the tip and moving down the midrib of lower leaves is a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plant regain its healthy green color.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naagbee ni eyaa shi yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my lowland rice field need standing water around the plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi ebɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Standing water suppresses weeds that compete with rice for nutrients and helps control soil temperature. While rice roots can survive in water, the water primarily acts as a natural weed barrier.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ lolo lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ lɛ anaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔlɛ yaa hiɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa shishifãi baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ nu mli moŋ, shi nu tsuɔ nii titri akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ jwɛi anaa.

english: How can I tell that my cassava plants are ready for harvesting without digging up every stem?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ o-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ obaakpa ni okɛ tso fɛɛ tso tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the base of the stem begins to crack open due to the expanding tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves and catch maximum sunlight, which fuels tuber growth underground. Staking also keeps leaves off damp soil, reducing fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ woɔ ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates drastically between very dry and very wet. Consistent watering and light shade during extreme heat can help fruit set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa teŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ lɛ nu daa ni aha lɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua aduawai lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, mites, or aphids sucking sap from the leaves, or by a virus they spread. Spraying with neem oil solution can help control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ nɔ. Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my groundnut plants push themselves down into the soil after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts have a unique growth pattern called pegging. Once the flower is pollinated above ground, it forms a peg that grows downward into the soil where the actual peanut pod develops and ripens.
ga: Peanuts yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛdaraa ni atsɛɔ lɛ pinning. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: Should I allow all the small shoots growing around my main plantain stem to keep growing?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maha ŋmeii bibii lɛ akwɛ̃? Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani mi plantain tsei titrii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛdaraa?

english: No, allowing too many shoots creates competition for water and food, leading to small plantain bunches. You should trim back extra shoots, leaving only the main mother plant, one medium shoot, and one small shoot.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii babaoo ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha akaŋshii aba kɛha nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa plantain lɛ bafeɔ jwɛi bibioo ko. Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ. Tso lɛ nyɛ titri lɛ pɛ, teŋgbɛ tso 1 kɛ tso bibioo 1 pɛ eshwɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct sunlight, which burns their leaves and dries out topsoil moisture. Keeping shade trees protects young seedlings until their roots mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ. Tso lɛ ni oooha ehi shi lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when there is heavy rainfall late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil. Excess water sitting around the roots cuts off oxygen, which causes root rot fungi to spread quickly and destroy the crop before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni fa fe nine ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani akpaa.

english: Why does my maize crop grow tall with big green leaves, but the corn cobs stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi ŋmãa lɛ ji bibioo kwraa lolo?

english: Too much nitrogen encourages leaf growth, but without enough phosphorus and potassium in the soil, the plant cannot develop healthy, full corn cobs.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo haa baa lɛ daa. Shi kɛji akɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, Tsei nyɛŋ afee ŋmãa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing fruit when the weather becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages tomato pollen, preventing flowers from pollinating. When flowers are not pollinated, the plant drops them to conserve energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ tomato mli ŋmeii. Ehaa fɔfɔi nyɛɛɛ afee pollination Beni fɔfɔii lɛ efeee pollination Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and twisted when I plant them without building high mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ feɔ bibii ni efiteɔ waa kɛ́ midu amɛ ni mifeee gɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers expand underground and need loose, deep soil to grow straight. Hard or compact soil restricts tuber expansion, resulting in misshapen and small yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ baatsi tuber lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efite ni amɛfee bibii.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take much longer to produce fruit when planted during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains require steady moisture to establish root systems. Planting in the dry season forces the plant into survival mode, delaying its overall growth and fruiting cycle.
ga: Plantains he miihia ni nu ahi shi daa koni enyɛ efee shishifãi. Dumɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ehi wala mli. Enɛ haa shweremɔ kɛ yibiiwoo be lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in high humidity and shade when air cannot circulate well through densely packed cocoa trees.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ cacao tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ amli lɛ,.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to buy new hybrid maize seeds every season instead of saving seeds from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ mahe ŋmãa dumɔwui heei ni akɛ hybrid fee lɛ daa afi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahere dumɔwui kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yields, but seeds saved from the harvested crop lose those parent traits, producing lower yields and uneven growth if replanted.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ nakai fɔlɔ sui lɛ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi ni ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and stop growing even when I water the farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking leaf sap or transmitting viruses, rather than a lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baa mli nu loo amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. yɛ nu ni baa shi lɛ najiaŋ

english: Why does my cowpea crop suddenly attract so many pests right when it starts flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo kɛji ebɔi fɔfɔii shwiemɔ pɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet nectar that attracts sap-feeding insects like thrips and pod borers, making the flowering stage the most vulnerable time for pest invasion.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ jieɔ nu ni gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ nu tamɔ thrips kɛ pod borers lɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ feɔ be ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Is it better for my crops if I water them every day, or should I wait a few days between watering?
ga: Ani ebaahi aha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo nɔ daa gbi? Aloo esa akɛ mamɛ gbii fioo komɛi yɛ nu ni mikɛhaa lɛ teŋ?

english: Waiting 3 to 4 days between watering encourages crop roots to grow deeper into the soil in search of moisture, making the plants stronger and saving you water compared to shallow daily watering.
ga: Gbii 3 kɛyashi 4 ni akɛbaamɛ yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛtao ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ waa ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ nu toɔ nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko daa gbi lɛ he.

english: What happens to my crops if I give them too much water all the time?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ nu babaoo ha amɛ be fɛɛ be?

english: Excessive watering fills all the tiny spaces in the soil with water and pushes out air, which suffocates plant roots, causes yellow leaves, and leads to root rot.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baaha he bibioo ko afite. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ eyi kɛ nu ni etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ baa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ

english: What simple irrigation methods can I use on my farm if I cannot afford expensive equipment?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ nu shwiemɔ gbɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. Mɛni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Ni kɛji akɛ minyɛɛɛ mahe nibii ni jara wa hu?

english: You can use simple surface irrigation techniques like digging small furrows or basins that use gravity to guide water from a source directly to the root zones of your crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ he ŋaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ nubu bibioo ko loo nubu ni afoɔ lɛ atsu nii. ni kɛ hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ nu kɛjɛɔ jɛɛhe ko mli kɛyaa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ

english: Why do some farmers dig shallow ditches or trenches across their farms before the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi tsaa nubui ni mli ekwɔɔɔ loo nubui ni mli ekɔɔɔ amɛshwieɔ amɛŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ dani nugbɔ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Digging trenches across your farm traps rainwater runoff so it settles and slowly soaks deep into the soil where crop roots can reach it, rather than washing away off your field.
ga: Kɛ́ atsa bu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ, ebaamɔ nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehiɔ shi ni eboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fiofio kɛyaa shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaashwie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ

english: How can I store rainwater on my farm land so my crops survive short dry spells?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ nugbɔ nu ato miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli?

english: Creating earth basins or trenches in key areas allows rainwater to collect and remain in place, keeping the surrounding soil moist for several days after the rain stops.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi loo ŋmeii ni afee yɛ hei titrii lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii babaoo beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Is it safe to let rainwater pool anywhere on my field after a heavy downpour?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mahã nugbɔ nu abua naa yɛ he fɛɛ he yɛ mishia lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: No, standing water directly around stems can rot crops like cassava or maize; rainwater should be guided into structured trenches or holding areas slightly away from plant stems.
ga: Dabi, nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Direct stems lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei afite. Esa akɛ ajie nugbɔ nu lɛ awo ŋshɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ loo he ko ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni kɛ tsei ashishifãi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo.

english: How does the slope or shape of my farmland affect how much water my crops get?
ga: Te bɔ ni miŋmɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi loo bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ saa nu babaoo ni miŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Water flows quickly off steep land, leaving plants on high spots dry, while lower areas become overwatered; understanding your land's slope helps you plan where water needs to be trapped.
ga: Nu hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ waa. tsei ni egbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, he ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ yɛ nu babaoo tsɔ. Kɛ́ onu bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ha lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni oto he ni okɛ nu baato lɛ he gbɛjianɔ.

english: Why does rainwater keep washing away my rich topsoil whenever it rains heavily on my sloping land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ shwieɔ mishikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rain gains speed moving down sloping land, carrying away fertile soil; digging channels across the slope breaks the water's speed and protects your topsoil from erosion.
ga: Nugbɔ baaha oyaiyeli ni akɛbaa shi yɛ gɔŋji lɛ anɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ otsa ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ aya oya, ni ebaabu oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my crops growing well in one section of my farm but yellowing or stunted in another section?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã ko mli shi amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛmiigbɔjɔ yɛ fã kroko lɛ?

english: Differences in land height cause water to settle too long in low spots or run off high spots, meaning different parts of your farm receive unequal amounts of moisture.
ga: Srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ taraa shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ loo ejɛɔ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fãi ni Oŋmɔ lɛ naa hulutsoo ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee.

english: How do I know if my soil is holding enough moisture for my crops after a rain or irrigation?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ loo nu ni awoɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Dig a few inches into the soil with your fingers; if the soil feels damp and holds its shape when squeezed into a ball, your crops still have enough water for a few days.
ga: Okɛ oniji atsu nii ni okɛfo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli inchi fioo komɛi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiɛɔ egbɛhe lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ebɔ he lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lolo kɛha gbii fioo komɛi.

english: Is it better to plant my maize right after the very first rain of the year or wait a bit?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooodu ŋmãa yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ loo ooomɛ fioo?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become steady. The very first rain is often followed by a short dry spell, which can dry out young seeds right after they germinate and ruin your crop.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ, ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui bibii lɛ agbi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ ni efite onibii lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the sunlight to produce energy. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, prevents leaves from rotting, and helps the underground tubers grow much bigger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu la lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite Ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up in the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh direct sunlight. Without shade trees nearby to protect them, heat stress causes the leaves to burn, turn yellow, and drop off.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei bɛ ni baaha hulutsoo ni abu he lɛ Heat stress haa baai lɛ shãa. Etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbee shi

english: Why are my tomato plants producing lots of yellow flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without making tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomatoi?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air is too hot or when the soil lacks moisture and essential nutrients during flowering. Regular watering and avoiding extreme heat help the flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ beaŋ. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa kɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and shrinking into tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips transmitting a virus. These pests feed on the plant sap and cause the leaves to deform.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛfiteɔ baai lɛ.

english: Why are my young maize leaves full of small holes and filled with greenish dirt in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani muji eŋɔli eyi mli obɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm attack. The caterpillars hide inside the central funnel of the plant during the day, eating the tender leaves before they fully unfold.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ he okadi. Kplukai lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ dani amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa kwraa.

english: How can I tell that my cassava is ready to harvest without digging up the whole root?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni okɛ shishifã muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually ready around 8 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and small cracks begin to appear in the soil around the base of the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. kɛ ŋmeii bibii Ebaabɔi kpojiemɔ yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Should I cut off some of the small plantain suckers growing around my main plant stem?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani ajie mitso titri lɛ?

english: Yes, you should keep only 2 or 3 healthy suckers per stool. Leaving too many suckers creates competition for soil nutrients and sunlight, which results in smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ okɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 2 loo 3 pɛ ato ŋmeii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ekɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la. Enɛ haa plantain lɛ feɔ bibioo.

english: Why does my maize plant grow very tall and dark green, but the corn cobs remain small and empty?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ waa lɛ? Shi ŋmãa lɛ ji bibioo lolo ni nɔ ko bɛ mli?

english: This happens when the soil has too much nitrogen but lacks phosphorus and potassium. Nitrogen makes the leaves and stem grow fast, but plants need phosphorus and potassium to build and fill out the cobs.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ fa tsɔ shi fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium bɛ mli. Nitrogen haa baai kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi daa oya. Shi tsei he miihia phosphorus kɛ potassium koni amɛkɛma ŋmei lɛ ni amɛwo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my farm soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots. When the plants harvested or rot back into the ground, they release this natural fertilizer into the soil for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akpa tsei loo amɛgboi ekoŋŋ kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient found in fertilizers or rich soil. Without enough nitrogen, the plant cannot make food properly and loses its rich green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni anaa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ ni baa nii amli lɛ mli Kɛji nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ ahoo nii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ babaoo baafite.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even when the leaves on top look healthy and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ moŋ?

english: If the soil is too hard or packed tightly, the plant puts its energy into growing top leaves instead of expanding its roots underground. Loosening the soil well before planting helps the tubers grow big and strong.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshishifãi lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani adu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa bulbs lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to strong, direct sunlight and high heat. They require temporary shade from plants like plantains or shade trees to protect them from burning and to hold moisture in the soil.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni la akatswa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Pepper plants often shed their blossoms when exposed to extreme heat or irregular watering. Heat stress forces the plant into survival mode, causing it to drop flowers rather than expend energy on growing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote la ni mli edɔ waa mli loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Dɔlɛ haomɔ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Enɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism plants use to conserve water during heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun, preventing moisture from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu nu he yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ.

english: Why do my bean plants grow very tall and thin but produce very few crop pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ daa ni ekwɛɔ waa ni efeɔ mlɛo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together or under deep shade, they stretch upward searching for sunlight. This rapid height growth wastes the energy the plant needs to develop strong stems, leaves, and crop pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tso lɛ baajie ehe kɛya ŋwɛi koni eyatao hulu la. Nɛkɛ dalɛ ni yaa oya nɛɛ haaa hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ená tsei, baai, kɛ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why is it better to plant my crops in straight rows rather than scattering the seeds across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni aaadu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows gives each crop equal space to access sunlight, water, and nutrients without competing with neighboring plants. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their improved traits in the next generation. Planting saved hybrid seeds often leads to uneven growth, higher susceptibility to disease, and a significantly lower harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baafite amɛsu kpakpai lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee baa. Helai ni baa mɔ nɔ oya ni ehaa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi waa

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the ground during heavy rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot when excess rainwater collects around the roots in poorly drained soil. Stagnant water deprives roots of air and creates an ideal environment for harmful fungus and bacteria to grow.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni ekã shi lɛ jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ adalɛ.

english: Cabbage heads split when a sudden heavy rain or overwatering follows a dry period. The inside of the cabbage head absorbs water quickly and expands faster than the outer leaves can stretch.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei lɛ tswaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa loo nu babaoo ba yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Kaabe yitso lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why does my soil dry out so fast after rain, and how can I keep the water in the ground longer for my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maha nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses water quickly to direct sun and wind. Covering the soil around your crops with dry leaves or straw (mulching) acts like a protective cover, slowing down evaporation and keeping soil moist for longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ laajeɔ nu oya koni ekɛtsi hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ naa. Mulching around Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulch) tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ, ni ehaa la ni hoɔ oya lɛ baa shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable crops a little bit every day or give them plenty of water a few times a week?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahã mitsei lɛ nu fioo daa gbi loo mahã amɛ nu babaoo shii fioo komɛi yɛ otsi mli?

english: Watering deeply a few times a week encourages roots to grow deeper into the soil where moisture stays longer, making your crops much stronger during hot and dry days.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli shii 2-3 yɛ otsi mli lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ adara kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni hulutsoo be lɛ baahi shi be kakadaŋŋ Enɛ haa onibii ni oŋmɔɔ lɛ mli wa waa yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ ni nu hɔmɔ bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Does adding animal manure or compost to my land help my soil hold onto water during dry weather?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yes, organic manure acts like a natural sponge in the soil. It absorbs water when it rains or when you irrigate, holding onto that moisture so your crop roots can feed on it over many days.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Ebaaŋɔ nu kɛji nugbɔ nɛ loo kɛ́ okɛ nu shwie nɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ bɔni afee ni otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aye lɛ gbii babaoo.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like ribbons during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ ŋmãa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When water levels in the plant drop due to intense heat, maize leaves roll up to shrink their surface area. This is the plant's natural defense mechanism to stop internal moisture from escaping.
ga: Kɛ nu ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ ba shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa hewɔ lɛ, Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ afee bibioo. Enɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛtsiɔ emli ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaje mli.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my pepper plants turn yellow and fall off during a long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: When soil water drops too low, pepper plants sacrifice their lower leaves to conserve water for the top growing shoots and fruit, preventing the whole plant from drying out completely.
ga: Kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ba shi tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ shaa afɔle koni amɛkɛ nu ato kɛha ŋmeii kɛ aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ akagbi kwraa.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves look wilted in the midday sun even though I watered them early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ahe baai tamɔ nɔ ni egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu leebi maŋkpa?

english: During intense sun, crops lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from the soil. They temporarily wilt to conserve moisture, but they usually bounce back in the evening as temperatures drop.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaagboi be kukuoo ko koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Shi amɛfɔɔ sɛɛkuu gbɛkɛ mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi.

english: How can I keep my freshly harvested leafy vegetables from shrinking and losing their freshness before I get to the market?
ga: Makwɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai ni akpa ehee lɛ anɔ. Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aha egbɔjɔ ni ehiɛ afee ehee dani aya jara nɔ?

english: Harvested vegetables lose internal water rapidly when exposed to heat and dry air. Keeping them in a cool, shady place and sprinkling a little clean water on them keeps their water level up and maintains freshness.
ga: Aduawai ni akpa lɛ mli nu lɛ laajeɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he. Okɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ ni okɛ nu ni mli tse fioo awo nɔ. Koni nu lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni eha ehe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my harvested yams lose weight and dry out when I store them in a closed room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ mli shwieɔ shi ni egbiɔ kɛ akɛto tsu ko ni aŋã mli lɛ?

english: Harvested yams are still living tissues that lose internal moisture through evaporation. Storing them in a cool, well-ventilated barn allows air to circulate and prevents rapid moisture loss and shrinkage.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni akpa lɛ ji fãji ni hiɛ ka lolo ni emli nu lɛ elaaje yɛ la ni hoɔ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛto ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli, ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi oya kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my tomatoes split open on the plant just when they start getting ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shwereɔ kɛ́ ebɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they take in a sudden, large amount of water after being dry for a while. The inside of the fruit swells faster than the outer skin can stretch, so maintaining steady water levels prevents cracking.
ga: Tomatoi tswaa kɛ́ amɛná nu ni tswaa trukaa beni amɛgbi be fioo sɛɛ lɛ. Yibii lɛ amli baafu oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nu lɛ mli tse be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my young seedlings die so quickly when I transplant them from the shade nursery into the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui bibii lɛ gboiɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young nursery plants are used to low heat and high moisture. Moving them straight to open sun causes water inside them to drop too fast before their roots can establish themselves to drink from the field soil.
ga: Tsei bibii biɔ la ni mli edɔ fioo kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ tee hulu la lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ aba shi oya tsɔ dani amɛshishifãi lɛ afee koni amɛnu nu kɛjɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep drying up and dying when I plant them out in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and delicate roots that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside them provides living shade and holds soil moisture to protect the seedlings until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know which way is up when pushing cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei nine ni atsiɔ awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi?

english: Look closely at the small leaf buds or nodes along the cassava stem; they should point upwards toward the sky like tiny arrows. Planting them upside down makes it difficult for shoots to emerge, resulting in weak growth and fewer tubers.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. loo nodes bibii Nyiɛmɔ ŋmei lɛ tso lɛ sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi tamɔ akpɔlɔ bibioo ko. Kɛ́ adu ŋwɛi ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃. Enɛ haa edalɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of flowers, but the flowers fall off before growing into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from sudden dry spells, extreme heat, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and using balanced fertilizers helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa, latsaa ni naa wa, loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ye tso lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli fũu be fɛɛ be, ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tsuɔ nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai lɛ ahiɔ shi.

english: Why does the soil around my vegetables dry out so fast even after a good rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-vegetables lɛ he lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses moisture quickly through heat and wind evaporation. Covering the soil around your crop roots with dry grass, straw, or leaves (mulching) acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the ground for much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛjɛɔ la ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Mulching around Ni akɛ jwɛi, jwɛi loo baai aha tso shishifãi ahe (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat ragged holes in the middle whorl of my maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ buji ni ekpɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-abele baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that hides inside the center of the maize plant. Checking your crops early and applying recommended neem-based sprays or bio-pesticides into the plant center can stop them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehe ewoɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii amli mra Ni okɛ neem sprays loo bio-insecticides ni ajieɔ yi yɛ tsei ahe nitsumɔhei lɛ atsu nii lɛ baanyɛ akpa nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant cowpeas or beans in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans absorb nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots, naturally enriching the soil. When grown with maize, they share this fertility, helping the maize grow better while reducing your need for expensive commercial fertilizers.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans shwieɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa Amɛbaaná babaoo tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa atsu nii.

english: Yam vines need to climb high off the ground so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to feed the tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves dry and away from soil diseases, leading to much larger yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya shɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ agbiɔ ni helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akashɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa.

english: Is it better for my garden crops if I water them in the hot afternoon or in the early morning?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: Watering in the early morning or cool evening is best because less water evaporates in the cool air, allowing roots to drink deeply. Hot afternoon watering wastes water through rapid evaporation and can stress hot plants.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ nu fioo pɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu waa Nu ni awoɔ yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baafite nu yɛ la ni hoɔ oya lɛ hewɔ. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ haomɔ aba tsei anɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant as many crop seeds as possible close together to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe bɔ ni manyɛ koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for limited soil nutrients and water, while their leaves block sunlight. Proper spacing ensures every single plant gets enough food and light to yield bigger, healthier crops.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni fa fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow green and strong. Adding fertilizer or animal manure feeds the soil and restores leaf health.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii titri ko ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ebaaha baai lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant beans or cowpeas on the same land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil, but beans naturally pull food from the air and put it back into the dirt through their roots, restoring soil fertility for future crops.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive and burn easily under harsh sunlight and strong winds. Leaving taller trees or planting fast-growing plantain shade crops protects the young cocoa so it can survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ fe tsutsu lɛ ni aaashi loo plantains ni shwereɔ oya ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up during hot dry afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane ni edɔ ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up during the hot afternoon to reduce the amount of leaf area exposed to the sun, which stops the plant from losing water too quickly.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ akafite nu oya tsɔ.

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, their roots fight over the same soil nutrients and water while their leaves block each other's sunlight, leaving all the plants underfed.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe hulu la lɛ naa Enɛ haa tsei lɛ fɛɛ náaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why is it necessary to clear weeds while my crop seedlings are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ daraaa kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crop plants and steal the water, fertilizer, and light needed by the crops, which can permanently stunt crop growth if not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la ni he hiaa tsei lɛ. ni baanyɛ atsĩ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa kɛya naanɔ kɛji ajieee amɛ mra.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes to expose their leaves to direct sunlight, which allows the plant to produce the energy required to grow big underground tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ koni amɛbai lɛ aje kpo yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ enáa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when there is sudden water stress, as the plant conserves its energy to stay alive rather than making fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu he haomɔ ba trukaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei kɛ hewalɛ toɔ koni amɛhi wala mli moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves dry up and fall off, and the earth around the base of the main stem starts to crack as the underground tubers swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's store-bought hybrid maize yield poorly compared to new seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii jogbaŋŋ nɛkɛ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to give high yields only in the first generation; planting saved seeds from a hybrid harvest results in weaker plants with smaller ears.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni toi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves of my cocoyam turning yellow and curling at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on cocoyam usually indicate a lack of key soil nutrients like nitrogen, or an attack by sap-sucking pests like aphids. Applying well-rotted animal manure and spraying with natural neem leaf extract can help restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ahe lɛ ahe baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli, loo akɛ ŋmeii ni nuɔ ŋmeii tamɔ aphids lɛ etutua amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii ni akɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it safe to harvest and cook leafy greens like kontomire if I notice tiny pest holes in them?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ abaakpa ni ahoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ contomir? Kɛji miyɔse kooloi bibii bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Yes, leaves with small insect holes are safe to cook and eat as long as you wash them thoroughly with clean water and salt. The holes just show that insects were feeding on them, which you can manage on future growth by applying mild organic pest sprays.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai ni kooloi bibii yɔɔ mli. Abaanyɛ ahoo ni aye shweshweeshwe. Shii abɔ ni okɛ nu ni mli tse kɛ ŋoo baafɔ ohe jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Bui nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii miiye amɛ. Obaanyɛ okwɛ wɔsɛɛ dalɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ kooloo mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is there a white, dusty powder covering the leaves of my garden egg plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sũ yɛŋ ehà eggplant lɛ baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: That white powder is a common fungal disease called powdery mildew, which develops when air circulation around the plants is poor during humid weather. You can control it by spacing your plants properly and removing the heavily affected leaves.
ga: Pauda yɛŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ he lɛ ehiii yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ. Obaanyɛ okudɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa ni ooojie baai ni ena naagbai waa lɛ nɔ.

english: When young cocoa gets too much sun, its leaves look pale yellow, get burnt brown edges, or drop prematurely. Planting shade crops like plantains nearby creates a protective canopy that keeps the cocoa leaves healthy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulu la babaoo shɛ cocoa yibii lɛ anɔ lɛ Ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eshishigbɛi lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. loo egbee shi oya Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni haa kookoo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aya hiɛ lɛ aba.

english: Can I harvest the leaves from my cassava plants for cooking without reducing my cassava root yield?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafo baai kɛjɛ ŋmei tso lɛ mli kɛha niyenii ni ŋmei tso lɛ yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi?

english: You can pick a few young cassava leaves for soup without hurting the roots, provided you leave most of the upper leaves intact. Since leaves make food for the roots, plucking too many leaves at once will result in smaller cassava tubers.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa bibii fioo komɛi atsu nii ni okɛfee shwiili ni ofiteee shishifãi lɛ. ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo bɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why do plantain leaves split into thin ribbons when there is a strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain baai lɛ fãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves naturally split along their side veins during strong winds to reduce wind resistance. This prevents the heavy wind from snapping the leaf stems or blowing the entire plant over.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛyaa sɛɛgbɛ fãji amli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli koni ekɛba kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ mɔ naa lɛ shi. Enɛ ji koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa akafo baa lɛ shishi loo etswa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their lower leaves after they start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miiho eshishigbɛ baai lɛ beni ebɔi fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shift their energy to producing flowers and fruit, causing older leaves near the bottom to yellow and drop naturally. However, if leaves drop quickly, it could be a soil-borne fungus spread by splashing rain, which mulching can prevent.
ga: Tomato tsei tsakeɔ hewalɛ amɛwoɔ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai. Enɛ haa baai momo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi oya lɛ, Ebaanyɛ efee tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni mulching baanyɛ atsĩ naa

english: Why are my maize leaves turning purple along the edges during the early rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ purple yɛ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize mean the plant is struggling to absorb phosphorus, often because cold, wet soil temporarily slows root activity. As the soil warms up and drains, or with a light fertilizer application, the leaves usually return to a healthy green.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miitao ni ejie fɔsfɔs. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni efɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ anitsumɔ baa shi yɛ be kukuoo mli. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ ni eho nu loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko fata he lɛ Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli ni yeɔ emuu lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing many dark green leaves but producing very few flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo shi fɔfɔi fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil makes leguminous plants like cowpeas put all their energy into growing foliage rather than flowers. Because beans make their own nitrogen in the soil, they do not need heavy nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii yeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛduɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii atsu nii.

english: How long does it take for pale crop leaves to turn dark green after applying fertilizer?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani baai bibii lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ yɛ be mli ni awo amɛ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Chemical nitrogen fertilizers like urea usually show results within 3 to 7 days after application, turning leaves dark green. Organic fertilizers like poultry manure break down more slowly, taking about 1 to 2 weeks to show noticeable improvements in leaf color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni ji nitrogen, tamɔ urea lɛ jieɔ nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ kpo yɛ gbii 3 kɛyashi 7 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni akɛwo mli lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa. Organic fertilizers tamɔ kooloi ashishifãi lɛ baafite blɛoo. Eheɔ aaafee otsi 1 kɛyashi 2 dani onaa hiɛyaa ni kadiɔ mɔ yɛ baai lɛ ahe su mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without producing any fruit during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato plants get stressed and cannot pollinate properly. The plant naturally drops its flowers to save energy and water until conditions become cooler.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ amɛhe ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Tsei baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my fresh pepper seedlings wilt and die when I move them to the open farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui heei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ tee ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have weak roots that cannot absorb water fast enough under intense heat. Transplanting them late in the afternoon or covering them with palm fronds for a few days protects them while their roots settle in.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa yɛ latsaa ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo shwane mli loo okɛ tsei ahe tsei ha amɛhe gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crops turn yellow when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excess rain fills up all the tiny air spaces in the soil, effectively drowning the roots. Without air, the roots cannot absorb nutrients like nitrogen, which causes the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground during heavy rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil to stay healthy. Waterlogged soil encourages fungal diseases that break down and rot the tubers beneath the ground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ ni efiteɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up if I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ kɛji mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct harsh sunlight and high temperatures. Leaving shade trees on the farm creates a cooler environment and keeps the soil moist for the young cocoa to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ he waa. Kɛ́ ashi tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni kookoo tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my plantain suckers grow very tall and thin with small fruit when planted very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The plant puts all its energy into growing tall to reach light instead of developing large fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara koni amɛná la. Mohu ɔ, e daa kɛ peeɔ yiblii ngua.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil or get full of dark powder when stored in a warm room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Warm, humid air encourages mold to grow and insect eggs to hatch inside stored grain. Maize needs to be fully dried and kept in a cool, well-ventilated place or sealed in airtight bags to remain safe.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, ni mli edɔ woɔ ŋmei dalɛ kɛ kooloo wuji ni efɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni ato mli lɛ mli. Esa akɛ ŋmãa lɛ agbi kwraa ni akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli loo akɛwo kotoku ko mli koni ehi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my harvested yams sprout leaves early while sitting in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miikwɛ baai oya beni mitara ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams naturally react to warm temperatures and humidity as a sign that it is time to grow again. Keeping the yam barn cool, dark, and elevated off the ground slows down early sprouting.
ga: Sweet potatoes tsuɔ nii yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ latsaa be mli. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ wɔda ekoŋŋ. Kɛ́ oha o-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔ, eyɛ duŋ, ni owó nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃ fioo.

english: Why do my pepper seeds fail to germinate when I plant them too deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds carry limited stored energy to push their first shoot above the surface. If buried too deeply, the shoot runs out of energy and dies before reaching sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ hewalɛ ni fa fioo ni amɛkɛbaatsi klɛŋklɛŋ tso lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, hewalɛ baaho yɛ tsei lɛ amli ni amɛbaagboi dani hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my planted crops after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that are naturally adapted to the local soil and weather, allowing them to absorb available water and nutrients much faster than domesticated crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ oya fe shia tsei ahe dumɔwui.
