english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving the young cocoa trees shade and keeping the soil moist so they can survive their first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha cacao tsei bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why does planting my corn seeds too close together give me smaller ears of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ bibioo lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots fight under the ground for nutrients and water, while their leaves block sunlight from each other. Spacing them properly ensures each plant gets enough food to make big, healthy fruits.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe Gbɛ ni sa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the plant food that builds strong green leaves. It can also happen when too much water in the soil drowns the roots and stops them from feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii kɛha tsei ni woɔ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni eha shishifãi lɛ shwie shi ni ekpa amɛ niyenii.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in their roots. When the plant dies, that trapped food stays in the soil to feed whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifãi amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, niyenii ni emɔ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know if the soil is ready for planting after the first rain of the season falls?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting after just one single rain is risky because the soil can quickly dry up and kill the young seeds. It is best to wait until two or three good rains fall so the soil holds enough deep moisture to keep seedlings alive.
ga: Dumɔ ni aaadu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni egbeɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ. Ehi akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ. shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why does spreading dry bush or straw around my crop stems help them stay alive during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni abɔle jwɛi loo jwɛi ni egbi lɛ ahe lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket that blocks the sun from drying out the soil, keeping water near the plant roots for much longer.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi. Ehaa nu hiɔ tso shishifãi ahe be babaoo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak even when I put fertilizer on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔji lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ?

english: Weeds have strong, aggressive roots that steal water and fertilizer faster than your crops can reach them. If you do not clear the weeds first, you end up feeding the weeds instead of your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa, ni yɔɔ basabasa. Enɛ juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe bɔ ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ aná. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, Ebaabi ni okɛ jwɛi lɛ aye niyenii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ najiaŋ.

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the center whorl of the corn plant and eat the soft leaves before they unroll, which can stunt the whole plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaai amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ dalɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground if I wait too long to harvest them during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mimɛ be kakadaŋŋ dani mikpa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain fills up all the air spaces in the soil with water, which smothers the cassava roots. Without oxygen, wet rot fungi easily attack and break down the cassava tubers under the ground.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yiɔ kɛ nu. ni kɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ Wet rot fungus lɛ tutuaa ŋmei shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ oya ni efiteɔ amɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they are stressed by extreme hot weather, lack of water, or too much chemical fertilizer. The plant sheds flowers to save its own strength to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means your soil is low in nitrogen, a key nutrient crops need to grow strong and green. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to the newest top leaves, leaving the older lower leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛɛmɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa ni amɛfee ŋmɔji. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Ha shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as intense heat during the day, insufficient water, or a shortage of essential plant food like potassium and phosphorus in the soil.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium kɛ phosphorus ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up tightly during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes during hot hours is a natural defense trick to save water. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the leaf surface exposed to the sun so it loses less water to the hot air.
ga: Tomato baai ni ajieɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli ŋaa ni akɛtsiɔ nu naa. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ baa baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nu fioo ni laajeɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yam tubers rot when the soil holds too much water after heavy rains. Waterlogged soil prevents air from reaching the roots, creating a moist environment where bacteria and fungi thrive and rot the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa ni bacteria kɛ fungi daa ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Instead of building thick stems and large cobs, the plants waste energy stretching upward to catch light.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ feɔ tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji moŋ. Mohu ɔ, tsehi puɛɔ he wami nɛ a ngɔɔ kɛ yaa hiɔwe ɔ konɛ a ná la.

english: Why does cassava grow bigger tubers when I plant the stem cuttings at a slant instead of straight into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava bulbs lɛ daa kɛji midu amɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛ amɛ baawo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a 45-degree angle allows roots to spread out horizontally near the topsoil where the earth is loose and nutrient-rich, giving the tubers room to expand evenly.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ji digrii 45 lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋwɛigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji he ko ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli etse ni niyenii kpakpai babaoo yɔɔ mli. Ha tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ alɛɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that protects the seedlings from heat and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How does growing groundnuts on my farmland help my next crop of maize grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which traps nitrogen gas from the air and fixes it directly into the soil through their roots. When groundnut roots decay, they leave nitrogen behind to feed the next crop.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni emɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fite Ebaashi nitrogen ni akɛbaatsu nii akɛ tsei aniyenii.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my plantain suckers with dry grass and crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he sũ? Dumɔwui ni jwɛi ni egbi kɛ tsei ahe baai yɔɔ mli

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves creates mulch. Mulch protects the soil from the drying sun, keeps root zones cool, stops weeds from growing, and breaks down into natural compost.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Mulch buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni hulu lɛ akaha egbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii

english: What causes ragged holes in my maize leaves and small black dirt inside the plant stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli kɛ muji diŋ bibii lɛ baa? yɛ tso ko shishi

english: Ragged holes and dark specks (caterpillar droppings) inside maize leaves are classic signs of fall armyworms. These pests hide inside the plant funnels during the hot day and feed on the leaves.
ga: Buu ni etse kɛ hei ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ (ŋmei fɔmɔ kotoku) ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa mli lɛ ji okadii ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ fall armyworm. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients too deep into the soil where roots cannot reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii lɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips that feed on leaf sap and spread viruses that stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa tsei lɛ adalɛ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. In heavy rain, waterlogged soil fills up all air spaces, suffocating the roots and allowing fungal rot to take over.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ eyi kɔɔyɔɔ mli obɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ nɔ.

english: Why does my farmland get hard and baked like brick shortly after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli wa ni eshã tamɔ brikii yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil bakes hard when it lacks organic matter like decayed leaves or manure. Organic matter acts like a sponge, keeping the soil soft and holding water longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ais kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ bɛ mli. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when I clear all the large trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi beni mijie tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. They need partial shade from taller plants or trees to keep them cool and prevent their leaves from burning.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ tsei loo tsei kakadaji adɛŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛtsi baai lɛ ashãa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too hot or when the plant does not get steady water, which prevents successful pollination.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa. Enɛ haaa pollination lɛ aye omanye.

english: Yam tubers become small and twisted when planted in hard, compact, or stony soil that physically blocks the tuber from expanding evenly downwards.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraaa ni amɛfiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni mli edɔ loo tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, ni no haaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do my cabbages stay flat with open leaves instead of forming a hard, round head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ ji ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baai lɛ egbele yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee yitso ni wa ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads fail to form if the crop lacks sufficient nitrogen early on or experiences dry spells, which causes the plant to spread its leaves outward rather than packing them tightly together.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei efeŋ kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa mra. aloo hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni enaa Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɛɔ ebaa lɛ eshwaa kponɔgbɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeebua amɛnaa shi shiŋŋ.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants whose seeds rest in the soil ready to burst into growth at the slightest rain, quickly taking up space and nutrients before cultivated crops catch up.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni dumɔwui yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ. He ni yɔɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ayeɔ oya dani tsei ni miida lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches at the top, making them top-heavy and easy for strong winds to push over unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni jwɛi ni mli tse yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo yɛ ŋwɛi, ni ewaaa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatsɔ mli. Ja nɔ ko ni akɛ tso fee lɛ yɛ.

english: If crops lack water, their leaves usually turn yellow, curl up, and look dry or limp during the hottest part of the day. If they have too much water, the leaves turn yellow, but the soil stays soggy and the leaves feel soft and squishy because the roots are suffocating.
ga: Kɛji nu bɛ tso ko mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbi loo amɛhe ejɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Kɛji nu fa babaoo lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Shi shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔtɔ lolo. Ni baai lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛhe efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like tubes when there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing water in the hot sun. It is the plant's natural way of saving moisture inside its leaf tissues until it gets water again.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ ebaa lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nu lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I use water straight from a nearby river or lake to water my vegetables during the dry season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa loo ŋshɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii tɛ̃ɛ koni mikɛwo aduawai anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, river or lake water is generally good for crops, but if the water is too salty, polluted, or full of thick mud, it can harm delicate vegetables or block your watering equipment.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, nu ni yɔɔ faai loo kpaakpoi amli lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Shi kɛ́ nu lɛ mli ŋoo tsɔ, ewo muji, loo eyi kɛ muji ni mli tse hu? Ebaanyɛ eye aduawai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ awui loo egba nibii ni okɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruits when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When heat is too strong and soil moisture drops, the plant gets stressed and sheds its flowers to save energy and water for its own survival instead of feeding new fruit.
ga: Beni latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ baa shi lɛ. Tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha yibii heei

english: Is it better for my crops if I water them early in the morning or late in the afternoon?
ga: Ani ebaahi kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo mli leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil absorbs the moisture before the sun gets too hot, allowing the roots to drink up enough water to handle the heat of the day.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ adɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkɛtsu latsaa ni baa nakai gbi lɛ he nii.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass keep the ground wet longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass acts like a protective blanket that blocks the hot sun from evaporating earth moisture, keeping the root area cool and wet for much longer.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he, ni ebuɔ hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants fall off during a long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during droughts to stop water from evaporating through them. The plant enters a sleeping state to stay alive, and it will sprout fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu lɛ akatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Tsei wɔɔ koni amɛhi shi. Ni ebaajie baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Will watering my crops during the middle of the hot day burn their leaves?
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tsei amli yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ani baai lɛ baashã?

english: Midday watering causes water to evaporate rapidly before roots can take it in, and water droplets resting on leaves under intense midday sun can act like tiny magnifiers, scorching tender leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ nu yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ nu lɛ. Ni nu mli nu ni shwieɔ shi ni kpɛtɛɔ baai ahe yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ afee tamɔ glase bibii ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo. ni shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ

english: Why do my pepper plants need watering almost every day while my cassava can survive for months without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni awo mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ nu aaafee daa gbi lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi-cassava lɛ baanyɛ aya nyɔji babaoo ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Pepper plants have shallow roots and soft leaves that lose water rapidly, while cassava develops deep, sturdy roots underground that store food and moisture for long dry periods.
ga: Pepper tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni nu fiteɔ oya. Beni ŋmei lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ato be kakadaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How does salty underground well water affect the growth of my garden crops?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli edɔ lɛ saa mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: High salt levels in well water make it hard for plant roots to draw in moisture—even if the soil looks wet—causing plants to look thirsty, turn brown at the leaf tips, and grow poorly.
ga: Nu ni fa babaoo yɛ nubu mli nu lɛ mli lɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaajie ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni edɔ po Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni kumai miiye lɛ. Baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ feɔ blɔfo. ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ

english: How can I tell if my harvested maize is dry enough to store safely without rotting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛto shweshweeshwe ni efiteee?

english: When maize is harvested, it still holds moisture inside the grain. If you store it wet, mold grows quickly, causing rot. A simple test is biting a grain or using the salt test: if the grain makes a sharp 'crack' sound and doesn't dent, the moisture is low enough for long-term storage.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmãa lɛ, ehiɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lolo. Kɛ akɛto he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, Mold lɛ daa oya, ni ehaa egboɔ. Kaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo Eji kɛtsɔ ŋmaa lɛ ŋmɔmɔ loo ŋmei kaa lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmaa lɛ feɔ ‘pop’ gbɛɛmɔ ni naa wa ni ebɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, no lɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Rice grains break during milling mostly if they were dried unevenly under scorching afternoon sun or harvested too late when brittle. Drying harvested rice slowly in thin layers prevents cracking so the whole grain stays intact during processing.
ga: Omɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baagbala yɛ be mli ni aŋmɔɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ agbi amɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. aloo akpa sɛɛ tsɔ beni egbɔjɔ Kɛ́ akpa ŋmãa lɛ blɛoo blɛoo yɛ ŋmãa bibioo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmãa naa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni atsuɔ he nii lɛ.

english: Why do buyers offer me lower prices when my harvested grain has small stones and dirt mixed in it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nihelɔ lɛ kɛ jara ni baa shi ha mi lɛ? Akɛni mi dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ mli tɛi bibii Kɛ muji ni efutu mli lɛ yɔɔ mli hewɔ lɛ?

english: Stones and trash damage processing machines and reduce the food's market value. Clean, well-sieved grain meets standard quality guidelines, allowing processors to offer you top price without taking on extra cleaning costs.
ga: Tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ fiteɔ tɛi kɛ jwɛi, ni ehaa niyenii ni jara wa lɛ baa shi. Dumɔwui ni he tse ni akwɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni kɔɔ bɔ ni amɛhi ha lɛ kpãa gbee. Enɛ haa mɔ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ haa bo jara ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ ni ekɛ shika kroko fataaa he kɛsaa he.

english: Why do my stored cowpeas and beans get eaten by small black insects even when kept in sealed bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii diji bibii yeɔ mi tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ akɛto kotokui ni atsĩ naa mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils lay invisible eggs inside the seeds while the crop is still in the field. After harvest, those eggs hatch inside the bag. Using hermetic (airtight) storage bags suffocates the insects and stops them from destroying your crop.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa amɛ yɛ dumɔwui amli be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. kpamɔ sɛɛ Nakai ŋmeii lɛ baafɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ kotoku ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (vacuum) tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha kooloi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: If I am not ready to sell my harvest immediately, how can I safely hold my crop until prices go up?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mifeee klalo akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ minibii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ hu? Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ato shweshweeshwe kɛyashi jara baaya ŋwɛi?

english: To safely hold crops, store them off concrete floors on wooden pallets, away from damp walls, and in a well-ventilated storage room or warehouse. This prevents moisture buildup and keeps pests from ruining your grain while you wait for better market prices.
ga: Bɔni afee ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ato shweshweeshwe To amɛ yɛ kɔnkrit shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ. kɛjɛ gbogboi ni mli efɔ kɛ nitoohe loo nitoohe ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni baa lɛ naa ni ebaatsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite oŋmaa lɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why does my bag of harvested maize weigh less after sitting in storage for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baagi ni mikɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ tsiimɔ baa shi beni mikɛto otsii fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grain naturally loses water weight as moisture evaporates into the air during drying. Grain borers and small pests also eat the inside of the seeds, which reduces the overall weight of your bag.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa ehee lɛ nu lɛ mli tsiimɔ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Dumɔwui amli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii hu yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Enɛ haa obaagi lɛ mli tsiimɔ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my cocoa beans turn black and moldy while drying on the mat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa beans mold when they stay wet for too long or get caught in rain. Cocoa needs constant sunlight, warm airflow, and regular turning on raised wooden mats so all sides dry fast before mold fungi can take over.
ga: Cocoa yibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ loo nugbɔ nɛ. Cocoa hia hulu la daa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ, kɛ saatso lɛ gbelemɔ daa. Enɛ baaha fãi lɛ fɛɛ agbi oya dani ŋmɔtɔ abaye nɔ.

english: What happens to my groundnuts if I leave them in the soil too long before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani mikpa?

english: If groundnuts stay buried past maturity, the stems attaching the pods to the plant weaken and snap, leaving nuts lost in the dirt. Over-mature groundnuts also attract soil fungi and termites that spoil the seed quality.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ tee nɔ afu aahu kɛyashi eda kwraa lɛ, Tso lɛ shishifãi ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ tso lɛ he lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ebaakumɔ. ni haa ŋmeii lɛ laajeɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii ni egbɔ fe nine lɛ hu gbalaa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Why does a dangerous green or yellow powder form on my stored maize when the room is warm and humid?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powda ko ni yɔɔ oshara ni ji eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ nɔ beni tsu lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ?

english: That powder is a harmful mold known as aflatoxin, which thrives when moist crops are kept in hot, unventilated spaces. Aflatoxins make the crop toxic and unsafe for humans and animals to eat, ruining your crop's market value.
ga: Nakai powda lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ oshara ni atsɛɔ lɛ aflatoxin. Enɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni mli efɔ lɛ wo mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Aflatoxins haa tsei feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni ebɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha adesai kɛ kooloi ni amɛyeɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ jara ni okɛwoɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: How do modern cleaning machines separate dirt and light husks from my harvested grain?
ga: Te ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ muji kɛ ŋmeii ni waaa kɛjɛɔ miŋmaa ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Cleaning machines use strong air blowers and vibrating screens with different mesh sizes. The wind blows away light dust and husks, while the screens separate heavy stones and dirt from the good, solid grains.
ga: Mɔ ni tsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ muji lɛ kɛ tsɔne ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ mli wa waa kɛ tsɔnei ni hosoɔ ni tsɔnei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ dalɛi srɔtoi tsuɔ nii. Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ sũ kɛ ŋmeii bibii, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni tsii kɛ muji gbalaa dumɔwui bibii ni wa lɛ ateŋ.

english: Which specific type of maize should I plant if I want to make my own nutritious feed for my livestock?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ esa akɛ makwɛ kɛji miisumɔ ni mafee niyenii ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli maha mikooloi lɛ?

english: Quality Protein Maize (QPM) varieties like 'Obatanpa' are best for feed because they contain higher levels of essential amino acids (lysine and tryptophan). This helps livestock grow faster and stay healthier compared to feeding them regular white maize.
ga: Protein ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ (QPM) tamɔ ‘Obatanpa’ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha niyenii ejaakɛ amino acids ni he hiaa yɛ mli. (lysine kɛ tryptophan) ni fa babaoo lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛnáa hewalɛ kɛ akɛto ŋmãa yɛŋ ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ he.

english: Why do poultry farmers prefer growing yellow maize instead of white maize for chicken feed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi akwɛlɔi sumɔɔ ni amɛdu ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ moŋ fe ŋmãa yɛŋ akɛ kooloi aniyenii lɛ?

english: Yellow maize contains natural pigments called carotenoids. When chickens eat yellow maize, these pigments naturally make the egg yolks a rich yellow color and improve the yellow skin color of meat chickens, which market buyers prefer.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni atsɛɔ amɛ carotenoids yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ mli. Kɛji kooloi ye ŋmãa ni ji ŋmɔtɔ Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔi nɛɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli. ni eha tsina loo lɛ hewolo nɔ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ Enɛ ji nɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ sumɔɔ.

english: Why are my soybean leaves turning pale yellow even though the plants are getting water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi soybean baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ miiná nu moŋ lɛ?

english: Soybeans need helpful bacteria in the soil to capture nitrogen from the air. If the soil lacks these bacteria or proper soil nutrients, the leaves turn yellow because the crop cannot produce enough nitrogen to grow green and healthy.
ga: Soybeans he miihia bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni enyɛ emɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ bacteria loo niyenii ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ejaakɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to feed fresh raw cassava directly from the farm to my farm animals?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mahã ŋmei ŋmɔŋ ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ? Kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛtee miŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ anɔ?

english: Raw cassava roots contain natural toxic chemicals called cyanogenic glycosides that can harm or kill animals. You must peel, chop, and thoroughly sun-dry or ferment the cassava first to safely remove these toxins before feeding them.
ga: Tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni atsɛɔ lɛ cyanogen glycosides ni baanyɛ aye kooloi awui loo egbe amɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii shishifãi ni ahoko lɛ amli. Esa akɛ ofolɔ, ofolɔ, ni ogbi loo okɛwo ŋmei lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ koni ojie nɛkɛ tsofai fɔji nɛɛ shweshweeshwe dani okɛ niyenii aha lɛ.

english: Why does sorghum survive long dry spells better than maize during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa hiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Sorghum has a deeper root system that reaches underground moisture, and its leaves roll up tightly during heat to stop water loss. It can go dormant when it is dry and start growing again as soon as rain falls.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔtɔ he. Ni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛ́ edɔ amɛ koni nu ni hoɔ lɛ akpa. Ebaanyɛ ehi shi kɛji egbi ni ebɔi dalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ pɛ.

english: How does planting cowpea alongside my maize crop help my maize grow better?
ga: Te cowpea ni akɛfataa ŋmãa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpea is a legume that pulls nitrogen gas from the air and stores it in the soil through its roots. The neighboring maize plant feeds on this extra soil nitrogen, helping it grow larger and greener without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abɛi tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ sũ mli nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni edaa ni ekɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kpãaa gbee ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why does my harvested maize develop mold and rot quickly when I store it in sacks right after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa oya ni egboɔ kɛ́ mikɛwo kotokui amli beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grain holds trapped moisture. If you bag it before drying it thoroughly under the sun to a low moisture level, heat builds up inside the bag, causing deadly molds like aflatoxin to ruin the crop.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa ehee lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛwo kotoku mli dani ogbi lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ, Dɔlɛ baabua ehe naa yɛ kotoku lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni gbeɔ mɔ tamɔ aflatoxin baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do I pick the right cassava stems to ensure my new planting yields big tubers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tso ni sa koni mitso hee ni midu lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji?

english: Select mature, healthy stems from the middle section of a harvest-ready plant that is 8 to 12 months old. Avoid stems that are too young, thin, dry, or showing signs of insect disease, as they will not sprout strong roots.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni edara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni esa akɛ akpa ni amɛye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ ateŋ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni darako tsɔ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni egbi, loo ni jieɔ kooloi ahela he okadii akpo lɛ ahe. Ejaakɛ ebaaha shishifãi lɛ akafee nɔ ni wa.

english: How can I tell the exact time my soybean crop is mature enough to harvest before the pods burst open?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni mi-soybeans lɛ eda bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa dani ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Soybeans are ready when most of the leaves dry up, turn yellow, and fall off, leaving brown pods on the stem. If you shake a pod and hear the seeds rattling inside, harvest immediately before the hot sun cracks the pods open.
ga: Soybean lɛ efee klalo beni baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo egbi lɛ. Etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbeeɔ shi, ni eshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ji ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛji okpokpo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ni onu dumɔwui lɛ ni miihoso yɛ Harvest mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli agbala.

english: Why should I alternate planting groundnuts and maize on the same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii atsake yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously depletes the soil and attracts pests like fall armyworms. Rotating with groundnuts restores natural nitrogen to the soil and starves maize pests, giving you a bigger maize yield in the next season.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ be fɛɛ be ni egbalaa ŋmeii tamɔ fall armyworms. Peanut ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. ni hɔmɔ aye kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmãa babaoo yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if a piece of land is suitable for planting my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ko hi kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Good land for maize has dark, rich soil that drains water well and is not full of large rocks. If water sits on the ground for days after rain, or if the soil is too dry and sandy, your crops will struggle to grow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛha ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ ni baa nii. Etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni tɛi wuji bɛ Kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ Ebaawa kɛha onibii ni oduɔ lɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my crops grow well on one side of my farm but stay small and weak on the other side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ? Shi eji bibioo ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ afã kroko lɛ nɔ.

english: Soil quality can change even across a small piece of land. Some areas may have deeper, richer soil with better water retention, while other spots might have hidden rocks, poor nutrients, or hard clay that stops roots from growing.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su baanyɛ atsake yɛ hei bibii po. Ekolɛ hei komɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni nu yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni hiɛɔ nu jogbaŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni otii krokomɛi Ekolɛ tɛi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ. niyenii ni esaaa loo shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni tsiɔ shishifãi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃

english: How does clearing and loosening the soil before planting actually help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni mijieɔ ni mijieɔ lɛ dani miduɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Clearing removes weeds that steal water and plant food from your crops. Loosening the soil allows roots to spread easily, helps rain sink into the ground, and lets air reach the roots so the crop stays healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ otsi ohe lɛ, ebaajie jwɛi ni juɔ nu ni oduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe koni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I clear weeds and clear my land early, will it help my crops perform better when rainy season starts?
ga: Kɛji mifo jwɛi ni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mra Ani ebaaye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Yes, preparing your land early gives the soil time to settle and retains moisture. It also ensures your crops get a clean start without competing against fast-growing weeds as soon as the first rains fall.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ he saamɔ mra. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná be ni ekɛba shi ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Ehaa onibii ni oduɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ hu ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ pɛ lɛ akaŋ.

english: How do I decide how many cassava stems I should plant on my plot of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ ŋmei tsei enyiɛ ni esa akɛ madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he?

english: The number of cassava stems depends on the size of your land and the correct spacing between plants. Leaving about one meter between plants ensures each crop gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and water to produce large tubers.
ga: Kasava tsei lɛ ayibɔ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ kɛ he ni sa ni tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi gbɛ ni miihe ashɛ mita kome yɛ tsei ateŋ koni tso fɛɛ tso aná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for light, water, and plant food. This leads to tall, thin, weak plants that produce very low yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tsei amli. Enɛ haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo kwraa lɛ baa.

english: Why do some crops need full sunlight while others do better with shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa he hiaa tsei komɛi lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi taoɔ hulu la babaoo lɛ?

english: Crops like maize and tomatoes need full sunlight to make food and grow strong. Other plants, like young cocoa, burn easily in harsh sun and need shade from taller plants like plantains to survive their early months.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ tomato he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔni afee niyenii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Tsei krokomɛi, tamɔ kookoo bibii, shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Ni ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji lɛ amli.

english: Is it good for me to plant the exact same crop on the same piece of land every single year?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi?

english: No, planting the same crop in the same spot every year drains the specific plant foods that crop needs and allows pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Changing crops keeps the soil balanced and healthy.
ga: Dabi, tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni adu yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ baajie tso lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant legumes like beans together with my main crops to improve my yield?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa, tamɔ ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa titri koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Yes, legumes like beans or cowpeas add natural food back into the soil, which helps companion crops grow better. They also cover the ground to stop weeds from taking over.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni fata he lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ. Amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu koni jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: How does planning what to plant ahead of time help me get a better harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mito nɔ ni mikɛbaadu lɛ he gbɛjianɔ kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua mi ni maná ŋmaa kpakpa?

english: Planning helps you choose the right seeds for your soil, buy the right amount of supplies, and plant at the right time before the rains start, ensuring your crops reach full strength.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo yeɔ ebua bo ni ohalaa dumɔwui ni sa kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ. Hemɔ nibii ni sa. ni odu yɛ be ni sa mli dani nugbɔ lɛ aje shishi. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná hewalɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Applying NPK fertilizer or well-decomposed animal manure around the root area helps restore healthy green leaves and improves crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni ehaa tsei lɛ ayibii yaa hiɛ.

english: Is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize?
ga: Ani tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa baadu lɛ he baaba sɛɛnamɔ kɛha mi?

english: Yes, planting legumes like cowpeas alongside maize improves soil health. Legumes capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, which helps feed the maize crop naturally.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa kɛfata ŋmãa he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Legumes lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmãa lɛ aye kooloi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is often caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips sucking the plant juices, or viruses spread by insects. Spraying neem seed oil extract or appropriate insecticides helps manage these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa Neem dumɔwui amli fɔ ni ajieɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akwɛ nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ anɔ.

english: This condition is known as blossom end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often made worse by irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture consistent helps tomato roots take up calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Ni bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa hela lɛ he okadii lɛ mli woɔ wu yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tomato shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Premature drying of yam leaves is commonly caused by a fungal leaf disease called anthracnose. Planting disease-resistant yam varieties and practicing crop rotation prevents the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato baai lɛ agbiɔ oya. Sweet potato henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ koni helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when stressed by dry weather, poor soil nutrients, or insect attacks like mirids. Maintaining shade trees and protecting trees from insects encourages flowers to turn into full pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni tutuaa mɛi tamɔ atatui. Tso lɛ ni oooha ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni etsɔɔ baai ni eyi obɔ.

english: Plantains have shallow roots and become heavy when fruiting, making them vulnerable to wind and root pests like nematodes. Supporting the main stem with strong bamboo forks or wooden poles prevents them from falling.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛhe wa kɛji amɛwo yibii. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes lɛ nyɛɔ efiteɔ lɛ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni wa fĩ tso titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekagbee shi.

english: Cassava tubers rot underground when water collects around the roots due to poor soil drainage during rainy seasons. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ hewɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Will planting my seeds very close together give me a higher yield at harvest?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha yibiiwoo babaoo aba kɛ́ akpa?

english: No, planting too close forces crops to compete for sunlight, water, and nutrients, resulting in small and weak plants. Giving crops proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough resources to produce a full yield.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaafite hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha efee tso bibioo ni bɛ hewalɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo eŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to weed my farm when the crops are still tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? He ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops are weak and grow slowly if weeds steal their nutrients, water, and sunlight. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks allows your crops to establish strong root systems early.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaada oya kɛji jwɛi ju amɛ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli wa mra.

english: Why are the maize seeds I bought from the local market sprouting unevenly compared to certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ kwɛɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Certified seeds undergo strict quality checks to ensure high germination rates and strong growth. Uncertified market seeds may be mixed with old, damaged, or low-quality grains that fail to sprout properly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni amɛhi ha lɛ mlikwɛmɔi ni mli wa mli koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdaraa waa. Abaanyɛ akɛ jarayeli dumɔwui ni bɛ he odaseyeli lɛ afutu dumɔwui ni egbɔ, ni efite, loo ni ehiii ni nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why are my yam vines staying stunted and thin despite receiving plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ? He ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ lɛ?

english: Using infected seed yams or applying unverified soil treatments can damage the root system, preventing the crop from absorbing nutrients and water efficiently even during rainy weather.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ sweet potatoes ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ tsu nii loo akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsofai ni anaaa odaseyeli tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kɛ nu jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli po.

english: Why did my cassava leaves turn yellow and drop right after I applied a roadside weedkiller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ trukaa ni amɛgbee shi beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ gbɛjegbɛ he lɛ tsu nii sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Substandard or counterfeit agrochemicals often contain harsh, unapproved ingredients or improper chemical mixes that burn and shock crop foliage instead of selectively killing weeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, agrochemicals ni esaaa loo amalei lɛ mli nibii ni mli wa ni bɛ he odaseyeli loo tsofai ni esaaa yɔɔ mli. ni shãa tso lɛ baai lɛ ni ekpokpoɔ Yɛ jwɛi ni ahalaa lɛ agbemɔ najiaŋ

english: Why are fall armyworms still eating my maize after I sprayed them with pesticide?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ yeɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ lolo beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ eshwie nɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fake or expired pesticides sold by unauthorized dealers lack the correct active ingredients to control pests, leaving your crops unprotected despite being treated.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi amalei loo ni amɛbe eho ni mɛi ni hɔ̃ɔ ni amɛhaaa hegbɛ lɛ hɔ̃ɔ lɛ bɛ nibii ni sa ni tsuɔ nii ni akɛyeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, kɛ́ atsa po lɛ, abuuu onibii ahe.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off instead of turning into fruits after using a growth booster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai beni mikɛ tsofa ko ni haa mɔ daa lɛ etsu nii sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Unregulated growth chemicals can create toxic chemical stress or nutrient imbalances in plants, causing flowers to drop prematurely instead of setting fruit.
ga: Tsofai ni anyɛɛɛ akudɔ ni haa tsei lɛ daraa lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ejaaa aba tsei amli. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: How can I tell if the spots on my plantain leaves are from a crop disease or from chemical burn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi plantain baai lɛ anɔ lɛ jɛ tso hela ko mli loo tsofa ko ni shãa lɛ mli?

english: Chemical burns appear rapidly as dry, erratic patches where spray drops landed, whereas biological leaf diseases spread slowly and naturally from leaf to leaf across your farm.
ga: Tsofai ni shãa lɛ jeɔ kpo oya yɛ gbɛ ni egbi, ni bɛ shiŋŋ nɔ, ni nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ tsei amli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa fiofio. kɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛjɛɔ baa nɔ kɛyaa baa nɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why did my cowpea crop die after I sprayed the neighboring maize field with pest control?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ gbo beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie ŋmãa ŋmɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Strong agrochemicals can drift through the air onto neighboring delicate crops, poisoning their leaves and stopping their natural growth process.
ga: Okwaayeli mli tsofai ni mli wa baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ ni he hiaa waa lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa ebaai lɛ feɔ poison ni ehaa bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa lɛ kpaa adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is my pepper farm producing very large leaves but failing to grow any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ baai wuji waa shi enyɛɛɛ ewo pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Using fake or improperly balanced fertilizers high in nitrogen encourages the plant to put all its energy into growing tall leaves rather than forming flowers and fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛfee loo ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu baai kakadaji ni yaa hiɛ lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe ni eeewo fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai.

english: Why are buyers rejecting my cocoa beans even though the pods looked healthy on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ mi-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Using unapproved farm chemicals can leave harmful chemical residues inside the cocoa beans, causing them to fail safety and quality checks conducted by export buyers.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔji ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ ashi tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ kookoo ŋmeii amli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, eshɛɛɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ kɛ kpakpafeemɔ he kwɛmɔi ni mɛi ni heɔ nibii kɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ feɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables spoil so quickly on the way to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ fite oya yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops treated with poor nutrients or harvested too soon after applying unregulated sprays lack firm plant tissue, causing them to rot rapidly during transport.
ga: Tsei ni akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ loo ni akpaa mra tsɔ yɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akudɔɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baaná tso mli fãji ni etse. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akɛ amɛ tee gbɛfaa mli.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the soil runs out of nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to keep leaves green and strong.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ba shi. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so plant roots can soak it in; putting it on dry soil can burn and damage the roots instead of feeding the crop.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã ni efite shishifãi lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farmland before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmãa?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, which naturally fertilizes the ground for heavy feeding crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight, so fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as natural umbrellas to shade the young cocoa.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, kookoo tsei ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋtayaai, ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo.

english: When planted too close together, crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks and small, weak cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and getting smaller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies sucking on the leaves.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmei mli lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Egbɛɔ eshwaa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nuɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: High humidity and continuous rain help fungal spores spread through water splashes, causing Black Pod disease to quickly rot the cocoa pods.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni mli wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ haa ŋmeii amli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nu mli ŋmeii amli. Ekɛ black pod hela baa, ni no haa cocoa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering, as the plant tries to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tso lɛ miitao ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato koni wala akafite.

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal fertilizer and soil nutrients much faster than your crops can absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Cassava is usually mature when its bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off naturally, and the soil near the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yuccas lɛ daa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a cry for food, specifically nitrogen. When the soil lacks nitrogen or when heavy rains wash away the nutrients, the plant cannot make enough food to stay green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji niyenii he foomɔ. titri lɛ nitrogen Kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ laajeɔ. Tsei nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛhi shi ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do people say that planting groundnuts on my farmland will make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, which means they have a special relationship with helpful soil bacteria. They pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant there next.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyɛ wekukpaa krɛdɛɛ ko kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ jɛmɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow very tall with many green leaves but refuse to produce any flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo shi ewooo fɔfɔi loo aduawai ko lɛ?

english: This usually happens when the plant gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich manure. The plant uses all its energy to grow big stems and leaves, forgetting to make flowers and fruits, so you need to balance the soil with nutrients like phosphorus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo tsei agboi kɛ baai. Kɛtsɔ hiɛ ni oookpa fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai afeemɔ nɔ No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs lɛ ato shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds early instead of waiting for them to grow big on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mamɛ ni jwɛi lɛ adara yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Weeds are like greedy neighbors; they drink the water, steal the manure, and block the sunlight meant for your crops. Removing them early stops them from starving your crops while they are still weak.
ga: Jwɛi tamɔ akutsoŋbii hiɛjoolɔi. Amɛnuɔ nu, amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ anaa. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni hɔmɔ akaye amɛ be mli ni amɛgbɔjɔ lolo lɛ.

english: Why must I put sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tso yɛ shikpɔŋ koni mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce energy that builds big tubers underground. Staking raises the leaves off the damp ground, giving them maximum light while protecting them from rot and pests.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato baai lɛ amɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi hulutsoo bei wuji baa lɛ. Staking baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa kane babaoo yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui ahe.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings droop and die shortly after I move them from the nursery bed into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Moving seedlings causes 'transplant shock' because their delicate roots get disturbed and dried out. Moving them late in the afternoon or on cloudy days, and watering them immediately, helps them settle in without dying.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ lɛ haa Amɛnaa ‘transplant shock’ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ haoɔ ni amɛgbiɔ. Tsi ohe leebi maŋkpa loo yɛ gbi ni atatu yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, ha amɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛkagboi.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rain collects and stays in the soil without draining away, the roots suffocate and harmful fungal diseases attack, causing them to rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ babaoo buaa ehe naa ni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ mli. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ tutuaa amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without turning into small tomatoes during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato bibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the weather gets extremely hot and dry, the tomato plant gets stressed to conserve water. It drops its flowers to save energy because it feels it cannot support new fruits without enough water.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu nu he. Ekɛ efɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he ejaakɛ enuɔ he akɛ enyɛŋ ekwɛ aduawai heei anɔ kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree leaves burn and dry up when I cut down all the large timber trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mifo tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ? Kookoo tsei fɛɛ?

english: Cocoa plants, especially young ones, naturally prefer partial shade. Removing surrounding large trees exposes them to harsh, direct sunlight and strong winds, which scorches their leaves and dehydrates the plant.
ga: Cocoa tsei, titri lɛ gbekɛbii lɛ, sumɔɔ hulutsoo fioo. Tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa. Enɛ baa shã baai lɛ ni eha tso lɛ mli agbɔjɔ nu.

english: Why do caterpillars destroy my cabbage leaves much faster during the rainy season than in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fiteɔ kaabii baai yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli oya fe hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: The cool, moist weather in the rainy season creates the perfect conditions for moths to lay eggs on cabbage leaves, causing many more hungry caterpillars to hatch quickly and eat the crop.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ amɛwui yɛ kaabe baa nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii babaoo ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ fɔɔ oya ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize needs nitrogen nutrient. When there isn't enough food in the soil, the maize plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves and sends it to the top to keep the new growth alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen niyenii he miihia o-abele lɛ. Kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Abɛi lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni ekɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha shweremɔ hee lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning black and rotting before they get chance to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium inside the fruit. It often happens when watering is uneven, which makes it hard for plant roots to pull calcium out of the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow so many bushy leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ hiɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Using too much chemical fertilizer high in nitrogen makes cowpeas spend all their energy growing leaves instead of flowers. Cowpeas naturally make their own nitrogen from the air, so extra nitrogen prevents good pod growth.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa cowpea kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ ebaa lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe efɔfɔi lɛ. Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ baatsi pod kpakpa ni eda lɛ naa.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like pencils during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ pensil yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's natural defense against heat. By curling its leaves inward, the maize plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun to protect itself from losing water.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Abɛi haa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ ebaai ni ekɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava stem cuttings take so long to sprout leaves when I plant them in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei ni afolɔ mli lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani baai lɛ shwereɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings need moisture to awake their sleeping roots and buds. In dry soil, the stem pauses its growth to save energy until rains come.
ga: Cassava tso ni afo lɛ he hiaa nu koni ekɛte shishifãi ni ewɔ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashi. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato kɛyashi nugbɔ baa.

english: A cocoa tree produces many more flowers than it can feed. The tree naturally drops most of its flowers so it only saves energy for the pods it has enough water and nutrients to grow.
ga: Kookoo tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ ekwɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ náa hewalɛ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaadara.

english: Why did my mango tree yield plenty of fruits last year but gave me almost nothing this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango wo yibii babaoo yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli shi afi nɛɛ ewooo kwraa lɛ?

english: Mango trees often practice 'alternate bearing.' Producing a huge harvest uses up almost all the tree's stored food reserves, so it spends the next year building up strength instead of making fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɔɔ mango tsei lɛ ‘Alternating bearing’ Nibii babaoo ni anáa lɛ yeɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ tso lɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ekɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛtswaa hewalɛ emaa shi moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking juices from the young leaves, which damages the leaf tissues as they expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Enɛ baafite baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ be mli ni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to stay short and weak even when there is bright sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ kuku ni egbɔjɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa po lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that act like extra mouths in the ground, stealing water and soil nutrients before your crop's roots can drink them.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ daaŋ krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ.

english: Why is it necessary to heap soil around my yam plants instead of planting them on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ okɛ sũ ato sweet potato tso he moŋ fe ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ?

english: Yam tubers grow downwards into soft soil. Making soil mounds creates loose dirt so the tuber can expand easily into a large, straight yam without fighting hard, compacted ground.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ. Gɔŋ ko ni afee lɛ haa muji ni mli tse baa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni ja ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ hei ni wa ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ akpee.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and burning at the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiishã yɛ amɛnaagbee lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very delicate and burn easily under direct sunshine. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains near them creates a living canopy that shelters young cocoa leaves from scorching heat and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava leaves look crumpled, twisted, and yellowish instead of bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ekpɔtɔ, etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is usually caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting certified, disease-resistant stem cuttings stops the virus from spreading and ensures your plants produce large tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Adumɔ tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ Ebaakpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do I see small holes and chewed edges on my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? kɛ ŋmeii ni atsɔ mli yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: This damage is typically caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the central leaves of young maize plants and feed on them. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended natural or chemical controls saves the growing tip so the plant can yield full corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai amli ni eyeɔ amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu dalɛ he ŋaawoi lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ anyɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to grow big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ koni ekɛwo bulbs wuji lɛ?

english: Yam plants manufacture food in their leaves using sunlight. Climbing up tall stakes lifts the leaves off the ground so they catch maximum light and fresh air, which sends essential energy down into the ground to build bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ, ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aba babaoo. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛfee yitso ni da.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push stalks down into the dirt after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miitsi eshishifã lɛ kɛmiiya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni ewo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut flowers bloom above ground, but once pollinated, the plant grows specialized stalks called 'pegs' that bend down and push into the soil. The actual groundnuts grow and ripen underground, where they stay safe from sun damage and surface pests.
ga: Peanut fɔfɔii fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ pollinated Tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ ‘pegs’ ni shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peanuts kwɛ̃ɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Amɛbaafee shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ hulu kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when the weather gets extremely hot or when soil moisture bounces between too dry and too wet. Giving plants steady, consistent water and mulch keeps soil cool and helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ shwie shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni edɔ tsɔ teŋ. Nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa, ni afeɔ amɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why are my maize plants turning pale yellow and staying small even during heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ bibioo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall can wash essential soil food like nitrogen down deep into the earth where plant roots cannot reach it. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer puts nutrients back near the surface so plants regain dark green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba ebɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ aná baai eŋɔli ni eda waa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops give me smaller harvests when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too tightly, every plant competes for the same limited soil nutrients, ground moisture, and sunlight. Spacing plants according to recommended guidelines gives roots enough room to spread and collect food.
ga: Beni adu dumɔwui lɛ babaoo tsɔ Tsei fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei ni akɛto he yɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni atsɔɔ lɛ naa lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛbua niyenii naa.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small, light bunches when I leave all the suckers growing around the mother tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ daa bibii ni ehiɛ waaa beni mishwieɔ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: Having too many shoots around one mother plantain tree drains vital nutrients away from the main stem. Cutting away weaker suckers and leaving only one or two healthy shoots lets the main tree direct all its food into growing a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Ni aaana yitsei babaoo ni ebɔle Dumɔwu kome he lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii bibii ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aŋɔ eniyenii fɛɛ ni eda ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava stem cuttings rot in the soil instead of sprouting leaves during dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings need a small amount of soil moisture to start growing roots and leaf buds. Planting cuttings into completely dried-out soil causes the wood to lose moisture and die before root growth can begin.
ga: Cassava tso lɛ mli tsei ni afolɔ lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fioo ko koni shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ aje shishi amɛdara. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni afolɔ awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ mli nu lɛ afee shoo ni egbo dani shishifãi lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why are my tomatoes developing black, rotten spots at the bottom before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is usually blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium or uneven watering. Giving your tomatoes regular water and adding wood ash or lime to the soil helps prevent the bottoms from rotting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ eji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni faaa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato lɛ nɔ daa ni okɛ tso sũ loo lime fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ akafite.

english: Tomato leaves curl and turn yellow due to heat stress, dry soil, or viral sicknesses carried by tiny insects like whiteflies. Keeping the soil moist and controlling small pests helps protect the leaves.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni akudɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomatoes split open while they are still growing on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli gbalaa be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Tomatoes crack open when they get a sudden rush of water after a dry spell, causing the inside to grow faster than the skin can stretch. Watering your crop regularly keeps the skin stretching evenly.
ga: Tomato baatswa kɛji nu lɛ je kpo trukaa beni egbi sɛɛ. Enɛ haa mligbɛ lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaha ehewolo lɛ agbɛ ashwã pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing huge green leaves but failing to produce any flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi enyɛɛɛ ewo fɔfɔi loo aduawai lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes tomato plants spend all their energy growing leaves instead of fruits. Using balanced fertilizers with phosphorus helps the plant produce plenty of flowers and fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai amli yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni phosphorus yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai babaoo.

english: Why does my lettuce rot and turn soft right near the soil before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-lettuce lɛ miifite ni efee blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ masɛi dani akpa lɛ?

english: Lettuce rots at the bottom when wet soil constantly touches the lower leaves, causing fungal disease. Planting on raised beds and watering only around the roots helps keep the leaves dry and healthy.
ga: Lettuce fiteɔ yɛ baai lɛ ashishi kɛji shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ kpe be fɛɛ be, ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa. Kɛ́ adu yɛ saatsoi ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ ni awo shishifãi lɛ pɛ nu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is my lettuce growing tall with flower shoots and tasting bitter?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-lettuce lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Ani eyɛ fɔfɔii ashishifãi kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa?

english: When hot weather sets in, lettuce prepares to make seeds by growing tall and producing bitter juices. Harvesting lettuce early in the morning and planting during cooler periods keeps it sweet and fresh.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, Lettuce saa ehe kɛha dumɔwui kɛtsɔ shweremɔ ni ekɛ nu ni ŋɔɔ baa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ otsi lettuce leebi ni odu yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli ejɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehiɛ afee fɛo ni eha mɔ tsui anyɔ emli.

english: Why are small green worms eating big holes in my lettuce leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miiye buji wuji ni yɔɔ mi lettuce baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those green worms are caterpillars hatched from eggs laid by moths. Picking them off by hand early in the morning or using natural neem leaf sprays keeps your crop undamaged for buyers.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ onine shwie amɛ leebi loo okɛ adebɔɔ mli neem tso ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why are tiny white insects hiding underneath the leaves of my vegetable plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yɛŋ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-vegetable tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Those insects are whiteflies, which hide on the underside of leaves to suck plant sap and spread diseases. Spraying underneath the leaves with mild soapy water or neem oil helps wash them away.
