ga: Nakai kooloi lɛ ji ŋmeii yɛŋ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ashishi koni amɛnu tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛgbɛ helai amɛshwã. Ni akɛ nu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ. Aloo neem fɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni afɔ he.

english: Why do my vegetable crops suffer from dark leaf spots mostly during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɛ baai diji yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain splashes mud carrying fungal spores onto lower leaves, and damp weather helps diseases spread fast. Trimming the bottom leaves and giving plants space allows air to dry them quickly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ muji ni hiɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Kɛ́ afo baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni aha tso lɛ gbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni egbiɔ oya.

english: How can I prevent my harvested tomatoes from crushing and spoiling on the way to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-tomato lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ ni efite yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Harvest tomatoes early in the morning while it is cool, transport them in wooden or plastic crates instead of heavy sacks, and keep them shaded to stop them from softening and rotting.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ tomato leebi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Okɛ tomato awo tso loo plastic adekai amli moŋ fe kotokui ni tsii. Ni ha tomatoi lɛ ahi he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ koni amɛkafee blɛoo ni amɛkafite.

english: What is eating the leaves of my young maize plants and leaving tiny holes inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni ji mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai ni ayeɔ ni ashiɔ bu bibii? Yɛ tsɔne lɛ mli?

english: This is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They burrow into the leaf whorls of maize during early growth, so early detection and applying targeted pest control like neem extract or recommended insecticides early in the morning is essential.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛfoɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, mra ni ana kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ neem mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ he miihia waa.

english: Why are the leaves of my hot pepper plants curling upward and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is often caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips, aphids, or mites, or by a plant virus they carry. Spraying soapy water or suitable organic pest controls helps clear the insects so new leaves can grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ ŋmeii tamɔ thrips, aphids loo mites, loo tsei amli helai ni amɛhiɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ koni baai heei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow tall with plenty of leafy stems, but the tubers underground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes cassava focus all its energy on leaf and stem growth instead of expanding its underground tubers. Cassava needs balanced nutrients with enough potassium to develop thick, healthy roots.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baa kɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, Cassava he miihia niyenii ni sa kɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni mli wa aba.

english: Cowpeas and beans are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in their roots. When the crop season ends, decaying roots release this natural fertilizer into the soil for the next crop to feed on.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Beni dumɔ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Shishifãi ni miifite lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aye.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat, dry winds, or irregular watering. Covering the soil with organic mulch and watering regularly keeps the soil cool and moist, helping flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Kɛ́ okɛ organic mulch wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni okɛ nu wo mli daa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii

english: Why do the edges of my plantain leaves turn brown and dry up during the sunny dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ ashishigbɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves have large surface areas that lose moisture quickly under hot sun. When the soil lacks enough water, the plant cuts off water supply to leaf edges to protect its main stem.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni da ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ fiteɔ oya. Beni nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ ŋmɛɔ nu ni yaa baai lɛ ahe lɛ mli koni ekɛbu tso lɛ shishigbɛ titri lɛ he.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete against each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in thin, weak stalks that fall over easily and produce small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya ni amɛhaa ŋmeii bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings scorch easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantains provide living shade to cool the seedlings and keep moisture in the soil during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo ni haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn soft and black before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni eyɛ ediŋŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot and happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by uneven watering. Consistent watering routines help prevent this problem.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot ni ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are yellow spots appearing on my garden egg leaves and making them drop off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ miije kpo yɛ eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ ni ehaa amɛshwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellow spots that turn brown are usually caused by fungal leaf spot diseases triggered by too much dampness and lack of airflow around the plant. Spacing plants well and removing infected bottom leaves stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ tso lɛ he lɛ mli baa. Tsɔɔmɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jogbaŋŋ ni ojie shishigbɛ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ koni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is lacking nitrogen, which acts as essential food for leaf growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or planting legumes in the field during the previous season helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo adu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant groundnuts or cowpeas together with our maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkɛ wɔ ŋmãa lɛ adu ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are special crops that take invisible food from the air and feed it into the soil. This natural soil food helps your maize grow bigger and stronger without relying entirely on expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni hiɛɔ niyenii mli nibii ni anaaa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa o-ŋmã lɛ ni edara ni ewaa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when heavy rain falls for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii babaoo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water stays around them for too long because the roots cannot breathe underground. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather becomes extremely hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ lɛ?

english: When the weather gets too hot and dry, pepper plants drop their flowers to save water and protect themselves from drying out completely. Covering the soil around the plants with dry grass keeps the roots cool and retains water.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni egbi Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi kwraa. Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ tsei ahe jwɛi ni egbi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, won't I harvest more food from my small piece of land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ makpa niyenii kɛjɛ he bibioo ko. Ani manyɛ maná mi nɔ babaoo?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water, leading to thin stalks and tiny corn cobs. Giving each plant proper space ensures every single plant grows full and yields a bigger harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋ, ni no haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ehaa edaa jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly and produce smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛmiiwo yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast growers that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early in the crop's life ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ gbekɛbiiashi lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their young flowers before producing tiny cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi bibii dani amɛwoɔ cacao ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from sudden dry spells, lack soil food, or get attacked by sap-sucking insects like mirids. Keeping shade trees overhead and protecting the trunk keeps the flowers attached.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ hewɔ. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ pollen lɛ tutuaa. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo ha yɛ yiteŋ ni abuɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny whitefly insects that pass a plant sickness to your crop while feeding on the leaves. Controlling these insects early and keeping the field clean prevents the sickness from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. No kɛ helai baa onibii amli beni oyeɔ baai lɛ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni aaakwɛ koni he atse lɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: How do insects get inside my dried maize grains even when I keep them inside tied bags?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kooloi bibii boteɔ mi ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ mli? Kɛ mikɛwo kotoku ni akɛfi mli po?

english: Insects or their invisible eggs often hide inside the maize cobs while the crop is still standing in the field before harvest. Drying your maize completely on clean surfaces under the hot sun and using airtight bags kills these pests before they multiply.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi loo ŋmeii ni anaaa lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii amli yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ damɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo dani akpaa ŋmãa lɛ. Abɛi ni agbiɔ yɛ he ko ni he tse yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Ni akɛ vacuum bags tsuɔ nii lɛ gbeɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛshwereɔ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting green shoots even while sitting inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ŋmɔji be mli ni mita mi-shĩa lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that start sprouting when they feel warmth and trapped moisture, thinking it is time to grow a new plant. Keeping your storage barn well-ventilated, cool, and shaded slows down this natural sprouting process.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni hiɛ ka ni jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji amɛnu he akɛ edɔ amɛ ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Jwɛŋmɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ odu tso hee. Kɛ́ oha otsu lɛ mli kɔɔyɔɔ bote mli jogbaŋŋ, eyɛ fɛ̃i, ni eyɛ hulutsoo lɛ, ebaaha bɔ ni ŋmɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ehaa lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or that heavy rains have flooded the roots, preventing them from taking up plant food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha shishifãi lɛ eyi mli obɔ. Ehaa anyɛɛɛ aye tsei aniyenii

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up when I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ egbi beni mifoɔ tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the topsoil before their roots can grow deep enough to reach hidden moisture.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ aya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛyashɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped in the soil for too long, depriving the roots of air and allowing soil fungi to multiply and attack the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. ehaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ fãa ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ babaoo ni amɛtutuaa shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my plantain suckers very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ banana tsei lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting plantains too close makes them compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in small bunches and weak stems that fall over in strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji niji bibii kɛ tsei akutsei ni bɛ hewalɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ mli.

english: What causes tiny holes in the leaves of my growing maize crops?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Mi ŋmãa ni miida lɛ baai lɛ anɔ

english: Holes in maize leaves are typically caused by caterpillars like Fall Armyworms, which feed on the fresh, soft leaves inside the center of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa.

english: Why do farmers cover the soil around their plants with dry grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛtsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass keeps the soil cool, stops moisture from escaping into the hot air, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaje kpo yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot, when the soil gets too dry or too wet, or when the plant does not get enough nutrients like phosphorus.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo edɔ tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa tamɔ fɔsfɔs nɔ.

english: The first rain is often followed by a heatwave or a dry spell; if you plant too early, the seeds will sprout but quickly dry up and die before the real rainy season starts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, latsaa loo nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji adu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagbi oya ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ aba.

english: Planting maize in the same spot repeatedly drains the specific nutrients maize needs from the soil and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abele lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do weeds lower the amount of crops I harvest at the end of the season?
ga: Te jwɛi feɔ tɛŋŋ ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ baa shi?

english: Weeds steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer intended for your crops, leaving your plants weak, small, and unable to produce maximum yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why should I start my tomato seeds in a nursery before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔi tomato dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ aya shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato seeds are very tiny and fragile. Starting them in a nursery allows you to protect young plants from heavy rains, hot sun, and pests while they are weak, ensuring only strong seedlings are moved to the main farm.
ga: Tomato dumɔwui lɛ daraaa kwraa ni amɛhe waaa. Kɛ́ obɔi tsei adumɔ yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ obuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. hulu la ni mli edɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lolo Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: When is the best time of day for me to transplant my pepper seedlings to the main farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ pepper dumɔwui awo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: It is best to transplant in the late afternoon or on a cloudy day. This keeps the sun from scorching the tender seedlings and gives them the cool night air to adjust to their new soil.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu tsei yɛ shwane mli. loo yɛ atatu gbi nɔ Enɛ baatsi hulu lɛ naa koni ekashã dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Ni ehaa amɛnáa gbɛkɛ ni mli ejɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for planting sweet peppers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha ŋmeii akwɛmɔ?

english: Sweet peppers need well-draining soil that does not collect standing water after rain. Soil rich in organic matter that feels loose and dark brown or black is ideal for their roots to grow easily.
ga: Bell peppers he miihia shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nu ni damɔ shi lɛ ehiɛɛɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ nɔ ni nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ediŋŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shishifãi ni yaa hiɛ oya.

english: Why do tomato crops perform differently when planted in different parts of Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ kɛ́ akwɛ amɛ yɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ? ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ

english: Tomatoes react strongly to local weather, air humidity, and soil type. Areas with cooler night temperatures and moderate humidity usually produce better fruit with fewer fungal diseases than hot, constantly damp areas.
ga: Tomato yɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe. kɔɔyɔɔ mli fɛ̃i kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔ Hei ni hulutsoo be mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa lɛ fɔɔ yibii kpakpai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ fioo fe hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be lɛ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing tall with lots of green leaves, but no flowers or fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miida ni amɛhe baai babaoo yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi fɔfɔii loo aduawai bɛ jɛmɛ?

english: This usually happens when plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer or lack enough sunlight. The plant uses all its energy to grow leaves instead of developing flowers that turn into tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ loo hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ enɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔ tomato.

english: Why do the leaves on my sweet pepper plants start curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi bell pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a defense sign. It is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding on the leaves, or by the plant trying to save water during extreme heat.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni buɔ mɔ he. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Aloo tsei ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu he yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It is not caused by an insect, but by a lack of calcium in the fruit, usually brought on by irregular watering while the tomato is growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Jeee koolooi kɛbaa. Shi nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni tomatoi lɛ miida lɛ.

english: How often should I water my vegetable crops during the dry period?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Young plants need light watering every day or two to keep the top soil moist, while mature plants prefer deeper watering every two to three days to encourage roots to grow deep into the ground.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni afɔ amɛ nu fioo daa gbi loo gbii enyɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ákɛ onukpai lɛ, amɛsumɔɔ nu ni mli kwɔ be fɛɛ be. Gbii enyɔ loo etɛ dani shishifãi lɛ adara kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to test a small sample of seeds before planting my whole field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maka dumɔwui bibii komɛi aka lɛ? Dani abaadu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Testing a small sample shows you how many seeds will actually sprout (germination rate). This saves you time, money, and land preparation efforts if the seeds turn out to be bad.
ga: Nɔkwɛmɔnɔ bibioo ko ni akaa Etsɔɔ dumɔwui enyiɛ ni baakwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ (kwɛ̃mɔ he akɔntaabuu). Enɛ baaha be, shika kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ mli kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɔi fitemɔ.

english: Can I plant sweet peppers on the exact same piece of land every season?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu bell peppers yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi?

english: It is better not to. Planting crops from the same family in the same place every year builds up specific pests and diseases in the soil. You should rotate them with crops like maize, cassava, or beans.
ga: Ehi akɛ ofeee nakai. Tsei ni jɛ weku kome mli ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa atsake.

english: Young cocoa plants have very tender leaves and shallow roots that burn quickly under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside your cocoa creates a protective canopy that keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii waa kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means your maize lacks nitrogen fertilizer. The plant is moving its remaining nutrients from the older bottom leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii. Tso lɛ miitsi niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛmiijɛ baai ni eda ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant groundnuts or beans on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans put natural fertilizer back into the earth. Their roots fix nitrogen from the air into the soil, which helps restore richness to your land for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ nuts kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground after long periods of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water settles around the roots for too long without draining away, the roots suffocate and rot from soil fungi.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu taraa shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf decay and encouraging larger yams.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa sweet potato lɛ ni edaraa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during rainstorms even when the stem looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbee shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli eyɛ mli akɛ etso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that do not dig deep into the earth. When the plant grows a heavy bunch of fruit, the top becomes heavy and strong winds easily pull the shallow roots out of wet soil unless supported with wooden poles.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛfooo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ tso lɛ wo aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ tsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ. Ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ oya ja tso ni akɛfiɔ sɛɛ

english: What is eating small ragged holes into the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-bibii ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeli?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the central funnel of the maize plant. Spraying safe treatment early in the morning or evening reaches them when they come out to feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Spray ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ baashɛ amɛhe beni amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye niyenii lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and wet before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔtɔ dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp, and overly shady farms. Pruning thick branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the farm and stop the disease.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ tsɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Nibii ni afoɔ ni mli wa lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gĩɔ ni ehaa helai kpaa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips that spread plant viruses. Controlling these small insects early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. ŋmeii bibii akudɔmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather becomes extremely hot and dry or when water is inconsistent. High heat damages the flower's pollen, causing the plant to shed the flower instead of producing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa. aloo kɛ́ nu lɛ ejaaa lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kpataaa fɔfɔii amli ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why are some maize seeds coated in red or blue chemical powder when I buy them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma powda tsuru loo bluu wo ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ahe beni miheɔ lɛ?

english: The red or blue coating is a protective chemical treatment (fungicide or insecticide) that prevents soil insects, fungi, and birds from eating or damaging the seeds before they sprout.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ji tsofa ni buɔ mɔ he. (Fungicide loo insecticide) ni tsiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi, ŋmeii, kɛ okpoi anaa koni amɛkaye loo amɛfite dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: If I buy improved hybrid seeds this season, can I save some seeds from my harvest to plant next year?
ga: Kɛji mihe dumɔwui ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui komɛi ni jɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu afi ni baa lɛ?

english: It is not recommended because hybrid seeds lose their special strength and uniform growth in the second generation, leading to smaller crop yields and lower resistance to disease.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa ejaakɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ amɛdalɛ ni tamɔ amɛhe yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi, ni helai ni nyɛɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do pesticide bottles have different color bands like green, yellow, or red on their labels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ tsɛnsii amli lɛ yɛ sui srɔtoi tamɔ eŋɔli, ŋmɔŋ, loo etsuru yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The color bands show how strong and dangerous the chemical is: green means low toxicity, yellow means moderate toxicity, and red means highly toxic, requiring extra safety gear when spraying.
ga: Nibii ni akɛ sui ewo mli lɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni tsofai lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ bɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ oshara ha. Green tsɔɔ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ faaa. Yellow tsɔɔ akɛ eyɛ tsofa ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. ni red tsɔɔ akɛ tsofa ni yɔɔ gbeyei waa. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ he nibii krokomɛi afata he kɛ́ ashɛreɔ tsofa lɛ.

english: Can I mix two different liquid chemicals together in my knapsack sprayer to save time?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofai enyɔ ni ji nu afutu mli yɛ sɛɛgbɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛ be akafite?

english: You should be careful because mixing incompatible chemicals can destroy their effectiveness or create a reaction that burns your crop leaves. Always ask an extension officer before mixing.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ ohe jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ tsofai ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite bɔ ni amɛtsuɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ loo ebaanyɛ ekɛ nɔ ko aba ni shãa tso lɛ baai lɛ. Bi mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be dani okɛfutu.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in heavy moisture and excess shade. Pruning overhead tree branches allows sunlight and air to dry the farm and reduce the disease.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gĩɔ, ni ehaa helai baa shi.

english: What is the difference between white granular fertilizer and the colored compound fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ kɔla teŋ?

english: White fertilizer (like Urea) gives the plant nitrogen for fast leaf growth, while colored compound fertilizer (like NPK) provides a balanced diet of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium for overall plant health, root strength, and fruiting.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yɛŋ (tamɔ urea) haa tsei lɛ nitrogen koni baai lɛ adara oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nibii ni yɔɔ kɔlai amli (tamɔ NPK) lɛ haa nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium ni sa kɛha tso lɛ hewalɛnamɔ fɛɛ. Shishifã hewalɛ kɛ yibii ni ato

english: Why are the leaves on my young corn plants turning yellow instead of healthy green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away from the roots, which can be fixed by applying nitrogen fertilizer or manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Abaanyɛ atsake enɛ kɛtsɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Does the reddish color of the soil on my farm mean it is good for growing crops?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ tsuru ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Red soil often contains iron and can be slightly acidic, which can lock up important nutrients like phosphorus. Adding organic compost or poultry manure helps unlock those nutrients for your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dade yɛ shikpɔŋ tsuru mli, ni ebaanyɛ efee acid fioo. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs ato. Kɛ́ okɛ organic compost loo kooloi ashishifãi fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbele nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ anaa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How can I safely test a new planting method without risking my entire harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka gbɛ hee ko ni mitsɔɔ nɔ mikwɛɔ nii lɛ makwɛ shweshweeshwe ni mikɛ mikpamɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ wooo oshara mli?

english: You can try the new method on a small portion or trial plot of your farm while keeping the rest under your usual practice, allowing you to compare the results easily at harvest time.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka gbɛ hee nɛɛ okwɛ yɛ fãi bibii amli. loo shikpɔji ni akɛkaa nibii akwɛɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ha nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi tamɔ bɔ ni ofeɔ daa lɛ. Bɔni afee ni okɛ nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ato he mlɛo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why is it better to plant cassava in straight rows rather than planting randomly across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduɔ ŋmei yɛ ŋsɔɔdoi ni ja mli? Ani ehi fe ni aaadu nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli trukaa?

english: Planting in straight rows ensures every plant gets equal sunlight and nutrients, makes weeding much faster, and helps you accurately estimate how much fertilizer you need.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yaa oya kwraa. ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni osusuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa bo lɛ ahe pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young plantain suckers turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young plantain suckers usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or there is too much water trapped around the roots. Adding organic compost and improving soil drainage will help the leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu babaoo damɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ organic compost fata he ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when strong winds blow across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches. If underground pests like root nematodes or stem borers damage the roots, the plant loses its grip in the soil and collapses easily under strong wind.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ewoɔ aduawai babaoo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo stem borers lɛ fite shishifãi lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkuɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa shishi.

english: Why should I cut off the purple flower bulb at the bottom of the plantain bunch after the fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli beni aduawai lɛ ebɔi sɛɛ?

english: Removing the male purple flower head prevents the plant from wasting food on parts you will not eat. It forces the plant to redirect all its energy into making the plantain fingers grow larger and heavier.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie violet fɔfɔi hii lɛ ayitsei lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite niyenii ni kulɛ oyeee lɛ. Enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii koni eha plantain niji lɛ adara ni amɛtsii.

english: A plantain bunch is ready to harvest when the individual fingers become full and rounded rather than sharp-cornered, and when the tiny dried flower tips at the ends of the fruit snap off easily.
ga: Plantains kuu ko efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji inchi fɛɛ inchi eyi ni efee kokroo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeehiɛ ŋwɛigbɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni kɛ́ fɔfɔi bibioo lɛ naa gbi lɛ Yibii lɛ naa lɛ jeɔ kpo mlɛo.

english: What causes black spots on my plantain leaves, and will it reduce my harvest?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ plantain baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa? Ni ani ebaaha mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi?

english: Black spots are caused by a fungal leaf disease known as Black Sigatoka. It damages the leaf surface so the plant cannot process sunlight effectively, leading to smaller bunches and early fruit ripening.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Sigatoka ni jɛɔ baai amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Efiteɔ baa lɛ hiɛ hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa akui bibii kɛ aduawai lɛ shwereɔ oya.

english: Why do plantain suckers taken from an old farm often fail to produce good fruit in a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, plantain tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji momo amli lɛ wooo yibii kpakpai yɛ ŋmɔji heei amli lɛ?

english: Suckers from old farms frequently carry hidden pests like microscopic root worms or stem borer grubs inside them. Cleaning the roots and treating suckers before planting in new soil prevents spreading these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni jɛ ŋmɔji momo amli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, tamɔ shishifãi bibii ni shwieɔ shi loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii, yɛ amɛmli. Kɛ́ atsumɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni atsa amɛ ŋmeii lɛ dani adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the fingers on my plantain bunch rotting and turning soft before they are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni yɔɔ mi plantains kuu lɛ nɔ lɛ miifite ni amɛmiifee blɛoo dani amɛshwere lɛ?

english: Fruit rot is usually caused by fungal infections spread by insect bites or excess moisture trapping in dense leaves. Pruning dead leaves allows sunlight and air to flow through, keeping the fruit bunches dry.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kooloi ŋmɔɔ lɛ kɛ aduawai fiteɔ baa. aloo ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni emɔɔ yɛ baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli Baai ni egboi lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. aduawai ni egbi lɛ akuu

english: Why do experienced farmers tell me to plant plantains alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu plantains yɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and easily scorched by hot sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: It is best to leave only two or three suckers of different ages around the main stem—one main plant, one medium sucker, and one small shoot. Leaving too many suckers creates competition for soil food and reduces bunch size.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi ŋmeii 2-3 ni eye afii srɔtoi yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he: ŋmeii wulu 1, ŋmeii 1 ni dalɛ ji teŋgbɛ, kɛ ŋmeii bibii 1. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha niyenii he akaŋshii aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ ayibɔ aba shi.

english: Why does the soil in my plantain farm dry out so fast during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses moisture quickly to sun heat and dry harmattan winds. Covering the ground around the base of your crops with dry leaves, weeds, or crop residues retains moisture in the soil much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛji hulu kɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ ha edɔ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ ni akɛ baai ni egboi, jwɛi, loo tso mli nibii ni efite lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them in an open field without any bigger trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong direct sunlight scorches their tender leaves and dries out the soil rapidly. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain or cassava protects them until they grow sturdy enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo cassava lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas over young cocoa plants. They provide necessary shade and cool soil moisture during the cocoa plant's vulnerable early years.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo yɛ kookoo tsei bibii anɔ. Ha hɔɔŋ ni he hia kɛ sũ mli nu ni mli ejɔ yɛ kookoo tsei ni waaa lɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is a vital nutrient for leafy growth, or that the soil is overly waterlogged. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehiɛ afee eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my maize seeds very close together in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to produce larger and healthier cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil and helps feed the maize crop, leading to better yields without extra cost.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eye ebua ni eha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa anáa nibii kpakpai ni shika kroko fataaa he.

english: How do I know when my cassava plants are ready for me to harvest under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ makpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You can tell it is maturing when the lower leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off, or by carefully digging up the soil around one plant to inspect tuber size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ henɔ lɛ nɔ Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baa ko egbɔ kɛji baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. aloo kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle Plant lɛ he lɛ ni ooofo jogbaŋŋ koni okwɛ bɔ ni bulb lɛ da ha lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden sticks in the soil for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei kakadaji lɛ? kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni mi sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves toward the sun to make food efficiently. Staking keeps leaves off the wet ground, preventing leaf diseases and encouraging larger tuber growth underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ni esa akɛ ewo ebaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ he koni ehoo niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni ehaa tsei wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too hot, when watering is uneven, or when insects damage the blooms. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting in the right season prevents flower drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ fɔfɔii Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ dumɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ ashishijee naa.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops sunlight from drying out the ground too quickly. It traps moisture, keeps plant roots cool during hot afternoons, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Should I plant my crop seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year falls?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become regular. The first rainfall is often followed by a short dry stretch that can dry out and destroy newly germinated seeds in the ground.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kukuoo ko nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ agbi ni efite dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen, which is their primary food for growth. It can also happen when heavy rain leaves the soil waterlogged, preventing the roots from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tso lɛ daa lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo nu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is eating small holes in my maize leaves and leaving dark dirt inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli?

english: That is likely caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves of the maize plant during the day, feeding on young leaves and leaving behind waste that looks like wet sawdust.
ga: Ekolɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nakai feemɔ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ni amɛshiɔ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ amɛshwieɔ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Will adding dry animal dung or decayed plant waste to my farm soil actually help my crops grow?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egboi ni eshwɛ lɛ ni mikɛbaafata miŋmɔ lɛ mli sũ lɛ he lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdara diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, adding organic waste like animal dung or decayed plants feeds the soil with natural nutrients and acts like a sponge, helping the soil hold onto water longer during hot days.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ kooloi ashishifãi loo tsei ni egboi ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why should I wait for the heavy rains to settle properly before planting my seeds instead of planting right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa dani madu dumɔwui yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain after a dry period can trick seeds into sprouting, but if a week of hot, dry weather follows, the tender young seedlings will dry up and die before the main rains begin.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui akwɛ̃. Shi kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ otsi kome lɛ, Tender dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting. You will notice the lower leaves turning yellow and falling off, and you can gently dig around one plant stem to check if the tubers are thick.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Ni obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli. A light trunk Koni akɛkwɛ kɛji yitso lɛ mli edɔ loo ebɛ ŋmɔlɔ

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning soft and black before they even turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ediŋŋ dani efeɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering where the soil goes from completely dry to very wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa kɛtee nɔ ni edɔ waa nɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the leaves, or by a plant virus carried by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni ji mɛi ni kɛ nakai kooloi lɛ baa lɛ anɔ

english: What happens if I plant my crops very close together so I can fit more plants on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mihe waa koni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak plants that produce smaller yields than plants given proper space.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo fe tsei ni yɔɔ he ko ni sa lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after I clear and weed the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mijie jwɛi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can lie dormant in the soil for years. When you clear the land, you expose those seeds to direct sunlight and rain, allowing them to germinate much faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ awɔ. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo Kɛ́ ojie jɛmɛ lɛ, hulu la kɛ nugbɔ baashɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh sunlight. Without enough shade trees or plantains around them, direct heat scorches their delicate leaves and drains their soil moisture, causing the leaves to dry up and fall.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii bɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ Ha hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa Dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaajie nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: How long do I have to wait after planting a cashew seedling before it starts bearing nuts?
ga: Kɛ́ midu cashew tso lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani ekɛ dumɔwui awo?

english: Standard cashew seedlings usually take about 3 to 5 years to start producing nuts, while grafted varieties can start fruiting sooner, around 2 years, if given good soil and proper care.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cashew dumɔwui ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ ŋmeii feemɔ shishi. Yɛ be mli ni tsei srɔtoi ni akɛwo mli lɛ baanyɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi aaafee afii 2 mra kɛji amɛná shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa.

english: How far apart should I space my coconut trees when planting them on my land?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ abɔ he beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Coconut trees need about 7 to 9 meters of space between each tree so their wide roots and giant fronds do not fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients.
ga: Kokoo tsei biɔ ni jɛkɛmɔ ni miihe ashɛ mitai 7 kɛyashi 9 ahi tso fɛɛ tso teŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ kɛ baai wuji lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akaŋ.

english: Why do my cashew trees produce plenty of flowers but very few nuts actually grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Cashew flowers need insects like bees to pollinate them before nuts can form. Strong winds, heavy rains during flowering, or insect pests can destroy the blossoms before pollination happens.
ga: Cashew fɔfɔii biɔ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii afee amɛ pollen dani ŋmeii aba. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Aloo tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ afite fɔfɔi lɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: What causes my coconut tree to drop its young fruits before they are fully mature?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi ŋmei tso lɛ shwieɔ eyibii bibii lɛ dani amɛdaraa?

english: Early coconut drop usually happens because of sudden dry weather, lack of key soil nutrients like potassium, or attacks by sap-sucking insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋshɔŋlooi ni shwieɔ shi mra lɛ baa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa lɛ hewɔ. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium, loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutuamɔ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in wet conditions. Excess rain and trapped moisture inside overcrowded trees help the fungus spread rapidly from pod to pod.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ amli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmei kome mli kɛyaa ŋmei kroko mli.

english: Can I plant food crops like cassava between my young cocoa trees, or will it ruin the farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii, tamɔ ŋmei, yɛ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ? loo ebaafite ŋmɔ lɛ

english: You can plant food crops temporarily when cocoa is young to provide shade and income, but fast-spreading or hungry crops like cassava should not be planted too close because their heavy roots steal nutrients from the cocoa.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be kukuoo mli beni kookoo lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo koni ekɛ hulutsoo kɛ shika aha. Shi esaaa akɛ aduɔ tsei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya loo hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ, tamɔ yucca lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi ni tsii lɛ juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ kookoo lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color distinctly—green pods turn bright yellow, and red or purple pods change to a reddish-orange color when mature.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su yɛ faŋŋ mli. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ni ŋmeii tsuru loo purple lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii-tsuru kɛji amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Is it helpful to trim off the lower branches of my growing cashew trees?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ mafolɔ mi-cashew tso ni miida lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, pruning lower branches allows sunlight to reach the base, improves airflow to prevent disease, and makes it easier for you to walk around and collect fallen nuts.
ga: Hɛɛ, afoɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛshishigbɛ. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ koni helai akamɔ bo ni eye ebua bo ni okɛ ohe awo mli Ni efee mlɛo akɛ oooŋɔ ŋmeii ni egbee shi lɛ.

english: What main signs show buyers and traders that my dried cocoa beans are good quality?
ga: Mɛni ji okadii titrii ni tsɔɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii kɛ jarayelɔi akɛ mi-kookoo ni egbi lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Traders look for properly fermented beans that have a deep brown color, dry skin that cracks cleanly when pressed, and no signs of mold, slatey dark grey insides, or insect damage.
ga: Jarayelɔi taoɔ ŋmeii ni edɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni ji ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Hewolo ni egbi ni etseɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ anyɛ nɔ Ni ŋmɔtɔ he okadi ko bɛ jɛmɛ. Mli lɛ yɛ woji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. loo kooloi bibii efite

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or animal manure gives the plants what they need to turn green again and produce big, healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my farm soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ nii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have small nodules on their roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil, creating natural plant food for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛkpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsei niyenii baa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and soil diseases that target that crop to multiply. Rotating different crops keeps the soil balanced and healthy.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tsɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ mli srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava is typically mature around 9 to 12 months after planting, when lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and the soil right at the base of the stem begins to crack from expanding tubers underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shɛɔ shweremɔ he aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ bulb ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ mli.

english: Why do many of the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from water stress during dry spells, insect damage from pests like mirids, or a lack of nutrients. Providing shade and proper soil nutrients helps trees hold their flowers to form pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji amɛna nu he haomɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen fiteɔ kooloi. loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Yam leaves need full sunlight to make food for the underground tubers. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so they get enough sun and stay away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Hulu ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ená hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ehe akabɔ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Curled, wrinkled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck plant sap and spread viruses, preventing healthy leaf development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni haa baa lɛ mli waaa

english: Why do my tomato fruits get black, rotten bottoms before they fully ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato yibii lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋɔ dani amɛshwereɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: This black patch is called blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium in the growing fruit. It happens most often when soil moisture fluctuates heavily, preventing the roots from taking up calcium.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ fã diŋ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa, ni no haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ calcium lɛ.

english: Extra suckers steal water, light, and nutrients from the main stem. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the main plant to produce a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo tso wuji babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why do my crop seeds rot in the soil when I plant them right after a heavy flood?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nu afua ni naa wa ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need oxygen in the soil to breathe and sprout properly. Completely flooded soil drives out all the air, causing the seeds to suffocate and get infected by water-loving rot fungi.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ kwraa lɛ baajie kɔɔyɔɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii ni sumɔɔ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that provide living shade, keeping young cocoa plants cool and moist while they establish roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo. Ehaa cacao tso bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa edɔɔ yɛ be mli ni efeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the buds pointing upward toward the sky. Planting them upside down forces the shoots to grow backwards first, which weakens the plant and reduces your root yield.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Dumɔ ni akɛ ŋwɛi tsɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ada kɛya sɛɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni shishifãi ni baa lɛ aba shi.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the seedlings fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food and space to grow thick and produce well.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa niyenii kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a major food source for plants. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or NPK will help the crop regain its deep green color and vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii jɛɛhe titri kɛha tsei Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo NPK fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛ su ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture natural nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. The maize you plant next season feeds on this restored soil nutrient and grows much better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abɛi ni obaadu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ baaye niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni aku sɛɛ afee lɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ni ebaada jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot in the ground when we receive continuous heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ wɔná nugbɔ ni naa wa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot when standing water builds up around their roots and prevents them from breathing. Planting yams on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely, protecting the tubers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu ni ekã shi lɛ bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaaa amɛmu. Sweet potatoes ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe. Ye obua ni abu yitso lɛ he

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ewo pepper yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants often drop flowers when they suffer from heat stress and dry soil. Regular watering during dry and sunny spells keeps the plant cool and helps flowers stay attached so they can mature into peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha tso lɛ mli ajɔ ni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Cocoa flowers often drop because of sap-sucking pests like mirids or excessive shade blocking sunlight. Trimming heavy shade branches slightly and managing pests will help more flowers mature into healthy pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ tamɔ pollen loo shade ni tsiɔ hulu la babaoo naa lɛ hewɔ. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo waa lɛ ni afolɔ fioo kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: What makes my tomato plant leaves curl up and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Tomato leaf curling is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies that transmit leaf curl viruses. Controlling whiteflies early prevents the virus from spreading and damaging your field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ whiteflies, ni hiɛ hela ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Whitefly Nɔkwɛmɔ Mra Ebaatsi helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ni ekɛ fitemɔ aba oyale mli.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops by stealing sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Weeding your field early gives your crops full access to the resources they need to grow big and produce high yields.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛjuɔ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ye obua onibii lɛ ni amɛná nibii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ fɛɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because full sunlight and dry winds scorch their delicate leaves. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain or cassava alongside young cocoa protects them from direct heat until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ. Enɛ, kɛ kookoo ni mli jɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ he kɛyashi amɛbaadara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing maize leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or growing leguminous crops like cowpeas before maize helps correct this nutrient deficiency.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni tsei ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he loo adu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmɔshi nibii dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni asaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa nɛɛ.

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell they are mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo hiɔ shi aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ amɛdara kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when soil moisture fluctuates too much. Watering your tomato plants consistently at the base helps the flowers stay on the vine and develop into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ daa yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi wain tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔ yibii.

english: Weeds compete directly with crops for nutrients, water, and sunlight in the soil. When weeds grow faster than crops, they steal these resources, leaving your crops weak and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Beni jwɛi lɛ daraa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii Amɛjuɔ nibii nɛɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaagbɔjɔ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves toward sunlight, allowing the leaves to produce more food for the growing tuber under the ground. It also keeps leaves off the damp soil, protecting them from fungal diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii babaoo kɛhaa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ he. Buu amɛhe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why should I plant beans or cowpeas on the same plot of land with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. This naturally feeds the soil, helping nearby maize plants grow better while keeping the soil fertile.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in the leaves at the center of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi-abɛi tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ

english: This damage is typically caused by caterpillars such as the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the growing tip of young maize plants. Early inspection and timely pest management protect the crop before major loss occurs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani fitemɔi wuji baa.

english: How does covering the soil around my vegetable crops with dried grass help them stay alive?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ haa tsei lɛ hiɔ shi?

english: Covering soil with dried grass—called mulching—keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation from the sun, and suppresses weeds, allowing your crops to retain water during hot spells.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ - ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching - yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ afee mlɛo. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa Eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant pepper on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows plant-specific pests and diseases to build up in the field, leading to poorer yields over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei pɔtɛɛ ahe helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the crop even produces cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tsei lɛ po jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate that the soil is running low on nitrogen, which the crop desperately needs to stay green and grow tall. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or poultry manure early in the plant's growth stage restores the green color and supports healthy cob development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ehe hia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloi ashishifãi wo mli mra yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tso lɛ su lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it better to plant cassava stem cuttings at an angle instead of laying them completely flat under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmei niji yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni aaawo amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a 45-degree angle encourages roots to grow deeper into the soil where moisture stays longer during dry periods, and it creates a single strong point from which tubers can swell, making harvesting much easier.
ga: Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ 45 degree angle mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Fɛ̃i lɛ baahi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. ni ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta kome ni wa ni haa yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Ehaa nikpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa

english: How does planting cowpeas together with maize help my maize crop grow better?
ga: Te tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This nitrogen acts as a natural fertilizer for nearby maize, while the bushy cowpea leaves cover the ground to trap soil moisture and prevent weeds from sprouting.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ. yɛ be mli ni cowpea baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eha jwɛi akakwɛ̃.

english: What causes small holes in the leaves of my young cabbage plants, and how can I protect them?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-cabbage tso bibioo lɛ baai lɛ anɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛnaa?

english: Small holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by hungry caterpillars or small beetles feeding on tender foliage. Spraying a mild neem leaf extractions solution or recommended organic pesticide early in the morning kills these pests before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ loo ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ baa ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu ni mli ejɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I clear away all the big shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie cacao tsei wuji kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to intense heat and sunburn. Large shade trees act like natural canopy umbrellas that protect tender cocoa leaves from direct sunlight and keep the soil damp enough for young roots to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulutsoo he waa. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up tightly during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling during hot afternoons is a natural defense mechanism where tomato plants reduce their leaf surface area to prevent water from evaporating into the hot air. Giving plants adequate water at the root level early in the morning reduces heat stress.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he. Tomato tsei lɛ baaha amɛbaai lɛ anɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ aba shi koni nu akatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe leebi lɛ haa dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa shi.

english: Why shouldn't I store seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant again during the next farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni maduɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to give high yields only in their first generation. If you plant saved seeds from that harvest, the resulting crop will lose its vigor, grow unevenly, and yield much smaller cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tso ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli. shweremɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni amɛwoɔ cob ni ji bibioo kwraa

english: What causes the bottoms of my pepper fruits to turn black and rot while still hanging on the plant?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper aduawai lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni ekã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Rotting at the bottom of peppers, known as blossom-end rot, happens when plants cannot absorb enough calcium due to irregular watering during fruit formation. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps plants transport calcium to growing peppers.
ga: Rot ni yɔɔ peppers shishi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ blossom end rot lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ woɔ yibii lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium yaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ aŋɔɔ.

english: Why are my garden egg plants producing plenty of flowers but falling off without turning into vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi egbeeɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off garden egg plants when insects like bees are not visiting to pollinate them, or when plants face sudden moisture stress from dry spells. Ensuring good flower pollination and steady soil watering keeps flowers attached until fruits form.
ga: Fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ eggplant tsei amli yɛ abɔɔi amli beni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii eyaaa amɛŋɔɔ koni amɛbawo amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ. aloo beni tsei naa hulutsoo be mli trukaa lɛ. Pollination kpakpa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.
