english: What happens to my crops if I plant maize seeds very close to each other in a single row?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmãa kome mli?

english: Planting seeds too closely forces crops to compete aggressively with one another for soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight. This results in thin, weak stalks that produce very small cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii kwraa loo amɛwooo ŋmeii ko kwraa.

english: Soil dries out fast when exposed directly to hot sun and wind. Covering the bare ground around your plants with dry leaves or straw, known as mulching, traps moisture in the soil so your crops stay hydrated longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ enɔ. Atsɛɔ he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ ni akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi haa he lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: You should plant cassava cuttings about one meter apart. Giving them enough space prevents the roots from fighting each other for nutrients and water, allowing the cassava tubers to grow thick and healthy.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava niji lɛ abɔ he aaafee mita kome. Kɛ́ aha he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkawuu amɛhe kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Ehaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: It is best to wait until the ground receives two or three steady rains so the soil is moist deep down. Planting after just one light rain can cause your seeds to sprout and then die if the rain stops for a few days.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Nɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii fioo komɛi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to build strong leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or the right nitrogen fertilizer will supply the food your maize needs to turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei lɛ he hiaa koni amɛfee baai ni wa Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaaha o-ŋmei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer around my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is when the soil is damp after a light rain, a few weeks after the seeds sprout. Applying fertilizer when the soil is completely dry can burn the plant roots, and applying it during heavy rainfall washes the food away.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. loo otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii lɛ afite.

english: Should I cut off the extra shoots growing around the bottom of my plantain tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni bɛŋkɛ plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yes, you should remove the extra shoots, leaving only one or two strong suckers next to the main plantain tree. If too many shoots grow together, they steal food and water from the main tree, resulting in small plantain bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ ojie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ. Shi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ plantain lɛ fã titri lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ abua ŋmeii babaoo anaa lɛ, Ebaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains bibii bibii.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat holes inside the growing center of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ hei ni mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which attack young corn plants. Catching them early and spraying recommended safe chemicals or neem oil solutions directly into the center leaf of the plant will protect your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem fɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ afɔ otsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads in cold, damp, and shady farms. Pruning excess branches to allow sunlight and fresh air into your farm helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔji ni mli ejɔ, ni edɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, poor soil, or insect damage. Planting shade trees nearby and protecting the crop from pests during dry periods helps the flowers stay on the tree and turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ, ni abuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Weeds are native wild plants that have adapted to absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than domesticated crops. Clearing weeds early in the season stops them from stealing food and sunlight from your planted farm.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ shia lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dried leaves and palm fronds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egboi kɛ tsei ahe tsei aha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil around crop stems—a practice called mulching—keeps the ground cool under the hot sun, holds moisture in the dirt longer, and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ tsei ahe - nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching - yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it bad to put fertilizer on my crops when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so the plant roots can absorb it. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the crop's roots and ruin your investment.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛshwie shi bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite shika ni okɛwo mli lɛ.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my small plot?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too close makes crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to grow strong and produce bigger yields.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni eda ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Does clearing tiny weeds early on really make that much difference to my final crop yield?
ga: Jwɛi bibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shishijee Ani ebaaha srɔtofeemɔ aba minaagbee nibii lɛ amli diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, young weeds steal nutrients and water right when your crop is trying to establish its root system. Clearing weeds early lets your crop get all the nourishment it needs.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi bibii baaju niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛji otso lɛ bɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ shishifãi ama shi pɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa onibii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to produce the energy needed to grow large tubers underground. Keeping leaves off the damp ground also protects them from fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young cocoa trees turning brown and dry at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need partial shade from faster-growing crops like plantain or cassava to protect their delicate leaves while they grow strong roots.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo yucca amli. Koni abu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ shishifãi ni wa lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape along the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing in a V-shape on lower maize leaves usually means the crop lacks nitrogen. Adding compost or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea early in the season keeps the leaves green and productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ tamɔ V ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ebaaha yibii kpakpai aba.

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by a plant virus spread by tiny whitefly insects. Managing whiteflies early with neem oil sprays helps protect your crop from getting damaged.
ga: Tso mli hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ Neem Oil Spray nɔ lɛ, obaabu onibii ahe kɛjɛ nibii ni efiteɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before any peppers actually form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering helps the plant hold its blossoms and produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ latsaa mli haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ amli.

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the main stem becomes thick and woody, which typically happens 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ tsei Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do some cassava varieties spoil just a few days after harvesting while others stay fresh longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa henɔi komɛi fiteɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni henɔi komɛi hiɔ shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots spoil quickly after harvest due to rapid chemical reactions when exposed to air. Improved crop varieties have been bred with thicker skins and different root properties that slow down this spoilage, giving you more time to sell them at the market.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ yɛ tsofa ni tsuɔ nii oya kɛji akɛ amɛbote kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Atsake tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi srɔtoi. Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Enɛ haa onáa be babaoo ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ amɛ yɛ jara nɔ.

english: What causes my stored maize to go bad and rot so quickly after harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akpa?

english: Maize spoils in storage mainly when it is put away while still holding water, which allows mold to grow and insects to breed. Drying your grain thoroughly before putting it into airtight bags protects it from both moisture and pests.
ga: Nɔ ni he hiaa ji akɛ, ŋmãa fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie kɛjɛ mli ni nu yɔɔ mli lolo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa ni kooloi babaoo hu faa. Kɛ́ ogbala dumɔwui lɛ dani okɛwo vacuum kotokui amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: How can I be sure that a new seed variety will actually perform well on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwui heei lɛ baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: New seed varieties undergo years of field testing by agricultural researchers in different soil types and weather conditions across Ghana to prove they can withstand local pests and weather before being released to farmers.
ga: Dumɔwui heei lɛ etsɔ afii babaoo ni okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi eka amɛkwɛ yɛ shikpɔji kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi anɔ. Ghana fɛɛ Koni etsɔɔ akɛ ebaanyɛ edamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi anaa dani ejie lɛ kpo etsɔɔ okwaafoi.

english: Why do seeds bought from the agricultural office grow better than the seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds naturally lose their strength over generations and can carry over diseases from the previous harvest. Certified seeds are carefully bred for high vigor, uniform growth, and resistance to common local crop diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli, ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ helai ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ ashwã. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛná hewalɛ. shweremɔ ni yɔɔ ekomefeemɔ kɛ helai ni afɔɔ naa yɛ tsei amli lɛ ahe hewalɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow even when there is enough rain falling on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant is missing essential food like nitrogen from the soil, or that waterlogged soil is choking the roots and preventing them from taking up nutrients.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ miitsi shishifãi lɛ anaa ni etsĩ tso lɛ naa niyenii.

english: Why does planting the same crop on the same land every season reduce my harvest over time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni miduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific pests and diseases to build up in the field. Rotating different crops helps restore soil nutrients and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi baa ŋmɔ lɛ mli Nibii srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni ekpaa helai lɛ asɛɛkuu.

english: Why do some crops wither quickly during a short dry spell while others stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi gboɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Crops with deep root systems can reach water stored far underground during dry periods, while shallow-rooted crops rely entirely on topsoil moisture, which dries out fast under intense sunshine.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná nu ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kwraa. ni egbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi lɛ

english: Why do fungal diseases spread so quickly across my vegetable crops during damp weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ mi-vegetables lɛ fɛɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Fungi rely on water to reproduce. Warm, humid weather leaves moisture on crop leaves, which acts as a bridge for fungal spores to sprout, enter the plant, and spread rapidly from leaf to leaf.
ga: Fungi damɔ nu nɔ koni amɛfɔ bii. Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ, ni mli edɔ lɛ haa fɛ̃i baa tso baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ blɔfo kɛha fungal spores koni amɛkwɛ̃, amɛbote tso lɛ mli, ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya kɛjɛ baa nɔ kɛya baa kroko nɔ.

english: Why should I plant my seeds in straight rows instead of scattering them across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja moŋ fe ni magbɛ amɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Row planting ensures each crop gets the exact right amount of sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing with nearby plants, while also making weeding, fertilizing, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Row planting haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do my pepper plants shed their flowers before growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when they experience stress from intense heat, lack of soil moisture, or poor pollination. The plant drops its flowers to save energy so it can survive harsh conditions.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo pollination ni ehiii Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential food for plants. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure around the roots helps the leaves stay green and produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo ni akɛfataa tso lɛ he. Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Should I put fertilizer on my crop fields immediately after planting the seeds?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ni adu nii yɛ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: It is best to wait about 1 to 2 weeks after seeds germinate before applying fertilizer. Young roots need a little time to establish so they can absorb nutrients without being burned by strong fertilizers.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ otsi 1 kɛyashi 2 beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli. Shishifãi bibii lɛ he miihia be fioo dani amɛfee bɔni afee ni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa eshãaa amɛ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes right inside the center of my young maize shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn shoots lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that loves feeding on soft young maize leaves. Catching them early by dropping neem oil extract or recommended pesticides directly into the leaf funnels will stop them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni sumɔɔ ni eye ŋmãa baai bibii. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ neem mu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ ni oooshwie baa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil constantly moist and applying wood ash or agricultural lime to the soil helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ tso sũ loo okwaayeli mli sũ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop so many leaves when the dry Harmattan wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ baai babaoo kɛji Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ tswa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed their leaves during dry weather to save water from evaporating. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains and placing dry grass around the base of the cocoa trees holds moisture in the soil to protect them.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni nu lɛ akatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains, ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo kookoo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ebu amɛhe.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetables with dry grass or cocoa husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Aduawai ni akɛ jwɛi loo kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ewo mli

english: Covering soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, stops the sun from baking the ground dry, keeps plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Ebaatsi hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my plantain plant produce so many small suckers at the bottom, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Lots yɛ shishigbɛ Ni esa akɛ majie loo esaaa akɛ majie?

english: Plantain plants produce suckers to reproduce, but if too many grow at once, they steal food and water from the main mother plant. Removing all but 2 or 3 healthy suckers ensures your main plant grows large, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Plantains woɔ ŋmeii kɛha fɔmɔ. Shi kɛji odu babaoo shikome lɛ Ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ shi 2 loo 3 pɛ lɛ, ebaaha otso titri lɛ adara ni etsɔ ŋmeii akuu agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in full sunshine to make food for the tuber underground. Staking holds the vines up toward the light and keeps the leaves off the damp ground where fungal diseases spread.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni efee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking haa wain tso lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi kɛyaa la he ni ehaaa tso lɛ baai lɛ ahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and the stem base becomes thick and woody.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ tsei

english: Why do experienced farmers say planting groundnuts together with maize improves my soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots. When groundnut roots rot in the ground, they release free fertilizer into the soil that helps neighboring maize grow better.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛji ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛjieɔ ŋmei ni aheee nɔ ko kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and turn yellow when I cut down all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ mifo tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade from larger trees to protect them from direct harsh sunlight and heat. Without shade, the sun burns their leaves and dries out the moisture in the soil that they need to grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛji hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ Hulu lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni egbiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close to each other on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete against each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. This makes all the plants grow weak and thin with small yields.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ daa ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ ni yibii fioo pɛ ewoɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves, but the roots inside the ground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or leaf growth energy, the cassava plant puts all its strength into leaves instead of storing energy in the tuber roots underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo hewalɛ babaoo kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ ebaa lɛ mli moŋ fe ni ekɛ hewalɛ baato eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take natural plant food from the air and feed it into the soil. This helps fertilizer-loving plants like maize grow better without buying as many chemicals.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni sumɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛhe tsofai babaoo.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests and soil diseases that feed on maize to multiply in your field.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ babaoo yɛ oŋmɔji amli.

english: Why do I need to place tall sticks for my yam vines to climb as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ beni edaa lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to climb high to catch as much sunlight as possible, which helps build big tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves off wet ground so they don't catch soil diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato baai lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni enyɛ emɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni afeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: How does covering dry leaves or grass around my crop plants help them handle the hot sun?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkpeɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa?

english: Covering the ground with organic material (mulching) acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli (mulch) ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaa jwɛi hu shwereɔ

english: What is causing small, ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny dirt left inside the funnels?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu bibii ni etse ehe yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli kɛ muji bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa? ni eshwɛ yɛ kɔni lɛ mli lɛ

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide deep inside the green leaves during the hot day and chew on the young leaves at night.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli mli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli, ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off the stem before any tomato fruits appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat, dry soil, or lack of water. Stress causes the plant to protect itself by shedding flowers it cannot feed.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni bɛ lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Haomɔ haa tso lɛ buɔ ehe he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni enyɛŋ eye lɛ ni ekɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my young maize turn yellow and stall in growth when heavy rains flood my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby abele lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa dalɛ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When soil gets completely soaked in water, the crop roots cannot breathe air. Excess water also washes away nutrients deeper into the ground where young roots cannot reach.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kwraa Tso shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu kɔɔyɔɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hu hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and dry up during the Harmattan dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves dry up because direct sunlight and dry winds steal moisture faster than the roots can drink it. Plantain trees or shade trees planted alongside cocoa act like green umbrellas, keeping the air cool and protecting the tender leaves from burning.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ juɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Dumɔwui loo shade tsei ni adu yɛ kookoo masɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela eŋɔli. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa baai bibii lɛ ashã.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the fruits are growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya beni aduawai lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees do not have strong deep wood roots like hardwood trees; they have shallow fiber roots. As the fruit bunch grows heavy, strong winds can easily pull the roots out of the soft wet ground, which is why farmers support heavy fruiting stems with bamboo prop sticks.
ga: Dumɔwui bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa tamɔ tsei ni wa. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ da waa lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ajie shishifãi kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ oya. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni okwaafoi fiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ asɛɛ kɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very tender leaves that burn under direct sunshine. Planting food crops like plantain next to them creates a natural canopy that provides shade, keeps the soil moist, and protects the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii waa ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yam vines naturally like to climb to reach maximum sunlight, which allows their leaves to produce food for the crop. Staking keeps the leaves up off the hot ground, preventing rot and helping the plant channel its energy into growing large underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei sumɔɔ ni amɛkwɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa ebaai lɛ woɔ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii. Staking haaa baai akwɛ̃ yɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Plantains have shallow roots and heavy fruit bunches, which make them easily top-heavy. Clearing out extra suckers around the base and using bamboo poles to support stems with heavy bunches keeps the plant stable in rough weather.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. ni haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ebaafee nɔ ni tsii Ajieɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni ebɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ ni akɛ ŋmeii tsei tsuɔ nii koni akɛfi ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ asɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii amli.

english: Yellowing starting from the leaf tips usually means the maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it needs to stay green and grow tall. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ baai lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ko ni he hiaa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do elders advise me to plant groundnuts on the same plot where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, which means they take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their root nodules. When the groundnuts harvest and roots decay, that stored nitrogen fertilizes the soil naturally for crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛjieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmei ni shishifãi lɛ egbo Nitrogen ni ato lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei.

english: Why does my cassava have very tall, bushy green leaves but very thin, tiny roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kɛlɛ waa shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or too much water, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing leaves instead of stem storage. The plant needs balanced nutrients and good drainage so it stops growing foliage and starts expanding its tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai moŋ fe ni eeekpa ŋmeii. Niyenii ni sa kɛ nu kpakpa he miihia tsei. Koni ekpa baai lɛ adalɛ ni ebɔi ŋmeii lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up, shrinking, and showing light green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miihoso, amɛmiigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiitsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. The disease stops the plant from making normal leaves, so planting disease-resistant cassava stems is the best way to prevent it.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Kooloi bibii eyɛŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Hela nɛɛ haaa tsei afee baai ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ helai anaa.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they get stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps the flowers stay attached and turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũu be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: This rot at the bottom of the fruit is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by inconsistent watering while the tomatoes are forming.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ shishi nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni tomato lɛ miifee lɛ.

english: Why should I plant cover crops like mucuna on my field during the dry season when I'm not growing food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mucilaginous cover crop yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni miduuu niyenii?

english: Cover crops grow densely over the bare earth to shield the soil from harsh sunlight and heavy rains that cause erosion. When plowed back into the ground, they decompose into rich organic matter that improves future harvests.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii kwɛ̃ɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ koni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ he. Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ etee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛfiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa. Enɛ baaye abua ni wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmaakpamɔi lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves get scorched and dry up when I cut down all the tall trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei kakadaji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight. Tall trees provide shade that protects the young cocoa leaves from burning, keeps the soil moist, and lowers the field temperature so the cocoa plants can grow healthy.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi koni eha kookoo tsei lɛ adara waa.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize crop turning pale yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores the nutrients so the plant can make food and stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni tsei lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my cassava farm growing very tall stems with plenty of leaves, but the cassava tubers under the ground are very thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei lɛ kɛlɛ waa kɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ waa?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves and tall stems above ground instead of sending stored energy down to swell the tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai agboi kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu hewalɛ ni ebua naa lɛ kɛya shi ni eha yitso ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of yellow flowers, but the flowers drop off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi ko gbeeɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too hot or when the plant doesn't get enough water. Heat stress stops the flowers from pollinating properly, causing the plant to drop them to save its energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Heat haomɔ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Ha tsei agbo koni akɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land before I plant my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ baawo ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu mi ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen food out of the air and put it back into the earth. Planting them first naturally fertilizes the soil so your next maize crop grows much stronger.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ji nitrogen lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, o-maise ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ waa.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak with small yields when I put many seeds together in one small hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli tseee ni ebɛ hewalɛ shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo fata bu bibioo kome he lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures every single plant gets enough food and space to grow big fruits.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why should I spread dry grass or leaves on top of the soil around my vegetable beds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ashwã shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the ground from the direct heat of the sun. It prevents water from evaporating quickly, keeps the roots cool, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves in the sunlight, which helps them create food. Leaving vines to spread on the hot ground exposes them to diseases and reduces the size of the tuber in the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ aje kpo yɛ hulu la mli. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii baa Kɛ́ aŋmɛ wein tsei lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ekɛ helai baa ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ayibɔ baa shi.

english: Why should I cut down extra small shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and plant nutrients from the main plantain tree. Removing them leaves only one or two strong shoots, ensuring the main plant gets full nourishment to bear a large bunch.
ga: Tsofai krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ juɔ nu kɛ tso mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shishifã kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi, ni ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛkwɛ̃ ŋmei agbo ko.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up and look weak in the hot afternoon sun, but stand up straight again in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi shidaamɔ tɛ̃ɛ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ?

english: When the sun is hot, pepper leaves curl up to reduce the leaf area exposed to heat so they do not lose too much water. Once the air cools down in the evening, the plant relaxes and recovers.
ga: Kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baai lɛ baabɔle ehe koni ekɛba he ni baa lɛ yɔɔ ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ shi bɔni afee ni nu babaoo akaje mli. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baajɔ ehe ni ehiɛ baajɔ ehe.

english: Why do some of my maize varieties need more fertilizer while others produce okay without it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele henɔi lɛ ekomɛi he hiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo awo mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni abaanyɛ awo ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi amli kɛji ŋmeii bɛ lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties have different 'characters' or nutrient demands. Hybrid varieties are bred to produce heavy yields, but they need plenty of food (fertilizer) to do so, whereas traditional local varieties have adapted to survive on fewer nutrients in native soil.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ ‘sui’ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ srɔtoi. Akwɛɔ Hybrid henɔi lɛ koni amɛná yibii babaoo. Shi niyenii (fertilizer) babaoo he miihia amɛ koni amɛfee nakai. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi lɛ etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi kɛtsɔ niyenii fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: If all plants grow in the same dirt, why do my tomatoes need a different fertilizer from my cassava?
ga: Kɛji tsei fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ srɔto fe mi-cassava lɛ?

english: Even though crops share the same soil, every plant takes in different ingredients to build its fruit or root. Tomatoes need high calcium and potassium to build solid fruit without rotting, while cassava needs nitrogen early on and potassium later to expand its heavy underground tubers.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ kome pɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ Shi tso fɛɛ tso kɛ nibii srɔtoi tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ eyibii loo eshishifãi. Tomato he miihia calcium kɛ potassium babaoo koni enyɛ ewo aduawai ni wa ni efiteee. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei he hiaa nitrogen mra. kɛ potassium sɛɛ mli lɛ koni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: How do my crops actually make their own food when I only give them water and manure?
ga: Te miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii amɛha tɛŋŋ? Akɛni nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii pɛ mihaa amɛ hewɔ lɛ.

english: Crops use their green leaves like small kitchens. Through a process called photosynthesis, the leaves trap sunlight and mix it with air and water from the roots to create sugars, which feed the plant so it can grow and fruit.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ baai eŋɔli tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋtayaa bibioo ko. Etsɔɔ gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ fotosintɛsis lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ mɔ̃ɔ hulu la lɛ ni amɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu ni jɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ futuɔ mli koni ekɛfee sugars ni haa tso lɛ hewalɛ koni eda ni ewo yibii.

english: If I plant cassava and maize together on the same land, will they fight for food?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fee ekome yɛ he kome. Ani ebaatswa niyenii he akaŋ?

english: Yes, if planted too close, crops will fight for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. However, because maize matures quickly in a few months while cassava takes longer, proper spacing allows them to share the land without starving each other.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ, shi kɛlɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa heɔ be babaoo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa lɛ he lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ jaa he ni hɔmɔ yeee amɛhe.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up tightly during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a self-defense habit. When the sun gets too hot, the pepper plant rolls its leaves inward to hide them from direct sunlight, reducing water loss through the leaves so the plant does not dry out.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji su ko ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he. Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛkɛtee hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi koni tsei lɛ akagbi.

english: Why does my young cocoa need shade trees, while my maize dies if it gets any shade at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibi cocoa lɛ he hiaa shade tso lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mi-abele lɛ gboɔ kɛji ená shade kwraa?

english: Every plant has a preference for sunlight. Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under full sun and prefer a cool shaded environment, while maize is a high-energy plant that requires full sunlight all day to grow strong grains.
ga: Tsei fɛɛ sumɔɔ hulu la. Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi, ni amɛsumɔɔ he ko ni mli ejɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni he wa waa ni he hiaa hulu muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli koni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why does chicken manure make my vegetables green up fast, but cow manure takes longer to work?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina fɔmɔ nii haa mi-vegetables lɛ feɔ eŋɔli oya lɛ? Shi ani tsina ŋmei tsuɔ nii be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Different animal manures contain different nutrient mixes. Chicken manure is rich in quick-release nitrogen that plants absorb almost immediately, while cow manure contains high fiber that breaks down slowly, improving soil water retention over time.
ga: Nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi amli. Nitrogen ni ajieɔ lɛ oya lɛ fa babaoo yɛ tsina ŋmɔ mli, ni tsei lɛ nuɔ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Shi tsina ŋmei lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ fiber ni fiteɔ fiofio. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my yam leaves turn completely yellow and dry up when the tubers are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kwraa ni amɛgbiɔ beni ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves at maturity show that the plant has finished its job. The yam stops sending food to its leaves and transfers all remaining sugars down into the underground tuber before going dormant.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji amɛdara kwraa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe enitsumɔ lɛ naa. Sweet potatoes kpaɔ niyenii ni ekɛmajeɔ baai lɛ ni ekɛ amɛ sugars ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ woɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli dani amɛyaa wɔɔhe.

english: Why are the flowers on my garden eggs dropping off without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when plants lack specific nutrients like potassium or boron, or when there are not enough insects like bees to carry pollen between flowers to complete the fruit-making process.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ko, tamɔ potassium loo boron. aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, kɛ pollen ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ fɔfɔi ateŋ koni amɛgbe aduawai lɛ afeemɔ naa.

english: Why do my plantain trees grow tall and weak with small bunches when I crowd them together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ kui bibii amli lɛ? Beni abua naa lɛ

english: When plantains are planted too close, they stretch upward to compete with their neighbors for sunlight. They spend all their energy growing tall trunks to reach the light instead of storing energy to build big, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Plantains baagbala amɛhe koni amɛkɛ amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ abɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛduɔ tsei kakadaji koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Mohu ɔ, a buaa he wami nya konɛ a kɛ pee tso yiblii nguahi nɛ a he wa.

english: How do I know if a sunny spell means the dry season is starting or if more rain is still coming for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hulutsoo be lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ miije shishi? Aloo nugbɔ lɛ miinɛ lolo kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Short sunny breaks often happen in the middle of the rainy season; checking local radio weather forecasts or observing changes in wind direction can help you know whether to expect sudden rain or a prolonged dry stretch.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa be kuku Bei pii lɛ, ebaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ teŋgbɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ redio ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli loo okadi tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ole kɛji nugbɔ baanɛ trukaa loo nugbɔ baanyɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why did my seeds fail to sprout even though I planted them during a sunny break when rain seemed near?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli beni etamɔ nɔ ni nugbɔ miiba lɛ?

english: Seeds require continuous soil moisture to germinate. If strong sun dries out the soil completely before steady rains arrive, the seeds dry up and die underground.
ga: Dumɔwui biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa dani amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ hulu la lɛ mli wa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi kwraa dani nugbɔ lɛ aya nɔ anɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What happens to my vegetable crops if a heavy downpour falls suddenly after days of hot sun?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛbatsɔ Nugbɔ ni naa wa ni nɛɔ yɛ gbii babaoo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli trukaa?

english: Sudden heavy rain after a hot dry spell shocks plants, which can cause soft fruits like tomatoes or peppers to crack open due to rapid water intake.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni mli edɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe feɔ shoo. Enɛ baanyɛ aha aduawai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ tamɔ tomato loo ŋmɔtɔ mli agbala kɛjɛ nu ni anuɔ oya lɛ mli.

english: Why is it bad to leave my harvested cocoa beans outside when sudden rain catches them on the drying mat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaashi kookoo yibii ni akpa lɛ yɛ kpo nɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ trukaa yɛ tsɔne ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rainwater gets absorbed back into partially dried cocoa beans, creating high moisture that leads to internal mold growth and ruins the bean quality.
ga: Akɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ fã ko shwieɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ amli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa, ni no haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ ni efiteɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ahe nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested cassava chips turn dark and spoil when the sun stops shining during the drying process?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ feɔ duŋ ni efiteɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ kpa la ni tsoɔ yɛ be mli ni egbiɔ lɛ?

english: Without strong, continuous sunlight to evaporate moisture quickly, trapped water allows bacteria and fungi to grow, causing the cassava to discolor and rot.
ga: Kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ bɛ ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ atsɔ oya. Nu ni atsĩ naa lɛ haa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii daa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ su tsakeɔ ni egboɔ.

english: How can I safely dry my harvested pepper when the weather keeps switching between hot sun and unexpected rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ magbi mi-pepper ni akpa lɛ shweshweeshwe? Beni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsakeɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ teŋ.

english: Drying peppers on raised wooden platforms or moveable tarps allows you to quickly cover them or carry them indoors whenever rain clouds appear suddenly.
ga: Pepper ni ooogbi yɛ tso ni awo nɔ loo tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ nɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛhaa nɔ oya loo okɛwoɔ shia lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ atatui baaje kpo trukaa.

english: Why do my maize plants droop in the afternoon sun even when the soil was wet from rain this morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ejaakɛ nugbɔ nɛ ŋmɛnɛ leebi?

english: When hot sun follows rain, the air warms up fast, causing leaves to lose water quicker than roots can absorb it from the soil, leading to temporary daytime wilting.
ga: Kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nyiɛ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baadɔ oya. Enɛ haa baai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do my crops grow plenty of green leaves very fast when rain returns after a sunny break, but fail to produce flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔlii babaoo oya nɛkɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa beni hulu lɛ eje kpo sɛɛ shi jeee fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Sudden rain after a sunny period causes a rapid release of nitrogen in the soil, which pushes the plant to focus all its energy on leaf growth rather than flowering.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ hulutsoo be ko sɛɛ lɛ haa nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jeɔ kpo oya. Enɛ tsirɛɔ tsei koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii.

english: Should I clear and burn weeds on my field during a hot sunny period or wait until the rains start?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo jwɛi ni mikɛshã miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo mamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baabɔi nɛmɔ?

english: Clearing and drying weeds during sunny days allows for a clean burn, but you must complete it right before the rains start so the ash nutrients soak into the soil when you plant.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baaye abua ni shãa lɛ he atse. Shi esa akɛ ogbe jwɛi lɛ ogbe naa dani nugbɔ lɛ abɔi nɛmɔ. Enɛ ji koni sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni oduɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my crops as soon as rain falls after a dry sunny break?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ gbee pɛ?

english: Weeds have hardy, wild seeds that lie waiting in the dry soil and react instantly to rain, absorbing moisture and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ koo mli dumɔwui ni mli wa ni mɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni amɛtsuɔ he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ. Eheɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani adu aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when water is irregular. The plant gets stressed by extreme heat or drought and drops its flowers to save energy rather than feeding new fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu lɛ bɛ shiŋŋ. Dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa waa lɛ eha tso lɛ ehao. Ni okɛ fɔfɔii ashwie shi koni okɛ hewalɛ akafite moŋ fe ni oooha aduawai heei.

english: Why do the bottoms of my young tomatoes turn black and soft while they are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo be mli ni amɛdaraa lolo lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, which is usually caused by dry spells or uneven watering while the fruit is developing.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be beni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to tie my tomato plants to wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fĩɔ tsei ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi lɛ ni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Staking keeps leaves and fruits off damp soil where fungal diseases and insects live. It also lets air circulate through the plant and ensures full sunlight reaches the leaves.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai kɛ aduawai akahiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ kooloi bibii baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ lɛ. Eha kɔɔyɔɔ hu tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli ni eha hulu la babaoo shɛɔ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do seeds saved from my last tomato harvest produce smaller fruit than the original store-bought seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ minaagbee tomato ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ wo yibii bibii fe shishijee dumɔwui ni mihe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Many store-bought seeds are hybrids designed for one strong season. The seeds collected from those fruits lose their special strength in the next generation, leading to smaller, uneven crops.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni afee aha be ni mli wa. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nakai aduawai lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ kroko lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni bɛ ekomefeemɔ baa.

english: Yellowing starting from the bottom leaves usually means the soil is low in nitrogen. The plant takes nitrogen from its older lower leaves and sends it to feed new green leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛmajeɔ koni eyaye baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crop plants grow tall and skinny with few fruits when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are overcrowded, they compete for sunlight. The plants waste energy stretching upwards to catch light instead of developing strong stems and growing heavy fruits.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fa tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Tsei fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛgbalaa amɛhe koni amɛhe la. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ tso nɛ mi wa nɛ e woɔ yiblii nɛ tsii.

english: Can I plant tomatoes directly under large trees on my farm to protect them from the sun?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tomato yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ koni mikɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu lɛ he?

english: Vegetables like tomatoes need direct, unshaded sunlight all day to produce food and fruit. Tree shade blocks the light, and tree roots will steal water and nutrients from your crops.
ga: Aduawai, tamɔ tomato, biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo bɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli koni amɛná niyenii kɛ aduawai. Tsei lɛ ahe hulutsoo lɛ tsiɔ la lɛ naa. Ni tsei shishifãi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: Why do my pepper plant stems rot at the soil level after a few heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water around the stem, oxygen is cut off, allowing soil fungi to attack and rot the base of the plant.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ tsɔ tso lɛ he lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ shishi shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do tiny green insects gather under my plant leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ashishi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These insects (aphids) hide under leaves to shelter from the hot sun while sucking sap from the plant. They multiply quickly in dry weather because heavy rains are not around to wash them off.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ (aphids) kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai ashishi koni amɛná he ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli beni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Amɛfɔɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli ejaakɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ nyɛŋ afɔ amɛ.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to poor soil and hard weather. Their roots spread faster to steal available water and food from the soil before your crop roots get established.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai anɔ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ afee.

english: How many years can my pepper plants keep bearing fruits before I need to clear them and plant new ones?
ga: Afii enyiɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii dani ehe baahia ni ajie lɛ ni adu ekoŋŋ?

english: Pepper plants usually give their best harvest in the first year to eighteen months; after that, yields drop drastically and diseases build up in the plant, so it is best to clear and replant.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ amɛhe nitsumɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi kɛyashi nyɔji nyɔŋma kɛ kpaanyɔ mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi waa ni helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ tsei lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ajie amɛ ni adu amɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How long can a single cocoa tree keep producing cocoa pods before it gets too old?
ga: Be enyiɛ cacao tso kome baanyɛ ajie cacao ŋmeii dani egbɔ tsɔ?

english: A well-cared-for cocoa tree can continue bearing fruits for 30 to 40 years, with its peak production years usually occurring between 10 and 25 years of age.
ga: Kakao tsei ni akwɛɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ awo yibii afii 30 kɛyashi 40, ni bei pii lɛ, afii ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ baa yɛ afii 10 kɛyashi 25 teŋ.

english: If I leave my cassava in the ground for more than two years, will the roots keep growing bigger or will they turn bad?
ga: Kɛ mishi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ fe afii enyɔ lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ baafee wuji ni amɛbaafee wuji. Aloo ebaagbo?

english: Leaving cassava in the soil too long makes the roots become woody, tough, and lose starch; eventually, heavy rain will cause the roots to rot underground.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee tso, amɛhe wa ni amɛmli ŋmei lɛ baaje mli. Yɛ naagbee lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my plantain tree grow small shoots around its base, and what should I do with them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni bɔleɔ amɛshishi lɛ he lɛ ni mɛni esa akɛ mafee?

english: Those small shoots are called suckers and act as children of the main plant; you can dig them up carefully and plant them in new locations to grow whole new plantain trees.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ tso titri lɛ seshibii. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu nii ni okɛdu yɛ he ko hee koni ona plantain hee kwraa.

english: Should I leave all the small suckers growing around my plantain tree, or should I remove some?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi ŋmeii bibii komɛi yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ahe loo majie ekomɛi?

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight with the main tree for soil nutrients and water, which results in small bunches; it is best to prune away extra suckers and leave only one or two strong ones.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi suckers babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ awuu koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Enɛ haa anáa tso bibioo ko. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oshi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pineapple plants grow extra shoots after I harvest the main fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pineapple tso lɛ naa ŋmeii babaoo beni mikpa aduawai titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pineapples naturally produce side shoots called slips or suckers after fruiting; these are the plant's way of multiplying, and you can detach them to start your next crop.
ga: Pineapple woɔ sɛɛ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ slips loo suckers beni amɛwo yibii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbɛɔ tsei ashwaa. Ni obaanyɛ ogbala mli koni oje ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do some of my pawpaw trees produce plenty of flowers but never grow any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mipapaya tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Pawpaw trees can be male or female; male trees only produce pollen to fertilize female flowers and will never grow fruits of their own.
ga: Pawpaw tsei baanyɛ afee nuu loo yoo. Tsei hii feɔ pollen pɛ koni amɛkɛwo fɔfɔi yei. Ni gbɛ ko bɛ ni ebaatsɔ nɔ ewo yibii yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe.

english: Tomato blossoms drop when heat is too high, watering is irregular, or when wind and insects are not present to shake pollen inside the flowers to fertilize them.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji la lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa Aloo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ni kooloi bibii shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛha amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Can I save seeds from the maize I harvested this season to plant on my farm next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni mikpaa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli afi ni baa lɛ?

english: If you planted hybrid maize seeds, saving seeds from that harvest will result in weak plants and low yield; it is safer to buy fresh certified seeds for planting each season.
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ŋmãa Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ kɛjɛ kpamɔ mli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ afee nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli akɛ ooodu yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if the seed yams I saved in my barn are still good to plant for the next rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui ni ato yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi lolo kɛha dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Good seed yams should feel firm to the touch, show clean sprouting eyes at the head, and be free from soft rot, white mould, or heavy insect damage.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ afee nɔ ni wa kɛji mɔ ko ta he. Ayɛ ŋmeii ni he tse ni miida yɛ yitso lɛ nɔ. ni helai ni fiteɔ, ŋmeii yɛŋ, loo kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ nii waa bɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, sheltering the young cocoa from direct sun and keeping the soil moist during their early growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ

english: Fertilizer works best when applied in two stages: first about two weeks after planting when seedlings emerge, and second when the maize reaches knee-height (around four to five weeks). This supplies nutrients right when the plants are growing most rapidly.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli yɛ fãi enyɔ mli: Klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ ji aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni adu dumɔwui lɛ. kɛ fã ni ji enyɔ lɛ beni ŋmãa lɛ shɛɔ enaji ahe lɛ. (aaafee otsii ejwɛ kɛyashi enumɔ) Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa oya fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stems to plant for a healthy crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu koni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Select mature, healthy stems from plants that are 8 to 12 months old and show no signs of disease. Cut stem sections from the middle part of the stalk, about 20 to 25 centimeters long with 4 to 6 healthy buds, as these sprout the strongest.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni edara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 ni hela he okadi ko bɛ amɛhe lɛ amli. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ ji aaafee sɛntimitai 20 kɛyashi 25 kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni ŋmeii 4 kɛyashi 6 yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ejaakɛ enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ ada waa fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do we need to build high mounds of soil before planting yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni wɔfee shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani wɔdu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers require soft, deep, and loose soil to grow large and straight without restriction. Building mounds improves soil drainage, protects tubers from rotting in standing water, and makes harvesting much easier.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛdara ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ ni naatsii ko bɛ he. Gɔŋ ni afee lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ babaoo. Ebuɔ ŋmeii ahe koni amɛkafite yɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli. Ni ehaa nikpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why should I clear all weeds from my land before planting seeds instead of after?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Weeds aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from young crop plants. Clearing weeds before planting gives your crops a clean start so they can establish deep roots and grow strong without competing for resources.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ oya. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi dani odu lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛdaraa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛye akaŋ yɛ nibii ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise us to plant cowpeas or groundnuts together with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ ŋmãa adu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil, helps your maize grow better, and allows you to harvest two different crops from the same field.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni eha okpa ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Yellow leaves on pepper plants usually mean the soil has too much water, lacks nitrogen nutrients, or the plants are infested by tiny pests like aphids under the leaves. Ensuring good soil drainage and checking under leaves for insects helps fix this issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ni faaa Aloo tso lɛ yɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ aphids yɛ baai lɛ ashishi. Kɛ́ akwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ, ni akwɛ kɛji kooloi yɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why are flowers dropping off my tomato plants without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when weather temperatures become too hot, when soil moisture changes suddenly between very dry and very wet, or when plants receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to grow leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wo la tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa yɛ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛ nɔ ni mli edɔ waa teŋ. aloo kɛ́ tsei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ewo baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: How can I tell if Fall Armyworm is attacking my maize field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ Fall Armyworm miitutua mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Look closely at the central funnel of the maize leaves for ragged, chewed holes and small heaps of yellowish, sawdust-like waste. Catching these signs early allows you to treat the crop with recommended sprays or neem extracts before major crop loss occurs.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛha buji ni egbala ni atsɔ mli kɛ ŋmãa bibii ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa. Ni ooomɔ okadii nɛɛ mra Ehaa okɛ neem sprays loo nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsuɔ he nii lɛ tsuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nii. dani ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ baafite

english: How do I know if the first rains of the season are enough for me to start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛjeɔ dumɔ shishi?

english: Avoid planting immediately after the very first rainfall because the soil beneath the surface remains dry. Wait until the soil is thoroughly wet to a depth of about 15 centimeters (a hand's length) after two or three steady rainfalls before sowing seeds.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli egbi lolo. Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ kwraa kɛyashɛ aaafee sɛntimita 15 (tso kome lɛ kɛlɛ) yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Why do my neighbors prefer growing millet instead of maize when rainfall is very low in our region?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ sumɔɔ ni edu ŋmãa fe ŋmãa lɛ? Akɛni wɔkpokpaa lɛ nɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo kwraa hewɔ lɛ.

english: Millet has very deep roots and special leaves that conserve water, allowing it to survive and produce grains even during long dry spells where maize would dry up and die.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ waa kɛ baai krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli po. Abɛi lɛ baagbi ni ebaagbo.

english: Why do my sorghum stalks stay green and keep growing tall even during extremely hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sorghum tsei lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli po lɛ?

english: Sorghum is naturally built for heat; its deep root system draws moisture from deep underground, and its leaves roll up during hot hours to trap water inside the plant.
ga: Abɔ sorghum kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli koni ekɛ dɔlɛ aba. Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli. Ni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ koni nu ahi tso lɛ mli.

english: Why do birds attack my sorghum crop so much more than my soya farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi babaoo tutuaa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fe mi soybean ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Birds are attracted to sorghum because its grain heads sit open and exposed at the top of tall stems, whereas soya seeds are hidden inside tough, hairy pods that birds cannot easily break.
ga: Okpoi sumɔɔ ŋmei ejaakɛ edumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ gbeleɔ amɛhe ni amɛjeɔ kpo yɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ anɔ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, akɛ soybean dumɔwui ewo ŋmeii ni wa ni yitsɔi yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. ni okpoi nyɛŋ akumɔ mli mlɛo lɛ

english: How does planting soya beans on my farm make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ soybeans ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soya bean plants work with helpful bacteria in the soil to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which enriches the ground naturally for the next season's crop.
ga: Soybean tsei kɛ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young soya plants turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi soybean tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually show that the plant lacks nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that the soil is waterlogged and drowning the plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ sũ lɛ mli, loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miiho nu.

english: Why do my soya bean pods pop open and drop seeds on the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi soybean ŋmɔji lɛ gbeleɔ ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Soya bean pods dry out quickly once mature; prolonged exposure to hot sun causes the dry pods to burst open naturally, meaning you must harvest as soon as the leaves turn brown and fall off.
ga: Soybean ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛ ehe wo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛmli agbala. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni okpa ŋmaa lɛ kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbee shi pɛ.

english: Why should I avoid planting sorghum in the exact same spot on my farm every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil repeatedly and allows specific pests and crop diseases to multiply in that plot.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. daa Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsei ahe helai komɛi ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested millet grains get moldy and spoil after a short time in the storage room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sorghum dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Grains spoil in storage when bagged before drying thoroughly in the sun, because trapped moisture encourages mold and insects to grow.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baafite yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli dani agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii adalɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Do I need to apply the exact same type of fertilizer to my soya crop as I do to my millet field?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mi-millet ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ nɔŋŋ awo mi-soybean tsei lɛ amli?

english: No, millet requires external nitrogen fertilizer to grow well, whereas soya plants generate their own nitrogen from the air and need fertilizers higher in phosphorus instead.
ga: Dabi, ŋmãa biɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kponɔgbɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni soybean tsei feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ. ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ awo mli moŋ

english: What does it mean if a buyer offers me a contract agreement to grow crops like soya or sorghum?
