ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ kɛji akɛ mɔ ko ni heɔ nii lɛ ha mi nibii tamɔ soybeans loo sorghum?

english: A contract farming agreement means a buyer commits before planting season to purchase your harvest at an agreed price, often providing you with quality seeds and technical guidance to ensure a good yield.
ga: Okwaayeli he kpaŋmɔ ni akɛfee kpaŋmɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, mɔ ni heɔ lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ baashɛ akɛ ebaahe onibii lɛ yɛ jara ni amɛkpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, amɛhaa bo dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋaawoo ni kɔɔ ŋaa he koni ona yibiiwoo kpakpa.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I planted fail to sprout even after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi kwɛɛɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ po lɛ?

english: Seeds need the right balance of moisture, soil warmth, and planting depth. If seeds are buried too deep, planted in waterlogged soil, or are too old and poorly stored, they will rot in the ground instead of germinating.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ ni sa. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ kɛ dumɔ mlibotemɔ Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwui lɛ mlibotemɔ tsɔ Adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. loo egbɔ tsɔ ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Dumɔwui lɛ baagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃.

english: You should wait until the rain has soaked the soil deeply at least two or three times, rather than planting after the very first light shower, which can quickly dry up and scorch weak seedlings.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ hoo lɛ shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ agbi oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and looking weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal that the soil is running low on vital nutrients like nitrogen, or that water is trapping around the roots and suffocating them. Adding compost or manure helps rebuild the soil's strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo nu ko ebɔle he. shishifãi kɛ suffocates Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewaje shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up and droop during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have large leaves that lose water very quickly in full sun. During intense heat, the leaves droop to reduce their exposure to the sun and conserve moisture inside the stem.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai agboi ni nu fiteɔ oya waa kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni hulu la lɛ aba shi ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi tso lɛ mli.

english: Why are little worms eating the leaves of my young corn before it even flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii Koɔ ni amɛyeɔ mibi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ baai dani efɔ lɛ?

english: These are likely fall armyworms that hide inside the growing top of young corn. Catching them early and treating the center of the plant protects the main growing tip so the corn can produce ears.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa bibii ni miida lɛ amli. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni oookwɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmeii titrii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ ahe. koni ŋmãa lɛ anyɛ awo toi

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads in damp, overly shaded farms. Trimming extra branches lets in sunlight and breeze to keep pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔji ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tsei lɛ amli tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, acting as natural food for your maize without exhausting the land.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa o-corn lɛ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteee.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I leave dry weed leaves on top of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mishi jwɛi baai ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving dry organic matter on the soil creates mulch, which keeps the ground cool, holds in rainwater longer, and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ Toɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous harvest yield less than fresh certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii ni faaa fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops gradually lose their vigor and disease resistance over time, whereas fresh certified seeds are specially bred to give strong growth and high yields every season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ daa fiofio. Hewalɛ kɛ helai ni ekɛteɔ shi ewoɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo daa be mli.

english: Why are my yam tubers coming out small and twisted instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams require soft, deep, and loose soil or high mounds to expand easily. When planted in hard, stony, or compacted ground, the roots struggle to push through and become misshapen.
ga: Sweet potatoes biɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ hei ni wa Rocky loo compacted Shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ mli ni amɛbaafee mɛi ni efite.

english: How do I know the right number of fertilizer bags to buy for my farm size?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ayibɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ mahe kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ?

english: The amount of fertilizer needed depends directly on the size of your land and the specific crop type. Measuring your acreage correctly helps you match the exact number of bags needed so you do not waste money or under-feed your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ osusu he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni okɛ baagi ayibɔ ni he hiaa bo lɛ akpã gbee pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ ji koni okafite shika loo okaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Will adding extra bags of fertilizer beyond the recommended amount give me double the harvest?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata kotoku ni ajieɔ yi lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha mikpamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ shii enyɔ?

english: No, crops can only absorb a specific amount of nutrients. Applying too much fertilizer can burn the crop roots, damage the soil, and waste your money without increasing your yield.
ga: Dabi, tsei baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ shishifãi ashã. efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni efiteɔ shika ni ekɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ eyaaa hiɛ

english: Is it better to apply all my fertilizer at once or split it during the season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ atsu nii shikome loo mijara mli yɛ be kɛ bei amli?

english: It is best to split the application. Young crops need smaller amounts to grow, and applying fertilizer in stages ensures nutrients are available when the plant is strong enough to use them efficiently.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni agbala nibimɔi lɛ amli. Tsei ni darako lɛ biɔ nɔ fioo ko dani amɛdara. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ahi shi beni tsei lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce very little when I clear a large acreage that I struggle to maintain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo pɛ beni mijieɔ shikpɔŋ wulu ko ni mibɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni makwɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When you plant more land than your physical strength or budget can care for, crops suffer from delayed weeding and poor care. It is better to properly manage a smaller farm well than to spread your resources too thin over a large area.
ga: Beni oduɔ shikpɔŋ babaoo fe bɔ ni ogbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛ loo oshika he gbɛjianɔtoo baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ jwɛi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛ kwɛmɔ ni ehiii hewɔ. Ehi akɛ oookwɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko nɔ jogbaŋŋ fe ni ooogbɛ onibii lɛ ashwã he ko ni da fioo tsɔ.

english: What should I do if I get too tired to keep up with weeding across my whole farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ etɔ mi tsɔ ni manyɛ mafo jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, light, and water from crops. If labor is limited, prioritize weeding high-yielding sections first or use safe, recommended herbicide options to reduce physical strain.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, kane, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Kɛji nitsumɔ faaa lɛ, Ha jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ hei ni yibii babaoo woɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ. Aloo okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ajieɔ yi lɛ atsu nii ni okɛba gbɔmɔtsoŋ nɔnyɛɛ shi.

english: Why do my young crops look weak and pale green early in the growing period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Young crops look weak when they lack essential nutrients like nitrogen or when roots are struggling to establish. Giving them the right balance of starting fertilizer helps them build strength.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ́ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ amɛmli, loo kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛfee shishifãi. Kɛ́ aha amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why do crops planted too close together grow tall and thin with very small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ yibii bibii kwraa lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong stems and full fruits.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛbaatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ aduawai ni eyi obɔ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do some crops on one part of my land grow fast while others on the same farm stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã kome nɔ lɛ daa oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: Soil fertility varies across different spots on a field. Areas with lower nutrients or poor water retention cause crops to stunt unless given extra targeted organic manure or fertilizer.
ga: Esoro bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baa nii ehaa lɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli. Hei ni niyenii mli hewalɛ faaa loo nu ni ehiii lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ. Ja amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ krɛdɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops yield less every year even though I use the same soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ henɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Continuous farming removes natural nutrients from the soil over time. Replenishing the ground with a mix of organic compost and chemical fertilizer restores the soil's strength.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ organic compost kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops drop their leaves and flowers during hot, dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa kɛ fɔfɔii fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes crops to lose moisture faster than their roots can draw water from the soil. The plant sheds leaves and flowers to protect itself and stay alive during drought.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai kɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe ni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees keep drying up and dying when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade from fast-growing plants like plantains or shade trees to protect their delicate leaves and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an important plant food. Adding well-rotted animal manure or the right fertilizer gives the soil the nutrients the plant needs to grow green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni sa ni akɛfata he lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: These pests are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the growing center of maize plants. Checking your field early and applying recommended pest treatments or natural remedies like neem water can save your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ hei ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ. Onibii ni odu lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛbaatsu nii ni akɛtsaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem nu lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ahere onibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my yam seeds very close together so I can harvest more yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni manyɛ makpa sweet potato babaoo?

english: When yams are planted too close, their roots fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to form large, heavy yam tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu sweet potatoes ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii agboi ni tsii.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, lack of water, or tiny insect pests. Keeping the soil moist and protecting plants from pests helps the flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii komɛi ye tso lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsei ahebuu kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the land where I just harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmãa yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil, but crops like cowpeas and groundnuts put nitrogen back into the earth. Rotating crops keeps your soil rich without buying expensive chemical fertilizers every season.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei kɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ daa be.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big roots in some seasons but small roots in others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishifãi wuji yɛ bei komɛi amli shi shishifãi bibii yɛ bei krokomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Cassava needs steady moisture during its early root growth stage, along with loose soil. If the ground is too hard or there is a drought when roots are forming, the roots stay small.
ga: Cassava he miihia ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi daa yɛ shishijee be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ. Kɛfata shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ he Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ loo egbi be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miifee shishifãi lɛ baafee bibii.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my vegetables after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-vegetables lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds produce thousands of wild seeds that lie hidden in the dirt waiting for rain. Because weeds are wild plants, they grow faster and steal water and plant food from your garden vegetables.
ga: Jwɛi woɔ koo mli dumɔwui akpei abɔ ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni amɛmiimɛ nugbɔ. Ejaakɛ jwɛi ji koo mli tsei Amɛdaraa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ obɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting or sprouting so fast in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ loo shweremɔ oya waa yɛ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot when stored in warm, poorly ventilated places or when wounded during harvest. Keeping them in a cool, shaded, well-ventilated barn stops rot and slows down early sprouting.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto hei ni edɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ. aloo kɛ́ amɛpila yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ amɛ awo ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Ekpaa fitemɔ ni ehaa ekwɛ̃ɔ fioo.

english: Why is it good practice to prune or remove some lower leaves from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing lower leaves allows fresh air to blow through the plant, which prevents leaf diseases caused by damp weather. It also helps the plant send its energy into making larger tomatoes.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ baa helai ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛbaa lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ hu ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ tomatoi wuji.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily burn and dry out under direct sunlight. Planting plantains or shade trees provides a canopy that blocks intense heat, keeps the soil moist, and protects the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo ni naa wa lɛ haa hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn into white powder after keeping it in the barn for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ beni akɛto ŋmɔ mli nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The powder is caused by tiny insects called weevils that bore inside the dried grains to feed and lay eggs. Drying your maize thoroughly on clean surfaces and storing it in airtight bags or treated granaries stops these insects from destroying your harvest.
ga: Akɛ kooloi bibii feɔ powda nɛɛ. Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmei. ni shwieɔ dumɔwui ni egbi mli koni amɛtao niyenii ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ko ni he tse nɔ. ni akɛtoɔ vacuum kotokui loo ŋmɔji ni atsa mli lɛ amli. Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafite onibii.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the plant's main food for leaf growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer to the soil helps the plant turn green and produce healthy, full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii titri kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up small and bent instead of growing long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, soft earth to grow deep and expand easily. If the soil is hard, stony, or poorly tilled, the tuber struggles to push downwards, causing it to bend, split, or stop growing.
ga: Sweet potato tubers he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛdara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo atsuuu he nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Tso lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsi ehe kɛya shi, ni no baaha ebɔle, efo, loo ekpa dalɛ.

english: What causes the dark black spots on my cocoa pods that make them rot before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii anɔ ni haa amɛgboiɔ dani akpaa lɛ baa?

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, shaded environments. Clearing weeds, cutting away dead branches, and letting sunlight into the farm helps dry out damp air and stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ hulutsoo. jwɛi ni afoɔ niji ni egboi lɛ ni aaaŋmɛ gbɛ ni hulu la lɛ akpɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ agbi ni ekpa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and showing patchy yellow marks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus carried from plant to plant by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension officers prevents this disease from stunting your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni hela nɛɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava cuttings during the peak of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings require soil moisture to sprout their first roots and leaves. If planted during dry weather, the stem dries out and dies before roots can form to collect water from deep underground.
ga: Cassava tso lɛ mli tsei ni afo lɛ biɔ ni sũ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i dani klɛŋklɛŋ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ Tso lɛ tso lɛ gĩɔ ni egboɔ dani shishifãi lɛ feɔ koni amɛbua nu naa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall, thin, and weak when I plant maize and groundnuts very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough light and air to grow thick, sturdy stems and yield well.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ tsei ni mli wa ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when daytime heat gets too high or when soil moisture changes suddenly from dry to wet. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting during cooler windows helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu yɛ samflɛ ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop during the sunny afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: Pepper plants lose water quickly through their leaves under the intense afternoon heat. Drooping is their natural way of saving water; as long as the soil has moisture, the leaves will bounce back upright once evening temperatures drop.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane latsaa ni naa wa lɛ shishi. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ nu toɔ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ.

english: If I give my maize crop plenty of fertilizer, do I still need to worry about watering it regularly?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ, Ani ehe miihia ni mahao lolo yɛ nu ni mikɛbaafɔ nɔ daa lɛ he?

english: Yes, fertilizer and water work together. Fertilizer is like food for plants, but plants can only drink their food when it is dissolved in water. Without enough water, fertilizer sits in dry soil and can even burn the roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tamɔ niyenii kɛha tsei. Shi tsei baanyɛ anu niyenii kɛ́ akɛwo nu mli pɛ. Kɛji nu faaa lɛ, Fɛ̃i baaya nɔ ahi shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable garden lightly every day or give it a heavy soak twice a week?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu fioo daa gbi loo mawo nu mli waa shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli?

english: A heavy soak twice a week is usually better because deep water encourages roots to grow deep into the soil. Light daily watering keeps roots near the surface, where they dry out quickly under the hot sun.
ga: Nu ni mli wa ni akɛwoɔ mli shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ fioo daa gbi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbi oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and roll inwards during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon is a natural reaction to heat. The plant rolls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun, which stops water from evaporating too fast from the leaves.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni jɛɔ hulutsoo be mli baa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ aba shi. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ akajɛ baai lɛ amli oya tsɔ.

english: Yellow lower leaves mean the soil is running out of nitrogen. When nitrogen is low, the plant takes food from its old bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves, making the bottom leaves turn yellow and die.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, drought, or overwatering. The plant drops flowers to conserve its energy and keep itself alive until conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji dɔlɛ, hɔmɔ, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ fe nine lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛkwɛ amɛhe kɛyashi shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cassava plants look tall and thin when I plant them under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava needs direct sunlight to grow strong stems and thick roots. Under big shade trees, the plants stretch upwards searching for sunlight, making them tall, weak, and thin.
ga: Hulu la he miihia Yucca tɛ̃ɛ koni ekwɛ̃ tsei ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli tse. Tso agbo ni haa hulutsoo lɛ shishi Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛtao hulu la, ni amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa.

english: If I plant my pepper seeds very close together, won't I get more peppers from the same piece of land?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani manyɛ maná ŋmɔtɔ babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Planting too close causes plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Overcrowded plants remain small, weak, and produce far fewer peppers overall.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ yɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if there is enough soil in the field for all of them?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni manyɛ akwɛ amɛ fɛɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal water, sunlight, and plant food before your crop roots can reach them. They essentially starve your crops even if the soil looks large enough.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei amli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Nɔ titri ni amɛhaa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii lɛ kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eda bɔ ni sa po.

english: Why should I trim off the lower leaves of my tomato plants near the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Trimming lower leaves stops fungal diseases in the soil from splashing onto the plant during heavy rain, and allows air to flow better around the stem to keep the plant dry and healthy.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ bɔleɔ Tso lɛ shishi lɛ etee hiɛ. Koni tsei lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ

english: Maize draws the same nutrients out of the soil every year and attracts specific pests that hide in that soil. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or beans helps rebuild the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi ni egbalaa kooloi bibii pɔtɛɛ ni kɛ amɛhe ewo nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ama shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to build green leaves. Feeding the soil with well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do farmers plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the farm before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ amɛŋmɔji amli dani amɛduɔ ŋmãa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants decompose, that nitrogen stays in the soil, acting as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei fite Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Leaf curling and yellow mosaic patterns are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Using disease-resistant stem cuttings provided by agricultural officers prevents this from destroying your yield.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ mosaic ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Okwaayeli he nitsulɔi ni kɛ tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛkpaa lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ baatsi enɛ naa koni ekafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do I find small holes in my young corn leaves with brown dust inside the center shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii ni yɔɔ sũ ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central leaves of the corn plant. Spraying recommended treatments directly into the plant's leaf whorl early in the morning reaches and stops the caterpillars.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ afɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaashɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe ni ekpa amɛ.

english: Why do my stored cowpea seeds get tiny round holes and turn to powder after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina dumɔwui ni ato lɛ yɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ? ni etsɔɔ powda yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: This damage is caused by seed beetles (weevils) that lay eggs on the grains. Storing thoroughly dried seeds in airtight Purdue Improved Crop Storage (PICS) bags suffocates the insects without needing dangerous chemicals.
ga: Dumɔwui amli ŋmeii (weevils) ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmaa lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ Purdue Enhanced Crop Storage (PICS) kotokui ni akɛ tsɔne ni haaa nu mli ewo mli lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui tsuuu nii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Keeping larger shade trees or planting temporary crops like plantains provides shade and keeps the surrounding air moist while the young cocoa roots grow deep.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo be mli lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ haa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants drooping in the middle of the day even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: On hot afternoon days, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can draw it from the soil, causing temporary wilt. Placing dry grass mulch around the base of the plant cools the soil and reduces heat stress.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli baa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adɔ ni ebaaha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when high temperatures stress the plant or when water levels change too drastically between dry and wet spells. Keeping soil moisture steady through regular watering helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. aloo be mli ni nu lɛ mli shwereɔ waa yɛ be ni hulu enyɔ shi kɛ be ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ teŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni aaakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are my yams growing short and bent instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ kuku ni ebɔleɔ shi moŋ ni eeefee kakalɛ kɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Hard or stony soil blocks yam tubers from pushing straight down into the earth. Building tall, soft soil mounds or ridges allows the yam tubers to expand freely into smooth, large roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi tsiɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi amɛhe kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afee lɛ haa ŋshɔŋlooi lɛ agbɛɔ amɛshwãa amɛfeɔ shishifãi wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over right when the fruit bunch begins to get heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi trukaa beni aduawai akutsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛtsiɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow close to the soil surface, making the stem unable to support heavy fruit bunches during strong winds. Supporting the main stalk with a sturdy wooden prop or bamboo pole prevents the tree from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ anɔ Abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa fi tso titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ loo eshishijee.

english: How do I know the right time to spray medicine on my crops to keep pests away?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni mikɛshwie kooloi bibii?

english: Chemical sprays work best when applied early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the air is calm and cool. Spraying in hot sunshine evaporates the medicine, while spraying right before heavy rain washes it away before it can work.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo mli leebi loo shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni edɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsofa lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Beni ekɛ tsofa lɛ shwieɔ shi dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ, efoɔ ehe dani enyɛɔ etsuɔ ​​nii.

english: What causes black spots to appear on my cocoa pods before they turn completely rotten?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔi diji dani amɛfiteɔ?

english: Black spots on cocoa pods are usually caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, damp conditions. Clearing surrounding weeds and pruning tall shade trees lets light and air in to keep the pods dry.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ he lɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ ni ofolɔ tsei kakadaji lɛ koni kane kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha pods lɛ agbi.

english: Yellow leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, an important food crop roots draw from the soil. It can also happen when heavy rain swamps the farm and prevents roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii tsei ni he hiaa ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ashishifãi. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha ŋmɔ ko mli nu ni eha shishifãi lɛ shwie shi.

english: Is it better for me to apply fertilizer when the ground is dry or after rain has fallen?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should apply fertilizer when the soil is damp after a soft rain. Dry soil cannot dissolve fertilizer for roots to drink, while heavy downpours will wash fertilizer away down the hill.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nyɛŋ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni shishifãi lɛ anu nu. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even after spending nearly a year in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii lolo eyɛ mli akɛ amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aaafee afi moŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots stay thin if planted in hard, compacted soil where they cannot expand easily, or if strong weeds steal nutrients from the soil. Loose soil and regular weed clearing encourage fat tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ baafee bibioo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ ni nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo lɛ nɔ. Aloo kɛji jwɛi ni mli wa ju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ fɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that struggle to hold heavy bunches of fruit when soil becomes soft and muddy. Supporting the main stem with strong Y-shaped wooden poles or bamboo prevents wind damage.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛmɔmɔ aduawai babaoo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ muji. Kɛ́ akɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni tamɔ Y fiɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ naa.

english: Why do wild weeds seem to grow faster than my planted food crops whenever rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native plants naturally adapted to local conditions, so their roots absorb water and soil food faster than domesticated crops. Clearing weeds early stops them from shading and choking your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ shia lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkatsi hulu lɛ naa ni amɛkafite otsei bibii lɛ.

english: How can I prevent my pepper plants from drooping and drying up during the hot dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-pepper tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi ni amɛkagbi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Pepper plants droop because their shallow roots lose water quickly under the hot sun. Covering the ground around the stems with dry grass or leaves traps soil moisture and keeps root temperatures cool.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ gboiɔ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eye ebua ni shishifã lɛ mli fɛ̃i lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my young tomato plants collapse and die right after moving them to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tsei bibii lɛ gbee shi ni amɛgboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ajie amɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young tomato seedlings suffer from transplant shock if moved during hot mid-day sun. Moving seedlings late in the afternoon and watering them right away helps them root safely overnight.
ga: Tomato dumɔwui lɛ naa piŋmɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli kɛji ajie amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shwane mli ni awo amɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi shwereɔ shweshweeshwe nyɔɔŋ kome.

english: How can I tell when my groundnuts under the soil are mature enough to pull up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafo kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: You can check by pulling up two or three sample plants across the farm. If the inner shells have dark brown markings and the seeds are firm with full color, the whole field is ready for harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ tsei ahe nɔkwɛmɔnii enyɔ loo etɛ ni ooogbala yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ mligbɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ yɛ okadii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ amli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ, Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa.

english: This usually means your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow green and healthy. When the plant runs out of food in the soil, it pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ tsei bɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli ni ekɛhaa ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help make my soil richer for my next corn crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that can take nitrogen directly from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants die, that stored nitrogen stays in the dirt as natural food for your next crop.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava plants are mature and ready for harvesting without digging up the roots?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni o-cassava tso lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaakpa ni okɛ shishifãi lɛ efooo?

english: When cassava gets mature, the stems change color and harden, the plant begins to produce small flowers, and the bottom leaves naturally dry up and fall off, leaving a bare stem.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ baatsake amɛhe su ni amɛbaafee shiŋŋ. Tso lɛ miibɔi fɔfɔi bibii namɔ. ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Tso lɛ tso lɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni eshwɛ.

english: Why does my plantain stem die right after it yields only one bunch of plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ gboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ miye ŋmei kome pɛ niyenii lɛ?

english: A plantain stem is designed by nature to flower and bear fruit only once. Once the bunch matures, that stem dies, but it passes its life down to the small shoots (suckers) growing at its base.
ga: Adebɔɔ ji nɔ ni fee plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ. Kɛji kuu lɛ da Nakai tso lɛ baagbo. Shi ewala baa shi kɛyaa tsei bibii (tsei) ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ anɔ.

english: Groundnut flowers bloom above the ground, but once they are pollinated, the stem grows downward into the earth so the actual nuts can grow safely hidden under the soil away from the sun.
ga: Peanut fɔfɔii fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ afee lɛ pollination lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. So really nuts No hewɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eda shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni hulu la akashɛ ehe.

english: Cocoa trees drop their leaves to protect themselves from losing too much water during dry spells. Dropping leaves acts as a survival trick to keep the tree alive until rainy days return.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ko ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni tso lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ gbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress caused by extreme heat or unequal watering. The plant drops the flowers to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ ni ejaaa lɛ mli baa lɛ hewɔ. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight to make energy. When the leaves get plenty of sunlight without being shaded by weeds, they can feed and swell the tubers under the ground.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni jwɛi ehiɛɛɛ amɛhe nɔ lɛ, Ebaanyɛ ena niyenii ni eha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my rice stalks fall down flat on the wet soil just when the seeds are getting full?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa toi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? He ni dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛyiɔ lɛ?

english: This is called lodging, which happens when the stalks grow too tall and thin—often from too much fertilizer—or when heavy grains and high winds bend weak stems rooted in soft, mud-soaked ground.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ abobaahe. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ dara tsɔ ni amɛfee mlɛo—bei pii lɛ, ejɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli—loo kɛ́ dumɔwui ni tsii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ha tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi shwie shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli ewo muji lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my garden egg plants curling up and feeling sticky on the back?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ esɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tiny insects like aphids are living under the leaves and sucking out the plant juice. They leave behind a sticky liquid that causes the leaves to curl and turn black with mold.
ga: Kplukai bibii, tamɔ aphids, hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ tsei amli nu. Amɛshiɔ nu ko ni shwieɔ shi ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Can I save seeds from my current maize harvest to plant again next season, or do I always have to buy new ones?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpaa amrɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli? Aloo esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui heei be fɛɛ be?

english: It depends on the type of seed you bought. If you plant Open-Pollinated Varieties (OPVs), you can save and replant those seeds for one or two seasons. However, if you plant hybrid seeds, saved seeds will produce a much lower yield, so you must buy fresh hybrid seeds every season.
ga: Edamɔ dumɔwu henɔ ni oheɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji odu open pollinated (OPV) henɔi lɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ ato ni okwɛ nɔ kɛyashi be kome loo enyɔ. Shi, kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ, Stored dumɔwui lɛ baaná yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ohé hybrid dumɔwui heei daa be.

english: What does an extension officer mean when they tell me a seed is an OPV seed?
ga: Mɛni extension nitsulɔi lɛ tsɔɔ beni amɛkɛɛ mi akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ji OPV dumɔwui lɛ?

english: OPV stands for Open-Pollinated Variety. These are crops pollinated naturally by wind or insects, which means seeds from the harvest can be saved and replanted for up to two seasons while still producing good yields similar to the original plant.
ga: OPV damɔ shi kɛha Nɔ ni Akɛwoɔ Mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji tsei ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ abaanyɛ ato dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ ni adu ekoŋŋ kɛyashi bei enyɔ. yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai ni tamɔ shishijee tsei lɛ lolo lɛ.

english: What happens to my farm if I keep replanting saved seeds year after year for five years?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ afi fɛɛ afi kɛyashi afii enumɔ?

english: Over time, saved seeds lose their vigor and purity. Yields will drop significantly, and the plants will become more vulnerable to local pests and diseases. It is best to buy fresh certified seeds after two seasons.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ amɛhetsemɔ baa shi. Nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi waa. Ni tsei lɛ baafee mɛi ni helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baanyɛ atswa amɛ oya. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ bei enyɔ sɛɛ.

english: Which seeds are better for a smallholder farmer with a tight budget, hybrid seeds or OPV seeds?
ga: Mɛɛ dumɔwui hi kɛha okwaafoi bibii ni bɛ shika babaoo lɛ? Hybrid dumɔwui loo OPV dumɔwui

english: OPV seeds are usually better for farmers on a tight budget because they cost less to purchase initially and allow you to save seeds to replant for a couple of seasons without buying new ones right away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, OPV dumɔwui lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha okwaafoi ni yɔɔ shika fioo lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shika ni akɛheɔ nii lɛ faaa fe shishijee lɛ. Ni ehaa okɛ dumɔwui toɔ koni okɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ bei fioo komɛi amli ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé dumɔwui heei amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: What makes certified seeds from agricultural dealers better than the crop seeds I buy to eat at the local market?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni jɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi adɛŋ lɛ hi fe dumɔwui ni miheɔ koni miye yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially grown, cleaned, and treated to ensure almost every seed sprouts, resists diseases, and gives high yields. Grains bought at the food market may not sprout evenly and can carry plant diseases to your soil.
ga: Aduɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ, atsuuɔ he ni atsuɔ he nii. Enɛ haa nɔ ni miihe ashɛ dumɔwui fɛɛ dumɔwui baakwɛ̃, amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ helai, ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Ekolɛ ŋmaa ni aheɔ yɛ niyenii ajarayelihei lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsei ahe helai aya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does potassium in fertilizer help my crops grow better?
ga: Te potassium ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mitsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Potassium acts like a strength builder for crops. It strengthens plant stems so they do not fall over in the wind, helps the plant hold water during dry spells, and improves the size and weight of your harvest.
ga: Potassium tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hewalɛ. Ewajeɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ akatswa amɛ kɛya. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. ni oha okpamɔ lɛ dalɛ kɛ etsitsinɔnii aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce less yield if I keep planting on the same farm without adding fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛji midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ?

english: Every time you harvest crops, they take essential nutrients like potassium and nitrogen out of the soil. If you do not replenish these nutrients using fertilizer or manure, the soil becomes exhausted and cannot feed future crops.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii Amɛjieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium kɛ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli ekoŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafo ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ tsei ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Plants low in potassium usually show yellowing or scorching along the edges of their older leaves, making them look burnt. Stems may also become weak and produce small, light fruits or grains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni potassium faaa yɛ mli lɛ jieɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kpo. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ashã Tso lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ afee gbɔjɔmɔ ni ewo yibii loo dumɔwui bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why is it helpful for me to join a local farmers' group in my community?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ mihe baawo okwaafoi akuu ko ni yɔɔ mikutso lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Joining a farmers' group allows you to learn successful farming techniques from other farmers, share the cost of farm inputs, access loans or government extension support easily, and negotiate better prices when selling your crops.
ga: Okwaafoi akuu ko ni okɛ ohe woɔ mli lɛ haa okaseɔ okwaayeli he ŋaai ni yeɔ omanye kɛjɛɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi adɛŋ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo mlijaa Na nɔyeli nyɔmɔwoo loo yelikɛbuamɔ oya ni okɛ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ agba he sane kɛji oohɔ̃ɔ oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why did my crop yield drop during the second season even though I used saved seeds from a great first harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ wulu ko mli lɛ tsu nii moŋ.

english: Saved seeds naturally lose some of their genetic strength in the second generation, and the first crop likely consumed much of the soil's nutrients. Replenishing soil fertility and using fresh seeds restores high yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ lɛ fiteɔ amɛfɔmɔ su mli hewalɛ ko yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Ni ekolɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ye niyenii mli nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ekoŋŋ kɛ dumɔwui heei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa yibii babaoo baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and turn brown during the bright sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ mli egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight because their root systems and young leaves are delicate. They need shade trees or plantains planted next to them to block the intense heat and trap soil moisture until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai bibii lɛ waaa. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ ji koni akafee dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa, ni aha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves as a natural defense to save water and survive drought. The plant is not dead; it goes dormant, and as soon as the rain returns, it will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli. Tso lɛ gboko lolo, efee kpoo ni beni nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ kɛkɛ. Ebaakwɛ baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience severe heat or water stress. When the weather gets too hot or dry, the plant saves its energy to survive rather than using energy to produce fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ ba amɛnɔ. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ loo edɔ tsɔ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi moŋ fe hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my crops grow so rapidly and look extra green right after the first heavy rains of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida oya ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔji babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The dry soil accumulates nitrogen during the hot dry season, and the first rains release a sudden burst of this trapped nutrient all at once. This natural process feeds the plants an instant dose of energy, making them sprout quickly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ buaa nitrogen naa yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Ni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni amɔmɔ lɛ fɛɛ shikome. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ha amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: Yellowing on lower leaves is a clear sign that the soil is running low on nitrogen, which plants need to make food and stay green. The maize plant naturally pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed its young growing top leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Abɛi jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni ekɛhaa ŋwɛi baa bibii lɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in my field make my next maize crop yield better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen out of the air and stores it in the soil through their roots. When these plants die, they leave natural fertilizer behind for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ tsei nɛɛ gboi lɛ, amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry grass or dry leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Dumɔ nibii ni jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi yɔɔ mli.

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves keeps the hot sun from drying out the earth too quickly. It keeps the roots cool, holds water in the soil longer, and stops weeds from taking over the land.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akagbi shikpɔŋ lɛ oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Haa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩ jwɛi anaa koni ekaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my plantain plants produce small fruit bunches when I leave many shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii bibii lɛ? Beni ashiɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ

english: All the extra stems competing around the main plantain plant steal water and nutrients from the soil. By cutting away extra shoots and keeping only a few, the plant puts all its energy into growing big, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Trunks krokomɛi lɛ fɛɛ ni miitswa akaŋ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ. Dumɔwu titri lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni akɛ baai fioo komɛi pɛ ahi shi lɛ nɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out high off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the leaves create energy, which is sent down into the soil to grow big, heavy tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eha bulb lɛ adara ni etsii.

english: Why are there small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny black dirt in the center leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni egbɛ eshwa ni eyɛ muji diji bibii Yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This is caused by the fall armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the soft inner leaves of the maize plant to feed. The dark dirt is the caterpillar's waste, indicating an active infestation that needs treatment.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji fall armyworm ŋmeii. ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei amli baai bibii lɛ amli koni ekɛye Muji ni tsuɔ waa lɛ ji ŋmãa mli jwɛi. Enɛ tsɔɔ hela ko ni he hiaa ni atsa lɛ.

english: Why are the stems or branches of my cocoa trees getting swollen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ akutsei loo amɛniji lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Swelling on cocoa stems or shoots is a major sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease. It happens when sap-sucking insects like mealybugs infect the tree, causing the plant tissues to swell, which eventually weakens the tree and reduces your harvest if not managed.
ga: Kookoo tsei loo ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ ji okadi ko ni he hiaa ni tsɔɔ akɛ kookoo bud virus hela eba. Ebaa kɛji kooloi ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ mealybugs, ye tsei anɔ hela. ehaa tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ shwieɔ shi Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ naagbee ni ehaa ŋmaa lɛ baa shi kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes my crops to develop strange swollen bumps on specific spots of their stems?
ga: Mɛni miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee nɛkɛ shwiemɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɛɛ? yɛ tso lɛ mli hei pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ

english: Localized swelling is usually caused by plant viruses or microscopic pests that disrupt normal plant cell growth in the exact spot where the pest bit or infected the plant, leading to unusual tissue buildup.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli hela ko loo tsɛŋemɔ hela bibioo ko ni gbalaa tso lɛ mli wala yibii lɛ adalɛ ni sa yɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ eŋɔ tso lɛ loo etswa lɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fuumɔ ni yɔɔ he kome lɛ baa. Enɛ haa fãji ni ejaaa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa.

english: How can I tell if a crop is getting sick before the whole plant dies?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela mɔ ŋmɔshi nibii dani fɛɛ egbo?

english: Look out for early physical changes on individual parts of the plant, such as localized swelling on stems, discolored or yellowing leaf veins, stunted leaves, or sudden wilting in small areas of the crop.
ga: Taomɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ tsakemɔi mra yɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã mli, tamɔ he ko ni efuu yɛ tso lɛ shishi. Baai lɛ ahe fãji ni etsake loo etsɔ ŋmɔŋ, baai ni egbɔjɔ, loo ni egbo trukaa yɛ tso lɛ hei bibii.

english: Why do some crop diseases start in just one spot of the plant instead of affecting everything at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai komɛi jeɔ shishi yɛ he kome yɛ tso lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaafite nɔ fɛɛ nɔ shikome lɛ?

english: Diseases usually start right where an insect feeds or where infected sap enters the plant. The plant responds first at that exact entry point—causing local swelling or spots—before the sickness slowly spreads through the rest of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛji aye kooloi lɛ pɛ loo kɛ́ nu ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ bote tso lɛ mli. Tsei hereɔ nakai shishijee lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Ekɛ fuumɔ loo he ko ni yɔɔ he ko lɛ baa Dani hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ fiofio.

english: Why is it important for me to act quickly as soon as I see swollen spots on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee nɔ ko oya kɛji mina hei ni efuu yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ pɛ?

english: Swelling often indicates a contagious viral or fungal infection. Acting quickly to isolate or remove infected plants stops pests and diseases from spreading to nearby healthy crops and damaging your entire yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fuumɔ tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ. Feemɔ oya ni ojie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mli loo ojie amɛ. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. ni efite onibii fɛɛ.

english: Should I immediately cut down a crop tree if I notice its main stem is swelling?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo tso ko amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mina akɛ eshishifã titri lɛ efuu?

english: For serious viral diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot, chemical sprays cannot cure the tree once stem swelling appears. Cutting down and removing infected trees is often necessary to stop the sickness from spreading to surrounding healthy trees.
ga: Kɛha helai ni mli wa ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli tamɔ Cocoa Swollen Shoot lɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ atsa tso lɛ kɛji tso lɛ shishi efuu. Bei pii lɛ, ehe hiaa ni afolɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajie amɛ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ.

english: How do diseases that cause stem swelling move from one crop to another in my farm?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni hela ko ni haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ajɛ tso kome mli kɛya ekroko mli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: These diseases are mostly spread by tiny insects like mealybugs or aphids, which feed on an infected plant and then crawl or get carried by ants and wind to nearby healthy plants, transferring the sickness through plant sap.
ga: Helai nɛɛ ateŋ babaoo jɛɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs loo aphids mli. Amɛyeɔ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛkpãa loo ŋmeii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ woɔ amɛ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. Kɛtsɔ hela ni akɛtsɔɔ tso mli nu nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does a sick crop seem to spread infection faster to crops planted very close to it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ gbɛɔ hela amɛshwaa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ?

english: When crops are planted close together and their branches or roots touch, disease-carrying insects can easily crawl between them, and infected sap or fungi can travel directly from plant to plant much faster.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe ni amɛniji loo amɛshishifãi lɛ taa amɛhe. Kplukai ni kɛ helai baa lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ nakai tsei lɛ ateŋ mlɛo. Ni nu loo ŋmei ni hela emɔ lɛ baanyɛ aya tso kome nɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛya tso kroko nɔ oya kwraa.

english: Can a tree naturally heal itself and recover after its stem starts swelling from a sickness?
ga: Ani tso ko baanyɛ atsa ehe yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ beni eshishifã lɛ ebɔi fũu kɛjɛ hela mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Most viral crop sicknesses that cause swelling cannot be cured by the plant itself. Without farmer action to remove the infected plant parts or spray for carrier insects, the sickness usually worsens until the plant dies.
ga: Tso he helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ateŋ babaoo lɛ, tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ nyɛŋ atsa. Kɛji okwaafoi ejieee tso lɛ fãi ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ loo amɛshwieee kooloi ni kɛ hela lɛ baa lɛ anɔ lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ mli woɔ wu kɛyashiɔ tso lɛ gboɔ.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to check for swollen stems and leaf sickness?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ kɛji tsei lɛ efuu kɛ baai hela?

english: It is best to inspect your farm weekly, especially during the rainy season when moisture encourages insect activity and plant diseases to grow and spread rapidly.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa otsi. Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli Fɛ̃i woɔ kooloi bibii kɛ tsei ahe helai hewalɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow before they even start producing corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani amɛje ŋmãa po shishi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, or the soil has too much standing water that is choking the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni ekã shi babaoo ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests every year even though I plant at the exact same time every rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ be kome mli daa nugbɔshiimɔ be moŋ lɛ?

english: Soil loses its strength when the same crop draws out the same nutrients repeatedly without a break or proper fertilizers to restore the soil's nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he waaa kɛji tsei komekomei lɛ jie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ. ni efiteee loo ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fataaa he koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba

english: How do crop boosters help my plants grow better than using regular soil fertilizers alone?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nibii ni haa tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ pɛ?

english: Crop boosters feed the plant directly through its leaves, giving it a quick energy lift to build stronger roots and absorb soil nutrients much faster.
ga: Tso mli nibii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ oya koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa ni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya kwraa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop all their flowers before any green pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from sudden hot weather or lack essential nutrients needed to support the extra weight of growing pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ miipiŋ amɛ loo amɛbɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni baaye abua ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli tsiimɔ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plant leaves curl up tightly during the sunniest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is the plant's natural way of protecting itself from severe heat and saving water so its leaves do not dry out.
ga: Baai lɛ ni aaakpɛtɛ he lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni ekɛbuɔ nu he. koni baai lɛ akagbi

english: Why are my pepper plants staying small and refuse to grow taller after transplanting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ji bibioo kwraa ni ekpooɔ akɛ ebaada babaoo yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Stunted pepper plants usually mean weeds are stealing their food, or the soil around the roots is too hard and dry for them to spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ jwɛi miiju amɛ niyenii loo shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli wa ni egbi tsɔ ni enyɛŋ egbɛ eshwa.

english: What makes my green cocoa pods turn black and rot while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ tsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboi beni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly during heavy rains and cool, damp weather, especially when cocoa trees are crowded together without enough fresh air.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ kookoo tsei eyi amɛhe obɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli.

english: Is it better to apply pest control products when my crops are young or wait until I see insects eating the leaves?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ atsu nii beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lolo loo mamɛ kɛyashi mana kooloi ni miiye baai lɛ?

english: It is best to protect young crops early so insects do not destroy the leaves before the plant grows strong enough to produce fruit.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooobu tsei bibii ahe mra. Enɛ ji koni kooloi akafite baai lɛ dani tso lɛ adara ni ewo yibii.

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots are fully ready to dig up without pulling up the whole crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ ni ajieee ŋmãa lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Why do my harvested grains spoil and get full of tiny holes while sitting in my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ egbo ni bu bibii eyi mli obɔ lɛ? Beni mita mi shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grains spoil in storage mainly because they were bagged while still damp, which attracts weevils that lay eggs inside the soft grain.
ga: Nibii ni fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ titri ji akɛ, awoɔ amɛ kotoku mli be mli ni amɛmli edɔ lolo. Enɛ gbalaa ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. It often happens when heavy rains wash away nutrients from the topsoil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and looking tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee bibioo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, mites, or aphids sucking the sap from young leaves, or passing a leaf-curl virus to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo ekɛ hela ko ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly on land where heavy earth-moving machines recently cleared trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsɔnei ni tsii ni akɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ejie tsei lɛ anɔ pɛŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy machinery scrapes away the fertile topsoil and packs the earth down very hard. This stops crop roots from breathing, spreading easily, or finding nutrients.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ anɔ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya loo enaa niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines high up to catch light and keeps leaves off damp soil where diseases easily spread.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ koni enine ashɛ la nɔ, ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ he ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops do better on raised earth mounds than on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ fe gɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Raised soil mounds keep the soil loose so roots can spread easily, and they help excess rainwater drain away so crop roots do not rot in standing water.
ga: Gɔŋ ni awo nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. ni ehaa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa No hewɔ lɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ egbooo yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli.

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when temperatures get too high or when there is sudden water stress. Without pollination during favorable weather, the flower simply drops off.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu he haomɔ ba trukaa. Kɛji akɛ pollination bɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni hi amli lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over when a light storm comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ ahum be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that stay near the topsoil. When the heavy fruit bunch matures, the plant becomes top-heavy and needs support stakes so wind does not uproot it.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni aduawai akuu ni tsii lɛ edara kwraa lɛ Tsei lɛ tsii ni ehe miihia ni akɛ sɛɛfimɔ tsei atsu nii koni kɔɔyɔɔ akajie amɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are rotting under the ground before digging them up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mafo amɛ?

english: When cassava roots rot from wet soil, the top leaves turn yellow, wilt, and drop early, and the stem base may turn dark or emit a foul smell.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fite kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛgboɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya, ni ŋmei shishifã lɛ baanyɛ afee diŋŋ loo eŋɔɔɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea pods get small holes and caterpillars inside them right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea pods lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii yɛ mli dani akpaa.

english: Moth pests lay eggs inside cowpea flowers. Once hatched, the tiny caterpillars bore directly into the growing pods to feed on the tender beans.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ cowpea fɔfɔi amli. Beni amɛfɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ boteɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛye ŋmeii bibii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I clear all the big trees from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. They need temporary shade trees, like plantains, to shield them and keep the surrounding air and soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛbu kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ he ni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when I clear all the big trees off my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Leaving taller trees or planting temporary crops like plantains provides living shade that shields young cocoa from sun damage and keeps soil moisture from evaporating.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. tsei kakadaji ni ashiɔ Aloo, be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo be ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the crop even produces corncobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ woɔ abele ŋmeii po lɛ?

english: Yellowing on lower leaves usually signals a lack of nitrogen in the soil. The maize plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed new growing leaves, indicating that your soil needs nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ baai momo mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha baai heei ni miida lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli.

english: Why are my plantain bunches getting smaller over time even though I am using the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ.

english: When a plantain root grows too many young shoots (suckers) around its base, all those shoots compete for soil nutrients and water. Pruning away extra suckers and keeping only two or three per main stand allows the plant to form large, heavy bunches.
ga: Beni plantain shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii (shishifãi) ​​babaoo tsɔ ni bɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ. Nakai tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni okɛ enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ahi shi yɛ shidaamɔhe titri kome mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ afee kui wuji ni tsii.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are mature enough to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
