ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efolɔɔɔ mli?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack or swell due to expanding tubers beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Ashiɔ tso lɛ shishi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ loo efuɔ be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant cowpeas together with my maize crop on the same farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmãa baafata ŋmãa he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas alongside maize is beneficial. Cowpeas are legumes that fix nitrogen from the air directly into the soil, which helps feed the maize plant naturally and improves soil fertility.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he. Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni haa nitrogen lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to clear wood sticks and stake my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tso lɛ ni madu sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on wooden stakes spreads the leaves out to catch sunlight, which powers root growth to produce bigger yam tubers. It also keeps leaves off damp ground to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ebaa ni egbɛ eshwa koni ekɛhere hulu la lɛ atuu. Enɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji. Ehaa baai lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience severe heat stress or lack of water during flowering. Keeping soil consistently moist and planting windbreaks or light shade can protect blossoms so they can set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu koni kɔɔyɔɔ loo hulutsoo aba lɛ baanyɛ abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: How does covering the soil around my pepper plants with dry grass help them grow better?
ga: Bɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi woɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Spreading dry grass around crops acts as mulch. Mulch blocks direct heat from sun rays, slows down water evaporation from the soil, prevents weed seeds from sprouting, and decays into nutrients over time.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛbaabɔle Crops lɛ he lɛ baatsu nii akɛ mulch. Mulch tsiɔ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. Etsiɔ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli

english: Holes in the central funnel of young corn plants are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide deep inside the leaves to feed, so checking early and treating the funnels protects the plant's growing center.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye nii. No hewɔ lɛ, kwɛmɔ mra. Ni gbɛ ni tsɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ he.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist and plants are actively growing—usually 2 to 3 weeks after crop sprouting. Avoid applying fertilizer on dry soil or right before continuous heavy rainfall, which can wash nutrients away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei miida lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ tso lɛ kwɛ̃mɔ sɛɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ he. ni baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ mli

english: Why is it important to apply liquid fertilizer to my crops on the exact day I mix it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ gbi ni mikɛ amɛ futuɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Once mixed with water, liquid fertilizers can lose their strength or chemically break down over time. Applying the mixture immediately ensures your crops get the full strength of the nutrients.
ga: Kɛ akɛ nu futu mli lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite hewalɛ loo tsofai baanyɛ afite yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ tsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa niyenii ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Can I mix different fertilizers together in one sprayer to save time on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafutu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ tsɔne kome mli koni mikɛ be akafite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you can combine certain fertilizers like nitrogen boosters with other liquid nutrients, but you must be careful. Mixing incompatible products can cause them to clump up or damage the leaves of your plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen boosters awo mli. kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni ji nu, shi esa akɛ okwɛ ohe jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni okɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛfee ekome loo efite otso lɛ baai.

english: Does the time of day I spray fertilizer on my plant leaves make any difference?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwieɔ tsei ahe yɛ gbi lɛ mli be mli lɛ haa srɔtofeemɔ baa?

english: Yes, it is best to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon. High midday sun can dry up the liquid before leaves absorb it, or even burn the wet leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ afɔse nɔ leebi loo shwane. Hulu la ni tsoɔ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ aha nu lɛ agbi dani baai lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Even wet leaves can burn.

english: What does nitrogen actually do to help my crops grow?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni nitrogen feɔ diɛŋtsɛ? Koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Nitrogen acts like building food for plants. It helps them build strong stems and leafy growth, giving them a healthy dark green color so they can make energy to grow.
ga: Nitrogen acts like food for plants. Eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛtswaa tsei ni wa kɛ baai ni daraa. Ha amɛ su ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ji eŋɔli ni mli edɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛdara.

english: How can I tell if my crops are hungry for nitrogen fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛha nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: When crops lack nitrogen, their leaves turn pale green or yellow starting from the bottom leaves, and the plant stays small and weak instead of growing bushy.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen Ebaai lɛ baafee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Ni tsei lɛ baakã he ahi shi bibii ni amɛhe waaa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ yɛ kui amli.

english: How will I know if my crops like a liquid fertilizer I applied?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ nu ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ egbɔ?

english: Within a few days to a week after application, a crop that responds well will show perkier leaves, a deeper green color, and fresh new shoots.
ga: yɛ gbii fioo komɛi kɛyashi otsi kome mli yɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ Tsei ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baajie baai ni yɔɔ miishɛɛ babaoo kpo. Eyɛ su eŋɔli ni mli edɔ fe tsutsu lɛ. ni ŋmeii heei jeɔ kpo

english: What happens if I give my crops too much nitrogen fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen makes plants produce huge soft leaves, but it can delay flowering and fruiting, attract pests, and cause the plants to fall over during heavy winds.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Shi ebaanyɛ eha fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo asɛɛ afo. Egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa tsei shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli.

english: What is Miller Activa, and how does it help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni ji Miller Activa ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Miller Activa is a liquid nutrient booster sprayed on plant leaves. It supplies essential micronutrients that help plants absorb soil food better and stay strong during dry weather.
ga: Miller Activa ji tsofa ko ni haa mɔ he waa ni ji nu ni akɛshwieɔ tsei ahe baai anɔ. Ehaa niyenii bibii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Is a foliar spray booster like Miller Activa the same as standard sack fertilizer like NPK?
ga: Ani Miller Activa foliar spray ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ NPK kotoku mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ yeɔ egbɔ?

english: No, sack fertilizers like NPK provide the main heavy meal through the roots, while foliar boosters act like quick vitamins sprayed on leaves to give crops an instant energy kick.
ga: Dabi, ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli tamɔ NPK lɛ haa niyenii titri lɛ kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni haa tso lɛ baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ vitamini ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ oya koni eha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do some crops react faster to spray fertilizers on their leaves than fertilizers put in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaves have small openings that can drink liquid nutrients directly and fast, whereas soil fertilizers rely on moisture to dissolve and root systems to take them up slowly.
ga: Baai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni baanyɛ anu nu mli niyenii tɛ̃ɛ oya Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ damɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ koni etsɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ koni amɛŋɔ niyenii nɛɛ fiofio.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make food and grow strong. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores this nutrient so the maize can regain its rich green color and grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛdara waa Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ niyenii nɛɛ aku sɛɛ aba. Koni ŋmãa lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting the exact same crop on my farm every single year make my harvest smaller each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ji ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ? afi, ni no haa mikpamɔ lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests that feed on that crop to build up in the dirt. Rotating crops—like planting legumes or beans after maize—allows the soil to rebuild its richness naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ tsei lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ ehe woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct, harsh sunlight burns their leaves and dries out their tender roots. Keeping canopy trees or planting food crops like plantains alongside them creates a cooler environment that protects the young cocoa.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi bibii lɛ agbi. Tsoi bibii akwɛmɔ loo niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa.

english: Why do my planted seeds fail to sprout when I put them in the ground during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji mikɛwo shikpɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Seeds need moisture to break their outer shell and start growing. If the soil stays completely dry, the seed remains inactive or dries out inside the dirt before it ever gets the chance to shoot up.
ga: Dumɔwui he hiaa nu koni amɛgbala kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ ni amɛbɔi dalɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa lolo Dumɔwui lɛ baakã he ahi shi ni amɛtsuuu nii loo amɛbaagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛná hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes in the center leaves of my maize during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ? Ni maye bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele baai lɛ ateŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which target the soft tender leaves inside the funnel of young maize. Inspecting fields early and applying recommended pest control methods protects the growing plant before the pest destroys the yield.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli lɛ anɔ. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii kɛgbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei ni miida lɛ ahe dani tsɛŋemɔ helai akpãtã ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water sits in the soil around them without draining away. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow off, keeping the roots firm and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ ni efooo kɛyaa. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of yellow flowers, but the flowers drop off without forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when the plant experiences extreme dry spells. Maintaining steady soil moisture through regular watering or mulching helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ ni naa wa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why does trimming away some of the side branches on my pepper plants help them produce bigger peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-pepper tsei lɛ asɛɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ pepper wuji lɛ?

english: When a pepper plant has too many extra branches and leaves, it spends its energy maintaining leaf growth instead of growing fruit. Removing small or unnecessary branches redirects that energy directly into making larger, healthier peppers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tso lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai babaoo tsɔ Ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii. niji bibii ni ajieɔ Loo niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ tsɔɔ nakai hewalɛ lɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ koni eha ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and heavy, water-filled stems that struggle to hold up heavy bunches in strong winds. Propping up the main stem with sturdy wooden Y-sticks provides extra support until harvest time.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ tsei ni tsii ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛmɔ ŋmeii wuji amli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni tamɔ Y ni akɛ tso ni wa fee lɛ to tso wulu lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha eye ebua babaoo kɛyashi kpamɔɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds growing around my crops cause my plants to stay small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mihe lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiha mitsei lɛ miifee bibii ni amɛhe waaa?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. Clearing weeds early ensures that all the nutrients and moisture in the dirt go straight to feeding your crops.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to make leaves green and healthy. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the soil the food the plant needs to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my cassava plant growing very tall with thick green leaves, but the tubers underground are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen from overly rich soil, it spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing energy in its roots. Giving the plant balanced nutrients with potassium helps it focus on making big roots instead of just big leaves.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii babaoo lɛ nɔ lɛ Ekɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Niyenii ni sa ni potassium yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛhaa tso lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi wuji ni baakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe baai wuji kɛkɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains on the same farm where I am growing young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ kookoo tsei bibii yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive and can easily get scorched by intense sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa seedlings need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa, ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ha kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops produce a smaller yield when I plant the seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for the same water and nutrients in the soil, and their leaves block each other from sunlight. Spacing them correctly allows each plant to get enough food and light to produce a maximum yield.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu he. Kɛji akɛ ato he ko jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before turning into actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ tomato diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or irregular watering. If the soil gets too dry while it is hot, the plant sheds its flowers to save water; keeping the soil evenly moist helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ be mli ni edɔ lolo lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my green pepper plants dropping their small fruits before they can grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bell pepper tso lɛ miiho aduawai bibii lɛ? dani eda

english: Pepper plants drop young fruits when they do not get a steady supply of water or when the soil lacks essential minerals like calcium. Watering regularly and maintaining healthy soil helps the plant hold onto its fruit until harvest time.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ aduawai bibii kɛji amɛnáaa nu daa loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ eyibii lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do I find armyworms damaging my maize crop early in the morning and late in the evening, but not during midday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa akɛ ŋmeii miifite mi-abele ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ? Shi jeee shwane mli?

english: Armyworms dislike direct heat and bright sunlight, so they hide deep inside the center of the maize plant or in the soil during the hottest parts of the day. They only come out to feed when it cools down, which is why early morning or late afternoon is the best time to check for them.
ga: Armyworms sumɔɔɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli shɔŋŋ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbatao niyenii pɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, be nɛɛ ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ okwɛ amɛ.

english: Why do weeds seem to make my crops grow slower even when I use good seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ daa blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kpakpai tsuɔ nii moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast growers that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from the soil before your crops can reach them. Clearing weeds early ensures that your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow fast and strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why do I have to erect tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mato tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up to catch as much sunlight as possible, which powers the growth of the tubers under the ground. Staking also lifts the leaves off the wet ground, protecting them from soil diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. ni tsirɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ adalɛ Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni helai akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the roots of my crops start rotting when water sits on my field for several days after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboɔ kɛ́ nu hi miŋmɔji amli gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen from the soil to breathe just like human beings do. When heavy rain sits on the land without draining, it fills up all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots and causing them to rot.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tsei shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu bɛ mli Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Cocoa trees need protection from scorching heat. Without shade plants, direct sunlight burns the leaves and dries out the tree faster than its roots can take up water from the soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu koko tsei ahe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ lɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha tso lɛ agbi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when there is heavy rainfall late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess water sits in the field without proper drainage, the roots drown from a lack of oxygen and begin to rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔ ko ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are too high or air is too dry, preventing proper pollination. Without pollination, the plant sheds the flower instead of growing a tomato.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Koni akɛtsi pollination naa jogbaŋŋ Kɛji pollination bɛ Tsei baafɔ yɛ tomato najiaŋ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves turn light yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow maize leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient that helps plants build green leaves and grow strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Eji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛ kwɛ̃ɔ tsei ni wa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize in the exact same field season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground over time.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees grow smaller bunches if I let all the shoots grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ mli gbalaa kɛfeɔ kui bibii kɛji miha ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: Extra shoots act like extra mouths to feed, stealing plant food and water from the main stem. Removing extra shoots leaves all the nutrients for one stem to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tsoi krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ daaŋ krokomɛi ni akɛyeɔ nii. Amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei amli, ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ haa tso kome feɔ ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: When crops are crowded, leaves block each other's sunlight and roots fight for the same water, causing all plants to grow weak and yield less food.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe hulu la lɛ naa. ni shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ yɛ nu kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why does cutting off the lower leaves of my crop help produce bigger fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔ lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ yibii wuji lɛ?

english: Removing lower, shaded leaves stops the plant from wasting energy on old leaves and directs all its water and nutrients into growing larger fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ, ehaaaa tso lɛ afite hewalɛ yɛ baai momo lɛ anɔ, ni etsɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni eda ni etsɔ aduawai wuji lɛ gbɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa fiofio eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong, fast-growing roots that steal water and fertilizer nutrients right away, leaving your crops hungry and thirsty despite your efforts.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni daa oya ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ha hɔmɔ kɛ kumai aye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ mɔdɛŋ ni obɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies hiding under the leaves and sucking out plant juice, which damages the leaf tissue as it grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe tee baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Can I plant my maize under big shade trees, or do they need direct sunlight to grow well?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋtayaa agbo ko shishi? Aloo esa akɛ enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ tɛ̃ɛ dani eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Maize needs full, direct sunlight to produce strong stalks and large cobs. Growing them under heavy shade makes the plants tall, thin, and weak, resulting in little to no grain harvest.
ga: Abɛi he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji aba. Kɛ́ adu yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee kakadaŋŋ agbo, amɛhe afee mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni no baaha dumɔwui fioo pɛ aba loo abaakpa kwraa.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to extreme heat and direct sunlight. They need temporary shade trees or plantains around them to protect their soft leaves from burning while their root system gets established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei loo plantains ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko he miihia amɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe. Enɛ buɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he beni shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the stems of my tomato plants rot and turn soft at the ground level during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess dampness and water standing around the base of the plant create a cold, flooded environment that encourages soil fungi to attack the roots and lower stem, causing them to rot.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ nu ni bɔleɔ Tsei ashishitoo lɛ he lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ fɛ̃i baa. Enɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua shishifãi kɛ shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Will leaving extra water in my yam mounds during the wet season hurt my crop?
ga: Ani nu ni fa fe nine ni mashi yɛ ŋmeii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, yam tubers need well-drained soil. When the mounds stay too damp and cold for long periods, air cannot reach the roots, causing the yams to rot underground before you can harvest them.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ he miihia sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ. Beni gɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves start curling up when we have cold, wet mornings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ kɛji wɔyɛ leebi ni fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Cold temperatures combined with high soil moisture stress the pepper plants, slowing down their ability to take up nutrients and making them susceptible to fungal diseases and leaf curl.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni mli ejɔ ni akɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ babaoo fata he lɛ haoɔ pepper tsei. Hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ baa shi. ni ehaa amɛhe feɔ oya kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: What will happen if I plant my maize seeds very close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ bu kome mli?

english: Planting seeds too close creates intense competition for light, water, and soil nutrients. The crowded plants shade each other out, leading to weak stems and tiny or empty cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa kɛha la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ shade. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. loo nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Why do my cabbages stay small and leafy instead of forming hard, round heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ ji bibioo ni eyɛ baai yɛ yitsei ni wa ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to head when conditions are too hot or when plants are crowded too closely together. They require proper spacing and stable soil moisture to cool the root zone and form tight heads.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ awo cabbage yitso be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ. Amɛmiitao gbɛ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ koni amɛha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛfee bulbs ni mli wa.

english: Why do I need to cover my vegetable seedbed with palm fronds after sowing the seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ ŋmei tsei aha mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ beni midu dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fragile seeds and new sprouts can easily be destroyed by direct heat from the sun or washed away by heavy rain. The palm fronds regulate the environment by keeping the soil moist, cool, and shaded.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ afite dumɔwui ni waaa kɛ dumɔwui heei lɛ oya loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo amɛ. Palm baai lɛ kudɔɔ shihilɛ lɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni amɛhaa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa hulutsoo baa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my onion seedlings suddenly collapse and die in large numbers in the nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onion dumɔwui lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛmiigboi babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by excessive moisture and poor airflow in a crowded nursery bed, which creates a damp environment where damaging fungi thrive and cut off the tiny plant stems at the soil line.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo ni fa fe nine kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni hoɔ yɛ gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhei ni eyi obɔ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. ni haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa Biɛ ji he ni ŋmei ni fiteɔ nii lɛ daa ni efoɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my fresh plantain suckers take so long to start growing when planted in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei heei lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛjeɔ dalɛ shishi kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers need high moisture and warm soil to wake up from transplant shock. In dry, harsh soil, the sucker stops growing to protect itself from drying out entirely until moisture returns.
ga: Plantain suckers lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ni fa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ koni amɛte shi kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ mli. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni mli wa nɔ lɛ Suckers lɛ baakpa amɛdalɛ koni amɛkagbi kwraa kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do seeds like maize or cowpea sprout into tiny plants when I put them in moist soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ kɛfeɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Be ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Inside every healthy seed is a tiny living baby plant and a packed storage of food. When the seed absorbs water from the damp soil, it softens its outer skin and uses that stored food to grow its first root and leaf before it can feed from the soil.
ga: Dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli lɛ, ŋmei bibioo ko ni hiɛ kã yɔɔ mli. kɛ niyenii ni akɛtoɔ he jogbaŋŋ Kɛji dumɔwui shwie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ Ebaaha kponɔgbɛ lɛ afee blɛoo. ni okɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ afee klɛŋklɛŋ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ dani eye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii.

english: Why does a seed yam start growing green shoots in my storage barn even without soil or water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ mi shĩa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ loo nu bɛ jɛmɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: A yam tuber is a large storage storehouse filled with water and food saved by the plant. When the season changes and the air gets warm, the yam uses its own stored food to grow new shoots, even before it is planted in the ground.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji nitoohei wuji ni nu kɛ niyenii ni tso lɛ toɔ lɛ eyi mli obɔ. Beni bei lɛ tsakeɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli woɔ la lɛ, Sweet potatoes kɛ amɛ niyenii ni amɛto lɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo ŋmeii heei. Dani abaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants spread out wide towards the sun during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa babaoo kɛyaa hulu lɛ he yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves work like kitchens for the plant. They use sunlight to turn air and water into sweet plant food, so they spread out wide to catch as much sunlight as possible to build big tubers underground.
ga: Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nitsumɔhe ŋtayaai. Amɛkɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛtsakeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii ni ŋɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa he fɛɛ he koni amɛmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ ni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔnei wuji.

english: When the soil does not have enough nutrients, the plant behaves like a mother feeding her baby first. It moves stored food out of its old, bottom leaves up to the top to keep the young leaves and developing corn cobs growing.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Tso lɛ baafee enii tamɔ nyɛ ni haa ebii lɛ niyenii. Ejieɔ niyenii ni ato lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi lɛ ashishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni baai bibii akwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato plant leaves roll up tightly during the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling up leaves is a defense trick. By curling its leaves, the plant hides them from the scorching heat so it doesn't lose too much body water through sweating in the hot sun.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛtsɔɔmɔ ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa. kɛtsɔ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ baate baai lɛ kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, ejieɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ latsaa ni ekɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do some flowers fall off my pepper plants without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi komɛi shwieɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: If a plant feels it is short on water or soil food, it drops extra flowers. It does this to save its limited energy so it can focus on maturing just a few healthy pepper fruits instead of dying from overload.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ nu he akɛ nu loo niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi. Feemɔ enɛ koni okɛ hewalɛ fioo pɛ ato. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmeii fioo komɛi pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni oookwɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbo kɛjɛ nitsumɔ ni fe nine mli lɛ

english: Why do bees and flies buzz around the flowers on my garden watermelon vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii tswaa gbee lɛ? Yɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ watermelon wain tso ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ he?

english: Watermelon plants have male and female flowers. Bees carry tiny yellow powder called pollen from the male flower to the female flower, which tells the female flower to start swelling into a sweet fruit.
ga: Watermelon tsei yɛ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei. Wuobii hiɛɔ powda bibii ni ji ŋmɔŋ. Atsɛɔ no akɛ pollen ni jɛɔ fɔfɔi nuu lɛ mli kɛyaa fɔfɔi yoo lɛ mli. Enɛ kɛɛ fɔfɔi yei lɛ akɛ amɛje shishi amɛfu ni amɛtsɔ aduawai ni ŋɔɔ.

english: Why do tall maize plants grow short red roots above the ground right at the bottom of the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ yɛ shishifãi kukuji tsuru ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: These extra upper roots work like support poles holding up a tall tent. They anchor the heavy stem firmly into the dirt so strong wind and rain do not knock the plant down.
ga: Nɛkɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi nɛɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsei ni fiɔ buu kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ. Amɛkɛ tsei akutsei ni wa lɛ fĩɔ shikpɔŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ akashwie tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa leaves are delicate like human infants and burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. They need companion plants like plantains to act as natural umbrellas until their roots grow strong.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo tamɔ abifabii, ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni fata amɛhe, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Why does putting decomposed cow manure around my crop roots make the leaves turn dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ awo he lɛ? Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miiha baai lɛ miitsɔ eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa lɛ?

english: Manure contains rich natural food called nitrogen. When roots drink it up, it gives the plant the materials it needs to make green leaves that can produce plenty of growth energy.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli niyenii babaoo ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ enu nu lɛ egbe naa lɛ Tso lɛ baaná nibii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfee baai eŋɔli ni baanyɛ ajie hewalɛ babaoo kɛha dalɛ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so quickly when left out in the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: High heat speeds up the internal ripening and breathing process of tomatoes, causing them to break down and decay quickly. Storing them in a cool, shaded area slows this process down and extends their freshness.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ baaha tomatoi lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛmu oya. Enɛ haa tomatoi lɛ fãa ni amɛfiteɔ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha nifeemɔ nɛɛ aya hiɛ fioo, ni ebaaha amɛhe ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does my harvested cassava turn dark and unusable just a few days after digging it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ mli ewo duŋ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ ni mikɛfo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots lose their source of nutrients immediately after harvest, triggering a rapid internal chemical reaction that causes rot. Processing them quickly or storing them in moist soil or cool containers keeps them usable longer.
ga: Beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ laajeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ. Enɛ haa tsofa ko ni yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ oya ni ekɛ fitemɔ baa. Feemɔ oya loo okɛto shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ loo nɔ ko ni mli ejɔ mli koni akɛtsu nii be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my leafy green vegetables wilt and die within hours after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmɔji lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni mikpa amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Leafy greens release water through their leaves continuously. Once harvested, they can no longer draw water from the soil, so keeping them in cool, dark, or moist places prevents rapid water loss and wilting.
ga: Aduawai ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ jieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ akpa Amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni duŋ ewo, loo he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ akafite oya ni amɛkagbo.

english: How does keeping fresh vegetables in a cold space or cool box keep them good for weeks?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni aduawai heei ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni mli ejɔ loo adeka ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛhi shi otsii babaoo?

english: Cold temperatures put crops into a sleeping state by slowing down their respiration rate and stopping bad bacteria from growing, which allows vegetables to stay fresh for a month or longer.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni mli ejɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ wɔɔhe kɛtsɔ amɛmumɔ ni amɛmuɔ lɛ ni ehaa amɛmuɔ fioo lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa helai fɔji ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ daalɛ kpaa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ hiɔ shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ nyɔŋ kome loo nɔ ni fe nakai.

english: Why do green plantains ripen and turn soft so fast after I harvest the whole bunch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains eŋɔli lɛ shwereɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo oya beni mikpa ŋmɔ muu fɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Harvested plantains produce a natural ripening gas called ethylene that builds up and speeds up soft rot. Keeping them separated and stored in a cool place slows down ethylene activity.
ga: Plantains ni akpaa lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni haa mɔ shwereɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene. Enɛ baabua ehe naa ni eha fitemɔ aya hiɛ oya. Kɛ́ agbala amɛmli ni akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ lɛ, ehaa ethylene nitsumɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my harvested onions rot quickly when I store them inside closed fertilizer sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onions ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kotokui ni aŋã mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Closed sacks trap moisture and heat released by the onions, creating a hot environment where rot fungi thrive. Onions need cool, circulating air so they can stay dry and last for months.
ga: Saak ni aŋã lɛ baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dɔlɛ ni ŋmei lɛ jieɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ baanyɛ ada yɛ mli lɛ baa. Sabala he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni bɔleɔ ehe koni egbi ni ehi shi nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why do some crops like maize need to be dried in the sun to last long while vegetables need shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni tsei komɛi, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni aduawai ahe hiaa ni amɛná hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Grains like maize must lose water so mold cannot grow on them during storage, whereas leafy vegetables need to retain their water to stay fresh and spoil if exposed to drying heat.
ga: Nibii tamɔ ŋmãa fiteɔ nu. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ shwereee yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ahi nu mli koni amɛhi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfite kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa mli.

english: Why do fresh garden eggs shrink and lose their shine after staying in my kitchen for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni afee ehee yɛ abɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhi ŋtayaai amli gbii fioo komɛi?

english: Garden eggs lose moisture through their thin skin when kept in warm room conditions. Keeping them in cool storage or a damp cloth sack prevents water evaporation.
ga: Abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛhewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ mli lɛ To he ko ni mli ejɔ loo mama kotoku ni mli efɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni nu lɛ akafee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What makes some harvested yams stay good for months in a barn while others decay early?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ekomɛi hiɔ shi nyɔji babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli? Yɛ be mli ni henɔi komɛi fiteɔ oya lɛ?

english: Yams remain alive and durable after harvest if kept in well-ventilated, cool, and dry yam barns that prevent moisture accumulation and fungal attack.
ga: Sweet potatoes hiɔ shi ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ kɛji akɛ akɛto sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli, ni mli ejɔ, ni egbi ni tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ naa lɛ mli.

english: How can I store my harvested pepper seeds so they do not rot before the next planting season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ mi-pepper dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ato koni amɛkafite dani be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba?

english: Drying seeds thoroughly removes water that attracts mold, and keeping them sealed in a cool, dark container protects their vitality until the next planting season.
ga: Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ nu ni gbalaa ŋmeii lɛ kɛyaa. Ni kɛ́ akɛwo tsɛnsi ko ni mli ejɔ ni mli ewo duŋ mli lɛ, ebaabu ehewalɛ he kɛyashi shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow, and how can I fix it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. Applying well-rotted manure, compost, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea around the roots will help the crop regain its deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji tsei ni niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa lɛ yɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea wo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eku esɛɛ eba eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts on the same land where I grow cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has the natural ability to take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them alongside cassava leaves free nutrients in the soil that help the cassava roots grow larger.
ga: Peanuts ji legume weku lɛ mlinyo, ni eyɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni ekɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: This is caused by a fungal condition known as Black Pod disease, which thrives in damp, dark environments. You can protect your crop by pruning extra shade leaves to let sunlight in and promptly removing any infected pods so the fungus does not spread.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod hela kɛ enɛ baa. ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ duŋ yɔɔ lɛ Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ babaoo ni oookpa koni hulu la babaoo abote mli lɛ nɔ. Ni jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are small worms eating the leaves and stems of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ?

english: These are likely fall armyworms, a common pest that attacks young crops. You can manage them by inspecting your farm regularly early in the morning and applying approved organic or chemical control methods into the central whorl of the plant before they cause severe damage.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni fɔɔ baa ni tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni oookwɛ daa leebi lɛ nɔ. ni akɛ gbɛi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ atsu nii yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai lɛ amli dani amɛfite nii waa.

english: Leaf curl is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread a plant virus while feeding on leaf sap. Controlling these insects early with neem oil spray and pulling out severely damaged plants prevents the virus from spreading to healthy crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni gbɛɔ tsei amli helai amɛshwãa be mli ni amɛyeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Okɛ neem fɔ afɔ nɔ ni ojie tsei ni efite waa lɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant many seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to develop strong roots and produce heavy fruit or grain.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo shishifãi ni wa ni ekɛwo yibii loo dumɔwui ni tsii.

english: How do I know the right time to put my seeds into the ground at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: It is best to wait until the rains become steady for about two weeks and the soil remains consistently moist. Planting after just one early light rain can cause seeds to germinate and then wither if a dry spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be aaafee otsii enyɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbo kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be ko ba ni nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Weeds grow much faster than main crops and steal essential water, light, and fertilizer from the soil. Clearing weeds within the first four weeks after planting gives your crop a strong start without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tso ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ nu, kane kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa onibii lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds instead of planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni makwɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially tested and bred to grow uniformly, resist common local diseases, and produce higher yields. Saved seeds often lose their strength over generations, leading to smaller harvests and weaker plants.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ akwɛɔ krɛdɛɛ ni akwɛɔ amɛ koni amɛdara daa. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa yibii bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why does my harvested maize get damaged by insects while sitting in my storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii fiteɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ beni mita mi nitoohe lɛ?

english: Insects like grain weevils thrive when stored grain still holds moisture. Fully drying your maize in the sun until it is hard, and storing it in airtight bags or clean, dry containers, prevents insects from destroying your harvest.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmaa ŋmeii yeɔ omanye kɛji dumɔwui ni ato lɛ mli edɔ lolo. Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi ebaawa. ni okɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo tsɛnsi ko ni mli tse ni egbi mli. Ebaatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite onibii.

english: Why do some tree crops take many years to produce fruits while crops like maize yield in just a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Short-term crops like maize spend all their energy growing fast leaves and seeds quickly. Tree crops like mango, orange, or cocoa need several years first to build strong trunks and deep roots so they can survive for decades and support heavy harvests year after year.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ baai kɛ dumɔwui oya. Tso tsei tamɔ mango, citrus, loo cocoa he miihia afii babaoo koni amɛma amɛshishifãi ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ koni amɛhi shi afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni amɛye amɛbua ŋmaakpamɔ ni tsii afi fɛɛ afi.

english: How long can a crop like cocoa or oil palm keep producing fruit before the tree becomes too old?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo loo ŋmei fɔ baanyɛ awo yibii dani tso lɛ agbɔ tsɔ?

english: With good pruning, weed control, and soil care, tree crops like cocoa or oil palm can produce heavy yields for 25 to 30 years or more before their production naturally begins to decline.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akwɛ jwɛi ni afoɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, tsei tamɔ kookoo loo mu tso baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo afii 25 kɛyashi 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai. dani adebɔɔ mli nibii ni afeɔ lɛ ajeɔ shishi ebaa shi

english: Is it good practice to leave big old trees standing on my land when clearing for new crops?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ mashi tsei wuji momoi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ miikpa tsei heei?

english: Yes, leaving selected large shade trees helps protect young crops from intense heat, prevents heavy rains from washing away topsoil, and creates fallen leaves that turn into natural plant food.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ashi tsei ni eda ni haa hulutsoo lɛ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. Etsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. ni ebɔɔ baai ni egbee shi ni bafeɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need shade trees to survive their first few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa tso ni haa hulu tsoɔ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that dry out easily under full tropical sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains or leaving canopy trees creates a gentle environment that shelters the young plants until they grow tough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ shishi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni ashiɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli jɔ ni akɛbaahã tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi amɛbaadara waa.

english: Can I plant timber trees alongside food crops like plantain and cassava on the same plot?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu tsei yɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains kɛ cassava ahe. Ani ebaanyɛ ehi shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, this system allows you to harvest food crops for quick food and income in the early years while the timber trees grow slowly overhead to provide shade and high long-term financial value.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbɛjianɔtoo nɛɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha niyenii oya ni onáa shika yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tso ni atsɛɔ lɛ log lɛ daa fiofio. nɔ koni ekɛ shade aha ni ená shika helɛtemɔ ni nɔ kwɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli

english: Why are my crop yields dropping on land that my family has planted on for over twenty years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ eba shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miweku lɛ etsu nii nɔ ni fe afii nyɔŋmai enyɔ nɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops constantly pull food out of the ground. When the same land is farmed for decades without resting or adding manure and compost, the soil nutrients get exhausted and must be restored.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Kɛji akɛ atsu okwaayeli yɛ he kome afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni ajɔɔɔɔ he loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ faaa ni esa akɛ aku sɛɛ akɛba.

english: How do leaves that fall from trees onto my farm help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni jɛɔ tsei anɔ shwieɔ shi kɛbaa miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: As fallen leaves rot on the ground, they turn into organic humus. This natural fertilizer adds vital nutrients back into the earth, retains moisture in the soil, and keeps the ground cool.
ga: Kɛji baai ni egbee shi lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Amɛbaatsɔ organic humus. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: How do tree roots affect the soil and other crops growing near them over a long time?
ga: Tso shishifãi náa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei krokomɛi anɔ hewalɛ. ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Etsɛ enyiɛ?

english: Deep tree roots break up hard underground soil and draw up minerals from far below. However, if crops are planted too close to a large tree, they may have to compete with its surface roots for water.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ gbálaa sũ ni wa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli ni egbalaa shika tsuru kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ adu tso lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso agbo ko tsɔ lɛ, Ekolɛ ehe baahia ni amɛkɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ abɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu.

english: How do trees planted around my farm help protect my crops during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Te abaafee tɛŋŋ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Trees act as windbreaks that slow down hot, dry winds which strip moisture from crop leaves. They also shade the ground, keeping the farm cooler and helping the soil hold onto water longer.
ga: Tsei tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ baa shi. ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu nɔ. ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why do the branches of tall old trees sometimes stop rain and sunlight from helping my short crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsei kakadaji aniji haa nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be yeɔ ebuaaa miŋmɔshi nibii kukuji lɛ?

english: If a tree canopy grows too thick, it blocks essential sunlight that short crops need to make energy, and heavy leaves can catch light rains. Pruning higher branches allows sun and water to reach the crops below.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli wa tsɔ Ebaatsi hulu la ni he hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii kukuji he hiaa koni amɛná hewalɛ lɛ naa. Ni baai ni tsii lɛ baanyɛ aha nugbɔ anɛ waa. Niji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ nu shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and sensitive to direct heat; they require shade crops like plantains or leguminous trees to protect them from excessive sunlight and soil evaporation during their first few years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛnuɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ he. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo legumes koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni fe nine kɛ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ he.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my maize seeds very close to each other to try to get more crops on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni maná ŋmãa babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting crop seeds too close together forces them to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak, thin stalks and smaller harvests overall.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: How do I know the best time to start planting my cassava when the rain season begins?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ mabɔi ŋmei dumɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava is best planted right after the major rainy season begins when the soil stays consistently moist, as this provides enough moisture for the stems to grow strong roots before any dry period.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu cassava amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ je shishi beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ jɛmɛ koni tsei lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil, which can be fixed by applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or adding composted animal manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abaanyɛ atsake enɛ kɛtsɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens to my soil if I put dry grass around the bottom of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ jwɛi wo mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishi?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating quickly out of the soil, keeps the roots cool, and prevents wild weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa koo mli jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Can I save seeds from the hybrid maize I buy at the market and plant them again next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid corn ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ato ni madu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Saving and planting seeds from hybrid crops usually results in weak plants and very small yields because hybrid seeds lose their strength after the first harvest; it is best to buy fresh certified seeds every season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni jɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ ahewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa be.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before they turn into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛmiitsɔ pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme afternoon heat, erratic watering, or attacks from tiny insects like thrips that eat the flower stems.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he haomɔ he. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo tutuamɔi ni jɛɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni yeɔ fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ adɛŋ.

english: Why do wild weeds seem to grow much faster than the cassava and maize I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that are already adapted to survive under harsh local soil conditions, so they absorb available moisture and nutrients much faster than cultivated farm seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛheɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Trimming unnecessary side branches, called suckers, allows the plant to send its food energy directly into developing large, healthy tomatoes instead of growing extra leaves.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ sɛɛ ni he ehiaaa, ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ ni afolɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ ni ekɛhaa lɛ koni ekɛwo tomatoi wuji ni mli wa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ baai krokomɛi

english: Why do people tell me not to plant maize on the exact same spot on my land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko miikɛɛ mi akɛ mikadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop year after year drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests and soil diseases that feed on that crop to build up in large numbers.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa babaoo.

english: Why do my older crop trees look weak and stopped growing, even though my new young seedlings look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni ekpa dalɛ lɛ? Shi kɛlɛ, mitso hee lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ.

english: Older crops often exhaust the nutrients in the soil after years of production or suffer from accumulated root pests. Young plants still have fresh root systems and access to unused topsoil nutrients, which makes them look healthier in comparison.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni edara lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ yɛ afii babaoo ni akɛdu lɛ sɛɛ loo amɛyeɔ amanehulu kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni buaa amɛshishifãi anaa lɛ ahe. Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi heei lolo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni akɛtsuuu nii lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ waa kɛ akɛto amɛhe.

english: Why do my young crops wilt during the hot afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji mikɛ nu wo nɔ leebi po.

english: In intense heat, young plants lose water through their leaves faster than their small root systems can pull it from the soil. This temporary wilting protects them from heat stress, and they usually recover once the sun goes down.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli Tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. ni baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nɛkɛ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: What causes my mature crops to produce smaller fruits and look weaker than they did last season?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi tsei ni eda lɛ miiwo tsei bibii ni tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa fe nyɛsɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Soil naturally loses its strength and nutrients as crops draw from it season after season. Without adding organic matter or plant food back into the soil, crops gradually get weaker and produce smaller yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ ebɔɔ su mli hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ beni ŋmɔshi nibii gbalaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsei aniyenii fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ lɛ, fiofio lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: How can I tell if my crop is yellowing because of a disease or because it lacks food in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ yɛ hela loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ?

english: A lack of plant food usually causes the whole plant or its lower leaves to turn pale green or yellow evenly over time. Diseases, on the other hand, usually cause strange spots, rotting, leaf curling, or sudden drying on specific leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso niyenii ni bɛ lɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ loo baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ po. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, helai kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ, ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ baa baai komɛi anɔ.

english: What does it actually mean when an extension officer says a crop medicine or fertilizer is 'organic'?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛ́ sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔmɔ he nitsulɔ ko kɛɛ tso tsofa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ji ‘organic’?

english: Organic inputs come from natural sources like plants, animals, or natural minerals rather than harsh man-made chemicals. They help build up soil health over time without leaving dangerous chemical residues on your food crops.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ tsei, kooloi, loo adebɔɔ mli shika tsuru mli. Yɛ tsofai ni gbɔmɔ fee ni mli wa najiaŋ lɛ Amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa ni amɛtswaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛshiii tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni eshwɛ yɛ oniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: How do organic fertilizers help my soil differently than strong chemical fertilizers?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni esoroɔ lɛ yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ahe?

english: Chemical fertilizers give crops a quick boost of food but can harden the soil over time. Organic fertilizers feed the living organisms in the soil, making the ground softer and better at holding water for a longer period.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii oya shi ebaanyɛ eha sũ lɛ mli awa yɛ be ni sa mli. Organic fertilizers haa nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Can organic crop sprays kill pests as quickly as chemical sprays?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbe kooloi bibii oya tamɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: Organic sprays usually work slower because they repel pests, disrupt their feeding, or weaken them naturally rather than instantly poisoning them. While they take longer to show full results, they are safer for your health and do not burn your crops.
ga: Organic sprays lɛ tsuɔ nii blɛoo ejaakɛ amɛshwieɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Niyenii ni gbaa mɔ naa loo egbɔjɔɔ amɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ tsofa fɔŋ awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ Eyɛ mli akɛ eheɔ be babaoo dani etsɔɔ nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ fɛɛ moŋ. Shi eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha ohewalɛ ni eshãaa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is it dangerous to apply double the amount of crop medicine if I want faster results on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli shii enyɔ baatsu nii kɛji miitao nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Applying too much crop medicine can burn plant leaves, damage root systems, and poison the soil. Following the recommended dose ensures the plant gets enough help without suffering chemical shock or damage.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei lɛ ahe baai, efite shishifãi lɛ, ni efite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛhaa lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ náa yelikɛbuamɔ ni sa ni tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe loo efiteee lɛ.

english: Why am I advised to apply liquid fertilizer bit by bit rather than giving the crop a huge dose at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo mli fiofio lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo shikome lɛ

english: Giving plants too much liquid fertilizer at once causes excess food to wash away deep into the soil where roots cannot reach it. Applying small amounts gradually ensures the crop continuously absorbs nutrients as it grows.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli tse babaoo ha otso lɛ shikome lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ fioo ko wo tso lɛ mli fiofio lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aya nɔ eŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: Mixing crop medicines without expert advice can cause a chemical reaction that destroys the active ingredients or creates a mixture that burns your crops. You should only mix inputs if an extension officer confirms they are compatible.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ tsei amli ni ŋaawolɔi komɛi bɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai ni fiteɔ nibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ aba loo ekɛ nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii shãa lɛ aba. Esa akɛ okɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ afutu pɛ kɛji nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ ma nɔ mi akɛ amɛkɛ amɛhe kpãa gbee.

english: Can I grow food crops inside plastic buckets around my house instead of on a big field?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii yɛ plastic baagi mli ni mabɔle he. Ani abaanyɛ adu tsũi yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli kwɔlɔ amli moŋ?

english: Yes, planting in buckets or small containers works very well for vegetables and herbs. It allows you to control the soil quality, manage water easily, and grow fresh food even if you do not own a large plot of farm land.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tanki mli loo tsɛnsii bibii amli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa aduawai kɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Okwɛɔ nu nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni oduɔ niyenii heei Kɛji obɛ ŋmɔ agbo po.

english: How do I keep crop roots from rotting when I plant them in a bucket?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tsei shishifãi anaa koni amɛkafite beni mikwɛɔ amɛ yɛ tanki mli lɛ?

english: You must make small holes at the bottom of the bucket so excess water can drain out. While crop roots need moist soil to absorb water, trapped water will suffocate the roots and cause them to rot.
ga: Esa akɛ ofee bu bibioo ko. yɛ tanki lɛ shishi koni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ nu moŋ, Shi nu ni emɔ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Do crops planted in containers need different care than crops planted directly in field soil?
ga: Ani tsei ni aduɔ yɛ tsɛnsii amli lɛ biɔ kwɛmɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, container crops dry out faster because the soil volume is small, so they need more regular watering. They also run out of nutrients quickly, requiring you to add compost or manure more often.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ baagbi oya ejaakɛ amɛbɛ shikpɔŋ babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni afɔ amɛ nu daa babaoo. Kɛfata he lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Enɛ haa okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli shii abɔ.

english: Why is it important to wash seeds or planting materials before putting them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afɔ dumɔwui loo nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe dani adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Washing planting materials removes dirt, harmful fungi, and pest eggs that might be clinging to the outside. Starting with clean material helps prevent early crop diseases and gives your plants a healthy start.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ he nibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie muji. Fung ni yɔɔ oshara kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela fɛɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni baanyɛ ahi kpo nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni he tse je shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni otsi tsei ahe helai anaa mra, ni ebaaha otsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will washing planting materials damage the nutrients inside them that the plant needs to sprout?
ga: Ani tso lɛ mli nibii ni afɔɔ he lɛ baafite niyenii ni yɔɔ mli ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: No, washing the outer surface does not strip away the internal nutrients. Seeds store essential food inside their hard hulls, which stays protected and feeds the young plant as it begins to sprout.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ afɔ kponɔgbɛ he lɛ, ejieee niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛɛɛ mli. Dumɔwui kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ toɔ ŋmei ni wa mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni abu tso bibioo lɛ he ni eha lɛ niyenii be mli ni ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ.

english: What actually happens inside a seed after I plant it in wet soil?
ga: Mɛni baa dumɔwui lɛ amli beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When a seed absorbs soil moisture, it wakes up and uses its internal stored nutrients to grow tiny roots downward for stability and a shoot upward toward sunlight to start making its own food.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwie nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Eteɔ shi ni ekɛ niyenii ni ato yɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi bibii amli. Edaa kɛyaa shi kɛha shifimɔ. ni ŋmeii lɛ teɔ shi kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he koni amɛje amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii feemɔ shishi.

english: If I put my harvested crops through a processing machine, does it ruin the nutrients?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ wo tsɔne ko ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli Ani ebaafite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ?

english: No, machine processing simply cleans, strips, or grinds the crop into useful forms. Most nutrients remain intact in the food product or in the leftover bits that come out of the machine.
ga: Dabi, tsɔne ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkɛ, ejieɔ loo efoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli koni efee nɔ ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ateŋ babaoo hiɔ niyenii ni afee lɛ mli loo niyenii ni eshwɛ ni jɛɔ tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: Can I use crop waste left over from processing machines back on my farm soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni jɛ tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ amli lɛ aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: Yes, crop residues from processing machines still contain rich organic minerals. Mixing this organic material back into your soil feeds beneficial soil organisms and enriches the earth for your next planting season.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ amli lɛ yɛ organic minerals babaoo lolo. Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli nɛɛ ku sɛɛ wo oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi kɛha okwɛ̃mɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How does joining a group to machine-process crops help me as a farmer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kuu ko ni kɛ tsɔne tsuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nii lɛ ni mikɛ mihe wo mli lɛ ye ebua mi akɛ okwaafonyo lɛ?

english: Processing crops as a group allows you to share expensive processing machines that clean, preserve, and package produce efficiently. This reduces post-harvest loss and turns raw crops into high-value goods that sell for better market prices.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ babaoo lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ tsɔnei ni jara wa ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ, ni buɔ nibii ahe, ni nibii ni akɛwoɔ paketii amli lɛ feɔ lɛ jaa. Enɛ haa nɔ ni laajeɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɛɛ lɛ feɔ nibii ni jara wa ni abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ.

english: How do young crops take up nutrients from the soil to grow bigger?
ga: Te dumɔwui feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛjieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛdara?

english: Plants drink up nutrients dissolved in soil water through tiny root hairs. These nutrients act as food, helping the plant build strong stems, broad green leaves, and healthy flowers and fruits.
ga: Tsei nuɔ niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ anɔ. Nibii nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmaa shishifãi ni wa. baai eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ kɛ agbɛnɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai ni mli wa

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and healthy. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer like NPK will help the leaves regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when there is heavy rainfall on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water on the farm for too long, the roots drown and rot. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away easily.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers fall off the tree branches without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?
