english: Cocoa flowers often drop off if the tree is stressed by excessive heat, lack of water, or lack of pollination by small insects. Keeping shade trees in your cocoa farm helps cool the air and retains soil moisture so flowers can set into pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ha tso lɛ haoɔ, nu bɛ mli, loo kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ o-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my corn plants grow thin and yield small ears when I plant many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ toi bibii kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Planting one or two seeds per hole with proper spacing gives every plant enough resources to produce thick stalks and large corn ears.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui kome loo enyɔ yɛ bu kome mli ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso aná nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii agboi.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up and droop during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl and droop in the heat to reduce water loss through their leaves. While this is a normal defense against heat, putting dry grass mulch around the base of the plant keeps the soil cool and moist longer.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛji akɛ amɛwo la mli koni nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ aba shi. Eyɛ mli akɛ enɛ ji hulutsoo hebuu ni yaa nɔ daa moŋ. Shi kɛ́ okɛ sũ wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are small caterpillars destroying the fresh leaves inside the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miifite baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which feed on the tender inner leaves of young maize plants. Inspecting your field early and applying neem leaf extract or recommended treatments inside the plant whorls will control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ ŋmei tsei bibii amli baai lɛ. Akwɛɔ hei ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mra Kɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsuɔ he nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akutsei lɛ amli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special bacteria in their roots that catch nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the legumes are harvested, this natural fertilizer remains in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi ni yeɔ ebuaa ni emɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa nɛɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my yam vines grow better and yield bigger tubers when I stake them with wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji kɛ mikɛ tso tswa lɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves out in the sunlight. Sunlight helps the leaves manufacture food, which is then sent down to build large, heavy tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ aje kpo yɛ hulu la mli. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, atsuɔ lɛ kɛyaa shi koni efee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to harvest so the roots do not turn hard and woody?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa? No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ waaa ni amɛji tsei?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves start turning yellow and dropping off. Harvesting at this stage ensures the tubers remain soft and full of starch before they become tough.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ahiɔ shi blɛoo ni ŋmeii eyi mli obɔ dani amɛwaa.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings wilt and die shortly after I move them from the nursery bed into the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings experience shock when suddenly moved from a shaded nursery to direct sunlight and wind. Slowly exposing them to sunlight for a few hours each day before planting, and transplanting them late in the afternoon, prevents this shock.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ he baajɔ lɛ kɛ́ trukaa lɛ Ojie lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli kɛtee hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Okɛ amɛ awo hulu la lɛ mli fiofio. ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi daa gbi dani adu Ni adu yɛ shwane mli lɛ baaye abua ni akafee shoo.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct harsh sunlight and dry winds. Planting plantains or shade trees alongside them creates a natural umbrella that cools the air and keeps moisture in the soil to protect the young trees.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni tswaa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ emasɛi. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ebu tsei bibii ahe.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars chewing holes in the funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which feed on the delicate growing center of the maize plant. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts directly into the leaf funnel kills them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baagbe amɛ dani amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my farm make my maize crop yield better in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha mi ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that take nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When the groundnuts are harvested, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil and acts as natural food for your next maize crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ebaafee adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha oŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground even when the top leaves look green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi eyɛ mli akɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava rot is usually caused by water sitting in heavy soil for too long, which breeds underground fungi. Creating raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away from the tubers so they stay dry and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava fitemɔ baa. ni kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii baa Gɔji loo ŋmeii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni afeɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Koni ehi shi ni egbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do I get bigger maize cobs when I leave space between seeds instead of planting many close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa wuji anɔ beni mishiɔ gbɛ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu ŋmãa babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing ensures each individual plant gets enough nutrients to produce thick stalks and big, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do certified seeds from the farm store give a bigger harvest than the seeds I save from last year's crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni jɛ ŋmɔ mli shwapo ko mli lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi ni midu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially selected and bred by experts to resist local diseases and yield well. Seeds saved from past harvests lose these strong traits over time and produce weaker plants with lower yields.
ga: Ahala dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni ŋaalɔi ekwɛ nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baafite sui nɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. ni ebaaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off without growing into fruits during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the pepper plant, causing it to drop its flowers to save energy and water. Mulching the soil around the plant with dry grass keeps the roots cool and helps the plant retain its flowers until peppers form.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa pepper tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite. Mulching around Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi jeɔ shishi lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔii amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ.

english: Why is it so important to clear weeds within the first three weeks after my crop sprouts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ lɛ mli beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crop sprouts have tiny roots and are easily overpowered by fast-growing weeds. Clearing weeds early removes the competition for soil nutrients during the plant's most critical growth stage.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii. ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ yeɔ nɔ kunim oya Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mra Ejieɔ akaŋshii ni yaa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ kɛyaa.

english: Why should I snap off the side shoots from my tomato plants while they are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ asɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli be mli ni tomato lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Removing side shoots forces the plant to send its food energy directly to the main stem and flowers, resulting in larger tomatoes instead of lots of unnecessary leaves and bushy branches.
ga: Kɛtsɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli kɛyaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tomato lɛ feɔ agbo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni okɛ baai kɛ tsei niji babaoo ni he ehiaaa baatsu nii lɛ.

english: Why do black spots appear on my tomato leaves and cause the bottom leaves to wither and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji lɛ? Ni eha baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi?

english: Black spots are fungal leaf spot diseases that spread when rain bounces mud onto the lower leaves. Pruning off the bottom leaves near the soil stops fungal spores from jumping onto the main plant.
ga: Black spot ji baa mli hela ko ni ŋmei ko kɛbaa, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ ni etswa sũ ni yɔɔ baa lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ lɛ, ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ tso titri lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or leaving some tall trees provides shade and keeps the soil moist so the seedlings can survive.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, loo ashi tsei kakadaji komɛi ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small shoots growing around my main plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Too many shoots compete with the main plant for soil nutrients and water. Removing extra shoots ensures the main plant gets enough food to produce large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy plant growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the corn stay green and grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have holes in them with tiny caterpillars hiding inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛtee mli?

english: This is likely Fall Armyworm damage. These pests hide inside the leaves to feed on the growing center, but applying approved pest controls early can protect your crop.
ga: Enɛ baanyɛ afee Fall Armyworm fitemɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai amli koni amɛye hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ. Shi mra be mli ni akɛ tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsuɔ nii Ebaanyɛ ebu onibii ahe.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the plant reaches 8 to 12 months old, lower leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off naturally, and small cracks appear in the soil near the base of the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛji tso lɛ eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ Ejeɔ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to put wooden tall poles for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they can catch full sunlight to make food for the plant, which leads to much larger and healthier yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo ni amɛkɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and turning wrinkly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking juice from the leaves, or by a virus transmitted by those insects. Controlling tiny pests early stops the curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Kɛ́ akwɛ kooloi bibii lɛ anɔ fioo klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akpa ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the yellow flowers on my tomato plants dropping off without producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of insects like bees to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii, tamɔ wuobii, ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ ni bɛ

english: Why do some farmers cover the soil around their plants with dry grass or dry leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛtsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This practice is called mulching. It keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and stops weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaa jwɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I wait until the soil is moist from rain before applying chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ nugbɔ mli dani okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ afata he?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so the roots can soak it in. Applying fertilizer on dry soil can burn and destroy the plant roots instead of feeding them.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ abote mli. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei shishifãi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha amɛ niyenii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food crops use to build strong green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plants regain their deep green color and vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii tso titri ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni wa, eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant groundnuts on my farmland before I plant maize in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmei yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Groundnuts and other legumes trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, that trapped plant food stays in the soil to nourish heavy-feeding crops like maize naturally.
ga: Peanuts kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Mɔɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa amɛ Tsei aniyenii ni amɔmɔ amɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha kooloi aniyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ aná hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods turning black and rotting right on the tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in damp, shady conditions. Pruning excess branches lets sunshine and air into your farm, drying out the moisture so the fungus cannot survive.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ nyɛɛɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up into small tight balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee bɔɔlu bibii lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from under the leaves and passing viruses to the plant. Spraying neem oil or an appropriate pesticide controls these insects before they stunt your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ shishi ni amɛkɛ hela lɛ haa tso lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ baaye kooloi nɛɛ anɔ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when heavy rains fall for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When soil stays soaked in standing water, fungal diseases grow rapidly and rot the roots, so planting on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ Fungal helai daa oya ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ atsɔ mli.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the underground tuber. Climbing tall stakes spreads the leaves out to catch solar energy, which results in much larger, healthier yams.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. climbing tall poles Egbɛɔ ebaa lɛ eshwaa koni enine ashɛ hulu hewalɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when the fruit bunches start getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches against strong wind. Supporting the main stem with a bamboo fork or pole absorbs the extra weight and prevents the roots from ripping out of the ground.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua aduawai akui ni tsii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Kɛ́ okɛ fɔk loo ŋmei tso fi tso titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaajie muji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ akajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering during flowering. Giving your plants consistent moisture at the roots and mulching the soil helps keep the flowers attached until tomatoes form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ mli haomɔ loo nu ni bɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shishifãi lɛ be fɛɛ be, ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Why did the seeds I saved from my last maize harvest grow into weaker plants with smaller yields this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ dara ni amɛbatsɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni wooo yibii babaoo yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Many modern high-yield maize seeds are hybrids meant for one season only. Saved seeds lose their hybrid strength in the second generation, leading to smaller yields and uneven plant growth.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ji ŋmãa ni akɛfee be kome pɛ. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baafite hybrid hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu daaa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee.

english: Weeds are aggressive thieves that steal nutrients, water, and sunlight directly from your crop's roots. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the resources they need to grow strong and produce well.
ga: Jwɛi ji julɔi ni juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ naa nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why should I plant the Yellow Dwarf coconut variety instead of the traditional tall coconut trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu Yellow Dwarf ŋmeii yɛ blema ŋmeii tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow Dwarf coconut trees grow shorter and start bearing fruit much earlier—usually within 3 to 4 years—making them easier to manage and harvest compared to tall varieties.
ga: Yellow dwarf coconut tsei lɛ daa kuku ni amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi oya waa, bei pii lɛ yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, ni no haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaakwɛ nɔ ni akpaa amɛ kɛ akɛto tsei srɔtoi ni kɛlɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Will Yellow Dwarf coconut trees grow well and produce good fruit in our local Ghanaian climate?
ga: Ani ŋmei tso bibioo ni ji yellow dwarf lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii yɛ wɔ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, Yellow Dwarf coconuts adapt very well to warm temperatures and regular rain, producing high yields of sweet coconut water and rich flesh if planted in well-drained soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, akokooi bibii ŋmɔŋ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛhaa dɔlɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa ŋmei nu ni ŋɔɔ kɛ he babaoo baa kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ.

english: What local crops can I grow on my farm to process into Tom Brown cereal powder for extra income?
ga: Mɛɛ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛfee Tom Brown ŋmaa powder koni maná shika kroko?

english: You can grow grains like maize, sorghum, or millet alongside legumes like soybeans and groundnuts, which are roasted and milled together to make nutritious Tom Brown.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmaa tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa kɛfata ŋmãa tamɔ soybeans kɛ ŋmãa he. ni ashãa ni agbɛɔ ashwieɔ shi koni akɛfee Tom Brown ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Which of my farm crops can I easily process into crispy chips to sell at the local market?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ manyɛ mafee lɛ mlɛo ni mafee ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mikɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ?

english: Root tubers like cassava, sweet potato, and cocoyam, as well as green plantains, can be easily sliced and fried or baked into popular, long-lasting chips.
ga: Shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ kookoo, kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ŋmei ŋmɔŋ Abaanyɛ afolɔ amɛ ni ashã loo ashã amɛ ni amɛfee ŋmei ni ehe gbɛi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Can I process my harvested cassava or sweet potato into flour for baking bread and biscuits?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akpa lɛ mafee ashikishaŋ kɛshã blodoo kɛ biskit?

english: Yes, drying and milling high-quality cassava or sweet potato roots creates fine flour that can replace part of expensive imported wheat flour in baking bread and biscuits.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei loo ŋmei shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni agbiɔ ni ashwieɔ lɛ haa anáa ashikiŋsha kpakpa ni baanyɛ aye ŋmaa ashikishaŋ ni jara wa ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ fã ko najiaŋ yɛ blodoo kɛ biskit ni ashãa lɛ mli.

english: Why is it better for me to process my excess fruit and seeds into finished foods rather than selling them raw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee aduawai kɛ dumɔwui ni fa fe nine lɛ niyenii ni afee klalo moŋ fe ni mahɔ̃ɔ amɛ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Raw fruits spoil quickly during peak season when market prices drop. Processing them into foods like chips, porridge mix, or flour preserves them and allows you to sell at higher prices year-round.
ga: Yibii ni ahoo lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ be mli ni jarayeli be lɛ jara baa shi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ fee niyenii tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛfutu loo ashikishaŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛhiɔ shi ni ehaa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ amɛ yɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my grains spoil or mold quickly if I try to grind them into Tom Brown immediately after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmaa lɛ fiteɔ loo efoɔ oya kɛji mibɔ mɔdɛŋ akɛ mafolɔ mli ni efee tomboy lɛ? Brown beni akpa kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ

english: Freshly harvested grains contain high moisture that encourages mold growth. You must thoroughly dry the seeds first so the ground cereal stays fresh and safe to eat.
ga: Nibii ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo, ni woɔ ŋmɔtɔ dalɛ he hewalɛ. Esa akɛ ogbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ klɛŋklɛŋ bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmaa lɛ ahi shi ehee ni efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ.

english: How does harvest timing affect the quality of my cassava and plantain when making porridge or chips?
ga: Te be ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ saa mi-cassava kɛ plantains lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mifee ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Harvesting at full maturity ensures maximum starch content, giving your chips a crunchy texture and ensuring porridge thickens properly without becoming watery.
ga: Nikpamɔ kɛji ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ haa starch babaoo yɔɔ mli. Ehaa o-fries lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ekwɛɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ ni efeee nu.

english: Why do my root crops start rotting so quickly after I dig them up if I don't process them immediately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mifo amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Ni kɛ́ mitsuuu he nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ hu?

english: Root crops like cassava have high water content and breathe rapidly after harvest. Processing them into dry flour or dried chips removes water and stops natural decay.
ga: Nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei mli ni amɛmuɔ oya kɛji akpa amɛ. Kɛ́ afee lɛ powda loo woji ni egbi lɛ, ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekpaa fitemɔ.

english: What crop characteristics should I look for if I want produce that works well for both fresh eating and food processing?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ matao kɛji miitao ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛ nɔ ni atsuɔ he nii fɛɛ mli?

english: Look for crops with high solid starch or firm flesh and good natural oil or sugar content, as these features maintain flavor and texture whether consumed fresh, boiled, or dried into processed snacks.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli fɔ loo sugars babaoo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ haa ŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ hiɔ shi kɛji akɛ aye lɛ ehee, ahoo, loo egbi akɛ niyenii ni afee lɛ mlɛo.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to build strong leaves. It can also happen if the soil is too soaked with water after heavy rains, preventing the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni mli wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ batsɔ nu tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: What is eating small holes into the leaves of my young maize crop and leaving brownish powder inside?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Ani ebote mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ amli ni eshi powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the center whorl of the maize plant during the day and feed on the leaves, leaving behind chewed holes and droppings that look like sawdust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaai amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ. Amɛshiɔ bu ni atsɔ mli kɛ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english: You can check by looking for cracks in the soil around the base of the plant, which shows the roots are expanding. You can also carefully dig up just one root to inspect its size while leaving the rest of the plant in the ground.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli lɛ taomɔ nɔ, ni tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ miigbɛ amɛshwã. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa shishifã kome pɛ hu koni okwɛ bɔ ni edara ha, ni oshi tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their young flowers and tiny pods before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ amli fɔfɔi bibii kɛ amɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ miifite lɛ? dani eda kwraa

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop extra flowers they cannot support, but heavy dropping usually happens due to lack of water, insufficient shade, or insect pests like mirids (capsids) attacking the young pods.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aye. Shi bei pii lɛ, nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi waa lɛ baa. Shade ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ jɛmɛ. loo kooloi bibii tamɔ mirids (capsids) ni tutuaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ.

english: If too many sucker shoots grow together, they all fight for the same soil nutrients and water, resulting in smaller bunches. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong stems to produce bigger plantain fruits.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii lɛ fee ekome kɛdara tsɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii bibii baa. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni ekɛ plantains wuji aba.

english: Yam vines need support to lift their leaves up towards sunlight, which helps the plant turn light into energy to grow big tubers underground. Staking also keeps the foliage off the damp ground, reducing fungal disease.
ga: Yelikɛbuamɔ he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Enɛ haa tsei tsakeɔ kane lɛ amɛwoɔ hewalɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi

english: Why do my tomato plants droop during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil feels moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po

english: Extreme heat causes tomato leaves to lose water faster than the roots can pull it up from the soil, making them temporarily wilt. If they recover in the cool evening, it is normal heat stress, but if they stay wilted, it could be a soil disease.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tomato baai lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa egbɔjɔɔ be kukuoo ko Kɛji ehiɛ ba ehe nɔ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ, eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛjɛɔ latsaa he haomɔ mli. Shi kɛ́ etee nɔ egbi lɛ, ekolɛ hela ko yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap from the undersides of leaves, or by a viral infection spread by these same insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ nɔŋŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: Does rice need to stand in deep water during its entire growing period?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmã awo nu ni mli kwɔ mli yɛ be fɛɛ ni ekwɛɔ lɛ mli?

english: While rice loves water, flooded water mainly helps control weeds and keeps soil temperature steady. Rice actually needs less water during early growth and should be drained completely a few weeks before harvest so the grain can dry evenly.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa sumɔɔ nu moŋ Shi nu afua mli nu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa titri ni ekwɛɔ jwɛi anɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ. Yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, ŋmãa biɔ nu fioo yɛ be mli ni edaa mra lɛ. Ni esa akɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ mli kwraa otsii fioo komɛi dani akpa. Koni ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ agbi pɛpɛɛpɛ

english: How does covering the soil with dried grass or leaves around my crop stems help them grow?
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni ebɔle he lɛ shwieɔ nɔ Te mi tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dried grass or leaves keeps the soil cool during hot days, traps moisture so you water less, prevents weeds from sprouting, and slowly turns into rich plant food as it breaks down.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ bɔni afee ni oná nu fioo Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni fiofio lɛ etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii ni jara wa be mli ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn pale yellow even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, not just thirsty. Plants need regular nutrients alongside water to build healthy green leaves and produce strong ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Jeee ni kumai yeɔ amɛ kɛkɛ Tsei lɛ he miihia ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛfata nu he koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops give a smaller harvest if I plant maize on the same field every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa yibii fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil over and over. Switching to crops like beans or groundnuts gives the soil a rest and puts essential nitrogen back into the earth.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ be fɛɛ be ni Seasons lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hejɔɔmɔ ni ekɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees drooping and turning brown under the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a living umbrella, protecting the young cocoa until it is mature enough to withstand the sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la lɛ gbɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and droop during the hottest hours of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This is the plant's natural trick to survive heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun so it loses less moisture through evaporation.
ga: Enɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli ŋaa ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ fioo.

english: How do my crops know when it is time to start producing flowers and seeds?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ leɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛje fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui afeemɔ shishi?

english: Crops react naturally to changes in light, temperature, and rainfall. When the rains arrive or days get longer, internal signals trigger the plant to stop spending energy on leaves and start making flowers and fruit.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ la, dɔlɛ, kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ mli lɛ he nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ba loo gbii lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ Okadii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ kpaɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii yɛ baai anɔ lɛ ni ebɔi fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai feemɔ.

english: Planting seeds too close forces them to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough resources to grow big and yield abundantly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaadara ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: If I trim away some of the extra branches on my tomato plants, won't that hurt them?
ga: Kɛji mifo niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, Eyeŋ amɛ awui, aloo jeee nakai?

english: Trimming unnecessary leaves and side shoots actually helps the tomato plant. It directs energy away from extra foliage and focuses it entirely on growing bigger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Kɛ́ ofolɔ baai kɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii ni he ehiaaa lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua o-tomato tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Ejieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni eshwɛ lɛ amli ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it better to apply fertilizer to my crops early in the morning or at noon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli leebi loo shwane?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer early in the morning or late afternoon when the soil is cool. Apply it during midday heat, and the sun can scorch the plant roots and evaporate nutrients before the crop can drink them.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooowo ŋmɔshi nibii amli leebi loo shwane be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Kɛtsu nii yɛ shwane mli Hulu la shãa tsei ashishifãi ni ehaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tsei lɛ nuɔ.

english: Leaf curling is a clear signal that the plant is under attack by tiny pests like aphids or mites. The crop curls its leaves in response to damage, indicating it needs pest treatment to recover.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii miitutua tso lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ nɔ ni efite lɛ hetoohamɔ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni atsa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ koni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do weeds always grow so much faster than my crops right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii be fɛɛ be beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild and tough, so they naturally absorb water and nutrients much faster than domestic crops. Clearing them quickly prevents them from stealing the food and sunlight your crops need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ koo mli ni eyɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe shia tsei. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ oya lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛshwere lɛ.

english: What type of fertilizer should I buy to help my crops grow better this season?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ mahe koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: You can use new fertilizers such as urea or ammonia, which supply essential nutrients that help your crops grow strong and healthy.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei tamɔ urea loo ammonia atsu nii. Amɛhaa niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Can I use ammonia fertilizer on my farm, and how does it help my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ammonia ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Ni te nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Yes, ammonia is a suitable fertilizer that feeds your soil with key nutrients, helping your crops get the food they need to develop properly once applied.
ga: Hɛɛ, ammonia ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii titrii. Kɛ akɛtsu nii pɛ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: When should I start counting the days for my crop growth schedule after working on my land?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mabɔi gbii ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ akanemɔ beni mitsu nii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should start counting from the exact day you pour your fertilizer onto the soil, rather than the day you prepare or till the land.
ga: Esa akɛ oje shishi kɛjɛ gbi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, ligbi nɛ o dlaa o he aloo o tsuɔ zugba a he ní ɔ ji ligbi ɔ.

english: How many days should I count after applying fertilizer like urea to my farm?
ga: Beni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea wo ŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ lɛ, gbii enyiɛ esa akɛ akane?

english: Once you pour the fertilizer onto your soil, you should count 80 days from that application date to track your crop's development cycle.
ga: Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okane gbii 80 kɛjɛ gbi ni okɛwo mli lɛ nɔ koni okwɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ ehaa.

english: If I tilled my soil last week but applied urea today, which date is my starting point?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsu nii yɛ otsi ni eho lɛ mli shi mikɛ urea tsu nii ŋmɛnɛ. Mɛni ji mishishijee gbi?

english: Today is your starting point. You must count your 80 days from the day the fertilizer actually touches the soil, not from when you tilled the ground.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛ ji oshishijee be. Esa akɛ okane gbii 80 kɛjɛ gbi ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ta shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Jeee kɛjɛ gbi ni otsu shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I make sure I am keeping the right schedule for my fertilized crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mikɛ be ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwo mli lɛ miitsu nii?

english: Mark the exact day you spread your urea or ammonia fertilizer on the land, and count 80 days forward from that day to keep your farm management on track.
ga: Kadimɔ gbi pɔtɛɛ ni okɛ urea loo ammonia shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni okane gbii 80 ni nyiɛ sɛɛ kɛjɛ nakai gbi lɛ nɔ koni okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is tilling my land enough to make my crops grow fast without adding fertilizer?
ga: Ani mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ oya ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli?

english: No, tilling only prepares the soil structure. Your crops need the extra plant food provided by fertilizers like urea or ammonia to feed and grow well.
ga: Dabi, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitsumɔ ji shikpɔŋ lɛ shishitoo lɛ he saamɔ pɛ. Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ biɔ tsei niyenii kɛfata ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ammonia he. Koni eha niyenii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ

english: Why is the day I apply fertilizer more important for my crop timing than the day I till the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbi ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli lɛ he hiaa waa kɛha dumɔ be lɛ fe gbi ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Tilling breaks up the dirt, but fertilizer provides the actual nutrients. Plants only begin their accelerated growth cycle when those nutrients hit the soil, so timing starts on fertilizer day.
ga: Tilling gbálaa muji lɛ mli. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ diɛŋtsɛ aba. Tsei jeɔ amɛdalɛ oyaiyeli lɛ shishi pɛ kɛji nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kpe. No hewɔ lɛ, be lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ gbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why doesn't my crop development timeline start on the day I dig and turn the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ be lɛ ejeee shishi yɛ gbi ni mifoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni mitsakeɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Digging the soil gets the ground ready, but the real boost in crop behavior happens only after fertilizer is added, which is why the timeline begins at fertilizer application.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akumɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee klalo. Shi tso lɛ subaŋ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ baa yɛ be mli ni awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii pɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ ni haa be he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ.

english: Does urea fertilizer start feeding my crops immediately after I put it on the soil?
ga: Ani urea jeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, once poured onto the land, the fertilizer begins interacting with the soil to feed your crops, making that application day the correct starting point for your 80-day count.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ afɔse shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baabɔi shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ koni ekɛha onibii lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa gbi ni akɛwoɔ fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ feɔ shishijee ni ja kɛha gbii 80 ni okaneɔ lɛ.

english: Is it good for me to burn all the bushes on my farmland before planting my new crops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã tsei bibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani madu tsei heei?

english: Burning may clear the land quickly, but it destroys essential nutrients, useful soil insects, and organic matter in the ground. Clearing without burning leaves organic materials that decay into natural manure, helping your soil stay moist and fertile for longer.
ga: Shãa baanyɛ ajie he ni eyɔɔ lɛ oya. Shi efiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ashãaa lɛ baaha nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ akumɔ ni etsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant on the same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Soil gets tired just like human beings. Planting the same crop on the same plot every season drains all the nutrients from the earth; resting the land or alternating with crops like beans restores nutrients naturally.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ etɔ tamɔ adesai. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hoɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ he ajɔɔ loo okɛ tsei tamɔ ŋmeii atsake koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die whenever the long dry season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong direct sun without shelter. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains around young cocoa provides shade and preserves soil moisture so the seedlings can survive the heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ kɛji amɛbɛ he ko ni amɛhiɔ. Kɛ́ adu nurse tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ, awo kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ adamɔ hulutsoo be lɛ naa.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa trees turning black and rotting while still on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy weather and high humidity. Clearing excess leaves to let in sunlight and harvesting ripe pods quickly prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ jɛɔ ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie baai ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ, ni akpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Yellowing starting from the leaf tips moving inward indicates that the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to grow green and strong. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the growth period fixes this.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anaa ni yaa mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he mra yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: What is making ragged holes in my corn leaves with small dirt particles inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni muji bibii eyi mli obɔ? yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the center of young corn leaves and eat them from the inside, so applying biological or recommended treatments into the leaf funnel early stops them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ baai amli mra lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi amɛnaa.

english: Why do I need to cut long bamboo or wood sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii loo tsei kakadaji koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants use their leaves to catch sunlight and make food for the tubers buried underneath. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground away from dampness and disease, allowing them to gather light to form bigger yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛmɔ hulu la ni amɛfee niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni afu amɛ yɛ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai akabote mli. Ye obua amɛ ni amɛbua la naa koni amɛkɛfee sweet potatoes wuji.

english: How do I know the best time to harvest my cassava so the roots do not spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Koni shishifãi lɛ akafite?

english: Cassava roots are generally ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves begin to turn yellow and drop. Leaving cassava in the soil too long turns the roots woody and tough to cook.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee tso ni ehoomɔ wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tightly and stopping the plant from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekadara lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking juice from the underside of leaves and passing viruses to the plant. Controlling these insects early with natural oil sprays protects the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛkɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni buɔ baai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ.

english: Which plantain shoots are best for me to dig up when starting a new farm?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain henɔ hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mafo beni mijeɔ ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Look for maiden or 'sword' suckers, which have thick bases and thin, spear-like leaves. These grow faster and produce larger bunches than 'water suckers' that have broad leaves and thin bases.
ga: Taomɔ oblayoo loo ‘klante’ tsei, ni yɔɔ shishi ni mli tse kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ. Enɛɛmɛi daa oya ni amɛwoɔ panicles wuji fe ‘suckers’ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ kɛ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when I clear all the large trees from my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants require shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their sensitive leaves and dries out the soil. Leaving some tall trees or planting fast-growing plants like plantains provides necessary shade and keeps the soil cool.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ. tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni ashiɔ Aloo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ koni ekɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat the center leaves of my young maize plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that hides inside the whorl (center) of the maize leaves during the day and feeds at night. Inspecting crops early and applying neem extracts or approved treatments into the plant center can control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli (teŋgbɛ) yɛ shwane mli, ni eyeɔ nii gbɛkɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni adu lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ yɛ tsei ahe nitsumɔhe ko tsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ nibii ni adu lɛ.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, often triggered by irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the tomato plants absorb the calcium they need from the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. ni jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ mli baa Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli ni ejaaa lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa o-tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tips downward even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa shishi lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate that the soil is lacking nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure around the base of the plants restores healthy green foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ baafata he lɛ Tso lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why should I spread animal manure or compost on my field before planting crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ashwie miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ dani madu nii?

english: Animal manure and compost enrich the soil with nutrients, help the ground hold moisture longer during dry spells, and improve soil texture so plant roots can grow easily.
ga: Manure kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii kpakpai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ mlɛo

english: How do I know which part of the cassava stem to cut and plant for a good harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni esa akɛ ofo ni odu koni oná yibii kpakpai?

english: The best planting material comes from the mature middle section of a healthy cassava stem. Avoid the soft green top and the overly woody base, and ensure the leaf buds point upward when planted into the soil.
ga: Nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ jɛɔ ŋmei tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ teŋgbɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shishi fe nine lɛ ahe. Ni kwɛmɔ ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do we build big earth mounds to plant yam tubers instead of planting them directly in flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔmaa sũi wuji ni wɔkɛduɔ ŋmeii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, soft soil to expand freely without obstruction. Mounds provide loose earth for easy tuber growth and prevent water from pooling around the roots, which causes rot.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii amɛ gbɛ. Gɔji yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni bulb lɛ anyɛ adara oya ni eha nu akabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with small yields when I place many seeds in a single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo woɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Putting too many seeds together causes overcrowding, forcing the plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each seed proper spacing ensures strong stems and larger harvests.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baaha mɛi ayi obɔ fe nine. Enɛ haa tsei wuɔ kɛha hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe waa ni amɛkpaa nibii babaoo.

english: Why do some of my plantain trees fall over easily during strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over when their roots are damaged by tiny soil pests like nematodes or root weevils, or when planted too shallowly. Using clean planting suckers and planting at the correct depth ensures strong roots that anchor the tree.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes loo shishifãi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fite shishifãi lɛ. aloo kɛji adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ tsɔ Sucker ni he tse ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ dumɔ yɛ he ni sa lɛ haa shishifãi ni wa ni hiɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth, or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away and waterlogged the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ akwɛ̃ Aloo, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa tsei lɛ amli lɛ ni eha shishifãi lɛ etsɔ nu.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their tiny flowers before any pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Mɛi babaoo dani pods lɛ ba?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce far more flowers than they can support, but excessive flower drop happens when the tree suffers from water stress during dry spells, poor soil nutrients, or a lack of midges to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Kookoo tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi fe nine lɛ baa beni tso lɛ naa nu he haomɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ afeɔ fɔfɔii lɛ ni bɛ

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during strong rains even when they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top. If soil insects like nematodes or stem borers damage the roots, the plant loses its grip in wet, loose soil and blows over.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo stem borers fite shishifãi lɛ, Tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the ground before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in poorly drained or heavy clay soils, creating wet conditions that allow soil fungi to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa bulb lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my young mango trees drop almost all their tiny fruits short after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango tso lɛ miifite eyibii bibii lɛ? Nɔ ni miihe ashɛ fɛɛ yɛ fɔfɔii ni ewo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Mango trees drop excess fruit naturally, but losing almost everything is usually caused by dry soil during fruit formation or fungal diseases like anthracnose attacking the small stems.
ga: Mango tsei shwieɔ aduawai ni fa fe nine lɛ amɛshwieɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Shi nɔ ni miihe ashɛ nibii fɛɛ ni laajeɔ lɛ jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ yibiiwoo be mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ anthracnose ni tutuaa tsei bibii lɛ ahewɔ.

english: Curling leaves in pepper plants are typically caused by tiny pests like mites or whiteflies sucking the plant juices, or by a viral infection spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: Why are small green insects covering the undersides of my vegetable leaves and leaving a sticky liquid?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ haa aduawai ahe baai ashishigbɛ ni amɛshiɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: These insects are aphids, which suck sap from the leaves and secrete a sugary waste called honeydew, which can attract black mold and slow down plant growth.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ji aphids. Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛjieɔ muji ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ sugar ni atsɛɔ lɛ nectar lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ agbala ŋmeii diji kɛba ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do my crops yield smaller harvests when I plant seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete with each other for limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in weak plants with smaller yields.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni faaa Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans in my farm make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas have special bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a free natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas yɛ helai krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting green shoots in the barn before I take them to market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ je shishi ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani akɛba jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that naturally come out of their resting state when exposed to warm temperature and humidity, signaling the tuber to start growing a new plant using its stored food.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni amɛjoɔ amɛhejɔɔmɔ shihilɛ lɛ naa foi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tsɔɔmɔ bulb lɛ koni ebɔi tsei heei akwɛmɔ kɛtsɔ niyenii ni ato lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and dying during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots and thin leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantain or banana alongside them provides living umbrellas that protect the leaves from burning and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo. ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ Dumɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo banana yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ ashãmɔ naa ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my young maize plants light green or yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ji eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Heavy rains often wash this nutrient away, so applying fertilizer or organic manure early in the plant's life helps restore its health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛyaa. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli afata he mra. yɛ tso lɛ wala mli lɛ baaye abua ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots soft rot when there is too much rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits around the roots without draining away, the soil stays waterlogged, suffocating the roots and causing the tubers to rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kpɛtɛ shishifãi ahe ni ejeee kpo lɛ Nu baafee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi

english: Why are my crops smaller and weaker when I plant cassava and maize very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Crops planted too close to each other must fight for the same water, sunlight, and soil food. Giving each crop enough space ensures their roots and leaves have room to grow without starving neighboring plants.
ga: Esa akɛ tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ atswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛdaraa ni hɔmɔ yeee tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in the middle whorl leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai bibii lɛ yɛ bu ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This pattern of leaf damage is usually caused by young fall armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the central growing point of the maize plant, where they feed on tender leaves before the stalk fully expands.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fall armyworm caterpillars, ni kɛ amɛhe teeɔ hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani ŋmeii lɛ mli shwereɔ kwraa.

english: Why does putting dry grass around the base of my tomato plants keep them from wilting so fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛfataa mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ shwieee oya lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, acts like a shield against the sun. It traps moisture in the ground longer, cools the root zone, and stops weeds from stealing water.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ gãimlibii ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi lɛ aju nu

english: When the weather gets extremely hot and dry, pepper plants drop their blossoms to preserve water and survive. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot spells helps the plant hold onto its flowers and form fruit.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my garden egg plants twisting up and turning small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsi amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii lɛ?

english: Curled and distorted leaves are often a sign that tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies are feeding on the leaves and spreading plant viruses that stunt new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe ni etsɔ ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies lɛ miiye baai lɛ ni amɛmiigbɛ tsei amli helai ni tsiɔ dalɛ hee naa lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why is it taking several years for my new cashew trees to give me a big harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani mi-cashew tso hee lɛ woɔ yibii ni sa kadimɔ waa lɛ?

english: Perennial tree crops spend their early years building deep taproots and thick stems to anchor themselves and store energy. They only focus on producing large amounts of nuts once their framework is strong enough.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ yeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ ni amɛdaraa. Koni afee taproots ni mli kwɔ kɛ stems ni mli tse ni baaha amɛhe ahi shi ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato. Amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii babaoo ni amɛbaafee lɛ nɔ pɛ kɛji akɛ shishitoo lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why didn't my cowpea seeds come up after I buried them deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds carry only a limited supply of stored energy to sprout. If buried too deep, the young shoot exhausts all its energy trying to push through the heavy soil before it ever reaches the sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui bɛ hewalɛ ni ato kɛha amɛkwɛ̃mɔ. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen nutrients or when excessive water around the roots prevents the plant from breathing and absorbing food properly.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. aloo be mli ni nu ni ebɔle tso lɛ Shishifãi babaoo tsɔ lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekamu ni enyɛŋ eŋɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava produce big leafy branches but only thin, weak roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ niji kɛ baai wuji shi shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava is planted in soil with too much nitrogen or shaded by big trees, the plant uses all its energy to grow tall branches and leaves to reach sunlight instead of expanding its underground tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɔɔ mli loo tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo shishi lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo niji kɛ baai kakadaji amli koni ená hulu la, moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshishifãi lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off without setting fruit when daytime temperatures become too high, when water is irregular, or when there are no insects around to help pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu lɛ ebɔle ehe loo be mli ni kooloi bibii bɛ he Koni eye ebua ni fɔfɔii lɛ afee pollination

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my pepper plants even when the pepper bushes are already tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ ekwɛ momo moŋ?

english: Weeds compete silently with pepper plants for fertilizer and water in the soil, and they also shelter hidden insect pests that transfer damaging viruses to your crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli dioo. kɛ pepper tsei koni ana ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ni amɛbuɔ he hu kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni gbɛɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii eshwaa onibii amli lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my plantain suckers taking so long to produce fruit after I planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains are heavy feeders that require rich soil full of organic matter and steady moisture; without enough manure or water during dry spells, their growth slows down dramatically.
ga: Plantains ji niyenii ni tsii ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni eyi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli daa. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Amɛdalɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why am I finding small caterpillars eating holes inside my maize stems during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ ŋmãa tsei amli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pests like the Fall Armyworm thrive in warm dry weather, laying eggs on young leaves so their hatched caterpillars can hide deep inside the plant funnel to feed protected from sun and spray.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ baai bibii anɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni ŋmeii ni afɔ lɛ lɛ anyɛ ahi tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye niyenii ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ ahe.

english: Heavy rain creates high air humidity that spreads a water mold fungus causing Black Pod disease; trimming dense shade trees lets sunlight and air in to keep pods dry and healthy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo babaoo baa ni egbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ eshwaa. Tsei ni afolɔ mli lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ba koni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize in the same farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu cowpeas loo beans kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, which naturally feeds the surrounding soil and helps neighboring maize plants grow bigger without extra fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. ni kɛ niyenii haa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmãa kroko afata he.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves curl up and droop in the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: Plants roll or curl their leaves in intense afternoon heat to cut down on water loss through transpiration; as long as the soil has moisture, they usually bounce back once the sun cools down.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ loo amɛfoɔ amɛ yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ aba shi. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛji hulu lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Why did some of the seeds I planted fail to sprout out of the ground completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi yeee omanye kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they were planted too deep for the shoot to reach the surface, if the soil dried out right after planting, or if soil insects ate the seeds before they could sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu lɛ Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ye dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Can someone put a curse on my farm to make my crop leaves turn yellow and die, or is it a plant sickness?
ga: Namɔ baanyɛ alomɔ miŋmɔ lɛ koni eha mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi? Aloo eji tso hela?

english: Crop sickness is caused by living germs like viruses, bacteria, or fungi, not by spiritual curses or witchcraft. Just as human beings get sick from germs in the air or water, plants get sick when these tiny organisms attack their leaves, stems, or roots.
ga: Helai ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ virus, bacteria loo fungi kɛ tsei ahe helai baa, shi jeee mumɔŋ loomɔi loo abɛi. Taakɛ bɔ ni adesai yeɔ hela kɛjɛɔ helai ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ loo nu mli lɛ amli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Tsei yeɔ hela kɛ́ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ye amɛnɔ. Enɛɛmɛi tutuaa ebaai, eshishifãi loo eshishifãi.

english: What does it mean when an extension officer says my crop has a viral disease?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛ́ extension official lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa?

english: A viral disease means microscopic germs called viruses have invaded your plant's body. Unlike pests that you can spray and kill directly, plant viruses live inside the crop's sap, so infected plants usually need to be removed to stop the sickness from spreading.
ga: Virus hela tsɔɔ akɛ muawai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ virus lɛ ebote tso lɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli. Tso mli helai tamɔɔɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni obaanyɛ okɛshwie nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni ogbe amɛ. Tse mli helai hiɔ tsei amli nu lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are my coconut palms suddenly drying up and losing leaves even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, akokoso tsei lɛ gbiɔ trukaa ni amɛbaai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: When palm trees dry up during the rainy season, it is usually caused by a wilt disease like Cape St. Paul Wilt. This sickness attacks the plant's internal tubes, blocking water and nutrients from reaching the top leaves until the tree dies.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ gĩɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli Bei pii lɛ, helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe tamɔ Cape St. Paul Wilt lɛ kɛbaa, ni hela nɛɛ tutuaa tsei amli ŋmeii lɛ. Etsiɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyashi tso lɛ gboɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are dying from sun heat or from a real disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa loo hela miigbe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Heat or drought makes all crops in a field drop their leaves evenly, and they revive when night comes or rain falls. A disease usually starts on a few plants, leaves spots or rot, and rain will not make the infected plants recover.
ga: Dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baa lɛ fiteɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. ni ebaate shi ekoŋŋ kɛ́ gbɛkɛ shɛ loo nugbɔ nɛ. Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ tsei fioo komɛi amli. leaf spot loo rot Ni nugbɔ haŋ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Do crops get sick by taking in bad food or dirty water from the soil?
ga: Ani hela mɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ niyenii gbonyo ni ayeɔ loo nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: Crops do not eat like animals, but they absorb soil moisture. Sickness enters through wounds in roots, tiny holes in leaves, or when insects like leafhoppers bite the plant and inject germs directly into its sap while feeding.
