ga: Ayeee ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kooloi. Shi ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. Hela lɛ tsɔɔ pilamɔi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli, bu bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ ŋmɔ tso lɛ ni amɛkɛ helatsɛmɛi awo tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: If my neighbor's farm has sick plants, can that sickness travel to my crops?
ga: Kɛji okutsoŋnyo ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ Ani hela lɛ baanyɛ aya miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Yes, plant sickness can easily cross farm borders. Insects, wind, flowing rainwater, and even farm boots or cutlasses carrying infected dirt can carry germs from your neighbor's field straight to your healthy crops.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ahe helai baanyɛ afo ŋmɔ mli husui, kooloi bibii, kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ mli oya. kɛ bɔɔtu loo dade po ni hiɛ shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ mli lɛ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛjɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛya onibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How does a crop disease suddenly appear in a village where we have never seen it before?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tso hela ko aba trukaa yɛ akrowa ko ni wɔnako eko dã lɛ mli?

english: New plant diseases usually arrive when farmers unknowingly bring infected seedlings, suckers, or soil from another region, or when disease-carrying insects fly in from affected areas looking for fresh crops.
ga: Tsei ahe helai heei Bei pii lɛ ebaa kɛji okwaafoi kɛ dumɔwui, dumɔwui, loo shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛjɛ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ lɛ ba ni amɛleee. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni kɛ helai baa lɛ fãa kɛjɛɔ hei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛbaa koni amɛyatao nibii heei ni amɛbaakwɛ.

english: How do agricultural officers know what exact disease is killing my crops when they take plant samples away?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ amɛle hela ni miifite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni amɛŋɔ tsei ahe nɔkwɛmɔnii lɛ?

english: Officers take samples of sick leaves or stems to a laboratory where they use special microscopes and chemical tests to look inside the plant tissue and identify the exact germ causing the damage.
ga: Nitsulɔi lɛ kɛ helatsamɔ baai loo tsei ahe nɔkwɛmɔnii yaa laboratori. Ekɛ tsɔne krɛdɛɛ ko ni akɛkwɛɔ nibii bibii kɛ tsofai ni akɛkaa nibii bibii lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei amli fãji amli. ni oyoo hela pɔtɛɛ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa lɛ.

english: Can washing my cutlass and boots stop crop diseases from spreading on my farm?
ga: Ani mi-daggers kɛ mi-boots lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsei ahe helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa?

english: Yes, washing your cutlass and farm boots with clean water and soap or bleach removes infected plant sap and soil particles, preventing you from transferring germs from a sick tree to a healthy one.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli tse kɛ samla loo bleach tsu dadei kɛ ŋmɔ mli atadei ahe nii lɛ, ebaajie tso lɛ mli nu kɛ muji ni hela emɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ bo gbɛ koni okajie helatsɛmɛi kɛjɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: If I cut down a tree that died from a disease, can I leave the wood on the farm to rot into fertilizer?
ga: Kɛji ofo tso ni hela egbo lɛ Ani abaanyɛ ashi tso yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni egbo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: No, leaving a diseased tree on your farm leaves the germs and insects active inside it, allowing them to jump to surrounding healthy trees. Diseased plants should be cut down, removed, and burned or buried far away.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ oshi tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha helatsɛmɛi kɛ kooloi bibii atsu nii waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛjoɔ foi kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ. Esa akɛ afo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ajie, ashã loo afu amɛ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ.

english: Can I use chicken droppings as fertilizer on my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei atsu nii akɛ ŋmei yɛ kookoo tsei anɔ?

english: Yes, chicken manure is rich in nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus that help cocoa trees grow strong and produce more pods, but it should be dried or composted before application so it does not burn the roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii mli nibii tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus babaoo yɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo. Shi esa akɛ agbi loo afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ dani akɛtsu nii. koni akashã shishifãi lɛ

english: Will putting too much animal manure around my cocoa trees cause the pods to rot?
ga: Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo woɔ mli Ani mi-cacao ŋmɔji lɛ baafite?

english: Using excessive fresh manure can create too much dampness around the base of the tree and burn the roots, which attracts fungi and increases the risk of diseases like black pod rot.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ hee babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔtɔ aba tso lɛ he. Tsoi ashishifãi babaoo ni haa shishifãi lɛ shãa Enɛ gbalaa ŋmeii ni ehaa helai tamɔ black pod rot lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops grow bigger and yield more when I add chicken manure to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo kɛ́ mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Chicken manure improves soil structure, feeds beneficial soil organisms, and slowly releases essential food that helps crop roots absorb water and nutrients more effectively over time.
ga: Kooloo ŋmei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ fɛo. Ehaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ niyenii ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ kpo fiofio.

english: Is it safe to apply fresh wet manure directly onto my crop roots?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii hee baawo mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, fresh wet manure produces high heat and strong ammonia as it decomposes, which can burn young crop roots and damage plants; it is best to let it dry or turn into compost first.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii ni efɔ ehee lɛ jieɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ ammonia ni mli eyi obɔ kpo beni efiteɔ lɛ. ni baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii ashishifãi ni efite tsei Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha egbi loo otsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: How does rain help the fertilizer or manure I place on the farm ground to start working?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni ebɔi nitsumɔ?

english: Rainwater dissolves the nutrients in the fertilizer or manure on the soil surface, washing them down into the root zone where the crop roots can drink them in.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Kɛkɛ lɛ, efoɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ ahe he ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ yɛ lɛ.

english: Should I spread fertilizer on top of the ground or bury it in the soil on my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo mafu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli sũ lɛ mli?

english: Lightly working manure or fertilizer into the top soil prevents rain from washing it away, though spreading it around the tree canopy ring before light rains also allows nutrients to seep down naturally.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko fata sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ egbɛ eshwa Tso lɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ he dani nugbɔ fioo lɛ nɛɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ hu ni ekɛ ehe woɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What happens to manure left on the soil surface if a heavy downpour of rain falls?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmeii ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa?

english: Heavy downpours can wash away loose manure on top of the soil before the crops can absorb it, which is why placing it in shallow soil rings around crops is safer.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ kooloi ashishifã kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani ŋmɔshi nibii anyɛ aŋɔ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ amɛ baawo shikpɔŋ ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli ni bɔleɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to rot on the tree during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ fiteɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Cocoa pod rot is usually caused by fungal spores that spread quickly in dark, damp, and cool rainy conditions, especially if there is limited air circulation through the farm canopy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal spores ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cocoa tso fitemɔ baa. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ faaa.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are getting enough nutrients to produce a bigger harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Nutrient-rich cocoa trees display deep green leaves, produce plenty of healthy flowers, and carry firm, well-formed pods without dropping them early.
ga: Cacao tsei ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa. Ha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Ni ŋmeii lɛ yɛ su ni mli wa ni amɛgbeee shi oya.

english: Why do some fertilizers take longer to show results on crop growth than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi heɔ be babaoo dani ejieɔ nɔ ni jɛɔ tsei adalɛ mli baa lɛ kpo fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Organic materials like manure break down slowly with rain and biological activity over time, providing long-lasting nutrient benefits, whereas quick-release chemical fertilizers act fast but wash away sooner.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ kooloi ashishi lɛ, fiteɔ fiofio. nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ anitsumɔi ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ yɛ be mli ni haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni shwieɔ oya lɛ tsuɔ nii oya shi amɛhoɔ oya fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: The best time to spray is early in the morning before 10 AM or late in the afternoon after 4 PM. During the hot midday hours, intense sun causes the chemical to evaporate too quickly, which can waste your medicine and burn the crop leaves.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔse tsofa lɛ ji leebi dani 10:00 a.m. loo shwane mli yɛ 4:00 p.m. sɛɛ. yɛ shwane mli kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Hulu la ni tsoɔ babaoo lɛ baaha tsofai lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ otsofa lɛ ni ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ baai lɛ.

english: Why does the crop medicine I spray seem less effective when I apply it around midday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsofa ni mikɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo mihe yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: High afternoon temperatures cause liquid chemicals to evaporate rapidly into the air before the leaves or pests can absorb them, greatly reducing the strength and effectiveness of the medicine.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ haa tsofai ni ji nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani baai loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsofa lɛ hewalɛ kɛ bɔ ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and roll up during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants roll and droop their leaves in the heat of the day to protect themselves and conserve water. It is a natural defence mechanism to stop moisture from evaporating too fast until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbi ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe ni amɛbu nu he. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni haa ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi oya tsɔ kɛyashiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why did my crops turn yellow after I sprayed them with medicine on a very hot day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ tsofa shwie nɔ yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Spraying liquid chemicals on crops under direct, intense sunlight causes chemical burn. The chemical droplets on hot leaves act like small magnifying glasses, scorching the leaves and causing them to turn yellow or brown.
ga: Tsofai ni ji nu ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha tsofai ashã. Tsofai ni shwieɔ baai ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ glase bibii ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo. Eshãa baai lɛ ni ehaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ.

english: How does hot afternoon soil affect how my crops absorb plant food and liquid fertilizers?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa bɔ ni mitsei lɛ shwieɔ tsei aniyenii kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When the soil gets very hot around midday, crop roots slow down their activity to protect themselves from drying out. This prevents them from taking up water and liquid nutrients effectively until the soil temperature drops.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ Tsei shishifãi lɛ baa amɛnitsumɔ lɛ shi koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ he. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ nu kɛ nu mli niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I avoid using heavy motorized spraying machines on my farm between 10 AM and 4 PM?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsɔnei ni tsii ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ leebi ŋmɛji 10:00 kɛyashi shwane ŋmɛji 4:00 teŋ lɛ he?

english: Carrying heavy machinery in extreme heat puts severe stress on your body, leading to heat exhaustion. Additionally, high heat makes chemical fumes stronger and easier for you to inhale, increasing health risks.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii ni akɛwoɔ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa baa gbɔmɔtso lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe yɛ dɔlɛ mli. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa hu haa tsofa mli lasu lɛ mli waa ni efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa bo akɛ ooomu. ni haa hewalɛnamɔ he osharai yaa hiɛ lɛ

english: Why do extension officers warn us against doing heavy chemical spraying during the hottest hours of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ bɔɔ kɔkɔ yɛ tsofai ni tsii ni akɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Peak heat hours between 10 AM and 3 PM pose high health dangers to farmers, such as dizziness and chemical poisoning through sweat, while also causing poor chemical coverage and leaf damage on the crops.
ga: ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ waa yɛ 10:00 AM kɛ 3:00 PM teŋ lɛ kɛ hewalɛnamɔ he osharai ni yɔɔ hiɛdɔɔ baa okwaafoi anɔ, tamɔ tsitsi ni tsɔɔ tsitsi nɔ kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛtsɔɔ latsaa nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ haaa ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe baai.

english: Why don't weedkillers work properly on weeds when I spray them in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ mikɛshwie nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During hot afternoon hours, weeds close the tiny breathing pores on their leaves to save water. Because these pores are closed, the weeds cannot soak up the weedkiller, making the spray far less effective.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Jwɛi baatsi mumɔ buji bibii anaa. yɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni akɛbu nu Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ efo. No hewɔ lɛ jwɛi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: Is it bad to water my vegetable crops in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehiii akɛ oooha aduawai nu yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, watering in hot sunshine causes most of the water to evaporate immediately into the air before reaching root level, and applying cool water to hot soil can shock delicate roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli ejɔ tsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ egba shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young crops need shade trees or intercropping to survive intense afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ he hiaa tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa loo ni aduɔ yɛ amɛteŋ koni amɛnyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ shwane latsaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings have thin leaves and tender stems that burn easily in full sun. Shade plants block direct heat between 10 AM and 4 PM, keeping the soil cool and preserving moisture for the young crops to grow.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii yɛ baai bibii kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Tsei ni yɔɔ shade mli lɛ tsiɔ dɔlɛ naa tɛ̃ɛ yɛ 10 a.m. kɛ 4 p.m teŋ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛhaa tsei bibii ni miida lɛ.

english: Maize leaves curl up during hot hours to reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to the sun, which helps the plant save water and stop itself from drying out.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni hulu la ni baa amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu toɔ ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbi.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable crops early in the morning or in the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo aduawai anɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning allows the soil to absorb moisture before the sun gets too hot, preventing water from evaporating too fast and keeping the plant leaves from getting heat-damaged.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani hulu lɛ mli woɔ la tsɔ. Tsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. ni ehaa tsei ahe baai lɛ fiteɔ kɛtsɔ la ni tsoɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the plant is short on nutrients like nitrogen or is getting too much water, causing it to send its remaining food to the newest leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, loo eyɛ nu babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ majeɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers keep falling off the plant before any fruits start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they face heat stress, lack sufficient water, or receive too much nitrogen, as the plant tries to save energy to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo nitrogen babaoo ni anáaa Enɛ ji akɛ, tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why does my groundnut plant push its flowers down into the dirt after they blossom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ efɔfɔi lɛ awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants naturally push their fertilized blossoms underground so the actual nuts can grow and ripen safely protected inside the soil.
ga: Peanut tsei tsiɔ fɔfɔi ni awo mli fɔ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Koni afee ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ Ebaanyɛ eda ni ekwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and hard when the soil gets very firm and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe wa be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ wa waa ni egbi lɛ?

english: Cassava needs soft, loose soil to swell up; when the ground is too hard, the roots cannot easily expand to store food and water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse he miihia cassava koni efuu. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni amɛkɛ niyenii kɛ nu ato.

english: Staking holds yam leaves high off the ground where they can catch maximum sunlight, helping the plant make more food to grow larger yams underground.
ga: Staking duɔ sweet potato baai lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la babaoo yɛ. Ye obua tsei ni amɛwo niyenii babaoo koni amɛdu ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cowpea plants have plenty of bushy green leaves but very few seed pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ hiɛ baai ŋmɔji babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi dumɔwui ŋmɔji fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Giving cowpeas too much fertilizer high in nitrogen makes the plant spend all its energy growing big leaves instead of making flowers and pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tsina ŋmei mli fe nine lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ.

english: Why do my plantain shoots take much longer to produce fruit when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting too close makes the trees fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, which slows down their growth and delays fruit production.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. nibii ni haa mɔ he waa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ, ni haa ŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa aduawai lɛ hu sɛɛ tsɛɔ

english: Young cocoa leaves will turn yellow or brown around the edges, dry up, and curl if they do not have enough shade trees protecting them from full sun.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ. Egbi ni ebɔle ehe kɛji tsei ni haa hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he lɛ bɛ.

english: How do I know when my palm nuts are ripe enough to harvest from the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-palm dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Palm nuts are ready for harvest when a few loose reddish-orange fruits naturally fall from the bunch to the ground around the tree trunk. Harvesting at this stage ensures the nuts have reached their highest oil content.
ga: Palm tsei lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni aduawai fioo komɛi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ lɛ. natural tree trunk Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ amli mu lɛ fa fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do my harvested palm nuts spoil and go bad so quickly if I do not sell them immediately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-palm yibii ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ ni efiteɔ oya kɛji mihɔ̃ɔɔ amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Once a palm bunch is cut from the tree, natural enzymes inside the nuts start breaking down the oil rapidly into free fatty acids. This causes fermentation and spoilage within two to three days unless they are processed, boiled, or kept cool.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afolɔ tsei akui kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ Adebɔɔ mli enzymes ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbalaa mu lɛ oya ni efeɔ fatty acids ni bɛ nyɔmɔwoo. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni efiteɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli. ja atsu he nii, ahoo, loo akɛto he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ

english: Why is my young oil palm tree producing flowers, but no fruits are forming on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso bibioo lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi shi ebɛ yibii lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees produce separate male and female flowers. Very young trees often produce mostly male flowers first, or there may not be enough tiny pollinating insects in the area to transfer pollen to the female flowers to form fruit.
ga: Mu tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii waa lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi hii babaoo klɛŋklɛŋ. Aloo ekolɛ kooloi bibii ni feɔ pollin lɛ yɛ jɛmɛ. He ko bɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ ajie pollen awo fɔfɔi yei lɛ amli koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and turn brown when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that scorch easily in direct, intense sunlight. Canopy trees or temporary shade plants like plantains act as living umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting young cocoa from leaf burn until it gets older.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋwɛi ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ baai ni shãa lɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I allow all the small sucker shoots growing around my plantain tree to stay?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Midumɔwui lɛ yɛ biɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: When too many suckers grow around a plantain tree, they steal water, plant food, and sunlight from the main mother tree. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the plant to direct its energy into producing large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu ko he lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, niyenii ni miida, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso titri ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja ekome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with large green leaves, but producing tiny roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Baai wuji eŋɔli shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen from soil or fertilizer, it spends all its energy growing heavy leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in its tuber roots. Avoiding high-nitrogen fertilizers helps the plant focus on root growth.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ. Ebaafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaa kɛ eshishifãi ni tsii lɛ baakwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ niye ní toɔ a tuber sisi a mi. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi lɛ adalɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my green maize plants turning yellow starting from the tips down the middle vein?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛyashi amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the main vein of maize leaves is a sign that the soil is low in nitrogen, which the crop needs to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore healthy green growth.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai wuji lɛ ahe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kooloo ŋmãa ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmãa ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmãa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yam vines climb toward sunlight to make the food needed to expand their tubers deep underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the damp ground, which prevents leaf diseases caused by damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he koni amɛfee niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa baai lɛ ahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ foliar helai ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences stress from excessive heat, sudden heavy rain, or dry soil. Mulching around the roots and keeping soil moisture consistent helps the plant retain its flowers until fruit forms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni fe nine. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi, ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do the center leaves of my young corn plants look ragged with holes and filled with coarse sawdust-like dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni etse ni eyɛ bu ni muji eyi mli obɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar feeding inside the central leaf funnel of the corn plant. The sawdust-like material is the insect's waste, which can be controlled by applying biological sprays early in the morning when the pest is active.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ. Nibii ni tamɔ sawdust ji kooloi amli jwɛi. Abaanyɛ akudɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii anɔ yɛ leebi be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ tsuɔ nii waa lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I choose crops that will keep selling well in Ghanaian markets in the coming years?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmɔshi nibii ni baajara jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana jarayelihe lɛ yɛ afii ni baa lɛ amli?

english: Crops like coconut, cassava, and vegetables stay in high demand because our growing population needs them daily for cooking, food processing, and local industries, making them reliable long-term investments.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ aduawai lɛ kã he eji nɔ ni ataoɔ waa. Ejaakɛ wɔ gbɔmɛi ayibɔ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ he miihia tsei nɛɛ daa gbi kɛha niyenii homɔ. Niyenii ahe nitsumɔ kɛ maŋ lɛ mli nitsumɔhei Enɛ haa efeɔ shika ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What is the benefit of planting long-term tree crops like coconut instead of only planting quick seasonal food crops?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni aduɔ yɛ be mli niyenii pɛ ni aduɔ lɛ he?

english: Seasonal crops like maize give fast cash within months, but tree crops like coconut require patience initially and then provide steady harvests and income for several decades without needing replanting every season.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be mli, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ woɔ nyɔmɔ oya yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli, shi nibii ni aduɔ daa, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ biɔ tsuishitoo yɛ shishijee mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa yibiiwoo ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ shika afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni adu ekoŋŋ daa be mli.

english: Why does a coconut tree take several years before it produces its first fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani akokoshi tsei woɔ amɛklɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ?

english: Coconut trees spend their early years building deep roots and a thick trunk to support the massive weight of heavy coconut bunches later in life, ensuring the tree stays strong and productive for over 50 years.
ga: Kokoo tsei yeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ ni amɛdaraa. Koni afee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ni mli tse ni baaye abua ŋmeii ni tsii ni tsii lɛ ahe muji wulu lɛ yɛ amɛwala naagbee. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fe afii 50 sɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my coconut trees drop their tiny young flowers before they turn into full coconuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi bibii dani ebafeɔ ŋmei ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Dropping young flowers usually happens when the palm experiences water stress during dry weather or lacks potassium in the soil, causing the tree to save energy by shedding flowers it cannot feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji akɛ tsei ni ji palms lɛ na nu he haomɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi loo potassium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ buɔ amɛhewalɛ he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛshwieɔ yɛ he ni amɛnaaa niyenii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do coconut palms grow so well near coastal areas where other crops fail?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋshɔnaa he ni tsei krokomɛi nyɛɛɛ akwɛ lɛ?

english: Coconut palms have very flexible roots and a high tolerance for salt and sandy soil, allowing them to suck up deep underground water in areas where other farm crops dry up and die.
ga: Kokoo tsei lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe waa, ni amɛŋmɛɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ nɔ amɛtsui shi waa. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ashɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɔɔ lɛ. Ebaanyɛ egbi ni egbo.

english: Can I grow vegetables or cassava between my young coconut trees on the same land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ateŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, while coconut trees are still young and small, plenty of sunlight reaches the ground, so you can plant short-term crops between them to earn money while waiting for the coconuts to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ ji gbekɛ ni hulu la babaoo shɛɔ shikpɔŋ moŋ, No hewɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ odu be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmei tsei ateŋ koni oná shika yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: What will happen to my tree crops if I plant them too close to each other on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If tree crops are planted too close together, their leaves block each other from sunlight and their roots fight over water, resulting in tall, thin trees that yield very few fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ haa hulu lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu he akaŋshii mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young crop plants turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for help showing that the crop is lacking essential soil nutrients like nitrogen or that heavy rains have trapped too much water around the roots, preventing them from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji yelikɛbuamɔ he bolɔmɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ emɔ nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni eha amɛmiigbɔjɔ.

english: Why does a crop that looked healthy yesterday suddenly wilt and dry up from the base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nyɛ lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgbiɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting often means soil diseases or root rot have damaged the plant's underground water pipes, stopping water from traveling up from the soil to the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ ni egboɔ trukaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko eba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shishifãi ni egbo lɛ efite tso lɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu paipii lɛ. Enɛ haa nu nyɛɛɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya baai lɛ anɔ.

english: How does adding fertilizer actually help my crops grow bigger fruits?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Fertilizers feed the soil with key elements like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium, which act like food for the plant, giving it energy to grow strong stems and pump goodness into expanding fruits.
ga: Nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasiam haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛha tsei Ehaa hewalɛ kɛha tsei akutsei ni wa lɛ adalɛ ni ekɛ ekpakpafeemɔ pɔmpiɔ kɛyaa mlilɛɛmɔ mli

english: Will using heavy machinery to clear my bush land harm the soil or my crop roots?
ga: Ani nibii ni tsii ni mikɛbaatsu nii kɛjie mi koo lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baaye mishikpɔŋ lɛ loo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ awui?

english: Heavy machinery can crush the topsoil and compact it, making it hard for crop roots to breathe and absorb water. It can also damage hidden underground root systems, so it is important to check the ground after clearing and loosen hard soil before planting.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii baanyɛ akumɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni efee lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi akɛ amɛaamu ni amɛŋɔ nu. Ebaanyɛ efite shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ hu. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni ajie shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli ni ajie lɛ dani adu nii.

english: How do I protect my young plantain stems from being destroyed when laborers or machines clear my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛjɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɔ beni nitsulɔi loo tsɔnei miitsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You can place tall wooden stakes or bright flags next to young plantain shoots before clearing starts. This makes them visible to workers and machine operators so they can clear around them without cutting or trampling them.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsei kakadaji loo aflaŋaa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ama plantain tsei bibii lɛ ahe dani aje shishi ajie tsei lɛ. Ehaa nitsulɔi kɛ tsɔnei ahe nitsulɔi naa lɛ Bɔni afee ni onyɛ ojie nibii ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. ni afolɔɔɔ loo ashɛɛɛ he

english: Why do new shoots keep coming up around my plantain stem even after the stem is cut down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii heei ebɔle he fɛɛ lɛ? Mi plantain tsei lɛ yɛ be mli ni mifo tso lɛ po sɛɛ?

english: Plantains grow from an underground root base called a corm. When the main stem is cut or harvested, the plant naturally directs its energy to produce new shoots, called suckers, to continue its life cycle.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni atsɛɔ amɛ rhizomes lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ afo loo akpaa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛfee ŋmeii heei, ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii, koni amɛkɛtsa amɛwala shihilɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop or turn yellow shortly after the surrounding land is cleared?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni ajie he ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: When dense bush around plantains is cleared, the plants suddenly get exposed to strong direct sunlight and heat. This causes temporary environmental shock, but with enough soil water, the plant will adapt and grow fresh leaves.
ga: Beni ajie jwɛi ni ebɔle The plantains lɛ ahe lɛ. Hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ hu baashɛ tsei lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ kɛ shihilɛ mli tsakemɔi baa be kukuoo ko mli. Shi kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ baatsake ehe ni ebaakwɛ baai heei.

english: How long does a plantain plant usually take from planting until the fruit is ready for harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui adumɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni aduawai lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Most plantain varieties take between 11 to 15 months to yield harvestable fruit. The plant flowers around 8 to 10 months, and the bunch takes another 3 to 4 months to mature fully.
ga: Plantain henɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ aaafee nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 15 dani amɛwoɔ yibii ni abaanyɛ akpa. Fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 10 ni fɔfɔi lɛ aheɔ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 krokomɛi dani amɛdaraa.

english: How far apart should I space my plantain suckers when planting a new farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ makɛ plantain tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ abɔ he tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmɔ hee?

english: Plantain suckers should be planted about 2 to 3 meters apart. Proper spacing gives each plant enough access to sunlight, soil nutrients, and rainfall, leading to bigger bunches and healthier stems.
ga: Esa akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ aaafee mitai 2 kɛyashi 3 kɛjɛ amɛhe. He ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ aniji daraa ni amɛtso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can I grow plantains together on the same land with young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu plantains yɛ he kome kɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Yes, planting plantains with young cocoa is a very good practice. The wide leaves of the plantain provide vital shade to shield sensitive young cocoa trees from harsh sunlight while providing food and income early on.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo bibii kwɛɔ lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa waa. Plantain tso lɛ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo be ni he hiaa ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛhaa niyenii kɛ shika mra.

english: What should I look for in the existing crops when buying an already established farm from another person?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ matao yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ momo lɛ amli kɛ́ mihe ŋmɔ ko ni ato ama shi momo kɛjɛ mɔ kroko dɛŋ?

english: Inspect the general health of the standing plants, checking for disease spots, pest damage, soil erosion, and how well the farm was cleared or weeded. Healthy roots and strong underground corms show the farm can keep producing well.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ ahewalɛ fɛɛ, kwɛmɔ kɛji helai kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii yɛ amɛhe. shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi kɛ bɔ ni jwɛi loo jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni wa tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii.

english: How big is one hectare of farmland, and why is knowing this important for my crops?
ga: Te okwaayeli shikpɔŋ hectare kome da ha tɛŋŋ? Ni mɛni hewɔ enɛ ni mile lɛ he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: One hectare is equal to a plot of land measuring 100 meters by 100 meters, roughly the size of a standard football field. Knowing your exact land size helps you calculate how many crop suckers to buy and how much labor or fertilizer you need.
ga: Hectare kome kɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji mitai 100 x 100 yeɔ egbɔ, ni no ji shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ tamɔ bɔɔlutswaa he ko ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ole bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ da ha pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni obu tsei ni shwieɔ nu lɛ ayibɔ ni esa akɛ ohe lɛ he akɔntaa. kɛ nitsumɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni he hiaa bo lɛ.

english: How can I tell when a bunch of plantains on the field is ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni plantain ko ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Plantains are ready for harvest when the individual fruits swell and lose their sharp ridges, looking rounded. The fingers near the top of the bunch will also change from dark green to a lighter shade of green.
ga: Plantains efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko fũu ni esɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ sɛɛ fo ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Niji ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmɔ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ baatsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛya eŋɔli ni mli tseee.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and easily get scorched by intense sunlight. Plantains grow very quickly and provide broad leaves that create necessary shade and retain soil moisture for the young cocoa trees until they mature.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ ahe waaa ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛhaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to make green leaves and grow strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Which way should I face the small buds when I plant cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu ŋmei niji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, te esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei bibii lɛ akpee tɛŋŋ?

english: Cassava stem buds must always point upwards toward the sky. If planted upside down, the plant spends too much energy trying to turn its sprouts upward, leading to weak stem growth and very small tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei lɛ tso lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo baatsu nii ni ekɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃. Enɛ haa tso lɛ dalɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ bulbs bibii waa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulching around the roots helps prevent heat stress so flowers can form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛhaaa daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akɛ sũ awo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akatsi dɔlɛ he haomɔ naa koni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii.

english: Black cocoa pods are caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod disease, which spreads rapidly in warm, wet weather. Clearing weeds and pruning branches to let sunlight and air into the farm helps prevent this fungus from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ kookoo diji baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ jwɛi amli kɛ tsei ni afoɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Yam vines naturally climb toward sunlight to make food for their underground tubers. Raising the vines off the damp ground on stakes prevents leaf diseases and ensures the plant gets enough sunlight to grow large yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Wein tsei ni aaakwɛ nɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ tsei lɛ ahe helai anaa, ni ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ ŋmɔtɔ agboi.

english: Rolling leaves is a plant's natural way of protecting itself from losing water. By rolling up, the leaves reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and wind, keeping moisture inside the plant during dry hours.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ nu ni elaajeɔ lɛ he. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: How do groundnuts form nuts under the ground when the flowers bloom above the soil?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii feɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ beni fɔfɔii lɛ fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated above ground, the plant grows long pegs that bend downward and grow into the soil. Once hidden under the earth, the tips of these pegs swell up to develop into groundnut pods.
ga: Beni atswa ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ daa ni etsɔɔ ŋmei kakadaŋŋ ni shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni edaa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛtee shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ashishifãi lɛ fũuɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up tight and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni ehaa tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the underside of leaves. Controlling these insects early allows new leaves to open up properly and let the plant grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni haa chili baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaha baai heei lɛ agbele jogbaŋŋ ni eha tso lɛ ada.

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil. Planting legumes like cowpeas afterwards naturally restores fertility because their roots trap nitrogen from the air and return it to the soil for future crops.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni adebɔɔ mli nibii babaoo aba ekoŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni akɛdu nii wɔsɛɛ.

english: When leaves turn yellow from the tip downward, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or the soil is waterlogged, which stops the roots from absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛba shi lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I place fertilizer a short distance away from the plant stem instead of dumping it directly against the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii fioo yɛ he ko ni kɛ tsei ashishifãi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshɛrɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashwie tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ.

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem can burn and damage the plant tissues, whereas placing it a few inches away puts it right where the active feeding roots can safely absorb it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ shãa aba ni efite tso lɛ fãji. Yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni kɛ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo lɛ, ebaaha tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does spreading dry leaves or grass around the base of my crops help them grow better during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mitso lɛ shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Covering the soil with organic material, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation, and slowly breaks down to feed nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fiofio ni efiteɔ fiofio koni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too high, when the plant experiences water stress, or when there is too much nitrogen causing the plant to produce leaves instead of setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni tsei naa nu he haomɔ Aloo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo ni haa tso lɛ woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very bushy leaves above ground but produces very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil or overuse of rich manure encourages the plant to spend all its energy growing leafy stems instead of storing starch in the roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baawo tsei hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ atsu nii moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn under direct sunlight. They require shade crops like plantains or cassava to shield them and keep the surrounding air humid during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo cassava. Enɛ ji koni abu amɛhe ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee fɛ̃i yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Overcrowded crops compete heavily for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing them to stretch upward for light while lacking the energy needed to form full, healthy cobs.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ehe bahiaa ni tsei lɛ ashɛ amɛhe koni amɛná la yɛ be mli ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛfee ŋmei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eyi obɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it harmful to plant peppers on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously in one spot allows soil-borne diseases and pests to build up in large numbers while completely draining the soil of the specific nutrients that crop relies on.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ yɛ he kome lɛ kɛ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ babaoo baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ kwraa.

english: Why do weeds lower my crop yield even after I have applied fertilizer to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔji amli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing, aggressive root systems that absorb water and fertilizer nutrients faster than your crops can, effectively starving your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa. Enɛ baajie nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I see ragged holes in my young maize leaves and a substance like wet sawdust inside the central funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii ni etse yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli kɛ nɔ ko tamɔ ŋmeii ni efɔ yɛ ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing point of the maize stem, eating the soft inner leaves and leaving behind waste material.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ amli. Ye baai bibii lɛ amli ni oshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away from the roots or when the soil holds too much water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo.

english: Why are the tips of my maize cobs missing grains when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui bɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ naagbee beni mikpaa lɛ?

english: When maize cobs have empty tips, it usually means the plant experienced high heat or drought while the silks were receiving pollen. Without enough water or fertilizer during that critical week, the top grains fail to form.
ga: Beni ŋmãa lɛ naagbee lɛ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ naa dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa waa yɛ be mli ni siliki ŋmei lɛ nine shɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ nakai otsii ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli lɛ, Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ efeŋ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop many flowers, but heavy dropping happens when there are not enough tiny insects in the farm to pollinate them, or when the tree is stressed by harsh sun, dry weather, or poor soil nutrients.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi tso lɛ yibii ni shwieɔ shi waa lɛ baa beni kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ afee pollination lɛ. aloo be mli ni tso lɛ shɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in cool, wet conditions. It thrives when there is too much shade or dense weed growth around the cocoa trees, trapping moisture on the pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be babaoo loo jwɛi babaoo ebɔle cacao tso lɛ he, ni ekɛ nu ni mli ewo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli lɛ mɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up with yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves with yellow spots are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease. It is spread by tiny whitefly insects and by planting stems cut from already sick plants, which prevents the roots from growing large.
ga: Baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Eji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Agbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii bibii anɔ. kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ momo lɛ ashishifãi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ akadara.

english: Why are my yam tubers rotting in the mound before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ gɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot underground when water cannot drain out of the soil mound after heavy rain, or when tiny soil worms called nematodes attack the skin of the tuber and let rot-causing fungi inside.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu nyɛɛɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ tutua ŋmeii lɛ ahewolo ni amɛha ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ boteɔ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers when the afternoon weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat makes tomato pollen dry up or become sticky, preventing proper flower fertilization. When the flower cannot produce seeds, the plant drops it to save its energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha tomato pollen lɛ agbi loo etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ afɔmɔ naa Kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo dumɔwui Tsei lɛ baashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants drooping and falling off during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their lower leaves during dry spells as a survival effort to reduce water loss, keeping what little water they have focused on the stems and developing fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛtsɔ nu fioo ni amɛbua naa lɛ nɔ lɛ amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ekome ni amɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves dry up and burn if I put fertilizer right next to the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain concentrated salts. When placed directly against the stem or main roots, they pull moisture out of the plant tissue instead of feeding it, causing the plant to dry out and look burned.
ga: Fertilizer lɛ yɛ ŋoo babaoo. Kɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi loo shishifã titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ Ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ fãji amli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛshã.

english: Why do my plantain trees lose their outer leaves and turn brown from the bottom up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have large leaves that lose water very quickly. During dry months, the plant deliberately shuts down and drops its older outer leaves so it can conserve water for the central stem and the fruit bunch.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai wuji ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya waa. yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ, ajɛɔ yiŋ aŋmɛɔ tso lɛ ni ashiɔ kponɔgbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ ni ehiɛɛɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko. bɔni afee ni akɛ nu ato kɛha tso lɛ teŋgbɛ kɛ aduawai akui lɛ

english: How long does it take for a newly planted cocoa tree to start giving me pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties start producing pods in about 2 to 3 years after planting, while older traditional varieties usually take 4 to 5 years before your first real harvest.
ga: Kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, kusum kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani okpaa oklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa diɛŋtsɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my maize after planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the leaves and husks turn completely brown and dry, and the kernels become hard and dry to the touch, usually around 90 to 120 days after planting.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa ni amɛgbi. ni dumɔwui lɛ mli wa ni egbi kɛji oota he. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ gbii 90 kɛyashi 120 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ.

english: Which crops grow best during the short rainy season in southern Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ be kukuoo mli yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ?

english: Fast-maturing crops like cowpeas, vegetables, and early-maturing maize varieties do best during the short rainy season because they reach harvest before the dry season sets in.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ oya tamɔ tsina ŋmei, aduawai kɛ ŋmei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli. Ejaakɛ abaakpa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ashɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants curl up and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava sheds its leaves during long dry spells to save water and protect its roots from drying out. Once the rains return, the plant will quickly grow fresh leaves and keep growing.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu shishifãi lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to survive harsh conditions, so they aggressively steal water, sunlight, and food from the soil before your crop plants can get established.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli dani onibii lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why should I space my tomato plants far apart instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ato he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ fe bɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, air movement, and soil nutrients, which keeps them healthy and prevents fungal diseases from spreading rapidly between touching leaves.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. kɔɔyɔɔ ni nyiɛɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya yɛ baai ni taa he lɛ ateŋ.

english: Why do my crops yield less food even when I plant the same amount of seeds every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ faaa eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo daa afi moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same soil year after year drains specific nutrients without giving the earth time to recover. Rotating your crops or adding compost restores soil power for bigger harvests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Oŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsake loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he lɛ baaye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Why does rainwater stay on top of my field for days instead of sinking into the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔji amli gbii babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy clay soil or hard-packed earth blocks water from draining properly, which can suffocate plant roots and cause root rot unless you form raised planting mounds or drainage ridges.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ tsiɔ nu naa koni ekaho jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Ja ooma gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ loo nu homɔ he ko.

english: What causes small holes in my cabbage leaves, and how does it reduce my income?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ kaabeji baai anɔ Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eba shika ni mináa lɛ shi?

english: Tiny caterpillars feed on the leaves, creating holes that weaken the plant's ability to grow properly, leading to small or damaged cabbage heads that sell for lower prices at the market.
ga: Kplukai bibii lɛ yeɔ baai lɛ, ni amɛfeɔ bu ni haaa tso lɛ ada jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa cabbage yitsei bibii loo efite ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni baa shi nɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do my harvested grains spoil so quickly when I store them after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛto beni akpa kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grains spoil rapidly if they are not dried completely under the sun before storage, as leftover moisture creates mold and attracts insects that eat away your harvest profits.
ga: Nibii ni ŋmaa fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ agbiko amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani akɛto. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni egbalaa kooloi bibii ni yeɔ sɛɛnamɔi ni onáa kɛjɛɔ okpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller and produce less every year even though I work hard on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee bibioo ni amɛmiiwo yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mitsuɔ nii waa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops take up food nutrients from the soil every time they grow. If you plant on the same land every season without adding organic manure, fertilizer, or letting the soil rest, the soil becomes exhausted and can no longer feed new plants properly.
ga: Tsei gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni amɛbaadara. Kɛji odu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he loo ohaaa sũ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akwɛ tsei heei anɔ jogbaŋŋ dɔŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and curling up even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow and curled leaves are often a sign that pests like fall armyworms are eating the leaves from the inside, or that the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen. Rain keeps plants hydrated, but plants also need protection from insects and proper soil nutrients to stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ miiye baai lɛ kɛmiijɛ mli. Aloo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nugbɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Shi tsei hu he miihia ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: How can I keep my farm safe from crop diseases before they start showing on my plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ tsei ahe helai ahe dani amɛje shishi amɛjie amɛhe kpo yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ?

english: You can prevent crop diseases by planting certified disease-free seeds, rotating different types of crops each season, clearing weed harborages, and spacing your plants so air flows easily between them to stop moisture-loving fungi from growing.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsi tsei ahe helai anaa kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni helai bɛ mli ni awo he odase akɛ ooodu lɛ nɔ. Tsɔmɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi. yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ Tsumɔ he ni jwɛi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Ni ŋmɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ amɛteŋ mlɛo. Koni ŋmeii ni sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ akpa dalɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I squeeze as many seeds as possible close together so I get more crops from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo shwieɔ shi bɔ ni manyɛ koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition results in weak, thin plants with very tiny harvests instead of strong plants with full yields.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni adu lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ baa. Mohu ɔ, e ji tso nɛ ngɛ he wami nɛ e woɔ yiblii saminya.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and stays around the roots in heavy soil, causing fungal diseases to grow. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii mli, ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli ni eye ebua ni ewaje shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why did many of the maize seeds I buried in the ground fail to grow into young plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mifu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ edako ni etsɔko dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are buried too deep into the dirt, if the soil dries out completely, or if insects and birds eat the seeds before they sprout. Planting seeds at a moderate depth in moist, well-prepared soil ensures they sprout reliably.
ga: Dumɔwui ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii kɛ okpoi ye dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ, ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Covering the soil around the roots with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool and moist, helping flowers stay on the plant.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Jwɛi ni egbi (mulching) ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and burn during the dry sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides living shade umbrellas that protect seedlings until they are strong enough for full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni haa wala hiɔ shi ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: How do weeds growing near my crops slow down the growth of my farm crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ haaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ fioo?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm because their roots steal water and nutrients from the soil, and their tall leaves block sunlight from reaching your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the resources they need.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Ni amɛbaai kakadaji lɛ tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa koni ekashɛ onibii ahe. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná nibii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why is my harvested grain getting spoiled by small insects while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii fiteɔ miŋmaa ni mikpaa lɛ be mli ni mikɛtoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils attack stored grain if the grain was not dried completely in the sun before storage, or if the storage container has holes. Thoroughly drying your grain until it is hard and storing it in clean, airtight bags prevents insects from surviving and multiplying.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii tutuaa dumɔwui ni ato lɛ. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa yɛ hulu lɛ mli dani akɛto, Aloo kɛji akɛ tsɛnsi lɛ mli bu yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ni ooogbi kɛyashi ebaawa ni okɛto kotoku ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ baatsi kooloi bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkajo foi ni amɛshwere.

english: Look closely at the small buds along the stem where leaves used to grow; these buds must point upwards toward the sky. Planting stems upside down forces the new shoots to grow downward first, causing weak plants and low tuber yields.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi he ni baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ be ko ni eho lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ yitso lɛ hiɛ shi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ shi klɛŋklɛŋ. Ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ yibii ni baa shi.

english: Why does planting my crops too close together make them tall and thin with very small harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ni miduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ kukuji ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ amɛwoɔ lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to get the sunlight and soil food it needs to grow strong and yield big fruits or tubers.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ ená hulu la kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii loo bulbs wuji.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizers like Urea or well-decomposed animal manure helps restore green color and leaf strength.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmeii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts in my farm make the soil richer for next season's crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Legume crops like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the crop is harvested and its roots rot in the soil, that stored food stays in the ground to nourish the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛshishifãi lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Niyenii ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from drying out the ground too quickly. It keeps the roots cool, holds water in the soil longer, and breaks down over time to feed the soil naturally.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaatsi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Haa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. ni efiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Young cocoa trees have very soft, sensitive leaves that easily burn under direct hot sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby creates a protective umbrella that shields young cocoa plants until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ waa ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ cacao tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: What causes small ragged holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding in the middle shoot?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli Ehiɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the tender leaves inside the funnel of the plant. Checking fields early and applying appropriate recommended treatments directly into the plant funnel helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni sa ni atsɔɔ akɛ aduɔ lɛ baatsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ dumɔwui akui lɛ anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ he lɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow back much faster after rainfall than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that have adapted to survive harsh conditions and absorb soil water and food much faster than farm crops. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing light, water, and soil nutrients from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli, ni amɛheɔ sũ mli nu kɛ niyenii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Ni oootsi ohe mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why is it risky to plant my crop seeds right after the very first rainy day of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain is often followed by several hot, dry weeks before the main rainy season settles in. If your seeds sprout during that single rain, the young shoots will dry up and die when the hot weather returns.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ otsii babaoo ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baashɛ. Kɛji odumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nakai nugbɔshiimɔ kome lɛ mli lɛ, Young shoots lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures become too hot or when the soil swings from very dry to sudden heavy watering. Keeping soil moisture steady and protecting plants from direct intense heat helps flowers stay on and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ nu babaoo nɔ kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛtee nu babaoo nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ tsei ahebuu kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up when I plant them in an open field without tall trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Without shade crops like plantains or taller canopy trees to protect them, the harsh sun burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil moisture they need to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋwɛi ŋwɛi ni buɔ amɛhe lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kɛha wala lɛ mli egbiɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but leave me with very small tubers at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi kɛ́ akpa lɛ, eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or grows in extremely rich soil, it spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in the roots to form large tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmei yɔɔ nɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛma baai kɛ tsei ashishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔ sisije ɔmɛ a mi konɛ e pee bulb nguahi.

english: What is eating holes in the central leaves of my young maize plants and leaving tiny waste powders inside?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni eshiɔ powda bibii bibii yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing tip of maize plants to feed. Early detection and applying targeted control measures are necessary to protect your harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ ashishi koni amɛye nii lɛ. Nibii ni anaa mra Ni gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ nii lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he miihia waa koni akɛbu okpamɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do the bottom ends of my tomato fruits turn dark and soft before they even turn ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato aduawai shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant lacks calcium or experiences irregular watering during fruit formation, preventing key nutrients from reaching the bottom of the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ calcium loo amɛnáa nu ni ejaaa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, niyenii titri ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shɛɛɛ aduawai lɛ ashishi.

english: How does covering the bare soil around my crops with dried leaves or straw help my crops survive dry periods?
ga: Mulching bare soil around Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ bei amli?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material (mulching) blocks direct sunlight from evaporating water from the soil, keeps plant roots cool, and gradually breaks down into natural soil nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni fiofio lɛ efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my land make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts absorb nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots with the help of beneficial soil bacteria, leaving natural nitrogen fertilizer in the soil for future heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ shwieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli kɛtsɔ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ aye abuamɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines on wooden poles instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?
