english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves upward to catch maximum sunlight needed for tuber growth while keeping the leaves off damp ground, which prevents soil-borne fungal diseases from spreading to the plant.
ga: Staking sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ ni he hiaa kɛha tuber lɛ dalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tsei amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over during strong winds right when they start producing bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli kɛji amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily when too many suckers grow from one main plant, competing for root space, or when underground pests like nematodes weaken the root anchor system.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ kɛjɛ tso titri kome mli. Shishijee he ni shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he akaŋ Aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ nematodes lɛ, haa shishifãi lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do my maize seeds rot in the ground when I plant them immediately after the very first small rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain often warms the soil without providing deep, lasting moisture; if a dry spell follows immediately, the seeds absorb a little water to sprout but die from dehydration before reaching the surface.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ ni hiɔ shi daa haaa. Kɛji hulutsoo be nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Dumɔwui lɛ baaŋɔ nu fioo koni amɛkwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagboi yɛ nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ hewɔ dani amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I avoid planting garden eggs on the exact same plot of land where I harvested tomatoes last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmeii adumɔ he yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ he ni mifo mi-tomato lɛ yɛ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Tomatoes and garden eggs belong to the same plant family and share similar soil pests and diseases. Planting them back-to-back on the same land allows pests to build up in the soil and attack the new crop.
ga: Tomato kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii yɛ tsei akuu kome mli, ni amɛyɛ sũ mli ŋmeii kɛ helai ni tamɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct heat and sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains around them to block the intense midday sun, their delicate leaves dry out and burn before their roots can establish deep in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo lɛ bɛ he fɛɛ he ni baatsi hulutsoo be lɛ naa lɛ Amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa dani amɛshishifãi lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Yellowing leaves, especially starting from the bottom of the plant, usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant produce chlorophyll and turn green and healthy again.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ titri lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛfee klorofil ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the small buds on the stem pointing upwards toward the sky. If planted upside down, the stems struggle to grow upward, resulting in weak plants and lower tuber yields.
ga: Esa akɛ adu cassava tsei ni afo lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ tso ko ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi nɔ Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baaná naagba yɛ edalɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tuber yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: What is eating small holes into my young corn leaves and hiding inside the central funnel?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Botemɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ni okɛ ohe awo teŋgbɛ funnel lɛ mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves during the heat of the day to feed on soft plant tissue, which can severely reduce your harvest if left untreated.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛ teeɔ baai lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be mli koni amɛ ye tso lɛ fãji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ aba shi waa kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I avoid burning cleared weeds on my field before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ jwɛi ni ajie yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ashãa dani madu nii lɛ he?

english: Burning cleared weeds destroys valuable organic matter, kills beneficial soil organisms, and leaves the soil vulnerable to erosion. Allowing cleared weeds to decay naturally adds rich organic nutrients back into your farmland.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajie lɛ ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Ekpãtãa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahiɛ. ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ oshara mli akɛ ebaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ oha jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop in the afternoon heat even when the ground is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can draw it up from the soil. This temporary wilting is a natural protective behavior to conserve moisture, and the plant usually recovers by evening as temperatures cool.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli nɛɛ ji adebɔɔ mli su ko ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Ni bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ he baajɔ amɛ gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do you recommend planting cowpeas or beans on the land where I just harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmãa yɛ nɔ kɛkɛ nɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize crops use up a lot of nitrogen from the soil. Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and fix it back into the ground, naturally restoring soil fertility for your next crop without expensive fertilizers.
ga: Abɛi kɛ nitrogen babaoo ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa he ehiaaa.

english: Yam vines need vertical support to spread their leaves high up toward sunlight. Better leaf exposure to sunlight helps the plant make food efficiently, which directly leads to bigger and healthier yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia yelikɛbuamɔ ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaa lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi kɛya hulu lɛ he. Kɛ́ baai lɛ shɛ hulu la he jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ kɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ shishi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are ready to harvest from under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-peanuts lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the main leaves turn yellow and dry up. You can test by pulling up one plant; if the inner skin of the harvested shell has turned a dark brownish-black color instead of white, they are mature.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai titrii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ tso kome ni ooogbala kɛya ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei ni akpa lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ batsɔ ŋmei-diŋ yɛ ŋmei najiaŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ahoo amɛ.

english: When maize plants are crowded, they compete fiercely with each other for light, soil nutrients, and water. This competition results in tall, thin, weak stalks that produce very small or empty ears of corn.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ baa, ni no haa ŋmãa toi bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build healthy green leaves. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure will help the maize regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the underside of the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects. Sprinkling soapy water or applying suitable organic or chemical pesticides early helps protect the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛ saamɔ baashwie nɔ loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofa ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli mra Ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat or dry soil, which prevents proper pollination inside the flower. Keeping the soil evenly moist with regular watering and mulching helps the plant hold onto its flowers and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ naa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight and lose moisture faster than their small roots can absorb it. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides living shade umbrellas that protect them during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi, ni amɛmli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe shishifãi bibii lɛ. Abaanyɛ aŋɔ awo mli. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ tsei nɛɛ ahe yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller and weaker when I plant seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing roots and leaves compete fiercely for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Following recommended plant spacing ensures each crop gets enough space and food to produce a big harvest.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ sɛɛnyiɛmɔ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekpa nii babaoo.

english: The first rain of the year is often followed by a long dry spell, which causes newly sprouted seeds to dry up and die in the hot soil. Waiting until the rainy season fully settles ensures consistent moisture so your seeds can survive and grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ sũ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaho lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba be fɛɛ be bɔni afee ni odumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ahi shi ni amɛdara.

english: Cassava roots rot when planted in flat or heavy soil that holds excess rainwater, suffocating the roots and attracting fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Kasava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests when I plant maize in the exact same field every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce low yields even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa yibiiwoo aba miŋmɔshi nibii amli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight intended for your crops. Clearing weeds early in the season ensures your crops receive all the nutrients from the fertilizer.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Kɛ́ agbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why do crops grown inside a greenhouse or net house look healthier than crops in my open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ greenhouse loo trellis mli lɛ feɔ fɛo fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu yɛ miŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Greenhouses create a physical barrier that keeps out harmful insect pests and protects crops from harsh weather and excessive heat. This reduced stress allows crops to grow faster, suffer fewer diseases, and produce cleaner fruit than open-field crops.
ga: Greenhouses lɛ feɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ko ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ boteɔ mli. ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he. Nɛkɛ haomɔ ni baa shi nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya. hela bɛ emli ni ewoɔ yibii ni he tse fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth, or that water is sitting around the roots for too long. Adding animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps bring back the healthy green color and supports stem growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Aloo nu ko ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ ŋmei lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ adara.

english: My farm used to produce big harvests, but now my crops stay small even when I plant on time. What is happening to my land?
ga: Kulɛ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ nibii babaoo. Shi amrɔ nɛɛ, miŋmɔshi nii lɛ faaa lolo eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ be naa moŋ. Mɛni ba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Farming the same piece of land year after year removes essential nutrients from the soil, making it weak. You can heal the land by resting it, rotating your crops with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts, and adding organic compost to restore soil nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kome nɔ okwaayeli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ha egbɔjɔ Obaanyɛ obu oshikpɔŋkuku lɛ he kɛtsɔ hejɔɔmɔ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Ni okɛ organic compost afata he koni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Burning destroys rich organic matter and kills beneficial insects and micro-organisms in the soil. Letting cleared weeds rot creates natural manure (mulch), which cools the soil, retains rainwater, and feeds your future crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo lɛ, ni egbeɔ kooloi kɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ jwɛi lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa. (Mulch) Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi, ni ehaa onibii ni obaadu wɔsɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Cassava drops its leaves to save water when the rain stops. The plant enters a resting state so it does not dry out, keeping its energy stored safely in the roots underground until the next rainy season begins.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi koni akɛbu nu he kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa. Tso lɛ boteɔ shihilɛ ni mli wa mli koni ekagbi. Ha hewalɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli kɛyashi nugbɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baaje shishi.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin without producing fruit when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, space, and food. They stretch upward rapidly to get sun instead of developing thick stems and heavy fruits.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, ŋwɛi kɛ niyenii he akaŋ. Amɛshwereɔ oya koni amɛmɔ hulu lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaana tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni midu jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native plants that have adapted to survive tough conditions. They have deep root systems that quickly grab water and food from the soil before your domesticated crop seeds can fully establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ agbala nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya dani dumɔwui ni yɔɔ oshia lɛ mli lɛ anyɛ ama shi kwraa.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress from high heat, lack of soil moisture, or a missing nutrient like potassium. It can also happen if beneficial insects like bees are not visiting to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ potassium ni bɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔii amli ŋmeii.

english: Why do seeds saved from my last maize harvest produce smaller cobs when I plant them again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmeii bibii beni midu amɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Many modern seed varieties (hybrids) are bred to give their highest yield only in the first generation. Planting seeds saved from that harvest causes the plant to lose its hybrid strength, resulting in smaller cobs and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui srɔtoi babaoo (hybrid) koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ akafee hybrid hewalɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ bibii, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus, or severe stress from heat and irregular watering. Protecting young plants with nets or using organic neem sprays can reduce insect attacks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo haomɔ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa mli baa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋshɔŋlooi bu tsei bibii ahe loo akɛ organic neem spray tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha kooloi ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need plantain shade, but mature cocoa trees need more sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ taoɔ hulutsoo lɛ? Shi kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have soft leaves that burn easily in strong sunlight, so broad-leafed plantains provide necessary shelter and humidity. As cocoa trees grow older, they need direct sunlight to produce plenty of flowers and cocoa pods.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, plantain ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ haa wɔɔhe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa. Kɛji kookoo tso lɛ eda lɛ Amɛmiitao hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ kookoo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their leaves during dry spells to save water and protect themselves from dying. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ ŋmeii heei ni ebaada bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants curl up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl inward during peak sun hours to reduce the surface area exposed to heat, which helps the plant trap internal moisture and prevent water loss.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulutsoo lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ emli, ni ehaa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that do not go deep into the earth. When heavy fruit bunches develop, the plant becomes top-heavy and easy for strong winds to uproot.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo akɛ tso ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ tsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ amɛshishi oya.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees drying up when planted in open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sun. They need shade crops like plantains or cassava around them to provide shade and cool moisture while their young stems and roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo yucca ni ebɔle amɛhe. koni ekɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ aba yɛ be mli ni eshishifãi bibii kɛ eshishifãi lɛ daa waa lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up and look twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfite lɛ?

english: Twisted or rolled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaf undersides, or by a virus carried into the farm by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni etsɔ loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod disease, which spreads quickly when the farm is too shady, damp, or lacks good air movement.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ shia mli, hulutsoo be tsɔ, loo kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli.

english: High temperatures and irregular watering cause stress to tomato plants, leading them to drop their blossoms to preserve energy rather than growing tomatoes.
ga: He ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ aba amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ tomato.

english: Why is it bad to plant maize on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains specific soil nutrients and allows maize-eating pests and diseases to build up in the soil season after season.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaho. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli.

english: Why do my crop leaves look pale green or yellowish even when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowish leaves often indicate that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed to produce green foliage and healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hia kɛha baai eŋɔli kɛ hewalɛ feemɔ.

english: Yam tubers rot underground when soil holds too much water without proper drainage, creating wet conditions where fungal infections thrive and destroy the tubers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni nu tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ baa ni ŋmeii baanyɛ adara ni amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and drying up in the direct sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to intense heat and light. Without shade from temporary companion plants like plantains or young shade trees, direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out their stems, causing them to wither.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ la ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo bɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni fata he be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains loo dumɔwui ahe lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha amɛshishifãi lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔtɔ

english: Excess moisture during the rainy season creates a wet environment where black pod fungus thrives. The fungus attacks the pod skin, spreading quickly and turning the whole pod black and unusable if infected pods are not removed early.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni black pod fungus lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ Ŋmei lɛ tutuaa pod lɛ hewolo lɛ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii kɛji ajieee ŋmɔtɔ ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ mra.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the soft inner leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn lɛ baai bibii lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which target the tender, sweet center leaves of young maize plants. If left untreated, they destroy the growing point of the plant, which stops it from growing healthy corn ears.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ Ebaafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ. Enɛ haaa ŋmãa toi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to stay green. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant moves its remaining nutrients to the newer top leaves, leaving the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tso lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni baaha ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ lɛ Kɛ́ nitrogen lɛ faaa Abɛi tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with thick stems but produces tiny roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eshishifãi lɛ mli tse shi shishifãi bibii yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to focus all its energy on growing leafy branches instead of storing food in the tubers. Hard, unplowed soil can also prevent tubers from expanding properly underground.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ tsei niji kɛ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuuu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ atsĩ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants keep falling off without growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from heat stress, dry soil, or a lack of key nutrients like phosphorus. When the plant feels stressed, it drops its flowers to survive rather than spending energy growing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ amɛmli lɛ hewɔ. Ebaashi fɔfɔi yɛ esɛɛ koni ehi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai

english: Having too many suckers forces them to compete with the main tree for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong shoots, ensuring the main plantain tree produces a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Nibii ni shwieɔ shi babaoo lɛ haa amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii he. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ baahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha plantain titri lɛ awo niji agboi ni tsii.

english: Why do my yam vines produce bigger tubers when I train them onto tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ naa bulbs wuji beni mitsɔseɔ amɛ yɛ tsei kakadaŋŋ anɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves off the ground into sunlight, allowing them to absorb energy efficiently. Better sunlight exposure lets the leaf canopy produce more food, which is sent down to feed and grow large underground tubers.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛheɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. Hulu la ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ afee niyenii babaoo. ni atsu amɛ kɛba shi koni amɛbaha niyenii ni amɛdu shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji

english: Why do the bottom tips of my ripening tomatoes turn black and rotten?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by calcium deficiency in the fruit, often brought on by irregular watering. When soil dries out repeatedly, the plant roots cannot absorb calcium properly to build strong fruit walls.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi shii abɔ lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi nyɛŋ aŋɔ calcium jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkɛma aduawai gbogboi ni wa.

english: Why does my rice crop grow better when planted in fields flooded with standing water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋmɔ ni nu ni damɔ shi eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Standing water suppresses weeds that would normally crowd out young rice plants. Rice has special hollow tissue in its stems that allows oxygen to travel down to its roots even when submerged in water.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ baatsi jwɛi ni bei pii lɛ ebɔleɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ahe lɛ anaa. Omɔ yɛ fã krɛdɛɛ ko ni mli ewo muji yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli kɛ́ awo lɛ nu mli po.

english: How can I cut cocoa pods off my tree without damaging the trunk or future pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafolɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni mifiteee tso lɛ shishifã lɛ loo ŋmeii ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Always place a sharp harvesting hook right under the neck of the pod stem to make a clean cut. Avoid pulling or tearing pods off by hand, as tearing damages the flower cushions on the trunk where next season's pods must grow.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ awo pod tso lɛ kuɛ shishi koni ekɛfo mli ni he tse. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ ni okɛ oniji aaagbala loo oootsi lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ atse lɛ, ebaafite fɔfɔii akutsei ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishi ni baatsɔ be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Cocoa pods change color when ripe, turning from green to bright yellow, or from red to orange-yellow. Harvesting when pods are fully yellow ensures the beans inside are fully developed for fermentation.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su be mli ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Tsakemɔ kɛjɛ eŋɔli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo kɛjɛ etsuru kɛtee ŋmɔŋ-ŋɔli Nikpamɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ kwraa lɛ haa kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwereɔ kwraa kɛha ŋmeii.

english: Why shouldn't I leave my harvested cocoa pods sitting on the ground for many days before splitting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ mi-kookoo ni mikpa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ gbii babaoo dani mijaraa mli lɛ?

english: Leaving cut pods on the humid ground invites fungal diseases and rodents to penetrate the shell. It can also cause the seeds inside to sprout or rot before you get to ferment them.
ga: Ni aaashi ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ Enɛ baaha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii abote ŋmeii lɛ amli. Ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hu akwɛ̃ loo amɛfite dani okɛwo mli.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather. Removing infected pods immediately and pruning extra branches to let sunlight in helps stop the disease from destroying your whole farm.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya, ni ofolɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi amli koni hulu la aba mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akafite oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: What causes tiny dark spots on my young cocoa stems and makes the shoots die back?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii baa? yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ ni ehaa kookoo lɛ tsei lɛ gboiɔ.

english: These spots are caused by capsids (mirids), tiny insects that suck sap from young stems and pods. Spraying approved insecticides during their peak season protects the shoots from dying back.
ga: Capsids (mirids), ni ji kooloi bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baa. ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ fa babaoo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagboi.

english: Why do I need to trim off the extra shoots growing out of my cocoa tree trunks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These extra shoots, called chupons, waste the tree's energy and food. Removing them allows the tree to send all its strength into growing heavy, healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons nɛɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa kookoo ŋmeii ni tsii ni mli wa ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Should I cut down all large trees around my farm or keep some above my cocoa crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei wuji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Miŋmɔ lɛ loo mikɛto mi koko tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Keeping some tall shade trees protects young cocoa from harsh sunlight and drying winds. Shade keeps the soil moist and reduces heat stress on the crops.
ga: Tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo be ha kookoo tso lɛ, ebaabu ehe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ he. Shade yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni baa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Flowers fall off when the tree is stressed by dry weather, poor soil nutrients, or lack of tiny insects that pollinate them. Proper mulching and keeping shade helps the tree hold its flowers until they turn into pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ, ŋmeii ni sa kɛ hulutsoo baanyɛ aye abua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛyashi ebaafee ŋmeii.

english: Why do weeds hurt my cocoa crop yields even when the trees are already tall and mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miifite mi-kookoo lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛdara moŋ?

english: Weeds steal water and nutrients from the soil that your cocoa roots need. They also trap moisture around the base of the trunk, creating an environment where fungal diseases can easily thrive.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa o-cocoa shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ hu yɛ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ko baa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ oya.

english: How do I know if my cocoa farm needs fertilizer to produce more pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: If your cocoa leaves turn pale yellow, growth slows down, or pod yields decrease despite good rains, the soil is low on nutrients. Applying cocoa-recommended fertilizer at the start of the rainy season restores soil strength.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ, amɛdaraa blɛoo loo pod ni amɛfeɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ Etsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops produce less yield when I plant on the exact same plot of land year after year without resting the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ mihe lɛ?

english: Soil gets tired and drained of nutrients when cropped continuously. Giving land a fallow break or adding organic compost restores essential food in the soil so future crops can grow strong again.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔ̃ɔ ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ ashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ waa ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my maize seeds when the rainy season in Ghana starts late?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ Ghana sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the soil receives steady rainfall for a few days to ensure deep soil moisture, rather than planting right after the first light drizzle which can dry up and ruin the seeds.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be gbii fioo komɛi koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni mli kwɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo lɛ. Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ, ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛfite.

english: Why are the leaves on my vegetable plants turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for help indicating that the soil lacks nitrogen, or that too much water around the roots is preventing the plant from taking in food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji yelikɛbuamɔ he bolɔmɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. loo nu ni yɔɔ he fɛɛ he lɛ Shishifãi babaoo haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye nii.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds while my cassava crops are still young and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ be mli ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ darako ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal vital sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing them early ensures your cassava gets all the resources it needs to form thick tubers.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa. Ehe saamɔ mra Enɛ baaha o-cassava lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni mli tse.

english: Why do extension officers advise planting plantains alongside young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nitsumɔhe lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense tropical sun. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that create temporary natural shade, protecting the young cocoa until it is mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo be kukuoo ko baa. Buu kookoo bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: What causes small ragged holes in my young corn leaves and how does it affect my harvest?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ anɔ Ni te enaa mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Those holes are caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm feeding on the leaf heart. If untreated, they damage the growing point of the plant, reducing the size and number of corn ears produced.
ga: Nɛkɛ buji nɛɛ ji nɔ ni kooloi tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ baai tsuii lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ Ebaafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmãa toi ni ajieɔ lɛ dalɛ kɛ amɛyibɔ ​​ba shi.

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole causes plants to crowd and fight each other for sunlight and soil nutrients, resulting in tall, thin stalks with very small ears.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ekome ni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni toi bibii waa yɔɔ mli.

english: Why should I alternate planting maize with beans or cowpeas on my farm from season to season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsake be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas naturally pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, which naturally fertilizes the soil for the next maize crop and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Legumes, tamɔ cowpeas, yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni efo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe sɛɛkuu lɛ mli

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground when water collects on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Standing water starves roots of oxygen, causing them to drown and rot from soil fungi.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: Is it better to use seeds saved from my previous harvest or buy certified hybrid seeds from an agro-dealer?
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ baatsu nii loo ohe dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ.

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to resist local diseases and yield higher harvests, whereas saved seeds gradually lose their vigor and produce smaller yields over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baafite fiofio Hewalɛ ni ebaawo yibii fioo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How close together can I plant my maize so I can fit more on my small piece of land?
ga: Te manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tɛŋŋ koni ekɛwo he bibioo ko mli? Mihe babaoo?

english: If you plant maize too close together, the plants compete for sunlight, water, and soil food, which makes the stalks grow tall and weak and produces very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ. ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why do some of my crops grow better when I plant them together with other crops instead of alone on the plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ tsei krokomɛi du amɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mikome too mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mixing certain crops allows them to help each other; for example, one crop can shade the soil to keep it moist while the other protects against pests or feeds nutrients back into the dirt.
ga: Kɛ́ amɛfutu ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa amɛhe. Ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kome baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. yɛ be mli ni ekroko lɛ buɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe loo ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry weather to reduce water loss, entering a resting state that keeps its underground roots alive until the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni egbiɔ lɛ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. ni eboteɔ shihilɛ ni bɛ shihilɛ mli ni baaha shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato plants keep drooping and wilting even though I give them plenty of water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miigboi ni amɛmiigboi eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu babaoo daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much water drowns the roots by filling all the air pockets in the soil, causing root rot which actually stops the plant from taking up water.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni akɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ, ni no haaa tso lɛ aŋɔ nu.

english: Leaf curling happens when tiny sucking insects like thrips attack the plant or pass on a virus, which disrupts how the leaves grow and feed the plant.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ thrips, tutua tsei loo amɛgbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amɛshwã. Enɛ tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ kɛ tsei lɛ aniyenii naa.

english: Why is it good for me to plant cowpeas or beans on my land right after harvesting my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Corn takes a lot of food out of the soil, but beans put essential plant food called nitrogen back into the dirt, restoring soil strength for the next planting season.
ga: Abele jieɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Mohu ɔ, ngmɔ ngɔɔ tso niye ní nɛ he hia nɛ a tsɛɛ ke nitrogen ɔ kɛ woɔ zugba a mi ekohu. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛhaa shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn pale green or yellow when I grow them on the same small plot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tseee beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop on the same spot repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year, starving the new plants and turning their leaves yellow.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Ehaa tsei heei yeɔ hɔmɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does my okro crop have plenty of big leaves but very few flowers and pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tso lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Using too much chemical fertilizer high in nitrogen encourages the plant to spend all its energy growing green leaves instead of making flowers and fruits.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ tsei ahe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai najiaŋ

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on to give me big tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni ekɛkwɔ koni ekɛha ŋmeii wuji lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to catch direct sunlight, which gives the plant the energy it needs to make food and grow large tubers underground.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni hulu la lɛ aba nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii ni ekɛdu ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How does spreading dry grass around my vegetable roots actually help them grow better?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass acts like an umbrella that keeps the soil cool, traps rainwater longer so you water less, and blocks weeds from stealing your crop's food.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ bɔni afee ni okɛ nu lɛ akawo mli fioo. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekaju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: How can I keep tiny insects like weevils from eating my harvested corn while it sits in the storage room?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkaye mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ be mli ni eta mi-nitoohe lɛ?

english: Weevils thrive when corn is stored while still damp or in moist rooms. Drying your corn thoroughly in the sun until the grains are hard, and storing them in airtight storage bags (like PICS bags), keeps insects out without needing harmful chemicals.
ga: Weevils lɛ yaa hiɛ waa kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa to be mli ni edɔ lolo loo yɛ tsu ko ni mli edɔ mli. Okɛ ŋmãa lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni okɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku) mli koni ebu he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe ni akɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara tsuuu nii.

english: How do I know if my harvested corn is dry enough to safely put into storage bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mawo baagi mli shweshweeshwe?

english: A simple trick is to bite a grain or press your thumbnail into it; if it leaves a mark or feels soft, it is still wet and will spoil in bags. Dry corn should feel as hard as stone and make a sharp cracking sound when crushed.
ga: Lakamɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo Eji ni okɛ ohe awo ŋmaa lɛ mli loo onyɛ o-thumbnail lɛ nɔ. Kɛji eshi okadii loo enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo ni ebaanyɛ egbo yɛ kotoku lɛ mli. Esa akɛ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ anu he akɛ ewa tamɔ tɛ ni efee gbee ni tswaa kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen or the soil is too soaked with rain water. Adding a bit of urea fertilizer or compost helps the leaves turn deep green so the plant can grow healthy ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etsɔ nugbɔ nu. Kɛ́ akɛ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii fioo fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ koni ŋmãa tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but producing tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or excessive early rain, it spends all its energy growing leaves and stems instead of roots. Reducing rich fertilizer allows the plant to send its nutrients down to build large cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo loo nugbɔ babaoo nɔ mra Ebaahe be dani ebaa kɛ ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shishifãi lɛ najiaŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ atsu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛba shi koni amɛfee ŋmei shishifãi wuji.

english: Why do my groundnut plants bend their flowers down and push them into the dirt after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: That is how groundnuts naturally grow. After the flower opens, the stem grows downward and buries itself in the soil so the nut can safely grow hidden underground away from heat and animals.
ga: Nakai ji bɔ ni ŋmeii daa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Beni fɔfɔi lɛ efɔ sɛɛ lɛ Tso lɛ daa kɛyaa shishi ni efuɔ ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛteeɔ amɛhiɛ amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni hulutsoo kɛ kooloi bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my corn seeds very close together to get more crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and plant food. This leaves you with thin, weak stalks and small or empty cobs, whereas proper spacing yields bigger, healthier corn.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ tsei aniyenii ahe akaŋshii mli. Enɛ baaha oná tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tsei bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaha ŋmãa agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba.

english: Why do my crops grow so strong in the first year after clearing bush land, but produce less in the years that follow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwere waa nɛkɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi ni mijie miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ? Shi ani ebaawo yibii fioo yɛ afii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli?

english: Freshly cleared land contains rich plant food built up over many years. Once you start farming, crops use up these nutrients quickly, so you need to add manure, compost, or fertilizer to restore the soil for the next season.
ga: Niyenii nibii babaoo ni abua naa yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ hee ni ajie lɛ nɔ. Kɛ oje okwaayeli shishi lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ nɛkɛ niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ oya. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: What makes the flowers on my tomato plants fall off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or sudden heavy rains. Keeping soil moist with mulch around the base of the plant helps protect the flowers so tomatoes can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ ye tso lɛ nɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni oookɛwo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Shishitoo lɛ buɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni tomatoi lɛ anyɛ afee.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn black and rot while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads in cold, damp, and shady environments. Trimming extra shade tree branches to let sunlight reach the cocoa trees helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni mli ejɔ, fɔ́, shade kɛbaa. Kɛ́ afolɔ hulutsoo be kroko mli koni hulu la ashɛ kookoo tso lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kookoo tso lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli egbi ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is causing tiny holes and chewed edges on the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? kɛ ŋmeii ni atsɔ mli yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the center funnel of the plant. Checking the central funnel early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract can stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baanyɛ akpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my plantain plants growing so slowly and taking too long to produce fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ miida blɛoo waa ni ekɛ be babaoo tsuɔ nii dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Plantains need nutrient-rich soil, reliable moisture, and weed control to grow quickly. Poor soil fertility, drought, or heavy weed competition can severely delay their development and fruiting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni niyenii kpakpai babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia plantains. hulutsoo ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛ jwɛi ni akudɔɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya Shikpɔŋ ni ehiii, hɔmɔ, loo jwɛi akaŋshii ni naa wa baanyɛ aha jwɛi lɛ ashweremɔ kɛ yibiiwoo lɛ asɛɛ afo waa.

english: How long does it normally take for a new plantain plant to give me harvestable fruit?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani dumɔwu hee ko woɔ yibii ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: In Ghana, a healthy plantain sucker typically takes between 12 to 15 months from planting to yield a mature bunch ready for harvest, depending on rainfall and soil care.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, bei pii lɛ, sucker dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ dani amɛshɛɔ kuu ni eda ni esa kɛha kpamɔ lɛ he. Edamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain bunches come out small and light even after the plant stays in the soil for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe waaa nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Small bunches occur when the soil lacks essential nutrients or when too many shoots are growing from the same stem, forcing the mother plant to share its food with too many suckers.
ga: Kpoji bibii baa kɛji niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo ni jɛ tso kome mli lɛ fa babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tso nyɛ lɛ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ aja niyenii babaoo tsɔ.

english: What causes my plantain leaves to turn yellow and dry up before the crop finishes growing?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi plantain baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani tso lɛ eda?

english: Yellowing leaves often indicate a shortage of plant nutrients like nitrogen, insufficient water during dry spells, or root damage caused by pests like nematodes and stem borers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ mli niyenii tamɔ nitrogen bɛ, ni nu hu faaa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. loo shishifãi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ nematodes kɛ stem borers lɛ kɛbaa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain stems break or fall over easily when wind blows or bunches start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ fãa loo amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa loo jwɛi lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that can be destroyed by underground pests or weakened by soft soil. Using wooden or bamboo props to support heavy bunches prevents the plants from falling over.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi baanyɛ afite loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ baanyɛ aha egbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni akɛfiɔ ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: How can I select the right plantain suckers so my farm doesn't fail?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni sa koni miŋmɔ lɛ akafite?

english: Choose healthy 'maiden suckers' that have narrow, spear-shaped leaves and strong roots. Avoid taking suckers from diseased mother plants or picking shoots with broad, floppy leaves.
ga: Halamɔ ‘bamboo tsei’ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ lance kɛ shishifãi ni wa. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ashishifãi ni ooonu loo tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe.

english: How many shoots or suckers should I leave around one plantain plant?
ga: Esa akɛ mashi ŋmeii loo ŋmeii enyiɛ mabɔle dumɔwu kome he?

english: It is best to leave only 2 or 3 healthy suckers of different ages around the main plant. Pruning excess suckers ensures the main plant gets enough food to produce big bunches.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi tsei 2 loo 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eye afii srɔtoi yɛ tso titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo tsei niji wuji.

english: How far apart should I plant my plantain suckers to get the best results?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-banana tsei lɛ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ he tɛŋŋ koni nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ aba?

english: Planting plantains about 3 meters apart gives each plant enough space, sunlight, and soil nutrients to mature properly without competing with neighboring plants.
ga: Plantains lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3 lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akaŋ akaŋ.

english: How can I prepare my plantain suckers before planting to prevent pest trouble?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa plantain tsei lɛ ahe dani madu koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafee bo?

english: You can trim off the old roots and dark spots from the corm, then dip the corm in clean water or treat it with recommended organic ash or botanical extracts to kill hidden pests before planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofo shishifãi momoi kɛ hei ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ kɛjɛ rhizomes lɛ amli. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ yitso lɛ awo nu ni mli tse mli. Aloo okɛ organic ashwiili loo tsofai ni ajieɔ yi akɛ ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ atsu nii ni okɛgbe kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ dani okɛdu.

english: Can I plant other crops like maize or vegetables together with my plantains?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi-plantains lɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai?

english: Yes, you can intercrop young plantains with leguminous crops or maize during their first few months. This protects the soil and provides extra food while the plantains are still small.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa adu dumɔwui bibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli. Enɛ baabu shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni ebaaha niyenii krokomɛi aba be mli ni plantains lɛ ji bibii lolo lɛ.

english: How long can I safely store my harvested mangoes before they start to spoil?
ga: Be enyiɛ manyɛ makɛ mi-mango ni mikpa lɛ ato shweshweeshwe dani amɛje shishi amɛfite?

english: Fresh, unpeeled mangoes usually last about one to two weeks at room temperature. If you want them to last for several months, you must process them by solar drying, freezing, or preserving them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango hee ni ajieee lɛ hiɔ shi otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ yɛ shĩa mli dɔlɛ mli. Kɛji oosumɔ lɛ, too nyɔji babaoo. Ehe miihia ni otsu he nii kɛtsɔ hulutsoo be mli ni oooha egbi, ni ooofee ais loo okɛto he lɛ nɔ.

english: If I peel my mangoes before storing them, will they last longer or spoil faster?
ga: Kɛ́ otsi mango ko he dani okɛto lɛ, ani ebaahi shi be kakadaŋŋ loo ebaagbo oya?

english: Peeling mangoes removes their natural protective skin, which causes them to lose moisture and spoil within a day or two unless they are dried, frozen, or cooked immediately.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie mango lɛ, ejieɔ ehewolo ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ. Enɛ baaha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaafite yɛ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ mli. ja egbi, ewo fɛ̃i mli, loo ehoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: What is the best simple way to make my excess fruit harvest last for up to four months?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ maha mi yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nyɔji ejwɛ?

english: Solar drying is one of the most effective methods in Ghana. Slicing and drying fruit removes water so bacteria and mold cannot grow, keeping the fruit good for four to six months.
ga: Hulu ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ ji gbɛi ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana lɛ ateŋ ekome. Kɛ́ afo aduawai lɛ ni agbi lɛ, ejieɔ nu lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli. Muawai kɛ ŋmeii edaaa. Enɛ haa yibii lɛ hiɔ shi nyɔji ejwɛ kɛyashi enumɔ.

english: Why do my mangoes get soft and rot when I keep them tightly sealed in a box for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mangoi lɛ yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛgboi lɛ? Beni atswa adeka lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ gbii 2-3?

english: Harvested fruits continue to breathe after picking. When trapped in an airtight container, heat and moisture build up quickly, creating the perfect environment for rot and mold.
ga: Yibii ni akpa lɛ yaa nɔ emuɔ beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛwo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli lɛ, dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i buaa ehe naa oya. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baa.

english: How long should I leave my harvested fruit in a treatment liquid to make sure it lasts during storage?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mashi mi-fruit ni mikpa lɛ yɛ nɔ ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli koni ehi shi yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Treatment dips usually only require a few minutes to kill surface germs; leaving fruits in liquid for days will break down the skin and cause them to rot faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ minitii fioo pɛ dani tsofa lɛ gbeɔ helai ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi aduawai lɛ yɛ nu mli gbii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha ehewolo lɛ akumɔ ni egbo oya.

english: How do I know when it is time to replace the preservative treatment in my crop storage area?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ matsake nɔ ni akɛbuɔ nii ahe yɛ he ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii toɔ lɛ?

english: You should refresh or replace storage treatments when the original fresh smell disappears, when you notice moisture buildup, or according to the manufacturer's recommended timeline.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ehe awo mli loo otsake gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛtoɔ lɛ mli beni shishijee ŋmɔlɔ hee lɛ laajeɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ona akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ebɔle ehe loo taakɛ be ni mɔ ni fee lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my stored fruits lose their natural sweet smell after sitting in storage for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi aduawai ni mikɛto lɛ efo amɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ mli beni mikɛto otsii fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: As harvested crops age, their natural aroma oils evaporate and moisture drops, which reduces their fresh scent and signals that the fruit is losing its quality.
ga: Beni tsei ni akpa lɛ daraa lɛ, Adebɔɔ mli mu ni ŋɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa ŋmɔlɔ hee lɛ baa shi, ni eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ aduawai lɛ ehiii dɔŋŋ.

english: Can I put freshly picked mangoes into the same container with older mangoes that have been stored for weeks?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ mango ni ajie ehee lɛ afata he. Ani manyɛ mikɛwo tsɛnsi kome mli kɛ mango ni ehi shi otsii babaoo lɛ?

english: It is best to keep them separate because older fruits release ripening gases that make fresh fruits spoil faster, and any rot on the old fruit can easily spread.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ amɛ ato he kroko ejaakɛ aduawai momoi jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa aduawai heei fiteɔ oya lɛ kpo. Ni aduawai momo ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo.

english: Why do my fruits spoil faster if they get bruised or scratched during harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ loo atswa lɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: A scratch or bruise breaks the crop's protective outer skin, creating an open doorway for air, bacteria, and fungal spores to enter and decay the fruit from the inside.
ga: Hewolo nɔ fã ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ mli fã ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ fãa. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ, muawai, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ boteɔ mli ni ehaa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ mli.

english: Do I need to thoroughly clean my storage room before putting in a newly harvested batch of crops?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni matsumɔ he ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani mikɛ ŋmaa hee awo mli?

english: Yes, always clean and dry the storage area because leftover fungal spores, dust, and pests from previous crops will immediately attack your fresh harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ha he ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ he atse ni egbi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii, sũ, kɛ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni odu tsutsu lɛ amli lɛ baatutua onibii heei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains creates a protective umbrella that keeps the soil cool and moist for young cocoa to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shade ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa koni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plant leaves need to stay dark green and build stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni esa akɛ tso baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni efee ŋmeii.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water settles in the soil without draining, the roots drown and soil microorganisms attack the tubers, causing them to rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu gbee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni nu hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni nibii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baatutua ŋmeii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during strong winds when they start bearing heavy fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli beni ebɔi yibii ni tsii womɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can easily get weakened by microscopic root pests called nematodes or waterlogged soil, leaving the heavy plant without strong anchor roots.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni shishifãi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ oya. Enɛ haa tsei ni tsii ni shishifãi ni wa bɛ amɛhe lɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when there is sudden drought stress, because the plant sheds flowers to conserve water and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ ba. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the juices from fresh leaves, or by a virus transmitted into the plant by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai heei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ nɔ

english: Why am I finding small holes in my maize leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside the center shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hatches from eggs laid on the plant and feeds on the soft, young leaves developing inside the shoot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the air so their leaves can trap direct sunlight, which gives the plant the energy it needs to produce large tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni awó sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ashɛ hulu la lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings collapse at the soil surface and die right after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This is called 'damping-off,' a fungal disease caused by keeping seedling beds too wet and overcrowded, which creates a damp environment where soil fungi thrive and attack soft stems.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ ‘Damp-down’, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ dumɔwui asaji ni akɛhaa tsɔ ni eyiɔ obɔ lɛ mli baa Enɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli hulutsoo baa. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ daa ni amɛtutuaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans on my field help my maize grow better in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have special microbes in their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and leave it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ nibii bibii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛshiɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants full of holes and covered in small green dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu ni muji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ehà amɛhe lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which eats maize leaves from the inside of the plant. Checking your field early and using appropriate organic or recommended sprays will protect your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mra. Ni kɛ okɛ tsofai ni sa loo ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tsofai fɔji tsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the juices from the leaves or spreading a virus. Controlling these pests early helps the plant grow healthy new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa baai heei ni mli wa.

english: This is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, usually because watering is uneven. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the tomato plant carry calcium to the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa o-tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛkɛ calcium yaa aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why should I wait for the rain before putting fertilizer on my maize farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ omɛ nugbɔ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔji amli?

english: Fertilizer needs water in the soil to dissolve so the plant roots can drink it up. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can waste it through evaporation or even burn your crop roots.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛtsɔ tsei shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi loo ni eshãa lɛ nɔ.

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which traps nitrogen from the air and puts it into the soil through their roots. This leaves natural plant food behind for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ shĩɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii yɛ sɛɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Leaving too many young shoots makes them compete with the main plant for food, sunlight, and water. Keeping only two or three healthy shoots ensures the main stem produces large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii bibii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ abɔi niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu he akaŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei bibii fioo komɛi pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ awo plantain tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Yam plants use their leaves to catch sunlight and make food for the tuber underground. Staking holds the vines up high so the leaves get maximum sunlight, resulting in bigger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛmɔ hulu la ni amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Okɛ wain tso lɛ awo ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná hulu la babaoo. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baafee wuji.

english: Why is it so important to clear weeds from my farm during the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛdu nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are weak and grow slowly if weeds steal their sunlight, water, and soil nutrients during early growth, which permanently reduces your final yield.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaadara blɛoo kɛji jwɛi ju hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛ shishijee dalɛ beaŋ. Enɛ baaha onaagbee yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi kwraa.

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during hot, dry periods to save water and protect themselves from drying out. Planting shade trees and mulching around the base keeps the soil moist and reduces leaf drop.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the base of the stem starts to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ.

english: How do I know when the rains have properly settled so I can safely plant my maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ eba shi ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ adu ŋmãa?

english: Wait until you receive two or three heavy rains that soak the soil deeply within a single week, rather than planting after the very first light shower which can leave seeds dry and scorched.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ otsi kome mli. Moŋ lɛ, dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ fioo ni nɛ lɛ sɛɛ, ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛshã.

english: Why is it bad to apply fertilizer to my crops right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli ŋmɔshi nibii dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer away from the crop's root zone into drains and streams, wasting your investment before the plants have a chance to absorb the nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli kɛyaa nu tsɔji kɛ faai amli. Enɛ haa shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ dani tsei lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and look sad during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ awerɛho yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants temporarily roll their leaves during peak afternoon heat to reduce moisture loss and protect themselves from sun stress, usually standing firm again by evening.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli. Koni ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni obu ohe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ he. ni bei pii lɛ edamɔ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, causing the plant to pull stored nutrients from its older, lower leaves to feed the young growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily in open sunlight; fast-growing plantain trees act as natural umbrellas that provide shade and keep the soil moist during the cocoa's early years.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni mli tse mli. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋtayaai, ni amɛhaa hulutsoo ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ kookoo lɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on instead of creeping on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeefo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to catch maximum sunlight and improves airflow around the plant, which prevents leaf diseases and helps the plant grow larger tubers.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni no tsiɔ foliary hela naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Why should I plant leguminous crops like groundnuts after harvesting maize from my plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa, tamɔ ŋmãa, beni mikpa ŋmãa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Groundnuts naturally capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, restoring soil fertility that heavy-feeding crops like maize consume.
