ga: Peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo tamɔ ŋmãa yeɔ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: What happens if I plant my pepper seeds too deep into the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu pepper dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ?

english: Seeds planted too deep run out of stored energy trying to reach the surface light, resulting in weak sprouts that die before breaking through the soil.
ga: Dumɔwu ni adu yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛto lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eshɛ la ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ gboiɔ dani amɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Will heavy rain hurt my tomato plants when they are full of blossoms?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaye mi-tomato tsei lɛ awui beni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Strong rains can knock flowers off the stem and wash away pollen, which prevents the flowers from forming into tomato fruits.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi agbee shi kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni ekɛ pollen lɛ afɔ. Enɛ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ tomato aduawai.

english: How do I know my groundnuts are ready for harvest under the ground without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi kpamɔ ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Groundnuts are typically ready when the outer leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the inside lining of a test sample pod shows dark brown spots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii feɔ klalo kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni kaa nɔkwɛmɔnɔ pod lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when they get too much direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily in high heat and full sun. They need shade crops like plantain or banana trees nearby to block harsh sunlight and keep the soil moist until the cocoa plants grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ hulu la mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo banana tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ koni amɛtsi hulu ni naa wa lɛ naa ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or that heavy rains have washed nutrients out of reach. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or farmyard manure helps restore the rich green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe ni anyɛɛɛ ashɛ he. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does my yam grow very bushy green leaves above ground but produces tiny tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii akui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi eyɛ bulbs bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Giving yam plants too much nitrogen fertilizer causes them to focus all their energy on growing tall stems and heavy leaves rather than storing food underground in the tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen wo o-sweet potato tsei lɛ amli fe nine lɛ, ehaa amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni tsii ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ niyenii ato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ oyitsoŋ lɛ

english: Cassava roots rot when water settles around them in poorly drained soil during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away so the roots can breathe and stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do fall armyworms appear suddenly and destroy my entire maize farm in just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworm lɛ ba trukaa ni efite mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fall armyworm moths lay hundreds of eggs overnight that hatch all at once into hungry caterpillars. Because they feed heavily on the central leaves of young maize plants, a large swarm can destroy a field quickly if not noticed early.
ga: Fall caterpillar moths lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ nyɔɔŋ kome mli ni baatsɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ shikome. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛyeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai babaoo. Shwɛmɔi wuji baanyɛ akpata he ko oya kɛji akɛ akadiko amɛ mra.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures get extremely hot or when water supply drops suddenly. Irregular watering and a lack of soil minerals like calcium stop the flowers from turning into fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ba shi trukaa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ minerals ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium lɛ baatsi fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkatsɔ aduawai.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn dusty and get full of holes when I keep it in my store room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli eyi kɛ sũ ni bu eyi mli obɔ beni mikɛwoɔ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Weevils and grain beetles attack maize that is put into storage with too much moisture or in a room without proper air movement. Thoroughly sun-drying grains before storing them in airtight or treated bags prevents insect infestations.
ga: Weevils kɛ grain moths tutuaa ŋmãa ni akɛtoɔ he ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. loo yɛ tsu ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli Gbimɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulu mli dani okɛwo vacuum kotokui loo kotokui ni akɛ tsofa ewo mli lɛ amli. Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ ŋmeii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ anaa.

english: Why does planting pepper in the exact same spot every year result in lower yields each season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that plant needs and allows crop-specific diseases and pests to accumulate in the soil. Rotating pepper with leguminous crops like cowpeas restores soil balance.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ tsei anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Peppers ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ cowpeas tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ekome ekoŋŋ.

english: How do weeds stop my crops from growing big even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ atsĩ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo amɛmli po lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water, space, and fertilizer away from your crops before the crop roots can absorb them. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the added nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, he ko, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni yeɔ emuu.

english: What should I do if a strange crop disease starts spreading quickly across my farm and my neighbors' farms?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji tso hela ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ba? Mijeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ kɛ mikutsoŋbii lɛ aŋmɔji amli?

english: When a fast-spreading disease strikes, isolate or destroy heavily infected plants immediately and report the problem to a local agricultural extension officer so government assistance and targeted remedies can be mobilized to stop the outbreak.
ga: Kɛ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ ba lɛ, tsimɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ waa lɛ ahe loo okpãtã amɛhiɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. ni amɛbɔ naagbai ahe amaniɛ amɛtsɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ Koni amɛbua nɔyeli yelikɛbuamɔ kɛ tsabaai ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni akɛkpa hela lɛ.

english: What is this 'Akate' pest doing to my cocoa trees, and why is it bad for my yield?
ga: Mɛni nɛkɛ ‘Acate’ tsɛŋemɔ hela nɛɛ feɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ enaa minitsumɔ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii lɛ?

english: Akate, or capsids, suck the sap from young cocoa shoots and pods, leaving dark spots and damaging the wood. This starves the plant, causing leaves to drop and pods to die, which drastically reduces the amount of cocoa you can harvest.
ga: Akate loo capsids lɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ kookoo tsei amli lɛ. Eshiɔ hei ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ tso lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii lɛ gboiɔ. Enɛ baaha kookoo ni obaanyɛ okpa lɛ aba shi waa.

english: How many times in a season am I supposed to spray my cocoa farm to keep Akate away?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu yɛ be kome mli koni akat lɛ akashɛ he?

english: To effectively control Akate, you should spray your farm four times during the main pest season—typically starting around August when pest numbers begin to grow—to disrupt their breeding cycles.
ga: Bɔni afee ni okwɛ tsu lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Esa akɛ okɛ nu afɔ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ shii ejwɛ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe be titri lɛ mli—bei pii lɛ, ejeɔ shishi yɛ August aaafee be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ayibɔ jeɔ shishi eyaa hiɛ lɛ—koni ekɛkpa amɛbotemɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn brown and dry up on the stem before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This usually happens when capsids (Akate) bite young pods to feed on them, introducing damage that rots the outer skin and kills the pod before it can fully develop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ capsid (akatate) lɛ ŋmɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibioo lɛ koni eye. Enɛ haa fitemɔ ni haa kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ fiteɔ ni egbeɔ pod lɛ dani ebaanyɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: How do I measure the right amount of chemical to put in my spraying machine for cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu tsofai ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛwo mi-kookoo tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Always follow the specific mixing ratio recommended by your extension officer or product label. Using too little chemical will not kill the pests, while using too much can burn the cocoa leaves and waste your money.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ nyiɛmɔ futumɔ mlijaa pɔtɛɛ ni onihɔɔmɔ najiaŋdamɔlɔ loo nibii ahe okadi lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ be fɛɛ be. Tsofa fioo ko pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ egbeŋ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ. Shi kɛ akɛtsu nii babaoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã kookoo baai lɛ ni efite shika.

english: Can I mix different pesticides together in one spray tank to save time on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi babaoo afutu yɛ tsɔne kome mli koni mikɛ be akafite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should only mix chemicals if your extension officer confirms they are compatible. Mixing wrong chemicals can ruin their strength, waste inputs, or produce a liquid that harms your trees.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsofai afutu pɛ kɛji akɛ extension official lɛ ma nɔ mi akɛ amɛkɛ amɛhe kpãa gbee. Tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ afite hewalɛ. Waste volume Aloo ebaanyɛ efee nu ni baanyɛ aye otsei lɛ awui.

english: What happens if I don't use all the chemical mixture I prepared in my knapsack sprayer?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni mifee yɛ misɛɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii amli lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Mixed chemicals can lose their strength or separate if left standing for too long. It is best to mix only what you need for the day and handle any leftovers carefully according to official safety guidelines.
ga: Tsofai ni efutu lɛ baanyɛ afite hewalɛ loo amɛgbala kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ nɔ ni he hiaa bo kɛha gbi lɛ pɛ afutu mli ni okɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ he gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni amralo lɛ kɛha lɛ naa.

english: What time of day is best for me to spray chemical treatments on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ kookoo tsei anɔ?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon when temperatures are cooler and there is less wind, so the chemical does not evaporate or drift away from the trees.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔse nɔ lɛ leebi loo shwane mli. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ faaa No hewɔ lɛ, efoŋ loo efooo kɛjɛɛɛ tso lɛ he.

english: Why should I wear full protective clothing when spraying pesticides on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo atadei ni buɔ migbɔmɔtso muu lɛ fɛɛ he kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi miifɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Agrochemicals can easily soak through regular clothes or enter your body through breathing and eyes, causing long-term health problems like skin rashes, dizziness, or lung damage.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ baanyɛ abote atadei folo amli. Aloo eboteɔ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli mlɛo kɛtsɔɔ mumɔ kɛ hiŋmɛi nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ ekɛ helatsamɔ mli naagbai ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tamɔ hewolo nɔ tsɔi, yitsoŋ tsɔi, loo fɛ̃i fitemɔ aba.

english: Will spraying chemicals on my cocoa trees harm the flowers and reduce my crop?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kookoo tsei anɔ lɛ baaye fɔfɔi lɛ awui ni ebaaha miyibii lɛ aba shi?

english: If you spray heavy pesticides directly on open flowers, you might kill insects like midges that pollinate cocoa, which leads to fewer pods setting on the tree.
ga: Kɛji okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi babaoo shwie fɔfɔi ni agbele nɔ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, Obaanyɛ ogbe kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ kookoo mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ayibɔ aba shi.

english: How do I know if my farm needs to be sprayed again sooner than expected?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ehe miihia ni afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ tsofa ekoŋŋ mra fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ?

english: Regularly check your cocoa trees for fresh dark spots on young shoots or new pod damage; if you see active pests or fresh feeding marks, it means the previous treatment has worn off.
ga: Kwɛmɔ o-cacao tsei lɛ amli daa koni ona ŋmeii diji heei ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ anɔ loo ŋmeii heei ni efite lɛ. Kɛji ona tsɛŋemɔ helai loo niyenii hee he okadii Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsofa ni akɛtsu nii tsutsu lɛ efo.

english: Why should I leave part of my farmland to rest for a season instead of planting crops on it every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ fã ko ajɔɔ ehe be kome moŋ fe ni makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii daa afi lɛ?

english: Leaving land to rest, also known as fallowing, gives the soil time to rebuild its natural nutrients and organic matter. It also helps break the life cycle of pests and diseases that build up in the soil when crops are grown continuously.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe, ni ale lɛ akɛ defoliation lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatswa ehe adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ekoŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ashihilɛ mli beni aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii daa lɛ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts in the same farm with my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. Planting them with maize naturally adds fertilizer to the soil, helping your maize grow stronger and greener.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ abele duɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni efee hewalɛ ni efee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen in the soil. The plant pulls the remaining nitrogen from its older lower leaves and sends it to the top to keep new growth alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ ŋɔɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha shweremɔ hee lɛ aya nɔ.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry periods as a self-defense trick to save water. Because plants lose moisture through their leaves, shedding them helps the plant survive under the hot sun until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ amɛhe nɔ koni akɛbu nu he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ ashi baai lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do I need to clear tall trees and put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei kakadaji ni makɛ tsei ama shi koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb tall stakes so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. Sunlit leaves produce the energy and food that the plant sends underground to grow large, heavy yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Baai ni hulu lɛ ewo mli lɛ haa hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni tso lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do some of my tiny cocoa pods dry up and turn black before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii No hewɔ lɛ minɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ dani edaa lɛ?

english: This is often caused by a natural process called cherelle wilt, where the tree discards extra small pods it cannot support with available water and nutrients. However, it can also be caused by fungal black pod disease if the weather is very wet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Cherelle Wilt, ni tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. ni nyɛŋ aye abua nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ Shi kɛlɛ, fungal black pod hela lɛ hu baanyɛ aha eba kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures are too high or when the plant suffers from water stress. Extreme heat damages the pollen inside the flower, preventing fruit formation.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ nu he haomɔ hewɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Tsi yibiiwoo naa

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small cups and turning hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee kɔɔpoi bibii ni wa lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking juices from the underside of the leaves. Their feeding damages the leaf tissues and distorts normal plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper leaf curl baa. Amɛ niyenii lɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni efiteɔ tso lɛ dalɛ ni sa.

english: Why do weeds sprout and grow so much faster than my planted crop seeds right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ ni amɛdara oya fe dumɔwui ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are very tough and can sleep in the dry soil for months without dying. The moment the first rain falls, they absorb water instantly and germinate faster because they are naturally adapted to the wild environment.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui wa waa ni ebaanyɛ ehi shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ nyɔji babaoo ni egbooo. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ Amɛbaaŋɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ oya. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo koo mli shihilɛ mli.

english: Why is it bad for me to save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ baato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Commercial hybrid seeds are specially bred from two unique parent plants for high yield. The seeds harvested from that crop lose their special genetic strength in the next generation, resulting in uneven growth and smaller cobs.
ga: Akɛ jarayeli dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ tsei enyɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ fɔmɔ nii ahe hewalɛ ni fa lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do my young maize leaves curl up during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during extreme heat as a natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun. This helps the plant trap moisture inside and stop itself from drying out until the temperature cools down.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ emli lɛ ni ehaaa egbi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants get dark spots when I spray water over the top of them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ nu shwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Sprinkling water directly over leaves leaves them wet for long periods, creating a warm, damp environment where fungal diseases thrive. Watering close to the soil keeps the foliage dry and healthy while still feeding the roots.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nu shwie baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Biɛ ji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ ada yɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛhaa shishifãi lɛ niyenii lolo.

english: Why are my vegetable crops growing very tall and thin instead of bushy and strong in my small plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ miida waa ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ yɛ bushy kɛ hewalɛ najiaŋ yɛ mi shikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete with each other for sunlight. Each plant stretches upward as fast as possible to reach light, making the stem thin and weak instead of sturdy and productive.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko tsɔɔ ehe oya bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni eshɛ la lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa moŋ fe ni amɛaafee hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my pepper plants before any peppers grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ŋmɔtɔ lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from heat or inconsistent watering. If the plant feels it does not have enough steady water to support fruit, it drops the flowers to save its own energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo latsaa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ bɛ Ebaajie fɔfɔii koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehewalɛ.

english: Why do my garden eggs look wilted during the day even though the ground around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli egbi moŋ lɛ? Ani ebaafee ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Too much standing water suffocates plant roots by cutting off their air supply. Damaged or drowning roots cannot pump water up to the stem, causing the plant to wilt even when surrounded by wet soil.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi ni efite loo ni ebote nu shishi lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ nu kɛyashɛ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ ebɔle amɛhe po.

english: Why do my cassava plants shed almost all their leaves when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa lɛ babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during prolonged dry spells to lower its water needs. The plant goes into a dormant state above ground while keeping its energy stored safely in the underground roots until rain returns.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei baa shwieɔ shi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni nu he hiamɔ aba shi. Tso lɛ boteɔ shihilɛ ni bɛ shihilɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Is it better to give my crops a lot of water once a week or a small amount of water every day?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔ midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ nu shikome yɛ otsi mli loo maha amɛ nu fioo daa gbi?

english: Giving crops regular, moderate water encourages roots to grow deep into the soil where it stays cool. Frequent shallow watering keeps roots near the surface, where they quickly dry out under the heat.
ga: Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli shii abɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ abɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbi oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ lɛ shishi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cabbage turning yellow while the new inner leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ shishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni mligbɛ baai heei lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When soil nutrients are low, cabbage plants take stored food from older bottom leaves and send it to feed new leaf growth. Yellow bottom leaves indicate the plant needs extra nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Kɛji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ, Kabeji tsei lɛ ŋɔɔ niyenii ni ato kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli ni amɛkɛmajeɔ koni eyaha baai heei ni daraa lɛ niyenii. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia niyenii krokomɛi, tamɔ nitrogen.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my young okra seedlings in the same soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe okra dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to pull water and nutrients out of the ground much faster than cultivated crops. If not cleared early, weeds steal the water and light your okra needs to grow.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛjie nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Kɛji ajieee mra lɛ Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu kɛ la ni he hiaa okra koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomatoes crack open right after a heavy rain following a dry week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ mli fãa trukaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa yɛ otsi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When a dry tomato plant suddenly gets a sudden surge of water, the inside of the fruit swells very fast. The outer skin cannot stretch quickly enough to hold the extra water, causing it to split open.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei ni egbi lɛ ná nu ni fa trukaa lɛ, aduawai lɛ amli fũuɔ oya waa. Hewolo lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ ehe oya bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ahi shi. kɛ mligbalamɔ baa

english: Why is it important for me to mound soil around my crops quickly after bringing them to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mabua muji naa kɛbɔle he lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ oya beni akɛ amɛ etee ŋmɔ mli sɛɛ?

english: Mounding soil quickly around crop roots protects them from drying out under the hot sun, keeps the root structure cool and moist, and gives the young plants solid anchor support against strong rains and winds.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ooobɔle tsei shishifãi ahe oya lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ akagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa shishifã lɛ mli fɛ̃i ni edɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he

english: How does building raised soil mounds help my root crops grow bigger?
ga: Te gɔŋ ni awo nɔ lɛ ni ooofee lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Loose, mounded soil creates soft earth that allows roots like cassava and yam to expand easily without pushing against hard, compacted dirt, resulting in larger and healthier tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni gɔji yɔɔ nɔ lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni fiɔ shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei sɛɛ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ tsuuu nii. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ agbo ni eyɛ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has enough moisture for me to start planting at the beginning of the rainy season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli eyi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Squeeze a handful of topsoil into a ball; if it holds its shape without dripping excess water or crumbling into dry dust, the soil has the right moisture balance for seeds to germinate safely.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ fioo ko ni okɛfee bɔɔlu. Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni nu ni fa fe nine shwieee shi loo efolɔɔɔ mli ni etsɔɔɔ sũ ni egbi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná ŋmɔtɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings droop and turn yellow when they receive full sunlight all day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ hulu lɛ tsoɔ amɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are shade-loving in their early years. Direct, harsh sunlight scorches their soft leaves and drains their soil moisture before their root systems are strong enough to drink enough water.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii sumɔɔ hulutsoo yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ ni ebaajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ kɛya dani shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛnu nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my seedlings wither so fast if I leave them sitting in their bags for a few days before putting them into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ oya kɛji miha amɛhi kotoku lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi dani mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings in bags have limited soil and root space. Once removed from nursery shade, their exposed container roots overheat and dry out rapidly, causing severe shock and death if not planted immediately.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ kotokui amli lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ shishifãi babaoo. Kɛji ajie kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, tsɛnsi ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ shishifãi lɛ baadɔ fe nine ni amɛbaagbi oya. Ekɛ shoofeemɔ ni naa wa kɛ gbele baa kɛji aduuu amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why does my maize crop grow thin and pale when I leave weeds growing close to the stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ mishi jwɛi yɛ ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Weeds act as aggressive neighbors that steal sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients directly from your maize, effectively starving your crop before it can form full ears.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ akutsoŋbii ni yɔɔ basabasa ni juɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ o-corn lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani amɛwo baai ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce thick green leaves but very few pods after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen-rich fertilizer pushes the crop to spend all its energy growing heavy foliage and stems instead of producing flowers and setting pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsirɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo baai kɛ tsei ni tsii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ pods ni ekɛtoɔ lɛ

english: Why should I lay out my harvested cocoa beans in a thin layer on raised drying mats rather than leaving them in a high pile?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-kokoo yibii ni mikpa lɛ awo tsɔne bibioo ko nɔ yɛ tsɔne ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mashi amɛ yɛ tsɔne ni nɔ kwɔ mli?

english: Spreading wet cocoa beans thinly allows warm air to circulate beneath and over them, ensuring they dry evenly and preventing damp mold from ruining the cocoa quality.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ ni agbɛɔ ashwãa fioo Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ tsɔɔ shishi kɛ ŋwɛi fɛɛ. Enɛ haa kookoo yibii lɛ gĩɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. ni etsĩɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ naa koni ekafite kookoo lɛ mlihilɛ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and rot directly on the branch before they are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Black pod rot is caused by a water-loving fungus that thrives in damp, dense foliage; pruning extra branches and clearing wet weeds helps sunlight dry out the trees and stop the disease.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ hydrophilic fungus ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ baai ni mli efɔ, ni mli ewo muji mli lɛ kɛbaa. Tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi ni afoɔ kɛ jwɛi ni efɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la lɛ haa tso lɛ gĩɔ ni ekpaa helai.

english: Why do I need to heap and cover my fresh cocoa beans for a few days right after breaking the pods open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibuaa kookoo ŋmeii heei anaa gbii fioo komɛi beni ajie ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Fermenting the beans under banana leaves kills the bean seed inside so it stops sprouting, burns off the sweet sticky pulp, and develops the rich chocolate flavor required by buyers.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ wo banana baai ashishi lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ gboiɔ bɔni afee ni amɛkakwɛ̃, ni eshãa ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ, ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ tsokolate ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ waa lɛ baa.

english: Why do two crop varieties look identical when I plant them, but perform very differently when rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei enyɔ feɔ ekome kɛ́ midu amɛ lɛ? Shi amɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto kwraa nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ miinɛ.

english: Seeds of different crop varieties can look exactly the same on the outside, but their internal genetic traits determine how well they handle heavy rain, poor drainage, or disease.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi amli dumɔwui baanyɛ afee nɔ kome pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ. Shi fɔmɔ nii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baatsɔɔ bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ atsu nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ amɛha. Te nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo helai srɔtoi hi ha tɛŋŋ?

english: How can I know which seed variety to buy for my rainy area if all the seeds look the same at the shop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male dumɔwui ni esa akɛ mahe kɛha mi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli kpokpaa lɛ? Kɛji dumɔwui fɛɛ tamɔ nɔ kome yɛ shwapo lɛ mli?

english: You cannot tell a seed's strength just by looking at it. Always ask an agricultural extension officer or certified seed dealer for varieties specifically labeled for rain tolerance or flood resistance.
ga: Onyɛŋ ole bɔ ni dumɔwu ko mli wa ha kɛtsɔ ehiŋmɛi ni oookwɛ kɛkɛ nɔ. Bi o-agricultural extension agent loo dumɔwui ahe nitsulɔ ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni aŋmala nɔ tɛ̃ɛ akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛshi nugbɔ loo nu afua lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crop roots start to rot when water sits on my farmland after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛ́ nu eshwɛ yɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need oxygen from the soil to breathe and stay healthy. When standing water covers the ground and cannot drain, it starves the roots of air and causes soil fungi to rot the plant.
ga: Tsei shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu ni ekã shi lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ ana kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agboi.

english: Why do my crops grow well when the soil absorbs rainwater quickly, but die when the water pools on top of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ oya lɛ? Shi egboɔ kɛ́ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Absorbed water stays in tiny spaces in the soil where roots can safely drink it, while pooled water blocks fresh air from reaching the roots, causing them to drown and decay.
ga: Nu ni aŋɔ lɛ hiɔ he bibioo ko. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu shweshweeshwe Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni ebua naa lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ.

english: What can I do on my farm if my land cannot absorb rainwater fast enough during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nugbɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: You can dig drainage channels or plant your crops on raised mounds and ridges so excess rainwater flows away from plant stems and roots.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nu homɔ gbɛi loo odu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ kɛ ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ koni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I test if my farm soil drains water well enough before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho nu jogbaŋŋ dani mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: Dig a small hole, pour water into it, and see how fast it sinks. If the water stays standing for many hours, the land has poor drainage and will need ridges or compost to help water pass through.
ga: Tsɔmɔmɔ bu bibioo ko, ni ofɔse nu awo mli, ni okwɛ bɔ ni eshiɔ oya. Kɛji nu lɛ hi shi ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ni esa akɛ ŋshɔ loo ŋmɔ ko ahi shi koni eye ebua nu ni etsɔ mli.

english: Why do my cassava or yam tubers rot underground during the peak rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Tubers rot when soil stays waterlogged for too long because stagnant water creates ideal conditions for soil bacteria and fungi to attack oxygen-starved roots.
ga: Tubers fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atutua shishifãi ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yeɔ amɛ lɛ.

english: Can my crops look green and healthy above the ground while their roots are rotting in wet soil?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, plants often look green at first while roots begin to rot underground, but once the roots are completely damaged, the entire plant will suddenly wilt and collapse.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, bei pii lɛ tsei feɔ eŋɔli yɛ shishijee mli beni amɛshishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Shi kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ fite kwraa lɛ, tso muu lɛ fɛɛ baagbo trukaa ni ebaakumɔ shi.

english: Why do some crops handle heavy rainfall easily as long as the soil drains well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ gbɛ mlɛo, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When soil drains properly, excess rainwater passes right through, leaving behind fresh air and just enough moisture for roots to drink without drowning.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ho jogbaŋŋ Nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baatsɔ mli. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ shwieɔ shi koni shishifãi lɛ anu nu ni nu lɛ shwieee amɛmli.

english: Why does rain harm crops in one section of my farm while crops in another section stay healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ awui lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hei krokomɛi lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lolo.

english: Different parts of your farm may have different soil types; low areas with heavy clay hold onto water and cause rot, while higher or sandy areas drain excess water safely.
ga: Ekolɛ oŋmɔ lɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi srɔtoi. Hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni shikpɔŋ ni sũ shwieɔ shi lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ mli ni ehaa egboɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, yɛ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋã yɔɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ ajie nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: How do I know the right amount of fertilizer to apply so I don't waste my money?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa? No hewɔ lɛ jeee shika fitemɔ ni?

english: You can determine the right amount by using small measures like bottle caps per plant or asking for soil testing. Applying just the suitable amount saves money and prevents damaging your crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona bɔ ni sa kɛtsɔ gbɛjianɔtoi bibii tamɔ tɔ mli tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tso fɛɛ tso mli loo ni ooobi ni aka shikpɔŋ lɛ akwɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ shika ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha okɛ shika akafite, ni ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii akafite.

english: If I add extra fertilizer to my maize, will it automatically give me a bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata ŋmãa lɛ he Ani ebaaha mi ŋmãa babaoo lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: No, adding too much fertilizer does not mean more yield. Over-applying can burn crop roots and waste your money, reducing your overall profit.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ yibiiwoo lɛ baaya hiɛ. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii babaoo lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni efite shika. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji sɛɛnamɔi fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ nɔ ni baa shi.

english: Can placing fertilizer directly against my crop's stem harm the plant?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye tso lɛ awui?

english: Yes, placing chemical fertilizer directly against the stem or leaves can burn the plant. Fertilizer should be placed a few inches away in the soil so the roots can reach it safely.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi loo baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi 2-3 koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe.

english: What happens to fertilizer if heavy rain falls right after I apply it?
ga: Mɛni baaba ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa beni mikɛwo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can wash the fertilizer away before the roots absorb it, wasting the inputs you bought and leaving your crops without proper nourishment.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa.

english: Why do some farmers in my village make more profit even when we grow the exact same crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ náa sɛɛnamɔ babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ wɔduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komekomei moŋ?

english: Profits depend on how well costs are managed. Farmers who apply only the necessary amount of fertilizer and avoid unnecessary expenses keep more of the income they earn.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔ damɔ bɔ ni akwɛɔ shika nɔ jogbaŋŋ ahaa lɛ nɔ. Okwaafoi ni kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa pɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shika ni he ehiaaa lɛ he lɛ baanyɛ ahi amɛshika lɛ mli.

english: Why should I avoid spending too much money on farm inputs if my budget is small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ shika babaoo ni mifiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ahe lɛ he kɛji akɛ mishika he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ faaa?

english: High input costs do not guarantee high profits. Spending moderately on what your crops actually need ensures you don't run into debt if yields or market prices fluctuate.
ga: Nibii ni afee lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo ni fa babaoo lɛ haaa sɛɛnamɔ babaoo aba. Ehe miihia ni ofite shika ni sa yɛ nɔ ni he hiaa onibii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ he. Ebaaye ebua ni ona nɔmimaa akɛ okɛ ohe wooo nyɔmɔ mli kɛji nibii ni afee loo jarayeli jara tsake.

english: When plants are crowded, they fight for nutrients, sunlight, and water. Proper spacing gives each crop enough room to grow strong and produce good yield.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Is it better to plant a small part of my farm well before trying to plant the entire land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooodu nii yɛ he bibioo ko? Yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni madu shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Yes, planting a manageable area allows you to provide the right care and input amounts effectively, ensuring higher productivity before you expand.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔ yɛ he ko ni anyɛɔ akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ohaa niyenii ni mɔɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa nibii ni afee lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ dani agbɛɔ ashwãa.

english: Why do my crops grow very well on one part of my land but poorly on another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã kome nɔ shi amɛkwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ fa kroko lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil conditions vary across different areas of a farm. Some spots naturally have more nutrients or moisture, while poorer spots need specific attention.
ga: Esoro shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli he fɛɛ he. He komɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. yɛ be mli ni hei ni ehiii fe fɛɛ lɛ biɔ hiɛdɔɔ krɛdɛɛ.

english: Should I apply the exact same amount of fertilizer to every piece of land I farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni falɛ tamɔ nakai pɛpɛɛpɛ atsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ fɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, because soil quality differs from place to place. Fertile soil needs less extra fertilizer, while poorer soil requires a suitable balanced amount to support growth.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ esoro bɔ ni sũ lɛ yɔɔ ha yɛ he fɛɛ he. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii babaoo lɛ biɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he fioo. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔji ni ehiii fe fɛɛ lɛ biɔ nibii ni sa ni baaye abua dalɛ.

english: What is the main reason for putting wooden poles or stakes next to my climbing crops?
ga: Mɛni ji yiŋtoo titri hewɔ ni mikɛ tso loo tso ko ma mi tsei ni mikɛkwɔɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Stakes give climbing plants a solid structure to grow upward, keeping leaves exposed to sunlight and keeping the fruit off the soil where it can easily rot or catch diseases.
ga: Stakes haa tsei ni kwɔɔ lɛ náa gbɛjianɔtoo ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ koni amɛdara kɛya shɔŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hulu la. ni etsĩ aduawai anaa koni amɛkahi sũ lɛ mli he ni amɛgboiɔ oya loo helai baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ.

english: What happens to my crops if I remove or disturb their support poles while they are growing?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mijie loo migbala tsei ni fiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ amli be mli ni amɛmiida lɛ?

english: Removing support poles causes the plant extra stress, forcing it to stretch wildly for light and leading to weaker stems, lower yields, and an early death for the crop.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie sɛɛfimɔ tsei lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tso lɛ akpã mli koni enine ashɛ la nɔ. ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ, yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboiɔ oya.

english: Can the way I stake my plants affect how much harvest I get at the end of the season?
ga: Ani bɔ ni mikɛ mitsei lɛ woɔ tso mli lɛ baaná ŋmaa babaoo ni minine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, proper staking ensures the plant uses its energy to produce maximum fruit rather than wasting energy just trying to stay upright and reach sunlight.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ lɛ, bɔɔmɔdɛŋ kɛkɛ ni ote shi tɛ̃ɛ ni omɔ hulu la lɛ.

english: My crop vines are growing very long stems, but why am I getting so little fruit?
ga: Miwein tso lɛ yɛ tsei kakadaji waa. Shi mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibii fioo ko nɔ nɛkɛ?

english: When a plant puts all its nutrients into growing long, stretched-out vines, it runs out of energy to build thick stems and strong fruits, resulting in a small harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ wo wain tso lɛ mli lɛ, edaa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa. Hewalɛ ni ekɛbaafee tsei ni mli tse kɛ aduawai ni mli wa lɛ baaho. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii fioo pɛ ni afeɔ.

english: Why do some of my crops die off in their second year while other farmers' crops last much longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi gboiɔ yɛ amɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni okwaafoi krokomɛi aŋmɔshi nibii hiɔ shi be babaoo lɛ?

english: Crops die early when they suffer physical stress, bad staking techniques, or poor care, whereas properly managed crops can easily reach their full lifespan of 3 to 4 years or more.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gboiɔ oya kɛ́ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nɔnyɛɛ kpe amɛ. staking techniques ni ehiii loo nɔkwɛmɔ ni ehiii Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aná wala be ni yeɔ emuu ni ji afii 3 kɛyashi 4 loo nɔ ni fe nakai yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ.

english: Why does a plant produce smaller harvests when its main vines stretch too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei woɔ yibii fioo beni wain tso titri lɛ kɛlɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Overly long vines require too much water and nutrients just to stay alive, leaving very little food left for the plant to develop full-sized crops.
ga: Wein tsei ni kɛlɛ tsɔ lɛ biɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo tsɔ koni amɛhi shi. Enɛ haa niyenii fioo pɛ eshwɛɔ ehaa tso lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo.

english: How long should I expect multi-year vine crops to keep producing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa wain tso ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ gbɛ akɛ ebaawo yibii?

english: With proper support, watering, and soil care, many vine crops can reliably produce food for 3 to 4 years, and sometimes even longer.
ga: Kɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni sa, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ. Wein tsei babaoo baanyɛ awo niyenii yɛ gbɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 4, bei komɛi po lɛ, etsɛɔ fe nakai.

english: Why do I still get a small harvest even when my crop is damaged or stressed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibii fioo nɔ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii efite loo eyɛ haomɔ mli moŋ?

english: Plants naturally try to produce seeds and fruit before dying as a survival mechanism, but a stressed plant will only produce a fraction of its normal yield.
ga: Tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛwo dumɔwui kɛ aduawai dani amɛgboi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi. Shi tsei ni haoɔ amɛhe lɛ woɔ amɛyibii ni amɛwoɔ daa lɛ fã ko pɛ.

english: How can I help my crops reach their full 4-year lifespan instead of dying early?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi afii 4 moŋ fe ni amɛgboi mra?

english: You can extend your crop's life by avoiding structural damage to stems, leaving support stakes in place, and keeping plants well-nourished throughout their life cycle.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha onibii lɛ ashihilɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ shishitoo mlai ni baafite tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni oootsi ohe kɛjɛ he lɛ nɔ. Shi akulashiŋi ni fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. ni amɛkwɛ tsei anɔ koni amɛná niyenii kpakpa yɛ amɛwala be fɛɛ mli

english: Why is my total harvest much lower than what extension agents say the crop should produce?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ fɛɛ lɛ baa shi fe nɔ ni hiɛyaa najiaŋdamɔlɔ lɛ kɛɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ awo lɛ?

english: Lower yields usually happen when growth conditions force the plant to fight for survival—such as losing support structures—instead of focusing energy on fruit production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ baa kɛji shihilɛi ni haa tso lɛ daa lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ewuu koni ehi shi, tamɔ nɔ ni ekɛfiɔ esɛɛ lɛ baa shi. Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ o he wami ɔ kɛ tsu yiblii nɛ o maa wo ɔ he ní.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, which is an essential nutrient for green growth, or that the soil is waterlogged and preventing roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why does my field produce smaller crop yields every year when I plant maize on the same piece of land over and over?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii abɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving the land time to recover, which depletes soil fertility unless you rotate crops or add compost.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ aba shi. Ja otsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into my maize leaves and destroying the center of the young plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-abɛi lɛ amli ni amɛfiteɔ tsei bibii lɛ amli shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworms, which attack young maize plants; early application of suitable organic or chemical control measures can prevent them from destroying the growing shoot.
ga: Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni sa ni akɛkwɛɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ anɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra ni sa. Ebaanyɛ etsĩ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ afitemɔ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up, turning yellow, and becoming small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe lɛ? tsɔ ŋmɔŋ Ni ani eji bibioo?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, a viral infection spread by tiny whitefly insects that feed on the plant's sap.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni yeɔ tsei amli nu lɛ

english: Why do the flowers drop off my pepper plants without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers often drop when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, prolonged dry spells, or a lack of moisture in the soil during the flowering period.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa miigba tso lɛ naa. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily in direct sun, so they need shade crops like plantains to protect them while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kookoo tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small, thin bunches when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ jwɛi bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight over water and nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from reaching each other, resulting in smaller fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why do my crops grow so poorly when I let weeds grow close to their roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Beni mihaa jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal vital soil nutrients, sunlight, and groundwater that your main crop needs to develop healthy roots and stems.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni he hiaa tsei ni okɛ amɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ koni amɛná shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni wa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves droop and wilt during the afternoon sun even when the soil has some moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: In intense heat, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can suck it up from the ground, causing temporary wilting until the sun goes down.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Tomato baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: How do I know when my yam tubers are fully matured and ready to be dug out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yam tubers are ready for harvest when the green leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and completely dry up, signaling that the plant has stored all its energy underground.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai eŋɔli kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbi kwraa lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ eto shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when there is direct sunlight on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that scorch easily under harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees above them to keep the leaves cool and retain soil moisture while their root system develops.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei, koni amɛha baai lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass or palm fronds help them grow?
ga: Mulching around Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ jwɛi loo ŋmei baai koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Covering the ground, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket that traps moisture in the soil, keeps the roots cool during hot days, and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to produce green leaves and grow strong stalks. Adding compost or manure can help restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so that the plant roots can soak it up. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn and damage the roots instead of feeding the crop.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ ashã ni efite yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the specific nutrients that crop loves and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating with beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ be fɛɛ be Bei lɛ hoɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii sumɔɔ lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops yield smaller fruits when I plant them close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving less energy for the plants to grow big fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwo aduawai loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: Why should I cut off the extra shoots growing around the bottom of my plantain trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and food away from the main plantain tree. Removing most of them leaves more energy for the main stem to produce a larger bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsoi loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛbaakwɛ plantains babaoo.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients, because the plant feels it does not have enough energy to raise fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ nuɔ he akɛ ebɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot in the ground when heavy rains stay on the farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits on the farm without draining, the roots drown and soil bacteria cause them to rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha amɛgboi.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes in the leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are pests like Fall Armyworms that hatch from eggs laid by moths on soft green leaves. Checking your farm early allows you to pick them off or treat the crops before they destroy the growing points.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworms ni fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ amli. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ojieɔ amɛ loo otsaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani amɛfiteɔ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains grown nearby to block the intense heat, the leaves lose moisture quickly, dry out, turn yellow, and drop to keep the plant alive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ koni abu he kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he lɛ bɛ lɛ, Baai lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya, amɛgbiɔ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ. ni egbee shi koni tso lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why does my plantain tree take so long to produce a heavy bunch if I leave all the small shoots growing around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani efeɔ ŋmeii ni tsii kɛji mishi ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: The small side shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plant for food, water, and sunlight. If you do not prune them to leave only one or two strong suckers, the main plant becomes weak and takes much longer to fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ suckers. Amɛkɛ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛji ofolɔɔɔ amɛ ni amɛfee ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Tso titri lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ be babaoo woɔ yibii.

english: If I plant my cassava cuttings at a slant instead of standing straight up, how does it affect the crop?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei lɛ ni ekɛ ehe shwie shi moŋ fe ni eeefee nɔ ni ja Te ebaaná dumɔ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slant encourages the tubers to grow shallow and horizontally under the soil. This makes harvesting much easier and allows the tubers to spread out and grow bigger compared to planting vertically.
ga: Kasava shishifãi ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa cassava shishifãi lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni eyaaa shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa ni eyeɔ ebuaa bulb lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa ni edaraa kɛ akɛtoɔ bɔ ni akwɛɔ amɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning reddish-purple instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ red-purple yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize are a sign of phosphorus deficiency. This happens either because there is not enough phosphorus in the soil or because cold, waterlogged soil is preventing the roots from soaking up nutrients.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa. Enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have natural microbes on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the soil as free fertilizer for crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa tsei tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why shouldn't I put all my crop fertilizer in the ground on the exact day I plant the seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbi ni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Seeds and fresh seedlings have very small roots that can be burned and damaged by heavy fertilizer. Applying fertilizer in split doses gives the plant nutrients right when it is actively growing and needs them most.
ga: Dumɔwui heei kɛ dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii waa ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi wo tsei amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehe hiaa amɛ fe fɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves in the center of my corn plants filled with holes and what looks like fine sawdust?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ eyi kɛ bu ni amɛtamɔ ŋmeii kpakpai lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides inside the growing center of the corn plant during the day, eating the tender leaves and leaving behind waste that looks like brown sawdust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Eyeɔ baai bibii ni eshiɔ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants shrinking and curling upward like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the underside of the leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects that distorts the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ nii yɛ baa lɛ shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ nɔ

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out suddenly, or when too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of setting fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ trukaa Aloo be mli ni nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo haa tsei kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my yam vines even after they have already climbed up the stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ Kɛji amɛkwɔ tso lɛ nɔ po

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make energy for growing large tubers underground. Weeds around the base steal water and soil nutrients, reducing the final weight of your yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Jwɛi ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa sweet potato lɛ naagbee tsiimɔ baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for healthy leaf growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK helps restore their green color and boosts plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ ni mli wa Kɛji akɛ nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo NPK fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How does growing groundnuts or cowpeas make my soil better for the next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas have special bacteria in their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the plant roots decay, that natural nitrogen acts as free fertilizer for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ helai krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tso shishifãi fite lɛ Adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants dry up and burn when there is hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains or Gliricidia next to them creates a canopy that protects the cocoa from harsh heat and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ tsei bibii loo glicidia yɛ emasɛi. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my pepper plants with dried grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dried grass, known as mulching, works like an umbrella for the ground. It keeps the soil cool, stops water from evaporating too fast in the sun, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: When crops are crowded together, they compete with one another for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil. This struggle makes the plants grow tall, thin, and weak, which results in very low crop yields.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome yɛ kui amli lɛ, amɛshiɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ tsei niyenii yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ nɔmɔ nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa, amɛfeɔ mlɛo, ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ, ni no haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Why do I need to lift my yam vines off the ground with wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso awo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce the energy required to grow big underground tubers. Staking lifts the vines so sunlight reaches all the leaves without them being shaded by weeds on the ground.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tsei lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni hulu la lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ fɛɛ ahe ni jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akatsĩ amɛnaa.

english: Why do my pepper plants look droopy and wilted in the afternoon heat even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo ni egbo yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, pepper leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can drink it up from the soil. The leaves temporarily droop to conserve moisture and will bounce back once the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔɔ. Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Baai lɛ baagbee shi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. ni ebaaku esɛɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures become extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to soaked suddenly. Keeping soil moisture consistent and providing light shade during intense heat prevents blossom drop.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ la ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni latsaa waa lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the center of the plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni Akɛtee tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which love to feed on tender young maize leaves. Applying recommended sprays or picking them off early protects the growing center of the plant from being destroyed.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni sumɔɔ ni amɛye ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Akɛ spray tsuɔ nii loo ajieɔ mra Ebaabu tso lɛ dalɛ he lɛ he koni ekafite.

english: When soil stays flooded with water, it starves the cassava roots of air. Without air, soil fungi easily infect the tubers and cause them to rot, which is why planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds helps excess water drain away.
ga: Beni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ akashɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Fungi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha bulbs lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi oya. Enɛ hewɔ ni ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo gɔji anɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil. When soil lacks nitrogen or heavy rains wash it away, the plant moves food to its newest growth, causing older bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii kɛyaa shweremɔ hee ni fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas together with my maize help my crop?
ga: Te ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When planted alongside maize, they release this nutrient into the soil, acting as a natural food supply for the maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa Amɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha ŋmãa.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to harsh sunlight. Without shade trees to cover them, the young leaves lose water faster than the roots can suck it up from the ground, causing the seedling to scorch and die.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji tsei komɛi bɛ ni haa baai bibii lɛ ahe lɛ Baai bibii lɛ baafite nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ ashã ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall down so easily when strong winds blow or when the fruit bunch gets heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa loo kɛ́ aduawai akutsei lɛ amli tsii lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep root systems; their roots spread out near the top of the soil. When the heavy fruit bunch grows, the plant becomes top-heavy, making it easy for wind to pull the shallow roots right out of the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Eshishifãi lɛ gbɛ eshwa nɔ ni miihe ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ. Kɛ́ aduawai akuu agbo ko da Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ aaajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the middle growing leaves of my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-abele lɛ teŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets young maize. They hide deep inside the central leaf funnel where it is moist, chewing on tender new growth before the plant can open up.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa bibii amli. Akɛ amɛ ewo baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli. Okɛ tsofa hee ni eda lɛ atsu nii blɛoo dani tso lɛ ajie ehe kpo.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up, shrinking, and turning hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso, amɛmiigbɔjɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids that suck the juice from young leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects. The feeding damages leaf cells, making them twist and curl as they grow.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Niyenii kpataa baa mli wala yibii lɛ ahiɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkuɔ amɛhe beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before any tomatoes start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when plants experience water stress. Extreme heat prevents proper pollination inside the flower, so the plant sheds the unfertilized bloom.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni afɔɔɔ amɛ.

english: Cassava tubers rot when soil stays waterlogged for too long due to poor drainage. Excessive water suffocates the roots, allowing soil fungi and bacteria to attack and decompose the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Nu babaoo baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps leaves make food that travels down to feed and expand the tuber beneath the soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi koni amɛyaye niyenii ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why should I plant my cassava stem cuttings at a slanted angle instead of flat on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei niji yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a 45-degree angle allows the underground buds to form strong roots deep in the soil while keeping upper buds close to the surface so shoots can easily sprout toward sunlight.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ji 45-degree lɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ feɔ shishifãi ni wa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha ŋwɛi ŋmeii lɛ abɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ hulu la lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: How do I know when my old cocoa trees have stopped producing well and need to be replaced?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cacao tsei momo lɛ ekpaa yibiiwoo jogbaŋŋ ni ehe baahia ni atsake amɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce best between 10 and 25 years of age. When trees get too old, their yield drops significantly, branches become brittle, and they become easily infected by diseases like Swollen Shoot, signaling it is time to replant or rehabilitate the farm.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ beni amɛye kɛjɛ afii 10 kɛyashi 25, beni tsei lɛ egbɔ tsɔ lɛ. Nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi waa. brittle branches Ni helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ baanyɛ atswa amɛ oya, ni eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ adu ekoŋŋ loo asaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to prune extra small branches off my fruit and cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? Baai krɛdɛɛi ni jɛ aduawai kɛ cacao tsei amli?

english: Pruning removes non-producing branches so sunlight and air can circulate freely through the tree canopy. This directs the plant's energy and nutrients directly into growing larger, healthier pods and fruits instead of excess leaves.
