ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii lɛ. Enɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ. Enɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ koni eha ŋmeii kɛ aduawai lɛ adara ni amɛná hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeená baai babaoo tsɔ

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crops curl up tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the intense sun, which prevents excess water loss. If the leaves unroll when evening cools down, the crop is managing stress, but persistent curling means it severely lacks moisture.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa hulu la ni naa wa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji baai lɛ shwieɔ shi beni amɛhe jɔɔ lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ miikpe. Shi kɛ́ tso lɛ shwie shi be fɛɛ be lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ faaa kwraa.

english: Why do my young cassava stems drop their leaves shortly after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai miifite beni adu lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: This is a normal response called transplant shock. The young stem sheds older leaves to conserve moisture while its underground roots work to establish themselves in the soil. Fresh, healthy leaves will sprout once roots take hold.
ga: Enɛ ji hetoo ni afɔɔ namɔ ni ale lɛ akɛ transplant shock. Tsoi bibii lɛ shwieɔ baai ni egbɔ koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. yɛ be mli ni eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛma amɛhe shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛji shishifãi lɛ je shishi pɛ.

english: How does an unexpected early end to the rainy season affect my flowering crops?
ga: Te nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ saa mi tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Crops need a reliable water supply to nourish flowers into full fruits. Early drought causes flowers to drop off prematurely and leaves fruits small or dried up, severely reducing your final harvest yield.
ga: Nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ he miihia tsei koni amɛha amɛfɔfɔi lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛwo yibii ni eyi obɔ. Hɔmɔ ni baa mra lɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni ehaa aduawai bibii loo egbi baa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, naagbee yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to compete aggressively for soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight. This results in tall, thin, weak plants that yield small produce, while creating a dense environment where fungal diseases spread quickly.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo pɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why do my crops grow so much faster and greener right after I clear weeds from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji beni mijie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital soil nutrients, moisture, and sunlight from your crops. Once you remove them, your crops receive the full benefit of the soil and sunlight, allowing them to grow rapidly.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛji ojie amɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná shikpɔŋ kɛ hulu la lɛ he sɛɛ kwraa. Ha amɛdara oya.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise planting plantains near my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu plantains yɛ mi kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade, keeping the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa trees establish themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ maa amɛhe shi lɛ.

english: Can planting leguminous crops like cowpea between my main crops help keep my soil cool and rich?
ga: Ani ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, ground-covering crops shade the topsoil to prevent moisture from evaporating under direct heat, while their root nodules fix nitrogen from the air into the soil to nourish your main crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ akaho yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha onibii titri lɛ niyenii.

english: Why shouldn't I place fertilizer directly against the stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Concentrated fertilizer chemical salts can cause severe burns to tender plant stems and shallow feeder roots. Placing fertilizer a few inches away in a ring allows roots to draw in nutrients safely as moisture dissolves it.
ga: Tsofai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ ashã waa. Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛ jɛmɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbala niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and build strong stems, so feeding the soil with compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekɛ ŋmãa ni wa aba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛ su ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do cowpea crops help make my soil better for future crops?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina tso ko aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that feed the soil by taking nitrogen from the air and storing it in small bumps on their roots. When the plant leaves and roots rot after harvest, this trapped nitrogen stays in the ground to feed your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛbuaa naa yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ beni baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn quickly in harsh, direct sunlight. They need soft, filtered light from shade plants like plantains or shade trees until their foliage grows thick enough to protect them.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya kɛji hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao la ni mli jɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo shia tsei amli. kɛyashi baai lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni baabu amɛhe

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly during hot afternoon weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural survival trick tomato plants use to save water. By curling their leaves inward, they expose less leaf surface to the hot sun, preventing precious moisture from escaping into the air.
ga: Baai akumɔ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ ŋaa ni tomato tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni aaatsɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ baajie amɛhiɛ kpo yɛ hulu la ni mli edɔɔ fioo lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jara wa lɛ naa koni ekajo foi kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny green caterpillars inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli buji ni etse kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that hides inside the growing center of the maize plant. The caterpillar feeds on young leaves, making holes that expand as the leaves unroll.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai yeɔ baai bibii. Enɛ haa buji ni mli lɛɛɔ be mli ni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa.

english: When too many shoots grow around a single plantain stem, they fight with the main tree for soil nutrients and water. Removing extra shoots leaves only the strongest stem, allowing it to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ Plantain kome he lɛ Ekɛ tsei ni ji gbɔi lɛ baawu koni ená niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ. Efeɔ plantains ni dara ni tsii

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers fall off without growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as intense midday heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. When stressed, the plant drops flowers to save energy for survival.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiihao, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Yam vines naturally spread out to search for sunlight. Staking holds the leaves up off the damp ground where diseases spread, allowing the leaves to catch maximum sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛyatao hulu la. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ akashɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ. Ha baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Cassava shows it is mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving bare stems. Digging up one stem to check if the tubers are thick and firm confirms whether the field is ready for harvest.
ga: Yucca tsɔɔ akɛ eda beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Ashi tso lɛ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ tso kome ni okwɛ kɛji bulbs lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ koni oma nɔ mi akɛ amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa.

english: Watering early in the morning allows crop roots to absorb moisture before the midday heat arrives. Watering in the hot sun causes water to evaporate before roots can drink it, and can stress the hot leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ baa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani shishifãi lɛ anu. ni ekɛ haomɔ baa baai ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do I need to plant shade trees like plantain near my young cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. Shade plants protect them from getting heat-stressed and help keep moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hulutsoo be lɛ naa.

english: Why do I have to cut away extra suckers from my plantain stem instead of leaving all of them to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ plantain tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ?

english: If you leave too many suckers, they all fight with the main plant for soil nutrients and water, which results in small bunches. Keeping only one or two healthy suckers ensures large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo Amɛkɛ tsei ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ baawu koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ kui bibii. Kɛ́ okɛ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha plantain lɛ afee agbo ni etsii.

english: Why should I stake my yam vines off the ground using tall wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ atsu nii ni mikɛdu mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up into the sunlight so the plant can make food efficiently, while also keeping the leaves away from damp soil where diseases can rot them.
ga: Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ahoo nii jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni helai yɔɔ nɔ lɛ he. Ebaanyɛ egbo

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their deep green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before growing into full tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛdara ni amɛbatsɔ tomato ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when water is irregular, or when key soil nutrients are missing, which stops the flower from setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni niyenii titri ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ kpaa yibiiwoo.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up tightly and stop the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ehaaa eda lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, or viruses spread by them. Removing damaged leaves and controlling insects prevents it from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, whiteflies, loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ ajie baai ni efite lɛ, ni akudɔ kooloo lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Why does my cassava rot under the soil when the rainy season gets too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Excess waterlogged soil starves the roots of air, allowing rot-causing fungi and bacteria to invade the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni kɛ fitemɔ baa lɛ boteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When they grow, they naturally add this free nutrient back into the soil for future crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ amɛdara lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ Amɛkɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ kuɔ sɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why does my land produce smaller maize harvests if I plant maize on the same plot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil continuously and gives pests a permanent home, leading to lower yields over time.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aná shia ni baahi shi daa Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why can swamp rice survive standing in flooded water while my maize dies in waterlogged soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ nu afua mli lɛ? Beni mi ŋmãa lɛ gboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal pathways that carry oxygen down from the leaves directly to the roots underwater, whereas maize roots drown because they lack this feature.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ mligbɛ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shi tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ baafo nu mli ejaakɛ amɛbɛ nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my yams so they don't spoil in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii? koni ekafite yɛ sũ lɛ mli

english: Yams are ready for harvesting when the leaves turn yellow and start to dry up. Harvesting at this right time prevents the tubers from rotting in the ground or getting attacked by pests.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbɔi gbimɔ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii lɛ yɛ be naa lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmeii akatutua amɛ.

english: Why are some of my yams growing very small while my neighbor gets big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ ji bibioo nɛkɛ yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ tubers wuji lɛ?

english: Yam size depends heavily on soil softness and nutrients. Making deep, loose soil mounds and adding organic manure gives the tubers plenty of soft space and food to stretch and grow big.
ga: Bɔ ni o-sweet potato lɛ da ha lɛ damɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ waa. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni afee ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ baaha bulb lɛ aná he ko kɛ niyenii babaoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala amɛhe ni amɛdara.

english: Can I harvest yams twice from the same plant in one season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa sweet potatoes shii enyɔ kɛjɛ tso kome mli yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, through a practice called double-harvesting. You can carefully remove the main early tuber while leaving the root system intact so the vine can produce a second, smaller seed yam.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛtsɔ nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ ojie ŋmei titri lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni oshiɔ shishifã lɛ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni wain tso lɛ anyɛ awo sweet potato ni ji enyɔ ni ji bibioo fe no.

english: If I harvest a lot of yams at once, how can I store them safely in the village without them rotting?
ga: Kɛji mikpa ŋmeii babaoo shikome Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛto shweshweeshwe yɛ akrowa lɛ mli ni efiteee?

english: You can construct a traditional raised yam barn using wooden poles and thatch. Tying the yams individually to vertical poles in a shaded, well-ventilated barn keeps them dry, cool, and safe from rot for months.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsei kɛ jwɛi ama kusum naa sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni awo nɔ. Kpɛtɛ sweet potatoes lɛ he komekomei yɛ tsei ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ ahe yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛgbiɔ, amɛhe jɔɔ, ni amɛfiteɔ nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why do my stored yams start growing shoots on their own after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikɛto lɛ bɔi shweremɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that naturally wake up after a period of rest to try to grow new plants. Carefully breaking off these early sprouts prevents the tuber from losing its energy and flesh strength.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni hiɛ ka ni teɔ shi yɛ hejɔɔmɔ be ko sɛɛ koni amɛka tsei heei amɛkwɛ. Tsei bibii lɛ amli gbalamɔ jogbaŋŋ baatsi bulb lɛ naa koni amɛkafite amɛhewalɛ kɛ loo hewalɛ.

english: Why do yam prices fall so low in the market when every farmer harvests at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato jara baa shi yɛ jara nɔ yɛ be mli ni okwaafoi fɛɛ miikpa ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: When many farmers bring yams to market all at once, supply becomes much higher than demand. Because buyers have so many options, market prices drop, which is why saving some yams to sell later gets you better profits.
ga: Kɛ okwaafoi babaoo kɛ ŋmeii ba jara nɔ shikome lɛ, Nɔ ni Akɛhaa lɛ baafee nɔ ni fe nɔ ni ataoɔ lɛ kwraa. Ejaakɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ yɛ nibii babaoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhala. No hewɔ lɛ jara lɛ ba shi. Nɔ hewɔ ni kɛ́ okɛ sweet potato to koni okɛhɔ̃ɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha oná sɛɛnamɔ kpakpa lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to sell my yams at my farm gate or take them to the big town market?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shinaa lɛ naa loo mikɛya maŋ lɛ jarayelihe wulu lɛ?

english: Selling at the farm gate is easy and saves transport costs, but town markets offer much higher prices. If you can cover or share transport costs, taking them to town gives you better income.
ga: Nihɔɔmɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ shinaa lɛ naa lɛ waaa ni ehaa shika ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ baa shi. Shi maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ kwraa haa. Kɛji obaanyɛ okɛ shika ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ aha loo okɛ amɛ agba he sane. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ ba maŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha oná shika kpakpa.

english: How should I pack my yams when transporting them from the village to avoid damage?
ga: Kɛ́ akɛmiijɛ akrowa lɛ mli lɛ, te esa akɛ afee tɛŋŋ awo sweet potato mli koni ekafite?

english: Yams bruise easily. Stack them carefully in transport trucks with dry straw or grass between layers to act as cushions, because bruised or cracked skin causes the tuber to decay quickly.
ga: Atomɔ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Okɛ amɛ ato tsɔnei ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ, ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ atsu nii akɛ kushɛni. Hewolo ni etse loo egbɛ eshwa lɛ baaha tuber lɛ agbo oya.

english: How does forming or joining a farmers' group help me sell my harvested yams better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ okwaafoi akuu ko shishijee loo mihe ni mikɛaawo mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni mahɔ̃ɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: When farmers join forces, you can combine your crop volume to negotiate directly with major buyers for higher prices and rent larger transport vehicles together at a much lower cost per person.
ga: Kɛ okwaafoi fee ekome kɛtsu nii Obaanyɛ okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ayibɔ afee ekome ni okɛ jarayelɔi wuji agba sane tɛ̃ɛ koni onine ashɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ. ni amɛha tsɔnei wuji ni akɛyaa he fɛɛ he lɛ ekome kɛha jara ni baa shi kwraa kɛha mɔ kome.

english: How can working in a group help me during the heavy work of preparing yam mounds?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kuu mli nitsumɔ baanyɛ aye abua mi yɛ nitsumɔ ni wa ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ mli?

english: By forming traditional labor-sharing groups with neighboring farmers, you can take turns working on each other's fields. This gets heavy work like land clearing and mounding done much faster without paying daily wages.
ga: Kɛtsɔ kusum nitsumɔ mlijaa kui ni okɛ okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ baafee lɛ nɔ Nyɛbaanyɛ nyɛtsake nyɛhe ni nyɛtsu nii yɛ nyɛteŋ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ŋmɔ mli. Enɛ haa nitsumɔ ni tsii tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ shwiemɔ kɛ gɔji afeemɔ yaa oya kwraa ni ehe ehiaaa ni awo daa gbi nyɔmɔ.

english: Leaves turn yellow mainly when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the plant food responsible for green leafy growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps the plants regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ titri kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ nitrogen. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ daa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛdara hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants grow very tall with huge leaves but produce very few small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ daa kɛ baa wuji shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes plants to focus all their energy on growing tall leaves and stems rather than making fruits. Switching to fertilizers rich in phosphorus and potassium encourages flowering and fruit development.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting inside the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot underground when soil holds too much water due to poor drainage, or when left unharvested long past maturity. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. aloo kɛ́ ashi ni akpaaa be kakadaŋŋ Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and dry up on the trees during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cold, wet, and humid conditions. Regularly picking off infected pods and pruning cocoa branches to let in sunlight and air helps prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ni afoɔ kookoo tsei lɛ amli daa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up early before the tubers have grown big underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya dani bulb lɛ daa agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Early drying of yam vines is often caused by heat damage when vines lie directly on hot soil, or from vine rot diseases. Staking the vines with sticks keeps them off the hot ground and lets them capture sunlight safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ ji dɔlɛ ni fiteɔ amɛ kɛ́ akɛ wain tsei lɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. aloo kɛjɛ wain tso hela mli Kɛ́ akɛ niji wo wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni wain tso lɛ akashɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, ni ebaaha wain tso lɛ aná hulu la shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce many flowers but all the blossoms drop off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, when soil moisture fluctuates unpredictably, or when insects fail to pollinate them. Irrigating regularly and mulching the soil surface helps keep moisture steady and preserves the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ gbɛ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba loo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee pollination Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi daa ni eha fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up tightly and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, mites, or aphids sucking sap from the leaf undersides. Spraying with neem oil or appropriate organic remedies early on prevents leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Akɛ neem fɔ loo nibii ni sa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa koni akafite baai lɛ.

english: Why do my crops yield less every year if I plant maize on the same farm patch continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛji akɛ miyaa nɔ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting the exact same crop repeatedly exhausts specific soil nutrients and lets crop-specific pests accumulate in the soil. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores natural nitrogen to the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ lɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite ni eha tso pɔtɛɛ ko mli tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Rotate corn with legumes like cowpeas loo peanuts. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my planted seeds fail to sprout out of the ground even after I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ moŋ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if planted too deep in the earth, if the soil is packed too tight for air to enter, or if seeds were spoiled by moisture before planting. Planting seeds at a depth equal to roughly twice their size gives them the best chance to break through.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli, loo kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ná ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli dani adu Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ aaafee amɛdalɛ shii enyɔ lɛ haa amɛ hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛboteɔ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during heavy rainstorms when the fruits start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni aduawai lɛ miibɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and become top-heavy as fruit bunches grow. Supporting the main stem with bamboo or wooden props before the fruit gets heavy prevents strong winds from knocking the tree down.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ be mli ni aduawai akuu lɛ daa lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo tsei ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ fi tso lɛ yibii lɛ asɛɛ dani tso lɛ yibii lɛ afee nɔ ni tsii lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekatswa tso lɛ shi.

english: Why are my crops not producing as much harvest as they used to years ago on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akpaaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ babaoo tamɔ afii ni eho lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil acts like a bank account. Every time you harvest crops without adding manure or fertilizer back into the earth, you take away plant food. Over time, continuous farming drains the ground of its natural strength.
ga: Shikpɔŋ tsuɔ nii tamɔ shikatoohe akaunt. Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii efataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ lɛ, Obaaŋɔ tsei aniyenii kɛya. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ baafite ebɔɔ su mli hewalɛ.

english: Can the soil run out of food for plants if I keep farming on it every season?
ga: Ani niyenii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha tsei lɛ kɛji midu amɛ daa be?

english: Yes, plants feed on nutrients in the ground to grow. If you farm the same land continuously without adding manure, plant food, or allowing the land to rest, the soil loses its nutrients and crops become weak.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛdara. Kɛji oya nɔ otsu okwaayeli yɛ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he, oduuu niyenii, loo ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ baaje mli, ni ŋmɔshi nibii hu baagbɔjɔ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is tired and needs extra help before I plant my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite ni ehe miihia yelikɛbuamɔ kroko dani madu dumɔwui?

english: Signs of tired soil include crops growing very slowly, leaves turning pale yellow early, the soil becoming hard like rock, and your harvest getting smaller season after season.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efite lɛ he ji: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ daa blɛoo waa. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya. Shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tamɔ tɛ. Ni okpamɔ lɛ baafee bibioo daa afi.

english: Is it really necessary to add plant food or manure to my crops after planting them in the ground?
ga: Ani ehe miihia diɛŋtsɛ akɛ mikɛ tsei aniyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata miŋmɔshi nibii ahe beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: While soil naturally feeds plants, repeated farming drains those natural nutrients quickly. Adding manure or fertilizer feeds the plants directly, helping them grow stronger, resist diseases, and give you a much larger harvest.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa tsei niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa moŋ, Shi okwaayeli ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nakai adebɔɔ mli niyenii lɛ hoɔ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa waa, amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ helai, ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: What happens to my crops if I just plant the seeds and leave them to grow naturally without adding anything?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni miha amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni mikɛ nɔ ko fataaa he?

english: If your soil is fresh, crops may grow well at first. However, on older farmlands, leaving crops without extra nutrients often leads to stunted growth, yellow leaves, and very poor yields.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ ji ehee Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishijee mli, shi kɛlɛ, yɛ okwaayeli hei momo lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ krokomɛi fataaa he lɛ, ehaa amɛdaraa oya, amɛbaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Why do some farmers put dried animal waste or compost on their farm when the ground is already dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ amɛŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ ji sũ momo?

english: Dirt just holds the plant's roots, but compost and animal manure contain concentrated plant food. Manure also acts like a sponge, helping the soil hold onto water longer during dry weather.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ miimɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛkɛ. Shi tsei amli niyenii ni fa babaoo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Manure hu tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: When is the right time for me to put fertilizer or manure around my growing crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikwɛɔ lɛ ahe?

english: It is best to feed your plants when they are young and actively growing—usually a few weeks after sprouting—and again when they are preparing to flower or produce fruits.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha otsei lɛ niyenii beni amɛji bibii ni amɛmiida—bei pii lɛ, yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ—kɛ agbɛnɛ hu beni amɛsaa amɛhe koni amɛwo fɔfɔi loo amɛwo yibii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop is hungry, particularly for nitrogen. Without enough food in the soil, the plant cannot make green leaves to absorb sunlight properly.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye ŋmɔshi nii lɛ. titri lɛ nitrogen Kɛji niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee baai eŋɔli ni baanyɛ aŋɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops start growing strong during the early rains but slow down and become weak later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ mli lɛ? Shi sɛɛ mli lɛ, okɛ ohe awo mli blɛoo ni ogbɔjɔ?

english: Heavy rains can wash away the top layer of natural food in the soil, or the growing plants quickly consume the little food available. Without extra plant food added, they run out of energy before harvest.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Aloo tso lɛ baaye niyenii fioo ni yɔɔ lɛ oya. Kɛji akɛ akɛ tso niyenii krokomɛi fataaa he lɛ Hewalɛ baaho dani akpa.

english: Can planting crops like beans or groundnuts together with my main crop help my soil?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, leguminous plants like beans take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. Planting them alongside or in rotation with crops like maize leaves natural food in the ground for your next harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa du yɛ masɛi loo yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha okpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow big. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away or when water sits on the field for too long, choking the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ. aloo kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni eha shishifãi lɛ shwie shi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the sap. It can also be caused by a virus spread by whiteflies, which stops the plant from growing normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Virus ni whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ hu baanyɛ ekɛba. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ adara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves wilt and drop in the hot afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull water from the soil. The leaves wilt temporarily to protect themselves and save water, and they usually stand back up once the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Baai lɛ baagbee shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe ni amɛbu nu he. ni bei pii lɛ, eteɔ shi ekoŋŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when the soil holds too much water for a long time, especially during heavy rainy seasons. The excessive wetness allows soil fungi to attack and decay the tubers before you dig them up.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo be kakadaŋŋ. Titri lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ dani obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ atsu nii.

english: Yams need loose, soft soil to expand and grow long tubers underground. Building high mounds gives the roots plenty of loose earth to grow deep while keeping them safe from sitting in excess rainwater that could rot them.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni egbɛ eshwa ni ekwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kakadaji. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa shikpɔŋ ni mli tse babaoo ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ehiɔ shi shweshweeshwe koni ekatara nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine, ni baanyɛ afite lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily dry out and burn under strong, direct sunlight. They need the shade from taller trees or shade crops like plantains to keep the air humid and protect them during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa oya. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ahi shi ni ebu amɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that do not go very deep into the ground. When a fruit bunch gets heavy, the weight pulls the whole tree down, especially during strong winds, so you must prop the stem up with a strong wooden stick.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ tsii lɛ Muji lɛ baagbala tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛba shi. Titri lɛ, yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ tso ni mli wa atsu nii ni okɛfi sɛɛ.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when there is an uneven water supply. Extreme heat stresses the plant, making it drop its flowers to save energy rather than try to produce fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni baa lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Ha fɔfɔi lɛ agbee shi koni okɛ hewalɛ akafite moŋ fe ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni owo yibii.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my land help the soil grow better maize next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Cowpeas are part of the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When the cowpea plants die and rot, that nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas fata legume weku lɛ he, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa ni emɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni tsina tsei lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why must I dry my harvested maize under the sun until it is completely hard before putting it in sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa kwraa dani mikɛwo kotokui amli lɛ?

english: If maize is put into bags while still damp, heat builds up and creates moisture that breeds dangerous molds, insects, and poisons called aflatoxins. Proper sun-drying ensures the grains stay safe and good to eat for many months.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmãa lɛ wo kotoku lɛ mli be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo lɛ, Dɔlɛ buaa ehe naa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ, kooloi bibii kɛ tsofai fɔji ni atsɛɔ amɛ aflatoxins lɛ baa. Hulu ni akɛgbiɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why does almost everyone in my district focus on growing maize instead of other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yɔɔ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ema ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ moŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Maize is a staple food with high market demand that adapts very well to the soil and rainfall patterns in many Ghanaian districts, offering reliable yields and quick financial returns compared to long-term tree crops.
ga: Abɛi ji niyenii ni jara wa waa. Ekɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ Ghana kpokpai babaoo anɔ lɛ kpãa gbee jogbaŋŋ. Amɛhaa yibiiwoo ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛ shika ni anáa oya kɛ akɛto tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know which specific crops will grow best in my local district?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Different districts have unique soil types, temperatures, and rainfall patterns. Looking at what successfully dominates local farming—such as maize or cassava—gives a strong clue about what soil and climate conditions naturally favor in your area.
ga: Kpokpai srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi, hulutsoo, kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi srɔtoi. Ehe miihia ni asusu nɔ ni eye omanye yɛ maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli nɔyeli mli, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ebaaha ona nɔ ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do crops that grow well in a neighboring district fail when I plant them in my own town?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpokpai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ jogbaŋŋ beni mikwɛɔ amɛ yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mimaŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soil composition, groundwater levels, and micro-climates vary from district to district in Ghana. A crop variety bred for wet forest conditions will struggle in areas with drier soil or different rainfall timing.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi bibii lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ kpokpaa nɔ kɛyaa kpokpaa nɔ yɛ Ghana. Tsei srɔtoi ni akwɛɔ amɛ kɛha koo mli shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ waa yɛ hei ni shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo nugbɔshiimɔ shihilɛi srɔtoi yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Is it really possible for me to grow healthy food crops right here in the middle of town?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ makwɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ maŋ lɛ teŋgbɛ biɛ?

english: Yes, urban farming works well when using small plots, backyards, or containers for quick-growing, high-value crops like peppers, garden eggs, and leafy greens that do not require vast acres of farmland.
ga: Hɛɛ, maŋtiase mli okwaayeli tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛ hei bibii, sɛɛgbɛ, loo tsɛnsii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, ni jara wa tamɔ ŋmeii, abɔɔ mli ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni biɔ okwaayeli shikpɔji wuji lɛ tsu nii.

english: What are the best crops for me to plant if I only have a small space near the street in town?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ makwɛ kɛji miyɛ he ko bibioo? Ani ebɛŋkɛ maŋ lɛ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ?

english: Fast-maturing vegetables like tomatoes, peppers, and kontomire (cocoyam leaves) are ideal for small urban spaces because they grow fast, take up little room, and sell quickly in nearby town markets.
ga: Aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ tomato, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ contomir (kookoo baa) lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha maŋtiasei bibii. Ejaakɛ aduawai daa oya Eheɔ he ko fioo ni ahɔ̃ɔ oya yɛ jarayeli hei ni yɔɔ maji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli

english: Are crops planted close to busy town roads safe for my family to eat?
ga: Ani tsei ni adu yɛ maŋ lɛ gbɛjegbɛ ko ni mɛi fa babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha miweku lɛ ni amɛye?

english: Roadside crops can collect dust and exhaust fumes on their leaves. Washing the harvested produce thoroughly with clean water removes surface dust and makes the food safe to eat.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ gbɛjegbɛ he lɛ baanyɛ abua sũ kɛ lasu ni jɛɔ mli lɛ anaa yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli tse tsu okpamɔ nii lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ sũ ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ, ni ehaa niyenii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ.

english: Will my crops produce as much food in a small town plot as they would on a big village farm?
ga: Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaha niyenii babaoo aba yɛ maŋ bibioo ko mli. Ani etamɔ ŋmɔ ko mli yɛ akrowa agbo ko mli?

english: Small town plots can produce very high yields per square meter because they are easier to water, weed, and protect, even though the total farmland size limits your overall harvest volume.
ga: maŋ bibioo shikpɔŋ lɛ Baanyɛ ewo yibii babaoo waa yɛ sqɛɛ mita kome mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ewaaa akɛ aaaha amɛ nu, ajieɔ jwɛi, ni abuɔ amɛhe. Shi kɛlɛ, bɔ ni oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ ji lɛ fɛɛ baatsi okpamɔ fɛɛ naa.

english: How can I tell if my maize plants are suffering from too much heat and lack of rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ miipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ hewɔ?

english: When maize is thirsty and stressed by sun, its broad leaves roll inward like narrow tubes to conserve moisture. If leaves stay rolled up early in the morning, the crop urgently needs water.
ga: Kɛ́ kumai ye ŋmãa ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ ehe lɛ, ebaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ shwieɔ mli tamɔ tsɔne bibioo ko. koni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe leebi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia tso lɛ oya.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow after heavy rains hit my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rains can wash key nutrients like nitrogen deep into the soil beyond the reach of roots, or waterlog the ground so roots cannot breathe. Applying a top-dressing nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green again.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha niyenii mli nibii titrii, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ aya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. aloo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I plant vegetables alongside my main maize crop without them killing each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi-staple corn lɛ adu aduawai ni amɛgbeee amɛhe?

english: Yes, intercropping maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts works well because legumes add natural nitrogen back into the soil, helping feed the maize while maximizing your farm space.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii kɛ nitrogen kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ ŋmãa yɛ be mli ni ehaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli he lɛ yaa hiɛ babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen. As the plant grows, it pulls nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei lɛ dara Ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tsei heei ni dara yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which can capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This leaves natural fertilizer behind for high-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji legumes, ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: When too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they compete for food, water, and sunlight. Cutting back extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, which results in larger and heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ ebɔle ehe Plantain kome Amɛyeɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves towards sunlight to make energy for growing heavy tubers under the ground. Staking keeps leaves off the damp ground, reducing disease and maximizing foliage exposure to light.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛya hulu la lɛ he koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha bulbs ni tsii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ehaa helai baa shi, ni ehaa la shɛɔ baai lɛ ahe babaoo.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungal infection that thrives in high moisture and cool shade. Damp rainy conditions allow fungus spores to multiply quickly and spread from pod to pod via water splashes.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kɛ black pods baa. Nugbɔshiimɔ shihilɛ haa ŋmeii amli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ feɔ babaoo oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛjɛɔ pod kome mli kɛyaa pod kome mli kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, or a virus they transmit. These insects feed on the sap underneath leaves, distorting their normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ amɛdalɛ ni sa lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too hot or when soil gets too dry, causing pollination to fail. Without successful pollination, the plant sheds flowers to conserve water and food.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji pollination ni nyɛɛɛ atsu nii. Kɛji pollination lɛ yeee omanye lɛ Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ nu kɛ niyenii ato.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers under the soil are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Cassava is usually ready when lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, typically 9 to 12 months after planting depending on the variety, indicating energy has shifted entirely to root storage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ni enɛ damɔ tso lɛ henɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ atsake hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛtee shishifãi lɛ anaabuamɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and dry up when planted in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. They need temporary shade trees like plantain or gliricidia to block excessive heat and retain humidity while roots establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo glicidia. Enɛ haaa dɔlɛ ni fe nine aba ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be mli ni shishifãi lɛ maa lɛ.

english: How does covering the soil around my vegetables with dry grass help them grow during dry weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-vegetables lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Covering soil with dry grass creates mulch that blocks direct sunlight, keeping the ground cool and preventing soil moisture from evaporating quickly while also stopping weeds from growing.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ jwɛi ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ oya lɛ naa, yɛ be mli ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ hu shwereɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa plants need to survive their first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, the plants compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow tall and thin with very small cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, amɛhe kwɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmeii bibii waa yɔɔ mli.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to capture sunlight for making plant food. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where diseases live and helps the plant direct energy into growing big tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛmɔ hulu la ni amɛkɛfee niyenii ni akɛ tsei fee. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela baanyɛ aba. ni ehaa tsei tsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need for green growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the soil where roots cannot reach it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, acts like a blanket. It stops the hot sun from drying out the soil water quickly and breaks down over time into natural fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Mulching, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ehaaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi oya. ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the soil when the rainy season gets too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves the ground waterlogged for days, water fills all the air spaces in the soil, causing the tubers to suffocate and rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo. Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures become extremely hot or when water supply drops suddenly. The heat prevents the flowers from forming seeds, so the plant drops them to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ba shi trukaa. Dɔlɛ lɛ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee dumɔwui. No hewɔ lɛ tsei shwieɔ amɛdumɔwui lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in the central leaves of my green maize?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa eŋɔli lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ

english: Those holes are usually caused by caterpillars like the fall armyworm hiding inside the growing funnel of the plant. Checking your field early allows you to control them before they destroy the whole stalk.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tsei ni daraa lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okudɔɔ amɛ dani amɛfiteɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the sap under the leaves. They can also spread plant viruses that stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ebaanyɛ egbɛ tsei amli helai ni tsiɔ tsei adalɛ naa lɛ hu eshwã.

english: If too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they steal food and water from the main mother plant. Removing extra suckers ensures the main plant gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe Plantain kome Ejuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow big and green. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the soil so the leaves stay green and produce good ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ agbo ni efee ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ koni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha toi kpakpai aba.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests if I plant maize on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize pulls the exact same nutrients out of the soil every season, leaving the ground exhausted. Switching crops every year—especially planting beans, groundnuts, or cowpeas—puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally and improves future yields.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ daa afi Titri lɛ, ŋmeii, ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and showing bright yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kpɛɔ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves with yellow patches are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. You can prevent this by planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties provided by extension officers.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmei bibioo lɛ ji nɔ ni hiɛɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmei henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni ŋmei shweremɔ he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛhaa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are large holes appearing in my cabbage leaves overnight when I do not see any bugs during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kaabaji baai lɛ feɔ bulɛi wuji nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ? Be mli ni onyɛɛɛ ona kooloi bibii komɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli?

english: Caterpillars and leaf-eating worms usually feed at night when it is cool and hide under the leaves or in the soil during the hot day. Inspecting the underside of leaves early in the morning helps you catch them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Kplukai kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛtsu nii waa gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. ni ekɛ ehe ewo baai ashishi loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ baai lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in open sunlight without any other crops around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under the harsh sun. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides shade and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye hulu lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I plant my pepper seeds very close together, won't I get more pepper fruits from my land?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani mana ŋmɔtɔ babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting pepper too closely forces the plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to tall, weak stems with very few fruits. Proper spacing gives each plant room to branch out and produce a heavy harvest.
ga: Pepper ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ aduawai fioo ko pɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni ekɛ niji baaje kpo ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into tomatoes during the hot dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air cause severe stress to tomato plants, making the blossoms drop before they can form fruit. Watering the plants regularly at the roots and providing light shade during the hottest months helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Kɛ́ afɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ nu daa ni aha amɛ hulutsoo yɛ nyɔji ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow twisted and small instead of long and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee bibii moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers become twisted when the soil underneath them is hard, compacted, or full of stones that stop the tuber from expanding downward. Making deep, soft soil mounds or ridges gives the yam tubers room to grow straight and large.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa, ebɔle ehe, loo tɛi ni tsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã kɛya shi lɛ eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ́ afee shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ nɔ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko lɛ, ebaaha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adara tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Weeds are wild plants that adapt quickly and drink up water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops can. Clearing weeds within the first three to four weeks after planting gives your crop the head start it needs to grow without competition.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe oya ni amɛnuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aje shishi oya ni akaŋ akaŋ.

english: How do I know that my groundnuts are fully mature and ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmeii lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the outer leaves start turning yellow and dry, and the inside lining of the shell turns dark brown when you crack a pod open. Harvesting too early results in shriveled nuts that spoil easily in storage.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii efee klalo beni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Ni ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ waa kɛji ogbele ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni kɛ́ akɛto lɛ, efiteɔ oya.

english: How do I know if the eyes on my seed yams are healthy enough to sprout well after planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ beni amɛdu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The 'eyes' are the growing buds on a yam tuber. Healthy eyes should look firm, clean, and slightly raised or swollen; if they are dry, black, or mushy, the tuber will not produce strong shoots.
ga: Buds’ lɛ ji fɔfɔii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ sweet potato tuber lɛ nɔ lɛ. Esa akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ afee nɔ ni wa, ehe tse, ni ewo ŋwɛi fioo loo efuu. Kɛji amɛgbi, amɛji ediŋŋ, loo amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, bulb lɛ wooo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the growing buds on my young crops turn dark and die off right after they open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miida yɛ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ duŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Dying buds are often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids damaging the soft leaves, or by intense heat burning the tender tips before the plant gets established.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ thrips loo aphids, ni tutuaa baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni gboɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni shãa ŋmeii bibii lɛ ashishifãi dani tso lɛ baanyɛ ada lɛ mli.

english: Why do some eyes on my cassava cuttings sprout quickly while others on the same stem fail to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi ni yɔɔ mi-cassava niji lɛ anɔ lɛ daa oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ edaaa oya lɛ?

english: Buds closer to the top of the stem are younger and sprout faster, while older buds near the bottom or cuttings taken from dry, stored stems may stay dormant or die.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni bɛŋkɛɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ ji gbekɛbii ni amɛdaraa oya. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ loo niji ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni egbi ni ato lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛhiɛ aka shi loo amɛgboi.

english: Why does a thick white liquid come out of my cassava stem whenever I cut it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu yɛŋ ni mli edɔ jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ ŋmei tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni mafolɔ lɛ?

english: That milky white liquid is natural latex sap. The cassava plant produces it naturally as a protective barrier to seal wounded stems and deter insects from eating it.
ga: Nu yɛŋ ni tamɔ mliki lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli latɛs. Yucca tsei lɛ feɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛha tsei ni epila lɛ ahe, ni ekɛtsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye amɛ.

english: Why does a smelly white liquid ooze out when I squeeze the stem of my tomato plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu yɛŋ ni shãa mɔ jeɔ kpo kɛ́ mikɛ mimɔ tomato tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Oozing white liquid accompanied by rot is a sign of a bacterial infection. The bacteria break down the inside of the stem into a watery paste, causing the plant to wilt and die.
ga: Nu yɛŋ ni hoɔ kɛ fitemɔ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hela ko ni gbeɔ mɔ. Muawai gbálaa tso lɛ mli ni etsɔɔ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ baanyɛ agbi ni egbo.

english: Is it normal for white watery drops to form on the leaves of my crops in the morning?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ baaje miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baa lɛ nɔ leebi?

english: Yes, when soil has plenty of water and the air is cool at night, plants naturally push out excess water through special pores on their leaf edges. This shows the roots are actively taking up moisture.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ. Tsei tsiɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛtsɔɔ bu krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ahe lɛ amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ miihe ŋmɔtɔ waa.

english: Why do I find worms living inside my maize stalks when I split them open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii ni hiɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli beni mijara amɛ mli lɛ?

english: Those worms are stem borers. Moths lay eggs on the leaves, and when the caterpillars hatch, they bore into the stem to feed and live safely inside, which weakens the whole plant.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tso lɛ mli. Kplukai fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ baai anɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ Amɛfoɔ tsei amli koni amɛna niyenii ni amɛhi mli shweshweeshwe. ni haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ

english: How do insects get inside my sweet potatoes to live without leaving big holes on the outside?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kooloi bibii boteɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ mli ni amɛshiii buji wuji yɛ kponɔgbɛ?

english: Yam and sweet potato weevils crawl through small cracks in dry soil to lay tiny eggs directly on the tuber. The hatched larvae bore inside to feed, creating hidden tunnels.
ga: Sweet potato kɛ yam ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ koni ekɛ ŋmeii bibii awo eyitso nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Lala ni efɔ lɛ shwieɔ mli koni ena niyenii. ni afee tsɔne ko ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ

english: Why is there a white, sticky cotton-like mass under the leaves of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ mi-kokoo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: That white mass is made by mealybugs. They cover themselves and their eggs in sticky white wax for protection while they suck juices from the plant leaves and stems.
ga: Mealybugs ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ futafuta lɛ baa. Amɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni mli tse haa amɛhe kɛ amɛwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli nu lɛ.

english: What causes tiny dark spots to spread all over my pepper leaves like tiny stars?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ tamɔ ŋulamii bibii?

english: Spreading spots are usually fungal or bacterial leaf spot diseases. They spread when rain splashes water from infected soil onto leaves or when crowded crops stay wet for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji fungal loo bacteria baa ŋmɔtɔ. Amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛɔ ni ekɛ nu ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ baai anɔ. aloo be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why should I strip all the husks off my maize cobs before feeding them into a shelling machine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli dani mikɛha mɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Removing the husks prevents the shelling machine from clogging up and ensures that the machine leaves you with clean, undamaged maize grains ready for storage or sale.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie ŋmeii lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni ekatsi. ni ekwɛɔ koni tsɔne lɛ afee ŋmãa ni he tse ni efiteee ni esa akɛ akɛto loo ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: What is the main advantage of using a mechanical corn sheller instead of shelling by hand?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi titrii ni yɔɔ tsɔne ni akɛjieɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ lɛ he?

english: A mechanical sheller saves a huge amount of time and heavy labor, allowing you to process large harvests quickly before pests or damp weather can spoil your cobs.
ga: Mɛkanikal ni akɛfeɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ haaa be babaoo kɛ nitsumɔ ni tsii aba shi. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsuɔ nibii babaoo ahe nii oya dani tsɛŋemɔ helai loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa o-cobs lɛ fiteɔ.

english: How can I tell if my maize is dry enough to go through a shelling machine without getting crushed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ etsɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli ni etswaaa lɛ?

english: Your maize is dry enough when the kernels feel glass-hard and make a sharp cracking sound when you bite one; if the grains feel soft or springy, the machine will mash them into paste.
ga: Abɛi lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ mli wa tamɔ glase. kɛ gbee ni tswaa kɛji akɛ eeŋmɔ Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ loo amɛyɛ fɛ̃i Mli tsɔne lɛ baatsɔ mli ni efee ŋmɔtɔ ni tamɔ nɔ kome.

english: Why does my maize break into crushed pieces when I put it through the sheller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ mikɛwoɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grain breakage usually happens if the maize is too dry, if the sheller is running at the wrong speed, or if unstripped husks force the machine to grind the cobs roughly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa mligbalamɔ baa kɛji akɛ ŋmaa lɛ egbi tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ miiho kɛ oyaiyeli ni ejaaa Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo ni ajieee lɛ nyɛɔ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ nɔ koni tsɔne lɛ atswa ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli waa.

english: How do storage chemicals protect my harvested maize from weevils?
ga: Te tsofai ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe lɛ buɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ he kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Storage chemicals create a protective shield around the grain that kills or repels insects like weevils before they can bore holes into the kernels and destroy your harvest.
ga: Tsofai ni yɔɔ nitoohe lɛ feɔ gbɛtsii nii ko ni buɔ amɛhe. Ŋmaa ni gbeɔ loo eshwieɔ kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, dani amɛboteɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli ni amɛfiteɔ onibii lɛ.

english: Is it safe to apply pest control chemicals to maize that my family will eventually eat?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baatsu nii yɛ ŋmãa ni miweku lɛ baaye yɛ naagbee lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, it is safe as long as you use approved food-grade storage insecticides, apply the exact recommended dose, and wait the required safety period before eating or selling the grain.
ga: Hɛɛ, eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa ni akɛtoɔ niyenii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii. Kɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛha lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ. ni amɛmɛ be ni ato ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ dani amɛye loo amɛhɔ̃ɔ ŋmaa

english: Why does the strength of my pest control chemical seem to wear off after a few months in the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛwo shwapo lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Chemicals naturally break down over time when exposed to air, heat, and moisture, which is why chemical treatment must be combined with airtight storage to keep pests away long-term.
ga: Tsofai fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ kɛji akɛ amɛbote kɔɔyɔɔ, dɔlɛ, kɛ hulutsoo be mli, no hewɔ ni esa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛtsaa hela lɛ afata he ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni nɔ ko bɛ mli koni akɛye tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How do I keep my harvested maize clean before I carry it to the sheller?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ he atse dani mikɛya he ni ajieɔ ŋmãa lɛ yɛ lɛ?

english: Place your harvested cobs on clean tarpaulins or raised wooden platforms off the bare ground so dirt, mud, and chicken droppings do not mix with your crop.
ga: Okɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ awo tarp ni he tse loo tso ni awo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni muji, sũ kɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ akafutu oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my maize cobs start growing mold while waiting to be shelled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn cob lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni ajie ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Mold grows when moisture gets trapped under damp husks in warm weather, so you should remove the husks and spread the cobs out to dry in the sun as soon as possible after harvesting.
ga: Fungus lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsi omɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ojie ŋmeii lɛ ni ogbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashwã koni amɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akpa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: What useful things can I do with all the empty cobs and husks left over after shelling?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ manyɛ mafee kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko kɛ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni ajie lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: You can burn empty cobs as clean cooking fuel, feed dried husks to farm animals like goats, or bury them in the soil to break down into rich organic manure for next season.
ga: Obaanyɛ oshã ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ akɛ tsofa ni he tse ni akɛhooɔ nii. Ha ŋmɔ mli kooloi tamɔ tooi ŋmei ni egbi loo ofumɔ shikpɔŋ koni efite ni etsɔ ŋmei ni fa babaoo kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: A greenhouse is a plastic or glass structure that shields crops from harsh sunlight, heavy rains, and insect pests. This protected environment allows vegetables like peppers to stay healthy, grow faster, and produce higher yields all year round.
ga: Greenhouse ji plastic loo glase nɔ ko ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni abuɔ he nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa aduawai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Why do pepper plants seem to produce larger fruits and grow faster inside a greenhouse facility?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni pepper tsei woɔ yibii wuji ni amɛdaraa oya yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Inside a greenhouse, the temperature, moisture, and sunlight are kept at ideal levels, while insect pests are kept out. Because the plants do not have to fight off pests or extreme weather, they direct all their energy into growing quickly and producing bigger fruits.
ga: Yɛ greenhouse lɛ mli lɛ, akwɛɔ dɔlɛ, fɛ̃i kɛ hulu la lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ajieɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛjɛɔ jɛmɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni tsei kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ awuu. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii wuji.

english: Can I grow hot peppers inside a covered structure during the heavy rainy season without them rotting?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmeii ni mli edɔ lɛ yɛ tsũ ko ni awo nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli ni amɛgbooo?

english: Yes, covered structures like greenhouses protect peppers from excessive rainwater hitting the leaves and roots, which prevents soil flooding and fungal rot that usually destroy pepper crops during heavy rains.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsũi ni akɛ nɔ ko eha nɔ tamɔ tsũi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ buɔ ŋmeii ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni saa baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu afua kɛ ŋmeii ni bei pii lɛ efiteɔ ŋmeii tsei yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: How are the seed varieties distributed by agriculture officers different from the seeds I save from my own farm harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ jaa lɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaa ni akpaa yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Distributed high-yield seeds are specially bred to resist local diseases, tolerate weather stress, and produce uniform, high-quality vegetables that command better market prices compared to traditional saved seeds.
ga: Atsɔ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekɛte shi ewo maŋ lɛ mli helai. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe haomɔi ni ekɛ aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yaa nɔ daa ni haa jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ lɛ ahe lɛ baa.

english: If I receive a batch of new vegetable seeds, how should I handle them so every farmer in our group gets good results?
ga: Kɛji wɔnine shɛ aduawai dumɔwui akuu hee nɔ lɛ, te wɔbaafee tɛŋŋ wɔkwɛ nɔ koni okwaafoi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ wɔkuu lɛ mli lɛ aná yibii kpakpai?

english: New seeds should be nursed carefully in clean, well-drained seedbeds or trays with adequate shade and controlled watering, ensuring healthy nursery seedlings are shared equally for field planting.
