ga: Esa akɛ akwɛ dumɔwui heei anɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ dumɔwui atsu ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. aloo yɛ trati ni hulutsoo be ni sa yɔɔ mli ni akudɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aná hewalɛ ni aja mli pɛpɛɛpɛ. nubu kɛha dumɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress caused by extreme heat, prolonged drought, or a sudden lack of soil nutrients, causing the plant to drop its buds to survive.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ trukaa Enɛ haa tsei he hiaa hiŋmɛi nɔ tsofa koni amɛhi shi.

english: What causes the leaves of my vegetable plants to curl up and turn yellow in the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-vegetables lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are often caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck plant juices and transmit viruses, especially during dry, warm weather when pest populations increase.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛhaa helai baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Enɛ ji be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ayibɔ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops die quickly when water sits on the farm field after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboiɔ oya kɛ́ nu ŋmɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When excess rainwater pools around the base of plants, it suffocates the roots by cutting off oxygen, causing root rot and leading to the sudden wilt and death of the plant.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nu babaoo bua ehe naa yɛ tsei ashishigbɛ lɛ, ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ gboɔ trukaa ni egboɔ.

english: Why should I consider growing vegetables like peppers to earn income instead of relying only on traditional staple crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu aduawai tamɔ ŋmeii akwɛmɔ he koni maná shika moŋ fe ni mikɛ mihe aaafɔ̃ blema nibii ni aduɔ lɛ anɔ?

english: Vegetables like peppers have short growing cycles and high continuous demand in local markets, allowing you to harvest and sell multiple times a year for quicker, steady cash flow compared to long-season staple crops.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ chili peppers lɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli ni amɛdaraa, ni amɛtaoɔ babaoo yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ni ohɔ̃ɔ shii abɔ yɛ afi mli kɛha shika ni baa oya, ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ ahe.

english: How can growing vegetables in a controlled environment help me get higher prices at the market?
ga: Te aduawai ni miduɔ yɛ he ko ni akudɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná jara ni nɔ kwɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Growing vegetables in a protected environment yields cleaner, unblemished, and insect-free produce during off-seasons when open-field crops are scarce, allowing you to sell at top market prices.
ga: Aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni abuɔ he lɛ haa yibii ni he tse, ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he, ni kooloi bɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ, be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ faaa lɛ. Ehaa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ yɛ jara nɔ.

english: Why do mango trees stay standing strong even during big rainstorms and high winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei damɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa po mli lɛ?

english: Mango trees grow a deep, strong taproot that digs far into the ground. This anchors the tree firmly in the soil while its thick stem gives it the structural strength to withstand heavy winds without falling over.
ga: Mango tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. koni ekɛmɔ tso lɛ mli shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ shishi ni mli tse lɛ haa tsɔne lɛ mli wa. Ebaanyɛ edamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa ni egbeee shi.

english: Why do crops like maize fall over easily in strong wind, but mango trees stay upright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa hewɔ lɛ? Shi ani mango tso lɛ baanyɛ adamɔ shi shiŋŋ lolo?

english: Crops like maize have shallow roots near the surface of the soil, making them easy to push over. Trees like mangoes build deep root systems and strong woody trunks that grip the earth firmly for many years.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaatsi Tsei tamɔ mango feɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni wa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi shiŋŋ afii babaoo.

english: Is it better for me to plant mangoes from seeds or buy grafted seedlings from a nursery?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ dumɔwui adu mango loo ooohe dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe?

english: Grafted seedlings are usually better because they grow into strong, fruit-bearing trees much faster—usually in 3 to 4 years—and they stay at a manageable height while producing sweet, high-quality fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛwo tso mli lɛ hi fe tsutsu lɛ ejaakɛ amɛdaraa oya ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni he wa ni woɔ yibii. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 ni amɛbaakã he amɛhi shi yɛ he ko ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ aduawai ni ŋɔɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How long does it usually take for a newly planted mango tree to start giving good fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mango ni adu ehee lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai?

english: If you plant a grafted mango seedling, it will start giving strong yields in about 3 to 4 years. Trees grown directly from local seeds can take 5 to 7 years or longer to mature.
ga: Kɛji odu mango dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ Ebaabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa womɔ yɛ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli. Tsei ni akwɛɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahe afii 5 kɛyashi 7 loo nɔ ni fe nakai dani amɛshɛ shweremɔ he.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for growing strong mango trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha mango tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ akwɛmɔ?

english: Mango trees need deep, loose soil so their long roots can dig down easily without hitting solid rock or standing water. If your land drains well and isn't swampy, mango roots can grow deep and strong.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ hia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi kakadaji lɛ baanyɛ afo shi oya ni amɛtswaaa tɛi ni wa loo nu ni damɔ shi. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nu shwieee nɔ. Mango shishifãi baanyɛ ada kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe awa.

english: How can I protect my young mango seedling from getting scorched by the hot sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi mango tso lɛ he koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akashã lɛ?

english: Young seedlings need time to build strength. Placing dry grass mulch around the base keeps the soil cool and moist, while temporary shade structures protect the delicate leaves until the plant establishes strong roots.
ga: Be he miihia tsei bibii koni amɛná hewalɛ amɛma shi. Ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ he ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulutsoo be kukuoo ko baabu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛyashi tso lɛ baaná shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Should I cut off the lower branches of my young mango tree as it grows?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ mi mango tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: Yes, trimming the lowest branches helps the tree build a single, thick main trunk that stands firm and upright, allowing the canopy to spread high enough for easy work underneath.
ga: Hɛɛ, niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ ni aaafolɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ tso titri kome. ni mli tse ni baanyɛ adamɔ shi shiŋŋ Enɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔ ni sa ni efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaatsu nii yɛ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my mango tree turning yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during dry months mean the tree is losing moisture faster than its roots can pull from the soil. Watering deeply at the base helps the tree maintain its strength until the rainy season returns.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ miifite oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni mli kwɔ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ehewalɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why does my mango tree drop many of its small flowers before they turn into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Babaoo dani ewo yibii?

english: A mango tree naturally sheds excess flowers if it does not have enough water or nutrients. It keeps only as many fruits as its branches and roots are strong enough to support.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛbɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ebaanyɛ ekpa yibii babaoo bɔ ni eniji kɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfiɔ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my mango tree yield plenty of fruit one year and very few fruits the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-mango lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afi kome mli shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is a natural behavior called alternate bearing. After carrying a heavy harvest, the tree spends the following year recovering its strength and gathering nutrients before it can produce a big harvest again.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli subaŋ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ nɔ kroko ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli. Yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni mli wa sɛɛ Tso lɛ baahe be yɛ sɛɛ mli afii lɛ amli koni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni ebua niyenii mli hewalɛ naa dani enyɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops refuse to grow well when I plant them under big forest trees without clearing the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi yɛ koo agbo ko mli ni mijieee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Most crops need direct sunlight to produce their own food and grow strong. When large forest trees block the sunlight, your crops become weak, thin, and pale, making it very difficult for them to yield fruit or grains.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛye niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ koo mli tsei wuji lɛ tsi hulu la lɛ naa lɛ Onibii ni oduɔ lɛ baafee mlɛo, ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni no baaha ewa aha amɛ akɛ amɛaawo yibii loo dumɔwui.

english: Should I cut down every single tree on my land before I start planting my crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: No, you do not always need to clear every tree. While some crops need full sun, retaining specific shade trees can protect delicate young crops from harsh sunlight, prevent the soil from drying out too fast, and stop heavy rains from washing away topsoil.
ga: Dabi, jeee be fɛɛ be ehe baahia ni ojie tso fɛɛ tso. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei komɛi biɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa moŋ, Shi tsei ni akɛhaa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ baanyɛ abu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Tsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya tsɔ. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Do the heavy roots of old forest trees steal food and water from my young crops?
ga: Ani tsei momo lɛ ashishifãi ni he wa lɛ miiju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli?

english: Yes, large tree roots spread far and deep, pulling away much of the moisture and plant food in the soil. Clearing heavy tree roots from your planting area gives your young crops full access to the nutrients they need.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tso agbo ko shishifãi gbɛ eshwa shɔŋŋ kɛ shɔŋŋ. Ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ojie tsei shishifãi ni tsii kɛjɛ he ni okwɛɔ lɛ lɛ, ebaaha onibii bibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does water coming from an overhead pipe or heavy rainfall affect my crop leaves and soil?
ga: Te nu ni jɛɔ paipii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa mitso lɛ baai kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Overhead water cools the crops and washes leaves, but if the flow is too forceful or continuous, it can wash away rich topsoil, damage fragile young shoots, and create damp conditions that invite plant diseases.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ yiteŋ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli jɔɔ ni efɔɔ baai lɛ ahe. Shi kɛji akɛ nu lɛ hoɔ waa tsɔ loo eyaa nɔ tsɔ Nu lɛ baanyɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ. Fitemɔ ni baa oblahii kɛ oblayei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ anɔ. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni baanyɛ ekɛ tsei ahelai aba lɛ baa

english: Why do the roots of my crops rot when water sits on my field for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ashishifãi fiteɔ kɛ́ ashi nu yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air in the soil to breathe. When standing water covers the soil for too long, it cuts off air to the roots, causing them to suffocate, turn soft, and rot.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli, efeɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ.

english: How can I tell if my plants are receiving enough sunlight on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mitsei lɛ miiná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If plants are not getting enough light, they will stretch tall and thin towards any open sky, and their leaves will look light green or yellow. Well-lit plants stay sturdy with deep green leaves.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni agbele naa lɛ nɔ. Ni baai lɛ yɛ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ. Tsei ni kane fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ mli lɛ baaná hewalɛ ni amɛbaaná baai ni tsuɔ waa.

english: What happens to newly cleared forest soil after it is exposed to strong sunlight?
ga: Mɛni baa koo mli shikpɔŋ ni ajie ehee lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ eshɛ enɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Newly cleared forest soil is rich in natural leaf food, but direct sun heats it up fast, drying out the moisture and causing organic matter to break down quickly. Covering the exposed soil with mulch helps retain that richness.
ga: Koo mli shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ ehee lɛ mli eyi kɛ baai amli niyenii babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔɔ oya, ehaa nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli egbiɔ, ni ehaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɔ nakai emuuyeli lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and stay small even after I clear away all the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛji bibii lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves and slow growth mean the soil is low on essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil is too hard for roots to spread. Feeding the soil with compost or fertilizer will help plants regain their green color and grow.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená eŋɔli su ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why is it helpful for me to visit a demonstration farm before trying a new crop on my own land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ maya ŋmɔ ko ni afeɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ mli dani maka ŋmɔshi nibii hee ko makwɛ yɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Demonstration farms let you observe practical techniques and crop behavior firsthand. Seeing how experienced farmers clear land, space crops, and manage water helps you avoid expensive mistakes on your own farm.
ga: Nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ŋmɔji haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ tsei akwɛmɔ gbɛi kɛ sui lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Ehi waa akɛ ooona bɔ ni okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ jieɔ shikpɔŋ, amɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni amɛkwɛɔ nu nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tɔmɔi ni jara wa he yɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ oŋmɔ mli?

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields when I plant them very close to each other to save space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni mikɛha he ko akafee nɔ ko lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight one another for limited sunlight, root space, soil food, and water. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to grow full and produce high yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baawuu koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, shishifãi ahe he, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: If I plant tree crops like cocoa or cashew, how many years can I expect them to keep producing fruit for me?
ga: Kɛji midu tsei tamɔ kookoo loo cashew nuts lɛ, Afii enyiɛ mli manyɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ tsei nɛɛ baawo yibii aha mi?

english: Tree crops usually have a very long life cycle, often producing fruit for 25 to 30 years or more if you care for them well, making them a long-term investment for your family.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe tsei lɛ wala be kakadaŋŋ waa. Bei pii lɛ, amɛhiɔ shi afii 25 kɛyashi 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kɛji okwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ha efee shika ni okɛwoɔ oweku lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How long does it usually take for long-term tree crops to give a full harvest after planting?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani tso ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baakpa kwraa beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: While short-term crops like maize produce in months, tree crops take a few years to start bearing fruit, but once mature, they continue to give reliable harvests for over two decades.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli moŋ, Shi tsei heɔ afii fioo komɛi dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Shi beni amɛdara kwraa lɛ Tsei nɛɛ etee nɔ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ nɔ ni fe afii nyɔŋmai enyɔ nɛ.

english: How do I know when my old cocoa or palm trees have reached the end of their lifespan?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo tso loo mi-palm tso momo lɛ eshɛ esɛɛnamɔ shihilɛ naagbee?

english: When trees reach the end of their natural life cycle—usually around 25 years—their fruit yields start to drop significantly even with good care, signaling that it is time to replant new seedlings.
ga: Kɛ tso ko shɛ ebɔɔ su shihilɛ naagbee Be ko sɛɛ (bei pii lɛ aaafee afii 25) lɛ, tso lɛ yibiiwoo baaje shishi eba shi waa, kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ po. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui heei.

english: Why is it so important to give special care to my crop seedlings when they are still very young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ beni amɛdarako kwraa lɛ?

english: Young crops are fragile and vulnerable; nurturing them well with shade, water, and weed control early on establishes strong roots that allow the plant to survive for many years and give high yields.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛhe waaa. Ehe miihia ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ shade, nu, kɛ jwɛi ni agbeɔ mra lɛ nɔ. Ewajeɔ shishifãi lɛ, ni no yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi afii babaoo ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: What happens if I plant tree crops and leave them to grow on their own without nursing them?
ga: Kɛ́ midu tso ni miha eda lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni mikwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ, mɛni baaba?

english: If you do not nurture young trees, pests, weeds, and strong sunlight can stunt their growth or kill them, preventing them from ever reaching their full harvest potential.
ga: Kɛji okwɛɛɛ tsei bibii, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, jwɛi, kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ nɔ Ebaanyɛ eha amɛdalɛ afee mlɛo loo egbe amɛ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, amɛnyɛŋ amɛkpa amɛŋmɔshi nii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds harm my young seedlings so much more than full-grown trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ awui fe mi tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have small roots and compete directly with weeds for food, water, and sunlight, whereas older trees have deep roots and larger leaves that block out weeds.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛkɛ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la, yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai wuji ni tsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa.

english: How can I protect my new crop seedlings from dying during the dry season in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu tsei ahe dumɔwui heei ahe koni amɛkagboi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli yɛ Ghana?

english: You can protect young plants from heat stress during the dry season by watering them regularly, placing grass mulch around their base to trap moisture, and providing partial shade.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he yɛ hɔmɔ be mli kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha amɛ daa lɛ nɔ. Okɛ mulch awo shishigbɛ lɛ he koni ekɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni ekɛ hulutsoo be ko aha

english: Why should I trim off some of the branches from my trees while they are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tso niji komɛi yɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or excess branches so the plant doesn't waste energy, allowing sunlight and air to reach the tree and encouraging bigger, healthier fruit growth.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni egboi loo ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ koni tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe. ni eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Do I still need to feed the soil with manure or fertilizer after my trees are already full-grown?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo beni tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, long-lasting crops draw food from the soil every year; adding compost or fertilizer regularly replaces lost nutrients so the tree stays strong and produces well throughout its lifespan.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Kompost loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he daa lɛ baaye niyenii ni elaaje lɛ najiaŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ mli wa ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai yɛ ewala be fɛɛ mli.

english: Can I plant short-term food crops like plantain or vegetables next to my young tree seedlings?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii ni heɔ be kukuoo, tamɔ plantains loo aduawai, yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, planting quick-growing crops alongside young tree seedlings provides you with food and income while giving the small trees useful shade as they develop.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni oookwɛ yɛ dumɔwui bibii ahe lɛ baaha oná niyenii kɛ shika. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. be mli ni edaa lɛ hu

english: Yellowing that starts from the bottom leaves and moves upward usually means your soil is low in nitrogen. The maize plant naturally pulls nitrogen from its older leaves to keep the young, growing leaves on top alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baa lɛ shishi ni eyaa ŋwɛi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni eha baai bibii lɛ aya nɔ akwɛ̃ yɛ nɔ lolo.

english: Why does planting cowpeas together with my maize make the land better for the next planting season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni mikɛ mi ŋmãa duɔ lɛ haa mi ŋmãa lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ ŋmãa be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes with special root nodules that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which acts as natural food for your next batch of crops.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive under direct, intense sunlight because their tender leaves burn and dry out quickly. They need shade trees or food crops like plantain to protect them during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains koni ebu amɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop and curl during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ harmattan be ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains naturally fold and split their leaves during dry weather to reduce water loss. This self-defense behavior helps the plant save moisture until the rains return.
ga: Plantains lɛ fɔ̃ɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛjaraa amɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Nɛkɛ hebuu su nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my sweet pepper flowers keep falling off without growing into pepper fruits during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bell pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ pepper aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, pepper plants drop their flowers because extreme heat damages pollen and prevents fruit from setting properly.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi ejaakɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen lɛ ni ehaaa aduawai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when there is too much rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ? Ani nugbɔ miinɛ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Excess water fills up all the tiny air spaces in the soil, suffocating the cassava roots and allowing waterborne fungi to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ amli, ni ehaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni oha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ atutua ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfite.

english: Why do many tiny flowers on my cocoa tree drop off without growing into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of blossoms, but drop most of them if tiny midges do not pollinate them or if the tree lacks enough water and soil nutrients to feed all the developing pods.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi amɛteŋ babaoo baagbee shi kɛji akɛ atswaaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ loo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baaye abua ŋmeii fɛɛ ni miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil, usually because watering is irregular or the soil dried out while fruits were forming.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ ji nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster after I burn my cleared farm plot instead of clearing without fire?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa yɛ be mli ni mishã ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ sɛɛ fe nɔ ni mishã ni la bɛ mli lɛ?

english: The heat from burning triggers buried weed seeds to wake up and germinate all at once, while destroying the natural plant cover that would normally block weeds from getting sunlight.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ la ni ashãa lɛ mli lɛ ha jwɛi dumɔwui ni afu lɛ te shi ni amɛkwɛ̃ shikome. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kulɛ ebaatsi jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaná hulu la lɛ ahiɛ.

english: How do I know if my yam setts are healthy enough to sprout properly after planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Healthy yam setts should feel firm to the touch, have dry and clean cuts, show visible growing buds or 'eyes' on the skin, and have no signs of soft wet rot or insect holes.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ afee nɔ ni wa kɛji mɔ ko ta he. Pilamɔ lɛ mli egbi ni ehe tse. Ayɛ ŋmeii loo ‘hiŋmɛii’ ni miida yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ ni okadi ko bɛ ni tsɔɔ akɛ egbo loo kooloi bibii ni mli efɔ.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my plantain plants when grass covers the soil well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ beni jwɛi shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with plantains for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds allows the plantain roots to absorb all available nourishment so the plant can grow big and produce a strong harvest.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ plantains yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa plantain shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ adara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa.

english: If I leave weeds growing near my main crop, will it reduce the size of my harvest?
ga: Kɛji mishi jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔ titri lɛ masɛi Ani ebaaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayibɔ aba shi?

english: Yes, heavy weed growth starves your main crop of essential nutrients and moisture, which leads to stunted plant growth and smaller, lower-quality produce.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi ni yaa hiɛ waa lɛ baajie niyenii kɛ nu ni he hia tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii ni ehiii kwraa.

english: Do I need to completely clear my plot before planting plantains, or can I plant directly among existing bush?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni majie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ dani madu dumɔwui? Aloo obaanyɛ odu yɛ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ momo lɛ ateŋ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Clearing the land before planting gives young plantain suckers an ideal start without competing with aggressive wild plants for sunlight, space, and soil food.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ dani adu lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ basabasa lɛ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, ŋwɛi, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii.

english: What happens to my plantain crops if I add plenty of manure or fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi plantain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii babaoo wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Plantains are heavy feeders. Adding rich nutrients helps the plant grow a thick stem and large leaves, which directly leads to bigger, healthier bunches of fruit.
ga: Plantains ji niyenii ni tsii. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa babaoo ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa kɛ baai wuji. Enɛ kɛ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How does keeping my farm clean and fertilizing the soil lead to better quality plantains?
ga: Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔ lɛ mli tse ni mikɛ sũ lɛ awo mli lɛ baaha mi-plantains lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: When a plantain plant doesn't have to fight weeds for food and receives extra soil nutrients, it puts all its energy into swelling the fruit fingers, making them large and delicious.
ga: Beni ehe ehiaaa ni plantains lɛ kɛ jwɛi awui koni amɛna niyenii ni amɛná niyenii krokomɛi ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛha aduawai lɛ aniji lɛ agbɔjɔ. Feemɔ amɛ agboi ni amɛ ŋɔɔ.

english: How can I tell if my plantain plant is receiving enough nutrients from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi dumɔwui lɛ miiná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: A well-nourished plantain plant develops deep green, broad leaves, a sturdy trunk, and produces large, full bunches when it flowers.
ga: Plantains ni ayeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni ji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ. tso ni mli wa Ni kɛ́ efɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaaje kpo yɛ kui wuji amli ni ebaayi tso muu lɛ fɛɛ mli obɔ.

english: Should I feed the soil right when I plant my suckers or wait until the plant grows big?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmeii loo mamɛ kɛyashi tsei lɛ adara?

english: Providing nutrient-rich soil right from planting gives young shoots the energy to establish strong roots, which sets the foundation for a giant plant later on.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli ni akɛaaha kɛjɛ dumɔ mli lɛ baaha tsei bibii lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛshishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃. Enɛ baato shishitoo kɛha tsei wuji ni baaba sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: How long does it usually take for a plantain crop to yield fruit after planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani dumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii beni adu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: With proper weed control, adequate water, and good soil nutrients, a plantain plant typically produces mature fruit within 12 to 15 months.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akwɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ Nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ baawo yibii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 mli.

english: Why do some tree crops take many years to produce results while plantains yield much faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni plantains woɔ yibii oya kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantains are fast-growing herbaceous plants that focus energy on rapid fruit production within a year, whereas long-term tree crops spend years building thick trunks and deep roots to bear fruit for decades.
ga: Plantains ji tsei ni yɔɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ yibii ni amɛwoɔ oya yɛ afi kome mli lɛ he nii. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ, amɛwoɔ yibii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: I want a crop that provides food and money quickly for my family rather than waiting for years—is plantain a good choice?
ga: Miitao tso ko ni baaha miweku lɛ aná niyenii kɛ shika oya moŋ fe ni mamɛ afii babaoo. Ani plantain ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, plantain is a great choice because good farm maintenance allows you to harvest mature food bunches in just over a year, providing quick returns compared to long-term tree crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ kɛji okwɛ ŋmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ obaanyɛ oná ŋmaa ni eda yɛ nɔ ni fe afi pɛ mli. Enɛ haa sɛɛnamɔ baa oya kɛ akɛto tsei ni aduɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them in a bare, open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse, ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense heat from the sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain next to them creates living umbrellas that shade the seedlings and keep the soil moist until the cocoa is mature enough to withstand full sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo tsei ni yɔɔ wala mli ni haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hulutsoo be lɛ naa.

english: Why should I cover the dry earth around my cabbage and vegetable roots with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle kaabii kɛ shishifãi ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves—called mulching—acts like a blanket. It stops soil moisture from evaporating quickly in the sun, prevents weeds from popping up, and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi haa - ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching - lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ mli nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekaje kpo ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops turning light yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food green plants need to grow strong leaves. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea will help restore their green color and health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei eŋɔli koni baai lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ená hewalɛ kpakpa.

english: How does growing cowpeas or groundnuts make my land better for maize next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have tiny beneficial bacteria on their roots that draw nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. When the crops harvest, that nitrogen stays behind to fertilize the next crop naturally.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ helai bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji akpa tsei lɛ Nitrogen baakã he ahi shi koni ekɛha tso lɛ aná ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot when the rains become too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays waterlogged for too long because the roots cannot breathe and fungi easily grow in excess water. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Ni ŋmɔtɔ daa oya kɛ́ nu babaoo yɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers before any tomatoes actually grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miishwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani tomato lɛ eda diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants often drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress or prolonged dry periods. Ensuring regular watering during hot weather prevents the plant from getting stressed and dropping its flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo latsaa mli loo amɛhe egbi be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ akahao ni eha efɔfɔi lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and develop small ears if I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ toi bibii kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to feed and grow large cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Fertilizer feeds any plant growing in the soil, including weeds. If you do not clear weeds before applying fertilizer, the weeds will steal the food meant for your crops and overtake the farm.
ga: Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii haa tsei fɛɛ ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii. Jwɛi fata he. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ baaju niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni ebaaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are there ragged holes chewed into the center whorl of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ ŋmei ni atsɔ mli yɛ amɛteŋ lɛ?

english: This leaf damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that burrows into the growing center of maize. Catching them early and applying safe insect control prevents them from destroying the whole field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni shwieɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ tsui mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite jɛmɛ fɛɛ.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips, which spread plant viruses. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves flat and healthy so the plant can produce fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips. ni gbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tsei amli Nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa bɔni afee ni tso lɛ awo yibii.

english: Why should I plant my crops in neat rows instead of just planting them randomly across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo nɔ moŋ fe ni madu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ trukaa lɛ?

english: Planting in intentional rows creates clear order on your land. It makes it easier to walk through the farm, apply fertilizers, remove weeds, and harvest without damaging your crops.
ga: Dumɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa gbɛjianɔtoo kɛ gbɛjianɔtoo baa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ooonyiɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, okɛ jwɛi awo mli, ni okpa ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni ofiteee oŋmɔshi nibii

english: Do I always need to pull ropes and drive pegs into the ground to get straight rows before planting?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni magbala kpãa lɛ be fɛɛ be ni mikɛ ŋtayaa awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni mafee ŋtayaai ni ja dani madu?

english: No, you do not always need to use ropes and pegs. If you use a mechanical seed planter, the machine forms straight rows automatically as it moves, saving you from doing pre-lining manually.
ga: Dabi, jeee be fɛɛ be kpãa kɛ ŋmeii he hiaa bo. Kɛji akɛ okɛ tsɔne ni akɛduɔ dumɔwui miitsu nii lɛ Tsɔne lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baato ehe gbɛjianɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ beni enyiɛɔ lɛ. Ehereɔ bo kɛjɛɔ pre-lining lɛ ni bo diɛŋtsɛ obaafee lɛ mli.

english: How does keeping equal space between crop rows help my plants grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbɛ ni kã tsei akutsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ ni oooha ehi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mitsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Proper row spacing ensures that every plant gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and water without competing heavily with nearby crops, leading to healthier growth and better harvests.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ akaŋ waa Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ekpaa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is a planting machine, and how does it save me time during planting season?
ga: Mɛni ji dumɔ nii? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua ni akɛ be akafite yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: A planting machine, or planter, opens the soil, drops seeds at regular distances, and covers them up in straight rows as it moves. It completes planting rapidly without needing extra workers to measure lines beforehand.
ga: Mɔ ni duɔ nii loo mɔ ni duɔ nii lɛ baagbele shikpɔŋ lɛ. Dumɔ dumɔwui yɛ be kɛ bei amli. ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni ja mli yɛ be mli ni enyiɛɔ lɛ Agbeɔ dumɔ naa oya ni ehe ehiaaa ni nitsulɔi krokomɛi afata he koni amɛsusu ŋta lɛ he dani.

english: How can I reduce the number of laborers I need to hire when setting up my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafo nitsulɔi ayibɔ ni esa akɛ maŋɔ amɛ beni mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ toɔ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Using a mechanical seed planter eliminates the manual labor required for measuring, pulling ropes, and digging individual holes, allowing you to plant large areas with very few people.
ga: Kɛ akɛ tsɔne ni akɛduɔ dumɔwui tsu nii lɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ niji atsu nii kɛsusu, agbala kpãi, ni atsa bu fɛɛ bu. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ hei wuji ni gbɔmɛi fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: Is using a seed planter suitable for a farmer who doesn't know how to do technical field measurement?
ga: Ani dumɔwui adumɔ tsɔne ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ sa okwaafoi ni leee bɔ ni asusuɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ahe yɛ ŋaa gbɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, seed planters are designed to make straight rows automatically without requiring technical knowledge or complex pre-lining techniques from the farmer.
ga: Hɛɛ, afee dumɔwui adumɔ tsɔnei koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfee ŋwɛi ŋta ni ja. Ebiii ŋaa nilee loo ŋaa ni mli wa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ dani ashɛɔ ŋmɔshi nii kɛjɛɔ okwaafoi adɛŋ.

english: How does planting crops in straight lines make chemical spraying easier on my farm?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ aha miŋmɔ lɛ mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ afee mlɛo?

english: Straight rows leave wide, clear pathways for you to walk or drive through with spraying equipment. This ensures you spray all crops evenly without accidentally missing areas or stepping on young plants.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ yɛ gbɛjegbɛi ni mli tse ni abaanyɛ atsɔ mli loo atsɔ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ he ko kwraa shwieee shi loo okɛ onaji shwieee tsei bibii anɔ yɛ oshara mli.

english: What is a boom sprayer, and how does it work on a crop field?
ga: Mɛni ji boom tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ? Ni te amɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔji amli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: A boom sprayer is a spraying machine with long extended arms fitted with nozzles. It allows you to spray liquid fertilizer or pesticides over multiple rows of crops at the same time.
ga: Boom sprayer ji tsɔne ko ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ ni nine kakadaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ yɔɔ mli. Ehaa okɛ nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo anɔ shikome.

english: Why works best to use a boom sprayer on a field planted in rows rather than a scattered field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ boom sprayer atsu nii yɛ hei ni adu yɛ sɛɛkuu mli moŋ fe hei ni egbɛ eshwã lɛ?

english: A boom sprayer requires open pathways to move smoothly. When crops are planted in straight rows, the machine can pass down the field without crushing plants or tangling its long spray arms.
ga: Esa akɛ boom sprayers lɛ aná gbɛ ni agbele nɔ koni amɛya nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ ookwɛ tsei yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ Tsɔne lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji amli ni etswaaa tsei loo ekɛ e-spray shaft kakadaŋŋ lɛ ebɔko.

english: Will planting in clear rows help me control weeds on my farm more easily?
ga: Ani dumɔ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni agbele mli lɛ baaye abua mi ni manyɛ makudɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mlɛo?

english: Yes, because rows create defined spaces between crops, allowing you to clearly see and clear weeds manually or with machinery without accidentally cutting down your crop stems.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ rows feɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ mli yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ. Ehaa onyɛɔ onaa jwɛi lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ onine loo tsɔne jieɔ amɛ ni okɛ tsɔne efooo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ oshara mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer around the base helps restore green leaves and boost yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii baafata he lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I bother weeding around my cassava plants once they are already tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Mi yucca tso lɛ be mli ni ekwɛ momo lɛ?

english: Even tall cassava plants lose nutrients, water, and soil space to fast-growing weeds. Keeping the ground clear around the stems ensures all the food in the soil goes down into developing large cassava tubers.
ga: Cassava tsei kakadaji po laajeɔ niyenii, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ kɛhaa jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ. He ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Kɛ́ oha tso lɛ yibii lɛ agbele lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aya shi ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: How can I tell if my pepper crop is getting too much water from the rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-pepper tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo kɛmiijɛ nugbɔ lɛ mli?

english: When pepper plants get too much water, their leaves wilt, turn light green or yellow, and start falling off because the soaked roots cannot breathe. Ensuring good soil drainage helps protect them during heavy rains.
ga: Kɛji pepper tsei lɛ ná nu babaoo lɛ Baai lɛ baagboi. Tsakemɔ kɛya ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ Ni ebɔi gbee ejaakɛ shishifãi ni efɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛ́ akwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu amɛhe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the daytime heat is too high, when the soil dries out completely, or when there are no insects around to pollinate them. Consistent watering during dry weeks helps save the blooms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii bɛ he ni amɛbaawo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa yɛ otsii ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔii lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why is it beneficial to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground through their roots. Planting them refreshes your soil naturally so your next grain crop grows much stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Tsei nɛɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ odumɔwui ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ waa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees are planted too close, their leaves block sunlight from each other and their roots fight for nutrients. Crowding also traps damp air, which leads to diseases like black pod disease.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Baai tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa ni shishifãi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ hu mɔ̃ɔ. ni kɛ helai tamɔ black pod hela baa

english: What causes my yam tubers to grow twisted and bent instead of straight and large?
ga: Mɛni haa mi sweet potato tubers lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ebɔleɔ ehe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ja ni eda?

english: Yam tubers twist when they encounter hard, compact soil or buried rocks while pushing downward. Clearing stones and building high, soft soil mounds gives the yams room to grow smooth, straight tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ baatsɔ kɛji akɛ akɛmiimɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni mli edɔ nɔ loo akɛ tɛi wo mli. Tɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ gɔji kakadaji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa sweet potatoes ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛfeɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do caterpillars seem to attack my vegetable crops more during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii babaoo tutuaa mi-aduawai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The warm humidity and abundance of fresh, tender foliage in the rainy season create perfect breeding conditions for butterflies and moths to lay eggs that hatch into hungry caterpillars.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni mli edɔ kɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ babaoo ni yɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii fɔmɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni amɛwo amɛwui ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my soil become dry and cracked just a day or two after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ egbi ni egbɛ eshwa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil dries out quickly when exposed directly to the hot sun without organic matter to hold water. Covering bare soil with dry leaves or grass mulch keeps moisture trapped underground much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni nɔ ko bɛ ni baaha nu ahi mli lɛ shɛ enɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo ŋmɔtɔ shwie shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How does cutting off extra suckers help my plantain plants produce bigger bunches?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi plantain lɛ ni ehaa jwɛi wulu baa?

english: Each sucker steals food and water from the main mother plantain. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, forcing all the plant's energy into developing a larger, heavier fruit bunch.
ga: Sucker lɛ eko fɛɛ eko juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ aba ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enyɛɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ nɔ koni etsɔ aduawai akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do people always advise me to plant plantain together with cocoa on a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa be fɛɛ be akɛ mikɛ plantains ni akɛ kookoo ewo mli lɛ adu yɛ ŋmɔji heei amli lɛ?

english: Plantains grow much faster than cocoa trees and provide early shade that protects young cocoa seedlings from harsh sunlight. They also give you early food and income while you wait for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Plantains daa oya fe cacao tsei ni amɛhaa mra be mli hulutsoo be ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Amɛhaa bo niyenii kɛ shika hu be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and small root systems that cannot handle direct, strong sunlight. Without shade from companion plants like plantains or shade trees, hot sun dries out the plant and soil faster than the roots can drink water.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko bɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni fata he tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ahe lɛ Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa tsei kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu.

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start flowering and bearing small pods in 2 to 3 years, while older traditional varieties can take 4 to 5 years before producing their first crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahe afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛwo amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ.

english: Can I keep growing plantains on the exact same spot year after year without moving them?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ plantains yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi ni mikɛ amɛ eyaaa he kroko?

english: Over time, plantains remove heavy nutrients from the soil, and soil-borne pests like nematodes build up around the roots. Yields will start to drop, so refreshing the soil, managing suckers, or rotating crops keeps production high.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Plantains jieɔ niyenii ni tsii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes lɛ baabua amɛhe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni yibiiwoo lɛ baaje shishi eba shi. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsakemɔ Bud nɔkwɛmɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli tsakemɔ, ni no haa nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Does applying fertilizer to my cocoa trees really make a big difference in how many pods I harvest?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni mikɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ tsakeɔ ŋmeii ayibɔ ni mikpaa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, every time you harvest cocoa pods, nutrients are removed from the soil. Fertilizers replace key nutrients like potassium and phosphorus, which helps trees form more flowers, resist diseases, and grow bigger pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa kookoo ŋmɔtɔ. Ajieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium kɛ phosphorus najiaŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi babaoo, eshiɔ helai, ni ehaa ŋmɔji lɛ daraa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the tree lacks essential nutrients in the soil, is suffering from long periods of drought, or is under attack by pests like capsids or diseases like cocoa swollen shoot.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Piŋmɔ ni jɛɔ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ mli baa. aloo kɛtsɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids loo helai tamɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn completely black and rot on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy weather when water stays on the pods. Clearing weeds, pruning branches for air flow, and spraying approved fungicides helps control it.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ mli. weeding Tsei ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli Ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ jwɛi lɛ.

english: What causes my plantain trees to fall over easily whenever a strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni haa mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi mlɛo be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that can easily be weakened by root-eating pests like nematodes and weevils. Supporting heavy fruiting stems with bamboo poles and treating root pests helps keep the plant upright.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ shishifãi tamɔ nematodes kɛ weevils baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii fiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ asɛɛ, ni atsaa shishifãi amli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why should I prune the extra branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso ni eda lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or excess branches so the tree can focus its energy on growing healthy fruit instead of extra leaves. It also allows light and air to pass through, reducing disease-causing dampness.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni egboi loo ni fa fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe baai krokomɛi ni ekɛbaafata he lɛ. Ehaa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hu tsɔɔ mli. Ha hulutsoo ni kɛ hela baa lɛ aba shi

english: Why do extension officers tell us to reduce tall shade trees on old cocoa farms instead of leaving them fully dense?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔfo tsei kakadaji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ momo ko mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa lɛ.

english: While young cocoa needs heavy shade, mature cocoa needs dappled sunlight to produce maximum pods. Too much shade traps moisture, promoting fungal diseases like black pod and reducing overall harvest.
ga: yɛ be mli ni kookoo gbekɛ lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ni mli wa. Kookoo ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Shade babaoo baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods baa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my crops producing lower yields even though I plant on the same land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi moŋ?

english: Over time, crops absorb essential nutrients from the soil to grow. If you do not replenish these nutrients using fertilizers like NPK, the land gets tired and produces smaller harvests.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK tsuuu nii ekoŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ebaawo yibii babaoo.

english: Will applying chemical fertilizer to my farm destroy or ruin my soil over time?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baafite loo ebaafite mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: No, fertilizer will not harm your land if it is used correctly according to instructions. It simply replaces the natural nutrients that your crops harvested from the soil.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii yeŋ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ awui kɛji akɛ okɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ taakɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi tsɔɔ lɛ. Ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni oŋmɔshi nibii kpataa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ najiaŋ kɛkɛ.

english: How does feeding nutrients to the land help me get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni mikɛyeɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni makpã nii babaoo?

english: Just like people need good food to work hard, crops need plant nutrients to develop strong stems, healthy leaves, and large fruits, which leads to a bigger yield at harvest time.
ga: Taakɛ gbɔmɛi sumɔɔ niyenii kpakpa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. koni etsu nii waa Dumɔwui hu he miihia tsei amli niyenii koni amɛná ŋmeii ni wa, baai ni wa, kɛ aduawai wuji. Enɛ haa anáa yibii babaoo yɛ kpamɔ be mli.

english: What does NPK mean when people talk about crop fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni ji NPK shishi kɛji gbɔmɛi wie ŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: NPK stands for Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Potassium. These are the three main nutrients that crops must eat to grow well and yield high harvests.
ga: NPK damɔ shi kɛha naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasiam. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii titrii etɛ ni esa akɛ tsei aye koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my crops need nitrogen to grow well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitrogen he hiaa mi tsei lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Nitrogen is the main nutrient that gives plants healthy green leaves and strong stems. Without enough nitrogen, leaves turn yellow and growth slows down.
ga: Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. Kɛji nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdalɛ baafee mlɛo.

english: What work does phosphorus do in the soil for my crops?
ga: Mɛni fɔsfɔs feɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Phosphorus helps plants grow deep, strong roots when they are young, and helps them develop flowers and healthy seeds as they mature.
ga: Fosfɔs yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa beni amɛdarako lɛ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui ni mli wa kɛ́ amɛmiida.

english: Why is potassium important for my crops during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ potassium he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Potassium helps crops manage water inside their stems, making them stronger against drought, heat, and plant diseases.
ga: Potassium yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkwɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Ehaa ehe waa kɛshiɔ hɔmɔ, dɔlɛ, kɛ tsei ahe helai.

english: How can I tell if my farm land is lacking nitrogen?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nitrogen bɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli?

english: If your plant leaves look pale green or yellow instead of dark green, and the plants remain small and stunted, your soil is likely low in nitrogen.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Ni tsei lɛ yɛ bibii lolo ni amɛgbɔjɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it safe for me to follow the advice of agricultural researchers when choosing fertilizer?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ manyiɛ okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi aŋaawoo sɛɛ kɛ́ mihala ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, researchers and extension officers test soil and plants to guide you on which nutrients your land needs so you can get high yields without damaging your field.
ga: Hɛɛ, niiamlitaolɔi kɛ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kaa shikpɔŋ kɛ tsei amɛkwɛɔ koni amɛwo bo ŋaa yɛ niyenii ni he hiaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ oná yibii babaoo ni okpataaa oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why does my neighbor's land give more crops than mine even when we plant at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo shikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe mi nɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ wɔduɔ yɛ be kome mli moŋ?

english: Different soils have different levels of nutrients. If your neighbor adds essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium to their soil, their crops will grow faster and produce more.
ga: Shikpɔji srɔtoi yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛi srɔtoi. Kɛji okutsoŋnyo lɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni amɛbaawo yibii babaoo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green leaf growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen out of the soil, so adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea will help your maize stay green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua o-ŋmei lɛ ni ehi shi ŋmɔŋ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my pepper crop produce small, weak fruits even though I give them plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu babaoo moŋ?

english: Water alone is not enough; pepper plants need balanced soil nutrients like phosphorus and potassium to grow large, healthy fruits. If the soil lacks rich organic matter or balanced fertilizer, the plant will not have the energy to build big peppers.
ga: Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa. Pepper tsei hia niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasiam. Koni adu aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa Tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛduɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Transplanted plantain suckers spend their early months building a strong root system underground before growing leaves and fruit above ground. Clearing weeds around the base and mulching with dry leaves keeps the soil moist and speeds up their growth.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu lɛ baahe be fioo yɛ shishijee mli dani amɛdara. Koni afee shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni mli wa Dani abaadu baai kɛ aduawai yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he kɛ baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shweremɔ yaa hiɛ.

english: This is called Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during damp, rainy conditions. Pruning excess shade tree branches to let sunlight and fresh air reach the cocoa trees helps dry out moisture and stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ kookoo tso lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ akafee ŋmɔtɔ ni ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa.

english: Cassava roots rot in heavy rain when water gets trapped in flat soil, cutting off oxygen to the roots and encouraging rot diseases. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa kɛ nu tsɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa lɛ faaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the leaves of my yam plants curling up with tiny insects hiding underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni kooloi bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? Akɛtee shishi?

english: The leaf curling is caused by tiny sap-sucking insects called aphids that attach to the underside of leaves and drink the plant's sap. Spraying your crops with a mild soap-and-water mixture or organic neem oil will clear the insects away.
ga: Koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ akpokpomɔ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ aphids Ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni enuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ samla kɛ nu ni mli ejɔ Loo organic neem fɔ shwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akashɛ he.

english: Why do caterpillars attack my cowpea flowers right when the plant starts flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ kɛji tsei lɛ je shishi amɛfɔ̃ɔ pɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers attract pod-boring moths that lay eggs in the flower buds so their caterpillars can feed on young pods. Inspecting your field early and applying neem extract or approved pest controls at the first sign of flowering will protect your yield.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ aye ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Odumɔi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ewo fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants experience extreme heat or dry soil stress, which prevents proper pollination. Watering your plants consistently at the base and providing light shade during extremely hot afternoons keeps flowers healthy so they turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli baa lɛ kpe. ni tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa yɛ eshishigbɛ, ni aha lɛ hulutsoo yɛ shwane mli ni edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why should I alternate planting maize and beans on the same piece of land across seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ he kome yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, while maize feeds heavily on soil nitrogen. Rotating these crops naturally restores soil fertility and prevents pests that target only one crop type from building up.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Ejɛɔ adebɔɔ mli emɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa yeɔ nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nibii nɛɛ ni aaatsake lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba ekoŋŋ. ni etsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ tso henɔ kome nɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote shi.

english: Why does planting my crops in neat rows give a better harvest than scattering seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni agbɛɔ ashwãa he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Planting in straight, spaced rows ensures every crop gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing with neighboring plants. Row planting also makes weeding, fertilizing, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja, ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ hu haa jwɛi lɛ akwɛmɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade and moisture to survive. During hot, dry periods like the Harmattan, direct sunlight heats the plant too much, causing it to drop leaves to save water and protect its main stem from drying out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛhi shi. Yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni edɔɔ tamɔ Harmattan lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ adɔ fe nine. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite ni amɛtsi tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ naa koni ekagbi.

english: What causes small green caterpillars to eat holes inside the stems of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm. The caterpillars hide deep inside the leaves and feed on tender stem tissues, which can stunt growth or destroy the crop if not managed early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ shishi fãji bibii lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ dalɛ naa loo efite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra.

english: Why does my cassava produce very tall green leaves but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai eŋɔli ni nɔ kwɔ waa lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: This usually happens when the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or fresh manure. The plant uses all its energy to grow tall branches and foliage instead of sending energy underground to build thick tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii heei babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ niji kɛ baai kakadaji. Mohu ɔ, e tsuɔ he wami kɛ yaa zugba a sisi konɛ e pee yi nɛ mi wa.

english: Why should I cut off extra small shoots growing around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Special ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishi.

english: If too many small shoots (suckers) grow around the main stem, they fight with it for soil nutrients, water, and light. Removing extra suckers leaves only two or three strong ones, allowing the main plant to produce much bigger bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo ni miida yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ Ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ la mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii fioo komɛi pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji babaoo.

english: Groundnuts belong to a plant family called legumes that can take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the dirt. When the groundnut crop is harvested, that natural fertilizer stays in the soil to feed the next maize crop.
ga: Peanuts fata tsei akuu ko ni atsɛɔ amɛ legumes lɛ he. ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmeii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: When is the right time to put fertilizer on my crops so the heavy rain doesn't carry it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni nugbɔ akanɛ waa?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist, but not during heavy downpours or flooding. Splitting the fertilizer into small doses at critical growing stages—such as early growth and flowering—helps the roots soak it up before rain washes it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo nu afua be mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amlijaa yɛ bibii bibii amli Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ ni he hiaa tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ mra kɛ fɔfɔi ni baa lɛ Enɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ aná nu dani nugbɔ lɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: This is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit. It commonly occurs when watering is uneven or when dry spells prevent roots from carrying nutrients from the soil to the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ loo kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Yam leaves need direct light to capture sunlight and convert it into food for the growing tuber underground. Staking holds the leaves up into the light and off the hot ground, leading to healthier leaves and bigger tubers.
ga: La he miihia sweet potato baa lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni enyɛ emɔ hulu la lɛ ni etsɔ niyenii eha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni miida lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ hiɔ la ni tsoɔ waa mli, ni amɛyaa hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ náa hewalɛ kɛ yitsei wuji.

english: Is it better for my pepper plants if I water them in the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mi-pepper tsei lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛmli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: It is best to water early in the morning at the base of the plant. Afternoon heat causes water to evaporate rapidly before reaching the roots, and leaving leaves wet under hot sunshine can burn them and encourage fungal growth.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi yɛ tso lɛ shishi. Gbi gbɛkɛ latsaa lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni ashiɔ baai lɛ ni efɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ ashã ni ewo ŋmeii adalɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers spread dry leaves and grass on top of the soil around their crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ shwieɔ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ lɛ? Amɛŋmɔshi nibii?

english: This practice is called mulching. Spreading dry material keeps the soil cool, prevents moisture from escaping in the sun, stops weeds from growing, and gradually breaks down into natural food for the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Nibii ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekajo foi kɛya hulu lɛ mli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dying when I plant them in an open field with full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. They need temporary shade crops like plantains to act as natural umbrellas until they grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close to one another, the crops compete for sunlight and soil nutrients. The plants waste their energy stretching upwards to reach the sun instead of using that energy to grow big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei fiteɔ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni amɛkpãa kɛyaa hulu lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛdu ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big leafy bushes above ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ yɛ jwɛi wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: Cassava plants put all their energy into leafy growth when the soil has too much nitrogen or excess water. To grow large starch tubers underground, the plant needs balanced nutrients rather than high-nitrogen leafy growth.
ga: Yucca tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛhaa baai lɛ adalɛ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Bɔni afee ni akwɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ starch yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ Tsei biɔ niyenii ni sa jogbaŋŋ fe baai ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to produce bunches when I plant them directly into hard, unplowed soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ ŋmeii beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni mikɛtsuuu nii lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and need loose, soft soil to spread out and absorb food. Hard soil stops the roots from expanding, which slows down the plant's overall growth and delays fruiting.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã. Enɛ haa tso lɛ dalɛ fɛɛ baa shi ni ehaa aduawai lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why do my pepper crops drop all their flowers without producing any peppers during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛ pepper ko baaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers as a survival trick when they suffer from intense heat and lack of moisture. Dropping flowers allows the crop to save its limited water and energy to stay alive until wet conditions return.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛhi shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ fioo ko he koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi be mli ni shihilɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wither fast even when I pour plenty of water on them in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ miigbo oya eyɛ mli akɛ miyɛ Nu babaoo Yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Watering crops during the hot afternoon causes the moisture to evaporate quickly into the hot air before root absorption happens, and heating water in the soil can stress and burn sensitive root tips.
