ga: Kɛ́ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ni kɛ́ akɛ nu ni mli edɔ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli la lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni eha amɛhe afee shoo.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a water-loving fungus that multiplies when rain, high humidity, and dense tree branches trap moisture around the pods for long periods without air circulation.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni sumɔɔ nu. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ, ni hulutsoo be lɛ fa babaoo, ni tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mɔmɔ hulutsoo ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Pods lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and turning yellow during the rainy period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaf curling during wet seasons is usually a sign of a virus spread by tiny insects like whiteflies, which attack plants when warm, humid weather creates ideal conditions for pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Amɛtutuaa tsei kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ, ni no haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and die early if I leave them to trail on the bare ground instead of using wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ gĩɔ ni egboɔ oya kɛji mishi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛ tso ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ baatsu nii lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes to expose their leaves to maximum sunshine and air. Leaving vines on the bare ground exposes leaves to hot soil surfaces, soil pests, and fungal diseases that kill the vine early.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛbaa lɛ aná hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo. Kɛ́ ashi wain tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ ajie shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Kplukai ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ wain tsei lɛ mra.

english: Why do my harvest yields get smaller every year even though I plant the exact same crop in the exact same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiba shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop year after year drains the specific nutrients that crop loves out of the soil. It also lets pests and diseases that target that specific plant build up in the soil permanently.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei sumɔɔ lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ lɛ hu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa.

english: How long can I safely keep my packed cocoa beans in storage before they spoil?
ga: Be enyiɛ manyɛ makɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni awo mli lɛ ato shweshweeshwe dani amɛfite?

english: If cocoa beans are properly dried to about 7% moisture and kept in clean jute bags in a dry, cool room off the ground, they can stay in good condition for several months without going bad.
ga: Kɛji akɛ agbi kookoo yibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli aaafee 7% ni akɛto jute kotokui ni he tse mli yɛ tsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Cocoa ŋmeii baanyɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ nyɔji babaoo ni amɛfiteee.

english: Is it okay to stack my packed cocoa bags directly on a concrete floor in my storehouse?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ akɛ kookoo kotokui ni awo mli lɛ ato kɔnkrit shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi nitoohe lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, concrete floors pull dampness from the ground, which dry cocoa beans will absorb like a sponge, leading to mold and rot. Always stack bags on raised wooden pallets.
ga: Dabi, kɔnkrit shikpɔŋ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ tamɔ sponji Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baa. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ kotokui ato tsei ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa beans develop mold inside the bags even after I thought I dried them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ misusu akɛ migbi amɛ moŋ?

english: Beans mold because they still held hidden moisture inside when you bagged them, or moisture got into the storage area. Trapped moisture creates a warm, damp space where mold grows quickly and ruins the cocoa.
ga: Nuts mold ejaakɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli lolo ni akɛtee beni okɛwoɔ baagi mli lɛ. loo ŋmɔtɔ ni boteɔ he ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ Fɛ̃i ni amɔmɔ lɛ haa he ko ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Fɔ̃ɔ lɛ daa oya ni efiteɔ kookoo lɛ.

english: How can I easily test if my cocoa beans are fully dried and ready to be packed into bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka mikwɛ kɛji mi-kookoo lɛ egbi kwraa ni esa akɛ mikɛwo kotoku mli?

english: Take a handful of beans and squeeze them; if they are properly dry, they will make a sharp crackling sound, and the outer skin will rub off easily without the bean feeling soft or spongy.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni okɛ onine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni okɛmimɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha gbee ni naa wa waa aba. Ni hewolo ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni ehaaaa kɔfi yibii lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ loo ehiɛ ŋmeii.

english: Why must I pack my cocoa in jute bags instead of using plastic sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ kookoo woɔ jute kotokui amli moŋ fe plastic kotokui lɛ?

english: Jute bags allow air to flow through the beans so they can stay cool and dry, whereas plastic bags trap heat and sweat inside, which will quickly spoil your cocoa.
ga: Jute kotokui lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛha amɛhe ajɔɔ ni amɛgbi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, plastic kotokui lɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ kɛ latsaa yɛ mli. Enɛ baaha okokoo lɛ afite oya.

english: Can I mix freshly dried cocoa beans with older beans I stored a few weeks ago in the same bag?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi ehee lɛ afutu momo ni mikɛto otsii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ yɛ kotoku kome mli?

english: It is best not to mix them. Older beans may have absorbed unseen moisture or pests during storage, which can spread to your fresh batch and ruin the overall quality.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ amɛ akafutu. Beans ni egbɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo kooloi ni anaaa lɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kui heei amli ni efite nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: What happens to the cocoa beans if I leave ripe pods hanging on my trees for too long?
ga: Mɛni baa kookoo ŋmeii anɔ kɛji mishi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Overripe pods attract diseases like black pod and pests, and the seeds inside will start to sprout, which reduces their quality and makes them unacceptable to buyers.
ga: Pods ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ gbalaa helai tamɔ pods diji kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baabɔi kwɛ̃mɔ. Enɛ haa nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa mɛi ni heɔ lɛ ekpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa beans turn bitter and flat if I dry them immediately after opening the pods without fermenting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa yibii lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji migbi amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni migbele ŋmeii lɛ amli ni mikɛwooo mli lɛ?

english: Fermentation is what kills the seed inside the bean and triggers the natural chemical reaction that creates the rich chocolate flavor and brown color buyers look for.
ga: Nɔ ni gbeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni gbeɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni haa tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa.

english: How do I prevent insects from attacking my cocoa bags while waiting for the buyer to pick them up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkatutua mi-kookoo kotokui lɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni mɛi ni baahe nii lɛ abaŋɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Keep your storage room clean and dark, seal holes in the building, and keep bags stacked away from walls so pests do not have warm, dark places to hide and multiply.
ga: Ha onitoohe lɛ mli atse ni efee duŋ, ŋamɔ bu fɛɛ bu ni yɔɔ tsu lɛ mli lɛ, ni oha kotokui ni ato amɛhe lɛ akashɛ gbogboi ahe. Enɛ ji koni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akaná he ko ni yɔɔ duŋ ni mli edɔ ni amɛtee amɛhe amɛwo mli ni amɛfɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease caused by a water-loving fungus. Pruning your cocoa trees and clearing weeds helps sunlight and air dry out the farm, stopping the disease from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela ni ŋmei ko ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ kɛbaa. Kookoo tsei lɛ ni afoɔ ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ akashɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ. ni ekpa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ

english: Why does my maize crop mature much faster than my yam crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ miida oya fe mi-sweet potato tso lɛ?

english: Maize is a grain crop with a short life cycle designed to produce seeds within 3 to 4 months. Yams are heavy root tubers that require 8 to 10 months to continuously absorb soil nutrients and store energy underground before they are fully formed.
ga: Abɛi ji ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala be kukuoo ko ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni ekɛ dumɔwui awo yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli. Sweet potatoes ji shishifãi ni tsii ni heɔ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 10 dani enyɛ eŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ be fɛɛ be ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi dani efee kwraa.

english: Why do my yam leaves and vines turn yellow and dry up before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: The yellowing and drying of yam vines is a natural sign of crop maturity. It shows that the plant has stopped growing new leaves and has transferred all its nutrients into the underground tuber for storage.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ nɔ ni egbi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa baai heei ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ, ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ ewo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli koni akɛto.

english: Why do yams need so many months in the ground compared to regular vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ŋmeii ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔji babaoo kɛ akɛto aduawai krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Leafy vegetables only focus on growing leaves and stems above ground, which happens quickly. Yams must build a large, dense tuber beneath the soil, which requires many months of sunlight, water, and leaf activity to swell completely.
ga: Aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ pɛ nɔ, ni no baaba oya. Esa akɛ sweet potatoes afee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii. Akɛ nyɔji babaoo tsuɔ nii yɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ baai anitsumɔ mli dani efuɔ kwraa.

english: Can I harvest some of my yam tubers early and leave the vine to keep growing?
ga: Minyɛ mikpa sweet potato ŋmeii komɛi mra. Ni aha wain tso lɛ aya nɔ eda?

english: Yes, this practice is known as 'milking' or double-harvesting. You can carefully harvest the early mature tuber without damaging the main root system, allowing the vine to produce smaller seed yams later in the season.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ ‘mliki’ loo ŋmaakpamɔ shii enyɔ. Obaanyɛ okpa ŋmeii ni eda lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ofiteee shishifã titri lɛ. Enɛ haa wain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni dumɔwui yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli.

english: Is it better for me to harvest all my yams at once or dig them up bit by bit?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makpa ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ shikome loo mafo amɛ fiofio?

english: Harvesting yams bit by bit leaves the remaining tubers preserved naturally in the dry soil. This prevents storage losses, ensures a steady supply of food for your family, and allows you to sell when market prices are higher.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii bibii bibii lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ baaye abua ni akafite nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Ye obua ni niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa aha oweku lɛ. Ni ehaa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ kɛ́ jara lɛ tee ŋwɛi.

english: How do I know the exact time my yam tubers are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams are ready for full harvest when the above-ground foliage complete dies off during the dry season, and the top neck of the tuber turns brown rather than soft or white.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kwraa kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ. ni tsitsi ni yɔɔ yitso lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ najiaŋ.

english: Why are yams usually harvested after December or January in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, akpaa ŋmeii yɛ December loo January sɛɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: By December and January, the rains have stopped and the yam plant enters dormancy. Starch content inside the tuber peaks during these dry months, making the yams higher quality and less likely to rot after harvest.
ga: Yɛ December kɛ January mli lɛ Nugbɔ lɛ baakpa ni sweet potato tsei lɛ baabote shihilɛ ni mli wa mli. Starch falɛ ni yɔɔ bulb lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli Enɛ haa sweet potato lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni etsɛɛɛ ni efiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Which crops can I count on harvesting during the dry months like March or April?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ makpa yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ tamɔ March loo April mli?

english: Deep-rooted tuber crops like late-season yams and cassava store well underground during dry months like March and April, offering fresh produce before the new rainy season starts.
ga: Akɛ ŋmeii ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni shwereɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ tamɔ March kɛ April mli. Koni akɛ nibii heei aha dani nugbɔshiimɔ be hee lɛ aje shishi.

english: What happens to my maize if I leave it on the farm too long after it dries?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni egbi sɛɛ?

english: Leaving dry maize on the farm for too long exposes the ears to pest infestations like weevils, fungal mold from unexpected dew or rain, and damage from birds or rodents.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmãa ni egbi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha toi lɛ afite kɛtsɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmãa loo nugbɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ nɔ. kɛ nɔ ni okpoi loo ŋmeii fiteɔ lɛ.

english: How does planting early in the rainy season affect when I will harvest my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nidumɔ yɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ saa nikpamɔ be lɛ he?

english: Planting early allows your crops to maximize early rainfall and mature on schedule, letting you harvest fast crops like maize early in the year when market demand and prices are high.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Ye obua onibii ni nugbɔ nɛɔ oya ni amɛdara yɛ be naa. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa oya yɛ afi lɛ shishijee mli be mli ni jarayeli nibii biɔ kɛ jara ni wa lɛ.

english: What happens if I just cut a diseased plant at the stem instead of digging out its roots?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mifo tso ni hela emɔ lɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ eshishifã lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mafo shishifãi lɛ hu?

english: Cutting a plant at the stem leaves the root system alive. The plant will often sprout fresh shoots again from the base, which will still carry the disease and continue to infect nearby crops.
ga: Tsei ni afoɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei ekoŋŋ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ. ni yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ helai ahe nibii ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli

english: Why do old crop stumps start growing new leaves even after I cut them down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso momo lɛ jeɔ baai heei shishi kɛji mifo lɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Many crops store energy in their roots underground, causing them to sprout again at the base unless the entire root system is properly removed or treated.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ babaoo kɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Ha amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛdara yɛ shishigbɛ. ja ajie shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ loo atsa amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I cure a crop disease on my own just by trimming off the bad leaves?
ga: Ani manyɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli helai kɛtsɔ baai gbohii lɛ ni mafolɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Trimming leaves rarely cures a plant disease because the infection usually remains inside the stem and roots, causing infected shoots to grow back at the base.
ga: Baai ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaaa ni etsaa tsei ahelai. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ hiɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa amɛshishi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops keep getting the same disease season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa helai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: The disease is likely surviving in old plant roots and stumps left in the ground. When these stumps re-sprout at the base, they pass the old disease directly to your new crops.
ga: Ekolɛ hela lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ tsei shishifãi momoi kɛ tsei akutsei ni eshwɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ. Kɛji nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ kwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ Amɛbaajie helai momoi kɛya onibii heei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are my new crops getting sick even though I cleared the old diseased plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mijie tsei momo ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ moŋ?

english: If the old diseased plants were not removed completely, they can sprout new growth from the base beneath the soil, carrying the infection straight into your newly planted crops.
ga: Kɛji ojieee tsei momoi fɛɛ ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ, Amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli. ni ekɛ hela lɛ aba tsei ni adu ehee lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ

english: Can a crop disease remain active in old plant stumps when I plant fresh seedlings?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baanyɛ ahi tsei akutsei momo amli kɛ́ midu dumɔwui heei?

english: Yes, diseases can survive inside old stumps and roots. When those stumps sprout again at the base, the disease becomes active and attacks your fresh seedlings.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, helai baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ tsei akutsei kɛ shishifãi momo amli. Kɛ nakai tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ Hela lɛ baatsu nii ni ebaatutua odumɔwui heei lɛ.

english: Is it safe to plant new crops right next to a plant that was recently sick?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu tsei heei yɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ ahe?

english: It is risky because a sick plant can produce new infected shoots from its base that will quickly spread the disease to any neighboring crops.
ga: Oshara yɛ ejaakɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmeii heei ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ, ni baanyɛ agbɛ hela lɛ ashwã tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli oya.

english: How does a disease travel from an old crop to new crops on the same field?
ga: Te helai feɔ tɛŋŋ kɛjɛɔ tsei momoi amli kɛyaa tsei heei ni yɔɔ he kome lɛ amli?

english: When an infected old crop is left in the soil, it sprouts again at the base and acts as a living source of infection that easily jumps to nearby young plants.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi tsei momo ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ekwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ shishigbɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ hela jɛɛhe ni baanyɛ atsɔ mli oya kɛya tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I contact an agricultural officer when I notice a strange disease on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maya okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ aŋɔɔ beni mina hela ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extension officers have the technical knowledge to identify the exact disease and handle it properly so it doesn't re-sprout or destroy your harvest.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ helatsamɔhe lɛ yɛ ŋaa nilee ni amɛkɛyooɔ hela pɔtɛɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii akafee ehee loo okɛfite.

english: What is the best step to take as soon as I see a crop disease spreading on my land?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ matsɔ nɔ kɛji mina tso hela ko ni miigbɛ eshwa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ?

english: You should report it immediately to an extension officer so they can technically treat or remove the infected plants before the disease re-sprouts and spreads across your entire farm.
ga: Esa akɛ obɔ o-extension officer lɛ sane nɛɛ he amaniɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsa loo amɛtsɔ ŋaa gbɛ nɔ amɛjie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Dani hela lɛ baatsake ni egbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong, direct sunshine because their leaves burn easily. Plantains grow very quickly and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving the young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs during its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why am I finding small green caterpillars hiding deep inside the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abɛi bibii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms. Moths lay eggs inside the growing center of the young maize plant, and once the caterpillars hatch, they feed on the soft, hidden leaves before you notice the damage on the outside.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ he ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ. Dani obaana nɔ ni efite yɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ

english: Why are the top leaves of my cassava plants curling up and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ ayitsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. The disease stops the leaves from making food properly, which prevents the roots underneath from growing big.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Kplukai bibii yɛŋ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Hela nɛɛ haaa baai lɛ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ adara.

english: Why are my maize cobs coming out very small when I plant three or four seeds in one single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ beni midu ŋmeii etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water, light, and soil nutrients. Because no single plant gets enough food, all of them end up weak and produce small cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and rot before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛmiitsɔ etsuru lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil, usually because watering is uneven or the soil dried out too quickly while the tomatoes were forming.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee loo shikpɔŋ lɛ ni egbiɔ oya tsɔ be mli ni tomatoi lɛ feɔ lɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to pollinate them so fruits can grow. If the farm is too dry or lacks rotting plant material where midges breed, the flowers remain unpollinated, dry up, and drop off.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ midges akɛ pollinators koni aduawai anyɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo tsei ni fiteɔ lɛ bɛ mli lɛ, biɛ ji he ni dwarfs lɛ fɔɔ yɛ. Fɔfɔi lɛ baakã he ahi shi ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ, amɛbaagbi ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: Why does my land yield less harvest every year even though I use the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Every crop takes food out of the soil to grow. If you plant the same crop on the same piece of land year after year without adding animal manure, compost, or letting the land rest, the soil runs out of nutrients.
ga: Nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ heɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe lɛ fataaa he lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers whenever the sun becomes extremely hot during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ shi be fɛɛ be ni hulu lɛ baadɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Severe heat causes pepper plants to lose water faster than their roots can take it up. To save energy and keep itself alive during hot periods, the plant sheds its flowers so it does not have to feed developing peppers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa chili tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Koni okɛ hewalɛ ato ni oha ohe ahi wala mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do weeds harm my young yam plants more than my fully grown yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiye mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ awui fe mi-sweet potato tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young yam plants have small roots and need full sunlight to grow their early leaves. Weeds steal the sunlight and ground water before the young yam can establish strong stems, whereas tall, mature yam vines can shade out weeds.
ga: Sweet potato tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni ehe hiaa hulu la ni fa bɔni afee ni baai lɛ akwɛ̃ oya. Jwɛi juɔ hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu dani ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ afee ŋmeii ni wa. yɛ be mli ni sweet potato wain tsei ni kɛlɛ ni eda lɛ haa jwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm get very dry and hard just a few days after the rain stops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli egbi ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses moisture quickly to the hot sun. Covering the soil around your crops with dried grass or leaves (mulching) blocks direct sunlight, keeps the ground cool, and traps rain moisture in the dirt much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ enɔ. Mulching around Kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi baaha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe (mulching) lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ nugbɔ mli baa lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ

english: What does it mean when a seed variety is described as a '90-day' corn?
ga: Kɛ́ atsɔɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ko amli akɛ ‘gbii 90’ ŋmãa lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: A 90-day corn variety is an early-maturing crop that completes its growth cycle from planting to harvest in about three months. This helps farmers get food quickly and harvest before late-season droughts begin.
ga: Gbii 90 ŋmãa ji ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra ni egbeɔ edalɛ be lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ dumɔ mli kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ mli yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛnáa niyenii oya ni amɛkpaa dani hɔmɔ ni baa yɛ naagbee be lɛ mli lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Why are there so many different varieties of yam, and how do I choose the right one for my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi babaoo yɔɔ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala nɔ ni sa kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Different yam varieties have unique characteristics; some mature quickly, some store well for months, and others yield better in specific soil types. Choosing the right one depends on whether you want early food, long storage, or market sales.
ga: Sweet potato henɔi srɔtoi yɛ sui pɔtɛɛ komɛi Ekomɛi daa oya. Abaanyɛ akɛ henɔi komɛi ato nyɔji babaoo. ni henɔi komɛi woɔ yibii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi komɛi anɔ. Bɔ ni ooohala nɔ ni sa lɛ damɔ kɛji niyenii lɛ he baahia bo oya, ni okɛto be kakadaŋŋ, loo ni ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ.

english: While you can save seeds, improved or hybrid varieties lose their yield potential in the next generation. Buying fresh certified seed each season ensures strong plants, uniform growth, and higher yields.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ obaanyɛ obu dumɔwui lɛ ahe moŋ Shi dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ loo dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ baafite amɛ yibiiwoo he nyɛmɔ lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa afi lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ. Dalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ. ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo

english: Can a virus attacking my cassava plants spread to my corn or beans?
ga: Ani hela ni tutuaa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mi ŋmãa loo mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ?

english: Most plant viruses are specialized and only attack specific crop families. A virus causing disease in cassava generally cannot infect cereal crops like corn or legumes like beans.
ga: Tsei amli helai babaoo ji nɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto ni amɛtutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi pɛ. Virus ni kɛ cassava hela baa lɛ nyɛŋ atswa ŋmaa nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava turning yellow and twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow, crumpled leaves are a common sign of Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny sucking insects called whiteflies or by planting stems cut from already infected plants.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni ekpɔtɔ ji okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ cassava mosaic hela lɛ he. ni ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu ni atsɛɔ amɛ whitefly loo ŋmeii ni miida ni afolɔ kɛjɛ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ momo lɛ amli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: How do crop viruses get into my field if I planted clean soil?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai abote miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ?

english: Viruses are usually introduced into a clean field by insect pests like aphids or whiteflies that carry the virus from infected farms, or by using infected stem cuttings and seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ baa hei ni he tse kɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ aphids ni hiɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela loo whiteflies ni jɛ ŋmɔji ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei kɛ dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Why is it beneficial to plant beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Beans are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This enriches the land and acts as a natural fertilizer for the maize growing alongside it.
ga: Beans ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome.

english: Why does millet withstand hot, dry weather better than my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nu ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ jogbaŋŋ fe mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Millet has deep root systems and a plant structure designed to conserve water efficienty, making it naturally resilient to heat and drought compared to maize.
ga: Sorghum yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tso he gbɛjianɔtoo ni afee koni ekɛbu nu he jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ eshiɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ akɛtoɔ ŋmãa he.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow tall leaves but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai kakadaji shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to focus its energy on growing heavy foliage above ground instead of transferring nutrients down into building thick tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ baai ni tsii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, e ngɔɔ niyenii kpakpahi kɛ yaa si konɛ e pee tubers nɛ mi wa.

english: How can I keep my seed yam from rotting in the soil after planting?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ akafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yam setts rot easily if planted in overly wet soil or if cut surfaces are left unsealed. Coating the cut pieces with wood ash or an approved fungicide helps protect them until sprouts form.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ nɔ loo kɛji akɛ ashi he ni afo lɛ nɔ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he. Kɛ́ okɛ tso sũ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ wo hei ni afo lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaabu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaakwɛ̃.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build strong stems and green leaves. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or adding well-rotted animal manure restores their healthy green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea, loo kooloi ashishifãi ni egbo jogbaŋŋ afata he lɛ atsu nii. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ su ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my farmland soil has enough plant food without taking it to a laboratory?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ tsei amli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛyaaa laboratori?

english: You can judge soil health by observing crop behavior: healthy, fast-growing plants with dark leaves indicate rich soil, while stunted growth, pale leaves, or reddish-purple leaf edges show the soil lacks vital nutrients like nitrogen or phosphorus.
ga: Obaanyɛ okojo shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ tsei lɛ ajeŋba ni oookwɛ lɛ nɔ: tsei ni daa oya ni amɛhe wa ni amɛbaai lɛ yɛ ediŋŋ lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni edaaa oya, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, loo baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo phosphorus bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating small holes in the central heart of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ mi ŋmãa tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on young corn shoots. Spraying early in the morning or late evening with recommended insecticides or applying clean neem leaf water directly into the leaf funnel helps destroy them.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ loo okɛ neem baa nu ni he tse tsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efite amɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot directly on the tree branches during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in high humidity and damp shade. Pruning overhead branches to allow sunlight into the farm and removing infected pods quickly stops the fungus from spreading to healthy trees.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ. Niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ejieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ baatsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli oya.

english: What causes my tomato plants to drop all their flowers before any tomatoes can grow?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifo amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani tomato lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, usually from extreme heat, dry soil from irregular watering, or a lack of calcium and potassium in the soil.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiihao. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kɛjɛ nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ hewɔ. aloo calcium kɛ potassium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli

english: Is it better to plant my cassava stem cuttings flat, straight up, or slanting in the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmei niji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ, loo ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at an angle (slanted) gives the best yield because it allows tubers to grow evenly near the surface, making them grow larger and easier to harvest than stems planted completely straight or flat.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ (tilt) lɛ haa yibiiwoo ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ ehaa cassava shishifãi lɛ daa pɛpɛɛpɛ. ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni akpamɔ waaa fe tsei ni ja loo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kwraa.

english: Why should I plant cowpea or groundnuts on the same plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Maize consumes a lot of soil nutrients, but legume crops like cowpea and groundnuts actually extract nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, naturally enriching the soil for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Shi ŋmeii, tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why do extension officers advise planting plantains around young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under bright sunlight. Plantain plants grow quickly and produce large leaves that provide shade and trap moisture, protecting the fragile cocoa trees during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei ni waaa lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Is it better to burn dry weeds when clearing my land or cut them to cover the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaashã jwɛi ni egbi beni ajieɔ shikpɔŋ loo afoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Leaving cut weeds on the soil as mulch protects the land from heat, retains moisture, and rots into free organic manure, whereas burning destroys natural soil nutrients and kills helpful soil organisms.
ga: Jwɛi ni afolɔ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ mulch lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni efiteɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko. Yɛ be mli ni shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni efiteɔ sũ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines completely dry up and die off when the crop is ready underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kwraa ni amɛgboiɔ beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efee klalo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When yam tubers finish growing and reach full maturity, the plant naturally stops sending water to the leaves above ground and stores all its energy in the tuber, signaling that it is time to harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ dara ni amɛdara lɛ, yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, tso lɛ kpaɔ nu ni ekɛyaa ebaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ toɔ bulb lɛ mli. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nikpamɔ be eshɛ.

english: Why do my crops start wilting and dying so quickly when the rain stops for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya ni egboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Crops need water to suck up plant nutrients from the soil and to keep themselves cool under hot weather. When rain stops, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink from the dry ground, causing them to wilt and eventually die.
ga: Tsei hia nu koni amɛhe niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛhi shi fɛ̃i yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gboɔ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egboɔ.

english: Which crops can I plant on my farm that can survive better during long periods of no rain?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni manyɛ mahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: Crops like cassava, millet, sorghum, and cowpeas have deep roots or low water requirements, making them much tougher during hot dry spells compared to water-hungry crops like maize or leafy vegetables.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo nu ni he ehiaaa tsɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛto tsei ni he hiaa nu tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ahe.

english: How can I keep the dirt on my farm moist for longer even when the sun is hot and rain is scarce?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha ŋmɔ mli muji lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ, yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ tsɔ po lɛ?

english: Covering the ground around your plants with dry grass, leaves, or crop leftovers—a practice called mulching—acts like a blanket. It blocks direct sunshine from drying out the earth and traps moisture in the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ—ni ji nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching—ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi, ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize curl up tightly and turn yellow during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up like small tubes during heat to hide from direct sunlight and slow down water loss. The yellowing happens because the plant cannot absorb food from the dry soil without water to carry it.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ baabɔle amɛhe ni amɛbaafee ŋmeii bibii. Kɛji akɛ edɔ lɛ koni ekɛ ehe akawo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli ni ekɛha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Su ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa ejaakɛ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni nu bɛ ni ekɛwoɔ mli.

english: Does leaving more space between my plants help them survive better when there is little rainfall?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ mitsei lɛ to he ko lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛ?

english: Yes, giving your crops extra space prevents their roots from competing with neighboring plants for the limited water trapped in dry soil, helping each plant drink enough to stay alive.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ oha onibii lɛ gbɛ babaoo lɛ, ebaatsi amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ akaŋ koni amɛná nu ni emɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi fioo nɔ lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nuɔ nu bɔ ni sa koni ehi wala mli.

english: What is the best time of day for me to hand-water my crops so the water doesn't dry up immediately?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛ minine baashwie mitsei lɛ anɔ nu? Bɔni afee ni nu lɛ akagbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Watering early in the morning or late in the evening allows the soil to absorb moisture deeply while the weather is cool, preventing the intense afternoon sun from evaporating the water off your field.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu ni mli kwɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ naa koni ekafee nu ni jɛɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ.

english: How does putting animal manure or compost into my farm soil help my crops during hot weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Organic materials like manure and compost act like sponges in the dirt. They hold onto moisture far longer than bare soil, giving your plants a reliable drink between dry days.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ. Ha otsei lɛ agbi yɛ gbi lɛ mli.

english: Why are my young seedlings dying off much faster than my fully grown crops when the rains delay?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ gboiɔ oya fe tsei ni eda lɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have short, tender roots near the top of the ground where heat dries out moisture first, while older plants have deep root systems that can reach hidden water deeper down.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ. Dɔlɛ lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi klɛŋklɛŋ. Shi tsei ni edara lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ ashɛ nu ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ he.

english: How do I know when it is safe to sow my seeds so they don't germinate and die right after?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ehi akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ? Bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ akakwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi yɛ no sɛɛ.

english: It is best to wait until the rainy season is fully established and has soaked the ground deeply. Planting after just one light early rain can trick seeds into sprouting, only for them to dry out when hot weather returns.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baagbe naa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ alaka dumɔwu ko ni ekwɛ̃. Shi ebaagbi pɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Can leaving shade trees on my farmland protect my crops from drying out during intense heat?
ga: Ani tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa ni mashiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Yes, scattered shade trees lower the temperature around your crops, shield them from severe sun scorch, and slow down the rate at which water evaporates from the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ egbɛ eshwã lɛ haa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ baa shi, ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eha bɔ ni nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ aba shi

english: Why are my crops turning weak and producing less food even though I am farming on the same land as before?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwooo niyenii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii tsutsu lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ mitsuɔ nii yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When you farm on the same plot continuously without letting it rest, crops exhaust the vital nutrients underground. Without leaving the land fallow or adding the right soil nutrients, crops become malnourished and yield much less.
ga: Beni otsuɔ okwaayeli he nii be fɛɛ be yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni ohaaa ejɔɔ ehe lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ laajeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baaná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ebaawo yibii babaoo kɛji amɛshieee shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ loo amɛkɛ niyenii ni sa fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Why do crops need added inputs today when farmers used to grow food without chemicals years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nibii krokomɛi he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii ŋmɛnɛ lɛ? Beni okwaafoi duɔ niyenii ni amɛkɛ tsofai tsuuu nii afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: In the past, farmers could leave farmland to rest for years so the soil regained its natural power. Today, because available farmland is shrinking as towns expand, soil gets tired from non-stop farming and needs added nutrients to feed crops.
ga: Be ko ni eho lɛ, okwaafoi baanyɛ ashi amɛŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ koni amɛyajɔɔ amɛhe afii babaoo. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ ana ebɔɔ su hewalɛ ekoŋŋ. Ŋmɛnɛ, taakɛ okwaayeli shikpɔji ni yɔɔ lɛ miiba shi be mli ni maji lɛ amli miilɛɛ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ etɔ kɛjɛ okwaayeli ni afeɔ daa lɛ mli, ni ehe miihia ni niyenii krokomɛi afata he koni ekɛye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do I know which fertilizer is the right one for my crops when there are so many imported products in the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Beni nibii ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ baa lɛ babaoo yɛ jara nɔ lɛ

english: Different crops require different nutrients—like nitrogen for leafy growth or phosphorus for root development. Checking with an extension officer or testing your soil helps you pick the exact input your specific crop needs rather than guessing.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi taoɔ niyenii srɔtoi, tamɔ nitrogen kɛha baa dalɛ loo phosphorus kɛha shishifãi adalɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ extension agent loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii akwɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ohala nibii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa bo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ko. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooosusu he

english: Will applying a larger amount of fertilizer make my crops grow much faster and bigger?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara oya ni amɛdara?

english: No, giving crops too much fertilizer can 'burn' their roots and damage the soil. Crops can only absorb what they need at a time, so excess application wastes money and can destroy your plants.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ‘ashã’ shishifãi lɛ ni efite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nɔ pɛ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ be kome mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛtsu nii babaoo lɛ, eji shika fitemɔ, ni ebaanyɛ efite otsei lɛ.

english: Can I plant my crops closer together so I can harvest more food from my small plot?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni manyɛ makpa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition leaves you with thin, weak plants and smaller harvests instead of more food.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛwuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa onáa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo fioo yɛ niyenii babaoo najiaŋ.

english: How can I make my crops produce a higher yield without buying more land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii babaoo ni miheee shikpɔŋ babaoo?

english: You can harvest more from a small area by planting high-quality improved seeds, applying the correct type and amount of fertilizer, and keeping the field free of weeds that steal nutrients from your plants.
ga: Obaanyɛ oná ŋmaa babaoo kɛjɛ he ko bibioo kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni atsake lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Use the correct type and amount of fertilizer. ni oha jwɛi ni juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli lɛ akafee he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow shortly after planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop is starving for key nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is too dry or waterlogged for the roots to feed properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ ni enyɛŋ eha shishifãi lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops look dry and stressed even when it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbi ni amɛhaoɔ amɛhe eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Overused soil often loses its structure and cannot hold water well. Adding organic matter like manure or compost helps the soil act like a sponge, keeping moisture around the crop roots longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ fɔɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ fiteɔ, ni ehiɛɛɛ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ ahiɔ nu mli yɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why should I buy packaged seeds instead of just planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni akɛwo kotoku mli moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Packaged, improved seeds are bred to mature faster, resist common local diseases, and produce higher yields on small plots, whereas saved seeds lose their strength over time and yield less.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ paketi lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛshwere oya. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo yɛ shikpɔji bibii anɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Which types of crops are best to plant if I only have a small piece of land?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ makwɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ fioo pɛ miyɔɔ?

english: Fast-maturing, high-value crops like vegetables (tomatoes, peppers, okra) or cassava are ideal because they maximize small spaces and allow you to harvest and sell quickly.
ga: Nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni jara wa waa tamɔ aduawai (atomo, ŋmɔtɔ, okra) loo ŋmɔtɔ. Amɛhi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛkɛ he bibioo ko tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. ni eye ebua bo ni okpa ni ohɔ̃ɔ oya.

english: Why shouldn't I plant cassava on the exact same spot where I harvested cassava last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ he ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly in the same soil drains the exact same nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Changing crops breaks this pest cycle and gives the soil time to recover.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ baafite. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe.

english: What happens to my soil if I keep growing maize on the same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nitrogen. Growing it continuously on the same land rapidly weakens the soil, causing your yield to drop over time and encouraging stubborn weeds like Striga to invade your farm.
ga: Abele haa nitrogen babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ agbɔjɔ oya. Enɛ haa nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. ni owo jwɛi ni yitsoŋ wa tamɔ Striga lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛbatutua oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Is it helpful to plant groundnuts or beans on my farm after harvesting a cereal crop like maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa sɛɛ?

english: Yes, leguminous crops like groundnuts and beans pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, naturally restoring the fertility that heavy-feeding crops like maize took away.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ amɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii babaoo ni tsei ni yeɔ niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ jieɔ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do farmers heap and mound soft soil around the roots of growing yam and potato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi buaa sũ ni mli jɔ ni amɛduɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Heaping soft soil around tuber crops gives the growing roots space to expand easily underground, protects them from harsh sunlight, and prevents them from greening or rotting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni ebɔle Tubers he lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa shishifãi ni miida lɛ akɛ amɛbaagbɛ shikpɔŋ shishi he lɛ amɛshwã. Buu tsei ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛkafite.

english: Why is it necessary to dig and loosen hard soil around my growing crops during the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo shikpɔŋ ni wa ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ mli ni mafolɔ mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa nɔ lɛ?

english: Loosening hard soil creates air spaces and pathways for water, allowing roots to breathe, drink easily, and spread deeper into the earth for stronger growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui kɛ gbɛi ni nu tsɔɔ nɔ lɛ baa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ muɔ, amɛnuɔ nu mlɛo, ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Does digging up the ground to clear weeds around my crops damage their roots?
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni mifoɔ koni mijie jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efite eshishifãi lɛ?

english: If done carefully, shallow digging removes weeds that steal water and food, while breaking up the hard surface crust so rain can sink deeper to feed the crop's roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ Shallow digging lɛ baajie jwɛi ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii lɛ kɛya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, efoɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni wa lɛ mli bɔni afee ni nugbɔ lɛ anyɛ abote mli jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ashishifãi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the leaves of my crop turn yellow even when the farm gets enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the plant is starving for nutrients—especially nitrogen—or that pests or underground diseases are damaging the root system.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai. titri lɛ nitrogen loo shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi loo helai miifite shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall with green leaves but fail to produce plenty of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli shi ewooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: This happens when the plant gets too much nitrogen but lacks phosphorus and potassium, causing it to spend all its energy making leaves instead of flowers and fruit.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei ná nitrogen babaoo shi amɛbɛ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and fall over suddenly in the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting often means soil-borne bacteria or tiny worms (nematodes) are attacking the roots, blocking the plant from drawing up water to withstand the hot sun.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ni baa trukaa lɛ tsɔɔ helai bibii ni yɔɔ sũ mli loo ŋmeii bibii. (Nematodes) lɛ miitutua shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ato nu koni amɛdamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why do my crops grow faster and look healthier when I mix decayed organic matter into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ waa kɛ́ mikɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egboi futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Decayed matter acts like a sponge and natural food; it keeps moisture in the soil longer during dry days and continuously feeds crops with healthy nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. ni akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa aha tsei daa

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Maize is a heavy feeder, and when it runs out of nitrogen, it moves whatever food it has left from its lower leaves up to the new top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ji niyenii ni tsii. Ni kɛ́ nitrogen lɛ fite lɛ Ejieɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to plant groundnuts or beans on my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ midu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ́ mikpa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Maize takes away a lot of nourishment from the soil. Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which means they take nitrogen from the air and feed it back into the ground, naturally restoring soil fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni okɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Tall trees provide shade to cool the soil and shield young cocoa from harsh heat until the seedlings are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot or when the plant doesn't get enough water. High heat stresses the plant, causing it to shed its blossoms to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔii ni akɛtoɔ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when the heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air to live just like they need water. When water stays pooled around the roots for too long, oxygen gets cut off, causing the tubers to drown and rot.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛhi shi tamɔ bɔ ni nu he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni egboɔ.

english: Yam plants use their leaves to catch sunlight and make food that builds the big tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves off the hot soil and spreads them out into the light, preventing leaf rot and increasing tuber size.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛmɔɔ hulu la ni amɛfeɔ niyenii, ni no haa bulbs agboi baa shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa la mli. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ni ehaa tuber lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the fruit bunch gets big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots holding them to the ground. As the fruit bunch gets heavy, the plant becomes top-heavy, so propping the trunk with a strong bamboo or wooden stick keeps the wind from knocking it over.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni fiɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ tsii lɛ Tso lɛ baafee tsii waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo tsei ni mli wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ naa koni ekagbee shi.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin with very small cobs when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛmli ŋmeii bibii waa yɔɔ mli lɛ, kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the young plants fight with each other for water, soil food, and sunlight. Giving each plant proper space ensures it gets enough food to grow strong stalks and big cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Ha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa koni ená niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and twisting into small shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsɔ amɛhe bibii bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper is caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the juices from young leaves. This damages the leaf tissue as it grows, causing it to wrinkle and twist.
ga: Nɔ ni haa pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ji kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji beni edaa lɛ. Ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa.

english: Why does swamp rice need standing water on the field to grow well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmãa mli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Standing water kills unwanted weeds that try to steal food from the rice, and it keeps the soil soft so rice roots can grow quickly and take in water easily.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi ni ataooo ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛŋɔ niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ ada oya ni amɛŋɔ nu oya.

english: After I harvest my cocoa and remove the seeds, what can I do with the empty pod husks left on the farm?
ga: Kɛ́ mikpa kookoo lɛ ni mijie dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Mɛni mifeɔ kɛ pod ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko ni eshwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You can pile and rot the empty cocoa pod husks into rich organic fertilizer (compost), which puts vital nutrients back into the ground for your crops to feed on.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ ato ni ofite ni ofee humus (compost) ni jara wa. Enɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee nɔ ni ayeɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need fertilizer if the soil already looks dark and rich?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ he hiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii momo lɛ?

english: Every time your trees produce pods, they pull nutrients out of the earth. Fertilizer acts like a daily meal that replaces what was taken out so the trees do not become weak.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni otso lɛ baajie ŋmɔtɔ Ebaajie niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ daa gbi niyenii ni yeɔ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ najiaŋ. koni akagbɔjɔ tso lɛ

english: Is it good to leave cut leaves and weed clearings lying on the ground around my crop bases?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashi baai ni afolɔ kɛ jwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ he?

english: Yes, leaving dead plant material on the soil acts as mulch, keeping the ground moist in hot weather and breaking down over time into free natural fertilizer.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni egboi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up in full daylight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are like human infants—their leaves cannot handle harsh direct sunlight and require shade trees, like plantains, to shield them until they grow stronger.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ abifabii. Baai lɛ nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Ni ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa.

english: If I plant my cocoa trees very close to each other, will I harvest more pods?
ga: Kɛ midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani mana pods babaoo?

english: No, planting too close forces trees to fight each other for water, soil food, and sunlight, resulting in tall, thin trees with very few pods.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi nu, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ, ni no baaha tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ aba.

english: Why should I cut off the soft new shoots growing out near the bottom stem of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tso hee ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Those extra shoots, called chupons or suckers, steal water and fertilizer away from the main trunk where your flowers and pods need to grow.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons loo tsei lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli, ni no ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ofɔfɔi kɛ o-pods lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ.

english: Is there any other benefit I get from growing cocoa besides selling the dried seeds to the buying clerk?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔi krokomɛi yɛ ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo dumɔ mli kɛfata dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ ni mihɔ̃ɔ mihaa nitsulɔi ni heɔ nii lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, apart from selling beans, the farm waste from cocoa pods can be reused to fertilize other crops, and the husk ash can be used locally to make soap.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛfata ŋmeii ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ he. Abaanyɛ akɛ cocoa pod ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ hu atsu nii ekoŋŋ ni akɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi amli ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Ni abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔtɔ afee samla yɛ maŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do many flowers on my cocoa branches fall off without forming into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo niji lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Flowers often drop when the tree lacks sufficient water or fertilizer, or when there are not enough tiny insects (midges) in the farm to pollinate them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii (teŋgbɛ nibii) ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ afee pollination.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn completely black and soft while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ kwraa beni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: That is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, overly damp conditions, especially when trees are bushy and air cannot flow freely.
ga: No ji black pod hela. Fuŋ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ ni edɔ fe nine lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ tso lɛ mli eyi kɛ ŋmɔji ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does the dry Harmattan season affect my farm crops, and how can I keep them alive?
ga: Te Harmattan hɔmɔ lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahi shi?

english: Harmattan winds dry out the air and soil quickly, causing trees to drop leaves to save water; clearing around stems and adding mulch holds moisture in the soil longer.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Ha tsei agbee shi koni nu akafite. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ shishi kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need from the soil to stay green and grow big.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and lets soil diseases and pests build up in that field over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eha shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What does mixing animal manure into my farm land actually do for my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni mikɛfutuɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Manure acts like long-lasting food for the soil, helping it hold moisture during hot days and releasing nutrients slowly to keep crops healthy.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii fiofio koni eha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava sticks too close to one another in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛɔ he tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need space underground to expand into large tubers. Planting them too close makes them fight for water and sunlight, resulting in small roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ hulu la he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ daraaa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so poorly even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal soil nutrients, water, and sunlight away from your main crops before the crops can use them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why do people cover the bare soil around vegetable plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni ebɔle aduawai ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass keeps the soil cool, stops rainwater from evaporating quickly, and blocks weeds from getting sunlight to sprout.
ga: Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo mli koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya. ni amɛtsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni hulu la akashɛ amɛnɔ kɛyashi amɛbaakwɛ̃

english: Why should I cut off extra shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Extra shoots suck away water and food from the main mother plant. Leaving only one or two strong shoots ensures the main stem produces large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ afee plantain tso agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Tomato leaves curl to protect themselves from losing too much water in extreme heat, but if they stay droopy in the cool morning, the soil lacks water.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite fe nine yɛ latsaa be mli. Shi kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ leebi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ Nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do small insects like whiteflies cause my pepper leaves to wrinkle up?
ga: Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies haa mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi?

english: Insects suck the vital sap and energy out of the leaves and spread plant diseases that distort the leaves and stop the plant from bearing fruit.
ga: Kplukai lɛ shwieɔ nu ni he hiaa waa kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai ni fiteɔ baai lɛ ni ehaaa tso lɛ awo yibii lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: Why do certified seeds from the agriculture office grow better than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni Bureau of Agriculture lɛ wo he odase lɛ kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are carefully selected and treated to resist common diseases and drought, whereas saved seeds lose their strength and yield less over time.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni atsuɔ he nii koni amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai ni afɔɔ namɔ kɛ hɔmɔ. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Since it rained on my farm yesterday, do I still need to water my young crops today?
ga: Ejaakɛ nugbɔ nɛ nyɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ani ehe miihia ni mawo mitsei bibii lɛ nu lolo ŋmɛnɛ?

english: No, a good rain usually provides enough deep soil moisture for a few days, so you should check if the top soil is dry before adding more water to avoid rotting the roots.
ga: Dabi, bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ kpakpa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa gbii fioo komɛi, no hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ okwɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã lɛ mli egbi dani okɛ nu kroko afata he koni shishifãi lɛ akafite.

english: Is water stored inside a plastic polytank safe to use for watering my vegetable crops?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛto plastic poly tanki mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛbaatsu nii kɛha mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu?

english: Yes, water from a clean polytank is completely safe for crops and is a great way to store extra water for your farm during dry days.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni jɛɔ poly tanki ni he tse mli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kwraa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Ni eji gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ nu krokomɛi toɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Can I use borehole water directly on my crops, or will it hurt how they grow?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛɔ nubu lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Aloo ebaana hewalɛ gbonyo yɛ tsei adalɛ nɔ loo ebaafee nakai?

english: Borehole water is generally good for crops, but if the water is too salty or heavy with minerals, it can slow down plant growth, so testing it or mixing it with rainwater is ideal.
ga: Nu ni jɛɔ nubui amli lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Shi kɛji nu lɛ mli ŋmei tsɔ loo eyɛ minerals babaoo Ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo. No hewɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni akɛkaa loo akɛfutuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my vegetables so they stay healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Early morning is the best time to water because the plant absorbs the moisture before the sun gets too hot, which prevents the water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔse nu ejaakɛ tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu dani hulu lɛ mli dɔɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haaa nu lɛ atsɔ oya.

english: How often do I need to water my pepper plants if the weather is very dry?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni mawo mi-pepper tso lɛ nu kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa?

english: Pepper plants need consistent moisture, especially when flowering. In dry weather, watering them deeply every 2 to 3 days keeps the soil moist and helps them produce healthy peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ hia ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. titri lɛ kɛ́ ewo fɔfɔi yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ Nu ni awoɔ mli waa daa gbii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my pepper leaves are drooping because of too little water or too much water?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji nu fioo loo nu babaoo hewɔ ni o-pepper lɛ baa lɛ miiho lɛ?

english: If the soil feels dry and crumbly when leaves droop, the plant needs water. If the soil is wet and leaves are yellowing and drooping, the roots are getting suffocated by too much water.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi ni egbɔjɔ beni baai lɛ gbee shi lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ he miihia nu. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni baai lɛ efee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tsɔ.

english: Pepper plants often drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or dry soil without enough water, as a way to save energy to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni mli edɔ waa he loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni akɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha wala

english: Why do extension officers recommend growing peppers in neat raised rows instead of just planting seeds randomly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu chili yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ dumɔwui ni aduɔ trukaa lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Growing peppers in raised rows allows excess water to drain away from roots, makes weeding easier, and gives each plant enough space and light to grow big.
ga: Pepper ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli. ni oha tso fɛɛ tso he kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ agbo.

english: How does putting dry grass around the base of my pepper plants help them grow?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te pepper tsei ashishitoo yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the ground, keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Mulching ni egbi (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Can I still grow a successful pepper crop in an area where groundwater is scarce?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ pepper tsei ni yeɔ omanye lolo yɛ hei ni shikpɔŋ shishi nu faaa yɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, but you will need to store rain water in tanks or practice mulching and water-saving irrigation methods so your peppers get a steady supply of water throughout the season.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi ehe baahia ni obua nugbɔ nu lɛ naa yɛ baagi mli loo okɛ ohe awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni okɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ baaha o-peppers lɛ aná nu be fɛɛ be yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to grow leaves and stalks. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps turn them green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni baa kɛ ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ Nitrogen ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛwo mli lɛ baaye abua ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: The best time is when the soil is moist and young roots have developed, usually 2 to 3 weeks after sprouting. Applying it in dry soil burns roots, while heavy rain right after application can wash it away.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni shishifãi lɛ darako, bei pii lɛ otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 sɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaashã shishifãi lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be mli ni akɛtsu nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahoo.
