english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when soil stays flooded because roots need air to stay alive. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi lɛ koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when plants get stressed by extreme heat or a lack of regular water, which prevents pollination. Consistent watering during hot spells helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. ni tsiɔ pollination naa Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe daa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: What is causing holes in my young corn leaves and droppings inside the stalks?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a pest that feeds on young corn leaves. Spraying with recommended organic or chemical controls early in the morning helps protect the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛbuɔ he lɛ shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Weeds steal food, sunlight, and water from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow big and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to make energy for growing tubers underground. Staking holds the vines up off the wet ground so leaves catch sunlight and avoid diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tuber ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ wain tso lɛ wo ŋwɛi kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe ni ebaatsi hela naa.

english: Trimming branches allows sunlight and air to move freely through the tree canopy. This prevents damp conditions that cause black pod disease and helps the tree focus energy on pods.
ga: Tso lɛ mlifomɔ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ maa pods lɛ anɔ.

english: Planting maize in the same spot continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or cowpeas restores nutrients naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Wait until the ground gets two or three good, heavy rains that soak deep into the soil before planting, rather than planting after the very first light shower which can leave seeds to dry up and die.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa fioo komɛi ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani okɛdu. Mohu ɔ, duɔ ngɛ hiɔmi kekleekle nɛ ɔ se, nɛ lɔ ɔ ma nyɛ ma ha nɛ duwu ɔmɛ nɛ a gbi nɛ a gbo.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and small after growing on the same piece of land for three years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ bibii beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii etɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava pulls food out of the soil every season. Without adding manure or resting the land, the soil becomes empty of nutrients, causing the plant leaves to turn yellow and the roots to stay small.
ga: Cassava gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baafite ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ ko bɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong direct sunlight because it burns their leaves and dries out their roots; keeping temporary shade plants like plantains protects them while they are small.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ ebaashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ to be kukuoo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put dry leaves over my yam mounds after planting the seed yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ baai ni egboi aha ŋmeii ni ato lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Covering yam mounds with dry leaves keeps the soil cool and moist under the hot sun, which prevents the seed yam from baking and rotting before it sprouts.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egbi ha ŋmɔtɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Enɛ haaa sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ashã ni amɛkagbo dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: This usually happens when the plant lacks calcium or gets irregular watering, causing the bottom of the tomato fruit to break down and rot as it grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ calcium bɛ tso lɛ mli loo akɛ nu haa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Enɛ haa tomatoi lɛ ashishi fãa ni egboɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, wasting their energy growing tall to reach light instead of building large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ekɛ hewalɛ ni fa babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛshɛɔ la lɛ he moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmei agbo.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already damp after a light rain, and cover it with a little soil near the plant roots so it dissolves into the ground instead of being carried off by heavy downpours.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. ni okɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko aha nɔ Ebɛŋkɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my pepper plants after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-pepper tsei lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with very strong roots that steal water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated seedlings, so clearing them early lets your peppers get the food they need.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli wa waa ni baanyɛ aju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji otsi ohe mra Enɛ baaha o-chili lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the maize seeds I saved from my last harvest yield less than certified seeds from the shop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni shwapo lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially produced to resist diseases and give high yields, whereas seeds saved from past harvests naturally lose their strength and can pass on diseases.
ga: Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai amɛshwã.

english: Leaving too many suckers forces the main plant to share its food and water with all of them, resulting in smaller plantain bunches instead of one large, healthy cluster.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi suckers babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ tso titri lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ niyenii kɛ nu aha amɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ haa panicles bibii baa yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ.

english: Is it better to water my crops directly at the roots or spray water over the leaves?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ nu yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ loo mafɔ nu yɛ baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Watering directly at the roots is much better because plants drink water through their root systems, not their leaves. Wetting the leaves too much wastes water through evaporation and creates damp conditions that encourage leaf diseases.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ tso lɛ nuɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ, shi jeee kɛtsɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ ashɛ baai lɛ ahe fe nine lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ afite kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni woɔ foliar hela he hewalɛ baa.

english: What is drip irrigation, and how can it help my farm during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni ji nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Drip irrigation is a system that uses thin pipes to deliver small drops of water directly to the base of each plant. It saves a lot of water, keeps soil moist constantly, and allows you to farm and harvest crops year-round without relying on rain.
ga: Drip irrigation ji gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni akɛ paipi bibioo ko tsuɔ nii ni akɛ nu bibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kɛyashi tso fɛɛ tso shishi tɛ̃ɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni akɛ nu babaoo baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be. Ni ehaa onyɛɔ otsuɔ okwaayeli ni okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ nugbɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt in the afternoon heat even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ nɔ leebi moŋ?

english: In hot weather, crops lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it out of the soil. The leaves curl or droop to conserve water, but as long as the soil stays moist, the plant will usually recover by evening.
ga: yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgbeeɔ shi koni amɛhiɛ nu mli. Shi be fɛɛ be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsei lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense crop behavior where the plant tries to reduce water loss during intense heat. Yellowing usually signals that the plant is missing essential soil nutrients or getting uneven amounts of water.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu subaŋ. He ni tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛha nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo enine shɛɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn pale green or yellow after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tseee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall can wash away nitrogen and other nutrients from the topsoil deeper down where roots cannot reach. Without nitrogen, crops cannot maintain their dark green color and struggle to produce food.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Shi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Kɛji nitrogen bɛ lɛ, Dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ amɛsu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo niyenii.

english: Why do sticky droplets appear on my pepper leaves, and is it harmful?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi miije kpo yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ lɛ? Ni ani eyɛ oshara?

english: Sticky droplets are usually liquid sap left behind by tiny pests like aphids or mealybugs hiding under the leaves. These insects suck nutrients out of the plant, which weakens crop growth and can lead to black mold on the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni shwieɔ shi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nu ni kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mealybugs shiɔ yɛ baai anɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei amli. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ dalɛ agbɔjɔ. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ ŋmeii diji aba baai lɛ anɔ

english: Crops need space to stretch their roots and leaves. When maize is planted too close together, the individual plants compete for sunlight, water, and soil food, leaving none of them with enough energy to grow big cobs.
ga: He ko he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛgbala amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli. Beni adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tso fɛɛ tso kɛ ehe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei komɛi bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are flowers falling off my pepper plants before any peppers grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei anɔ dani ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, drought, or too much fertilizer. The crop sacrifices its flowers to save energy and keep the main stem and roots alive.
ga: Tsei baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ kɛ fɔfɔi shaa afɔle koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he ni eha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahi shi.

english: How can I tell if my cassava plants are getting too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo tsɔ?

english: When cassava gets waterlogged, its lower leaves turn yellow and drop early, and the growth slows down. Underground, excessive moisture causes the tubers to rot and smell bad instead of growing big.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ mli edɔ Eshishigbɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ oya ni amɛbaagbee shi. ni dalɛ baafee mlɛo Shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔtɔ babaoo haa bulb lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ agbo.

english: Why do my crops grow very fast during the first month and then suddenly stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tee hiɛ oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no sɛɛ lɛ ekpa ŋmɔshi nibii trukaa lɛ?

english: Young plants grow quickly on the food stored inside the seed and topsoil, but once they exhaust those quick nutrients or hit hard, compacted soil below, their growth stalls until you loosen the soil or add nutrients like compost.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ daa oya yɛ niyenii ni ato yɛ dumɔwui lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ nakai niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa oya lɛ fite loo amɛtswa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni edɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Amɛdalɛ baakpa kɛyashi obaaŋmɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ loo okɛ niyenii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he.

english: Should I clear the ground weeds first or prune the tree branches first when working on my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi klɛŋklɛŋ loo mafolɔ tsei lɛ aniji klɛŋklɛŋ kɛ́ mitsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should always clear the ground weeds underneath first so the space is open. If you cut top branches into uncleaned weeds and brush, the field becomes cluttered and your work will be much more difficult.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be fɛɛ be koni he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ahi shi. Kɛji ofo tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ, jwɛi kɛ brɔshi ni he tseee baafee. Gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli baafee basabasa ni onitsumɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa kwraa fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to weed under my crop trees before I start cutting off high branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie jwɛi ni yɔɔ tsei ashishi lɛ dani mabɔi tsei niji ni kɛlɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ lɛ?

english: Clearing the ground under your trees first keeps your workspace open and safe. If heavy branches fall into thick undergrowth, it becomes very hard to walk around, chop up the debris, or gather the wood later.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie he ni tsei lɛ yɔɔ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaha onitsumɔhe lɛ ahi shi ni ehi shi shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ tso nine ni tsii gbee shi yɛ tsei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ amli lɛ, ebaawa akɛ ooonyiɛ jɛmɛ, ooofo tso, loo oooŋɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: How does opening up space around the base of my crop trees help me maintain them?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbɛ ni mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he ni migbeleɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni makwɛ amɛ nɔ?

english: Clearing the base makes the area accessible so you can easily reach high branches, manage fallen debris safely, and keep light and air moving around the base of your trees.
ga: Shishitoo lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa anyɛɔ ashɛɔ jɛmɛ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ oyashɛ tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ahe mlɛo. Tsu sũ ni miigbee shi lɛ he nii shweshweeshwe. ni oha la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aya nɔ abɔle otso lɛ shishi

english: What happens to my tree crops when I trim down the top branches?
ga: Mɛni baa mitso lɛ nɔ kɛ́ mifo niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: When you cut down the top branches, they fall to the ground, opening up the top of the tree canopy to bring in sunlight and make the crop easier to care for.
ga: Kɛ́ ofo ŋwɛi nine lɛ Ebaagbee shikpɔŋ. Kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi fã ni agbeleɔ koni hulu la lɛ abote mli lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ feɔ mlɛo.

english: What happens if I cut tree branches directly down into thick brush and tall grass on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mifo tsei aniji tɛ̃ɛ miwo jwɛi ni mli tse kɛ jwɛi kakadaji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli?

english: Cutting branches into uncut brush creates a messy, tangled pile. It makes it very difficult to move around the farm or cut the fallen branches down further.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ mli awo brɔshi ni afolɔko mli lɛ baaha amɛbua amɛhe naa ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaafã kɛya he fɛɛ he. Tsɔɔmɔ loo ŋmɔ niji ni egbee shi krokomɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my tall farm trees become hard to work on if I let the top branches grow too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii waa kɛji miha amɛniji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ dara tsɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy top branches create shade and obstruct work, and when they are eventually cut, they bring down a large volume of wood that can overwhelm an uncleared farm floor.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni tsii lɛ haa hulutsoo baa ni amɛtsiɔ nitsumɔ naa. Ni beni naagbee lɛ afo amɛ lɛ Nɛkɛ tsei niji nɛɛ gbalaa tsei babaoo ni baanyɛ aha ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni ajieee lɛ awo nu mli lɛ.

english: How do I know when I have completely finished pruning my crop trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni migbe mitso lɛ he ŋmɔshi nii lɛ naa?

english: Pruning is complete once you have cleared the ground below, cut the top branches down to the ground, and chopped up all fallen branches so they can lie flat and dry out.
ga: Pruning lɛ egbe naa kɛji ogbe shishigbɛ he lɛ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ. Ni ofolɔ tsei niji ni egbee shi lɛ fɛɛ koni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbi.

english: Why should I chop up the branches I cut off into smaller pieces instead of leaving them whole on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji ni afo lɛ amli bibii bibii moŋ fe ni mashi amɛ fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Chopping fallen branches with a knife into smaller pieces allows them to lie flat and dry out much faster under the sun, keeping your farm paths clear.
ga: Niji ni egbee shi lɛ ni akɛ ŋmei ŋmɔɔ lɛ bibii bibii Enɛ haa amɛkãa shi ni amɛgbiɔ oya kwraa yɛ hulu lɛ shishi. Ha oŋmɔ lɛ gbɛ lɛ mli aka shi faŋŋ

english: Why do cut tree branches need to dry out properly on the farm floor after pruning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ agbi ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ beni afo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Allowing pruned branches to dry out thoroughly makes them lighter, easier to break down or clear away, and prevents wet brush piles from harboring pests near your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ agbi kwraa lɛ, ebaaha amɛhe afee mlɛo. Efoɔ oya loo egbeeɔ shi ni etsĩɔ jwɛi ni efɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkabua tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ onibii lɛ.

english: Is it fine for me to leave large, whole pruned branches lying under my crop trees?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashi tsei niji wuji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yɛ mitsei lɛ ashishi?

english: No, whole branches take up too much space and dry out slowly. Chopping them into smaller pieces right where they fall helps them dry quickly and keeps the farm neat.
ga: Dabi, tso nine muu lɛ fɛɛ heɔ he babaoo tsɔ ni egbiɔ fiofio. ni afoɔ mli bibii Yɛ hei ni amɛgbee shi yɛ lɛ, enɛ baaye abua ni amɛgbi oya ni eye ebua ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli ahi shi fɛfɛo.

english: Why does my rice crop need to stand in shallow water while it is growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ adamɔ nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Rice plants thrive in standing water because it acts as a natural shield against common land weeds and keeps the soil cool and moist, making it easier for the plant's roots to take up nutrients.
ga: Omɔ tsei yeɔ omanye yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli ejaakɛ etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ jwɛi ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young rice plants turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the rice crop is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow leaves, or the roots are drowning in water that isn't draining properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Aloo akɛ shishifãi lɛ ewo nu ni hoɔɔɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my rice seeds taking so long to sprout after I sow them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rice seeds need both warmth and moisture to wake up; if they are buried too deep in heavy mud or planted in soil that is too dry, the seeds will sleep longer or rot before sprouting.
ga: Omɔ ŋmeii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i fɛɛ koni amɛte shi. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ yɛ muji ni tsii mli tsɔ loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ nɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakã shi be kakadaŋŋ loo amɛbaafite dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do some of my rice plants produce many branch stems while others only grow one thin stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ ekomɛi yɛ niji babaoo yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii bibii pɛ lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally spread out and produce extra stems (tillers) when they have enough space, sunlight, and fertilizer; planting seeds too close together forces each plant to stay thin and single-stemmed.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaafee ŋmeii krokomɛi (ploughs) kɛji akɛ aha amɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei aŋkroaŋkroi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ shishifã kome lɛ aba.

english: Why do grass and weeds grow much faster than my rice plants in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kɛ jwɛi bibii daa oya fe mi ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, aggressive plants naturally adapted to steal water and light faster than cultivated rice, which is why early clearing is necessary until the rice leaves grow big enough to block the sun from the soil.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu kɛ la oya fe ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ. Yɛ yiŋtoo nɛɛ hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ajie ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baa lɛ adara bɔ ni sa ni baatsi hulu la ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my tall rice plants fall over flat on the ground when heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ lɛ? Minɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ shi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa?

english: Rice plants fall over (called lodging) when their stems are weak—often caused by using too much nitrogen fertilizer—or when heavy seed heads become soaked with water and top-heavy in strong winds.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi (ni atsɛɔ lɛ shĩa) kɛ́ amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. (bei pii lɛ, nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛbaa) loo kɛ́ dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii lɛ tsɔ nu ni amɛyitsei lɛ tsɔ tsii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do birds attack my rice field heavily only at a specific time in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi tutuaa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ waa yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko mli pɛ?

english: Birds target rice right after flowering during the 'milky stage' because the young forming grains are filled with a sweet, liquid juice that is very easy for birds to swallow.
ga: Okpoi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ewo fɔfɔi yɛ ‘mliki be’ lɛ mli ejaakɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmãa mli nu kɛ nu ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛha okpoi akɛ amɛmi.

english: Why are some of the hulls on my rice heads completely empty with no grain inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa yitso lɛ nɔ lɛ efee efolo aahu akɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty hulls (chaff) happen when severe heat, drought, or cold weather hits the plant during flowering, which stops the flower from pollinating and forming a solid grain inside.
ga: Bark ni bɛ nɔ ko (chaff) baa kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo fɛ̃i ba tso lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination ni efee dumɔwui ni wa yɛ emli.

english: How do I know when my rice plant is fully ripe and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Rice is ready for harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grain heads turn from green to a warm golden-yellow color, and the individual grains feel hard when you bite down on them.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni ŋmaa yitsei lɛ amli aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa shika tsuru ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Ni ŋmãa lɛ eko fɛɛ eko baanu he akɛ ewa kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa lɛ wo ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my rice grains break into tiny pieces after they go through processing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli fãi bibii lɛ? Beni atsu he nii sɛɛ?

english: Grains crack inside while still on the stalk if harvest is delayed too long or if the harvested paddy was dried too quickly under direct, intense sunlight instead of slow drying in the shade.
ga: Omɔ ŋmeii lɛ baagbala yɛ mli be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo kɛji akɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ tsɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ egbi oya tsɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbi fiofio yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and curling up under the direct sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under strong sunlight because they are sensitive to intense heat. Providing temporary shade using plantain trees protects the young cocoa shoots until they are mature enough to handle direct sunlight.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi ejaakɛ amɛnuɔ dɔlɛ he waa. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo ni dumɔwui kɛhaa lɛ baabu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi tsei lɛ adara bɔ ni sa ni hulu la baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and wrinkling like old paper?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ wolo momo lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from the underside of the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or appropriate sprays stops the curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi kɛ tsei amli helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ neem fɔ loo spray ni sa tsu nii lɛ, abaanyɛ akpa curling.

english: What causes these little caterpillars to eat holes inside the funnel of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn leaf cones lɛ amli?

english: These caterpillars are fall armyworms, which feed on the tender growing center of maize plants. Applying recommended sprays or neem leaf extracts into the leaf funnel early in the morning destroys them before they damage the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni daraa blɛoo lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo neem tso lɛ mli nu ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛshwie nɔ lɛ wo tso lɛ mli tsɔnei lɛ anɔ leebi lɛ, efiteɔ amɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting under the ground before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water pools in the soil for too long, causing fungal infections. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain off, keeping the tubers safe.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ, ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni oyitso ahi shi shweshweeshwe

english: Yellowing leaves and stunted growth usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Adding animal manure, compost, or NPK fertilizer provides the nitrogen your maize needs to grow tall and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo NPK ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha o-ŋmei lɛ aná nitrogen ni he hiaa bo koni ekwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ.

english: How does planting cowpeas on my farm help my maize crop grow better in the next season?
ga: Te tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the cowpea plants decay after harvest, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil to naturally feed the next crop like maize.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsina tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Nakai nitrogen ni aŋã lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii aha sɛɛ mli tsei, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant or irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and adding lime or poultry manure helps the plant get enough calcium.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ lime loo kooloi ashishifã ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛná calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because plants absorb water before the hot afternoon heat, and leaves dry quickly in the sun, which prevents fungal diseases from growing.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ tsei lɛ baaŋɔ nu lɛ dani shwane mli la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ aba. Ni baai lɛ baagbi oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ akaya hiɛ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to catch more sunlight and keeps them off damp soil where diseases spread. Sunlight helps the leaves produce energy to grow large, healthy yam tubers underground.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, ni no ji he ni helai shwereɔ yɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Too many young shoots compete with the main plantain tree for water and soil nutrients. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main tree has enough energy to grow a heavy bunch.
ga: Tsobii bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso lɛ yibii ni tsii.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so quickly when left in the sun on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested crops continue to breathe and lose water. Direct heat speeds up this process and encourages bacteria, causing fruits to soften and rot quickly. Keeping crops shaded and cool slows down aging and spoilage.
ga: Nibii ni akpa ehee lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛnuɔ nu. Dɔlɛ ni yaa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa nɛkɛ nifeemɔ nɛɛ yaa oya ni ekanyaa helatsɛmɛi lɛ. Makes the fruit soft and rot quickly. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛhe jɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛdara ni amɛfite oya.

english: Will putting my harvested vegetables in a cold place or refrigerator damage them?
ga: Ani aduawai ni akpa lɛ ni akɛaawo he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ loo friji mli lɛ baafite amɛ?

english: Most harvested vegetables benefit from cold storage because low temperatures slow down the natural rotting process, keeping crops fresh, firm, and hydrated for a much longer time before going to market.
ga: Aduawai ni akpaa lɛ ateŋ babaoo náa friji mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ he sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulutsoo be ni baa shi lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ehee, eyɛ shiŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ be babaoo dani eshɛɔ jara nɔ.

english: Why do my peppers start rotting faster at the spots where they were squeezed during picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ oya yɛ hei ni ashɛre amɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crushed or bruised, their outer protective skin breaks. This releases juices that attract fungi and bacteria, which easily enter the fruit and cause rapid rotting at the damaged spot.
ga: Kɛji akɛ atswa ŋmɔshi nibii loo atswa lɛ Kponɔgbɛ hewolo ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ fãa. Enɛ jieɔ nu ni gbalaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ. ni boteɔ aduawai lɛ amli oya ni ehaa he ni efite lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Why do green fruits ripen and go soft much faster when placed next to already ripe fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai eŋɔlii lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo oya waa kɛ akɛto amɛhe lɛ? Yibii lɛ ekwɛ̃?

english: Ripe fruits produce a natural ripening gas called ethylene. When green produce is stored near ripe fruits, this gas causes the green produce to mature and soften much faster than normal.
ga: Yibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni haa ekwɛ̃ɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ kpo. Kɛji akɛ akɛ aduawai kɛ aduawai to aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ahe Gas nɛɛ haa aduawai kɛ aduawai shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo oya fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ.

english: What time of day is best for me to harvest leafy crops like cabbage or lettuce?
ga: Mɛɛ be hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ kaabe loo lettuce?

english: Harvesting in the early morning or late evening is best because crops are filled with moisture absorbed overnight. Harvesting in the hot afternoon causes crops to lose water instantly and wilt quickly.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa yɛ leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ tsei lɛ ayiɔ obɔ kɛ nu ni baajɛ mli aba nyɔɔŋ kome mli. Nikpamɔ yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ oya.

english: Why do my fruits get bruised when I pack them into deep woven sacks for transport?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miyibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ akɛwo kotokui ni mli kwɔ ni akpɛ mli koni akɛmaje lɛ?

english: Deep sacks place too much weight on the crops at the bottom. The heavy pressure crushes the lower fruit tissues, causing soft spots and rotting during transit to the market.
ga: Saji ni mli kwɔ lɛ kɛ muji babaoo baa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ. Nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ aduawai lɛ ashishigbɛ fãji lɛ. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ ni efiteɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ.

english: What do big supermarkets look for before buying fresh produce directly from smallholder farmers?
ga: Mɛni shwapoi wuji taoɔ dani amɛheɔ nibii heei kɛjɛɔ okwaafoi bibii adɛŋ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Supermarkets look for clean, uniform produce free of pest damage, dirt, or bruises, and cooled properly so it stays fresh on store shelves for several days.
ga: Shwapoi wuji taoɔ nibii ni he tse, ni yaa nɔ daa. Ebɛ nɔ ko ni tsɛŋemɔ helai, muji loo ŋmeii efiteee lɛ, ni akɛwo friji mli jogbaŋŋ koni ehi shwapoi amli gbii babaoo.

english: How does sorting and grading my crops by size and appearance help me earn more money?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mihalaa kɛ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ naa lɛ baaye abua mi ni maná shika babaoo?

english: Buyers pay higher prices for uniform, high-quality produce. Grouping your crops by quality allows you to sell top-grade items to premium markets instead of selling everything mixed together at a low price.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ jara ni nɔ kwɔ kɛha nibii ni amɛfeɔ daa, ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni ooofee kui yɛ bɔ ni amɛhi ha lɛ naa lɛ haa onyɛɔ ohɔ̃ɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛyaa jara ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohɔ̃ɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni akɛfutu mli lɛ yɛ jara ni baa shi nɔ.

english: What is a pack house, and how does bringing my crops there help my harvest stay fresh?
ga: Mɛni ji pack shia? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaa jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mikpamɔ lɛ ni ehiɔ shi ehee?

english: A pack house is a clean, covered facility where crops are safely cleaned, graded, and stored in cool temperatures right after harvest, preventing heat damage and extending shelf life.
ga: Pack shĩa lɛ ji he ko ni he tse, ni nɔ ko nɔ ko yɔɔ he. Atsuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe, atoɔ amɛhe gbɛjianɔ ni akɛtoɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Etsiɔ dɔlɛ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ naa ni ehaa shihilɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Should I wash my harvested root crops with water right before storing them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ nu aho tsei ni mikpa lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe dani mikɛto?

english: Washing introduces moisture that can cause molds to grow if the crop is not completely dried afterward. It is usually better to brush off loose soil and store crops dry unless you can dry them fully before packing.
ga: Nibii ni afɔɔ he lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni baanyɛ aha ŋmɔtɔ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbiko kwraa yɛ no sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie shikpɔŋ ni etse lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni oha amɛgbi. Ja obaanyɛ ogbi kwraa dani okɛwo tsɔne mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the vital shade and moisture cocoa seedlings need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or that the soil is overly waterlogged. Adding nitrogen-based fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps the plants regain their deep green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ nitrogen fee, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ ni amɛdara waa ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because excess water prevents air from reaching the root zone. Without oxygen, fungal diseases thrive and cause the tubers to decay before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ Fungal helai daa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ dani akpaa.

english: How do I know if worms are damaging my farm, and how do I protect my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii miifite miŋmɔ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Signs of pest worms include ragged holes in leaves and fine sawdust-like waste inside the leaf whorls. Spraying early with recommended botanical remedies like neem oil or approved pesticides protects crops before major damage occurs.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe ji buji ni etse ehe yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akɛwoɔ tsofa mli ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii, tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ afɔ nɔ mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe dani efite waa.

english: Is it better for me to plant my crops in straight lines rather than broadcasting the seeds?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu tsei yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui?

english: Planting in straight lines ensures correct spacing so each plant gets equal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. It also makes weeding, fertilizing, and harvesting much easier compared to broadcasting.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa anáa gbɛ ni sa bɔni afee ni tso fɛɛ tso aná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ falɛ kome. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛ akɛto adafitswaa he.

english: How can I tell when my sweet potatoes are ripe enough to dig out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potato lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Sweet potatoes are usually ready when the vines and leaves begin to turn yellow and dry up, typically three to four months after planting. You can carefully dig up one plant to check if the tubers are full-sized.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ klalo kɛji wain tsei lɛ kɛ baai lɛ je shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee nyɔji 3-4 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu tso kome he nii koni okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ ayi fa.

english: Why do flowers drop off my tomato plants without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when weather temperatures become too hot or when the soil goes from dry to wet too suddenly. Maintaining consistent watering and using mulch around the base keeps the plants stable enough to set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli trukaa tsɔ lɛ. Kwɛmɔ nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ he daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Shishitoo lɛ haa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni ewo yibii.

english: Why is it good for me to plant beans or groundnuts in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the field, they naturally feed the soil and improve the growth of neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛhaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to apply fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer early in the morning or late in the afternoon when temperatures are cool. Applying chemical fertilizer during the hot midday heat on dry soil can burn plant leaves and roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi loo shwane be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ baai kɛ shishifãi ashã.

english: Why must I thoroughly dry my harvested corn before putting it in storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mahã mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ dani mikɛwo kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii amli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Drying corn reduces moisture that attracts mold, fungal toxins, and destructive grain insects. Properly dried corn stays safe for consumption and market sale for many months without spoiling.
ga: Abele ni agbiɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baa shi. Mycotoxins kɛ dumɔwui amli kooloi ni fiteɔ nii Abele ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha niyeli kɛ jarayeli yɛ jara nɔ nyɔji babaoo ni efiteee.

english: Why is flat land usually considered better for planting food crops than land on a hill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ abuɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ akɛ ehi kɛha niyenii adumɔ fe shikpɔŋ ni gɔji yɔɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Flat land holds onto topsoil and moisture much better than hills. When you plant on flat ground, rain sinks into the soil to feed crop roots instead of washing away the soil and fertilizer downhill.
ga: Hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ hiɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ fe gɔji lɛ. Kɛji odu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ Nugbɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ niyenii aha tso shishifãi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛya gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ

english: Can farming on a steep hillside cause my crops to fail completely?
ga: Ani okwaayeli ni mifeɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha minibii lɛ afite kwraa?

english: Yes, because heavy rains can strip away the rich topsoil where plant nutrients live. Without good topsoil, crops become weak, stunted, and produce very little harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afite ŋwɛi sũ ni baa nii ni haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii kpakpai lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ kpakpa bɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baagbɔjɔ, amɛbaagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: How do I know if my farm land is too steep to plant cassava or corn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwɔ tsɔ ni minyɛɛɛ madu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: If rainwater forms fast-moving streams that dig deep grooves or channels into your dirt after a rainstorm, the slope is too steep to plant safely without building soil barriers first.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nu lɛ fee faa ko ni hoɔ oya ni shwieɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ kɛyaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Gbɛjegbɛ lɛ nɔ kwɔ tsɔ ni anyɛɛɛ adu shweshweeshwe ni amaaa gbogbo ni akɛfiɔ he lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: How can I stop heavy rain from washing away my crops and topsoil when I farm on a hill?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekashwie miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni miitsu okwaayeli yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: You can plant grass strips or make dirt ridges across the slope along the hillside. This slows down flowing rainwater, giving it time to soak into the ground instead of carrying your soil away.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu jwɛi yɛ sɛɛkuu mli loo ofee ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni tsɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ shishigbɛ. Enɛ baaha nugbɔ nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Enɛ haa enáa be ni ekɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeewo sũ lɛ kɛya.

english: Why does soil on a hillside dry out much faster after rain than land down in the valley?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Gravity pulls rainwater downhill quickly, so water does not stay long in hillside soil. In lower areas, water settles and remains in the dirt longer, keeping crop roots wet.
ga: Nibii ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbalaa nugbɔ nu kɛbaa shi oya. No hewɔ lɛ, nu sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ yɛ sũ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ mli. yɛ shishigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ Nu lɛ baaho shi ni ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be babaoo. Okɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ afɔ.

english: What simple steps can I take to keep moisture in the soil on my hillside farm during hot days?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafee nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Mɛni yɔɔ ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi gɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔ ko mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli?

english: You can cover the ground around your crops with dried grass, leaves, or straw. This acts as a protective blanket that shields the dirt from the hot sun and keeps moisture trapped longer.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi, baai, loo jwɛi aha he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ, ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ muji he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and rot when I plant them in the wet land at the base of a hill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko shishi lɛ?

english: Water collects at the bottom of hills and drowns the roots of most crops, preventing them from taking in air. Most regular food crops need well-drained soil where water does not sit for too long.
ga: Nu buaa ehe naa yɛ gɔji lɛ ashishi ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekabote Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni nu lɛ eshwɛɛɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ

english: What kinds of crops grow best in low, watery areas at the bottom of hills?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni baa shi ni nu yɔɔ yɛ gɔji ashishi lɛ?

english: Crops that naturally love plenty of water—such as rice, sugarcane, cocoyam, and leafy vegetables—grow very well in valley bottoms where water settles.
ga: Tsei ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ amɛsumɔɔ nu babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kookoo, kɛ aduawai ni baai yɔɔ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ.

english: How does water flowing down from the top of a hill affect the crops I plant at the bottom?
ga: Te nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ gɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Flowing water brings good topsoil and nutrients down to the valley, making it fertile. However, if too much water rushes down at once, it can flood your fields and bury young crops in mud.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kɛ niyenii kpakpai baa jɔɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ babaoo. Shi kɛlɛ, kɛji nu babaoo ho shikome lɛ, Ebaanyɛ ekɛ nu awo oŋmɔji amli ni efu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ awo muji lɛ mli.

english: How does clearing all the trees on a hill affect farming for the rest of the village down below?
ga: Te tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ saa okwaayeli he ahaa akrowa ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Trees on hills act like giant sponges and anchors for the soil. Clearing them causes rainwater to rush down uncontrolled, causing soil loss on the hill and flooding or destroying crops on farms in the valley below.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji wuji ni amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ shi ni anyɛɛɛ akudɔ. ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ fiteɔ kɛ nu afua loo efiteɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ jɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: This is often caused by the cassava mosaic virus, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stems and controlling insects prevents the leaves from curling and keeps the roots growing big.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whitefly lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Kɛ akɛ ŋmei tsei tsu nii kɛtsi helai anaa kɛ kooloi akudɔmɔ lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe ni ebaaha shishifãi wuji adara.

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and causes their pollen to dry out, so flowers drop off unpollinated. Providing light shade and keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plants hold onto their flowers and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni pollination bɛ mli. Shade ni mli tse ni akɛhaa kɛ sũ mli fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔii ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do weeds make my maize grow short and yellowish even when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa mi ŋmãa lɛ feɔ kuku ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your maize for plant food (nutrients) in the soil. Even with plenty of water, the weeds steal the food first, leaving your maize starved and stunted unless you clear them early.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ o-corn lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha tsei aniyenii (nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ) yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ moŋ. Jwɛi baaju niyenii klɛŋklɛŋ. Ha hɔmɔ aye o-corn lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ja ojie amɛ kɛjɛ ohe klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that scorch under direct sunlight. Leaving larger shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains nearby protects the seedlings from heat and keeps the soil moist while they establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo adu dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: The season's first rain usually wets only the surface soil, which dries out quickly under the heat of the following days. Waiting for two or three steady rains ensures deep soil moisture so seeds can sprout safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Enɛ baagbi oya yɛ gbii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli latsaa be mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛkɛ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Will planting cowpeas between my rows of maize damage my maize crop?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaye mi ŋmãa lɛ awui?

english: No, cowpeas actually help maize because they are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them together improves soil nutrients and gives you two different harvests from one field.
ga: Dabi, cowpea yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa diɛŋtsɛ. Ejaakɛ eji ŋmãa ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei enyɔ lɛ fee ekome lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ. ni amɛfee nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why does my land produce a huge harvest in the first year after clearing, but much less in the second year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wo yibii babaoo nɛkɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli beni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii lɛ? Shi nɔ ni baa shi kwraa yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli?

english: Clearing fresh bush releases a burst of natural nutrients into the soil for your first crop. However, crops quickly consume these nutrients, so without adding compost, manure, or fertilizer, the soil loses its strength for the next season.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie sũ tsei lɛ, ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kpakpai kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli kɛha oklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, shi kɛlɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ niyenii nɛɛ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite hewalɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: How do I know when my maize is fully ripe and ready to harvest from the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Maize is ready when the outer husks turn dry and brown, the silks turn dark brown, and the grains inside are hard with a small dark mark at the base where they attach to the cob.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. Siliki lɛ etsɔ asarasu ni tsuɔ waa. ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ wa ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ yɔɔ mli. At the base attached to the corn cob

english: Yams rot when stored in hot, poorly ventilated places or when bruised during harvesting. Keeping tubers on raised racks in a cool, well-shaded, and airy barn prevents moisture buildup and stops rot fungi from growing.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto hei ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli. aloo kɛji akɛ egbɔjɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni awo nɔ lɛ to shĩa ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe, ni ebaatsi ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni shwereɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why should I prune some of the lower branches on my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Removing lower, unproductive branches allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the inner parts of the plant and stops soil diseases from splashing onto the leaves, directing the plant's energy into growing bigger peppers.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni wooo yibii lɛ ni afolɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ mli. ni ehaa helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ naa hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize plants keep turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen deep into the ground where small roots cannot reach it, or the soil may need fertilizer or compost added.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. anyɛɛɛ ashɛ he Aloo ekolɛ ehe baahia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes, which means they can pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This acts like natural fertilizer for your maize while also protecting the soil from washing away during heavy rains.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha o-corn lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hu he koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akahole lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce much smaller maize yields when I plant it in the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo kwraa beni miduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. It also allows pests and soil diseases that feed on maize to multiply, so rotating with other crops keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ hu yaa hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi atsake. Ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to harsh sunlight and need partial shade to survive. Tall trees act like protective umbrellas that keep the seedlings cool and hold moisture in the soil until the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa ni amɛtaoɔ hulutsoo fioo koni amɛhi shi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta, ni amɛhaa dumɔwui lɛ amli jɔɔ ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa waa.

english: Does it matter which direction I insert a cassava stem cutting into the soil when planting?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ akɛ ŋmei tsei ni afo lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, planting cassava stems upside down will cause weak shoots or prevent them from growing entirely. You should look for the tiny buds on the stem and make sure they are pointing upward toward the sky before pushing the stick into the ground.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ loo ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ kwraa. Esa akɛ otao ŋmeii bibii. yɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni okwɛ akɛ amɛmiitsɔɔ ŋwɛi dani okɛ tso lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I pinch off the small side branches growing on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei niji bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Pruning extra side shoots forces the plant to send its energy and water into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes instead of wasteful leaves. It also allows air to flow through the branches, which prevents fungal diseases.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛbaakpa tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ baaha tso lɛ atsu ehewalɛ kɛ nu lɛ he nii ni ekɛfee tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo moŋ fe ni eeefite baai lɛ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hu tsɔɔ tsei lɛ aniji amli, ni no tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers without growing any peppers during hot spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shi ni eduuu pepper ko kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, pepper plants experience heat stress and drop their blossoms to save energy and survive. Adding dried grass or mulch around the roots helps keep the soil cool and moist during hot periods.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ kɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ kpeɔ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo sũ ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ.

english: Why do dark, sunken rot spots appear on the bottom of my tomatoes before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ tomatoi ashishi dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit, usually due to irregular watering. When the soil swings from very dry to very wet, the plant cannot transport nutrients evenly, damaging the developing fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ shihilɛ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni shɛɛɛ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ ni faaa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ he ni egbi waa kɛtee he ni edɔ waa lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aya he fɛɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai ni miida lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow and spread so much faster than my crop seeds after the first rainy season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to survive hard conditions, so their seeds sprout immediately at the first sign of water. Crop seeds take longer to wake up and start growing, giving weeds an early advantage.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛdumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛji amɛna nu he okadi klɛŋklɛŋ. Dumɔwui heɔ be babaoo dani amɛteɔ shi ni amɛjeɔ dalɛ shishi. Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ náa sɛɛnamɔ mra.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start to rot quickly when I store them under a metal roof?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ oya beni mikɛto dade tsũ ko shishi lɛ?

english: Metal sheets trap extreme heat, which bakes the harvested yams and speeds up decay and rot. Yams need a cool, shaded, and airy shelter—like a wooden yam barn or grass-thatched roof—to stay fresh for months.
ga: Dade tsɔji lɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa. ni shãa ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ yaa oya. He ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ he miihia sweet potatoes. kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni tsɔɔ mli, tamɔ tso ni akɛfee sweet potato shĩa loo jwɛi ni akɛwo ŋwɛitsu nɔ Koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ nyɔji babaoo.

english: What does potassium fertilizer actually do to my crops to make them perform better?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni potassium ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ? Koni tsei lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Potassium acts like an immunity booster for plants. It helps crops grow strong stems, fight off diseases, and hold onto water during dry spells, which leads to bigger fruits and tubers like cassava, yam, and plantain.
ga: Potassium tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni haa gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli hewalɛ ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ yaa tsei. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni wa, amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ helai ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Enɛ haa anáa aduawai kɛ ŋmeii wuji, tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, kɛ ŋmei.

english: How do I know if agrochemicals will help my crops or if they will damage my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji agrochemicals lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii loo ebaaye mishikpɔŋ lɛ awui?

english: When used in the correct amounts, agrochemicals safely kill destructive pests and weeds so your crops can grow without competition. However, overusing them or using the wrong type can spoil the soil, so following extension guidelines is key.
ga: Kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ bɔ ni sa mli lɛ, Agrochemicals lɛ gbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ jwɛi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ shweshweeshwe. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli. Shi kɛlɛ, kɛ́ akɛtsu nii fe nine loo akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ fɔŋ nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite sũ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni anyiɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni kɔɔ shweremɔ he lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why should I talk to an agricultural officer before deciding what inputs to buy for my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ okwaayeli he najiaŋdamɔlɔ awie dani makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ nibii ni mikɛbaahe kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Agricultural extension officers can test your soil and evaluate your land to tell you exactly what nutrient or chemical your crops need, preventing you from wasting money on chemicals that won't work on your specific farm.
ga: Okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aka oshikpɔŋ lɛ akwɛ ni ekwɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛɛ bo niyenii loo tsofai pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. Enɛ ji koni akafite shika yɛ tsofai ni tsuuu nii yɛ oŋmɔ pɔtɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dry before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a cry for help showing that the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that water is sitting around the roots for too long, preventing the plant from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji yelikɛbuamɔ he bolɔmɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ nu eta shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi

english: Why do my young cocoa pods shrivel up and drop off the trees early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigbee shi kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ oya nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Young pods wilt when the tree does not have enough food or water to feed all of them at once, or when sap-sucking insects attack. Proper fertilization, especially with potassium, helps the tree carry pods to maturity.
ga: Pods bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛ fɛɛ amɛye shikome. aloo kɛ́ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutua fɔmɔ nii ni sa Titri lɛ kɛ potassium, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ etsitsii lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa kwraa.

english: Will spraying weed killers on my farm harm my crops while killing the grass?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui yɛ be mli ni egbeɔ jwɛi lɛ?

english: Selective weedicides target only specific weeds and leave crops unharmed, while non-selective weedicides destroy any plant material they touch. You must use the right type and spray carefully so crop leaves are not coated.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ahalaa lɛ tsɔɔ jwɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi pɛ anɔ ni amɛshiɔ tsei lɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efeee amɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni halaaa lɛ fiteɔ tso mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. ni amɛtaa he Esa akɛ akɛ nɔ ni ja lɛ atsu nii ni akɛshwie nɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni ekɛ tsofa akawo tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: How can securing financial support like a bank loan help improve my harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shika he yelikɛbuamɔ tamɔ shikatoohe nyɔmɔwoo ni maná lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni mikpamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Having financial support allows you to buy certified seeds, fertilizers, and land clearing services on time, ensuring you plant right at the start of the rains instead of missing the best growing window.
ga: Shika yelikɛbuamɔ haa onyɛɔ oheɔ dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔi ni awo he odase yɛ be naa. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ nii kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ lɛ shishijee mli tɔ̃ɔ moŋ fe ni oookpa dumɔ be ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do crops grow better when I loosen the soil deeply before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani midu lɛ?

english: Deep soil preparation breaks hard ground so roots can easily spread out to search for food and water deep underground. It also allows heavy rains to soak into the earth rather than washing away your topsoil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni asaa he lɛ gbalaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya koni amɛyatao niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeefɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Dropping leaves is a self-defense mechanism for cassava to save moisture during hot weather. The plant goes to sleep above ground while safely storing its energy in the underground tubers until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni ŋmei tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe. Bɔni afee ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ toɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How do spray chemicals protect my vegetables from being eaten by insects?
ga: Te tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu mi-vegetables lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi akaye amɛ lɛ he aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Pesticides either coat the leaves to create a bitter, poisonous barrier that deters insects, or kill pests directly on contact when they try to feed on the crop's soft tissue.
ga: Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ haa baai lɛ ahe koni ekɛfee gbɛtsii nii ko ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ poison ni baatsi kooloi lɛ anaa. aloo egbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛji amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛye ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen. Maize plants are smart—when food is scarce, they move nitrogen from older bottom leaves to feed young top leaves, so adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure will solve this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei lɛ yɛ nilee. Kɛ niyenii faaa Ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni eda ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and droop in the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni mifeee nakai lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: Under strong sunshine, pepper leaves lose water faster than their roots can drink it up. The leaves curl to protect themselves from losing too much water, and as long as they recover by evening, it is just a normal reaction to midday heat.
ga: yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. Ni be fɛɛ be ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ Eji nɔ ko kɛkɛ ni afeɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ he.

english: Why would I plant my tomatoes inside a plastic greenhouse structure instead of directly in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tomato yɛ plastic greenhouse mli moŋ fe ni madu yɛ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Greenhouses shield tomato plants from heavy rain that washes away soil nutrients and spreads diseases. The cover also keeps out destructive insect pests, allowing the crop to grow healthier and yield good fruit all year round.
ga: Greenhouses buɔ tomato tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni shwieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni egbɛɔ helai eshwaa lɛ he. Nɔ ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ hu buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe. Ha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit during very hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat makes tomato pollen dry up and become sterile, so the plant cannot form seeds. Without seed formation, the plant sheds the useless flower to save energy for when weather conditions improve.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato mli ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Tso lɛ nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui. Kɛji akɛ abɔɔɔ dumɔwui ko lɛ Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ lɛlɛ lɛ hi.

english: Plantains have shallow roots that do not go deep into the earth. When the fruit heavy bunch grows, it changes the plant's center of gravity, so strong winds can easily pull the roots up unless you prop the tree with a bamboo pole.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji aduawai akui babaoo dara lɛ Ebaatsake tso lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi oya. Ja okɛ ŋmei tsei tsu nii kɛfi tsei lɛ asɛɛ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and dry up right on the tree branches?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a water-loving fungus that multiplies in high moisture and heavy shade. Clearing surrounding weeds and trimming shade trees lets in air and sunlight, which dries up the damp environment the fungus needs to survive.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni sumɔɔ nu, ni nɔ ni kadiɔ lɛ ji hulutsoo ni fa kɛ hulutsoo babaoo. Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Ni afolɔ tsei lɛ amli koni amɛha hulutsoo koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa ŋmei lɛ koni ehi shi lɛ mli agbiɔ.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow tall and thin with very tiny cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: Planted too closely, maize seeds compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The stalks stretch tall to fight for sunlight instead of building strong stems and large cobs.
ga: planted too close Abele dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tso lɛ mli tsei lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛkɛ hulu lɛ awuu, moŋ lɛ, amɛfeɔ tsei ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do some of my planted seeds sprout in three days while others in the same row take a week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ gbii etɛ mli ni ekrokomɛi hu kwɛɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ line kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ, ehiɔ shi otsi kome.

english: Seeds sprout at different times if they were planted at different depths or if the soil moisture is uneven. Planting seeds at the same shallow depth ensures they absorb water equally and sprout at the same time.
ga: Dumɔwui baakwɛ̃ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ hei srɔtoi ni mli kwɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ejaaa. Dumɔwui lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa dumɔwui lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu babaoo tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ. kɛ amɛhe feɔ ekome ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli

english: Young cocoa leaves are delicate and burn under full sunshine. Tall trees or companion crops like plantains create a shaded, cool micro-environment that shields young cocoa plants until they grow tough enough to handle direct sunlight.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei kakadaji loo tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ plantains lɛ feɔ shihilɛ bibioo ko ni mli ejɔ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo. Enɛ buɔ cacao tso bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa ni enáa hulu la tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How does clearing weeds around my cassava mounds help the tubers under the ground grow bigger?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni bɔle ŋmei ŋtayaa lɛ he lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Weeds consume the soil water, sunlight, and nutrients that cassava leaves need to produce food. When you keep the plot clean, the plant directs all its extra energy down into expanding the underground tubers.
ga: Jwɛi yeɔ sũ mli nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa simɔ baa koni ená niyenii. Kɛji oha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ he tse lɛ Tso lɛ tsuɔ ehewalɛ ni fa lɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛgbala ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why are some farmers growing their vegetables inside transparent plastic houses instead of open fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ aduawai yɛ plastic tsũi ni mli tse mli moŋ fe ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Growing crops inside a greenhouse protects them from harsh sunlight, heavy rains, and pests. It creates a controlled environment where moisture and temperature stay steady, helping plants grow faster and produce better yields all year.
ga: Tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ greenhouse mli lɛ buɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Bɔɔ shihilɛ ni akudɔ ni hulutsoo kɛ latsaa yɔɔ mli daa Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How does growing crops inside an enclosed structure stop insects from destroying the leaves?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsũ ko ni afo mli lɛ mli lɛ atsĩ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafite baai lɛ?

english: The greenhouse structure acts as a physical net or barrier that keeps destructive pests like whiteflies and caterpillars outside. This protects the crops without needing to spray heavy chemical pesticides constantly.
ga: Greenhouse lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋshɔŋloo loo gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ni haa kooloi ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ jeɔ kpo. Enɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni tsii ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ashwie nɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Which specific crops grow best inside a greenhouse setup?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Delicate and high-value crops like tomatoes, sweet peppers, cucumbers, and lettuce thrive best because they are sensitive to heavy rains, extreme heat, and insect attacks in open fields.
ga: Tsei ni waaa, ni jara wa waa tamɔ tomato, shito, kukumba, kɛ lettuce daa jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ nuɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɛ koolooi ni tutuaa amɛ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ahe waa.

english: Why do vegetables grown in a controlled greenhouse usually look bigger and cleaner than open-field crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni akudɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe tse fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Inside a greenhouse, plants do not have to fight against weeds, strong winds, or heavy mud splash from rain. Because they stay stress-free, all their energy goes directly into growing large, clean, and healthy fruits.
ga: Yɛ greenhouse lɛ mli Ehe ehiaaa ni tsei kɛ jwɛi, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, loo muji ni tsii ni nugbɔ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ akpee. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbɛ haomɔ ko. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ aduawai wuji ni he tse, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can I grow high-value vegetables like tomatoes if I work a full-time job in town and cannot be on the farm every day?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu aduawai ni jara wa tamɔ tomato kɛji mikɛ be fɛɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli shi minyɛɛɛ maya ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbi?

english: Yes, by using an automated greenhouse system, automated timers and sensors take care of daily watering and feeding for you. This allows you to manage a successful farm while only visiting occasionally to check on progress.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ tsɔne ko ni haa jeŋ dɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Be he nibii ni tsuɔ nii diɛŋtsɛ kɛ nibii ni nuɔ he lɛ kwɛɔ nu ni okɛhaa bo daa gbi kɛ niyenii ni ohaa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ ŋmɔ ko ni yeɔ omanye nɔ yɛ be mli ni oyasaraa yɛ bei komɛi amli pɛ koni okwɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ ehaa.

english: How can my crops receive water automatically when I am not around on the farm?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa nu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛ́ mibɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Automated drip systems use timers or soil moisture sensors connected to water tanks. They automatically turn on to deliver exact amounts of water directly to the roots of your plants at scheduled times during the day.
ga: Nu ni shwieɔ shi ni haa nu shwieɔ shi lɛ kɛ be loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni nuɔ he ni akɛtsa nu tanki mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Etsuɔ ehe koni ekɛ nu abɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ aba otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli.

english: What key things should I inspect when I drop by to check on my automated farm once a week?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii ni he hiaa esa akɛ makwɛ mli kɛ́ mibakwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome yɛ otsi mli?

english: When you visit, check that the irrigation drip lines are flowing smoothly without blockages, inspect the leaf color for signs of nutrient shortages, and look closely for any early signs of disease or pests.
ga: Kɛ oyasara lɛ Kwɛmɔ akɛ drip line lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii enaa. Kwɛmɔ baa lɛ su kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa. Ni okwɛ hela loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe okadii mra.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and dry up when the afternoon sun becomes too harsh?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ ni egbiɔ beni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa shwane lɛ?

english: During intense afternoon heat, leaves lose water faster through evaporation than the roots can suck up from dry soil. Keeping soil moisture steady or shading the plants stops them from wilting under strong heat.
