ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee aduawai gbogboi ni wa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa kɛ nu afua ni baa oya

english: How does covering the soil with dry grass around my vegetable crops help them survive hot dry days?
ga: Mulching shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni ebɔle he Te mi tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ amli tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like an umbrella that blocks direct sunlight from evaporating soil moisture, keeps roots cool, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Mulching kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers keep dropping off before growing into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛmiitsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when they suffer stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or too much water standing around their roots. It can also happen when tiny pests feed on the flower stems.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji kooloi bibii ye fɔfɔi lɛ ahe tsei lɛ.

english: When crops are crowded, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and food. They stretch upward quickly to reach sunlight before their neighbors do, making stems thin and fragile.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe oya koni amɛná hulu la lɛ dani amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ hu. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings die when I move them directly from nursery shade into full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie amɛ kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛtee hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings grown in shade have soft, tender stems that get burned easily in direct sun. They need a few days of gradual exposure to morning sun first so they can toughen up before final planting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu shãa amɛ oya. Ehe miihia ni amɛye gbii fioo komɛi fiofio yɛ leebi hulu la lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ bɔni afee ni amɛhe wa dani amɛdu naagbee.

english: Why don't the seeds I save from my harvest produce plants as strong as the packaged seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ wooo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tamɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli ni miheɔ lɛ?

english: Many commercial seeds are specially bred hybrids designed for one strong generation. The seeds saved from those crops lose those parent traits, producing uneven plants with smaller yields.
ga: Jarayeli dumɔwui babaoo ji dumɔwui ni afee amɛ krɛdɛɛ aha yinɔi ni wa. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛfɔlɔi asui lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ ekome ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: How do I know the exact time a crop will be ready for harvest after planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Different crops have specific maturity cycles. Knowing the expected maturity time and checking physical signs—like yellowing leaves on maize or firm pods on beans—helps you harvest at peak quality before crops begin to spoil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ni amɛdaraa. Be ni akpaa gbɛ akɛ ebaakwɛ lɛ ni ooole kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii tamɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ loo ŋmãa ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmãa lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ nɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ jeɔ shishi efiteɔ.

english: Why do some crops take three months to yield while leafy vegetables take only a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi heɔ nyɔji etɛ dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ heɔ otsii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Crops develop at different speeds based on their type. Leafy greens only need to grow leaves, while grain or root crops take months to build flowers, seeds, or tubers that store energy.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli yɛ amɛhenɔi lɛ anaa. Ehe miihia ni akɛ baai pɛ adu tsei ni yɔɔ baai. Yɛ be mli ni dumɔwu loo tso ni shishifãi yɔɔ lɛ heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani ekɛ fɔfɔi, dumɔwu loo bulb ni kɛ hewalɛ toɔ lɛ baa.

english: Can I harvest my crops early if I need quick money, or will that reduce my yield?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii mra kɛji shika he miihia mi oya? Aloo ebaaha nitsumɔ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ aba shi?

english: Harvesting too early usually results in undersized, watery, or immature produce that spoils fast and sells for lower prices, so waiting for full maturity gives the best return on your effort.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nibii ni akpaa mra tsɔ lɛ haa nibii bibii, ni nu yɔɔ mli, loo ni edako ni fiteɔ oya ni ahɔ̃ɔ kɛ jara ni baa shi baa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi amɛdara lɛ, ebaaha oná mɔdɛŋ ni obɔ lɛ he sɛɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: What causes my crops to dry up and wither just one month after planting?
ga: Mɛni haa midumɔ nii lɛ gĩɔ ni egboɔ yɛ nyɔŋ kome pɛ sɛɛ beni midu lɛ?

english: Early withering is usually a sign of environmental stress, such as a sudden lack of rainfall, nutrient-poor soil, or root damage caused by soil pests and fungal diseases.
ga: ni egboɔ mra Bei pii lɛ eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ shihilɛ mli nibii miihao, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa loo shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli. loo shishifãi ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛbaa lɛ.

english: Will I incur financial losses if my crop takes longer to mature than the seed seller told me?
ga: Ani shika baafite mi kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ fe bɔ ni dumɔwui ahɔ̃ɔlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi lɛ?

english: A longer growing period requires extra labor and weeding costs, but as long as the crop remains healthy, a delayed harvest will still yield sellable produce rather than a total loss.
ga: Be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ jwɛi lɛ biɔ nitsumɔ kroko kɛ shika babaoo kɛha jwɛi lɛ ajiemɔ. Shi be fɛɛ be ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baahi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ Nikpamɔ ni baa sɛɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ lolo moŋ fe nɔ ni baafite kwraa.

english: What happens if I leave mature crops in the farm past their harvest time?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi ŋmɔshi nibii ni eda yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛho kpamɔɔ be lɛ he?

english: Leaving ripe crops in the field causes them to dry out excessively, rot, or get attacked by birds and field insects, which ruins their quality and leads to heavy losses.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛgbi tsɔ, amɛgboi, loo okpoi kɛ kooloi bibii baatutua amɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni ekɛ nibii babaoo laajeɔ.

english: How do I tell if my plant is withering from disease or just drying up naturally before harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mitso lɛ miigbo yɛ hela hewɔ loo eegbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛkɛ dani akpa?

english: Natural drying happens evenly across the whole field when plants reach maturity, whereas disease causes patchy wilting, spotted leaves, or soft stems on plants that are still growing.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ baa mli pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ. yɛ be mli ni hela lɛ haa tsei ni miida lolo lɛ ahe fãi ni egbo, baai ni yɔɔ srɔtoi, loo tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ baa.

english: Why should I try new crop varieties from agricultural researchers instead of my traditional seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni jɛ okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi adɛŋ lɛ makwɛ moŋ fe mishishijee dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Researched seed varieties are bred specifically to grow faster, yield more produce, and withstand local droughts or pests better than traditional farm-saved seeds.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atao mli lɛ amli pɔtɛɛ koni amɛdara oya. ewoɔ dumɔwui ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ loo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ babaoo fe dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ blema ŋmɔji amli lɛ.

english: How can I prevent my crops from dying if the rains stop earlier than expected?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbo kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ?

english: You can cover the soil around your crops with dried grass (mulching) to retain groundwater, or plant fast-maturing seeds that finish growing before the dry weather sets in.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Okɛ jwɛi (mulch) atsu onibii ahe nii koni shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ ahi shi. Aloo dumɔ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni baakwɛ̃ dani hulutsoo be lɛ aba.

english: Is it better for a farmer to plant short-duration crops or long-duration crops for reliable income?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ okwaafoi baadu ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kukuoo loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ koni amɛná shika ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ?

english: Short-duration crops provide quick cash flow multiple times a year, while long-duration crops often yield larger quantities; combining both spreads out your financial risk.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ haa shika baa oya shii abɔ yɛ afi mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo. Kɛ́ okɛ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaha oshika he oshara lɛ afee srɔtoi.

english: Why can't I rely on the traditional rain patterns from past decades to know when to plant my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mikɛ mihe afɔ̃ blema nugbɔshiimɔi ni yɔɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni eho lɛ anɔ koni male be ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Climate patterns have shifted over time, making rainfall far more unpredictable than in previous decades. Farmers now need to rely on modern seasonal forecasts and use fast-maturing seed varieties that can yield food before dry spells set in.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsakeɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Enɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ atsɔɔ mli fe afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni eho lɛ. Amrɔ nɛɛ ehe miihia ni okwaafoi kɛ amɛhe afɔ̃ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ be he gbalɛi anɔ. ni okɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra ni baanyɛ awo yibii dani hulutsoo be lɛ aba lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow and stay small even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efeɔ bibii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow and stunted leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food for crops. Adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer gives the maize the nutrients it needs to turn deep green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii Kɛ́ akɛ organic fertilizer loo nitrogen fertilizer fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ ŋmãa ni mli edɔ ni etsɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is my farmland producing smaller harvests every year even though I farm the exact same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikwɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same piece of land year after year drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating your crops, especially by planting legumes like beans or groundnuts, puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri kɛtsɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in direct, intense sunlight. Keeping large trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides necessary shade and preserves soil moisture while the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa, ni kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, amɛshãa oya. Tsei wuji akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do I get smaller crops when I plant seeds very close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii anɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing allows its roots and leaves to spread out and produce bigger yields.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Yam tubers grow under the ground and need loose, soft earth to expand smoothly. Planting yams in high, well-mounded earth ridges makes it easy for the tubers to grow deep and straight.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ mlɛo.

english: Curled and patchy leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. Planting stem cuttings from certified disease-resistant cassava varieties stops the disease from taking over your farm.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Aduɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe ni ana he odase akɛ amɛduɔ lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni helai akaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce far less food if I leave them in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo kwraa kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, water, and soil food directly from your crops. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks of planting ensures your crops get all the resources they need to yield well.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds instead of saving seeds from my last harvest to plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni madu?

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred to resist local pests, tolerate dry spells, and produce high yields. Saved seeds lose these strong qualities over time, leading to weaker crops and lower harvests.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Enyɛɔ shiɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛ lɛ laajeɔ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa shi ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do insects destroy my stored beans and maize after just a few months in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miifite mi ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ nyɔji fioo pɛ ni mikɛhi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Grains attract storage pests like weevils if they are not dried completely or if they are stored in open containers. Drying grains thoroughly and storing them in sealed, airtight bags cuts off oxygen and stops insects from surviving.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ baagbala kooloi ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe, tamɔ ŋmeii, kɛji akɛ amɛgbiko kwraa loo akɛtoɔ tsɛnsii ni agbele mli. Nibii ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ kotokui ni akɛ vacuum efo mli lɛ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ, ni ehaa kooloi bibii lɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth, or the soil is waterlogged. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or improving soil drainage helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops now compared to when I started farming it years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii faaa fe beni mibɔi okwaayeli afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Over time, growing crops repeatedly removes natural nutrients from the soil. Without resting the land, adding compost, or applying proper fertilizers, the soil becomes exhausted and yields naturally decline.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Tsei ni miida lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli shii abɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa atsu nii. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafite ni nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why does burning my cleared farm bushes make the soil poor after just a couple of seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ashãa yɛ miŋmɔ ni ajie lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ bei fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: While burning clears land quickly, the extreme heat destroys essential organic matter and beneficial soil organisms that feed your crops. Over time, it leaves the soil hard, dry, and depleted of natural nutrients.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, la ni ashãa lɛ haa jɛmɛ tseɔ oya. Shi dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni he hiaa ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa, ni egbiɔ, ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and small when I plant the cuttings close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their root systems compete with each other for space, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and food to grow large, healthy tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I plant leguminous crops like cowpeas together with my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ?

english: Legumes take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil for neighboring crops while providing an additional harvest from the same field.
ga: Legumes lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha tsei ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ajieɔ nibii krokomɛi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops even when they start at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛje shishi yɛ be kome mli moŋ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants adapted to quickly steal water, sunlight, and nutrients from the soil. Clearing them early in the season ensures your young crops get the resources they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛju nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha otsei bibii lɛ aná nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Sowing immediately after the very first rain is risky because the soil can quickly dry up if the rain stops. It is best to wait until the rains become regular and the soil remains consistently moist for a few days.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyɛ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aku esɛɛ aba bɔ ni sa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ gbii fioo komɛi.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop during the middle of the day even when the soil is not completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbiko kwraa lɛ?

english: In intense heat, leaves lose water faster than the roots can suck it up from the ground. The plant temporarily droops its leaves to save moisture, and it usually recovers as the temperature cools down in the evening.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baashwie baai lɛ shi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are the flowers and tiny fruits on my pepper plants falling off before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai bibii No hewɔ lɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Flower and fruit drop usually happens when plants suffer from water stress, sudden heat spikes, or attacks by tiny pests like thrips. Regular watering and safe pest control during flowering can prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni baa shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ naa nu he haomɔ. Dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ trukaa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa daa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do my young plantain suckers wither and die when exposed to strong afternoon sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young suckers have limited root systems and broad leaves that lose water very quickly in direct heat. Providing light shade or placing mulch around the base keeps the soil cool and moist until the roots establish.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni faaa kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni nu fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni haa hulutsoo loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔleɔ he lɛ Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baaje shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need to be planted under shade trees when they are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ yɛ hulutsoo shishi lɛ? Ani eji bibioo lolo?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely tender and vulnerable to heat. Shade trees act as natural umbrellas, protecting the tender leaves from burning in strong sunlight and helping the soil retain moisture until the cocoa trees grow old enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni hulutsoo baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ oya. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade. Buu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ adamɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why are my tomato seedlings falling over and dying just a few days after sprouting in the nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This usually happens because young seedlings are very delicate and susceptible to dampness and fungal attack at their base. Excess water and crowded growth create rot; keeping proper spacing and avoiding overwatering protects tender stems while they establish roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ dumɔwui lɛ darako waa ni amɛnuɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni baa amɛshishi lɛ ahe waa. Nu ni fa fe nine kɛ shweremɔ ni mli wa lɛ kɛ fitemɔ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ ni okɛ nu awo mli fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: How do I care for my newly transplanted pepper seedlings so they survive the transplanting shock?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ mi-pepper dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shoofeemɔ ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ mli?

english: Transplanting disturbs tender young roots. Water the seedlings thoroughly right after moving them, plant them late in the afternoon when the sun is down, and shade them slightly for the first few days so they can recover without losing water to the heat.
ga: Shishifãi ni aduɔ awoɔ he kroko lɛ gbaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni darako lɛ anaa. Kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ he kroko lɛ, ha dumɔwui lɛ nu jogbaŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Dumɔ yɛ shwane mli beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ. kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli tse yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii fioo lɛ amli koni eha ehe ajɔ lɛ ni nu ni jɛɔ latsaa lɛ mli baa lɛ akafee lɛ.

english: Yam vines naturally want to spread upward to catch sunlight. Guiding the vines onto tall stakes lifts the foliage off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and ensuring the leaves gather enough light energy to build large underground tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ fɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewo tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ baai ahe helai anaa ni ekwɛɔ koni baai lɛ abua la hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa naa koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: A plantain stalk has limited nutrients to feed its growth. Allowing too many young suckers to grow at the same time creates competition, leaving the main mother plant weak and leading to smaller bunches of plantains.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa amɛdaraa. Oblahii kɛ oblayei babaoo ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ be kome mli lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa. Ehaa fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ekɛ dumɔwui bibii baa.

english: Why do my young maize crops turn yellow and stop growing early in their growth stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi bibi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpa dalɛ yɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually signal a lack of nitrogen or roots choked by waterlogged soil. Early care like light weeding, proper drainage, and applying a small amount of starter fertilizer helps the young root system take off.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli loo akɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nibii ni akwɛɔ mra tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ fioo proper drainage Ni akɛ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko fataa he lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi bibii lɛ agbo.

english: Why is early weeding so critical for my cassava crop in its first two months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ he hiaa mi kɛha mi-cassava dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings are slow to develop full leaves early on. Fast-growing weeds easily steal sunlight, water, and nutrients from young cassava sprouts, permanently stunting root development if not cleared early.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ adara fiofio yɛ shishijee mli. Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei tsei bibii amli oya. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ kwraa kɛji ajieee amɛ mra.

english: How can I protect my young garden egg plants from insect attacks when they are still small?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu eggplants ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni baatutua amɛ lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Tender young leaves attract leaf-eating insects easily. Inspect the underside of leaves weekly, remove infected leaves early, and apply recommended organic or mild chemical sprays to safeguard the plant during its soft growing phase.
ga: Baai bibii lɛ gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ baa lɛ oya. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi daa otsi. Jiemɔ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli loo tsofai ni mli ejɔ ni ajieɔ yi lɛ atsu nii kɛbu tsei ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their first blossoms instead of growing peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiwo eklɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi lɛ moŋ fe ni eeedu pepper lɛ?

english: When a plant is young or under stress from excessive heat or dry soil, it sheds its initial blossoms to save energy for survival. Once the plant matures and receives steady water, it will hold flowers and bear fruit.
ga: Beni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ loo eyɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli baa lɛ Tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi shishijee mli koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato koni amɛhi shi. Beni tsei lɛ edara kwraa ni amɛnáa nu daa lɛ. Ebaafɔfɔi ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my bean plants produce plenty of leafy green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes bean plants to focus all energy on leaf and branch growth instead of flower production. Balancing soil nutrients encourages the plant to shift its energy into flowering and setting pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ niji ni miida lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhewalɛ kɛyaa fɔfɔi kɛ pod setting nɔ.

english: Can I grow rice on my land anywhere in Ghana, or does it only grow in specific regions?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ Ghana he fɛɛ he? aloo abaanyɛ adu yɛ kpokpai komɛi pɛ anɔ

english: Rice is a very versatile crop that can be cultivated in almost every region of Ghana, provided you select the right variety for your soil type and rainfall level.
ga: Omɔ ji ŋmɔshi nii ni yɔɔ srɔtoi ni abaanyɛ adu yɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ Ghana kpokpai fɛɛ nɔ. Kɛji ohala tso ni sa kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ henɔ kɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa lɛ.

english: Why is rice considered a good crop for farmers in Ghana to invest in?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abuɔ omɔ akɛ eji ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpa ni okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛ amɛshika awo mli lɛ?

english: Rice has a high and growing demand across Ghana, adapts well to different land environments, and yields reliable harvests that support both household feeding and commercial market sales.
ga: Amɛmiitao ŋmãa waa ni amɛmiiya hiɛ yɛ Ghana fɛɛ. Eyɛ nyɛmɔ kpakpa ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ shihilɛi srɔtoi amli. ni ekɛ yibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ aba Enɛ fiɔ shia niyenii kɛ jarayeli jarayeli fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are parts of my crop leaves turning dark brown and drying up as if they were burnt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ ekomɛi miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi tamɔ nɔ ni ashã lɛ?

english: This symptom is called necrosis, which occurs when plant tissue dies due to infections from bacteria, fungi, or severe nutrient deficiencies.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ nekrosis, ni baa kɛji tso mli fãji gboi yɛ muawai, ŋmei, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa waa hewɔ.

english: How can I stop necrosis from spreading to the rest of my healthy crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi necrosis naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli?

english: To control necrosis, promptly cut off and destroy infected plant parts, maintain clean farm tools, and ensure proper plant spacing so air flows freely through your crops.
ga: koni akɛkudɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ Kpãa tso lɛ fãi ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ahiɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ha ŋmɔ mli nibii ahe atse. Ni kwɛmɔ ni tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa ahi shi koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ onibii amli oya.

english: Can necrosis completely ruin my harvest if I do not treat it early?
ga: Ani gangrene baanyɛ afite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kwraa kɛji mitsaaa lɛ mra?

english: Yes, because necrosis destroys leaf tissue, preventing the plant from making food through sunlight, which leads to stunted growth, lower yields, or plant death.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ necrosis fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ afee niyenii kɛtsɔ hulu la nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ dalɛ baa shi, yibiiwoo baa shi loo egboɔ.

english: How do I know if a new seed variety will grow well on my farm before planting a big field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui heei baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ agbo ko mli?

english: You can plant a small test patch on your land and monitor how well it grows, checking if it resists local pests and diseases before spending money on large-scale planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu kaa ŋmɔ bibioo ko. yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni okwɛ bɔ ni edaa jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ kwɛmɔ nɔ kɛji enyɛŋ eshi he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai. Dani abaafite shika yɛ dumɔwui wuji ahe

english: What unusual signs should I look for when walking through my farm to catch crop diseases early?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ esa akɛ matao beni mitsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mana ŋmɔshi nibii amli helai mra?

english: Check for strange spots on leaves, yellowing, sudden wilting, stunted growth, or patches of dry and dead plant tissue.
ga: Kwɛmɔ kɛji hei ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ, ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ, ni amɛmiigbo trukaa. shweremɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo tso lɛ mli fãi ni egbi ni egboiɔ

english: Why do my crops look healthy one week but suddenly start developing disease spots the next week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ otsi kome mli, shi trukaa lɛ, helai ahe tsɔi jeɔ shishi amɛnaa yɛ otsi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Disease organisms can remain hidden until changes in weather, like heavy rain or high humidity, trigger them to rapidly grow and attack vulnerable plants.
ga: Muawai baanyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo hulutsoo be ni mli wa. Enɛ woɔ amɛ hewalɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛtutua tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ.

english: Where can a small farmer like me go to get expert advice on improving crop yields in Ghana?
ga: Nɛgbɛ okwaafoi bibii tamɔ mi baanyɛ aya koni amɛná ŋaawoo ni he esa yɛ bɔ ni amɛbaafee amɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛduɔ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ Ghana lɛ he?

english: You can connect with local agricultural extension officers, ministry representatives, or specialized crop development foundations that provide free training and farming guidance.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyana okwaayeli he nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nitsumɔhe lɛ najiaŋdamɔlɔ loo Specialized Crop Development Foundation ni haa okwaayeli he tsɔsemɔ kɛ ŋaawoo ni aheee nɔ ko lɛ.

english: What should I do if I find a disease on my crops that I have never seen before?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina hela ko yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni minako dã lɛ anɔ?

english: Avoid spraying unknown chemicals right away; instead, bring a sample of the affected plant to your local extension officer so they can properly diagnose the issue and recommend the right treatment.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni aleee ni okɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Mohu ɔ, ngɔ tsohi nɛ a ná he wami ɔ a he nɔ hyɛmi ní kɛ ya he nɛ o ngɛ ɔ mi ɔ. Enɛ ji koni amɛnyɛ amɛna naagba lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛtsɔɔ tsofafeemɔ ni sa.

english: Officer, if a tree on my farm appears dead or is cut down, can it grow back on its own?
ga: Ofisa Ni kɛji tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi loo afolɔ amɛ hu? Ani ebaada lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, many tree species have deep root systems that remain alive even after the trunk is cut. Given rain and sunshine, hidden buds on the stump or roots can shoot up new sprouts.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei babaoo yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni afo amɛshishifãi lɛ po sɛɛ. Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tsei akutsei loo shishifãi anɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmeii heei.

english: If new shoots start sprouting from an old tree stump on my land, should I let all of them grow?
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii heei bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ kɛjɛ tso momo ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli Ani Esa akɛ mahã fɛɛ akwɛ̃?

english: No, you should cut away the weaker shoots and leave only the single strongest sprout. If you let all shoots grow, they will compete for nutrients and turn into weak, bushy stems.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ni oshi tsei ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ. Kɛji oha ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ dara lɛ, no lɛ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmeii.

english: How does cutting off dead or dying branches help my tree crops?
ga: Te niji ni egboi loo ni miigboi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Removing dead branches prevents rot and pests from spreading to the healthy parts of the tree, while allowing the plant to direct its energy into growing fresh leaves and fruits.
ga: Niji ni egboi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tso lɛ hei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ aduawai heei.

english: Why is it important for me to clear the thick weeds and wild bushes from around my tree crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie jwɛi ni eyi obɔ kɛ koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Clearing around your tree crops removes competition so your trees get full access to soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, while also protecting them from hidden pests and wild bushfires.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Enɛ jieɔ akaŋshii kɛjɛɔ mli bɔni afee ni otsei lɛ aná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛ koo mli la hu ahe.

english: What is the difference between leaving my land as a wild forest and turning it into a cultivated farm?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni mashi akɛ koo kɛ ŋmɔ ni matsɔ mli lɛ teŋ?

english: A wild forest grows untamed brush and mixed trees that compete with each other, while a cultivated farm is cleared and organized so specific crops get maximum nutrients, light, and care to yield well.
ga: Koo lɛ mli tsei bibii ni yɔɔ amɛkomekomei kɛ tsei ni efutu ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ajieɔ ŋmɔji ni aduɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ amli ni atoɔ he gbɛjianɔ bɔni afee ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi aná niyenii babaoo, la, kɛ kwɛmɔ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Should I completely pull out tree stumps when clearing land, or can I leave them in the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ miitsumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ani esa akɛ majie tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fɛɛ loo mashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: If you are planting crops like maize or cassava, removing stumps makes land tilling easier. For tree crops, leaving stumps can prevent soil erosion, but you must regularly cut back any green shoots that sprout from them.
ga: Kɛji oodu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ŋmãa ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitsumɔ afee mlɛo. kɛha tsei tsei Tso shishifãi ni ashiɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa. Shi ehe miihia ni ofolɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ daa.

english: Why should I wait a little bit after clearing fresh overgrown bush before I start planting my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ be fioo beni mijie jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ dani mije dumɔwui ashishi lɛ?

english: Waiting allows the cut bush to dry and decay into natural soil manure, while giving you time to spot and clear aggressive weeds or sprouts that try to come back.
ga: Mɛmɔ baaha jwɛi ni afo lɛ agbi ni etsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa be ni okɛtaoɔ jwɛi loo dumɔwui ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛba ekoŋŋ lɛ ni ojie.

english: How can I tell if an overgrown piece of land will be good for planting crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Look at the soil and the wild plants growing there. Dark soil and thick, green leaves on wild vegetation usually mean the soil has rested well and is rich in nutrients for your crops.
ga: Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ koo mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ kɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ koo mli tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ehi shi jogbaŋŋ, ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ babaoo yɛ mli kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly when large forest trees are blocking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ koo mli tsei wuji tsi amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Big forest trees block sunlight from reaching your crops underneath. Crops need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food and grow strong.
ga: Tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ onibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ ahe. Tsei hia hulu la ni tsoɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛye niyenii ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What will happen to my tree crops if I do not clear the wild vegetation around them regularly?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mijieee koo mli tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ daa?

english: The wild vegetation will grow faster than your crops, stealing water, fertilizer, and light, which will cause your crop leaves to turn yellow, stunt their growth, and lower your harvest.
ga: Koo mli tsei baakwɛ̃ oya fe onibii ni oduɔ lɛ, ni amɛbaaju nu, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ la, ni no baaha otsei lɛ baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ. ha odalɛ aba shi ni oha nibii ni otsuɔ lɛ aba shi

english: Young cocoa plants need shade and steady moisture because their delicate leaves burn easily under strong heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them protects them from direct sunlight and keeps the soil cool until they grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ

english: Why are small worms eating the fresh center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai heei ni jɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These worms are Fall Armyworms, which love to feed on the tender leaf funnels of growing maize. Inspecting your farm early and applying natural solutions like neem leaf extract or recommended bio-pesticides directly into the leaf funnel can protect your crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛye ŋmãa ni miida lɛ baai ni agbele lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsabaai tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ atsu nii lɛ baanyɛ abu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water builds up because the roots need air in the soil to breathe. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away quickly, preventing the roots from sitting in soggy soil and rotting.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni ekã shi lɛ ba. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli ni amɛkafite.

english: Tired soil shows when crops grow slowly, produce small yields, or turn pale light-green and yellow instead of dark green. Adding animal manure or the right mineral fertilizer restores essential nutrients like nitrogen that plants need to thrive.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ jieɔ ehe kpo kɛ́ tsei lɛ dara blɛoo. Ehaa yibiiwoo fioo loo etsɔɔ eŋɔli ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ falɛ ni sa wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoots growing around my plantain tree instead of leaving them all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ eje kpo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi fɛɛ

english: If too many shoots grow around one stem, they compete for nutrients, light, and water, which results in thin plants and small plantain bunches. Keeping only the main stem and one or two strong suckers ensures maximum nutrients go to producing a large bunch.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso kome he lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, la, kɛ nu, ni no haa tsei bibii kɛ plantain tsei bibii baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ kɛ tso lɛ mli nu kome loo enyɔ ni mli wa pɛ to lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa fe fɛɛ aba koni ekɛfee ŋmei agbo.

english: Why does covering the soil around my tomato plants with dry leaves help them stay healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egboi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle o-tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves, known as mulching, stops moisture from evaporating quickly under the hot sun. It keeps the roots cool, prevents weeds from taking over, and slowly decays into rich soil food.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baatsi nu ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekaho oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye nɔ ni amɛfite fiofio akɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it risky to plant tomatoes on the exact same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni tomato ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ ji oshara lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly allows pests and soil diseases that feed on that crop to build up in large numbers. Rotating tomatoes with crops from a different family, like maize or beans, breaks disease cycles and keeps the land productive.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abua amɛhe naa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tomato ni akɛ tsei ni jɛ wekui krokomɛi amli, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni jɛmɛ yaa nɔ ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings fall over and die near the soil line right after coming up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ he beni amɛba shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by a fungal condition called damping-off, which happens when seedling beds stay too wet and crowded. Spacing your seeds properly and watering gently without over-soaking the soil prevents fungal growth around tender stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ damp-off, ni baa kɛji dumɔwui asaji lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Gbalamɔ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ nu awo mli blɛoo. Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ akakwɛ̃. tsɔne ni yɔɔ blɛoo

english: How do I know if the first rain of the season is enough for me to start planting my crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: The very first rainfall often only wets the top layer of soil, which quickly dries out if a dry spell follows. It is safer to dig into the ground and verify that the soil is moist at least hand-deep before planting, so seeds do not dry up after germinating.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Ni baagbi oya kɛji hɔmɔ be ko ba ni nyiɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oootsa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni okwɛ koni kɛ hoo lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ afee ekome dani odu. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ egbiɛɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: Yam leaves use sunlight to manufacture the food that builds the tuber underground. Staking raises the vines toward the light and keeps the leaves off the hot ground, allowing the plant to catch more sun and grow larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii ni feɔ ŋmeii. Staking baaha wain tso lɛ akwɛ la lɛ hiɛ ni ebaaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ akabote hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ naa hulu la babaoo ni ekwɛ̃ɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Why do some crop varieties mature much faster in Ghana than the traditional varieties I am used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ shwereɔ oya fe blema ŋmɔshi nibii ni mile jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties are specifically bred to adapt to local soil and sunlight conditions, allowing them to complete their growth cycle rapidly and produce food quickly before dry weather sets in.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kɛ hulu la shihilɛi amli. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ niyenii oya dani hulutsoo be lɛ baa.

english: Why does my cassava crop stay in the ground for months while my vegetables are ready in a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔji babaoo yɛ be mli ni mi-vegetables lɛ feɔ klalo yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Vegetables store their energy in quick-growing leaves and fruits above ground, whereas root crops like cassava need many months to slowly build up starch in tubers hidden beneath the soil.
ga: Aduawai kɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛbaai kɛ amɛyibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei lɛ heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani amɛbuaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli fiofio.

english: What is the best way to inspect my crop leaves step-by-step to catch diseases early?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ amli fiofio koni ana hela mra?

english: Walking through your field regularly and checking plants row-by-row from the bottom leaves up to the young shoot allows you to spot color changes, spots, or pest damage before they spread to the whole farm.
ga: Kɛji onyiɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli daa ni okwɛ tsei lɛ amli sɛɛkuu kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyashi ŋmeii bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona su ni etsake, ŋmeii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ dani egbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are a signal that the plant lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that the roots are suffering from either too much water logging or extreme dryness.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo shishifãi lɛ miina naagbai ni kɔɔ nu ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛmli fe nine loo amɛgbiɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why do crops grow at different speeds when moved from one town or region in Ghana to another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ kɛ́ ajɛ maŋ loo kpokpaa kome nɔ yɛ Ghana kɛtee ekroko nɔ lɛ?

english: Different regions have variations in soil richness, daily temperature, and rainfall patterns, all of which directly speed up or slow down how fast a plant absorbs food and develops.
ga: Kpokpai srɔtoi yɛ srɔtofeemɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. daa gbi latsaa kɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa lɛ Nibii nɛɛ fɛɛ baaha oyaiyeli ni tsei lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni amɛyaa hiɛ lɛ aya hiɛ loo ebaa shi oya tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees struggle to survive if I plant them in direct, open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ehi shi kɛji midu lɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under intense heat; they require shade crops like plantains to act as natural umbrellas while their root systems develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it better to plant my crops step-by-step in straight lines rather than scattering seeds freely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu tsei fiofio fiofio yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ dumɔwui oshwã oya?

english: Planting in straight lines ensures every single plant gets its own space, equal sunlight, and fair share of water, while also making weeding and harvesting much easier for you.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛhe. Hulu la lɛ falɛ ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ yɛ jɛmɛ. ni oná nu ni sa Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo.

english: Why should I clear my farm land gradually without burning all the bushes on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ lɛ blɛoo? Ajie ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni ashãaa jwɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Burning destroys rich organic matter and beneficial organisms in the soil, whereas clearing without fire allows decaying leaves to act as natural fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni la bɛ mli ni ajieɔ lɛ haa baai ni egboi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before forming any fruit during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high and water is low, tomato plants drop their flowers to save energy and protect themselves from dying of extreme stress.
ga: Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni nu lɛ hu faaa lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ haomɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why is it important for me to remove small weeds around my crop shoots as early as possible?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi bibii ni bɔle mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe oya bɔ ni manyɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than main crops and will quickly steal all the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your young plants if they are not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛbaaju nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ kɛha otsei bibii lɛ oya kɛji ajieee amɛ mra.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh, direct sunlight. Without shade trees or temporary companion plants like plantains, the intense heat scorches the delicate leaves and dries out the topsoil before the young roots can establish.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei ni fata he be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains bɛ lɛ, la ni naa wa lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ agbi dani shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: What makes the cocoa pods on my tree turn black and rot before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a water-borne fungus that thrives in cool, humid conditions and excessive shade. Regular weeding, pruning overgrown branches to let air flow, and removing infected pods quickly help stop it from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nu mli tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ kɛ hulutsoo babaoo ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa Niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli Ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why are the small flowers on my cocoa trees falling off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees rely on tiny insects called midges to transfer pollen from flower to flower. Extreme heat, drought, or spraying chemical pesticides at the wrong time can kill these pollinators or cause the tree stress, leading to flower drop.
ga: Kookoo tsei yeɔ kooloi bibii. Ale midges akɛ amɛjieɔ pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be ni esaaa mli lɛ baanyɛ agbe nɛkɛ kooloi ni shwieɔ ŋmeii nɛɛ loo eha tso lɛ aná haomɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ni shwieɔ shi.

english: How can I tell the exact right time to pluck cocoa pods from my trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ majie kookoo ŋmeii kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Pods are ready to harvest when their color changes completely, usually from green to yellow or from dark red to bright orange. Harvesting unripe green pods leaves you with flat, bitter beans, while waiting too long causes the beans inside to sprout.
ga: Pods lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa kɛji amɛhe su tsake kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo kɛjɛɔ etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa akutu ni mli tse nɔ. Pods eŋɔli ni ekwɛko lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha oná ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ omɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why must I heap my harvested cocoa beans under plantain leaves for several days before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ toɔ plantain baai ashishi gbii babaoo dani migbiɔ lɛ?

english: Fermentation heats up the beans to kill the embryo so it won't sprout, breaks down the sweet pulp surrounding them, and produces the natural rich chocolate flavor and brown color that buyers look for.
ga: Fɛ̃i haa ŋmeii lɛ mli dɔɔ koni egbe fɔmɔ kotokui lɛ. koni ekakwɛ̃ Efiteɔ loo ni ŋɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. ni ehaa enáa tsokolate ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ kɛ su ni ji ŋmɔtɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do produce buyers complain when I dry my cocoa beans on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nibii ni anáa lɛ wieɔ huhuuhu kɛ́ migbi kookoo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Drying cocoa beans directly on the ground introduces dirt, small stones, and mold, and allows animals to walk over them. Drying them on raised wooden mats keeps the beans clean, allows air to circulate underneath, and ensures even drying.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa muji, tɛi bibii kɛ ŋmeii baa, ni ehaa kooloi nyɛɔ amɛnyiɛɔ nɔ mlɛo. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa amɛhe tseɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ shishi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kɔfi yibii lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ

english: Can I plant cassava alongside my young cocoa trees to harvest while waiting for the cocoa to grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cassava yɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe koni makpa be mli ni mimɛɔ ni cacao lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cassava is a heavy feeder that aggressively competes with young cocoa trees for nutrients and soil moisture, often stunting the cocoa's growth. Plantains or legumes are better choices because they provide gentle shade and enrich the soil.
ga: Cassava ji niyenii ni tsii ni kɛ cacao tsei bibii yeɔ akaŋ yɛ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsiɔ kookoo lɛ dalɛ naa. Plantains loo legumes ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning light yellow while the veins stay dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ be mli ni fãji lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: This yellowing pattern, called chlorosis, is a clear sign that the tree is lacking nutrients like iron or nitrogen from the soil. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or appropriate cocoa fertilizer will restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ akɛ chlorosis. Enɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ dade loo nitrogen ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Will cutting off extra branches and shoots reduce the number of pods my cocoa tree produces?
ga: Ani niji kɛ tsei tsei krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baaha ŋmeii ni mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ lɛ ayibɔ aba shi?

english: No, pruning actually increases your crop yield. Removing unwanted suckers (chupons) and dead branches allows sunlight and air to reach the trunk where pods grow, while directing the tree's energy into making healthier, larger pods.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayibii yaa hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni ataooo (chupons) kɛ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: What is causing the young green shoots on my cocoa branches to dry up and look burned?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo niji lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã?

english: This damage is typically caused by mirids, tiny sap-sucking insects that inject toxic saliva into young cocoa shoots and pods. Spraying approved treatments during peak mirid seasons protects the branches from drying out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mirids ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni ji kooloo bibioo ko ni nuɔ nu ni kɛ nu ni yɔɔ gbeyei woɔ kookoo ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii amli Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei niji ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why are the young leaves on my new cocoa seedlings turning brown and drying up in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui heei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hulu lɛ etswa amɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. They need shade from plants like plantain or forest trees to keep them cool and hold moisture in the soil until their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantain loo koo mli tsei adɛŋ koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ mli baawo shɔŋŋ.

english: If too many shoots grow around one plantain tree, they all fight for the same water and food in the soil. Cutting away extra shoots leaves only one or two strong suckers, which helps the main tree produce a bigger bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ, ŋmeii fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ baahi shi, ni no yeɔ ebuaa tso titri lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why are my maize leaves suddenly filled with small holes and looking chewed up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii trukaa ni etamɔ nɔ ni ashɛre lɛ?

english: Small holes in maize leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that eat the young leaves. Catching them early and applying approved pest treatments or neem spray protects your maize crop from heavy damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ afite. Ni tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem spray ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu o-corn tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ fitemɔ ni mli wa he.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn plants turning yellow from the tip downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing on older leaves usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost helps the plant regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛdalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess water sits in the ground without draining away, it chokes the roots and allows fungal rot to develop inside the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ efo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli. Ebaafite shishifãi lɛ ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo yɛ bulb lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to place tall wooden sticks next to my yam plants for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi koni wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to feed the tubers growing underground. Lifting the leaves off the wet ground also prevents leaf diseases caused by soil fungi.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛfi bulb ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ sɛɛ. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ baa helai ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anaa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without making fruit when the weather gets too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when the soil lacks nutrients like calcium and nitrogen needed during flowering.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni niyenii tamɔ calcium kɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking sap from the leaves or passing along a virus. Spraying insecticidal soap or neem oil helps manage these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ loo helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekwɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts together in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ afee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This natural fertilizer helps the maize grow better without exhausting the soil.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ehaaa sũ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I spread dry grass or leaves on top of the soil around my crop rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi mashwã shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, traps moisture so you water less, and stops weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi haa lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akashwie nɔ fioo ni otsĩ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better for me to try a new crop on a small patch of land first before planting it on my whole farm?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi akɛ maka tso hee ko ni makwɛ yɛ he bibioo ko lɛ makwɛ? Dani abaadu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Yes, starting with a small plot allows you to see how the crop performs in your soil and weather without taking big financial risks. Once you see good results and learn how to manage the crop, you can safely expand.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Ehaa onaa bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii amɛhaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli ni okɛ shika he oshara kpele ko wooo mli. Beni ona yibii kpakpai ni okase bɔ ni ooofee okwɛ onibii anɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli shweshweeshwe.

english: Can I plant maize on the same piece of land where I have just planted young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmãa tsei bibii amrɔ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting maize among young cocoa trees works very well. The tall maize stalks provide temporary shade to protect the young cocoa from strong sunlight, and you get to harvest food while waiting for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ateŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Abɛi tsei kakadaji haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko koni ebu kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ni obaanyɛ okpa niyenii yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why should I spend time growing food crops like maize and rice if cocoa is my main income source?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite be kɛdu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa? Akɛni kookoo ji shika titri ni mináa hewɔ lɛ.

english: Cocoa yields cash only during specific harvest seasons, but food crops like maize and rice mature quickly in just three to four months. Growing them provides your family with food and extra income throughout the year.
ga: Cocoa woɔ yibii yɛ kpamɔ be ni ato lɛ mli pɛ, shi niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya yɛ nyɔji etɛ loo ejwɛ pɛ mli. Nibii nɛɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaha oweku lɛ aná niyenii kɛ shika kroko yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: What kind of land on my farm is best suited for growing rice alongside my cocoa?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ mi-kookoo lɛ masɛi?

english: Cocoa prefers well-drained, fertile soil on higher ground, whereas rice thrives in wet, low-lying valleys or swampy areas (inland valleys) that hold moisture easily.
ga: Cocoa sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni kwɔ waa lɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jɔɔ lɛ mli loo hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. (mligbɛ jɔɔ lɛ) ni ŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli mlɛo

english: How many years will I have to wait after planting new cocoa before I start seeing pods?
ga: Kɛ́ wɔdu kookoo hee lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ wɔmɛ dani wɔje shishi wɔna ŋmeii?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start producing their first pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, compared to older traditional varieties that took 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ afeemɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, ni akɛtoɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 he kɛha blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees dry up and turn brown when there are no shade trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are naturally sensitive to extreme heat and direct sunlight. Without shade trees to cover them, the sun scorches their leaves and dries out the soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ lɛ Hulu lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to grow strong, so adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ afee eŋɔli.

english: Plant maize seeds about 75 centimeters between rows and 40 centimeters between holes. Proper spacing ensures the plants do not fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients.
ga: Dumɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui aaafee sɛntimita 75 yɛ ŋtayaai ateŋ kɛ sɛntimitai 40 yɛ buji ateŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe wooo hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ.

english: Does rice always need a flooded field to grow, or can I grow it on normal rainwater?
ga: Ani esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔji ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ amli loo abaanyɛ adu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ nɔ?

english: Not all rice needs flooded fields. While swamp rice needs plenty of standing water, upland rice varieties are bred to grow on dry land using regular rainfall, just like maize.
ga: Omɔ henɔi komɛi biɔ nu afua. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo he miihia peat moŋ, shi atsɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmãa ni akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛtsɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ nɔ. tamɔ ŋmãa nɔŋŋ

english: Why do weeds grow much faster in my rice field than in my maize field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have narrow leaves that let sunlight reach the wet soil, encouraging weed seeds to germinate quickly. Maize grows taller and has broader leaves that shade the ground and block weeds.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ baai bibii ni haa hulu la shɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya. Abɛi daa ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which happens when heavy rains wash nutrients out of the soil. Adding fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some farmers plant groundnuts or beans together in the same field as maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni amɛduɔ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. This acts like a natural fertilizer that feeds the maize and keeps the soil healthy for longer.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How does spreading dry grass around my pepper plants help them survive the heat?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te pepper tsei yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Dry grass acts like a blanket on top of the earth, called mulch. It stops sunlight from drying out the soil, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing and taking water from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛheɔ nu kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: What causes small caterpillars to hide inside the central shoots of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: These are usually Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid by small moths. They hide inside the funnel of the maize plant where the leaves are softest to eat them before the plant matures.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fɔɔ lɛ amli. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli he ni baai ni mli tse lɛ yeli waaa fe fɛɛ dani tso lɛ daa kwraa lɛ.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips that suck the juice out of young leaves, or transmit a plant virus that distorts how the leaves grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo egbɛɔ tsei amli helai ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ eshwaa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up when the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, wet weather. Pruning extra branches to let sunlight and fresh air into the farm helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i, fɛ̃i be mli lɛ kɛbaa. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits on the farm for too long without draining, the roots drown and rot away due to soil fungi.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahewɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers before any fruit can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when they get stressed, especially when the weather becomes too hot or when the soil suddenly shifts from very dry to very wet.
ga: Tomato fɔ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ.

english: Yam leaves need plenty of sunlight to manufacture food for the tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they catch sunshine and stay free from leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking jieɔ tsei ahe tsei kɛjɛɔ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ enine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ ni tsei ahe helai bɛ ehe.

english: When is the best time for me to apply chemical fertilizer so the rain does not waste it?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo mli koni nugbɔ lɛ akafee yaka?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already damp, but not during heavy rainfall. Burying the fertilizer slightly in the soil next to the crop keeps rain from carrying it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko wo shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni ekafɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout when I plant them in dry soil before the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛ?

english: Seeds need moisture to soften their outer shell and activate growth. Planting in completely dry soil keeps the seeds dormant or leaves them vulnerable to insects and heat before they can germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ nu koni eha kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ afee blɛoo ni eha amɛdara. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aya wɔɔ. Aloo shi dumɔwui lɛ ni kooloi kɛ dɔlɛ baanyɛ atswa amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and weak when I plant many seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete against each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, causing all of them to grow tall, thin, and unproductive instead of strong.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ ebaatswa hulu la he akaŋ Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, egbɔjɔɔ ni ewooo yibii moŋ fe ni eeehi hewalɛ.

english: What actually happens to my cassava crops when I spread fertilizer on the farm?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Fertilizer supplies essential food elements like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium into the soil, which roots absorb to grow stronger, produce greener leaves, and build larger root tubers.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasium boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni shishifãi lɛ baaŋɔ koni amɛdara waa lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ ayitsei wuji feɔ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop is starving for nitrogen in the soil or struggling with poor drainage, which prevents the plant from making green energy to grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni haa amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die if I don't leave bigger trees or plantains around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ gbo kɛji mishiii tsei wuji loo plantains komɛi yɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have fragile leaves that burn quickly under full direct sunlight. Taller crops like plantains provide living shade and keep the air humid so the young cocoa can survive its early stage.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai ni waaa ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fũuɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛshishijee bei amli.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or water shortage, as the plant tries to preserve its energy to stay alive rather than carrying fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi shi moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop during the afternoon heat even when the ground has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu yɛ moŋ?

english: During intense midday sun, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull it from the ground, causing temporary wilting to protect the plant from drying out.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, hulu lɛ mli wa waa. Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha tso lɛ agbi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ekagbi.

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, which acts as a natural fertilizer for the neighboring maize crop.
