ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ

english: Why do my yam tubers end up small and bent when planted in hard clay soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, soft soil so they can expand easily underground. Hard, compacted soil blocks their expansion, forcing the roots to stay small or become twisted.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ bɔni afee ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ tsiɔ shweremɔ naa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii loo etsakeɔ

english: Why do weeds cause my main crops to produce a very poor harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kɛ yibiiwoo ni yɔɔ gbeyei miiba miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and steal water, fertilizer nutrients, and sunlight directly from your main crops, leaving your plants underfed and incapable of producing good yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ otsei titrii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ anine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in a V-pattern from the tip inward, the plant is usually lacking nitrogen. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow, but heavy rains in Ghana often wash this nutrient deep into the ground where crop roots cannot reach it.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baa ko shishigbɛ fã lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni efee V su kɛjɛ enaagbɛ kɛtee mligbɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, nitrogen bɛ tsei amli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa. Shi bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ Ghana lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed so many leaves and lose their flowers during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-koko tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai babaoo ni amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during the Harmattan to save water when the air becomes very dry and hot. Without enough soil moisture or protective shade, the tree enters survival mode and sheds leaves and flowers to keep its trunk and main roots alive.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ Harmattan beaŋ koni amɛkɛbu nu he beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa ni edɔ waa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ loo hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Tso lɛ yaa wala shihilɛ mli ni eshwieɔ baai kɛ fɔfɔi koni eha eshishifã lɛ kɛ eshishifãi titrii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and tall with very small yields when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they fight one another underground for water and soil nutrients, and above ground for sunlight. Instead of putting energy into making big fruits or grains, they stretch upwards quickly just to reach the light.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛwuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni amɛwuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛfee aduawai loo ŋmaa bibii wuji Amɛheɔ oya koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he.

english: Why is it recommended that I plant plantains alongside my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛɔ akɛ midu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily scorched by direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have wide leaves that act as living shade umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa plants cool and conserving moisture in the soil.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year if I plant maize on the exact same land without resting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season without giving the earth time to recover. It also allows specific pests and soil diseases to build up in that plot.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ baaya nɔ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi kɛ helai komɛi hu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves around plants is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that shields the soil from the hot sun, keeps moisture in the ground longer, and prevents weeds from taking root.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa Tsei ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekawo shishifãi.

english: What is causing holes in my young maize leaves and leaving tiny worms inside the leaf funnels?
ga: Mɛni miiha bu yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli ni eshiɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central funnel of the maize plant to feed on tender leaves. Checking farms early and applying approved treatments or neem oil can protect the growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Okwaafoi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo neem fɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ abu tip ni miida lɛ he.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the soil during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays waterlogged for too long, starving the roots of air and allowing soil fungi to infect them. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ hela Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer that causes the plant to produce leaves instead of setting fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛi, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo, ni no baaha tso lɛ awo baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: How do weeds reduce my crop yield even when they are not touching my plants directly?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ aba shi eyɛ mli akɛ amɛkɛ mitsei lɛ bɛ tsakpaa tɛ̃ɛ moŋ?

english: Underneath the soil, weed roots grow fast and steal water and plant food meant for your crops. Above ground, weeds harbor dangerous pests and block the natural flow of air around your crops.
ga: Yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, jwɛi shishifãi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, jwɛi lɛ hiɛɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara ni amɛfiteɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔleɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot tolerate full sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain alongside them provides living shade that protects the leaves from burning and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛŋmɛɛɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ tsei nɛɛ ahe lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do the pods on my cocoa trees turn black and rot before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in high humidity and excess shade. Clearing weeds, pruning dense leaves to let in air, and removing infected pods early helps protect the healthy trees.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ he ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo be ni fa fe nine lɛ mli. weeding Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei ahe tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he ni eha ehe awa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale light yellow instead of rich green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost gives the plant the essential nutrition it needs to regain its healthy green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why am I finding small holes and sawdust-like material in the center of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? kɛ nɔ ko ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that feeds on the soft growing heart of the plant. Checking your field early and spraying safe, recommended insecticides or organic treatments keeps them from destroying the crop yield.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni yeɔ tsei ni miida blɛoo lɛ atsui. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ afɔ nɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni tsei akafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when left in waterlogged soil because they cannot get oxygen. Plant cassava on raised mounds or ridges so excess rainwater drains away freely from the roots.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Dumɔ ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ bɔni afee ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ shishifãi lɛ amli aba oya.

english: Yam vines need to reach sunlight to produce energy for tuber growth underground. Staking raises the leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and helping the plant produce larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tuber dalɛ. Staking baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tso helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ bulbs wuji.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients like phosphorus. Consistent watering and feeding the soil with balanced fertilizer helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, often triggered by irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist allows the roots to absorb the calcium needed to build healthy fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium ni he hiaa koni amɛwo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why is it recommended to plant groundnuts on the same field where I planted maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmei yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally captures nitrogen from the air and enriches the soil. Rotating maize with groundnuts restores soil fertility without spending extra money on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni afiteee shika babaoo yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ahe.

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve so crop roots can absorb them. Applying fertilizer to bone-dry soil can burn plant roots or blow away in the wind without benefiting the crop.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛshwie shi bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi tamɔ wu nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso shishifãi lɛ ashã loo kɔɔyɔɔ atswa amɛ, ni sɛɛnamɔ ko bɛ he kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What is the main difference between Frafra potato and the regular sweet potato I buy at the market?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ Frafra ŋmɔtɔ kɛ daa ŋmɔtɔ ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ teŋ?

english: Frafra potato is a smaller, native African tuber crop that is well adapted to drier northern soils, while sweet potato produces larger tubers, grows on long trailing vines, and is widely cultivated across many different regions of Ghana.
ga: Frafra ŋmɔtɔ ji ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni jɛ Afrika. Amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ kooyigbɛ shikpɔji ni egbi lɛ anɔ. yɛ be mli ni yams woɔ ŋmeii wuji. Ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ wain tsei kakadaji ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ anɔ. ni aduɔ babaoo yɛ Ghana kpokpai srɔtoi babaoo anɔ

english: How can I tell the difference between a sweet potato plant and a Frafra potato plant before harvesting them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ sweet potato tso kɛ Frafra potato tso teŋ dani akpa?

english: You can tell them apart by their stems and leaves; Frafra potato plants have upright, squarish stems with slightly scented leaves similar to mint, whereas sweet potato plants grow trailing vines along the ground with heart-shaped or deeply lobed leaves.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyoo amɛ kɛtsɔ amɛ tsei kɛ amɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Frafra ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ yɛ tsei ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛ baai ni tamɔ sqɛɛ. Eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ fioo ko ni tamɔ mint baai. yɛ be mli ni sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ anɔ ni baai lɛ tamɔ tsui loo amɛmli ŋmeii lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do I need to make mounds or ridges in the soil before planting my sweet potato cuttings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee gɔji loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Tubers need loose, soft soil to grow large and expand easily. Making mounds or ridges creates space for the potatoes to grow under the soil while improving drainage so the roots do not rot in standing water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia bulb lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã mlɛo. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni afee lɛ haa gbɛ ni atomoi baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baa, yɛ be mli ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Koni shishifãi lɛ akafite yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli.

english: Can I plant fresh sweet potato vines directly into the soil to grow a new crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu sweet potato wain tsei heei awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni makwɛ tsei heei?

english: Yes, sweet potatoes are easily propagated using stem cuttings. You can cut healthy vine tips about 20 to 30 centimeters long and plant half of the stem beneath moist soil to sprout new roots and tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, akɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛgbɛɔ ŋmeii ni mli ŋɔɔ lɛ ashwãa oya. Obaanyɛ ofo wain tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ naa kɛyashɛ aaafee sɛntimita 20 kɛyashi 30 ni okɛ tso lɛ fã awo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ shishi koni shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃.

english: Will Frafra potatoes grow well on my farm if the rainy season in my area is short?
ga: Ani Frafra ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ faaa yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, Frafra potatoes are naturally hardy and resilient to dry spells, making them ideal for areas with shorter rainy seasons or poorer soils where other demanding crops might fail.
ga: Hɛɛ, Frafra ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni wa kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa. Enɛ haa ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be kukuoo loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii yɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ yɛ lɛ. baanyɛ afee nɔ ni ehiii

english: Is it good practice for me to plant sweet potatoes on the exact same piece of land every season?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ he kome daa be mli?

english: No, planting tubers on the same plot every season leads to a buildup of soil pests and diseases. Rotating your potatoes with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas helps keep the soil healthy and improves yields.
ga: Dabi, bulbs ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii atsake ŋmeii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ

english: Why do my sweet potato vines spread all over the soil instead of standing upright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ miigbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes naturally grow as trailing vines to cover the ground, which helps shade the soil, keep it moist, and form new roots along the nodes to support underground tuber growth.
ga: Sweet potatoes kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe tamɔ wain tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shishifãi heei feɔ shishifãi heei yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe koni eye ebua shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ.

english: Do root tubers like sweet potatoes need heavy rain right up until harvest time?
ga: Ani shishifãi tamɔ sweet potato he miihia nugbɔ ni naa wa kɛyashi kpamɔɔ be?

english: No, while tubers need consistent moisture during early growth, too much rain close to harvest can cause the fully formed potatoes to absorb excess water, crack, or rot underground.
ga: Dabi, eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔtɔ biɔ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee be mli moŋ. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo ni bɛŋkɛɔ kpamɔ be lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmeii ni afee amɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ, amɛgbala loo amɛgbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How do I know when my root tubers are ripe and ready to be dug up from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ atsa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Root tubers are generally ready to harvest when the leaves of the plant begin to turn yellow and dry up naturally, usually around 3 to 5 months after planting depending on the specific variety.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa beni tso lɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 5 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Edamɔ tso pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my sweet potatoes rot quickly after I store them inside my house?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛto shĩa lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya lɛ?

english: Potatoes rot quickly when kept in warm, damp, or unventilated places. To store them longer, place them in a cool, dark, dry area with good airflow, ideally elevated off the ground on dry grass or elevated wooden racks.
ga: Atomo fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he ni edɔɔ, fɛ̃i yɔɔ, loo kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji oosumɔ ni okɛto be kakadaŋŋ lɛ Okɛwo he ko ni jɛmɛ ejɔ, ni edɔ, ni egbi, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu boteɔ mli. Esa akɛ awó nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ jwɛi ni egbi nɔ loo yɛ tso ni awó nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. Maize needs a lot of nutrients to stay green and grow big cobs, so applying fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure early in the season helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tso lɛ. Niyenii babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ ŋmãa wuji. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why is it bad if I plant maize on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains all the specific nutrients from the soil and lets maize-loving pests build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛi fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni oha kooloi ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stem to cut and plant for my new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mafolɔ ni madu kɛha miŋmɔ hee lɛ?

english: You should pick the middle section of a mature, healthy cassava stem that is about as thick as your thumb. The top part is too soft and rots easily, while the bottom part is too hard and slow to sprout.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala ŋmei tso ni mli wa, ni edara ni miihe ashɛ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã lɛ he. kɛ oshishifa lɛ Yiteŋgbɛ fã lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ tsɔ ni egboɔ oya. yɛ be mli ni shishigbɛ fã lɛ wa tsɔ ni edaa fiofio.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the plant. When you stake the vines, you spread the leaves out to catch the sun, which sends energy down into the ground to make big, heavy tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Kɛji okɛ wain tso lɛ fĩ lɛ Ehe baahia ni ogbɛ baai lɛ ashwã koni onine ashɛ hulu la lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ koni ekɛfee yitso agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa trees falling off before they can turn into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi dani amɛfee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop when the soil becomes too dry, when the tree lacks shade, or when small insects like mirids attack them. Keeping proper shade trees and protecting the farm from insects helps the flowers set into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Beni tsei bɛ hulutsoo Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii tutuaa amɛ. Kɛ́ aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo ni sa ni abu he kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Which young shoots should I dig up when I want to plant new plantains?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei bibii esa akɛ mafo kɛji miisumɔ ni madu dumɔwui heei?

english: Look for 'sword suckers', which have narrow, spear-like leaves and a strong base. Avoid suckers with broad, flat leaves because they grow into weak plants that produce small bunches.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante ŋmɔlɔ’ ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tseee ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ kɛ shishitoo ni wa. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe beni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that spread a plant disease, or by extreme heat and dry soil. Protecting young plants with neem oil and keeping the soil moist helps stop this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ tsei ahe helai eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Tsei bibii ahe ni akɛ neem fɔ abuɔ he kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni afee ni edɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akpa enɛ.

english: Why are my pepper fruits turning black and rotting at the bottom while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper yibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This issue, called blossom end rot, happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often due to irregular watering. Watering your peppers consistently prevents this from happening.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo ŋmeii lɛ amli daa lɛ, ebaatsi enɛ naa.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the soil during hot days and stops weeds from growing around your crop's roots.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni ŋmɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ yɛ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How do weeds actually hurt my crops if I leave them in the farm for too long?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil food. When weeds grow close to your crops, they steal those essential resources, leaving your crops small, weak, and unproductive.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ Amɛbaaju nakai nibii ni he hiaa lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, onibii lɛ baafee bibioo, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: Why do seeds imported from foreign countries sometimes fail to produce good yields on my farm in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ dumɔwui ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ wooo yibii kpakpai yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Foreign seeds are often bred for different weather conditions, soil types, and daylight hours. When brought to Ghana, they may struggle with our local heat, drought spells, or native pests that they were never developed to handle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afɔɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi, shikpɔŋ henɔi kɛ hulutsoo be. Beni akɛbaa Ghana lɛ Ekolɛ ehe baahia ni amɛkɛ dɔlɛ, hɔmɔ, loo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni afeee wɔ kɔkɔɔkɔ koni wɔkɛtsu nii lɛ akpee.

english: Is it better for me to buy certified seeds every season or just replant the seeds I harvest from my own crops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase yɛ be fɛɛ mli loo madu dumɔwui ni mikpaa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ moŋ?

english: Certified seeds are carefully bred for high yields and uniform growth. If you plant saved seeds—especially from hybrid crops—the next generation usually loses strength, producing smaller harvests and uneven plant sizes.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛdara daa. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ato titri lɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ Yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sumɔɔ ni efite hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ faaa ni tsei lɛ adalɛ hu jeee ekome.

english: Why do some seeds I plant sprout quickly while others in the same field fail to sprout at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi ni miduɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ kwɛɛɛ kwraa lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are stored in damp conditions before planting, planted too deep in the soil, or lack enough moisture. Damaged or low-quality seed batches also have naturally lower germination rates.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ dani adu. ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ loo hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli Dumɔwui akui ni efite loo ni ehiii lɛ hu yɛ adebɔɔ naa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ fioo.

english: Why are my crops growing very tall with deep green leaves but failing to produce big fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa shi enyɛɛɛ ewo yibii wuji lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer makes them spend all their energy growing leaves and stems. Plants need balanced nutrients, especially phosphorus and potassium, to form strong flowers and large fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo baai kɛ ŋmeii. Niyenii ni sa he miihia tsei. titri lɛ, fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium ni haa fɔfɔi ni wa kɛ aduawai wuji baa

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and stunt during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can waterlog the soil, suffocating the roots so they cannot breathe or absorb food. Excessive water also washes away essential nutrients like nitrogen deep into the ground where roots cannot reach.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha nu akpa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu loo amɛmu niyenii. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hu shwieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant them close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition makes all the plants weak and thin, resulting in a smaller total harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afee lɛ fɛɛ ni baa shi.

english: Why are some crop varieties able to survive heavy rains and pest attacks while others die quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni kooloi srɔtoi komɛi gboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Certain plant varieties have natural defenses bred into them, such as tougher skin, stronger root systems, or natural chemicals that deter bugs and resist fungal diseases common in hot, humid climates.
ga: Tsei komɛi yɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu, tamɔ hewolo ni mli wa. Shishifãi ni mli wa loo adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni tsiɔ kooloi bibii anaa ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Plants drop flowers when stressed by extreme weather, sudden dry spells, or lack of nutrients. Without proper moisture and pollination, the plant sheds flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Tsei baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni naa wa waa hao amɛ. trukaa ŋmɔlɔ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Kɛji hulutsoo kɛ pollination ni sa bɛ lɛ, Tsei laajeɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why do market women prefer to buy crop varieties that I didn't grow, even when mine look fine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayeli yei hɔɔ tsei ni miduuu lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ minɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ.

english: Traders look for specific variety traits like longer shelf-life, firmness during transport, or cooking quality that consumers want. Some varieties rot fast on the way to market, making buyers avoid them.
ga: Jarayelɔi taoɔ sui srɔtoi, tamɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe. tightness yɛ gbɛfaa mli loo bɔ ni ahoɔ nii ahaa ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ Srɔtoi komɛi fiteɔ oya yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ amɛhe.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year when I plant the exact same crop on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ faaa daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and soil diseases to multiply over time.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa tsei pɔtɛɛ anɔ lɛ ayi fa babaoo yɛ be kɛ bei amli.

english: Can I grow everyday staple crops anywhere in Ghana, or do they only do well in specific regions?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu daa gbi ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ Ghana he fɛɛ he? Aloo ebaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpokpai komɛi pɛ anɔ?

english: Many common staple crops like cassava and maize are highly adaptable and can grow successfully across almost all ecological zones in Ghana, provided they receive basic rainfall and sunlight.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni afɔɔ dumɔ yɛ mli lɛ ateŋ ekomɛi ji ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa. Enyɛɔ etsakeɔ ehe waa ni ebaanyɛ eda yɛ omanyeyeli mli yɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ he fɛɛ he ni bɔɔ nii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ yɔɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ. Kɛji onine shɛ shishijee nugbɔ kɛ hulu la nɔ

english: How do I know if my soil is suitable for planting general household crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha shia ŋmɔshi nibii ni afɔɔ feemɔ?

english: Most common crops in Ghana are hardy and tolerate a wide range of soil types, as long as the ground has good water drainage and isn't overly waterlogged.
ga: Tso ni afɔɔ naa waa yɛ Ghana lɛ wa ni eŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ henɔi srɔtoi ahe gbɛ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nu ehiɛɛɛ mli tsɔ.

english: How much harvest can I realistically expect from my land if I care for my crops properly?
ga: Nikpamɔ enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: With good farm management, proper spacing, and improved seeds, high-yielding crop varieties in Ghana can produce up to 6.5 tons per hectare.
ga: Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa nɔ lɛ, sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ Ghana lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii ni shɛɔ tɔn 6.5 yɛ hectare kome mli.

english: Why is my harvest volume much lower than the maximum yield other farmers talk about?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ falɛ baa shi kwraa fe yibiiwoo ni fa fe fɛɛ ni okwaafoi krokomɛi tsĩ tã lɛ?

english: Low yields usually happen because of poor seed selection, overcrowding plants, poor weed control, or irregular rainfall during critical growth stages.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ baa yɛ dumɔwui ni ahalaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Tsei ni eyi obɔ kɛ jwɛi lɛ nyɛɛɛ akudɔ jwɛi loo nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ dalɛ bei ni he hiaa lɛ amli.

english: Are there crops I can plant in Ghana that will be ready to harvest in just three months?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ madu yɛ Ghana ni baafee klalo kɛha kpamɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ pɛ mli?

english: Yes, short-duration crops like early-maturing maize, cowpeas, and certain vegetables complete their growth cycle within 90 days, allowing for fast food production.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra, tsina ŋmãa kɛ aduawai komɛi baagbe amɛdalɛ be lɛ naa yɛ gbii 90 mli, ni no baaha anyɛ afee niyenii ni ayeɔ oya.

english: Do crops that mature in three months require extra care compared to long-season crops?
ga: Ani tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli lɛ he miihia ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛto tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ahe?

english: Short-season crops don't necessarily need more total inputs, but they require timely weeding and fertilizer because their fast growth gives them less time to recover from neglect.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ biɔ nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli. Shi jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia amɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Akɛni amɛdaraa oya hewɔ lɛ, amɛnáaa be babaoo ni amɛkɛbaatsa amɛhe kɛjɛ hiɛ ni akuɔ ashwieɔ amɛnɔ lɛ mli.

english: What kind of crops should I plant to protect my household when local food prices keep going up?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ madu koni mikɛbu mishia lɛ he beni maŋ lɛ mli niyenii jara yaa hiɛ waa lɛ?

english: Planting fast-growing staple crops provides direct food for your family and extra income to sell at local markets, helping buffer your finances against general price increases.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ oya ni oookwɛ lɛ baaha oweku lɛ aná niyenii tɛ̃ɛ, ni ebaaha oná shika kroko ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ oshika kɛjɛɔ jara ni yaa hiɛ lɛ mli.

english: Some farmers refer to certain crops as an 'engine' for the farm—what does that mean?
ga: Okwaafoi komɛi tsɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi akɛ ‘Engine’ kɛha ŋmɔ ko, mɛni ji no shishi?

english: An 'engine' crop is a quick-turnaround crop that grows reliably and sells fast, generating continuous cash flow and keeping your farming business financially active.
ga: Engine’ ŋmɔshi nibii ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsɔɔ oya. ni daa ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni ahɔ̃ɔ oya Ha shika ni yaa nɔ ni oha okwaayeli nitsumɔ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ shika gbɛfaŋ

english: Is it safer for a beginner like me to plant daily food crops or focus on high-risk cash crops?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha mɔ ni jeɔ shishi tamɔ mi lɛ akɛ ebaadu daa gbi niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii loo ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama shika ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ oshara waa lɛ anɔ?

english: Starting with daily food crops is safer because there is always a guaranteed local demand every day, meaning you can easily sell your harvest or feed your family.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooobɔi kɛ daa gbi niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ejaakɛ daa gbi nibii ni ataoɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ he nɔmimaa yɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ onibii loo oha oweku lɛ niyenii yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ.

english: How does planting short-term crops help me make money faster throughout the year?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná shika oya yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Short-term crops allow you to plant and harvest multiple times within a single major rainy season, giving you income every few months rather than once a year.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ nii ni okpaa nii shii abɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri kome mli. Ha oná shika daa nyɔji fioo moŋ fe shikome yɛ afi mli

english: Why do I see so many black insects and ants whenever I lift up decaying leaves on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii diji kɛ ŋmeii babaoo be fɛɛ be ni mawo baai ni egboi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When leaves lie on the ground, they trap moisture and create shade. This creates a safe home where soil insects and ants gather to feed on the organic material and break it down.
ga: Kɛji baai lɛ gbee shikpɔŋ lɛ Ebaahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni efee hulutsoo. Enɛ haa shia ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe baa ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa koni amɛye nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛfite.

english: What is actually happening underneath the crop leaves lying on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe baai lɛ ashishi?

english: Underneath those leaves, active soil organisms like insects and microbes are constantly chewing and decomposing dead plant matter, converting it into nutrient-rich organic food for your crops.
ga: Nakai baai lɛ ashishi Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii tamɔ kooloi bibii kɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ shwieɔ tsei amli nibii ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be. Tsɔmɔmɔ lɛ ni efee niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛha onibii.

english: Are the black ants living under my plant residues harmful to my crops?
ga: Ani ŋmeii diji ni hiɔ mi tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Most ants living under crop residues are beneficial because they help break down plant waste and prey on smaller crop pests, though a few species can protect sap-sucking insects like aphids.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni hiɔ tsei amli ŋmeii ashishi lɛ ateŋ mɛi babaoo ahe ejaakɛ amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa ni amɛfoɔ tsei amli ŋmeii ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii bibii. Eyɛ mli akɛ, kooloi srɔtoi fioo ko pɛ nyɛɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids lɛ ahe moŋ.

english: Why do small insects prefer living under piles of plant waste instead of open soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii sumɔɔ ni amɛhi tsei amli jwɛi ni abua naa lɛ shishi moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Open soil gets hot and dry under the sun, which kills many soil creatures. Plant waste acts as a protective cover that keeps the ground cool, wet, and filled with food.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni agbele naa lɛ baadɔ ni ebaagbi yɛ hulu lɛ shishi. ni gbeɔ kooloi babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei amli jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ni niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii eyi mli obɔ.

english: Does seeing many small bugs in my soil when I turn it mean my land is unhealthy?
ga: ni minaa kooloi bibii E babaoo yɛ mi muji lɛ mli beni mitsɔ mli lɛ. Ani enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ?

english: No, seeing active insects in your soil is actually a sign of healthy land with rich organic matter, as these organisms are essential for naturally renewing soil nutrients.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ ona kooloi bibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, eji he ko ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ lɛ he okadi. Enɛ ji akɛ nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ he hia kɛha adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ feemɔ.

english: Why am I advised to keep turning over decaying crop waste on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ awoɔ mi ŋaa koni maya nɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Turning decaying crop waste introduces air into the material, helping soil insects and microbes break it down faster into rich compost while preventing foul smells and disease buildup.
ga: Nibii ni adu mli ni fiteɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ nibii lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi bibii kɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii gbohii kɛ helai ni buaa amɛhe naa lɛ naa.

english: How can I control the soil bugs that scatter when I turn over plant residue?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makudɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji mitsɔ tsei amli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ?

english: You do not need to eliminate all soil bugs because most are helpful decomposers. Practicing crop rotation and avoiding unnecessary chemicals naturally keeps pest populations balanced.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni ojie kooloi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kwraa ejaakɛ kooloi babaoo ji nibii ni fiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ tsofai ni he ehiaaa ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ayibɔ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will the black insects feeding under decaying leaves move on to eat my fresh crop roots?
ga: Ani kooloi diji ni yeɔ baai ni egboi lɛ baafã koni amɛyaye mi tsei heei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ?

english: Most insects found in decaying leaves prefer dead plant matter. They will generally not attack fresh roots unless the soil becomes extremely dry or the plant is already sick.
ga: Kplukai babaoo ni anaa yɛ baai ni egboi amli lɛ sumɔɔ tsei ni egboi lɛ ahe nibii. Bei pii lɛ, amɛtutuuu shishifãi heei ja shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi waa loo hela emɔ tso lɛ momo.

english: Is it beneficial to turn old crop leaves into the soil before planting my next crop?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ aaaku sɛɛ akɛ tso baai momo awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, turning old crop leaves into the soil feeds the living organisms in the ground, which releases vital nutrients like nitrogen and improves the soil's ability to hold water.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni etsɛ ni adu lɛ ahe baai ni atsakeɔ awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ aná niyenii. Enɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hia tamɔ nitrogen ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: How can I keep plant waste on my soil to protect it without breeding dangerous farm pests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahã tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni mabu shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni mikɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ akafɔ?

english: Spread the plant waste in a thin, even layer across your farm instead of leaving it in thick, deep piles. This protects your soil while allowing enough sunlight to keep pest numbers under control.
ga: Gbalamɔ tso lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ mli yɛ gbɛ bibioo ko nɔ, ni egbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi lɛ yɛ ŋtayaa ni mli kwɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ebu oshikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛtsɔ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ebaaha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ ahi shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the plant lacks nitrogen. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the newer top leaves, which shows that your soil needs nitrogen-rich fertilizer, animal manure, or compost.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves, but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or grows in overly rich soil, it spends all its energy growing branches and leaves above ground instead of tubers below. Cassava needs balanced soil with adequate potassium to help the roots swell into large tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii babaoo nɔ. Ebaafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ tsei niji kɛ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ shishi. Yucca he miihia shikpɔŋ ni ja kɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings drying up and dying during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong direct sunlight because their leaves dry out quickly. Planting shade crops like plantain or shade trees next to young cocoa provides living umbrellas that shield them from intense heat until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei yɛ kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to produce food for the plant, which travels down into the ground to make the yam tuber grow big and heavy.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baa lɛ ni ewoɔ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ. ni gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ koni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛtsii.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves and small dirt-like powder in the center whorl?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ nibii bibii ni tamɔ muji lɛ? Yɛ kooyigbɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This is a clear sign of Fall Armyworm damage. The caterpillars feed inside the growing tip of the plant and leave behind waste that looks like sawdust, which can destroy the plant's growth if not managed early.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ efite nii. Kplukai lɛ yeɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛshiɔ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmei. Enɛ baanyɛ afite tsei adalɛ kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking juices from the leaves, or by a virus transmitted by these insects. Controlling these pests early with neem leaf extract or appropriate sprays stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Kudɔmɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra Kɛtsɔ neem tso mli nu ni sa loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa baa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit while it is forming, often triggered by irregular watering. Keeping the soil moisture consistent and adding agricultural lime or compost helps correct this.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli beni efeɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ lime loo okwaayeli mli ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do my swamp rice fields need to be kept under standing water during growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi-swamp rice ŋmɔji lɛ ahi nu shishi yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Flooding rice fields prevents weeds from growing because most weed seeds cannot germinate under water. It also keeps the soil at a steady, warm temperature and ensures the rice roots have constant moisture.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli lɛ haaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ ejaakɛ jwɛi dumɔwui babaoo nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ nu shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa ŋmɔtɔ daa.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farmland after harvesting maize instead of planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmãa ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nitrogen out of the soil, but legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts put nitrogen back into the soil through their roots. Rotating them restores soil fertility naturally so your next crops grow better without high fertilizer costs.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛhaa nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nyɔmɔwoo babaoo akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over when they carry heavy bunches or during rainstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ yaa nɔ egbeeɔ shi kɛ́ miwo ŋmeii wuji loo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that can easily be weakened by pests like root nematodes or banana weevils. Cutting off excess suckers so only two or three stalks grow per stool and propping heavy fruiting stems with strong wooden poles keeps them stable.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ oya. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ koni tsei 2-3 pɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ sɛi kome mli, ni akɛ tsei ni wa ni akɛfiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ asɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on one of my cocoa trees turning yellow while the surrounding trees look healthy and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ eko nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Etamɔ nɔ ni ehe wa ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ

english: Yellow leaves on a single tree can be an early warning sign of stress, nutrient deficiency, or an emerging disease like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus. Identifying it early helps prevent the problem from spreading to nearby healthy trees.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ tso kome nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ mɔ ko miiye haomɔ mra. niyenii ni esaaa loo helai ni miiba tamɔ cocoa bud virus lɛ ayɔsemɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni naagba lɛ akagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if a yellow leaf on my cocoa tree is just old or if the tree is sick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ egbɔ kɛkɛ loo hela mɔ tso lɛ?

english: Old leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off one by one from the lower branches. When a tree is sick, whole sections or young leaves turn yellow, often accompanied by spots, swollen stems, or stunted growth.
ga: Baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shishigbɛ niji lɛ anɔ komekomei. Kɛ tso lɛ hela mɔ lɛ, efãi muu lɛ fɛɛ loo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, bei pii lɛ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, eshishifãi lɛ efuu, loo ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: I noticed three cocoa trees standing next to each other all have yellow leaves. Does disease move from tree to tree?
ga: Miyɔse kookoo tsei etɛ ni damɔ shi yɛ sɛɛ mli, ni fɛɛ yɛ baai ŋmɔŋ. Ani hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ?

english: Yes, many crop diseases spread from an infected tree to neighboring ones through touching branches, shared roots, wind, or sap-sucking insects like mealybugs, causing sick trees to appear in clusters.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai babaoo gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni amɛtaa he lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi ni ajaa, kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mealybugs lɛ haa tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ kui amli.

english: Why do crop diseases usually start in one small patch of the farm before spreading everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ tsei ahe helai jeɔ shishi yɛ hei bibii lɛ? Okwaafoi lɛ ateŋ ekome dani egbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he?

english: Diseases usually begin where an insect lands or where damp conditions favor fungus. Once established on one tree, the infection multiplies and moves outward to the closest trees first.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela jeɔ shishi kɛ kooloi bibii ni baa shi loo hei ni ŋmɔtɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ aba lɛ. Kɛji eba tso kome nɔ lɛ Hela lɛ yaa hiɛ ni efãa kɛyaa tso ni bɛŋkɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Do insects carry sickness from one cocoa tree to neighboring trees?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii kɛ helai jɛɔ kookoo tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, pests like mealybugs feed on sick trees, pick up viruses or bacteria, and crawl or get carried by ants to neighboring healthy trees, spreading the disease across your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ tsei tamɔ mealybugs lɛ yeɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ. Buamɔ helai loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ naa ni ŋmeii shwieɔ shi loo amɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. koni egbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: What should I do immediately if I find a single sick cocoa tree in the middle of my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji mina kookoo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: You should mark the tree, carefully inspect neighboring trees for early symptoms, and report it to an extension officer. Removing or treating an infected tree quickly protects the rest of your farm from infection.
ga: Esa akɛ okadi tso lɛ. Kwɛmɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni ona okadii ni tsɔɔ hela lɛ mra. ni okɛ amaniɛbɔɔ aha hiɛyaa he nitsulɔ lɛ Oya ni ooojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ loo otsa amɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he kɛjɛ hela he.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to check the color and health of my crop leaves?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ ahe su kɛ amɛhewalɛ?

english: Walking through your farm at least once a week allows you to notice subtle changes, like leaf discoloration on a single tree, before an infection turns into a widespread outbreak.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, kɛ́ onyiɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ebaaha ona tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo, tamɔ tso kome nɔ baai ni tsakeɔ. dani hela lɛ baatsɔ hela ni gbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he

english: Why is it risky to ignore just one or two yellowing cocoa trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ maku mihiɛ mishwie cacao tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: A single sick tree acts as a continuous source of infection. Delaying action allows pests and wind to carry the sickness from that single tree to surrounding healthy ones, increasing your yield loss.
ga: Tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni helai baa mɔ nɔ daa. Nifeemɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ helai baa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Can poor soil cause my cocoa leaves to turn yellow, or is it always a disease?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ? Aloo eji hela be fɛɛ be?

english: Poor soil lacking nutrients like nitrogen can cause leaves to turn yellow across large areas of your farm. Unlike diseases, nutrient deficiencies usually affect trees uniformly rather than in small, expanding patches.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen bɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli hei wuji. Esoro niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ yɛ hela he yɛ gbɛ ni ji akɛ, efɔɔ tsei anɔ hewalɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ moŋ fe hei bibii. atsake mli

english: How does the amount of shade on my farm affect leaf color and tree health?
ga: Te hulutsoo be ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa baa lɛ su kɛ tso lɛ hewalɛnamɔ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Too much shade creates damp conditions that encourage leaf fungi, while too little shade exposes cocoa leaves to harsh sunlight, turning them yellow and stressed. Balanced shade keeps leaves healthy and dark green.
ga: Shade ni fa fe nine lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni woɔ ŋmɔtɔ he hewalɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulutsoo fioo ko pɛ baaha hulu la ni naa wa lɛ ashɛ kookoo baai lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni haoɔ amɛhe. Susumɔ ni ja lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli kwɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for plant growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps restore their healthy green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have beneficial bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a natural fertilizer for the crops you plant next.
ga: Muawai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa mli yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or whiteflies sucking the sap from the leaves, or by viruses spread by these same insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ nɔŋŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ

english: What is eating small, round holes in my cabbage leaves, and how do I protect them?
ga: Nɔ ko ni ŋmei yɔɔ mi-cabbage baa lɛ nɔ lɛ yeli Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by caterpillars such as the Diamondback Moth larvae. You can manage them by inspecting leaves regularly, handpicking caterpillars, or using neem-based organic sprays.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ diamondback ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ obaai lɛ ni oookwɛ daa lɛ nɔ. Halamɔ ŋmeii Aloo okɛ neem spray ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from water stress, excessive heat, or attacks from pests like mirids (capsids). Providing moderate shade and managing pests helps the flowers stay on the tree.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛ́ nu he haomɔ miipiŋ amɛ. hulutsoo ni fe nine loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mirids (capsids) lɛ tutuamɔ. Shade ni sa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii ahi tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during heavy rain or winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems and top-heavy fruit bunches. Pests like root nematodes or banana weevils can weaken the roots underground, causing the entire plant to collapse under wind or heavy fruit weight.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo banana ŋmeii baanyɛ aha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ loo aduawai ni tsii hewɔ.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground toward the sun and keeps them dry, preventing soil-borne fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ ateshi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kɛya hulu lɛ he ni eha amɛgbi. Koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni sũ kɛbaa lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when water stays on my field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits on the field, it smothers the roots and creates a warm, wet environment where rotting fungi thrive.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ Nu lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ ada yɛ.

english: What causes my tomatoes to split open on the plant right when they start turning red?
ga: Mɛni haa tomatoi shwereɔ kɛ́ amɛbɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Tomatoes split when they receive a sudden surge of water after a dry period. The inner part of the tomato expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to crack.
ga: Tomatoi fiteɔ kɛ́ amɛná nu ni fa trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Tomato lɛ mligbɛ lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Why is it important to keep standing water in my rice field during the growing period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ nu ni damɔ shi awo ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Keeping a controlled layer of water in low-land rice fields prevents weeds from growing and competing with the rice while helping the crop easily absorb nutrients from the soil.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ baatsi jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkɛ ŋmãa lɛ akabɔ akaŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya.

english: How many times a day should I water my vegetable nursery during the dry season in Tamale?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi-greenhouse lɛ nu daa gbi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli yɛ Tamale?

english: During hot dry seasons in places like Tamale, high heat dries out the topsoil quickly. Watering two or three times a day—early morning, mid-day shade, and late afternoon—keeps the soil cool and prevents tender roots from drying out.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni hulutsoo be mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli yɛ hei tamɔ Tamale lɛ, hulutsoo be ni naa wa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gĩɔ oya. Nu lɛ shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ daa gbi, tamɔ leebi maŋkpa, shwane mli, kɛ shwane mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ebaatsi shishifãi bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi.

english: Will watering my crops three times every day hurt them if the weather isn't very hot?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ shii etɛ daa gbi lɛ baaye amɛ awui kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ?

english: Yes, watering too often when it is cool or cloudy can soak the ground too much. Overwatered roots cannot breathe and will begin to rot, which turns the crop yellow and stops growth.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ afɔ nu shii abɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ loo atatu ewo lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. Shishifãi ni awo amɛ nu fe nine lɛ nyɛŋ amu ni amɛbaabɔi fitemɔ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpa dalɛ.

english: Why do crops grow differently here in Tamale compared to crops grown in southern Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Tamale biɛ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ kɛ akɛto nɔ ni aduɔ yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Northern Ghana has a shorter rainy season and much higher heat than the south. Crops react directly to local heat and soil moisture, so farming schedules and watering amounts must be adjusted for the northern weather.
ga: Ghana kooyigbɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ faaa, ni edɔ waa fe anaigbɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli dɔlɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ atsake okwaayeli he gbɛjianɔtoo kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ mli bɔ ni sa kɛha kooyigbɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ.

english: How does the harsh heat in northern Ghana affect my young plants during the afternoon?
ga: Te hulutsoo ni naa wa ni yɔɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ saa mi dumɔwui lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ yɛ shwane mli?

english: Strong heat makes plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the soil. This causes young crops to wilt in the afternoon to protect themselves from losing moisture.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi lɛ he.

english: How do I judge the right time to start planting at the beginning of the rainy season?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ akojo be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje dumɔ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: You should start planting only after the first major rains have soaked the soil deeply for a few consecutive days. Planting too early after just one light shower will cause seeds to dry up and die in the hot ground.
ga: Esa akɛ oje dumɔ shishi pɛ kɛkɛ ni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do young crop seedlings need more careful daily monitoring than mature crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui bibii biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ daa gbi fe tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have small, shallow roots that cannot reach underground moisture. They need close attention and regular water until their root systems grow deep enough to survive tough conditions.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Amɛbiɔ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni aha amɛ nu daa kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baaya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why do crops planted too close together in a group grow weak and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ kui amli ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots fight each other for the limited water and food in the soil, while their leaves block sunlight from one another. Giving each plant proper space helps them all grow strong.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni edaraa waa.

english: Does planting legumes alongside my main crops help them grow better?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, crops like groundnuts or cowpeas share the soil well with grains like maize. Legumes take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the ground, acting as a natural food supply for surrounding crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei baanyɛ aja shikpɔŋ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmaa tamɔ ŋmei. Legumes heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ.

english: Is it true that applying fertilizer multiple times a week makes crops produce more food?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli shii abɔ yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awo niyenii babaoo?

english: No, giving fertilizer too frequently burns the roots and damages the plant. Crops only need food at specific development stages, usually once or twice during the whole season.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli shii abɔ lɛ, ebaashã shishifãi lɛ ni efite tso lɛ. Niyenii he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ amɛshweremɔ bei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli pɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are often a signal that the crop lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that too much water is drowning the roots and stopping them from absorbing food.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu babaoo miiha shishifãi lɛ mii shi ni ekpa niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection because harsh, direct sun can scorch their delicate leaves and dry out the soil. Fast-growing plantain trees produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool soil moisture it needs until it gets older.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa.

english: Yam vines produce leaves that need maximum sunlight to make food for the plant. When you stake the vines, the leaves spread out toward the sun instead of bunching on the wet ground, which helps the plant send more energy down to grow bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ baai ni he hiaa hulu la babaoo koni ekɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Beni okɛ wain tso lɛ fĩɔ lɛ Baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa hulu lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaabua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛ bulbs wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Maize plants roll their leaves inward as a natural protection mechanism when heat is intense. By reducing the leaf area exposed to hot sun and dry wind, the plant conserves water so it does not dry out and die.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa. Kɛtsɔ he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei hiɛɔ nu koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why are my tomato plants shedding their blossoms instead of forming fruits when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When tomatoes experience extreme heat or erratic rainfall, the plant gets stressed and sheds its flowers to save energy for its own survival rather than putting resource into growing new fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomatoi lɛ shɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he lɛ Tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai heei

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn plants turning yellow while the tops stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛyiteŋgbɛi lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that the soil is running low on nitrogen. The crop automatically moves whatever nitrogen it has left from its older, lower leaves up to feed the young green leaves growing at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do extension officers tell me that rotating groundnuts or cowpeas on my land makes the soil richer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ, kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsake lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas work with small beneficial bacteria in their roots to capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground. When the crop dies, that natural nitrogen remains in the soil to feed your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii kɛ helai bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii gboi lɛ Nakai adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do small caterpillars attack the inside funnel of my young maize stalks instead of the outer leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ tutuaa mi-babi corn tsei lɛ amligbɛ gbɛi lɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm crawl into the center whorl of the maize plant because the leaves there are soft, tender, and moist. Hiding deep inside the stalk also protects them from sunlight, rain, and birds.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli ejaakɛ baai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ mɔ ko kɛ ehe tee tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ, no hu buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hulu, nugbɔ, kɛ okpoi ahe.

english: What makes this purple-flowered weed attach itself directly to the roots of my maize and stunt its growth?
ga: Mɛni haa nɛkɛ jwɛi ni fɔfɔi yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ kpɛtɛɔ mi-abele shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ ni ehaa edalɛ sɛɛ foɔ?

english: That weed is Striga, a parasitic plant that cannot survive on its own. It locks onto crop roots beneath the soil to steal water and plant food directly from your maize, causing the maize leaves to turn yellow and stop growing.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji Striga, ni ji tso ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe. Ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ shishifãi ahe koni eju nu ni ekɛdu niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa dalɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and tall with very small yields when I plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ daa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of growing thick stems and heavy fruits, the plants waste all their energy stretching upward to escape the shade of their neighbors.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Mohu ɔ, a woɔ tsohi nɛ a he wa, nɛ a woɔ yiblii nɛ mi wa. Mohu ɔ, tso ɔ puɛɔ e he wami ɔ tsuo kɛ guɔ e he nɛ e kplɛɛɔ konɛ e kɛ e weku ɔ hɛ mi nɛ je e he ɔ nɔ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready to harvest under the soil without digging them all up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni okɛ amɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: As cassava reaches maturity between 9 to 12 months, its lower leaves turn yellow and drop off naturally. You will also notice cracks forming on top of the soil right around the stem base, showing that the tubers underneath are swelling.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli lɛ, eshishigbɛ baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaagbee shi. Obaana ŋmeii ni miifee sũ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ hu. Etsɔɔ akɛ yitso ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ efuu.

english: Why do some cocoa trees on my farm produce many heavy pods while others produce almost nothing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni tsii waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi wooo ŋmeii kwraa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees respond directly to regular care. Trees that get regular pruning, weeding, and pest control can direct all their energy into producing pods, whereas neglected trees spend their energy struggling against weeds, shade, and pests.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ daa. Tsei ni afolɔ amɛ daa, ni ajieɔ jwɛi, ni akudɔɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛfee ŋmeii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni aku hiɛ ashwie amɛnɔ lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛwuɔ ashiɔ jwɛi, shade kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui.

english: How does clearing weeds around the base of my cocoa trees help the pods grow bigger?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ajiemɔ Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kookoo tso lɛ shishi yeɔ ebuaa kookoo tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ?

english: Weeds steal water and plant food from the soil that your cocoa roots need. When you clear the weeds, all the soil nutrients go straight to the cocoa tree, allowing it to build larger, healthier pods.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii ni he hiaa o-cocoa shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji ojie jwɛi lɛ Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii fɛɛ yaa kookoo tso lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce most of their ripe pods around September instead of throughout the whole year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ eyibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɛ September mli moŋ fe afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees follow the rainy season pattern. The heavy rains trigger flowering, and it takes about five to six months for those flowers to grow into full, mature pods ready for the main harvest in September.
ga: Cocoa tsei nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa fɔfɔi baa. Ni fɔfɔi nɛɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji enumɔ kɛyashi enumɔ dani amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni eda ni asaa amɛhe kɛha kpamɔ titri lɛ yɛ September mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their leaves during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is the tree's natural way of saving water. Fewer leaves mean less water evaporates from the tree, helping it survive hot, dry weather until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ. Baai fioo tsɔɔ akɛ nu fioo pɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the tiny flowers on my cocoa trunk falling off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Ani mi-kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed excess flowers if they lack sufficient water, nutrients, or insect pollinators. The tree only keeps as many flowers as its overall strength can support to mature into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛbɛ nu, niyenii mli hewalɛ loo nibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ. Tso lɛ baahiɛ fɔfɔi babaoo bɔ ni ehewalɛ fɛɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eda ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: This is black pod disease, which is caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, dark conditions. Keeping the farm well-pruned allows sunlight and airflow to dry out moisture and prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela, ni ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ mli kɛbaa. Gbɛjegbɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ haa fɛ̃i lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaaa ŋmɔtɔ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why should I cut off the fresh green shoots growing near the bottom of my cocoa trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: These shoots, called chupons, act like parasites on the main tree. They steal nutrients and water without producing pods, which reduces your crop yield if you do not remove them.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ tso wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ. Amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu ni amɛfeee ŋmeii. Enɛ baaha otso lɛ yibiiwoo aba shi kɛji ojieee lɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need shade trees planted near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he hiaa ni adu tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sunshine. Shade trees protect young cocoa from harsh heat and keep the soil moist while the young roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi bibii lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: A mature pod changes color completely from green or dark red to bright yellow or orange. Harvesting at this stage ensures the seeds inside have fully developed sugary pulp necessary for good processing.
ga: Pods ni eda lɛ tsakeɔ su kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo akutu ni mli tse. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ ni mli ŋɔɔ ni he hiaa kɛha nitsumɔ kpakpa.

english: Why must I cover my harvested cocoa beans with plantain leaves for a few days before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ plantain baai haa kookoo ni akpa lɛ nɔ gbii fioo komɛi dani migbiɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the fresh beans with plantain leaves allows them to ferment. Fermentation generates heat, which kills the seed inside, stops it from sprouting, and creates the rich chocolate flavor buyers look for.
