ga: Kɛ́ akɛ plantain baai ha ŋmeii heei ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii. Fɛ̃i haa dɔlɛ baa. Enɛ gbeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ehaa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ, ni ehaa tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and scorched during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that easily burn under strong sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or Gliricidia planted alongside them to block direct heat and keep moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo glicidia ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni akɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in the shape of a V from the tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves in maize starting from the center vein usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, which is its main food for growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or manure helps the leaves regain their deep green color and feed the growing cob.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tso lɛ daa lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni baa lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni eha niyenii aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and shrinking into tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee kɔɔpoi ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically a sign that tiny insects like thrips or mites are sucking sap from underneath the leaves, or that a plant virus is present. The plant curls its leaves as a stress response to losing sap and water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites miinu nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ shishi lɛ mli. aloo hela ko yɛ tso lɛ mli Tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ nu kɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ hetoohamɔ mli.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when day or night temperatures get too hot, or when soil moisture changes drastically. Heat stress prevents pollen from fertilizing the flower, causing the plant to shed unfertilized flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa shwane loo gbɛkɛ. aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsake waa Heat stress tsiɔ pollen naa koni ekawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ. Ha tsei ajie fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why should I cut away extra suckers growing around my main plantain tree instead of letting them all grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha amɛ fɛɛ amɛdara

english: Extra suckers steal water, food, and sunlight from the main mother plant. By leaving only one or two strong suckers, all the plant's energy goes into producing a heavy, healthy bunch of plantains rather than many tiny, weak fruits.
ga: Suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Eshiɔ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ yaa plantains ni tsii ni ehe wa lɛ feemɔ mli. Yɛ yibii bibioo ko najiaŋ lɛ, mɛi babaoo ni bɛ hewalɛ

english: Yam vines produce food for the underground tuber using their leaves in sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves into the light and away from damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and helping the plant produce much bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ baai ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ ahi he ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ, ni ekɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ akabɔ he. Etsiɔ tso helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ bulbs ni da fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground if heavy rains fall right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa dani kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to survive. When heavy rain saturates the earth for too long, water displaces air, causing roots to suffocate and allowing soil fungi to rot the cassava tubers rapidly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Nu baaye kɔɔyɔɔ najiaŋ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ oya.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field help my maize crop grow better next season?
ga: Te ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop dies, that nitrogen stays in the soil and acts as natural fertilizer for the next crop, like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii gboi Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why does my lowland rice crop grow better when standing water covers the base of the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-flat rice lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ ha shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lowland rice stems have special air passages that allow them to breathe underwater, while most competing weeds suffocate and die in flooded fields. Standing water also keeps the root temperature stable and nutrients dissolved.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ tsei lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsui krɛdɛɛi ni haa amɛmuɔ yɛ nu shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ ateŋ mɛi babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ mli dɔlɛ kɛ niyenii ni mli ewo muji lɛ hiɔ shi daa.

english: Why do my vegetable crops droop and wilt on hot sunny afternoons even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: On hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up. Temporary wilting is a survival trick where the plant reduces leaf surface exposed to the sun; as long as the soil has moisture, leaves recover by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Be kukuoo mli shwiemɔ ji wala yiwalaheremɔ ŋaa ni tsei haa baa lɛ nɔ hulu la baa shi. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, baai lɛ baaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow even when the soil looks dark and rich?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is missing key nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are getting too much water and suffocating. Even rich soil can run out of specific food that crops need to stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ miiná nu babaoo ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ lɛ po baanyɛ aná niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why are my sweet potato vines spreading everywhere on the ground, but the tubers underneath stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes sweet potatoes to put all their energy into growing leafy green vines instead of storing food in the root tubers below the ground.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛduɔ wain tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaato niyenii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and skinny without forming big corn ears when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeee abele toi agboi beni midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of putting energy into making big corn ears, the plants stretch upward just to reach the sun.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmãa toi agbo lɛ Tso lɛ baajie ehe kpo ni eshɛ hulu lɛ he.

english: Why do my cabbage heads split open right before they are ready for me to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ mli gbalaa dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ makpa lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads split when they take in too much water too quickly after a dry period. The inside grows faster than the outer leaves can stretch, causing the head to burst open.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei lɛ baajara kɛji akɛ aha amɛ nu babaoo mra tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ. Mligbɛ lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. ha yitso lɛ atswa

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruits during the peak dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat makes tomato pollen dry up and become inactive. When flowers are not pollinated, the plant drops them to conserve energy and water instead of forming fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato mli ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii. Beni fɔfɔii lɛ bɛ pollination lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up like small cups when the weather gets hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ebɔle ehe tamɔ kɔɔpoo bibioo ko lɛ? Be ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually a reaction to stress from extreme heat, or damage caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips and whiteflies that feast on the leaf sap.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo nɔ ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips kɛ whiteflies ni yeɔ baa mli nu lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my piece of land produce smaller yields every year even though I plant the exact same crop every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi moŋ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year. Rotating different crops, especially beans or peanuts, helps restore missing nutrients and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ afite kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi titri lɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii ni elaaje lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous harvest grow weaker crops than the packaged seeds I buy from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ fe dumɔwui ni awo mli ni mihe yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specially bred for high strength and yield in their first generation. Seeds collected from those harvested crops lose those special qualities in the next planting, producing weaker plants.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nakai tsei ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ yɛ dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why does my harvested cassava spoil so fast within just two or three days after I dig it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli beni mifo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots continue to breathe and lose water rapidly after harvest. Natural chemical reactions inside the root break it down quickly once detached from the stem, which is why it must be processed or sold quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shishifã lɛ he pɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni esa akɛ atsu he nii loo ahɔ̃ɔ oya lɛ.

english: How does drying my harvested chili peppers prevent them from rotting before I get them to the market?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mikpamɔ lɛ ni mikɛaagbi lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ amɛnaa koni amɛkafite dani mikɛ amɛ aya jara nɔ?

english: Drying removes moisture from the peppers, which stops mold and bacteria from growing. Without water, these microbes cannot survive, allowing the peppers to stay fresh and usable for many months.
ga: Kɛ́ egbi lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. Kɛ́ nu bɛ lɛ, nibii bibii nɛɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi. Enɛ haa chili lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii nyɔji babaoo.

english: When maize plants are packed too tightly, they fight each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough resources to grow strong stalks and produce big, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tsei ni he wa ni ewo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yams grow underground and need soft, loose soil to expand into large tubers. High mounds give the tubers room to grow long and wide while keeping excess water from drowning the roots.
ga: Sweet potatoes kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ehe miihia ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni etse ehe lɛ aya hiɛ ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Gɔŋ ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ naa koni ekabote shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when there is direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that easily burn under full sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them creates a living umbrella that keeps the cocoa cool and moist until it matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ emasɛi Ehaa hulutsoo ni haa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa.

english: Why do people advise me to plant beans on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil, but beans naturally put food back in. Beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground, restoring soil fertility for your next planting season.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii kɛ niyenii baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Beans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Koni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha okwɛ̃mɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean your maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to stay green. Adding compost or fertilizer around the base helps feed the plant so the green color returns to new growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni aha tso lɛ niyenii koni enyɛ etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my pepper flowers falling off before any peppers actually grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ miida diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they get stressed, usually from sudden dry spells or extreme heat. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji amɛhao. Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ba lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants drooping and wilting even when the soil is very wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigboi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa moŋ lɛ?

english: Too much water can rot the roots and prevent them from breathing, causing the plant to wilt from root damage. Soil should stay damp like a wrung-out sponge rather than soaked like a puddle.
ga: Nu babaoo baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo ni amɛgbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ hewɔ. Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ sponji ni ajie lɛ kpo, moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ nugbɔshiimɔ.

english: What causes the leaves on my cassava plants to curl up and get yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by a plant sickness spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Removing infected plants early and planting clean, healthy stem cuttings prevents the sickness from spreading across your farm.
ga: Tso hela ko ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra Ni odu tsei niji ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaatsi hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Weeds are wild plants built to survive tough conditions and sprout quickly. Because they steal water and food from your crops, clearing them while they are still small gives your planted crops the advantage.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni ama koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ́ otsi ohe yɛ be mli ni oji gbekɛ lolo lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ.

english: How do tiny insects get inside my dried corn cobs while they are stored in the barn?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kooloi bibii boteɔ mi-ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ mli be mli ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils often lay invisible eggs on the corn while it is still in the field. Drying your corn thoroughly before storing it and keeping your storage space clean prevents those eggs from hatching and eating your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa amɛ yɛ ŋmeii anɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa dani okɛto ni oha he ni okɛtoɔ lɛ he tse lɛ, ebaatsi nakai ŋmãa lɛ naa koni amɛkafɔ ni amɛkaye onibii ni okɛwo mli lɛ.

english: Can I actually grow enough food to feed my family if I only have a small backyard space?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛha miweku lɛ diɛŋtsɛ? Kɛji miyɛ sɛɛgbɛ he bibioo ko pɛ.

english: Yes, small backyard spaces can produce plenty of food if you plant high-yielding crops like hot peppers, garden eggs, tomatoes, or green vegetables, which take up little room and yield food repeatedly over many weeks.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛtsu bibioo ko baanyɛ aha niyenii babaoo aba kɛji odu tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo tamɔ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ, abɔɔ mli ŋmeii, tomato, loo aduawai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. Eheɔ he ko fioo pɛ ni ekɛ yibii ni anyɛɔ atĩɔ mli baa. amɛfee ekome otsii babaoo

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help them regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if the soil behind my house is good enough for growing vegetables without using expensive chemicals?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oshia lɛ sɛɛ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ni obaanyɛ odu aduawai ni okɛ tsofai ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, soft to dig, holds water well, and contains earthworms. If your soil is pale and hard, mixing in decayed leaves, kitchen scraps, or animal manure will naturally rebuild its richness.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su tsuɔ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛtsaa mli, ehiɛɔ nu jogbaŋŋ, ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egboi, niyenii ni eshwɛ, loo kooloi afɔfɔi futu mli lɛ, ebaaha ehewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing small and twisted instead of long and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow twisted when the soil is too hard or full of stones for the roots to push through easily. Building high, loose mounds of soft topsoil allows the tuber to grow deep, straight, and large.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ ni no haaa shishifãi lɛ abote mli mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni kɛlɛ ni etse ehe lɛ ni afee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa bulbs lɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ, amɛfeɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when the soil dries out completely during hot days or when they receive too much water at once. Keeping the soil consistently damp by watering regularly near the root area helps the flowers stay on.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ kwraa yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli loo kɛ́ amɛná nu babaoo shikome. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ he ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, often brought on by dry soil. Keeping the moisture balanced and mixing wood ash into the soil helps prevent these spots.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ akwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aya nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ tso sũ lɛ afutu mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔi nɛɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why are my okra plants growing very tall like trees, but giving me very few okra pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ daa tamɔ tso lɛ? Shi ha okra pods fioo ko pɛ?

english: Okra grows overly tall with few pods if it gets too much shade or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Okra needs direct sunlight for most of the day and balanced nutrients to produce heavy yields.
ga: Okra baakwɛ̃ tsɔ kɛ ŋmeii fioo komɛi kɛji enine shɛ hulutsoo be babaoo loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Okra he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei babaoo mli, kɛ niyenii ni sa koni enyɛ ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Leaf curling in cassava is caused by the cassava mosaic virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. You can prevent this by obtaining virus-resistant cassava cuttings from your local agricultural extension officer.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ baa ŋmei baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni nyɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ni ooobi kɛjɛ okwaayeli he nitsumɔhe ni kwɛɔ okwaayeli nɔ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same garden alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ abɔɔ kome mli yɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, they naturally feed the soil and make your maize grow healthier without buying extra fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛbaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛha o-ŋmã lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: How can I protect my harvested maize from insects without spraying harmful chemicals on food my family will eat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ahe ni mikɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui shwieee niyenii ni miweku lɛ baaye lɛ nɔ?

english: You can protect your harvested maize by drying the grains in the sun until they are completely hard, then storing them in airtight bags or mixing them with clean, dry wood ash or neem leaf powder.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu o-abele ni okpa lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni oooha amɛgbi kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa lɛ nɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli loo okɛ tso sũ ni he tse ni egbi loo neem baa powda afutu mli.

english: Yes, crops growing close together compete for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. If you plant them with proper spacing, both crops can share the land successfully, but crowding them will reduce the yield of both crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei henɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ baanyɛ aja he ko yɛ omanyeyeli mli. Shi kɛji akɛ abɔ he lɛ, tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ yibii lɛ baa shi.

english: If I plant my seeds very close to each other so I can fit more plants on my farm, will I get a bigger harvest?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni manyɛ makwɛ tsei babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli hu? Ani maná nitsumɔ babaoo?

english: No, planting seeds too close together forces the crops to fight for soil food and space. This results in weak, thin plants with small harvests. Giving crops enough distance allows each plant to grow big and produce well.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa kɛ ŋmaa fioo ko baa. Kɛ́ aha gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso fɛɛ tso adara ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is starving for nitrogen in the soil or getting too much water, which prevents the roots from taking up nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ onibii lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting cassava on the exact same plot of land every single year make my harvest smaller each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop on the same spot repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving the ground time to recover, causing the soil to become weak and unfertile.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ. Ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, sũ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ewooo yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and drop leaves when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛbaai lɛ fiteɔ beni mijieɔ tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need partial shade from larger plants or shade trees to protect their foliage and keep the nearby soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo hulutsoo tsei amli koni amɛbu amɛbaa lɛ he ni amɛha shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How can I tell if heavy rain is harming my crops instead of helping them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ miifite miŋmɔshi nibii moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua amɛ?

english: When crops get soaked with too much standing water, their roots drown from lack of air. This causes the leaves to turn yellow, droop, and the whole plant to stop growing.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ Tse lɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛshwieɔ shi, ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kpaɔ dalɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and make my main crop stop growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni ehaa mitso titri lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds naturally consume water and soil food much faster than farm crops. If left unchecked, weeds drink up all the fertilizer and water before your main crop can reach it.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, jwɛi yeɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ baanu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu lɛ fɛɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ abashɛ.

english: Why should I cut off extra stems from my tomato plants when I want more fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ tomato tsei amli lɛ mli be mli ni miitao aduawai babaoo lɛ?

english: Cutting away unnecessary side shoots helps the plant direct all its food and energy into producing bigger, healthier tomatoes instead of spending energy on extra leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ tsei ni he ehiaaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ eniyenii kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ gbɛ koni ekɛwo tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress from excessive heat, lack of moisture, or too much nitrogen, which causes the plant to focus on leaf growth instead of fruiting.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fa babaoo, ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai ni amɛbaawo lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings look weak and almost dead for a few days right after I move them into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni eshwɛ fioo ni amɛbaagbo yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni mikɛ amɛ wo saatso wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is transplant shock. When seedlings are moved, their delicate roots get disturbed and need a few days in moist soil to settle in before they can start absorbing water normally again.
ga: Enɛ ji tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Be ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui Amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ mli ewo wu ni ehe hiaa ni amɛhi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ gbii fioo komɛi koni amɛhi shi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ nu bɔ ni sa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn brown and dry up during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry winds and direct intense sunlight strip moisture from cocoa leaves faster than roots can absorb it. Shade trees or plantain plants help break the dry wind and trap air humidity, protecting the cocoa leaves from drying out.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Tsei ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ loo plantains yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛtsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ naa ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ. Ebuɔ kookoo baai ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: What causes tiny holes in my maize leaves with stuff that looks like sawdust inside the stem?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-abɛi lɛ amli ŋmeii bibii lɛ miifee? Ni nɔ ko yɛ ni tamɔ ŋmei yɛ tso lɛ shishi?

english: This is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the plant's growing center. Early spraying with recommended organic or chemical insecticides kills the caterpillars before they destroy the whole plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni naa niyenii yɛ tso lɛ mli he ni edaa lɛ. Akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra. Egbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfiteɔ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my pepper and tomato flowers keep falling off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers fall when plants get stressed by severe heat, irregular watering, or a lack of specific soil nutrients like calcium and boron. Keeping the soil consistently moist and feeding the soil early helps flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium kɛ boron. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni oooha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii mra Enɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen or that excessive water is choking the roots. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea helps the plant regain its dark green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu babaoo miitsi shishifãi lɛ anaa. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa su ni mli kwɔ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: When is the right time for me to apply the first fertilizer to my maize farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-abele ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best time for the first fertilizer application is about 7 to 14 days after the seeds germinate, when young roots are strong enough to take in nutrients for early stem and leaf growth.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii klɛŋklɛŋ ji aaafee gbii 7 kɛyashi 14 beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji be mli ni shishifãi bibii lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ yɛ shishijee mli.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas out of the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. When harvested, they leave behind enriched soil that feeds the next crop like maize or cassava naturally.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Be ni esa akɛ akpa Amɛshiɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii koni akɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha sɛɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Why should I plant cassava or plantain next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo plantain yɛ cacao tso bibioo ko masɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing food crops like plantains provide broad leaf shade and cool soil conditions that protect young cocoa during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Niyenii tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ. Enɛ buɔ kookoo bibii ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to stay small even if it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibioo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal soil nutrients, sunlight, and space directly from your main crop. Clearing weeds early in the first month ensures your crop gets all the rainwater and food available in the ground.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, hulu la, kɛ he ko kɛjɛɔ tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa onibii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off small extra branches and shoots from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli?

english: Cutting off unproductive shoots (chupons) allows air and sunlight to pass freely through the tree canopy. This prevents fungal pod diseases like Black Pod and forces the tree to direct energy into growing large pods.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii ni wooo yibii (chupons) lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ tso lɛ shishi oya. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ anaa, ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ hewalɛ yaa ŋmeii agboi ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the soil cool under hot weather, reduces water evaporation, and stops weeds from popping up around your crops.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi ni otsi jwɛi ni shwereɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ naa.

english: Can I use the same fertilizer I put around my cocoa trees for my rice field?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ kookoo tsei ahe lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii kɛha mi ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Yes, many common fertilizers can nourish both cocoa and rice, but they require different amounts and timing. Applying fertilizer near the root zone helps rice grow strong just as it does for cocoa trees, provided it is applied in the right quantity.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo kɛ ŋmãa fɛɛ aná hewalɛ. Shi yibɔi kɛ bei srɔtoi he miihia. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo he ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ, taakɛ eji yɛ kookoo tso lɛ hu he kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli bɔ ni sa lɛ.

english: Will putting fertilizer near the roots of my young plants burn or damage them?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaawo midumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ baashã loo ebaafite amɛ?

english: Fertilizer will not harm your plants if applied correctly. Placing it a few centimeters away from the main stem allows the roots to absorb the nutrients safely without scorching the plant.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ eyeee tsei awui kɛ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛto tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe sɛntimita fioo ko pɛ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ shweshweeshwe ni eshãŋ tso lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is suitable for growing rice?
ga: Te wɔɔfee tɛŋŋ wɔle kɛji wɔshikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmãa loo esaaa?

english: Rice prefers soils that retain water well, such as clay or lowland valley soils. If your land holds moisture during the rainy season without draining away too quickly, it is likely good for rice.
ga: Omɔ sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ yɔɔ nɔ loo jɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli ni nu shwieee nɔ oya tsɔ. Etamɔ nɔ ni ehe baaba sɛɛnamɔ kɛha ŋmãa.

english: How long after applying fertilizer should I expect to see my crops respond?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baatsu nii beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Within one to two weeks after application, you should notice crop leaves turning a deeper green color and the plants producing new shoots and foliage.
ga: Yɛ otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ mli beni akɛtsu nii sɛɛ Obaana akɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa. ni tso lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai heei.

english: Where do the new high-yielding rice seeds come from, and are they safe to plant?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni ŋmãa dumɔwui heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ jɛɔ? Ni ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu?

english: Improved seeds are developed by agricultural researchers and certified seed producers to resist local pests and dry spells. They are thoroughly tested before release and are safe for your farm.
ga: Okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi kɛ dumɔwui ahe nitsulɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ ji mɛi ni fee dumɔwui ni atsake lɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ. Akwɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani ajie lɛ kpo ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why do crops like rice need direct sunlight while crops like cocoa prefer shade when young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei tamɔ ŋmãa he hiaa hulu la tɛ̃ɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei tamɔ kookoo sumɔɔ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛdarako lɛ.

english: Different plants have different sunlight requirements. Rice needs full, direct sunlight to fuel grain development, whereas young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily in strong direct heat.
ga: Tso fɛɛ tso yɛ hulu la he hiamɔ nii sɔrɔtoi. Omɔ he hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekanya dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Do I need to be an experienced farmer to try growing new crop varieties on my land?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mafee okwaafonyo ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ dani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, any passionate farmer can try new varieties. You can start on a small plot of land to learn how the crop behaves before planting it across your entire farm.
ga: Dabi, okwaafoi ni yɔɔ miishɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aka ŋmeii heei amɛkwɛ. Obaanyɛ oje shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Koni okase bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa dani odu amɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What is the purpose of visiting a community demonstration farm?
ga: Mɛni ji yiŋtoo ni yɔɔ akutso lɛ mli nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ŋmɔ lɛ saramɔ sɛɛ?

english: Demonstration plots allow you to observe how new crop varieties and planting methods perform under local soil and weather conditions before spending money on inputs for your own farm.
ga: Demo plots haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi kɛ bɔ ni aduɔ amɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ashishi. Dani obaafite shika yɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ bo diɛŋtsɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe

english: If I see a new farming method on television, how should I test it on my farm?
ga: Kɛji mina okwaayeli gbɛ hee ko yɛ tɛlivishiŋ nɔ Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Always test television advice on a tiny portion of your farm first. This allows you to see if the technique works with your local soil type and water availability without risking your main harvest.
ga: Kaa TV he ŋaawoi lɛ okwɛ yɛ fãi bibii amli. of oŋmɔ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be klɛŋklɛŋ Enɛ haa onyɛɔ onaa kɛji ŋaa gbɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛha shikpɔŋ henɔi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kɛ nu ni yɔɔ. ni ekɛ ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ wooo oshara mli

english: Can smallholder farmers participate in trials organized by extension officers?
ga: Ani okwaafoi bibii baanyɛ amɛkɛ amɛhe awo kaai ni mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ toɔ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ amli?

english: Yes, extension officers encourage active participation from local farmers because your daily feedback and field observations help determine which crops grow best in the community.
ga: Hɛɛ, mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe awo mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji akɛ, odaa gbi hetoo kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni okwɛɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ona ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ akutso lɛ mli.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings dying in the full sun while my older trees are doing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ hulu lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mi cacao tsei lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate like babies and cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a living umbrella, protecting them until their roots are strong enough.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ waaa tamɔ abifabii ni amɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛ kpɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Buu tso lɛ he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: How can I tell if my maize crops are hungry and need fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye mi-ŋmã lɛ ni ehe miihia ni awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nii?

english: When maize plants lack nutrients, their lower leaves start turning yellow from the tip down the center line. This shows the plant is starving and pulling energy from its lower leaves to feed the younger growth at the top.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛyashi amɛteŋgbɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ miijɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha gbekɛbii ni daraa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know if my land is too tired to grow crops for another season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ tsɔ akɛ manyɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii be kroko?

english: Tired soil produces slow-growing, thin crops with light green or yellow leaves even with good rains. If wild, stubborn weeds like spear grass take over easily, the soil is exhausted and needs organic manure or a rest period.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ haa tsei lɛ daa blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo. Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po. Kɛji akɛ koo mli jwɛi ni wa tamɔ spear jwɛi lɛ ye nɔ oya lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafite ni ehe baahia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo hejɔɔmɔ be aba.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize in the exact same mound to save space?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋtayaa kome mli koni he akafite?

english: Planting cassava and maize in the same hole makes them compete directly for water, light, and soil nutrients. Spacing them properly allows the maize to grow high without choking the cassava roots below.
ga: Kasava kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nu, la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa lɛ he lɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ daa ni ekɛ ŋmãa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ shwieee shi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and yellow even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing, aggressive roots that steal water and soil food before your crops can reach them. They also block sunlight, making your crops weak and nutrient-starved.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa. Enɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Etsiɔ hulu la hu naa. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnáaa niyenii kpakpa.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up tightly during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense trick. By rolling its leaves up, the tomato plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun, helping it hold onto water and avoid drying out.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli ŋaa ni buɔ mɔ he. Kɛ́ okɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaaha tomato tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛmuɔ nu ni ehaaa amɛgbi.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by intense heat, lack of water, or low soil nutrients. The plant drops flowers to conserve its energy to survive rather than trying to feed growing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo sũ mli niyenii ni faaa lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha aduawai ni miida lɛ niyenii

english: Why do some of my seed yams rot in the soil before they even sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ po lɛ?

english: Yam seeds rot when planted in heavy, waterlogged soil without proper drainage, or when bruised seed pieces are attacked by soil fungi before they can grow protective skin and roots.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Aloo kɛ́ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutua dumɔwui lɛ fãi ni efite lɛ dani amɛdara koni amɛbu hewolo lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my cassava roots staying thin and woody instead of getting fat with starch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ starch lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need soft, loose soil to swell up easily. If the soil is hard or compacted, the roots cannot expand and will turn tough and thin instead of producing thick, starchy tubers.
ga: Kassava shishifãi taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni efuu oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo ebɔle ehe Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã ni ebaafee nɔ ni wa ni eyɛ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmei ni mli tse ni tamɔ powder.

english: Why is my old cocoa tree producing far fewer pods than it did a few years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei momo lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo kwraa fe afii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees grow older, they develop overgrown, crowded branches that block sunlight and feed unnecessary wood. Pruning off old branches allows sunlight in and directs the tree's energy back into growing flowers and pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ da lɛ, Niji lɛ baanyɛ adara fe nine ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni no tsiɔ hulu la naa ni ehaa tsei niyenii ni he ehiaaa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji momo lɛ koni hulu la lɛ abote mli ni okɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aya fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli.

english: I want to try growing cassava for the first time on my land, but how do I know if my soil is good enough for it?
ga: Miisumɔ ni maka ŋmei dumɔ makwɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha lɛ?

english: Cassava is very resilient, but it grows best in loose, sandy-loam soil where water drains easily. If your land stays waterlogged after heavy rains, the cassava roots will rot underground before they can mature.
ga: Cassava lɛ nyɛɔ etsakeɔ ehe waa. Shi edaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ nu eyi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ. Cassava shishifãi lɛ baagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛdara.

english: I am thinking of switching from growing maize to growing pepper, but is it safe to clear my entire farm and start this new crop all at once?
ga: Mimiisusu tsakemɔ ni mafee kɛjɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli kɛya ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli lɛ he. Shi ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ majie miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ ni mabɔi tsei heei fɛɛ dumɔ shikome?

english: It is safer to start small by testing pepper on a small portion of your farm first while keeping some maize. This lets you observe how pepper behaves in your soil and learn its care without risking your entire seasonal income.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooobɔi bibioo, ni oka ŋmɔtɔ lɛ okwɛ yɛ he ko bibioo. yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ ni obua ŋmãa ko naa. Enɛ haa okwɛɔ bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni okaseɔ bɔ ni ooofee okwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ shika ni onáa yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ wooo oshara mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil, or the roots are drowning in too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps them turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo shishifãi lɛ ebote nu mli tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: I noticed small white insects and tiny eggs under my tomato leaves, so why are the leaves curling up?
ga: Miyɔse kooloi bibii yɛŋ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi-tomato lɛ baai lɛ ashishi. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ baai lɛ miihoso lɛ?

english: Those tiny white insects are whiteflies that suck plant sap and spread viral diseases. The leaf curling is the plant's reaction to the virus and damage caused by the insects feeding on them.
ga: small white insect Nomɛi ji ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ amɛshwãa. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji bɔ ni tso lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa yɛ muawai kɛ fitemɔ ni koolooi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ he.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience stress from prolonged dry spells, poor soil nutrients, or lack of shade. Providing moderate shade trees and keeping soil moist helps flowers stay on the branches and turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ mli. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo hulutsoo ni bɛ hulutsoo ni sa ni akɛhaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do people tell me not to plant my maize seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko miikɛɛ mi akɛ mikadu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough room and food to produce large, heavy ears.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛtoi wuji ni tsii baakwɛ̃.

english: How do I know if my crop failed because I planted the seeds too deep in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii ejaakɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ?

english: If seeds are buried too deep, they spend all their stored energy trying to reach the surface, resulting in weak, pale yellow shoots that emerge late or fail to sprout at all.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ Amɛkɛ amɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ahe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdaraa blɛoo loo amɛdaraaa kwraa.

english: I tried spraying my cabbage farm for caterpillars for the first time and it didn't work, so what could I have done wrong?
ga: Mika akɛ mikɛ tsofa baashwie mi-cabbage ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa koni mikɛgbe ŋmeii. Shi etsuuu nii. Mɛni esa akɛ mafee ni ejaaa?

english: Spraying can fail if you apply chemicals under hot afternoon sun when water evaporates quickly, use the wrong chemical dosage, or spray when caterpillars are already hidden deep inside the cabbage heads.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni ehiii kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai tsu nii yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi beni nu lɛ shwieɔ oya lɛ. Tsofai ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii Loo ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ beni ŋmeii lɛ ehiɛ amɛhe momo yɛ kaabe yitso lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over during windstorms before the fruit is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbee shi yɛ ahum ko mli dani aduawai lɛ fee klalo lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily when their root systems are damaged by tiny soil worms called nematodes or stem borers. Planting clean, healthy suckers and building up soil around the base gives the roots strong support.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ sũ mli ŋmeii bibii fite amɛshishifãi lɛ. Atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers. Aduɔ tsei ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni aduɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ afee shiŋŋ.

english: If my yam tubers rot inside the soil before harvest, does it mean my land is ruined forever?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa hu? Ani enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ baafite kɛya naanɔ?

english: Yam rot is caused by fungi or bacteria in the soil or infected seed yams, not permanent destruction of your land. Rotating your field with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts for a season helps clean the soil of those diseases.
ga: Fungi loo helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ sũ mli loo sweet potato ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛ sweet potato fitemɔ baa. Jeee oshikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛkpatamɔ kɛya naanɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ajie nakai helai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die if I do not plant shade trees like plantains around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo kɛji miduuu shade tsei tamɔ plantains yɛ ehe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that get scorched by direct, intense sunlight. Shade trees act like protective covers, reducing heat stress and keeping moisture in the soil until the cocoa plants grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ ni amɛshãa amɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he. Tsɔɔmɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ shi ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baadara ni ená hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow when the plants grow too close together under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tsei lɛ shwereɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to make their own food through photosynthesis. When crops are heavily shaded or overcrowded, they cannot capture enough light energy, which causes their green leaves to lose color and turn yellow.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛfee amɛ niyenii kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. Kɛ tsei lɛ ná hulu la babaoo loo amɛhe eyi obɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ la hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa baai eŋɔli lɛ su fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How do fertilizers help my cassava plants grow bigger roots underground?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aye abua mi-cassava tsei lɛ ni amɛná shishifãi wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Fertilizers provide essential mineral nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium that act as energy boosters for crops. When the soil has these nutrients, the plant can produce extra sugar and store it in its roots, making the cassava grow larger.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasium. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hewalɛ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii nɛɛ Tsei baanyɛ afee sugar kroko ni amɛkɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Ha ŋmei lɛ afee agbo

english: Why does my land give me smaller maize harvests when I plant it on the exact same field every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil faster than nature can replace them. Without adding nutrients or rotating crops, the soil loses its energy, leaving future crops weak and low-yielding.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni adebɔɔ baanyɛ atsake amɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fataaa he. Enɛ haa wɔsɛɛ tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: What does adding dry animal manure to my farm soil actually do for my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni egbi ni mikɛfataa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Animal manure feeds the tiny beneficial living things in the soil and improves its ability to hold water. It releases steady nutrients over time, giving crops a continuous supply of energy for healthy growth.
ga: Koolooi amli ŋmɔshi nibii haa nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ niyenii, ni ehaa nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu lɛ yaa hiɛ. Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Ehaa tsei naa hewalɛ ni yaa nɔ kɛha dalɛ kpakpa.

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism crops use to save water. By curling their leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the dry air and sun, preventing moisture from escaping.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hiɛ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi kɛ hulu la baa shi lɛ baa shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaje mli.

english: Why are my bean plants dropping their flowers before any pods develop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi dani ŋmeii lɛ daa lɛ?

english: When crops experience extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of soil nutrients, they drop flowers to conserve energy and survive. The plant prioritizes its own survival over producing seeds during stressful conditions.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ ná latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi koni amɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi. Tsei kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala nɔ fe dumɔwui ni amɛwoɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli lɛ.

english: Why do I get smaller yields if I plant my tomato seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibii fioo nɔ kɛji midu tomato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When plants grow too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition leaves all the plants weak and unable to produce large fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei dara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii wuji.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa po?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal food, root space, and sunlight directly from your crops. Even with enough rain, your crops cannot get the light and soil energy they need because weeds absorb it first.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná la kɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛkɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ baaŋɔ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Why should I trim off extra side shoots from my tomato plants while they are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Trimming extra stems prevents the plant from wasting energy on growing excess leaves. Removing these shoots directs the crop's natural energy toward producing larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ shishifãi krokomɛi amli lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai krokomɛi lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie nɛkɛ suckers nɛɛ, ehaa tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ lɛ yaa nɔ ehaa tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ waa baa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for strong green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the maize regain its dark green color and grow faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua o-ŋmei lɛ ni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: If I keep planting maize on the exact same piece of land every year, why does my harvest keep reducing?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ebaa shi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up in the field. Alternating maize with crops like cowpeas, groundnuts, or beans returns nitrogen to the soil and resets its health.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ aduɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my maize stems grow thin and fall over when I plant three or four seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the seedlings fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. This overcrowding causes them to grow tall, weak, and thin, making them easy to break during heavy rain or wind.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ mɛi ni eyi amɛhe obɔ fe nine nɛɛ haa amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa amɛkuɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that easily burn under strong, direct tropical sun. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides temporary living shade and keeps the air moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be lɛ yɔɔ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kukuoo ko, ni ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa.

english: The first rain of the season often moistens only the surface soil, and a long dry spell usually follows. Planting too quickly causes seeds to sprout, but they soon dry up and die before the steady rains actually begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ pɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Shi etsɛɛɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔ lɛ tee nɔ nɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers just dry up and drop off without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgbeɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko kwraa.

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil gets too dry, or when tiny insects attack the blossoms. Keeping the soil evenly damp and providing light shade helps flowers stay healthy and develop into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tutua fɔfɔi lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni eyɛ hulutsoo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards into tight, wrinkled cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe kɛmiifee kɔɔpoi ni ebɔle amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the underside of new leaves. Protecting the plants with organic spray or recommended treatments early keeps the leaves expanding normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai heei lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ loo tsofai ni akɛtsaa amɛ mra lɛ abuɔ tsei ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa bɔ ni sa.

english: How is my cassava crop able to stay alive and green through long dry seasons when there is no rain?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli fɛɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its older leaves to save water and uses deep roots to draw moisture and nutrients stored in its underground tubers during hot dry periods, making it a very tough drought-resistant crop.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa momo lɛ shi koni ekɛbu nu he, ni ekɛ eshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛjieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni ato yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ tso ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa waa.

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes gets the leaves higher up into full sunlight and off damp soil, which prevents foliage rot. More sunlight on the leaves allows the plant to send more food down into the ground to build huge yam tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ adara yɛ hulutsoo be mli, ni ebaajie ehe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ akafite. Hulu la ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ tsuɔ niyenii babaoo kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I cut off extra small shoots coming up around my plantain stem instead of letting all of them grow together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajieɔ nɔ ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ Mi plantain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha fɛɛ afee ekome kɛda lɛ

english: When multiple sucker shoots grow around one plantain plant, they compete heavily for soil nutrients, causing all of them to produce small bunches. Keeping only one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant produces large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii babaoo dara yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo plantain jwɛi agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to build strong green leaves. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure around the roots will help the leaves turn deep green and grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni aná baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni ebɔleɔ he lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Weeds have very strong roots that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer faster than your crops can. When you apply fertilizer without weeding first, you are mostly feeding the weeds, which leaves your main crops weak and hungry.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa waa ni baanyɛ aju nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe otsei lɛ. Beni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli ni ogbeee jwɛi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ Okɛ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ nii babaoo. Enɛ haa onibii titrii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Which side of the cassava stem cutting am I supposed to push into the soil when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oofolɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ, mɛɛ fã esa akɛ okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: You must plant the cassava cutting with the small buds pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant the cutting upside down, the new shoots will struggle to grow upwards, wasting the plant's energy and giving you a very small harvest.
ga: Ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmeii bibii adu ŋmei tso lɛ. tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji odu tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ, Tsei heei baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara. Efiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekpaa nii fioo ko pɛ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close to each other, won't I harvest more cobs from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani makpa ŋmãa babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the maize plants to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks with small or empty cobs, whereas proper spacing gives each plant room to produce large, full cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ tsei bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tso lɛ tsu fɛɛ tsu woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are my harvested yams growing in twisted, strange shapes instead of straight smooth tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miida ni amɛmiitsɔ yitsei ni ja ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers twist and bend when they hit hard, stony soil or compacted clay as they push downwards. Making tall, soft earth mounds or deep loose ridges gives the developing tuber room to expand straight and smooth.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ amɛhe kɛji amɛtswa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ beni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shi lɛ. Gɔŋ kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo loo ŋshɔ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni afee lɛ baaha tuber chamber ni miiya hiɛ lɛ mli alɛɛ, etsɔ tɛ̃ɛ, ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are all the flowers on my cocoa trees falling off before turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the tree suffers from dry weather, poor soil nutrients, or attacks by small sap-sucking insects like mirids. Providing shade trees and protecting the farm from insects helps the tree keep its flowers long enough to produce pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na shihilɛi ni mli egbi. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mirids lɛ tutuaa amɛ. Kɛ́ afee ŋmɔ lɛ he shade ni abu he kɛjɛ kooloi ahe lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ hiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo ŋmeii.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus, or by extreme heat and drying out. Keeping the soil moist and controlling whiteflies early keeps the leaves open so they can feed the growing tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akudɔ mra Enɛ baaha baai lɛ agbele koni amɛye amɛbua tomato ni miida lɛ.

english: Why is my full-grown plantain tree falling over even when there is no strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ waaa moŋ?

english: Plantain trees fall over when tiny microscopic worms called nematodes or stem borer insects destroy the underground roots. Using clean planting suckers and keeping the base of the plant clean protects the roots so the tree stays firmly anchored.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ kpata shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsɔne ni mli tse tsu nii ni aha tso lɛ shishi he tse lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu shishifãi lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my seeds rot under the ground when I plant them right after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds need air in the soil just as much as they need moisture to sprout. When heavy rain leaves the soil completely soaked and flooded, oxygen cannot reach the seeds, causing them to drown and rot in the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tamɔ bɔ ni ehe hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi ni nu shwieɔ nɔ. Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa amɛshwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their green peppers on the ground before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miishwie pepper eŋɔli yɛ shikpɔŋ dani ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop young fruit when they experience stress from irregular watering or sudden weather changes from hot to cold. Watering your peppers consistently and mulching the soil surface keeps soil moisture stable so fruits stay on the branch.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii kɛji amɛna haomɔ ni jɛɔ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli kɛyaa fɛ̃i mli lɛ mli. Nu ni oooha ŋmɔtɔi lɛ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, aduawai lɛ kpɛtɛɔ tso nine lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and heat. Shade trees act as a protective blanket, cooling the soil and preventing the young plants from drying out before their roots are fully established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa diɛŋtsɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa dumɔwui lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ atswa shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do farmers in my area plant cassava and maize together on the same plot instead of separate fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ duɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ sɔrɔtoi anɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows quickly and matures in a few months, while cassava grows slowly over a year. Planting them together uses space efficiently, provides early food from maize, and leaves the cassava to take over the field after the maize is harvested.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni eshɛɔ shweremɔ he yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei daa fiofio yɛ afi kome mli lɛ. Hefatalɔi dumɔ kɛ he ko tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Niyenii ni jɛɔ ŋmãa tsei amli kɛ ŋmãa ni ashiɔ koni ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce small, weak fruits when I plant seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, their roots fight for the same soil nutrients and water, while their leaves block each other from getting sunlight. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food and light to bear large fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he lɛ. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo yibii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize requires a lot of nitrogen to grow green and strong, so when the soil lacks this nutrient, the plant pulls it from older lower leaves to support new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni ehe wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii nɛɛ Tso lɛ gbalaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli koni eye ebua dalɛ hee.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have natural beneficial bacteria in their root nodules that trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food, naturally enriching the soil for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ naa bacteria ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why shouldn't I keep planting tomatoes on the exact same patch of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every year and allows soil-borne pests and diseases that target tomatoes to build up in the ground, leading to poorer harvests over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaya nɔ ajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Yam leaves need to capture as much sunlight as possible to make food that gets stored underground in the tuber. Staking keeps leaves lifted off the damp soil, exposing them to full sun while protecting them from fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii ni ato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Staking haa anyɛɔ ajieɔ baai lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛnáa hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai hu ahe.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and droop during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a defense mechanism plants use to conserve water. By rolling up their leaves during hot hours, plants reduce leaf surface area exposed to the sun and slow down moisture loss.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Baai ni ajieɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa tso lɛ baa lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my bean plants drop their flowers without forming any pods during long dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ shwie fɔfɔii ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ko baaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When a plant experiences heat or water stress, it sheds its flowers to save energy and protect itself from dying. Without adequate water, the plant cannot afford to spend resources developing seeds and pods.
ga: Kɛ tsei kɛ dɔlɛ loo nu he haomɔ kpe Eshwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ gbele he. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ amɛkɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛfee dumɔwui kɛ ŋmeii.

english: Why do I need to prune off the extra small branches growing out from the stem of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? Tso krɛdɛɛ ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ tomato tso lɛ shishi.
