english: Extra side shoots consume nutrients and water that would otherwise go toward developing fruit. Removing them redirects the plant's energy into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Lateral shoots lɛ yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu ni baanyɛ aha aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ. Tomato ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ yaa tomato ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my maize grow much better when I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the farm first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap natural food from the air and leave it in the soil. When you plant maize there afterwards, the maize feeds on this leftover food and grows much stronger.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni eshiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ jɛmɛ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baaye niyenii ni eshwɛ nɛɛ ni ebaada waa babaoo.

english: Why do I get smaller cassava roots when I plant my stem cuttings very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmeii bibii anɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots fight each other under the ground for water and plant food. Spacing them properly gives each cassava plant enough room and soil nutrients to swell into large roots.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ tsei niyenii. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ ŋmei tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa ŋmei tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ shishifãi wuji.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars destroying the young leaves inside the heart of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ? Koni makpãtã baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ ahiɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms that hide inside the funnel of the maize plant to feed away from direct sunlight. Checking your field early in the morning allows you to spot them early before they damage the whole crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei amli koni amɛye nii yɛ he ko ni hulu la kpɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona amɛ mra. dani efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny white insects or spread when you plant cuttings from sick plants. Planting strong, disease-resistant cassava varieties stops this problem from happening.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ Akɛwoɔ loo agbɛɔ ashwãa kɛji ojie ŋmeii kɛjɛ tso ko ni hela mɔ lɛ mli. Kasava henɔi ni wa ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni naagba nɛɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do insects attack my tomato crop worse if I plant tomatoes in the same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ mli woɔ wu waa kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Pests that love tomatoes stay hidden in the soil after harvest. If you keep planting tomatoes in the same spot, you keep feeding those pests, whereas switching to a different crop like maize starves the pests and clears the land.
ga: Nibii ni gbeɔ mɔ ni sumɔɔ tomato lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu tomato yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ Obaatsa nɔ oha nakai kooloi lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi, tamɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ, ni ebaaha jɛmɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Fertilizer acts like dry food that needs water to dissolve so plant roots can drink it. Putting fertilizer on dry soil under a hot sun can burn the plant roots or cause the fertilizer to wash away into the air as vapor.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni egbi ni he hiaa nu koni etsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi loo eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli akɛ lasu.

english: Yellowing starting from the leaf tips usually means your soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the main plant food that keeps leaves green and helps the crop grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni jɛɔ tsei amli ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, prevents the sun from drying out water too quickly, and stops weeds from taking over your garden.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Buu he kɛjɛ hulu la he ni otsi nu lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya tsɔ. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye obɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Too many young shoots around one plantain tree will steal water and plant food from the main mother tree. Leaving only two or three healthy shoots ensures the main tree produces large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tso bibii babaoo ni bɔle dumɔwu kome he lɛ baaju nu ni amɛkwɛ niyenii kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi niji enyɔ loo etɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crops use to grow healthy leaves. It can also happen when the soil is too wet, preventing roots from breathing and absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ baai ni wa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛhe niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Curling leaves is a natural self-defense mechanism. The plant rolls its leaves to reduce the surface exposed to direct sunlight, which prevents moisture from evaporating too quickly during high heat.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la ni baa amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ akafo oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato blossoms falling off the plant without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when stressed by severe dry spells or high heat. When the plant senses it does not have enough water to support fruit, it drops the blossoms to save its own life.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo latsaa ni naa wa hao amɛ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ bɛ Ebaafɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ makpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when heavy rainwater collects in the soil and stays flooded without draining away. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps water drain off so the roots do not suffocate.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu afua baa ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why does my lowland rice field need standing water around the plants during early growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi ebɔle ehe lɛ? Yɛ dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ oya be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Rice plants tolerate waterlogged soil very well, but most weeds cannot grow underwater. Flooding the field acts as a natural barrier to drown out weeds while keeping the root environment cool.
ga: Omɔ tsei kpɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ. Shi jwɛi babaoo nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ nu shishi. Nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni tsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa yɛ be mli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ ahe shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why are small caterpillars chewing holes right through the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. Moths lay eggs on the leaves, and once hatched, the young caterpillars crawl into the soft funnel of the plant where leaves are tender and easy to eat.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Kplukai fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ baai anɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai bibii lɛ amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli, ni eyɛ mlɛo akɛ amɛyeɔ nii.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my young crops so much more than fully grown crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa mi tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fe mi tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young crops have shallow roots and small leaf canopies, so weeds easily steal their water, sunlight, and fertilizer. Older crops have wide leaves that shade out light, preventing new weeds from growing.
ga: Tso gbekɛ lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baa bibioo ko. Jwɛi baanyɛ aju nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya. Tsei ni edara lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulutsoo. Etsiɔ jwɛi heei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃

english: Why do my crops yield smaller fruits when I plant the seeds very close together in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight underground for the same food and water, while their leaves block sunlight from neighboring plants. Spacing gives each plant enough room to thrive.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ naa. Gbɛ ni kã tso lɛ teŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda.

english: Why is my maize harvest getting smaller every season when I keep using the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ baa shi daa be mli ni miyaa nɔ mikɛ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Planting maize on the same plot every season drains the soil of the specific nutrients maize needs. Rotating your field with beans or groundnuts puts vital nutrients back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abele lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake nibii ni odu lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why does fertilizer fail to work if I spread it when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuuu nii kɛji midu be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Roots cannot eat dry fertilizer granules. Fertilizer needs soil moisture from rain or irrigation to dissolve into liquid so that the plant's roots can soak up the dissolved nutrients.
ga: Shishifãi nyɛŋ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni jɛɔ nugbɔ loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ nu mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni etsɔ mli lɛ.

english: If I bring seed varieties from another country to plant on my farm in Ghana, will they grow well right away?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ dumɔwui jɛ maŋ kroko nɔ kɛba ni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli. Ani dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Seeds brought from outside Ghana are bred for different weather, soil, and pest conditions. Without proper testing and approval by local authorities, foreign seeds may fail to yield, fall sick easily, or introduce unknown crop diseases to your soil.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛbaa kɛjɛɔ Ghana kponɔgbɛ lɛ fɔɔ kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, shikpɔji kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai srɔtoi. Kɛji akɛ aka lɛ akwɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akutsoŋ onukpai lɛ ekpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ. Ekolɛ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui nyɛŋ awo yibii, hela baamɔ amɛ oya, loo amɛkɛ tsei ahe helai ni aleee aba oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and delicate roots that burn under full, direct sunlight. Shade trees or companion crops like plantains act like umbrellas, shielding young cocoa plants from heat while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei ni fata he tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ ambrela. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Yellow lower leaves mean your maize crop is starving for nitrogen, an essential plant food. The plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves and moves it up to keep new growth alive, showing that your soil needs fertilizer or compost.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eha tsei heei ni eda lɛ ahi shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and drop during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is the cassava plant's defense mechanism to save water. By shrinking its leaf surface area exposed to dry winds and heat, the plant reduces water loss through evaporation so it can survive until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛhaa ŋmei tsei koni amɛbu nu he. Baai lɛ anɔ he ni baa shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ dɔlɛ kpe. Tsei haa nu ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cowpea plants shed their flowers before setting any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas drop their flowers when the plant experiences heavy stress, usually caused by insect pests like flower thrips attacking the buds, or when the weather is extremely hot and dry during flowering.
ga: Cowpeas shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa kpe. Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ fɔfɔi thrips ni tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. aloo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa ni edɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very leafy and tall, but the tubers underground remain small and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni kɛlɛ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ lolo?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil forces cassava to spend all its energy growing leaves and stems instead of storing food in its roots. Hard, unplowed soil can also physically prevent roots from swelling.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuuu he nii lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafu.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce small, weak fruits when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ beni mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots struggle against each other for soil nutrients and water, while their leaves fight for sunlight. This competition leaves the plants with very little energy to grow large fruits.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la he akaŋ lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haaa tso lɛ aná hewalɛ fioo ko ni ekɛbaawo yibii wuji.

english: Why does striga weed make my maize plants look yellowish and stunted even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ striga jwɛi lɛ haa mi-abɛi tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ bɔ ni sa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Striga is a parasitic weed that attaches its roots directly to the roots of maize underground. It steals water, minerals, and plant food straight out of the maize plant before the crop can use them.
ga: Striga ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni ekɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpãa ŋmãa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ, ni ejuɔ nu, shika tsuru, kɛ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ dani ŋmãa lɛ baanyɛ ekɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout out of the ground when I bury them deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni mifuɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds contain only a limited amount of stored energy to sprout. If buried too deep, the young shoot exhausts all its food reserves pushing through the heavy soil and dies before reaching the surface light.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko ni ato kɛha amɛkwɛ̃mɔ. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni ato ni tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛshɛɔ la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do the bottoms of my developing tomato fruits turn black and rotten before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni miiya hiɛ lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This black patch, called blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot absorb enough calcium while building the fruit. It is usually caused by uneven watering, dry soil spells, or highly acidic soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ fã diŋ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade because strong direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries up soil moisture before their roots grow deep enough to survive on their own.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhi shi.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or beans on the same land where I grow my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds the corn plants.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa tsei niyenii

english: Planting cassava too close makes the roots compete for food and water under the ground, resulting in many small, thin roots instead of large tubers.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu he akaŋshii mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa yɛ bulb wuji najiaŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the soil is too dry, when temperatures get too high, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer in the ground.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why do my tomato fruits turn black and rotten at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ yɛ shishigbɛ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often due to irregular watering.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why does my stored harvested maize get full of tiny holes after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ

english: Insects called weevils lay eggs inside the grain, and their larvae eat the maize from the inside out if the grain was not dried completely before storage.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii amli. Ni amɛ ŋmeii lɛ baaye ŋmãa kɛjɛ mli kɛya kpo kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when strong rain and wind come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and heavy trunks filled with water, making them top-heavy and easy for strong winds to uproot unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tsei ni tsii ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ tso ni tsii, ni ewaaa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatse lɛ. Ja nɔ ko ni akɛ tso fee lɛ yɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow and spread much faster on my farm than the actual crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli oya fe tsei diɛŋtsɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally tough and adapt quickly to steal water, sunlight, and soil food before domesticated crops can use them.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni tsakeɔ amɛhe oya koni amɛju nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani shia tsei lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on to give a good yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni akwɔ koni ewo ŋmaa kpakpa lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to spread out high in the sunlight to produce food that travels down to make large underground tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni ekɛ niyenii ni tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi ni efee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because their delicate leaves burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them creates natural shade and keeps the soil cool and moist during the seedling's first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ebaaha adebɔɔ mli shade aba. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ dumɔwu lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yam plants need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce enough energy to grow big tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the wet ground, exposing leaves to sunlight while preventing fungal diseases caused by contact with damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la he ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni akɛkpeɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ naa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, a key plant nutrient. The plant copes by pulling remaining nitrogen out of its older bottom leaves and sending it to the new top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ mli niyenii titri ko bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Tsei tsuɔ enɛ he nii kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛkɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei amli koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara lɛ nɔ.

english: How is my cassava crop able to survive and stay green during dry spells when my other crops die?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi-cassava tso lɛ ahi shi ni ehi shi eŋɔli yɛ fɛ̃i be mli beni mitsei krokomɛi lɛ gboi lɛ?

english: Cassava plants have very deep root systems that search far below the topsoil for hidden moisture. During dry seasons, cassava can also drop some leaves to reduce water loss, allowing it to survive harsh droughts.
ga: Cassava tso lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni taoɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ abaanyɛ ajie Cassava baai hu koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa shihilɛi amli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly flooded. Extreme heat makes the pollen sterile, stopping the flower from developing into a tomato.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa lɛ nɔ kɛyaa nu afua ni baa trukaa lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ haa pollen lɛ feɔ nɔ ni bɛ fɔmɔ kotoku. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tomato.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop-specific pests multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ shii abɔ He kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ bii. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do fall armyworms cause so much damage to my maize farm so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall worms lɛ miifite mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Fall armyworms feed inside the hidden central leaf funnel of the maize plant where rain and sprays can't easily reach them. They eat continuously at night and reproduce rapidly, allowing them to destroy whole fields in days.
ga: Fall armyworms lɛ taoɔ niyenii yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ amli. ni nugbɔ kɛ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ bɛ mlɛo. Amɛyeɔ nii be fɛɛ be gbɛkɛ ni amɛfɔɔ oya. Enɛ ha amɛnyɛ amɛfite ŋmɔji muu fɛɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up in the afternoon sun even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. When midday heat causes water to evaporate from leaves faster than roots can drink it, the plant curls its leaves to expose less surface area to the sun and preserve moisture.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛha hulu la ni shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: How does adding dried poultry manure help my vegetable farm grow better than using no fertilizer?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ, ebaada jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ?

english: Poultry manure is rich in essential nutrients like nitrogen and organic matter. It improves soil structure, helps the ground hold water longer, and feeds helpful soil organisms that break down food for plant roots.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ kooloi ashishifã mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ yaa hiɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. ni amɛyeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni gbálaa niyenii kɛhaa tsei shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do the lower fronds of my young oil palm trees turn yellow and droop after heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can wash away nutrients from sandy soil and cause waterlogging around the roots, preventing them from breathing. Wet conditions also promote leaf fungal spots, which turn older lower fronds yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ ŋã sũ mli lɛ ni eha nu abɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni eha amɛmumɔ agbɔjɔ. Shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ hu haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ baaha shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in a field without any shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn under strong direct sunlight. Planting food crops like plantain alongside cocoa provides natural shade and keeps the air cool, protecting the young trees until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Niyenii nibii tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ cocoa masɛi lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔŋ mli jɔɔ. bu tsei bibii ahe Kɛyashi tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning pale yellow long before the corn is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it needs to stay green and grow. It can also happen if the roots are sitting in flooded soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or improving field drainage will restore the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii titrii ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi ni ekwɛ̃. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ eta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo oha nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaha efee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why am I seeing small holes in my maize leaves and caterpillars hiding inside the shoot of the crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. The young caterpillars feed on the growing shoot of the maize plant, which can stunt its growth or stop it from producing ears if you do not treat it early with approved pest controls.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ. Kplukai bibii yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ amɛdalɛ naa loo eha amɛtoi lɛ akadara. Kɛji otsaaa lɛ mra lɛ, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ

english: What causes my cassava roots to turn soft and rot underground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa?

english: Cassava root rot happens when water stays trapped around the roots in heavy or poorly drained soil, especially during heavy rains. The lack of air in soggy soil allows fungal diseases to develop and destroy the tubers beneath the ground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu tsɔ ehe. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli Kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii helai baa ni amɛfiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Yes, staking yam vines lifts the leaves off the wet ground so they can catch direct sunlight to produce food for the tubers. Leaves left on the damp ground easily catch fungal diseases and rot, resulting in much smaller yams.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, sweet potato wain tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha bulb lɛ. Baai ni ashiɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yeɔ amɛ oya. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii kwraa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without turning into actual tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot, when the plant doesn't get enough water, or when you apply too much nitrogen fertilizer. Maintaining steady watering during flowering helps the tree set fruit successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo be mli ni okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fataa he. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and turning wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the plant juice, or by viruses spread by these insects. Controlling these pests early helps keep the new leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Kudɔmɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai heei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but not during heavy downpours. The best time is early in the morning or late afternoon a day after light rain, making sure to place it near the crop roots and cover it lightly with soil.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli beni nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ. Esa akɛ akɛma tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni akɛ sũ fioo aha nɔ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil empties specific soil nutrients and lets pests and soil diseases build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpea or groundnuts puts natural nitrogen back into the soil and breaks the cycle of pests.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni efo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe sɛɛkuu lɛ mli

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and thicker than my planted crops after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have tough, deep root systems and seeds already buried in the soil ready to burst open with the first rain. Because weeds naturally absorb water and plant nutrients faster than crops, early clearing is needed so your crops do not starve.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa kɛ dumɔwui ni afu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli momo, ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaatse kɛji nugbɔ nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii oya fe tsei. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ajie mli mra. koni hɔmɔ akaye onibii lɛ

english: How do I know if my cocoa pods are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: Cocoa pods change color when mature, usually turning from green or deep red to a bright yellow or orange. Harvesting them when fully ripe ensures the beans inside have developed proper sugars necessary for fermenting well.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse. Kɛ́ akpa amɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ náa sugar ni sa yɛ mli koni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens if I harvest cocoa pods while they are still green?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Green pods contain unripened beans that lack essential natural sugars. Harvesting them too early means they will not ferment or dry properly, resulting in bitter, slate-colored beans that degrade overall crop quality.
ga: Green pods lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni edako ni bɛ adebɔɔ mli sugars ni he hiaa. Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwieŋ loo amɛgbiŋ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ slate, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do some pods on the same cocoa tree ripen faster than others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi ni yɔɔ cacao tso kome nɔ lɛ daa oya fe cacao tsei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Pods flower at different times throughout the growing season and receive varying amounts of sunlight depending on where they are on the trunk or branches, causing them to reach maturity at different speeds.
ga: Pods lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ bei srɔtoi amli yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ. ni amɛnáa hulu la srɔtoi Enɛ damɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi loo tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha amɛdara yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli.

english: Why is it important to dry my cocoa beans completely before selling them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbi kookoo ŋmeii lɛ dani ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Drying removes excess water from the beans. Selling wet or partially dried beans leads to internal rot, mold growth, and a bad taste, which damages crop reputation and lowers selling prices.
ga: Kɛ́ egbi lɛ, ejieɔ nu ni fa fe nine kɛjɛɔ kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ amli. Beans ni efɔ loo ni egbi fioo lɛ ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ kɛ mligbɛ fitemɔ baa. fungal growth kɛ bad taste Enɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛi kpakpa ni ehaa jara ni akɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: What is the best way to dry cocoa beans under the sun?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbiɔ kookoo ŋmeii yɛ hulu shishi?

english: Spread the beans evenly on raised wooden mats or bamboo drying tables off the ground and turn them regularly. This allows fresh air to circulate around all beans while keeping them clean from ground dirt and pests.
ga: Gbalamɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli pɛpɛɛpɛ. Okɛto tso ni awo nɔ loo ŋmei okpɔlɔ ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ daa. Eyeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni ebɔleɔ he. kɔfi yibii muu fɛɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ koni ehe atse kɛjɛ muji kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: How long should I ferment cocoa beans under plantain leaves before drying them?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mafee kookoo ŋmeii lɛ yɛ plantain baai lɛ ashishi kɛyashi amɛbaagbi?

english: Cocoa beans usually need 5 to 7 days of heap fermentation under clean plantain leaves, turning them over on the third day. Proper fermentation develops the rich chocolate flavor and deep brown color buyers look for.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cocoa ŋmeii biɔ ni akɛ gbii 5 kɛyashi 7 awo mli yɛ plantain baai ni he tse shishi. ni akuɔ sɛɛ yɛ gbi ni ji etɛ lɛ nɔ Fɛ̃i ni sa lɛ haa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ ni mli wa kɛ su ni mli kwɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa.

english: What should I do if it starts raining while my harvested crops are drying outside?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ yɛ be mli ni mikpamɔ lɛ miiho yɛ kpo lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cover the drying crops immediately with clean, waterproof tarpaulins or move them under shelter. Re-wetting crops that have started drying encourages rapid mold growth and spoils the harvest.
ga: Oya nɔŋŋ ni okɛ tarp ni he tse aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ ahe loo okɛ amɛ aya shishi. Tsei ni ebɔi gbimɔ lɛ ni oookɛ nu awo mli ekoŋŋ lɛ baawo ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ oya ni ebaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Should I keep bad or unripened cocoa beans separate from my good ones?
ga: Ani esa akɛ magbala mi-kookoo ni ehiii loo ni eshɛko lɛ mli kɛjɛ mi-kookoo ni hi lɛ mli?

english: Yes, always separate flat, insect-damaged, or under-ripened beans from well-dried ones. Mixing poor-quality beans with good ones ruins the whole batch and can cause purchasing officers to reject your crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ ajie ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ amli. Dumɔwui ni kooloi efite Loo ŋmeii ni eshɛko lɛ jɛɔ dumɔwui ni egbi mli be fɛɛ be. Beans ni ehiii ni akɛfutuɔ dumɔwui kpakpai Ebaafite dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ ni ebaanyɛ eha nihɔɔmɔ he nitsulɔi lɛ akpoo oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested crops develop mold when stored inside sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛji akɛ akɛto kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Mold grows when crops are put into bags before moisture has fully left the beans, or when storage rooms are damp. Trapped moisture creates a hot, humid environment where fungi thrive.
ga: Fuji lɛ daa kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wo kotoku lɛ mli dani ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ eshi kɔfi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. aloo kɛ́ nitoohe lɛ mli edɔ Fɛ̃i ni amɔmɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli ni ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ adara yɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why are buyers so strict about the quality and dryness of cocoa beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ feɔ amɛnii waa yɛ bɔ ni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ hi ha kɛ bɔ ni amɛgbiɔ amɛhaa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Ghana has a global reputation for producing premium, high-grade cocoa that international chocolate makers pay top prices for. Maintaining high standards protects farmer earnings and national trade relationships.
ga: Ghana ehe gbɛi yɛ je lɛŋ fɛɛ akɛ efeɔ kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni majimaji ateŋ tsɔklatefeelɔi woɔ jara waa. Teŋgbɛ nibii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ okwaafoi anibii ni amɛnáa kɛ maŋ lɛ jarayeli wekukpaai ahe.

english: Why does my rice field need standing water when crops like maize will die if water sits on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ he hiaa nu ni damɔ shi yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa baagboi kɛji nu ni damɔ shi yɛ lɛ?

english: Rice has special hollow tubes in its stems and roots that allow air to travel down from the leaves underwater. Maize lacks these tubes and smothers in wet soil. Standing water also acts as a natural weed barrier for rice.
ga: Omɔ yɛ tsɔnei krɛdɛɛi ni mli ewo muji yɛ eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi amli ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa nu shishi. Abele bɛ nɛkɛ tsɔnei nɛɛ kɛ muji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ hu tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli jwɛi gbɛtsii nii kɛhaa ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why are my rice stalks falling flat onto the ground right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei shwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani akpaa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: This is called lodging. It happens when the stalks are too weak to hold up heavy grain heads, usually caused by applying too much fertilizer, planting seeds too close together, or heavy rain and wind.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ wɔɔhe. Ebaa beni tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua dumɔwu yitso ni tsii lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa

english: Why is it better to plant my crops in straight rows rather than scattering seeds freely by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni akɛ niji baagbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Row planting gives every plant equal space to catch sunlight and absorb soil nutrients. It also leaves clear pathways for you to remove weeds, apply fertilizer, and harvest without damaging the crops.
ga: Tso ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ koni ená hulu la ni ekɛjie niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa gbɛ hu haa onyɛɔ okɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli, ni okpaa nibii ni okɛfiteee onibii lɛ.

english: Why should I avoid planting rice on the exact same piece of land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be mli lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows soil-borne pests and diseases that target rice to build up to dangerous levels.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tsɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni yɔɔ oshara.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young rice plants turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the crop lacks nitrogen. The plant naturally moves available nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to feed the fresh, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛha baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the leaves of my crop curl up tight during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a survival trick. By curling its leaves inward, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to direct sunlight, which traps moisture and keeps the plant from drying out.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaa. Tsei haa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai ni amɛfoɔ mli kɛyaa mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ tso lɛ mli ni ehaaa tso lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my rice grains break into tiny bits during milling, making buyers offer me low prices?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli fãa bibii bibii yɛ be mli ni mikɛ mihe woɔ mli lɛ, ni no haa mɛi ni heɔ lɛ haa mi jara ni baa shi lɛ?

english: Rice grains crack easily if left in the field too long to over-dry before harvest, or if dried too rapidly under intense heat after harvesting. Harvesting at the right grain moisture prevents breakage.
ga: Omɔ ŋmeii lɛ fãa oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni amɛgbiɔ tsɔ dani akpaa. aloo kɛji egbi oya tsɔ yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa shishi yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ Nikpamɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni mli edɔ ni sa yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anaa.

english: Your rice is ready when about 80 to 85 percent of the seed heads turn from green to a golden-yellow color, and the grains at the base of the head feel hard when bitten.
ga: O-rice lɛ efee klalo beni dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ mli lɛ. Ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ yitso lɛ shishi lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛhe wa kɛ́ akɔmɔ amɛ.

english: Why do swarms of insects attack my crop right when the flowers begin to open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ bɔi fɔmɔ pɛ?

english: Young developing grains contain a soft, sweet, milky liquid right after flowering. Insects target the field at this time because that liquid is an easy and nutritious food source for them.
ga: Dumɔwui ni miida lɛ feɔ nu ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni ŋɔɔ, tamɔ mliki kɛji amɛwo fɔfɔi amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kplukai kɛ amɛhiɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli ejaakɛ nu lɛ ji niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni haa amɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do some of my rice heads turn completely white and dry up without producing any grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa yitsei komɛi efee futafuta kwraa ni egbi ni dumɔwui ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: White heads are typically caused by stem borer insects. The worm-like larvae burrow inside the stalk and chew through the plant's food pipes, stopping nutrients from reaching the grain head.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni boteɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ yitsei yɛŋ baa. Lalabii ni tamɔ ŋmei lɛ boteɔ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛyeɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ niyenii paipii lɛ amli. Enɛ haaa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ayashɛ dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know the right distance to leave between my maize plants when sowing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni sa ni kã ŋmãa tsei ateŋ kɛ́ midu nii?

english: Spacing gives each crop enough room to stretch its roots and feed on nutrients without fighting neighboring plants. For maize, leaving about 75 centimeters between rows and 40 centimeters between plants ensures high yield and big cobs.
ga: He ni akɛtoɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛgbala eshishifãi lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ awuu. kɛha ŋmãa He ni yɔɔ ŋmãa teŋ aaafee sɛntimitai 75 kɛ tsei ateŋ aaafee sɛntimitai 40 koni anyɛ ana ŋmãa babaoo kɛ ŋmãa wuji.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I plow and clear the land before the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikpa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Plowing loosens hard soil so plant roots can grow deep and absorb rainwater easily. Preparing the ground before the rains start gives seeds a soft, moist bed to sprout quickly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei shishifãi baanyɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe nugbɔ nu lɛ oya. Shikpɔŋ ni asaa dani nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why should I leave a portion of my farmland to rest without planting anything for a season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ fã ko koni mihe ajɔɔ mi ni miduuu nɔ ko yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Leaving land fallow allows the soil to rest, recover lost nutrients, and regain its natural fertility. Just like a person needs sleep to regain strength, soil needs rest to produce healthy crops again.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii ni elaaje lɛ ekoŋŋ. ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii babaoo aba ekoŋŋ Taakɛ bɔ ni ehe hiaa ni gbɔmɛi awɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ hu he miihia ni ejɔɔ ehe koni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: If I divide my farm into two plots, why should I switch which crop I grow on each plot next year?
ga: Kɛji mijara ŋmɔ lɛ mli miwo shikpɔji enyɔ Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔji lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Rotating crops prevents pests and diseases that prefer specific plants from building up in the soil. It also stops the soil from losing all of one particular nutrient.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai komɛi ni sumɔɔ tsei lɛ akabua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii kome ko kwraa shwieɔ shi kwraa.

english: If I plant cassava on part of my land, can I plant cowpeas in the remaining space between them?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ani manyɛ madu tsina ŋmei yɛ he ni eshwɛ yɛ amɛteŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, planting legumes like cowpeas with cassava is a great practice called intercropping. Cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and add it to the soil, which helps feed the cassava plants while maximizing your land.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa ni ale lɛ akɛ intercropping. Cowpeas mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni akwɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ anɔ kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni eha he ni eyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo.

english: Why do agricultural officers recommend planting plantains or shade trees inside a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji heei amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa trees and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my main crops after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are naturally aggressive at taking up water and nutrients from the soil. Removing them early prevents them from stealing food and sunlight from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni he wa ni feɔ basabasa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛmuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛ ni ooojie mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen, or it is suffering from water stress or pests. Adding compost or manure can help restore its health and green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu mli haomɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ miipiŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ená hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ baai kɛji edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses pepper plants, causing them to drop flowers to save water and stay alive. Mulching the soil around the base and watering early in the morning helps keep the soil cool.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ nyɛɔ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ wo shishigbɛ lɛ he, ni akɛ nu wo mli leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: How can I tell if my yam tubers in the ground are fully mature and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: When yams are fully mature, the green leaves and vines dry up and turn yellow naturally. This shows that the plant has stopped growing leaves and stored all its energy into the tuber below.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ, baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kpaɔ ebaa lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ toɔ bulb ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and getting scorched in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because intense direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the topsoil. Planting plantains alongside young cocoa provides shade and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ. Kɛ́ adu plantains yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why are my corn leaves turning pale yellow from the leaf tips inwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛjɛ mligbɛ ŋwɛigbɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip often indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Applying manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy green leaves so the corn can produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba. koni ŋmãa anyɛ awo ŋmãa wuji

english: What makes my cassava roots rot under the soil before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long in heavy or flat soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away, protecting the roots from rotting.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ Ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite

english: Why do my yam vines need long sticks to climb on instead of just spreading on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ kɛ tsei kakadaji tsuɔ nii kɛkwɔɔ ŋwɛi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up to catch maximum sunlight, which the plant uses to make food. When the leaves get enough light, the plant can direct energy down into growing larger, healthier tubers.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo nɔ, ni tso lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii kɛhooɔ nii. Kɛji baai lɛ ná la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛkudɔɔ amɛhewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa shi koni amɛtsɔmɔ bulbs ni dara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Should I cut away the small shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ he Ani ajie mi plantain shishifãi lɛ?

english: Leaving too many side shoots causes them to steal nutrients and water from the main plant. Keeping only two or three healthy shoots ensures the main plantain tree produces a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi sɛɛ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛju niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwu titri lɛ afee niji agboi ni tsii.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in the middle whorl leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yeɔ bu bibioo ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei gbekɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Holes inside the center of maize leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworms. Checking the plants early and applying approved organic or chemical treatments into the leaf whorls stops them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ tsei lɛ amli mra. ni okɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ awo baai lɛ ahe. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants experience extreme heat or lack of steady water. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting during cooler windows helps the flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu yɛ samflɛ ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Growing maize in the same spot repeatedly drains specific soil nutrients and lets soil pests build up. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas returns nitrogen to the soil naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. ni aŋmɛ gbɛ ni kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ abua amɛhe naa Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Upward curling on pepper leaves is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids. Controlling these insects early prevents leaf damage and keeps the plant producing healthy peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ afitemɔ naa ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds slow down my crops even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, soil nutrients, and root space. Clearing weeds during the first few weeks after planting gives your crops all the resources they need to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli Kɛ́ okwɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya.

english: Officer, why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and drying when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When sunlight and heat get too intense, crops lose water faster than their roots can draw it from the soil. Curling their leaves is the plant's natural defense to reduce water loss and protect itself from sunburn.
ga: Beni hulu lɛ kɛ latsaa lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe koni ekɛba nu ni efiteɔ lɛ shi ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into fruit during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Very high heat stresses the crop and prevents proper pollination. When temperatures get too high, tomato plants will drop their flowers to save energy for basic survival instead of producing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni etsĩɔ pollination ni sa naa. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha shishijee wala moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my maize plants look weak and wilted during the afternoon heat even when the soil has some moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: Strong sun heat causes water to evaporate through the leaves faster than roots can replace it. This temporarily makes the plant lose firmness during the hottest parts of the day, but they usually recover by evening when temperatures drop.
ga: The intense heat from the sun causes water to evaporate through the leaves faster than the roots can replace it. This causes the plant to temporarily lose its stability during the hottest part of the day. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehiɛɔ shi gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Can excessive sun heat cause the edges of my young cassava leaves to dry up and turn brown?
ga: Ani hulu ni tsoɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha mi-cassava baai lɛ ashishigbɛ agbi ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Yes, intense heat combined with strong sunlight can scorch leaf tissue, especially around the edges where water leaves the plant fastest, causing them to look burnt.
ga: Yes, extreme heat combined with bright sunlight can scorch leaf tissue. Especially around the edges where water leaves the plant fastest. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baa shãa

english: Officer, why are my garden egg plants producing much smaller fruits now than when I first started harvesting them?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kwraa fe be mli ni mibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: As crops get older and time passes, their internal organs become less efficient at absorbing nutrients, and the soil energy decreases, leading to smaller fruit sizes late in their lifecycle.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ daraa kɛ be ni hoɔ lɛ Amɛmli gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli. ni hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ feɔ bibii yɛ wala be lɛ naagbee gbɛ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my cowpea plants turn yellow and drop off as the plant gets older?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cowpea tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi beni tso lɛ miida lɛ?

english: This is a natural part of crop aging. As time passes, the plant shifts its energy and nutrients away from older bottom leaves toward the newer leaves, flowers, and developing seed pods.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni haa tsei lɛ daa. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Tsei jieɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa baai heei ni miiya hiɛ, fɔfɔii, kɛ ŋmeii amli.

english: Why has my old cocoa farm stopped giving me as many pods as it produced ten years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ momo lɛ kpa kookoo ŋmeii babaoo ni efee afii nyɔŋma ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees have a peak age for production. As a lot of time passes, older trees naturally produce fewer pods as their stems and root systems grow tired and less active.
ga: Cocoa tsei ji tsei ni yeɔ wala be babaoo fe fɛɛ. As time passes Older trees naturally produce fewer pods. This is because their trunks and root systems become tired and less active.

english: Officer, what kinds of things can cause my yam leaves to suddenly turn pale green instead of dark green?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni miiha mi sweet potato baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ?

english: Multiple factors can cause leaf pale greening, including high sun heat, lack of plant nutrients in the soil, poor drainage after heavy rains, or pest damage at the roots.
ga: Nibii babaoo baanyɛ aha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli. Nɔ ni fata he ji dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Lack of plant nutrients in the soil Poor drainage after heavy rain or pests destroy the roots

english: Why are my plantain leaves splitting into thin strips during dry and hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miigbɛ amɛmiifee woji bibii lɛ? Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi kɛ latsaa be mli

english: Plantain leaves split naturally along their veins in high heat and wind to reduce wind resistance and prevent the main stalk from snapping under environmental stress.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ baaja yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ fãji lɛ ahe kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ. koni ekɛba kɔɔyɔɔ ni nyɛɔ etswaa lɛ shi ni ekɛtsiɔ tso titri lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ yɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔ hewɔ.

english: What causes my okra plants to stay short and refuse to grow tall this season?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi okra tsei lɛ miifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkpoo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Stunted growth can be triggered by several things working together, such as poor soil nutrients, excessive heat stress early in growth, or hard soil that prevents root extension.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii, tamɔ sũ mli niyenii ni ehiii lɛ baanyɛ aha dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. Dɔlɛ ni fe nine yɛ be mli ni edaa mra loo shikpɔŋ ni wa ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ asɛɛgbɛ

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize plants curl up tightly like pencils during the mid-day sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ pensil yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll inward as a natural protective reaction to extreme heat and sunlight. By curling up, the leaf reduces its exposed surface area, which slows down water loss through evaporation and helps the plant survive dry afternoon hours.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa he. Curling haa baa lɛ hiɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and fall off when the hot Harmattan wind starts blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ je shishi etswa lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan wind sucks moisture out of leaves faster than cocoa roots can pull water from the soil. The cocoa tree responds to this extreme heat stress by dropping leaves to protect its trunk and main branches from drying out completely.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni kookoo shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Cacao tsei tsuɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa he nii kɛtsɔ amɛbaai ni amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛbu amɛshishifã lɛ kɛ amɛniji titrii lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi kwraa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds seem to sprout and grow much faster than my crops right after the first rain comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ eba lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds naturally lie dormant in dry soil and are built to wake up and absorb the very first drops of rain instantly. Because they are wild plants, they use soil nutrients quickly to outpace planted crops in the race for sunshine.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui sumɔɔ ni amɛka shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni afee amɛ koni amɛte shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛmu nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ. Akɛni amɛji koo mli tsei hewɔ lɛ No hewɔ lɛ amɛkɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii oya koni amɛye tsei ni miida yɛ hulu la he akaŋshii mli lɛ anɔ kunim.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over by itself just when the bunch of fruits is getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ? Ni aduawai lɛ miije shishi amɛmiifee agbo?

english: Plantain stems are made of soft layers, and their roots grow near the surface of the soil. As the fruit bunch grows heavy, it pulls the plant's weight forward, so without wooden stakes to support the stem, the roots easily pull out of the ground.
ga: Akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo fee plantain tsei lɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daa ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji aduawai akuu lɛ tsii Ebaagbala tso lɛ tsiimɔ kɛya hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji tso ko bɛ ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baaje shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya.

english: Why do I need to put long sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei kakadaji lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need plenty of sunlight on their leaves to make food. Climbing up high on tall stakes keeps the leaves exposed to light and away from shade and moisture on the ground, which builds larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛhoo nii. Tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni akwɔɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa la ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he. Enɛ haa tuber agbo ko baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my tomato plants develop dark spots and dry up after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain hits bare ground, it splashes mud containing microscopic fungus spores onto the lowest leaves. The warm moisture on those leaves allows the fungus to grow quickly, causing leaf spots and blight.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ ni naa wa nɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Ebaashɛrɛ muji ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ ashwie baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ. Fɛ̃i ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ nakai baai lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei lɛ ni edaa oya. Ekɛ baa mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do people say that planting cowpeas or beans makes the ground richer for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have special microbes living in their roots that pull nitrogen gas out of the air and turn it into natural soil food. When the crop finishes growing, that leftover nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the next crop of maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ nibii bibii krɛdɛɛi ni hiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa efeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tso lɛ egbe naa lɛ Nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground if I leave them in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains soak the ground for long periods, water displaces the soil air, causing the tuber to suffocate and rot from fungal and bacterial attack.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɔ̃ɔ be kplaŋŋ. Nu baaye kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme afternoon heat, drought, or a lack of soil nutrients like calcium. Without proper moisture and mild temperatures, the flower fails to set fruit and drops off.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hao amɛ. Fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: Why is it harmful to spread dry chemical fertilizer right on top of dry soil around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ tsofa ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ oshara mli.

english: Chemical fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve and work properly. If applied to completely dry soil, the concentrated salts in the fertilizer will pull water out of the plant's roots instead, causing the crop to burn and wither.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli ni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ lɛ Nu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baajie nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ. Ehaa tsei shãa ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily under full direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and produce broad leaves that shade the cocoa trees, keeping the soil moist and helping the seedlings survive their early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to manufacture food that grows big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the soil so they catch maximum sunlight and stay safe from rot and crawling pests.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ́ akwɛ bulb lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. ni eyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to build strong green leaves and stalks, which you can fix by applying balanced fertilizer or well-rotted manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba. Abaanyɛ atsake enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil, restoring fertility for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Abele jieɔ niyenii kpakpai babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni ekɛ fɔmɔ aku sɛɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Can I put fresh manure from my piggery directly around my vegetable plants?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ hee awo he tɛ̃ɛ. Ani manyɛ madu mi aduawai lɛ?

english: Fresh animal manure is too hot and strong for young crop roots, which can burn and kill the plants. You must dry and compost the manure for a few weeks until it turns into dark earth before adding it to your crops.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ kɛha tsei bibii ashishifãi. ni baanyɛ ashã ni egbe tsei Ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli otsii fioo komɛi kɛyashi ebaatsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli dani okɛfata oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the inside of my young corn plants' stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These pests are Fall Armyworms. They hide inside the central funnel of the corn plant where soft leaves grow, and early treatment with appropriate organic or chemical sprays is needed before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi ni baa bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ amli. ni ehe miihia ni atsa lɛ mra. kɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ dani efiteɔ he ni edara lɛ.

english: Curling yellow leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stems provided by extension offices prevents this disease from spreading.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni Extension Office lɛ kɛha lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa.

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water stays trapped in the soil around them. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows heavy rain to drain away easily so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo bote shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ oya. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil dries out completely. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting shade crops nearby helps flowers stay on and produce fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why does covering the soil around my pepper plants with dry grass help them grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, which covers the soil to block direct heat from the sun. This keeps soil moisture from evaporating fast during dry spells and stops weeds from growing and stealing nutrients.
ga: Hay tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up under the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ shwane hulu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and delicate root systems that cannot handle direct sunlight for long periods. Severe sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out moisture faster than roots can absorb it, causing the leaves to turn yellow and drop.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni egbiɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Maize leaves curl up tight during hot days as a self-defense mechanism to reduce water loss. Rolling their leaves hides the tiny pores from direct heat, trapping moisture inside so the plant doesn't dry out before evening.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ amɛhe koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ teeɔ. kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. koni tsei lɛ akagbi dani jenamɔ aba

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with thick green leaves, but the roots underneath stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen (often from excessive fresh animal manure), cassava plants put all their energy into leafy branches above ground instead of storing food underground in the roots.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ (Bei pii lɛ, ejɛɔ kooloi aŋmei heei babaoo mli.) Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ yaa eniji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their yellow flowers without growing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates unevenly. High temperatures prevent pollination from happening inside the flower, so the plant sheds the unproductive flower to save energy.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ tsiɔ pollination naa koni ekafee fɔfɔi lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni wooo yibii lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and turn brown completely at a certain time of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ egbi kwraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally dry out and die back when the tuber beneath the soil reaches full maturity. The plant goes into a natural resting stage to survive the dry season, keeping all its food packed safely inside the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ. Tsei boteɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be mli koni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Akɛ niyenii lɛ fɛɛ toɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli shweshweeshwe.
