english: Why do my plantain trees break easily at the base whenever strong winds blow across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ fãa oya yɛ shishigbɛ be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trunks can be weakened from the inside by microscopic soil worms (nematodes) or stem borers that eat through root tissues. This deprives the plant of strong anchors, making it snap easily under wind pressure.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni anaa lɛ baanyɛ aha plantain tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛjɛ mli. (Nematodes) loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ bɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ni wa. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaakumɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hewalɛ shishi.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow thin, tall, and weak when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛkwɛɔ, ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete heavily for sunlight and soil nutrients. The stalks stretch rapidly upward toward light instead of growing thick trunks, making them weak and fragile.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ yaa oya kɛyaa kane lɛ he moŋ fe ni eeetsɔ tso ni mli edɔ. ni ehaa egbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ

english: Why do my freshly harvested peppers rot so quickly when I harvest them during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni akpa ehee lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akpa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Peppers picked in wet weather carry excessive surface water and airborne fungal spores on their skins. Moisture trapped inside storage containers or bags speeds up decay and mold growth.
ga: Peppers ni akɛtoɔ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa fe nine kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ahewolo nɔ. Fɛ̃i ni atsĩ naa yɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli loo kotokui amli lɛ baaha fitemɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aya hiɛ oya.

english: Why do my cabbage plants look wilted in the afternoon even when the soil around them is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ?

english: On very hot afternoons, water evaporates from large cabbage leaves faster than the roots can drink water from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to conserve water, then bounces back when temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Nu shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ kaabii agboi amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛ nu ahi mli. Kɛkɛ ni ekuɔ esɛɛ ebaa ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my sweet potatoes grow thin like pencil roots instead of expanding into fat potatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ feɔ pensil-mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes require loose, well-drained soil to swell. Hard or tightly packed clay soil acts like a wall, preventing the roots from expanding freely into fat tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia sweet potato koni efuu. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni mli edɔ tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbogbo. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã amɛfee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ fɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in an open field without big trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei wuji komɛi bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Shady plants like plantains or mature forest trees protect young cocoa from sunburn and keep the soil moist while the cocoa roots establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei ni eda lɛ baaye abua ni ebu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Maize continuously drains specific nutrients like nitrogen from the soil. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts the ground and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ adu nii shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ fiteɔ, ni ehaa helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans alongside my cereal crops help my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds nearby crops like maize or millet.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛyeɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: When crops are crowded, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This stress causes plants to grow thin and weak, producing small or empty cobs.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ nɔnyɛɛ nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. ni kɛ cob bibioo loo efolo baa

english: Flower drop is a sign of stress, usually caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. When stressed, the plant sheds flowers to conserve energy for survival.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ ji haomɔ he okadi. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry spells as a survival mechanism to reduce water loss. Once the rains return, the plant uses stored energy in its roots to sprout fresh green leaves.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ.

english: Leaf curl is often a reaction to heat and water stress or a viral infection spread by tiny insects like whiteflies. The plant curls its leaves to try to protect itself from losing water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ kɛ nu he haomɔ kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ, tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do weeds always seem to grow much faster than the crops I intentionally plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni mito he gbɛjianɔ akɛ makwɛ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to compete aggressively for resources. Their roots spread quickly to absorb available soil nutrients and water before young domestic crops can capture them.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhe awo nibii ni he hiaa lɛ ahe akaŋshii mli waa. Amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya koni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni yɔɔ lɛ dani shia ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why should I remove the extra side shoots growing near the base of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie sɛɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Pruning extra shoots, or suckers, prevents the plant from wasting energy on unnecessary stems and leaves, redirecting vital nutrients into growing larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aya tomatoi ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know when my groundnuts are fully ripe and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-peanuts lɛ egbɔ kwraa ni esa akɛ mafo?

english: Groundnuts are mature when the leaves start turning yellow and dry out. Checking a few pods underground will confirm maturity if the inside of the shells shows dark veins and the seeds are full.
ga: Peanuts lɛ shɛɔ shweremɔ he beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akwɛ ŋmeii fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, ebaama nɔ mi akɛ ekwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii kɛ dumɔwui eyi ŋmeii lɛ amli obɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop leaves need to stay green and healthy. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the leaves turn green and produce strong ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei ahe koni amɛya nɔ amɛfee eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni ŋmãa lɛ toi lɛ hu aná hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that cannot handle full sunlight without losing water too quickly. Planting temporary shade trees like plantains protects them until they grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ aná hulu la ni fa ni nu lɛ sɛɛ efooo oya tsɔ. Tsei ni haa tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baaje shishi.

english: Why is it better to apply fertilizer when the soil is damp rather than when it is very dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaawo ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fe be mli ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Plant roots can only drink up fertilizer when it dissolves in water. If you place fertilizer on dry soil, the roots cannot absorb it, and the concentrated chemical can actually burn and damage the plant roots.
ga: Tso shishifãi baanyɛ anu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ atsɔ nu mli pɛ. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ. Ni tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei shishifãi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together so I can get more crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition results in weak, thin plants that produce smaller fruits or tubers than well-spaced plants.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni woɔ yibii loo ŋmeii bibii fe tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baa.

english: Planting the same crop year after year drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests that like that crop to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like beans or groundnuts puts nutrients back into the soil and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni sumɔɔ tsei lɛ ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up to catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to grow large tubers underground. Keeping the leaves off the damp ground also prevents diseases from spreading.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni helai akagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the nourishment they need to grow big and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are small ragged holes appearing in the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by destructive caterpillars like Fall Armyworms feeding on the tender plant tissues. Inspecting the central funnel of the plant early allows you to treat them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ Fall Armyworms ni yeɔ tsei ahe fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa ŋmeii bibii amli. Tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa amɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when they sit in waterlogged soil because the excess water cuts off the air supply to the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ amɛta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kpaɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme stress, such as very hot days, dry soil, or sudden heavy rains. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch helps protect the blossoms.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ ko he, tamɔ yɛ gbi ni edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: How much maize can I expect to harvest from one hectare of land if I use improved seed varieties?
ga: Kɛji akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ŋmãa enyiɛ manyɛ makpa kɛjɛ hectare kome mli?

english: Improved hybrid seed varieties can produce up to 5 to 6 metric tons per hectare under good farm management, which is about three times higher than yields from traditional local seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ awo nibii ni shɛɔ mɛtrik tɔn 5 kɛyashi 6 yɛ hectare kome mli yɛ ŋmɔ mli nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa shishi. Enɛ fa fe yibiiwoo ni jɛɔ blema maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui amli lɛ aaafee toi etɛ.

english: Why do some farmers harvest much more maize than others on the exact same size of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kpaa ŋmãa babaoo fe okwaafoi krokomɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ tamɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yield differences usually come down to using high-yielding certified seeds, applying fertilizer at the right times, controlling weeds early, and managing soil moisture properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ yibiiwoo mli lɛ jɛɔ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ hewɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli Jwɛi lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ

english: What makes hybrid crop seeds perform better than the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for strength, disease resistance, and uniform growth. Seeds saved from a previous harvest lose these strong traits, resulting in weaker plants and lower yield.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ, helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ baafite sui ni mli wa nɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does my maize crop turn yellow and stop growing tall even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa kwɛ̃mɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen. Rain alone isn't enough; crops need balanced fertilizers to build strong green leaves and grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nugbɔ pɛ kɛkɛ faaa. Tsei he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why do buyers weigh my maize in standard 50-kilogram bags instead of measuring with local buckets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ susuɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ he yɛ 50kg kotokui ni afɔɔ feemɔ mli moŋ fe ni amɛaawo maŋ lɛ mli tsɛnsii amli lɛ?

english: Standard 50-kilogram bags ensure accurate weight and fair pricing for both you and the buyer, making it easier to calculate your total profit and compare prices across different markets.
ga: 50kg kotokui ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ amɛtsiimɔ ja kɛ jara ni sa kɛha bo kɛ mɔ ni heɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaabu sɛɛnamɔ fɛɛ he akɔntaa ni akɛ jara ato jarayeli hei srɔtoi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do maize prices drop so low right after the harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa jara baa shi nɛkɛ yɛ kpamɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: During harvest, almost all farmers sell their crops at the same time, flooding the market with maize. High supply lowers the market price, while scarcity during the dry season pushes prices back up.
ga: kpamɔ be mli Nɔ ni miihe ashɛ okwaafoi fɛɛ hɔ̃ɔ amɛŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be kome mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji ŋmãa ni fa fe nine yɛ jara nɔ. Nibii ni akɛhaa babaoo lɛ baaha jarayeli jara lɛ aba shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nibii ni faaa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ baaha nibii ajara aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I decide whether to sell my harvested maize immediately or keep it in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo makɛto?

english: Selling immediately provides quick cash and avoids crop loss from storage pests, but holding well-dried grain in safe storage allows you to sell later during off-peak months when prices are much higher.
ga: Nihɔɔmɔ baaha shika aba oya amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ebaatsi ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ ahe lɛ naa. Shi dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni oookɛto he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ eshɛɛɛ be mli ni jara wa waa lɛ.

english: Why do crop buyers from neighboring countries like Togo and Burkina Faso come to buy grain in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ maji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tamɔ Togo kɛ Burkina Faso lɛ baa Ghana koni amɛbahe ŋmaa lɛ?

english: Neighboring countries often experience dry weather or grain shortages, creating high demand. When Ghanaian farmers produce a strong surplus, foreign traders travel to buy grain to supply their own markets.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, maji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo ŋmaa ni faaa hewɔ. ni kɛ nibii ni ataoɔ babaoo baa Beni Ghana okwaafoi lɛ fee nibii babaoo ni fa fe nine lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ maŋsɛɛ jarayelɔi fãa gbɛ koni amɛyahe ŋmaa koni amɛkɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ jarayeli hei lɛ.

english: How does cross-border trading with neighboring countries affect the price of maize in my local market?
ga: Te husui asɛɛ jarayeli kɛ maji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ saa ŋmãa jara ni yɔɔ mimaŋ jarayelihe lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When foreign traders buy large quantities of local grain, it reduces the overall supply remaining in local markets, which helps drive crop prices up for local farmers.
ga: Kɛ maŋsɛɛ jarayelɔi he maŋ lɛ mli ŋmaa babaoo Enɛ baaha nibii fɛɛ ni eshwɛ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ aba shi. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jara aya hiɛ aha maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi lɛ.

english: What simple steps can I take to protect my stored maize from insects so I can sell it later for higher profit?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma nyɛɛ blɔ nya tomi komɛ a nɔ. koni akɛbu ŋmãa ni ato lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ahe koni sɛɛ mli lɛ anyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ ni ana sɛɛnamɔ babaoo.

english: Dry your maize completely to low moisture levels before bagging, treat the grain with approved protective storage dust, and store the bags off the floor on wooden pallets in a dry, ventilated room.
ga: Ha o-corn lɛ agbi kwraa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi dani okɛwo kotoku mli. Kɛ sũ ni abuɔ he ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ atsu dumɔwui ahe nii. ni okɛ kotokui lɛ ato shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ yɛ tsu ko ni mli egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: This yellowing is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize requires a lot of nitrogen to grow green and healthy, so when soil nutrients are low or washed away by heavy rain, the plant pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ su ni ji ŋmɔŋ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ, Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Tomato plants often drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant focus on growing leaves instead of fruit. Irregular watering can also stress the plant and cause flower drop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mli. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai. Kɛ́ afɔɔɔ nu be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ aná haomɔ ni eha efɔfɔi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do the maize seeds I saved from my previous harvest yield much smaller ears than the ones I bought in the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mijie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ha toi bibii kwraa fe ŋmãa ni mihe yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yields in their first generation. When you save and replant those seeds for a second season, they lose that special vigor and split back into weaker traits, resulting in smaller plants and lower yield.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Beni obuaa nakai dumɔwui lɛ anaa ni oduɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ amɛhewalɛ ni fa lɛ ni amɛjaraa amɛhe ekoŋŋ kɛyaa sui ni bɛ hewalɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei bibii kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: Why are my small green cocoa pods turning black and drying up on the trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is likely caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in cool, wet, and shady conditions. It can also be caused by cherelle wilt, which is the cocoa tree's natural way of shedding extra pods it cannot support with nutrients.
ga: Ekolɛ black pod hela lɛ kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Cherry wilt hu baanyɛ ekɛba. Enɛ ji cacao tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye abua niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: What is making ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving sawdust-like dirt inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni amɛshiɔ muji ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central growing shoot (the funnel) of the maize plant during the day, eating the tender leaves and leaving behind coarse waste that looks like saw dust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ (cone) lɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Eyeɔ baai bibii ni eshiɔ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots decaying and smelling bad underground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Root rot in cassava is caused by fungi that thrive in waterlogged or heavy clay soils with poor drainage. When water sits around the roots for too long without air, the roots suffocate and rot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ yɛ ŋmei mli lɛ baa ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baafo ni amɛbaagboi.

english: What is this weed with pink flowers that makes my maize stay short and turn yellow as if it lacks water?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ jwɛi ni hiɛ fɔfɔi ni tsuɔ tamɔ pinki ni miiha mi-ŋmei lɛ miifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ nɔ ni nu efo mli lɛ?

english: This weed is called Striga, or Witchweed. It attaches its roots directly to the roots of maize and sucks away water and nutrients before the crop can use them, causing severe stunting.
ga: Nɛkɛ jwɛi nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ Striga loo Witchweed lɛ kɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ, ni ejieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ dani tso lɛ baanyɛ ekɛtsu nii. ni kɛ shwiemɔ ni naa wa baa

english: Why should I plant plantains alongside my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide crucial shade and keep the soil moist during the first few years until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa waa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daraa waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye hulutsoo be lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: How does planting groundnuts together with maize help my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. Planting them with maize improves soil fertility, provides extra food, and covers the soil to stop weeds from growing.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii babaoo. kɛ niyenii krokomɛi aha ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akakwɛ̃.

english: How does covering the soil with dry leaves around my pepper plants help during dry weather?
ga: Mulching kɛ baai ni egbi ni ebɔle he lɛ Te mi-pepper tso lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tɛŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry organic matter, called mulching, blocks direct sunlight from drying out the soil. It traps moisture, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weed seeds from getting sunlight to grow.
ga: Mulching kɛ nibii ni egbi ni wala yɔɔ mli Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ atsĩ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ akashɛ hulu la he koni amɛdara

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, a key nutrient they need to grow, or they are getting too much water. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps them regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara Aloo amɛmiiná nu babaoo tsɔ. Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of water stresses the tomato plant, causing it to drop its flowers to save energy. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the root zone helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni bɛ lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ebɔle he lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni ehiɔ shi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the plant's sap, or by a virus carried by insects. Spraying neem oil or insecticidal soap helps control these pests and saves the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni eye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay tiny even when the leaves on top look big and leafy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe yɔɔ baai moŋ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too hard, cassava puts its energy into growing green leaves on top instead of big tubers below. Loosening the soil deep enough allows the roots to expand properly.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli yɛ nɔ moŋ fe bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow twisted and hard to harvest instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewa akɛ abaakpãtã yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eja lɛ?

english: Yam tubers twist when they push against hard stones or dense, unplowed soil underground. Planting yams in high, soft mounds of loosened topsoil allows the tubers to grow straight and smooth.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ tsɔɔ kɛji akɛ amɛtsi amɛ kɛtee tɛi ni wa loo shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji ni atsuuu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu sweet potato yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does my field produce less harvest when I plant maize on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmaa lɛ baa shi fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize pulls the same specific nutrients out of the ground every season, making the soil weak. Rotating your maize with crops like cowpea or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil and restores its strength.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ Abele ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei tsakeɔ Enɛ baaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha ehewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds after the rainy season starts?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the rain falls steadily for a few days in a row so the soil is wet down to about a hand's depth. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to dry out if the sun returns quickly.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ be fɛɛ be gbii fioo komɛi dani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ aaafee nine kome. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kɛji hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba oya.

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole makes the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and small cobs. Spacing them out gives every plant enough resources to produce large cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. He ni ato lɛ baaha nitsumɔhe fɛɛ nitsumɔhe aná nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee cob agbo.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong direct sunlight because their foliage is delicate. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa acts as a living umbrella to protect them until they grow mature and tough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ waaa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni baabu tsei nɛɛ ahe kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides inside the central whorl of young maize leaves. Inspecting your farm early and pouring a bit of clean sand, neem seed extract, or recommended bio-pesticide into the funnel helps kill them.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaai amli lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra ni okɛ ŋã ni mli tse awo Neem dumɔwui amli loo tsofa fioo ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni egbe amɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa tree leaves turn yellow and dry up when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight because their leaves are tender and dry out quickly. Shade trees or plantain plants shield young cocoa from the hot sun, keeping the soil cool and moist so the cocoa can grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Akɛni baai lɛ ji bibii ni amɛgbiɔ oya hewɔ lɛ Shade tsei loo plantains yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots store soft starch as they grow, but after reaching full maturity, the plant starts converting that stored starch into tough plant fiber (woodiness) to support itself, making the root hard and unpleasant to eat.
ga: Cassava shishifãi kɛ starch ni yɔɔ blɛoo toɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Shi kɛ́ tso lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, ebaaje shishi etsake starch ni ato lɛ ewo tso mli tsɔi ni wa mli. (woodiness) ni akɛyeɔ abuaa mɔ ko Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning pale green and light yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: When maize leaves turn yellow from the middle outwards, it means the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key food nutrient in the soil responsible for healthy leaf growth and green color.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ teŋgbɛ kɛtee kponɔgbɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa baai lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji.

english: Why should I cut away the extra shoots growing at the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Each extra shoot (sucker) acts like a hungry mouth drinking water and taking plant nutrients from the main stem. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main plantain gets enough food to produce a heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ tso lɛ yitso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko tsuɔ nii tamɔ daaŋ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ, enuɔ nu ni ejieɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii titrii lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii ni tsii aba.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when weather conditions get too hot or dry, which causes stress to the plant and prevents the pollen inside the flower from fertilizing the seed to create fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji shihilɛi lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo egbi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ akawo dumɔwui lɛ amli koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do I see tiny holes and dirt like sawdust inside the heart of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bu bibii kɛ muji tamɔ ŋmei yɛ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: That dirt and hole pattern is caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the tight center leaves of the maize plant where they chew fresh tissue and leave behind their waste.
ga: Muji kɛ ŋmeii lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmei tsei ateŋ baai ni mli wa lɛ amli lɛ amli. Amɛyeɔ fãji heei ni amɛshiɔ jwɛi yɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why is it helpful to cover the soil around my crops with dry leaves and straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi yɔɔ mli lɛ baye ebua mi.

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves (mulching) acts like an umbrella for the soil. It blocks the scorching sun, keeps water from evaporating quickly out of the ground, and stops weeds from getting sunlight to grow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi haa (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni hulu la akashɛ amɛnɔ

english: Why does my land produce smaller crops when I plant maize in the exact same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific soil nutrients that crop loves without giving the soil time to recover, while also allowing pests and diseases that attack maize to multiply in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tsei sumɔɔ lɛ pɛ ni ehaaa sũ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ feɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up tight during the middle of hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling up leaves is a plant's natural self-defense against heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the leaf surface exposed to the burning sun, helping it trap moisture and prevent drying out.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Tsei haa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbi.

english: Why does planting groundnuts alongside my main crops make the soil better for the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, which means their roots have a special natural ability to take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, enriching the ground with natural fertilizer for nearby plants.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛgbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ afee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees on my farm before I plant my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide the necessary shade and moisture for cocoa seedlings to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa koni kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why did some of my maize seeds fail to sprout after I buried them deep in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds buried too deep use up all their stored energy trying to push through heavy soil before reaching sunlight, causing them to die underground.
ga: Dumɔwui ni afu amɛ tsɔ lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ ni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ mli dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do farmers say planting groundnuts makes the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo lɛ kɛɛ akɛ ŋmei dumɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in their roots. When the plants die, this trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmei tso ko ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifãi amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nɛkɛ nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my yams grow short and twisted instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ kuku ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni efee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, deep soil to expand downward easily. Hard soil or underground stones block their path, causing the tubers to bend, split, or stay short.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛya shi oya. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ tsiɔ gbɛ lɛ naa, ni no haa yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi, emli gbalaa, loo ebaa shi.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water suffocates them by cutting off air in the soil. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ ŋmɛ shi, ni ekɛ mumɔ baa kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Upward leaf curling in pepper plants is often caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites feeding on the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Treating these pests early prevents severe leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Kɛ́ atsa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite baa lɛ waa.

english: Why do small holes appear in my bean leaves and pods during the flowering stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu bibioo ko yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ ŋmei baai kɛ ŋmeii ahe yɛ fɔfɔi be lɛ mli?

english: These holes are caused by insect pests like caterpillars and pod borers that attack fresh leaves and flowers. Using recommended organic or chemical sprays early protects your yield.
ga: Nɛkɛ bu nɛɛ jɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ pod borers ni tutuaa baai kɛ fɔfɔi heei. Akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants face heat stress or sudden drought, which prevents normal pollination. Keeping soil moist and providing light shade during extreme heat helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ naa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do weeds growing near my young crop seedlings make them grow so slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa amɛdaraa blɛoo waa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your seedlings for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. Clearing weeds around the base of young crops ensures they get full nutrition to grow fast.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ odumɔwui lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Tsei bibii lɛ ashishitoo lɛ haa amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛdara oya.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct sunlight because their roots are small and cannot absorb enough water quickly. Planting shade crops like plantains nearby protects them from severe sun and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ daraaa, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why is my maize growing tall but the leaves are light green instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ kɛlɛ shi baai lɛ ji eŋɔli ni mli tse yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn light green or yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build healthy leaves. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its deep green color and produce bigger cobs.
ga: Abele baa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni wa Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛbatsɔ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ni amɛwo ŋmɔji wuji.

english: Cassava leaves curl and turn yellow when tiny insects called whiteflies spread cassava mosaic disease to the plant. Removing infected leaves early and planting disease-resistant cassava varieties stops the sickness from spreading across your farm.
ga: Yucca baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ cassava mosaic hela lɛ eshwaa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra Ni odu ŋmei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela akagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my corn plants produce small cobs when I plant many seeds close together in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When corn seeds are planted too close together, the roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. Spacing the plants properly ensures each stem gets full sunshine and enough soil food to make large cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tso lɛ tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa hulu la ni fa kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni efee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Pepper flowers drop off without making fruit when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering during flowering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch during hot spells helps the flowers stay attached and form peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni ewooo yibii kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni ekɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛtoɔ ŋmeii ahe gbɛjianɔ.

english: Why are my yam tubers rotting in the ground before it is time to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot underground when heavy rainwater pools around the roots without draining away, encouraging harmful fungal growth. Planting yams on high mounds or ridges helps excess rain drain off safely so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nu babaoo bua amɛhe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni amɛhooo. Ehaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ daa. Sweet potatoes ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why does my land yield less harvest when I plant maize on the same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize on the same land every season drains the exact same nutrients from the topsoil without giving the soil time to recover. Rotating maize with nitrogen-fixing crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores soil richness naturally.
ga: Growing corn on the same area every time Seasons drain the same nutrients from the topsoil without giving the soil time to recover. Rotate corn with nitrogen-fixing crops such as peanuts or cowpeas. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds cause my young vegetable crops to grow much slower than expected?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi-aduawai bibii lɛ miida blɛoo kwraa fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight that your vegetables need to develop. Clearing weeds within the first four weeks of planting gives your vegetables a clear path to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa o-aduawai lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ ni okɛdu lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha o-vegetables lɛ aná gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kɛya dalɛ ni mli wa nɔ.

english: Why are there tiny worms inside my garden eggs when I cut them open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli beni mifoɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Worms inside garden eggs come from eggs laid on the flowers by adult moths, which hatch into caterpillars that burrow into the young fruit. Inspecting plants early and using recommended, crop-safe treatments keeps the fruits free from pests.
ga: Abɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii fɔɔ fɔfɔi anɔ lɛ amli. ni fɔ̃ɔ kɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni fɔɔ aduawai bibii lɛ amli Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra ni akɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ esaaa tsei ahe lɛ atsu nii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ akafee nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants droop in the afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu wo amɛmli leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In intense heat, tomato plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck water out of the soil, causing temporary wilt. Covering the soil with dried grass or leaves helps keep the root zone cool and moist throughout hot afternoons.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I clear away all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight and excessive heat. Retaining some large trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides necessary shade and preserves soil moisture, allowing young cocoa trees to survive their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. Tsei wuji komɛi akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow lush green leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-decomposed animal manure gives the maize the food it needs to regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. This is the main nutrient that plants need to grow lush leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-digested manure will give corn the nourishment it needs to turn green and grow strong.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to dig up if the tubers are underground?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni esa akɛ atsa ŋmei kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically mature between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You can tell it is ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, or you can carefully dig around the base of one test plant to see if the roots are thick enough.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Depends on the variety You can tell the lower leaves are ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off. Aloo obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli. Test the base of the plant carefully to see if the roots are thick enough.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant cowpeas in the same farm as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil. Planting them alongside maize improves soil fertility without needing to buy extra chemical fertilizers, helping both crops yield better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ Kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Helps both types of plants produce better yields.

english: What are these tiny caterpillars eating the central leaves of my young maize, and how do they harm the plant?
ga: Mɛni nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ yeɔ yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ anɔ? Ni te amɛyeɔ tsei awui amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on the soft growing core of young maize plants. If left untreated, they destroy the plant's leaves and prevent normal growth, which drastically reduces your final grain harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni miida lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ Ebaafite tso lɛ baai lɛ ni ebaatsi dalɛ ni sa lɛ naa. Enɛ baaha onaagbee ŋmaa ni obaakpa lɛ nɔ aba shi waa.

english: Why do I need to cut long wooden poles for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei kakadaji lɛ? Koni eha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi?

english: Yam plants are vines that need to spread their leaves to catch sunlight, which powers the growth of big tubers underground. Staking keeps leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases and helping the plant capture maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato tso ji wain tso ni esa akɛ egbɛ baai eshwã koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ. ni tsirɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs lɛ adalɛ Staking baaye abua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Tsi fungal helai anaa ni eye ebua tsei ni amɛná hulu la babaoo

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die even when there is plenty of moisture in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is usually caused by bacterial or fungal wilt diseases in the soil. The disease blocks the water-carrying tubes inside the stem, preventing water from reaching the upper leaves even when the roots are wet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ni ji bacteria loo fungal wilt hela ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli edɔ trukaa lɛ baa. Hela nɛɛ tsiɔ paipii ni kɛ nu yaa lɛ anaa yɛ tsɔne lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa nu ayashɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛji shishifãi lɛ edɔ po.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ ekomɛi? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: When too many shoots grow from one plantain mat, they compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. Removing extra shoots leaves energy for the main plant and one secondary shoot, resulting in larger and heavier plantain bunches.
ga: Beni dumɔwui babaoo tsɔ jɛ dumɔwui akuu kome mli lɛ, Plantains lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni ji enyɔ lɛ náa hewalɛ ko ni eshwɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, plantain lɛ feɔ agbo ni etsiiɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl upward during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in high heat is a natural defense response crops use to reduce the amount of surface area exposed to the sun. This helps the plant conserve internal water and prevent drying out during the hottest hours of the day.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu toɔ emli ni ehaaa egbi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why is it harmful to put fresh chicken manure straight from the coop onto my tender crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei hee ni jɛ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ baawo miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fresh animal manure is too strong and produces high heat and ammonia gas as it breaks down, which burns plant roots and kills young crops. Allowing manure to dry and decompose fully into compost makes it safe and beneficial for soil.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsɔ ni ekɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ ammonia gas baa kɛji efite. Enɛ baashã tsei shishifãi ni ekpata ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahiɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi kwraa ni efite ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ehaa efeɔ shweshweeshwe ni ehe baa sɛɛnamɔ kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to prune or cut extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo maŋɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy, allowing sunlight and air to reach all parts of the cocoa tree, which keeps the pods healthy and reduces damage from insects.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ ashɛ kookoo tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ waa, ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baa shi.

english: Will cutting away leaves and small branches hurt my cocoa crop's growth?
ga: Baai kɛ niji bibii ni afoɔ Ani kpojee baaná kookoo tso lɛ dalɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii?

english: No, removing extra branches actually helps the tree direct its energy into growing healthier cocoa pods rather than wasting energy on excess leaves.
ga: Dabi, eji tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ diɛŋtsɛ. Enɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe ni eeefite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ.

english: Is doing continuous pruning on my farm worth all the time and hard work?
ga: Ani be kɛ nitsumɔ ni wa ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mifoɔ daa lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ?

english: Yes, continuous pruning is very rewarding because well-maintained trees stay healthier, suffer far less from pest attacks, and give you better yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni afoɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ náa hewalɛ. Ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baaa piŋmɔ babaoo ni ekɛ yibii kpakpai baa

english: How does sunlight helping my cocoa trees actually affect the pods?
ga: Te hulu la ni yeɔ ebuaa mi cacao tsei lɛ saa ŋmeii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Sunlight reaching the tree warms and dries the pods, creating an environment where healthy cocoa can develop without being ruined by damp-loving pests.
ga: Hulu la ni shɛɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tsei lɛ amli dɔɔ ni egbiɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ko baa ni kookoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni kooloi ni sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ efiteee lɛ.

english: Why does my cocoa farm need good air movement between the trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ mi-cocoe ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he hiaa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Good air flow dries off damp leaves and pods quickly, stopping the buildup of trapped moisture where harmful insects like to gather.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ haa baai ni mli efɔ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Ekpaa nu ni mli ewo muji ni buaa ehe naa yɛ he ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ buaa amɛhe naa lɛ.

english: What happens to cocoa pods if my trees become too bushy and overcrowded?
ga: Mɛni baa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ kɛji mi tsei lɛ bafee ŋmɔji ni eyi obɔ kɛ mɛi babaoo?

english: Overcrowded trees block out sunlight and trap still air, creating a dark, humid environment that attracts destructive insects to your crop.
ga: Tsei babaoo ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa ni amɛmɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli edɔ ni gbalaa kooloi ni fiteɔ nii kɛbaa onibii amli lɛ baa.

english: How does letting sunshine into my cocoa farm keep insects away naturally?
ga: Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ ni hulu la ni miaha eshɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aaashwie kooloi bibii yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Many harmful insects thrive in dark and damp shade. Direct sunlight makes the tree environment warm and uncomfortable for insects, driving them away naturally.
ga: Koolooi babaoo ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ he ni efɔ, ni yɔɔ duŋ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ he lɛ feɔ hulutsoo ni haaa ŋmeii lɛ aná hejɔɔmɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ amɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can I protect my cocoa trees from pests without relying entirely on expensive sprays?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ni mikɛ tsofai ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: Properly pruning your farm to let air and light move through the trees creates a natural defense system that stops insects from settling on your cocoa.
ga: Kɛ́ ofolɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la atsɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ko baa ni haa kooloi bibii baagbee okoo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do insects seem to attack trees in heavy shade more than trees in sunny areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii tutuaa tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ fe tsei ni yɔɔ hei ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ lɛ?

english: Insects prefer calm, shady, and humid hiding spots. Bright light and fresh air disrupt their habitat, making sunny trees far less attractive to pests.
ga: Kplukai sumɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ dioo, shade, kɛ nu ni mli ejɔ. La ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa gbalaa amɛshihilɛhe lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tsei ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ŋmei sumɔɔɔ kwraa.

english: What is the simplest farm practice I can do to naturally lower insect damage on my cocoa?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔ mli nifeemɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ mafee koni mikɛba kooloi ni fiteɔ mi-kookoo lɛ nɔ lɛ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Clearing out thick upper branches to let sunshine and wind pass through the trees is the simplest and most effective way to protect cocoa pods from insects naturally.
ga: Niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote tso lɛ mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ ni mɔɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ kookoo ŋmeii ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is everyone telling me to plant my crops as soon as the first rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ kɛɔ mi akɛ madu tsei lɛ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ je shishi pɛ?

english: Early rains provide the soil with fresh moisture and cool temperatures that help seeds sprout quickly and build strong roots before dry spells hit.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hee kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ baa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni wa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa.

english: What happens to my crops if the rainfall comes earlier than expected in the season?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ mra fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ yɛ be lɛ mli?

english: When rain comes early, it gives your crops a longer period to grow and absorb soil nutrients, which usually leads to stronger plants and a higher harvest yield.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ oya Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná be babaoo ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ ni amɛŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkpaa yibii babaoo.

english: How do early rains affect the weeds on my farm compared to my young crops?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ saa jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ akɛto miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe?

english: Early rains wake up weed seeds in the soil at the same time as your crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing water and nutrients from your young plants.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ baate jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashi. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: How much water does rice actually need to grow well on my farm?
ga: Nu enyiɛ he hiaa koni ŋmãa akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Rice requires a lot of water compared to other crops, especially when young. It thrives in very wet or flooded soil because water delivers nutrients directly to its roots and keeps the plant cool.
ga: Omɔ biɔ nu babaoo kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe. Titri lɛ, beni miji oblanyo fioo lɛ. Ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji akɛ, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my rice leaves turn yellow when the ground stays dry for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Rice leaves turn yellow in dry soil because the plant cannot absorb essential nutrients like nitrogen without water, which slows down its growth.
ga: Omɔ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Enɛ ji akɛ, tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛhe niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛji nu bɛ, ni no haa amɛ dalɛ baa shi.

english: When is the best time for me to start clearing my land for planting rice?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mabɔi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛduɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: You should clear and break up your land just before the rainy season starts so the ground is clean, soft, and ready to catch the very first rains.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ofite dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ he atse, ni efee blɛoo ni efee klalo akɛ ebaaná klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I buy my farm seeds early instead of waiting until planting day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmɔ mli dumɔwui mra? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ kɛyashi dumɔ gbi lɛ nɔ?

english: Buying seeds early ensures you get high-quality, healthy seeds before local shops run out, allowing you to plant immediately when the rain falls.
ga: Dumɔwui ahemɔ mra Enɛ baaha ona dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ dani shwapoi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ asɛɛ afo. Ehaa oduɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ.

english: Is it better to buy my farming seeds from a local dealer nearby or travel to the main city?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooohe dumɔwui kɛjɛ jarayelɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ dɛŋ loo oooya maŋ wulu ko mli?

english: Buying from a reliable local dealer saves you transport money and ensures the seeds are already suited to the climate and soil conditions of your immediate area.
ga: Kɛ́ ohe nii kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli nihɔɔlɔ ko ni oheɔ oyeɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha okɛ shika akafite yɛ nibii ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ he. ni oye obua ni okwɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ sa kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ momo.

english: How do I know if the seeds I am buying nearby will actually sprout and give me a good crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ baakwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛha mi ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Good seeds look clean, whole, free from insect holes, and are certified by seed inspectors. You can test a few in wet cloth to see if they sprout before planting the whole field.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe tse, dumɔwu muu lɛ fɛɛ mli bɛ kooloi ahiɛ. ni mɔ ko ni kwɛɔ dumɔwui anɔ lɛ ema nɔ mi Obaanyɛ okɛ mama ni mli efɔ aka amɛ okwɛ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ dani odu ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: What basic steps must I complete before putting my seeds into the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii esa akɛ mafee dani mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Before planting, you must clear weeds, loosen the topsoil so young roots can penetrate easily, and have your certified seeds ready so you don't waste precious rainy days.
ga: Dani obaadu lɛ, ehe miihia ni ojie jwɛi lɛ. Loosen the top layer of soil so that young roots can easily penetrate it. And stock up on certified seeds so you don't waste precious time on a rainy day.

english: What does it mean when people say I should use organic methods on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ kɛji mɔ ko kɛɛ esa akɛ mikɛ organic gbɛi atsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Organic methods mean using natural materials like decomposed animal manure, compost, and friendly shade trees instead of synthetic chemical fertilizers. This builds rich, healthy soil that naturally holds water longer and keeps your crops strong across rainy and dry seasons.
ga: Organic gbɛi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ kooloi aŋmei ni efite, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baatsu nii lɛ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwereɔ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baanyɛ ahi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni eye ebua ni onibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why does the soil on my farmland dry out so quickly a few days after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses moisture very quickly through direct heat from the sun. Covering the ground with dried leaves or growing ground-cover plants keeps the earth cool and traps moisture beneath the surface so crop roots stay hydrated.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔ hulutsoo ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Koni tso shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: How can planting trees on my farmland help my crops instead of stealing their plant food?
ga: Te tsei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ moŋ fe niyenii ni maju kɛjɛ tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Certain trees drop organic leaves that decay into rich food for the soil. Their deep roots also bring up water and hidden nutrients from deep underground, while their branches give soft shade that protects your crops from burning.
ga: Tsei komɛi shĩɔ baai ni fiteɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ, ni no haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii babaoo. Amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ hu gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛniji lɛ haa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni buɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow and dry during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaves turn yellow and dry up when plants receive too much direct, intense sunlight without enough soil moisture. Providing partial shade with taller plants or organic shade trees keeps the temperature down so the leaves stay green.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛ hulu la babaoo nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo fã ko ha tsei ni kɛlɛ loo tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi bɔni afee ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli.

english: Why do my crops grow big leaves but do not yield many fruits or seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ dara shi ebɛ aduawai loo dumɔwui babaoo lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen from ungrounded fertilizers, the plant spends all its energy producing leaf stems instead of flowers. Balanced organic nutrients encourage the crop to shift its energy into growing healthy fruits and seeds.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ lɛ mli. Yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ lɛ, tsei kɛ amɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ feɔ baa tsei. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ja yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsakeɔ hewalɛ amɛwoɔ aduawai kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ amli.

english: Flowers drop off when a crop experiences shock from extreme sun heat or irregular watering. Keeping moisture in the soil through leaf cover and giving young plants shade helps them hold onto flowers until fruits form.
ga: Flowers fall off when plants are exposed to heat from intense sunlight or inconsistent watering. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛhaa kɛtsɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni akɛhaa tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔii amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my crops growing very slowly and staying tiny compared to plants on nearby farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo waa ni amɛfee bibioo kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Stunted growth happens when the soil is too hard for roots to spread or lacks basic nutrients. Digging well-rotted manure or compost into the planting hole loosens hard earth and gives roots easy access to plant food.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã loo niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ atsa ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ awo dumɔ bu lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná tsei niyenii oya.

english: Why do pests attack my crop every single season even after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mijie he ni miŋmɔ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ moŋ?

english: Insects and plant diseases live on in the soil when you grow the same crop in the same spot repeatedly. Switching crops each season breaks the life cycle of pests because the new crop is not food they like to eat.
ga: Kplukai kɛ tsei ahe helai hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome shii abɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashihilɛ mli ejaakɛ tsei heei lɛ jeee niyenii ni amɛsumɔɔ.

english: How can I protect my crop leaves from insects without spending money on chemical sprays?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe ni mikɛ shika tsuuu nii yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ahe?

english: You can make natural organic mixtures using crushed neem leaves or garlic stirred in water, or plant strong-smelling herbs nearby to naturally repel insects without harming the crops or soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni akɛfutuɔ nii kɛtsɔ neem baai ni atswa loo galiki ni akɛwo nu mli lɛ nɔ. Aloo dumɔ tsofai ni he yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ waa yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo. Koni ekɛshwie kooloi bibii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeee ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ awui

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are buried too deep in hard earth, dried out by heat, or eaten by ground insects. Planting seeds at a shallow depth in moist, loose soil allows seedlings to easily push through into the sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa mli tsɔ. egbi kɛ latsaa loo kooloi yeɔ lɛ Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni etse ehe lɛ nɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ boteɔ hulu la lɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Why do I need to spray my cocoa trees regularly even if I don't see any bugs on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ nu afɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ daa lɛ? Ni minaaa kooloi bibii komɛi?

english: Diseases and tiny insects like capsids can infect your cocoa before you notice visible damage. Regular spraying acts like preventive medicine, keeping hidden fungal spores and pests from destroying your crop before it starts producing.
ga: Helai kɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ capsids baanyɛ aŋɔ o-cocoa lɛ mli dani ona nɔ ko ni anaa ni efite. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofa ni tsiɔ hela naa. Etsiɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite onibii dani amɛje yibiiwoo shishi.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to strong, direct heat and sunlight. Keeping canopy trees or planting food crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides shade and preserves moisture, protecting the seedlings while their root systems establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei bibii anɔ loo odu niyenii tamɔ plantains kɛfata kookoo bibii ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo be aba ni ebaaha hulutsoo be ahi shi. Buu dumɔwui lɛ ahe be mli ni shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ.

english: What causes the pods on my cocoa trees to turn black and rot before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in humid, wet conditions. Pruning excess branches to let air flow through and removing infected pods quickly keeps the fungus from spreading across your entire farm.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Will using heavy machinery to clear my farm hurt my soil and crops in the long run?
ga: Ani tsɔnei ni tsii ni mikɛbaatsu nii kɛjie miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Heavy machines can scrape away the rich topsoil and pack the dirt too tightly. When soil is compacted, crop roots struggle to push deep into the ground and water cannot soak in properly, which can reduce your farm's productivity over time.
ga: Tsɔnei ni tsii baanyɛ ajie sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ ni ekɛ muji lɛ afee ekome tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ebɔle lɛ Tso shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni nu nyɛŋ aŋɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha nibii ni anáa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crops are starving for nutrients, particularly nitrogen, or that water is trapped around the roots. Adding organic manure or fertilizer gives the plants the strength to make green leaves and build food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ onibii amli. titri lɛ nitrogen Aloo nu ko yɛ ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaa eŋɔli ni efee niyenii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seedlings very close together to get a bigger harvest from my plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tsei ahe dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the dirt. Giving crops proper distance allows each plant to grow big, healthy stems and produce a higher total yield.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei ni akɛhaa yɛ he ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni edaa, ni ewoɔ yibii fɛɛ ni fa babaoo.

english: Why does cutting off branches from my cocoa trees help them grow more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi cacao tsei lɛ aniji ni mifoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches that waste the tree's energy. It lets sunlight enter the tree canopy and improves air circulation, which prevents fungal diseases and encourages the tree to put its strength into producing flower cushions and pods.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa ni haa tso lɛ hewalɛ hoɔ lɛ. Ehaa hulu la boteɔ tso lɛ mli ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ afee fɔfɔi akushɛi kɛ ŋmɔji.

english: Weeds steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your crops. Because weeds grow very fast, they can easily choke young crops and starve them of the resources they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsi ŋmɔshi nibii bibii anaa oya ni amɛjie nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdu nii lɛ kɛjɛ amɛdɛŋ.

english: Why are the flowers on my crop plants falling off without turning into fruit or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii lɛ?
