english: Flowers drop when plants face stress from extreme heat, dry soil, poor nutrients, or damage from sap-sucking insects. Ensuring the crop has enough water and protection during flowering keeps the blossoms attached so they can set fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, kɛ niyenii ni esaaa mli. loo nɔ ni kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ fiteɔ Tsei lɛ ahe nu jogbaŋŋ ni abuɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do crops grow poorly on land where topsoil was dug up or disturbed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni atsa ŋwɛi sũ loo ni agbala mli lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The top layer of dirt contains almost all the natural organic matter and beneficial organisms that feed crops. When that layer is stripped away or polluted, the remaining deep soil lacks the food and air structure needed for healthy crop roots.
ga: Nɔ ni miihe ashɛ muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ fɛɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nibii kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii niyenii. Beni ajie nakai fã lɛ loo awo mli muji lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ bɛ niyenii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni he hiaa kɛha tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, which is the main food plants need to grow green and strong, or the roots are flooded with water and cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Aloo nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu.

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants drop off before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani aduawai lɛ miikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when the soil gets too dry, as the plant tries to conserve water and energy rather than producing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do the leaves on my plantain trees roll up during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves roll up under intense afternoon sun to protect themselves from losing too much moisture, and they naturally unfold again when the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ he. Ni ebaajie ehe kpo ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are my vegetable seedlings growing tall, thin, and weak instead of standing strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ miida, amɛmiifee mlɛo ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaadamɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seedlings stretch out and become thin when they are planted in too much shade, as they spend all their energy growing upward to search for sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baagbala amɛhe ni amɛbaafee mlɛo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛtaoɔ hulu la.

english: Why do the bottoms of my ripening tomatoes turn black and sunken?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efo mli lɛ?

english: This issue happens when soil moisture fluctuates between very wet and very dry, which stops the tomato plant from absorbing enough calcium to build healthy fruit skins.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake yɛ nɔ ni efɔ waa kɛ nɔ ni egbi waa teŋ. Enɛ haaa tomato tso lɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee aduawai ahe tsɔi ni mli wa.

english: If I plant cowpea together with my maize, will the cowpea steal food from my maize?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmãa du tsina ŋmãa Ani tsina ŋmãa baaju niyenii kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: No, cowpea actually feeds the soil by taking nitrogen from the air and placing it into the ground, which helps your maize grow better alongside it.
ga: Dabi, tsina ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii diɛŋtsɛ kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa o-corn lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ emasɛi.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants twisting and curling upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miitsi amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus, or by extreme heat stress making the leaves curl to trap moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, the main stem turns woody and thick, and small cracks appear in the soil near the base.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso titri lɛ tsɔɔ tso ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ Ejeɔ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa seeds fail to sprout when I plant them in nursery bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa yibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mikɛwo grow bag mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa seeds spoil quickly once removed from the pod, so if they dry out before planting or are buried too deep in wet soil, they rot instead of germinating.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli pɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbi dani adu loo afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ tsɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ baagboi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly in the barn after I store them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikɛto lɛ?

english: Yams rot easily if they were scratched or cut during harvest, or if they are stored in warm rooms without fresh air movement, allowing mold to enter through the wounds.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ loo afo amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. aloo kɛji akɛ akɛwo tsu ko ni mli edɔ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli Enɛ baaha ŋmeii abote pilamɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay small and thin even when the leaves look big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara ni amɛhe wa eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa moŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava plants focus their energy on growing tall stems and thick leaves when there is too much nitrogen in the soil or when planted too close together. To get large, starchy tubers, the plant needs well-drained soil with good potassium levels and enough space for the roots to expand.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ susuɔ amɛshishifãi ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ ahe fe fɛɛ kɛ́ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Koni aná yitso agbo kɛ ashikishaŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia tso lɛ. Eyɛ potassium kpakpa kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell they are ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and digging up one sample root shows a firm, thick tuber with white or yellowish inner flesh.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo hiɔ shi aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ amɛfee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. Afo nɔkwɛmɔnɔ kome mli ni ana akɛ eyɛ ŋmei ko ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ loo yɛŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ mli.

english: Why do my mango trees drop most of their blossoms before tiny fruits can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ mi mango tso lɛ fɛɛ miiwo fɔfɔi dani aduawai bibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Mango trees drop flowers mainly due to dry spells during flowering, heavy winds, or fungal attack like anthracnose. Supplying light water at the base during early flowering and keeping the tree free from pests helps the flowers develop into full fruits.
ga: Mango tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ babaoo yɛ fɔfɔi be, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, loo ŋmeii tamɔ anthracnose hewɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ blɛoo yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ shwereɔ mra lɛ, ni aha tso lɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko akafee nɔ ko lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my sweet orange tree turning light yellow between the green veins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-orange tso ni ŋɔɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ teŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing between leaf veins usually means the orange tree lacks key mineral nutrients like zinc or magnesium in the soil, or that waterlogged roots are unable to absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ tso lɛ baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ ateŋ ŋmɔŋ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ o-citrus tso lɛ bɛ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ zinc loo magnesium yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo, shishifãi ni nu ewo mli lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I stop worms from ruining the inside of my guava fruits?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii ni fiteɔ mi-guava aduawai lɛ amli lɛ anaa?

english: Worms inside guavas come from fruit flies that lay eggs under the skin of young fruits. You can protect them by covering young growing fruits with small paper or cloth bags, or by hanging fruit fly traps around your orchard.
ga: Guava ŋmeii lɛ jɛɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ aduawai bibii ahewolo shishi lɛ amli. Obaanyɛ obu amɛhe kɛtsɔ wolo kotoku bibioo loo mama ni oookɛha aduawai ni miida lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ obɔɔ lɛ he lɛ nɔ

english: Why do the leaves of my crops curl up during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural defense mechanism to conserve water. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to hot sun and wind, preventing moisture from escaping too quickly.
ga: Baai ni ebɔleɔ ehe lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo koni ekɛbu nu he. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ baa shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ.

english: How does changing the crop I plant on my plot each season help my harvest?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ daa afi lɛ ni mitsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi yɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Rotating different types of crops breaks the life cycles of soil pests and diseases that target specific plant families. It also balances soil nutrients, as different plants feed on and return different minerals to the ground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ Efiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ tsei awekui pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ lɛ ashihilɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso henɔ fɛɛ tso yeɔ nibii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ekɛkuɔ sɛɛ ekɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the roots of my young plants growing swollen knobs and bumps?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ efu ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Swollen bumps on roots are caused by tiny microscopic worms called root-knot nematodes. They attack the root system, preventing the plant from taking up water and food, which leads to stunted growth.
ga: Kɔlɔji bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ root-knot nematodes lɛ kɛ shishifãi fuumɔ baa. Amɛtutuaa shishifãi lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná nu kɛ niyenii. ni haa dalɛ kpaa

english: What causes a white, powdery substance to spread across my plant leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa nɔ ko ni tamɔ powda yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa mitsei lɛ baai lɛ anɔ?

english: This white coating is a fungal disease called powdery mildew. It thrives in warm, humid weather with poor air movement, blocking sunlight from the leaf surface and weakening the plant.
ga: Nɛkɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni eyaaa jogbaŋŋ Etsiɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ naa ni ehaa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ

english: Why should I trim the main top shoot of my young fruit tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi tsei bibii lɛ ashishifã titri lɛ?

english: Cutting the main top stem stops the tree from growing only tall and thin. It encourages side branches to spread out, creating a stronger structure that can hold more fruit and make harvesting easier.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ yiteŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shwereɔ ni ehaaa efee mlɛo. Eyeɔ ebuaa niji ni yɔɔ afã lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa. Bɔɔ tsɔne ni mli wa ni baanyɛ ahiɛ aduawai babaoo ni eha ŋmaakpamɔ afee mlɛo

english: Soil testing shows you what nutrients are already present in your field so you know exactly what your crops need, rather than guessing and wasting money.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa baatsɔɔ bo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ole nɔ tuuntu ni he hiaa oŋmɔshi nibii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooosusu he ni ofite shika

english: How do officers take a soil sample from my farm to test it?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni onukpai lɛ abua shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii anaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛka amɛkwɛ?

english: Small scoops of dirt are collected from different spots across your field and mixed together to get a clear picture of your land's chemical balance.
ga: Abuaa muji bibii anaa kɛjɛɔ hei srɔtoi. oŋmɔji lɛ fɛɛ nɔ ni okɛfutu mli koni ona tsofai ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he mfoniri ni mli ka shi faŋŋ.

english: How often do I need to test the soil on my farm?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni maka shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ makwɛ?

english: It is best to test your soil every two to three years, or whenever you notice your crop yields are dropping despite good care.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooka oshikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ daa afii enyɔ loo etɛ, loo be fɛɛ be ni obaana akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayibɔ eba shi yɛ bɔ ni okwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: What is the best time of year for me to collect soil samples from my field?
ga: Mɛɛ afi lɛ mli be hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaabua shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best time is after harvest or a few months before the planting season begins, before you apply any new manure or chemicals.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ loo nyɔji fioo komɛi dani ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ aje shishi. Dani obaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai heei afata he

english: My farm soil looks dark and rich, so why do I still need to test it?
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli ewo duŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maka lɛ makwɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Dark soil usually has good organic matter, but it might still lack specific chemical nutrients that your crops need to produce high yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ fɔɔ nibii kpakpai ni wala yɔɔ mli. Shi ebɛ tsofai pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ lolo.

english: Can I just buy any popular fertilizer from the market and put it on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mahe ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehe gbɛi waa yɛ jara nɔ ni mikɛwo miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, because applying fertilizer without knowing what is already in your soil can harm your crops, waste your money, or add chemicals your ground does not need.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oleee nɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli momo lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ŋmɔshi nibii awui, efite shika, loo ekɛ tsofai ni he ehiaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ afata he.

english: What happens to my land if I put too much chemical fertilizer on my soil?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsofai babaoo wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Adding too many chemicals can burn crop roots, make the soil too acidic or salty, and prevent plants from absorbing water properly.
ga: Tsofa babaoo ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi ashã. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ acid loo ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ. ni etsĩ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Do chemical fertilizers from last season stay in my soil, or do they all wash away?
ga: Ani tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni jɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo loo nu lɛ efo mli kwraa?

english: Some chemical nutrients stay in the ground for a long time while others wash away with rain, which is why testing shows what remains before you add more.
ga: Tsofa mli niyenii komɛi hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ, be mli ni nugbɔ hoɔ ekrokomɛi kɛyaa. Nɔ ni haa kaa lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ni eshwɛ dani okɛfataa he lɛ.

english: How can I know the exact amount of fertilizer to put on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛwo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A soil test reveals which nutrients are missing, allowing extension officers to give you the exact quantity and type of fertilizer your field needs.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa jieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni elaaje lɛ kpo. Enɛ haa mɔ ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa bo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayibɔ pɔtɛɛ kɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ mli.

english: Why are my crops turning yellow even after I poured fertilizer on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo ŋmɔji lɛ amli po lɛ?

english: If your soil already had high levels of certain chemicals, adding more can block your plants from absorbing nutrients properly or damage their roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsofai komɛi ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fa babaoo momo lɛ, Tsofai komɛi ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ loo efite shishifãi lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential plant food. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green again so the crop can grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist and the plants are actively growing, usually right after the first good rains. Applying fertilizer during a dry drought or right before a heavy downpour can waste it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ebaafee nɔ ni fiteɔ nii.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, damp conditions. Pruning extra shade branches to let in sunlight and air helps dry out the farm and prevents the pods from rotting.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ akafiteɔ.

english: What are these tiny caterpillars eating holes in the center of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ ni yeɔ nakai bu ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that destroys maize. They hide inside the center funnel of the plant, so applying recommended control sprays or neem extract directly into the center early in the morning can stop them.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni fiteɔ ŋmãa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faa lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛbuɔ hela lɛ he loo neem ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ wo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa amɛ.

english: Yes, always make sure the small leaf buds on the stem cut are pointing upward toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the roots and shoots will struggle to grow, resulting in very low tuber yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, kwɛmɔ be fɛɛ be akɛ ŋmeii lɛ afee bibii. Yɛ tso ni afo lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ baawa akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni anáa lɛ faaa kwraa.

english: Too many young shoots compete with the main plant for food, sunlight, and water. Keeping only one or two strong suckers allows the main stem to focus its energy on growing a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama plantain tsei wuji ni tsii ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise me to plant groundnuts or beans on my plot after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and fix it naturally back into the ground. Planting them after maize restores soil nutrients so your next crop will grow better without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛsaa lɛ ekoŋŋ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fataaa he.

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dried leaves or straw help my plants?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi shwie miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ?

english: This practice is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket that keeps the soil cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly in the sun, and stops weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up and curl during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a survival trick plants use to save water. By curling their leaves, they reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun, preventing moisture from escaping until temperatures cool down.
ga: Baai ni atsiɔ lɛ ji wala yiwalaheremɔ ŋaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ baa shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaje mli kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baa shi.

english: Why are the bottoms of my developing tomatoes turning black and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato shishi ni miiya hiɛ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efee blɛoo lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often brought on by irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist with steady watering prevents this damage.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ.

english: If it rains early in March, should I start planting my seeds right away?
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ March shishijee gbɛ lɛ, ani esa akɛ mije dumɔwui adumɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Not always. Early rains in March can sometimes be a false start followed by weeks of dry weather, which can dry up and kill newly planted seeds. It is best to wait until the rainfall becomes consistent before planting.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be, bei komɛi lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ March shishijee gbɛ lɛ baanyɛ afee amale shishijee. Nɔ ni nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ ji otsii babaoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa dani odu.

english: Why is the rainy season changing and not starting at the usual time like it used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ tsakeɔ ni ejeee shishi yɛ be ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Changes in global weather patterns, known as climate change, cause rainfall schedules to shift. This means rains can start earlier or later than expected, making traditional farming calendars unpredictable.
ga: Tsakemɔi ni baa jeŋ muu fɛɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ tsakeɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔ baanyɛ aje shishi mra loo sɛɛ mli fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ blema okwaayeli kalandai lɛ.

english: What happens to my maize seeds if a sudden dry spell occurs right after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna ŋmɔlɔ trukaa beni midu amɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: If a dry spell hits after planting, seeds may fail to germinate, or young seedlings will wither and die from lack of moisture, requiring you to buy new seeds and plant again.
ga: Kɛji hɔmɔ shihilɛi ba yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ Ekolɛ dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃. Aloo tso bibioo lɛ baagbo ni ebaagbo yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa ehe bahiaa ni ohé dumɔwui heei ni okɛdu ekoŋŋ.

english: Is heavy rain early in the farming season good or bad for my crops?
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ okwaayeli be lɛ shishijee mli Ani ehi loo ehiii kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: While rain is necessary, excessive early rain can wash away topsoil, flood seedbeds, rot seeds before they sprout, and wash away fertilizers before plants can use them.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ he miihia moŋ Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine mra lɛ baanyɛ ahoo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ashishi nu ni hoɔ Dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsu nii dani tsei lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: How do I know if my crops are wilting because of too much heat or because of a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ latsaa babaoo hewɔ loo hela hewɔ?

english: Heat wilting usually happens during the hottest part of the afternoon and plants recover by morning. Disease wilting causes plants to stay droopy, turn yellow, or dry up permanently regardless of the temperature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, latsaa ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baa yɛ shwane mli be ni latsaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli. Ni tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ leebi. Wilt hela lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi. tsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo egbi daa ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ he

english: How can I protect my soil from drying out too fast when there is no rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya tsɔ beni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: You can cover the soil around your plants with dry grass, straw, or leaves. This practice, called mulching, keeps the soil cool and traps moisture in the ground for a longer time.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Abaanyɛ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, jwɛi, loo baai akwɛ tsei. Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow after a long period of continuous rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Continuous rain can saturate the soil, suffocating plant roots so they cannot breathe or absorb nutrients. Heavy rains also wash essential nutrients like nitrogen deeper into the soil, out of reach of the roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ. ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi Enɛ haa amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu loo amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu hoɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ, kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Are there seed types I can buy that will yield well even if the rain stops early?
ga: Ani dumɔwui srɔtoi komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ mahe ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai aba kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra po?

english: Yes, there are fast-maturing and drought-tolerant seed varieties available that require less water and mature quickly before dry weather sets in.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui komɛi yɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ nu hɔmɔ naa, ni nu fioo pɛ he hiaa amɛ, ni amɛdaraa oya dani kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ.

english: Why are my crop yields lower than before even though I am farming on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ baa shi fe tsutsu lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ miitsu nii moŋ?

english: Unpredictable rainfall patterns, combined with soil nutrient loss over time, stress crops during key growing stages, leading to smaller harvests if soil management and planting times are not adjusted.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ nɔ haomɔ baa yɛ be mli ni ekwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ. Enɛ haa nikpamɔ faaa. Kɛji akɛ atsakeee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ dumɔ be lɛ mli

english: What can I do on my field to catch and store rainwater for my plants when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mabua nugbɔ nu lɛ naa ni mikɛto mitsei lɛ ahe kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa?

english: You can dig small basins around plants or build low soil ridges across slopes to slow down rainwater, allowing it to soak deep into the soil instead of running off your field.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsɛnsi bibioo ko abɔle tso lɛ he loo ofee ŋshɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ. Fo ŋshɔ lɛ naa koni nugbɔ nu lɛ aba shi. Ha ni ekɛ ehe awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni eeejo foi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How much of my farm land should I set aside for food crops instead of cocoa?
ga: Miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ mlijaa enyiɛ esa akɛ mato kɛha niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ kookoo najiaŋ?

english: Dividing your farm so that a portion (such as one-third) is reserved for food crops like cassava or plantain ensures your family has food to eat while your long-term cash crops like cocoa grow and mature over the years.
ga: Kɛ́ oja oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ fã ko (akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, mlijaa etɛ mli ekome) ni okɛtoɔ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa oweku lɛ náa niyenii ni amɛyeɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shika ni anáa be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ kookoo lɛ daa ni edara yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli.

english: Should I plant my whole farm with cocoa at the same time or divide it up over time?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu kookoo ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ shikome loo majara mli yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Dividing your farm into different sections and planting them gradually helps you manage your work better and guarantees a continuous, steady yield over a ten-year period rather than having all your trees age out at once.
ga: Kɛ́ ojara oŋmɔ lɛ mli owo fãi amli ni odu fiofio lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni okwɛ onitsumɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni eha nɔmimaa akɛ abaaya nɔ afee nibii ni yaa nɔ daa kɛyashi afii nyɔŋma. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha otsei lɛ fɛɛ agbɔ shikome lɛ.

english: Why is cocoa considered a long-term investment compared to food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abuɔ kookoo akɛ eji shika ni akɛwoɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ kɛ akɛtoɔ niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Food crops like maize and vegetables give you quick harvests within months, while cocoa trees take several years to mature but can continue producing pods for ten years or more if well maintained.
ga: Niyenii nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ aduawai haa onáa ŋmãa oya yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛdaraa. Shi amɛbaanyɛ amɛya nɔ amɛwo ŋmeii afii nyɔŋma kroko loo nɔ ni fe nakai kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to clear and cut weeds in a circle around each cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kooloo ko mabɔle cacao tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ?

english: Clearing a clean ring around the base of each tree stops weeds from stealing moisture and nutrients, and prevents crawling pests from climbing up to destroy your young cocoa pods.
ga: Ring ni he tse ni ebɔle Tso fɛɛ tso shishi lɛ he saamɔ tsiɔ jwɛi naa koni ekaju ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. ni etsĩɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkahole amɛhe ni amɛfite o-cocoa ŋmɔji bibii lɛ.

english: What happens if I don't clear the bush surrounding my cocoa farm boundary?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mijieee jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Mɛni ji mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli shweremɔ?

english: If you leave thick bush along the edges of your farm, pests and diseases like pod borers or black pod can easily cross over into your farm and wipe out your entire harvest.
ga: Kɛji oshi jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai tamɔ pod borer loo black pod borer baanyɛ afo kɛba oŋmɔ lɛ mli oya ni amɛfite onibii fɛɛ.

english: How does clearing a wide border around my cocoa farm protect it during the dry season?
ga: He ko ni da ni ebɔle he lɛ mli ni ajieɔ Te mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cutting back weeds and brush around your farm perimeter creates a barrier that stops bushfires from jumping into your land and destroying your long-term crop investment.
ga: Jwɛi ni afoɔ kɛ jwɛi ni akɛshwieɔ shi Oŋmɔ lɛ baafee gbɛtsii nii ko ni baatsi koo mli la ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa ni efiteɔ onibii ni okɛwoɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ.

english: Can I plant plantain and cassava on the same plot where I am growing young cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu plantains kɛ cassava yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo bibii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting food crops alongside young cocoa provides shade to protect the delicate seedlings from hot sun while giving you food and income during the cocoa's early non-bearing years.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baaha hulutsoo be aba koni ebu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii kɛ shika yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli beni afeee kookoo lɛ.

english: How do I make sure my food crops don't starve my cocoa trees of nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa baaa mi-cacao tsei lɛ amli?

english: Spacing your food crops properly and keeping them a safe distance from the cocoa tree roots ensures both crops get enough soil food without competing directly against each other.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ oniyenii tsei lɛ to he jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ kookoo shishifãi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛkɛ amɛhe akaŋ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods if I let branches grow too wild around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛji miha niji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ fee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Unpruned trees waste their energy on excess leaves and shade out sunlight; cutting back unnecessary growth directs the tree's strength into producing healthy pods for many years.
ga: Tsei ni afolɔɔɔ amɛhe lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ yɛ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Kɛ́ afo tso ni he ehiaaa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ekɛwo ŋmeii ni mli wa afii babaoo ni baa lɛ.

english: How can I make sure my cocoa farm stays healthy and productive for ten years or more?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii afii nyɔŋma loo nɔ ni fe nakai?

english: Consistent ring-weeding, timely pruning, protecting crop borders from pests, and balancing your farm land with food crops keep your soil healthy and sustain high cocoa yields over a long period.
ga: Ring jwɛi lɛ ahe jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa Be ni sa mli Buu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe husui ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ahe kɛ oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa kookoo yibii babaoo yaa hiɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Officer, why is it important for me to trim or prune the leaves near the base of my crops?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ baai ni bɛŋkɛ mitso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Pruning the lower leaves prevents pests and soil-borne diseases from jumping onto your crop. It also helps the plant direct its nutrients upward to produce stronger stems and better yields.
ga: Kɛ́ ofolɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akabote onibii amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ hu ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ŋwɛi koni ekɛfee shishifãi ni wa ni ewo yibii kpakpai.

english: Does cutting off extra shoots near the bottom of my plant help it produce better fruit?
ga: Ani tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ lɛ haa aduawai woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, removing lower side shoots stops the plant from wasting energy on extra leaves. This allows the crop to send maximum strength and nutrients toward developing bigger fruits or pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haaa tso lɛ afite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii kpakpai babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛyaa aduawai loo ŋmeii wuji ni baa lɛ amli.

english: I see some farmers putting plastic sheets on the ground around their crops; what does that actually do for the plant?
ga: Mina okwaafoi komɛi ni kɛ plastic tsɔji ewo shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni no feɔ tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Covering the ground around crops with plastic sheets traps moisture in the soil so the soil stays wet longer. It also blocks sunlight from reaching weed seeds, stopping weeds from choking your plants.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ plastic ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle onibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ. Etsiɔ hulu la hu naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkafite otsei lɛ.

english: Why does soil covered with plastic or mulch stay wet longer than bare farm ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ plastic loo ŋmɔtɔ ehà nɔ lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ fe ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses water quickly because the hot sun causes water to evaporate into the air. Covering the ground creates a barrier that holds the water in the soil right where the plant roots need it.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nu fiteɔ oya ejaakɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Mulching lɛ feɔ gbɛtsii nii ko ni tsiɔ nu naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi he hiaa yɛ lɛ.

english: What is the simplest way to prevent weeds from growing right around my crop stems?
ga: Gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ yɛ he fɛɛ he. Mɛni ji mi tsɔne lɛ?

english: Clearing the soil at the base of the stem and covering that area with ground cover or plastic mulch prevents weed seeds from getting the light they need to grow, keeping the base of your crops clean.
ga: Kɛ́ asaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo plastic ŋmɔtɔ ha he lɛ, ebaatsi jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa la ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ. ni oha otso lɛ shishitoo lɛ he atse

english: How long does it take for a young seedling to adapt and start growing after I plant it in the farm?
ga: Beni adu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani dumɔwu ko baanyɛ atsake ehe ni ebɔi dalɛ?

english: If the soil is moist and properly prepared, most young seedlings recover from transplanting and settle into the soil within just two to three days.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni asaa he jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ babaoo baaná hewalɛ kɛjɛ amɛdumɔ mli ni amɛbaahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ mli.

english: How do I safely remove seedlings from plastic nursery bags without damaging them during planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ majie dumɔwui ni yɔɔ plastic ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli shweshweeshwe ni mifiteee amɛ yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Carefully cut or slip off the plastic bag so the soil ball surrounding the roots stays unbroken. Keeping the root area intact helps the plant settle quickly into the ground without dying.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ loo okɛ plastic kotoku lɛ awo mli jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni sũ ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ akagbala. Kɛ́ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ hi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya ni egbooo.

english: After I finish planting seedlings out of plastic nursery bags, should I collect the bags or leave them on the farm?
ga: Beni midu dumɔwui kɛjɛ plastic ŋmɔ mli kotokui amli sɛɛ lɛ, Ani esa akɛ mikɛ kotoku lɛ ahi shi loo mashi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should always collect all plastic nursery bags from the field. Plastic does not rot in the soil, and leaving it behind blocks future root growth and harms the soil quality.
ga: Esa akɛ obua plastic gbekɛbii askul kotokui anaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Plastic lɛ fiteee yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni baai ni shwieɔ sɛɛ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa wɔsɛɛ ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii.

english: Why should I mark out set paths and walk in organized rows when setting up my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mato gbɛ ni atsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni manyiɛ yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli beni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ toɔ lɛ?

english: Planting in organized rows and paths ensures each crop gets enough sunlight and space to grow. It also prevents you from accidentally stepping on young plants when weeding or spraying.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ kɛ gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ fɛo nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛdaa. Etsiɔ bo gbɛ hu koni okashɛ tsei bibii ahe yɛ oshara mli beni okɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shi loo okɛ tsofa miishwie nɔ lɛ.

english: How does keeping my farm pathways clean and clear help my crops stay healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe tsemɔ ni mli tse lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Clear pathways allow air to flow freely across the field, which reduces crop diseases. Clean paths also make it easier for you to move around and prevent dangerous pests like snakes from hiding near your crops.
ga: Gbɛ ni mli tse lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya. ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii amli helai baa shi Gbɛ ni he tse hu haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa bo akɛ oooya he fɛɛ he. ni otsi kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara tamɔ onufui lɛ anaa koni amɛkatee amɛhe yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I start my seeds in a nursery instead of planting them directly into my main farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui akwɛmɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu nii yɛ miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ

english: Nursing seeds in a protected space allows young plants to grow strong, healthy stems and roots away from harsh field conditions, heavy rains, and pests before they are exposed to the main field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ hei ni abuɔ he lɛ haa tsei bibii daa waa, amɛshishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni wa. Shihilɛi ni mli wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui dani eshɛ he titri lɛ he.

english: How long do I need to keep my seeds in the nursery before they are ready for the field?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ makɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahi ŋmɔ mli dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaadu?

english: Most seeds need a standard nursing period, usually around 6 weeks, so that the seedlings can sprout properly and mature enough to handle transplanting.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo biɔ tsɔsemɔ be ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ aaafee otsii 6 dani dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu amɛ.

english: Why do my seedlings sometimes fail to grow well when I sow seeds straight into hard soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ midumɔwui lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Direct soil planting makes it hard for young seeds to break through tough dirt and form roots. Starting them in a nursery gives them soft, nutrient-rich soil so every part of the plant develops beautifully.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa dumɔwui bibii lɛ akɛ amɛaabote shikpɔŋ ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛfee shishifãi. Tsei ni ajeɔ shishi yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo aba mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã kwɛ̃ɔ fɛfɛo.

english: Does taking care of seeds in a nursery early on really change my final harvest?
ga: Dumɔwui akwɛmɔ mra yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsakeɔ mi naagbee ŋmaa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, proper early nursery care ensures that your crops develop strong root systems and uniform growth, which directly improves crop quality and overall yield at harvest time.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbekɛbii askul mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ dalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ yibiiwoo fɛɛ yaa hiɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: What is the advantage of nursing my crop seeds in seed trays instead of on a nursery bed on the ground?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ mi aduawai dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ dumɔwui atoohei amli moŋ fe ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he?

english: Seed trays give each plant its own individual space, allowing the roots to develop into strong, neatly formed root balls without tangling with neighboring plants.
ga: Dumɔwui atoohei haa tso fɛɛ tso naa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛhe. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi akui ni wa, ni yɔɔ fɛo ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ ebɔko amɛhe.

english: How does nursing help my young plants grow better roots?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔsemɔ baanyɛ aye abua mi dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛná shishifãi kpakpai?

english: In a nursery setting, soil conditions are kept loose and moist, which makes it easy for delicate early roots to spread out, absorb water, and build a solid foundation.
ga: yɛ daycare lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shishijee shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã, amɛmɔmɔ nu, ni amɛfee shishitoo ni ma shi shiŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my seedlings in the nursery have developed enough to be transplanted?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ aŋɔwo amɛ?

english: Seedlings are ready to move to your field when they have spent the required weeks in the nursery and have developed strong, visible root clusters and healthy green leaves.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu amɛ awo oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ́ amɛye otsii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni ená shishifãi akui ni mli wa ni anaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni mli wa.

english: If I receive high-quality seeds distributed by the government, do I still need to nurse them?
ga: Kɛji minine shɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ kɛjɛ nɔyeli lɛ dɛŋ Ani ehe miihia ni makwɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lolo?

english: Yes, even improved government-supplied seeds perform much better when nursed first, as this gives the high-quality genetic traits inside the seeds the best environment to sprout and thrive.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni nɔyeli lɛ kɛhaa ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ po tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kwraa kɛji akɛ atsa amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehaa su ni hi fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli lɛ kɛ shihilɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha shweremɔ kɛ dalɛ.

english: What can I do in the nursery to make sure all my seeds germinate and grow evenly?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni midumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛdara pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Using consistent nursery soil, proper shade, and seedling trays ensures that every seed receives equal moisture and care, resulting in beautiful, uniform plant growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ haa hulutsoo ni sa Ni dumɔwui atoohe lɛ baaha dumɔwui fɛɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kwɛmɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ náa fɛo ni amɛdaraa po.

english: Will using seed trays make it easier for me to transplant my crops without damaging them?
ga: Ani dumɔwui atoohei ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaha efee mlɛo aha mi akɛ madu tsei ni mifiteee amɛ?

english: Yes, crops grown in seed trays can be popped out easily with their soil and root structure intact, preventing root shock and stress when you plant them in the main farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ dumɔwui atoohei amli lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ oya ni shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ efiteee. Tsi shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi kɛ haomɔ naa beni oduɔ nii yɛ oŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to produce green leaves and grow strong. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have tiny beneficial organisms on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil, acting as a natural food source for the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi ni heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why do my maize crops produce small cobs when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants compete against each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space allows it to get enough resources to make large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ tso agbo ni mli wa.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with tall sticks instead of letting them lie on the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu sweet potato wain tsei ni tsei kakadaji yɔɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha ekã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food that feeds the growing tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil into the air and sun, which increases tuber size and prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la mli. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa foliar helai baaa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets extremely hot, when there is not enough water in the soil, or when the plant lacks key nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ehi shi pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots get soft and rot inside the ground when there is heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Excess rain causes water to sit around the roots, blocking air from reaching them and creating conditions where soil fungus thrives. Without air in the soil, cassava roots drown and decay.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ he ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni baanyɛ aha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ adara Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ Cassava shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi.

english: What is causing ragged holes to appear in the top leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa bu ni mli ewo muji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Holes in the center leaves of young maize are typically caused by leaf-eating pests like the Fall Armyworm. They hide in the soft center roll of the plant and chew the new leaves before they open up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ baa, tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai heei dani amɛgbeleɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and burn easily under harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, protecting young cocoa from hot sun and dry winds.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ shãa oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants roll up during the hottest hours of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl inward during intense heat to reduce the amount of surface area exposed to the sun, which stops water from evaporating out of the plant too quickly.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ latsaa be mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ.

english: Why should I avoid placing fertilizer right against the stem of my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated salts that can burn tender plant stems and shallow roots if placed directly against them. Placing fertilizer a short distance away allows the roots to safely draw in the nutrients.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko lɛ yɛ mli kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli tɛ̃ɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ he ko ni jɛkɛɛɛ fioo lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai amɛwoɔ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tip down to the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ eshishigbɛ kɛmiiya teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tips usually means your soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to make leaves green and build strong stems.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛma tsei ahe tsei ni wa.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with bushy leaves but produce very small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tsei lɛ kɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, amɛtsɔɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ gbɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms fall off the plant before turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or inconsistent watering, which prevents proper pollination from taking place.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa amɛfee pollination jogbaŋŋ.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the juices from underneath the leaf, which distorts its growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni kɛ dalɛ ni ejaaa baa

english: Why do I need to cut away extra suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Leaving too many suckers allows them to steal water and food from the main mother plant, resulting in smaller plantain bunches at harvest time.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, plantains lɛ baafee bibii yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes helps the leaves catch more sunlight to feed the crop while keeping the leaves off wet soil to prevent fungal rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo ni amɛkɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni ŋmeii akafite.

english: Why do leaves on my young cocoa seedlings burn and dry up when planted in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that cannot handle direct harsh sunlight, so they need shade from plants like plantains until their roots and branches mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni kookoo tsei lɛ aná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains adɛŋ kɛyashi amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛniji lɛ baadara.

english: Why do farmers plant cowpeas or beans together with maize on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ tsina loo ŋmeii kɛfataa ŋmãa he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, which helps feed the nearby maize and keeps the soil fertile.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni aha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ niyenii ni eye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my young oil palm trees produce flowers that don't yield any fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tɛŋ tsei bibii fɔɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Young oil palms produce male flowers first to release pollen before they are old enough to produce female flowers, which are the ones that grow into fruit bunches.
ga: Mu tso dumɔwui woɔ fɔfɔi hii klɛŋklɛŋ ni amɛjieɔ pollen dani amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi yei ni daa ni amɛfeɔ aduawai akui.

english: Why does paddy rice need to stay flooded with water while it is growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ aŋɔ nu be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: Flooding fields smothers weeds naturally and ensures the shallow roots of the rice plant stay wet enough to easily absorb nutrients from the soil.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ jieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya.

english: Why should I avoid burning the leaves and grass on my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ baai kɛ jwɛi ni ashãa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu nii lɛ he?

english: Burning destroys the rich organic matter and nutrients in the soil that crops need to feed on. Leaving the plant materials to decompose naturally creates dark, fertile soil and holds water much better.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehe hiaa ni tsei aye lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei ahe nibii fite yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni hiɛɔ nu jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow tall, thin, and weak, resulting in very small or missing maize cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa ŋmãa bibii waa loo amɛbɛ ŋmãa.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the maize plant is hungry, usually lacking a key nutrient called nitrogen. Applying the right fertilizer early in the plant's growth will make the leaves green and help it produce big cobs.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye ŋmãa tsei lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, niyenii ko ni he hiaa ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen lɛ bɛ amɛmli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo tso lɛ mli mra yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni eye ebua ni ŋmeii wuji lɛ aba.

english: Planting maize in the same spot every season drains the soil of the specific nutrients maize needs and allows pests to build up in the soil. Rotating with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nutrients naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How do I know when my cassava is fully grown and ready for harvesting under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the base of the plant starts to crack open as the tubers expand beneath the surface.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or too much fertilizer. Keeping the soil evenly moist and mulched helps the flowers stay on the plant and turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow and spread much faster than my main crops after a rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally built to absorb water and nutrients much faster than domestic crops. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing the food and water your crops need to survive.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni abɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya fe shia tsei. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa oŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛhi shi lɛ.

english: Black spots are caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which loves heavy shade and moisture. Pruning extra tree branches to let in sunlight and air helps dry out the pods and stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Pod, ni sumɔɔ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji krokomɛi amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ ni ehaa helai gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: In the hot sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the soil, causing them to temporarily droop. Mulching around the roots with dry grass helps keep the soil cool and moist all day.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and drying up in the full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct heat and sunlight. They need temporary shade from fast-growing plants like plantains or shade trees to protect their leaves and keep the soil moist while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Enɛ buɔ baai lɛ ahe ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow from the center while the plants stay short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ yɛ kuku lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually show that the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the food plants need to stay dark green and grow tall. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii kɛha tsei ni miisumɔ ni amɛfee eŋɔli ni amɛdara lɛ. Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa dalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people tell me to cover the bare soil around my crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi yaa nɔ amɛkɛɛɔ mi akɛ mikɛ sũ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni ebɔle ehe lɛ awo mli lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ jwɛi?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or dead leaves, called mulching, keeps the soil cool under the sun, holds moisture longer so you don't need as much rain, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la shishi. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ No hewɔ lɛ nugbɔ babaoo he ehiaaa bo. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with small green dirt inside the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etse kɛ muji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Yɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: Holes in leaves accompanied by green droppings mean Fall Armyworm caterpillars are eating the growing heart of the plant. Detecting this early allows you to control the pest before it destroys the whole crop.
ga: Bu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmɔtɔi lɛ miiye tso lɛ tsui ni miida lɛ. mra be mli Ehaa onyɛɔ oyeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and covered with sticky white spots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Curled leaves with white sticky residue are caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or mealybugs sucking juices from the plant. This weakens the cassava and prevents the roots from swelling into large tubers.
ga: Baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ nɔ ko ni shwieɔ shi yɛŋ ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mealybugs ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ kɛbaa. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are my tomatoes developing black rotten spots on the bottom while they are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɔɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lolo lɛ?

english: Black rotten patches on the bottom of green tomatoes happen when the plant isn't getting enough calcium or when water in the soil goes dry and wet unevenly during fruit development.
ga: Black rot ni yɔɔ tomato eŋɔli shishi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ gĩ ni efɔ shi yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ aduawai lɛ akwɛmɔ be mli.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my maize in neat straight lines instead of scattering seeds across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo ni ja nɔ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in measured rows gives every single plant enough light, air, and room to drink soil nutrients without competing with neighboring plants, and it makes weeding much faster.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ he ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛnuɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ. Ni ejieɔ jwɛi oya kwraa.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients away from the main mother tree. Removing most of them lets the main plant focus all its energy on growing one heavy, high-quality bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie mɛi babaoo lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aye ehe koni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama plantains ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ akuu ko ni eduɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Peppers and tomatoes belong to the same crop family and suffer from the same pests and soil diseases. Planting them right after each other lets those diseases multiply in the ground and attack the new crop.
ga: Pepper kɛ tomato yɛ tso weku kome mli ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛyɔɔ sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai kome. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ baaha nakai helai lɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtutua ŋmɔshi nibii heei.

english: Groundnuts are legumes that capture natural nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots rot after harvest, they release this free fertilizer into the soil for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛbaajie nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for green leaves. Applying manure or urea fertilizer will supply the required nutrients to make the leaves green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo urea fata he lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is my cowpea crop growing plenty of green leaves but not producing any beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewooo ŋmeii ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes cowpea plants to focus all their energy on growing tall stems and thick leaves instead of flowers and pods. Avoid using high-nitrogen fertilizers on leguminous crops so they can produce fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni mli tse ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ Tsi ohe kɛjɛ nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ he koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when the weather is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn quickly under intense direct sunlight. They require fast-growing shade plants like plantains or temporary shade trees to shield them from excessive heat and conserve soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo oya, tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Enɛ ji koni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he, ni koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures become extremely hot or when watering is irregular. The heat causes stress to the plant, making it shed its blossoms to conserve energy for survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ nu lɛ efɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Dɔlɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Ha tsei lɛ afee fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha wala.

english: Cassava roots require air in the soil to remain healthy. Waterlogged soil caused by heavy rain deprives the roots of oxygen, creating conditions for bacteria and fungi to thrive and rot the roots.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛbaa lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni bacteria kɛ fungi baanyɛ adara ni amɛfite lɛ baa.

english: Curled and twisted leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or a viral disease transmitted by these insects. Controlling the insects using recommended organic or chemical sprays helps prevent this leaf curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo helai ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Kooloi ahe nitsumɔ kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akafee baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi.

english: How do I know when my yam tubers are ready for harvesting after planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When the yam vines and leaves stop growing green and turn completely yellow and dry, it indicates that the plant has transferred all its energy to the underground tuber, signaling that the yam is fully mature and ready to harvest.
ga: Beni sweet potato wain tsei kɛ baai lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kwraa ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ etee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Groundnut flowers bloom above ground, but after pollination, the plant grows a stalk called a peg that grows downward into the soil. The actual groundnut pod develops and ripens under the dirt to stay protected.
ga: Peanut fɔfɔii fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi yɛ pollination sɛɛ Tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bean ŋmɔji lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi kɛha hebuu.

english: Why does my main plantain tree yield small bunches when there are many young shoots around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso titri lɛ woɔ aduawai bibii bibii lɛ? Akɛni ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ he fɛɛ he hewɔ lɛ

english: The small shoots, or suckers, growing around the main plantain tree compete with the mother plant for nutrients, sunlight, and water. Pruning away extra suckers leaves energy for the main stem to yield larger, heavier fruit bunches.
ga: ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Dumɔwu titri lɛ kɛ tso nyɛ lɛ baatswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa hewalɛ babaoo baa tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ nɔ koni ekɛwo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are my oil palm trees producing only male flowers and no palm nut bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi hii pɛ ni ŋmeii akui ko bɛ lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees produce male flowers instead of female fruit-bearing flowers when they experience severe drought or nutrient stress. Providing adequate water and proper fertilizer encourages the trees to produce female flowers that grow into fruit bunches.
ga: Mu tsei woɔ fɔfɔi hii yɛ fɔfɔi yei najiaŋ kɛ́ amɛna hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ he haomɔ. Nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi yei ni daa ni amɛfeɔ aduawai akui.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong direct sunlight and can burn easily. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide shade and keep the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be mli ni kookoo bibii lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key food the plant uses to make leaves green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛ baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, lack of regular watering, or a lack of insects like bees to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛhaaa daa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollin lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips hiding underneath the leaves and sucking out the plant's juices, causing twisted growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni kɛ dalɛ ni ejaaa baa

english: Why do my crops produce smaller fruits when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots fight over the same water and nutrients in the dirt, and their leaves block sunlight from each other, leaving less energy to grow large fruits.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haaa hewalɛ ni akɛduɔ aduawai wuji lɛ faaa.

english: Why does cassava manage to stay green and grow even when there is no rain for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots store water and food deep underground, and the plant can shed some of its leaves to reduce water loss during dry weather.
ga: Cassava shishifãi kɛ nu kɛ niyenii toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Ni tsei baanyɛ ajie amɛbaai lɛ ekomɛi ashwie shi koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant cowpea on the same field where I previously harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmãa yɛ mli tsutsu lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that fix nitrogen from the air into the dirt, naturally enriching the soil with nutrients that the next crop can feed on.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak even if I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and will steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight before your crops get a chance to use them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo. Ni ebaaju ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in the sunlight to produce the food energy required to grow big tubers underground, and climbing stakes helps them catch the maximum light.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã hulu la lɛ mli koni ekɛ niyenii hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛwo bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba. Ni tso lɛ nɔ kwɔɔ haa anyɛɔ ajieɔ ehe kpo babaoo.

english: Why does adding dried chicken manure to my farm help my soil stay moist longer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ tsina ŋmei ni egbi fata miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Chicken manure adds organic matter to the soil, which acts like a sponge to hold onto rainwater and slow down how fast the sun dries out the ground.
ga: Kooloo ŋmei kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni emɔɔ nugbɔ nu ni ehaa oyaiyeli ni hulu lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade to protect their soft leaves from harsh sun exposure while their root systems develop, which is why farmers plant them under temporary shade crops like plantains or under tall canopy trees.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo koni amɛkɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni okwaafoi duɔ kookoo yɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋwɛi lɛ ashishi lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show a lack of nitrogen in the soil. The maize plant naturally pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves and sends it to the newer top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abɛi jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli ni ekɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei amli koni eya nɔ eda.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my plot make my next harvest of corn grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmãa ni makpa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants have small nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and convert it into rich fertilizer in the soil, which feeds whatever crop you plant after them.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ yɛ bɔɔt bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni oduɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my cassava produce very tall, leafy stems but small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni eyɛ baai lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants are spaced too close together, cassava puts all its energy into growing branches and leaves above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen babaoo loo tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Yucca kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa tsei niji kɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do my yam tubers stay thin and weak if I do not clear weeds early in the season?
