ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ amli tsei ni amɛhe waaa kɛji mikɛ jwɛi shwieee amɛ nɔ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with young yam vines for water and soil food during the early tuber forming stage, stealing the energy the yam needs to bulk up under the soil.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ sweet potato wain tsei bibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli yɛ shishijee bei ni tuber lɛ feɔ lɛ mli. ni juɔ hewalɛ ni he hiaa ni sweet potato lɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants drying up and falling off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry spells cause heat stress in tomatoes, preventing pollen from fertilizing the flowers, which causes the plant to drop its blossoms to conserve energy and water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ kɛ dɔlɛ haomɔ baa tomato mli. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ fɔmɔ nii. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ baa fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown and soft on the tree during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High humidity and wet leaves allow fungal spores—commonly called black pod disease—to spread quickly from pod to pod, causing them to rot before ripening.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ haa fungal spores, ni afɔɔ lɛ tsɛmɔ akɛ black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgboiɔ dani amɛbaa.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling inward and staying small instead of spreading open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli ni amɛfeɔ bibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the leaf sap and spreading plant viruses, which stunts leaf growth and twists their shape.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tso lɛ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Enɛ haaa baai lɛ adara ni efiteɔ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ha lɛ.

english: Why do I see ragged holes in my corn leaves and caterpillars inside the young shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa baai amli kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that feeds on the central growing shoot of maize plants, eating through leaves before they fully unfold.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa ni miida yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai lɛ dani amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa kwraa.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop in the afternoon even when the soil is still damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: During peak afternoon heat, leaves lose water into the air faster than roots can absorb it, causing temporary wilting to protect the plant until temperatures drop in the evening.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa fe fɛɛ mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: What is NPK fertilizer, and how does it help my maize crop grow?
ga: Mɛni ji NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni te eyeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: NPK stands for Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Potassium, which are the main foods plants need. Nitrogen makes the leaves green and big, Phosphorus helps build strong roots, and Potassium helps the plant fight off diseases and produce full, heavy maize grains.
ga: NPK damɔ shi kɛha Nitrogen, Phosphorus kɛ Potassium, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei. Nitrogen haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa. Fosforo yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ maa. Ni potassium yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ helai. ni amɛfee ŋmãa ni tsiimɔ fɛɛ

english: Is it good to apply fertilizer at the exact same time I plant my seeds?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli yɛ be kome too mli ni aduɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yes, applying fertilizer during planting gives young seeds immediate food as soon as they sprout. This helps the young roots grow fast and strong right from the start, giving your crops a head start.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii yɛ be mli ni aduɔ nii lɛ, ebaaha ana dumɔwui bibii lɛ niyenii kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi bibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛhe wa kɛjɛɔ shishijee. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ

english: Why does maize need fertilizer so early in its life cycle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa he hiaa ŋmãa yɛ ewala be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Maize is a fast-growing crop that consumes a lot of nutrients quickly. Feeding it early ensures the plant establishes strong stems and deep roots that help it survive dry weather and produce large cobs later.
ga: Abɛi ji tso ko ni daa oya ni eyeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo oya. Niyenii kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Ebaaha tso lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli, ni sɛɛ mli lɛ ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Should fertilizer touch the seeds directly when I am putting them in the ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dumɔwui lɛ akpe tɛ̃ɛ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: No, fertilizer should not touch the seed directly because concentrated chemical fertilizer can burn or damage the tender seed before it sprouts. It should be placed slightly to the side or underneath the seed.
ga: Dabi, esaaa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dumɔwui lɛ kpeɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã loo efite dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃. Esa akɛ akɛ amɛ awo dumɔwui lɛ afã loo amɛshishi fioo.

english: How do crop roots actually take in food from the fertilizer I put in the soil?
ga: Te tsei shishifãi yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Roots can only drink in fertilizer when it dissolves in water. Rain or soil moisture breaks down the fertilizer granules, allowing the plant's roots to soak up the dissolved nutrients and carry them throughout the stalk.
ga: Shishifãi baanyɛ anu ŋmɔshi nibii pɛ kɛji akɛ amɛwo nu mli. Nugbɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ akumɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbalaa niyenii ni mli edɔ ni amɛyaa tso lɛ tso lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What is a fertilizer spreader, and how does it work?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwãa nii? Ni te etsuɔ ​​nii ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: A fertilizer spreader is a tool or machine that drops fertilizer evenly across your field or along planting rows. It helps you distribute nutrients steadily so every plant gets an equal share without wasting fertilizer.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji dɛŋdade loo tsɔne ko ni shwieɔ ŋmɔ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋmɔ loo dumɔwui akuu mli. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni ojaraa niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso fɛɛ tso aná gbɛfaŋnɔ ni tamɔ nakai ni efiteee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can using a mechanical planter make my planting work easier?
ga: Te tsɔne ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha midumɔ lɛ afee mlɛo aha tɛŋŋ?

english: A planter automates the heavy work by opening the soil, dropping seeds at the right depth, and covering them up in one motion. This saves you from bending down repeatedly and speeds up your work significantly.
ga: Okwaafoi kɛ nitsumɔ ni wa tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo he ni sa. ni okɛha dumɔwui lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ. Enɛ haaa okɛ ohe awo mli shii abɔ. ni eha onitsumɔ lɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: How do modern planting tools help me combine seed planting and fertilizing into one step?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nibii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni mikɛ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ?

english: Modern planters have separate compartments for seeds and fertilizer. As you push or pull the machine, it drops the seed and places the fertilizer nearby at the same time, cutting your field work time in half.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui yɛ hei srɔtoi ni akɛ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli. Kɛji otsi loo ogbala tsɔne lɛ Tsɔne lɛ duɔ dumɔwui ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ, ni efoɔ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ be lɛ mli enyɔ.

english: What happens to my crops if fertilizer is spread unevenly across the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji akɛ aja ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: If fertilizer is uneven, crops that get too much can suffer from leaf burn, while crops that get too little will grow thin and yellow. Even distribution ensures your whole field grows uniformly and matures at the same time.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyaaa nɔ lɛ Tsei ni naa babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ana baa shãa. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni nine shɛɔ nɔ fioo tsɔ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Jajemɔ po haa oniji fɛɛ niji lɛ daraa pɛpɛɛpɛ ni amɛfeɔ ekome kɛdaraa.

english: Can I use the same fertilizer spreader for maize as well as other crops on my farm?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwãa ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi. yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, a fertilizer spreader can be used for many different crops like maize, rice, or sorghum. You just need to adjust the machine's opening to release the correct amount of fertilizer for each specific crop type.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwãa ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ atsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Ehe miihia ni otsake tsɔne lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ pɛ koni ojie ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko lɛ kpo.

english: When the lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape, your soil is running low on nitrogen. The plant is moving the limited nitrogen it has from its older lower leaves up to feed the new top growth.
ga: Kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, no lɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei miitsi nitrogen fioo ko kɛmiijɛ baa ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli kɛmiiya ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋmeii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my land produce smaller maize harvests when I plant it on the exact same plot three seasons in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo beni miduɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ bei etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop loves most and allows soil pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or peanuts restores nitrogen and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei lɛ sumɔɔ waa lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa Rotating corn kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen aba ekoŋŋ, ni eye ebua ni ewaje shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate intense, direct sunlight. Large trees act as a natural canopy that protects tender young cocoa leaves from burning and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni eda lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do I need to cut long wooden poles to stake my yam vines instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei kakadaji lɛ? koni akɛ sweet potato wain tsei awo tso nɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves toward the sun. Maximum sunlight exposure helps the plant make food energy, which travels down to swell the tuber beneath the ground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Hulu la ni fa babaoo yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii hewalɛ. ni tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi koni eha tuber lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without draining. Excessive water starves the roots of oxygen and creates ideal conditions for fungal diseases to attack the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Nu babaoo baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. ni efee shihilɛ ni sa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baatutua ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow when I plant them right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ akwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain after a long dry season often creates a 'false start' where only the top layer of soil gets wet. If a long dry spell follows immediately, the germinated seeds dry up and die before their roots reach deep water.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ fɔɔ A ‘amale shishijee’ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kɛji hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the sap under the leaves, or by a virus carried by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli latex lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or water is irregular. Severe heat or moisture stress prevents successful pollination, so the plant sheds the blossom instead of forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ loo hulutsoo ni naa wa tsiɔ pollination naa koni ekaye omanye. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees snap or fall over easily right when the bunches start getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ fãa loo amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ niji lɛ je shishi amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and very fibrous stems that get heavy at the top when fruiting. Without strong windbreaks or bamboo support props, heavy winds easily push them over.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ kɛji amɛwo yibii. Kɛji obɛ kɔɔyɔɔŋ tsɔne loo ŋmei nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ, Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatsɔ mli mlɛo.

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and steal valuable nutrients, sunlight, and fertilizer from the soil, essentially starving your crop even if water is plentiful.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa po yɛ.

english: Why do some of my planted maize seeds fail to grow out of the soil even after I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ amɛmli moŋ?

english: Seeds need the right planting depth and soil moisture to germinate. If buried too deep, the young shoot runs out of stored food energy before reaching the light; if planted too shallow, the seed dries out or gets eaten by birds.
ga: Dumɔwui biɔ dumɔ mlibotemɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nu ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, niyenii hewalɛ ni ato lɛ baaho dani amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baagbi loo okpoi baaye amɛ.

english: How can I tell if the cocoa seeds I harvested are healthy enough to raise in my nursery?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ kookoo yibii ni mikpaa lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Healthy cocoa seeds come from fully ripe, disease-free pods. A simple test is to place fresh seeds in water—seeds that sink are full of moisture and energy for growth, while seeds that float are light, weak, or damaged.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni hela bɛ mli lɛ amli. Kaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo ji ni akɛ dumɔwui heei awo nu mli Dumɔwui ni awo nu shishi lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hewalɛ ni haa amɛdaraa. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni hoɔ yɛ nu mli lɛ he waaa, amɛhe waaa, loo amɛfite.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that cannot handle full, direct sunlight. Shade trees act like protective canopies, shielding young plants from harsh sun heat and keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ hulutsoo be. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping during the dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry conditions to save water and prevent the plant from drying out completely. Once the rainy season starts again, the stem will sprout fresh leaves.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛtsi tso lɛ naa koni ekagbi kwraa. Kɛji akɛ abote nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ, tso lɛ yitso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei.

english: Why does my maize grow tall and dark green on one side of my farm, but short and pale yellow on the other side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ miida ni eyɛ ŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ? Shi fã kroko lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ kuku.

english: Soil fertility is not the same everywhere on a plot. Yellow, stunted plants usually signal a lack of nitrogen in that part of the field, which can be improved by adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeee ekome yɛ he fɛɛ he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii ni ji yellow dwarf lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ jɛmɛ. Abaanyɛ aha enɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ kooloi aŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes the specific soil nutrients that plant relies on and allows soil pests to build up. Rotating with legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei lɛ damɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii atsake lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and shady conditions. Pruning excess tree branches allows air and sunlight through, which dries the pods and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ hulutsoo kɛbaa. Tso niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the underside of leaves. As they feed, they transfer plant viruses that distort growth and stunt fruit development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. be mli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii Amɛjieɔ tsei amli helai ni fiteɔ aduawai lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛshweremɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I trim off extra side branches from my tomato plants instead of letting them grow naturally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ moŋ fe ni mahã amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Pruning extra branches prevents the plant from wasting nutrients on leaves it doesn't need. This forces the plant to direct its energy into producing larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli nibii krokomɛi lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ baai ni ehe ehiaaa lɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ atsu nii koni amɛwo yibii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants have huge green leaves above ground, but the roots underneath are very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or too much water, the plant uses all its energy to build leaves and stem height above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo nu babaoo Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛmaa baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ahi tuber lɛ mli yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ

english: Why do my maize stalks bend and fall over when they produce a very heavy harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ amɛmiiwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii lɛ?

english: When crops produce an abundant harvest, the top becomes heavy. If the soil lacks nutrients like potassium or the plants are planted too close together, the stems remain weak and cannot support the extra weight of the heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii wo yibii babaoo lɛ, yitsei lɛ anɔ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ niyenii tamɔ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛji akɛ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Tso lɛ baaya nɔ egbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ cob ni tsii lɛ mli muji ni fata he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow many lush green leaves but produce very few flowers and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ woɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo shi fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai fioo pɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer makes them spend all their energy growing tall stems and green leaves instead of producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen babaoo ha otsei lɛ, ebaaha amɛfite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛkwɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom mean your soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build food and stay green.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli.

english: Why does my harvested cassava start rotting within just two days of digging it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ mli beni mifo lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers continue to breathe rapidly once harvested and lose moisture quickly. Without processing them into products like gari or flour right away, natural rot sets in very fast.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ oya kɛji akpa amɛ ni amɛmli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Kɛji akɛ afeee lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni afee nibii tamɔ gari loo ashikishaŋ. Adebɔɔ mli fitemɔ baa oya.

english: Why does my paddy rice break into tiny pieces when I take it to the milling machine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli fãa bibii bibii lɛ? Beni okɛ penti tsɔnei baa maŋsɛɛ?

english: Rice grain cracks inside the husk if it is dried too fast under harsh direct sunlight or harvested when it is already over-dry in the field.
ga: Omɔ ŋmeii lɛ baagbala yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛji amɛgbi oya tsɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. loo akpaa be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ

english: How do I know that my yam tubers under the ground are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Yam tubers are mature when the leaves and vines on top stop growing green, turn dry, and start dying off, showing the plant has transferred all its nutrients into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa kwraa kɛ́ baai kɛ wain tso ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kpa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛgbi, ni amɛbɔi gbele, ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ fɛɛ ewo ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their tiny young pods during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: During hot dry spells, cocoa trees shed young pods automatically to save water and energy so the main tree can survive until the rains return.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbii bibii lɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Bɔni afee ni tso titri lɛ anyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny invisible insects sucking the liquid out of young leaves, which distorts their shape as they try to grow.
ga: Koolooi bibii kɛ baai lɛ akumɔ baa. Nɔ ni anaaa lɛ nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai bibii amli. Enɛ haa amɛhefɛo lɛ fiteɔ beni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara lɛ.

english: Why do government-approved improved seeds perform better than the seeds I save from my own farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni atsake ni nɔyeli lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved seed varieties are specially bred to grow faster, withstand local pests, and make better use of water and soil nutrients compared to seeds saved over many years.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛdara oya. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. kɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ Kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni akɛto afii babaoo lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my plantain suckers grow tall and thin without producing big bunches when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmeii wuji kɛ́ midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting too close forces the suckers to fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil food, making all of them thin and unproductive.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha suckers lɛ awuu kɛha hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ shwɛm ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow after heavy rains flood my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa eha miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When heavy rains submerge your field, water fills all the tiny air spaces in the soil. Without air, the roots cannot breathe or absorb vital plant food like nitrogen, which causes the leaves to lose their green color and turn yellow.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie oŋmɔji lɛ amli Kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ, nu eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amɛmu loo amɛhe tso niyenii ni he hia tamɔ nitrogen, ni no haa baai lɛ laajeɔ amɛ su eŋɔli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: What will happen to my cassava tubers if rainwater sits around them for several days?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu ebɔle he? Cassava shishifãi gbii babaoo?

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil to stay healthy and grow large. If water sits on the roots for too long, it cuts off oxygen, which causes the tubers to rot and spoil under the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara. Kɛji nu hi shishifãi lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaakpa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why should I dig small channels on my farm to let excess rainwater flow away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo nubu bibioo ko? Yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli?

english: Digging channels helps direct floodwater away from your crops so it does not pool around the roots. This prevents root rot and stops heavy water flow from carrying away your rich topsoil.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni ooofo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. koni nu afua akabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe Enɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ agbomɔ naa ni ebaatsi nu agbo ni hoɔ lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa lɛ nɔ.

english: Can my young cocoa trees survive if my farm experiences sudden flooding?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ baahi shi kɛji nu afua ba trukaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cocoa trees can survive brief flooding if the water moves off quickly. However, if water stands around the roots for too long, the roots will suffocate and die, and fungal diseases like black pod will spread much faster.
ga: Cacao tsei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ nu afua mli kɛji nu lɛ tee oya. Shi, kɛji nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baafo ni amɛgboi. Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pods lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kwraa.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants roll up tightly during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's natural way of protecting itself from losing too much moisture. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface exposed to the hot sun and keeps water inside its stem and roots.
ga: Baai ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni efiteɔ lɛ he. Tsei haa he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ amɛhe ni amɛtoɔ nu yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I keep the soil around my tomato plants moist when the dry season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ afee fɛ̃i yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: You can cover the soil around your tomatoes with dried grass or leaves, a practice called mulching. This layer acts like a shade cover, preventing the hot sun from evaporating the water stored in the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Tomato ni jwɛi loo baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching. Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo. Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee nu ni ebua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why does rainwater run off the surface of my farm instead of sinking into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ hiɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When soil becomes very dry and bare, it forms a hard upper crust that acts like concrete. Adding compost or dry leaves softens the ground so it can act like a sponge and soak up water when it rains.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi waa ni ebɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni wa ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ kɔnkrit. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai ni egbi fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo bɔni afee ni etsu nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekɛ nu shwie shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to hand-water my garden crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛ minine baafɔ mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ anɔ nu?

english: The best time to water your crops is early in the morning or late in the evening. During these cooler hours, water stays in the soil longer so the roots can drink it, whereas afternoon heat causes most water to evaporate quickly.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu ji leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli ejɔ lɛ mli lɛ Nu lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anu. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shwane mli latsaa lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ oya.

english: Is it safe for me to use water from a nearby stream to irrigate my vegetable crops?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ baafɔse mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu?

english: Yes, stream water is generally good for crops, but it is best to pour it directly around the soil and root area instead of splashing it on the leaves, as wet leaves can attract leaf diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, faa mli nu lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Shi gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni afɔse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeshwie baai lɛ anɔ Enɛ ji akɛ, baai ni efɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbala baai helai.

english: Why do my vegetable crops grow faster when I irrigate them regularly compared to relying only on the rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ daraa oya kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ daa fe be mli ni mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ɔ nugbɔ nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Regular irrigation gives your plants a steady, uninterrupted supply of food and moisture. Rain can be unpredictable, and when plants dry out between rains, their growth stops while they try to survive.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ daa lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii kɛ nu ni yaa nɔ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛyeɔ be fɛɛ be. Anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ. kɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ gĩɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ Dalɛ kpaɔ be mli ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ehi shi lɛ.

english: Why did my maize field produce so much more grain this season compared to last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma ŋmɔ lɛ miiwo ŋmaa babaoo yɛ be nɛɛ mli fe nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Maize yields increase significantly when there is a good balance of rainwater, properly timed planting, and healthy soil. When weather conditions stay favorable, maize plants develop larger, fuller cobs across the entire farm.
ga: Abɛi ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ waa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔ yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ŋmɛ gbɛ. Abɛi tsei lɛ daa ni amɛtoi eyiɔ obɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How do I store a huge harvest of maize so that it does not spoil in the barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ ŋmãa babaoo ni mikpa lɛ ato koni ekafite yɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: When you harvest a large amount of maize, pests like weevils and mould can ruin it quickly if it remains damp. Drying the grains thoroughly in the sun until they are hard and storing them in airtight bags protects your abundance for many months.
ga: Kɛ́ okpa ŋmãa babaoo lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ afite lɛ oya kɛji akɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa ni okɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaabu fɔmɔ he nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why does taking care of a large crop of maize require so much daily effort on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei wuji akwɛmɔ biɔ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo daa gbi lɛ?

english: A heavy crop harvest requires continuous work to clear aggressive weeds, apply fertilizers at the right growth stages, and guard against destructive insects like the fall armyworm that can quickly spread across dense fields.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni akpaa lɛ biɔ nitsumɔ be fɛɛ be koni akɛjie jwɛi ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ kɛya. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ be ni sa ni edaa lɛ mli. ni abu he kɛjɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli oya lɛ ahe.

english: Why do maize prices drop in the local market right after everyone finishes harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ jara baa shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ gbe ŋmãa lɛ naa lɛ?

english: When almost every farmer harvests at the same time, there is an abundance of maize available in the market. When supply is higher than demand, prices fall, which is why proper storage helps you wait and sell later when prices rise.
ga: Beni nɔ ni miihe ashɛ okwaafoi fɛɛ kpaɔ nii yɛ be kome mli Abele babaoo yɛ jara nɔ. Kɛ́ nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ fa fe nɔ ni ataoɔ lɛ, jara lɛ baa shi, no hewɔ ni nibii ni akɛtoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa onyɛɔ omɛɔ ni ohɔ̃ɔ sɛɛ mli kɛ́ jara lɛ tee hiɛ lɛ.

english: Can buyers from nearby countries like Togo or Burkina Faso buy maize directly from my farm?
ga: Nihɔɔlɔi ni jɛ maji ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ Togo loo Burkina Faso Ani manyɛ mahe ŋmãa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, cross-border traders travel across West Africa to purchase grain when local harvests are high, provided your maize is well-dried, free of insects, and meets standard quality expectations.
ga: Hɛɛ, jarayelɔi ni tsɔɔ husui lɛ anaa lɛ fãa gbɛ kɛtsɔɔ Afrika Anaigbɛ koni amɛyahe ŋmaa beni maŋ lɛ mli ŋmaa lɛ fa babaoo lɛ. Kɛji akɛ o-ŋmã lɛ mli egbi, ni kooloi bɛ mli, ni eshɛɔ nɔ ni akpaa gbɛ akɛ ehi jogbaŋŋ lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow instead of rich green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are hungry for nitrogen in the soil. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores their green color and keeps them growing strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔji ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes tiny holes to appear in the center leaves of my growing maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa bu bibioo lɛ feɔ? Eje kpo yɛ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ.

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by caterpillars, such as the fall armyworm, feeding inside the whorl. Checking your crop early and applying recommended treatments stops them before they damage the growing cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ armyworms ni egbee shi, ni yeɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa ŋmeii bibii amli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ mra kɛ tsamɔ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsuɔ he nii Ehaa tso lɛ kpaa nitsumɔ dani efiteɔ ŋmei ni miida lɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the maize plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients. This causes them to grow tall and thin with smaller cobs that easily break or fall over in heavy wind.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Abɛi tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, amɛhe kwɔ ni amɛhe tseee ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni fãa loo egbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ

english: Is it better to plant seeds saved from my last maize harvest or buy fresh certified seeds?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi naagbee ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli loo mahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli?

english: Certified seeds are bred to grow uniformly, resist diseases, and give higher yields. Seeds saved from previous harvests gradually lose their strength and usually give smaller yields over time.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ koni amɛdara daa. Enyɛɔ helai anaa ni ehaa yibiiwoo babaoo Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Amɛhewalɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ ni amɛfɔɔ yibiiwoo fioo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How can I tell if my harvested maize is dry enough to pack without rotting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mawo mli ni efiteee?

english: A simple way to test dryness is to press a grain with your thumbnail; if it leaves a dent, it is still wet. Dry maize grains should feel rock hard and make a sharp, metallic sound when shaken together in a container.
ga: Gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni atsɔɔ nɔ akaa ŋmɔtɔ ji ni akɛ mfoniri bibii anyɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ Kɛji efee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, no lɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo. Esa akɛ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ anu he akɛ ewa tamɔ tɛ ni efee dade ŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ ekome yɛ tsɛnsi lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and moisture shelter it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ he ni ehiɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ mli.

english: Is it safe for me to plant cassava and maize together on the same land at the same time?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, cassava and maize share space well because maize grows fast and matures early, while cassava grows slowly at first and expands underground later, allowing both crops to share resources without crowding each other out.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa jaa he ko jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa daa oya ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni sɛɛ mli lɛ egbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ jaa nibii ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ ni amɛboteee amɛhe mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green. Rain provides water, but without rich soil or manure to feed the crop, it loses color and vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Nugbɔ haa nu, shi kɛji shikpɔŋ ni baa nii loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ Ebaaha tso lɛ su kɛ hewalɛ afite.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing tall and green but refusing to produce any flowers or peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miida ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ shi ewooo fɔfɔi loo pepper ko lɛ?

english: When pepper plants get too much nitrogen food from the soil, they spend all their energy making leaves and branches instead of fruits. The plant needs balanced food with phosphorus to trigger flowering.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ná niyenii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Yɛ aduawai najiaŋ lɛ, amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai kɛ tsei aniji. Niyenii ni ja ni phosphorus yɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia tsei koni amɛwo fɔfɔii.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting groundnuts before planting maize on the same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei dani adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen food from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. When harvested, they leave behind rich soil that nourishes the maize crop that follows.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akpa lɛ, eshiɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii koni ekɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Yam vines need to reach sunlight to make food for the growing tubers underground. Staking provides an avenue for the leaves to spread in the sun while keeping them off damp ground where diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa gbɛ ni baa lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ hulu la lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaaa baai lɛ ahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why will my maize crop give smaller cobs if I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ naa ŋmeii bibii kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, individual crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Because no single plant gets enough food, they all grow weak and produce small yields.
ga: Beni adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tso henɔ fɛɛ henɔ kɛ ehe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ eko kwraa enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ tsei fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without forming fruits during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes stress to the plant and dries up the pollen inside the flowers. When pollination fails due to heat, the plant drops its flowers to conserve water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ egbiɔ. Kɛji pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ dɔlɛ hewɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: How can I tell if heavy rains are causing my cassava roots to rot under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha ŋmei shishifãi egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When cassava roots rot from excess water, the lower leaves will turn yellow and drop off early, the base of the main stem will become soft or dark, and the soil around the crop will give off a bad smell.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fite kɛjɛ nu ni fa fe nine mli lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya. Tso titri lɛ shishi baafee bɔdɔɔ loo ediŋŋ, ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ baafu waa.

english: Why do wild weeds harm my crops so much if they are all just plants growing in the same soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii awui waa kɛji akɛ amɛji tsei kɛkɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and are tougher than farm crops, so they aggressively steal the soil food, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. If weeds take over, your crops will starve and fail to produce heavy fruit.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. No hewɔ lɛ amɛkɛ ekãa juɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji jwɛi ye nɔ lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye hɔmɔ ni amɛwoŋ yibii ni tsii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before setting any pods when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii dani amɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: High temperatures and dry spells cause water stress in cocoa trees. To save energy and moisture for survival, the tree naturally sheds its delicate flowers instead of using resources to grow pods.
ga: Latsaa ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ haa nu he haomɔ baa kookoo tsei amli. Koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ato koni enyɛ ehi shi. Tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii baatsu nii kɛdu pods

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the top leaves are still bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellowing of the bottom leaves usually means the soil is running low on nitrogen. Maize needs lots of nitrogen to grow, so when soil supplies run low, the plant steals nitrogen from older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ falɛ faaa Tsei lɛ juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda yɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil when we get heavy rains late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ wɔna nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Heavy rain fills up all the empty spaces in the soil with water, suffocating the roots and creating perfect conditions for fungal diseases that rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hei ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ yiɔ kɛ nu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha fungal tuber rot hela lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn dark brown and soft before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: Dark, soft bottoms on tomatoes are caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, often triggered by uneven soil moisture when dry spells are followed by heavy watering.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato ni shishi yɔɔ blɛoo ni tsuɔ waa lɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shiŋŋ beni nu ni hoɔ babaoo nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during light winds even when they look healthy and full of leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni waaa lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ ni eyi obɔ kɛ baai moŋ.

english: Plantain trees do not have deep taproots like oak trees; their roots spread out shallowly near the surface. When heavy bunches of fruit grow, the plant becomes top-heavy and can easily tip over without support.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ odum tsei. Eshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa fioo ni bɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ be mli ni aduawai babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Tsei lɛ tsii ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛku amɛsɛɛ oya kɛji mɔ ko bɛ ni fiɔ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why are my harvested yams coming out with strange, bent shapes instead of long and straight tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ ebɔle ehe yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ yitso kakadaŋŋ ni ja najiaŋ?

english: Hard, compacted soil or underground rocks block growing yam tubers from expanding downward smoothly. As the tuber pushes against hard soil, it bends and twists around obstacles.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ loo tɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ tsiɔ sweet potato ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ dozer yitso lɛ wa Ebaabɔle ehe ni ebɔle gbɛtsii nii ahe.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push their flower stems into the dirt after they bloom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ efɔfɔi lɛ awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants are unique because after their flowers are pollinated in the air, the flower stems (called pegs) bend down and grow into the soil so the nuts can safely mature underground.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ srɔto ejaakɛ kɛ́ ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ awo kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ŋmeii (ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs) lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the fresh leaves on my pepper plants curling up and shrinking into tight balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on young leaves and transmitting viruses that distort plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai bibii ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do my cowpea pods look green and healthy on the outside but end up full of holes and worms inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ? Shi bu kɛ ŋmeii eyi mli obɔ.

english: Moths lay tiny eggs on cowpea flowers and young pods. Once the eggs hatch, the caterpillars bore small holes straight inside to feed on the tender developing seeds hidden within.
ga: Moths woɔ wɔji bibii. yɛ cowpea fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii bibii anɔ Beni ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ lɛ Ŋmei lɛ baafo bu bibioo ko. mli koni eye dumɔwui ni miida ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛtee mli lɛ.

english: Why do my young oil palm trees produce small fruit bunches that turn brown and rot right on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso bibioo lɛ woɔ aduawai bibii lɛ? No tsɔɔ blɔfo ni egboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Young oil palm trees often suffer from poor pollination or lack enough stored nutrients to carry early fruit bunches to maturity, causing the tree to abandon and abort those unviable bunches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei bibii lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ ŋmeii ni ehiii lɛ ahewɔ loo amɛbɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ato ni baaha amɛwo yibii mra kɛyashi amɛda. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ shiɔ nakai niji ni wala bɛ mli lɛ ni ekɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are black spots spreading on my cocoa pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji gbɛɔ eshwaa kookoo ŋmeii anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black spots on cocoa pods during heavy rains are caused by Black Pod disease, which thrives in wet and dark conditions. Pruning extra tree branches to let in sunlight and fresh air helps keep the farm dry and stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ hela ni ji black pod disease, ni yaa hiɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei ahe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baa. Niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa aba lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gĩɔ ni ehaa helai gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the trees lack enough moisture, face insect attacks, or miss out on natural pollinators like tiny midges. Keeping shade trees and protecting small beneficial insects helps flowers stay on and grow into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. hiɛ kooloi ni baatutua amɛ loo adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa tamɔ kooloi bibii ni elaaje Tsei akwɛmɔ haa hulutsoo kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ pods.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen or the soil is too soaked with water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or creating small channels to drain excess water helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen loo nu ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaafata he loo gbɛi bibii ni afee Koni ajie nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Maize turning to powder in storage is caused by insects called weevils eating the inside of the seeds. Drying your maize until it is completely hard and storing it in airtight bags keeps weevils out.
ga: Abɛi ni tsɔɔ powda yɛ nitoohe lɛ ji nɔ ni kooloi ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa kɛyashi ewa kwraa ni akɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akabote mli.

english: Yam vines naturally reach upward to get sun so they can feed the underground tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf decay and helping the plant produce bigger yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ shɛɔ ŋwɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná hulu la bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ sweet potatoes wuji.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants twisting and changing to light green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Curled and discolored cassava leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems stops the sickness before it starts.
ga: Kasava baai ni ebɔle amɛhe ni etsake amɛhe lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Amɛji mɛi ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Cassava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni hela akpa dani eje shishi.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow lots of tall green leaves but very few peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaŋŋ agboi babaoo shi pepper fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes pepper plants put all their energy into growing leaves instead of fruits. Switching to fertilizers rich in phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to bloom and set more peppers.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni miida lɛ he nii moŋ fe aduawai. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes tomato flowers to dry out and fall off before they can form tomatoes. Watering early in the morning and providing light shade helps keep the plants cool so they can produce fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ tomato. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ leebi kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ amli jɔɔ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why does burning my bush before planting make the ground dry out faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii ni ashãa dani aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the layer of dry leaves and organic matter that acts like a blanket to keep water in the soil. Leaving cleared weeds on top of the soil as mulch keeps the ground cool and moist.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ baai ni egbi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni haa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahiɛ. Shi jwɛi lɛ ahe tse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key food they need to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen when the ground stays too wet for too long, preventing the roots from taking in air.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ.

english: Does it mean my cassava is ready for harvesting as soon as the stem starts flowering?
ga: Ani enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ mi-cassava lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji ŋmeii lɛ je shishi amɛwo fɔfɔi pɛ?

english: Not necessarily. Flowering is just a natural step in the plant's top growth, but cassava tubers mature based on time underground—usually between 9 to 12 months depending on the variety—and soil conditions.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Fɔfɔii ni yaa nɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ko kɛkɛ ni haa tso lɛ daa babaoo. Shi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ be ni sa mli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12, ni enɛ damɔ tso lɛ srɔtoi lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my small young cocoa pods turn black and dry up while still tiny on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi beni eji gbekɛ lolo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is often a natural behavior called cherelle wilt. The cocoa tree produces more tiny pods than it can feed, so it naturally sacrifices some to focus its energy on growing the remaining pods to maturity.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli subaŋ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ cherry wilt. Cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii. Miná nɔ ni fe nɔ ni manyɛ maye. No hewɔ lɛ, cacao tso lɛ kɛ ekomɛi shaa afɔle yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ ama ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ kɛyashi amɛdara.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when the plant lacks enough water during flowering, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil causing the plant to grow leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni tsei bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ fɔfɔi be mli loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ha tsei lɛ aná baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow better when I plant cowpeas alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, which means they pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When they share the soil with maize, they release food into the ground that helps the maize grow taller and greener.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛgbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni amɛkɛ ŋmãa lɛ jaa shikpɔŋ lɛ Amɛjieɔ niyenii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛɔ ni ekɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kpaaa gbee.

english: Why do my plantain bunches stay small if I leave all the suckers growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ bibii nɛkɛ kɛji mishi ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: All the suckers compete with the mother plant for sunlight, water, and soil food. When there are too many suckers, the main stem does not get enough nourishment to form a large, heavy cluster of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii fɛɛ kɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Beni ŋmeii lɛ fa tsɔ lɛ Tso titri lɛ nine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ ni baaha efee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips hiding under the leaf and sucking out juices, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies. Heat and severe drought can also cause leaves to curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves droop during the hot afternoon sun but stand up straight again in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛdamɔ shi jaŋŋ ekoŋŋ leebi lɛ?

english: Drooping is a protective habit where plants close their leaf pores to stop losing precious moisture during peak heat. Once the air cools down at night, the roots absorb groundwater to refill the stem and perk the leaves back up.
ga: Defoliation ji hebuu subaŋ ko ni tsei ŋmɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛkpa nu ni he hiaa ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ koni ekɛwo tso lɛ shishi ekoŋŋ ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why don't my harvested yam tubers start sprouting immediately after I bury seed pieces in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikpa lɛ ejeee shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers go through a natural sleeping phase called dormancy right after harvest. During this rest period, the tuber refuses to sprout until internal chemical changes complete, which usually takes two to three months.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ boteɔ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe be ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ hejɔɔmɔ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛyashi tsofa tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baagbe naa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ.

english: Why do crops planted close under big shade trees grow thin and tall without bearing good fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsei wuji ahe lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛkwɔ shi amɛwooo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to produce energy and food for fruit development. When shaded, plants stretch upward towards the light, wasting all their energy on weak stems instead of developing strong roots and fruits.
ga: Tsei he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛ niyenii kɛha aduawai lɛ adalɛ. Beni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tso lɛ baashɛ ehe kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya la lɛ he. Kɛtsɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni efiteɔ yɛ tso ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeená shishifãi kɛ yibii ni mli wa

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential food for the crop, or that the soil is waterlogged and the roots cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: If my farm already gives me enough food to feed my family, why should I spend money to buy fertilizer?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ haa miweku lɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa momo Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Fertilizer replaces nutrients taken from the soil so your land produces much higher yields, giving you extra crops to sell for profit while keeping the soil fertile for future seasons.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, oshikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe nakai. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ koni oná sɛɛnamɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ bei.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or beans makes my soil better for maize in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots, acting like natural plant food for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. They need shade trees or plantains planted next to them to block direct light and keep the air moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii yɛ amɛmasɛi. koni ekɛtsi kane ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when excess water settles around them for too long because the roots cannot get air. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ mli.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking juices from the underside of the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ amli

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without turning into tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants, causing them to drop their flowers to save energy instead of forming fruit, especially if the soil dries out.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomatoi lɛ agbo koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii. Titri lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi.

english: Why do my yam plants need wooden stakes to climb on instead of trailing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ yɛ tso ni ekɛkwɔɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeenyiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves up to catch maximum sunlight, which helps the plant manufacture enough energy to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia shishitoo ni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main mother plant. Cutting away surplus suckers leaves enough food for the main plant to produce big bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal soil nutrients and root space, preventing your crops from getting the nourishment they need.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni ekɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plants lack nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient they need to grow strong. This often happens when the soil is worn out or after heavy rains wash fertilizer away from the root area.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha shweremɔ kpakpa Enɛ fɔɔ baa beni shikpɔŋ lɛ efite loo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or beans on my farm to help the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that pull natural nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When these roots break down in the ground, they feed natural nutrients back into the soil for other crops to use.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji shishifãi nɛɛ gbee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛhaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni tsei krokomɛi kɛtsu nii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn under harsh direct sunlight. Keeping tall trees provides living shade that cools the seedlings and keeps moisture in the soil until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ haa hulutsoo ni haa dumɔwui lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up so they can catch full sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers underground. It also keeps the leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ nɔ koni ekɛfee hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ hu ehiɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ. Tsi fungal helai anaa

english: Leaving too many suckers forces them to fight with the main plantain stem for food, water, and sunlight. Pruning extra suckers ensures the primary stem gets full nourishment to produce thick, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei bibii babaoo yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ewo yibii ni mli wa ni tsii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids or thrips feeding on the leaf sap, or by plant viruses transmitted by these insects that disrupt normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ. ni tsiɔ dalɛ ni sa naa lɛ

english: Why do I see small holes and dirt inside the central funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Kɛ muji ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaa lɛ mli lɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest that crawls deep inside the center funnel of the maize plant to feed on tender developing leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm caterpillars, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni eye baai ni miida blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants face heat stress, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer, which tricks the plant into growing stems and leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai shwereɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Cassava roots need air pockets in the soil to stay healthy. Excessive rain floods the soil and starves roots of oxygen, allowing soil fungi to infect and rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ anáa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ hela ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) acts as a protective shield that keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation from the sun, and stops weeds from taking root.
ga: Mulching (mulching) tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu ni jɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekawo shishifãi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when there are no plantain trees planted near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni aduko dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Fast-growing crops like plantains act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the air humid so the young cocoa leaves do not dry out and burn.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Enɛ baatsi kookoo baai bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi ni amɛkashã.

english: When soil lacks nitrogen, the maize plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves and sends it to the newer top leaves to keep growing. Yellowing bottom leaves are the crop's way of showing it needs more nitrogen food or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen lɛ Abɛi lɛ heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli ni ekɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei amli koni eya nɔ eda. Yellow ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsɔɔ akɛ niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ he miihia tso lɛ.

english: If I plant groundnuts in the same farm with my cassava, will the groundnuts steal food from the cassava roots?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmei Ani ŋmei baaju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmei shishifãi amli?

english: No, groundnuts actually feed the soil. Groundnuts capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, which releases natural fertilizer into the soil to help your cassava grow better without competing for space.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Akpɔlɔi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua o-cassava lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ he ko akaŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from extreme heat or lack of water. Dropping flowers is the plant's natural self-defense mechanism to save its remaining energy and water when growing conditions are too tough.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he koni ekɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ he kɛji shihilɛi ni haa edaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ.

english: Why did my maize seeds fail to sprout after I buried them deep in the soil to protect them from birds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mifu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni mikɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ okpoi ahe lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize seeds need oxygen and heat near the surface to wake up and grow. If you plant them too deep, the seed runs out of stored food energy pushing through the heavy soil before its green shoot can reach the sunlight.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ dɔlɛ ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ koni amɛte shi ni amɛdara. Kɛji odu mli tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ niyenii hewalɛ ni ato lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni amɛtsiɔ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ nɔ dani ŋmeii eŋɔli lɛ shɛɔ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay thin and small when I plant the stems very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa beni miduɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need open soil space to stretch and swell into thick tubers. Planting them too close forces the roots to fight each other for water and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni agbele naa lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi lɛ koni amɛgbala amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni mli tse. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ kɛ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa yibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly into tubes during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl during intense heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and trap moisture inside. It is the plant's natural way of sweating less and protecting itself from drying out.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ latsaa be mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni emɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ latsaa baa shi ni ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔlɔ he.

english: Why do my yam leaves and vines turn yellow and dry up completely when it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kwraa yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing yam vines mean the plant has finished its job above ground. The plant naturally dies back after transferring all its leaf energy into stored food inside the underground yam tuber.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe nitsumɔ naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ egbɔmɔtso mli beni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ebaa lɛ mli lɛ ewo niyenii ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato tubers mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants suddenly wilt and turn weak after I clear weeds close to their stems with a hoe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ beni mikɛ ŋmei jie jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas have delicate feeding roots right near the surface of the dirt. Scraping deep with a hoe cuts these shallow roots, making it hard for the plant to absorb water until it grows new roots.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei shwie shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, efoɔ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ nɛɛ, ni ehaa ewaa ahaa tso lɛ akɛ ebaaŋɔ nu kɛyashi shishifãi heei baaje kpo.

english: Why does my cassava yield get smaller every year when I plant it on the exact same piece of land without resting the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛ́ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ mihe lɛ?

english: Cassava drains specific nutrients out of the earth every season. Planting it repeatedly in the exact same spot starves the soil of those essential nutrients and allows crop-specific pests to accumulate in the ground.
ga: Cassava jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be, ni kɛ́ adu amɛ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ afite. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: I saw small caterpillars eating holes in the middle of my young maize leaves overnight, what are they doing to my crop?
ga: Mina ŋmei bibioo ko Ye bu ko yɛ mibi lɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ nyɔɔŋ kome. Mɛni amɛfeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms. They target the soft, growing heart of the young maize plant to eat, which can stop the plant from developing proper leaves or corn ears if they are not treated quickly.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms. Amɛtutuaa ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ atsui ni miida lɛ koni amɛye. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ akafee baai loo ŋmãa toi ni sa kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ oya.

english: Why do insects seem to invade and destroy my crops more when there is a short dry spell during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii shii abɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo ko yɛ lɛ?

english: Warm, dry weather speeds up how fast insect eggs hatch into hungry caterpillars. At the same time, dry conditions make plants thirsty and weak, making it much easier for pests to chew through them.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni jɛmɛ egbi lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa kooloi akui ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ. yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ Shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ haa kumai yeɔ tsei ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ.

english: When a plant lacks nitrogen food in the soil, it moves whatever food it has left from its older lower leaves to feed the new upper growth. Yellow lower leaves mean your soil needs nitrogen fertilizer or manure.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ejieɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: My pepper leaves curl up tightly into a tube during the hot afternoon. Is my crop sick?
