ga: Mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ paipii ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hela mɔ amɛ?

english: Leaf curling in hot weather is actually the plant protecting itself. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun to hold onto its water and keep from drying out.
ga: Bɔ ni tso lɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji bɔ ni tso lɛ buɔ ehe he diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baa lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekagbi.

english: What will happen if I put three or four corn seeds into one hole to make sure something grows?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa etɛ loo ejwɛ wo bu kome mli koni mana nɔmimaa akɛ nɔ ko eda?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole creates competition. The young plants will fight each other for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, resulting in weak, thin stalks that yield tiny ears of corn.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa. Tsei bibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do experienced farmers plant cassava bushes around the outer edges of their vegetable fields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ duɔ ŋmei tsei yɛ amɛ aduawai ŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Cassava plants act as a living wall or windbreak. They slow down hot, harsh winds that can snap delicate vegetable plants, while also marking your field boundary and providing cassava tubers later.
ga: Yucca tsei tsuɔ nii akɛ gbogboi ni hiɛ ka loo kɔɔyɔɔ tsii. Amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni naa wa ni baanyɛ akumɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baa shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, kadimɔ oŋmɔji lɛ husui lɛ ni oyahe ŋmei ŋmeii yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: My tomato plants are covered in yellow flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without forming tomatoes. Why is this?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ ahe eyi kɛ fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato. Mɛni he je nɛ e ba jã a?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to stress from extreme heat or lack of water, or because insects like bees haven't visited them to spread pollen so the fruit can start growing.
ga: Nɔ ni fɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa ji haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ mli baa. Aloo akɛni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii eyaaa amɛŋɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ pollen amɛshwã bɔni afee ni aduawai lɛ aje shishi eda lɛ hewɔ?

english: Why do my okra plants keep growing very tall like trees but are producing very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tso lɛ daa tamɔ tso shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: When plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer without phosphorus, or when planted too closely in the shade, they focus all their energy on growing tall stems and lush leaves instead of making fruits.
ga: Kɛji tsei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ ni phosphorus bɛ mli loo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ maa tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni kwɔlɔ kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do white powdery spots appear on my garden egg leaves after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powder yɛŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: That white coating is a fungal disease called powdery mildew. It thrives when humidity is high and wet leaves stay crowded together without fresh air flowing between the plants.
ga: Nakai nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Akɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ ebɔ he babaoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ko bɛ ni hoɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if I leave them growing near the stems for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui? Kɛji miha eda yɛ tso lɛ he otsii fioo komɛi.

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors. Their roots spread fast to steal the water and fertilizer meant for your crop, while their leaves block sunlight, causing your crops to grow stunted and yield less.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya koni amɛju nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa Enɛ haa onibii lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and curling up during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight and high heat. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block the harsh sun and keep the soil cool, the leaves burn, turn yellow, and dry up.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ni baatsi hulu ni naa wa lɛ naa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i lɛ, baai lɛ baashã, amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbi.

english: Why do my maize plants have small ragged holes in their leaves when they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ baai lɛ anɔ beni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the center whorl of young maize plants during the day and eat the tender leaves as they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaai amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni oye baai bibii lɛ beni amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop almost all their leaves when the dry Harmattan wind starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ kɛ́ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves naturally during dry periods to reduce water loss and protect itself from drought. Once the rains return, the stem will quickly grow fresh new leaves.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni ekɛba nu ni efiteɔ lɛ shi ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba Tso lɛ shishi lɛ baakwɛ baai heei oya.

english: Why is it helpful to leave dead weeds and dried plant leaves around the base of my plantain suckers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ashi jwɛi ni egboi kɛ tsei ahe baai ni egbi lɛ abɔle he? No hewɔ lɛ, midumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo lɛ baye ebua mi.

english: Covering the ground around plantains with dry plant materials, called mulching, keeps the soil cool, traps moisture during dry weather, and breaks down into natural food for the roots.
ga: Mulching ni bɔleɔ Plantains he lɛ Akɛ tsei ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ haa nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli ni egbɛɔ etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off to the ground without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni pepper ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off mainly when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or irregular watering. When a plant lacks enough water, it sheds its blossoms to save its own life.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Beni tsei lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Ebaafɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Why do I need to clear tall tall sticks and place stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni mikɛ tsei ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up into the sunlight so they can catch more energy to grow bigger tubers underground, while also keeping leaves off damp soil to prevent disease.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli bɔni afee ni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛkɛkwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akabote shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ koni hela akamɔ bo.

english: How soon after planting maize seeds should I apply the first round of fertilizer?
ga: Beni adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, mɛɛ be esa akɛ akɛ ŋmãa klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ awo mli?

english: The first fertilizer application should be done about 10 to 14 days after the seeds sprout, giving young seedlings an immediate boost of nutrients to grow strong roots and thick stems.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli klɛŋklɛŋ aaafee gbii 10 kɛyashi 14 sɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui bibii lɛ ana niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛha shishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with cassava help my farm soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa fataa ŋmãa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, which means their roots capture nitrogen directly from the air and store it in the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for nearby crops like cassava.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmei.

english: Why do my garden eggs and vegetables die when water stands on the field for days after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ gboiɔ beni nu hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When water stands around root zones for too long, it smothers the roots, causes root rot, and kills the plant.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu damɔ shishifã lɛ he be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ, ni ehaa amɛgboɔ ni efiteɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off low-hanging branches and extra shoots from my cashew trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji ni shwieɔ shi shi kɛ tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pruning lower branches opens up the tree so air can flow and sunlight can reach all leaves, which reduces fungal diseases and encourages the tree to produce more nuts on top.
ga: Shishigbɛ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ naa koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli ni hulu la ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ fɛɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo ŋmeii babaoo yɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: How should I arrange cocoa trees on my land so they fit properly and grow well?
ga: Te esa akɛ ato kookoo tsei ahe gbɛjianɔ aha tɛŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛhi ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Proper spacing (typically 3 by 3 meters) ensures each tree gets adequate sunlight, soil nutrients, and airflow. Arranging them neatly allows you to maximize your land without overcrowding the plants.
ga: sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni sa (bei pii lɛ mitai 3 x 3) haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa ni hoɔ lɛ Gbɛjianɔtoo ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ haa onáa he ko babaoo ni okɛ tsei lɛ eyimɔ obɔbɔ.

english: How do I know how many cocoa trees my piece of land can carry?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kookoo tsei enyiɛ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ?

english: You calculate tree capacity based on recommended planting distances. On one acre, standard spacing allows for about 435 cocoa trees to fit properly without competing for light and water.
ga: Obuɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ he akɔntaa kɛdamɔɔ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ adu lɛ nɔ. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre kome nɔ lɛ, Standard spacing lɛ haa aduɔ kookoo tsei aaafee 435 jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ la kɛ nu akaŋ akaŋ.

english: What happens if I plant my cocoa trees too close together on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Overcrowding creates dense shade and high humidity, which makes it easier for fungal diseases like Black Pod to spread. It also forces trees to compete for soil nutrients, reducing overall harvest.
ga: Mɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo baa. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Enyɛɔ tsei anɔ hu koni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nikpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ ba shi.

english: Is it really possible for a single cocoa tree to produce up to four hundred pods?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba mli diɛŋtsɛ akɛ cacao tso kome baanyɛ awo ŋmeii ni fa fe ohai ejwɛ?

english: Yes, high-yielding improved varieties under ideal field management and good soil conditions can carry hundreds of pods over a full crop season, though average yields are usually lower.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei sɔrɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ mli nɔkwɛmɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atere ŋmeii ohai abɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli fɛɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ yibiiwoo ni anáa lɛ faaa moŋ.

english: How many pods should I expect a healthy mature cocoa tree to yield in a year?
ga: Pods enyiɛ esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ cacao tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eda lɛ baawo yɛ afi kome mli?

english: While a tree's maximum potential can reach a few hundred pods under perfect conditions, a well-managed hybrid tree typically yields between 80 to 200 good pods per year across major and minor seasons.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ baanyɛ ashɛ ŋmeii ohai fioo komɛi ahe yɛ shihilɛi ni yeɔ emuu shishi moŋ, shi bei pii lɛ, tsei ni akɛfee tsofai krokomɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa fe 80 kɛyashi 200 daa afi yɛ shishijee kɛ sɛɛ mli be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Which cocoa varieties give the highest pod yields for farmers in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ kookoo henɔ haa okwaafoi lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana?

english: Hybrid varieties (often developed by the Cocoa Research Institute of Ghana) are bred to bear more pods, flower earlier, and show better resistance to local conditions compared to older traditional varieties.
ga: Akwɛɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi (ni bei pii lɛ Ghana Cocoa Research Institute lɛ feɔ) koni amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo, amɛwo fɔfɔi mra, ni amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe kɛ akɛto shishijee ŋmeii ni etsɛ lɛ ahe.

english: What causes my cocoa trees to produce far fewer pods than they are capable of bearing?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo?

english: Yield reduction is usually caused by obstacles such as capsid insect attacks, Black Pod disease, poor soil fertility, prolonged dry weather, or lack of proper pruning.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbɛtsii nii tamɔ capsid kooloi ni tutuaa mɔ, black pod hela, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi lɛ baa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo tsei ni afolɔ jogbaŋŋ ni bɛ

english: Why do young cocoa pods on my tree shrink and turn black before reaching maturity?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiitsɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This can be caused by natural self-thinning (cherelle wilt) if the tree carries more pods than it can feed, or by fungal infections like Black Pod disease which attack young pods.
ga: Enɛ baanyɛ ajɛ adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ hewɔ. (wilt) kɛji tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni abaanyɛ aye loo ŋmeii hela ko tamɔ black pod hela ni tutuaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: How do pests like capsids prevent my cocoa trees from reaching their full harvest?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ capsids lɛ atsĩ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkashɛ amɛkpamɔ ni fa lɛ he?

english: Capsids damage young shoots and pods by sucking sap, which kills leaves and reduces the tree's strength. This prevents the tree from forming and carrying its full capacity of pods.
ga: Capsids fiteɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛtsɔ nu ni amɛnuɔ lɛ nɔ. ni fiteɔ baai lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ baa shi Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafee ni enine ashɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ yɛ bɔ ni enyɛɔ etsuɔ ​​nii eha lɛ naa.

english: What steps can I take to help my cocoa trees reach their maximum yield potential?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni maye mabua mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛná nɔ ni amɛfeɔ lɛ he sɛɛ babaoo?

english: To help trees produce fully, maintain clear field arrangement, prune regularly to allow light, spray to prevent pests and diseases, and apply fertilizer to enrich the soil.
ga: Koni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛwo amɛyibii fɛɛ. Kwɛmɔ he ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa koni eha la aba. Spray koni akɛtsi kooloi kɛ helai anaa. ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ

english: Yellow leaves dropping during the dry or Harmattan season are a defense mechanism against water loss. Excessive leaf loss happens when cocoa trees lack sufficient shade trees, like plantains or leguminous shade trees, to protect them from direct sunlight and harsh winds.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be loo harmattan be mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ naa. Baai ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ baa kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei lɛ bɛ tsei ni fa bɔ ni sa ni haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, tamɔ dumɔwui loo ŋmeii tsei ni haa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Bɔni afee ni abu kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why do many small cocoa flowers drop off the tree without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa flowers require tiny insects called midges for pollination. If there are few midges or weather conditions are too dry, flowers fall off unpollinated. Leaving decomposing leaf litter and shade on the farm floor provides a breeding ground for these helpful midges.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ nakai midge kɛha ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji akɛ amɛyi faaa loo kɔɔyɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni pollination bɛ mli. Baai ni egboi kɛ hulutsoo ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ haa nɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ naa he ko ni amɛfɔɔ bii.

english: Why do my maize plants stay small and pale yellow even after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ feɔ bibioo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pale yellow maize usually lacks nitrogen. Heavy rains can leach nutrients deep into the soil where roots cannot reach. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK around the base of the plant helps it turn dark green and grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa ni mli tse lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo NPK, wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: How can I stop insects from eating my harvested maize while it is stored in sacks?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye mi-ŋmãa lɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Insects thrive when grain is stored with too much moisture. Maize must be dried until the kernels are hard before storage. Using airtight (hermetic) storage bags or approved grain preservation dust prevents weevils from damaging the crop.
ga: Kplukai shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli. Esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa dani akɛto. Kɛ akɛ vacuum ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe (vacuum) loo sũ ni akɛbuɔ dumɔwui ahe lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is typically mature between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and cracks begin to appear in the soil around the base of the stem due to expanding roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe Ni ŋmeii bɔi kpojiemɔ yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli yɛ shishifãi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ hewɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my young yam mounds so frequently?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miyaa nɔ mijieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young yam vines grow slowly at first and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Keeping the field clean during the first three months allows the plant to build strong roots and large tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tse yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or mites, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early with neem oil spray or approved insecticides stops the damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids loo mites, loo helai ni whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akpa nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: What is causing small holes in my tomato leaves and dark rot on the fruits?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ tomato baai kɛ aduawai ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ mli?

english: Holes in leaves and fruit damage are commonly caused by caterpillars or fruit borers. Inspecting plants early, destroying damaged fruits, and applying safe biological or chemical controls prevents pests from destroying the harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ aduawai amli buji kɛ aduawai amli fitemɔ baa. Tsei amli kwɛmɔ mra yibii ni efite lɛ akpãtãmɔ Kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top. Staking the stems with strong wooden poles or planting them in sheltered areas reduces damage from high winds.
ga: Dumɔwu lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii yɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni wa fĩ tso lɛ shishi loo okɛdu yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Is it better to put fertilizer right against the stem of my crop or further away?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mitsei lɛ ashishi loo he ko ni kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the plant tissue. Fertilizer should be placed in a small ring or side-band about a hand-span away from the stem where feeder roots can safely absorb the nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ fãji. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmeii bibii amli. loo sɛɛ ŋtayaa ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee nine kome Feeder shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: How do I know if my crop is sick with a disease or just needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela miimɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ loo ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛkɛ?

english: Diseases often cause unusual yellow mosaic patterns, spots, or soft rot, whereas nutrient shortages usually show up as a uniform light green or yellow fading across the leaf, especially between the leaf veins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai kɛ mosaic ŋmɔŋ ni ejaaa, ŋmɔtɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ jeɔ kpo akɛ su ni ji eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ fɛɛ mli. titri lɛ, yɛ baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ ateŋ

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow with patchy patterns?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: When leaves turn yellow with mosaic or patchy patterns, it usually indicates a viral infection like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Disease. If the yellowing is smooth and uniform, it is more likely a lack of plant nutrients in the soil.
ga: Beni baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ mosaic loo patchy mfoniri. Bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli, tamɔ kookoo tsei ni efuu. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni po Ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe niyenii.

english: Why do the veins on my leaves stay bright green while the rest of the leaf turns yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fãji ni yɔɔ mibaai lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni baa ni eshwɛ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When leaf tissue turns pale while the veins remain green, it means your crop is suffering from a nutrient deficiency in the soil, such as a lack of iron or magnesium, rather than an insect attack or viral disease.
ga: Beni baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ eŋɔli lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miipiŋ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ, tamɔ dade loo magnesium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni kooloi ni baatutua mɔ loo hela ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ

english: What causes a mosaic or marble-like pattern to appear on my young leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa mibaai bibii lɛ feɔ mosaic loo marble he mfoniri?

english: Mosaic patterns are usually caused by plant viruses spread by small insects like mealybugs. The virus disrupts the green pigment in the leaves, leaving light and dark green patches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei amli helai ni kooloi bibii, tamɔ mealybugs gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ mosaic he mfonirii lɛ baa. Virus lɛ gbalaa tsofai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ amli. Ashiɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my young crops turn yellow as soon as they start growing bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji ebɔi agbojee pɛ?

english: Rapid growth requires a lot of food from the soil. If the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, the plant cannot feed its new growth, causing the young leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nɔ ni yaa hiɛ oya lɛ biɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsei nyɛŋ amɛwo dalɛ hee. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How can I tell if bad soil is making my plant leaves look pale?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ gbonyo miiha mitso lɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: If the soil around your plant is exhausted or dry, the whole leaf usually turns a uniform pale green or yellow color because the roots cannot extract enough food and water to feed the plant.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle tso lɛ he lɛ mli egbo loo egbi lɛ Bei pii lɛ, baa muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni tamɔ nɔ kome. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua tso lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to check the soil around the base and roots of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Checking the tree's base helps you spot root rot early, inspect soil moisture, and confirm whether fertilizer is reaching the roots before severe symptoms show up on the leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ otso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona shishifãi ni egbo mra. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni okwɛ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ lɛ eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe dani okadii ni mli wa aba yɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: What makes the soil around the base of my tree look dark and rotten?
ga: Mɛni miiha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ miifee tamɔ nɔ ni edɔ ni efite?

english: Poor soil drainage and standing water around the base can breed fungal diseases that rot the roots and trunk base, causing the bark to soften and the plant to struggle.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nu damɔ shi ebɔle he. Shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ fiteɔ aba. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ.

english: How can I tell if a damaged cocoa pod has a disease or was just cut during harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ efite, hela emɔ amɛ loo afolɔ amɛ kɛkɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: Harvest damage leaves a clean cut or scratch that dries up, while a disease causes dark, spreading spots, soft decaying tissue, or powdery growth on the pod.
ga: Nikpamɔ mli nibii ni efite lɛ baaha ŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ ni he tse, ni egbi. yɛ be mli ni hela lɛ kɛ fãji diji ni egbɛ eshwã ni fiteɔ loo powda shwereɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ baa

english: Can I spread sickness to healthy cocoa trees when I cut off diseased pods?
ga: Ani manyɛ magbɛ hela ashwã cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli kɛ́ mifo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, cutting a diseased pod leaves bad germs on your harvesting knife. If you cut a healthy pod right after without cleaning your tool, you can transfer the disease directly to the healthy plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ baashi helatsɛmɛi gbohii yɛ o-kpamɔ tsɔne lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ofo pod ni hi jogbaŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni otsuuu dɛŋdade lɛ he lɛ, Obaanyɛ ogbɛ hela lɛ oshwã tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do I know the exact number of weeks my crop will take from planting until it is ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male otsii pɔtɛɛ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ baahe kɛjɛ dumɔ mli kɛyashi be mli ni ebaakpa?

english: Every crop variety has a specific growth cycle, usually measured in weeks or months. You can determine harvest time by checking the maturity period of the seed variety, tracking your planting date, and watching for visual signs of maturity like leaf yellowing or dry pods.
ga: Tso henɔ fɛɛ tso yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko ni etsɔɔ nɔ edaa. Bei pii lɛ, asusuɔ he yɛ otsii loo nyɔji amli. Obaanyɛ ole kpamɔ be lɛ kɛtsɔ be ni dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ. Nyiɛmɔ gbii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ asɛɛ Ni otao okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ eshɛ, tamɔ baai ni miifee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmeii ni egbi.

english: Why does the timing of crop growth matter so much to the total yield I get at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be ni tsei lɛ daa lɛ he hiaa waa kɛha yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni minine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Proper growth timing ensures that critical plant stages—like flowering and seed formation—happen when soil moisture and weather conditions are optimal. If timing is off, flowers may fall off or seeds may not fill properly, leading to a smaller harvest.
ga: Be ni sa ni tso lɛ daa lɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ tso lɛ fãi ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui afeemɔ lɛ yaa nɔ. Ebaa be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi hi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ atsɔɔɔ be lɛ Fɔfɔi baanyɛ agbee shi loo dumɔwui lɛ ehiɛɛɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kpamɔ fioo.

english: Why is it important for me to plant my crops at the exact start of the rainy season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Planting at the start of the rainy season ensures your crops receive continuous moisture during their critical early growth stages. If you plant late, the rainy season might end before your crops finish maturing, leading to dried-up plants and crop loss.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ mra yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ mra be mli dalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli. Kɛji odu nii yɛ sɛɛ mli Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baanyɛ aba naagbee dani onibii lɛ ashɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hu laajeɔ.

english: If I only have about two months of rainy season left, what kind of crops should I plant on my farm?
ga: Kɛji nyɔji enyɔ pɛ eshwɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ adu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When the remaining rainy season is short, you should plant short-duration or early-maturing crop varieties, such as short-season maize, cowpeas, or quick vegetables. These crops complete their growth cycle in a short time before the dry season sets in.
ga: Beni nugbɔshiimɔ be ni eshwɛ lɛ faaa lɛ Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ ŋmãa ni yeɔ be kukuoo, tsina ŋmei, loo aduawai ni yeɔ mra. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ gbeɔ amɛdalɛ be kukuoo mli dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow slower or faster depending on the time of year I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo loo oya yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni miduɔ lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Crop growth speed depends on sunlight, temperature, and soil moisture. Warm, sunny, and moist conditions speed up plant processes like photosynthesis, shortening the time needed to mature, while cold or dry weather slows growth down.
ga: Tso dalɛ oyaiyeli damɔ hulu la, dɔlɛ kɛ sũ mli fɛ̃i nɔ. Dɔlɛ, hulu, kɛ fɛ̃i shihilɛ haa tsei anifeemɔi tamɔ fotosintɛsis yaa oya. Ehaa be ni ekɛbaa lɛ feɔ kuku. yɛ be mli ni shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ loo hulutsoo be lɛ haa shweremɔ baa shi.

english: Can unfavorable weather conditions delay the number of weeks my crops need to mature in the field?
ga: Ani kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii lɛ baanyɛ aha otsii abɔ ni ehe baahia ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ asɛɛ afo?

english: Yes, dry spells or prolonged periods without sunlight cause crop stress, which slows down growth. This stress forces the plant to spend extra days or weeks recovering, extending the total time it needs on the field before harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi loo be kakadaŋŋ ni hulu la bɛ mli lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. ni haa tso lɛ dalɛ baa shi Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ gbii loo otsii babaoo tsuɔ nii dani ehiɛɔ shi. Enɛ haa be fɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani akpaa kpamɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: How do I estimate how many total days or weeks I will need to spend working on my farm during a crop season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu gbii loo otsii fɛɛ ni he baahia ni matsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: You calculate this by adding up the labor days needed for major activities throughout the crop's lifecycle: field preparation, planting, routine weeding, fertilizer application, and final harvesting. Fast-maturing crops require fewer total labor days overall.
ga: Obuɔ enɛ he akɔntaa kɛtsɔ nitsumɔ gbii ni he hiaa kɛha nitsumɔi titrii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashihilɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ: ŋmɔ mli saamɔ, dumɔwui, jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ naagbee ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni daa oya lɛ biɔ be fioo yɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: If my crop takes around eight to ten weeks to mature, when should I begin preparing my equipment and storage for harvest?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ heɔ aaafee otsi kpaanyɔ kɛyashi nyɔŋma dani eshɛɔ lɛ Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mabɔi nibii kɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ he kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ he saamɔ?

english: You should begin preparing harvest equipment, bags, and dry storage areas about two to three weeks before the target harvest date. This ensures everything is clean and ready, preventing delays that could cause mature crops to rot in the field.
ga: Esa akɛ oje okpamɔ nibii, kotokui, kɛ he ni okɛ nibii ni egbi lɛ toɔ lɛ he saamɔ shishi otsii enyɔ loo etɛ dani gbi ni okɛkpamɔ lɛ aba. Koni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ he atse ni asaa he. Etsiɔ sɛɛkuu ni baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii afite yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ naa.

english: How can I tell the difference between a crop that is still growing and one that is ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lolo kɛ nɔ ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ teŋ?

english: A growing crop actively produces new green leaves, stems, or flowers. A crop ready for harvest stops growing, starts drying out or changing color (like turning from green to brown or yellow), and produces hard seeds or ripe fruits.
ga: Tsei ni miida lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli heei, tsei ashishifãi, loo fɔfɔi. Nibii ni asaa he kɛha kpamɔ lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ. Ejeɔ shishi egbiɔ loo etsakeɔ esu (ni ji, etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa asarasu loo ŋmɔŋ mli) ni ewoɔ dumɔwui ni wa loo aduawai ni ekwɛ̃.

english: What will happen to my crops if I harvest them a few weeks late?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikpa yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Leaving mature crops in the field for too long exposes them to pests, field fires, and rotting from late rains. Over-mature grains may also shatter and fall onto the soil, causing you to lose a large part of your yield.
ga: Nibii ni eda ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Enɛ baaha tsei nɛɛ aná tsɛŋemɔ helai, ŋmɔ mli la kɛ fitemɔ ni jɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ. Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ akumɔ ni amɛgbee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa onibii ni ofeɔ lɛ babaoo fiteɔ

english: Young cocoa plants have very sensitive leaves that dry out and burn easily in direct sunlight. They need shade trees or food crops like plantains grown beside them to block strong sun and keep the air cool while they are young.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa. Egbiɔ ni etswaa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo niyenii tsei, tamɔ plantains, ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ehaa amɛhe jɔɔ be mli ni amɛdarako lolo lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which gives plants their rich green color and strength. Adding animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps the plant turn green and grow strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmɔŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts in the same farm where I plant my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Beans and groundnuts pull natural food (nitrogen) out of the air and put it into the soil through their roots. This feeds your maize crop naturally and keeps the soil fertile without having to buy as many artificial fertilizers.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbalaa niyenii (nitrogen) kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha o-corn tsei lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food for the plant. Lifting the leaves off the ground with sticks keeps them healthy, prevents leaves from rotting on damp soil, and helps the plant build bigger tubers underground.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni ekɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei niji tsu nii ni akɛwo baai anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of big leaves but giving me tiny roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cassava lɛ daa shɔŋŋ nɛkɛ lɛ? Baai wuji shi shishifãi bibii?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen or grows under too much shade, it spends all its energy growing upper leaves and stems instead of root tubers. Proper spacing and balanced soil nutrients encourage the plant to send its energy down into making large roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tsɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋwɛi tsei lɛ amli yɛ shishifãi lɛ najiaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ja lɛ haa tsei lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni shishifãi wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why are small worms eating holes inside the middle leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides in the center fold of young maize plants to chew tender leaves. Inspecting your fields early and applying botanical solutions like neem extract or recommended pest treatments protects your yield.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Odumɔi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ neem mli nu loo tsofai krokomɛi ni ajieɔ yi akɛ gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baaye abua ni abu onibii ahe.

english: Why is it good practice to cover the soil around my pepper plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle o-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass or dry leaves, called mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It traps moisture in the soil so plants stay hydrated longer, keeps the roots cool during hot afternoons, and stops weed seeds from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahi shi yɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃

english: Why shouldn't I sow my maize seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain after a long dry season often dries up quickly, leaving the soil hot and dry again. If seeds sprout and the rain stops for weeks, the young seedlings will die. It is safer to wait until two or three heavy rains confirm the rainy season has truly started.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ fɔɔ gbee oya. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adɔ ni egbi ekoŋŋ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii babaoo. Tso bibioo lɛ baagbo. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ aba koni oma nɔ mi akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eje shishi diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Why are the bottom tips of my green tomatoes turning soft and black before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ naji lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni eyɛ ediŋŋ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when tomato plants do not get enough calcium or suffer from irregular watering while setting fruit. Watering your plants consistently and adding well-rotted manure or lime to the soil helps fix it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ loo amɛnáaa nu yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ. Nu ni oooha tsei lɛ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsake naagba lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I place strong chemical fertilizer directly touching the stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii amli lɛ woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer contains concentrated mineral salts that can burn tender plant stems and roots if placed directly against them. It is best to place fertilizer in a small ring or pocket a few inches away from the stem where the outer roots can safely reach it.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ mineral salts ni mli eyi obɔ ni baanyɛ ashã tsei ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ amɛshishifãi kɛji akɛ akɛma shi shiŋŋ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo ŋmeii bibii amli. Aloo baagi ko ni kɛ tsɔne lɛ mli tsɔne lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ. ni kponɔgbɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sun. Without shade from larger forest trees or nurse crops like plantains, the harsh sun scorches their tender leaves, causing them to turn yellow, dry up, and die.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ koo mli tsei wuji loo tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ bɛ hulutsoo be lɛ, hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛgbiɔ, ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The plants stretch upward to catch light instead of building thick stems and producing big cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe koni amɛhe la lɛ, moŋ lɛ, amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is it bad to save seeds from my high-yielding hybrid maize harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ oookɛ ŋmãa ni ji hybrid dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ato koni adu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially crossed to give high yields only in the first harvest. If you plant the seeds saved from that harvest, the offspring will lose their vigor, resulting in small cobs and poor yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ pɛ mli. Kɛ́ odu dumɔwui ni hiɔ shi yɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Gbekɛ lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ yibiiwoo ni ehiii baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning pale yellow even though we get plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves despite good rainfall usually mean the soil has run out of vital plant food like nitrogen. Water alone is not enough; crops need nutrients from fertile soil, compost, or fertilizer to stay green and grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen. Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa. Tsei hia niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mli, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara.

english: Cowpeas and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural fertilizer in the soil. This extra plant food feeds the corn and improves soil fertility for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Tso niyenii krɛdɛɛ nɛɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off before turning into actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani ebatsɔ anɔkwa yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or lack of pollination. When the plant gets too hot or thirsty, it drops its flowers to protect itself from dying.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo pollination ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kumai miiye lɛ Eshiɔ fɔfɔi yɛ esɛɛ koni ekɛbu ehe kɛjɛ gbele he.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into tight balls during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ bɔɔlu ni mli wa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up to reduce the leaf surface area exposed to the sun, which helps the plant save water. However, leaf curling can also be caused by tiny sucking pests like mites or thrips hiding under the leaves.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba baa lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ nu toɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does letting weeds grow around my yam mounds reduce the size of my harvested tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni oha jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mi sweet potato pile lɛ eha ŋmeii ni akpaa lɛ ayibɔ eba shi.

english: Weeds have strong roots that quickly steal water, manure, and fertilizer away from your yams. When yams are starved of nutrients, they cannot store energy to grow large tubers underground.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu, ŋmei, kɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmei mli lɛ oya. Beni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waaa lɛ bɛ sweet potatoes lɛ Enyɛŋ ekɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ bulbs wuji lɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I prune the lower branches and extra shoots off my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni majie ŋmeii krokomɛi ni fata mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Pruning lower leaves stops rainwater from splashing soil-borne diseases onto the plant. Removing extra side shoots also forces the plant to send its food energy directly into producing bigger, healthier fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu lɛ akagbɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛbaa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ. Nibii ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ hu nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni etsɔɔ niyenii hewalɛ gbɛ koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully mature so they do not rot in the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ kɛ́ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, amɛgboŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves yellow and shed, usually between 9 to 12 months after planting. Leaving tubers in wet ground too long after maturity causes them to become woody, watery, or rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afee tsei. Nu loo egbo

english: Does my yam vine really need a wooden stake, or can I just let it crawl on the bare ground?
ga: Mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he miihia tso tso diɛŋtsɛ. Aloo obaanyɛ oha etsɔ shikpɔŋ ni agbele nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Staking holds the leaves up so they can catch maximum sunlight to produce food, which leads to much bigger tubers. Letting vines crawl on the ground leaves them exposed to heat from the soil and disease.
ga: Staking haa baai lɛ ŋmɛɔ shi bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii. Enɛ kɛ yitso ni da kwraa baa. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ wein tsei lɛ gbɛ ni amɛkplekeshi shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ kɛ helai.

english: Why are the leaves on my yam vines turning yellow even though it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? He ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the soil lacks nutrients like nitrogen, or the ground is holding too much water around the roots, causing waterlogging which suffocates the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiɛ nu babaoo ni ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa nu shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why is my yam plant growing small bulbs on the stem up in the air instead of growing big yams in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? yɛ tso ko nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmei agbo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Some yam varieties naturally grow aerial tubers on the vine, but if underground growth is poor, it often means the soil is too hard, lacks potassium, or the plant received too much nitrogen.
ga: Sweet potatoes komɛi kwɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ŋmeii yɛ wain tsei anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi shweremɔ lɛ ehiii Bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Potassium ni bɛ loo tsei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wilt and die when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade trees or food crops like plantain above them to protect them from heat stress and keep the moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo niyenii tsei, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsi dɔlɛ he haomɔ naa ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop all their flowers before any pods start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by drought, extreme heat, or a lack of beneficial insects to pollinate the tiny flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni baaha fɔfɔi bibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ hao amɛ.

english: Why do some of my small green cocoa pods turn black and shrivel while hanging on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ No hewɔ ni minɔ lɛ tsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo beni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This can be caused by 'Black Pod disease,' which spreads in damp, overly shaded farm areas, or 'cherelle wilt,' which is the tree's natural way of dropping extra pods it cannot support.
ga: Nɔ ni baanyɛ aha enɛ aba ji ‘black pod hela’, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ mli hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli fe nine lɛ, loo 'Cherelle wilt', ni ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni tso lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to clear weeds around the outer edges of my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds at the edge of your farm create a bridge for insect pests like mealybugs and capsids to crawl from wild plants directly onto your crop trees.
ga: Jwɛi ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ feɔ blɔfo kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mealybugs kɛ capsids. Koni okɛ ohe awo koo mli tsei amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛya oŋmɔ mli tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why did my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but gave me very thin roots at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi kɛ́ akpa lɛ, ewoɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, cassava puts all its energy into growing top leaves and stems rather than storing food underground in the roots.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ toɔ zugba a sisi ngɛ tso ɔ sisi.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up into tight tubes during the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the maize plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, preventing moisture from evaporating too quickly during hot hours.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he yɛ ŋmãa tsei amli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: How close can I safely plant yams near the border of my cocoa trees without harming either crop?
ga: Te manyɛ madu sweet potato shweshweeshwe yɛ he ni mabɛŋkɛ cacao tso lɛ naa tɛŋŋ ni mayeee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko kwraa awui?

english: Yams and cocoa should be planted far enough apart so the climbing yam vines do not wrap around young cocoa stems and smother them, and so their roots do not fight for the same water and nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ adu sweet potatoes kɛ cocoa yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛ bɔ ni sa. Enɛ ji koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akabɔle kookoo niji bibii lɛ ahe ni amɛtsi kookoo niji lɛ anaa. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe wooo nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need shade plants like plantains growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and have broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa from heat stress and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, damp, and cold conditions. Excess rain combined with thick tree branches traps moisture, allowing the fungus to spread quickly between pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ hei ni mli ejɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ tsei niji ni mli tse yeɔ ebuaa ni emɔɔ fɛ̃i. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ oya.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, a key food crop plants need to grow. It can also happen when heavy water sitting in the soil starves the roots of air, preventing them from soaking up soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii tso ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ muji ni abua naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ha hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋwɛi shishifãi lɛ. Etsiɔ enaa koni ekaŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist, but not during heavy rainfall. Burying or lightly covering the fertilizer with topsoil near the plant roots keeps the rain from washing the plant food away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli tseee ni akɛ ŋwɛi sũ lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baafu loo akɛha nɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni nugbɔ akafɔ tso niyenii lɛ nɔ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients that crop relies on. It also gives pests and soil diseases that feed on maize a permanent place to multiply year after year.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ ekwɛɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii ni yɔɔ srɔto ni tso lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ nɔ lɛ. Ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ hu naa he ko ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ daa afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce small roots when weeds cover the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ shishifãi bibii yɔɔ be mli ni jwɛi ha ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your cassava plants. When weeds are left to grow, your crop does not get enough food to develop big, thick tubers underground.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ o-cassava tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Beni aŋmɛ jwɛi gbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛná ŋmeii wuji ni mli tse.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce tiny fruits when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots fight each other underground for water and plant food, while their leaves block sunlight from one another, resulting in weak plants with small harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ tsei niyenii. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa fioo ko baa.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make energy for the tubers growing under the dirt. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground into the light and keeps them clean from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa la ni tsoɔ waa mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ he tseɔ kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the middle leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds on the central leaves of young corn plants. They chew through the growing center, which damages new leaves before they open and reduces the crop's ability to grow.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ. Amɛfoɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ. Enɛ baafite baai heei lɛ dani amɛgbele. ni ebaa nyɛmɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air gets too hot, when the plant lacks moisture, or when insects like bees are not around to pollinate them. Watering regularly and shading during extreme heat helps save the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ nu Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ jɛmɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Excessive water fills the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the plant roots and washing away essential nutrients like nitrogen, which causes the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any fruit during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the tomato plant, causing it to shed its blossoms to save energy and water rather than investing resources into growing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ amɛfɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii baawo aduawai akwɛmɔ mli lɛ

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their young pods during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ eshishifãi bibii lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed young pods, a process called pod wilt, to conserve water and survive severe dry weather.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbii bibii lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ pod wilting. Koni akɛbu nu he ni ahi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa amli.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on to give big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni ekɛkwɔ koni ekɛ bulbs agboi akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yams need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food; staking spreads the leaves out so the plant can feed its underground tuber effectively.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potatoes yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛhoo. Staking lɛ gbɛɔ baai lɛ eshwaa bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ aye abua ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground if I do not harvest them before the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ akpaaa amɛ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Mature cassava roots absorb too much excess water during heavy rains, which causes the roots to soften, crack, and rot in the soil.
ga: Kasava shishifãi ni eda lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo ni fa fe nine yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo, amɛgbalaa ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weed seeds grow much faster than my planted crops after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ dara oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weed seeds are naturally adapted to sprout instantly with minimal water, while cultivated crops take longer to absorb moisture and break dormancy.
ga: Akɛ jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ koo mli lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ nu fioo ko pɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni adu lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛmuɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfoɔ ŋmiŋmi ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves or spreading viruses to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ loo amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn brown and dry up prematurely from the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi oya kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: This is often a sign of fungal diseases like Black Sigatoka or water shortage, where the plant cannot transport enough nutrients to keep its large leaves alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko tamɔ Black Sigatoka loo nu ni bɛ lɛ he okadi. Biɛ ji he ni tso lɛ nyɛŋ ekɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekwɛ ebaai wuji lɛ anɔ lɛ aya.

english: Why do my crop roots stay shallow near the surface instead of going deep into the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ he ko ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaaya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Hard, compacted soil underneath the surface acts like a barrier, preventing roots from pushing downward and forcing them to grow sideways.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ebɔle ehe ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ ashɛ shi ni enyɛ amɛnɔ koni amɛdara yɛ afã.

english: Why do seeds saved from my last harvest of hybrid maize produce smaller yields when I replant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛji midu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for one generation; saving and replanting their offspring causes the crops to lose their vigor, producing weaker plants and smaller cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛhaa yinɔ kome. Seshi ni ahereɔ kɛyaa he kroko ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe waaa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ hu feɔ bibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep drying up when I plant them in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that easily burn in harsh direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain or cassava beside young cocoa acts like a protective umbrella, providing the cool shade and soil moisture the cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei, tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa kookoo koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ haa.

english: Why do my corn plants grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ hewɔ lɛ

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. The plants stretch upward trying to reach light, which leaves them with weak stems and little energy to grow thick cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tso lɛ baatsi ehe kɛya ŋwɛi yɛ mɔdɛŋ ni ebɔɔ koni ekɛ la aha. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnáaa hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛkɛbaatsɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and grow leaves. The plant pulls food from its old bottom leaves to keep the young top leaves alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Tsei gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni baai bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge green leaves but small, thin roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ?

english: When soil is too hard or packed tightly, cassava roots cannot expand underground to store food. Cassava needs loose, well-tilled soil or raised mounds so the roots can easily spread and thicken into large tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ, Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkɛ niyenii ato. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni atsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ he miihia cassava bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm help my maize grow better?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have tiny bumps on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the ground. When planted with maize, they naturally enrich the soil with free fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Be ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni ŋmãa bɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt or fungal rot living in the soil. These germs block the tiny water pipes inside the plant stem, preventing water from reaching the upper leaves even if the roots are sitting in moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ muawai ni fiteɔ loo fungal rot ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ tsiɔ nu paipii bibii ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ anaa, ni no haaa nu ayashɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ amli edɔ po.

english: Why are small worms eating holes inside the funnels of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These worms are likely Fall Armyworms, which prefer to hide inside the moist center roll of young corn plants where tender new leaves develop, eating them before they can fully open.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhi amɛhe yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ amli he ni baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ shwereɔ yɛ lɛ ni amɛyeɔ amɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe kwraa lɛ.

english: Why do all the blossoms on my pepper plants drop off without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience heat stress, lack of soil moisture, or irregular watering. The plant sheds its flowers to save water and energy so it can survive the harsh condition.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛnyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why do weeds come up much faster than my crops after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds naturally lie waiting in the top layer of the soil and are adapted to sprout immediately with the slightest moisture, while planted crops take longer to absorb water and break out of their seed coats.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui mɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni atsakeɔ lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛmɔɔ nu ni amɛjieɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffocating from too much rain and waterlogging?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ hewɔ?

english: When soil stays flooded with water for days, the plant roots cannot breathe in air. As a result, the crop leaves turn light green or pale yellow, growth completely stops, and the roots turn black and soft.
ga: Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ Tse lɛ shishifãi nyɛŋ amu kɔɔyɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ. Dalɛ kpaɔ kwraa. ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo

english: Why does my rice crop turn yellow and stop growing when the rain stops for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Rice plants need constant moisture to draw food from the soil. When dry spells happen, the roots cannot absorb nitrogen, which makes the leaves turn yellow and stalls the plant's growth.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ hia nu ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛgbala niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji hɔmɔ he okadii ba lɛ Shishifãi nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nitrogen. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etsĩɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: How do I know when it is the right time to plant my seeds when the rainy season keeps changing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa akɛ adu dumɔwui? Beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: It is best to plant after the soil has received at least two or three heavy, soaking rains. Planting in dry or slightly damp soil causes the seeds to dry out and die before they can fully sprout.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu beni kɛ hoo lɛ, nugbɔ nɛ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo nɔ ni mli edɔ fioo nɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: How can I keep my crops alive if the rains stop earlier in the season than expected?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahi shi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, traps moisture in the ground for much longer and protects plant roots from drying out in the sun.
ga: Mulching around Kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni ebuɔ tsei shishifãi ahe koni hulu lɛ akagbi

english: If I clear a larger piece of land to farm, why don't my harvests automatically double?
ga: Kɛji mijie he ko ni da kɛha okwaayeli Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ eyaaa hiɛ shii enyɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: A larger field requires more seeds, fertilizer, and labor to weed. If you spread your limited resources too thin over a big plot, the crops will suffer from competition and yield less per acre.
ga: Hei wuji biɔ dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nitsumɔ babaoo koni akɛjie jwɛi. Kɛji akɛ ogbɛ onibii fioo ni oyɔɔ lɛ oshwã he ko ni da waa lɛ, akaŋshii naa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo ni baa lɛ faaa yɛ acre kome mli.

english: Why is it important for me to plow and break up the soil before sowing my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mifoɔ mli dani miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Loosening hard ground allows young plant roots to easily grow deep into the earth to search for food and groundwater, while also allowing rainwater to soak into the soil instead of running off.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ daa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ oya koni amɛyatao niyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, aŋmɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ gbɛ ni eboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeejo foi.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant them without applying any fertilizer or manure?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsuuu nii?

english: Crops feed on nutrients in the soil just like humans need food. Without extra fertilizer or compost to replenish used-up nutrients, crops grow weak, produce small fruits, and give poor yields.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ bɔ ni niyenii he hiaa adesai lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi bɛ ni akɛbaawo niyenii ni efite lɛ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baagbɔjɔ, ebaawo yibii bibii ni ebaaná yibiiwoo fioo.

english: Why do some types of rice grow well in muddy, flooded swamp areas while others rot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli ewo muji amli shi ekrokomɛi hu fiteɔ lɛ?

english: Lowland rice varieties have special stems that carry air down to their roots underwater, whereas upland rice varieties need air directly from dry soil and will rot if submerged in standing water.
ga: Omɔ henɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baa shi kɛyaa nu shishi shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa henɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he hiaa kɔɔyɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ. ni ebaagbo kɛji akɛ awo nu ni damɔ shi mli.

english: Why does planting the same crop on the same farm plot every year make my yields drop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Repeatedly planting one crop drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and encourages soil pests to multiply. Rotating different crops keeps the soil balanced and healthy.
ga: Tso kome ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ lɛ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛshwere Nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni sũ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Weeds are wild, native plants with deep root systems that quickly grab water and plant food before your cultivated crops can get established, which is why early weeding is necessary.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shwieɔ nu oya ni amɛduɔ niyenii dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ daa. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia

english: Why shouldn't I just save and plant seeds from my previous harvest instead of buying fresh certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, hɔɔ dumɔwuhi ehehi nɛ a wo he odase ɔ.

english: Seeds saved from harvested crops naturally lose their vigor and disease resistance over time, resulting in weaker plants and smaller yields compared to carefully selected certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akpaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni ahala jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my maize crops turn pale and grow slowly when weeds are left around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ mli tse ni edaa fiofio be mli ni jwɛi eshwɛ ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Crops compete aggressively with weeds for essential soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. When weeds are allowed to grow unchecked, they steal these vital resources, leaving your maize starving and weak.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, nu kɛ hulu la. Beni aŋmɛɔ jwɛi gbɛ ni amɛkwɛɛɛ nɔ Amɛbaaju nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye o-abele lɛ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why does planting my crops too close together make them tall and thin with poor yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mitsei lɛ ni miduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they stretch upward to fight each other for sunlight instead of spending energy on growing thick stems, deep roots, or healthy fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛye hulu la he akaŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafite hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni mli tse, shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, loo aduawai ni mli wa.

english: How does leaving cut grass around the base of my tomato plants help them stay healthy during dry periods?
ga: Jwɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ Teɔ tɛŋŋ ni tomato tsei ashishitoo yeɔ ebuaa ni tomato lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dried grass acts like a protective blanket that traps moisture in the ground, keeps the soil cool, and prevents the sun from baking the shallow roots of your crops.
ga: Mulch ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni ŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa hulu la lɛ ashã ŋmɔshi nibii ashishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot when I leave diseased pods hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ mishi ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Fungal diseases like black pod produce invisible spores on rotten pods that spread to healthy green pods through rain splashes and air currents, destroying your crop before harvest.
ga: Fungal helai tamɔ black pods lɛ feɔ spores ni anaaa yɛ pods ni egboi anɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa pods eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ. ni fiteɔ onibii dani akpaa.

english: How does trimming off unwanted branches help my cocoa trees yield more pods?
ga: Te niji ni ataooo lɛ ni ooofo lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-cacao tso lɛ ni ewo ŋmeii babaoo lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Pruning removes non-producing branches so the tree can focus all its food and nutrients directly into growing healthy pods, while also allowing light and air to pass through to stop diseases.
