ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni wooo yibii lɛ koni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama eniyenii kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ tsei ni miida ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni ekɛtsi helai anaa.

english: Why do my crops still suffer from pest damage even after chemical spraying has been done?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ fiteɔ lolo yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: If sprays are applied at the wrong time of day, mixed incorrectly, or fail to hit the underside of leaves where pests hide, the insects will survive and continue feeding on your crops.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashwie tsofa lɛ yɛ be ni ejaaa mli Futumɔ ni ejaaa Aloo kaabote baai lɛ ashishi he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ. Kplukai lɛ baahi shi ni amɛya nɔ amɛye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What happens to my cassava roots if I delay harvesting them past their maturity time?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ be ni ato lɛ sɛɛ fo?

english: Overripe cassava roots turn tough and woody inside, losing their starch quality and becoming more vulnerable to soil pests and root rot, which reduces their market value.
ga: Kasava shishifãi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ bafeɔ nɔ ni wa ni efeɔ tso yɛ emli. Ashikishaŋ kpakpa ni elaajeɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ oshara waa kɛha shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ. Enɛ baaha jarayeli jara lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my yam plants need tall wooden stakes to climb as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ he hiaa tsei kakadaji ni amɛkwɔ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbing vines that need their leaves spread out in direct sunlight to manufacture food for building large, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni shwieɔ shi ni biɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni baaha ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my beans grow better when I plant them in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Beans are soil-building plants that feed natural nitrogen from the air into the dirt, which acts as a free boost of plant food for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Beans ji tsei ni maa shikpɔŋ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni hoɔ oya ni akɛfataa niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa he.

english: Why does applying fertilizer during a severe dry spell burn my crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli lɛ haa baai shãa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need soil water to dissolve safely; without moisture, concentrated salts in the fertilizer draw water out of the plant roots, causing the leaves to dry up and scorch.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni etsɔ shweshweeshwe. Kɛji hulutsoo be bɛ Nuŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa.

english: What is pollination, and why does my cocoa farm need it to grow pods?
ga: Mɛni ji pollination? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛ pods lɛ?

english: Pollination is how pollen moves from flower to flower so they can turn into fruit. Without pollination, the flowers on your cocoa trees will simply drop off without ever forming pods.
ga: Pollination ji be mli ni pollen lɛ jɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli koni ebatsɔ aduawai. Kɛji akɛ pollination bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii kɔkɔɔkɔ.

english: Why do so many flowers fall off my trees without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo miiho kɛmiijɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when they are not properly pollinated by insects or by hand, or when the tree lacks enough water and nutrients to support all the growing pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii loo nine eshɛɛɛ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ. aloo be mli ni tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha eshishifãi fɛɛ ni miida lɛ aye abua lɛ.

english: What happens to my crop harvest if there are no midges or insects around to pollinate the flowers?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ anɔ? Kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii loo kooloi bibii komɛi bɛ he ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Without pollinating insects like midges, very few flowers get fertilized, which drastically reduces the total number of pods your farm will produce.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pollinators tamɔ midges bɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi fioo ko pɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi. Enɛ baaha pods ni oŋmɔ lɛ baawo lɛ fɛɛ ayibɔ aba shi waa.

english: Is hand pollination actually worth doing, or is it just extra work for the farmer?
ga: Nine nɔ pollination he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ diɛŋtsɛ. Aloo eji nitsumɔ krɛdɛɛ ko kɛkɛ kɛha okwaafoi?

english: Hand pollination directly transfers pollen to the flowers, which helps ensure that a much higher percentage of flowers successfully turn into full pods compared to relying on insects alone.
ga: Nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ kɛ pollen yaa fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi ni baaye omanye ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ amli oha mlijaa 100 lɛ fa babaoo. Kɛ akɛto kooloi bibii pɛ ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ he

english: How many pods can one cocoa tree reasonably produce in a season?
ga: Kakao tso baanyɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii enyiɛ yɛ be kome mli?

english: A normal tree might give around 100 pods, but exceptionally healthy and well-pollinated trees can produce hundreds or even up to 1,000 pods under ideal conditions.
ga: Tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɛnɛ lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmeii aaafee 100, shi titri lɛ tsei ni wa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmeii ohai abɔ loo nɔ ni fa fe 1,000 yɛ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ mli.

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees give a lot of pods while others right next to them barely give any?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ be mli ni nɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ? Ani ebɛ eko kwraa?

english: Each tree has different access to sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, and individual trees also differ naturally in strength and how well their flowers get pollinated.
ga: Tso fɛɛ tso náa hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ yɛ srɔtoi Tsei srɔtoi hu yɛ amɛhewalɛ kɛ bɔ ni amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is my total harvest usually lower than what I calculate based on my best-performing tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, mikpamɔ fɛɛ baa shi fe bɔ ni mibuɔ he akɔntaa yɛ mi tsei ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Not every tree on a farm gets ideal conditions; natural factors like pests, shade, and uneven pollination mean the average yield across your whole farm will always be lower than your single best tree.
ga: Jeee tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni ahaa shihilɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ. Adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, hulutsoo kɛ pollination ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ yibiiwoo ni baa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ baafee nɔ ni baa shi be fɛɛ be fe tso kome ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do tiny young pods sometimes stop growing and dry up on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsei bibii kpaa kwɛ̃mɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is called cherelle wilt, which happens when the tree realizes it does not have enough water or nutrients to feed all the young pods, so it naturally drops some to save the rest.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ yɔse akɛ ebɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ eshishifãi bibii lɛ fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ bɔ ni eji lɛ, ebaatsɔ ekomɛi anɔ koni ekɛbu nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Can hand pollination help trees that normally don't produce any pods to start bearing fruit?
ga: Ani nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tsei ni bei pii lɛ amɛwooo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ni amɛwo yibii?

english: Yes, many trees that seem unproductive are simply not getting visited by pollinating insects, so manually pollinating their flowers can trigger them to start producing pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsei babaoo ni tamɔ nɔ ni wooo yibii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ eyasaraaa amɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛje shishi amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: How does hand pollination actually work if I want to try it on my farm?
ga: Te nine nɔ fɔfɔi ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛji miisumɔ ni maka fɔfɔi ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ makwɛ?

english: Hand pollination involves carefully taking the pollen-bearing part of a healthy cocoa flower and touching it to the female receptor of another flower on the tree to ensure fertilization.
ga: Nɔ ni fata nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ he ji ni ajie ŋmɔtɔ fã ni yɔɔ kookoo fɔfɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. kɛ fɔfɔi kroko ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yoo ni heɔ nii lɛ he ni ooota koni ekwɛ akɛ fɔmɔ eba.

english: Why are my young tomato plants falling over and dying soon after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu amɛ lɛ?

english: This often happens because of a soil-borne disease called damping-off or because the soil is too hot and wet. Young seedlings need gentle shade, well-draining soil, and careful watering so their tender stems do not rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa ni atsɛɔ lɛ dampening, loo akɛni sũ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ tsɔ hewɔ lɛ, enɛ baa. Tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo blɛoo. Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ akafite.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling during the hottest hours is often the plant's natural way of protecting itself from losing too much water. If the leaves bounce back in the evening, it is normal heat stress, but if they remain curled, it could indicate pest damage or dry soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ ji gbɛ ni tso ko tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe koni nu babaoo akafite lɛ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛba gbɛkɛ mli lɛ No ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli. Shi kɛji akɛ ebɔle lolo Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui efite loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi.

english: How do I know when my maize crop needs fertilizer to grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-ŋmei lɛ he baahia ni awo mi ŋmɔshi nii koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: When maize lacks essential nutrients, its lower leaves start turning pale yellow in a V-shape from the tips inward. Feeding your maize crop with fertilizer at the right stage gives it the energy to grow strong stalks and produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ Eshishigbɛ baai lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ V su mli kɛjɛ emligbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo ŋmãa mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha ená hewalɛ ni ekɛkwɛ tsei ni he wa ni ekɛ ŋmãa wuji aba.

english: How does adding animal manure to my farm soil help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Animal manure acts as slow-release food for your crops while improving the soil's ability to hold water. Mixing well-rotted manure into the ground enriches the soil with nutrients and keeps it soft enough for roots to spread easily.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni jieɔ ehe blɛoo kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ futu sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo.

english: How often should I water my crops during the dry season so they do not dry up?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛkagbi?

english: Crops need consistent soil moisture, but too much water can rot their roots. It is best to water early in the morning or late in the afternoon every few days, ensuring the water reaches deep enough into the root zone.
ga: Tsei hia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa. Shi nu babaoo baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu lɛ leebi loo shwane mli daa gbii fioo komɛi koni nu lɛ ayashɛ shishifã lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my cocoa trees turning brown and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop lower leaves when they suffer from extreme dry weather or direct, intense sunlight. Providing shade plants and maintaining good soil moisture helps keep the leaves green and prevents severe water loss.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baa lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ye amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ hulutsoo ha ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa baahi shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ebaatsi nu ni fiteɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why is my cassava taking so long to produce large roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani efeɔ shishifãi wuji lɛ?

english: Cassava spends its early months building strong leaves and stems before it starts storing energy in its underground roots. Being patient and keeping the field clean of weeds gives the plant the time and space it needs to build large tubers.
ga: Cassava heɔ be yɛ shishijee mli. Koni afee baai kɛ tsei ni mli wa dani abɔi hewalɛ ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ Tsuishitoo kɛ jwɛi lɛ ahe tsemɔ baaha tso lɛ aná be kɛ he ko ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are flowers falling off my okra plants without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ mi gumbo lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Okra plants drop their flowers when they experience severe heat stress, irregular watering, or a shortage of plant nutrients. Maintaining steady soil moisture and feeding the plant properly helps flowers turn into healthy pods.
ga: Roselle tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe hulutsoo ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo tso lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ tso lɛ niyenii ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Weeds are fast-growing competitors that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your main crops get all the food and light they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni yaa hiɛ oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha tso ni hereɔ lɛ lɛ aná niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops produce less yield if I plant the same crop in the same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up. Rotating your crops, such as planting legumes like beans after maize, restores soil nutrients and stops disease cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi aba. Tsɔmɔmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ no sɛɛ lɛ ŋmãa ni ooodu. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekpaa helai lɛ asɛɛkuu.

english: Why do some farmers leave banana trees growing right next to plantain trees in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shiɔ banana tsei amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ? Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Bananas and plantains belong to the same plant family and share similar growth needs. Planting them together allows farmers to maximize land use and provide wind protection, but they must be spaced properly so they do not fight for the same soil nutrients and water.
ga: Banana kɛ plantains yɛ tsei akuu kome mli, ni amɛhiɛ taomɔ nii ni tamɔ amɛhe koni amɛdara. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa okwaafoi lɛ kɛ amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ heɔ amɛhe. Shi esa akɛ amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa bɔni afee ni amɛkatswa akaŋ yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ hu he.

english: How can I tell if two different crops planted together in my field are helping or hurting each other?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ ni adu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiye amɛmiibua amɛhe loo amɛmiiye amɛhe awui?

english: You can observe their growth signs: if both plants have dark green leaves, sturdy stems, and good fruit yield, they are compatible. If one plant turns yellow, stops growing, or wilts, it means the crops are competing for sunlight, water, or root space.
ga: Obaanyɛ otao okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiida: Kɛji tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ, amɛshishifãi ni wa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai. Amɛhiɔ shi kɛkɛ. Kɛji tso ko tsɔ ŋmɔŋ, ekpa dalɛ, loo egbo lɛ No tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii miitswa hulu la, nu loo shishifãi ahe akaŋ.

english: Why does planting plantains next to my young cassava cause the cassava to grow thin stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain ni aduɔ yɛ mibi lɛ ŋmei lɛ masɛi lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves are very broad and create thick shade. Cassava needs full, direct sunlight to build strong stems and big roots, so heavy shade from plantains slows down cassava root development.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ mli lɛɛ waa ni ehaa hulutsoo be mli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Cassava he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ená tsei ni wa kɛ shishifãi wuji. No hewɔ lɛ, hulutsoo ni mli tse ni jɛɔ plantain mli lɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ fioo.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain suckers turning yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves turn yellow when the plant is stressed by lack of water and high heat. The plant sheds older leaves to save moisture for its core stem and roots during dry periods.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tso lɛ miihao yɛ nu ni bɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ. Tsei shwieɔ baai momoi koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy leaf canopy and fruit bunches at the top. Supporting the main stem with a strong wooden pole or bamboo prop helps hold the plant upright during windy storms.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni tsii kɛ aduawai akui ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa fi tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: How many shoots or suckers should I allow to grow around one main plantain stand?
ga: Esa akɛ maŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei loo tsei enyiɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ ehe? Plantain titri kome

english: It is best to leave only 2 to 3 shoots of different ages per stand—the mother plant, one medium shoot, and one small shoot. Allowing too many suckers to grow causes them to steal nutrients from each other, resulting in smaller bunches.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi tsei 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ ni eye afii srɔtoi yɛ shidaamɔhe kome mli: tso lɛ nyɛ, teŋgbɛ tso kome, kɛ tso bibioo kome. Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaaha amɛju niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: What causes dark spots to appear on my green plantain leaves before the bunch is mature?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ plantain baai eŋɔli lɛ anɔ lɛ baa dani panicles lɛ daa?

english: Dark spots are typically caused by leaf spot diseases like Black Sigatoka, which spread in humid and rainy weather. Pruning away infected leaves reduces the spread and keeps the plant strong enough to fill its fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe tamɔ Black Sigatoka, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black spot baa. Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha hela lɛ gbɛ eshwa, ni ebaaha tso lɛ aya hiɛ bɔ ni sa ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Is it safe to leave old harvested banana stems standing in my farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mashi banana tsei ni akpa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Leaving old harvested stems standing can attract pests like banana stem weevils and spread diseases. Cutting the old stem down near the ground and chopping it into small pieces helps it rot quickly into useful manure.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei momo ni akpa lɛ ni ashi yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbala kooloi tamɔ banana ŋmeii kɛba ni egbɛ helai ashwã. Kpɔ̃ɔ tso momo lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ofolɔ mli bibii bibii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni efiteɔ oya ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Why should I cover the ground around the base of my plantain plants with dry leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle midumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic matter (mulching) keeps the soil moist, reduces soil heat during sunny days, stops weeds from growing, and adds organic fertilizer to the roots as it rots.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔlɛ shi yɛ gbii ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli woɔ shishifãi lɛ amli be mli ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ.

english: What is the main difference in how sweet bananas and cooking plantains grow in the field?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titri ni yɔɔ bɔ ni ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni akɛhooɔ nii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ mli?

english: Plantains generally grow taller, take longer to mature, and consume more soil nutrients than sweet bananas. Sweet bananas tend to produce smaller bunches faster and produce shoots more rapidly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantains lɛ kɛlɛ fe tsutsu lɛ. Eheɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ɔ ni eyeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fe ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ Aŋmei ni ŋɔɔ lɛ mli gbalaa kɛyaa ŋmeii bibii amli oya ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning yellow from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Leaves turning yellow starting from the tips usually means your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure will help the leaves turn green again so the plants can produce healthy, large ears.
ga: Baai ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, o-corn tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ naa toi wuji ni mli wa.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water and lacks good drainage during heavy rains. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo tsɔ ni nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa lɛ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my tomato plants without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without making fruit when the weather becomes too hot or dry, or when the plants do not get enough water. Giving your plants steady water and covering the soil with dry grass to keep it cool will help the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ waa. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ ni okɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo nɔ koni ehiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do I have to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tso ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground, exposing maximum leaves to sunlight while protecting them from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ, yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ hu ahe.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and food to produce big, full maize ears.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmãa toi wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my garden vegetables with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mibɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, traps moisture in the soil so you water less often. It also prevents weeds from growing and stops the hot afternoon sun from baking the tender plant roots.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni onyɛ okɛ nu awo mli shii abɔ. Ehaa jwɛi hu shwereɔ, ni ehaaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ akagbi tso shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, or a virus they carry. Spraying the plants early with neem leaf extract or recommended soap-based solutions helps control these insects and stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛhiɛɔ lɛ Ashwieɔ tsei anɔ mra Kɛtsɔ neem baa mli nu loo samla ni ajieɔ yi lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ anɔ ni ehaa baa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do farmers say planting groundnuts or cowpeas makes the soil better for maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni baaba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes, which can pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When you harvest them, that natural fertilizer stays in the soil to feed the maize crop planted in the next season.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ agbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni okpaa Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛye be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoot suckers around my plantain stand instead of letting them all grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Mi plantain lɛ eje kpo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha amɛ fɛɛ amɛdara

english: When too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they compete for food and water with the main mother plant. Keeping only two or three strong shoots ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce a heavy, large bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe Plantain kome Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo tsei babaoo ni tsii.

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow, the crop is lacking nitrogen. The plant naturally moves nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the young, growing leaves at the top.
ga: Beni ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling upwards and looking pale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl upwards when small insects like whiteflies infect the crop with a virus, or when the plant experiences extreme heat and dry soil, curling its leaves to reduce water loss.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies lɛ ye tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛ́ tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli. Ha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and provide wide leaf canopy coverage that shields young cocoa plants from heat while preserving soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ehaa baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, yɛ be mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and wet before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔtɔ dani amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during heavy rains when the farm has too much shade and damp air trapped around the trees.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni ŋmɔji lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ emɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots staying thin and woody instead of growing big and full of starch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei moŋ fe ni amɛaafee wuji ni amɛfee starch lɛ?

english: Cassava roots become thin and woody when planted in hard, compacted soil or when left in the ground past their ideal harvest time without enough rainfall.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ. aloo kɛ́ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛho kpamɔɔ be ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ he ni nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa enɛɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and put wooden sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mihe lɛ? Ni okɛ tso ko afee ni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground, preventing rot and improving light exposure.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa ni ehaa nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather becomes too hot or when soil moisture suddenly shifts from dry to very wet, causing the crop to drop blooms to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛyaa nɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Ha ŋmɔshi nibii afee fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay soft and open instead of forming hard, tight balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe lɛ? Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ nɔ́ ko nɛ wa nɛ e mi mi wa.

english: Cabbages fail to form tight heads when they don't get enough sunlight or when given too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces leaves to grow loose and fast rather than wrapping tightly.
ga: Cabbage nyɛŋ afee yitsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ agbo ni amɛdara oya moŋ fe ni amɛaabɔle amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever a light rainstorm comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi mlɛo be fɛɛ be ni ahum baatswa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that spread horizontally near the topsoil rather than deep into the ground. When heavy fruit bunches mature, the top-heavy trees unroot easily in strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋwɛigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ akuu lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ shwieɔ tsei ni tsii fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ oya.

english: Why do my cowpea pods have tiny holes and dry seeds inside before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea pods lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni dumɔwui ni egbi yɛ mli dani akpaa.

english: Tiny holes in cowpea pods are caused by insect pests like pod borers that lay eggs on flowers; the hatching caterpillars burrow inside to feed directly on developing seeds.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ tsina ŋmeii amli lɛ jɛɔ kooloi tamɔ pod borers ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ amli. Kplukai ni efɔ lɛ shwieɔ mli koni amɛye dumɔwui ni miiya hiɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Leaves usually turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green growth. It can also happen if the ground has too much standing water, which suffocates the roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps bring back the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from heat stress, lack of water, or poor nutrients in the soil. Giving the plants consistent water and shade during extremely hot days helps the flowers stay attached and produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni esaaa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo ha tso lɛ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites that suck the juice from leaves, or by viral diseases spread by these insects. Spraying the plants with neem oil or targeted insect sprays helps stop the leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo kooloi ni akɛtaoɔ kooloi amli lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ekpa baai lɛ afitemɔ.

english: Why do I need to place wooden poles next to my growing yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso ko ama sweet potato tso ko ni miida lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam is a vine plant that naturally climbs to find sunlight. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground where it can get maximum light to make food, resulting in much larger tubers under the ground.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni jɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli amɛkwɔɔ koni amɛyana hulu la. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná kane babaoo ni amɛkɛhoo nii yɛ nɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa.

english: These extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and food from the main mother plant. Keeping only one or two healthy shoots ensures the main tree gets enough strength to grow a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers nɛɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hi shi lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛdumɔwui wuji ni tsii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why is it important for me to weed around my young cassava plants early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Cassava tsei yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal soil nutrients, sunlight, and water from young plants. Clearing weeds during the first three months allows cassava roots to establish properly without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ sũ mli niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ama shi jogbaŋŋ ni akaŋshii ko bɛ mli.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the farm field where I planted maize last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni midu ŋmei yɛ mli nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which pull natural nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them restores the soil's strength so the next crop grows much better without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei nɛɛ adumɔ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ kwraa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa waa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on my farm right before a big rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away loose fertilizer from the top of the soil before the plant roots can absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already damp or lightly bury it near the roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo loo kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ooofu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ fioo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some of the small green cocoa pods on my trees turn shriveled and black before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ yɛ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ egbo ni etsɔ ediŋŋ dani eda.

english: Young cocoa pods naturally wither if the tree lacks enough water or nutrients to support all the pods it created. However, if it spreads fast across many pods, it can also be a sign of black pod disease, which needs fungal treatment.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ baagboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua ŋmeii fɛɛ ni abɔ lɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ egbɛ eshwa oya yɛ ŋmeii babaoo amli lɛ, Ebaanyɛ efee ŋmeii diji hela hu he okadi, ni biɔ ni atsa lɛ.

english: Why are my cabbages failing to form tight, hard heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ ewaaa lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form tight heads if the weather is too hot, if they don't receive enough water, or if there is a shortage of nutrients in the soil. Regular watering and nutrient-rich soil encourage the leaves to wrap tightly around each other.
ga: Kaabaji efeŋ yitsei ni mli ewo wu kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji onine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni oooha daa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my maize after the first rains fall?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje ŋmãa dumɔ shishi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize seeds need steady soil moisture to germinate properly. It is best to wait until the soil stays moist for a few consecutive days after the first rain so the seeds do not sprout and then dry out in warm weather.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ gbii fioo komɛi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akakwɛ̃ ni amɛkagbi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crop plants bend towards one direction instead of growing straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛakwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Crops naturally bend toward the direction of strongest sunlight to capture maximum light energy for their leaves, a behavior known as phototropism.
ga: Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛyaa he ni hulu la ni naa wa fe fɛɛ lɛ yaa lɛ koni amɛmɔ la hewalɛ ni fa fe fɛɛ kɛha baai lɛ. Enɛ ji subaŋ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ fototropism.

english: Leaf curling in the midday sun is a survival response. The plant rolls its leaves to reduce the leaf area exposed to direct heat, which helps it conserve water and prevent drying out.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji wala yiwalaheremɔ hetoo. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba he ni baa lɛ yɔɔ ni la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbi.

english: How can I tell if my young crops are getting enough water in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Check the top few inches of the soil around the roots; if it feels dry and powdery, the plant needs water. Healthy crops with enough water will have firm, upright leaves rather than soft, drooping ones.
ga: Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi inchi fioo ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ. Kɛji enu he akɛ egbi ni efee powder Tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nu. Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni nu yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ baai ni mli wa ni ja. Mohu ɔ, baai ɔmɛ peeɔ blɛoo nɛ a gboɔ.

english: What causes my tomato flowers to fall off before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛwo yibii?

english: Tomato plants often drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress, lack of water, or uneven soil moisture, as the plant attempts to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shiŋŋ lɛ kpe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tso lɛ miitao ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato koni ehi wala mli.

english: Why do some of my cassava plants grow tall with very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ ekomɛi daa ni amɛshishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava plants receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or are planted in hard, packed soil, they put most of their energy into growing top leaves rather than expanding their underground tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo nɔ loo adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ. Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ babaoo kɛkwɛɔ baai yɛ ŋwɛi moŋ fe ni amɛaagbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize turning yellow while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the crop is short on nitrogen. The plant moves nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to nourish the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What happens to my vegetables if I plant the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete for limited soil nutrients, sunlight, and water, leading to weak, skinny plants that produce smaller fruits or lower yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu ni faaa lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni woɔ yibii bibii loo nɔ ni baa shi lɛ baa.

english: How do I know when my plantain bunch is ripe enough to harvest from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi plantain tsei lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: A plantain bunch is ready for harvest when the individual fruits lose their sharp, angular edges and become plump and rounded, and the dry flowers at the tips rub off easily.
ga: Plantains kuu ko efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko sɛɛ efo ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Ni fɔfɔi ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ amɛnaagbee lɛ oya.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start sprouting or going soft shortly after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ loo efeɔ blɛoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living plant parts that react to warmth and moisture. If stored in a warm or humid place, or if damaged during harvest, they will either break dormancy to grow new shoots or begin to rot.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji tso lɛ fãi ni hiɛ ka ni tsuɔ nii kɛji edɔ kɛ fɛ̃i. Kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ loo he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ loo kɛji akɛ efite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli lɛ Dormancy baanyɛ aba koni eha ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ loo amɛje shishi amɛgboi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings scorch and die when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their tender leaves lose water faster than their small root systems can absorb it. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain beside them provides living shelter and creates a humid microclimate that protects the young cocoa until its roots mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ. E nibii lɛ baafee nɔ ni shwieɔ nu. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ haa hulutsoo be bibioo ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa ni ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa.

english: Why does my main plantain tree produce very small bunches when many small shoots grow around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain titri lɛ shwereɔ bibii bibii waa be mli ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛi babaoo ni miida yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ he?

english: The small shoots, known as suckers, compete with the main parent tree for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Removing most extra suckers and keeping only one or two leaves all the soil food for the main tree, allowing it to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ suckers. Amɛ kɛ tso ni amɛyɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajie baa kome loo enyɔ pɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha tso titri lɛ, ebaaha niji agboi ni tsii aba.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants rolling up tightly into tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔji yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during the hottest part of the day to reduce the leaf surface area exposed to the sun, which keeps moisture from evaporating too quickly. It is a natural protection mechanism that helps the plant survive short dry spells.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Koni akɛba baai ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape pattern?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually indicates that the maize plant is running out of nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for leafy green growth. The plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves, signaling that it needs nitrogen fertilizer or manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmei tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Tso lɛ baaha shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ aye hɔmɔ koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii. Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia.

english: Why do my cassava roots soft-rot under the ground when the rainy season gets too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because water replaces air spaces in the earth, effectively suffocating the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges creates channels for excess rainwater to drain away, keeping the root zone oxygenated.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu yeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ najiaŋ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ tsɔɔ gbɛ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ naa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa

english: Why do my yam vines produce bigger tubers when I force them to climb tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ daa bulbs wuji beni minyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkwɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb up stakes so their leaves can spread out and catch maximum sunlight without overlapping on the wet ground. Capturing full sunlight allows the leaves to convert light into food, which moves downward to feed and expand the underground tuber.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ ni amɛkafo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baa lɛ ni etsakeɔ la lɛ ewoɔ niyenii mli. Enɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi koni eye niyenii ni ekɛgbala ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when night temperatures are too high or when the plant experiences sudden drought stress or poor nutrient levels. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering helps the flowers set into healthy tomato fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ gbɛkɛ. aloo be mli ni tsei kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ trukaa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ kpeɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling upward and turning wrinkled and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of young leaves, or from a virus transmitted by these insects. Controlling these pests early prevents leaf deformation and keeps the plant growing normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ amli Kudɔmɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra Ebaatsi baai lɛ ashishi ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa.

english: How do my cowpea crops help make the soil better for the next crop I plant in the same land?
ga: Te mi-cowpea tso lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that work with helpful natural soil bacteria to take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the cowpea plants die after harvest, the stored nitrogen breaks down in the soil, providing free food for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ adebɔɔ mli sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji tsina tsei gboi yɛ kpamɔ sɛɛ Nitrogen ni ato lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ebafeɔ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does covering the bare soil around my crops with dry grass keep them greener during hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi Ani miŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ jwɛi woɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks direct heat from reaching the topsoil. This traps moisture beneath the surface, stops weed seeds from sprouting, and keeps root zones cool during dry periods.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsĩɔ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ shishi lɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli

english: Why are there suddenly so many tiny insects swarming on my cassava leaves this month?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo ebɔle mi-cassava baai lɛ ahe trukaa yɛ nyɔŋ nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: These insects, such as mealybugs or whiteflies, multiply rapidly during warm, dry spells. They gather on leaves to suck sap, but spraying a mild neem leaf extract or soapy water solution helps control their numbers before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni fata kooloi nɛɛ ahe ji mealybugs loo ŋmeii yɛŋ. Amɛfɔɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni edɔ lɛ mli. Amɛbuaa amɛhe naa yɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛnu nu lɛ. Shi neem tso mli nu ni mli ejɔ loo samla ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ amɛyibɔ ​​dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing very small and thin this harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: When yam mounds are placed too close together or the soil is too hard, the roots compete heavily for space and nutrients, preventing the tubers from expanding fully underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni abua naa lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ waa. Etsiɔ tubers naa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi kwraa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and drooping even though it is the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ? Ani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ji lolo?

english: Too much standing water chokes the plant roots, preventing them from taking up oxygen and nutrients like nitrogen. Creating simple drainage channels helps excess water flow away so leaves stay green.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen kɛtsɔ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ ni ooofee lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Baai lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli.

english: Is it the hot dry season that is making my pepper plants drop their flowers before fruiting?
ga: Ani hulutsoo be lɛ ji nɔ ni haa mi-pepper tsei lɛ woɔ yibii dani amɛwoɔ yibii?

english: Yes, extreme heat causes heat stress in pepper plants, leading them to shed blossoms to survive. Spreading dry grass around the base as mulch helps keep the roots cool and moist so flowers stay on.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa pepper tsei amli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ pepper tsei lɛ afɔ fɔfɔi bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi. Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my plantain trees roll up tight during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural defense mechanism to reduce its surface area exposed to the sun, preventing excessive water loss through evaporation during peak afternoon heat.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa ehiɛ he ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Tsi nu ni laajeɔ fe nine kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ shwane mli la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ.

english: What kind of feed should I give my tomato plants to get big fruits instead of just bushy leaves?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii esa akɛ maha mi-tomato tsei lɛ koni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo moŋ fe baai ni abua naa kɛkɛ?

english: High-nitrogen fertilizers make leaves grow fast, but potassium and phosphorus are needed for flowering and fruiting. Switching to a potassium-rich fertilizer like wood ash or balanced NPK when flowers appear boosts fruit growth.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha baai lɛ adara oya. Shi potassium kɛ phosphorus he miihia kɛha fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo. Ni aaatsake kɛya potassium ni fa babaoo tamɔ tso sũ loo NPK ni ja nɔ kɛji fɔfɔii je kpo pɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni eha tso yibii lɛ ada.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow well in poor soil where my maize crop fails?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ aahu akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which means their roots work with beneficial soil bacteria to capture nitrogen directly from the air, feeding themselves even in low-nutrient soil.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ ŋmãa weku lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ. ni ebaanyɛ eye ehe niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa lɛ po nɔ

english: How long does it take for improved variety oil palm trees to start bearing fruit after planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani mu tso ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Improved varieties like the Tenera palm begin producing fruit bunches within 3 to 4 years after field planting, which is much faster than traditional wild varieties that take up to 7 years.
ga: Tsoi srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ Tenera palm lɛ baaje aduawai akui afeemɔ shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ yaa oya fe blema koo mli nɔ ni heɔ afii kpawo lɛ.

english: What causes black spots to spread rapidly across my cocoa pods before they mature?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii diji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ oya dani amɛdaraa?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, overly shaded farms. Pruning shade trees and removing infected pods early stops the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fɔ̃ɔ ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ ni hulutsoo babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: How do I know if the insects eating my cabbage leaves are pests or helpful bugs?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ?

english: Insects that chew holes in leaves or roll up inside them (like caterpillars) are pests. Insects like ladybugs or spiders that move quickly and do not chew leaves are beneficial predators that eat the pests.
ga: Abuɔ kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ baai amli bu loo amɛshwieɔ amɛmli (tamɔ ŋmeii) lɛ akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Kplukai tamɔ ladybugs loo ŋmeii ni nyiɛɔ oya ni amɛyeee baai lɛ ji kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ ŋmeii.

english: These worms are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana. They hide inside the young growing leaves of maize and eat them, which can severely weaken the plant if not caught early using recommended pesticides or local solutions like placing clean ash in the leaf funnel.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii amli ni amɛyeɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ amɔmɔɔɔ lɛ mra. kɛtsɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ, tamɔ sũ ni he tse ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long or when there is a fungus in the soil. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away quickly so the roots do not sit in soggy soil.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ loo kɛji ŋmeii yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ taraaa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my neighbors plant beans inside the same farm field as their maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ miidu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ amɛŋmei lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes naturally collect nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them alongside maize helps fertilize the soil naturally, giving you healthier maize and an extra crop to harvest.
ga: Beans kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Buaa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa o-abele lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni onáa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni obaakpa.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen fertilizer or is getting improper amounts of water. Adding compost or balanced fertilizer to the base of the plant helps restore its green color and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo enine shɛɛɛ nu ni sa nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdaraa ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and cool moisture they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Weeds are wild native plants that are strong and adapted to local soil, so they quickly steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing them early gives your young crops a fair chance to grow big and strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo jɛmɛ shikpɔji lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Ni oootsi ohe mra Enɛ baaha otsei bibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Should I plant my maize seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ afi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains are regular and steady. The first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell, which can heat up the soil and kill seeds that have just started to sprout.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baanɛ fiofio ni ebaa shi. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adɔ ni efite dumɔwui ni je shishi amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my garden vegetables?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ aduawai anɔ nu yɛ ŋtayaai abɔɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best time to water is early in the morning. This gives the plants moisture to drink before the hot afternoon sun dries up the soil, and prevents leaves from staying wet overnight, which causes leaf diseases.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ nu ji leebi maŋkpa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nuɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ. ni otsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ nyɔɔŋ kome. ni ji nɔ ni kɛ baa hela baa lɛ

english: Is it good for me to save seeds from this year's maize harvest to plant next season?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ oookɛ afi nɛɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ato koni okɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: If you planted high-yielding hybrid seeds, saving them for the next season usually yields smaller and weaker crops. It is better to buy fresh certified seeds each year or use improved open-pollinated varieties.
ga: Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ, bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ okɛto kɛha be ni baa lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Esa akɛ ahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa afi loo akɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni agbeleɔ naa lɛ atsu nii.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my maize for dry grain storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa koni akɛto ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ he?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the leaves and husks turn dry and brown, and a tiny black mark forms at the base of the corn kernel where it attaches to the cob.
ga: Abɛi lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ egbi ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni okadii diji bibii yɛ jɛmɛ. Ebaa yɛ ŋmãa ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ he lɛ shishi.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries up soil moisture rapidly. Keeping existing shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains provides the protective canopy young cocoa needs until it matures.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gĩɔ oya. Tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ momo lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaha kookoo bibii lɛ aná ŋwɛi ŋta ni he hiaa amɛ ni amɛbu he kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baadara.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow and drying up from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient plants need to make green leaves and food. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or organic manure around the roots helps the maize return to a healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai eŋɔli kɛ niyenii Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni bɔleɔ he lɛ tsuɔ nii Shishifãi lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmei lɛ aku esɛɛ aba eŋɔli su lɛ mli kwraa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when there is heavy rain for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because standing water blocks oxygen from reaching the roots, causing them to suffocate and attract fungal decay. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni haa wala yibii lɛ ayashɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa mɔ mumɔ shwieɔ shi ni egbalaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without producing fruit when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil consistently moist and feeding the soil proper nutrients helps the flowers set into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni bɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting groundnuts alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmei lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally absorbs nitrogen from the air and releases it into the soil. Planting groundnuts next to maize improves soil fertility, allowing the maize to feed on that extra nitrogen and grow better.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa akɛ nitrogen ni fa fe nine haa ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars hiding inside the central leaves of my corn and making holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abɛi lɛ ateŋ ni amɛmiifee bu yɛ mli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a destructive pest that feeds on the soft growing tips of maize plants. Spraying suitable biopesticides or applying neem leaf extracts early in the morning when the insects are active helps control them.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ ŋmeii tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ loo okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu tsu nii leebi be mli ni kooloi lɛ miitsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb stakes so their broad leaves can catch maximum sunlight to manufacture energy, which is then sent underground to grow large, healthy tubers. Unstaked yam leaves stay shaded on the ground and produce much smaller yields.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Akɛ enɛɛmɛi yaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulb agboi ni he wa. Akɛ sweet potato baai ni shishifãi bɛ lɛ ebɔle shikpɔŋ lɛ he, ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow thin and produce very small harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee mlɛo ni amɛmiiwo yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks after planting gives your main crop full access to food and space so it can grow strong and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha otso titri lɛ aná niyenii kɛ he ko kwraa. Bɔni afee ni eda waa ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my plantain suckers grow tall and thin with small bunches when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ kui bibii lɛ? Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe

english: Planting plantain trees too close together causes them to shade each other out and compete heavily for root space and soil food. Spacing them about three meters apart gives each plant enough sunlight and nutrients to produce thick trunks and heavy bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ afee amɛhe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛye akaŋ waa koni amɛná shishifãi kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni kã tsei ateŋ lɛ ji aaafee mitai 3, ni ehaa tso fɛɛ tso hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ tsei ashishifãi ni mli tse kɛ jwɛi ni mli tse.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on leaf sap and spread plant viruses. Controlling these insects with organic sprays or insecticides prevents leaf damage and allows normal fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite tso lɛ yibii lɛ, ni ebaaha aduawai lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when I plant them in an open field without tall crops around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight and lose moisture quickly. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to young cocoa provides a living umbrella that protects the seedlings from intense heat while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛmli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cassava stem cuttings fail to grow when I plant them upside down in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca ni afo lɛ lɛ edaaa kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava stems have small leaf nodes or buds that must point upward toward the sky. If planted upside down, the shoots struggle to reach the surface and the roots cannot develop properly, leading to weak or failed growth.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ yɛ baai bibii loo ŋmeii. ni esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛji adu ehiɛ shi lɛ Tsobii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ nu lɛ hiɛ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ adara jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ loo sɛɛkuu.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my growing maize plants turning yellow in the middle of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the soil has run out of nitrogen, which maize needs in high amounts to stay green and healthy. Adding manure, compost, or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea restores healthy leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi he miihia lɛ babaoo koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Legume crops like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. This acts as a free natural fertilizer that enriches the soil for nearby or subsequent maize crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ loo sɛɛ mli ŋmãa.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the base of my pepper plants keep them healthy in warm weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni jwɛi shwieɔ shi lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, mi-pepper tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) blocks direct sunlight from drying out the dirt. It retains water in the soil longer, keeps plant roots cool, and slowly decomposes into rich food for the soil.
ga: Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni otsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni oha muji akagbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni jara wa kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark dirt inside the center shoot?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli ni eshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central leaves of maize plants. Checking crops early and applying neem extracts or recommended sprays early in the morning helps control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei amli baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni akwɛɔ mli mra Ni akɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baatsu nii leebi lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ nibii ni adu lɛ dani efite nibii ni adu lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava bushes develop yellow patches and curl up into distorted shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, a viral infection spread by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension officers prevents this disease from reducing your harvest.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni hela nɛɛ akaha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: What happens if I sow my maize seeds too close together in the farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the crowded plants compete with one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes thin stalks and tiny, poorly filled corn cobs instead of healthy, full yields.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Mohu ɔ, e ji nɔ́ ko nɛ yeɔ emuu nɛ e ngɛ he wami.

english: How can I tell that the soil is ready for planting maize after the rains start?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu ŋmãa beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until your land receives steady, heavy rain for two or three consecutive days rather than planting after the very first light shower. This ensures there is enough deep moisture for seeds to sprout and survive short dry periods.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa gbii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ahum lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa baa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing huge green leaves but failing to produce fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ebɛ yibii lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer causes tomato plants to spend all their energy producing thick leaves and stems instead of flowers. Trimming extra non-fruiting branches (suckers) and reducing nitrogen helps the plant focus on growing fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo mli lɛ, ebaaha tomato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo baai kɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse. yɛ fɔfɔii najiaŋ Niji krokomɛi ni wooo yibii (tsoji) ni afolɔ mli kɛ nitrogen ni aba shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa aduawai ni miida lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do plastic nursery bags for young plants need to have holes in the bottom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plastic ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui akwɛmɔ kotokui amli lɛ yɛ bu yɛ amɛshishi lɛ?

english: Without drainage holes, excess water stays trapped inside the bag. This suffocates the seedling's roots and causes root rot, which will kill the young plant before it can be transplanted to your farm.
ga: Kɛji nu homɔ bu ko bɛ Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baabote kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha dumɔwu lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ agboi dani abaanyɛ adu amɛ awo oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Does using a larger seedling bag help my crop grow better before I plant it in the farm?
ga: Ani dumɔwui kotoku ni da ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ dani mikɛ amɛ adu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, a larger bag gives the seedling's roots more space to expand without getting root-bound or tangled. A plant with a bigger, healthier root system settles faster and grows stronger once moved to the main field.
ga: Hɛɛ, kotoku ni da fe no lɛ haa dumɔwu lɛ shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ babaoo ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ dara ni amɛhe wa lɛ baatswa amɛhe shi oya ni amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ ajie amɛ kɛtee saatso wulu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings droop and look like they are dying right after I move them from the nursery to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ miiho ni etamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiigboi beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ lɛ mli nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: This is transplant shock, caused by disturbing delicate roots and suddenly exposing the plant to strong sunlight. Moving your seedlings late in the afternoon and watering them immediately helps reduce shock.
ga: Enɛ ji tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni agbalaa amɛnaa kɛ tso lɛ ni akɛwoɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ trukaa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ otsi dumɔwui lɛ shwane mli ni okɛ nu wo amɛmli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shoofeemɔ aba shi.

english: How can I tell if I am giving my nursery seedlings too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ nu babaoo miiha mibii akwɛmɔhe lɛ?

english: Overwatered seedlings often turn pale yellow, and their stems become soft and weak while the soil stays muddy. Soil in nursery bags should feel moist like a wrung-out damp cloth, not waterlogged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni awo amɛ nu fe nine lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ be mli ni sũ lɛ mli ewo muji lolo lɛ. Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ grow bag lɛ mli lɛ anu he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ, tamɔ mama ni edɔ ni jeee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains to shade my young cocoa trees?
