ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains koni mikɛwo mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe shade lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under intense full sun. Plantains grow fast and provide heavy leaf shade and soil moisture, protecting the cocoa until it matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ehaa baai lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ekwɛɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning light yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmã tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen. The maize plant pulls nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed fresh top growth, indicating your crop needs fertilizer or compost.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛyitsei lɛ aya nɔ akwɛ̃ ehee. Etsɔɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia otso lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural response plants use to reduce leaf surface area and prevent moisture loss during extreme afternoon heat. Consistent watering at the root level helps lower this heat stress.
ga: Baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hetoo ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba baa lɛ hiɛ shi ni amɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ naa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifã lɛ he daa lɛ baaye abua ni eha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin when I plant them in hard clay soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need loose, well-drained soil to expand properly. Heavy clay soil packs tightly around the roots, physically preventing them from swelling into thick, fleshy tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni akɛmiibɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ Tsĩɔ enaa koni ekafu ni etsɔ ŋmei ni mli edɔ.

english: What happens to my harvest if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete heavily with each other for sunlight, water, and ground nutrients. The stalks will grow thin and tall, but the ears of corn will remain tiny or fail to develop grain.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Tsoi ashishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛkɛlɛ. Shi ŋmãa lɛ toi lɛ baafee bibii lolo loo dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ.

english: Weeds naturally grow faster than crops and steal crucial soil nutrients and root space that your crops need. Even with good rain, crops suffer if weeds eat up all the food in the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ shishifãi ni he hiaa otsei lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ, shi Dumɔwui hu naa amanehulu kɛji jwɛi ye niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my maize seeds taking so long to sprout after I planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize seeds require consistent moisture and warm soil to germinate. If the soil is too dry after planting or if the seeds were buried too deep, germination will be delayed or the seeds may dry up and die in the soil.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui taoɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ loo kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ Ekwɛ̃mɔ baahe sɛɛ loo dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if the ground is wet enough for me to start planting my crops at the start of the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: You should not plant after just the first light rain. Wait until the rain soaks the soil deep enough to wet your hand when pushed into the ground (about 10 to 15 centimeters) so that seeds have continuous moisture to survive.
ga: Esaaa akɛ oduɔ nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ. Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ oniji afɔ beni otsiɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ (aaafee sɛntimita 10 kɛyashi 15) koni eha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni yaa nɔ amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Yellowing leaves often mean the plant is lacking key soil nutrients like nitrogen, getting irregular water, or being attacked by sap-sucking pests like mites or whiteflies under the leaves.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, ni enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. aloo ni ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ miinu nu.

english: Why do my crops wilt in the hot afternoon sun even if the ground was moist in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ leebi po

english: During intense afternoon heat, leaves lose water faster than roots can pull it from the ground. Covering the soil around the crop with dry grass or leaves keeps the roots cool and preserves soil moisture.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mulching around Nibii ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, long dry spells, or when given too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on leaf growth instead of fruiting.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Be ni hulutsoo be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo be mli ni anáa nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe yibiiwoo.

english: Why are my bean plants growing lots of tall green leaves but producing very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaŋŋ agboi babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Beans naturally make their own nitrogen in the soil. If you give them extra nitrogen fertilizer, the plant focuses completely on growing leaves and neglects to produce flowers and seed pods.
ga: Beans lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ nitrogen fertilizer kroko ha Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ fɛɛ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ ni amɛkuɔ amɛhiɛ amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui ashishifãi anɔ.

english: Why are my tomatoes turning black and rotting at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ yɛ shishigbɛ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Dark rot at the bottom of tomatoes is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium uptake due to irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant draw nutrients evenly into the fruit.
ga: Diŋ ni fiteɔ yɛ tomato shishi lɛ ji fɔfɔii anaagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he yɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɛɔ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ woɔ aduawai lɛ amli pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow thin and make small cobs when I plant many seeds in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛtsɔɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ Dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When crops are planted too closely together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil. Giving each seed proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough nutrients to produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni amɛdu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa kã dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: This is caused by Black Pod fungal disease, which spreads quickly in wet and shady conditions. Pruning cocoa branches to let sunlight and air into the farm helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod fungal hela, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ hulutsoo. Kookoo tsei ni afoɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by moth caterpillars eating the crop. Checking under leaves early in the morning and applying natural sprays like neem oil helps keep insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi leebi ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ, tamɔ neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi akabote mli.

english: Why should I shade my seedbeds with palm leaves after sowing seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmei baai awo midumɔwui ashishi lɛ mli beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Shading seedbeds protects delicate seeds and emerging sprouts from excessive heat, retains soil moisture, and prevents heavy rainfall from washing away tiny seeds before they establish root systems.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔlɔ wo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni miiba lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni otsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ. Dani abaabɔ shishijee gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ

english: What is the best time of day for me to transplant seedlings into my field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is best to transplant seedlings in the late afternoon or on a cloudy day. Transplants experience less stress because the soil is cooler, allowing roots to recover overnight before facing the harsh sun.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu dumɔwui yɛ shwane mli. loo yɛ gbi ni atatu yɔɔ nɔ lɛ Nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haaa mɔ aná haomɔ babaoo ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mli ejɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ he waa nyɔɔŋ kome dani hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ.

english: How can I tell if young seedlings in a nursery are strong enough to survive on my main farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Healthy, field-ready seedlings should have thick, sturdy stems, vibrant green leaves without spots or chewing damage, and well-developed, bright root systems that hold soil gently together.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ aná tsei ni mli wa ni wa. Baai eŋɔli ni mli tse ni nɔ ko bɛ he loo nɔ ko ni efite kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ mli. kɛ shishifãi ni kpɛɔ ni ehiɛ edɔ jogbaŋŋ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome blɛoo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves typically signal a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen helps plants produce chlorophyll for growth, so applying compost, manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer can restore healthy green foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ klorofil kɛha dalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with huge leaves but yield very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛ baa wuji shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen causes cassava to spend energy growing lush top leaves rather than storing nutrients in roots. Uncompacted soil and balanced nutrients encourage plants to direct energy into root expansion.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋwɛi baai ni yɔɔ fɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baato eshishifãi lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ ni atswaaa shi kɛ niyenii ni ja lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ yaa shishifãi ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling in the heat is a natural survival behavior to reduce the leaf surface area exposed to sunlight and slow down moisture loss. If leaves uncurl by evening, the plant is managing heat stress normally.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yibiiwoo su. Bɔni afee ni ajie baai ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ shi ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aba shi. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwieee shi gbɛkɛ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ baanyɛ atsu dɔlɛ he haomɔ he nii bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my plants grow thin, weak, and tall when I plant seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛlɛɔ be mli ni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe kpaakpa lɛ?

english: Crowded plants compete intensely with neighboring seedlings for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing them to stretch upward for light rather than growing thick, supportive stems.
ga: Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha hulu la fioo, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Enɛ haa amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛmɔmɔ la lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaatsɔ tsei ni mli tse ni fiɔ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why do my crop seeds rot in the soil instead of germinating when I plant them deep?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi aduawai dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ kɛ́ midu amɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too deep starves them of oxygen and forces them to use up all stored energy before reaching the surface, leaving them vulnerable to fungal rot under wet soil.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ haaa amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ, ni enyɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ atsu nii dani amɛshɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii baanyɛ afite dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do tomato seedlings fall over and die at ground level shortly after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: This collapsing condition, known as damping-off, is caused by soil-borne fungal micro-organisms that thrive in overly wet, overcrowded conditions. Raising beds and avoiding overwatering protects fragile young stems.
ga: Nɛkɛ shikpɔŋhosomɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ damping lɛ, jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ fe nine ni gbɔmɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ owó saatso lɛ nɔ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei bibii ni waaa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and wither when planted in open fields without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and underdeveloped root systems that cannot pull water fast enough to withstand full, direct tropical sunlight. Shading with taller crops like plantains shields them until mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni edako jogbaŋŋ ni nyɛɛɛ ajie nu oya bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be lɛ yɔɔ lɛ naa kwraa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ tamɔ plantains wo tso lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛyashi ebaashɛ shweremɔ he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients too deep into the soil where roots cannot reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Curled leaves are usually a sign that tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips are attacking young leaves, or that the plant has caught a leaf-curl virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips lɛ miitutua baai bibii. Aloo etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ hela ko ni ji leaf curl virus ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ emɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn dark brown or black before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ dani ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the soil lacks calcium or when water supply is uneven, making it hard for the plant to draw calcium up into the growing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji calcium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei akɛ amɛbaaŋɔ calcium ni yɔɔ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers but most of them fall off without turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii babaoo shi amɛteŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop extra flowers naturally if they do not have enough water or nutrients to feed all potential pods. It can also be caused by insect attacks from mirids or inadequate shade during dry periods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi kɛjɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua tso muu lɛ fɛɛ bɛ. Kooloi tutuamɔi ni jɛɔ hulu la mli loo hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli hu baanyɛ ekɛba.

english: Why do my yam vines grow very tall and bushy with leaves, but the tubers under the soil turn out very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or fresh manure, the yam plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food down in the root tuber.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii heei babaoo Sweet potato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛduɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why are my cassava roots small, hard, and woody instead of big and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ ji bibioo, ewa ni eyɛ tso yɛ agbo ni eyɛ blɛoo najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots turn hard and woody if they are left in the ground too long past their harvest time, or if they were planted in hard, unplowed soil that prevents the roots from swelling.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa ni ebaafee tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni atsuko nɔ koni shishifãi lɛ akafu.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster after I clear my farm with a cutlass compared to using a hoe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya waa yɛ be mli ni mikɛ dade shwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ fe bɔ ni mikɛ ŋmei tsuɔ nii ahaa lɛ?

english: A cutlass only slices off the top of the weed, leaving the roots intact under the soil to shoot up new leaves again, whereas a hoe digs out the root system entirely.
ga: Kpãa ni akɛfoɔ nii lɛ shwieɔ jwɛi lɛ yiteŋ pɛ. Shi shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni baai heei akwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmei lɛ baafo shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce smaller bunches when planted too close to cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmeii lɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava and plantain roots both feed at the same soil depth. When planted too close, they fight for the same water and nutrients, resulting in smaller harvests for both crops.
ga: Ayeɔ ŋmei kɛ plantain shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli. Kɛ adu amɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni falɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nibii ni afee henɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: It is best to plant after two or three continuous heavy rains have thoroughly soaked the topsoil, so the seeds have enough deep moisture to germinate without scorching in hot soil.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ nu ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛshãaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my dried maize grains turn to powder and get full of small insects after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ feɔ powder ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? Edara kwraa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni akɛto lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Weevils lay eggs inside the grain while it is still on the farm or drying. If the maize is not dried completely before putting it into airtight sacks or storage bins, the insects hatch and eat the grain from the inside out.
ga: Weevils woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa mli be mli ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo loo eegbi. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛwo vacuum kotokui loo ŋmãa ni akɛtoɔ nii amli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ fɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow from the tips down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛmiiya amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip in a V-shape usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and build strong leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ baa lɛ naa yɛ V su mli lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ tsei lɛ amli ni amɛwo tsei ahe tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for surrounding crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa tsei ni ebɔle ehe tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller cobs when I plant seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ woɔ ŋmei fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots and leaves compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, leaving no single plant with enough energy to make big cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout when I plant them deep inside the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds need warmth and air near the soil surface to wake up. Planting them too deep starves them of air and runs out their stored energy before they can push up into the light.
ga: Dumɔwui hia dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ koni amɛte shi. Kɛ́ adu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ afite dani abaanyɛ ashɛre lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya la lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves as high as possible to catch maximum sunlight. The sunlight helps the leaves create energy, which travels down to swell the underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ ni yaa shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings scorching and turning brown under full sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense heat. They need temporary shade plants like plantains planted beside them to block direct sunlight and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Bɔni afee ni abu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with dark dirt inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ ni muji ni tsuɔ diŋ yɛ baai lɛ amli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the daytime to eat the soft young leaves away from heat and birds.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii ni hulutsoo kɛ okpoi bɛ he lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when plants don't get enough water during flowering, causing the plant stress so it sheds its flowers to stay alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nɔ haoɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot in the ground if I leave them after heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess water in flooded soil drives out air from around the roots, causing the mature cassava tubers to drown and rot due to fungal diseases in the wet earth.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi ni akwɛ̃ lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ ŋmei helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops weak even when I feed the field with fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii haa ŋmɔji lɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that absorb water and soil nutrients faster than your crops, effectively stealing the fertilizer before your main plants can use it.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. ni ejuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ dani oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I plant them directly in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because their young roots cannot draw enough water to balance the intense heat. Planting shade crops like plantains provides living cover that keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa roots mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ tso lɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbala nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha hulutsoo ni naa wa lɛ afee ekome. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ yaa hiɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ daa.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the seedlings compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough light and nutrients to develop thick stalks and large cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I alternate planting maize with beans or cowpeas on my farm instead of planting maize every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa ni miduɔ lɛ atsake ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu ŋmãa daa be lɛ

english: Planting maize continuously strips the soil of specific nutrients and attracts maize-loving pests. Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, which enriches the land for your next crop while breaking pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ be fɛɛ be, ni egbalaa kooloi ni sumɔɔ abele lɛ. Beans kɛ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves shaped like a V usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential for leaf growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-composted manure will restore the green color and boost plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tamɔ V lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become hard and woody if I leave them in the soil for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots store starch for the plant, but once the plant reaches full maturity, it stops storing starch and converts it into tough fiber. Harvesting on time keeps the tubers soft and suitable for eating or selling.
ga: Cassava shishifãi kɛ starch toɔ tso lɛ he. Shi kɛ́ tso lɛ da kɛyashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ Ebaakpa starch ni ehiɛɔ lɛ ni etsɔ tsɔji ni wa. Kɛ́ akpa yɛ be naa lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ ni esa akɛ aye loo ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are just wilting from the afternoon heat or if they are actually dying from a lack of water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho kɛkɛ kɛjɛ shwane latsaa lɛ mli? Aloo nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ miigboi diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Crops droop during hot afternoons to conserve moisture, but if they perk up by evening, they are healthy. If the leaves remain dry and floppy early in the morning when it is cool, the soil lacks water and the crops urgently need moisture.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Shi kɛ́ eda gbɛkɛnaashi lɛ, ebaahi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ egbi lolo ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ leebi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu efo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii oya.

english: What is making small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving brown powder inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni eshi powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ funnel lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the growing tip of the plant. Applying approved treatments or organic mixtures like neem oil directly into the central funnel stops the caterpillar before it destroys the plant.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ niyenii yɛ tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni akɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo tsofa ko ni akɛfutuɔ nii, tamɔ neem fɔ, baawo tsɔne ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ kpaa dani amɛfiteɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves curling upwards and getting twisted instead of growing flat and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Upward leaf curl in peppers is typically caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking the sap from young leaves. Controlling these pests early with insecticidal soap or neem spray helps new leaves grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem spray tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa heei ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of flowers, but the flowers fall off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, erratic watering, or a lack of pollination causes tomato flowers to drop off as a survival response. Keeping the soil consistently moist and allowing good air circulation helps the plants retain flowers and form fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa loo pollination ni fa bɔ ni sa Enɛ haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ wala yibiiwoo hetoo. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Weed seeds remain dormant in the soil and are naturally adapted to grow instantly with moisture. Clearing weeds early prevents them from taking away the water and fertilizer meant for your seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkajie nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha odumɔwui lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential food for plants. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has to the upper leaves to keep growing, leaving the older, bottom leaves to starve.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara. Shi baai momoi lɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ koni hɔmɔ aye amɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have small nodes on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground, naturally fertilizing the soil for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ nodes bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves and sawdust-like waste inside the leaf funnels?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli kɛ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of the plant during the day and eat the soft leaves, leaving behind waste that looks like fine sawdust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii, ni amɛshiɔ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmeii kpakpai.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants turning twisted, small, and covered in yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, bibii ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies and by using infected stems for planting. The virus prevents the leaves from absorbing sunlight properly, shrinking your yield.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ Virus lɛ tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do I need to keep large shade trees over my young cocoa trees, but cut back branches as they get older?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi tso agbo ko ni haa mihe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ kookoo tso bibioo ko nɔ lɛ? Shi ani esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ ahe kɛji amɛgbɔ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under bright sunlight and need heavy shade to survive. Once the cocoa trees grow mature and strong, they need more direct sunlight to produce plenty of pods.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni ehe hiaa ni amɛná hulutsoo be ni mli kwɔ koni amɛhi shi. Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ eda kwraa ni ehe wa Ehe miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo koni ekɛ ŋmeii babaoo aba.

english: Why should I cover the dry soil around my pepper plants with dried grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass is called mulching. It traps moisture in the soil so you water less, keeps the root area cool under the hot sun, and stops weeds from popping up.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni okɛ nu fioo pɛ awo mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my ripe tomato fruits crack open on the sides right after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ afãi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When tomato plants experience a dry spell followed by sudden heavy rain, the fruit absorbs water too quickly. The inside grows faster than the skin can stretch, causing the outer skin to split open.
ga: Beni tomato tsei lɛ naa hɔmɔ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Yibii shwieɔ nu oya tsɔ. Mligbɛ lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ fãa.

english: Why do my cassava roots become watery and rot if I leave them in the soil long after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛgboɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eje shishi be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once heavy rains begin, mature cassava tubers stop storing starch and start taking in excess water to sprout new branches, making the roots soft, watery, and quick to spoil.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, Cassava shishifãi ni eda lɛ kpaɔ starch ni amɛtoɔ lɛ ni amɛjeɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ numɔ shishi koni amɛkwɛ niji heei, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo, nu yɔɔ mli, ni amɛfiteɔ oya.

english: Why do my harvested yams start shrinking and growing stems while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shwiemɔ ni miida be mli ni mikɛtoɔ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living roots that continue breathing after harvest. As they sit in storage, they use up their own stored food and water to try to grow new sprouts, causing the tuber to dry up and shrink.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji shishifãi ni hiɛ ka ni yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. be mli ni amɛtaraa nitoohe lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni amɛto lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ dumɔwui heei. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn into powder and get full of tiny brown bugs after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ etsɔ powda ni ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ? Eyi obɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ

english: This is caused by maize weevils. If the grain was not dried completely before storing, or if the storage space isn't sealed, these insects hatch, bore into the seeds, and eat them from the inside out.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei ŋmei. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto loo kɛji akɛ aŋmɛɛɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kwraa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ fɔɔ, amɛfoɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli, ni amɛyeɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ.

english: Yam vines need their leaves fully exposed to sunlight to manufacture nutrients for big tubers. Staking keeps leaves off the wet soil, which maximizes sunlight exposure and prevents fungal diseases from spreading from the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo kɛha amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha amɛ bulbs wuji lɛ. Staking baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkajɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaaa ŋmeii helai agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Should I allow all the small shoots growing around my main plantain tree to stay?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maha ŋmeii bibii lɛ akwɛ̃? Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ baahi shi?

english: No, leaving too many shoots starves the main plant of water and nutrients. You should cut away most suckers and leave only one or two healthy ones so the main stem can produce a heavy bunch.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ, no baaha tso lɛ mli nu akafee nɔ ni he hiaa waa. Esa akɛ ofolɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo ni oshi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni ŋmeii titri lɛ anyɛ afee ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with dark waste inside the funnels?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ amli lɛ, ni nɔ ko ni eshwɛ ni ji ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Spraying approved insecticides or applying neem seed extracts into the leaf funnels early in the morning can stop them before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ loo ni akɛ neem dumɔwui amli nu woɔ baa lɛ mli leebi lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai nɛɛ akpa dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting and turning watery underground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite ni shikpɔŋ shishi nu eyi mli obɔ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Cassava root rot usually happens when rainwater settles around roots in heavy or flat soil. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away, preventing the roots from rotting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite

english: Why is my maize crop yielding less even though I planted on the exact same piece of land as last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ yibiiwoo faaa eyɛ mli akɛ midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu yɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop on the same plot continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and stops crop-specific pests from building up.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I tell if my pepper plants need fertilizer when they are still growing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii be mli ni amɛmiida lolo lɛ?

english: If pepper leaves turn light yellow instead of deep green, or if the plants stay small and stunted, the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen and requires organic manure or top-dress fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ loo kɛji tso lɛ ji bibioo ni egbɔjɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen ni esa akɛ ekɛ organic fertilizer loo fertilizer ni hi jogbaŋŋ atsu nii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants scorching and dropping off during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that dry out under strong sun and hot harmattan winds. Interplanting them with temporary shade plants like plantains protects them from sunburn and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni gbiɔ yɛ hulu ni naa wa kɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains du amɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do the bottom ends of my green tomatoes turn black and sunken before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efoɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom end rot, which occurs when plants experience irregular watering and cannot absorb enough calcium. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the fruits grow normally.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná nu ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Watering early in the morning allows soil to absorb water before heat causes evaporation, and it prevents wet leaves from getting scorched by the hot midday sun.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ nu shwieɔ shi dani la ni tsoɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni etsĩ baai ni efɔ lɛ anaa koni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akashɛ amɛhe yɛ gbi lɛ mli

english: How does covering the soil with dry grass around my crops help them grow better?
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛbaabɔle he lɛ Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops sunlight from drying out the ground quickly, keeps plant roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing around your crop.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away the top layer of soil on my farm, and how does that affect my crop yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni te no saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rainfall hits bare ground with great force, carrying away the dark topsoil which holds most of your plants' manure and nutrients. Without this layer, your crops lose their main source of food and struggle to yield well.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tswa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ, ni tso lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii mli nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ bɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafite amɛ niyenii titri ni amɛyeɔ lɛ ni amɛbaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my crops on raised mounds rather than flat ground when heavy rainy seasons start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gɔji anɔ moŋ fe hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Raised mounds lift your crops' roots above standing water, allowing them to breathe and preventing root rot when heavy rains flood the farm floor.
ga: Gɔŋ ni awo nɔ lɛ woɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛyaa nu ni damɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Ye obua amɛ ni amɛmu ni etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I dig water channels or gutters through my farmland before the heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo nubu loo nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba?

english: Channels guide excessive rainwater safely off your field instead of allowing it to sit in puddles that drown your crops or wash away your planted seeds.
ga: Funnels tsɔɔ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ gbɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha ehi nubui ni shwieɔ onibii amli loo ni shwieɔ dumɔwui ni odu lɛ anɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why does the soil in my field turn hard like cement after heavy floodwaters dry up under the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tamɔ simenti yɛ nu afua ni naa wa ni egbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rains break down the natural crumbly structure of soil into tiny particles. When flooded soil dries quickly in the hot sun, those fine particles stick together tightly, making it hard for crop roots to spread.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni jɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ mli lɛ fãa kɛfeɔ bibii bibii. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ gĩ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, Nakai nibii bibii lɛ baakpɛtɛ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa ewaa kɛhaa tso shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã

english: Why do my crop leaves start turning yellow after rain stays flooded on my land for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni nugbɔ enɛ eyi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air just like humans do. When standing water covers the soil for days, it chokes the roots, preventing them from taking up air and food, which causes the leaves to turn yellow and starve.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi hu he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ. Kɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ Buu he koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii akabote mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Can heavy and constant rainfall actually wash nutrients away from my plants, or does it just help them grow?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ amli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ loo eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara kɛkɛ?

english: While water is vital, continuous heavy rainfall drains deep into the earth and washes soluble fertilizers and soil food far below where plant roots can reach.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nu he hiaa moŋ Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ hoɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni efoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nu mli shwieɔ shi kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do black spots and rot appear on my cassava leaves right after a week of continuous heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ feɔ diji ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni eyaaa nɔ otsi kome sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Continuous rain creates high dampness and moisture on leaf surfaces, which is the perfect environment for plant diseases like fungi to sprout and spread fast.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ kɛ hulutsoo babaoo baa baa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji he ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei ahelai, tamɔ ŋmei, ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya.

english: Why do my young seedlings get pulled out of the soil or break so easily when it rains very heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo akumɔɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli oya lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have weak, shallow roots. Heavy rain drops hit the ground like tiny hammers, loosening soft soil and physically knocking down or uprooting delicate plants.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ hama bibii. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni eha tsei agbee shi loo ajie amɛ.

english: What type of crops can I safely plant in lower parts of my farmland that collect a lot of standing water during rainy periods?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu shweshweeshwe yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shishigbɛ hei ni hiɛɔ nu babaoo ni damɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Crops like rice or certain water-loving vegetables tolerate heavy, waterlogged soils much better than crops like maize, cassava, or groundnuts, which die quickly in swampy ground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai komɛi ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ kpɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ fe tsei tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo ŋmãa, ni gboiɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds seem to multiply and grow much faster than my crops right after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ faa babaoo ni amɛdaraa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and lie dormant in the dry soil; a sudden soak of heavy rain triggers thousands of them to sprout instantly and consume the fresh moisture faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛwɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ haa amɛteŋ akpei abɔ kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛkɛ nu hee ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii oya fe bɔ ni adu tsei lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to stay green. Heavy rains can wash this nitrogen deep into the ground where roots cannot reach, so adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plants recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe nɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aho nitrogen nɛɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: When pepper plants stay stunted, it often means the soil is too hard for the roots to spread, or tiny microscopic worms called nematodes are damaging the roots underground. Adding well-rotted animal manure helps loosen the soil and feed the roots.
ga: Beni pepper tso lɛ egbɔjɔ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Aloo ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ miifite shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ niyenii.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during rainy and humid weather. Clearing bush around the trees, pruning extra branches to let sunlight in, and removing infected pods early stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tsɔɔmɔ jwɛi ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ ni ofolɔ niji krokomɛi koni hulu la babaoo aba mli. ni ojie pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Koni tsɛŋemɔ hela akagbɛ ashwã

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava bushes curling up and showing light green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is cassava mosaic disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings and pulling out infected plants early stops the disease from spreading across your farm.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni yɔɔ kooloi bibii yɛŋ Akɛ nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ whiteflies lɛ yaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Dumɔ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why am I seeing small holes in my young maize leaves with tiny caterpillars hiding inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Akɛtee mli?

english: This is the work of Fall Armyworms, a common pest that eats tender leaves inside maize plants. Checking your farm early in the season and applying recommended organic or safe chemical treatments into the center leaf funnels will protect your crop.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai bibii lɛ anitsumɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra yɛ be lɛ mli ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ wo tso lɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil gets too dry during flowering. Covering the soil with dry grass mulching keeps the roots cool and moist, helping the flowers stay attached and form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ ni egbi shwie nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and die long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ egbi ni egbo be saŋŋ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Early drying of yam vines is often caused by a fungal leaf disease called anthracnose or poor soil drainage. Raising your soil ridges higher prevents waterlogging, and staking the vines so leaves stay off the damp ground keeps them healthy longer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbiɔ oya. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ ni ooowo nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni nu akafee nɔ ko. Ni kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ koni baai lɛ akatara hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do older farmers advise me to leave big shade trees standing in my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko wo mi ŋaa akɛ mashi tsei wuji yɛ mikookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees grow best when protected from intense direct sunlight. Big shade trees act as natural umbrellas, preserving soil moisture, protecting young cocoa leaves from heat stress, and keeping the farm productive for many years.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ abu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi Buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ aya nɔ awo yibii afii babaoo.

english: Plantain trees fall over when their root systems are weakened by stem borers or root nematodes eating inside the subterranean bulb. Planting clean, healthy suckers and heaped soil around the base of the plant gives them stronger support.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ stem borers loo nematodes ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ egbɔjɔ shishifãi lɛ. Adumɔ tsei ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ muji ni abua naa kɛbɔle amɛhe. Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua amɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas make my soil better for growing maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes, which means their roots can capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them and let their leaves rot into the soil, they act as free natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okpa lɛ ni oha ebaai lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ebaatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Leaves turn yellow when maize lacks nutrients, especially nitrogen, or when excessive rain washes nutrients out of the soil. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure gives the crop the food it needs to stay green and produce big ears.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ ŋmãa mli. titri lɛ nitrogen loo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ, ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni amɛwo toi wuji.

english: Why is my cassava plant growing very tall with many leaves, but the tubers underground are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants are planted too close together, cassava uses all its energy to grow stems and leaves above ground. Spacing your plants properly and avoiding excessive nitrogen allows the plant to send its energy down into expanding heavy tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ tsei kɛ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Tsei ni akɛtoɔ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ kɛ nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs ni tsii.

english: This rot is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, shady conditions during rainy seasons. Clearing surrounding weeds, pruning extra cocoa branches to let sunlight in, and harvesting ripe pods quickly stops the moisture that fuels the disease.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ kɛ hulutsoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he koni hulu la babaoo aba mli. Ni ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpaa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ hela lɛ baa lɛ kpaɔ oya.

english: What is making small holes in the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa gbekɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ?

english: These holes are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant to feed on tender leaves. Checking young plants early and spraying organic controls like neem leaf extract directly into the funnels protects the plant's growth point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Tsei bibii lɛ akwɛmɔ mra kɛ nibii ni yeɔ wala nɔ tamɔ neem baa mli nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ. tɛ̃ɛ kɛya ŋmei lɛ mli Ebaaye ebua ni ebu he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ he.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off wet soil, maximizing leaf exposure to the sun and preventing fungal diseases caused by leaves laying on damp ground.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo. ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa ni kã shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Multiple shoots (suckers) compete with the main plantain tree for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Pruning away smaller shoots and keeping only one strong replacement sucker ensures the main stem gets enough energy to bear large, heavy bunches.
ga: Tsoi babaoo (tsoji) kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. niji bibii ni afoɔ Jiemɔ ni okɛ tso kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ lɛ ato. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfi tsei niji wuji ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt and dry out quickly when rain stops for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses moisture very quickly under hot sun through evaporation. Covering the soil around your crops with dried grass or leaves (mulch) shades the ground, traps soil moisture, and keeps roots cool between rainfalls.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ laajeɔ nu oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Mulching around Okɛ jwɛi loo baai akpã oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. (Mulch) haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa hulutsoo. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it naturally in the soil through their roots. This enriches the soil with free fertilizer that nearby maize plants can use to grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii koni amɛdara waa.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil minerals like calcium. Keeping soil evenly moist and mulching root zones helps plants retain their blossoms long enough to form fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo minerals ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ daa ni akɛ muji awo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my okra plants stay thin and produce few pods when I sow seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo komɛi kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, seedlings fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving okra plants proper space allows each stalk to grow thick, branch out, and yield multiple large pods.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baawuu kɛha hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ oha okra tso lɛ he ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ejɛ niji amli, ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji babaoo aba.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow strong. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer, or planting leguminous crops like groundnuts before maize, helps restore the green color and boost crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii baafata he Loo aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii dani aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ aba ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of big green leaves but very few beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich organic matter, the cowpea plant puts all its energy into growing leaves instead of flowering. Cowpeas perform better in moderate soil because they can naturally make their own food from the air.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli loo eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo. Cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Cowpeas tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔji ni mli tse nɔ ejaakɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee niyenii kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits in the ground for too long, the roots drown and fungus grows, causing rot. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away safely.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni ŋmeii baakwɛ̃ kɛyashi amɛbaafite. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before growing any peppers during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwie efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani edu pepper lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when the weather gets too hot or when they lack sufficient water. The heat stresses the plant, forcing it to save energy by shedding flowers. Regular morning watering and light shade help flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ amɛhe. Dɔlɛ haa tsei haoɔ ni enyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛbu hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa leebi kɛ hulutsoo yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and feel dry during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛgbi yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward to protect themselves from severe heat and conserve moisture when the air and soil are too dry. Covering the soil around the plant base with dry grass helps keep the roots cool and retains soil moisture.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he, ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden sticks to climb up instead of growing on the flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ kɛ tsei tsuɔ nii ni ekɛkwɔɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants naturally climb toward sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and capturing maximum sunlight for bigger yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛfee hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Tsi foliar helai anaa ni omɔ hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ kɛha sweet potatoes wuji.

english: Groundnut plants are unique because their nuts grow completely underground. Once the flower is pollinated above ground, the stem bends downward and burrows into the soil so the nuts can safely grow away from heat and pests.
ga: Peanut tsei lɛ yɛ srɔto kwraa ejaakɛ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kwraa. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shishifã lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Plantains require full sunlight to manufacture energy quickly and build a heavy fruit bunch. Heavy shade from big trees slows down their growth process, delaying the time it takes for the bunch to develop.
ga: Plantains he miihia hulu ni tsoɔ waa koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba oya ni ekɛ aduawai akui ni tsii aba. Tsei wuji amli hulutsoo ni mli wa lɛ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, be ni akɛbaafee kuu lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ.

english: Why do my oil palm trees produce small, empty fruit bunches during long dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Oil palms require large amounts of water to fill out their fruits. During dry months, the tree conserves water by producing smaller or empty palm bunches until the rains return to nourish the fruits fully.
ga: Oil palm biɔ nu babaoo koni ekɛwo aduawai lɛ amli ekoŋŋ. yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ Tsei lɛ buɔ nu he kɛtsɔ ŋmei bibii loo nɔ ko ni bɛ nɔ ko ni amɛfeɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa koni ekɛ niyenii aha aduawai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay open and loose instead of forming a tight ball?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ egbele ni egbɔjɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Cabbages need consistent moisture, cooler temperatures, and steady nutrients to fold their leaves tightly into a ball. Irregular watering or extreme heat causes the plant to spread open rather than form a firm head.
ga: Kaabaji he miihia ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli daa. hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ kɛ niyenii ni yaa nɔ daa ni akɛbaabɔle baai lɛ ahe ni efee bɔɔlu kokroo Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo latsaa ni naa wa haa tsei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee bulbs ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves starting from the tip in a V-shape usually means your maize lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the nutrient that keeps plants green and healthy, so applying top-dressing fertilizer like Urea helps restore growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ V su mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋwɛi ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites, or a virus they transmit. Spraying the leaves with organic neem oil solution or recommended insecticides helps clear the pests and allows new healthy leaves to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ organic neem oil solution loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ shwie baa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni eye ebua baa heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because water displaces oxygen in the dirt, preventing the roots from breathing. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the tubers dry.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings wilt in the afternoon heat even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: In intense sun, seedlings lose water through their leaves faster than their shallow roots can pull it from the ground. Adding dry grass mulch around the base of plants traps soil moisture and keeps root temperatures cool.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ he ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ Shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli fɛ̃i lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: What is eating holes in the central leaf funnels of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni yeɔ yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the growing funnel of young maize plants. Applying approved pest control early or dropping a little clean sand into the funnels smothers the worms.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni daraa lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Aloo, ŋã ni he tse fioo ni oooshwie tsɛnsi lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ajie.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and soft while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato aduawai lɛ ashishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo beni edaa lɛ?

english: This black patch is called blossom-end rot, caused by calcium deficiency and irregular watering during fruit formation. Watering tomatoes consistently and applying wood ash or agricultural lime to the soil prevents the black rot.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ fã diŋ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni faaa kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be yɛ yibiiwoo be mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tomato nɔ daa ni okɛ tso sũ loo okwaayeli mli sũ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into the sunlight so they can manufacture more food to swell the tubers below ground. Leaving vines on the bare ground exposes leaves to hot soil and soil-borne diseases, reducing your yield.
ga: Staking haa hulu la shɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni niyenii babaoo aba ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ. Wein tsei ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ baa tsei lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Having too many suckers causes them to fight with the main plantain stem for light, water, and soil nutrients. Pruning extra suckers to keep only one main stem and one successor shoot ensures you get large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo haa amɛ kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ koni akɛto tso titri kome pɛ kɛ tso yibii kome ni gboshinii yɔɔ mli lɛ he lɛ baaha oná plantain tso agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their root nodules. When the plant roots decompose in the soil, that nitrogen stays behind to nourish the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Nitrogen baakã he ahi shi koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers without producing cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers if there are no tiny insects (midges) around to pollinate them, or when the tree suffers from shade loss and water stress. Maintaining partial shade trees keeps the humidity high and protects pollinating insects.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛji kooloi bibii (teŋgbɛ nibii) bɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaawo amɛhe fɔfɔi, loo kɛ́ tso lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ hulutsoo kɛ nu he haomɔ hewɔ. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo be lɛ aya hiɛ ni ebaabu he kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my bean plants seem to leave the soil better for the next crops I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-pea tsei lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Beans are special legumes that work with tiny beneficial organisms in the soil to trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground. When the bean roots and leaves decay, that trapped food stays in the soil, making it richer for crops like maize or cassava planted next.
ga: Beans ji ŋmãa henɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni kɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii. Ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni emɔɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji ŋmeii shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ fite lɛ Niyenii ni ekpɛtɛ he lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ fɛo waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni abaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: If I add a lot of fertilizer to my bean farm, will it automatically give me a bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata mi-bean ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ Ani ebaaha mi ŋmaa babaoo lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Not necessarily. If you give beans too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant gets confused and grows lots of green leaves instead of making flowers and pods. Legumes naturally prefer small, balanced amounts of nutrients.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Kɛji akɛ okɛ nitrogen fertilizer babaoo ha o-peas lɛ, Tso lɛ baafee basabasa ni ebaana baai eŋɔli babaoo yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni ebaawo lɛ najiaŋ. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ŋmeii sumɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ bibii ni sa.

english: Why do my bean flowers drop off the plants without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ ko lɛ?

english: Bean flowers drop when the plant gets stressed, especially by extreme hot weather, dry soil, or very heavy rains during the flowering stage. The plant sheds its flowers to save energy so it can survive.
ga: Pea fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao. Titri lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli. Tsei shwieɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do some bean varieties need wooden sticks to climb while others stay short on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei he hiaa ŋmeii komɛi koni amɛkwɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni kooloi srɔtoi komɛi hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa shi nɔ lɛ?

english: Different varieties have different natural growing habits. Climbing beans produce long, twisting vines that search for support to reach sunlight, while bush beans are bred to stay short and sturdy without needing any support.
ga: Henɔi srɔtoi yɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ sui srɔtoi. Beans ni kwɔɔ lɛ woɔ wain tsei kakadaji ni tsɔɔ amɛhe ni taoɔ yelikɛbuamɔ koni amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, atsɔse cowpea koni efee kuku ni ehe wa ni yelikɛbuamɔ ko he ehiaaa lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves turn yellow when the ground stays soaked after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When water sits on the field for too long, it drowns the roots by blocking air from reaching them. Root systems need oxygen to breathe and absorb nutrients; without it, the leaves turn yellow and the plant weakens.
ga: Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebaatsi naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa koni amɛmu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii. Kɛ́ ebɛ lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do cassava leaves drop off during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?
