english: Dropping leaves is the plant's natural defense against drought. By getting rid of its leaves, the plant reduces water loss through evaporation and goes into a resting state until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ he. kɛtsɔ baai ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ Tsei haa nu ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ ni amɛboteɔ hejɔɔmɔ shihilɛ mli kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How do tiny insects get inside my dried beans when I store them after harvest?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kooloi bibii boteɔ mi-beans ni egbi lɛ mli kɛ́ mikɛto beni akpa kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The insects, called bean weevils, actually lay microscopic eggs on the pods while the crop is still growing in the field. After harvest, those eggs hatch inside your dark storage bags and the young insects start eating the dried beans from the inside.
ga: Kpluka nɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ bean moth lɛ, woɔ ŋmeii bibii diɛŋtsɛ yɛ ŋmeii anɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii miida lolo yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ. kpamɔɔ sɛɛ Nakai ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ yɛ kotoku ko ni akɛtoɔ nibii amli ni su diŋɔ mli. kɛ kooloi bibii Ebɔi ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ yeli kɛjɛ mli.

english: Why are there big holes in my young maize leaves at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bulɛi wuji yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Those holes are usually caused by fall armyworms. These caterpillars hide deep inside the growing center of the maize plant during the daytime to escape the heat, eating the soft leaves before they unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nakai bu lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmei tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛjo hulutsoo lɛ naa foi. Kɛtsɔ baai bibii ni ayeɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens to my bean crop if I plant the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-bean tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. This competition results in thin, weak stems with very few pods on each plant.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni adu lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Pods fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko nɔ.

english: Why do some of the bean seeds I saved from last season fail to sprout after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni mijie kɛjɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can lose their ability to sprout if they were stored in hot or humid conditions, attacked by unseen insects, or harvested before they fully matured on the plant.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛnyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni edɔ loo hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Kplukai ni anaaa lɛ tutuaa lɛ loo akpaa lɛ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ kwraa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant plantains on the same land as my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get burned easily under the full sun and need protection when they are small. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that provide natural shade and keep the soil moist while the young cocoa trees get established.
ga: Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. ni ehe miihia ni abu he beni tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo lɛ Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the nutrient responsible for healthy green leaf growth. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves whatever food it has to the newest upper leaves, causing the bottom ones to yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni baai eŋɔli ni mli wa lɛ daraa Kɛji nitrogen faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why is it bad if I put my cassava stem cuttings too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji mikɛ mi-cassava niji lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are spaced too closely, their leaves block sunlight from each other and their roots fight under the ground for water and food. Giving them enough space ensures that each plant gets what it needs to produce large, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Ni eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛtaoɔ nu kɛ niyenii. He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of yellow flowers, but the flowers fall off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers usually fall off without producing fruit when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes suddenly from very dry to very wet. Extreme heat damages the flower's pollen, so the plant drops the flower to save energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛyaa nɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ pollen lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: How does leaving dry grass around my growing vegetables help them survive hot weather?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni ashiɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te mi-aduawai ni miduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground around your vegetables with dry grass or leaves acts like a blanket that traps soil moisture and stops the hot sun from drying out the earth quickly. It also prevents weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle o-vegetables lɛ he lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ehaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Etsiɔ jwɛi hu naa koni ekakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up tightly like little cups and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips hiding underneath the leaves and sucking out the juices. It can also be a virus spread by these insects, which distorts leaf growth and stops the plant from growing well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Ebaanyɛ efee hela ko hu ni nɛkɛ koolooi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Enɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni ehaaa tsei lɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall wood stakes and help my yam vines climb them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni maye mabua mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ ni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high off the ground so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to produce energy, which then travels down into the ground to feed and expand the yam tuber.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya shɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. Kɛkɛ lɛ, efãa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ koni eyaye sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ niyenii ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains specific soil nutrients and lets maize-loving pests and diseases multiply in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas returns nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops droop and look wilted during the afternoon sun even when the soil was moist in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During the hottest part of the day, leaves lose water vapor faster than the roots can suck up fresh water from the soil. The plant temporarily droops its leaves to reduce water loss, and it usually stands back up as the sun cools down in the evening.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Baai lɛ shwieɔ nu mli la oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ nu kpakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei feɔ amɛbaai lɛ kuku yɛ be kukuoo mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. ni bei pii lɛ, eteɔ shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: How can I tell if a stem cutting from a cassava stalk is healthy enough to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tso nine ni afo kɛjɛ ŋmei tso mli lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eda?

english: A good cassava stem cutting should come from the mature middle section of a healthy, pest-free plant that is 8 to 12 months old. The stem should have firm buds, no visible disease spots or insect damage, and produce white milky liquid when cut.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni afo lɛ ajɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ teŋgbɛ fã ni eda lɛ mli. Esa akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ aná ŋmeii ni mli wa. Helai ahe tsɔi loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii bɛ jɛmɛ. Ni kɛ́ afo lɛ, nu yɛŋ ni tamɔ atatu baaje kpo.

english: Why do some chemicals burn my cocoa leaves when I spray them on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai komɛi shãa mi-kokoo baai lɛ beni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Not all chemicals are safe for cocoa trees. Unapproved or harsh chemicals can scorch delicate leaves and blossoms, damaging the tree's health instead of protecting it.
ga: Ekolɛ tsofai komɛi bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha cacao tsei. Tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ loo ni mli wa baanyɛ ashã baai kɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Efiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛnamɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeebu ehe.

english: How do I know which chemicals are safe to spray on my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni esa akɛ mikɛshwie mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Safe chemicals are officially tested by agricultural officers to make sure they destroy pests without causing damage to the cocoa plant or leaving bad chemical residues in the beans.
ga: Okwaayeli he nitsulɔi eka tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ amɛkwɛ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ. Enɛ haa tsofai lɛ kpataaa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ahiɛ ni efiteee cacao tsei lɛ loo eshiuuu tsofai ni eshwɛ yɛ kɔfi ŋmɔji lɛ amli.

english: Can spraying the wrong chemical affect the quality or taste of my cocoa beans?
ga: Ani tsofai ni ejaaa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ loo amɛmli ŋɔɔ?

english: Yes, cocoa beans easily absorb chemical substances. Using unapproved chemicals can spoil the natural flavor of the beans and make them unsafe for chocolate production.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kookoo ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ tsofai amli mlɛo. Tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ afite bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ, ni eha efee nɔ ni bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha tsokolate feemɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers fall off after I spray my trees with chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi beni mikɛ tsofai eshwie tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers are very delicate. Harsh or strong chemicals can burn the flowers right off the branches, preventing pods from forming and lowering your yield.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa. Tsofai ni mli wa loo ni mli wa baanyɛ ashã fɔfɔi kɛjɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ tɔ̃ɔ. Etsiɔ pods naa koni ekafee ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why do insects keep destroying my cocoa even after I spray them with strong chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yaa nɔ amɛfiteɔ mi-kokoo lɛ beni mikɛ tsofai ni mli wa eshwie nɔ po lɛ?

english: Using incorrect or unapproved chemicals can cause pests to build resistance, meaning the chemical stops killing them while still stressing your cocoa tree.
ga: Tsofai ni ejaaa loo ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ hela lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsofai lɛ kpaɔ amɛgbemɔ yɛ be mli ni ehaa cacao tsei lɛ hu haoɔ.

english: Why do pests seem to attack my cocoa trees more when I use random chemicals from the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa mi-cacao tsei lɛ beni mikɛ tsofai ni jɛ jara nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii trukaa lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Unapproved chemicals often kill beneficial insects that naturally eat pests. Without those helpful insects, bad pests can multiply faster and harm your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Kɛji kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ lɛ Kooloi fɔji baafa oya ni amɛye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: Why do extension officers check my farm to inspect the chemical products I use on my cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ miikwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ tsofai ni mikɛ mi-cocoa lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Extension officers inspect farms to stop the use of dangerous chemicals, protect your cocoa trees from damage, and ensure your crop meets market standards.
ga: Extension nitsulɔi lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmɔji amli koni amɛkpa tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ. Buu o-cacao tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite. ni okwɛ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashɛ jarayeli he mlai lɛ ahe.

english: Why does spraying chemicals on my cocoa farm require so much physical effort and proper gear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ biɔ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo kɛ nibii ni sa lɛ?

english: Spraying requires carrying heavy equipment and reaching high branches. Using proper gear ensures the chemical covers the crop evenly without harming your body or wasting product.
ga: Nibii ni tsii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ biɔ ni eshɛɔ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ehaa tsofa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe pɛpɛɛpɛ ni eyeee gbɔmɔtso lɛ awui loo efiteee nibii ni adu lɛ.

english: How do agricultural experts test if a new chemical is harmless to cocoa trees?
ga: Te okwaayeli he nilelɔi baafee tɛŋŋ amɛka tsofa hee ko amɛkwɛ kɛji eyeee cacao tsei awui?

english: Experts test new chemicals on small trial farms to observe whether they weaken the plant, harm the soil, or affect bean quality before approving them for general farm use.
ga: Nileelɔi kaa tsofai heei amɛkwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔji bibii ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ lɛ amli koni amɛkwɛ kɛji amɛhaa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. ni yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ awui Aloo enaa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ? dani akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli fɛɛ

english: Is it safe for me to spray chemical weedkillers directly near the roots of my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ yɛ kookoo tso ko shishi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, weedkillers can be absorbed by the shallow roots of the cocoa tree, causing the leaves to turn yellow, slowing down crop growth, or killing young plants.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ, ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ. ehaa tso lɛ dalɛ baa shi loo ehaa tso bibioo lɛ gboɔ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop leaves to conserve water when the soil dries out and dry winds blow. Providing shade trees like plantains or Gliricidia helps protect young cocoa trees from severe heat and moisture loss.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛhiɛ nu mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswa amɛ ni amɛgbi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo gliricidia lɛ buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Pale yellow leaves usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to grow healthy. Applying a nitrogen-based fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ŋmãa he hiaa ni ekwɛ̃ waa Nitrogen ŋmãa tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmãa ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmãa ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: What is eating small holes in my maize leaves and leaving brown droppings in the stems?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. You can protect your crop by checking fields early and applying recommended insecticides or placing neem leaf powder directly into the plant whorls.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ ŋmɔji amli ni oookwɛ mra lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ atsu nii loo okɛ neem baa powda afata tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and small cracks appear in the soil around the base of the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi ni ŋmeii bibii komɛi ba Ejeɔ kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to tie our yam vines to wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ wɔkɛ sweet potato wain tsei akpɛtɛ tsei ahe lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam vines off the hot ground so their leaves catch more sunlight to feed the tubers underground, while also preventing humid soil from rotting the foliage.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ebaai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehãaa sũ lɛ mli atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbo.

english: Why are my tomato blossoms dropping off without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shwieɔ shi ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, water supply is irregular, or there is excessive nitrogen in the soil. Regular morning watering and light shade can help fruit set properly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi lɛ mli lɛ jeee nɔ ni sa. aloo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ amli daa leebi kɛ hulutsoo be fioo baanyɛ aye abua aduawai lɛ ni amɛma shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by small sap-sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites. Spraying the plants early with neem oil or an approved pesticide stops the insects from damaging the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ afɔ tsei anɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni kooloi akafite baai lɛ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas fix natural nitrogen from the air into the soil, acting as a free natural fertilizer that improves soil health and helps the neighboring maize grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to apply chemical fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Apply fertilizer early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the soil is moist after rain. Avoid applying during heavy rain, which washes it away, or during hot mid-day sun, which can burn plant roots.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi loo shwane be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ nitsumɔ he yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni shwieɔ nu lɛ mli. loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli, ni baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi ashã.

english: Why does letting weeds grow between my crops reduce my harvest size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ miŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi shwere yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ehaa mikpamɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need to grow strong and yield heavily.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, hulu la kɛ nu. Ehe hia ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: How can I tell if my harvested maize is dried well enough to store safely without rotting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛto shweshweeshwe ni efiteee?

english: You can test dried maize by biting a grain or tapping it with a hard object. If it cracks cleanly with a sharp sound and leaves no dent, the water inside has evaporated enough to safely store it without mold growing.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni oooŋmɔ loo okɛ nɔ ko ni wa atswa nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmɔlɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ Nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa bɔni afee ni anyɛ akɛto shweshweeshwe ni ŋmɔlɔ ko akaje mli.

english: Why do my cocoa beans become moldy even after I dry them on mats in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ hulutsoo be mli gĩ amɛ moŋ?

english: Mold grows when cocoa beans still contain hidden water inside or absorb dampness from the ground. Drying them evenly on raised wooden or bamboo mats allows cool air to flow underneath, carrying away all moisture so the beans dry completely.
ga: Fuji lɛ daa beni kookoo yibii lɛ yɛ nu ni akɛtee amɛmli lolo loo amɛjieɔ nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɔfi ŋmeii ni agbiɔ yɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ tsɔɔ amɛshishi. Ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mli bɔni afee ni kɔfi yibii lɛ agbi kwraa.

english: What is the best way to keep my fresh garden eggs from shrinking and losing water after harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii heei lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɔjɔ ni amɛkafite nu yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Garden eggs lose moisture quickly through their skin when left in heat and wind. Storing them in a cool, shady, and dark spot slows down water loss, keeping the skin smooth and the produce fresh for market.
ga: Abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛhewolo nɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ latsaa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni yɔɔ hulutsoo, ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ akafite oya. Ehaa hewolo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ feɔ ehee kɛyaa jara nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables spoil so quickly when left under the sun on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔi lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight heats up harvested crops, causing them to rapidly lose water and speed up decay. Placing fresh produce in a cool shade or under a thatch shelter immediately after harvesting preserves its moisture and quality.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ mli dɔɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nu fiteɔ oya ni ehaa efiteɔ oya. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii heei ni akwɛɔ lɛ wo he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ loo yɛ nɔ ko ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nibii ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ amɛhe afee fɛo.

english: What causes my yam tubers to turn soft and rot while stored in the yam barn?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ beni akɛtoɔ sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot when air cannot circulate around them or when heat builds up in the storage area. Storing tubers off the bare ground on open wooden racks in a shaded, well-ventilated barn keeps them cool and prevents water condensation that causes rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abɔle ehe loo kɛ́ dɔlɛ bua ehe naa yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Okɛ ŋmeii lɛ ato shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ yɛ tso shĩa ko ni agbele mli yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni ehaaa nu ni shwieɔ shi ni haa tsei lɛ fiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots go bad just two or three days after digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ sɛɛ beni atsa lɛ?

english: Once harvested, cassava roots react quickly to air and heat, losing water and causing internal decay. You can preserve fresh roots for a few extra days by burying clean, unbruised roots in cool, moist soil or sawdust under shade.
ga: Kɛji akpa Cassava shishifãi lɛ tsuɔ nii oya kɛha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ dɔlɛ, nu lɛ laajeɔ ni ekɛ mligbɛ fitemɔ baa. Obaanyɛ okɛ shishifãi heei ahi shi gbii fioo krokomɛi kɛtsɔ shishifãi ni he tse ni etseee lɛ ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ loo tsei ni atswaa yɛ hulutsoo shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I keep my saved crop seeds in a cool place inside a sealed container?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ midumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ yɛ tsɛnsi ko ni aŋã mli lɛ mli?

english: Heat and damp air damage the living embryo inside seeds and make them lose their vigor. Storing seeds in a cool, dry place prevents water from creeping in, protecting their quality so they germinate strong when planted.
ga: Dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ kpataa ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ ahiɛ. ni eha amɛhewalɛ sɛɛ fo. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui lɛ to he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi lɛ, ebaatsi nu naa koni ekaje mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni kɛ́ adu lɛ, amɛkwɛ̃ waa.

english: Why do the groundnut seeds I saved from last season fail to sprout when planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei dumɔwui ni mijie kɛjɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu lɛ?

english: If saved seeds were stored in a warm or humid room, the heat damages the seed's stored food supply before planting time. Storing groundnut pods off the floor in cool, dry conditions preserves their ability to sprout.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to tsu ko ni mli edɔ loo hulutsoo be mli lɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ fiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ aniyenii ni ato lɛ dani dumɔ be shɛɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ to shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛnyɛ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop during the hot afternoon even when I watered the farm in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛji Namɔ haa tsei lɛ nu leebi?

english: In intense sun, crops lose water through their leaves faster than the roots can take it up from the soil. The leaves wilt temporarily to protect the plant from losing too much water, usually recovering as the day cools down.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ebu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants turning brown and dry at the edges during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Dry leaf edges happen when heat causes water to evaporate out of the plant faster than the roots can supply it. Spreading dry grass mulch around the roots keeps the soil cool and locks in moisture for the plant.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni egbi lɛ baa kɛji dɔlɛ ha nu lɛ ho kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aha lɛ. Ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ he ni ebɔle he lɛ Shishifãi yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛhaa tso lɛ.

english: Why are my plantain trees producing such small bunches this harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii tamɔ nɛkɛ yɛ kpamɔ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains need plenty of water, rich soil nutrients like potassium, and proper space to grow. If trees are overcrowded or lack nutrients, the plant will not have enough energy to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia plantains. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa babaoo, tamɔ potassium, kɛ he ni sa kɛha shweremɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ mli eyi tsɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo niji wuji ni tsii.

english: What simple mistakes should I avoid so I don't ruin my plantain crop?
ga: Esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tɔmɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe. Mɛni obaanyɛ ofee koni plantain ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite?

english: Avoid letting weeds overrun your farm, do not ignore drying leaves hanging on trees, and do not leave too many suckers growing around one mother plant, as they steal nutrients needed for fruiting.
ga: Tsi ohe kɛjɛ jwɛi ni oooha oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he. Kaaku ohiɛ ofɔ̃ baai ni egboi ni fĩ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ anɔ. Ni kaahã ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he lɛ Nyɛ tso kome lɛ fa tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha yibiiwoo.

english: Does spacing between my plantain trees really affect how much fruit I get?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni kã plantain tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ saa aduawai babaoo ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ he diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, planting too close together causes plants to block each other's sunlight and fight for soil food, which leads to smaller plantain bunches and lower overall harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe hulu la lɛ naa, ni amɛshiɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa plantains bibii kɛ ŋmaa fɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ baa shi.

english: It is best to keep only 2 to 3 suckers (one main mother plant, one medium sucker, and one small shoot) so they do not compete for food and moisture.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohiɛ ŋmeii 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ (tso titri 1, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ 1, kɛ ŋmeii bibii 1) koni amɛkaye niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he akaŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is not getting enough water, lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or is suffering from leaf diseases like Black Sigatoka.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ naaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo tso lɛ mli helai tamɔ sigatoka diŋ.

english: What causes my plantain trees to easily fall over during heavy rainfall or winds?
ga: Mɛni haa mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli?

english: Underground pests like banana root weevils or worms often eat and destroy the roots, weakening the plant's grip on the soil. Supporting heavy trees with wooden poles helps prevent them from falling.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ banana shishifãi loo ŋmeii Bei pii lɛ eyeɔ ni efiteɔ shishifãi Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baa shi. Tsei ni tsii ni akɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ fiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkagbee shi.

english: How can government extension officers help me if my plantain yield is lower than expected?
ga: Te nɔyeli lɛ mli nitsulɔ ko ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi aha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ mi-plantain yibiiwoo lɛ faaa fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ lɛ?

english: Extension officers can visit your farm to inspect soil and plants, identify hidden crop diseases, teach better management techniques, and connect you with government programs for fertilizers and improved suckers.
ga: Mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aya oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛyakwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ. Kwɛmɔ tsei ahe helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ Tsɔɔmɔ gbɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ nɔ ni okɛ bo abɔ nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: How long does it usually take for a plantain sucker to produce fruit ready for harvest?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ plantain sucker heɔ dani ewoɔ yibii ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Most plantain varieties take between 12 to 15 months from the day you plant the sucker to the day you harvest the full bunch, depending on rainfall and soil fertility.
ga: Plantain henɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ aaafee nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 kɛjɛɔ gbi ni oduɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛyashiɔ gbi ni okpaa ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Edamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ falɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my plantains ripen and spoil so quickly after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mikpa amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains ripen rapidly when exposed to direct heat, sunshine, or rough handling during harvest. Storing harvested bunches in a cool, shaded area slows down ripening and keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Plantains lɛ shwereɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛwo hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ, hulu la, loo akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ gbeyei nɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ to he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛshweremɔ aya hiɛ fioo, ni ebaaha amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Can I plant plantain together with other crops like cassava or cocoa on the same land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu plantains kɛ tsei krokomɛi tamɔ ŋmei loo kookoo yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, plantains grow well alongside crops like cassava or cocoa. The wide leaves of plantains provide helpful shade to young cocoa trees while allowing you to harvest food from the same plot of land.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo kookoo he. Plantain baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very quickly and have large leaves that create a living canopy, giving the young cocoa shade and moisture until it is strong enough to survive the full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i kɛyashi kookoo bibioo lɛ mli baawa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu muu lɛ fɛɛ naa.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants usually show that the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a major food source plants need to stay green. Heavy rains can also wash this nutrient out of the upper soil where roots feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli lɛ jɛɛhe. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ afɔ niyenii nɛɛ he kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni shishifãi lɛ yeɔ nii yɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards into small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking juices from the underside of the leaves. It can also happen when the plant tries to protect itself from severe hot weather and lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji tsei bɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli lɛ he.

english: What is causing small holes to appear in the leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ

english: Small holes in young corn leaves are typically caused by caterpillars, such as the Fall Armyworm, eating the delicate leaves in the center of the plant. Checking your field early helps stop them before they ruin the whole crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa. He lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni akpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather becomes too hot or when the soil rapidly changes from very dry to very wet. The plant drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself from stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake oya kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ haomɔ he.

english: Yam vines need to climb sticks so their leaves can capture direct sunlight above the ground. The more sunlight the leaves catch, the more energy the plant generates to grow large yam tubers under the soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei aniji anɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he. Babaoo ni baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ baafee hewalɛ babaoo ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why is it bad to apply fertilizer right before a heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes fertilizer off the top of the farm or pushes it too deep into the ground where root systems cannot reach it. Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil during light rain or clear weather.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ yiteŋ loo ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli. loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tse

english: Covering the ground with dry grass acts like a blanket over the soil. It blocks direct heat from the hot sun, keeps moisture trapped in the ground longer, and stops weeds from growing easily.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ naa tɛ̃ɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ mlɛo

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to be harvested from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest when the lower stem becomes thick and woody, and the bottom leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off. You can also dig gently around one stem to check if the roots are long and thick.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa be mli ni shishigbɛ tsei lɛ egbɔ ni eyɛ tsei. ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Obaanyɛ okɛ blɛoo hu atsu nii. Abɔle tso kome he koni ana kɛji shishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to stay green and grow strong. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK at the right time will help turn them green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Which direction should the buds point when I put cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Beni ashɛɔ ŋmei niji ashwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ hiŋmɛii lɛ atsɔɔ?

english: Always plant cassava cuttings with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the shoots will struggle to reach the surface, leading to weak plants and small roots.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, dumɔ ŋmei niji ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji okɛ tsei shwie shi lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ shishifãi bibii baa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Tomato plants drop flowers mainly due to extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting at the right time of the rainy season helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu yɛ be ni sa mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why is it necessary for me to clear weeds during the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛdu nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young crop plants are weak and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early gives your young crops space and strength to grow well.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha odumɔwui lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the juice from under the leaves. Spraying them with neem oil water or safe insecticides clears the insects so new leaves grow healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ nu, neem fɔ, loo tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi lɛ koni baai heei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch enough sunlight with their leaves. When leaves get plenty of sunlight, the plant creates more energy to grow big, heavy yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ amɛbaa lɛ mli. Kɛji baai lɛ ná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛbaakwɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for water, light, and fertilizer. This results in tall, thin, weak stalks that produce very small cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa loo amɛwooo kwraa.

english: It is best to water early in the morning so roots can absorb water before the sun heats the ground. Watering during the hot afternoon causes water to dry up too fast and can shock the hot roots.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ dani hulu lɛ adɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ agbi oya tsɔ, ni ebaanyɛ etswa shishifãi ni edɔ fe nine lɛ ahe gbeyei.

english: Small shoots (suckers) steal water and food from the mother tree. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to keep enough energy to yield a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso bibii (tso lɛ) juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ ato hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo tso lɛ babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why is the damp soil left behind when the lake recedes good for planting vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ ashiɔ yɛ sɛɛ beni ŋshɔ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi lɛ ni sa kɛha aduawai adumɔ lɛ?

english: When floodwaters drop, they leave behind dark mud full of trapped nutrients and natural moisture, allowing crops like vegetables to grow fast without needing heavy irrigation.
ga: Kɛ nu afua lɛ ba shi lɛ Eshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli ni niyenii ni mli edɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli nu ni mli edɔ eyi mli obɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ aduawai ni amɛdaraa oya ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ nu babaoo awo mli.

english: Do I still need to water my crops if I plant them right at the edge of Volta Lake?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu lolo? Kɛji midu yɛ Volta Ŋshɔ lɛ masɛi

english: Yes, because the top layer of dirt dries out quickly under the hot sun. Young crop roots are too short to reach the underground water level, so they need manual watering until they grow deeper.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tse bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yɛ kuku tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ niji awo amɛ nu kɛyashi amɛbaatsɔ shɔŋŋ.

english: Which crops are safest to plant if I only have a short four-month window before lake water levels rise again?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei yɔɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu kɛji miyɛ nyɔji ejwɛ pɛ dani ŋshɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ aya ŋwɛi ekoŋŋ?

english: Short-duration crops like maize, tomatoes, peppers, and okra are ideal because they mature within 90 to 120 days, allowing you to harvest everything before the water comes back.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ ŋmãa, tomato, ŋmãa, kɛ okra lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛdaraa yɛ gbii 90 kɛyashi 120 mli, ni no haa onyɛɔ okpaa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ dani nu lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: How can I make sure my crops are ready for harvest around March or April?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔɔ yɛ March loo April aaafee?

english: You must match your crop's growth cycle with the calendar by planting quick-maturing seeds in late November or December as soon as the land dries enough to work.
ga: Osumɔɔ ni okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ be lɛ ato kalanda lɛ he kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra lɛ ni ooodu yɛ November loo December naagbee gbɛ lɛ nɔ, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ okɛtsu nii pɛ.

english: Why do crops grown near water bodies during the dry season mature faster than crops grown in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ nu jɛɛhei ahe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Strong, continuous sunlight combined with reliable underground moisture speeds up plant metabolism, making the crop flower and fruit faster than during cloudy rainy months.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa ni yaa nɔ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ yaa oya. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ atatu nyɔji amli.

english: What will happen to my crops if the water level rises before I finish harvesting?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji nu lɛ tee hiɛ dani migbe ŋmɔshi nii lɛ akpamɔ naa?

english: Excess water cuts off oxygen to plant roots, causing them to rot. Standing water for more than a few days will turn the leaves yellow and ruin the harvest.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa tsei lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ́ okɛwo nu mli fe gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni ebaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How do I know how many farm workers I need to hire for my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi enyiɛ ni esa akɛ maŋɔ amɛ?

english: You calculate labor based on land size and harvest timing; large farms or short harvest windows require dozens of workers so the crop is gathered quickly before it spoils or gets flooded.
ga: Okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ kɛ kpamɔ be lɛ buɔ nitsumɔ he akɔntaa. Gbɛjegbɛi wuji loo nikpamɔ bei kukuji biɔ nitsulɔi nyɔŋmai abɔ. No hewɔ lɛ abuaa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ anaa oya dani efiteɔ loo nu ashwieɔ nɔ.

english: How should I clear and prepare soil near a lake shore that was recently underwater?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ majie shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ ni ebote nu mli ehee lɛ naa lɛ ni masaa he?

english: Wait until the surface layer stops being sticky mud, then clear weeds and debris gently so you do not wash away or pack down the fertile top layer of silt.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi ŋwɛi fã lɛ baakpa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi kɛ jwɛi lɛ blɛoo. Enɛ ji koni ehe akahia ni okɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni fa babaoo lɛ afɔ shi loo omɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my crops growing near a large body of water seem to develop spotted leaves or mold easily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu agboi ahe lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ?

english: Large water bodies create high humidity and night fogs, keeping leaves damp for many hours, which creates the perfect conditions for fungal diseases to grow.
ga: Nui wuji kɛ hulutsoo babaoo kɛ afua baa gbɛkɛ. Ha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛlɛtswai babaoo. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ adalɛ.

english: Do I need to buy fertilizer if I am planting on land that was recently under lake water?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nu shishi pɛ yɛ ŋshɔ ko mli lɛ nɔ Ani ehe miihia ni mahe ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Even though flooded land receives natural sediment, intense cropping quickly uses up key nutrients, so adding a small amount of fertilizer helps maintain high yields.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ naa adebɔɔ mli sũ moŋ, Shi dumɔ ni mli wa lɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii titrii lɛ tsuɔ nii oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo.

english: When the lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape from the tip, your maize is starving for nitrogen. Nitrogen is a key food for plants, and when there isn't enough in the soil, the plant pulls it from its older bottom leaves to feed the growing top leaves.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ, no lɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei yeɔ. ni kɛ́ nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato fruits turning black and soft at the bottom before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo yɛ shishigbɛ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit. It usually happens when watering is uneven—either too dry or too wet—which prevents the plant from moving calcium from the soil up into the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa—eyɛ mli akɛ egbi tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ—ni haaa tso lɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya aduawai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plant flowers falling off instead of turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from temperature stress, poor soil nutrients, or uneven watering. If it gets too hot during the day or if the soil stays too dry, the plant sheds flowers to save its own energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ lolo lɛ Tso lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehewalɛ he.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under the strong sun. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as living shade umbrellas, keeping the young cocoa seedlings cool and moist during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb up instead of just growing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛkɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food that grows big underground tubers. Lifting the vines on stakes exposes leaves to sunlight and air, while keeping them off the wet ground protects them from fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Wein tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baa tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, wain tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I spread my dry granular fertilizer on my maize field when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi ni ji granular lɛ shwieɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve so that plant roots can drink them in. Spreading fertilizer on dry soil can burn the crop's roots and cause the fertilizer nutrients to evaporate into the air, wasting your investment.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nu ni mli edɔ bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. ni kɛ shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fitemɔ baa

english: Why do I find small caterpillars hiding inside the center funnels of my young maize stalks eating the fresh leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai heei lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that lays eggs in the central funnel of maize plants because the tender young leaves inside provide safe shelter and soft food for them to grow.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, baai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ haa he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛha dalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during rainstorms even when the stem looks strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Plantain trees fall over easily when invisible underground pests like banana weevils or microscopic root worms (nematodes) eat away the root system, leaving the heavy plant without strong anchor roots to hold it in wet soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni anaaa amɛ tamɔ banana ŋmeii loo shishifãi bibii ni anaaa lɛ shwieɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ oya. (Nematodes) lɛ yeɔ shishifãi lɛ. Shi tsei ni tsii ni shishifãi ni wa bɛ amɛhe koni amɛmɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn completely black and dry up right on the branch before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during wet, high-humidity weather. Spores travel through rain droplets and attack the outer skin of the pod, destroying the beans inside if left untreated.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Spores lɛ tsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi amli ni amɛtutuaa pod lɛ kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ. ni efiteɔ kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and showing sticky patches with tiny white flies under them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ yɔɔ shishi lɛ?

english: The tiny white insects are whiteflies that suck the sap from your cassava plants and pass along a germ called Cassava Mosaic Disease. As they feed, they excrete a sticky waste that attracts black mold, damaging the leaves.
ga: ŋmei bibioo yɛŋ Eji ŋmei yɛŋ ni shwieɔ ŋmei tsei amli nu lɛ ni ekɛ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ baa. be mli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii Ebaashwie jwɛi ni shwieɔ shi. jeɔ kpo, ni no gbalaa ŋmei diŋ lɛ ni efiteɔ baai lɛ

english: How should I correctly apply fertilizer to my farm right from the start of planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ shishijee?

english: Fertilizer should be placed a few centimeters away from the base of the plant rather than directly on it, and lightly covered with soil so rain doesn't wash it away and the roots can easily reach the nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai fioo komɛi moŋ fe ni akɛaawo nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ni okɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fioo koni nugbɔ lɛ akajie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ana niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ oya.

english: When is the best time during the crop season for me to put fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ mli ni mikɛbaawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when plants are young and actively growing, usually a few weeks after germination, and again when they start flowering or fruiting.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni tsei lɛ darako lolo ni amɛmiida lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Ni okɛfata he ekoŋŋ kɛ́ ebɔi fɔfɔi loo yibiiwoo.

english: Is it better to put all my fertilizer on the field at once or space it out?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be kome mli loo oookɛ he ko awo mli?

english: Spacing out fertilizer applications in split doses is usually better because crops use nutrients over time, and putting it all at once risks losing nutrients to heavy rainfall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojara fɔmɔ be lɛ mli awo mlijaa mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei yeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli shikome lɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baafite yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my land before I plant my seeds or after they sprout?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ loo beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ?

english: Basal fertilizer can be mixed into the soil during planting to help root development, but top-dressing fertilizer should be added after the crops have sprouted and established roots.
ga: Yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ. Shi esa akɛ akɛ top dressing awo nɔ beni tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I can only afford to apply fertilizer once this season?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji akɛ manyɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli shikome pɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: If you apply fertilizer only once, your crops will get a good start, but they may run low on nutrients later when producing fruit or seeds, resulting in a smaller harvest than a full application.
ga: Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli shikome pɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaje shishi jogbaŋŋ. Shi niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni faaa yɛ amɛmli yɛ sɛɛ mli beni amɛwoɔ aduawai loo dumɔwui lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibiiwoo fioo fe ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I get the best results from my crops if I don't have enough money to buy full bags of fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli? Ni kɛji akɛ mibɛ shika ni fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛbaahe ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli obɔ lɛ hu?

english: Target your application directly around the root zone of each plant rather than broadcasting it across the field, so every bit of fertilizer you can afford goes straight to feeding the crop.
ga: Okɛ ohe awo nitsumɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Tso fɛɛ tso shishifã he ni eyɔɔ lɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ ohe lɛ yaa tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Will my crops still give me a good harvest if I cannot afford any fertilizer at all?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai lolo kɛji minyɛɛɛ mahe ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi?

english: Crops will still grow using natural soil nutrients, but the yield will generally be lower, and plants may show signs of weakness or yellow leaves if the soil is tired.
ga: Tsei baaya nɔ amɛdara kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Shi yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi. Ni tsei baanyɛ ajie bɔjɔmɔ loo baai ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ he okadi kpo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse.

english: Why does my land seem to produce fewer crops now compared to when I first started farming it years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo tamɔ beni mibɔi okwaayeli afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Continuous farming removes nutrients from the ground with every harvest; without adding fertilizer or organic compost back into the soil, it gradually becomes exhausted over time.
ga: Okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni abaakpa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ lɛ, ebaaje mli fiofio yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How can learning from community farmer leaders help me improve my crop yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nikasemɔ ni jɛ akutsoŋ okwaafoi ahiɛnyiɛlɔi adɛŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: Farmer leaders have practical experience with local soil conditions and crop performance, so following their proven methods helps you avoid costly mistakes with planting and fertilizer.
ga: Okwaafoi ahiɛnyiɛlɔi yɛ niiashikpamɔ ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii yɛ maŋ lɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nitsumɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, gbɛi ni ana he odaseyeli lɛ ni ooonyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua bo ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tɔmɔi ni heɔ shika babaoo yɛ dumɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he.

english: Who can I turn to in my local village if I am confused about the right fertilizer to use for my crop?
ga: Namɔ manyɛ matswa yɛ mi akrowa lɛ mli? Kɛji akɛ miyiŋ efutu mi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he?

english: You can consult local extension officers or experienced lead farmers in your community who understand the area's soil type and can recommend the right fertilizer and application methods.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyabi okwaafonyo ni tsuɔ nii yɛ oakutso lɛ mli lɛ loo okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ ni yɔɔ oakutso lɛ mli ni nuɔ shikpɔŋ henɔi ni yɔɔ oakutso lɛ mli lɛ shishi ni ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ bo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛbaatsu nii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when the afternoon sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Beni shwane hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that dry out easily in direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside them provides living shade and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ, amɛgbiɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ Emasɛi lɛ adumɔ baaha hulutsoo aba ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I not plant maize in the exact same field year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously in the same soil drains all the specific nutrients maize needs and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with legumes like beans or cowpeas refills the soil with nitrogen naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa abɛi lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ hoɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii atsakeɔ Ebaaye ebua ni akɛ nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: No, planting too closely forces crops to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and smaller yields. Proper spacing gives each plant room to develop fully.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ abɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ tsu fɛɛ tsu aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are waterlogged from poor drainage. Adding well-rotted compost or manure helps restore leaf health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout when I plant them just before the main rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ dani nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need consistent moisture to germinate. Planting too early during erratic heat causes the soil to dry out, which kills the germinating seed before it can break through the surface.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ adu nii mra tsɔ yɛ latsaa ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gboiɔ dani amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ.

english: How does leaving dry grass around the roots of my crops help them survive dry weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground, shields roots from extreme heat, and stops weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Buu shishifãi ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes through the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ko kɛmiitsɔ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely pests such as Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the growing whorl of the maize plant to feed. Early detection and applying targeted pest control into the whorl can protect your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli koni eye niyenii. Nibii ni anaa mra Ni kɛji akɛ okɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and developing yellow patches on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Curled, patchy leaves are a clear sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Using disease-resistant stem cuttings for planting is the best way to prevent this.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ cassava mosaic hela lɛ yɛ. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Nibii ni afolɔ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii beni aduɔ nii lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: Why does letting weeds grow around my crops reduce the size of my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa mikpamɔ lɛ dalɛ baa shi?

english: Weeds grow aggressive root systems that steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your crops, leaving your plants starved and unable to produce full fruits or grains.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ feɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye otsei lɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo yibii loo dumɔwui kwraa.

english: Trimming excess leaves and non-fruiting branches focuses the plant's energy directly into producing larger, healthier fruits rather than wasting energy growing extra leaves.
ga: Baai ni fa fe nine kɛ niji ni wooo yibii lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ yaa yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ewoɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni eeefite hewalɛ ni ekɛbaa baa ni fa fe nine lɛ shweremɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or the ground has too much standing water, which smothers the roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or improving field drainage helps the plant regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni okɛbaafata he loo nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ mli lɛ ni ooofee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua otsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the roots and applying mulch helps cool the ground and keeps flowers attached.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha ebɔle he lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ Shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantains provide living shade to cool the soil, trap moisture, and protect the cocoa trees while their roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he be mli ni shishifãi lɛ ema shi lɛ

english: Why do my plantain plants produce small bunches when too many sucker shoots grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ feɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni ŋmeii lɛ daraa amɛbɔleɔ tso titri lɛ he tsɔ

english: Multiple sucker shoots compete with the main tree for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones allows the main plant to direct its energy into producing large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ niji babaoo kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni he wa lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ anyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii akui wuji ni tsii.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to chew holes in the center leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ bu yɛ mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the central leaves (the whorl) to feed. Checking your fields early and applying targeted organic or chemical treatments into the central whorl helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli (whorls) koni amɛye nii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli mra Ni kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ wo ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil for too long without draining, allowing fungal diseases to attack. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges prevents water from logging around the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela aba. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nu naa koni ekafo tsei ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer so that the rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is when the soil is already moist after light rain, but not during heavy downpours. Covering the fertilizer with a thin layer of soil near the base of the plant prevents water from sweeping it away.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛbaawo ŋmɔshi nibii ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaatsi nu naa koni ekaho.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas alongside my main crops help the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When the leaves and roots break down, they leave behind natural nutrients that feed neighboring crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ, amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I stake my yam vines with wooden poles instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei awo mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach up high into the sunlight so the leaves can produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves off damp soil, reducing the chance of leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni hulu la ashɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni baai lɛ anyɛ ajie hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaatsiɔ baai anaa koni ekahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa hegbɛ ni yɔɔ akɛ baa hela baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it bad practice for me to plant maize on the exact same patch of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ gbonyo akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously in the same place drains specific soil nutrients every season and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes restores soil fertility and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi hoɔ daa be mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni ehaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa.

english: My cocoa tree leaves are turning yellow and the tree is slowly dying, could it be a problem with the roots underground?
ga: Mikokoo baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tso lɛ gbo fiofio. Ani naagba ko baaba yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ahe?

english: Yes, crops can suffer from root rot, where unseen fungi or waterlogging destroy the roots underground. When roots rot, the tree cannot take up water or food, causing it to wither even if the soil looks okay.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ ana shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ he amanehulu. Yɛ hei ni ŋmei loo nu ni hoɔ ni anaaa lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ, kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ, tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu loo niyenii. Enɛ haa amɛgbiɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ po.

english: What causes dark spots and fast drying on my cocoa leaves and pods?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli egbi ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo baai kɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ baa?

english: That is often caused by blight or fungal diseases. Moisture and heat help these diseases spread quickly across leaves and pods, so removing infected parts early helps protect the rest of the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii kɛ nakai baa. Fɛ̃i kɛ latsaa yeɔ ebuaa ni helai nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ajieɔ fã ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ lɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: What is the 'blood spot' disease on cocoa, and how does it harm my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘lá mli ŋmɔlɔ’ hela ni yɔɔ kookoo mli? Ni te eyeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Blood spot is a serious disease that creates reddish or dark spots on plant tissues. It weakens the tree's internal system, reducing your harvest and potentially killing the plant if left untreated.
ga: Là mli ŋmɔtɔ ji hela ko ni naa wa ni haa ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ baa tso lɛ fãji anɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ mli gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. ehaa ŋmaa lɛ baa shi ni ebaanyɛ efite tso lɛ kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my crop's roots are sick without destroying the plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ hela mɔ amɛ ni mifiteee tso lɛ?

english: You can carefully dig away a little topsoil near the base of the stem to inspect the main roots. Healthy roots are firm and light-colored, while rotted roots look dark, feel soft or mushy, and may smell foul.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ koni okwɛ shishifãi titrii lɛ. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ wa ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. yɛ be mli ni shishifãi ni egboi lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛsu mli edɔ fe tsutsu lɛ. Ani enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ? ni ekolɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ gbonyo

english: If I see a strange disease on my farm that I don't understand, where can I take samples for testing?
ga: Kɛji ona hela ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni onuuu shishi lɛ Nɛgbɛ manyɛ maŋɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ko kɛka lɛ?

english: You can visit agricultural extension officers or cocoa research centers. Experts there can examine affected roots or plant tissues under microscopes to identify the exact disease and recommend the right treatment.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyasara okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ loo kookoo he niiamlitaomɔ he lɛ. Nileelɔi baanyɛ akwɛ tso lɛ shishifãi loo fãji ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ amli yɛ nɔ ko bibioo ko shishi koni amɛna hela pɔtɛɛ ni hela lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni amɛtsɔɔ tsofafeemɔ ni sa.

english: Why is it dangerous to ignore just a few sick trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ maku mihiɛ mashwie tsei fioo komɛi ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Diseases like root rot and blight spread easily through soil, water, and farming tools. Leaving a few infected trees allows the disease to multiply and destroy your entire farm over time.
ga: Helai tamɔ shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ okwaayeli nibii anɔ. Kɛ́ oshi tsei fioo komɛi ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni efite oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why should I pay attention to the non-cocoa trees growing inside my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu kokoo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mikookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe?

english: Other tree species on your farm interact with your cocoa trees. Some provide useful shade, but others can harbor cocoa diseases and pests or steal nutrients from the soil.
ga: Tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ o-cacao tsei lɛ yeɔ tsakpaa. Henɔi komɛi haa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Shi kooloi srɔtoi komɛi baanyɛ afee nɔ ni kɛ kookoo helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. loo amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Can wild forest trees growing nearby spread diseases to my cocoa crops?
ga: Ani koo mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, certain forest trees act as alternate host plants for diseases and insects that affect cocoa. Identifying and properly managing these non-cocoa trees helps prevent diseases from jumping onto your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, koo mli tsei komɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ tsei ni ji enyɔ ni helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ kookoo nɔ lɛ yeɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ oyɔse nɛkɛ kookoo tsei nɛɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai akabote onibii amli.

english: Should I put chemical fertilizer right away whenever my crop looks sickly?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ hela mɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Not always. Fertilizer helps healthy crops grow, but if the problem is caused by diseased roots or bad shade, applying fertilizer will not cure the disease and can waste your money.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa. Shi kɛji akɛ shishifãi ni hela emɔ amɛ loo hulutsoo ni ehiii ji nɔ ni kɛ naagba lɛ ba hu? Nibii ni akɛwoɔ fɔmɔ kotoku mli lɛ tsaŋ helai, ni eji shika fitemɔ.

english: Are traditional methods always enough to cure serious cocoa diseases on my land?
ga: Ani blema gbɛi lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛtsaa kookoo hela ni naa wa ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Traditional methods like 'mmirekyia' have value, but modern plant diseases often require expert advice and scientific practices combined with field maintenance to fully protect your cocoa.
