ga: Kusum gbɛi tamɔ ‘mmirekia’ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ, shi bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei ahe helai biɔ ŋaawoo ni he esa kɛ jeŋ nilee shishitoo mlai. Okɛ enɛ afata ŋmɔ mli saamɔ he koni obu o-cocoa lɛ he kwraa.

english: Why do farmers usually plant plantain shoots right beside new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ plantain dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? kookoo dumɔwui heei

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, shading the young cocoa while providing early food and income for the farmer.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hɔɔ kɛha kookoo bibioo lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eji niyenii jɛɛhe kɛ shika titri ni okwaafoi náa.

english: Will plantain plants steal all the nutrients and water away from my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani dumɔwui lɛ baaju niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: In the early years, plantains and young cocoa work well together. Plantains shade the ground to keep soil moist, and their root systems operate at slightly different soil levels, so they can share the space without harming young cocoa.
ga: Yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ, plantain kɛ kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Plantains haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni shishifãi lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ srɔto fioo nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ aja ŋwɛi mli ni akpataaa kooloi bibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: If cocoa trees get too much sun, their leaves will yellow, scorch along the edges, curl, and drop off early, causing the plant's overall growth to stunt.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ ná hulu la babaoo lɛ Baai lɛ hu baafee ŋmɔŋ, amɛbaashã yɛ amɛshishigbɛ, amɛbaabɔle amɛhe, ni amɛbaagbee shi oya. Enɛ haa tso lɛ dalɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: How long does it usually take for a newly planted plantain shoot to produce its first harvestable bunch?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ feɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: Plantains grow quickly and usually produce a mature fruit bunch within 12 to 15 months after planting, depending on rainfall and soil fertility.
ga: Plantains daa oya ni bei pii lɛ, ewoɔ aduawai kui yɛ nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ. Edamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ falɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does a cocoa tree take several years before it starts producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a long-term woody tree crop that must build a strong trunk, a deep root system, and a broad branch canopy before it has enough energy to support heavy cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa ji tso ko ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ewo tsei ni wa. shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli ni tsei lɛ aniji lɛ mli lɛɛɔ dani amɛnáa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfiɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Why do plantain plants grow and mature so much faster than cocoa trees on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ daa ni amɛdaraa oya fe cacao tsei ni yɔɔ he kome lɛ?

english: Plantains are fast-growing soft plants designed to absorb water and store energy rapidly, whereas cocoa is a hard, woody tree that grows slowly to live and yield for decades.
ga: Plantains ji tsei bibii ni daa oya, ni afee amɛ koni amɛŋɔ nu oya ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo ji tso ni wa ni daa fiofio ni ehiɔ shi ni ewoɔ yibii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: Planting cocoa trees too close together blocks air movement and sunlight, creating a humid environment where fungal diseases like black pod can spread rapidly and destroy your harvest.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ni hoɔ lɛ naa. shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni afee Fungal helai tamɔ black pods baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni efite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and droop quickly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and broad leaves that lose moisture quickly. When rain stops, the leaves droop and turn yellow to conserve water so the main plant can survive until the next rains.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ koni amɛkɛbu nu he koni tso titri lɛ anyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested plantain bunches ripen and spoil so fast when left in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain ni mikpa lɛ shwereɔ ni egboɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Harvested plantains release a natural ripening gas that acts faster when exposed to heat and sunlight, causing the skin to turn black and the fruit to rot quickly.
ga: Plantains ni akpa lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa mɔ shwereɔ ni tsuɔ nii oya kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo hulutsoo kɛ hulu la mli. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni aduawai lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: How does keeping my farm pathways and field roads clear help my crops produce better yields?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔ mli gbɛjegbɛi kɛ ŋmɔ mli gbɛjegbɛi ni mikɛhaa lɛ mli tse lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: Clearing pathways improves airflow through the farm to reduce crop disease, makes it easier for you to inspect for pests, and allows you to carry out field work and harvest crops quickly without damaging stems.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni agbele naa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ koni tsei ahe helai aba shi. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa bo akɛ oookwɛ kɛji ŋmeii yɔɔ mli Ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni otsuɔ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ ni okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii oya ni ofiteee ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves turn yellow when the plants are still short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tsei lɛ yɛ kuku lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing young maize leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or is too waterlogged. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer after weeding helps the leaves turn deep green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa bibii ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tsu nii yɛ jwɛi lɛ ni ajie lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli wa ni tsuɔ nii waa.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense sunlight and heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates protective shade that keeps the soil cool and moist while the trees grow.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa shade ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ baa.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my pepper plants help them survive the heat?
ga: Bɔ ni jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ pepper tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, shades the earth from direct sun. This prevents water from evaporating quickly and keeps the root area cool and moist during hot days.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ haaa nu lɛ atsɔ oya, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: What is eating tiny holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark dirt inside the stalk?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-abele baai bibii lɛ amli ni mishiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Inspecting your fields early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract directly into the center leaf roll helps protect the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli mra. Ni kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni ji bio-insecticide loo neem ni ajieɔ yi lɛ wo tso lɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into tight balls and stopping growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ bɔɔlu ni mli wa ni ekpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies. Spraying neem oil or mild soapy water under the leaves early on keeps these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni mli ejɔ baashwie baai lɛ ashishi kɛjɛ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do the leaves on my yam vines get black spots and turn brown during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black spots on yam leaves in wet weather indicate a fungal disease called Anthracnose. Staking vines properly to keep leaves off wet soil and leaving enough space between plants improves air flow and reduces disease.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ baai anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose. Wein tsei ni akɛwoɔ tso mli jogbaŋŋ koni baai lɛ akabote shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ ni ashi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ Haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa helai baa shi.

english: Plantain trees fall over when tiny pests like banana weevils or nematodes burrow into the underground root base and weaken it. Stacking fresh soil around the base and planting pest-free suckers prevents this.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ banana ŋmeii loo nematodes lɛ bote shikpɔŋ shishi shishitoo lɛ mli ni amɛha egbɔjɔ. Shikpɔŋ hee ni akɛbaabɔle Shishitoo kɛ ŋmeii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when plants suffer from sudden dry spells. Watering regularly at the base and keeping the ground cool with mulch helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ mli egbi trukaa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ daa ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How can I know when my cassava tubers are mature enough to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifã ko da bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is usually mature between 8 to 12 months after planting, when the bottom leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off. You can carefully harvest one plant to check if the tubers are large and firm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛbaagbee shi. Obaanyɛ okpa tso kome jogbaŋŋ koni okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ dara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why does my rice field produce tall green stems but very few grain heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kakadaji shi dumɔwui fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Rice grows lots of leaves without forming grains when it receives too much nitrogen or inconsistent water levels. Balancing your fertilizer with phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to form full grain heads.
ga: Omɔ baakwɛ baai babaoo ni dumɔwui bɛ mli kɛji enine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo kɛji nu lɛ mli ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ́ okɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium to o-fertilizer lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow before the corn is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow green and strong, or it could mean the roots are drowning from too much standing water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Aloo ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ miiho ejaakɛ nu lɛ ekã shi tsɔ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during cool, rainy seasons, especially when there is too much shade and leaves are left unpruned.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i be kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ ni afolɔɔɔ baai lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees snap or fall over so easily when a strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ fãa loo egbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches; if tiny pests like nematodes damage their underground roots, the tree loses its grip in the soil and easily gets knocked down by wind.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ewoɔ aduawai babaoo. Kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes fite shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa amɛ oya.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but giving me very small roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or green manure, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves and branches above ground instead of storing food in the tubers underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ niji wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Yam leaves need to reach maximum sunlight to feed the tuber below, and lifting the vines off the damp soil prevents leaf diseases and rotting.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni eye ebua ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Ni wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akafoli hela kɛ fitemɔ naa.

english: Extremely hot afternoon temperatures or a sudden drop in soil moisture stresses the plant, forcing it to drop its blossoms to conserve water and energy.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni baa shi trukaa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nyɛ tsei anɔ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants roll up into cups during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling up leaves is a natural defence mechanism; the plant shrinks its leaf surface area exposed to the sun to save water and keep from drying out.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebaatsi baa lɛ naa koni ekagbi.

english: How do I know if the rainy season has settled enough for me to start planting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: It is best to wait until you receive at least two heavy, continuous rains that soak deep into the soil, ensuring seeds won't dry up if a brief dry spell occurs right after planting.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi kɛ hoo lɛ, obaaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gĩii yɛ be kukuoo mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ mli. beni adu lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and gives crop-specific pests and diseases a permanent home to multiply.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni kɔɔ tsei ahe lɛ naa shia ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfɔ yɛ daa.

english: Why do wild weeds sprout and grow so much faster than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni midu jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that have adapted over centuries to survive harsh conditions, allowing their seeds to wake up and take over the land using very little moisture.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛdumɔwui lɛ teɔ shi ni amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because strong, direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or leaving selected trees in the field protects young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni ahala yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do I have to stake my yam vines with bamboo or sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii loo tsei niji awo mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves off the wet ground so they can catch more sunlight to feed the tuber below. It also prevents soil-borne fungal diseases from spreading onto the leaves.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛkɛha bulbs ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it better for me to water my pepper crops early in the morning instead of at midday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi moŋ fe shwane?

english: Watering in the early morning gives roots time to soak up moisture before the afternoon heat sets in. Watering during the hottest part of the day causes most of the water to evaporate quickly into the air before the plant can drink it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nu wo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani shwane mli latsaa lɛ baaje shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ nu wo amɛnɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ anu.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the tips usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-composted manure will give the soil the food the maize needs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen gas from the air into their roots. When the plant dies and rots, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil, acting as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei gboi ni amɛfite Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Why are caterpillars hiding right inside the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm hide in the central funnel of maize because it offers tender leaves to eat and shields them from birds and dry sunlight. Control treatments need to be directed into that central funnel to reach them.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli ejaakɛ amɛyɛ baai bibii ni amɛyeɔ ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ okpoi kɛ hulu la ni gbɛ́ɔ lɛ he. Esa akɛ akudɔ helatsamɔi lɛ kɛya nakai gbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ koni ashɛ he.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering helps the plant hold onto its blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni ashwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Look closely at the leaf nodes or small bumps along the stem cutting. The buds or 'eyes' on these bumps should point upward toward the sky so the shoots can grow straight out of the ground.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ tso lɛ fã ni afoɔ lɛ he lɛ, esa akɛ ŋmeii loo ‘hiŋmɛii’ ni yɔɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ anɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots spoil so fast within just two days of digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ gbii enyɔ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni mifo lɛ?

english: Once harvested, cassava roots quickly lose moisture and begin a natural chemical breakdown that causes soft, dark rot. Processing them into foods like gari or cassava flour immediately preserves them for long-term storage.
ga: Kɛji akpa Cassava shishifãi lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya ni amɛjeɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ baa lɛ mligbalamɔ shishi. Niyenii tamɔ gari loo ŋmei ashikiŋsha ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akɛtoɔ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni akɛto be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay small even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibioo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa po lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for plant nutrients in the soil and block sunlight. Even with enough water, your crops will stay small because the weeds are stealing the essential food required for growth.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná tsei amli niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni amɛhaa amɛhe feɔ hulu la. Kɛji nu fa bɔ ni sa po Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo ejaakɛ jwɛi miiju niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and turn yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have weak root systems and delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, strong sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains or shade trees alongside them protects the seedlings from heat, conserves soil moisture, and prevents the leaves from burning.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei tamɔ dumɔwui loo shade tsei ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni otsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants full of small holes and covered in dark waste?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni jwɛi ni tsuɔ waa eyi mli obɔ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the leaf whorls of maize. Early detection and applying recommended organic or chemical sprays directly into the center of the plant help protect your crop before the worms destroy the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ anaa mra kɛ nitsumɔ. Eyɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ, ni ebuɔ onibii ahe dani ŋmeii fiteɔ he ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests when I plant maize on the same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients like nitrogen. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot drains the soil completely. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally because legumes trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the ground.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen. Kɛ́ adu lɛ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu atsɔ mli kwraa. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa lɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa sũ lɛ mli.

english: How does leaving dead plant leaves on top of my soil help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ahe baai ni egboi ni mashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with plant leaves and crop clearings—called mulching—acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the soil cool under hot weather, traps rainwater so it stays moist longer, and breaks down over time to enrich the soil with organic food for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ tsei ahe baai haa ni ajieɔ tso lɛ - ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching - lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Tsɔɔmɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ koni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni efiteɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli koni ekɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli aha onibii lɛ afee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii.

english: How do I know the right time to dig up my cassava tubers without ruining them?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni sa ni esa akɛ okɛtsa ŋmei shishifãi ni ofiteee amɛ?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You can tell it is maturing when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil surrounding the base of the main stem begins to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ henɔ lɛ nɔ Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baa ko egbɔ kɛji baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso titri lɛ shishi jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: The first rain after a dry spell often clears the dust, but the underground soil remains dry. If a hot dry spell follows immediately, your newly germinated seeds will scorch and die before the main rainy season fully establishes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be sɛɛ lɛ jieɔ sũ lɛ kɛjɛɔ jɛmɛ. Shi shikpɔŋ shishi sũ lɛ mli egbi lolo. Kɛji hɔmɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ ba lɛ, ebaanyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ baashã ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ fɛɛ aba.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight each other underground for water and soil nutrients, and their leaves fight for sunlight. Proper spacing allows each individual plant to get enough food and grow thick, healthy yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni baai lɛ baawu koni amɛná hulu la. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ewoɔ tsei ni mli tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds around my young crops even if the weeds aren't touching the crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni bɔle mitsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ? Kɛji jwɛi lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaaa gbee po.

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that drink up the water and fertilizer from underground long before your crop's roots can reach them. Keeping the field clear ensures all soil nutrients go directly to your crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni nuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ oha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii fɛɛ ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aya onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines to climb tall sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɔ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves toward the sun, allowing the plant to capture light and make food efficiently. It also keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and resulting in larger yam tubers.
ga: Staking sweet potato wein tsei lɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he, ni no haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ emɔɔ la ni ehaa niyenii feɔ jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebaatsiɔ baai anaa koni ekahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi fungal helai anaa ni ekɛ yam ŋmeii wuji baa

english: Extreme heat and erratic watering cause stress to tomato plants, making them drop their flowers to save energy. Keeping the soil consistently moist through regular watering and mulching helps the plant hold onto its blossoms until fruits form.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do the leaves of my rice plants turn yellow when there is too much standing water in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nu ni damɔ shi babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess standing water stops air from reaching the roots. When roots cannot breathe, they stop absorbing nutrients from the soil, causing the rice leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ gbo lɛ, amɛkpaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɔmɔ. ni haa ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: How can I tell if my harvested rice grain is dry enough to store safely without spoiling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmaa ni mikpa lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛto shweshweeshwe ni efiteee?

english: You can test a grain by biting it with your front teeth. If it breaks with a loud, clean snap, it is dry enough for storage, but if it bends or squishes softly, it still holds water and will rot.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka dumɔwui lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ ohiɛ ŋmeii lɛ ni oookɛmɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ akumɔ kɛ gbɛɛmɔ ni naa wa ni he tse Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto. Shi kɛ́ obɔle lɛ loo omimɔ lɛ blɛoo lɛ, ebaahiɛ nu mli lolo ni ebaagbo.

english: Why do my young maize leaves turn purple around the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ purple yɛ ŋwɛigbɛi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking phosphorus in the soil, or the soil is too cold and wet for the roots to absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ ni edɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to remain small and thin even after many months in the ground?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo beni mikɛ nyɔji babaoo ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots fail to expand if the soil is packed too hard for roots to spread or lacks potassium, which gives the plant the energy to store starch and swell its roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã loo potassium bɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ starch toɔ ni eha shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ.

english: Extreme heat dries up the pollen inside tomato blossoms, preventing fertilization from taking place. The plant drops the unfertilized flowers to save its remaining water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni fɔmɔ bɛ mli lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl upward during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up to reduce the surface area exposed to direct heat, helping the plant save moisture, or because tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids are attacking the undersides.
ga: Akɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba ŋwɛigbɛ ni la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Aloo akɛni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids lɛ miitutua shishigbɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall, thin, and weak when I plant them close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the seedlings shade each other and stretch upward competing for sunlight, making them thin and fragile with smaller total crop yields.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛye hulu la he akaŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔɔ ni yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Black pod disease spreads rapidly in wet weather because cold dampness and trapped moisture allow fungi to infect the pods before they mature.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, fɛ̃i kɛ nu ni emɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ atswa ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛdara.

english: Why does my farm soil dry out completely just a few days after a big rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli egbi kwraa yɛ nugbɔ wulu ko ni nɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil low in organic matter cannot hold moisture. Adding compost, animal manure, or covering the soil with dead leaves acts like a sponge, keeping moisture in the ground longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa yɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii, loo baai ni egboi fata he akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my planted yam seeds rot in the soil before they start sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato dumɔwui ni midu lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Yam setts rot when planted in heavy, poorly drained soil that traps water, allowing fungi and bacteria to enter the soft tissue before roots can sprout.
ga: Sweet potatoes baafite kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ nɔ. ni toɔ nu Ha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ abote fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli dani shishifãi lɛ ada.

english: Yellow lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient it needs to build strong, green leaves and produce healthy cobs. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer can solve this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai eŋɔli ni mli wa ni afee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper on the exact same spot where I just harvested tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he ni mikɛ mi-tomatoi lɛ shwie shi kɛkɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Pepper and tomato belong to the same crop family and share the same soil pests and diseases. Planting them one after the other allows those hidden soil pests to easily attack your new crop.
ga: Pepper kɛ tomato yɛ tso weku kome mli ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛyɔɔ sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai kome. Kɛ́ odu amɛ komekomei lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ baatutua oŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted beside them to act as living umbrellas until their roots grow deep enough to handle the heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka kɛyashi eshishifãi lɛ mli baawo mli bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ etsu latsaa lɛ he nii.

english: What is making ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmeii?

english: Ragged holes inside the funnel of young maize leaves are typically caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm. They hide in the leaves during the day and eat the fresh growth, which weakens the plant if not managed early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ tso hee lɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii oya.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the heat is too severe, when the plant lacks steady water, or when insects damage the flowers. Keeping the root area cool with mulch and watering regularly helps the flowers stay on.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu bɛ tsei ahe be fɛɛ be loo be mli ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ fɔfɔii Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ mli jɔ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Why won't I get a bigger harvest if I crowd more seeds closely together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibii babaoo nɔ kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo futu bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants end up fighting each other for light, air, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with many small, sickly plants instead of a few strong ones that yield heavily.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Kɛji amɛto amɛhe shi pɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la, kɔɔyɔɔ, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Enɛ haa onáa tso bibioo ko. Nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ babaoo Moŋ lɛ, ná tsei fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the air to catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight helps the leaves manufacture food, which is then stored underground to make big, heavy yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. ni no sɛɛ lɛ akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni efee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Cassava roots store water instead of firm starch if the soil stays too soggy or if you harvest the plant before it has fully matured. Good soil drainage and waiting until the right harvest time are key to firm tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baahiɛ nu mli yɛ ŋmei ni wa najiaŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lolo loo kɛji okpa tso lɛ dani ekwɛ̃. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ mɛmɔ kɛyashi be ni sa ni akɛbaakpa nii lɛ ji nɔ titri ni haa bulbs lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Weeds act like aggressive thieves in your farm; they grow fast and steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your crops, causing your crops to grow slowly and yield poorly.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi ni yɔɔ basabasa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛdaraa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ daa fiofio ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Watering early in the morning allows the plant roots to take up moisture before the heat sets in. Afternoon watering causes most of the water to evaporate into the hot air before reaching the roots.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa ŋmɔtɔ dani hulutsoo be lɛ baa. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu shwane lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide essential shade and soil moisture needed for young cocoa seedlings to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to tie my yam vines onto tall wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ sweet potato wain tsei akpɛtɛ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ?

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need sunlight to produce energy for growing tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground to reach sunlight and prevents leaf rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Staking baawó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ ni eha amɛkafite.

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is essential for green leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea at the right growth stage helps restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Ni akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dalɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from heat stress, erratic watering, or unbalanced soil nutrients. Regular watering during hot spells and avoiding excessive nitrogen helps flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ejaaa Nu ni oooha daa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ he lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my main crops help my farm soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen from the air and deposits it into the soil. Planting them enriches the soil naturally for neighboring crops while providing an additional harvest.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii nɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ yɛ be mli ni ehaa yibii krokomɛi hu baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and stopping the fruit from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa aduawai lɛ adalɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is typically caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling whitefly populations early using appropriate organic or chemical sprays prevents the virus from stunting the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Whitefly Yibɔi Akudɔmɔ Mra Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ nɔ loo tsofa ni sa tsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ akafee tso lɛ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: What is making small holes in my cabbage leaves, and why is it harmful?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-cabbage baa lɛ nɔ Ni mɛni hewɔ eyɛ oshara lɛ?

english: Small holes in cabbage leaves are caused by caterpillars, such as the diamondback moth larvae, eating the foliage. Damaged leaves cannot catch sunlight efficiently, preventing the cabbage from forming a solid, heavy head.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai lɛ amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii, tamɔ diamondback moth lɛ mli ŋmeii, ni yeɔ baai lɛ. Baai ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haaa kaabii lɛ afee nɔ ni wa ni etsiii.

english: Cassava roots rot when water accumulates around them in heavy or poorly drained soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away from the root zone.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. Cassava shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ Cassava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my maize crop stay weak and small even when we get plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni eyɛ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall can wash essential nutrients deep down past the root zone where plants cannot reach them. Adding well-rotted manure or compost improves soil structure so it holds onto nutrients during rainy periods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo, ni ebaaha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔ be mli.

english: Why do my harvested groundnuts get moldy and spoil quickly in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts ni mikpa lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni efiteɔ kɛ akɛto lɛ?

english: Groundnuts spoil when they are harvested from overly wet soil or stored before being fully dried. Drying them thoroughly in the sun on clean tarpaulins until the seeds rattle inside the shell prevents mold and dangerous toxins.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmeii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ fe nine nɔ loo akɛto dani amɛgbi kwraa lɛ, ŋmeii fiteɔ. Akɛ tarp ni he tse tsuɔ nii kɛgbiɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ hosoɔ yɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli. Koni akɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa

english: My cocoa trees are getting very old, should I cut them all down and start over?
ga: Mi koko tso lɛ miigbɔ waa. Ani esa akɛ mafo fɛɛ mli kɛkɛ ni mabɔi ekoŋŋ?

english: You do not always need to cut old cocoa trees down. With proper care like pruning, disease control, and soil nourishment, older cocoa trees can continue to produce good yields for many decades.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni ofolɔ kookoo tsei momoi lɛ be fɛɛ be kɛ hiɛdɔɔ ni sa tamɔ ŋmɔlɔ, helai ahe nitsumɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ. Kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ awo yibii kpakpai afii nyɔŋmai abɔ.

english: Is it better to maintain my existing cocoa farm or clear new land to plant fresh crops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaakwɛ kookoo ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ momo lɛ nɔ loo ajie shikpɔŋ hee nɔ koni adu ŋmɔshi nibii heei?

english: Maintaining your existing farm through proper tree care is often better than clearing new land. Upkeeping established trees saves heavy clearing labor, protects the soil, and keeps your farm producing without waiting years for new trees to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ momo lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ tsei akwɛmɔ ni sa lɛ hi fe he hee ni abaajie. Tsei ni ama shi lɛ akwɛmɔ haaa aná nitsumɔ ni akɛjieɔ tsei lɛ, ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔ lɛ ni ekɛ nibii baa ni ehe ehiaaa ni omɛ afii babaoo dani tsei heei akwɛ̃.

english: Why do some farmers choose to keep and repair old cocoa farms instead of abandoning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi halaa akɛ amɛbaakwɛ kookoo ŋmɔji momoi lɛ anɔ ni amɛsaa amɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaashi amɛ?

english: Rehabilitating old farms works well because mature root systems are already deep in the ground. With careful pruning and proper dressing, these established trees recover and fruit faster than growing new seedlings from scratch.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi momoi ni akuɔ sɛɛ akɛbaa lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ shishifãi ni eda lɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ momo. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋwɛi atadewoo ni sa nɔ. Nɛkɛ tsei ni ama shi nɛɛ baaná hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii oya fe dumɔwui heei ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ shishijee.

english: What does pruning mean for my cocoa trees, and why is it important?
ga: Mɛni ji tso ni afoɔ lɛ tsɔɔ kɛha mi-kookoo tso lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa lɛ?

english: Pruning means carefully cutting off unwanted branches, diseased wood, and extra shoots. It opens up the tree canopy to sunlight and airflow, which prevents diseases and helps the tree focus energy on producing healthy pods.
ga: Niji ni ataooo lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ tsɔɔ. Ajieɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ shade lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baaa tso lɛ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ maa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ afeemɔ nɔ.

english: What is tree dressing, and how does it help my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni ji Tso Hesaamɔ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Tree dressing involves cleaning parasites off the trunk, treating bark wounds, and feeding the base with nutrients. It keeps the tree healthy and gives it the strength to keep producing fruit over time.
ga: Nɔ ni fata tso he saamɔ he ji ni ajie tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. Tso lɛ yibii ahe pilamɔi ni atsaa kɛ niyenii ni haa tso lɛ mli hewalɛ Ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa enáa hewalɛ ni eyaa nɔ ewoɔ yibii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How does removing excess branches from my cocoa tree prevent crop diseases?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni kɛ́ afolɔ tso niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ kookoo tso mli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai anaa?

english: Thick, overgrown branches create damp, shaded conditions where fungal diseases like black pod spread easily. Trimming extra branches allows sunlight in and keeps the tree dry, stopping diseases before they start.
ga: Niji ni mli tse, ni eda fe nine lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo baa. ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa hulu la boteɔ tso lɛ mli ni ehaa egbiɔ. Kpa hela dani eje shishi

english: What routine care steps should I take every year to keep my cocoa trees productive?
ga: Ani esa akɛ makwɛ daa afi gbɛjianɔtoo ko nɔ koni mi-cacao tsei lɛ aya nɔ awo yibii?

english: Each year, you should prune dead or overgrown branches, strip off parasitic plants like mistletoe, clear weeds around the roots, and apply fertilizer or compost to feed the soil.
ga: Daa afi lɛ, esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni eda fe nine lɛ fɛɛ. Jiemɔ tsei ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ tamɔ mistletoe lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How long can a single cocoa tree live and produce pods if I take good care of it?
ga: Be enyiɛ cacao tso kome baanyɛ ahi shi ni ewo ŋmeii kɛji mikwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: A well-cared-for cocoa tree can live and produce pods for over 50 to 60 years if it receives regular pruning, pest control, and proper soil management.
ga: Kakao tso ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi ni ewo ŋmeii fe afii 50 kɛyashi 60 kɛji akɛ afolɔ tso lɛ. tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa

english: Why have some of my older cocoa trees stopped bearing as many pods as before?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ ekomɛi bɛ ŋmeii babaoo tamɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees reduce yield when they become overcrowded with unpruned branches, covered in parasitic plants, or starved of soil nutrients. Clearing bad branches and feeding the tree usually restores pod production.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafite amɛyibii kɛji amɛyɛ niji babaoo ni afolɔko amɛ. Akɛ tsei ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ ehà nɔ. loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ niji ni ehiii ni ajieɔ kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa pod lɛ feɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Can an old cocoa tree still give me high yields like a young tree?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo lolo tamɔ tsei bibii?

english: Yes, an old cocoa tree can still produce high yields if you prune it correctly, remove harmful pests, and ensure the tree gets proper nutrients from the soil to support new pod growth.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii babaoo lolo kɛji ofolɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Jiemɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni okwɛ koni tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua ŋmeii heei ni amɛdara lɛ.

english: What kind of soil is best for me to start my crop seedlings in a nursery?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi koni mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Sandy loam soil is best for nurseries because it has the right balance of sand and clay. It allows water to move through easily without turning into sticky mud that traps delicate young seedlings.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ hi fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋã kɛ shikpɔŋ sũ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya ni etsɔɔɔ muji ni shwieɔ shi ni mɔ̃ɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: What does it mean when people recommend sandy loam soil for growing crops?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛ́ mɔ ko wo ŋã ni akɛduɔ tsei lɛ he ŋaa?

english: Sandy loam soil is dirt that has a healthy mixture of sand, silt, and a little clay. It gives your crops the best of both worlds by holding moisture while still draining extra water so roots do not rot.
ga: Sandy loam ji shikpɔŋ ni ŋã, sũ, kɛ shikpɔŋ sũ fioo efutu mli. Ehaa onibii lɛ naa nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ jeŋ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiɛɔ mli yɛ be mli ni ejieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ lolo lɛ nɔ. Koni shishifãi lɛ akafite

english: How can I tell if my soil is too sticky for nursery bags?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ kɛha grow bag?

english: If you add water to your soil and it rolls into heavy, wet clumps that stick to your fingers like thick paste, it has too much clay and will make it hard for tender young roots to breathe and grow.
ga: Kɛ okɛ nu fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ waa lɛ, no lɛ kpɛtɛɔ oniji ahe tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kpɛtɛɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ babaoo tsɔ. Ni ehaa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi bibii lɛ akɛ amɛaamu ni amɛdara.

english: Why does water sit on top of my soil instead of soaking down into my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Water sits on top when the soil contains too much sticky clay, which blocks water from passing through. You need soil with sandy loam properties so water can penetrate everywhere and reach deep roots.
ga: Nu hiɔ ŋwɛi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ fa tsɔ. ni haa nu nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli Ehe miihia ni oná shikpɔŋ ni ŋã kɛ sũ yɔɔ mli bɔni afee ni nu lɛ abote he fɛɛ he ni eshɛ shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops dry out so fast when I plant them in very sandy soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil with too much sand has large gaps that let water run away too quickly before plants can drink. Adding soil components that hold moisture turns it into sandy loam, keeping water around longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ tsɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni haa nu hoɔ oya tsɔ dani tsei nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi lɛ fata sũ lɛ he lɛ, ebaatsɔ ŋã. ni eha nu lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why is it important for water to penetrate evenly through the dirt around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni nu abote shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii daa

english: When water penetrates evenly everywhere in the soil, all parts of the root system get an equal drink. This encourages plants to grow strong, balanced root systems that can support heavy yields.
ga: Kɛ nu bote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ fãi fɛɛ nine shɛɔ nu ni anuɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ woɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ja ni baanyɛ aye abua ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my young nursery seedlings rot when I plant them in heavy wet soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ fiteɔ kɛ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy soil traps too much water because it lacks sand to help with drainage. When roots sit in trapped water for too long without air, they rot and kill the young seedling.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo tsɔ ejaakɛ ŋã ko bɛ ni baaye abua ni nu lɛ atsɔ mli. Beni shishifãi lɛ hiɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ. Amɛbaagboi ni amɛbaafite tsei bibii.

english: Why do my young crop sprouts struggle to emerge from the dirt after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛje kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains turn clay-heavy dirt into a sticky layer that bakes into a hard crust under the sun, creating a barrier that delicate young sprouts cannot push through.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni shãa ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa yɛ hulu lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa gbɛtsii nii ko baa ni dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ nyɛŋ abote mli.

english: What happens to my plants if my farm land has too much sticky clay in it?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitsei lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ sũ ni tsii tsɔ?

english: Too much sticky clay makes the soil heavy and tightly packed. It hardens when dry and becomes soggy when wet, making it difficult for roots to spread out and find nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni fa babaoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ewaa kɛji egbi ni efɔ̃ɔ kɛji edɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛna niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: How does the type of soil I choose for my nursery affect how fast my crop roots grow?
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mihalaa kɛhaa mi-nursery lɛ saa bɔ ni mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daa oya lɛ he.

english: Loose soil like sandy loam allows soft new roots to easily push through dirt and find moisture, while sticky or overly compact soil acts like a wall that slows down root growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ, tamɔ sũ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shishifãi heei ni darako lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya ni amɛnaa ŋmɔtɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ sũ loo sũ ni mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbogbo ni haaa shishifãi lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What should I do if the trunk of my cocoa tree starts rotting and attracting lots of insects?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ kookoo lɛ tsei lɛ bɔi fitemɔ ni egbala kooloi babaoo?

english: When a tree trunk rots, it attracts pests like beetles and termites that feed on decaying plant material. You should cut down the infected tree and clear the rotting wood to prevent the pests and disease from spreading to your healthy crops.
ga: Kɛ tso shishi lɛ fite Ebaagbala kooloi tamɔ ladybugs kɛ termites ni yeɔ tsei amli nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ. Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli ni ojie tsei ni egboi lɛ koni kooloi bibii kɛ helai akagbɛ ashwã onibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do I see so many insects coming out whenever a dead tree on my farm breaks open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa kooloi bibii babaoo ni miije kpo be fɛɛ be ni tso ko ni egbo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baagbele lɛ?

english: Dead and rotting wood acts as a natural shelter and food source where insects lay eggs and build colonies. Leaving dead trees on your field allows pest populations to multiply quickly and attack nearby healthy crops.
ga: Tso ni egbo ni efite lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛhe kɛ niyenii kɛha kooloi ni amɛwoɔ amɛwui ni amɛfeɔ kui. Kɛ́ oshi tsei ni egboi yɛ oyale mli lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ayi afa oya ni amɛtutua ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ.

english: Can a rotting tree trunk pass disease to other healthy crops planted near it?
ga: Ani tso shishi ni egbo lɛ baanyɛ agbala hela kɛya tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, fungal rot and insect pests inside a dying tree can easily spread through rain splash, underground root contact, or airborne pests to infect surrounding healthy plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tsei ni miigboi lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛtsɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ nɔ oya. kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi loo kɔɔyɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kpe koni ekɛ hela aba tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ

english: How do I stop insects from breeding inside old tree stumps on my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafɔ yɛ tsei akutsei momo ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli?

english: You can prevent insect infestations by completely digging up old stumps, burning the infested dead wood, or applying recommended wood treatments to stop decay before pests settle in.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsĩ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ anaa kɛtsɔ tsei akutsei momo ni oootsi kɛ tsei ni egboi ni oooshã lɛ nɔ. Aloo okɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsaa tso lɛ atsu nii koni ekpa fitemɔ dani tsɛŋemɔ helai ababote mli.

english: Is it bad to cut a sick cocoa tree all the way down to the ground?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ aaafo cacao tso ni hela mɔ lɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ?

english: Cutting a severely diseased tree down to the ground—a process called stumping—is often necessary to stop rot from spreading. In many cases, it allows fresh, healthy shoots to sprout from the base.
ga: Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ waa lɛ ni afoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ Atsɛɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii lɛ akɛ stumping. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ he hiaa koni ŋmeii akagbɛ ashwã, ni yɛ bei pii amli lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwereɔ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ.

english: Why does rainwater collect and stand inside the hollow parts of my farm trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ buaa ehe naa ni ekɛ ehe woɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli fãi ni mli ewo muji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Water collects in tree trunks when the inner wood has already rotted away due to fungal infection or pest damage. This standing water speeds up decay and creates a breeding site for harmful pests.
ga: Nu buaa ehe naa yɛ tsei akutsei amli kɛ́ tsei lɛ amli tsei lɛ egbo yɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahewɔ. Nu ni ekã shi nɛɛ haa nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ yaa oya, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ fɔɔ yɛ.

english: How can I tell if a cocoa tree is completely dead and needs to be removed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo tso ko egbo ni ehe miihia ni ajie lɛ?

english: A tree is usually dead if its bark peels easily, the inside of the trunk is soft and wet, no new leaves grow, and insects are swarming the decaying wood. Removing it protects the rest of your farm.
ga: Tso ko baanyɛ agbo kɛji eshishifãi lɛ shwie shi oya. Tso lɛ mli lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Baai heei komɛi ekwɛɛɛ. ni kooloi bibii shwieɔ tsei ni miifite lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ ojie lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why are the branches on my trees turning soft and wet inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛmli edɔ lɛ?

english: Soft, wet wood inside a branch is a sign of internal fungal decay caused by excess moisture entering through cuts or insect holes. Pruning the affected branch early can save the rest of the tree.
ga: Tso ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ tsei niji amli lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ni fiteɔ yɛ mli lɛ he okadi. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji nu ni fa fe nine ni boteɔ pilamɔi loo kooloi abu mli. Niji ni ena he sɛɛ lɛ ni afolɔ mra. Abaanyɛ abu tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Should I leave old tree stumps in the soil when preparing land for new cocoa plants?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi tso momo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni misaa shikpɔŋ lɛ koni mikɛdu kookoo tso hee lɛ?

english: It is best to remove old stumps because as they rot underground, they harbor root diseases and pests like termites that will attack newly planted cocoa seedlings.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojie ŋmei momo lɛ. Ejaakɛ be mli ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ Amɛhiɛɔ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni tutuaa kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ hu.

english: Who can I turn to for help if a strange disease destroys my cocoa farm and causes me heavy losses?
ga: Namɔ ŋɔɔ manyɛ mabi yelikɛbuamɔ? Kɛji hela ko kpata mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ hiɛ ni ekɛ shika babaoo ba mihe.

english: You can contact your local agricultural extension officer or representatives from the Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD). They inspect affected farms, diagnose diseases, and advise on rehabilitation programs or support available to farmers.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyana okpokpaa lɛ nɔ okwaayeli he nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ loo Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) najiaŋdamɔlɔ ko. Amɛkwɛɔ ŋmɔji ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ amli, amɛkwɛɔ helai ni amɛwoɔ ŋaa yɛ helatsamɔ loo yelikɛbuamɔ gbɛjianɔtoi ni akɛhaa okwaafoi lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my crops so they do not rot on the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Crops show clear physical signs when mature, such as leaves changing color, fruit turning firm or changing shade, or pods drying up. Harvesting too late causes crops to rot, attract pests, or drop to the ground and waste.
ga: Tsei jieɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ, tamɔ baai ni tsakeɔ. Yibii lɛ mli wa loo etsakeɔ ehiɛ su, loo ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Nikpamɔ ni akpa sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ fiteɔ. Egbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo egbeeɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ jwɛi

english: What causes my harvested cassava roots to turn dark and spoil just two days after digging them up?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni atsa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots start spoiling quickly after harvest because exposure to air triggers rapid deterioration. They should be consumed, processed into gari or flour, or kept properly stored within 48 hours of harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ oya kɛji akpa amɛ. Akɛni kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa efiteɔ oya hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ aye, afee lɛ gari loo ashikishaŋ. loo akɛto jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How can I protect my harvested maize from being eaten by insects while it is stored in my room?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ he koni kooloi akaye lɛ be mli ni mikɛtoɔ mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Insects thrive in damp grains. Drying your harvested maize thoroughly under the sun until the grains are very hard, and storing them in sealed airtight bags, prevents weevils from damaging your food.
ga: Kplukai shwereɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni mli efɔ mli. Abɛi ni akpa lɛ ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ mli wa waa. Ni kɛ́ okɛto kotoku ko ni akɛ vacuum efo mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii akafite oniyenii lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up tight during extreme heat to protect themselves and reduce water loss through evaporation. If they stay curled or turn yellow, it means the plant is thirsty and needs water or soil nutrients.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe ni amɛha nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ aba shi. Kɛji amɛkoto loo amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye tso lɛ ni nu loo niyenii he miihia lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving plants proper spacing allows each crop to spread out, catch sunlight, and yield healthy fruit.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tsei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛɔ eshwaa, enáa hulu la, ni ewoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil moist around the base of the plant helps flowers stay attached and form peppers.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ naa amanehulu kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle he lɛ Shishitoo lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my crops stay small and weak even though it rains on my farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Water alone is not enough for plants to grow; they also need food from the soil. If your soil lacks key nutrients, crops remain stunted until you enrich the soil with compost, manure, or fertilizer.
ga: Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa koni tsei akwɛ̃. Niyenii ni jɛ sũ lɛ mli hu he miihia amɛ. Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli nibii titrii lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baakã he ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why do my cowpeas seem to help the soil when I plant them alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-cowpeas lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to a family of crops that naturally gather nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. This naturally feeds the soil and helps neighboring crops like maize grow bigger and stronger.
ga: Cowpeas fata tsei akuu ko ni buaa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster on my land than the food crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ daa oya fe niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally tough and quick to consume soil nutrients and water. Removing them early stops them from stealing light and food away from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛhe wa ni amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves of my vegetable crops covered in tiny white sticky spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ahe eyi kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: White sticky spots are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like mealybugs or whiteflies. Spraying the leaves early with soapy water or natural neem oil helps clear them off before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mealybugs loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Ni ooofɔ baai lɛ anɔ mra Soap nu loo adebɔɔ mli neem fɔ lɛ baaye abua ni afɔ he dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need taller plants like plantains planted right beside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ aná tso kakadaŋŋ tamɔ plantain ni adu yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantains act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade, protecting young trees from hot winds, and keeping soil moisture in place.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo ni he hiaa Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. ni ekwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Is it better for me to plant my crops close together so I can fit more trees on my land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting crops too close causes them to fight over water, sunlight, and food in the soil, leading to thin trees and small harvests. Proper spacing gives each plant room to spread its branches and roots for maximum yields.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ nibii fioo pɛ baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso lɛ tsu fɛɛ tsu mli gbɛɔ eniji kɛ eshishifãi lɛ eshwaa koni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, wet, and humid conditions. Trimming extra branches for airflow, clearing weeds, and harvesting ripe pods quickly helps keep it away.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, fɔ́, kɛ fɔ́ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nibii krokomɛi ni afeɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli, jwɛi ni ajieɔ, kɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ni akpaa oya lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ ehe akabɔ he.

english: What causes tiny bugs to attack my crop leaves and make them curl up and dry?
ga: Nɔ ni haa kooloi bibii feɔ ŋmeii lɛ tutua mitsei lɛ baai lɛ ni eha amɛkpãtã ni amɛgbi.

english: Insects like capsids and aphids suck the liquid nutrients straight out of young leaves and shoots, weakening the tree. Spraying recommended treatments and keeping the farm clear of wild host plants helps control them.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ capsids kɛ aphids lɛ nuɔ nu mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai kɛ tsei bibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔji amli ni akɛhaa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋa nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akudɔɔ amɛ.

english: Why do I need to trim or prune branches off my healthy-looking crop trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ tsei ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aniji loo mijieɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or non-productive branches so the tree doesn't waste food on them. It opens the tree up to sunlight and fresh air, which prevents disease and directs energy into producing bigger fruits and pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni wooo yibii lɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ akashi niyenii yɛ amɛsɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe amɛhaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baa mɔ nɔ, ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do flowers fall off my trees without turning into fruits or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai loo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers usually drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as sudden dry weather, heavy rainfall, or insect damage. Keeping soil moist and managing pests ensures flowers complete their growth into healthy fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ kɛ haomɔi kpe, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, loo koolooi fitemɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akwɛmɔ haa fɔfɔi lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is my old farm giving me far fewer bags of cocoa now compared to ten years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ momo lɛ woɔ kookoo kotokui fioo kwraa fe afii nyɔŋma ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As crop trees pass 25 to 30 years of age, their natural productivity declines and they become weaker against pests. Gradually replanting older sections with fresh, high-yielding seedlings restores high production levels.
ga: Kɛ́ tso ko eye afii 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, nɔ ni ekɛbaa lɛ baa shi, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aye enɔ oya. Dumɔwui heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ni aduɔ fiofio lɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ aha nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo.

english: How can I tell if my soil has become weak and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: Weak soil shows in your plants through pale or yellow leaves, slow growth, and small harvests despite good rain. Adding fertilizer or organic compost puts back necessary nutrients like nitrogen and potassium into the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ baatsɔɔ tso lɛ kɛtsɔ baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ nɔ. shweremɔ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo kɛ ŋmaa fioo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium aba. ku osɛɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do my crops wither during the harmattan season, and how can I protect my farm soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboɔ yɛ harmatta be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Harmattan winds suck moisture out of leaves faster than roots can draw water from dry soil. Covering the ground around plant roots with dry grass or leaves (mulching) helps trap moisture in the soil during dry spells.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulching) ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli.

english: Cocoa pods are fully ripe when their color changes completely from green or dark red to bright yellow or orange. Harvesting at full color ensures the seeds inside have developed the full size and quality required for sale.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa kɛ́ amɛhe su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli kwɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse waa. Nikpamɔ ni yɔɔ su fɛɛ mli lɛ baaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aba koni amɛshɛ dalɛ kɛ su kpakpa ni he hiaa kɛha jarayeli lɛ he.

english: Is it better to plant cocoa seeds from my own harvest or buy certified seeds from the agriculture office?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ kookoo yibii kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli loo mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ?

english: Certified seeds from agricultural officers are specifically bred to resist common diseases, grow faster, and produce significantly higher pod yields than seeds saved from your existing harvest.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi ema nɔ mi yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ. shwereɔ oya ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo kwraa fe dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ okpamɔ ni okpa momo lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear away all the large trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that scorch easily under direct sunlight. They require shade from larger canopy trees or plantains during their first few years to retain soil moisture and protect them from heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ loo dumɔwui amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ahi shi ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he.

english: How far apart should I space my new cocoa seedlings when putting them in the ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo kookoo dumɔwui heei amli kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cocoa trees are typically spaced 3 meters by 3 meters apart to ensure their roots and leafy canopies have enough room to capture nutrients and light without competing with each other.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ kookoo tsei lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji mitai etɛ koni amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná niyenii kɛ la ni amɛkɛ amɛhe akaŋ akaŋ.

english: Can I grow cassava inside my young cocoa farm to harvest food while waiting for the cocoa to mature?
ga: Ma nyɛ ma du sino ngɛ kookoo ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli. Ani manyɛ makpa niyenii be mli ni mimɛɔ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Heavy crops like cassava grow aggressively and can choke young cocoa plants by stealing essential soil nutrients and sunlight, so lighter shade plants like plantain or cocoyam are better choices.
ga: Tsei ni tsii tamɔ yucca lɛ daa oya ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anaa kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ hulu la ni amɛjuɔ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ plantains loo cocoa tsei ji tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off fresh branches from my mature cocoa trees if the leaves still look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ tsei heei ni afolɔ kɛjɛ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ mli kɛji akɛ baai lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak, crowded, or excess branches so sunlight and air can pass through the tree, which keeps fungal diseases away and directs energy into growing cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni mli ewo wu, loo ni fa fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni etsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa kookoo ŋmɔji ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when there are not enough natural pollinating insects around, or when the tree is experiencing stress from extreme dry weather or poor soil nutrients.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ adebɔɔ mli fɔfɔii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ faaa. aloo be mli ni tsei kɛ haomɔ miikpe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ mli.

english: How often do I need to clear weeds from around my cocoa crops each year?
ga: Daa afi lɛ, esa akɛ majie jwɛi ni ebɔle jɛmɛ lɛ. Shii enyiɛ kookoo tsei kwɛ̃ɔ?

english: Weeding should be done 3 to 4 times a year, particularly during rainy periods, to stop fast-growing weeds from stealing groundwater and fertilizer from your cocoa roots.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ shii 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ afi mli, titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Enɛ ji koni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ akaju shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛɔ kookoo shishifãi amli lɛ.

english: How do I spot black pod disease on my cocoa trees before it spreads to my entire farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana black pod hela yɛ kookoo tsei anɔ dani egbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: Black pod disease starts as small brown spots on the pods that rapidly darken into full black patches, often accompanied by a white powdery coating during damp or rainy weather.
