ga: Black pod hela lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ, ni efeɔ duŋ oya ni etsɔɔ ŋmeii diji ni eyi obɔ Bei pii lɛ, akɛ powda yɛŋ woɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be loo nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ.

english: What causes the dark, burnt-looking spots on my young cocoa stems and pods during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni kɛ shãa ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ baa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: These dry spots are caused by mirid insects (capsids) that pierce the bark and pods to suck out sap, which causes the tissues to die and leaves dark wounds on the tree.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ hei ni egbi nɛɛ baa ji kooloi bibii babaoo (capsids) ni tsɔɔ tso lɛ yibii kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛnu nu lɛ mli nu lɛ. Enɛ haa fãji lɛ gboɔ ni eshiɔ pilamɔi diji yɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my farm's soil is missing key nutrients without taking it to a laboratory?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛji mikɛteee laboratorio?

english: Yellow leaves, weak stems, and trees that consistently produce tiny or stunted pods are strong signs that your soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, potassium, or phosphorus.
ga: baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ shishifã ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tsei ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii Dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, potassium, loo phosphorus bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants turn yellow while the crops are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for food, specifically nitrogen. When the soil lacks nutrients, the maize plant cannot make green leaves, which slows down its growth and reduces your final harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ji niyenii bolɔmɔ. titri lɛ nitrogen Beni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Abele nyɛŋ afee baai eŋɔli. Enɛ baaha shweremɔ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaaha onaagbee ŋmaa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm right after harvesting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji mikpa ŋmeii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas feed the soil naturally. Their roots pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth, which refreshes the soil for the next crop without buying expensive artificial fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei ji adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Amɛshishifãi lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tseɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and stop growing normally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ bɔ ni sa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap out of the young leaves, or passing a virus to the plant. This damages the leaf structure and stops the crop from growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo ekɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ haa tsei Enɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni ehaaa tso lɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my maize leaves and waste in the middle of the stalks?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baa?

english: This is a sign of the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It hides in the central whorl of the maize plant during the day and eats the tender leaves, which can ruin the farm if left untreated.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm he okadi. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii, ni baanyɛ afite ŋmɔ ko kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without turning into fruits during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry winds like the Harmattan cause flower drop. When temperatures get too high, the pollen inside the flower dries out, so fruit cannot form, and the plant drops the flower to save water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi tamɔ harmattan haa fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai nyɛɛɛ afee. Ni tsei baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he.

english: Why do crops generally grow much faster during the major rainy season compared to the minor rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii daa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ mli kɛ akɛto nugbɔshiimɔ fioo be lɛ he lɛ?

english: The major rainy season offers longer periods of steady moisture, warm soil, and consistent sunlight. This combination creates ideal conditions for plants to drink water, manufacture their food, and grow rapidly.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ daa. Nɛkɛ tsakpaa nɛɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsei ni amɛnuɔ nu, amɛwoɔ niyenii, ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the ground if heavy rain falls right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa dani akpa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains waterlog the land, water replaces the air in the soil, causing the roots to suffocate and decay quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu yiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu baaye kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting and becoming soft while stored in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo kɛ́ akɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are living seeds. When stored in warm, humid conditions, they break their natural rest period and use the moisture stored inside the tuber to grow new sprouts, making the yam shrink and turn soft.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii ji dumɔwui ni hiɛ ka. Kɛ akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ Ebaafite adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ. ni okɛ nu ni ato yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ atsu nii ni okɛkwɛ dumɔwui heei. Ha sweet potato lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee blɛoo.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when they start carrying heavy bunches of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ebɔi aduawai babaoo womɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees do not have deep taproots; their root systems are shallow and spread out near the surface. As the heavy bunch grows, it makes the plant top-heavy, requiring wooden props to support the weight.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Eshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji kuu lɛ da Ehaa tso lɛ tsiimɔ waa. Esa akɛ ekɛ tso atsu nii ni ekɛfi tsɔne ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Can the cutlass or pruning shears I use on one tree spread sickness to another tree on my farm?
ga: Ani dade loo tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ tsei ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ tso kome nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã tso kroko ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, farm tools can carry microscopic germs from a sick tree to a healthy one. When you cut a healthy tree with an uncleaned tool, you transfer the disease directly into its open wood.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔ mli nibii baanyɛ aŋɔ helai bibii ni anaa kɛjɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Beni okɛ dɛŋdadei ni he tseee shwieɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Obaagbɛ hela lɛ oshwã koo ni mli tse lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why is it important to clean or disinfect my farm tools before cutting my crop trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsumɔ miŋmɔ mli nibii amli loo mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ helai awo mli dani mafo tsei lɛ?

english: Cleaning your tools destroys hidden disease germs sitting on the blade. This stops you from accidentally infecting your trees when you prune branches or harvest fruit.
ga: Odɛŋdadei lɛ amli ni oootsumɔ lɛ kpataa helai ni yɔɔ tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ ahiɛ. Enɛ baatsi hela ni baa otso lɛ nɔ yɛ oshara mli beni ofoɔ tsei aniji loo okpaa aduawai lɛ naa.
